### Samples

#### Order the tree

A server handler reads the tree on each coalesced `tree-changed` event and submits `set-decoration` with only a `sort-key` for nodes whose key changed. It uses [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/), the [tree.read](/pages/capability-tree-read/) and [tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/) grants, [events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/), the [event list](/pages/api-events/) and [tree chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/).

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::tree;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetDecorationSpec;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct TreeOrder {
    keys: HashMap<NodeId, i64>,
}

impl Lifecycle for TreeOrder {}

impl Handler for TreeOrder {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::TreeChanged(nodes) = event else { continue };
            for node in nodes {
                let Some(view) = tree::get(node) else { continue };
                let key = sort_key(&view.title);
                if self.keys.get(&node) == Some(&key) { continue; }
                self.keys.insert(node, key);
                submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
                    sort_key: Some(key),
                    ..SetDecorationSpec::text(node, "order", "")
                })));
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}

// Alphabetical by the first four bytes of the lower-case title.
fn sort_key(title: &str) -> i64 {
    title.to_lowercase().bytes().take(4).fold(0, |key, byte| key * 256 + i64::from(byte))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as tree from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const keys = new Map<bigint, bigint>();
let next = 1n;

// Alphabetical by the first four bytes of the lower-case title.
const sortKey = (title: string): bigint =>
  [...new TextEncoder().encode(title.toLowerCase()).slice(0, 4)]
    .reduce((key, byte) => key * 256n + BigInt(byte), 0n);

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'tree-changed') continue;
      for (const node of event.val) {
        const view = tree.get(node);
        if (view === undefined) continue;
        const key = sortKey(view.title);
        if (keys.get(node) === key) continue;
        keys.set(node, key);
        submissions.push({
          intent: { tag: 'set-decoration', val: {
            node, slot: 'order', content: [], icon: undefined, sortKey: key, persist: false,
          } },
          correlation: next++,
          dedupKey: undefined,
        });
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### New group or folder

The client command `New group` cannot create nodes itself. It sends a message to its own server side, which submits `create-group` or `create-folder` and logs the outcome. Messages between the two sides of one plugin need no grant. Pages: [tree structure intents](/pages/api-intent-tree-structure/), [tree.write](/pages/capability-tree-write/), [tree.restructure](/pages/capability-tree-restructure/), [commands](/pages/api-commands/), [worlds and sides](/pages/worlds-and-sides/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{
    CreateFolderSpec, CreateGroupSpec, MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide,
};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::Placement;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};

// Client side: the command forwards the selected node and the wanted kind.
fn forward(selected: NodeId, kind: &str) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.tree".into(), side: PluginSide::Server, client: None },
        channel: kind.into(),
        payload: selected.to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
    }))
}

// Server side: Event::Message arrives with the same channel and payload.
fn create(channel: &str, payload: &[u8]) -> Option<Submission> {
    let parent = NodeId::from_le_bytes(payload.try_into().ok()?);
    let intent = match channel {
        "new-group" => Intent::CreateGroup(CreateGroupSpec {
            parent, title: "New group".into(), placement: Placement::InsideLast, children: vec![],
        }),
        "new-folder" => Intent::CreateFolder(CreateFolderSpec { parent, title: "New folder".into(), path: None }),
        _ => return None,
    };
    Some(Submission::keyed(intent, format!("{channel}-{parent}")))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

// Client side: the command forwards the selected node and the wanted kind.
const forward = (selected: bigint, kind: string): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'message', val: {
    to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.tree', side: 'server', client: undefined },
    channel: kind,
    payload: new Uint8Array(new BigUint64Array([selected]).buffer),
  } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});

// Server side: the message event carries the same channel and payload.
function create(channel: string, payload: Uint8Array): Submission | undefined {
  const parent = new DataView(payload.buffer, payload.byteOffset).getBigUint64(0, true);
  const intent = channel === 'new-group'
    ? { tag: 'create-group', val: { parent, title: 'New group', placement: 'inside-last', children: [] } } as const
    : channel === 'new-folder'
      ? { tag: 'create-folder', val: { parent, title: 'New folder', path: undefined } } as const
      : undefined;
  return intent && { intent, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: `${channel}-${parent}` };
}
```

#### Move and rename without overriding the user

A move keeps placement with `inside-last`. A rename carries `expected-revision` and the source `inferred`, so a name the user typed always wins. On `refused(conflict)` the plugin stops and does not retry. Pages: [intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{MoveNodeSpec, RenameNodeSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::Placement;

fn move_and_rename(node: NodeId, target: NodeId, title: &str, revision: u64) -> Vec<Submission> {
    vec![
        Submission::new(Intent::MoveNode(MoveNodeSpec {
            node, target, placement: Placement::InsideLast,
        })),
        Submission::new(Intent::RenameNode(RenameNodeSpec {
            node,
            title: title.into(),
            expected_revision: Some(revision),
        })),
    ]
}

fn on_completed(result: RequestResult) {
    if let Outcome::Refused(error) = result.outcome {
        if error.code == ErrorCode::Conflict {
            log::log(Level::Info, "manual name kept; not retrying");
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import type { Submission, RequestResult } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const moveAndRename = (node: bigint, target: bigint, title: string, revision: bigint): Submission[] => [
  { intent: { tag: 'move-node', val: { node, target, placement: 'inside-last' } },
    correlation: 10n, dedupKey: undefined },
  { intent: { tag: 'rename-node', val: { node, title, source: 'inferred', expectedRevision: revision } },
    correlation: 11n, dedupKey: undefined },
];

function onCompleted(result: RequestResult): void {
  if (result.outcome.tag === 'refused' && result.outcome.val.code === 'conflict') {
    log('info', 'manual name kept; not retrying');
  }
}
```

#### Bookmarks and locks

Bookmark and lock flags survive restarts and protect nodes from closing. The plugin keeps its own bookmark flag with `tree.set-metadata`, mirrors it with `set-bookmarked` and locks with `set-node-locked`, so a later `close-node` is refused with `refused(conflict)`. Pages: [tree.metadata](/pages/capability-tree-metadata/), [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/), [tree structure intents](/pages/api-intent-tree-structure/) and [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::tree;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{SetBookmarkedSpec, SetNodeLockedSpec};

fn protect(node: NodeId) -> Result<Vec<Submission>, PluginError> {
    tree::set_metadata(node, vec![1])?; // 1 = bookmarked, empty = not
    Ok(vec![
        Submission::new(Intent::SetBookmarked(SetBookmarkedSpec { node, bookmarked: true })),
        Submission::new(Intent::SetNodeLocked(SetNodeLockedSpec { node, locked: true })),
        // Refused with conflict while the lock is set:
        Submission::new(Intent::CloseNode(node)),
    ])
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as tree from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function protect(node: bigint): Submission[] {
  tree.setMetadata(node, new Uint8Array([1])); // 1 = bookmarked, empty = not
  return [
    { intent: { tag: 'set-bookmarked', val: { node, bookmarked: true } }, correlation: 20n, dedupKey: undefined },
    { intent: { tag: 'set-node-locked', val: { node, locked: true } }, correlation: 21n, dedupKey: undefined },
    // Refused with conflict while the lock is set:
    { intent: { tag: 'close-node', val: { node } }, correlation: 22n, dedupKey: undefined },
  ];
}
```

#### Remove empty groups

A group that loses its last child disappears unless it is locked or bookmarked. On `node-removed` the plugin looks up the former parent from its own map, and if it has no children and no flag it submits `close-node`. Pages: [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/), [lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::tree;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct EmptyGroups {
    parents: HashMap<NodeId, NodeId>, // child -> parent, refreshed on tree-changed
}

impl Lifecycle for EmptyGroups {}

impl Handler for EmptyGroups {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::TreeChanged(nodes) => {
                    for node in nodes {
                        if let Some(parent) = tree::get(node).and_then(|view| view.parent) {
                            self.parents.insert(node, parent);
                        }
                    }
                }
                Event::NodeRemoved(node) => {
                    let Some(parent) = self.parents.remove(&node) else { continue };
                    let Some(view) = tree::get(parent) else { continue };
                    let flagged = view.locked || tree::metadata(parent).is_some_and(|b| b == [1]);
                    if tree::children(parent).is_empty() && !flagged {
                        submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::CloseNode(parent)));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as tree from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const parents = new Map<bigint, bigint>(); // child -> parent, refreshed on tree-changed
let next = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'tree-changed') {
        for (const node of event.val) {
          const parent = tree.get(node)?.parent;
          if (parent !== undefined) parents.set(node, parent);
        }
      } else if (event.tag === 'node-removed') {
        const parent = parents.get(event.val);
        parents.delete(event.val);
        const view = parent === undefined ? undefined : tree.get(parent);
        if (parent === undefined || view === undefined) continue;
        const flagged = view.locked || tree.metadata(parent)?.[0] === 1;
        if (tree.children(parent).length === 0 && !flagged) {
          submissions.push({ intent: { tag: 'close-node', val: { node: parent } }, correlation: next++, dedupKey: undefined });
        }
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### Right-click menu for a node

A right click on a tree row sends `context-requested`. The plugin remembers the node and renders a `menu` from [collections](/pages/widgets-collections/) with the actions that apply to it. Choosing an item sends the matching intent.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Handler for TreeMenu {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            let Some(node) = action.key.strip_prefix("row-") else { continue };
            match (action.kind, action.value) {
                (ActionKind::ContextRequested, _) => self.menu_node = Some(node.to_string()),
                (ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(item)) if item == "lock" => {
                    return vec![Submission::new(Intent::SetNodeLocked(SetNodeLockedSpec {
                        node: node.parse().unwrap_or_default(), locked: true,
                    }))];
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

// In Views::render, when a node is selected for the menu:
fn menu(tree: &mut Tree, node: &str) -> NodeId {
    tree.menu("Node actions").items(vec![
        MenuItem::new("rename", "Rename"),
        MenuItem::new("lock", "Lock"),
        MenuItem::new("close", "Close").danger(),
    ]).key(format!("menu-{node}"))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let menuNode: string | undefined;

export const { handler } = definePlugin({
  handler: {
    onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
      const out: Submission[] = [];
      for (const event of batch) {
        if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || !event.val.key.startsWith('row-')) continue;
        const { kind, value, key } = event.val;
        const node = key.slice('row-'.length);
        if (kind === 'context-requested') menuNode = node;
        if (kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'text' && value.val === 'lock') {
          out.push({ intent: { tag: 'set-node-locked', val: { node, locked: true } }, correlation: 1n });
        }
      }
      return out;
    },
  },
});

// In the render function, when menuNode is set:
// tree.menu('Node actions', [{ id: 'rename', label: 'Rename' }, { id: 'lock', label: 'Lock' }, { id: 'close', label: 'Close', danger: true }]);
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.tree` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.tree/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.tree/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before-move` | hook (veto) | Refuse a drag or move of a node before the tree applies it. | node, from_parent, to_parent, index, source (mouse, keys, command, plugin) | standard |
| `before-close` | hook (veto) | Refuse closing a pane or group, for example while work is unsaved. | node, kind, has_children | standard |
| `node-sorts` | collect | Add a sort order to the tree Order By choice. | entry: id, title, slot (a decoration slot whose sort-key orders siblings) | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.tree/bookmarks`: list, add, remove: read and edit the project bookmarks

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.tree/changed`: { node, change } after any structural change

Decoration slots, row actions and display modes of every plugin are drawn by the tree.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.tree"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Refuses to close the pane that runs the build, with the reason `Build still running`

A package adds a `veto` handler. Handlers run until one refuses.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.tree/before-close"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.tree/before-close",
        "id": "keep-build-pane",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "keep_build_pane"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "keep_build_pane" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: node, kind, has_children
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Refuse("reason".into())
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'keep_build_pane') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: node, kind, has_children
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'refuse', val: 'reason' };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Layout

## Layout

The Layout plugin (`ilium.core.layout`, side both) owns split views and the arrangement of panes on screen: splitting four ways, mixed splits of terminal, editor and board panes, focus and navigation, and resizing with the mouse. The kernel keeps the layout solver. The plugin reads pane geometry, draws a layout preview panel and asks for splits and sizes with intents.

### What it covers

- Split views and layouts, four ways (Panes and layout, Split views).
- Mouse routing, hit targets, focus and navigation (Getting started, Using the mouse; Panes and layout, Focus and navigation).
- Board panes and editor panes in splits, so one screen can mix terminals, editors and boards (Panes and layout, Board panes and Split views).

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/03-mixed-splits.gif" alt="A terminal, an editor and a board share one screen in a mixed split" loading="lazy"><figcaption>A mixed split. Terminal, editor and board panes sit side by side, and focus moves between them.</figcaption></figure>

### Samples

#### Split four ways

A command splits the focused pane right, left, up or down. The client commands `Split right`, `Split left`, `Split up` and `Split down` send the focused pane to the server side, which submits `create-split` with a new terminal pane. Pages: [tree structure intents](/pages/api-intent-tree-structure/), [tree.restructure](/pages/capability-tree-restructure/), [commands](/pages/api-commands/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/). The direction of a split is `horizontal` or `vertical`; left and up place the new pane first.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{CreatePaneSpec, CreateSplitSpec, MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::SplitDirection;

// Client side: Event::CommandInvoked with command "split-left" and so on.
fn forward(command: &str, focused: NodeId) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.layout".into(), side: PluginSide::Server, client: None },
        channel: command.into(),
        payload: focused.to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
    }))
}

// Server side: create the pane first; its ok-node outcome carries the new id.
fn new_pane() -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::CreatePane(CreatePaneSpec::kind("ilium.terminal")))
}

fn join(focused: NodeId, created: NodeId, channel: &str) -> Submission {
    let (panes, direction) = match channel {
        "split-right" => (vec![focused, created], SplitDirection::Vertical),
        "split-left" => (vec![created, focused], SplitDirection::Vertical),
        "split-down" => (vec![focused, created], SplitDirection::Horizontal),
        _ => (vec![created, focused], SplitDirection::Horizontal),
    };
    Submission::new(Intent::CreateSplit(CreateSplitSpec { panes, direction }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

// Client side: event.tag === 'command-invoked' with command 'split-left' and so on.
const forward = (command: string, focused: bigint): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'message', val: {
    to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.layout', side: 'server', client: undefined },
    channel: command,
    payload: new Uint8Array(new BigUint64Array([focused]).buffer),
  } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});

// Server side: create the pane first; its ok-node outcome carries the new id.
const newPane = (): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'create-pane', val: {
    parent: undefined, title: 'shell', contentKind: 'ilium.terminal',
    cwd: undefined, command: undefined, initialInput: undefined,
  } },
  correlation: 2n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});

const join = (focused: bigint, created: bigint, channel: string): Submission => {
  const vertical = channel === 'split-right' || channel === 'split-left';
  const after = channel === 'split-right' || channel === 'split-down';
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'create-split', val: {
      panes: after ? [focused, created] : [created, focused],
      direction: vertical ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal',
    } },
    correlation: 3n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
};
```

#### Follow focus and size

The client keeps a map from pane to columns and rows from `pane-resized`. On `pane-focused` it reads `panes.info` and shows the title in its panel. Pages: [panes](/pages/api-panes/), [panes.read](/pages/capability-panes-read/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::panes;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct FocusTracker {
    sizes: HashMap<NodeId, (u16, u16)>,
    focused_title: String,
}

impl Lifecycle for FocusTracker {}

impl Handler for FocusTracker {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::PaneResized(resized) => {
                    self.sizes.insert(resized.node, (resized.columns, resized.rows));
                }
                Event::PaneFocused(Some(node)) => {
                    if let Some(info) = panes::info(node) {
                        self.focused_title = info.title;
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as panes from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/panes';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const sizes = new Map<bigint, [number, number]>();
let focusedTitle = '';

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'pane-resized') {
        sizes.set(event.val.node, [event.val.columns, event.val.rows]);
      } else if (event.tag === 'pane-focused' && event.val !== undefined) {
        focusedTitle = panes.info(event.val)?.title ?? focusedTitle;
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() { /* see the preview panel below */ return tree(paragraph([[span(focusedTitle)]])); },
});
```

#### Layout preview panel

A client panel draws the current split tree as boxes. It renders nested `layout` and `split` widgets with `separator` rules for the live split tree and a `canvas` thumbnail of the pane rectangles. Pages: [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/), [UI model](/pages/ui-model/), [retained mode](/pages/retained-mode/), [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/) and [data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{Shape, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::{Color, ColorRole};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Views for FocusTracker {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let left = tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("api")]]).key("left");
        let right = tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("main.rs")]]).key("right");
        let panes = tree.split(Direction::Horizontal).key("preview").position(500).child(left).child(right);
        let rule = tree.separator(Direction::Horizontal).label("Pane sizes");
        let thumbnail = tree
            .canvas((0.0, 100.0), (0.0, 50.0))
            .shapes(vec![
                Shape::rectangle(0.0, 0.0, 50.0, 50.0, Color::role(ColorRole::Accent)),
                Shape::rectangle(50.0, 0.0, 50.0, 50.0, Color::role(ColorRole::Muted)),
            ])
            .key("thumbnail");
        let root = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(6)])
            .child(panes)
            .child(rule)
            .child(thumbnail);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import {
  canvas, fill, layout, length, paragraph, separator, span, split, tree,
} from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import { role } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function renderPreview() {
  const left = paragraph([[span('api')]], { key: 'left' });
  const right = paragraph([[span('main.rs')]], { key: 'right' });
  const panes = split({ direction: 'horizontal', key: 'preview', position: 500 }, [left, right]);
  const rule = separator({ direction: 'horizontal', label: 'Pane sizes' });
  const thumbnail = canvas([0, 100], [0, 50], {
    key: 'thumbnail',
    shapes: [
      { tag: 'rectangle', x: 0, y: 0, width: 50, height: 50, color: role('accent') },
      { tag: 'rectangle', x: 50, y: 0, width: 50, height: 50, color: role('muted') },
    ],
  });
  return tree(layout({ direction: 'vertical', constraints: [fill(1), length(1), length(6)] },
    [panes, rule, thumbnail]));
}
```

#### Drag the divider

Dragging the divider in the preview resizes the real panes. The client handles the `view-pointer` drag on the `split` divider, converts it to columns and messages the server side, which submits `resize-pane`. It pauses while `view-visibility` is false. `api-pointer` describes the `view-pointer` record. Pages: [pointer](/pages/api-pointer/), [pane lifecycle intents](/pages/api-intent-pane-lifecycle/), [panes.lifecycle](/pages/capability-panes-lifecycle/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide, ResizePaneSpec};

// Client side
fn on_drag(&mut self, divider_column: u16) -> Option<Submission> {
    if !self.visible { return None; } // set from Event::ViewVisibility
    let columns = divider_column.saturating_mul(self.columns_per_cell);
    Some(Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.layout".into(), side: PluginSide::Server, client: None },
        channel: "resize".into(),
        payload: [self.focused.to_le_bytes().to_vec(), columns.to_le_bytes().to_vec()].concat(),
    })))
}

// Server side: refused(conflict) names the neighbour that blocks the size.
fn resize(pane: NodeId, columns: u16) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::ResizePane(ResizePaneSpec { pane, columns: Some(columns), rows: None }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

// Client side
function onDrag(dividerColumn: number): Submission | undefined {
  if (!visible) return undefined; // set from the 'view-visibility' event
  const columns = dividerColumn * columnsPerCell;
  const payload = new Uint8Array(10);
  new DataView(payload.buffer).setBigUint64(0, focused, true);
  new DataView(payload.buffer).setUint16(8, columns, true);
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'message', val: {
      to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.layout', side: 'server', client: undefined },
      channel: 'resize', payload,
    } },
    correlation: 4n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}

// Server side: refused(conflict) names the neighbour that blocks the size.
const resize = (pane: bigint, columns: number): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'resize-pane', val: { pane, columns, rows: undefined } },
  correlation: 5n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.layout` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.layout/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.layout/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layout-presets` | collect | Offer a named split layout in the layout chooser. | entry: id, title, template (nested split description with pane-kind placeholders) | standard |
| `before-split` | hook (veto) | Refuse a split, for example above a pane count the plugin allows. | node, direction, pane_count | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.layout/presets`: list, apply: list the layout presets and apply one to a group

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.layout/changed`: { group, split_count } after a split is added, removed or resized

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.layout"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds a three-pane review layout to the layout chooser

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.layout/layout-presets"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.layout/layout-presets",
        "id": "review-trio",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Review trio",
          "template": "h(agent, v(editor, terminal))"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Terminal

## Terminal

The Terminal plugin (`ilium.core.terminal`, side both) owns terminal panes as plugins see them: pane processes and their signals, screen reads, scrollback history, typed and pasted input, clickable links, pane titles from the terminal and screen transfer between panes. Emulation stays in the kernel. The plugin uses the [terminal primitive](/pages/primitives-terminal/) to read and write, and embeds a live pane with the `terminal-view` widget.

### What it covers

- Pane processes: each terminal pane runs one program (Panes and layout, Terminal panes).
- Terminal emulation and screen state (How it works, Client and server).
- The terminal view, scrolling, history and the scrollback budget (Panes and layout, Scrolling and history; Settings, Terminal).
- Input and paste, and the literal prefix (Getting started, Keys while a pane is focused).
- Clickable links in terminal output (Smart Copy, What Smart Copy recognises).
- Screen transfer between panes (Smart Copy, Screen transfer between panes).
- Pane titles set by the terminal with OSC sequences (Titles and instructions, When a title is applied).

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/05-screen-transfer.gif" alt="The screen of one terminal pane is pasted into another pane" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Screen transfer. The visible screen and history of the source pane arrive in the target pane as one paste.</figcaption></figure>

```json
        "regex": "[./A-Za-z0-9_-]+\\.[a-z]+:[0-9]+",
        "command": "link-open"
      }
    ]
  },
  "limits_tier": "first-party"
}
```

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terminal` | Terminal | `[terminal]` | Smart copy |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Terminal is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### Clickable links

Paths and URLs in terminal output become links that open the editor. The manifest declares a `link_detectors` entry for paths with a `:line` suffix. On `link-activated` the client submits `editor-open` with the path, the line and `placement: split`. Pages: [terminal primitive](/pages/primitives-terminal/), [commands.invoke](/pages/capability-commands-invoke/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{EditorOpenSpec, EditorPlacement};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::paths::FsPath;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Links;

impl Lifecycle for Links {}

impl Handler for Links {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::LinkActivated(link) = event else { continue };
            if link.detector_id != "path-line" { continue; }
            let Some((path, line)) = link.text.rsplit_once(':') else { continue };
            let Ok(line) = line.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::EditorOpen(EditorOpenSpec {
                path: FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: path.into() },
                line: Some(line.saturating_sub(1)),
                placement: EditorPlacement::Split,
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let next = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'link-activated' || event.val.detectorId !== 'path-line') continue;
      const cut = event.val.text.lastIndexOf(':');
      const line = Number(event.val.text.slice(cut + 1));
      if (cut < 0 || !Number.isInteger(line)) continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: { tag: 'editor-open', val: {
          path: { scope: 'project', path: event.val.text.slice(0, cut) },
          line: Math.max(line - 1, 0),
          placement: 'split',
        } },
        correlation: next++,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### Pane title from the terminal

OSC titles rename the pane unless the user named it. On `pane-title-changed` with `source: osc`, the server submits `rename-node` with `source: inferred`, so a manual name always wins. Pages: [terminal primitive](/pages/primitives-terminal/), [panes.read](/pages/capability-panes-read/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::TitleOrigin;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::RenameNodeSpec;

fn on_title(event: Event) -> Option<Submission> {
    let Event::PaneTitleChanged(change) = event else { return None };
    if change.source != TitleOrigin::Osc { return None; }
    Some(Submission::keyed(
        Intent::RenameNode(RenameNodeSpec {
            node: change.node,
            title: change.title,
            expected_revision: None,
        }),
        format!("osc-title-{}", change.node),
    ))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function onTitle(event: Event): Submission | undefined {
  if (event.tag !== 'pane-title-changed' || event.val.source !== 'osc') return undefined;
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'rename-node', val: {
      node: event.val.node, title: event.val.title, source: 'inferred', expectedRevision: undefined,
    } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `osc-title-${event.val.node}`,
  };
}
```

#### Screen transfer between panes

The visible screen and the history of one pane are pasted into another. The server reads rows with `terminal.read-screen` and asks for the history, trims trailing blank rows, then submits `send-input` with `delivery: pasted` to the target. `history-text` answers later through `take-history`. Pages: [terminal reads](/pages/primitives-terminal-reads/), [read-screen](/pages/capability-terminal-read-screen/), [history](/pages/capability-terminal-history/), [terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/), [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [send-input](/pages/api-intent-send-input/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, ScreenPart};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Delivery, SendInputSpec};

fn transfer(source: NodeId, target: NodeId) -> Option<Submission> {
    let screen = terminal::read_screen(source, ScreenPart::Visible, 500)?;
    let text = screen.text.trim_end().to_string(); // drop trailing blank rows
    if text.is_empty() { return None; }
    Some(Submission::keyed(
        Intent::SendInput(SendInputSpec {
            pane: target,
            text,
            delivery: Delivery::Pasted,
            prompt_epoch: None,
            stages: vec![],
            raw: None,
            mouse: None,
        }),
        format!("transfer-{source}-{target}-{}", screen.revision),
    ))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { readScreen } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function transfer(source: bigint, target: bigint): Submission | undefined {
  const screen = readScreen(source, 'visible', 500);
  if (screen === undefined) return undefined;
  const text = screen.text.trimEnd(); // drop trailing blank rows
  if (text === '') return undefined;
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'send-input', val: {
      pane: target, text, delivery: 'pasted', promptEpoch: undefined,
      stages: [], raw: undefined, mouse: undefined, ifCurrent: undefined,
      lockUserInput: false, journal: false,
    } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `transfer-${source}-${target}-${screen.revision}`,
  };
}
```

#### Live terminal in a panel

A client panel embeds a pane with its own scrollback. It renders a `terminal-view` of the selected pane inside a `block`, and the host handles scrolling and input. impl Views for Links {

```ts
function render(selectedPane: bigint) {
```

#### Interrupt and watch exits

Ctrl+C style interrupts and exit codes of pane processes. The server submits `signal-pane` with `interrupt`, then `terminate` after a timer, and logs the status and signal from `pane-exited`. Pages: [panes.signal](/pages/capability-panes-signal/), [panes](/pages/api-panes/), [intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::Signal;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SignalPaneSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};

fn interrupt(pane: NodeId) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::SignalPane(SignalPaneSpec { pane, signal: Signal::Interrupt }))
}

// Run from a timer 3 s later if the pane has not exited.
fn terminate(pane: NodeId) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::SignalPane(SignalPaneSpec { pane, signal: Signal::Terminate }))
}

fn on_exit(event: Event) {
    if let Event::PaneExited(exit) = event {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("pane {} exited status={:?} signal={:?}", exit.node, exit.status, exit.signal));
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const interrupt = (pane: bigint): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'signal-pane', val: { pane, signal: 'interrupt' } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});

// Run from a timer 3 s later if the pane has not exited.
const terminate = (pane: bigint): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'signal-pane', val: { pane, signal: 'terminate' } },
  correlation: 2n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});

function onExit(event: Event): void {
  if (event.tag === 'pane-exited') {
    log('info', `pane ${event.val.node} exited status=${event.val.status} signal=${event.val.signal}`);
  }
}
```

#### Visible rows that changed

`screen-changed` names the first and last changed row of a pane, at most ten times a second. The plugin reads only those rows when it looks for a prompt, so it does not re-read the whole screen.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, ScreenPart};

impl Handler for PromptWatch {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::ScreenChanged(change) = event {
                let Some(screen) = terminal::read_screen(change.pane, ScreenPart::Visible, 200) else { continue };
                let changed = &screen.rows[change.first_row as usize..=change.last_row as usize];
                if changed.iter().any(|row| row.ends_with("$ ")) {
                    self.prompt_seen.insert(change.pane);
                }
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'screen-changed') continue;
    const { pane, firstRow, lastRow } = event.val;
    const screen = terminal.readScreen(pane, 'visible', 200);
    const changed = screen.rows.slice(firstRow, lastRow + 1);
    if (changed.some((row) => row.endsWith('$ '))) promptSeen.add(pane);
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.terminal` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.terminal/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.terminal/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before-send-input` | hook (veto) | Refuse or end input that the user or a plugin sends to a terminal pane. | pane, length, source (user, paste, plugin:<id>), preview (first 120 characters) | high |
| `open-link` | hook (first) | Decide how a clicked link opens. The first handler that answers wins. | pane, link_kind, text; reply: action (open-external, run-command, ignore) and optional command | standard |
| `link-actions` | collect | Offer actions for a detected link kind in the terminal right-click menu. | entry: id, link_kind, title, command | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.terminal/transfer`: send-screen: copy the visible screen of one pane to another pane

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.terminal/screen-changed`: { pane, rows } when visible rows change, at most 10 per second

Link detectors from `contributes.link_detectors` feed the `link-actions` point.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.terminal"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds `Open ticket` to the right-click menu on a link of kind `ticket`

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.terminal/link-actions"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.terminal/link-actions",
        "id": "open-ticket",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "link_kind": "ticket",
          "title": "Open ticket",
          "command": "open-ticket"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Smart Copy

## Smart Copy

The Smart Copy plugin (`ilium.core.smart-copy`, side both) owns selection and copying in terminal panes: mouse selection of regions, the terminal right-click menu, Smart Copy light (paths, commands and hashes recognised from cell styles) and Smart Copy with the inference model choosing semantic regions.

### What it covers

- Text selection and the terminal right-click menu (Smart Copy, Selecting regions and Terminal right-click menu).
- Smart Copy light, which recognises paths, commands and hashes without a model (Smart Copy, Smart Copy light).
- Smart Copy (AI), where the inference model labels the regions worth copying (Smart Copy, Smart Copy (AI)).

#### Terminal right-click menu

A context menu is built when it opens, with entries that depend on the selection. The manifest declares a `context_menu` for target `terminal`, and the `menu-provider` export answers `menu-items`. #[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["menu-provider"])]
```rust
#[derive(Default)]
struct SmartCopy;

impl Lifecycle for SmartCopy {}
impl Handler for SmartCopy {}

impl MenuProvider for SmartCopy {
    fn menu_items(&mut self, context: MenuContext) -> Vec<MenuEntry> {
        let Some(pane) = context.pane else { return Vec::new() };
        let selected = terminal::selection(pane).is_some_and(|s| !s.text.is_empty());
        vec![
            MenuEntry::new("copy", "Copy")
                .disabled_reason(if selected { None } else { Some("nothing selected") }),
            MenuEntry::new("copy-path", "Copy path"),

    }
```

```ts
export const { lifecycle, handler, menuProvider } = definePlugin({

  onEvents() { return []; },

    if (context.pane === undefined) return [];
    const selected = (terminal.selection(context.pane)?.text ?? '') !== '';
    return [

  },
});
```

#### Select regions with the mouse

Drag selects a region and double click selects a word. The client claims the pointer, tracks `down`, `drag` and `up` in `pointer` events and keeps the selected rows and columns. Pages: [terminal pointer](/pages/primitives-terminal-pointer/), [terminal.pointer](/pages/capability-terminal-pointer/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, PointerKind};

#[derive(Default)]
struct Region { start: Option<(u32, u32)>, end: (u32, u32) }

impl Handler for SmartCopy {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::Pointer(pointer) = event else { continue };
            match pointer.kind {
                PointerKind::Down => {
                    self.region.start = Some((pointer.row, pointer.column));
                    self.region.end = (pointer.row, pointer.column);
                }
                PointerKind::Drag => self.region.end = (pointer.row, pointer.column),
                PointerKind::Up => { /* region is final: keep rows and columns */ }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn start(pane: NodeId) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    terminal::claim_pointer(pane)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { claimPointer } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import type { Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let start: [number, number] | undefined;
let end: [number, number] = [0, 0];

export const startSelecting = (pane: bigint): void => claimPointer(pane);

export function onPointer(event: Event): void {
  if (event.tag !== 'pointer') return;
  const here: [number, number] = [event.val.row, event.val.column];
  if (event.val.kind === 'down') { start = here; end = here; }
  else if (event.val.kind === 'drag') end = here;
  // 'up': the region is final; keep start and end.
}
```

#### Smart Copy light

The server recognises paths, commands and hashes from text and cell styles and sends the candidates to the client side. It reads styled cells with `terminal.read-cells`, matches the patterns and sends a `message`. Pages: [read-cells](/pages/capability-terminal-read-cells/), [terminal reads](/pages/primitives-terminal-reads/), [worlds and sides](/pages/worlds-and-sides/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, ScreenPart};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

fn candidates(pane: NodeId, first_row: u32, count: u32) -> Option<Submission> {
    let rows = terminal::read_cells(pane, ScreenPart::Visible, first_row, count)?;
    let mut found: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for row in rows.rows.iter().map(|cells| cells.iter().map(|cell| cell.text.as_str()).collect::<String>()) {
        for word in row.split_whitespace() {
            let is_path = word.contains('/') && word.contains('.');
            let is_hash = word.len() >= 7 && word.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit());
            if is_path || is_hash { found.push(word.to_string()); }
        }
    }
    Some(Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.smart-copy".into(), side: PluginSide::Client, client: None },
        channel: "candidates".into(),
        payload: found.join("\n").into_bytes(),
    })))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { readCells } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function candidates(pane: bigint, firstRow: number, count: number): Submission | undefined {
  const rows = readCells(pane, 'visible', firstRow, count);
  if (rows === undefined) return undefined;
  const found: string[] = [];
  for (const row of rows.rows.map((cells) => cells.map((cell) => cell.text).join(''))) {
    for (const word of row.split(/\s+/)) {
      const isPath = word.includes('/') && word.includes('.');
      const isHash = word.length >= 7 && /^[0-9a-f]+$/i.test(word);
      if (isPath || isHash) found.push(word);
    }
  }
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'message', val: {
      to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.smart-copy', side: 'client', client: undefined },
      channel: 'candidates',
      payload: new TextEncoder().encode(found.join('\n')),
    } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### Copy to the clipboard

The chosen region lands on the system clipboard. On the candidate `message` the client calls `clipboard.write-text` with the chosen region and reports a short status line. Pages: [clipboard](/pages/api-clipboard/), [clipboard.write](/pages/capability-clipboard/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::clipboard;

fn on_candidates(&mut self, payload: &[u8], chosen: usize) {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(payload);
    let Some(region) = text.lines().nth(chosen) else { return };
    match clipboard::write_text(region) {
        Ok(()) => self.status = format!("Copied {} characters", region.chars().count()),
        Err(error) => self.status = format!("Copy failed: {:?}", error.code),
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as clipboard from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clipboard';

let status = '';

function onCandidates(payload: Uint8Array, chosen: number): void {
  const region = new TextDecoder().decode(payload).split('\n')[chosen];
  if (region === undefined) return;
  try {
    clipboard.writeText(region);
    status = `Copied ${[...region].length} characters`;
  } catch (error) {
    status = `Copy failed: ${String(error)}`;
  }
}
```

#### Smart Copy picker

The model ranks regions and a popup lets the user pick one. The client asks `inference.complete` to label the regions, then shows them in a `popup` over a `clear`, with a `%list` and `key-hints`. Pages: [inference](/pages/api-inference/), [inference grant](/pages/capability-inference/), [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/), [collections](/pages/widgets-collections/) and [text](/pages/widgets-text/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ListItem, UiTree};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

async fn rank(screen: String) -> Vec<String> {
    let request = CompletionRequest {
        messages: vec![
            ChatMessage { role: "system".into(), content: "Return the three most useful strings to copy, one per line.".into() },
            ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: screen },
        ],
        max_output_tokens: None,
        json_schema: None,
        purpose: "smart-copy".into(),
    };
    match inference::complete(request).await {
        Ok(completion) => completion.text.lines().take(3).map(str::to_string).collect(),
        Err(_) => Vec::new(), // fall back to the light candidates
    }
}

fn picker(regions: &[String]) -> UiTree {
    let mut tree = Tree::new();
    let items = regions.iter().enumerate()
        .map(|(index, region)| ListItem::plain(&format!("{} {}", index + 1, region)))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let list = tree.list(items).key("regions");
    let hints = tree.key_hints(vec![("1-3", "copy"), ("Esc", "close")]).key("hints");
    let body = tree.clear().child(list).child(hints);
    let root = tree.popup("smart-copy").title("Smart Copy").modal(true).child(body);
    tree.finish(root)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { complete } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { clear, keyHints, list, popup, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

async function rank(screen: string): Promise<string[]> {
  try {
    const completion = await complete({
      messages: [
        { role: 'system', content: 'Return the three most useful strings to copy, one per line.' },
        { role: 'user', content: screen },
      ],
      maxOutputTokens: undefined,
      jsonSchema: undefined,
      purpose: 'smart-copy',
    });
    return completion.text.split('\n').slice(0, 3);
  } catch {
    return []; // fall back to the light candidates
  }
}

function picker(regions: string[]) {
  const items = regions.map((region, index) => ({ label: `${index + 1} ${region}` }));
  const regionList = list(items, { key: 'regions' });
  const hints = keyHints([{ keys: '1-3', label: 'copy' }, { keys: 'Esc', label: 'close' }], { key: 'hints' });
  return tree(popup('smart-copy', { title: 'Smart Copy', modal: true }, [clear([regionList, hints])]));
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.smart-copy` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.smart-copy/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recognisers` | collect | Teach Smart Copy a new kind of structure to select. | entry: id, kind, regex, multiline, label | standard |
| `after-copy` | hook (transform) | Change the copied text before it reaches the clipboard, for example to remove secrets. | text, kind, pane; reply: text | standard |

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.smart-copy/copied`: { kind, length } after text is copied

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.smart-copy"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Replaces anything that looks like an API token with `[removed]` before the copy

A package adds a `transform` handler. Each handler gets the previous output and may replace it.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy",
        "id": "strip-tokens",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "strip_tokens"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "strip_tokens" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: text, kind, pane
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Replace(new_payload_json)
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'strip_tokens') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: text, kind, pane
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'replace', val: newPayloadJson };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Editor

## Editor

<div class="note">
<p>Status: the editor is native in v1. This page describes the plugin form that arrives in Phase 7 (see the <a href="/pages/roadmap/">roadmap</a>).</p>
</div>

The Editor plugin (`ilium.core.editor`, side client) owns editor panes: buffers, syntax highlighting through a token provider, line numbers and the minimap, Markdown source and rendered views, the file explorer and picker, and creating an agent from an editor line. As the editor provider it owns buffer text while it runs.

### What it covers

- Editor panes (Editors and boards, Editor panes).
- Syntax highlighting, line numbers and the minimap (Editors and boards, Editor panes; Settings, Editor).
- Markdown source and rendered views (Editors and boards, Editor panes).
- The file explorer and file picker (Editors and boards, Editor panes).
- Creating an agent from an editor line (Automation, Create an agent from an editor line).

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor` | Editor | `[editor]` | Terminal |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Editor is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### Be the editor provider

The plugin owns buffer text and answers every editor call. It exports the editor provider, loads text on `editor-opened`, drops it on `editor-closed` and answers reads from its own rope. See [editor.provide](/pages/capability-editor-provide/), the [editor primitive](/pages/primitives-editor/), [editor.read](/pages/capability-editor-read/) and the [events](/pages/api-events/). The `editor-provider` service is described on the editor.provide page.

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views", "service-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Editor {
    ropes: HashMap<BufferId, ropey::Rope>,
}

impl Lifecycle for Editor {}

impl Handler for Editor {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::EditorOpened(opened) => {
                    let text = opened
                        .path
                        .as_ref()
                        .and_then(|path| fs::read("project", path).ok())
                        .unwrap_or_default();
                    self.ropes.insert(opened.buffer, ropey::Rope::from_str(&text));
                }
                Event::EditorClosed(buffer) => {
                    self.ropes.remove(&buffer);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Editor {
    // Answers a read call of the editor-provider service.
    fn line_text(&self, buffer: BufferId, line: u32) -> Option<String> {
        let rope = self.ropes.get(&buffer)?;
        (line as usize) < rope.len_lines()
            .then(|| rope.line(line as usize).to_string())
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as fs from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import * as editor from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const buffers = new Map<bigint, string[]>();

export const { lifecycle, handler, views, serviceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'editor-opened') {
        const opened = event.val;
        const text = opened.path === undefined ? '' : fs.readToString('project', opened.path);
        buffers.set(opened.buffer, text.split('\n'));
      } else if (event.tag === 'editor-closed') {
        buffers.delete(event.val);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() { /* panel views */ return tree(paragraph([[span('Editor')]])); },
  handle(call) { /* answers editor-provider reads from `buffers` */ return { tag: 'ok', val: new Uint8Array() }; },
});

export const lineText = (buffer: bigint, line: number): string | undefined =>
  buffers.get(buffer)?.[line];
```

#### Syntax highlighting

A token provider teaches the editor a language. This one implements `tokens(lines)` for TOML within the 10 ms deadline, and invalidates only the changed range from `editor-changed`. Pages: [token provider](/pages/api-token-provider/), the [editor primitive](/pages/primitives-editor/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::TokenProvider;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::token_provider::{Token, TokenKind};

impl TokenProvider for Editor {
    fn tokens(
        &mut self,
        _buffer: BufferId,
        first_line: u32,
        lines: Vec<String>,
        _state_in: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    ) -> (Vec<Token>, Option<Vec<u8>>) {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (offset, text) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            let line = first_line + offset as u32;
            let trimmed = text.trim_start();
            if trimmed.starts_with('#') {
                out.push(Token { line, start: 0, length: text.chars().count() as u32, kind: TokenKind::Comment });
            } else if trimmed.starts_with('[') {
                out.push(Token { line, start: 0, length: text.chars().count() as u32, kind: TokenKind::Type });
            } else if let Some(at) = text.find('=') {
                out.push(Token { line, start: 0, length: at as u32, kind: TokenKind::Variable });
                if text[at..].contains('"') {
                    out.push(Token { line, start: at as u32 + 1, length: (text.len() - at - 1) as u32, kind: TokenKind::String });
                }
            }
        }
        (out, None) // TOML needs no state between blocks
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Token } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export const { lifecycle, handler, tokenProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents() { return []; },
  tokens(_buffer, firstLine, lines): [Token[], Uint8Array | undefined] {
    const out: Token[] = [];
    lines.forEach((text, offset) => {
      const line = firstLine + offset;
      const trimmed = text.trimStart();
      if (trimmed.startsWith('#')) {
        out.push({ line, start: 0, length: text.length, kind: 'comment' });
      } else if (trimmed.startsWith('[')) {
        out.push({ line, start: 0, length: text.length, kind: 'type-name' });
      } else {
        const at = text.indexOf('=');
        if (at < 0) return;
        out.push({ line, start: 0, length: at, kind: 'variable' });
        if (text.slice(at).includes('"')) {
          out.push({ line, start: at + 1, length: text.length - at - 1, kind: 'string' });
        }
      }
    });
    return [out, undefined]; // TOML needs no state between blocks
  },
});
```

#### Edits, minimap and viewport

Edits apply safely and the minimap shows the shape of the file. The plugin submits `editor-apply-edits` with a `base-revision`, so a stale revision is refused with `refused(conflict)`. It draws a `minimap` that follows `editor-viewport-changed`. Pages: [editor viewport](/pages/primitives-editor-viewport/), [editor.edit](/pages/capability-editor-edit/), [data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/), [intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::EditorApplyEditsSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::editing::TextEdit;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::editing::{TextPosition, TextRange};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

fn replace_line(buffer: BufferId, revision: u64, line: u32, replacement: &str) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::EditorApplyEdits(EditorApplyEditsSpec {
        buffer,
        base_revision: revision,
        edits: vec![TextEdit {
            range: TextRange {
                start: TextPosition { line, column: 0 },
                end: TextPosition { line: line + 1, column: 0 },
            },
            replacement: format!("{replacement}\n"),
        }],
    }))
}

// On Event::EditorViewportChanged(viewport): keep the visible range.
fn minimap(tree: &mut Tree, density: Vec<u8>, first: u32, last: u32, total: u32) -> NodeHandle {
    tree.minimap(density).viewport((first, last)).total_lines(total).key("overview")
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { minimap } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const replaceLine = (buffer: bigint, revision: bigint, line: number, replacement: string): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'editor-apply-edits', val: {
    buffer,
    baseRevision: revision,
    edits: [{
      range: { start: { line, column: 0 }, end: { line: line + 1, column: 0 } },
      replacement: `${replacement}\n`,
    }],
  } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});

// On the 'editor-viewport-changed' event: keep the visible range.
const overview = (density: number[], first: number, last: number, total: number) =>
  minimap(density, { key: 'overview', viewport: [first, last], totalLines: total });
```

#### Markdown rendered view

A panel renders the buffer as Markdown with the source beside it. It shows a `code-view` of the source and a `markdown` widget of the same buffer in a `split`. Pages: [text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/), [media and embedded widgets](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) and [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Views for Editor {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let source = tree.code_view(self.current).key("source");
        let rendered = tree.markdown(self.source_text()).key("rendered");
        let root = tree
            .split(Direction::Vertical)
            .key("markdown-split")
            .position(500)
            .child(source)
            .child(rendered);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { codeView, markdown, split, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

function render(current: bigint, sourceText: string) {
  const source = codeView(current, { key: 'source' });
  const rendered = markdown(sourceText, { key: 'rendered' });
  return tree(split({ direction: 'vertical', key: 'markdown-split', position: 500 }, [source, rendered]));
}
```

#### Create an agent from a line

Clicking a TODO line starts an agent with that line as its prompt. On `editor-pointer` over a line that starts with `TODO`, the plugin submits `create-pane` with `initial-input` set to the line text. Pages: the [editor primitive](/pages/primitives-editor/), [panes.create](/pages/capability-panes-create/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [intents](/pages/api-intents/). `initial-input` also needs the `terminal.write` grant from the manifest.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::CreatePaneSpec;

fn on_pointer(event: Event) -> Option<Submission> {
    let Event::EditorPointer(pointer) = event else { return None };
    let text = editor::read_lines(pointer.buffer, pointer.position.line)?;
    if !text.trim_start().starts_with("TODO") { return None; }
    Some(Submission::keyed(
        Intent::CreatePane(CreatePaneSpec {
            parent: None,
            title: "TODO agent".into(),
            content_kind: "ilium.terminal".into(),
            cwd: None,
            command: Some(vec!["claude".into()]),
            initial_input: Some(text.trim().to_string()),
        }),
        format!("todo-{}-{}", pointer.buffer, pointer.position.line),
    ))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as editor from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function onPointer(event: Event): Submission | undefined {
  if (event.tag !== 'editor-pointer') return undefined;
  const text = editor.lineText(event.val.buffer, event.val.position.line);
  if (text === undefined || !text.trimStart().startsWith('TODO')) return undefined;
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'create-pane', val: {
      parent: undefined, title: 'TODO agent', contentKind: 'ilium.terminal',
      cwd: undefined, command: ['claude'], initialInput: text.trim(),
    } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `todo-${event.val.buffer}-${event.val.position.line}`,
  };
}
```

#### Changed lines from the editor

`editor-changed` gives the buffer, its new revision and the first and last changed line. The plugin re-lints only that range and leaves the rest of the decorations as they are.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl Handler for LintRange {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::EditorChanged(change) = event {
                self.dirty.entry(change.buffer).or_default().push(change.first_line..=change.last_line);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'editor-changed') continue;
    const { buffer, firstLine, lastLine } = event.val;
    markDirty(buffer, firstLine, lastLine);
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.editor` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.editor/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.editor/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before-save` | hook (transform) | Change buffer text just before it is written, for example to format it. | buffer, path, language, text; reply: text | standard |
| `file-openers` | collect | Choose which pane kind opens files with certain extensions. | entry: id, extensions, pane_kind, priority | standard |
| `line-badges` | collect | Add a marker in the editor gutter for lines that match. | entry: id, regex, glyph, tooltip | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.editor/buffers`: list, read, replace-range: read and edit open buffers

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.editor/saved`: { buffer, path } after a save

`languages` entries and the `token-provider` export colour the buffers this plugin shows.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.editor"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Removes trailing spaces on every line when a Markdown buffer is saved

A package adds a `transform` handler. Each handler gets the previous output and may replace it.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "client": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.editor/before-save"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.editor/before-save",
        "id": "trim-trailing",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "trim_trailing"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "trim_trailing" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: buffer, path, language, text
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Replace(new_payload_json)
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'trim_trailing') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: buffer, path, language, text
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'replace', val: newPayloadJson };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Kanban

## Kanban

<div class="note">
<p>Status: the board is native in v1. This page describes the plugin form that arrives in Phase 7 (see the <a href="/pages/roadmap/">roadmap</a>).</p>
</div>

The Kanban plugin has the id `ilium.core.kanban` and runs on the client side. It owns the board pane: a basic pane that draws cards in To do, Doing and Done columns. A board can be backed by a Markdown file. The plugin reloads the board when that file changes, and it adds the Kanban Board tab to the settings. Drawing a pane body and reading files are plain plugin work, so the board is a good first example of a pane kind that a plugin provides.

The pane itself, its place in the tree and its focus are kernel-native. The plugin declares a `board` pane kind and draws the body of that pane through the contract. It never touches the PTY or the layout solver.

### What it covers

- Kanban boards as a pane: columns, cards, a selected card (see Editors and boards, "Kanban boards").
- A board that is backed by a Markdown file, with automatic reload when the file changes (see Editors and boards, "Kanban boards").
- The Kanban Board settings tab: card preview and column width (see Settings, "Kanban Board").

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/08-kanban.gif" alt="A Kanban board with three columns while a card moves from To do to Doing" loading="lazy"><figcaption>A board pane with three columns. The selected card moves one column to the right.</figcaption></figure>
