### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kanban-board` | Kanban Board | `[kanban_board]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Kanban is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### A board pane kind

The plugin declares a `board` pane kind with the [basic primitive](/pages/primitives-basic/) and the grant in [panes.provide-kind](/pages/capability-panes-provide-kind/). It draws each column as a `block` inside a horizontal `layout` (see [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) and the [UI model](/pages/ui-model/)). The selected card stays in view state, so a redraw keeps it.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

const COLUMNS: [&str; 3] = ["To do", "Doing", "Done"];

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Kanban {
    cards: Vec<Vec<String>>, // one list of card titles per column
    selected: (usize, usize), // column, card
}

impl Lifecycle for Kanban {}

impl Handler for Kanban {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for Kanban {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let mut blocks = Vec::new();
        for (index, name) in COLUMNS.iter().enumerate() {
            let titles = self.cards.get(index).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
            let lines: Vec<Vec<Span>> = titles
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(row, title)| {
                    let marker = if self.selected == (index, row) { "> " } else { "  " };
                    vec![Span::plain(&format!("{marker}{title}"))]
                })
                .collect();
            let body = tree.paragraph(lines);
            blocks.push(tree.block().title(*name).child(body));
        }
        let mut row = tree.layout(Direction::Horizontal, vec![Constraint::Fill(1); 3]);
        for block in blocks {
            row = row.child(block);
        }
        tree.finish(row)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { block, fill, layout, paragraph, span, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const COLUMNS = ['To do', 'Doing', 'Done'];
const state = { cards: [[], [], []] as string[][], selected: [0, 0] as [number, number] };

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents() {
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    const blocks = COLUMNS.map((name, column) => {
      const lines = state.cards[column].map((title, row) => {
        const marker = state.selected[0] === column && state.selected[1] === row ? '> ' : '  ';
        return [span(`${marker}${title}`)];
      });
      return block({ title: name }, [paragraph(lines)]);
    });
    return tree(layout({ direction: 'horizontal', constraints: COLUMNS.map(() => fill(1)) }, blocks));
  },
});
```

#### Cards with check lists

Each card shows its sub-tasks as a `check-list` from [collections](/pages/widgets-collections/), placed in a `block` from [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/). A click on an item arrives as a `ui-action` event ([events](/pages/api-events/)) with the kind `changed` and an `item-state` value. The plugin toggles the item and marks the board dirty so it is saved.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::CheckItem;

fn card_body(tree: &mut Tree, card: &Card) -> NodeRef {
    let items: Vec<CheckItem> = card
        .tasks
        .iter()
        .map(|task| CheckItem::new(&task.id, &task.label).state(task.state))
        .collect();
    let list = tree.check_list(items).key(&format!("card-{}", card.id));
    tree.block().title(&card.title).child(list).into_node()
}

impl Handler for Kanban {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            let Some(card_id) = action.key.strip_prefix("card-") else { continue };
            if let (ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::ItemState(task_id, state)) =
                (action.kind, action.value)
            {
                self.set_task_state(card_id, &task_id, state);
                self.is_dirty = true;
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { block, checkList } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function cardBody(card: Card) {
  const items = card.tasks.map((task) => ({ id: task.id, label: task.label, state: task.state }));
  return block({ title: card.title }, [checkList(items, { key: `card-${card.id}` })]);
}

function onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || !event.val.key.startsWith('card-')) continue;
    const { kind, value, key } = event.val;
    if (kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'item-state') {
      setTaskState(key.slice('card-'.length), value.val[0], value.val[1]);
      state.isDirty = true;
    }
  }
  return [];
}
```

#### Read and write the Markdown file safely

The board file is written only if nobody changed it meanwhile. The plugin reads with a revision token and writes with the conditional write from [atomic writes and tail](/pages/api-fs-atomic-and-tail/). The grant is [fs.write](/pages/capability-fs-write/), and the scopes are explained on [file access](/pages/file-access/). On a conflict, the plugin reloads and applies the move again.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

const MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 3;

async fn move_card_in_file(path: &FsPath, card: &str, column: usize) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    for _attempt in 0..MAX_ATTEMPTS {
        let current = fs::read_with_revision(path).await?;
        let updated = apply_move(&current.bytes, card, column)?;
        match fs::write_atomic(path, updated, Some(current.revision)).await {
            Ok(_) => return Ok(()),
            Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Conflict => continue,
            Err(error) => return Err(error),
        }
    }
    Err(PluginError {
        code: ErrorCode::Conflict,
        message: "the board changed three times; try again".to_string(),
        retry_after_ms: None,
    })
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { readWithRevision, writeAtomic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';

export async function moveCardInFile(
  path: { scope: string; path: string },
  card: string,
  column: number,
): Promise<void> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
    const current = await readWithRevision(path);
    const updated = applyMove(current.bytes, card, column);
    try {
      await writeAtomic(path, updated, current.revision);
      return;
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'conflict') continue;
      throw error;
    }
  }
  throw new PluginError('conflict', 'the board changed three times; try again');
}
```

#### Reload when the file changes

Edits made in the editor or by an agent show up on the board. The plugin watches the file with [fs.watch](/pages/capability-fs-watch/) (see also [file access](/pages/file-access/)). On `fs-changed`, or on `editor-saved` for the same path, it parses the file again and asks the host to redraw. Both events are listed in [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::{EditorSavedEvent, FsChangedEvent};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::ViewTarget;

impl Lifecycle for Kanban {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: "docs/plan.md".into() };
        self.watch = Some(fs::watch(&path, false)?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for Kanban {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let is_board_changed = match event {
                Event::FsChanged(FsChangedEvent { watch, .. }) => self.watch == Some(watch),
                Event::EditorSaved(EditorSavedEvent { path, .. }) => path.ends_with("docs/plan.md"),
                _ => false,
            };
            if is_board_changed {
                self.reload_from_disk();
                let _ = ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Pane(self.pane));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { watch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { invalidate } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';

const BOARD = { scope: 'project', path: 'docs/plan.md' };
let boardWatch: bigint | undefined;

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {
    boardWatch = watch(BOARD, false);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      const isChanged =
        (event.tag === 'fs-changed' && event.val.watch === boardWatch) ||
        (event.tag === 'editor-saved' && event.val.path.endsWith('docs/plan.md'));
      if (isChanged) {
        reloadFromDisk();
        invalidate({ tag: 'pane', val: state.pane });
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render,
});
```

#### Open a board from a file

The user picks a Markdown file with the picker from [fs.pick](/pages/capability-fs-pick/). A `path-field` from [pickers](/pages/widgets-pickers/) starts it. The column width comes from the `column_width` `number` row, declared as described on [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) and [settings row types](/pages/reference-settings-rows/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, settings};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs::{PickKind, PickSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::PathKind;

fn open_field(tree: &mut Tree, shown: &str) -> NodeRef {
    tree.path_field(PathKind::OpenFile)
        .key("board-file")
        .display(shown)
        .extensions(vec!["md"])
        .into_node()
}

async fn pick_board() -> Result<Option<FsPath>, PluginError> {
    let spec = PickSpec {
        kind: PickKind::OpenFile,
        title: "Open board from file".to_string(),
        extensions: vec!["md".to_string()],
    };
    match fs::pick(spec).await {
        Ok(path) => Ok(Some(path)),
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Cancelled => Ok(None),
        Err(error) => Err(error),
    }
}

fn column_width() -> u16 {
    let values: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
    values["column_width"].as_u64().unwrap_or(24) as u16
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { pick } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';
import { pathField } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const openField = (shown: string) =>
  pathField('open-file', { key: 'board-file', display: shown, extensions: ['md'] });

export async function pickBoard() {
  try {
    return await pick({ kind: 'open-file', title: 'Open board from file', extensions: ['md'] });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'cancelled') return undefined;
    throw error;
  }
}

export function columnWidth(): number {
  const width = (JSON.parse(getJson()) as Record<string, unknown>)['column_width'];
  return typeof width === 'number' ? width : 24;
}
```

#### Drop marker during a drag

While a card is dragged over a column, the board sends `drag-over` with the target and the acceptance rule. The plugin shows a marker before or after the card that the drop will use, or nothing when the drop is refused.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, DropAccept};

impl Handler for DropMarker {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if let (ActionKind::DragOver, ActionValue::DragOver(over)) = (action.kind, action.value) {
                self.marker = match over.accept {
                    DropAccept::None => None,
                    accept => Some((over.target_key, over.index, accept)),
                };
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onAction(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'ui-action' }>): Submission[] {
  const { kind, value } = event.val;
  if (kind !== 'drag-over' || value.tag !== 'drag-over') return [];
  const { targetKey, index, accept } = value.val;
  marker = accept === 'none' ? undefined : { targetKey, index, accept };
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.kanban` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.kanban/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.kanban/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `card-actions` | collect | Add an action to the card context menu. | entry: id, title, command | standard |
| `card-moved` | hook (observe) | Learn that a card changed column. | board, card, from_column, to_column | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.kanban/boards`: list, get, move-card, add-card: read and edit boards

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.kanban/card-moved`: { board, card, to_column }

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.kanban"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Posts a toast when a card reaches the `Done` column

A package adds a `observe` handler. Every handler runs; replies are ignored.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "client": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.kanban/card-moved"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.kanban/card-moved",
        "id": "notify-done",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "notify_done"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "notify_done" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: board, card, from_column, to_column
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Pass
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'notify_done') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: board, card, from_column, to_column
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'pass' };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Agent detection

## Agent detection

The Agent detection plugin has the id `ilium.core.agent-detect` and runs on both sides. The server side owns agent identity and activity: it identifies agent CLIs from the process tree, classifies what each agent is doing, tracks `/goal` state and puts icons, spinners and badges in the tree. The client side draws the Agents panel and follows the display mode.

Walking the process tree and scraping the vt100 screen are kernel-native. The kernel runs the detection loop and hands the plugin process lists and screen snapshots through the `detector` export. The plugin is the pure classification step, which is why a new agent CLI is one signature entry and not a new branch of code.

### What it covers

- Agent identity from the process tree and the list of supported agent CLIs (see Agent monitoring, "How detection works" and "Supported agent CLIs").
- Activity classification and status indicators (see Agent monitoring, "Status indicators and their defaults").
- Pane status signals and the three icon slots in the tree (see Agent monitoring, "The three icon slots in the tree").
- Goal tracking and the `/goal` badge (see Agent monitoring, "The /goal badge").
- The Normal and Attention display modes, and custom signatures (see Agent monitoring, "Normal mode and Attention mode" and "The Agent Monitoring settings tab").
- Agent icons and identifiers in the tree.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/01-agent-activity.gif" alt="Tree rows whose agent icons change between working, idle and waiting" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Agent icons follow the activity of each pane: working, idle, awaiting approval, done.</figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/17-goal-indicators.gif" alt="A goal badge appears on a tree row while an agent pursues a goal" loading="lazy"><figcaption>The goal badge shows while an agent pursues a /goal and clears when the goal ends.</figcaption></figure>

### Interstitial prompts, signatures, states and status line

**Auto-answering interstitial prompts.** Ilium answers known one-time dialogs for the user. Today this is Claude Code's "resume full session" prompt, answered with one keystroke per agent process. The behaviour is on by default and is the key `auto_answer_interstitial_prompts` in the `[detection]` table. The plugin owns the rule and the toggle on the Agent Monitoring tab. The keystroke goes through `terminal.write`, once per process, and the plugin records the process so it never answers twice. [COR-011]

**Custom signatures.** A user adds an agent CLI in `config.toml`, and the plugin loads the entries into the signature registry.

```toml
[[detection.custom_signatures]]
process_name = "myagent"
agent_class  = "other"
```

A custom signature has the class `other`. It gets an identity and an icon, but no launch, resume or transcript contract, because Ilium has no verified contract for it. A plugin package can add a signature with [agent.signatures](/pages/capability-agent-signatures/) instead.

**Enums the plugin reports.** Do not invent values; use these.

| Enum | Values |
|---|---|
| Agent class | `claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`, `other(name)`. `antimatter` is accepted as a process-name alias of `antigravity` |
| Activity | `working`, `waiting-background`, `background-task-still-running`, `waiting-approval`, `done`, `idle` |
| Turn | `working`, `waiting-approval`, `waiting-subagents`, `settling`, `idle` |
| Goal state | `active`, `paused`, `blocked`, `usage-limited`, `reached` |
| Pane kind | `plain-shell`, `agent`, `editor`, `board`, `agent-unavailable` |

**Status line capture.** Claude Code and Antigravity can report a status line (model, context use). The kernel keeps the hidden helper commands that capture it, because they run inside the agent process and need no plugin. The plugin reads the captured values through `agent.read`. See [feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/) (F-111).

**Polling.** `working_poll_seconds` (default 10) and `idle_poll_seconds` (default 45) in `[detection]` set the adaptive loop. The loop itself stays in the kernel.

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-monitoring` | Agent Monitoring | `[ui]`, `[detection]` | Progress, Agent toolbar, Notifications |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Agent detection is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### Identify an agent CLI

A custom signature recognises a new agent CLI. The plugin declares it under [agent.signatures](/pages/capability-agent-signatures/) and implements the `detector` export from the [agent primitive](/pages/primitives-agent/). When the kernel accepts a match it emits `agent-identified` ([events](/pages/api-events/)), and the plugin logs the signature id.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{Classification, Detector, DetectorProcess, DetectorScreen};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentIdentifiedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["detector"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct AgentDetect;

impl Lifecycle for AgentDetect {}

impl Handler for AgentDetect {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::AgentIdentified(AgentIdentifiedEvent { node, signature }) = event {
                log::log(Level::Info, &format!("node {node} runs {signature}"));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Detector for AgentDetect {
    fn identify(&mut self, processes: Vec<DetectorProcess>) -> Option<String> {
        let found = processes.iter().any(|process| process.name == "example-agent");
        found.then(|| "example-agent".to_string())
    }

    fn classify(&mut self, _signature: String, screen: DetectorScreen) -> Classification {
        let shows = |text: &str| screen.rows.iter().any(|row| row.contains(text));
        let activity = if shows("Allow this command?") {
            AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval
        } else if shows("esc to interrupt") {
            AgentActivity::Working
        } else {
            AgentActivity::Idle
        };
        Classification { activity, objective: None, goal: None }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler, detector } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'agent-identified') {
        log('info', `node ${event.val.node} runs ${event.val.signature}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  identify(processes) {
    return processes.some((process) => process.name === 'example-agent') ? 'example-agent' : undefined;
  },
  classify(_signature, screen) {
    const shows = (text: string) => screen.rows.some((row) => row.includes(text));
    const activity = shows('Allow this command?')
      ? 'awaiting-approval'
      : shows('esc to interrupt')
        ? 'working'
        : 'idle';
    return { activity, objective: undefined, goal: undefined };
  },
});
```

#### Activity icons in the tree

Working agents get an animated icon and idle ones a still icon. The plugin reads agents under [agent.read](/pages/capability-agent-read/) and decorates rows under [tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/). On `agent-activity-changed` it submits `set-decoration`; the host steps the `frames` itself (see [tree and window chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/)). The event shape is on [events](/pages/api-events/), the agent types on the [agent primitive](/pages/primitives-agent/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, SetDecorationSpec, DecorationVisibility};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

fn activity_decoration(node: NodeId, current: AgentActivity) -> Submission {
    let (frames, glyph) = match current {
        AgentActivity::Working => (
            ["⠋", "⠙", "⠹", "⠸", "⠼", "⠴", "⠦", "⠧", "⠇", "⠏"]
                .iter().map(|frame| StyledText::plain(frame)).collect(),
            "⠋",
        ),
        AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval => (Vec::new(), "?"),
        _ => (Vec::new(), "●"),
    };
    Submission::keyed(
        Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
            frames,
            frame_ms: 100,
            icon: Some(glyph.into()),
            ..SetDecorationSpec::text(node, "activity", "")
        }),
        format!("activity-{node}"),
    )
}

fn on_events(batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
    batch
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|event| match event {
            Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. }) => {
                Some(activity_decoration(node, current))
            }
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

const SPINNER = ['⠋', '⠙', '⠹', '⠸', '⠼', '⠴', '⠦', '⠧', '⠇', '⠏'];

function activityDecoration(node: bigint, current: string): Submission {
  const working = current === 'working';
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'set-decoration',
      val: {
        ...baseDecoration(node, 'activity', ''),
        icon: working ? SPINNER[0] : current === 'awaiting-approval' ? '?' : '●',
        frames: working ? SPINNER.map((frame) => ({ spans: [{ text: frame }] })) : [],
        frameMs: 100,
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `activity-${node}`,
  };
}

export function onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  const out: Submission[] = [];
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag === 'agent-activity-changed') {
      out.push(activityDecoration(event.val.node, event.val.current));
    }
  }
  return out;
}
```

#### Status signals and goals

The goal badge and the signal slots follow the agent. On `agent-goal-changed` the plugin shows the goal in the `goal` slot. When the goal ends it submits `clear-decoration`, as described on [tree and window chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/). The plugin mirrors `signal-changed` into a second slot. Event fields are in [events](/pages/api-events/) and the agent view is on the [agent primitive](/pages/primitives-agent/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::{AgentGoalEvent, SignalChangedEvent};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{DecorationKey, Intent, SetDecorationSpec};

fn goal_submission(event: AgentGoalEvent) -> Submission {
    let AgentGoalEvent { node, goal } = event;
    match goal {
        Some(text) => Submission::keyed(
            Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec::text(node, "goal", format!("goal {text}"))),
            format!("goal-{node}"),
        ),
        None => Submission::keyed(
            Intent::ClearDecoration(DecorationKey { node, slot: "goal".into() }),
            format!("goal-clear-{node}"),
        ),
    }
}

fn signal_submission(event: SignalChangedEvent) -> Submission {
    let text = format!("{}: {}", event.signal, event.value);
    Submission::new(Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec::text(event.pane, "activity", text)))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export function goalSubmission(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'agent-goal-changed' }>): Submission {
  const { node, goal } = event.val;
  if (goal === undefined) {
    return {
      intent: { tag: 'clear-decoration', val: { node, slot: 'goal' } },
      correlation: 1n,
      dedupKey: `goal-clear-${node}`,
    };
  }
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'set-decoration', val: baseDecoration(node, 'goal', `goal ${goal}`) },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `goal-${node}`,
  };
}

export function signalSubmission(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'signal-changed' }>): Submission {
  const { pane, signal, value } = event.val;
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'set-decoration', val: baseDecoration(pane, 'activity', `${signal}: ${value}`) },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### Agents panel

A panel lists agents with a status badge and a spinner. The client side draws a `table` ([collections](/pages/widgets-collections/)), a `badge` per state and a `spinner` for working agents ([status and feedback](/pages/widgets-status-and-feedback/)), as a panel under [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/). The server side feeds it over the `message` channel.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::Area;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{TableColumn, TableRow, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Tone;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Views for AgentsPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let columns = vec![
            TableColumn::new("agent", "Agent").priority(9),
            TableColumn::new("state", "State").priority(5),
            TableColumn::new("goal", "Goal").priority(1),
        ];
        let rows = self.agents.iter().map(|agent| {
            let state = match agent.activity.as_str() {
                "working" => "⠹ working",
                "awaiting-approval" => "approval",
                other => other,
            };
            TableRow::new(vec![agent.name.clone(), state.into(), agent.goal.clone()]).id(&agent.id)
        }).collect();
        let table = tree.table(columns, rows).key("agents");
        let waiting = self.agents.iter().filter(|agent| agent.activity == "awaiting-approval").count();
        let badge = tree.badge().count(waiting as u32).tone(Tone::Warning).key("waiting");
        let busy = tree.spinner().label("Watching agents");
        let root = tree.layout(Direction::Vertical, vec![Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(1)])
            .child(badge).child(table).child(busy);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}

// In the server side: Intent::Message with channel "agents" and the rows as JSON bytes.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { badge, fill, layout, length, spinner, table, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const columns = [
  { id: 'agent', title: 'Agent', width: { tag: 'length', val: 10 }, priority: 9 },
  { id: 'state', title: 'State', width: { tag: 'length', val: 10 }, priority: 5 },
  { id: 'goal', title: 'Goal', width: { tag: 'fill', val: 1 }, priority: 1 },
];

export function render() {
  const rows = state.agents.map((agent) => ({
    id: agent.id,
    cells: [
      agent.name,
      agent.activity === 'working' ? '⠹ working' : agent.activity,
      agent.goal,
    ],
  }));
  const waiting = state.agents.filter((agent) => agent.activity === 'awaiting-approval').length;
  return tree(layout(
    { direction: 'vertical', constraints: [length(1), fill(1), length(1)] },
    [
      badge({ count: waiting, tone: 'warning', key: 'waiting' }),
      table(columns, rows, { key: 'agents' }),
      spinner({ label: 'Watching agents' }),
    ],
  ));
}

// The server side sends the rows with an intent of tag 'message' on channel 'agents'.
```

#### Normal and Attention modes

A display mode changes what the tree emphasises. The plugin declares `display_modes` in the manifest and listens for `display-mode-changed` ([events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/), [events](/pages/api-events/)). In Attention mode the panel lists only agents that need the user.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[derive(Default, PartialEq)]
enum Mode {
    #[default]
    Normal,
    Attention,
}

impl Handler for AgentsPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::DisplayModeChanged(mode) = event {
                self.mode = match mode.as_deref() {
                    Some("attention") => Mode::Attention,
                    _ => Mode::Normal,
                };
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl AgentsPanel {
    fn visible_agents(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &AgentRow> {
        self.agents.iter().filter(|agent| {
            self.mode == Mode::Normal || agent.activity == "awaiting-approval" || agent.activity == "done"
        })
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

let mode: 'normal' | 'attention' = 'normal';

export function onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag === 'display-mode-changed') {
      mode = event.val.mode === 'attention' ? 'attention' : 'normal';
    }
  }
  return [];
}

export const visibleAgents = (agents: AgentRow[]) =>
  agents.filter(
    (agent) => mode === 'normal' || agent.activity === 'awaiting-approval' || agent.activity === 'done',
  );
```

#### 6. Signals from the agent

A signal is a named value the agent reports, such as the branch it works on. `signal-changed` arrives coalesced per pane and signal, so the plugin stores only the latest value and updates the row for that pane.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl Handler for Signals {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::SignalChanged(change) = event {
                self.signals.entry(change.pane).or_default().insert(change.signal, change.value);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'signal-changed') continue;
    const bySignal = signals.get(event.val.pane) ?? new Map<string, string>();
    bySignal.set(event.val.signal, event.val.value);
    signals.set(event.val.pane, bySignal);
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Detection loop and budget

The poll loop is native and runs in the server. This plugin's detector runs on the plugin executor, one call per pane, in parallel with other plugins' detectors. One poll cycle spends at most 50 ms on detector calls. A slow call keeps the previous activity and counts as a breach, and the third breach in a row restarts this plugin side. The full rules are in the [detection loop](/pages/capability-agent-signatures/#detection-loop) section of the signatures page and in [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/).

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.agent-detect` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.agent-detect/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-detect/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `activity-rules` | collect | Add screen patterns that mean working, idle or awaiting approval for one signature. | entry: id, signature, state, regex, region (last-lines, status-row, whole-screen) | standard |
| `classify` | hook (transform) | Adjust the detected activity before it is published. | pane, signature, state, reason; reply: state | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.agent-detect/state`: get, list: current identity and activity of panes

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.agent-detect/state-changed`: { pane, signature, previous, current }

`contributes.signatures` entries register agent CLIs. This plugin turns them into identity.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.agent-detect"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Marks a pane as awaiting approval when the last lines contain the question

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-detect/activity-rules"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.agent-detect/activity-rules",
        "id": "build-waiting",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "signature": "claude",
          "state": "awaiting-approval",
          "regex": "Do you want to proceed\\?",
          "region": "last-lines"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Agent toolbar

## Agent toolbar

The Agent toolbar plugin has the id `ilium.core.agent-toolbar` and runs on both sides. It owns the per-agent chrome in the pane frame and the tree: the last-prompt banner, the toolbar and its actions, the model and context facts, the reserved terminal space, the recovery hint after an agent stops, the Configure agent action and the agent debug history. The server side reads agent facts and sends actions. The client side draws the slots and the popover.

The frame around a pane and the terminal underneath it are kernel-native. The plugin fills the frame slots that the kernel offers through `ui.chrome` and sends actions through `agent.control`.

### What it covers

- The last-prompt banner and the agent toolbar (see Agent monitoring, "Last prompt banner and agent toolbar").
- Configure agent (see Agent monitoring, "Last prompt banner and agent toolbar").
- Reserved terminal space (see Agent monitoring, "Reserved terminal space").
- Recover work after an agent stops (see Agent monitoring, "Recover work after an agent stops").
- Agent debug history (see Agent monitoring, "Troubleshooting").

### Toolbar action table

The toolbar shows the buttons that fit the detected agent. The same list of actions is registered as `toolbar-actions` entries (see Extension points), so a third-party plugin can add a button next to these. [COR-011]

| Action id | Label | What it does | Agents | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compact` | Compact | Shrinks the agent context | Claude Code, Codex | Sends `/compact`, or starts remote compaction when the [compaction](/pages/core-plugin-compaction/) plugin is set to remote |
| `clear` | Clear | Clears the conversation | Claude Code, Codex | Sends `/clear` |
| `configure` | Configure | Opens the agent configuration dialog | Claude Code, Codex | Calls the [agent setup](/pages/core-plugin-agent-setup/) service |
| `stop` | Stop | Interrupts the current turn | all agents | Sends the interrupt key |
| `copy-screen` | Copy screen | Copies the visible screen | all agents | Reads the screen |
| `smart-copy` | Smart Copy | Starts Smart Copy on the frozen screen | all agents | Calls the [smart copy](/pages/core-plugin-smart-copy/) service |
| `copy-last-message` | Copy last message | Copies the agent's last answer | Claude Code, Codex | Reads the transcript |
| `effort` | Effort | Chooses the reasoning effort | Claude Code, Codex | Sends the agent's own command |
| `model` | Model | Chooses the model | Claude Code, Codex | Sends the agent's own command |
| `fast-mode` | Fast mode | Switches fast mode | agents that have it | Sends the agent's own command |
| `exit` | Exit | Ends the agent | all agents | Sends the exit command |
| `text-selection` | Text selection | Lets the user select text with the mouse | all agents | Toggles the terminal selection mode |

The toolbar is shown when `agent_toolbar_enabled` is on (default). The user hides or reopens it from the pane icon or the right-click menu. `show_toolbar_labels` adds text after the icons. The last-prompt banner has its own key `last_prompt_enabled` and its line count `last_prompt_max_lines` (1 to 20, default 4). The kernel reserves these rows before terminal interaction begins.

### Samples

#### Last-prompt banner

The last prompt the user typed shows in the pane frame. The plugin reads prompts under [agent.read-prompts](/pages/capability-agent-read-prompts/). On `user-line-submitted` ([events](/pages/api-events/)) it submits `set-frame-slot` with the trimmed prompt in the banner slot of that pane, as described on [tree and window chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::UserLineEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, SetFrameSlotSpec};

const BANNER_CHARS: usize = 120;

impl Handler for Toolbar {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UserLineSubmitted(UserLineEvent { pane, text, .. }) = event else {
                continue;
            };
            let trimmed: String = text.trim().chars().take(BANNER_CHARS).collect();
            if trimmed.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            out.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetFrameSlot(SetFrameSlotSpec {
                pane,
                slot: "prompt".into(),
                content: RichText::plain(format!("> {trimmed}")),
                icon: None,
                tooltip: None,
            })));
        }
        out
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

const BANNER_CHARS = 120;

export function onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  const out: Submission[] = [];
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag !== 'user-line-submitted') continue;
    const trimmed = event.val.text.trim().slice(0, BANNER_CHARS);
    if (trimmed === '') continue;
    out.push({
      intent: {
        tag: 'set-frame-slot',
        val: {
          pane: event.val.pane,
          slot: 'prompt',
          content: { spans: [{ text: `> ${trimmed}` }] },
          icon: undefined,
          tooltip: undefined,
        },
      },
      correlation: 1n,
      dedupKey: undefined,
    });
  }
  return out;
}
```

#### Agent toolbar actions

Buttons in the tree toolbar and the hover strip run agent actions. The plugin declares them under [ui.chrome](/pages/capability-ui-chrome/). A click arrives as `command-invoked` ([events](/pages/api-events/)); the client side passes it to the server side with a `message` ([messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/)). The server side holds [agent.control](/pages/capability-agent-control/) and submits the `agent-action` intent, such as `compact` ([intents](/pages/api-intents/)).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{AgentActionSpec, Intent, MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

// Client side: forward the command with the pane id.
fn forward(invoked: &CommandInvokedEvent) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let Some(pane) = invoked.context.pane else { return Vec::new() };
    vec![Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.agent-toolbar".into(), side: PluginSide::Server, client: None },
        channel: invoked.command.clone(),
        payload: pane.to_string().into_bytes(),
    }))]
}

// Server side: run the action, once per pane and press.
fn run_action(channel: &str, payload: &[u8]) -> Option<Submission> {
    let pane: NodeId = String::from_utf8_lossy(payload).parse().ok()?;
    if channel != "compact" {
        return None;
    }
    Some(Submission::keyed(
        Intent::AgentAction(AgentActionSpec { pane, action_id: "compact".into() }),
        format!("compact:{pane}"),
    ))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// Client side: forward the command with the pane id.
export function forward(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'command-invoked' }>): Submission[] {
  const pane = event.val.context.pane;
  if (pane === undefined) return [];
  return [{
    intent: {
      tag: 'message',
      val: {
        to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.agent-toolbar', side: 'server', client: undefined },
        channel: event.val.command,
        payload: new TextEncoder().encode(pane.toString()),
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  }];
}

// Server side: run the action, once per pane and press.
export function runAction(channel: string, payload: Uint8Array): Submission | undefined {
  if (channel !== 'compact') return undefined;
  const pane = BigInt(new TextDecoder().decode(payload));
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'agent-action', val: { pane, actionId: 'compact' } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `compact:${pane}`,
  };
}
```

#### Model and context in the frame

The frame shows the model and how full the context window is. The server side reads typed facts with the [agent transcript primitive](/pages/primitives-agent-transcript/) under [agent.transcript](/pages/capability-agent-transcript/). On `agent-model-changed` ([events](/pages/api-events/)) it sends the model and a percentage to the client side as a `message` ([messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/)), which fills the header slot.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentModelEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

fn context_percent(used_tokens: u32, window: Option<u32>) -> Option<u32> {
    let window = window.filter(|size| *size > 0)?;
    Some((u64::from(used_tokens) * 100 / u64::from(window)) as u32)
}

fn model_message(event: AgentModelEvent, used_tokens: u32) -> Submission {
    let model = event.model;
    let percent = context_percent(used_tokens, model.context_window);
    let text = match percent {
        Some(value) => format!("{} · {value}% context", model.model),
        None => model.model.clone(),
    };
    let _ = agent::prompt_epoch(event.pane); // the epoch lets later inputs detect a newer prompt
    Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.agent-toolbar".into(), side: PluginSide::Client, client: None },
        channel: "model".into(),
        payload: format!("{}|{text}", event.pane).into_bytes(),
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export function contextPercent(usedTokens: number, window: number | undefined): number | undefined {
  if (window === undefined || window <= 0) return undefined;
  return Math.floor((usedTokens * 100) / window);
}

export function modelMessage(
  event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'agent-model-changed' }>,
  usedTokens: number,
): Submission {
  const { pane, model } = event.val;
  const percent = contextPercent(usedTokens, model.contextWindow);
  const text = percent === undefined ? model.model : `${model.model} · ${percent}% context`;
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'message',
      val: {
        to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.agent-toolbar', side: 'client', client: undefined },
        channel: 'model',
        payload: new TextEncoder().encode(`${pane}|${text}`),
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### Clear the banner and recover work

The banner and the slots clear when an agent stops, and a recovery hint appears. On `agent-activity-changed` ([events](/pages/api-events/)) the client side submits `clear-frame-slot` and sets the `recover` slot with the last prompt, using the intents on [tree and window chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{ClearFrameSlotSpec, Intent, SetFrameSlotSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

fn on_stop(event: AgentActivityEvent, last_prompt: Option<&str>) -> Vec<Submission> {
    if event.current != AgentActivity::None && event.current != AgentActivity::Done {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let pane = event.node;
    let mut out = vec![Submission::new(Intent::ClearFrameSlot(ClearFrameSlotSpec {
        pane,
        slot: "prompt".into(),
    }))];
    if let Some(prompt) = last_prompt {
        out.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetFrameSlot(SetFrameSlotSpec {
            pane,
            slot: "recover".into(),
            content: RichText::plain(format!("Stopped. Last prompt: {prompt}")),
            icon: None,
            tooltip: None,
        })));
    }
    out
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export function onStop(
  event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'agent-activity-changed' }>,
  lastPrompt: string | undefined,
): Submission[] {
  const { node, current } = event.val;
  if (current !== 'none' && current !== 'done') return [];
  const out: Submission[] = [{
    intent: { tag: 'clear-frame-slot', val: { pane: node, slot: 'prompt' } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  }];
  if (lastPrompt !== undefined) {
    out.push({
      intent: {
        tag: 'set-frame-slot',
        val: {
          pane: node,
          slot: 'recover',
          content: { spans: [{ text: `Stopped. Last prompt: ${lastPrompt}` }] },
          icon: undefined,
          tooltip: undefined,
        },
      },
      correlation: 2n,
      dedupKey: undefined,
    });
  }
  return out;
}
```

#### Debug history popover

A popover shows the recent journal of a pane. The server side reads the pane journal with [journal.read](/pages/capability-journal-read/) and sends the entries to the client side as a `message` ([messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/)). The client side opens a popover anchored to the tree row ([popovers](/pages/api-popovers/)) with a `table` of entries ([collections](/pages/widgets-collections/)).

**Rust**

```rust
// Server side.
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, journal};

fn history_json(pane: NodeId) -> String {
    let since = clock::now_unix_millis() - 3_600_000;
    let entries = journal::read(pane, since, 50);
    let rows: Vec<_> = entries
        .iter()
        .map(|entry| serde_json::json!({ "at": entry.at, "kind": entry.kind, "detail": entry.detail }))
        .collect();
    serde_json::Value::Array(rows).to_string()
}

// Client side.
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui::{self, AnchorSide, KeyAnchor, PopupAnchor, PopupOptions};

fn open_history(row_key: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    ui::open_popup_with(
        "history",
        PopupAnchor::AtKey(KeyAnchor { key: row_key.into(), side: AnchorSide::Right }),
        PopupOptions { modal: false, pinnable: true, dismiss_on_leave: true, close_on_escape: true },
    )
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// Server side.
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/journal';

export function historyJson(pane: bigint): string {
  const entries = read(pane, nowUnixMillis() - 3_600_000n, 50);
  return JSON.stringify(
    entries.map((entry) => ({ at: Number(entry.at), kind: entry.kind, detail: entry.detail })),
  );
}

// Client side.
import { openPopupWith } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';

export const openHistory = (rowKey: string) =>
  openPopupWith('history', { tag: 'at-key', val: { key: rowKey, side: 'right' } },
    { modal: false, pinnable: true, dismissOnLeave: true, closeOnEscape: true });
```

#### Goal line in the banner

`agent-goal-changed` carries the goal text, or nothing when the goal is cleared. The toolbar keeps the latest goal per pane and shows it under the last-prompt banner.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl Handler for GoalLine {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::AgentGoalChanged(change) = event {
                match change.goal {
                    Some(goal) => { self.goals.insert(change.node, goal); }
                    None => { self.goals.remove(&change.node); }
                }
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'agent-goal-changed') continue;
    if (event.val.goal === undefined) goals.delete(event.val.node);
    else goals.set(event.val.node, event.val.goal);
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.agent-toolbar` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.agent-toolbar/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-toolbar/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toolbar-actions` | collect | Add a button to the toolbar of panes that run a signature. | entry: id, signature, label, icon, command, requires_action | standard |
| `banner-segments` | collect | Add a short segment to the last-prompt banner. | entry: id, priority, max_width (the plugin fills it with `set-frame-slot`) | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.agent-toolbar/last-prompt`: get: last prompt text of an agent pane

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.agent-toolbar"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds a Review button to Claude panes

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-toolbar/toolbar-actions"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.agent-toolbar/toolbar-actions",
        "id": "run-review",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "signature": "claude",
          "label": "Review",
          "icon": "eye",
          "command": "start-review"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Fleet

## Fleet

The Fleet plugin has the id `ilium.core.fleet` and runs on both sides. It owns work with many agents at once: messaging one agent or all of them, Ask for update, `ilium panes`, `ilium broadcast`, `ilium new-pane` and the local HTTP API route `POST /create_agent`. It reaches other sessions on the same machine, and it reads cost figures from the service that the [Cost](/pages/core-plugin-cost/) plugin provides. The client side only draws the Ask for update dialog.

Spawning a PTY and typing into it are kernel-native. Fleet drives them through the `create-pane` and `send-input` intents and never touches a terminal directly.

### What it covers

- Agent messaging and Ask for update (see Automation, "Ask for update").
- The local HTTP API `POST /create_agent` (see Automation, "Local HTTP API", and Settings, "API").
- `ilium new-pane` (see CLI reference, "ilium new-pane").
- `ilium panes` (see CLI reference, "ilium panes").
- `ilium broadcast` (see CLI reference, "ilium broadcast").

### See it

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | API | `[api]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Fleet is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### ilium panes

A CLI subcommand lists panes across every running session. The plugin declares `panes` under [cli.contribute](/pages/capability-cli-contribute/) ([the cli API](/pages/api-cli/)) and reads sessions under [sessions.cross](/pages/capability-sessions-cross/) ([the sessions API](/pages/api-sessions/)). On `cli-invoked` ([events](/pages/api-events/)) it lists the sessions, asks each one for its panes and prints one JSONL line per pane.

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;

use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::sessions::{self, CrossRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::cli;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CliInvokedEvent;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Fleet {
    /// Request id to (invocation, session name).
    waiting: HashMap<RequestId, (u64, String)>,
    /// Invocation to the number of replies still expected.
    remaining: HashMap<u64, usize>,
}

impl Lifecycle for Fleet {}

impl Fleet {
    fn start_panes(&mut self, invocation: u64) {
        let live = sessions::list_live();
        let mut sent = 0;
        for session in &live {
            let request = CrossRequest {
                session: session.name.clone(),
                command: "list-panes".into(),
                arguments_json: "{}".into(),
            };
            if let Ok(id) = sessions::send(request) {
                self.waiting.insert(id, (invocation, session.name.clone()));
                sent += 1;
            }
        }
        self.remaining.insert(invocation, sent);
        if sent == 0 {
            cli::finish(invocation, 1);
        }
    }

    fn on_reply(&mut self, id: RequestId, is_ok: bool) {
        let Some((invocation, name)) = self.waiting.remove(&id) else { return };
        if let Some(text) = sessions::take_reply(id).filter(|_| is_ok) {
            let line = format!(r#"{{"type":"pane","session":"{name}","panes":{text}}}"#);
            let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
        }
        let Some(left) = self.remaining.get_mut(&invocation) else { return };
        *left -= 1;
        if *left == 0 {
            self.remaining.remove(&invocation);
            cli::finish(invocation, 0);
        }
    }
}

impl Handler for Fleet {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CliInvoked(CliInvokedEvent { invocation, name, .. }) if name == "panes" => {
                    self.start_panes(invocation);
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(done) => self.on_reply(done.request, done.outcome.is_ok()),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as cli from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/cli';
import * as sessions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions';

const waiting = new Map<bigint, { invocation: bigint; name: string }>();
const remaining = new Map<bigint, number>();

function startPanes(invocation: bigint): void {
  let sent = 0;
  for (const session of sessions.listLive()) {
    try {
      const id = sessions.send({ session: session.name, command: 'list-panes', argumentsJson: '{}' });
      waiting.set(id, { invocation, name: session.name });
      sent += 1;
    } catch {
      // A session that went away is skipped.
    }
  }
  remaining.set(invocation, sent);
  if (sent === 0) cli.finish(invocation, 1);
}

function onReply(id: bigint, isOk: boolean): void {
  const entry = waiting.get(id);
  if (entry === undefined) return;
  waiting.delete(id);
  const text = isOk ? sessions.takeReply(id) : undefined;
  if (text !== undefined) {
    cli.writeLine(entry.invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'pane', session: entry.name, panes: JSON.parse(text) }));
  }
  const left = (remaining.get(entry.invocation) ?? 1) - 1;
  remaining.set(entry.invocation, left);
  if (left === 0) {
    remaining.delete(entry.invocation);
    cli.finish(entry.invocation, 0);
  }
}

export const { handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'cli-invoked' && event.val.name === 'panes') startPanes(event.val.invocation);
      else if (event.tag === 'request-completed') onReply(event.val.request, event.val.outcome.tag === 'ok');
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

#### ilium broadcast

A message goes to agents in every matching session. For other sessions the plugin calls `sessions.send` ([sessions API](/pages/api-sessions/), [sessions.cross](/pages/capability-sessions-cross/)). In the current session it submits `send-input` with `delivery: submitted` ([send-input](/pages/api-intent-send-input/)). The trigger is `cli-invoked` ([events](/pages/api-events/)).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::sessions::{self, CrossRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, SendInputSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::Delivery;

fn broadcast(text: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
    // Other sessions: ask each one to run its own broadcast.
    for session in sessions::list_live().into_iter().filter(|session| !session.is_self) {
        let request = CrossRequest {
            session: session.name,
            command: "broadcast".into(),
            arguments_json: serde_json::json!({ "text": text }).to_string(),
        };
        let _ = sessions::send(request);
    }
    // This session: one send-input per agent pane.
    agent::agents()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|pane| {
            let spec = SendInputSpec {
                pane: pane.pane,
                text: text.to_string(),
                delivery: Delivery::Submitted,
                prompt_epoch: None,
                stages: Vec::new(),
                raw: None,
                mouse: None,
                if_current: None,
                lock_user_input: false,
                journal: true,
            };
            Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(spec), format!("broadcast-{}-{}", pane.pane, text.len()))
        })
        .collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as sessions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions';
import { agents } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function broadcast(text: string): Submission[] {
  for (const session of sessions.listLive().filter((entry) => !entry.isSelf)) {
    try {
      sessions.send({ session: session.name, command: 'broadcast', argumentsJson: JSON.stringify({ text }) });
    } catch {
      // The session went away; nothing to send.
    }
  }
  return agents().map((agent) => ({
    intent: {
      tag: 'send-input',
      val: {
        pane: agent.pane, text, delivery: 'submitted', promptEpoch: undefined, stages: [],
        raw: undefined, mouse: undefined, ifCurrent: undefined, lockUserInput: false, journal: true,
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `broadcast-${agent.pane}-${text.length}`,
  }));
}
```

#### Ask for update

A dialog sends a short request to one agent or to all of them. The client side shows a `dialog` ([layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/)) with a `text-input` and buttons ([input widgets](/pages/widgets-input/)) under [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/). On Send it submits a `message` to the server side ([messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/)), which submits `send-input` to each target ([send-input](/pages/api-intent-send-input/)).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

fn render_dialog(tree: &mut Tree, text: &str) -> NodeRef {
    let message = tree.text_input("Message", text.to_string()).key("update-text");
    let send = tree.button("Send").key("update-send").role(ButtonRole::Primary);
    let cancel = tree.button("Cancel").key("update-cancel");
    tree.dialog("ask-for-update", "Ask for update")
        .child(message).child(send).child(cancel)
        .into_node()
}

fn on_action(key: &str, kind: ActionKind, value: ActionValue, text: &mut String) -> Vec<Submission> {
    match (key, kind, value) {
        ("update-text", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(next)) => *text = next,
        ("update-send", ActionKind::Activated, _) if !text.trim().is_empty() => {
            return vec![Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
                to: MessageTarget { plugin: "ilium.core.fleet".into(), side: PluginSide::Server, client: None },
                channel: "ask-for-update".into(),
                payload: text.clone().into_bytes(),
            }))];
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    Vec::new()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { button, dialog, textInput } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let text = '';

export const renderDialog = () =>
  dialog('ask-for-update', {
    title: 'Ask for update',
    children: [
      textInput('Message', text, { key: 'update-text' }),
      button('Send', { key: 'update-send', role: 'primary' }),
      button('Cancel', { key: 'update-cancel' }),
    ],
  });

export function onAction(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'ui-action' }>): Submission[] {
  const { key, kind, value } = event.val;
  if (key === 'update-text' && kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'text') text = value.val;
  if (key === 'update-send' && kind === 'activated' && text.trim() !== '') {
    return [{
      intent: {
        tag: 'message',
        val: {
          to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.fleet', side: 'server', client: undefined },
          channel: 'ask-for-update',
          payload: new TextEncoder().encode(text),
        },
      },
      correlation: 1n,
      dedupKey: undefined,
    }];
  }
  return [];
}
```

#### Hand a request to the notifications plugin

When an agent asks for a user decision, the fleet plugin sends a one-way message to the notifications plugin so it raises a desktop notification. The fleet plugin needs `messages.peer:ilium.core.notifications` for that. The notifications plugin needs no grant to receive it.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

fn ask_user(pane_label: &str, question: &str) -> Submission {
    let payload = format!("{pane_label}: {question}").into_bytes();
    Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
        to: MessageTarget {
            plugin: "ilium.core.notifications".into(),
            side: PluginSide::Server,
            client: None,
        },
        channel: "agent-question".into(),
        payload,
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function askUser(paneLabel: string, question: string): Submission {
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'message',
      val: {
        to: { plugin: 'ilium.core.notifications', side: 'server', client: undefined },
        channel: 'agent-question',
        payload: new TextEncoder().encode(`${paneLabel}: ${question}`),
      },
    },
    correlation: 2n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

---

#### POST /create_agent

The kernel owns the HTTP listener, its port and its on/off setting (Settings, API tab). The fleet plugin owns only the route: it registers `POST /create_agent` with `http-api.route`, and the kernel returns 404 for the route while the plugin is disabled. [COR-010]

The local HTTP API creates an agent pane. The plugin routes `POST /create_agent` ([HTTP API](/pages/api-http-api/), [http-api.route](/pages/capability-http-api-route/)). On `http-called` ([events](/pages/api-events/)) it validates the JSON body and submits `create-pane` ([intents](/pages/api-intents/)). When the `request-completed` event carries the new node, it replies with the pane id.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http_api;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::HttpCalledEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{CreatePaneSpec, Intent};

#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct CreateAgent {
    title: String,
    command: Vec<String>,
}

fn answer(request: &HttpCalledEvent, pending: &mut std::collections::HashMap<u64, u64>) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let route_path = request.path.split('?').next().unwrap_or("");
    if request.method != "POST" || route_path != "/create_agent" {
        let _ = http_api::respond(request.call, 404, &[], &[]);
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let Ok(body) = serde_json::from_slice::<CreateAgent>(&request.body) else {
        let _ = http_api::respond(request.call, 400, &[], br#"{"error":"invalid json"}"#);
        return Vec::new();
    };
    let spec = CreatePaneSpec {
        parent: None,
        title: body.title,
        content_kind: "ilium.terminal".into(),
        cwd: None,
        command: Some(body.command),
        initial_input: None,
    };
    let submission = Submission::keyed(Intent::CreatePane(spec), format!("http-{}", request.call));
    pending.insert(submission.correlation, request.call);
    vec![submission]
}

fn on_created(call: u64, node: NodeId) {
    let headers = vec![("content-type".to_string(), "application/json".to_string())];
    let body = format!(r#"{{"pane_id":{node}}}"#);
    let _ = http_api::respond(call, 201, &headers, body.as_bytes());
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { respond } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http-api';
import type { HttpCalledEvent, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const pending = new Map<bigint, bigint>(); // correlation to http call
let nextCorrelation = 1n;

export function answer(request: HttpCalledEvent): Submission[] {
  const routePath = request.path.split('?')[0];
  if (request.method !== 'POST' || routePath !== '/create_agent') {
    respond(request.call, 404, [], new Uint8Array());
    return [];
  }
  let body: { title: string; command: string[] };
  try {
    body = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(request.body));
  } catch {
    respond(request.call, 400, [], new TextEncoder().encode('{"error":"invalid json"}'));
    return [];
  }
  const correlation = nextCorrelation++;
  pending.set(correlation, request.call);
  return [{
    intent: {
      tag: 'create-pane',
      val: { parent: undefined, title: body.title, contentKind: 'ilium.terminal',
             cwd: undefined, command: body.command, initialInput: undefined },
    },
    correlation,
    dedupKey: `http-${request.call}`,
  }];
}

export function onCreated(correlation: bigint, node: bigint): void {
  const call = pending.get(correlation);
  if (call === undefined) return;
  pending.delete(correlation);
  respond(call, 201, [['content-type', 'application/json']],
    new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ pane_id: Number(node) })));
}
```

#### Cost column from a service

`ilium panes` asks the Cost plugin for the spend per pane. The plugin holds `services.use:ilium.core.cost/usage` ([services](/pages/capability-services/)) and calls it with `services::call` ([services API](/pages/api-services/)). When the reply is ready (the `request-completed` event), the SDK future resolves with the reply text. The plugin merges the figures into the JSONL lines.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

async fn cost_by_pane() -> std::collections::HashMap<u64, f64> {
    let payload = r#"{"window":"session"}"#;
    match services::call("ilium.core.cost/usage", "usage", payload).await {
        Ok(reply) => {
            let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&reply).unwrap_or_default();
            parsed["panes"]
                .as_object()
                .map(|panes| {
                    panes.iter()
                        .filter_map(|(pane, cost)| Some((pane.parse().ok()?, cost.as_f64()?)))
                        .collect()
                })
                .unwrap_or_default()
        }
        Err(error) => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("cost service failed: {}", error.message));
            Default::default()
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { call } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export async function costByPane(): Promise<Map<number, number>> {
  const costs = new Map<number, number>();
  try {
    const reply = await call('ilium.core.cost/usage', 'usage', JSON.stringify({ window: 'session' }));
    const panes = (JSON.parse(reply) as { panes?: Record<string, number> }).panes ?? {};
    for (const [pane, cost] of Object.entries(panes)) costs.set(Number(pane), cost);
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `cost service failed: ${String(error)}`);
  }
  return costs;
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.fleet` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.fleet/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.fleet/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selectors` | collect | Add a named selector to `ilium panes`, `ilium broadcast` and the dialogs. | entry: id, title, rule (JSON rule over signature, state, session and tags) | standard |
| `before-broadcast` | hook (transform) | Change or end a message before it goes to many agents. | message, targets, source; reply: message | high |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.fleet/broadcast`: send: send a message to a selection
- `ilium.core.fleet/panes`: list: list panes of every session

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.fleet/broadcast-sent`: { targets, length }

Calls `ilium.core.cost/usage` for the cost column.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.fleet"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Lets `ilium broadcast --select reviewers` reach every pane tagged `review`

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.fleet/selectors"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.fleet/selectors",
        "id": "reviewers",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Reviewers",
          "rule": {
            "tag": "review"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Cost

## Cost

The Cost plugin has the id `ilium.core.cost` and runs on both sides. It owns spend and usage: session statistics and the stats dot, spend and quota indicators, sorting the tree by cost, the price table, reset forecasts for plan quotas, and the Agent Cost and Reset planning settings. The server side reads transcripts, computes the figures and decorates the tree. The client side draws the statistics panel. The plugin also serves its figures to other plugins as the service `ilium.core.cost/usage`.

Reading an agent's own session files is done by the kernel and exposed as typed transcript facts. The plugin only turns those facts into money and quota percentages.

### What it covers

- Session statistics and the stats dot (see Agent monitoring, "The stats dot and session statistics").
- Spend and quota indicators, and the choice of a unit (see Agent cost, "What the numbers mean" and "Choose a unit").
- Sorting the tree by cost (see Agent cost, "Sorting the tree by cost").
- The price table (see Agent cost, "Prices and [cost.prices]").
- Reset planning, the reset forecasts (see Automation, "Reset forecasts", and Settings, "Reset planning").
