### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-cost` | Agent Cost | `[cost]` | Fleet, Tree |
| `reset-planning` | Reset planning | `[reset_planning]` | Notifications |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Cost is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### Session statistics

The client side draws spend over time, spend per model and a table of sessions. It uses the data widgets from [data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/): a `sparkline`, a `bar-chart` and a `table` ([collections](/pages/widgets-collections/)), inside a panel granted by [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/). The server side computes the figures from the transcript facts ([agent transcript primitive](/pages/primitives-agent-transcript/)) and sends them to the client side.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::Area;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{BarGroup, BarItem, TableColumn, TableRow, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Views for CostPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let hourly = tree
            .sparkline(self.hourly_cents.iter().map(|cents| Some(*cents)).collect())
            .key("hourly");
        let bars = self
            .by_model
            .iter()
            .map(|(model, cents)| BarItem::new(*cents).label(model))
            .collect();
        let per_model = tree.bar_chart(vec![BarGroup::new("models", bars)]).key("models");
        let columns = vec![
            TableColumn::new("session", "Session").priority(9),
            TableColumn::new("model", "Model").priority(5),
            TableColumn::new("cost", "Cost").priority(9),
        ];
        let rows = self.sessions.iter().map(|session| {
            TableRow::new(vec![
                session.title.clone(),
                session.model.clone(),
                format!("${:.2}", session.cents as f64 / 100.0),
            ]).id(&session.id)
        }).collect();
        let table = tree.table(columns, rows).key("sessions");
        let root = tree.layout(Direction::Vertical, vec![Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(6), Constraint::Fill(1)])
            .child(hourly).child(per_model).child(table);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { barChart, fill, layout, length, sparkline, table, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export function render() {
  const bars = state.byModel.map(([model, cents]) => ({ value: cents, label: model }));
  const columns = [
    { id: 'session', title: 'Session', width: { tag: 'fill', val: 1 }, priority: 9 },
    { id: 'model', title: 'Model', width: { tag: 'length', val: 8 }, priority: 5 },
    { id: 'cost', title: 'Cost', width: { tag: 'length', val: 8 }, priority: 9 },
  ];
  const rows = state.sessions.map((session) => ({
    id: session.id,
    cells: [session.title, session.model, `$${(session.cents / 100).toFixed(2)}`],
  }));
  return tree(layout(
    { direction: 'vertical', constraints: [length(1), length(6), fill(1)] },
    [
      sparkline(state.hourlyCents, { key: 'hourly' }),
      barChart([{ label: 'models', bars }], { key: 'models' }),
      table(columns, rows, { key: 'sessions' }),
    ],
  ));
}
```

#### Quota gauges and spend history

One gauge per quota window, a thin line per pane, and a chart of recent days. The widgets are `gauge`, `line-gauge` and `chart` from [data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/). The daily totals live in project storage ([storage](/pages/api-storage/)), so the chart survives a restart.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::{self, Bucket};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{Axis, Dataset, GraphType, Marker};

fn save_day(day: u32, cents: u64) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    storage::put(Bucket::Project, &format!("day/{day}"), &cents.to_le_bytes())
}

fn load_days() -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
    storage::keys(Bucket::Project, "day/")
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|key| {
            let day: f64 = key.strip_prefix("day/")?.parse().ok()?;
            let bytes = storage::get(Bucket::Project, &key)?;
            let cents = u64::from_le_bytes(<[u8; 8]>::try_from(bytes).ok()?);
            Some((day, cents as f64 / 100.0))
        })
        .collect()
}

fn quota_widgets(tree: &mut Tree, windows: &[(String, f64)], pane_ratio: &[(String, f64)]) -> Vec<NodeRef> {
    let mut nodes = Vec::new();
    for (name, ratio) in windows {
        nodes.push(tree.gauge(*ratio).label(vec![Span::plain(&format!("{name} {:.0}%", ratio * 100.0))]).key(name).into_node());
    }
    for (pane, ratio) in pane_ratio {
        nodes.push(tree.line_gauge(*ratio).label(vec![Span::plain(pane)]).key(pane).into_node());
    }
    let history = tree
        .chart(
            vec![Dataset::new("cost per day", load_days()).marker(Marker::Braille).graph_type(GraphType::Line)],
            Axis { title: None, bounds: (0.0, 30.0), labels: vec![] },
            Axis { title: None, bounds: (0.0, 20.0), labels: vec![] },
        )
        .key("history");
    nodes.push(history.into_node());
    nodes
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';
import { chart, gauge, lineGauge, span } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export function saveDay(day: number, cents: bigint): void {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(8);
  new DataView(bytes.buffer).setBigUint64(0, cents, true);
  storage.put('project', `day/${day}`, bytes);
}

export function loadDays(): Array<[number, number]> {
  return storage.keys('project', 'day/').flatMap((key) => {
    const bytes = storage.get('project', key);
    if (bytes === undefined || bytes.length !== 8) return [];
    const cents = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, 8).getBigUint64(0, true);
    return [[Number(key.slice('day/'.length)), Number(cents) / 100] as [number, number]];
  });
}

export function quotaWidgets(windows: Array<[string, number]>, panes: Array<[string, number]>) {
  return [
    ...windows.map(([name, ratio]) => gauge(ratio, { key: name, label: [span(`${name} ${Math.round(ratio * 100)}%`)] })),
    ...panes.map(([pane, ratio]) => lineGauge(ratio, { key: pane, label: [span(pane)] })),
    chart(
      [{ name: 'cost per day', points: loadDays(), marker: 'braille', graphType: 'line' }],
      { bounds: [0, 30], labels: [] },
      { bounds: [0, 20], labels: [] },
      { key: 'history' },
    ),
  ];
}
```

#### Unit, display and sort by cost

Settings choose dollars or quota and what to display; the tree sorts by cost. The plugin declares a `choice` row for the unit and a `multi-choice` row for the display ([settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/), [settings row types](/pages/reference-settings-rows/)). It submits `set-decoration` with a `sort-key` taken from the spend ([tree and window chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/)).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, SetDecorationSpec};

fn unit_is_dollars() -> bool {
    let values: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
    values["unit"].as_str().unwrap_or("dollars") == "dollars"
}

fn cost_decoration(node: NodeId, cents: i64, quota_percent: u32) -> Submission {
    let text = if unit_is_dollars() {
        format!("${:.2}", cents as f64 / 100.0)
    } else {
        format!("{quota_percent}%")
    };
    Submission::new(Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
        sort_key: Some(-cents), // ascending order puts the highest cost first
        trailing: true,
        ..SetDecorationSpec::text(node, "cost", text)
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function unitIsDollars(): boolean {
  const values = JSON.parse(getJson()) as Record<string, unknown>;
  return (values['unit'] ?? 'dollars') === 'dollars';
}

export function costDecoration(node: bigint, cents: number, quotaPercent: number): Submission {
  const text = unitIsDollars() ? `$${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}` : `${quotaPercent}%`;
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'set-decoration',
      val: { ...baseDecoration(node, 'cost', text), sortKey: BigInt(-cents), trailing: true },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### Reset forecasts

Public status feeds predict when quotas reset. The plugin fetches the feed with `http.fetch` ([HTTP](/pages/api-http/), [http grant](/pages/capability-http/)) once an hour, using a durable timer ([durable timers](/pages/api-durable-timers/)), parses the reset times and stores the forecast. The completion arrives as `request-completed` ([events](/pages/api-events/)); the SDK future hides that event.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, Header, HttpRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::{self, Bucket};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

async fn refresh_forecast() {
    let request = HttpRequest {
        method: "GET".to_string(),
        url: "https://status.anthropic.com/api/v2/summary.json".to_string(),
        headers: vec![Header { name: "accept".into(), value: "application/json".into() }],
        body: None,
        timeout_millis: 5_000,
    };
    match http::fetch(request).await {
        Ok(response) if response.status == 200 => {
            if let Some(reset_at) = parse_reset_time(&response.body) {
                let _ = storage::put(Bucket::Global, "forecast/anthropic", &reset_at.to_le_bytes());
            }
        }
        Ok(response) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("status feed returned {}", response.status)),
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("status feed failed: {}", error.message)),
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { fetch as httpFetch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';

export async function refreshForecast(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const response = await httpFetch({
      method: 'GET',
      url: 'https://status.anthropic.com/api/v2/summary.json',
      headers: [{ name: 'accept', value: 'application/json' }],
      body: undefined,
      timeoutMillis: 5000,
    });
    if (response.status !== 200) {
      log('warn', `status feed returned ${response.status}`);
      return;
    }
    const resetAt = parseResetTime(response.body);
    if (resetAt !== undefined) {
      const bytes = new Uint8Array(8);
      new DataView(bytes.buffer).setBigUint64(0, BigInt(resetAt), true);
      storage.put('global', 'forecast/anthropic', bytes);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `status feed failed: ${String(error)}`);
  }
}
```

#### Serve usage to other plugins

Other plugins ask for spend per pane through a JSON service. The plugin implements `ServiceProvider` for `ilium.core.cost/usage` ([services API](/pages/api-services/), [services grant](/pages/capability-services/), [service catalogue](/pages/services/)). For cached figures it answers at once with `ServiceReply::Done`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{ServiceCall, ServiceReply};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["service-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct CostServer {
    /// Spend per pane in dollars, refreshed on every transcript change.
    by_pane: std::collections::BTreeMap<u64, f64>,
}

impl Lifecycle for CostServer {}

impl Handler for CostServer {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl ServiceProvider for CostServer {
    fn handle(&mut self, call: ServiceCall) -> ServiceReply {
        // The host has already checked the payload against the schema.
        let panes: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> = self
            .by_pane
            .iter()
            .map(|(pane, dollars)| (pane.to_string(), serde_json::json!(dollars)))
            .collect();
        ServiceReply::Done(serde_json::json!({ "panes": panes }).to_string())
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type ServiceCall, type ServiceReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

const byPane = new Map<bigint, number>(); // spend per pane in dollars

export const { lifecycle, handler, serviceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents() {
    return [];
  },
  handle(_call: ServiceCall): ServiceReply {
    const panes: Record<string, number> = {};
    for (const [pane, dollars] of byPane) panes[pane.toString()] = dollars;
    return { tag: 'done', val: JSON.stringify({ panes }) };
  },
});
```

#### Model and price per pane

`agent-model-changed` tells the plugin which model a pane now runs. The plugin keeps the model per pane and uses its context window for the context gauge, so a switch to a larger model is priced correctly from the next turn.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentModel;

impl Handler for ModelPricing {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::AgentModelChanged(change) = event {
                self.models.insert(change.pane, change.model);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn context_window(&self, pane: NodeId) -> Option<u32> {
    self.models.get(&pane).and_then(|model: &AgentModel| model.context_window)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'agent-model-changed') continue;
    models.set(event.val.pane, event.val.model);
  }
  return [];
}

function contextWindow(pane: string): number | undefined {
  return models.get(pane)?.contextWindow;
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.cost` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.cost/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.cost/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `price-sources` | collect | Supply a price table for models the built-in table does not know. | entry: id, model_pattern, input_per_mtok, output_per_mtok, cache_read_per_mtok, currency | standard |
| `quota-sources` | collect | Supply a plan quota or remaining allowance for a provider. | entry: id, provider, service (a service the plugin provides) | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.cost/usage`: get: spend and tokens per pane, session or day

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.cost/usage-changed`: { pane, total } when the total of a pane changes

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.cost"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Prices a local model at zero

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.cost/price-sources"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.cost/price-sources",
        "id": "local-llm",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "model_pattern": "qwen3-*",
          "input_per_mtok": 0,
          "output_per_mtok": 0,
          "currency": "USD"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Titles and organisation

## Titles and organisation

Titles and organisation is the plugin form of Ilium's AI naming and tree tidying. It turns each prompt you send to an agent into a short pane title, picks an icon for the row, names new sessions, and can reorganise the whole tree into groups that you undo in one step. Its id is `ilium.core.titles` and it runs on both sides: the server side asks the model and edits the tree, and the client side shows the preview panel. It needs a configured AI provider, which [Inference providers](/pages/core-plugin-inference/) supplies.

Ilium keeps one rule about names: a title that you typed by hand is never replaced by an inferred one. The host enforces it, so the plugin only has to submit and read the outcome.

### What it covers

- **Automatic pane titles and title style.** A submitted prompt yields a short title in the style you chose (Automatic titles, Title style in the user documentation).
- **Session naming.** New sessions get a name, and you can trigger a name by hand (Triggering titles manually).
- **Tree organisation.** The model proposes groups, and one undo step reverts them (Tree organization instructions; Tree organization in the privacy guide).
- **AI triggers.** Toggles decide which events start titling (the Triggers tab of Settings).
- **Custom instruction inputs.** Seven text inputs steer the titles (The seven instruction inputs).
- **Inferred-title icons.** The title also picks the icon of the row.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/03-contextual-titles.gif" alt="Pane titles change as the user sends prompts to agents" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Pane titles follow the prompts sent to each agent.</figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/01-ai-tree.gif" alt="The tree is reorganised into groups by the model" loading="lazy"><figcaption>The tree organised into groups.</figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/07c-settings-tour-c.gif" alt="A tour of the last Settings tabs, including the title options" loading="lazy"><figcaption>The title options in Settings.</figcaption></figure>

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `titles` | Titles | `[inference]` | none |
| `triggers` | Triggers | `[triggers]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Titles and organisation is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### 1. Automatic pane titles

On `input-submitted` the server asks [inference](/pages/api-inference/) for a title, with the [inference grant](/pages/capability-inference/) and the [prompt-reading grant](/pages/capability-agent-read-prompts/). The call returns a request id at once, so the plugin keeps the pair of request and pane, and on `request-completed` it submits `rename-node` with `source: inferred`. See [events](/pages/api-events/) and [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::RenameNodeSpec;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["inference",
//   "agent.read-prompts", "tree.read", "tree.write"] }
#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Titler {
    pending: Vec<(RequestId, NodeId)>,
}

impl Lifecycle for Titler {}

impl Handler for Titler {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::InputSubmitted(input) => {
                    let request = CompletionRequest {
                        messages: vec![
                            ChatMessage {
                                role: "system".into(),
                                content: "Reply with a title of at most four words.".into(),
                            },
                            ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: input.text },
                        ],
                        max_output_tokens: None,
                        json_schema: None,
                        purpose: "pane-title".into(),
                    };
                    match inference::complete_request(request) {
                        Ok(id) => self.pending.push((id, input.node)),
                        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("no title: {error:?}")),
                    }
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(done) => {
                    let Some(at) = self.pending.iter().position(|(id, _)| *id == done.request)
                    else { continue };
                    let (_, node) = self.pending.remove(at);
                    let Some(completion) = inference::take_completion(done.request) else { continue };
                    submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::RenameNode(RenameNodeSpec {
                        node,
                        title: completion.text.trim().to_string(),
                        expected_revision: None,
                    })));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { completeRequest, takeCompletion } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["inference",
//   "agent.read-prompts", "tree.read", "tree.write"] }
const pending = new Map<bigint, bigint>(); // request id -> node
let correlation = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'input-submitted') {
        const id = completeRequest({
          messages: [
            { role: 'system', content: 'Reply with a title of at most four words.' },
            { role: 'user', content: event.val.text },
          ],
          maxOutputTokens: undefined,
          jsonSchema: undefined,
          purpose: 'pane-title',
        });
        pending.set(id, event.val.node);
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && pending.has(event.val.request)) {
        const node = pending.get(event.val.request)!;
        pending.delete(event.val.request);
        const completion = takeCompletion(event.val.request);
        if (completion === undefined) continue;
        submissions.push({
          intent: {
            tag: 'rename-node',
            val: { node, title: completion.text.trim(), source: 'inferred', expectedRevision: undefined },
          },
          correlation: correlation++,
          dedupKey: undefined,
        });
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### 2. Inferred-title icons

The title also picks an icon. The plugin maps the topic of the title to an icon and submits `set-inferred-icon`, one of the [tree chrome intents](/pages/api-tree-chrome/). An icon that you set by hand is never replaced: the host answers `refused(conflict)`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetInferredIconSpec;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.decorate"] }

/// A small topic table. The plugin's own code, not part of the SDK.
fn icon_for_title(title: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let lower = title.to_lowercase();
    const TOPICS: [(&str, &str); 3] = [("fix", "🔧"), ("test", "🧪"), ("deploy", "🚀")];
    TOPICS.iter().find(|(word, _)| lower.contains(word)).map(|(_, icon)| *icon)
}

/// Submitted right after the rename. A manual icon wins: the host
/// answers refused(conflict) and the plugin leaves the row alone.
fn icon_submission(node: NodeId, title: &str) -> Option<Submission> {
    let icon = icon_for_title(title)?;
    Some(Submission::new(Intent::SetInferredIcon(SetInferredIconSpec {
        node,
        icon: Some(icon.into()),
        source: "titler".into(),
    })))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.decorate"] }
const TOPICS: Array<[string, string]> = [['fix', '🔧'], ['test', '🧪'], ['deploy', '🚀']];

function iconForTitle(title: string): string | undefined {
  const lower = title.toLowerCase();
  return TOPICS.find(([word]) => lower.includes(word))?.[1];
}

// A manual icon wins: the host answers refused(conflict).
export function iconSubmission(node: bigint, title: string, correlation: bigint): Submission | undefined {
  const icon = iconForTitle(title);
  if (icon === undefined) return undefined;
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'set-inferred-icon', val: { node, icon, source: 'titler' } },
    correlation,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### 3. Organise the tree, with undo

With the [tree.restructure grant](/pages/capability-tree-restructure/) the plugin submits `restructure` with up to 256 operations and a label, described under [tree structure intents](/pages/api-intent-tree-structure/). It keeps the returned token and submits `revert-restructure` when the user presses Undo. The token does not survive a server restart.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::RestructureSpec;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.read", "tree.restructure"] },
//           "contributes": { "commands": [{ "id": "undo-organise", ... }] }
impl Titler {
    /// Applies the proposal as one change. `plan_operations` is the
    /// plugin's own code: it builds move, create-group, ungroup and
    /// rename operations from the model's answer (at most 256).
    fn organise(&mut self) -> Submission {
        Submission::keyed(
            Intent::Restructure(RestructureSpec {
                operations: self.plan_operations(),
                label: "Group panes by project".into(),
            }),
            "organise".into(),
        )
    }

    fn on_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Vec<Submission> {
        match event {
            // ok-node carries the undo token; 0 means nothing changed.
            Event::RequestCompleted(done) => {
                if let Outcome::OkNode(token) = done.outcome {
                    if token != 0 {
                        self.undo_token = Some(token);
                    }
                }
                Vec::new()
            }
            Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command.ends_with("/undo-organise") => {
                self.undo_token
                    .take()
                    .map(|token| Submission::new(Intent::RevertRestructure(token)))
                    .into_iter()
                    .collect()
            }
            _ => Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.read", "tree.restructure"] },
//           "contributes": { "commands": [{ "id": "undo-organise", ... }] }
let undoToken: bigint | undefined;

// planOperations is the plugin's own code: move, create-group, ungroup
// and rename operations from the model's answer (at most 256).
export function organise(): Submission {
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'restructure', val: { operations: planOperations(), label: 'Group panes by project' } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: 'organise',
  };
}

export function onTreeEvent(event: Event): Submission[] {
  if (event.tag === 'request-completed') {
    const outcome = event.val.outcome;
    if (outcome.tag === 'ok-node' && outcome.val !== 0n) undoToken = outcome.val;
  } else if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command.endsWith('/undo-organise')) {
    if (undoToken === undefined) return [];
    const token = undoToken;
    undoToken = undefined;
    return [{ intent: { tag: 'revert-restructure', val: token }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined }];
  }
  return [];
}
```

#### 4. Preview the change

Before applying, the client panel shows the old and new outlines as a `diff-view` with a `paragraph` summary of the moves, both from [text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/). The server sends the two outlines to the client, which draws them; the apply button then calls the first function of the previous sample.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::Area;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{DiffHunk, DiffLayout, DiffLine, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] }
impl Views for TitlesPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let mut lines = vec![DiffLine::context(1, 1, "tree, 4 panes")];
        for (number, old) in self.old_outline.iter().enumerate() {
            lines.push(DiffLine::removed(number as u32 + 2, old));
        }
        for (number, new) in self.new_outline.iter().enumerate() {
            lines.push(DiffLine::added(number as u32 + 2, new));
        }
        let hunk = DiffHunk { header: "@@ tree @@".into(), lines };
        let diff = tree.diff_view(vec![hunk]).layout(DiffLayout::Unified).key("diff");
        let summary = tree
            .paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain(format!(
                "Moves: {}, new groups: {}",
                self.moves, self.groups
            ))]])
            .key("summary");
        let root = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(1)])
            .child(diff)
            .child(summary);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { diffView, fill, layout, length, paragraph, span, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] }
export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  render() {
    const lines = [
      { kind: 'context', oldLine: 1, newLine: 1, text: 'tree, 4 panes' },
      ...state.oldOutline.map((text, i) => ({ kind: 'removed', oldLine: i + 2, text })),
      ...state.newOutline.map((text, i) => ({ kind: 'added', newLine: i + 2, text })),
    ];
    const diff = diffView([{ header: '@@ tree @@', lines }], { key: 'diff', layout: 'unified' });
    const summary = paragraph(
      [[span(`Moves: ${state.moves}, new groups: ${state.groups}`)]],
      { key: 'summary' },
    );
    return tree(layout({ direction: 'vertical', constraints: [fill(1), length(1)] }, [diff, summary]));
  },
});
```

#### 5. Instructions and triggers

Settings hold the instruction text and which events trigger titling. The plugin declares `text-area` and `toggle` rows (see [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) and [settings row types](/pages/reference-settings-rows/)) and re-reads its values on `settings-changed`, an [event](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use serde::Deserialize;

// manifest settings rows (server scope):
//   { "type": "text-area", "key": "instructions", "title": "Instructions",
//     "max_length": 2000, "default": "" }
//   { "type": "toggle", "key": "name_from_prompts", "title": "Name panes",
//     "default": true }
#[derive(Deserialize, Default, Clone)]
struct TitleSettings {
    instructions: String,
    name_from_prompts: bool,
}

fn load_settings() -> TitleSettings {
    serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or_default()
}

impl Handler for Titler {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            // Re-read on every change so the next title uses the new text.
            if let Event::SettingsChanged(_) = event {
                self.settings = load_settings();
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

// manifest settings rows (server scope):
//   { "type": "text-area", "key": "instructions", "title": "Instructions",
//     "max_length": 2000, "default": "" }
//   { "type": "toggle", "key": "name_from_prompts", "title": "Name panes",
//     "default": true }
interface TitleSettings { instructions: string; name_from_prompts: boolean }

let settings: TitleSettings = JSON.parse(getJson());

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      // Re-read on every change so the next title uses the new text.
      if (event.tag === 'settings-changed') settings = JSON.parse(getJson());
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.titles` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.titles/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before-apply-title` | hook (transform) | Change a generated title before it is applied. | node, proposed, source (transcript, process, manual-trigger), previous; reply: proposed | standard |
| `title-styles` | collect | Add a title style to the style choice. | entry: id, title, instruction | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.titles/suggest`: title: ask for a title suggestion for text

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.titles/title-applied`: { node, title }

Calls `ilium:inference/provider` through the inference plugin.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.titles"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds a style that puts the ticket key first

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.titles/title-styles"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.titles/title-styles",
        "id": "ticket-first",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Ticket first",
          "instruction": "Start the title with the ticket key when the text names one."
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Inference providers

## Inference providers

Inference providers is the plugin form of Ilium's AI provider layer. It answers every model request that another plugin makes with the [inference](/pages/api-inference/) import, lists the available models, streams replies, and offers a Test provider button. Its id is `ilium.core.inference` and it runs on both sides: the server side talks to the provider over HTTP, and the client side draws the provider panel. It is the kernel-known `inference-provider` service, and it serves the model list as a catalogue.

The privacy controls stay in the kernel. The AI admission gate checks every request against the `purpose` that the caller named, whatever plugin serves the model, so this plugin cannot widen what is sent.

### What it covers

- **Providers, loading models, test provider.** Choose a provider, load its models, and send a short request to check it (Providers, Loading models, Test provider in the user documentation).
- **AI admission gate and privacy controls.** What is sent where, and the guidance on privacy (What is sent where, Privacy guidance).

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/07b-settings-tour-b.gif" alt="A tour of the middle Settings tabs, including the AI provider options" loading="lazy"><figcaption>The provider options in the Settings tour.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

The settings tab has the provider choice, the model choice read from a catalogue, the Test provider button and an info row. A test sends a short request and shows the reply as it arrives.

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inference` | Inference | `[inference]` | Titles, Recap, Search, Smart copy, Compaction, Voice |
| `llm-instructions` | LLM Instructions | `[inference.instructions]`, `[voice]` | Titles, Recap, Smart copy, Voice |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Inference providers is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### 1. An OpenAI-compatible provider

The plugin exports `inference-provider` (see [plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/) and [services](/pages/services/)) and holds the [inference.provide grant](/pages/capability-inference-provide/). `complete` accepts the call and returns at once. A task answers with `provider-reply` and the same call number.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, Completion, ProviderCall};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["inference.provide",
//   "http:api.openai.com", "http:localhost"] },
//   exports: ["inference-provider"]
#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["inference-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Provider;

impl InferenceProvider for Provider {
    /// Accepts the call and returns at once. A task answers later with
    /// provider_reply and the same call number.
    fn complete(&mut self, call: ProviderCall) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let number = call.call;
        let request = call.request;
        task::spawn(async move {
            // `ask_endpoint` is the plugin's own code: one HTTP round trip.
            let outcome = ask_endpoint(&request).await.map(|text| Completion {
                text,
                model: "gpt-5.6-terra".into(),
                input_tokens: 0,
                output_tokens: 0,
            });
            inference::provider_reply(number, outcome);
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    fn models(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        vec!["gpt-5.6-terra".into()]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { providerReply, type ProviderCall } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["inference.provide",
//   "http:api.openai.com", "http:localhost"] },
//   exports: ["inference-provider"]
export const { lifecycle, handler, inferenceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  // Accepts the call and returns at once; the promise answers later.
  complete(call: ProviderCall): void {
    // askEndpoint is the plugin's own code: one HTTP round trip.
    void askEndpoint(call.request).then(
      (text) => providerReply(call.call, {
        tag: 'ok',
        val: { text, model: 'gpt-5.6-terra', inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0 },
      }),
      (error: { code: string; message: string }) => providerReply(call.call, {
        tag: 'err',
        val: { code: error.code, message: error.message, retryAfterMs: undefined },
      }),
    );
  },
  models(): string[] {
    return ['gpt-5.6-terra'];
  },
});
```

#### 2. Stream tokens

Replies arrive piece by piece over server-sent events, using [HTTP streams](/pages/api-http-streams/) and the [http grant](/pages/capability-http/). The plugin appends each `http-stream-data` chunk and finishes the reply on `http-stream-closed`; see [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, HttpRequest, StreamFraming, StreamRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, Completion};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["http:api.openai.com"] }
fn open_reply_stream(body: Vec<u8>) -> Result<StreamId, PluginError> {
    http::open_stream(StreamRequest {
        request: HttpRequest {
            method: "POST".into(),
            url: "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions".into(),
            headers: vec![],
            body: Some(body),
            timeout_millis: 120_000,
        },
        framing: StreamFraming::ServerSentEvents,
        max_chunk_bytes: 16_384,
    })
}

impl Provider {
    fn on_stream_event(&mut self, event: Event) {
        match event {
            // The host parses the SSE framing: one chunk is one event payload.
            Event::HttpStreamData(data) => {
                self.text.push_str(&delta_from_payload(&data.chunk));
            }
            Event::HttpStreamClosed(closed) => {
                let outcome = closed.outcome.map(|_| Completion {
                    text: std::mem::take(&mut self.text),
                    model: "gpt-5.6-terra".into(),
                    input_tokens: 0,
                    output_tokens: 0,
                });
                inference::provider_reply(self.call, outcome);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { openStream } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import { providerReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import type { Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["http:api.openai.com"] }
export function openReplyStream(body: Uint8Array): bigint {
  return openStream({
    request: {
      method: 'POST',
      url: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions',
      headers: [],
      body,
      timeoutMillis: 120_000,
    },
    framing: 'server-sent-events',
    maxChunkBytes: 16_384,
  });
}

let text = '';

export function onStreamEvent(event: Event, call: bigint): void {
  if (event.tag === 'http-stream-data') {
    // The host parses the SSE framing: one chunk is one event payload.
    text += deltaFromPayload(event.val.chunk);
  } else if (event.tag === 'http-stream-closed') {
    const done = event.val.outcome;
    providerReply(call, done.tag === 'ok'
      ? { tag: 'ok', val: { text, model: 'gpt-5.6-terra', inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0 } }
      : { tag: 'err', val: done.val });
    text = '';
  }
}
```

#### 3. Models as a catalogue

The model choice row reads its options from the plugin instead of listing them. The plugin exports `catalog-provider` (see [catalogues](/pages/api-catalogs/) and [services](/pages/services/)), and the `choice` row, described in [settings row types](/pages/reference-settings-rows/), names the catalogue.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::CatalogItem;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::catalogs::{CatalogPage, CatalogQuery};

// manifest: "contributes": { "catalogs": [{ "id": "models" }] },
//   exports: ["catalog-provider"]; the settings row says
//   { "type": "choice", "key": "model", "source": { "catalog": "models" } }
impl CatalogProvider for Provider {
    fn query_catalog(&mut self, query: CatalogQuery) -> Result<CatalogPage, PluginError> {
        let items: Vec<CatalogItem> = self
            .models
            .iter()
            .filter(|name| name.contains(&query.filter))
            .map(|name| CatalogItem::new(name, name))
            .collect();
        Ok(CatalogPage { items, next: None, total: Some(self.models.len() as u32) })
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { CatalogPage, CatalogQuery } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/catalogs';

// manifest: "contributes": { "catalogs": [{ "id": "models" }] },
//   exports: ["catalog-provider"]; the settings row says
//   { "type": "choice", "key": "model", "source": { "catalog": "models" } }
const models: string[] = ['gpt-5.6-terra', 'gpt-5.6-luna'];

export const { lifecycle, handler, catalogProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  queryCatalog(query: CatalogQuery): CatalogPage {
    const items = models
      .filter((name) => name.includes(query.filter))
      .map((name) => ({ id: name, title: name, keywords: [] }));
    return { items, next: undefined, total: models.length };
  },
});
```

#### 4. Test provider

A `button` row runs a test call (see [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) and [settings row types](/pages/reference-settings-rows/)). When `request-completed` arrives, the plugin writes latency and model into an `info` row. The outcome model is in [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, inference, settings};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// settings rows: { "type": "button", "id": "test", "label": "Run test",
//     "command": "test-provider" }
//   { "type": "info", "id": "last_test", "title": "Last test",
//     "text": "Not run yet", "live": true }
impl Handler for Provider {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command.ends_with("/test-provider") => {
                    let request = CompletionRequest {
                        messages: vec![ChatMessage {
                            role: "user".into(),
                            content: "Reply with the word ok.".into(),
                        }],
                        max_output_tokens: Some(16),
                        json_schema: None,
                        purpose: "provider-test".into(),
                    };
                    self.started = clock::monotonic_millis();
                    self.test = inference::complete_request(request).ok();
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(done) if Some(done.request) == self.test => {
                    self.test = None;
                    let elapsed = clock::monotonic_millis() - self.started;
                    let text = match inference::take_completion(done.request) {
                        Some(c) => format!("{elapsed} ms, {}", c.model),
                        None => "failed".to_string(),
                    };
                    let _ = settings::set_info("last_test", &text);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { monotonicMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import { completeRequest, takeCompletion } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { setInfo } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

// settings rows: { "type": "button", "id": "test", "label": "Run test",
//     "command": "test-provider" }
//   { "type": "info", "id": "last_test", "title": "Last test",
//     "text": "Not run yet", "live": true }
let test: bigint | undefined;
let started = 0n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command.endsWith('/test-provider')) {
        started = monotonicMillis();
        test = completeRequest({
          messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Reply with the word ok.' }],
          maxOutputTokens: 16,
          jsonSchema: undefined,
          purpose: 'provider-test',
        });
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && event.val.request === test) {
        test = undefined;
        const completion = takeCompletion(event.val.request);
        setInfo('last_test', completion
          ? `${monotonicMillis() - started} ms, ${completion.model}`
          : 'failed');
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

#### 5. Provider picker panel

A small client panel switches provider with a `choice` control from [input widgets](/pages/widgets-input/) and writes the selection to the plugin's settings.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::Area;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] }
impl Views for ProviderPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let picker = tree
            .choice("Provider", self.providers.clone(), self.selected)
            .key("provider");
        tree.finish(picker)
    }
}

impl Handler for ProviderPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if let ("provider", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Index(i)) =
                (action.key.as_str(), action.kind, action.value)
            {
                self.selected = i;
                let patch = format!("{{\"provider\": {:?}}}", self.providers[i as usize]);
                let _ = settings::set_json(&patch);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { setJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';
import { choice, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] }
const providers = ['OpenAI-compatible', 'Local server'];
let selected = 0;

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || event.val.key !== 'provider') continue;
      if (event.val.kind === 'changed' && event.val.value.tag === 'index') {
        selected = event.val.value.val;
        setJson(JSON.stringify({ provider: providers[selected] }));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    return tree(choice('Provider', providers, selected, { key: 'provider' }));
  },
});
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.inference` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.inference/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.inference/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before-request` | hook (transform) | Rewrite or refuse an outgoing model request, for example to remove private text. | purpose, provider, model, messages_length, text; reply: text | high |
| `after-response` | hook (observe) | Learn that a request finished, with its token counts. | purpose, provider, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, millis | standard |
| `provider-profiles` | collect | Offer a ready-made provider setup in the provider chooser. | entry: id, title, base_url, models_path, key_name | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.inference/complete`: complete: one-shot completion through the chosen provider

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.inference/request-finished`: { purpose, provider, millis }

Providers implemented by plugins use the `inference-provider` export and `inference.provide`.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.inference"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Replaces home-directory paths in outgoing text with `~`

A package adds a `transform` handler. Each handler gets the previous output and may replace it.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.inference/before-request"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.inference/before-request",
        "id": "redact-paths",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "redact_paths"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "redact_paths" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: purpose, provider, model, messages_length, text
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Replace(new_payload_json)
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'redact_paths') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: purpose, provider, model, messages_length, text
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'replace', val: newPayloadJson };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Notifications

## Notifications

Notifications is the plugin form of Ilium's alerts. It plays sounds for events, shows desktop notices, draws in-app toasts, merges bursts of redundant task alerts, and marks tree nodes that need you for the Attention display mode. Its id is `ilium.core.notifications` and it runs on both sides: the server side reacts to agent events and submits sounds, notices and marks, and the client side draws the toasts inside the Ilium window.

The kernel keeps the policy. The look of an attention mark, the done prefix and the sound rate belong to the kernel, so the plugin only decides when to ask.

### What it covers

- **Sound alerts.** One sound per event kind, chosen in Settings (Sounds in the notifications guide).
- **Desktop notifications.** A notice from the operating system for events you may miss (Desktop notifications).
- **Coalescing of redundant alerts.** Task alerts that repeat inside a window are merged or skipped (How task alerts are merged or skipped).
- **Attention marks on nodes.** Nodes that need you carry a mark until you acknowledge it (Normal mode and Attention mode in the agent monitoring guide).

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/05-ask-for-update.gif" alt="Two agents idle and one at an approval prompt, the moment the notification plugin fires" loading="lazy"><figcaption>An agent asks for approval. The sound and attention mark fire on that prompt.</figcaption></figure>

The recording shows the approval prompt. No recording shows the desktop toast or the mute toggle, so those parts use renders.

### What the user sees

The first render is a toast in the corner with a countdown line and two actions. The second is the sound tab of Settings.

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sound` | Sound | `[sound]`, `[notifications]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Notifications is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### 1. Sound on approval prompts

On `agent-activity-changed` to awaiting approval, the plugin submits `play-sound` with the sound chosen in Settings. This needs the [sound.play grant](/pages/capability-sound-play/); see [notifications and sounds](/pages/api-notifications/) and [events](/pages/api-events/). The dedup key stops a repeat of the same prompt from sounding twice.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["sound.play", "agent.read"] },
//   "contributes": { "sounds": [{ "id": "ask", "file": "sounds/ask.wav" }] }
impl Handler for Notifier {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            if matches!(change.current, AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval) {
                // One sound per approval prompt; a new revision is a new prompt.
                submissions.push(Submission::keyed(
                    Intent::PlaySound(self.approval_sound.clone()),
                    format!("ask:{}:{}", change.node, change.revision),
                ));
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["sound.play", "agent.read"] },
//   "contributes": { "sounds": [{ "id": "ask", "file": "sounds/ask.wav" }] }
let approvalSound = 'ask';
let correlation = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'agent-activity-changed') continue;
      const change = event.val;
      if (change.current === 'awaiting-approval') {
        // One sound per approval prompt; a new revision is a new prompt.
        submissions.push({
          intent: { tag: 'play-sound', val: approvalSound },
          correlation: correlation++,
          dedupKey: `ask:${change.node}:${change.revision}`,
        });
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### 2. Desktop notification, coalesced

One notice for a burst of finished tasks. The plugin submits `notify` with a coalesce key and a 30,000 ms window, so notices inside the window replace each other. It needs the [notify.desktop grant](/pages/capability-notify-desktop/); the fields are in [notifications and sounds](/pages/api-notifications/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{NotifySpec, Urgency};

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["notify.desktop"] }
/// A burst of finished tasks becomes one notice: notices with the same
/// coalesce key inside the window (at most 60,000 ms) replace each other.
fn task_done_notice(count: u32) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Notify(NotifySpec {
        title: "Tasks finished".into(),
        body: format!("{count} tasks are done."),
        urgency: Urgency::Normal,
        sound: None,
        coalesce_key: Some("task-done".into()),
        coalesce_window_ms: 30_000,
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["notify.desktop"] }
// Notices with the same coalesce key inside the window (at most 60,000 ms)
// replace each other, so a burst becomes one notice.
export function taskDoneNotice(count: number, correlation: bigint): Submission {
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'notify',
      val: {
        title: 'Tasks finished',
        body: `${count} tasks are done.`,
        urgency: 'normal',
        sound: undefined,
        coalesceKey: 'task-done',
        coalesceWindowMs: 30_000,
      },
    },
    correlation,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### 3. In-app toast with actions

A toast offers Open and Dismiss. The client submits `toast` with tone, title and two actions, using [toast](/pages/api-toast/), the [notify.toast grant](/pages/capability-notify-toast/) and the [chrome intents](/pages/api-intent-chrome/). Each button names a command that the plugin declares, and a press arrives as a `command-invoked` [event](/pages/api-events/); the dismiss button then submits `dismiss-toast`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{ToastAction, ToastSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Tone;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["notify.toast"] },
//   "contributes": { "commands": [
//     { "id": "open-pane", "title": "Open the pane" },
//     { "id": "dismiss-toast", "title": "Dismiss" }] }
fn finished_toast(node: NodeId) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
        id: Some(format!("finished-{node}")),
        tone: Tone::Success,
        title: "Agent finished".into(),
        body: None,
        actions: vec![
            ToastAction { label: "Open".into(), command: "open-pane".into() },
            ToastAction { label: "Dismiss".into(), command: "dismiss-toast".into() },
        ],
        duration_ms: Some(10_000),
    }))
}

/// A press of a toast button arrives as command-invoked.
fn on_toast_command(command: &str, node: NodeId) -> Vec<Submission> {
    if command.ends_with("/dismiss-toast") {
        return vec![Submission::new(Intent::DismissToast(format!("finished-{node}")))];
    }
    Vec::new() // open-pane focuses the pane with the tree intents
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["notify.toast"] },
//   "contributes": { "commands": [
//     { "id": "open-pane", "title": "Open the pane" },
//     { "id": "dismiss-toast", "title": "Dismiss" }] }
export function finishedToast(node: bigint): Submission {
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'toast',
      val: {
        id: `finished-${node}`,
        tone: 'success',
        title: 'Agent finished',
        body: undefined,
        actions: [
          { label: 'Open', command: 'open-pane' },
          { label: 'Dismiss', command: 'dismiss-toast' },
        ],
        durationMs: 10_000,
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}

// A press of a toast button arrives as command-invoked.
export function onToastCommand(command: string, node: bigint): Submission[] {
  if (command.endsWith('/dismiss-toast')) {
    return [{ intent: { tag: 'dismiss-toast', val: `finished-${node}` }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined }];
  }
  return []; // open-pane focuses the pane with the tree intents
}
```

#### 4. Attention marks

Nodes that need the user get a mark until acknowledged. The plugin submits `mark-attention` with a reason, and on `attention-changed` it submits `ack-attention` for the same node. This needs the [tree.attention grant](/pages/capability-tree-attention/); the event is in [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::MarkAttentionSpec;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.attention", "tree.read"] }
impl Handler for Notifier {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::AgentActivityChanged(change) if is_waiting(change.current) => {
                    submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::MarkAttention(MarkAttentionSpec {
                        node: change.node,
                        reason: "waiting for you".into(), // at most 80 characters
                    })));
                }
                // The user looked at the node: clear the mark for the same node.
                Event::AttentionChanged(changed) if changed.marked && self.seen(changed.node) => {
                    submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::AckAttention(changed.node)));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.attention", "tree.read"] }
let correlation = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'agent-activity-changed' && isWaiting(event.val.current)) {
        submissions.push({
          intent: { tag: 'mark-attention', val: { node: event.val.node, reason: 'waiting for you' } },
          correlation: correlation++,
          dedupKey: undefined,
        });
      } else if (event.tag === 'attention-changed' && event.val.marked && seen(event.val.node)) {
        // The user looked at the node: clear the mark for the same node.
        submissions.push({
          intent: { tag: 'ack-attention', val: event.val.node },
          correlation: correlation++,
          dedupKey: undefined,
        });
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### 5. Mute sound with a toggle

The sound toggle in the toast sends `toggled` with a flag. The plugin stores the flag and skips `play-sound` while it is set. The flag is kept across restarts through the plugin's storage.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};

impl Handler for MuteToggle {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if let (ActionKind::Toggled, ActionValue::Flag(muted), "sound-mute") =
                (action.kind, action.value, action.key.as_str())
            {
                self.muted = muted;
                storage::put("muted", if muted { b"1" } else { b"0" });
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onAction(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'ui-action' }>): Submission[] {
  const { kind, value, key } = event.val;
  if (kind === 'toggled' && key === 'sound-mute' && value.tag === 'flag') {
    soundMuted = value.val;
    storage.put('muted', soundMuted ? '1' : '0');
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.notifications` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.notifications/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.notifications/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `before-notify` | hook (veto) | Mute or refuse a notification, for example at night. | event, pane, title, urgency, channels | standard |
| `channels` | collect | Add a delivery channel such as a chat webhook. | entry: id, title, service (a service the plugin provides that delivers one notice) | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.notifications/notify`: send: raise a notice with a title, a body and an urgency

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.notifications/raised`: { event, pane, urgency }

The `agent-question` channel of `ilium.core.fleet` arrives here as a peer message.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.notifications"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Refuses every notice with urgency `low` between 22:00 and 07:00

A package adds a `veto` handler. Handlers run until one refuses.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.notifications/before-notify"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.notifications/before-notify",
        "id": "quiet-hours",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "quiet_hours"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "quiet_hours" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: event, pane, title, urgency, channels
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Refuse("reason".into())
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'quiet_hours') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: event, pane, title, urgency, channels
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'refuse', val: 'reason' };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Voice

## Voice

Voice is the plugin form of Ilium's voice control. Hold F8 or press the voice button, speak, and Ilium either runs one of its own commands or types a prompt into an agent, asking for confirmation when the action is destructive. Its id is `ilium.core.voice` and it runs on both sides: the client side owns the microphone, the key and the dialogs, and the server side adds the `ilium voice say` command. Capturing audio from the operating system is a kernel service; the plugin drives it through the audio import.

### What it covers

- **Voice session.** F8 and the voice control button start and stop listening (Using F8 and the voice control button in the voice guide).
- **Confirmations and safety.** Destructive commands wait for a confirmation (Confirmations and safety).
- **ilium voice say.** Typed voice input from the command line, with JSONL output (Typed voice input; the `ilium voice say` entry of the CLI reference).
- **Onboarding.** The steps for turning voice on (Step by step: turning voice on).
- **Device selection and reconnect.** Choose a microphone and recover when it returns (Audio devices).

```json
  "capabilities": {

    "client": ["audio.microphone", "keys.intercept", "commands.invoke:*",

```

`commands.invoke:*` lets voice run any command, so the user confirms it at install and the plugin still asks before a destructive one.
