### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voice-control` | Voice control | `[voice]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Voice is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### 1. Push to talk on F8

Holding F8 records and releasing it stops. The plugin grabs the key with [keys](/pages/api-keys/) and the [keys.intercept grant](/pages/capability-keys-intercept/), starts capture on `key-pressed`, stops on `key-released`, and releases the grab when voice is turned off. See [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::keys::{self, GrabSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["keys.intercept"] }
#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Voice {
    grab: Option<u64>,
    listening: bool,
}

impl Lifecycle for Voice {}

impl Handler for Voice {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::KeyPressed(key) if key.grab == self.grab && !key.repeat => {
                    self.listening = true; // start capture, see the next sample
                }
                Event::KeyReleased(key) if key.grab == self.grab => {
                    self.listening = false; // stop capture, start transcription
                }
                Event::SettingsChanged(_) if !voice_enabled() => self.release_f8(),
                Event::SettingsChanged(_) if self.grab.is_none() => self.grab_f8(),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Voice {
    fn grab_f8(&mut self) {
        // Release reports need the kitty keyboard protocol in the terminal.
        let spec = GrabSpec { chords: vec!["F8".into()], pane: None, until_release: true };
        self.grab = keys::grab(&spec).ok();
    }

    fn release_f8(&mut self) {
        if let Some(grab) = self.grab.take() {
            keys::release(grab);
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { grab, release } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keys';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["keys.intercept"] }
let f8: bigint | undefined;
let listening = false;

function grabF8(): void {
  // Release reports need the kitty keyboard protocol in the terminal.
  f8 = grab({ chords: ['F8'], pane: undefined, untilRelease: true });
}

function releaseF8(): void {
  if (f8 !== undefined) release(f8);
  f8 = undefined;
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'key-pressed' && event.val.grab === f8 && !event.val.repeat) {
        listening = true; // start capture, see the next sample
      } else if (event.tag === 'key-released' && event.val.grab === f8) {
        listening = false; // stop capture, start transcription
      } else if (event.tag === 'settings-changed') {
        if (!voiceEnabled()) releaseF8();
        else if (f8 === undefined) grabF8();
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

#### 2. Capture microphone frames

Audio frames feed the speech model in a job. The plugin opens a 16 kHz capture with [audio](/pages/api-audio/) and the [audio grant](/pages/capability-audio/), buffers `audio-frames` events, and starts a transcription [job](/pages/api-jobs/) when the key is released.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{audio, jobs, log::{self, Level}};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["audio.microphone", "jobs.run",
//   "inference"] }, "contributes": { "jobs": [{ "kind": "transcribe",
//   "deadline_ms": 30000, "memory_mib": 512 }] }
impl Voice {
    fn start_capture(&mut self) {
        // 16 kHz, one channel: the format the speech model expects.
        self.capture = audio::open_capture(None, 16_000, 1).ok();
        self.samples.clear();
    }

    fn on_audio(&mut self, event: Event) {
        match event {
            Event::AudioFrames(frames) if Some(frames.capture) == self.capture => {
                self.samples.extend_from_slice(&frames.samples);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    fn stop_and_transcribe(&mut self) {
        if let Some(capture) = self.capture.take() {
            audio::close_capture(capture);
        }
        let pcm: Vec<u8> = self.samples.iter().flat_map(|s| s.to_le_bytes()).collect();
        task::spawn(async move {
            match jobs::start("transcribe", &pcm).await {
                Ok(text) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("heard {} bytes of text", text.len())),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("transcription failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        });
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as audio from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/audio';
import { start } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["audio.microphone", "jobs.run",
//   "inference"] }, "contributes": { "jobs": [{ "kind": "transcribe",
//   "deadline_ms": 30000, "memory_mib": 512 }] }
let capture: bigint | undefined;
let samples: number[] = [];

export function startCapture(): void {
  // 16 kHz, one channel: the format the speech model expects.
  capture = audio.openCapture(undefined, 16_000, 1);
  samples = [];
}

export function onAudio(event: Event): void {
  if (event.tag === 'audio-frames' && event.val.capture === capture) {
    samples.push(...event.val.samples);
  }
}

export async function stopAndTranscribe(): Promise<void> {
  if (capture !== undefined) audio.closeCapture(capture);
  capture = undefined;
  const pcm = new Uint8Array(new Int16Array(samples).buffer);
  try {
    const text = await start('transcribe', pcm);
    log('info', `heard ${text.length} bytes of text`);
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `transcription failed: ${String(error)}`);
  }
}
```

#### 3. Voice runs Ilium commands

A recognised phrase runs a command after confirmation. The plugin maps the transcript to a command id, shows a `dialog` from [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) for destructive ones, and then submits the `invoke-command` [intent](/pages/api-intents/). It needs the [commands.invoke grant](/pages/capability-commands-invoke/); see also [commands](/pages/api-commands/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::InvokeCommandSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::Constraint;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::PopupAnchor;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["commands.invoke:*", "ui.panels"] }
// `command_for` is the plugin's own phrase table: transcript -> command id.
impl Voice {
    fn on_transcript(&mut self, transcript: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let Some(command) = command_for(transcript) else { return Vec::new() };
        if is_destructive(&command) {
            // A dialog (rendered with dialog kind danger-confirm) asks first.
            self.waiting = Some(command);
            let anchor = PopupAnchor::Centered((Constraint::Length(52), Constraint::Length(7)));
            let _ = ui::open_popup("confirm-voice", anchor);
            return Vec::new();
        }
        vec![invoke(command)]
    }

    fn on_dialog(&mut self, key: &str, button: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
        match (key, button, self.waiting.take()) {
            ("confirm-voice", "ok", Some(command)) => vec![invoke(command)],
            _ => Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

fn invoke(command: String) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::InvokeCommand(InvokeCommandSpec {
        command,
        arguments_json: "{}".into(),
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { openPopup } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { length } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "client": ["commands.invoke:*", "ui.panels"] }
// commandFor is the plugin's own phrase table: transcript -> command id.
let waiting: string | undefined;

function invoke(command: string): Submission {
  return { intent: { tag: 'invoke-command', val: { command, argumentsJson: '{}' } }, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: undefined };
}

export function onTranscript(transcript: string): Submission[] {
  const command = commandFor(transcript);
  if (command === undefined) return [];
  if (isDestructive(command)) {
    // A dialog (rendered with kind danger-confirm) asks first.
    waiting = command;
    openPopup('confirm-voice', { tag: 'centered', val: [length(52), length(7)] });
    return [];
  }
  return [invoke(command)];
}

export function onDialog(key: string, button: string): Submission[] {
  const command = waiting;
  waiting = undefined;
  return key === 'confirm-voice' && button === 'ok' && command !== undefined ? [invoke(command)] : [];
}
```

#### 4. ilium voice say

Typed voice input from the command line reaches a client. On `cli-invoked` the server side calls `client_requests.request`, and the client answers its `client-request` with the JSONL result. See [client requests](/pages/api-client-requests/), the [command line](/pages/api-cli/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{cli, client_requests};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::{CliInvokedEvent, ClientRequestEvent};

// server manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["cli.contribute"] },
//   "contributes": { "cli": { "name": "voice", "output": "jsonl", ... } }
// client manifest: "client_requests": [{ "id": "voice-say", "timeout_ms": 5000 }]
impl Handler for VoiceServer {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::ClientAttached(client) => self.client = Some(client),
                Event::CliInvoked(CliInvokedEvent { invocation, argv, .. }) => {
                    let payload = serde_json::json!({ "text": argv.join(" ") }).to_string();
                    match self.client.map(|c| client_requests::request(c, "voice-say", &payload, 5_000)) {
                        Some(Ok(request)) => self.pending.push((request, invocation)),
                        _ => cli::finish(invocation, 1),
                    }
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(done) => {
                    let Some(at) = self.pending.iter().position(|(r, _)| *r == done.request) else { continue };
                    let (_, invocation) = self.pending.remove(at);
                    let line = client_requests::take_answer(done.request).unwrap_or_default();
                    let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
                    cli::finish(invocation, if done.outcome.is_ok() { 0 } else { 1 });
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

// Client side: answer the request with the JSONL result.
fn answer(event: &Event) {
    if let Event::ClientRequest(ClientRequestEvent { call, kind, payload_json }) = event {
        if kind == "voice-say" {
            client_requests::respond(*call, Ok(run_typed_voice_input(payload_json)));
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as cli from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/cli';
import * as clientRequests from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/client-requests';

// server manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["cli.contribute"] },
//   "contributes": { "cli": { "name": "voice", "output": "jsonl", ... } }
// client manifest: "client_requests": [{ "id": "voice-say", "timeout_ms": 5000 }]
let client: bigint | undefined;
const pending = new Map<bigint, bigint>(); // request id -> invocation

export const serverSide = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'client-attached') {
        client = event.val;
      } else if (event.tag === 'cli-invoked') {
        const payload = JSON.stringify({ text: event.val.argv.join(' ') });
        if (client === undefined) { cli.finish(event.val.invocation, 1); continue; }
        pending.set(clientRequests.request(client, 'voice-say', payload, 5_000), event.val.invocation);
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && pending.has(event.val.request)) {
        const invocation = pending.get(event.val.request)!;
        pending.delete(event.val.request);
        cli.writeLine(invocation, clientRequests.takeAnswer(event.val.request) ?? '{}');
        cli.finish(invocation, event.val.outcome.tag === 'ok' ? 0 : 1);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});

// Client side: answer the request with the JSONL result.
export function answer(event: Event): void {
  if (event.tag === 'client-request' && event.val.kind === 'voice-say') {
    clientRequests.respond(event.val.call, { tag: 'ok', val: runTypedVoiceInput(event.val.payloadJson) });
  }
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.voice` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.voice/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.voice/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `transcript` | hook (transform) | Correct the transcript before commands are matched. | text, confidence, language; reply: text | standard |
| `voice-intents` | collect | Add a spoken phrase that runs a command. | entry: id, phrases, command, confirm | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.voice/say`: type: type a sentence into the live voice session

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.voice/heard`: { text, command }

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.voice"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds the phrase `open the board`

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.voice/voice-intents"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.voice/voice-intents",
        "id": "open-board",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "phrases": [
            "open the board"
          ],
          "command": "open-board",
          "confirm": false
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Scheduler

## Scheduler

Scheduler is the plugin form of Ilium's delayed and queued input. It sends text to a pane after a countdown, even after a restart. It holds a prompt queue that delivers one prompt each time an agent finishes a turn. It sends multi-stage input that cannot interleave with your typing, and it retries safely when a delivery is uncertain. Its id is `ilium.core.scheduler` and it runs on both sides: the client side draws the schedule dialog and the queue dialog, and the server side owns the timers and the writes to the terminal.

Writing into a pane is a kernel service. The plugin only submits the `send-input` intent, and the kernel checks the grants, the dedup key and the preconditions before one byte reaches the PTY.

### What it covers

- **Scheduled input.** The menu entry is "Hit key(s) X time from now". A countdown of hours, minutes and seconds ends in a send of the text, then Enter. A pane has at most one pending schedule; a new one replaces the old one. It survives a restart (Scheduled input in the automation guide).
- **Prompt queue.** The menu entry is "Queue prompt...". One queued prompt is sent each time the agent finishes a turn, which is a Working to Idle or Done transition, not whenever it is idle (Prompt queue).

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/04-scheduled-input.gif" alt="A prompt is scheduled with a countdown and sent to the pane when the countdown ends" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Scheduled input arrives when the countdown ends.</figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/06-prompt-queue.gif" alt="Prompts are added to a queue and sent one by one as the agent finishes each turn" loading="lazy"><figcaption>The prompt queue sends the next prompt each time the agent finishes a turn.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

The first render is the schedule dialog **Schedule input for _pane name_**, with the countdown fields, the payload and the Send Enter switch. The second is the dialog **Queue prompt after agent finishes**, with the prompt text, the delivery mode and the repeat count. This is the baseline user interface; a calendar mode is not part of it.

### Behaviour contract

Every value below is the baseline value. A calendar mode or a queue panel with edit and move keys is not parity; if a build adds one it is listed as "New in the plugin build, not parity" and has no row here.

| Id | Rule | Exact value or text | Baseline source |
|---|---|---|---|
| scheduler-B01 | Menu entry for scheduled input | "Hit key(s) X time from now", on terminal panes only (shell or agent); editors and boards do not have it | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B02 | Dialog fields | Hours: any whole number, blank is 0. Minutes: 0 to 59, blank is 0. Seconds: 0 to 59, initial 30. Payload: single line, any Unicode. Send Enter: on by default | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B03 | Dialog keys | Tab and Shift+Tab move between fields, Space toggles Send Enter, Ctrl+Enter schedules, Esc cancels | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B04 | Zero delay | Refused: "Choose a delay of at least one second" | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B05 | Empty payload with Send Enter off | Refused: "Enter text, enable Send Enter, or use both" | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B06 | Minutes or seconds above 59 | Refused with a message naming the field. A non-digit typed in a number field is ignored | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B07 | Pending schedules per pane | One. A new schedule replaces the old one | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B08 | Text and Enter | The text is written, then Enter as a separate step, while the pane input gate is held so typed input cannot interleave. Text only writes no Enter. Enter only sends a single Enter | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B09 | Deadline passes | The scheduler waits for the input gate and, when the working directory of the pane is missing, retries after workspace recovery. It does not check whether the agent is idle | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B10 | Restart | The deadline survives a restart. The pane closing discards the schedule | `src/docs/automation.md#scheduled-input` |
| scheduler-B11 | Queue entry | Menu entry "Queue prompt..."; dialog "Queue prompt after agent finishes". Enter inserts a new line; Ctrl+Enter enqueues | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B12 | Delivery modes | Once; Run X times (count field default 2, a positive whole number); Enqueue forever, marked DANGER | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B13 | Warning text of Enqueue forever | "DANGER: this will re-send forever whenever the agent finishes. Do not run it unmonitored." | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B14 | Empty prompt | Refused: "Write a prompt before enqueueing it" | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B15 | Clear | Menu entry "Clear prompt queue", shown only while the queue is not empty | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B16 | Delivery trigger | One prompt per finished turn (Working to Idle or Done), not a timer | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B17 | Order | First in, first out. A repeating entry goes back to the tail with its count decreased | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B18 | Capacity | At most 100 entries per pane | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B19 | Fenced delivery | Before writing, the server records that it is about to deliver the head and saves the session. A prompt that may have reached the PTY is not replayed after a crash | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B20 | Record | Each delivery is recorded in the agent debug log as a queued prompt | `src/docs/automation.md#prompt-queue` |
| scheduler-B21 | Storage | Snapshot section `ilium.core.scheduler`, holding `scheduled_input` and `prompt_queue` per pane (see [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)) | `ilium-core/src/lib.rs` |

### Samples

#### 1. Schedule input for a pane

Text is sent when a countdown ends, even after a restart. The client draws three `number` rows for hours, minutes and seconds, a `text-input` for the payload and a `toggle` for Send Enter, all from [input widgets](/pages/widgets-input/). The state is kept in the snapshot section `ilium.core.scheduler`. The server arms a durable timer with [durable timers](/pages/api-durable-timers/) and [clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/), and sends on `durable-timer-fired` with the `send-input` [intent](/pages/api-intent-send-input/). See [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, timers};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SendInputSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::Delivery;

// server manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write"] }
// The client view draws the dialog fields:
//   tree.number("Hours", 0.0).key("hours").minimum(0.0)
//   tree.number("Minutes", 0.0).key("minutes").minimum(0.0).maximum(59.0)
//   tree.number("Seconds", 30.0).key("seconds").minimum(0.0).maximum(59.0)
//   tree.text_input("Payload", String::new()).key("payload")
//   tree.toggle("Send Enter", true).key("send-enter")
impl Scheduler {
    /// One pending schedule per pane: the timer is named `send:{pane}`, and a
    /// durable timer with the same name replaces the earlier one.
    fn arm(&mut self, pane: NodeId, form: &ScheduleForm) -> Result<(), String> {
        let delay_seconds = (form.hours * 60 + form.minutes) * 60 + form.seconds;
        if delay_seconds == 0 {
            return Err("Choose a delay of at least one second".into());
        }
        if form.payload.is_empty() && !form.send_enter {
            return Err("Enter text, enable Send Enter, or use both".into());
        }
        let name = format!("send:{pane}");
        let due_epoch_ms = clock::now_unix_millis() + delay_seconds * 1000;
        timers::at(due_epoch_ms, &name).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        self.pending.insert(pane, (form.payload.clone(), form.send_enter)); // snapshot section
        Ok(())
    }

    fn on_event(&mut self, event: Event) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let Event::DurableTimerFired(fired) = event else { return Vec::new() };
        let Some(pane) = self.pane_of_timer(&fired.name) else { return Vec::new() };
        let Some((text, send_enter)) = self.pending.remove(&pane) else { return Vec::new() };
        // A timer that came due while Ilium was stopped fires once, late.
        vec![Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(plain_send(pane, text, send_enter)), fired.name)]
    }
}

fn plain_send(pane: NodeId, text: String, send_enter: bool) -> SendInputSpec {
    // Submitted types the text, then sends Enter as a separate stage.
    let delivery = if send_enter { Delivery::Submitted } else { Delivery::Typed };
    SendInputSpec {
        pane, text, delivery, prompt_epoch: None, stages: vec![],
        raw: None, mouse: None, if_current: None, lock_user_input: false, journal: true,
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';
import { number, textInput, toggle } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// server manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write"] }
// The client view draws the dialog fields:
const hours = number('Hours', 0, { key: 'hours', minimum: 0 });
const minutes = number('Minutes', 0, { key: 'minutes', minimum: 0, maximum: 59 });
const seconds = number('Seconds', 30, { key: 'seconds', minimum: 0, maximum: 59 });
const payload = textInput('Payload', '', { key: 'payload' });
const sendEnter = toggle('Send Enter', true, { key: 'send-enter' });

const pending = new Map<bigint, { text: string; sendEnter: boolean }>();

// One pending schedule per pane: the durable timer is named `send:{pane}`
// and a timer with the same name replaces the earlier one.
export function arm(pane: bigint, form: { hours: number; minutes: number; seconds: number;
  payload: string; sendEnter: boolean }): string | undefined {
  const delaySeconds = (form.hours * 60 + form.minutes) * 60 + form.seconds;
  if (delaySeconds === 0) return 'Choose a delay of at least one second';
  if (form.payload === '' && !form.sendEnter) return 'Enter text, enable Send Enter, or use both';
  timers.at(nowUnixMillis() + BigInt(delaySeconds) * 1000n, `send:${pane}`);
  pending.set(pane, { text: form.payload, sendEnter: form.sendEnter }); // snapshot section
  return undefined;
}

export function onEvent(event: Event): Submission[] {
  if (event.tag !== 'durable-timer-fired') return [];
  const pane = BigInt(event.val.name.slice('send:'.length));
  const job = pending.get(pane);
  if (job === undefined) return [];
  pending.delete(pane);
  // A timer that came due while Ilium was stopped fires once, late.
  return [{
    intent: {
      tag: 'send-input',
      val: {
        pane, text: job.text, delivery: job.sendEnter ? 'submitted' : 'typed', promptEpoch: undefined,
        stages: [], raw: undefined, mouse: undefined, ifCurrent: undefined,
        lockUserInput: false, journal: true,
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: event.val.name,
  }];
}
```

#### 2. Prompt queue

Prompts wait in a list and one goes out each time the agent finishes a turn. The dialog "Queue prompt after agent finishes" collects the text, the delivery mode (once, run X times, forever) and the count. The server watches `agent-activity-changed` (see [agent primitives](/pages/primitives-agent/) and [events](/pages/api-events/)) and, on a Working to Idle or Done transition, submits `send-input` with `delivery: submitted` for the head of the queue. A repeating entry goes to the tail with its count reduced. The queue holds at most 100 entries per pane.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SendInputSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::Delivery;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

// server manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write", "agent.read"] }
// client dialog: tree.text_area(..).key("prompt"), a delivery select
// (Once, Run X times, Enqueue forever) and tree.number("Times", 2.0).key("times")
const QUEUE_LIMIT: usize = 100;

impl Handler for Scheduler {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            let finished_turn = matches!(change.previous, AgentActivity::Working)
                && matches!(change.current, AgentActivity::Idle | AgentActivity::Done);
            let Some(queue) = self.queues.get_mut(&change.node) else { continue };
            if !finished_turn || queue.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            // Fenced delivery: record the head as "about to deliver" and save the
            // snapshot section before the send, so a crash never replays it.
            let mut entry = queue.remove(0);
            let text = entry.text.clone();
            if entry.repeats_again() && queue.len() < QUEUE_LIMIT {
                queue.push(entry); // goes to the tail with its count decreased
            }
            submissions.push(Submission::keyed(
                Intent::SendInput(SendInputSpec {
                    pane: change.node, text, delivery: Delivery::Submitted,
                    prompt_epoch: None, stages: vec![], raw: None, mouse: None,
                    if_current: None, lock_user_input: false, journal: true,
                }),
                format!("queue:{}:{}", change.node, change.revision),
            ));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// server manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write", "agent.read"] }
// client dialog: textArea for the prompt, a delivery select and a number row.
interface QueueEntry { text: string; mode: 'once' | 'times' | 'forever'; remaining: number }
const QUEUE_LIMIT = 100;
const queues = new Map<bigint, QueueEntry[]>();

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'agent-activity-changed') continue;
      const change = event.val;
      const finishedTurn = change.previous === 'working'
        && (change.current === 'idle' || change.current === 'done');
      const queue = queues.get(change.node);
      if (!finishedTurn || queue === undefined || queue.length === 0) continue;
      // Fenced delivery: save the snapshot section before the send.
      const entry = queue.shift()!;
      if (entry.mode === 'times') entry.remaining -= 1;
      if ((entry.mode === 'forever' || (entry.mode === 'times' && entry.remaining > 0))
          && queue.length < QUEUE_LIMIT) queue.push(entry);
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'send-input',
          val: {
            pane: change.node, text: entry.text, delivery: 'submitted',
            promptEpoch: undefined, stages: [], raw: undefined, mouse: undefined,
            ifCurrent: undefined, lockUserInput: false, journal: true,
          },
        },
        correlation: BigInt(submissions.length + 1),
        dedupKey: `queue:${change.node}:${change.revision}`,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

#### 3. Multi-stage input without interleaving

A slash command and its argument arrive together. The plugin submits `send-input` with `stages` and `lock-user-input`, so typed keys queue until the stages finish. See [send-input stages](/pages/api-intent-send-input/), [terminal.input-lock](/pages/capability-terminal-input-lock/) and [terminal.raw-input](/pages/capability-terminal-raw-input/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{InputStage, SendInputSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::Delivery;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write",
//   "terminal.raw-input", "terminal.input-lock"] }
/// A slash command and its argument arrive together. Keys the user types
/// meanwhile are queued, not lost (the lock lasts at most 2 s).
fn slash_command(pane: NodeId, command: &str, argument: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let stages = SendInputSpec {
        pane,
        text: String::new(),
        delivery: Delivery::Typed,
        prompt_epoch: None,
        stages: vec![
            InputStage { text: command.into(), delay_ms: 0, delivery: Delivery::Typed },
            InputStage { text: argument.into(), delay_ms: 150, delivery: Delivery::Typed },
            InputStage { text: String::new(), delay_ms: 120, delivery: Delivery::Submitted },
        ],
        raw: None,
        mouse: None,
        if_current: None,
        lock_user_input: true,
        journal: true,
    };
    // A raw Escape (0x1b) clears a half-typed line first. It is its own
    // submission because raw bytes replace the other fields.
    let clear = SendInputSpec { raw: Some(vec![0x1b]), stages: vec![], ..stages.clone() };
    vec![
        Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(clear), format!("clear-{pane}")),
        Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(stages), format!("slash-{pane}-{command}")),
    ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write",
//   "terminal.raw-input", "terminal.input-lock"] }
// A slash command and its argument arrive together. Keys the user types
// meanwhile are queued, not lost (the lock lasts at most 2 s).
export function slashCommand(pane: bigint, command: string, argument: string): Submission[] {
  const base = {
    pane, text: '', delivery: 'typed' as const, promptEpoch: undefined,
    mouse: undefined, ifCurrent: undefined, journal: true,
  };
  return [
    {
      // A raw Escape (0x1b) clears a half-typed line first.
      intent: { tag: 'send-input', val: {
        ...base, stages: [], raw: new Uint8Array([0x1b]), lockUserInput: false } },
      correlation: 1n,
      dedupKey: `clear-${pane}`,
    },
    {
      intent: { tag: 'send-input', val: {
        ...base, raw: undefined, lockUserInput: true,
        stages: [
          { text: command, delayMs: 0, delivery: 'typed' },
          { text: argument, delayMs: 150, delivery: 'typed' },
          { text: '', delayMs: 120, delivery: 'submitted' },
        ] } },
      correlation: 2n,
      dedupKey: `slash-${pane}-${command}`,
    },
  ];
}
```

#### 4. Retry after uncertain delivery

A prompt is never sent twice. Each send has a dedup key. On `input-uncertain` the plugin checks the input journal, which needs [journal.read](/pages/capability-journal-read/), and retries once after a back-off, using [durable timers](/pages/api-durable-timers/), only if the entry is missing. The outcome model is in [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/); the events are in [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, journal, timers};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write", "journal.read"] }
// Every send carries a dedup key and journal: true. The host writes the
// journal entry before the PTY write.
impl Handler for Scheduler {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::InputUncertain(uncertain) => {
                    let since = clock::now_unix_millis().saturating_sub(60_000);
                    let seen = journal::read(Some(uncertain.pane), since, 50)
                        .iter()
                        .any(|entry| entry.payload_json.contains(&uncertain.dedup_key));
                    if !seen {
                        // Not delivered: retry once after a short back-off.
                        if let Ok(timer) = timers::set(2_000, None) {
                            self.retries.push((timer, uncertain.pane, uncertain.dedup_key));
                        }
                    }
                }
                Event::TimerFired(timer) => {
                    if let Some(at) = self.retries.iter().position(|(t, _, _)| *t == timer) {
                        let (_, pane, key) = self.retries.remove(at);
                        // Same key: if the first send did arrive, this is a duplicate.
                        submissions.push(self.resend(pane, key));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import * as journal from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/journal';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';

// manifest: "capabilities": { "server": ["terminal.write", "journal.read"] }
// Every send carries a dedup key and journal: true. The host writes the
// journal entry before the PTY write.
const retries = new Map<bigint, { pane: bigint; key: string }>();

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'input-uncertain') {
        const { pane, dedupKey } = event.val;
        const since = nowUnixMillis() - 60_000n;
        const seen = journal.read(pane, since, 50).some((e) => e.payloadJson.includes(dedupKey));
        if (!seen) {
          // Not delivered: retry once after a short back-off.
          retries.set(timers.set(2_000, undefined), { pane, key: dedupKey });
        }
      } else if (event.tag === 'timer-fired' && retries.has(event.timerId)) {
        const { pane, key } = retries.get(event.timerId)!;
        retries.delete(event.timerId);
        // Same key: if the first send did arrive, this is a duplicate.
        submissions.push(resend(pane, key));
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.scheduler` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.scheduler/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.scheduler/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule-sources` | collect | Add a trigger source such as a calendar or a reset forecast. | entry: id, title, service (returns the next fire times) | standard |
| `before-send-scheduled` | hook (veto) | Refuse a scheduled or queued input at the moment it would be sent. | pane, text_length, schedule, source | high |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.scheduler/queue`: enqueue, list, cancel: manage the prompt queue

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.scheduler/fired`: { schedule, pane }

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.scheduler"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Refuses scheduled prompts on days the plugin marks as holidays

A package adds a `veto` handler. Handlers run until one refuses.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.scheduler/before-send-scheduled"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.scheduler/before-send-scheduled",
        "id": "skip-on-holiday",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "skip_on_holiday"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "skip_on_holiday" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: pane, text_length, schedule, source
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Refuse("reason".into())
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'skip_on_holiday') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: pane, text_length, schedule, source
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'refuse', val: 'reason' };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Text triggers

## Text triggers

Text triggers are regular-expression rules that watch terminal output and send text to the pane that printed it. A typical rule answers a confirmation prompt such as `Continue? (y/n)` with `y`. The plugin id is `ilium.core.text-triggers` and it runs on both sides: the server side matches output and sends input, the client side draws the Text Triggers settings tab.

The pattern matching itself is done by the host filter, so the plugin never reads the full output stream. The plugin turns each rule into one output filter and answers each `output-matched` event with a `send-input` intent.

### What it covers

- Text triggers: rules with a pattern, a reply and an enabled switch, described in the Text triggers section of the automation guide.
- The Text Triggers settings tab, with one row group per rule.
- A notice for a pattern that does not compile, and a count of dropped matches when a pane floods the filter.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/16-text-triggers.gif" alt="A terminal asks for confirmation and a text trigger types the answer" loading="lazy"><figcaption>A rule matches a confirmation prompt and the reply is typed into the same pane.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Text Triggers ────────────────────────────────╮
│ Confirm prompts …………………………………… <span class="t-ok">on</span>              │
│   Pattern ……………………………… <span class="t-hi">\(y/n\)\s*$</span>             │
│   Reply ………………………………………………………… y               │
│ Accept edits ………………………………………… <span class="t-dim">off</span>              │
│   Pattern ……………………………… <span class="t-hi">Apply changes\?</span>         │

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text-triggers` | Text Triggers | `[text_triggers]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Text triggers is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### Declare the rule list

The rules live in a `group` row. Inside it, a `list` of strings with `item_format: "regex"` holds the patterns, which the host checks before writing, and a second `list` holds the replies in the same order. The panel draws each pattern and reply pair with an enabled `toggle`. See [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) and [settings row types](/pages/reference-settings-rows/).

**Rust**

```rust
// Manifest fragment: contributes.settings (a plain JSON string in the SDK).
const RULES_ROW: &str = r#"
{ "type": "group", "title": "Rules", "collapsed": false, "rows": [
  { "type": "list", "key": "patterns", "title": "Patterns",
    "item": { "type": "string" }, "item_format": "regex",
    "max_items": 32, "reorderable": true, "default": [] },
  { "type": "list", "key": "replies", "title": "Replies",
    "item": { "type": "string" }, "max_items": 32, "reorderable": true, "default": [] }
] }
"#;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// Manifest fragment: contributes.settings.
export const rulesRow = {
  type: 'group', title: 'Rules', collapsed: false, rows: [
    { type: 'list', key: 'patterns', title: 'Patterns',
      item: { type: 'string' }, item_format: 'regex',
      max_items: 32, reorderable: true, default: [] },
    { type: 'list', key: 'replies', title: 'Replies',
      item: { type: 'string' }, max_items: 32, reorderable: true, default: [] },
  ],
};
```

#### Match output and answer

Each rule becomes one output filter on every agent pane. A match raises `output-matched`, and the plugin answers with `send-input`. See [terminal.output-filter](/pages/capability-terminal-output-filter/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [send-input](/pages/api-intent-send-input/). The dedup key stops a repeated line from answering twice.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{add_output_filter, OutputFilter};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::OutputMatchedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Delivery, SendInputSpec};

fn watch_pane(pane: NodeId, rule_id: &str, regex: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    add_output_filter(pane, OutputFilter {
        id: rule_id.to_string(),
        regex: regex.to_string(),
        rate_per_second: 2,
    })
}

fn answer(matched: &OutputMatchedEvent, reply: &str) -> Submission {
    let spec = SendInputSpec {
        pane: matched.node,
        text: reply.to_string(),
        delivery: Delivery::Submitted,
        prompt_epoch: None,
        stages: Vec::new(),
        raw: None,
        mouse: None,
        if_current: None,
        lock_user_input: false,
        journal: false,
    };
    let key = format!("trigger-{}-{}-{}", matched.filter_id, matched.node, matched.row);
    Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(spec), key)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { addOutputFilter } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function watchPane(pane: bigint, ruleId: string, regex: string): void {
  addOutputFilter(pane, { id: ruleId, regex, ratePerSecond: 2 });
}

export function answer(
  m: { node: bigint; filterId: string; row: number },
  reply: string,
): Submission {
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'send-input', val: {
      pane: m.node, text: reply, delivery: 'submitted', promptEpoch: undefined,
      stages: [], raw: undefined, mouse: undefined, ifCurrent: undefined,
      lockUserInput: false, journal: false,
    } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `trigger-${m.filterId}-${m.node}-${m.row}`,
  };
}
```

#### Count matches

Each rule keeps a match count in session storage and writes one `info` log line per match. See [storage](/pages/api-storage/) and [log](/pages/api-log/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::{self, Bucket};

fn count_match(rule_id: &str, line: &str) {
    let key = format!("count/{rule_id}");
    let current = storage::get(Bucket::Session, &key)
        .and_then(|b| b.try_into().ok())
        .map(u64::from_le_bytes)
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let _ = storage::put(Bucket::Session, &key, &(current + 1).to_le_bytes());
    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("rule {rule_id} matched: {line}"));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';

export function countMatch(ruleId: string, line: string): void {
  const key = `count/${ruleId}`;
  const bytes = storage.get('session', key);
  const current = bytes && bytes.length === 8
    ? new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, 8).getBigUint64(0, true)
    : 0n;
  const next = new Uint8Array(8);
  new DataView(next.buffer).setBigUint64(0, current + 1n, true);
  storage.put('session', key, next);
  log('info', `rule ${ruleId} matched: ${line}`);
}
```

#### Floods and invalid patterns

When a pane prints the same prompt faster than the rate limit, the host drops matches and the next batch starts with `events-dropped`. The server logs the count. The client panel shows a `notice` for a pattern that does not compile and a `toggle` per rule. See [events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/), [status and feedback widgets](/pages/widgets-status-and-feedback/), [events](/pages/api-events/) and [input widgets](/pages/widgets-input/).

**Rust**

```rust
// Server side, inside on_events:
if let Event::EventsDropped(counts) = event {
    for dropped in counts.iter().filter(|d| d.event == "output-matched") {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!(
            "{} matches dropped for rule {:?}", dropped.count, dropped.source));
    }
}

// Client side, inside Views::render:
fn rule_row(tree: &mut Tree, index: usize, enabled: bool, error: Option<&str>) -> NodeHandle {
    let toggle = tree.toggle("Enabled", enabled).key(&format!("rule-{index}"));
    match error {
        Some(text) => {
            let warn = tree.notice(vec![text.to_string()]).tone(Tone::Warning);
            tree.layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(2), Constraint::Length(1)])
                .child(warn)
                .child(toggle)
        }
        None => toggle,
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { layout, length, notice, toggle } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// Server side, inside onEvents:
//   case 'events-dropped':
//     for (const d of event.val.filter((x) => x.event === 'output-matched'))
//       log('warn', `${d.count} matches dropped for rule ${d.source}`);

// Client side, inside views.render:
export function ruleRow(index: number, enabled: boolean, error?: string) {
  const switchRow = toggle('Enabled', enabled, { key: `rule-${index}` });
  if (error === undefined) return switchRow;
  const warn = notice([error], { tone: 'warning' });
  return layout({ direction: 'vertical', constraints: [length(2), length(1)] },
    [warn, switchRow]);
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.text-triggers` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.text-triggers/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rule-packs` | collect | Ship a group of rules the user can enable as a set. | entry: id, title, rules (list of pattern, reply, enabled) | standard |
| `before-fire` | hook (veto) | Refuse or end a rule that is about to send text. | rule, pane, match, reply_length | high |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.text-triggers/test-rule`: test: run a pattern against sample text

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.text-triggers/fired`: { rule, pane }

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.text-triggers"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Refuses rules marked `office` outside 09:00 to 18:00

A package adds a `veto` handler. Handlers run until one refuses.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "exports": [
    "hook-handler"
  ],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire",
        "id": "working-hours",
        "priority": 50,
        "handler": "working_hours"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl HookHandler for Plugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "working_hours" => {
                // call.payload_json holds: rule, pane, match, reply_length
                let _payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
                    Ok(value) => value,
                    Err(_) => return HookReply::Pass,
                };
                HookReply::Refuse("reason".into())
            }
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
definePlugin({
  handleHook(call) {
    if (call.extension !== 'working_hours') return { tag: 'pass' };
    // call.payloadJson holds: rule, pane, match, reply_length
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson);
    void payload;
    return { tag: 'refuse', val: 'reason' };
  },
});
```

A handler that is late, traps or returns a reply the mode does not allow counts as `pass`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#hooks).

# Progress

## Progress

Progress monitors let a long task show how far it is. An agent or a script registers a probe command with `ilium progress set`, the server runs the probe on an interval, and the tree and status bar show the result. `ilium progress set --wait` and `ilium wait` block until the task ends. The plugin id is `ilium.core.progress` and it runs on both sides: the server side owns the CLI, the probes and the watchers, and the client side draws the footer and the status bar segment.

### What it covers

- Progress monitor: a probe that prints one JSON object with a status, a percent and a message, described in the Progress monitor section of the automation guide.
- The `ilium progress` command and `ilium wait`, described in the CLI reference.
- Long-lived watchers that stream progress lines instead of being polled (new in the plugin build, not parity).
- The progress footer in the tree and the count in the status bar, described in the agent monitoring guide.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/07-progress-monitor.gif" alt="A progress monitor row fills while a long task runs and ends as done" loading="lazy"><figcaption>A registered monitor appears in the tree footer, updates on each probe run and settles when the task ends.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Progress ─────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">▶ RUNNING  42%</span> <span class="t-hi">████████</span><span class="t-dim">░░░░░░░░░░░░</span>            │
│ <span class="t-dim">  Running the unit tests, crate 9 of 22</span>        │
│ <span class="t-ok">✓ DONE  100%</span> <span class="t-ok">████████████████████</span>              │
│ <span class="t-dim">  Export of 412 sessions finished</span>              │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Two <code>progress-row</code> widgets with percent and message. Illustrative: the bar glyphs depend on the icon set.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium progress set --command '/opt/probe.sh' --wait
{"type":"progress_set","request_id":31,"pane_id":12,"monitor_id":4,
 "progress":{"monitor_id":4,"report":{"job_id":"export-412",
 "status":"running","percent":0,"message":"Exporting 412 sessions",
 "details":"","error":null},"monitor_health":{"state":"healthy"},
 "last_observed_unix_millis":1791800000000}}
{"type":"progress_wait","pane_id":12,"monitor_id":4,"outcome":"done",
 "exit_code":0,"waited_seconds":412,"composer_notice":"suppressed",

<span class="t-ok">0</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 80 columns or fewer. Illustrative. Each record is one line on a real terminal; it is wrapped here, and the text of <code>next</code> and the nested <code>progress</code> object are cut. The registration record comes first. The final <code>progress_wait</code> record ends the wait and the exit status is 0 for done.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Behaviour contract

Field order and names equal the baseline; extra fields are not allowed. The records are:

- `progress_set`: `{"type":"progress_set","request_id":<n>,"pane_id":<n>,"monitor_id":<n>,"progress":{"monitor_id":<n>,"report":{...},"monitor_health":{"state":"..."},"last_observed_unix_millis":<n>}}`
- `progress_wait`: `{"type":"progress_wait","pane_id":<n>,"monitor_id":<n>,"outcome":"done|error|monitor-failed|cleared|no-monitor|still-running","exit_code":<n>,"waited_seconds":<n>,"composer_notice":"suppressed|may-also-arrive|none","next":"...","progress":{...}}`

| Id | Rule | Exact value or text | Baseline source |
|---|---|---|---|
| progress-B01 | Exit status of `progress set --wait` and `progress wait` | 0 done, 2 usage or rejected (for example `monitor-ambiguous`), 3 task error, 4 monitor failed (outcome unknown), 5 monitor replaced or cleared, 6 `--timeout-seconds` elapsed | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-wait` |
| progress-B02 | `outcome` for each exit | 0 `done`, 3 `error`, 4 `monitor-failed`, 5 `cleared` or `no-monitor`, 6 `still-running` | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-wait` |
| progress-B03 | Text of `next` | `done`: "The task finished. Verify its output, then continue." `error`: "The task reported failure. Inspect its log or error, fix, and retry." `monitor-failed`: "The probe stopped working, so the task outcome is unknown. Check the task directly; do not assume success." `cleared`: "The monitor was cleared, or is not registered on this pane. Check `ilium progress status`." `no-monitor`: "This pane has no progress monitor. Register one with `ilium progress set`." `still-running`: "The task is still running. Run the same wait command again to keep waiting." A settled outcome adds " When you have handled it, remove this monitor with `ilium progress clear --monitor-id <id>`." | `ilium/src/progress_wait.rs` |
| progress-B04 | `composer_notice` | `suppressed` while a wait takes the outcome, `may-also-arrive` for a settled outcome without a wait, `none` otherwise | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-wait` |
| progress-B05 | Monitors per pane | At most 8. The 9th live monitor is rejected with code `too-many-monitors`. A settled monitor whose outcome was delivered makes room | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-set` |
| progress-B06 | `--interval-seconds` | Default 1, range 1 to 86400 | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-set` |
| progress-B07 | Probe size limits | Command line 16 KiB, stdout 64 KiB, stderr 16 KiB, `job_id` 256 bytes, `message` 2048 bytes, `details` 8192 bytes, `error` 4096 bytes | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#the-probe-contract` |
| progress-B08 | Probe run | One shell command line, run by the server with the session project root as working directory, at most 30 s (`timeout_millis: 30_000`) | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#the-probe-contract` |
| progress-B09 | Probe failure counting | After 3 consecutive probe failures the monitor becomes `failed` (monitor health), not the task | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#the-probe-contract` |
| progress-B10 | CLI reply wait | The CLI waits up to 45 s for the server reply | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-status` |
| progress-B11 | Same probe twice | Registering the same probe command again in the same pane while its monitor runs returns the existing monitor id | `src/docs/automation.md#progress-monitor` |
| progress-B12 | Restore after restart | A monitor is re-established only after one preflight probe returns the same `job_id`, and it gets a fresh monitor id | `ilium-server/src/persistence.rs` |
| progress-B13 | Delivery states | `not-queued`, `queued`, `attempted`, `delivered-to-pty`, `uncertain`, `not-deliverable`, `collected-by-waiter`. Only `queued` is retried after a restart. Undelivered outcomes are re-sent every 20 s | `ilium-server/src/agent_delivery.rs` |
| progress-B14 | Terminal result | Typed into the agent composer once (`composer_notice`); not typed when a running wait collected it | `src/docs/automation.md#progress-monitor` |
| progress-B15 | Rejection codes | `disabled`, `invalid-request`, `invalid-probe-report`, `probe-spawn-failed`, `probe-timed-out`, `probe-exited-non-zero`, `probe-output-too-large`, `probe-io-failed`, `pane-not-found`, `stale-monitor`, `too-many-monitors`, `monitor-ambiguous` | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#progress-status` |

### Settings it reads

The plugin owns no tab. It reads four keys of the User Interface table that the Agent Monitoring tab writes, through `settings.read-kernel:agent-monitoring`. Values and defaults are those of the baseline.

| Key | Default | Range or values | Baseline source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[ui] progress_monitor_enabled` | true | true or false. Off stops observation and rejects new registrations with `disabled` | `src/docs/automation.md#progress-monitor` |
| `[ui] progress_max_lines` | 4 | Footer lines, 1 to 20 | `src/docs/automation.md#progress-monitor` |
| `[ui] completed_progress_hide_after_seconds` | 60 | Steps of 30; 0 means never hide | `src/docs/automation.md#progress-monitor` |
| `[ui] task_progress_frames` | a preset | 2 to 13 printable frames, all one cell wide or all two cells wide | `src/docs/automation.md#progress-monitor` |

All four are written by the Agent Monitoring tab ([config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)); this plugin never writes them.

### Samples

#### ilium progress set and wait

`ilium progress set --wait` keeps its invocation open. The plugin writes the registration line, remembers the open invocation and finishes it when the monitor settles. When the user presses Ctrl+C the host sends `cli-cancelled`, and the plugin stops the probe. See [the CLI API](/pages/api-cli/), [cli.contribute](/pages/capability-cli-contribute/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::cli;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CliInvokedEvent;

impl Handler for Progress {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CliInvoked(CliInvokedEvent { invocation, name, argv, .. })
                    if name == "progress" =>
                {
                    let (monitor, progress) = self.register(&argv);
                    // Field order and names equal the baseline record.
                    let line = format!(
                        r#"{{"type":"progress_set","request_id":{},"pane_id":{},"monitor_id":{monitor},"progress":{progress}}}"#,
                        self.request_id, self.pane_id,
                    );
                    let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
                    if argv.iter().any(|a| a == "--wait") {
                        self.waiting.insert(monitor, invocation);
                    } else {
                        cli::finish(invocation, 0);
                    }
                }
                Event::CliCancelled(invocation) => self.stop_waiting(invocation),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as cli from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/cli';

export const { handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'cli-invoked' && event.val.name === 'progress') {
        const { monitor, progress } = register(event.val.argv);
        // Field order and names equal the baseline record.
        cli.writeLine(event.val.invocation, JSON.stringify({
          type: 'progress_set', request_id: requestId, pane_id: paneId,
          monitor_id: monitor, progress,
        }));
        if (event.val.argv.includes('--wait')) waiting.set(monitor, event.val.invocation);
        else cli.finish(event.val.invocation, 0);
      } else if (event.tag === 'cli-cancelled') {
        stopWaiting(event.val);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

#### Run the probe

A repeating timer fires on the probe interval. The plugin runs the probe command, parses the JSON object it prints and stores the status and percent. A non-zero exit is not a plugin error, it is a probe result. See [process control](/pages/api-process-control/), [process.run](/pages/capability-process-run/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::process::{self, ProcessSpec};

async fn run_probe(command: String, project_root: FsPath) -> Result<ProbeReport, PluginError> {
    let spec = ProcessSpec {
        // The probe is one shell command line, at most 16 KiB.
        program: "sh".to_string(),
        arguments: vec!["-c".to_string(), command],
        cwd: Some(project_root), // the session project root, as in the baseline
        stdin: None,
        environment: Vec::new(),
        timeout_millis: 30_000,
    };
    let exit = process::run(spec).await?;
    let report: ProbeReport = serde_json::from_slice(&exit.stdout)
        .map_err(|_| PluginError::invalid_argument("probe printed no JSON object"))?;
    Ok(report)
}

// In on_events: Event::TimerFired(timer) => spawn run_probe for the monitor of that timer.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { run } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export async function runProbe(command: string, projectRoot: string): Promise<ProbeReport> {
  // One shell command line, run in the session project root, at most 30 s.
  const exit = await run({
    program: 'sh', arguments: ['-c', command], cwd: projectRoot,
    stdin: undefined, environment: [], timeoutMillis: 30_000,
  });
  try {
    return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(exit.stdout)) as ProbeReport;
  } catch {
    throw new PluginError('invalid-argument', 'probe printed no JSON object');
  }
}

// In onEvents: case 'timer-fired': run the probe of the monitor that owns event.val.
```

#### Long-lived watcher

New in the plugin build, not covered by COR-041. A watcher is a child process that stays alive and prints one JSON line per progress step. Each line is a probe-format JSON object (`job_id`, `status`, `percent`, `message`, `details`, `error`), at most 64 KiB long, and at most 10 lines per second are applied; extra lines are coalesced to the latest. An invalid line counts as one probe failure. The plugin parses each `child-output` line and settles the monitor on `child-exited`. See [process.long-lived](/pages/capability-process-long-lived/), [process control](/pages/api-process-control/) and [events](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::process::{self, ProcessSpec, SpawnSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::OutputStream;

fn start_watcher(&mut self, monitor: u64, program: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let child = process::spawn(&SpawnSpec {
        process: ProcessSpec {
            program: program.to_string(), arguments: Vec::new(), cwd: None,
            stdin: None, environment: Vec::new(), timeout_millis: 0,
        },
        stdin_open: false,
        line_mode: true,
    })?;
    self.children.insert(monitor, child);
    Ok(())
}

// In on_events:
//   Event::ChildOutput(out) if out.stream == OutputStream::Stdout => self.apply_line(&out.bytes),
//   Event::ChildExited(exit) => self.settle(exit.child, exit.status),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as process from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';
import type { Child } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';

const children = new Map<bigint, Child>();

export function startWatcher(monitor: bigint, program: string): void {
  children.set(monitor, process.spawn({
    process: { program, arguments: [], cwd: undefined, stdin: undefined,
      environment: [], timeoutMillis: 0 },
    stdinOpen: false,
    lineMode: true,
  }));
}

// In onEvents:
//   case 'child-output': if (event.val.stream === 'stdout') applyLine(event.val.bytes); break;
//   case 'child-exited': settle(event.val.child, event.val.status); break;
```

#### Progress footer and status bar

The client side renders one `progress-row` per monitor and sets a status segment with the number of running monitors. When none remain it clears the segment. See [chrome intents](/pages/api-intent-chrome/), [status and feedback widgets](/pages/widgets-status-and-feedback/), [ui.chrome](/pages/capability-ui-chrome/) and [data display widgets](/pages/widgets-data-display/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetStatusSegmentSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::ProgressState;

fn footer_row(tree: &mut Tree, m: &Monitor) -> NodeHandle {
    tree.progress_row(&m.title)
        .state(ProgressState::Running)
        .percent(m.percent)
        .message(&m.message)
        .key(&format!("monitor-{}", m.id))
}

fn status_segment(running: usize) -> Submission {
    if running == 0 {
        return Submission::new(Intent::ClearStatusSegment("progress".into()));
    }
    Submission::new(Intent::SetStatusSegment(SetStatusSegmentSpec {
        segment: "progress".into(),
        content: RichText::plain(format!("{running} running")),
        tooltip: None,
        tone: None,
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { progressRow } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export const footerRow = (m: Monitor) =>
  progressRow(m.title, { key: `monitor-${m.id}`, state: 'running', percent: m.percent, message: m.message });

export function statusSegment(running: number): Submission {
  const intent = running === 0
    ? ({ tag: 'clear-status-segment', val: 'progress' } as const)
    : ({ tag: 'set-status-segment', val: {
        segment: 'progress', content: richText(`${running} running`),
        tooltip: undefined, tone: undefined } } as const);
  return { intent, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: undefined };
}
```

#### Status route on the loopback listener

New in the plugin build, not covered by COR-041. The plugin answers `GET /progress.json` on the loopback HTTP listener. Each `http-called` event is one request, and `respond` answers exactly that request, so a script can read progress without the terminal. The body is `{"monitors":[<progress object>]}`, where each element has the same shape as the `progress` field of a `progress status` record.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http_api;

impl Handler for StatusRoute {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::HttpCalled(call) = event else { continue };
            if call.method != "GET" || call.path != "/progress.json" { continue; }
            let body = serde_json::to_vec(&self.snapshot()).unwrap_or_default();
            let _ = http_api::respond(call.call, 200, &[("content-type".into(), "application/json".into())], &body);
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { respond } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http-api';

export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'http-called') continue;
    const { call, method, path } = event.val;
    if (method !== 'GET' || path !== '/progress.json') continue;
    respond(call, 200, [['content-type', 'application/json']], encode(snapshot()));
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.progress` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.progress/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.progress/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `footer-segments` | collect | Add a segment to the progress footer. | entry: id, priority, max_width | standard |
| `probe-kinds` | collect | Add a ready-made probe, such as a CI run or a build. | entry: id, title, command_template, interval_seconds | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.progress/report`: start, update, finish: report progress of a task the plugin runs

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.progress/changed`: { monitor, status, percent }

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.progress"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds a probe template for a CI run

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.progress/probe-kinds"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.progress/probe-kinds",
        "id": "ci-run",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "CI run",
          "command_template": "/usr/local/bin/ci-probe {run}",
          "interval_seconds": 30
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Chatroom

## Chatroom

The Chatroom is a shared message board for the agents of one project and for the user. Its messages live in a plain `CHATROOM.md` file at the project root, so every agent can read and append to it. The plugin id is `ilium.core.chatroom` and it runs on both sides: the server side owns the file and the tree row, and the client side draws the message view and the composer.

### What it covers

- The Chatroom row in the tree, with an unread count, and the shared `CHATROOM.md` file, described in the Chatroom section of the automation guide.
- `ilium chat`, described in the CLI reference. The command reads and appends to the same file the plugin tails.
- The message view and the composer.
- The context-injection output of `ilium chat context`, which the hooks that [Agent setup](/pages/core-plugin-agent-setup/) installs print into an agent prompt.

Agent setup owns the Setup tab, both instruction blocks and the hook entries. Chatroom asks Agent setup through the service `ilium.core.agent-setup/install` to install the chatroom block and hooks. At start, Agent setup repairs a missing or outdated chatroom hook when `CHATROOM.md` exists.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/14-chatroom.gif" alt="Two agents and the user exchange messages in the Chatroom view" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Agents append messages to the shared file and the Chatroom view shows them as timestamped rows.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

</pre>

### Behaviour contract

| Id | Rule | Exact value or text | Baseline source |
|---|---|---|---|
| chatroom-B01 | Record line | `- YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss +HH:MM \| <author> \| <content>`, local time with its offset | `src/docs/automation.md#file-format-and-limits` |
| chatroom-B02 | Escaping | Newline and tab in content are escaped as `\n` and `\t`, backslash as `\\`; other control characters are removed | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B03 | Message limit | At most 4000 characters; author and message must not be empty | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#ilium-chat` |
| chatroom-B04 | Default author | `$ILIUM_CHATROOM_AUTHOR`, then `$AGENT_NAME`, then `agent` | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#ilium-chat` |
| chatroom-B05 | Initial file | The title `# ILIUM CHATROOM`, the marker `<!-- ilium-chatroom: v1 -->`, the guidance paragraph of the prompt template `agent/coordination-guidance` byte for byte, and the heading `## Messages`. An existing file is never overwritten; a symlinked or non-regular file is refused | `src/docs/automation.md#set-it-up` |
| chatroom-B06 | Ignore lines | `.gitignore` gets the lines `/CHATROOM.md` and `/CHATROOM.archive.md`, created if needed. The baseline writes both (`CHATROOM_ARCHIVE_IGNORE`); the user guide names only the first and is corrected | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B07 | View limits | The view reads at most the last 8 MiB and shows the newest 200 messages; retention while reading is 4 MiB; the unread scan covers at most 2000 records | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B08 | Composer | Placeholder "Write message - Enter sends"; Enter sends; the author is `user`. Empty view: "No messages yet. Type below to post as user." | `src/docs/automation.md#use-it-in-the-tui` |
| chatroom-B09 | View rows | `<YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss> <author> <content>`, newest at the bottom, under the list "Agents in this project" | `src/docs/automation.md#use-it-in-the-tui` |
| chatroom-B10 | Command output | `init` prints `chatroom ready at <path>`; `send` prints `chatroom message sent`; `tail` prints `timestamp \| author \| content`, default 100 records | `src/docs/cli-reference.md#ilium-chat` |
| chatroom-B11 | Send errors | Printed as `ilium: <text>` on stderr with exit 1: `this project does not have a chatroom`; `chatroom author and message must not be empty`; `chatroom messages are limited to 4000 characters` | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B12 | Hook command | `ilium chat context --limit 40 --since-last-read --max-bytes 2048`, timeout 10 s, status message "Checking ilium chatroom" (installed by Agent setup) | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B13 | Context text | Rendered from the prompt templates `agent/chatroom-context`, `agent/chatroom-empty-context`, `agent/chatroom-omitted` and `agent/chatroom-context-row`, byte-identical to the baseline. A first read starts with "Ilium chatroom is enabled"; a since-last-read output starts with "New ilium chatroom messages" | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B14 | Output cap | When the output exceeds `--max-bytes`, 160 bytes are reserved for the omitted note and a cut row ends with the marker `…` followed by a newline. A session-start hook gets 4 times the budget | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B15 | Reader cursor | The file `.ilium/chat-readers/<first 32 hex chars of sha256(reader key)>` holds the 64-hex sha256 of `timestamp\0author\0content\0` of the last message read. The reader key is `--reader`, else `ILIUM_PANE_ID` | `ilium-client/src/chatroom.rs` |
| chatroom-B16 | Unread count | The tree row shows "(N new)", computed for the reader key `user`. New in the plugin build, not parity | none |
| chatroom-B17 | Locked append | Every append, from the CLI and from the composer, takes the exclusive advisory lock of the baseline (`ilium-platform` file lock on `CHATROOM.md`) and appends one line. A whole-file rewrite is allowed only for archive rotation, under the same lock | `src/docs/automation.md#file-format-and-limits` |

The test for chatroom-B17: 50 concurrent `ilium chat send` calls and 50 composer sends produce 100 records, none lost and none interleaved.
