```json
    ]
  },
  "limits_tier": "first-party"
}
```

### Action names, command ids and presets

The kernel owns the keymap table. The plugin owns the Keyboard tab and the key reference screen, so it shows exactly these 35 actions. Each action has a stable name (the key in `[keybindings]`), a global command id `kernel.<name>` that a plugin can read from `keymap.bindings`, and a default key after the prefix. [COR-011]

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">╭──────────────────────────────────────────────╮</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> Keyboard                                     <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> Preset………………… tmux      Prefix…… Ctrl+B      <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> Navigation prefix………………………… Ctrl+B           <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>                                              <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>  new_terminal ………………………………………… c             <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>  close_pane ……………………………………………… x             <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>  rename ………………………………………………… ,                <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>  focus_pane_left ……………………………… Left           <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>  quit ……………………………………………… &                   <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span></pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The Keyboard tab: the preset, the two prefixes and the first rows of the action list. The plugin draws the rows from the 35 action names; the kernel stores the choice.</figcaption>
</figure>

| Action name | Command id | Default | GNU Screen preset | tmux preset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `new_terminal` | `kernel.new_terminal` | `c` | `c` | `c` |
| `new_agent_worktree` | `kernel.new_agent_worktree` | `W` | `W` | `W` |
| `new_editor` | `kernel.new_editor` | `e` | `e` | `e` |
| `new_board` | `kernel.new_board` | `B` | `B` | `B` |
| `close_pane` | `kernel.close_pane` | `x` | `k` | `x` |
| `new_group` | `kernel.new_group` | `g` | `g` | `g` |
| `new_split_view` | `kernel.new_split_view` | `"` | `S` | `"` |
| `new_folder` | `kernel.new_folder` | `F` | `F` | `F` |
| `rename` | `kernel.rename` | unbound | `A` | `,` |
| `toggle_move` | `kernel.toggle_move` | `m` | `m` | `m` |
| `focus_tree` | `kernel.focus_tree` | `w` | `t` | `w` |
| `focus_pane` | `kernel.focus_pane` | `P` | `P` | `P` |
| `focus_next_pane` | `kernel.focus_next_pane` | `o` | `n` | `o` |
| `focus_previous_pane` | `kernel.focus_previous_pane` | `;` | `p` | `;` |
| `focus_pane_left` | `kernel.focus_pane_left` | `Left` | `H` | `Left` |
| `focus_pane_right` | `kernel.focus_pane_right` | `Right` | `L` | `Right` |
| `focus_pane_up` | `kernel.focus_pane_up` | `Up` | `K` | `Up` |
| `focus_pane_down` | `kernel.focus_pane_down` | `Down` | `J` | `Down` |
| `cycle_next_in_group` | `kernel.cycle_next_in_group` | `n` | `Down` | `n` |
| `cycle_previous_in_group` | `kernel.cycle_previous_in_group` | `p` | `Up` | `p` |
| `jump_next_group` | `kernel.jump_next_group` | `)` | `PgDn` | `)` |
| `jump_previous_group` | `kernel.jump_previous_group` | `(` | `PgUp` | `(` |
| `scrollback_up` | `kernel.scrollback_up` | `[` | `[` | `[` |
| `scrollback_down` | `kernel.scrollback_down` | `]` | `]` | `]` |
| `save` | `kernel.save` | `S` | `s` | `S` |
| `run_command` | `kernel.run_command` | `!` | `:` | `!` |
| `search` | `kernel.search` | `f` | `/` | `f` |
| `Help` | `kernel.Help` | `?` | `?` | `?` |
| `detach` | `kernel.detach` | `d` | `d` | `d` |
| `quit` | `kernel.quit` | `&` | `\` | `&` |
| `toggle_editor_view_mode` | `kernel.toggle_editor_view_mode` | `v` | `v` | `v` |
| `toggle_line_numbers` | `kernel.toggle_line_numbers` | `N` | `N` | `N` |
| `toggle_minimap` | `kernel.toggle_minimap` | `b` | `b` | `b` |
| `toggle_autosave` | `kernel.toggle_autosave` | `a` | `a` | `a` |
| `settings` | `kernel.settings` | `:` | `o` | `:` |

Rules that hold for all rows:

- The general prefix is `shortcut_base`, a `Ctrl` letter from `Ctrl+A` to `Ctrl+Z`, default `Ctrl+B`. The four tree actions `cycle_next_in_group`, `cycle_previous_in_group`, `jump_next_group` and `jump_previous_group` use the separate `navigation_shortcut_base`, so moving the general prefix to `Ctrl+A` keeps `Ctrl+B n` for tree traversal.
- The two presets are complete. The GNU Screen preset sets the prefix to `Ctrl+A`, and the tmux preset sets it to `Ctrl+B`. Choosing a preset replaces every key in the table. Actions that a preset does not name keep their default key.
- A key is bindable only when it is in the fixed list of printable keys, arrow keys and Page keys, and no other action uses it. The collision check runs for the picker and for preset load.
- Pressing the prefix twice passes it through to the program in the pane, which is how tmux inside Ilium keeps working.
- `rename` has no default key. It is in the table so a user can bind it.
- The plugin holds `settings.write-kernel:keyboard`. It is the only plugin that may write the `[keyboard]` and `[keybindings]` tables. Other plugins read the result with `keymap.read`. See [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab).

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keyboard` | Keyboard | `[keyboard]`, `[keybindings]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Keys and help is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### 1. Key reference

A panel reads every binding with `keymap.bindings`, turns each chord into its display form with `chord_label`, and draws the pairs as `key-hints`. It rebuilds when `keymap-changed` arrives, so a remap appears at once. See the [kernel settings and keymap API](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/), the [keymap.read grant](/pages/capability-keymap-read/), the [event catalogue](/pages/api-events/) and [text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{keymap, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::KeyHint;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Handler for KeysPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if matches!(event, Event::KeymapChanged) {
                ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Panel("keys".into()));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for KeysPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let hints: Vec<KeyHint> = keymap::bindings()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|binding| {
                let chord = binding.chords.first()?;
                Some(KeyHint::new(&keymap::chord_label(chord), &binding.command))
            })
            .collect();
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let panel = tree.key_hints(hints).key("hints");
        tree.finish(panel)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { bindings, chordLabel } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keymap';
import { invalidate } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { keyHints, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'keymap-changed') invalidate({ tag: 'panel', val: 'keys' });
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    const hints = bindings()
      .filter((binding) => binding.chords.length > 0)
      .map((binding) => ({ keys: chordLabel(binding.chords[0]), label: binding.command }));
    return tree(keyHints(hints, { key: 'hints' }));
  },
});
```

#### 2. Prefix and presets

The panel shows the prefix and the active preset by reading the Keyboard tab with `kernel-settings`, and refreshes on `kernel-settings-changed`. The plugin owns this tab and writes it with `settings.write-kernel:keyboard`; secrets would arrive as `<redacted>`. See the [settings.read-kernel grant](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/), the [kernel settings API](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/) and the [event catalogue](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::kernel_settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};

// Needs "settings.read-kernel:keyboard". Values are listed generically, so the
// panel follows whatever the Keyboard tab holds.
fn keyboard_lines() -> Vec<String> {
    let Ok(text) = kernel_settings::read("keyboard") else { return Vec::new() };
    let values: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap_or_default();
    values.as_object().map_or_else(Vec::new, |object| {
        object.iter().map(|(key, value)| format!("{key} = {value}")).collect()
    })
}

fn on_kernel_settings_changed(tab: &str, keys: &[String]) {
    if tab == "keyboard" {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("keyboard tab changed: {keys:?}"));
        // then invalidate the panel, as in sample 1
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

// Needs "settings.read-kernel:keyboard". Values are listed generically, so the
// panel follows whatever the Keyboard tab holds.
export function keyboardLines(): string[] {
  try {
    const values = JSON.parse(read('keyboard')) as Record<string, unknown>;
    return Object.entries(values).map(([key, value]) => `${key} = ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

export function onKernelSettingsChanged(tab: string, keys: string[]): void {
  if (tab !== 'keyboard') return;
  log('info', `keyboard tab changed: ${keys.join(',')}`);
  // then invalidate the panel, as in sample 1
}
```

#### 3. Remap a key

A `keybinding` row remaps one of the plugin's own commands. For a panel, a `key-capture` field records the next chord and, with the reserved-key check, warns when the kernel already binds it. See [settings rows](/pages/reference-settings-rows/) and [input widgets](/pages/widgets-input/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

// Manifest row: { "type": "keybinding", "key": "show_keys", "title": "Key reference",
//                 "command": "show-keys", "default": "?" }
impl Views for KeysPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let chord = tree
            .key_capture()
            .chord(self.chord.clone())
            .reserved_check(true)
            .key("chord");
        tree.finish(chord)
    }
}

// In on_events:
// ("chord", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(c)) => self.chord = Some(c).filter(|c| !c.is_empty()),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { keyCapture, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// Manifest row: { "type": "keybinding", "key": "show_keys", "title": "Key reference",
//                 "command": "show-keys", "default": "?" }
let chord: string | undefined;

export function render() {
  return tree(keyCapture({ key: 'chord', chord, reservedCheck: true }));
}

// In onEvents:
// if (key === 'chord' && value.tag === 'text') chord = value.val || undefined;
```

#### 4. Help topics

The panel lists topic ids in a `tree-list` and renders the chosen topic as `markdown`. `help.topic` returns the Markdown of any installed topic by its global id, `<plugin-id>/<local-id>`; there is no call that lists topics, so the plugin keeps its own list of ids. See the [help and plugins API](/pages/api-help-and-plugins/), the [help.read grant](/pages/capability-help-read/), [text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/) and [collection widgets](/pages/widgets-collections/). The topic ids shown are examples.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::help;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::TreeItem;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

const TOPICS: [(&str, &str); 2] = [
    ("ilium.core.keys-and-help/keys-overview", "Keys"),
    ("ilium/getting-started", "Getting started"),
];

impl Views for HelpPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let items: Vec<TreeItem> = TOPICS
            .iter()
            .map(|(id, title)| TreeItem::new(id, title).depth(0))
            .collect();
        let source = help::topic(&self.chosen).unwrap_or_else(|| "No such topic.".into());
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let list = tree.tree_list(items).key("topics");
        let page = tree.markdown(source).key("page");
        let both = tree
            .layout(Direction::Horizontal, [Constraint::Length(24), Constraint::Fill(1)])
            .child(list)
            .child(page);
        tree.finish(both)
    }
}
// In on_events: ("topics", ActionKind::Selected, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.chosen = id,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { topic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/help';
import { fill, layout, length, markdown, tree, treeList } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const TOPICS = [
  { id: 'ilium.core.keys-and-help/keys-overview', label: 'Keys', depth: 0 },
  { id: 'ilium/getting-started', label: 'Getting started', depth: 0 },
];
let chosen = TOPICS[0].id;

export function render() {
  const source = topic(chosen) ?? 'No such topic.';
  return tree(layout(
    { direction: 'horizontal', constraints: [length(24), fill(1)] },
    [treeList(TOPICS, { key: 'topics' }), markdown(source, { key: 'page' })],
  ));
}
// In onEvents: if (key === 'topics' && kind === 'selected' && value.tag === 'text') chosen = value.val;
```

#### 5. Palette and plugin manager

Commands declared in the manifest appear in the palette under their `category`. When the user runs the manager command, the plugin reads every installed plugin with `plugins.list` and turns one on or off with `plugins.set_enabled`. See the [command palette](/pages/api-command-palette/), the [plugins.manage grant](/pages/capability-plugins-manage/) and the [event catalogue](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::plugins;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;

// Manifest: commands with "category": "Help", as in the manifest above.
impl Handler for PluginManager {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, .. }) = event else {
                continue;
            };
            if command == "ilium.core.keys-and-help/show-plugins" {
                self.rows = plugins::list()
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|info| (info.id, info.name, info.enabled))
                    .collect();
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn toggle(plugin_id: &str, enabled: bool) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    plugins::set_enabled(plugin_id, enabled)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { list, setEnabled } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/plugins';

// Manifest: commands with "category": "Help", as in the manifest above.
let rows: Array<{ id: string; name: string; enabled: boolean }> = [];

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked'
          && event.val.command === 'ilium.core.keys-and-help/show-plugins') {
        rows = list().map(({ id, name, enabled }) => ({ id, name, enabled }));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});

export function toggle(pluginId: string, enabled: boolean): void {
  setEnabled(pluginId, enabled);
}
```

#### 6. Reload hints after a kernel change

The kernel settings tab for keys sends `kernel-settings-changed` with the keys that changed. The plugin reloads only the hint strings for those keys, not the whole reference.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl Handler for HintCache {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::KernelSettingsChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            if change.tab != "keys" { continue; }
            for key in &change.keys {
                self.hints.insert(key.clone(), kernel_settings::read("keys", key));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onEvents(events: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of events) {
    if (event.tag !== 'kernel-settings-changed' || event.val.tab !== 'keys') continue;
    for (const key of event.val.keys) {
      hints.set(key, settings.readKernel('keys', key));
    }
  }
  return [];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.keys-and-help` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.keys-and-help/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.keys-and-help/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key-hints` | collect | Add a hint to the status bar in a context. | entry: id, context, chord, label | standard |
| `help-sources` | collect | Add a help source, such as a remote documentation index. | entry: id, title, service | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.keys-and-help/bindings`: list: current key bindings with labels

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.keys-and-help/changed`: { reason } after a remap

`contributes.help` topics and `contributes.keybindings` appear in the key reference.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.keys-and-help"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Shows a hint while a board pane has focus

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.keys-and-help/key-hints"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.keys-and-help/key-hints",
        "id": "board-hints",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "context": "pane:board",
          "chord": "n",
          "label": "New card"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Workspace search

## Workspace search

The Workspace search plugin (id `ilium.core.search`, sides: server and client) is the plugin form of Ilium's workspace search. One panel finds agents, terminals and files by name, by the text on their screens, and by meaning, and shows the results in groups. The server side keeps the index and scans files. The client side draws the panel.

Reading a terminal's screen is a kernel service, and the plugin uses it through the `terminal.read-screen` grant. The vector maths for search by meaning is done by the host, so the plugin ships no search code of its own.

### What it covers

- **Workspace search.** Agents, terminals and files, grouped in one tree. See Workspace search in the Panes and layout page of the user documentation.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/10-workspace-search.gif" alt="The workspace search panel filters agents, terminals and files as the user types" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Workspace search: type a query, move through the grouped results and jump to a pane or file.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

### Manifest

This block is a fragment. It lists the contributions. The whole manifest is in [Complete manifest](#complete-manifest).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "ilium.core.search",
  "name": "Workspace search",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Ilium",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["job-runner"]
  },
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["views"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["inference.embed", "tree.read", "terminal.read-screen",
               "fs.read:project", "jobs.run"],
    "client": ["ui.panels"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [{ "id": "open", "title": "Search the workspace", "category": "Search" }],
    "keybindings": [
      { "command": "ilium.core.search/open", "chord": "/", "mode": "prefix" }
    ],
    "panels": [{ "id": "search", "title": "Search", "modal": true }],
    "jobs": [{ "kind": "scan-files", "deadline_ms": 120000, "memory_mib": 128 }]
  }
}
```

### Samples

#### 1. The search panel

A command bound to a chord submits `open-view`. The panel shows a `text-input` and a `%list`. Choosing a hit jumps to it and submits `close-view`. See the [UI API](/pages/api-ui/), the [ui.panels grant](/pages/capability-ui-panels/), the [intents](/pages/api-intents/), [input widgets](/pages/widgets-input/) and [collection widgets](/pages/widgets-collections/). `jump_to` and `jumpTo` are the plugin's own helpers.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::OpenViewSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::{ListItem, Tree};

fn panel() -> ViewTarget { ViewTarget::Panel("search".into()) }

impl Handler for SearchPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(c) if c.command == "ilium.core.search/open" => {
                    out.push(Submission {
                        intent: Intent::OpenView(OpenViewSpec { view: panel(), focus: true }),
                        correlation: 1,
                        dedup_key: None,
                    });
                }
                Event::UiAction(a) => match (a.key.as_str(), a.kind, a.value) {
                    ("query", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(text)) => self.query = text,
                    ("hits", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Index(i)) => {
                        self.jump_to(i as usize);
                        out.push(Submission {
                            intent: Intent::CloseView(panel()),
                            correlation: 2,
                            dedup_key: None,
                        });
                    }
                    _ => {}
                },
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        out
    }
}

impl Views for SearchPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let query = tree.text_input("Search", self.query.clone()).key("query");
        let rows: Vec<ListItem> = self.hits.iter()
            .map(|hit| ListItem::new(vec![hit.title.clone()]).id(&hit.id).trailing(&hit.kind))
            .collect();
        let hits = tree.list(rows).key("hits");
        let body = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(3), Constraint::Fill(1)])
            .child(query).child(hits);
        tree.finish(body)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { fill, layout, length, list, textInput, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const PANEL = { tag: 'panel', val: 'search' } as const;
let query = '';
let hits: Array<{ id: string; title: string; kind: string }> = [];

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const out: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'ilium.core.search/open') {
        out.push({ intent: { tag: 'open-view', val: { view: PANEL, focus: true } },
                   correlation: 1n, dedupKey: undefined });
      } else if (event.tag === 'ui-action') {
        const { key, kind, value } = event.val;
        if (key === 'query' && kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'text') query = value.val;
        if (key === 'hits' && kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'index') {
          jumpTo(value.val);
          out.push({ intent: { tag: 'close-view', val: PANEL }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined });
        }
      }
    }
    return out;
  },
  render() {
    const rows = hits.map((hit) => ({ id: hit.id, lines: [hit.title], trailing: hit.kind }));
    return tree(layout(
      { direction: 'vertical', constraints: [length(3), fill(1)] },
      [textInput('Search', query, { key: 'query' }), list(rows, { key: 'hits' })],
    ));
  },
});
```

#### 2. Search by meaning

The server embeds pane titles and screen snippets into a vector index, then answers a query by cosine similarity and returns the top 20 ids with scores. The host does the maths. See the [vector API](/pages/api-vector/) and the [inference.embed grant](/pages/capability-inference-embed/). An embed call takes at most 256 texts, so a large workspace is indexed in batches.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::vector;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::errors::PluginError;

const PURPOSE: &str = "workspace search";

pub struct MeaningIndex { index: u32 }

impl MeaningIndex {
    /// `items` holds (pane id, title and screen snippet).
    pub async fn build(items: &[(String, String)]) -> Result<MeaningIndex, PluginError> {
        let texts: Vec<String> = items.iter().map(|(_, text)| text.clone()).collect();
        let vectors = vector::embed(&texts, PURPOSE).await?;
        let dimensions = vectors.first().map_or(0, |vector| vector.len());
        let index = vector::create_index("workspace", dimensions as u16)?;
        let entries: Vec<(String, Vec<f32>)> =
            items.iter().map(|(id, _)| id.clone()).zip(vectors).collect();
        vector::upsert(index, &entries)?;
        Ok(MeaningIndex { index })
    }

    pub async fn query(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<(String, f32)>, PluginError> {
        let Some(first) = vector::embed(&[text.to_string()], PURPOSE).await?.into_iter().next()
        else { return Ok(Vec::new()) };
        vector::top_k(self.index, &first, 20)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { createIndex, embed, topK, upsert } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/vector';

const PURPOSE = 'workspace search';

export async function buildIndex(items: Array<[string, string]>): Promise<number> {
  const vectors = await embed(items.map(([, text]) => text), PURPOSE);
  const index = createIndex('workspace', vectors[0]?.length ?? 0);
  upsert(index, items.map(([id], position) => [id, vectors[position]] as [string, number[]]));
  return index;
}

export async function query(index: number, text: string): Promise<Array<[string, number]>> {
  const [vector] = await embed([text], PURPOSE);
  return vector === undefined ? [] : topK(index, vector, 20);
}
```

#### 3. Grouped results

Results sit in a `tree-list` with one parent row per kind (Agents, Terminals, Files). A `scrollbar` is bound to the list by its key. The plugin handles `ui-action` events for select and open. See [collection widgets](/pages/widgets-collections/), [layout widgets](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) and the [event catalogue](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ScrollbarOrientation, TreeItem};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Views for SearchPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut items = Vec::new();
        for (group, hits) in &self.groups {
            items.push(TreeItem::new(group, group).depth(0).expandable(true));
            for hit in hits {
                items.push(TreeItem::new(&hit.id, &hit.title).depth(1));
            }
        }
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let results = tree.tree_list(items).key("results");
        let bar = tree.scrollbar(ScrollbarOrientation::VerticalRight, "results").key("results-bar");
        let row = tree
            .layout(Direction::Horizontal, [Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(1)])
            .child(results).child(bar);
        tree.finish(row)
    }
}
// In on_events: ("results", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.open(&id),
//               ("results", ActionKind::Selected, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.preview(&id),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { fill, layout, length, scrollbar, tree, treeList } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const groups: Array<[string, Array<{ id: string; title: string }>]> = [];

export function render() {
  const items = groups.flatMap(([group, hits]) => [
    { id: group, label: group, depth: 0, expandable: true },
    ...hits.map((hit) => ({ id: hit.id, label: hit.title, depth: 1 })),
  ]);
  return tree(layout(
    { direction: 'horizontal', constraints: [fill(1), length(1)] },
    [
      treeList(items, { key: 'results' }),
      scrollbar('results', { orientation: 'vertical-right', key: 'results-bar' }),
    ],
  ));
}
// In onEvents: if (key === 'results' && kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'text') open(value.val);
//              if (key === 'results' && kind === 'selected' && value.tag === 'text') preview(value.val);
```

#### 4. Scan files in a job

File names and contents are scanned off the event handler. The server lists the project with `fs.scan`, starts a `scan-files` job with the paths, and follows `job-progress`. See the [jobs API](/pages/api-jobs/), the [file API](/pages/api-fs/) and the [event catalogue](/pages/api-events/). `indexFiles` is the plugin's own function, and the Rust job runner mirrors the one in the Compaction plugin.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, jobs};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::requests::RequestResult;

fn project(path: &str) -> FsPath { FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: path.into() } }

impl Handler for Scanner {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(c) if c.command == "ilium.core.search/rescan" => {
                    self.scan = fs::scan(&project(""), "**/*", 4096).ok();
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(RequestResult { request: RequestRef::Call(id), .. })
                    if self.scan == Some(id) =>
                {
                    let paths: Vec<String> = fs::take_entries(id)
                        .unwrap_or_default().into_iter().map(|(path, _)| path).collect();
                    self.scan = None;
                    self.job = jobs::start_request("scan-files", paths.join("\n").as_bytes()).ok();
                }
                Event::JobProgress(p) if self.job == Some(p.request_id) => {
                    self.percent = p.percent; // batches stream back as the job runs
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { scan } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { startRequest } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';

const project = (path: string) => ({ scope: 'project', path });
let job: bigint | undefined;
let percent = 0;

export const { lifecycle, handler, jobRunner } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'ilium.core.search/rescan') {
        void scan(project(''), '**/*', 4096).then((entries) => {
          const paths = entries.map(([path]) => path).join('\n');
          job = startRequest('scan-files', new TextEncoder().encode(paths));
        });
      } else if (event.tag === 'job-progress' && event.val.requestId === job) {
        percent = event.val.percent; // batches stream back as the job runs
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  run(_kind: string, input: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
    return indexFiles(new TextDecoder().decode(input).split('\n')); // runs in the job
  },
});
```

#### 5. Refresh results on filter change

The filter field sends `filter-changed` with the text, debounced to 150 ms by the kernel. The plugin reruns the query only when the text differs from the last run, so a quick retype does not start a second scan.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue};

impl Handler for LiveFilter {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if let (ActionKind::FilterChanged, ActionValue::Text(text)) = (action.kind, action.value) {
                if text == self.last_query { continue; }
                self.last_query = text.clone();
                return vec![self.query_submission(text)];
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function onAction(event: Extract<Event, { tag: 'ui-action' }>): Submission[] {
  const { kind, value } = event.val;
  if (kind !== 'filter-changed' || value.tag !== 'text') return [];
  if (value.val === lastQuery) return [];
  lastQuery = value.val;
  return [querySubmission(value.val)];
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.search` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.search/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.search/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sources` | collect | Add a source of results, such as issues or notes. | entry: id, title, kind, service (answers a query with ranked hits) | standard |
| `rank` | hook (transform) | Change the order of results before they are shown. | query, hits (id, kind, score); reply: hits | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.search/query`: query: search all sources

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.search"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds issues as a result kind

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.search/sources"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.search/sources",
        "id": "issues",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Issues",
          "kind": "issue",
          "service": "example.issues/search"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Ambient look

## Ambient look

The Ambient look plugin (id `ilium.core.ambient`, side: client) is the plugin form of the shared look of animated backgrounds. It owns the colour, palette, dithering and display controls that every scene gets, the Animations settings tab with its previews, the shared location that sky and map scenes read, and the semantic animation choice that picks a scene from what the workspace is doing.

Painting the background and applying colour, filters and dithering to each cell is done by the client kernel. The plugin supplies the controls and the preview. The scenes themselves are in the [Scenes plugin](/pages/core-plugin-scenes/), and they follow the look chosen here without any colour code of their own.

### What it covers

- **Shared look of animations.** Colour mode, palette, filters, brightness, contrast and more, as described under The shared look in the Animations page of the user documentation.
- **Shared dithering and display controls.** Dithering, panel placement, frame-rate cap, speed and density (see Shared dithering and Shared display controls).
- **Semantic animation and the Animations tab.** The scene list with previews, and the Loop and Live playback modes (see Semantic animation and Playback: Loop and Live).

The preview updates as the controls change.</figcaption></figure>

```json
                    "title": "Stars"
                  },
                  {
                    "value": "clouds",
                    "title": "Clouds"
                  }
                ]
              },
              {

      }

  "limits_tier": "first-party"

```

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animations` | Animations | project YAML `animation` | Scenes |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Ambient look is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### 1. Preview in Settings

A `preview` row is bound to the scene the user chose, and a panel draws the same frames on a `surface`. The plugin writes whole rows of pixels with `write_surface`. See [media and embedded widgets](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) and [settings rows](/pages/reference-settings-rows/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{PixelFormat, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

// Manifest row: { "type": "preview", "view": "scene-preview", "height": 4, "live": true }
impl Views for AmbientPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let preview = tree
            .surface(PixelFormat::Rgb8)
            .min_columns(40)
            .min_rows(4)
            .key("frame");
        tree.finish(preview)
    }
}

impl AmbientPanel {
    /// Called when the preview scene produced a new frame of `rows` full rows.
    fn show_frame(&self, pixels: &[u8]) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        ui::write_surface(ViewTarget::Panel("preview".into()), "frame", 0, PixelFormat::Rgb8, pixels)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { writeSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { surface, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// Manifest row: { "type": "preview", "view": "scene-preview", "height": 4, "live": true }
export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents() { return []; },
  render() {
    return tree(surface({ key: 'frame', format: 'rgb8', minColumns: 40, minRows: 4 }));
  },
});

/** Called when the preview scene produced a new frame of whole rows. */
export function showFrame(pixels: Uint8Array): void {
  writeSurface({ tag: 'panel', val: 'preview' }, 'frame', 0, 'rgb8', pixels);
}
```

#### 2. Shared location

One `location` row holds the observer position for every scene that needs it, and a `map` row keeps saved places. In a panel the `location-picker` binds to the row and geocodes a typed place name. The geocoder is [the geocode API](/pages/api-geocode/) with the [location.geocode grant](/pages/capability-location-geocode/); other pages used are [settings rows](/pages/reference-settings-rows/) and [pickers](/pages/widgets-pickers/). Place names are sent to the geocoding provider, so the settings row should say so.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::geocode::{self, GeocodeQuery};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

// Manifest rows: "location" (key "observer") and "map" (key "saved_places").
impl Views for AmbientPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let place = tree.location_picker().key("place").bind("observer").search(true);
        tree.finish(place)
    }
}

/// Starts a place search; the places arrive after `request-completed`.
fn find_place(text: &str) -> Result<RequestId, PluginError> {
    geocode::search(&GeocodeQuery { text: text.into(), near: None, limit: 5, language: Some("en".into()) })
}

fn place_names(request: RequestId) -> Vec<String> {
    geocode::take_places(request).unwrap_or_default().into_iter().map(|place| place.name).collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { search, takePlaces } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/geocode';
import { locationPicker, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

// Manifest rows: "location" (key "observer") and "map" (key "saved_places").
export function render() {
  return tree(locationPicker({ key: 'place', bind: 'observer', search: true }));
}

/** Starts a place search; the places arrive after request-completed. */
export const findPlace = (text: string) =>
  search({ text, near: undefined, limit: 5, language: 'en' });

export const placeNames = (request: bigint): string[] =>
  (takePlaces(request) ?? []).map((place) => place.name);
```

#### 3. Scene gallery

An `image` thumbnail for each scene and a `video` clip for the selected one. Both come from the package's assets. See [media and embedded widgets](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) and the [media.video grant](/pages/capability-media-video/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{MediaFit, ImageSource, VideoSource};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

impl Views for AmbientPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let thumb = tree
            .image(ImageSource::Asset(format!("thumbs/{}.png", self.selected)))
            .fit(MediaFit::Contain)
            .key("thumb");
        let clip = tree
            .video(VideoSource::Asset(format!("clips/{}.webm", self.selected)))
            .autoplay(true)
            .looped(true)
            .fit(MediaFit::Cover)
            .key("clip");
        let both = tree
            .layout(Direction::Horizontal, [Constraint::Length(20), Constraint::Fill(1)])
            .child(thumb).child(clip);
        tree.finish(both)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { fill, image, layout, length, tree, video } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

let selected = 'stars';

export function render() {
  const thumb = image({ tag: 'asset', val: `thumbs/${selected}.png` }, { key: 'thumb', fit: 'contain' });
  const clip = video({ tag: 'asset', val: `clips/${selected}.webm` }, {
    key: 'clip', autoplay: true, loop: true, fit: 'cover',
  });
  return tree(layout(
    { direction: 'horizontal', constraints: [length(20), fill(1)] },
    [thumb, clip],
  ));
}
```

#### 4. Semantic animation

When the user turns semantic animation on, the plugin proposes a scene. It keeps the last suggestion in global storage so the same choice returns after a restart. How the suggestion is chosen from the workspace state is the plugin's own logic. See [storage](/pages/api-storage/) and the [event catalogue](/pages/api-events/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{settings, storage::{self, Bucket}};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

const LAST_SCENE: &str = "last_suggestion";

impl Handler for AmbientPlugin {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::SettingsChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            if !change.keys.iter().any(|key| key == "semantic") {
                continue;
            }
            let values: serde_json::Value =
                serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or_default();
            if values["semantic"].as_bool() != Some(true) {
                continue;
            }
            let last = storage::get(Bucket::Global, LAST_SCENE)
                .and_then(|bytes| String::from_utf8(bytes).ok())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "stars".into());
            self.suggestion = Some(last); // offered as the starting scene
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn remember(scene: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    storage::put(Bucket::Global, LAST_SCENE, scene.as_bytes())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';
import { get, put } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';

const LAST_SCENE = 'last_suggestion';
let suggestion: string | undefined;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'settings-changed' || !event.val.keys.includes('semantic')) continue;
      const values = JSON.parse(getJson()) as { semantic?: boolean };
      if (values.semantic !== true) continue;
      const bytes = get('global', LAST_SCENE);
      suggestion = bytes ? new TextDecoder().decode(bytes) : 'stars'; // the starting scene
    }
    return [];
  },
});

export function remember(scene: string): void {
  put('global', LAST_SCENE, new TextEncoder().encode(scene));
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.ambient` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.ambient/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.ambient/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `palettes` | collect | Add a palette to the shared palette choice. | entry: id, title, stops (list of colours) | standard |
| `style-presets` | collect | Add a style preset: a full set of shared look values. | entry: id, title, values | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.ambient/look`: get: current shared look and palette

**Topics** (list under `contributes.topics.subscribes`):

- `ilium.core.ambient/look-changed`: { palette, mode }

Every scene receives the palette in its constructor.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.ambient"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds a four-colour palette

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.ambient/palettes"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.ambient/palettes",
        "id": "harbour",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Harbour",
          "stops": [
            "#0b1d2a",
            "#1f6f8b",
            "#99d5c9",
            "#f6f1d1"
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Scenes

## Scenes

The Scenes plugin (id `ilium.core.scenes`, side: scene) is the plugin form of the animated scenes themselves. A scene is a renderer that draws frames into a surface. The host runs it in its own animation world, applies the shared look from the [Ambient look plugin](/pages/core-plugin-ambient/) (palette, filters, dithering), and puts the result behind the panes. A scene never adds colour, brightness or dithering controls of its own.

The scene host, the cached loops and the frame pacing are part of the client kernel. The plugin supplies the renderers: natural, procedural, geometry, simulations and games, live data, maps and space, media scenes, packaged animations and the optional GPU path.

### What it covers

- **Natural cached-loop scenes.** See Built-in scenes with cached loops in the nature and abstract animations page of the user documentation.
- **Procedural quiet scenes and machines.** See Quiet procedural scenes and Machines and clocks.
- **Geometry scenes, pipes and wind.** See Geometry and mathematics, 3D pipes and Wind.
- **Simulations and games.** Galactic empires, Hex expedition and Vector TD, described in the media and games animations page.
- **Live-data scenes.** See Live data scenes in the maps, space and live data page. They fetch data over HTTP and need an `http:<host>` grant.
- **Maps, space, Wikipedia and voxel saved worlds.** See Stars overhead, OpenStreetMap and Voxel landscape.
- **Media scenes.** Video, audio spectrum and images, in the media and games page.
- **Packaged animations.** `.iliumanim` files, described under Animation packages. See also [porting an .iliumanim package](/pages/porting-iliumanim/).
- **Optional GPU backend.** Described under Background animations in How it works. The scene-side calls are an unstable development-build feature.

### See it

### Scene catalogue and single owners

Every scene below belongs to the Scenes plugin. The [Ambient look](/pages/core-plugin-ambient/) plugin owns only the shared controls (colour, palette, filters, dithering, display) and the shared observer location row. The kernel owns the scene host, the raster and the look painter. [COR-010] [COR-011]

| Family | Scenes | User documentation | Wave | Grants a scene package needs | Single owner of the feature |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Natural cached loops | Shoreline, Moonlit water, Sleeping ridge, Windy hillside, Tea steam, Kelp, Stone caustics, Cloudlets, Two ripples, Lily pads | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c | none | Scenes |
| Quiet procedural | Aurora, Pollen, Fireflies, Window sunlight, Frost, Lighthouse | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c | none | Scenes |
| Geometry and mathematics | Paper-fold trace, Embroidery orbit, Prime constellations, Turning wallpaper, Unfinished circle, Threads through a needle, Ink that hesitates, Crop circles, Delayed reflection, Almost touching, Hidden wheel | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c | none | Scenes |
| Pipes, wind, growth | 3D pipes, Wind, Growth | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c | none | Scenes |
| Dithered | Dithered water, Atlantic dusk, Dithered fBm clouds, Dithered waves, Dithr patterns | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c | none | Scenes (dithering algorithms stay shared) |
| Machines and clocks | Cube clock, Box machine, Machine screen | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c | none | Scenes |
| Carpet simulations | Mouse hunters, Autonomous Snake, Slow Life, chess (automated and Lichess TV), DVD ball, Planetary orbits, clocks | animations-nature-and-abstract | 4c; Lichess TV in 4d | `http:lichess.org` for Lichess TV | Scenes |
| Games | Galactic empires, Hex expedition, Vector TD | animations-media-and-games | 4c | none | Scenes |
| Video | Custom series, Germination series | animations-media-and-games | 4d | `media.video`, `fs.pick` | Scenes. Ambient only shows the preview clip |
| Audio spectrum | Audio spectrum | animations-media-and-games | 4d | `audio.loopback` | Scenes |
| Images | Images | animations-media-and-games | 4d | `fs.pick`, `codec` | Scenes |
| Wikipedia | Wikipedia | animations-media-and-games | 4d | `http:*.wikipedia.org` | Scenes |
| Maps and space | Stars overhead, Satellite clouds, Earth at night, Solar system, Topographic maps, OpenStreetMap | animations-maps-space-and-live-data | 4d | `http`, `cache`, shared location | Scenes. The location row belongs to Ambient |
| Live data | Earthquakes, aircraft, boats, live graphs | animations-maps-space-and-live-data | 4d | `http:<host>` per source | Scenes |
| Saved worlds | Voxel landscape | animations-maps-space-and-live-data | 4e | `minecraft-saves` scope, `codec.inflate`, jobs | Scenes |

[COR-011] covers the rule that a scene package follows the shared look. A scene that adds its own brightness, contrast, hue, palette or dithering control is refused by the check rules.

### Manifest

This block is a fragment. It lists the contributions. The whole manifest is in [Complete manifest](#complete-manifest).

A scene package has a `scene` entry and no server or client side. Each scene listed under `contributes.scenes` appears in the Animations tab. The `capabilities.scene` list holds the grants for media, the observer location, the GPU and a live-data host.

### Samples

#### 1. A procedural scene

The smallest scene is a renderer with `new(spec)`, `frames_per_second` and `render`. It writes tones, and the host applies the palette, filters and dithering. The renderer also keeps the palette that the host passes in the spec and in `set_palette`, as every scene should. See the [scenes API](/pages/api-scenes/) and [always-granted capabilities](/pages/capability-always-granted/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::renderer::{FrameInput, Renderer, SceneSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::surface::FrameSurface;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "scene")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Waves {
    palette: Vec<u32>,
}

impl Lifecycle for Waves {}

impl Renderer for Waves {
    fn new(spec: SceneSpec) -> Self {
        Waves { palette: spec.palette }
    }

    fn frames_per_second(&self) -> u32 {
        24 // the host caps it at frame_rate_cap from the manifest
    }

    // PALETTE (future plugin contract): colour scenes shift onto this palette.
    // A tone-only scene needs no code; the host colours the tones.
    fn set_palette(&mut self, palette_rgb: Vec<u32>) {
        self.palette = palette_rgb;
    }

    fn render(&mut self, frame: FrameInput, surface: &FrameSurface) {
        let seconds = frame.time_millis as f32 / 1000.0;
        let mut tones = Vec::with_capacity((frame.width * frame.height) as usize);
        for row in 0..frame.height {
            for column in 0..frame.width {
                let wave = (column as f32 * 0.2 + row as f32 * 0.1 - seconds * 2.0).sin();
                tones.push(((wave + 1.0) * 127.5) as u8);
            }
        }
        surface.write_tones(0, &tones);
        surface.present();
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { defineScene } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { FrameInput, SceneSpec } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/renderer';
import type { FrameSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/surface';

class Waves {
  private palette: number[];

  constructor(spec: SceneSpec) {
    this.palette = spec.palette;
  }

  framesPerSecond(): number {
    return 24; // the host caps it at frame_rate_cap from the manifest
  }

  // PALETTE (future plugin contract): colour scenes shift onto this palette.
  // A tone-only scene needs no code; the host colours the tones.
  setPalette(palette: number[]): void {
    this.palette = palette;
  }

  render(frame: FrameInput, surface: FrameSurface): void {
    const seconds = Number(frame.timeMillis) / 1000;
    const tones = new Uint8Array(frame.width * frame.height);
    for (let row = 0; row < frame.height; row++) {
      for (let column = 0; column < frame.width; column++) {
        const wave = Math.sin(column * 0.2 + row * 0.1 - seconds * 2);
        tones[row * frame.width + column] = Math.round(((wave + 1) / 2) * 255);
      }
    }
    surface.writeTones(0, tones);
    surface.present();
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, renderer } = defineScene(Waves);
```

#### 2. Text over pixels

A scene with `"glyph_plane": true` can draw text over its pixels. The clock face and hands go into the pixel plane, and the numbers go into the glyph plane, so the text stays sharp under dithering. See the [Glyph plane and frame receipts](/pages/api-surface-glyph-plane/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// Assumption of this sample: 2 pixels by 4 pixels per cell. The real factor depends
// on the dither mode, so a real scene derives it from the surface size.
const PIXELS_PER_CELL_X: u32 = 2;
const PIXELS_PER_CELL_Y: u32 = 4;

impl Clock {
    fn draw_numbers(&self, frame: &FrameInput, surface: &FrameSurface) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let columns = (frame.width / PIXELS_PER_CELL_X) as u16;
        let rows = (frame.height / PIXELS_PER_CELL_Y) as u16;
        surface.clear_glyphs();
        let mark = |text: &str, column: u16, row: u16| GlyphCell {
            column, row, text: text.into(), fg: Some(0xffffff), bg: None, add: Modifiers::BOLD,
        };
        surface.write_glyphs(&[
            mark("12", columns / 2 - 1, 0),
            mark("3", columns - 2, rows / 2),
            mark("6", columns / 2, rows - 1),
            mark("9", 1, rows / 2),
        ])
    }
}
// In render: draw the face ring and hands as tones with write_tones, then
// self.draw_numbers(&frame, surface) for the numbers, then surface.present().
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { FrameInput } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/renderer';
import type { FrameSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/surface';

// Assumption of this sample: 2 pixels by 4 pixels per cell. The real factor depends
// on the dither mode, so a real scene derives it from the surface size.
const PIXELS_PER_CELL_X = 2;
const PIXELS_PER_CELL_Y = 4;

export function drawNumbers(frame: FrameInput, surface: FrameSurface): void {
  const columns = Math.floor(frame.width / PIXELS_PER_CELL_X);
  const rows = Math.floor(frame.height / PIXELS_PER_CELL_Y);
  surface.clearGlyphs();
  const mark = (text: string, column: number, row: number) =>
    ({ column, row, text, fg: 0xffffff, bg: undefined, add: { bold: true } });
  surface.writeGlyphs([
    mark('12', Math.floor(columns / 2) - 1, 0),
    mark('3', columns - 2, Math.floor(rows / 2)),
    mark('6', Math.floor(columns / 2), rows - 1),
    mark('9', 1, Math.floor(rows / 2)),
  ]);
}
// In render: draw the face ring and hands as tones with writeTones, then
// drawNumbers(frame, surface) for the numbers, then surface.present().
```

#### 3. Video scene

The host decodes the video. The scene opens it from bytes bundled in the package, pulls one frame per tick scaled to the surface, and writes it as RGB. The `codec` import reads the poster image size without decoding it. See the [media API](/pages/api-media/), the [media.video grant](/pages/capability-media-video/) and the [codec API](/pages/api-codec/). A clip may be at most 16 MiB when opened from bytes.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::renderer::{FrameInput, Renderer, SceneSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::surface::FrameSurface;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{codec, media};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

static CLIP: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../assets/loop.mp4");
static POSTER: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../assets/poster.png");

struct VideoScene {
    video: Option<u64>,
}

impl Renderer for VideoScene {
    fn new(_spec: SceneSpec) -> Self {
        let video = media::open_video_bytes(CLIP, "video/mp4").ok().map(|(id, _info)| id);
        // The poster only supplies a size here; its pixels are not decoded.
        if let Ok(info) = codec::image_info(POSTER) {
            let _aspect = info.width as f32 / info.height as f32;
        }
        VideoScene { video }
    }

    fn render(&mut self, frame: FrameInput, surface: &FrameSurface) {
        let Some(video) = self.video else { return };
        if let Ok(Some(pixels)) = media::next_frame(video, frame.width, frame.height) {
            surface.write_rgb(0, &pixels);
            surface.present();
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { defineScene } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { imageInfo } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/codec';
import { nextFrame, openVideoBytes } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/media';
import type { FrameInput, SceneSpec } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/renderer';
import type { FrameSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/surface';

declare const CLIP: Uint8Array;   // bundled with the package
declare const POSTER: Uint8Array; // bundled with the package

class VideoScene {
  private video: bigint | undefined;

  constructor(_spec: SceneSpec) {
    try {
      this.video = openVideoBytes(CLIP, 'video/mp4')[0];
    } catch {
      this.video = undefined;
    }
    // The poster only supplies a size here; its pixels are not decoded.
    const info = imageInfo(POSTER);
    void (info.width / info.height);
  }

  render(frame: FrameInput, surface: FrameSurface): void {
    if (this.video === undefined) return;
    const pixels = nextFrame(this.video, frame.width, frame.height);
    if (pixels === undefined) return;
    surface.writeRgb(0, pixels);
    surface.present();
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, renderer } = defineScene(VideoScene);
```

#### 4. Stars overhead

The scene reads the observer position once with `location.current`, converts each star to altitude and azimuth for the current time, and plots the ones above the horizon. The position never leaves the scene. See the [location API](/pages/api-location/) and the [location.observer grant](/pages/capability-location-observer/). The sidereal-time formula is a simple approximation, good enough for a background.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::renderer::{FrameInput, Renderer, SceneSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::surface::FrameSurface;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::location;

/// A few bright stars as (right ascension in hours, declination in degrees).
const STARS: [(f64, f64); 6] = [
    (2.53, 89.26), (5.28, 46.0), (5.92, 7.41), (6.75, -16.72), (14.26, 19.18), (18.62, 38.78),
];

struct StarsOverhead {
    observer: Option<(f64, f64)>, // read once, latitude and longitude in degrees
}

impl Renderer for StarsOverhead {
    fn new(_spec: SceneSpec) -> Self {
        StarsOverhead { observer: location::current() }
    }

    fn render(&mut self, frame: FrameInput, surface: &FrameSurface) {
        let mut tones = vec![0u8; (frame.width * frame.height) as usize];
        if let Some((latitude, longitude)) = self.observer {
            let days = frame.now_unix_millis as f64 / 86_400_000.0 - 10_957.5; // since J2000
            let sidereal = (280.46061837 + 360.98564736629 * days + longitude) % 360.0;
            for (hours, declination) in STARS {
                let hour_angle = (sidereal - hours * 15.0).to_radians();
                let (lat, dec) = (latitude.to_radians(), declination.to_radians());
                let sin_alt = dec.sin() * lat.sin() + dec.cos() * lat.cos() * hour_angle.cos();
                if sin_alt <= 0.0 { continue } // below the horizon
                let altitude = sin_alt.asin();
                let azimuth = (-dec.cos() * hour_angle.sin())
                    .atan2(dec.sin() * lat.cos() - dec.cos() * lat.sin() * hour_angle.cos());
                let radius = 1.0 - altitude / std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
                let x = ((azimuth.sin() * radius + 1.0) / 2.0 * (frame.width - 1) as f64) as u32;
                let y = ((1.0 - azimuth.cos() * radius) / 2.0 * (frame.height - 1) as f64) as u32;
                tones[(y * frame.width + x) as usize] = 255;
            }
        }
        surface.write_tones(0, &tones);
        surface.present();
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { defineScene } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as location from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/location';
import type { FrameInput, SceneSpec } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/renderer';
import type { FrameSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/surface';

/** A few bright stars as [right ascension in hours, declination in degrees]. */
const STARS: Array<[number, number]> = [
  [2.53, 89.26], [5.28, 46.0], [5.92, 7.41], [6.75, -16.72], [14.26, 19.18], [18.62, 38.78],
];
const radians = (degrees: number) => (degrees * Math.PI) / 180;

class StarsOverhead {
  private observer = location.current(); // read once: [latitude, longitude] in degrees

  constructor(_spec: SceneSpec) {}

  render(frame: FrameInput, surface: FrameSurface): void {
    const tones = new Uint8Array(frame.width * frame.height);
    if (this.observer !== undefined) {
      const [latitude, longitude] = this.observer;
      const days = Number(frame.nowUnixMillis) / 86_400_000 - 10_957.5; // since J2000
      const sidereal = (280.46061837 + 360.98564736629 * days + longitude) % 360;
      for (const [hours, declination] of STARS) {
        const hourAngle = radians(sidereal - hours * 15);
        const lat = radians(latitude);
        const dec = radians(declination);
        const sinAlt = Math.sin(dec) * Math.sin(lat) + Math.cos(dec) * Math.cos(lat) * Math.cos(hourAngle);
        if (sinAlt <= 0) continue; // below the horizon
        const altitude = Math.asin(sinAlt);
        const azimuth = Math.atan2(
          -Math.cos(dec) * Math.sin(hourAngle),
          Math.sin(dec) * Math.cos(lat) - Math.cos(dec) * Math.sin(lat) * Math.cos(hourAngle),
        );
        const radius = 1 - altitude / (Math.PI / 2);
        const x = Math.floor(((Math.sin(azimuth) * radius + 1) / 2) * (frame.width - 1));
        const y = Math.floor(((1 - Math.cos(azimuth) * radius) / 2) * (frame.height - 1));
        tones[y * frame.width + x] = 255;
      }
    }
    surface.writeTones(0, tones);
    surface.present();
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, renderer } = defineScene(StarsOverhead);
```

#### 5. GPU kernels

Heavy scenes can hand a kernel to the graphics device. The GPU API is unstable and exists in development builds only, so every call needs a CPU path: check `available` first, and fall back when the call returns `unsupported`. See the [GPU API](/pages/api-gpu/) and the [gpu.kernels grant](/pages/capability-gpu-kernels/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::gpu::{self, GpuKernel};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

// Unstable: the GPU API is for development builds only and may change.
impl CloudScene {
    fn soften(&self, field: &[u8], width: u32, height: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
        if !gpu::available() {
            return self.soften_on_cpu(field, width, height); // portable fallback
        }
        match gpu::run(GpuKernel::Blur, field, width, height, &self.params_json) {
            Ok(output) => output,
            Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Unsupported => {
                self.soften_on_cpu(field, width, height)
            }
            Err(_) => field.to_vec(),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { available, run } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/gpu';

// Unstable: the GPU API is for development builds only and may change.
export function soften(
  field: Uint8Array, width: number, height: number, paramsJson: string,
  softenOnCpu: (field: Uint8Array, width: number, height: number) => Uint8Array,
): Uint8Array {
  if (!available()) return softenOnCpu(field, width, height); // portable fallback
  try {
    return run('blur', field, width, height, paramsJson);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'unsupported') {
      return softenOnCpu(field, width, height);
    }
    return field;
  }
}
```

### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.scenes` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.scenes/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.scenes/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scene-packs` | collect | Offer a bundle of scenes with preset controls. | entry: id, title, scenes (list of scene id and control values) | standard |
| `scene-data-sources` | collect | Provide live data to data scenes, such as a feed. | entry: id, title, service (returns data points) | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.scenes/catalog`: list: list scenes and their controls

`contributes.scenes` entries add scenes. This plugin hosts the built-in ones.

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.scenes"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Bundles a slow cloud scene

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "scene": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.scenes/scene-packs"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.scenes/scene-packs",
        "id": "calm",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Calm",
          "scenes": [
            {
              "scene": "clouds",
              "controls": {
                "speed": 0.2
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Recap

## Recap

A recap is a few factual sentences about what one pane is doing, written once in a short form (at most 40 words) and once in a long form (at most 250 words). `ilium recap` prints them for every selected agent and shell pane, as JSON lines or as Markdown. The plugin id is `ilium.core.recap` and it runs on both sides. The server side owns the command, reads the evidence, calls the model and writes the records. The client side holds the answer to one question the server cannot know: whether onboarding is finished.

The recap text comes from the AI provider the user configured under Inference and privacy. One model call covers both lengths of one pane. When automatic AI is off or onboarding is not finished, nothing is read and nothing is sent: each selected pane gets a `denied` record.

### What it covers

- The `ilium recap [selection]` command, with the same selection options as `ilium panes` and `ilium broadcast`, described in the CLI reference.
- Evidence for agent panes from the transcript of the pane's own verified session, never from the screen.
- Evidence for shell panes from the current screen, capped at 64 KiB.
- The six states of a record: `summarized`, `idle`, `denied`, `unavailable`, `stale` and `failed`.
- Goal lines read from the transcript, not written by the model.
- Redaction of secrets before any text leaves Ilium, and the rule that a pointer survives only when its path appears in the evidence, lies under the pane's project or folder, exists now and is not denied.

### See it

There is no recording of this feature yet. The renders below are illustrative.
