### Samples

#### The `recap` command with JSON lines

The command is declared with `output: "jsonl"`, `requires_server: true` and the `pane-selector` argument group, so the host resolves `--pane` and `--all-panes`. The richer selection options (`--match`, `--project`, `--state` and the rest) arrive in `argv` and the plugin resolves them against the pane list. One `recap` record is written per pane, then one `summary`. The exit code is 0 when the run finished, even if some panes failed. See [cli](/pages/api-cli/) and [capability-cli-contribute](/pages/capability-cli-contribute/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::cli;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CliInvokedEvent;

#[derive(Default)]
struct Run { invocation: u64, length: String, waiting: usize, summarized: u32, failed: u32 }

fn start(&mut self, event: CliInvokedEvent) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let length = flag_value(&event.argv, "--length").unwrap_or_else(|| "both".into());
    if !["short", "long", "both"].contains(&length.as_str()) {
        cli::write_stderr(event.invocation, "recap: --length must be short, long or both")?;
        cli::finish(event.invocation, 2);
        return Ok(());
    }
    let panes = self.select_panes(&event)?; // agent and shell panes, self skipped
    for pane in panes.iter().take(MAX_PANES) {
        self.start_job(event.invocation, *pane, &length)?;
    }
    if panes.len() > MAX_PANES {
        let warning = r#"{"type":"warning","message":"extra panes skipped"}"#;
        cli::write_line(event.invocation, warning)?;
    }
    self.runs.insert(event.invocation, Run { invocation: event.invocation, length, waiting: panes.len().min(MAX_PANES), ..Run::default() });
    Ok(())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as cli from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/cli';
import type { CliInvokedEvent } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function start(event: CliInvokedEvent): void {
  const length = flagValue(event.argv, '--length') ?? 'both';
  if (!['short', 'long', 'both'].includes(length)) {
    cli.writeStderr(event.invocation, 'recap: --length must be short, long or both');
    cli.finish(event.invocation, 2);
    return;
  }
  const panes = selectPanes(event); // agent and shell panes, self skipped
  for (const pane of panes.slice(0, MAX_PANES)) startJob(event.invocation, pane, length);
  if (panes.length > MAX_PANES) {
    cli.writeLine(event.invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'warning', message: 'extra panes skipped' }));
  }
  runs.set(event.invocation, { length, waiting: Math.min(panes.length, MAX_PANES), summarized: 0, failed: 0 });
}
```

#### The consent gate

Before any pane is read, the plugin asks two questions. Is automatic AI on? That is a read-only look at a kernel settings tab. Is onboarding finished? That state lives in the client, so the server side sends a client request and the client side answers. A closed gate turns every pane into a `denied` record. See [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/), [capability settings.read-kernel](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/) and [client requests](/pages/api-client-requests/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{client_requests, kernel_settings};

fn ai_is_on() -> bool {
    kernel_settings::read("inference")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|json| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&json).ok())
        .and_then(|value| value["automatic_ai"].as_bool())
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

fn ask_onboarding(&mut self, client: ClientId) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let request = client_requests::request(client, "onboarding-state", "{}", 2_000)?;
    self.gate_requests.insert(request);
    Ok(())
}

// Client side, on Event::ClientRequest(call) with kind "onboarding-state":
//   client_requests::respond(call.call, Ok(format!(r#"{{"finished":{}}}"#, self.onboarding_done)));
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as clientRequests from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/client-requests';
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';

export function aiIsOn(): boolean {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(read('inference')).automatic_ai === true;
  } catch {
    return false; // unreadable means closed
  }
}

export function askOnboarding(client: bigint): void {
  gateRequests.add(clientRequests.request(client, 'onboarding-state', '{}', 2_000));
}

// Client side, on event.tag === 'client-request' with kind 'onboarding-state':
//   clientRequests.respond(event.val.call, { tag: 'ok', val: JSON.stringify({ finished: onboardingDone }) });
```

#### Evidence from an agent transcript

For an agent pane the plugin reads only the transcript of the pane's own session. If the host has no verified session for the pane, the record is `unavailable` and the plugin never falls back to the screen. The read is bounded, and secrets are replaced with `[redacted]` before the text goes to a job. See [agent transcript](/pages/primitives-agent-transcript/), [agent.transcript](/pages/capability-agent-transcript/) and [agent](/pages/primitives-agent/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent::{self, TranscriptQuery};

fn agent_evidence(&mut self, pane: NodeId) -> Evidence {
    if agent::session(pane).is_none() {
        return Evidence::Unavailable; // no verified session id for this pane
    }
    match agent::transcript(TranscriptQuery { pane, last_turns: 40, max_bytes: 512 * 1024 }) {
        Ok(request) => {
            self.transcript_requests.insert(request, pane);
            Evidence::Pending
        }
        Err(_) => Evidence::Unavailable,
    }
}

fn redact(text: &str) -> String {
    SECRET_KEY.replace_all(text, "$1[redacted]").into_owned()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { session, transcript } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent';

export function agentEvidence(pane: bigint): 'unavailable' | 'pending' {
  if (session(pane) === undefined) return 'unavailable'; // no verified session id
  try {
    transcriptRequests.set(transcript({ pane, lastTurns: 40, maxBytes: 512 * 1024 }), pane);
    return 'pending';
  } catch {
    return 'unavailable';
  }
}

export const redact = (text: string): string => text.replace(SECRET_KEY, '$1[redacted]');
```

#### Evidence from a shell screen

A shell pane has no transcript. The plugin reads the visible screen only, at most 40 rows, and stops at 64 KiB. An empty screen is `idle`, not `failed`. See [terminal.read-screen](/pages/capability-terminal-read-screen/) and [terminal reads](/pages/primitives-terminal-reads/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, ScreenPart};

const SCREEN_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;

fn shell_evidence(pane: NodeId) -> Evidence {
    let Some(screen) = terminal::read_screen(pane, ScreenPart::Visible, 40) else {
        return Evidence::Unavailable; // not a terminal, or the pane was replaced
    };
    let mut text = screen.rows.join("\n");
    text.truncate(text.floor_char_boundary(SCREEN_BYTES));
    if text.trim().is_empty() { Evidence::Idle } else { Evidence::Text(redact(&text)) }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { readScreen } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';

const SCREEN_BYTES = 64 * 1024;

export function shellEvidence(pane: bigint) {
  const screen = readScreen(pane, 'visible', 40);
  if (screen === undefined) return { tag: 'unavailable' } as const;
  const text = new TextDecoder().decode(new TextEncoder().encode(screen.rows.join('\n')).slice(0, SCREEN_BYTES));
  return text.trim() === '' ? ({ tag: 'idle' } as const) : ({ tag: 'text', text: redact(text) } as const);
}
```

#### One job per pane

The model call can take seconds, far over the 20 ms event deadline, so each pane is one job of kind `recap-pane`. The job asks for both lengths in one call, reports its progress and stops when the run is cancelled (Ctrl-C or the timeout). The run limit `--max-concurrency` maps to the plugin's `concurrent_jobs`; extra jobs wait in the queue. See [jobs](/pages/api-jobs/), [jobs.run](/pages/capability-jobs-run/) and [inference](/pages/api-inference/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{inference, jobs};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::JobRunner;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};

impl JobRunner for Recap {
    fn run(&mut self, kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
        let job: RecapJob = serde_json::from_slice(&input).map_err(PluginError::invalid_argument)?;
        jobs::report_progress(10.0);
        let request = inference::complete_request(CompletionRequest {
            messages: vec![
                ChatMessage { role: "system".into(), content: RECAP_PROMPT.into() },
                ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: job.evidence },
            ],
            max_output_tokens: None,
            json_schema: Some(RECAP_SCHEMA.into()),
            purpose: "recap".into(),
        })?;
        jobs::wait_request(request, 55_000)?;
        if jobs::is_cancelled() { return Err(PluginError::cancelled()); }
        let completion = inference::take_completion(request).ok_or_else(PluginError::internal)?;
        jobs::report_progress(100.0);
        Ok(completion.text.into_bytes())
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { completeRequest, takeCompletion } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { isCancelled, reportProgress, waitRequest } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';

export function run(kind: string, input: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
  const job = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(input)) as RecapJob;
  reportProgress(10);
  const request = completeRequest({
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: RECAP_PROMPT },
      { role: 'user', content: job.evidence },
    ],
    maxOutputTokens: undefined,
    jsonSchema: RECAP_SCHEMA,
    purpose: 'recap',
  });
  waitRequest(request, 55_000);
  if (isCancelled()) throw { code: 'cancelled', message: 'run cancelled' };
  const completion = takeCompletion(request);
  if (completion === undefined) throw { code: 'internal', message: 'no completion' };
  reportProgress(100);
  return new TextEncoder().encode(completion.text);
}
```

#### Owner side: collect the fact sources

`fact-sources` is a collect point. Before it builds the evidence, the plugin lists the entries that other plugins contributed, in run order, and asks each entry's service for facts about the pane. Each fact is added to the evidence block. When contributions change, the kernel publishes the topic `ilium.extensions/changed` to the owner only, and the plugin lists again. See [events](/pages/api-events/), [services](/pages/api-services/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{extensions, services};

const FACT_SOURCES: &str = "ilium.core.recap/fact-sources";

fn reload_sources(&mut self) {
    self.sources = extensions::list(FACT_SOURCES).unwrap_or_default();
}

async fn gather_facts(&self, pane: NodeId) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut facts = Vec::new();
    for source in &self.sources {
        let entry: FactSource = match serde_json::from_str(&source.entry_json) {
            Ok(entry) => entry,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        let payload = format!(r#"{{"pane":{}}}"#, pane.0);
        if let Ok(reply) = services::call(&entry.service, "facts", &payload).await {
            facts.push(format!("{}: {}", entry.title, redact(&reply)));
        }
    }
    facts
}

// In on_events: Event::TopicPublished(t) if t.topic == "ilium.extensions/changed" => self.reload_sources(),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';
import { call } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';

const FACT_SOURCES = 'ilium.core.recap/fact-sources';
let sources: extensions.ExtensionEntry[] = [];

export const reloadSources = (): void => {
  try { sources = extensions.list(FACT_SOURCES); } catch { sources = []; }
};

export async function gatherFacts(pane: bigint): Promise<string[]> {
  const facts: string[] = [];
  for (const source of sources) {
    const entry = JSON.parse(source.entryJson) as { title: string; service: string };
    try {
      const reply = await call(entry.service, 'facts', JSON.stringify({ pane: Number(pane) }));
      facts.push(`${entry.title}: ${redact(reply)}`);
    } catch { /* a failing source never stops the recap */ }
  }
  return facts;
}

// In onEvents: if (event.tag === 'topic-published' && event.val.topic === 'ilium.extensions/changed') reloadSources();
```

#### Owner side: run the `before-recap` hook

`before-recap` is a transform hook. The plugin runs it once per length, with the pane, the kind and the text. `run-hook` returns a request id. When the matching `request-completed` arrives with outcome `ok`, `take-reply` gives the final text, with every handler's change applied in priority order. No reply means nobody changed the text. A handler that fails counts as `pass`, so a broken contributor can never block a recap. See [events](/pages/api-events/) and [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::requests::{Outcome, RequestResult};

const BEFORE_RECAP: &str = "ilium.core.recap/before-recap";

fn start_hook(&mut self, pane: NodeId, kind: &str, text: &str) {
    let payload = serde_json::json!({ "pane": pane.0, "kind": kind, "text": text }).to_string();
    match extensions::run_hook(BEFORE_RECAP, &payload) {
        Ok(request) => { self.hooks.insert(request, (pane, kind.to_string(), text.to_string())); }
        Err(_) => self.finish_text(pane, kind, text.to_string()),
    }
}

fn on_hook_done(&mut self, done: RequestResult) {
    let Some((pane, kind, original)) = self.hooks.remove(&done.request) else { return };
    let text = match done.outcome {
        Outcome::Ok => extensions::take_reply(done.request)
            .and_then(|json| serde_json::from_str::<HookText>(&json).ok())
            .map_or(original, |reply| reply.text),
        _ => original, // the point is a transform: any other outcome keeps the text
    };
    self.finish_text(pane, &kind, text);
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

const BEFORE_RECAP = 'ilium.core.recap/before-recap';

export function startHook(pane: bigint, kind: string, text: string): void {
  try {
    const request = extensions.runHook(BEFORE_RECAP, JSON.stringify({ pane: Number(pane), kind, text }));
    hooks.set(request, { pane, kind, original: text });
  } catch {
    finishText(pane, kind, text);
  }
}

export function onHookDone(request: bigint, outcome: { tag: string }): void {
  const pending = hooks.get(request);
  if (pending === undefined) return;
  hooks.delete(request);
  let text = pending.original;
  if (outcome.tag === 'ok') {
    const reply = extensions.takeReply(request);
    if (reply !== undefined) text = (JSON.parse(reply) as { text: string }).text;
  }
  finishText(pending.pane, pending.kind, text);
}
```

#### Keep only real pointers

A pointer is a path the recap names. The plugin keeps it only when the path appears in the evidence, lies under the pane's project, exists now and is not in a denied area. It counts the rest in `rejected_pointers`. The existence check uses the project file scope. See [fs](/pages/api-fs/), [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/) and [file access](/pages/file-access/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::paths::FsPath;

async fn keep_pointers(evidence: &str, project_relative: Vec<(String, String)>) -> (Vec<(String, String)>, u32) {
    let mut kept = Vec::new();
    let mut rejected = 0;
    for (path, note) in project_relative {
        let named = evidence.contains(&path);
        let allowed = !DENIED_PREFIXES.iter().any(|prefix| path.starts_with(prefix));
        let exists = fs::read(&FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: path.clone() }).await.is_ok();
        if named && allowed && exists { kept.push((path, note)); } else { rejected += 1; }
    }
    (kept, rejected)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';

export async function keepPointers(evidence: string, pointers: { path: string; note: string }[]) {
  const kept: { path: string; note: string }[] = [];
  let rejected = 0;
  for (const pointer of pointers) {
    const named = evidence.includes(pointer.path);
    const allowed = !DENIED_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => pointer.path.startsWith(prefix));
    const exists = await read({ scope: 'project', path: pointer.path }).then(() => true, () => false);
    if (named && allowed && exists) kept.push(pointer); else rejected += 1;
  }
  return { kept, rejected };
}
```


### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.recap` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.recap/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.recap/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fact-sources` | collect | Add facts to a recap, such as the ticket of a branch. | entry: id, title, service (returns facts for a pane) | standard |
| `before-recap` | hook (transform) | Change the recap text before it is shown or returned. | pane, kind (short, long), text; reply: text | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.recap/recap`: get: short or long recap of panes

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.recap"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds the ticket of the pane branch to every long recap

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.recap/fact-sources"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.recap/fact-sources",
        "id": "branch-ticket",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Branch ticket",
          "service": "example.tickets/for-pane"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Session conversion

## Session conversion

Session conversion lets a conversation continue under the other agent. A Claude Code conversation becomes a Codex conversation, or a Codex conversation becomes a Claude Code one, without starting over. The plugin id is `ilium.core.session-convert` and it runs on both sides. The client side adds the context menu entries and draws the progress dialog. The server side checks the pane, freezes it, runs the conversion as a job, and then replaces the frozen pane with a new pane that resumes the converted session.

The original transcript is read and never changed. Antigravity sessions cannot be converted. The conversion engine itself is the Rust crate `ilium-session-convert`, which reports steps, log lines and progress. The plugin turns those reports into the dialog.

### What it covers

- The entries **Convert to Codex** (for a Claude Code pane) and **Convert to Claude Code** (for a Codex pane). An entry appears only when the pane has a verified session, no other conversion is running, and the pane is not a worktree pane.
- The progress dialog with one row per step, a progress bar and a log.
- Claude Code to Codex: locate the transcript, inspect it, start a private `codex app-server`, import the session with Codex's own importer, verify the Codex rollout, stop the app-server.
- Codex to Claude Code: locate the rollout, parse it, convert it to Claude Code lines, write the Claude Code transcript, verify it, register it with Claude Code. User prompts, assistant text, and shell or tool calls with results are carried over. Reasoning and token events are dropped.
- Cancel with Esc, and the recovery choice after a failure: Enter resumes the original session, Esc closes the dialog.

### See it

<figure><img src="/assets/demos/26-convert-session.gif" alt="A Claude Code session converts to Codex, which still remembers the secret word, then converts back to Claude" loading="lazy"><figcaption>A session is converted from Claude to Codex and back while keeping its context.</figcaption></figure>

### What the user sees

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Pane ───────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Rename                                       │
│ Copy screen to pane…                         │
│ <span class="t-hi">Convert to Codex</span>                             │
│ <span class="t-dim">Convert to Claude Code  (Codex pane only)</span>    │
│ Close                                        │

### Samples

#### Menu entries with disabled reasons

The client side answers the dynamic menu with `menu-items`. It reads the agent session of the clicked pane and offers one entry. An entry that cannot run stays visible with a short reason. The click comes back as `command-invoked` with `{"item":"to-codex","node":42}` in `arguments_json`. See [menus](/pages/api-menus/), [the menu provider](/pages/api-menu-provider/) and [agent](/pages/primitives-agent/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::MenuProvider;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::menu_provider::MenuContext;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::MenuEntry;

impl MenuProvider for Convert {
    fn menu_items(&mut self, context: MenuContext) -> Vec<MenuEntry> {
        let Some(pane) = context.pane else { return Vec::new() };
        let Some(signature) = self.signatures.get(&pane) else { return Vec::new() };
        let (id, label) = match signature.as_str() {
            "claude" => ("to-codex", "Convert to Codex"),
            "codex" => ("to-claude", "Convert to Claude Code"),
            _ => return Vec::new(), // Antigravity and custom agents cannot be converted
        };
        let reason = if agent::session(pane).is_none() {
            Some("no verified session")
        } else if self.running.is_some() {
            Some("another conversion runs")
        } else if self.worktree_panes.contains(&pane) {
            Some("worktree pane")
        } else {
            None
        };
        vec![MenuEntry::new(id, label).icon("arrows-exchange").disabled_reason(reason)]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { session } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent';
import type { MenuContext, MenuEntry } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function menuItems(context: MenuContext): MenuEntry[] {
  if (context.pane === undefined) return [];
  const signature = signatures.get(context.pane);
  const choice = signature === 'claude' ? { id: 'to-codex', label: 'Convert to Codex' }
    : signature === 'codex' ? { id: 'to-claude', label: 'Convert to Claude Code' }
    : undefined;
  if (choice === undefined) return []; // Antigravity and custom agents cannot be converted
  const disabledReason = session(context.pane) === undefined ? 'no verified session'
    : running !== undefined ? 'another conversion runs'
    : worktreePanes.has(context.pane) ? 'worktree pane'
    : undefined;
  return [{ ...choice, icon: 'arrows-exchange', disabledReason }];
}
```

#### Freeze the pane and keep a journal

On the chosen entry the client side sends a message to the server side. The server checks that the source transcript exists, freezes the pane, writes the state to `storage` and adds a journal entry, so the plugin knows what it was doing after a crash. A durable timer is the safety net: if nothing finishes in ten minutes, the pane is unfrozen. See [storage](/pages/api-storage/), [durable timers and the journal](/pages/api-durable-timers/) and [pane lifecycle intents](/pages/api-intent-pane-lifecycle/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, journal, storage, timers};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::Bucket;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::FreezePaneSpec;

const WATCHDOG_MILLIS: u64 = 10 * 60 * 1000;

fn begin(&mut self, pane: NodeId, target: &str) -> Result<Vec<Submission>, PluginError> {
    let state = format!(r#"{{"pane":{},"target":"{target}","phase":"frozen"}}"#, pane.0);
    storage::put(Bucket::Session, &format!("convert/{}", pane.0), state.as_bytes())?;
    journal::log_event(Some(pane), "convert-started", &format!(r#"{{"target":"{target}"}}"#))?;
    timers::at(clock::now_unix_millis() + WATCHDOG_MILLIS, &format!("convert-watchdog/{}", pane.0))?;
    Ok(vec![Submission::keyed(Intent::FreezePane(FreezePaneSpec { pane }), format!("freeze-{}", pane.0))])
}

// Event::DurableTimerFired(fired) if fired.name.starts_with("convert-watchdog/"):
//   read storage "convert/<pane>", and when it is still there, submit UnfreezePane and remove the key.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import * as journal from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/journal';
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const WATCHDOG_MILLIS = 10n * 60n * 1000n;

export function begin(pane: bigint, target: string): Submission[] {
  const state = JSON.stringify({ pane: Number(pane), target, phase: 'frozen' });
  storage.put('session', `convert/${pane}`, new TextEncoder().encode(state));
  journal.logEvent(pane, 'convert-started', JSON.stringify({ target }));
  timers.at(nowUnixMillis() + WATCHDOG_MILLIS, `convert-watchdog/${pane}`);
  return [{ intent: { tag: 'freeze-pane', val: { pane } }, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: `freeze-${pane}` }];
}

// case 'durable-timer-fired': when event.val.name starts with 'convert-watchdog/' and the storage key is
// still set, submit an unfreeze-pane intent and remove the key.
```

#### Codex to Claude Code as a job

Parsing a rollout and writing Claude Code lines can take longer than the event deadline, so it runs as a job. The job reads the rollout from the read-only Codex sessions scope, keeps user prompts, assistant text and tool calls with results, and drops reasoning and token events. It reports progress as it goes and stops when cancelled. See [jobs](/pages/api-jobs/), [fs](/pages/api-fs/) and [file access](/pages/file-access/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, jobs};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::paths::FsPath;

fn codex_to_claude(input: &ConvertInput) -> Result<ConvertOutput, PluginError> {
    let rollout = FsPath { scope: "agent-sessions:codex".into(), path: input.rollout.clone() };
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&fs::read(&rollout, 0, 1_048_576)?).to_string(); // offset 0, at most 1 MiB
    let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
    let (mut out, mut kept, mut dropped) = (Vec::new(), 0u32, 0u32);
    for (index, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
        if jobs::is_cancelled() { return Err(PluginError::cancelled()); }
        match claude_line(line) {
            Some(converted) => { out.push(converted); kept += 1; }
            None => dropped += 1, // reasoning and token events
        }
        if index % 50 == 0 { jobs::report_progress(100.0 * index as f32 / lines.len() as f32); }
    }
    Ok(ConvertOutput { claude_jsonl: out.join("\n"), kept, dropped })
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { isCancelled, reportProgress } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';

export function codexToClaude(input: { rollout: string }) {
  const bytes = read({ scope: 'agent-sessions:codex', path: input.rollout }, 0n, 1048576); // offset 0n, at most 1 MiB
  const lines = new TextDecoder().decode(bytes).split('\n');
  const out: string[] = [];
  let dropped = 0;
  lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    if (isCancelled()) throw { code: 'cancelled', message: 'conversion cancelled' };
    const converted = claudeLine(line);
    if (converted === undefined) dropped += 1; // reasoning and token events
    else out.push(converted);
    if (index % 50 === 0) reportProgress((100 * index) / lines.length);
  });
  return { claudeJsonl: out.join('\n'), kept: out.length, dropped };
}
```

#### Write the Claude Code transcript and verify it

The new transcript is written with an atomic write whose expected revision is `none`, so an existing file is never replaced: a clash completes as `failed(conflict)`. After the write, the plugin reads the file back with its revision and checks the line count before it registers the session. See [atomic write and revisions](/pages/api-fs-atomic-and-tail/) and [fs.write](/pages/capability-fs-write/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;

async fn write_and_verify(path: FsPath, jsonl: String, expected_lines: usize) -> Result<String, PluginError> {
    let revision = fs::write_atomic(&path, jsonl.into_bytes(), None).await?; // None: the file must not exist
    let back = fs::read_with_revision(&path).await?;
    if back.revision != revision {
        return Err(PluginError::conflict("transcript changed after the write"));
    }
    let lines = back.bytes.iter().filter(|byte| **byte == b'\n').count() + 1;
    if lines != expected_lines {
        return Err(PluginError::internal("line count differs after the write"));
    }
    Ok(revision)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { readWithRevision, writeAtomic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import type { FsPath } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export async function writeAndVerify(path: FsPath, jsonl: string, expectedLines: number): Promise<string> {
  const revision = await writeAtomic(path, new TextEncoder().encode(jsonl), undefined); // undefined: must not exist
  const back = await readWithRevision(path);
  if (back.revision !== revision) throw { code: 'conflict', message: 'transcript changed after the write' };
  const lines = back.bytes.filter((byte) => byte === 0x0a).length + 1;
  if (lines !== expectedLines) throw { code: 'internal', message: 'line count differs after the write' };
  return revision;
}
```

#### Claude Code to Codex with a private app-server

Claude Code to Codex uses Codex's own importer, so the plugin starts a private `codex app-server` as a long-lived child and talks to it by lines. The child ends when the conversion ends, whatever the result. See [process control](/pages/api-process-control/), [process.run](/pages/capability-process-run/) and [process.long-lived](/pages/capability-process-long-lived/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::process::{self, ProcessSpec, SpawnSpec};

fn start_app_server(&mut self, conversion: u64) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let child = process::spawn(&SpawnSpec {
        process: ProcessSpec {
            program: "codex".into(), arguments: vec!["app-server".into()],
            cwd: None, stdin: None, environment: Vec::new(), timeout_millis: 0,
        },
        stdin_open: true,
        line_mode: true,
    })?;
    self.app_servers.insert(conversion, child);
    Ok(())
}

fn stop_app_server(&mut self, conversion: u64) {
    if let Some(child) = self.app_servers.remove(&conversion) {
        let _ = child.signal("terminate"); // dropping the handle also ends it
    }
}
// Event::ChildOutput(output): one JSON line per message; match it to the import request of the conversion.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { spawn, type Child } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';

const appServers = new Map<bigint, Child>();

export function startAppServer(conversion: bigint): void {
  const child = spawn({
    process: { program: 'codex', arguments: ['app-server'], cwd: undefined, stdin: undefined,
               environment: [], timeoutMillis: 0 },
    stdinOpen: true,
    lineMode: true,
  });
  appServers.set(conversion, child);
}

export function stopAppServer(conversion: bigint): void {
  appServers.get(conversion)?.signal('terminate'); // dropping the handle also ends it
  appServers.delete(conversion);
}
// case 'child-output': one JSON line per message; match it to the import request of the conversion.
```

#### The progress dialog

The server sends steps, log lines and progress to the client side as messages. The client side keeps them and draws a `dialog` with a step list and a `progress-row`. Esc is the cancel button. After a failure that came after the agent was stopped, the primary button resumes the original session. See [layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/), [data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/) and [ui](/pages/api-ui/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{DialogKind, ProgressState};

fn render_dialog(&self, tree: &mut Tree) -> NodeHandle {
    let steps: Vec<NodeHandle> = self.steps.iter().map(|step| {
        tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain(format!("{} {}", step.mark(), step.title))]])
    }).collect();
    let progress = tree
        .progress_row(&self.title)
        .state(if self.failed { ProgressState::Error } else { ProgressState::Running })
        .percent(self.percent)
        .message(&self.last_log)
        .key("progress");
    let body = tree.layout(Direction::Vertical)
        .constraints(vec![Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(1)])
        .child(tree.layout(Direction::Vertical).constraints(vec![Constraint::Length(1); steps.len()]).children(steps))
        .child(progress);
    tree.dialog("convert-progress", &self.title)
        .kind(DialogKind::Plain)
        .width(Constraint::Length(48))
        .height(Constraint::Length(14))
        .child(body)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { dialog, layout, length, fill, paragraph, progressRow, span } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export function renderDialog(state: ConvertState) {
  const steps = state.steps.map((step) => paragraph([[span(`${step.mark} ${step.title}`)]]));
  const progress = progressRow(state.title, {
    key: 'progress',
    state: state.failed ? 'error' : 'running',
    percent: state.percent,
    message: state.lastLog,
  });
  const body = layout({ direction: 'vertical', constraints: [fill(1), length(1)] }, [
    layout({ direction: 'vertical', constraints: steps.map(() => length(1)) }, steps),
    progress,
  ]);
  return dialog('convert-progress', {
    title: state.title, kind: 'plain', width: length(48), height: length(14),
    buttons: state.failed
      ? [{ id: 'resume', label: 'Resume original', role: 'primary', isCancel: false },
         { id: 'close', label: 'Close', role: 'secondary', isCancel: true }]
      : [{ id: 'cancel', label: 'Cancel', role: 'secondary', isCancel: true }],
  }, [body]);
}
```

#### Replace the frozen pane

On success the server creates a new pane that resumes the converted session in the other agent and closes the frozen one. On a failure after the agent was stopped, the user's choice decides: **Resume original** replaces the pane command with the original resume command and keeps the scrollback. See [pane lifecycle intents](/pages/api-intent-pane-lifecycle/), [intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [panes.create](/pages/capability-panes-create/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{CreatePaneSpec, ReplacePaneCommandSpec};

fn finish_ok(pane: NodeId, target: &str, new_session: &str, cwd: FsPath) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let command = match target {
        "codex" => vec!["codex".to_string(), "resume".into(), new_session.into()],
        _ => vec!["claude".to_string(), "--resume".into(), new_session.into()],
    };
    vec![
        Submission::new(Intent::CreatePane(CreatePaneSpec {
            parent: None, title: format!("{target} (converted)"), content_kind: "ilium.terminal".into(),
            cwd: Some(cwd), command: Some(command), initial_input: None,
        })),
        Submission::new(Intent::CloseNode(pane)),
    ]
}

fn resume_original(pane: NodeId, original: Vec<String>) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::ReplacePaneCommand(ReplacePaneCommandSpec {
        pane, command: original, cwd: None, keep_scrollback: true,
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { FsPath, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function finishOk(pane: bigint, target: string, newSession: string, cwd: FsPath): Submission[] {
  const command = target === 'codex' ? ['codex', 'resume', newSession] : ['claude', '--resume', newSession];
  return [
    { intent: { tag: 'create-pane', val: { parent: undefined, title: `${target} (converted)`,
        contentKind: 'ilium.terminal', cwd, command, initialInput: undefined } },
      correlation: 1n, dedupKey: undefined },
    { intent: { tag: 'close-node', val: pane }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined },
  ];
}

export const resumeOriginal = (pane: bigint, original: string[]): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'replace-pane-command', val: { pane, command: original, cwd: undefined, keepScrollback: true } },
  correlation: 3n, dedupKey: undefined,
});
```

#### Owner side: formats and `after-convert`

`formats` is a collect point. A contributor adds a transcript format with a direction and a service that reads or writes it. The plugin lists the entries to build its source and target choices, and lists again when the kernel publishes `ilium.extensions/changed`. `after-convert` is an observe hook: the plugin runs it once when a conversion finishes and ignores the replies. See [events](/pages/api-events/), [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;

fn formats(&self) -> Vec<Format> {
    extensions::list("ilium.core.session-convert/formats")
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| serde_json::from_str::<Format>(&entry.entry_json).ok())
        .collect() // each Format has id, title, direction and service
}

fn announce(&mut self, from: &str, to: &str, messages: u32, path: &str) {
    let payload = serde_json::json!({ "from": from, "to": to, "messages": messages, "path": path });
    if let Ok(request) = extensions::run_hook("ilium.core.session-convert/after-convert", &payload.to_string()) {
        self.observers.insert(request);
    }
}

// Event::RequestCompleted(done) if self.observers.remove(&done.request): log the outcome, nothing else.
// Event::TopicPublished(t) if t.topic == "ilium.extensions/changed": call self.formats() again.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

export const formats = () =>
  extensions.list('ilium.core.session-convert/formats')
    .map((entry) => JSON.parse(entry.entryJson) as { id: string; title: string; direction: string; service: string });

export function announce(from: string, to: string, messages: number, path: string): void {
  const request = extensions.runHook('ilium.core.session-convert/after-convert',
    JSON.stringify({ from, to, messages, path }));
  observers.add(request);
}

// case 'request-completed': if (observers.delete(event.val.request)) log the outcome, nothing else.
// case 'topic-published': if (event.val.topic === 'ilium.extensions/changed') formats() again.
```


### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.session-convert` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.session-convert/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.session-convert/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `formats` | collect | Add a transcript format that conversion can read or write. | entry: id, title, direction (read, write, both), service | standard |
| `after-convert` | hook (observe) | Learn that a conversion finished. | from, to, messages, path | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.session-convert/convert`: start: convert a transcript between two formats

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.session-convert"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds a third transcript format

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.session-convert/formats"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.session-convert/formats",
        "id": "gemini",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Gemini CLI",
          "direction": "both",
          "service": "example.gemini/convert"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Agent setup

## Agent setup

Agents work better in Ilium when their instruction files describe what Ilium offers. Agent setup installs two blocks of instructions into the files an agent reads at start. The Chatroom block tells agents how to talk to each other. The Progress block tells them how to report long jobs. The plugin id is `ilium.core.agent-setup`. The client side draws the Setup tab and asks before it changes a file. The server side reads and writes the files, because only the server holds the file grants.

Each block sits between two marker lines, so Ilium can find it, upgrade it and leave everything else alone.

### What it covers

- The two blocks, Chatroom and Progress, and the files they go into: the global Claude file `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (the path can be changed), the global Codex file `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, and for each open project a `CLAUDE.md` and an `AGENTS.md`.
- Markers: `<!-- ilium-agent-feature: chatroom -->` before the block and `<!-- /ilium-agent-feature: chatroom -->` after it. The Progress marker adds a version, as in `<!-- ilium-agent-feature: progress version=13 -->`, so an older block is upgraded and a newer block is left alone.
- Safety rules: text outside the markers is kept, a file over 512 KiB is not changed, a symbolic link stays a symbolic link, and look-alike text without markers is reported as "Instruction detected" and not touched.
- Timing: global blocks are installed and refreshed when a client attaches and when a project opens. Project copies are never added automatically. They come only from the Setup tab.
- The five statuses: Set up by Ilium, Ilium update required, Newer Ilium instructions detected, Instruction detected, Not set up.
- Chatroom setup also creates `CHATROOM.md` and the hooks that deliver messages.

### See it

There is no recording of this feature yet. The renders below are illustrative.

### Setup tab: statuses, rows and files

The Setup tab belongs to this plugin, and the Chatroom and Progress pages link here instead of describing it again. [COR-011]

| Status badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Set up by Ilium | The current managed block is present. |
| Ilium update required | An older managed block is present. It is refreshed automatically. |
| Newer Ilium instructions detected | The file was written by a newer Ilium. It is left untouched. |
| Instruction detected | Matching text that Ilium did not write. |
| Not set up | No block yet. |

Each feature has a **Global file** row (`Enter` changes the path, `R` restores `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`), a **Global** row per global file and a **Project** row for every open project. `Enter` on a target refreshes it. Setup is not an on/off switch, because removing a mandatory block would leave new agents uninformed. The paths are stored in `[agent_setup]` as `chatroom_global_file` and `progress_global_file`.

| Scope | Files edited |
|---|---|
| Global (Claude) | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or the custom path of that feature |
| Global (Codex) | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` |
| Each open project | `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the project root, only from the Setup tab |

Blocks sit between the markers `<!-- ilium-agent-feature: chatroom -->` and `<!-- /ilium-agent-feature: chatroom -->`. Only text between the markers is replaced or removed. The `ilium chat init` command installs the chatroom hooks; the Setup tab installs the instruction blocks. The two are separate actions with this plugin as the single owner of the files. [COR-011]

### Kernel tabs this plugin owns

This plugin is the single owner of the following built-in Settings tabs. It holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for each one (T1 only, one holder per tab, see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)). The values stay in the same `config.toml` tables as before, so no user setting moves. [COR-030] [COR-033]

| Tab id | Label | Config table | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setup` | Setup | `[agent_setup]` | none |

If the plugin is disabled, the tab stays in the rail with its stored values shown read-only and the notice "Agent setup is disabled. Values are kept." The kernel keeps reading the keys it consumes itself (listed in the Consumer column of the key table in [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/)). Behaviour that only this plugin provides is off. The exact result for this plugin is its row in [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/). [COR-022]

### Samples

#### Replace one marked block in place

The core of the plugin is one pure function and one safe write. The function finds the markers, replaces what lies between them, and returns the new text. If there are no markers it appends the block at the end. The write uses the revision that came with the read, so a change made by someone else in between ends as `failed(conflict)` and nothing is lost. See [atomic write and revisions](/pages/api-fs-atomic-and-tail/) and [fs.write](/pages/capability-fs-write/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::paths::FsPath;

const MAX_BYTES: usize = 512 * 1024;

fn with_block(text: &str, marker: &str, block: &str) -> String {
    let open = format!("<!-- ilium-agent-feature: {marker}");
    let close = format!("<!-- /ilium-agent-feature: {marker} -->");
    match (text.find(&open), text.find(&close)) {
        (Some(start), Some(end)) if start < end => {
            let end = end + close.len();
            format!("{}{}{}", &text[..start], block, &text[end..])
        }
        _ => format!("{}{}\n{}\n", text, if text.ends_with('\n') || text.is_empty() { "" } else { "\n" }, block),
    }
}

async fn install(path: FsPath, marker: &str, block: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let current = fs::read_with_revision(&path).await?;
    if current.bytes.len() > MAX_BYTES {
        return Err(PluginError::invalid_argument("file is over 512 KiB"));
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&current.bytes);
    let next = with_block(&text, marker, block);
    fs::write_atomic(&path, next.into_bytes(), Some(current.revision)).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { readWithRevision, writeAtomic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import type { FsPath } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const MAX_BYTES = 512 * 1024;

export function withBlock(text: string, marker: string, block: string): string {
  const open = `<!-- ilium-agent-feature: ${marker}`;
  const close = `<!-- /ilium-agent-feature: ${marker} -->`;
  const start = text.indexOf(open);
  const end = text.indexOf(close);
  if (start !== -1 && end > start) return text.slice(0, start) + block + text.slice(end + close.length);
  const gap = text === '' || text.endsWith('\n') ? '' : '\n';
  return `${text}${gap}\n${block}\n`;
}

export async function install(path: FsPath, marker: string, block: string): Promise<void> {
  const current = await readWithRevision(path);
  if (current.bytes.length > MAX_BYTES) throw { code: 'invalid-argument', message: 'file is over 512 KiB' };
  const next = withBlock(new TextDecoder().decode(current.bytes), marker, block);
  await writeAtomic(path, new TextEncoder().encode(next), current.revision);
}
```

#### Read the status of a target

A target has one of five statuses. The plugin reads the file and compares what it finds with the block it would write. A block with markers and the same version is "Set up by Ilium". An older version is "Ilium update required". A newer version is "Newer Ilium instructions detected". Text that looks like the block but has no markers is "Instruction detected". Nothing at all is "Not set up". See [fs](/pages/api-fs/) and [file access](/pages/file-access/).

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Status { SetUp, UpdateRequired, Newer, Detected, NotSetUp }

fn status_of(text: &str, marker: &str, current_version: u32) -> Status {
    let open = format!("<!-- ilium-agent-feature: {marker}");
    if let Some(start) = text.find(&open) {
        let line = text[start..].lines().next().unwrap_or("");
        let version = line.split("version=").nth(1)
            .and_then(|rest| rest.trim_end_matches("-->").trim().parse::<u32>().ok())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        return match version.cmp(&current_version) {
            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => Status::UpdateRequired,
            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => Status::Newer,
            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => Status::SetUp,
        };
    }
    if text.contains(LOOK_ALIKE_PHRASE) { Status::Detected } else { Status::NotSetUp }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export type Status = 'set-up' | 'update-required' | 'newer' | 'detected' | 'not-set-up';

export function statusOf(text: string, marker: string, currentVersion: number): Status {
  const open = `<!-- ilium-agent-feature: ${marker}`;
  const start = text.indexOf(open);
  if (start !== -1) {
    const line = text.slice(start).split('\n', 1)[0];
    const version = Number(/version=(\d+)/.exec(line)?.[1] ?? 0);
    if (version < currentVersion) return 'update-required';
    return version > currentVersion ? 'newer' : 'set-up';
  }
  return text.includes(LOOK_ALIKE_PHRASE) ? 'detected' : 'not-set-up';
}
```

#### The Setup tab as a check list

The tab is a `check-list` with one row per target. The status is the row's trailing text. The row key carries the block and the target, so the action can say what to refresh. Enter on a row sends a refresh request. See [collections](/pages/widgets-collections/) and [ui](/pages/api-ui/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::CheckItem;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Tone;

fn render_setup(&self, tree: &mut Tree) -> NodeHandle {
    let items: Vec<CheckItem> = self.targets.iter().map(|target| {
        CheckItem::new(format!("{}|{}", target.block, target.id), format!("{}  {}", target.block, target.title))
            .checked(target.status == Status::SetUp)
            .trailing(target.status.label())
            .tone(match target.status {
                Status::SetUp => Tone::Success,
                Status::NotSetUp => Tone::Neutral,
                _ => Tone::Warning,
            })
    }).collect();
    tree.check_list(items).key("targets").all_toggle(false)
}

// Event::UiAction(action) if action.key == "targets" && action.kind == ActionKind::Activated:
//   split the row id at '|' and call the install service for that block and target.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { checkList } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export function renderSetup(targets: Target[]) {
  return checkList(
    targets.map((target) => ({
      id: `${target.block}|${target.id}`,
      label: `${target.block}  ${target.title}`,
      checked: target.status === 'set-up',
      trailing: statusLabel(target.status),
      tone: target.status === 'set-up' ? 'success' : target.status === 'not-set-up' ? 'muted' : 'warning',
    })),
    { key: 'targets', allToggle: false },
  );
}

// case 'ui-action': when event.val.key === 'targets' and kind is 'activated',
// split the row id at '|' and call the install service for that block and target.
```

#### Choose the global file

Row "Global file" lets the user change the path. A `path-field` of kind `save-file` shows it. The value is saved after 600 ms, the usual rule for text inputs. A picked path outside the config scopes needs the pick grant, so the field uses the picker. R restores the default. See [pickers](/pages/widgets-pickers/) and [fs.pick](/pages/capability-fs-pick/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::{self, Bucket};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::PathKind;

const DEFAULT_GLOBAL: &str = "~/.claude/CLAUDE.md";

fn render_global_file(&self, tree: &mut Tree) -> NodeHandle {
    tree.path_field(PathKind::SaveFile).key("global-file").value(&self.global_file)
}

fn on_path_changed(&mut self, value: String) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    self.global_file = value.clone();
    storage::put(Bucket::Global, "global-file", value.as_bytes())?;
    Ok(())
}

fn restore_default(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    storage::remove(Bucket::Global, "global-file")?;
    self.global_file = DEFAULT_GLOBAL.to_string();
    Ok(())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';
import { pathField } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const DEFAULT_GLOBAL = '~/.claude/CLAUDE.md';

export const renderGlobalFile = (value: string) => pathField('save-file', { key: 'global-file', value });

export function onPathChanged(value: string): void {
  state.globalFile = value;
  storage.put('global', 'global-file', new TextEncoder().encode(value));
}

export function restoreDefault(): void {
  storage.remove('global', 'global-file');
  state.globalFile = DEFAULT_GLOBAL;
}
```

#### Refresh on attach with a durable timer

Global blocks are refreshed when a client attaches. A client may attach many times in a minute, so the plugin keeps one durable timer named `refresh`. A new attach moves the timer to two seconds from now. The timer survives a server restart. When it fires, the plugin runs one refresh pass, and a late timer still runs. See [durable timers](/pages/api-durable-timers/) and [clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, timers};

fn on_attach(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    timers::cancel_durable("refresh")?;
    timers::at(clock::now_unix_millis() + 2_000, "refresh")?;
    Ok(())
}

// Event::DurableTimerFired(fired) if fired.name == "refresh":
//   self.refresh_global_blocks();  // fired.late_by_millis may be large after a restart
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';

export function onAttach(): void {
  timers.cancelDurable('refresh');
  timers.at(nowUnixMillis() + 2_000n, 'refresh');
}

// case 'durable-timer-fired': when event.val.name === 'refresh',
// run refreshGlobalBlocks(). event.val.lateByMillis may be large after a restart.
```

#### Owner side: the veto hook before an install

`before-install` is a veto hook with high risk. The plugin runs it before every write with the target, the block and the path. A handler may refuse, for example a policy plugin that forbids edits to a shared team file. A refusal completes the request as `refused` with the code `extension.vetoed`. The plugin then shows the reason and writes nothing. See [events](/pages/api-events/) and [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::requests::{Outcome, RequestResult};

fn ask_before_install(&mut self, target: &str, block: &str, path: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let payload = serde_json::json!({ "target": target, "block": block, "path": path }).to_string();
    let request = extensions::run_hook("ilium.core.agent-setup/before-install", &payload)?;
    self.pending.insert(request, (target.to_string(), block.to_string()));
    Ok(())
}

fn on_hook_done(&mut self, done: RequestResult) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let Some((target, block)) = self.pending.remove(&done.request) else { return Vec::new() };
    match done.outcome {
        Outcome::Ok => self.write_block(&target, &block),
        Outcome::Refused(refusal) if refusal.code == "extension.vetoed" => {
            self.show_notice(format!("Install stopped: {}", refusal.message)); // no write happens
            Vec::new()
        }
        _ => {
            self.show_notice("Install stopped: the check did not finish".into());
            Vec::new()
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

export function askBeforeInstall(target: string, block: string, path: string): void {
  const request = extensions.runHook('ilium.core.agent-setup/before-install',
    JSON.stringify({ target, block, path }));
  pending.set(request, { target, block });
}

export function onHookDone(request: bigint, outcome: { tag: string; val?: { code: string; message: string } }) {
  const item = pending.get(request);
  if (item === undefined) return [];
  pending.delete(request);
  if (outcome.tag === 'ok') return writeBlock(item.target, item.block);
  if (outcome.tag === 'refused' && outcome.val?.code === 'extension.vetoed') {
    showNotice(`Install stopped: ${outcome.val.message}`); // no write happens
    return [];
  }
  showNotice('Install stopped: the check did not finish');
  return [];
}
```

#### Owner side: blocks and targets from other plugins

`instruction-blocks` and `targets` are collect points. A block entry names a marker and a file under `help/` that holds the text, so another plugin can add a third block, for example `review-rules`. A target entry names a path template, such as `{project}/GEMINI.md`, and a scope. The plugin lists both, builds its rows from them, and lists again when the kernel publishes `ilium.extensions/changed`. See [events](/pages/api-events/) and [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;

#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct BlockEntry { id: String, title: String, marker: String, file: String }
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct TargetEntry { id: String, title: String, path_template: String, scope: String }

fn reload(&mut self) {
    self.blocks = collect::<BlockEntry>("ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks");
    self.targets = collect::<TargetEntry>("ilium.core.agent-setup/targets");
}

fn collect<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(point: &str) -> Vec<T> {
    extensions::list(point)
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| serde_json::from_str(&entry.entry_json).ok())
        .collect()
}

// Event::TopicPublished(t) if t.topic == "ilium.extensions/changed": self.reload()
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

function collect<T>(point: string): T[] {
  try {
    return extensions.list(point).map((entry) => JSON.parse(entry.entryJson) as T);
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

export function reload(): void {
  blocks = collect<{ id: string; title: string; marker: string; file: string }>(
    'ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks');
  targets = collect<{ id: string; title: string; pathTemplate: string; scope: string }>(
    'ilium.core.agent-setup/targets');
}

// case 'topic-published': when event.val.topic === 'ilium.extensions/changed', call reload().
```


### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.agent-setup` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.agent-setup/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-setup/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instruction-blocks` | collect | Add a marker-delimited instruction block that Setup installs. | entry: id, title, marker, file (text under the plugin's `help/` folder) | standard |
| `targets` | collect | Add a file that Setup can edit, such as a new agent config file. | entry: id, title, path_template, scope (global, project) | standard |
| `before-install` | hook (veto) | Refuse writing a block to a file. | target, block, path | high |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.agent-setup/install`: install, remove, status: manage blocks

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.agent-setup"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Installs a block of review rules next to the Chatroom and Progress blocks

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks",
        "id": "review-rules",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "Review rules",
          "marker": "review-rules",
          "file": "help/review-rules.md"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# Diagnostics

## Diagnostics

Diagnostics helps when something goes wrong. It builds a report of facts about the install, it watches the warnings and errors that plugins write, and it helps the user attach the right log file to an issue. The plugin id is `ilium.core.diagnostics` and it runs on both sides. The server side reads the log file and builds the report. The client side shows the report and the warning list.

The Debug and About tabs, and the file logging switch, belong to the Settings plugin. Diagnostics does not draw them again. It reads the Debug setting without writing it, and it adds the report to the Debug tab through the Settings plugin's own extension, as an ordinary contribution.

### What it covers

- The log file: one file for each server lifetime, named `log-<local date and time>.txt`, under `/tmp/.ilium-<uid>/logs/<session-id>/` on Linux and macOS and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ilium\logs` on Windows. `ILIUM_DEBUG_LOG_DIR` replaces the root. The five newest logs of a session are kept and older ones are removed when the server starts.
- File logging is off by default. It records actions, errors and complete model text exchanges. Credential headers and URL parameters are redacted, but other text is not. Treat a log as sensitive.
- Log levels: trace, debug, info, warn, error. A plugin writes its own diary at these levels with the host log. The user reads it with `ilium plugin logs <id>`.
- The `ilium-logging` service of the server, which opens the file, applies the switch live to client and server, flushes on request and shuts down in order.
- The report: a text block of facts, one section for each contributor, at most 64 KiB for each section.
- Attaching a log to an issue: choose a file, see what the report holds, and read a warning about private content before anything leaves the machine.

### See it

There is no recording of this feature yet. The renders below are illustrative.

### Manifest

A literal absolute path is high risk and needs an explicit user grant. The example uses user id 1000, and the real grant is written at install from the user id.

```json
            "service": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          }
        },
        "max_entries": 32,
        "dynamic": false,
        "version": "0.1.0"
      }
    ]
  },
  "limits_tier": "first-party"
}
```

### Samples

#### Read the Debug setting without writing it

The file logging switch is a kernel setting, and the Settings plugin owns the screen. Diagnostics only needs to know the state, so it reads the `debug` tab with the read-only grant and listens for `kernel-settings-changed`. No plugin writes kernel settings. See [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/) and [settings.read-kernel](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::kernel_settings;

fn file_logging_on() -> bool {
    kernel_settings::read("debug")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|json| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&json).ok())
        .and_then(|value| value["file_logging_enabled"].as_bool())
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

// Event::KernelSettingsChanged(change) if change.tab == "debug" && change.keys.iter().any(|k| k == "file_logging_enabled"):
//   self.logging_on = file_logging_on();
//   self.tail_cursor = None; // a new server lifetime has a new file
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';

export function fileLoggingOn(): boolean {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(read('debug')).file_logging_enabled === true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

// case 'kernel-settings-changed': when event.val.tab === 'debug' and keys include 'file_logging_enabled':
//   state.loggingOn = fileLoggingOn(); state.tailCursor = undefined;
```

#### Tail the log file

The log can grow large, so the plugin never reads it whole. It keeps a cursor and asks for a chunk. A chunk holds the bytes, a new cursor and a flag that says the start was cut. The newest warning lines go to the warnings panel, and the size goes to the Debug tab. See [tail](/pages/api-fs-atomic-and-tail/) and [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::paths::FsPath;

async fn poll_log(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let path = FsPath { scope: "path:/tmp/.ilium-1000/logs".into(), path: name.into() };
    let chunk = fs::tail(&path, self.tail_cursor, 64 * 1024).await?;
    self.tail_cursor = Some(chunk.cursor);
    for line in String::from_utf8_lossy(&chunk.bytes).lines() {
        if line.contains(" WARN ") || line.contains(" ERROR ") {
            self.warnings.push_back(line.to_string());
            if self.warnings.len() > 200 { self.warnings.pop_front(); }
        }
    }
    if chunk.truncated { self.warnings.push_back("(earlier lines were skipped)".into()); }
    Ok(())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { tail } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';

export async function pollLog(name: string): Promise<void> {
  const chunk = await tail({ scope: 'path:/tmp/.ilium-1000/logs', path: name }, state.tailCursor, 64 * 1024);
  state.tailCursor = chunk.cursor;
  for (const line of new TextDecoder().decode(chunk.bytes).split('\n')) {
    if (line.includes(' WARN ') || line.includes(' ERROR ')) {
      state.warnings.push(line);
      if (state.warnings.length > 200) state.warnings.shift();
    }
  }
  if (chunk.truncated) state.warnings.push('(earlier lines were skipped)');
}
```

#### Write the plugin's own diary

Every plugin has a diary that the host keeps for it. It is separate from the Ilium log file. The plugin writes lines at five levels with the host log, at most 200 lines for each second. The user reads them with `ilium plugin logs ilium.core.diagnostics`. No import reads the diary back, so the plugin keeps what it needs itself. See [log](/pages/api-log/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};

fn note_report(&self, sections: usize, bytes: usize, slow: &[String]) {
    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("report built, {sections} sections"));
    for name in slow {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("section {name}: no reply in 2000 ms"));
    }
    if bytes > 200 * 1024 {
        log::log(Level::Debug, &format!("report is {} KiB", bytes / 1024));
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export function noteReport(sections: number, bytes: number, slow: string[]): void {
  log('info', `report built, ${sections} sections`);
  for (const name of slow) log('warn', `section ${name}: no reply in 2000 ms`);
  if (bytes > 200 * 1024) log('debug', `report is ${Math.floor(bytes / 1024)} KiB`);
}
```

#### Keep a journal of warnings

Warnings that matter to a pane go to the journal, so the story of that pane has them. The journal is durable and each entry has a kind and a JSON payload. The report reads the newest entries back. Reading entries that other plugins wrote needs the `journal.read` grant. See [durable timers and the journal](/pages/api-durable-timers/) and [journal.read](/pages/capability-journal-read/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::journal;

fn remember(&self, pane: Option<NodeId>, line: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let payload = serde_json::json!({ "line": line }).to_string();
    journal::log_event(pane, "diagnostics.warning", &payload)
}

fn recent_for_report(&self, pane: NodeId) -> Vec<String> {
    journal::read(pane, 0, 20)
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|entry| entry.kind == "diagnostics.warning")
        .map(|entry| entry.payload_json)
        .collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as journal from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/journal';

export const remember = (pane: bigint | undefined, line: string): void =>
  journal.logEvent(pane, 'diagnostics.warning', JSON.stringify({ line }));

export const recentForReport = (pane: bigint): string[] =>
  journal.read(pane, 0n, 20)
    .filter((entry) => entry.kind === 'diagnostics.warning')
    .map((entry) => entry.payloadJson);
```

#### Build the report in a service

The service `report/build` returns the text. It starts with its own facts, then asks each contributed section for text. A section that is slow or fails is named and skipped, so one bad contributor cannot stop the report. The result is cut at 256 KiB. The call is deferred, so the plugin answers when the sections are in. See [services](/pages/api-services/) and [client requests](/pages/api-client-requests/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{extensions, services};

async fn build_report(&mut self) -> String {
    let mut text = self.core_facts();
    for entry in extensions::list("ilium.core.diagnostics/report-sections").unwrap_or_default() {
        let Ok(section) = serde_json::from_str::<Section>(&entry.entry_json) else { continue };
        match services::call(&section.service, "text", "{}").await {
            Ok(reply) => {
                let body: String = reply.chars().take(64 * 1024).collect();
                text.push_str(&format!("\n## {} (from {})\n{}\n", section.title, entry.contributor, body));
            }
            Err(error) => {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("section {}: {}", section.id, error.code));
                text.push_str(&format!("\n## {}\n(not available)\n", section.title));
            }
        }
    }
    text.chars().take(256 * 1024).collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';
import { call } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export async function buildReport(): Promise<string> {
  let text = coreFacts();
  for (const entry of extensions.list('ilium.core.diagnostics/report-sections')) {
    const section = JSON.parse(entry.entryJson) as { id: string; title: string; service: string };
    try {
      const reply = await call(section.service, 'text', '{}');
      text += `\n## ${section.title} (from ${entry.contributor})\n${reply.slice(0, 64 * 1024)}\n`;
    } catch (error) {
      log('warn', `section ${section.id}: ${(error as { code: string }).code}`);
      text += `\n## ${section.title}\n(not available)\n`;
    }
  }
  return text.slice(0, 256 * 1024);
}
```

#### Owner side: run the `log-sinks` hook

`log-sinks` is an observe hook. Warnings and errors that the plugin finds in the log are sent to it, one payload for each line. Handlers may forward them to a chat tool or a metrics tool. Replies are ignored, and a handler that fails does not matter. The plugin lists the current contributors only to show the count in the panel, and it lists again on `ilium.extensions/changed`. See [events](/pages/api-events/) and [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::requests::{Outcome, RequestResult};

fn publish_line(&mut self, level: &str, plugin: &str, message: &str, time: &str) {
    if self.sink_count == 0 { return; } // nobody listens
    let payload = serde_json::json!({
        "level": level, "plugin": plugin, "target": "plugin", "message": message, "time": time,
    });
    if let Ok(request) = extensions::run_hook("ilium.core.diagnostics/log-sinks", &payload.to_string()) {
        self.observed.insert(request);
    }
}

fn on_completed(&mut self, done: RequestResult) {
    self.observed.remove(&done.request); // an observe hook has no reply to take
}

// Event::TopicPublished(t) if t.topic == "ilium.extensions/changed":
//   self.sink_count = extensions::list("ilium.core.diagnostics/log-sinks").map_or(0, |list| list.len());
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as extensions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

export function publishLine(level: string, plugin: string, message: string, time: string): void {
  if (state.sinkCount === 0) return; // nobody listens
  const request = extensions.runHook('ilium.core.diagnostics/log-sinks',
    JSON.stringify({ level, plugin, target: 'plugin', message, time }));
  state.observed.add(request);
}

export const onCompleted = (request: bigint): void => {
  state.observed.delete(request); // an observe hook has no reply to take
};

// case 'topic-published': when event.val.topic === 'ilium.extensions/changed',
// state.sinkCount = extensions.list('ilium.core.diagnostics/log-sinks').length.
```

#### Attach a log to an issue

The user picks a file to attach. A dialog warns that logs hold private text and shows the size. Only after the user confirms does the plugin copy the log to the place the user chose. The default button is Cancel. The copy is a plain read and write, so it keeps the original. See [dialogs](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/), [pickers](/pages/widgets-pickers/) and [fs.pick](/pages/capability-fs-pick/).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::DialogKind;

fn render_attach(&self, tree: &mut Tree) -> NodeHandle {
    let message = format!(
        "{} ({} KiB) can hold prompts, replies and file text. Remove private text before you share it.",
        self.picked_name, self.picked_kib
    );
    tree.dialog("attach-log", "Attach a log to an issue")
        .kind(DialogKind::DangerConfirm)
        .message(&message)
        .width(Constraint::Length(56))
        .height(Constraint::Length(10))
        .child(tree.path_field(PathKind::SaveFile).key("destination").value(&self.destination))
}

// Event::UiAction(action) if action.key == "attach-log" && action.kind == ActionKind::Activated
//   and the button id is "confirm": copy the file, then submit a Toast intent that names the destination.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { dialog, length, pathField } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const renderAttach = (state: AttachState) =>
  dialog('attach-log', {
    title: 'Attach a log to an issue',
    kind: 'danger-confirm',
    message: `${state.pickedName} (${state.pickedKib} KiB) can hold prompts, replies and file text. ` +
      'Remove private text before you share it.',
    width: length(56),
    height: length(10),
    buttons: [
      { id: 'confirm', label: 'Copy log', role: 'primary', isCancel: false },
      { id: 'cancel', label: 'Cancel', role: 'secondary', isCancel: true },
    ],
  }, [pathField('save-file', { key: 'destination', value: state.destination })]);

// case 'ui-action': when key is 'attach-log', kind is 'activated' and the button is 'confirm':
// copy the file, then submit a toast intent that names the destination.
```


### Extension points

Other plugins change what `ilium.core.diagnostics` does through the points below. The plugin owns each point (grant `extensions.provide:ilium.core.diagnostics/<point>`). Contributors need `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.diagnostics/<point>`. See [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) for the mechanism and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the five ways to work with a core feature.

| Point | Kind | What it does | Payload | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log-sinks` | hook (observe) | Receive log records, for example to forward them. | level, plugin, target, message, time (records at warn and above only) | standard |
| `report-sections` | collect | Add a section to the diagnostics report. | entry: id, title, service (returns text, at most 64 KiB) | standard |

**Services** (grant `services.use:<name>`):

- `ilium.core.diagnostics/report`: build: build the diagnostics report

**Replaceable:** yes. A replacement lists `"replaces": ["ilium.core.diagnostics"]` and provides the whole surface (see [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace)).

#### Example: Adds GPU facts to the report

A package adds this entry in its manifest. It needs no code.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.diagnostics/report-sections"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "ilium.core.diagnostics/report-sections",
        "id": "gpu",
        "priority": 50,
        "entry": {
          "title": "GPU",
          "service": "example.gpu/report"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

# 1. Agent badge

## 1. Agent badge

This step turns the template from the first plugin page into a real server plugin. It puts a badge on every agent row of the project tree: `working`, `idle` or `approve?`. The kernel sends the plugin batches of events. The plugin answers with submissions, and the kernel applies them. That event-in, intent-out loop is the core of every server plugin.

Tutorial plugin: `example.agent-tools`. Languages: Rust (target `wasm32-wasip2`) and TypeScript. Every code listing in this step is given twice, a **Rust** block and a **TypeScript** block, and both build the same component behaviour. Each later step is in the same project and builds on the code of this step.

### You need

- [Your first plugin in five minutes](/pages/getting-started-first-plugin/), which creates the project, `manifest.json` and `src/lib.rs`.
- The toolchain from [Toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/): Rust stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target. For the TypeScript version, Bun 1.2 or later (see also [TypeScript plugins](/pages/tutorial-08-typescript/)).
- Server grants: `agent.read` to receive `agent-activity-changed` events, and `tree.decorate` to set and clear decorations. Both are listed in the manifest in [The manifest](#the-manifest).
- At least one agent CLI, Claude Code or Codex, running in a pane of the project. Without an agent pane the plugin receives no activity events and draws nothing.

### What the step builds

The plugin listens for `agent-activity-changed` events. For each event it submits one intent:

- `set-decoration` when the new activity has a badge.
- `clear-decoration` when the new activity has no badge.

The decoration goes into the `badge` slot that the manifest declares. The kernel draws the slot on the tree row. The plugin never draws anything itself.
