### Surface used by this step

| Call or event | Side | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fs::scan(&path, glob, max_entries)` | server | async, `request-id` | Lists files that match a glob such as `**/*.rs`. `max_entries` is at most 65,536 (L3). |
| `fs::take_entries(request)` | server | sync, `Option` | The matched paths and entries, once. |
| `fs::read(&path, offset, max_bytes)` | server, job | sync, `Result` | Reads up to 1 MiB. A job uses the plugin's own grants (U29). |
| `jobs::start(kind, input)` | server | async, `request-id` | Starts a declared job kind with bytes as input. |
| `jobs::take_output(job)` | server | sync, `Option` | The job's bytes, once. |
| `jobs::report_progress(percent)` | job | sync | Reports 0 to 100. Only the newest value per job arrives. |
| `jobs::is_cancelled()` | job | sync, `bool` | True after a cancel. |
| `topics::publish(topic, payload_json)` | server | sync, `Result` | Publishes JSON to a declared topic under the plugin's id. |
| Event `command-invoked` | server | event | The scan command ran. |
| Event `request-completed` | server | event | A scan or job finished, with its outcome. |
| Event `job-progress` | server | event | The percent of a running job. |
| Event `topic-published` | client | event | The payload of a subscribed topic. |
| Intent `editor-open` | client | intent | Opens a file at a 0-based line, in a split pane. |
| Widgets `gauge` and `list` | client | UI tree | The progress bar and the hit list. |

Widget defaults come from the SDK builder (W1). A list sends `activated` with the row index on Enter (W11).

### Manifest

This step adds the entries below to the step 4 manifest. Keep every other entry from step 4. `exports` lists `job-runner`, so the host creates a job instance from the server component. The job's `deadline_ms` and `memory_mib` are requested limits. A value above the tier ceiling is clamped and logged, never refused. For a T1 plugin the ceilings are 60,000 ms of CPU and 512 MiB (L2).

```json
{
  "server": { "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["job-runner"] },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["fs.read:project", "jobs.run"],
    "client": ["fs.read:project", "editor.edit", "topics.subscribe:example.agent-tools/*"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [{ "id": "scan-todos", "title": "Scan the project for TODO lines" },
                 { "id": "show-todos", "title": "Show TODO results" }],
    "keybindings": [
      { "command": "example.agent-tools/scan-todos", "chord": "s", "mode": "prefix" },
      { "command": "example.agent-tools/show-todos", "chord": "t", "mode": "prefix" }
    ],
    "panels": [{ "id": "todos", "title": "TODO scan", "modal": false }],
    "jobs": [{ "kind": "todo-scan", "deadline_ms": 10000, "memory_mib": 64 }],
    "topics": { "publishes": ["example.agent-tools/todos", "example.agent-tools/scan-progress"] }
  }
}
```

### The pure search

The search makes no host calls, so `cargo test` runs it on the development machine.

**Rust**

```rust
// core/src/todo.rs. Finds TODO lines in one file's text.
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TodoHit {
    pub path: String,
    pub line: u32,
    pub text: String,
}

/// Returns every line that contains `TODO`, numbered from 1.
pub fn find_todos(path: &str, text: &str) -> Vec<TodoHit> {
    text.lines()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, line)| line.contains("TODO"))
        .map(|(index, line)| TodoHit {
            path: path.to_string(),
            line: index as u32 + 1,
            text: line.trim().to_string(),
        })
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn numbers_lines_from_one() {
        let hits = find_todos("src/a.rs", "fn a() {}\n// TODO: fix\n");
        assert_eq!(hits.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(hits[0].line, 2);
    }
}
```

### Server: scan, job and publish

`scan.rs` keeps the request id of the scan and of the job in two thread-local slots. A completion for any other request matches neither slot and is ignored. `run_job` runs on the worker bank, in a second instance of the plugin, under the manifest's CPU deadline and memory limit.

**Rust**

```rust
// server/src/scan.rs. TODO scan workflow on the server side.
use std::cell::Cell;

use agent_tools_core::todo::{find_todos, TodoHit};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, jobs, log::{self, Level}, topics};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

pub const SCAN_COMMAND: &str = "example.agent-tools/scan-todos";
pub const JOB_KIND: &str = "todo-scan";
pub const RESULTS_TOPIC: &str = "example.agent-tools/todos";
pub const PROGRESS_TOPIC: &str = "example.agent-tools/scan-progress";
const SCAN_GLOB: &str = "**/*.rs";
const MAX_FILES: u32 = 4096;
const MAX_READ_BYTES: u32 = 1024 * 1024;

thread_local! {
    static SCAN_REQUEST: Cell<Option<u64>> = Cell::new(None);
    static JOB_REQUEST: Cell<Option<u64>> = Cell::new(None);
}

fn project_path(path: &str) -> FsPath {
    FsPath { scope: "project".to_string(), path: path.to_string() }
}

/// Starts the scan. Its completion arrives later as `request-completed`.
pub fn start_scan() {
    match fs::scan(&project_path(""), SCAN_GLOB, MAX_FILES) {
        Ok(request) => SCAN_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.set(Some(request))),
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("scan not started: {}", error.message)),
    }
}

/// Returns true when the completed request belongs to this workflow.
pub fn on_request_completed(request: u64) -> bool {
    if SCAN_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.get()) == Some(request) {
        SCAN_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.set(None));
        start_job(request);
        return true;
    }
    if JOB_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.get()) == Some(request) {
        JOB_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.set(None));
        publish_results(request);
        return true;
    }
    false
}

fn start_job(scan_request: u64) {
    let Some(entries) = fs::take_entries(scan_request) else {
        log::log(Level::Warn, "scan finished without a result");
        return;
    };
    let paths: Vec<String> = entries.into_iter().map(|(path, _)| path).collect();
    let Ok(input) = serde_json::to_vec(&paths) else {
        log::log(Level::Warn, "scan result could not be encoded");
        return;
    };
    match jobs::start(JOB_KIND, &input) {
        Ok(job) => JOB_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.set(Some(job))),
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("job not started: {}", error.message)),
    }
}

fn publish_results(job: u64) {
    let Some(output) = jobs::take_output(job) else {
        log::log(Level::Warn, "job finished without output");
        return;
    };
    if let Err(error) = topics::publish(RESULTS_TOPIC, &String::from_utf8_lossy(&output)) {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("results not published: {}", error.message));
    }
}

/// Forwards job progress as a topic, so the panel can draw the gauge.
pub fn on_job_progress(job: u64, percent: f32) {
    if JOB_REQUEST.with(|slot| slot.get()) != Some(job) {
        return;
    }
    let payload = serde_json::json!({ "percent": percent }).to_string();
    if let Err(error) = topics::publish(PROGRESS_TOPIC, &payload) {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("progress not published: {}", error.message));
    }
}

/// The job body. Runs on the worker bank, not in the event handler.
pub fn run_job(kind: &str, input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
    if kind != JOB_KIND {
        return Err(plugin_error(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "unknown job kind"));
    }
    let paths: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_slice(input)
        .map_err(|error| plugin_error(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, &error.to_string()))?;
    let total = paths.len().max(1);
    let mut hits: Vec<TodoHit> = Vec::new();
    for (index, path) in paths.iter().enumerate() {
        if jobs::is_cancelled() {
            return Err(plugin_error(ErrorCode::Cancelled, "scan cancelled"));
        }
        let bytes = fs::read(&project_path(path), 0, MAX_READ_BYTES)?;
        hits.extend(find_todos(path, &String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes)));
        jobs::report_progress(((index + 1) * 100 / total) as f32);
    }
    serde_json::to_vec(&hits)
        .map_err(|error| plugin_error(ErrorCode::Internal, &error.to_string()))
}

fn plugin_error(code: ErrorCode, message: &str) -> PluginError {
    PluginError { code, message: message.to_string(), retry_after_ms: None }
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["job-runner"])]
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct AgentTools;

impl JobRunner for AgentTools {
    fn run(&mut self, kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
        run_job(&kind, &input)
    }
}
```

The handler in `server/src/lib.rs` gets these new arms. The step 4 arms are unchanged.

```rust
// server/src/lib.rs, new arms of the handler body.
Event::CommandInvoked(invocation) if invocation.command == scan::SCAN_COMMAND => {
    scan::start_scan();
}
Event::RequestCompleted(result) => {
    if let RequestRef::Call(request) = result.request {
        scan::on_request_completed(request);
    }
}
Event::JobProgress(progress) => scan::on_job_progress(progress.request_id, progress.percent),
```

Points to notice:

- A failed scan takes the same branch as a successful one. `take_entries` returns `None`, and the log says `scan finished without a result`.
- A second scan replaces the first id in its slot, so the first completion is ignored. The host holds that result for 30 seconds and then drops it (N16).
- A job failure never counts toward the plugin's restart rule (A22).

### Client: the results panel

The client keeps the last results and the last progress value. Enter on a row sends an `editor-open` intent.

**Rust**

```rust
// client/src/todos.rs. Results panel and the editor jump.
use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

use agent_tools_core::todo::TodoHit;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{EditorOpenSpec, EditorPlacement};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::ViewTarget;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

pub const PANEL: &str = "todos";
const RESULTS_TOPIC: &str = "example.agent-tools/todos";
const PROGRESS_TOPIC: &str = "example.agent-tools/scan-progress";

thread_local! {
    static HITS: RefCell<Vec<TodoHit>> = RefCell::new(Vec::new());
    static PERCENT: Cell<f64> = Cell::new(0.0);
}

/// Stores a topic payload. Returns true when the panel should redraw.
pub fn on_topic(topic: &str, payload_json: &str) -> bool {
    if topic == RESULTS_TOPIC {
        let hits: Vec<TodoHit> = serde_json::from_str(payload_json).unwrap_or_default();
        HITS.with(|cell| *cell.borrow_mut() = hits);
        PERCENT.with(|cell| cell.set(100.0));
        return true;
    }
    if topic == PROGRESS_TOPIC {
        let percent = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(payload_json)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value["percent"].as_f64())
            .unwrap_or(0.0);
        PERCENT.with(|cell| cell.set(percent));
        return true;
    }
    false
}

/// Opens the editor at the selected hit. Hit lines are 1-based, but the editor
/// takes a 0-based line (U32), so the line is converted here.
pub fn open_hit(index: u32) -> Option<Submission> {
    let hit = HITS.with(|cell| cell.borrow().get(index as usize).cloned())?;
    Some(Submission {
        intent: Intent::EditorOpen(EditorOpenSpec {
            path: FsPath { scope: "project".to_string(), path: hit.path },
            line: Some(hit.line - 1),
            placement: EditorPlacement::Split,
        }),
        correlation: u64::from(hit.line),
        dedup_key: None,
    })
}

/// A gauge for the scan progress above the list of hits.
pub fn render_panel() -> UiTree {
    let percent = PERCENT.with(|cell| cell.get());
    let rows: Vec<String> = HITS.with(|cell| {
        cell.borrow()
            .iter()
            .map(|hit| format!("{}:{}  {}", hit.path, hit.line, hit.text))
            .collect()
    });
    let mut tree = Tree::new();
    let gauge = tree.gauge(percent / 100.0).key("progress");
    let list = tree.list(rows).key("hits");
    let body = tree.layout(
        Direction::Vertical,
        vec![Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Fill(1)],
        vec![gauge, list],
    );
    let root = tree.block().title("TODO scan").child(body);
    tree.finish(root)
}

pub fn is_todos_panel(view: &ViewTarget) -> bool {
    matches!(view, ViewTarget::Panel(name) if name == PANEL)
}
```

```rust
// client/src/lib.rs, new arms of the handler body.
Event::TopicPublished(topic) => {
    if todos::on_topic(&topic.topic, &topic.payload_json) {
        ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Panel(todos::PANEL.to_string()));
    }
}
Event::UiAction(action) if todos::is_todos_panel(&action.view) => {
    if let (UiActionKind::Activated, UiValue::Index(index)) = (&action.kind, &action.value) {
        submissions.extend(todos::open_hit(*index));
    }
}
```

Points to notice:

- The panel reads no files. It shows what the server published.
- Results arrive once, when the job completes. The list does not grow during a scan, and the gauge moves on each progress value.
- Without `fs.read` for the path, `editor-open` is refused with `not-permitted` (E4).

### The same workflow in TypeScript

The TypeScript server uses the same commands, topics and manifest. `start` resolves with the job output and gives no job id (N5), so the scan sets a `scanning` flag and forwards each `job-progress` event while it is set. Errors are thrown as `PluginError`, and a `u64` such as the read offset is a `bigint` (S5).

**TypeScript**

```ts
// core/src/todo.ts. Finds TODO lines in one file's text. No host imports.
export interface TodoHit {
  path: string;
  line: number;
  text: string;
}

export function findTodos(path: string, text: string): TodoHit[] {
  const hits: TodoHit[] = [];
  text.split('\n').forEach((line, index) => {
    if (line.includes('TODO')) {
      hits.push({ path, line: index + 1, text: line.trim() });
    }
  });
  return hits;
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// server/src/scan.ts. TODO scan workflow in TypeScript.
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { read, scan } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { isCancelled, reportProgress, start } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { publish } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/topics';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { lifecycle as baseLifecycle } from './lifecycle'; // the lifecycle of step 8
import { findTodos, type TodoHit } from '../../core/src/todo';

const SCAN_COMMAND = 'example.agent-tools/scan-todos';
const JOB_KIND = 'todo-scan';
const RESULTS_TOPIC = 'example.agent-tools/todos';
const PROGRESS_TOPIC = 'example.agent-tools/scan-progress';
const MAX_READ_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
let scanning = false;

const projectPath = (path: string) => ({ scope: 'project', path });

async function runScan(): Promise<void> {
  scanning = true;
  try {
    const entries = await scan(projectPath(''), '**/*.rs', 4096);
    const paths = entries.map(([path]) => path);
    const output = await start(JOB_KIND, new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(paths)));
    publish(RESULTS_TOPIC, new TextDecoder().decode(output));
  } catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof PluginError ? error.message : String(error);
    log('warn', `scan failed: ${reason}`);
  } finally {
    scanning = false;
  }
}

function onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === SCAN_COMMAND) {
      void runScan(); // runScan handles its own errors
    } else if (event.tag === 'job-progress' && scanning) {
      publish(PROGRESS_TOPIC, JSON.stringify({ percent: event.val.percent }));
    }
  }
  return [];
}

function runJob(kind: string, input: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
  if (kind !== JOB_KIND) {
    throw new PluginError('invalid-argument', `unknown job kind ${kind}`);
  }
  const paths: string[] = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(input));
  const hits: TodoHit[] = [];
  for (const [index, path] of paths.entries()) {
    if (isCancelled()) {
      throw new PluginError('cancelled', 'scan cancelled');
    }
    const bytes = read(projectPath(path), 0n, MAX_READ_BYTES);
    hits.push(...findTodos(path, new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)));
    reportProgress(((index + 1) * 100) / paths.length);
  }
  return new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(hits));
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, jobRunner } = definePlugin({
  lifecycle: baseLifecycle,
  handler: { onEvents },
  jobRunner: { run: runJob },
});
```

### Test it

Run the search tests without the host, then start the plugin and try the panel.

**Rust**

```bash
cargo test -p agent-tools-core todo
ilium plugin dev
```

**TypeScript**

```bash
bun test core/src/todo.test.ts
ilium plugin dev
```

Press the prefix key and `s` to scan, then the prefix key and `t` to show the results. Press Enter on a row to open the editor at that line.

### Progress row in the panel

The gauge shows progress as a bar. The `progress-row` widget shows one job with a state glyph, a title, a percent and a message, so the panel can name the running scan. A builder call replaces the gauge call: `progress_row(state, title, percent, message)` in Rust, `progressRow({ state, title, percent, message })` in TypeScript. The states are `waiting`, `running`, `done` and `error`, drawn `○`, `▶`, `✓` and `!`. The panel code of this step keeps the gauge.

### Edge cases and errors

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| No `TODO` lines | The topic carries `[]`. The list is empty and the gauge reaches 100. |
| A file cannot be read | The job fails with the read's code, such as `not-found` or `io`. The panel keeps the last results. |
| `fs.scan` finds more than 4,096 `.rs` files | The scan completes as `failed(quota-exceeded)` and no job starts. The result is never truncated (E5). |
| A file is over 1 MiB | Only the first MiB is read. For the rest, call `fs::read` again with a larger offset. |
| 16 jobs already queued | `jobs::start` returns `busy` (C42). |
| Job runs past 10 seconds of CPU | The job fails as `timed-out`, and its output is dropped (A22). |
| Results over 64 KiB | `topics::publish` refuses the payload with `invalid-argument` (L3). A few hundred hits can reach that size. |

### What the user sees

The panel is one box with a gauge above a list. While the job runs, the list shows the hits of the last completed scan, and the gauge moves. When the job completes, the new hits replace the list.

# 6. Notes pane with drag and drop

## 6. Notes pane with drag and drop

This step adds a pane kind to the plugin. A notes pane is a basic pane: the kernel draws its frame,
title and footer line, and the plugin draws the body with `render`. Each note is one row. A row can be
dragged onto another row to change the order, and a text input at the bottom adds notes. The notes are
kept in node metadata, so they survive a restart. A command opens a new notes pane. While a note is dragged, the plugin tells the host which side of a row accepts the drop, and the host draws the insertion line.

### You will need

- [Tutorial step 5](/pages/tutorial-05-todo-scanner/) finished.
- Rust for the core, client and server crates, or TypeScript for the client module.
- `serde` and `serde_json` in the core and client crates. The core crate has no host calls.

Grants added in this step. Grants are per side.

| Side | Grant | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Client | `panes.provide-kind` | the `notes` pane kind and the `basic` imports |
| Client | `tree.metadata` | `tree::metadata` and `tree::set_metadata` |
| Server | `panes.create` | the `create-pane` intent sent by the command |

The server runs the command, so the client does not need `panes.create`.

<div class="note">
<p>Node metadata is one byte map per plugin per node. The server holds and replicates it, and both sides
read and write it with <code>tree.metadata</code>. This step writes it from the client only.</p>
</div>

### What changed from step 5

- `core/src/notes.rs` is new. It holds the note list and its rules.
- `client/src/notes.rs` is new. It renders the pane and applies drops and new notes.
- `client/src/lib.rs` routes `ui-action` events and the pane view to `notes.rs`.
- `server/src/lib.rs` gets one arm, which creates the pane.
- `manifest.json` adds the pane kind, the command, the keybinding and the grants above.

### How a drag reaches the plugin

A drag ends with one `ui-action` event of kind `dropped`. Its value is one `drop` value that carries
the source key, the target key and the insertion index. The plugin moves the note, saves the list and
invalidates the pane. The invalidate is needed because `set-metadata` does not change the node's
revision and sends no `tree-changed` event.

### Manifest

Merge these entries into the step 5 file. The pane kind id is `notes`, and its global id,
`example.agent-tools.notes`, is the content kind that `pane-info` reports. `wants_keys` stays false,
so the pane gets no raw key events. The text input sends its own `ui-action` events.

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["agent.read", "agent.control", "tree.read", "tree.decorate", "notify.desktop",
               "sound.play", "fs.read:project", "jobs.run", "panes.create"],
    "client": ["agent.read", "tree.read", "tree.metadata", "ui.panels", "editor.edit",
               "topics.subscribe:example.agent-tools/*", "panes.provide-kind"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [{ "id": "new-notes", "title": "New notes pane" }],
    "keybindings": [
      { "command": "example.agent-tools/new-notes", "chord": "n", "mode": "prefix" }
    ],
    "pane_kinds": [
      { "id": "notes", "title": "Notes", "icon": "notebook", "primitive": "basic",
        "wants_keys": false, "persist": "metadata" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`persist: "metadata"` keeps the pane node across a restart, together with its metadata.

### The surface this step uses

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metadata` | `tree::metadata(node)` | `treeHost.metadata(node)` | The bytes, or none or `undefined` when absent or the grant is declined |
| `set-metadata` | `tree::set_metadata(node, bytes)` | `treeHost.setMetadata(node, bytes)` | Writes the map. `quota-exceeded` above 64 KiB |
| `invalidate` | `ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Pane(node))` | `invalidate({ tag: 'pane', val: node })` | Asks for a new `render` |
| `set-status` | `basic::set_status(node, spans)` | `basic.setStatus(node, spans)` | Writes the one-line footer |
| `ui-action` | `Event::UiAction(UiAction)` | `{ tag: 'ui-action', val }` | Fields `view`, `key`, `kind`, `value` |
| `dropped` | `ActionKind::Dropped`, `ActionValue::Drop(source, target, index)` | `'dropped'`, `{ tag: 'drop', val: [source, target, index] }` | One drop |
| `submitted` | `ActionKind::Submitted`, `ActionValue::Text(text)` | `'submitted'`, `{ tag: 'text', val }` | Enter in the text input |
| `create-pane` | `Intent::CreatePane(CreatePaneSpec)` | intent `create-pane` | `parent: None` places the pane like a user pane |
| Row flags | `NodeFlags::DRAGGABLE`, `NodeFlags::DROP_TARGET` | `{ draggable: true, dropTarget: true }` | A drag source and a drop target |

### The pure note list

A note is a key and a text. The key is unique within the list and names the note in a drop.
`move_note` takes the note out and inserts it at `index`, counted after the removal. An index past the
end appends. An unknown key changes nothing and returns `false`, so nothing is saved. `add_note` joins
the words with single spaces, ignores blank text and gives the note the key `note-<n>`, where `n` is one
more than the count. No step removes notes, so that key is never in use.

**Rust**

```rust
// core/src/notes.rs. Note list and its rules. No host calls.
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// The global pane kind id, shared by the manifest and the server's create-pane intent.
pub const PANE_KIND: &str = "example.agent-tools.notes";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Note {
    pub key: String,
    pub text: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NoteList {
    pub notes: Vec<Note>,
}

/// Moves the note with `source_key` to `index`, counted after the removal.
/// Returns false when the key is unknown, so the caller saves nothing.
pub fn move_note(list: &mut NoteList, source_key: &str, index: usize) -> bool {
    let Some(position) = list.notes.iter().position(|note| note.key == source_key) else {
        return false;
    };
    let note = list.notes.remove(position);
    let target = index.min(list.notes.len());
    list.notes.insert(target, note);
    true
}

/// Appends a note. Blank text adds nothing and returns false.
pub fn add_note(list: &mut NoteList, text: &str) -> bool {
    let text = text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    if text.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    // Notes are never removed in this step, so count + 1 is never a key in use.
    let key = format!("note-{}", list.notes.len() + 1);
    list.notes.push(Note { key, text });
    true
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample() -> NoteList {
        let mut list = NoteList::default();
        for text in ["note a", "note b", "note c"] {
            add_note(&mut list, text);
        }
        list
    }

    #[test]
    fn moves_a_note_to_the_front() {
        let mut list = sample();
        assert!(move_note(&mut list, "note-3", 0));
        let keys: Vec<&str> = list.notes.iter().map(|note| note.key.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(keys, ["note-3", "note-1", "note-2"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_key_and_blank_text_change_nothing() {
        let mut list = sample();
        assert!(!move_note(&mut list, "zz", 0));
        assert!(!add_note(&mut list, "   "));
        assert_eq!(list, sample());
    }
}
```

### Client: the pane view, drops and new notes (Rust)

The client loads the list from metadata on every render. A drop or a submitted text loads the list,
changes it, saves it and invalidates the pane. An event handler returns submissions, not errors, so a
failed save shows `Not saved` in the footer instead.

**Rust**

```rust
// client/src/notes.rs. Notes pane: render, drop and add.
use agent_tools_core::notes::{add_note, move_note, NoteList};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{tree, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::basic;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::ColorRole;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, UiAction, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::{NodeFlags, Tree};

pub const NEW_NOTE_KEY: &str = "new-note";

/// A missing or damaged value is an empty list, so the pane still opens.
pub fn load(node: NodeId) -> NoteList {
    tree::metadata(node)
        .and_then(|bytes| serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).ok())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

fn save(node: NodeId, list: &NoteList) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(list).map_err(|error| PluginError {
        code: ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
        message: error.to_string(),
        retry_after_ms: None,
    })?;
    tree::set_metadata(node, bytes)
}

/// Routes one ui-action. Other views and kinds this pane does not use are ignored.
pub fn on_action(action: &UiAction) {
    let ViewTarget::Pane(node) = &action.view else {
        return;
    };
    let node = *node;
    let result = match (&action.kind, &action.value) {
        (ActionKind::Dropped, ActionValue::Drop(source, _target, index)) => {
            on_dropped(node, source, *index)
        }
        (ActionKind::Submitted, ActionValue::Text(text)) if action.key == NEW_NOTE_KEY => {
            on_added(node, text)
        }
        _ => return,
    };
    match result {
        Ok(()) => ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Pane(node)),
        Err(_) => {
            let status = Span::styled("Not saved", Style::role(ColorRole::Danger));
            let _ = basic::set_status(node, vec![status]);
        }
    }
}

fn on_dropped(node: NodeId, source_key: &str, index: u32) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let mut list = load(node);
    if move_note(&mut list, source_key, index as usize) {
        save(node, &list)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn on_added(node: NodeId, text: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let mut list = load(node);
    if add_note(&mut list, text) {
        save(node, &list)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// One draggable row per note, then the input for new notes.
pub fn render_pane(node: NodeId) -> UiTree {
    let list = load(node);
    let mut builder = Tree::new();
    let rows: Vec<_> = list
        .notes
        .iter()
        .map(|note| {
            builder
                .paragraph([note.text.as_str()])
                .key(note.key.as_str())
                .flags(NodeFlags::DRAGGABLE | NodeFlags::DROP_TARGET)
        })
        .collect();
    let input = builder.text_input("New note").key(NEW_NOTE_KEY);
    let mut constraints: Vec<Constraint> = rows.iter().map(|_| Constraint::Min(1)).collect();
    constraints.push(Constraint::Length(3));
    let mut root = builder.layout(Direction::Vertical).constraints(constraints);
    for row in rows {
        root = root.child(row);
    }
    builder.finish(root.child(input))
}
```

The handler arm and the views export route to the module:

**Rust**

```rust
// client/src/lib.rs. New arm of the handler body, and a new arm of the views export.
Event::UiAction(action) => notes::on_action(&action),

// views export: a pane of this kind is drawn by the notes module.
ViewTarget::Pane(node) => notes::render_pane(node),
```

### Client: the same module (TypeScript)

The TypeScript client stores the same JSON, so a list written by one client reads in the other. The pure note list of `core/src/notes.rs` is mirrored in the same file (`moveNote`, `addNote`), because a TypeScript plugin has no Rust core crate.

**TypeScript**

```ts
// client/src/notes.ts. Notes pane for the TypeScript client.
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as basic from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/basic';
import * as treeHost from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';
import { invalidate } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { layout, paragraph, span, textInput, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import { role, type Event, type ViewTarget } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const NEW_NOTE_KEY = 'new-note';

interface Note { key: string; text: string }
interface NoteList { notes: Note[] }

function isNote(value: unknown): value is Note {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
    && typeof (value as Note).key === 'string' && typeof (value as Note).text === 'string';
}

function loadNotes(node: bigint): NoteList {
  const bytes = treeHost.metadata(node);
  if (bytes === undefined) return { notes: [] };
  try {
    const notes: unknown = (JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)) as NoteList).notes;
    return Array.isArray(notes) && notes.every(isNote) ? { notes } : { notes: [] };
  } catch {
    return { notes: [] };
  }
}

function moveNote(list: NoteList, sourceKey: string, index: number): boolean {
  const position = list.notes.findIndex((note) => note.key === sourceKey);
  if (position === -1) return false;
  const [note] = list.notes.splice(position, 1);
  list.notes.splice(Math.min(index, list.notes.length), 0, note);
  return true;
}

function addNote(list: NoteList, rawText: string): boolean {
  const text = rawText.split(/\s+/).filter((word) => word !== '').join(' ');
  if (text === '') return false;
  list.notes.push({ key: `note-${list.notes.length + 1}`, text });
  return true;
}

/** Loads, changes, saves and redraws. A refused save (quota-exceeded) shows in the footer. */
function applyEdit(node: bigint, change: (list: NoteList) => boolean): void {
  const list = loadNotes(node);
  if (!change(list)) return;
  try {
    treeHost.setMetadata(node, new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(list)));
  } catch {
    basic.setStatus(node, [span('Not saved', { fg: role('danger') })]);
    return;
  }
  invalidate({ tag: 'pane', val: node });
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || event.val.view.tag !== 'pane') continue;
      const node = event.val.view.val;
      const { key, kind, value } = event.val;
      if (kind === 'dropped' && value.tag === 'drop') {
        const [sourceKey, , index] = value.val;
        applyEdit(node, (list) => moveNote(list, sourceKey, index));
      } else if (kind === 'submitted' && key === NEW_NOTE_KEY && value.tag === 'text') {
        applyEdit(node, (list) => addNote(list, value.val));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render(view: ViewTarget) {
    if (view.tag !== 'pane') return tree(paragraph(['This view is not a notes pane.']));
    const rows = loadNotes(view.val).notes.map((note) => paragraph([note.text], {
      key: note.key,
      flags: { draggable: true, dropTarget: true },
    }));
    return tree(layout({
      direction: 'vertical',
      constraints: [...rows.map(() => ({ tag: 'min', val: 1 })), { tag: 'length', val: 3 }],
    }, [...rows, textInput('New note', { key: NEW_NOTE_KEY })]));
  },
});
```

### Server: the command that creates the pane

The command arrives on the server as `command-invoked`. The intent names the content kind, which is
the pane kind id from the core crate. `parent: None` places the pane like one the user created.
`Submission::new` sends no dedup key, so a repeated command opens a second pane.

**Rust**

```rust
// server/src/lib.rs. New arm of the handler body.
const NEW_NOTES_COMMAND: &str = "example.agent-tools/new-notes";

Event::CommandInvoked(invocation) if invocation.command == NEW_NOTES_COMMAND => {
    submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::CreatePane(CreatePaneSpec {
        parent: None,
        title: "Notes".to_string(),
        content_kind: agent_tools_core::notes::PANE_KIND.to_string(),
        cwd: None,
        command: None,
        initial_input: None,
    })));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// server/src/main.ts. New branch of onEvents.
const NEW_NOTES_COMMAND = 'example.agent-tools/new-notes';
const NOTES_PANE_KIND = 'example.agent-tools.notes';

for (const event of batch) {
  if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === NEW_NOTES_COMMAND) {
    submissions.push({
      intent: {
        tag: 'create-pane',
        val: {
          parent: undefined,
          title: 'Notes',
          contentKind: NOTES_PANE_KIND,
          cwd: undefined,
          command: undefined,
          initialInput: undefined,
        },
      },
      correlation: 1n, // chosen by the plugin, unique per plugin, below 2^63
      dedupKey: undefined,
    });
  }
}
```

### Drag feedback

The host owns the drag, but the plugin decides what a drop would mean. While a drag hovers a row with `DROP_TARGET`, the host sends one `ui-action` of kind `drag-over` per change of target. Its value is a `drag-over-value` with `source-key`, `target-key`, `index` and `accept`. The plugin answers on the next render by setting the target's `accept` prop to `before`, `after`, `inside` or `none`. The host draws the insertion line (`before`, `after`) or the inside highlight, and scrolls the list near its edges. The event is coalesced per target.

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drag-over` | `ActionKind::DragOver`, `ActionValue::DragOver(DragOverValue)` | `'drag-over'`, `{ tag: 'drag-over', val }` | A dragged row is held over a target |
| `drop-accept` | `DropAccept::{None, Before, After, Inside}` | `'none'`, `'before'`, `'after'`, `'inside'` | The plugin's answer for that target |
| `pointer-events` | `NodeFlags::POINTER_EVENTS` | `{ pointerEvents: true }` | Opt-in for `pointer` actions with sub-cell positions. This step does not need it. |

The rule for the answer is pure, so it goes in the core crate and is tested like the rest. A row dragged downward lands after the target, a row dragged upward lands before it, and the row itself accepts nothing.

**Rust**

```rust
// core/src/notes.rs. Which side of a target accepts the drop.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DropSide { None, Before, After }

pub fn drop_side(list: &NoteList, source_key: &str, target_key: &str) -> DropSide {
    let position = |key: &str| list.notes.iter().position(|note| note.key == key);
    match (position(source_key), position(target_key)) {
        (Some(source), Some(target)) if source < target => DropSide::After,
        (Some(source), Some(target)) if source > target => DropSide::Before,
        _ => DropSide::None,
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// client/src/notes.ts. Mirrors drop_side in core/src/notes.rs.
type DropSide = 'none' | 'before' | 'after';

function dropSide(list: NoteList, sourceKey: string, targetKey: string): DropSide {
  const source = list.notes.findIndex((note) => note.key === sourceKey);
  const target = list.notes.findIndex((note) => note.key === targetKey);
  if (source === -1 || target === -1 || source === target) return 'none';
  return source < target ? 'after' : 'before';
}
```

The client calls `drop_side` from the `drag-over` arm of its action handler, keeps the answer with the target key, and invalidates the pane. `render` then sets the answer as the target row's `accept` prop. The SDK pages do not yet name the builder call that sets that prop, so this step stops at the pure rule and the event arm.

### Errors and edge cases

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Save over the 64 KiB metadata limit | `quota-exceeded` from `set-metadata`. Nothing is written. The footer shows `Not saved`. |
| Drop whose source key no longer exists | `move_note` returns `false`. Nothing is saved, and no error is shown. |
| Drop onto the row the note came from | The note returns to its own place, so the order does not change. |
| Index past the end of the list | Clamped. The note moves to the last place. |
| Metadata missing or damaged | Loads as an empty list. The next save replaces the damaged bytes. |
| Blank or spaces-only text | Nothing is added and nothing is saved. |
| `tree.metadata` grant declined or revoked | `metadata` returns none, so the pane shows no notes. `set-metadata` returns `not-permitted`. |
| Command runs twice | Two panes open. The intent has no dedup key in this step. |
| Drag over the source row itself | `drop_side` returns none, so no line is drawn. |
| Pane restarted after a save | The node and its metadata come back from the snapshot, so the list loads again. |

### Test it

Run the core tests, then run the plugin in development mode.

```bash
cargo test -p agent-tools-core notes
ilium plugin dev
```

For the TypeScript client, run the mirrored list functions under Bun, then the same dev loop:

```bash
bun test client/src/notes.test.ts
ilium plugin dev
```

Press the prefix key and `n`, type two notes into the input and press Enter, then drag one note onto
the other. Also check a drop onto the same row, and a pane that is reopened after a restart.

### What you see

At normal width, each note is one row with the input below. At a narrow width, long notes wrap. During a drag, the host draws an insertion line where the drop would land, and the note moves when the drop ends. The frame is the kernel's: rounded border, the chrome icons in the title, and a cyan border while the pane has focus.

# 7. Ambient scene

## 7. Ambient scene

This step adds an animated background to the agent tools plugin. A scene is a third component. It runs in the animation world `ilium:anim/base@0.1.0`, apart from the server and client worlds. The host creates one renderer for the scene, reads its frame rate and calls `render` once per frame. The scene writes tone values into a surface and calls `present`. The host then applies the shared look, the palette and the dither mode. The scene has no colour, palette or dithering controls of its own.

The scene draws rings that move outward from the centre of the panel. It has one setting, the ring count.

### What you need

- [Tutorial step 6](/pages/tutorial-06-notes-pane/) finished. The scene is a new component in the same project. The `server/` and `client/` components do not change.
- A `scene` component in a new crate `scene/`, built against `ilium:anim/base@0.1.0`.
- Rust stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, using `ilium-plugin-sdk`. Or Bun 1.2 or later with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, for the TypeScript version in this step.
- Grants: none. The scene side always has `log`, `clock`, its own `storage`, `codec`, and the `fs` scopes `package`, `data` and `cache`. This scene reads no file and makes no network call, so `capabilities.scene` is an empty list.
- Manifest values: `family` is `procedural` and `modes` is `["live"]`. The family names are `natural`, `procedural`, `geometry`, `simulation`, `live-data`, `maps-and-space`, `saved-world`, `media` and `other`. The mode names are `live` and `pre-rendered`. The first mode in the list is the default.

### What changed from step 6

- `core/src/rings.rs` is new. It holds the tone function and makes no host calls.
- `scene/` is a new crate. Its `lib.rs` implements the `renderer` resource.
- `manifest.json` adds the `scene` object and the `scenes` contribution.
- `server/` and `client/` are unchanged.

### The frame loop

<figcaption>The host owns the clock. The scene answers each frame with tone values, and the host adds the look and the dither.</figcaption>

The host reads `frames-per-second` once after the constructor returns, and again after each `reconfigure` that returns `true`. It never reads it per frame. A palette change reaches the scene through `set-palette`, between frames.

### Renderer surface

The scene implements the `renderer` resource. Rust names come from `ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::{surface, renderer}`, and TypeScript names from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/surface` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/renderer`.

| Member | Rust | TypeScript | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| constructor | `fn new(spec: SceneSpec) -> Self` | `constructor(spec)` | none | Called when the scene is shown and after a restart. |
| readiness | `fn readiness(&self) -> Readiness` | `readiness()` | `Ready` | `Ready`, `Preparing` or `Failed`. |
| frames per second | `fn frames_per_second(&self) -> u32` | `framesPerSecond()` | 30 | Requested rate, capped by `frame_rate_cap`. |
| pointer | `fn wants_pointer(&self) -> bool` | `wantsPointer()` | false | Enables `pointer` on the surface. |
| occupancy | `fn wants_occupancy(&self) -> bool` | `wantsOccupancy()` | false | Enables `occupancy` on the surface. |
| cell colours | `fn uses_cell_colors(&self) -> bool` | `usesCellColors()` | false | Enables `write_cell_colors`. |
| render | `fn render(&mut self, frame: FrameInput, surface: &FrameSurface)` | `render(frame, surface)` | required | Draws one frame. |
| palette | `fn set_palette(&mut self, palette_rgb: Vec<u32>)` | `setPalette(palette)` | ignored | Called when the palette changes. |
| settings | `fn reconfigure(&mut self, settings_json: String) -> bool` | `reconfigure(settings)` | `false` | Applies new settings. `false` makes the host restart the scene. |
| status | `fn status(&self) -> Option<String>` | `status()` | none | Short text shown beside the scene title while set. |

`FrameInput` holds the frame time and the surface size:

| Field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| time | `time_millis: u64` | `timeMillis: bigint` | Milliseconds since the scene started. |
| visible time | `wall_millis: u64` | `wallMillis: bigint` | Milliseconds since the scene was last made visible. |
| clock | `now_unix_millis: u64` | `nowUnixMillis: bigint` | Wall-clock time in Unix milliseconds. |
| size | `width: u32`, `height: u32` | `width`, `height` | Surface size in pixels: cells times the dither sub-cell factor. |
| palette | `palette_rgb: Vec<u32>` | `paletteRgb: number[]` | Current palette as `0xRRGGBB` values. Empty in greyscale and monotone modes. |

`FrameSurface` takes the tone rows. `write_tones(first_row, &[u8])` (`writeTones`) writes `gray8` rows, one byte per pixel. The other methods are `write_rows`, `write_cell_colors`, `occupancy`, `pointer` and `present`. A `render` call that returns without `present` drops that frame, and a warning is logged once per second.

The dither modes are `ordered`, `stippled`, `bayer2`, `bayer4`, `bayer16`, `blue-noise`, `gradient`, `halftone`, `lines`, `diagonal`, `crosshatch`, `white-noise`, `floyd-steinberg`, `atkinson` and `sierra-lite`. The user picks one in the shared Dither row. A scene never names a mode.

### Manifest

The manifest adds a `scene` object next to `server` and `client`. Required exports such as `renderer` are never listed in `exports`, so the list is empty. The `scenes` contribution declares the scene. The host reads it before it loads the component.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.agent-tools",
  "name": "Agent tools",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["job-runner"]
  },
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["views"]
  },
  "scene": {
    "entry": "scene.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:anim/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "agent.read", "agent.control", "tree.read", "tree.decorate",
      "notify.desktop", "sound.play", "fs.read:project", "jobs.run"
    ],
    "client": [
      "agent.read", "tree.read", "tree.metadata", "ui.panels", "editor.edit",
      "topics.subscribe:example.agent-tools/*", "panes.create", "panes.provide-kind"
    ],
    "scene": []
  },
  "contributes": {
    "scenes": [
      {
        "id": "rings",
        "title": "Rings",
        "family": "procedural",
        "modes": ["live"],
        "frame_rate_cap": 30,
        "settings_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "ring_count": {
              "type": "integer",
              "title": "Rings",
              "default": 3,
              "minimum": 1,
              "maximum": 12,
              "step": 1
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The other contributions from step 6 (commands, keybindings, panels, pane kinds, sounds, jobs, topics, settings) stay in the file. They are omitted here to keep the block short.

- `id` is local to the plugin. The global scene id is `example.agent-tools:rings`.
- `frame_rate_cap` is an integer from 1 to 60. The host caps the rate that the scene asks for at this value.
- `settings_schema` uses the JSON-Schema subset of the settings pages. The host checks new settings against it before the scene sees them.
- `clip_seconds` is used only in `pre-rendered` mode, which this step does not declare.

### The pure tone function

The drawing rule is a pure function with no host calls. The TypeScript scene mirrors it below, because a TypeScript plugin has no Rust core crate. For each cell it returns a tone from 0 (dark) to 255 (bright). The rings are cosine waves of the distance from the centre. A terminal cell is about twice as tall as it is wide, so the vertical gap counts double. The frame number moves the rings outward.

**Rust**

```rust
// core/src/rings.rs. Tone of one cell, no host calls.

/// Returns the tone of the cell at (`x`, `y`) for a frame. Zero is dark and 255 is bright.
/// Rings move outward as `frame` grows.
pub fn ring_tone(x: u32, y: u32, width: u32, height: u32, frame: u32, ring_count: u32) -> u8 {
    if width == 0 || height == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let centre_x = (width as f32 - 1.0) / 2.0;
    let centre_y = (height as f32 - 1.0) / 2.0;
    let delta_x = x as f32 - centre_x;
    // A terminal cell is about twice as tall as it is wide, so vertical distance counts double.
    let delta_y = (y as f32 - centre_y) * 2.0;
    let distance = (delta_x * delta_x + delta_y * delta_y).sqrt();
    let period = width.max(height) as f32 / ring_count.max(1) as f32;
    let angle = std::f32::consts::TAU * (distance / period - frame as f32 * 0.05);
    ((angle.cos() + 1.0) * 0.5 * 255.0) as u8
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn centre_is_brightest_at_frame_zero() {
        assert_eq!(ring_tone(2, 2, 5, 5, 0, 3), 255);
    }

    #[test]
    fn zero_size_is_dark() {
        assert_eq!(ring_tone(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rings_move_outward_between_frames() {
        assert_ne!(ring_tone(0, 0, 22, 6, 0, 3), ring_tone(0, 0, 22, 6, 8, 3));
    }
}
```

The `as u8` cast is safe. The value of `(cos + 1) * 0.5 * 255` stays between 0 and 255, and Rust's float-to-integer cast saturates in any case.

### The scene component in Rust

The scene implements the `renderer` resource. The constructor reads the spec: the settings arrive as JSON text, and the palette as a list of `0xRRGGBB` values. `render` writes one tone per cell and presents the frame. `reconfigure` takes new settings without a restart.

**Rust**

```rust
// scene/src/lib.rs. The rings scene, step 7.
use agent_tools_core::rings::ring_tone;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::renderer::{FrameInput, Renderer, SceneSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::anim::surface::FrameSurface;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use serde::Deserialize;

/// The tone function counts frames at this rate. The frame number comes from the scene clock,
/// so the ring speed does not change when the host runs the scene at a lower rate.
const RING_FRAMES_PER_SECOND: u64 = 30;

#[derive(Deserialize, Clone, Copy)]
#[serde(default)]
struct RingSettings {
    ring_count: u32,
}

impl Default for RingSettings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self { ring_count: 3 }
    }
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "scene")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct RingRenderer {
    settings: RingSettings,
    palette_rgb: Vec<u32>,
}

impl Lifecycle for RingRenderer {}

impl Renderer for RingRenderer {
    fn new(spec: SceneSpec) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: serde_json::from_str(&spec.settings).unwrap_or_default(),
            palette_rgb: spec.palette,
        }
    }

    fn frames_per_second(&self) -> u32 {
        30
    }

    fn render(&mut self, frame: FrameInput, surface: &FrameSurface) {
        let frame_number = (frame.time_millis * RING_FRAMES_PER_SECOND / 1000) as u32;
        let mut tones = Vec::with_capacity((frame.width * frame.height) as usize);
        for row in 0..frame.height {
            for column in 0..frame.width {
                tones.push(ring_tone(
                    column,
                    row,
                    frame.width,
                    frame.height,
                    frame_number,
                    self.settings.ring_count,
                ));
            }
        }
        surface.write_tones(0, &tones);
        surface.present();
    }

    fn set_palette(&mut self, palette_rgb: Vec<u32>) {
        self.palette_rgb = palette_rgb;
    }

    /// Returns `false` for settings it cannot read. The host then restarts the scene.
    fn reconfigure(&mut self, settings_json: String) -> bool {
        match serde_json::from_str::<RingSettings>(&settings_json) {
            Ok(settings) => {
                self.settings = settings;
                true
            }
            Err(_) => false,
        }
    }

    fn status(&self) -> Option<String> {
        Some(format!("{} rings", self.settings.ring_count))
    }
}
```

Notes on the code:

- The scene keeps `palette_rgb` for the palette contract. It does not draw colour, because the host maps tones to colour. Until a later change reads the field, the compiler reports it as never read. That is expected in this step.
- `impl Lifecycle for RingRenderer {}` is required because the scene exports `lifecycle` as well as `renderer`. The default methods are enough.
- `render` takes `&mut self`, as the SDK trait does. It takes the surface by reference.

### The same scene in TypeScript

The TypeScript version has the same behaviour. `defineScene` takes the class, and the spec arrives already parsed. `timeMillis` is a `bigint`, so the code converts it with `Number`. The `ringTone` function mirrors the Rust one line for line, so both builds draw the same frame.

**TypeScript**

```ts
// scene/src/main.ts. The rings scene, step 7, in TypeScript.
import { defineScene } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { FrameInput, SceneSpec } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/renderer';
import type { FrameSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/anim/surface';

const RING_FRAMES_PER_SECOND = 30;

interface RingSettings {
  ring_count: number;
}

function readRingSettings(value: unknown): RingSettings | undefined {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined;
  const ringCount = (value as { ring_count?: unknown }).ring_count;
  return typeof ringCount === 'number' ? { ring_count: ringCount } : undefined;
}

// Mirrors ring_tone in core/src/rings.rs.
function ringTone(
  x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, frame: number, ringCount: number,
): number {
  if (width === 0 || height === 0) return 0;
  const deltaX = x - (width - 1) / 2;
  const deltaY = (y - (height - 1) / 2) * 2;
  const distance = Math.sqrt(deltaX * deltaX + deltaY * deltaY);
  const period = Math.max(width, height) / Math.max(ringCount, 1);
  const angle = 2 * Math.PI * (distance / period - frame * 0.05);
  return Math.floor(((Math.cos(angle) + 1) * 0.5) * 255);
}

class Rings {
  private settings: RingSettings = { ring_count: 3 };

  constructor(spec: SceneSpec) {
    this.settings = readRingSettings(spec.settings) ?? this.settings;
  }

  framesPerSecond(): number {
    return 30;
  }

  render(frame: FrameInput, surface: FrameSurface): void {
    const frameNumber = Math.floor((Number(frame.timeMillis) * RING_FRAMES_PER_SECOND) / 1000);
    const tones = new Uint8Array(frame.width * frame.height);
    for (let row = 0; row < frame.height; row++) {
      for (let column = 0; column < frame.width; column++) {
        tones[row * frame.width + column] = ringTone(
          column, row, frame.width, frame.height, frameNumber, this.settings.ring_count,
        );
      }
    }
    surface.writeTones(0, tones);
    surface.present();
  }

  reconfigure(settings: unknown): boolean {
    const next = readRingSettings(settings);
    if (next === undefined) return false;
    this.settings = next;
    return true;
  }

  status(): string {
    return `${this.settings.ring_count} rings`;
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, renderer } = defineScene(Rings);
```

A scene test draws a frame through `FakeScene`, because a scene is not a view. In Rust, `FakeScene::new::<RingRenderer>("rings", 16, 4)` makes a scene of 16 columns and 4 rows, and `scene.frame(FrameInput::default())` returns a `Screen`. In TypeScript, `createFakeScene(renderer, 'rings', 16, 4)` does the same. Compare `screen.text()` with a golden file through `assert_golden`. See [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/#scenes).

### Errors and edge cases

The renderer returns no `plugin-error`, so a failure in the scene appears as a trap, a deadline breach, a dropped frame or a log line. The rules come from the frame budget, the restart rule and the settings check.

| Case | What happens |
|---|---|
| `ring_count` is 13 | The host refuses the value before the scene sees it, and the previous count stays. The message is `ring_count: 13 is above the maximum of 12`. |
| `reconfigure` returns `false` | The host discards the renderer and builds a new one from a new spec. This is a restart, not a failure. |
| `render` runs past the frame budget | The frame budget is 33 ms at 30 fps. The frame is skipped. The default `frame_deadline_ms` is that budget, with a ceiling of 50 ms. 30 breaches in a row trap. |
| `render` returns without `present` | The frame is dropped and a warning is logged once per second. |
| `write_tones` gets the wrong length | Only whole rows are written. A remainder is dropped and a warning is logged once per second. |
| `readiness` stays `Preparing` for over 10 s | Counts as `Failed`. `render` is not called until the renderer restarts. |
| A trap or a failed readiness | Counts as one failure. The restart waits 1 s after the first failure, 5 s after the second and 30 s after later ones. The third failure within 10 minutes disables the scene side of the plugin. |
| Ring count 12 on a small panel | Rings are closer together than a cell, so the pattern aliases. This is not an error. |

### Scene additions

A scene can ask for more than tones. These additions are optional and the rings scene does not need them, but they are how a scene such as a map or a chess board draws text and answers the pointer.

| Addition | Where | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Glyph plane | manifest `glyph_plane: true` | `surface.write_glyphs(&cells)` | `surface.writeGlyphs(cells)` | Text cells drawn over the pixels after dithering. At most 131,072 cells per frame. Glyph colours also go through the shared look. |
| Clear glyphs | surface | `surface.clear_glyphs()` | `surface.clearGlyphs()` | Removes every glyph cell. |
| Owner ids | surface | `surface.set_owner_ids(first_row, &ids)` | `surface.setOwnerIds(firstRow, ids)` | One `u16` per pixel, 0 for none. Maps pixels to logical objects. |
| Frame receipt | surface | `surface.last_receipt()` | `surface.lastReceipt()` | `frame`, `presented_at_millis`, `dropped_before` and the `pointer_owner` under the pointer. |
| Pointer | renderer | `fn wants_pointer(&self) -> bool` | `wantsPointer()` | A runtime answer, read after the constructor and after each `reconfigure`. `pointer` gives the cell, or none outside the scene. |
| Pre-rendered loop | manifest `prerender` | none | none | `{{ frames, fps, cache_mib }}`. The host calls `render` for the frames once, caches them (at most 128 MiB, 30 fps) and plays the loop. |
| Fonts | scene world | `Font::new(asset)` then `rasterize(text, size_px)` | `new Font(asset)` | TTF or OTF from package assets, at most 4 MiB, rasterized to `mask8`. |

A glyph cell is `column`, `row`, `text`, optional `fg` and `bg` colours as `0xRRGGBB`, and text modifiers. This draws the ring count in the centre of the panel:

**Rust**

```rust
// scene/src/lib.rs. In render, after surface.write_tones and before present.
// Needs "glyph_plane": true on the scene in the manifest.
let label = GlyphCell {{
    column: (frame.width / 2) as u16,
    row: (frame.height / 2) as u16,
    text: self.settings.ring_count.to_string(),
    fg: None,
    bg: None,
    add: Modifiers::default(),
}};
surface.write_glyphs(&[label]);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// scene/src/main.ts. In render, after surface.writeTones and before present.
// Needs "glyph_plane": true on the scene in the manifest.
surface.writeGlyphs([{{
  column: Math.floor(frame.width / 2),
  row: Math.floor(frame.height / 2),
  text: String(this.settings.ring_count),
  fg: undefined,
  bg: undefined,
  add: {{}},
}}]);
```

The glyph is drawn after the shared look, so it follows the palette and the colour mode like the rings do. The surface size in `frame.width` and `frame.height` is in pixels. A glyph cell uses cell coordinates, so a scene divides by the dither sub-cell factor; the SDK pages do not yet expose that factor to a scene, which the gap list notes.

A pre-rendered scene declares `modes: ["pre-rendered"]` and `prerender` in the manifest. The host runs the frames once and plays them with no further calls. A `prerender` on a scene that answers `wants_pointer` is the manifest error `manifest.scene-prerender`.

```json
{{
  "id": "rings-loop", "title": "Rings loop", "family": "procedural",
  "modes": ["pre-rendered"], "clip_seconds": 8,
  "prerender": {{ "frames": 240, "fps": 30, "cache_mib": 32 }}
}}
```

# 8. The same plugin in TypeScript

## 8. The same plugin in TypeScript

This step ports the badge logic of step 1 and the table rows of step 3 to TypeScript. The manifest stays the same, and the plugin behaves the same way. The step teaches the build. `ilium plugin build` bundles the TypeScript with Bun, then `componentize-js` turns the bundle into a component named `server.wasm`. The host loads that component through the same Wasmtime path as the Rust build. The Rust code and the TypeScript code are two implementations of one WIT contract, `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Every listing in this step is shown twice, first as **Rust** and then as **TypeScript**, so you can follow the port in either direction. The step ends with a short section that uses three widgets of the extended widget set (`badge`, `spinner` and `progress-row`) from both languages.

### You will need

- [Tutorial step 7](/pages/tutorial-07-ambient-scene/) finished, or at least the Rust project from step 3. The TypeScript port is a second project next to it, called `agent-tools-ts`.
- Bun 1.2 or later. It is the only global tool. `bun install` installs `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, which pins `jco` and `componentize-js` exactly. Run TypeScript with Bun, never with `node`.
- The `ilium` binary, with its `plugin` subcommand.
- Server grants `agent.read` (activity events) and `tree.decorate` (set and clear badges). The manifest below declares both.

### What changed from the Rust version

- The badge logic lives in `src/badge.ts`. It imports only types from the SDK, so it has no host calls, and `bun test` runs it directly.
- `src/server.ts` is the entry point. Its `definePlugin` call exports the `lifecycle` and `handler` objects that a server plugin needs.
- The manifest is the step 1 manifest, unchanged. The id `example.agent-tools` matches step 1, so both builds describe the same plugin.
- The build output is a component, the same as the Rust build. The host does not know which language made it.
- Names follow the SDK rule for TypeScript: camelCase for functions and fields, PascalCase for types, and kebab-case strings for variant tags and enum values.

### The sequence

A TypeScript build has two stages: the bundle, then the component. Bun makes the bundle. `componentize-js` embeds it in the WIT world, which it reads from `node_modules/@ilium/plugin-sdk/wit/`. The project never holds a copy of the WIT files. Both stages run on your machine.

### The surface this step uses

| Name | Import path | Kind and meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `definePlugin` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk` | Function. Declares the side and the export objects, and returns them. |
| `lifecycle.activate(context)` | export | Runs once when the instance starts. `context.plugin` holds the plugin id. |
| `handler.onEvents(batch)` | export | Receives a batch of events and returns submissions. Required on the server. |
| `Event`, `Submission` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk` | Types. `Submission` has `intent`, `correlation` and `dedupKey`. |
| `AgentActivity` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types` | String union: `'none'`, `'working'`, `'idle'`, `'awaiting-approval'`, `'done'`, `'menu'`. |
| `AgentActivityEvent` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types` | Payload with `node: bigint`, `previous`, `current` and `revision: bigint`. |
| `SetDecorationSpec`, `DecorationKey` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types` | Payloads of the `set-decoration` and `clear-decoration` intents. |
| `span(text, style?)`, `role(name)` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types` | Build styled text. `role` takes a colour role name such as `'accent'`. |
| `log(level, message)` | `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log` | Writes one line to the plugin log. |

### The pure logic

`badge.ts` is the port of `badge.rs`. It contains no host calls. The type import is erased at build time. The Rust original is listed after the TypeScript file, in the section "The Rust version of the same function".

**TypeScript**

```typescript
// src/badge.ts. Pure logic: type imports only, no host calls.
import type { AgentActivity } from "@ilium/plugin-sdk/types";

export type BadgeRole = "accent" | "muted" | "warning";

export interface Badge {
  text: string;
  role: BadgeRole;
}

/** Returns the badge for an activity, or undefined when the row needs no badge. */
export function badgeFor(activity: AgentActivity): Badge | undefined {
  switch (activity) {
    case "working":
      return { text: "working", role: "accent" };
    case "idle":
      return { text: "idle", role: "muted" };
    case "awaiting-approval":
      return { text: "approve?", role: "warning" };
    case "none":
    case "done":
    case "menu":
      return undefined;
    default:
      return assertNever(activity);
  }
}

/** A new activity in the generated bindings is a type error here, not a silent fallback. */
function assertNever(value: never): never {
  throw new Error(`unhandled activity: ${String(value)}`);
}
```

The tests run with `bun test` in TypeScript and with `cargo test` in Rust. They cover the same three cases.

**TypeScript**

```typescript
// src/badge.test.ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { badgeFor } from "./badge";

test("working agent gets accent badge", () => {
  expect(badgeFor("working")).toEqual({ text: "working", role: "accent" });
});

test("awaiting approval gets warning badge", () => {
  expect(badgeFor("awaiting-approval")?.role).toBe("warning");
});

test("none, done and menu have no badge", () => {
  expect(badgeFor("none")).toBeUndefined();
  expect(badgeFor("done")).toBeUndefined();
  expect(badgeFor("menu")).toBeUndefined();
});
```

**Rust**

```rust
// src/badge.rs, test module. The same three cases as src/badge.test.ts.
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn working_agent_gets_accent_badge() {
        let badge = badge_for(AgentActivity::Working).expect("working has a badge");
        assert_eq!(badge.text, "working");
        assert_eq!(badge.role, ColorRole::Accent);
    }

    #[test]
    fn awaiting_approval_gets_warning_badge() {
        assert_eq!(badge_for(AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval).expect("badge").role, ColorRole::Warning);
    }

    #[test]
    fn none_done_and_menu_have_no_badge() {
        assert!(badge_for(AgentActivity::None).is_none());
        assert!(badge_for(AgentActivity::Done).is_none());
        assert!(badge_for(AgentActivity::Menu).is_none());
    }
}
```

### The host glue

`server.ts` imports the SDK and turns each activity change into an intent. The names of the generated tags keep the WIT spelling, so the tag is `'agent-activity-changed'`. The Rust glue (step 1) matches `Event::AgentActivityChanged` instead, and both builds submit the same intent.

**TypeScript**

```typescript
// src/server.ts. Server side of agent-tools, the TypeScript port of step 1.
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from "@ilium/plugin-sdk";
import { log } from "@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log";
import {
  role,
  span,
  type AgentActivityEvent,
  type DecorationKey,
  type SetDecorationSpec,
} from "@ilium/plugin-sdk/types";
import { badgeFor, type Badge } from "./badge";

const BADGE_SLOT = "badge";

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: "server",
  activate(context) {
    log("info", `agent-tools active in ${context.plugin}`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === "agent-activity-changed") {
        submissions.push(decorate(event.val));
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});

/** Decorates one agent row. An activity without a badge clears the slot. */
function decorate(change: AgentActivityEvent): Submission {
  const badge = badgeFor(change.current);
  const intent = badge
    ? { tag: "set-decoration" as const, val: setDecorationFor(change.node, badge) }
    : { tag: "clear-decoration" as const, val: clearFor(change.node) };
  // The revision is a u64, so it is a bigint. Plugin correlation numbers stay below 2^63.
  return { intent, correlation: change.revision, dedupKey: undefined };
}

function setDecorationFor(node: bigint, badge: Badge): SetDecorationSpec {
  return {
    node,
    slot: BADGE_SLOT,
    content: [span(badge.text, { fg: role(badge.role) })],
    icon: undefined,
    sortKey: undefined,
    persist: false,
  };
}

function clearFor(node: bigint): DecorationKey {
  return { node, slot: BADGE_SLOT };
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs. Server side of agent-tools, the Rust original (step 1, shortened).
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{DecorationKey, SetDecorationSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Style;

mod badge;
use badge::badge_for;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct AgentTools;

impl Lifecycle for AgentTools {}

impl Handler for AgentTools {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        batch
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|event| match event {
                Event::AgentActivityChanged(change) => Some(decorate(change)),
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

fn decorate(change: AgentActivityEvent) -> Submission {
    let intent = match badge_for(change.current) {
        Some(badge) => Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
            node: change.node,
            slot: "badge".into(),
            content: vec![Span::styled(badge.text, Style::role(badge.role))],
            icon: None,
            sort_key: None,
            persist: false,
        }),
        None => Intent::ClearDecoration(DecorationKey { node: change.node, slot: "badge".into() }),
    };
    Submission { intent, correlation: change.revision, dedup_key: None }
}
```

Points to notice:

- In TypeScript `node` is a `bigint`; in Rust it is a `u64`. WIT `u64` maps to `bigint` in the TypeScript binding. `Number(node)` loses precision above 2^53, so the code never converts it.
- `dedupKey` is `undefined`. Decorations need no de-duplication, as in step 1.
- `persist: false` keeps the badge out of the snapshot. A restart clears the badges until the next activity change.
- `clear-decoration` on an empty slot returns `ok`, so the code does not check the slot first.

### The Rust version of the same function

**Rust**

The Rust `badge_for` uses the SDK's `AgentActivity` enum and a `match`. The compiler proves that every case is handled, as the `assertNever` line does in TypeScript.

```rust
// src/badge.rs. Same logic as src/badge.ts.
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::ColorRole;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

pub struct Badge {
    pub text: &'static str,
    pub role: ColorRole,
}

pub fn badge_for(activity: AgentActivity) -> Option<Badge> {
    match activity {
        AgentActivity::Working => Some(Badge { text: "working", role: ColorRole::Accent }),
        AgentActivity::Idle => Some(Badge { text: "idle", role: ColorRole::Muted }),
        AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval => {
            Some(Badge { text: "approve?", role: ColorRole::Warning })
        }
        AgentActivity::None | AgentActivity::Done | AgentActivity::Menu => None,
    }
}
```

The two versions differ in three places. Rust returns `Option<Badge>` and TypeScript returns `Badge | undefined`. Rust uses `ColorRole` values, and TypeScript uses the role names of `role()`. TypeScript reports a new activity only in a type check, not at run time, because the bindings are generated from the same WIT as the Rust enum.

### The table rows of step 3

The client panel of step 3 builds table rows. `tableRow` is pure text formatting, so it ports directly. The panel layout stays in the Rust client. To use the port, add the client side to the project and import `tableRow` from `src/client.ts`. The Rust original is listed below the TypeScript file.

**TypeScript**

```typescript
// src/table.ts. Row text for the agents panel, the port of step 3.
export interface AgentRow {
  name: string;
  activity: string;
  ageSeconds: number;
}

/** Formats one agent row. The age column reads "42 s" or "7 min". */
export function tableRow(row: AgentRow): string[] {
  const age =
    row.ageSeconds < 60 ? `${row.ageSeconds} s` : `${Math.floor(row.ageSeconds / 60)} min`;
  return [row.name, row.activity, age];
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
// src/table.rs. Row text for the agents panel (step 3).
pub struct AgentRow {
    pub name: String,
    pub activity: String,
    pub age_seconds: u64,
}

/// Formats one agent row. The age column reads "42 s" or "7 min".
pub fn table_row(row: &AgentRow) -> Vec<String> {
    let age = if row.age_seconds < 60 {
        format!("{} s", row.age_seconds)
    } else {
        format!("{} min", row.age_seconds / 60)
    };
    vec![row.name.clone(), row.activity.clone(), age]
}
```

### Build and test

Install the packages, run the tests, then build the component.

```bash
bun install
bun test
ilium plugin build agent-tools-ts
```

`ilium plugin build` prints JSONL, one object per line. Its `artifact` line gives the path and the SHA-256 of `server.wasm`, which is written next to `manifest.json`. Each author runs this build on their own machine. Then `ilium plugin install` verifies the inventory before it installs the plugin.

To replay events against the built component without the running app, use `ilium plugin test agent-tools-ts --fixture <file.json>`. The fixture holds `tree`, `panes`, `agents`, `settings` and `events`, with events written as `{"tag": "...", "val": ...}`. For trap positions in `src/`, build with `ilium plugin build --debug`, which keeps the bundle's source map.

### Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Activity is `none`, `done` or `menu` | `clear-decoration` for the badge slot, which returns `ok`. |
| The node was removed before the submission is accepted | `refused(not-found)`. |
| The slot `badge` is not declared in the manifest | `refused(invalid-argument)`. Declare it, as above. |
| More than 4,096 decorations for one server instance (default limit) | `refused(quota-exceeded)`. |
| `onEvents` runs longer than 20 ms (default `event_deadline_ms`) | Trap. The host restarts the plugin under the restart rule. |
| An exception is thrown inside `onEvents` | Trap, handled the same way. Catch errors that the handler can expect. |
| A new activity appears in a later SDK version | A type error at `assertNever`, found at build time. |

The limits and their codes are listed in [errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

### What you see

Each badge appears on its row as soon as the activity changes. The text uses the accent, muted or warning colour of the active theme. The kernel draws the badge, and the plugin never draws anything itself. A row whose activity is `done` has no badge. The tree below is the same tree as step 1, drawn by the TypeScript build. The Rust build draws the identical tree.

### Using three more widgets from the port

Further widgets are available that a client view can draw without a plugin call per frame. This part adds a small view to the client side of the port. It shows the number of open agents as a `badge`, a `spinner` while an index job runs, and a `progress-row` for the job. Nothing here changes the server build above.

Needs: `ui.panels` on the client side (the manifest of step 3 already has it). The widget names, props and builder argument order are those of [the widgets index](/pages/widgets-index/): the required prop is the first argument, and every optional prop is a chained setter in Rust and a field of the props object in TypeScript.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/views.rs. Client side. ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree; types::layout::{Constraint, Direction}; types::ui::{ProgressState, SpinnerFrames}; types::text::Tone
impl Views for AgentTools {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let open = tree.badge().count(self.open_agents).tone(Tone::Info).key("open");
        let busy = tree.spinner(SpinnerFrames::Braille).interval_ms(100).label("Indexing 412 sessions");
        let job = tree.progress_row("Indexing 412 sessions")
            .state(ProgressState::Running).percent(37.0).message("session 152 of 412").key("job");
        let root = tree.layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(1)])
            .child(open).child(busy).child(job);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
// src/client.ts. Client side of the port.
import { definePlugin } from "@ilium/plugin-sdk";
import { tree, layout, badge, spinner, progressRow } from "@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build";

export const { lifecycle, views } = definePlugin({
  side: "client",
  render(_view, _area) {
    return tree(
      layout({ direction: "vertical", constraints: [{ tag: "length", val: 1 }, { tag: "length", val: 1 }, { tag: "length", val: 1 }] }, [
        badge({ key: "open", count: openAgents, tone: "info" }),
        spinner("braille", { intervalMs: 100, label: "Indexing 412 sessions" }),
        progressRow("Indexing 412 sessions", { key: "job", state: "running", percent: 37, message: "session 152 of 412" }),
      ]),
    );
  },
});
```

The host steps the spinner frames itself, so the plugin is called only when `openAgents` or the job percent changes. With reduced motion the spinner shows one static frame. The view draws like this in the panel:
