# 9. Package and share

## 9. Package and share

This step packs the project into one `.iliumpkg` file that another person can install. The archive holds the manifest, the components built in steps 7 and 8, the assets, the help topic and the sounds. It also holds an inventory with the length and the SHA-256 of every entry. The person who receives the file sees a review dialog that lists each capability by side before the plugin is enabled.

Packing needs no grant and no code change, and it does not care which language made the components. A package can mix Rust and TypeScript components. The steps below produce an unsigned package, which the platform classes as tier T3. The section "Sign for T2" shows how to add a publisher signature, which makes the package tier T2.

### You will need

- [Tutorial step 7](/pages/tutorial-07-ambient-scene/) finished, with `server.wasm`, `client.wasm` and `scene.wasm` built. `ilium plugin build` writes them to `dist/`.
- [Tutorial step 8](/pages/tutorial-08-typescript/) is optional. A Rust build and a TypeScript build pack the same way.
- The `ilium` command with its `plugin` subcommands. `ilium plugin --help` lists them.
- A WAV (PCM) or OGG Vorbis file for each `contributes.sounds` entry, and a Markdown file for each help topic. A missing or differently formatted file fails the install check.
- Assets stay within the package size cap: 64 MiB for T2 and T3 packages, and 256 MiB for T1 bundled plugins. A larger package is refused with `manifest.asset-size`, as is a font asset over 4 MiB.
- A Linux machine for the person who installs the package when it is T2 or T3. Windows and macOS refuse T2 and T3 packages at install.

### Build the components first

`ilium plugin pack` packs what `ilium plugin build` wrote to `dist/`. Run the build for each project once, in the language you used. Both builds write the same files.

**Rust**

```bash
cd agent-tools
ilium plugin build
```

**TypeScript**

```bash
cd agent-tools-ts
bun install
bun test
ilium plugin build
```

### Commands of this step

This step uses `ilium plugin pack`, `inspect --verify`, `keygen`, `sign`, `trust` and `install`. Every flag, exit code and output record is in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/).

### What changed from step 7

- `manifest.json` gains a `description`, which the review dialog shows. The `publisher` field is shown in the dialog too.
- A source manifest may omit `files`. `pack` writes that field, so you never type the lengths or hashes yourself.
- `contributes.help` names the one help topic in `help/`. `contributes.sounds` names the sound file from step 4.
- No Rust or TypeScript code changes. The contract also has manifest keys and grants, shown under "Manifest keys for contributions and grants" below. A plugin that does not use them packs exactly as before.

### The package layout

The package is a deterministic ZIP32 archive. Its entries are stored without compression, the paths are sorted, the timestamps are fixed and no extra fields are written. Two builds of the same files therefore produce the same bytes.

| Entry | Required | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | yes | The manifest, with the `files` inventory that `pack` writes. |
| `server.wasm`, `client.wasm`, `scene.wasm` | for each declared side | Components that target `ilium:server/base`, `ilium:client/base` or `ilium:anim/base`. |
| `assets/**` | no | Read-only files, visible through the `package` file scope. |
| `help/*.md` | no | Help topics named in `contributes.help`. |
| `sounds/*` | no | Sound files named in `contributes.sounds`. |
| `src/**` | no | Sources for review. The host never loads them. |
| `signature` | T2 only | A detached Ed25519 signature over the canonical bytes of `manifest.json`. |

Every entry except `manifest.json` and `signature` must appear in `files`, with its length in bytes and its SHA-256 in lowercase hexadecimal. Each component also carries an `ilium:api-version` section. Its version must equal the manifest `api` value.

### Manifest

The source manifest in the project omits `files`:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.agent-tools",
  "name": "Agent tools",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Agent badges, a TODO scanner, a notes pane and an ambient scene.",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["job-runner"]
  },
  "client": { "entry": "client.wasm", "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["views"] },
  "scene": { "entry": "scene.wasm", "world": "ilium:anim/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["agent.read", "agent.control", "tree.read", "tree.decorate", "notify.desktop",
      "sound.play", "fs.read:project", "jobs.run"],
    "client": ["agent.read", "tree.read", "tree.metadata", "ui.panels", "editor.edit",
      "topics.subscribe:example.agent-tools/*", "panes.create", "panes.provide-kind"],
    "scene": []
  },
  "contributes": {
    "help": [{ "id": "agent-tools", "file": "help/agent-tools.md", "title": "Agent tools" }],
    "sounds": [{ "id": "finished", "file": "sounds/finished.wav" }]
  }
}
```

The packed `manifest.json` inside the archive gains the inventory. The entries are sorted by path:

```json
"files": [
  { "path": "client.wasm", "length": 524288, "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex digits>" },
  { "path": "help/agent-tools.md", "length": 2048, "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex digits>" },
  { "path": "scene.wasm", "length": 262144, "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex digits>" },
  { "path": "server.wasm", "length": 1048576, "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex digits>" },
  { "path": "sounds/finished.wav", "length": 40960, "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex digits>" }
]
```

The lengths and hashes shown here are placeholders. Your build writes the real values.

Points to notice:

- The help topic gets a global id, `example.agent-tools/agent-tools`. Topic ids always start with the plugin id.
- `description` and `publisher` appear in the review dialog. The dialog does not show the code.
- The `files` entry is required in a packed manifest only. The source manifest may leave it out.

### Manifest keys for contributions and grants

Contribution keys and grants need nothing special at pack time, because `pack` hashes whatever the manifest names. This fragment adds a tree toolbar button and a status bar segment to the source manifest. Both belong to the `ui.chrome` grant, which goes into the client list. The command id refers to a command that the plugin declares under `contributes.commands`, as in step 2.

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "client": ["ui.panels", "ui.chrome", "notify.toast"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "tree_toolbar": [
      { "id": "scan", "icon": "search", "label": "Scan TODO", "command": "example.agent-tools/scan",
        "caption": "TODO" }
    ],
    "status_segments": [
      { "id": "todo-count", "priority": 40, "max_width": 16 }
    ]
  }
}
```

Fixed caps apply per plugin: 4 `tree_toolbar` entries and 2 `status_segments`. More than the cap refuses the package with `manifest.contribution-limit`. The key `limits_tier: "first-party"` is accepted only for bundled T1 plugins whose id starts with `ilium.`; any other package that sets it is refused with `manifest.limits-tier` (decision D12). A third-party package therefore never sets it.

Nine of the grants are high risk: `terminal.history`, `terminal.input-lock`, `terminal.raw-input`, `panes.lifecycle`, `tree.restructure`, `sessions.cross`, `process.long-lived`, `agent.transcript` and `settings.read-kernel:api`. They always need an explicit choice, even for a T1 plugin, and the dialog draws them in the warning style.

### Pack and verify

Run the pack command from the project folder:

```bash
ilium plugin pack
```

The command prints one line per event. For this package the output has this shape:

```jsonl
{"type":"progress","step":"pack","message":"Computing the files inventory of 5 entries"}
{"type":"artifact","path":"dist/example.agent-tools-0.1.0.iliumpkg","sha256":"<hex>","bytes":187941}
{"type":"summary","duration_ms":412,"warnings":0,"errors":0}
{"type":"result","ok":true,"exit_code":0}
```

The `artifact` line gives the path relative to the project folder, the SHA-256 of the archive and its size in bytes. Use `--out <file>` to write the archive somewhere else.

To check the archive without installing it, run the verify command. It recomputes every hash of the package and compares it with the `files` list:

```bash
ilium plugin inspect dist/example.agent-tools-0.1.0.iliumpkg --verify
```

A clean package prints no `diff` record and exits with 0. A changed file prints one `diff` record per difference, and the command exits with 1 and the code `inspect.hash-mismatch`. The command works offline and needs no running Ilium.

### Sign for T2 (optional)

A T2 package is signed by a publisher key that the user trusts. It runs in the same sandbox as a T3 package, and the review dialog shows its signature state. Create the key pair once for each publisher, and keep the private key outside the project tree:

```bash
ilium plugin keygen --publisher-id com.example --publisher "Example Developer" --out ~/keys/example
ilium plugin sign dist/example.agent-tools-0.1.0.iliumpkg --key ~/keys/example/publisher.key
```

The `--publisher` value must match the `publisher` field of the manifest, and the plugin `id` must start with the publisher id and a dot (`com.example.`). Otherwise `sign` stops with `sign.publisher-mismatch`, or the install stops with `manifest.publisher-mismatch` or `manifest.id-publisher`.

Sign the archive last. A later `pack` writes a new archive without a signature, so the signature must be added again. The person who installs the package needs your `publisher.pub` file. They add it once:

```bash
ilium plugin trust add ~/keys/example/publisher.pub
ilium plugin install dist/example.agent-tools-0.1.0.iliumpkg
```

If the key is not trusted yet, the install dialog offers `Trust publisher` and shows the key fingerprint. Declining refuses the install.

### Review dialog

The dialog appears before the plugin is enabled. It shows the name, the version, the publisher, the package state and the description. Below that it lists one row per capability, grouped by side. A row with a HIGH label needs an explicit choice from the user.

The dialog is the canonical review dialog of [Security](/pages/security/#verifying-a-package). This is the same dialog for an unsigned package.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Install example.agent-tools 0.1.0 ──────────╮</span>
│ Name (self-declared): Example Developer      │
│ Unsigned T3 · dev badge after install        │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-dim">Server</span>                                       │
│ [x] Read agent events ………………… agent.read     │
│ [ ] <span class="t-warn">HIGH</span> Control agents … agent.control      │
│ [x] Read the workspace tree …… tree.read     │
│ [x] Read project files …… fs.read:project    │
│ <span class="t-dim">Client</span>                                       │
│ [x] Show panels …………………………… ui.panels        │
│ [ ] <span class="t-warn">HIGH</span> Read the agent transcript           │
│     agent.transcript                         │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Cancel   <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Install               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The review dialog for an unsigned package. HIGH rows start unchecked. The rows are shortened for the page, and the real dialog lists every grant.</figcaption>
</figure>

Points to notice:

- Normal rows are checked by default. HIGH rows are unchecked, and the user checks each one. `agent.control` is HIGH in this example.
- Keys: Up and Down move between rows, Space toggles a row, Enter activates the focused button and Escape cancels.
- A declined capability stays unchecked and dimmed. The plugin still loads without it. Its calls for that capability return `not-permitted`, and each first refusal writes a warn line to the log.
- Grants are per side. `agent.read` on the server and `agent.read` on the client are two separate rows.
- The high-risk grants (`agent.transcript` above) are drawn the same way as `agent.control`: unchecked, with the word HIGH.
- `Details` shows the description, the publisher key, the number and size of the files, the requested limits and the contributions.

Some capabilities ask again at first use, because the grant alone does not name the target. These are separate small prompts and not part of the install dialog:

- `open-external` asks once for each target origin, and the answer is remembered for the plugin (decision D25).
- `http:setting:<key>` hosts, which the plugin reads from its own setting, ask for each new host before the first request (decision D23).
- Geocoding through `location.geocode` shows a consent notice on first use, because place names go to the host's geocoding provider (decision D14).

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭  ≡ ● · Open link─────────────────────────────────────╮</span>
│ example.agent-tools wants to open                    │
│ https://docs.example.com/aurora in your browser.     │
│                                                      │
│        <span class="t-dim">N Cancel</span>        Y Open                        │
│ <span class="t-dim">Y/N answer · Enter confirm · Esc cancel</span>              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The confirmation for <code>open-external</code>, in the confirm style of the real client with the <code>Y</code> and <code>N</code> key hints.</figcaption>
</figure>

Install the unsigned package with the flag that the T3 tier needs:

```bash
ilium plugin install dist/example.agent-tools-0.1.0.iliumpkg --allow-unsigned
```

Without `--allow-unsigned`, the install stops before the dialog.

### After install

The plugin appears in Settings > Plugins. A T3 plugin keeps a `dev` badge there. Read the first lines of its log to confirm that the archive loads:

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.agent-tools --tail 3
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:02</span> <span class="t-ok">info </span>  example.agent-tools activated
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:03</span> <span class="t-ok">info </span>  example.agent-tools ready
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:04</span> <span class="t-warn">warn </span>  example.agent-tools refused notify: not-permitted
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The warn line shows a declined grant. A clean log has no warn or error lines from the first activation.</figcaption>
</figure>

Revoke a grant later with Settings > Plugins > example.agent-tools > Capabilities, or with `ilium plugin grants example.agent-tools --revoke notify.desktop`.

### Share

A registry is optional (decision D27). Without one, you share the file. With one, `ilium plugin publish <file> --registry <url>` uploads a signed package to a registry ([Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/)). The package is a file, and you pass it on by any channel you choose, such as e-mail, a shared folder or a file host. If the package is signed, send `publisher.pub` with it, and send the SHA-256 of the package and the key fingerprint by another route. The registry protocol is in [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/), and the steps in [Publishing guide](/pages/guide-publishing/). The full release routine, with changelog, support and key loss, is in [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/). Before every release you MUST run `ilium plugin check`, `lint` and `test`. [AUT-320]

- A newer version of an installed id is an update. The dialog shows only the new capabilities.
- A lower version is refused unless the person adds `--allow-downgrade`.
- Before you share, install the archive once on your own machine and read the log.

### Edge cases and errors

Each install check that fails writes one JSONL `error` line with its code and, when known, the file. The install stops before any code loads:

```jsonl
{"type":"error","code":"manifest.file-hash","message":"SHA-256 differs","file":"server.wasm"}
```

| Code or result | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.file-unlisted` | An entry is in the archive but not in `files`. | Run `pack` again. |
| `manifest.file-missing` | A listed file is absent, for example a declared `scene.wasm` that was never built, or a sound or help file that the manifest names. | Build the component or add the file, then pack again. |
| `manifest.file-length`, `manifest.file-hash` | A file changed after `pack`. | Pack again, and sign again if the package is T2. |
| `manifest.api-version` | A component was built against an older API, so its `ilium:api-version` differs from `api`. | Rebuild with the current SDK. |
| `manifest.signature-invalid` | The T2 signature does not verify. | Sign the final archive again with the right key. |
| `manifest.publisher-mismatch` | The manifest `publisher` differs from the key's recorded publisher. | Use the same name in `keygen` and in the manifest. |
| `manifest.grant-tier` | A T2 or T3 package asks for `process.run:sh`. The shell grant is for T1 bundled plugins only. | Remove the grant, or use a fixed program name. |
| `manifest.id-reserved` | The id starts with `ilium.`, which first-party plugins use. | Choose your own reverse-DNS id. |
| `manifest.unknown-key` | A manifest key is outside the schema, often a typo. | Remove or correct the key. |
| `manifest.sound-id-taken` | A sound id repeats, or it equals `chirping`, the bundled sound. | Give the sound a unique id. |
| `manifest.asset-size` | Package assets over 64 MiB (256 MiB for T1), or a font over 4 MiB. | Drop or shrink assets. |
| `manifest.limits-tier` | `limits_tier: "first-party"` in a package that is not a bundled T1 `ilium.` plugin. | Remove the key. |
| `manifest.contribution-limit`, `manifest.contribution-target` | More entries of a contribution key than its cap, or an `applies_to` or `slot` that names an unknown target or another plugin's slot. | Reduce the entries or name an own slot. |
| `manifest.when-key`, `manifest.visible-when`, `manifest.menu-depth` | An unknown `when` key, a `visible_when` that points to another plugin's key or forms a cycle, or a static menu nested deeper than 2. | Correct the key or flatten the menu. |
| `manifest.catalog-unknown`, `manifest.settings-source` | A `source` that names no known catalogue, or a row with both `options` and `source`, or neither. | Declare the catalogue or fix the row. |
| `manifest.row-format`, `manifest.cli-field`, `manifest.client-request-unknown`, `manifest.scene-prerender` | An invalid `item_format`, `steps` ladder or `special_values`, a bad `cli` field, a `client_requests` entry that the other side does not match, or `prerender` values out of range. | Correct the named key path. |
| Install refused, no flag | An unsigned package was installed without `--allow-unsigned`. | Sign the package, or add the flag. |
| Install refused, version | A lower version was installed over a newer one. | Add `--allow-downgrade` if the downgrade is intended. |
| Install refused, platform | A T2 or T3 package on Windows or macOS. | Install on Linux, or use a T1 bundled plugin. |

# 10. A settings tab of your own

## 10. A settings tab of your own

This step adds a tab to the Settings screen. The tab is called Clipboard history, and it uses seven of the 18 row types: a toggle, a choice, a number with a unit, a text field (also used as a secret), a keybinding, a file path and a button. One toggle is stored per project. The host draws the page from the manifest, saves each value as the user changes it, and sends `settings-changed` to the plugin. The plugin reads the saved values, reacts when they change, and checks one of them before the host saves it. The step also shows a row that hides itself, a row that applies after restart, a value stored per project, and the search filter. Every row type is on the [row gallery](/pages/reference-settings-rows/).

The tab belongs to the plugin. Its values are stored in `[plugins."example.clipboard-history"]` in `config.toml`, and the tab needs no grant. The kernel keeps every built-in tab as it was: a plugin tab can be added, but never changed.

Tutorial plugin: `example.clipboard-history`, version 0.1.0, API `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. The client side is shown in Rust and in TypeScript in every step.

### You will need

- A clipboard-history project with a client side that records copied text and exports `handler`. This step adds the settings tab to that code.
- Grants: none new. The plugin's own values are always granted, so `capabilities.client` stays empty for this step. The clipboard grants of the project stay as they are.
- Rust: the crates `serde` and `serde_json` (already in the project) and `regex-lite`, added for the check in step 5. TypeScript: nothing more, because `RegExp` is built in.
- The SDKs: the Rust crate `ilium_plugin_sdk` and the TypeScript package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.

### The surface this step uses

| Area | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest | `contributes.settings[]`, `kind: "tab"` | A tab in the rail. Its global id is `example.clipboard-history/history`. |
| Manifest | `sections[]`, row `type` | Each section has one `scope`. Value rows own a `key`. A `button` has an `id` and stores no value. |
| Manifest row field | `visible_when`, `scope: "project"`, `applies: "restart"` | Hide a row, store a value per project, mark a value that applies after restart. |
| Host | `settings::get_json()` / `getJson()` | Every own key, with the defaults filled in. |
| Export | `settings-validate` | Optional. Declared in `client.exports`. 100 ms, user and reset origins only. |
| Event | `settings-changed` | `SettingsChange { keys, origin, scope }`. |

`origin` is `user`, `plugin`, `reset`, `other-plugin` or `file`. `keys` is sorted and has no duplicates.

### The flow

A row on the page is saved by the host, not by the plugin. The host checks the value against the schema, calls the plugin's `settings-validate` for user and reset changes, and writes the value. Only then does it send `settings-changed`. A refused save keeps the old value, and the error replaces the row's description.

### Step 1: the manifest

The manifest gains two commands, one keybinding and one settings entry of kind `tab`. The button and the keybinding both name a command of the plugin, so both commands are listed under `contributes.commands`. The tab has three sections: Capture holds the three values of the history itself, Picker holds the secret filter and the key, and Sync and files holds the project toggle, the secret token, the path and the button.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.clipboard-history",
  "name": "Clipboard history",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Keeps a searchable history of copied text.",
  "icon": "clipboard-list",
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["settings-validate"]
  },
  "capabilities": { "client": [] },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "open-picker", "title": "Clipboard history: open picker" },
      { "id": "clear", "title": "Clipboard history: clear" }
    ],
    "keybindings": [
      { "command": "open-picker", "chord": "ctrl+alt+v", "mode": "global" }
    ],
    "settings": [
      {
        "kind": "tab",
        "id": "history",
        "title": "Clipboard history",
        "short_title": "Clipboard",
        "icon": "clipboard-list",
        "glyph": "⎘",
        "after": "text-triggers",
        "order": 500,
        "render": "rows",
        "keywords": ["copy", "paste"],
        "sections": [
          {
            "id": "capture",
            "title": "Capture",
            "scope": "client",
            "rows": [
              { "type": "toggle", "key": "enabled", "title": "Keep history",
                "default": true,
                "description": "Record text copied in panes and the editor." },
              { "type": "choice", "key": "store", "title": "Store", "default": "text",
                "options": [
                  { "value": "text", "title": "Text only" },
                  { "value": "rich", "title": "Text and HTML" }
                ],
                "description": "Which clipboard content is kept." },
              { "type": "number", "key": "max_entries", "title": "Maximum entries",
                "minimum": 10, "maximum": 5000, "step": 10, "unit": "entries",
                "default": 500,
                "description": "Oldest entries are removed first." }
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "picker",
            "title": "Picker",
            "scope": "client",
            "rows": [
              { "type": "toggle", "key": "hide_secrets", "title": "Hide secrets",
                "default": true,
                "description": "Skip copies that look like a key or a token." },
              { "type": "text", "key": "ignore_pattern", "title": "Ignore pattern",
                "max_length": 200, "placeholder": "regular expression",
                "default": "^sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}$",
                "visible_when": { "key": "hide_secrets", "equals": true },
                "description": "Copies that match are never stored." },
              { "type": "keybinding", "key": "picker_key", "title": "Picker key",
                "command": "open-picker", "default": "ctrl+alt+v",
                "description": "Opens the history picker." }
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "sync",
            "title": "Sync and files",
            "scope": "client",
            "rows": [
              { "type": "toggle", "key": "per_project", "title": "Separate per project",
                "default": false, "scope": "project",
                "description": "Keep one history for each project." },
              { "type": "text", "key": "sync_token", "title": "Sync token",
                "secret": true, "reveal_last": 4, "max_length": 128, "default": "",
                "applies": "restart",
                "description": "Stored as a secret. Applies after restart." },
              { "type": "path", "key": "history_file", "title": "History file",
                "picker": "file", "extensions": ["db"], "default": "",
                "description": "File picker; other folders need fs access." },
              { "type": "button", "id": "clear_now", "title": "Clear history",
                "label": "Clear now", "command": "clear",
                "confirm": "Delete every stored entry?" }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Points to notice:

- The keys `enabled`, `store`, `max_entries`, `hide_secrets`, `ignore_pattern`, `picker_key`, `per_project`, `sync_token` and `history_file` must be unique across the whole plugin. A clash fails the install with `manifest.settings-key-clash`. The button's `id` shares the same namespace.
- Every `default` must pass its own row. `max_entries` defaults to 500, which sits inside 10 to 5000. A default outside the range fails with `manifest.settings-default`.
- `visible_when` on `ignore_pattern` uses the shape `{ "key", "equals" }` on one own key. A hidden row keeps its value, and search skips it.
- `scope: "project"` on `per_project` stores that value for the open project. The project value wins while that project is open.
- `applies: "restart"` on `sync_token` draws the marker `↻` after the value and the note `Applies after restart.`
- `secret: true` with `reveal_last: 4` masks the value as `••••` and shows its last four characters. The kernel keeps the value out of logs.
- A `keybinding` row stores a remap of one of the plugin's own keybindings. Its command must be listed in `contributes.commands`, or the install fails with `manifest.settings-command`.
- `after` places the tab straight after Text Triggers. The tail of the rail (Debug, API, About and Setup) is pinned, so no plugin tab can appear after it.

<div class="note">
<p>The tab's first line reads "Added by example.clipboard-history 0.1.0", and each section title is drawn in capitals. The plugin cannot change either one, because the kernel draws them.</p>
</div>

#### What you see

Before the plugin is installed, the rail has no Clipboard entry. After it is enabled, the tab appears after Text Triggers. Its short title is used, because the full title does not fit the rail at 80 columns.

### Step 2: read the values

The plugin reads its values with one call. The call always returns every key of the tab with its default filled in, so the types need no optional fields. The plugin reads the values once when it activates, and again each time `settings-changed` arrives (step 3).

The `Config` type mirrors the keys. A `choice` row stores its option value, so `store` is a string. A `number` row stores an integer, and a `keybinding` or `path` row stores a string, so all of them map onto plain types. The full files are below. The Rust file is complete; the TypeScript file is complete too.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs. Client side of clipboard-history, 0.1.0.
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::{
    ilium_plugin, Activation, Event, FieldError, Handler, Lifecycle, PluginError,
    SettingsOrigin, Submission,
};
use serde::Deserialize;

/// The values of the `history` tab, keyed as in the manifest.
#[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
struct Config {
    enabled: bool,
    store: String,
    max_entries: u32,
    hide_secrets: bool,
    ignore_pattern: String,
    picker_key: String,
    per_project: bool,
    sync_token: String,
    history_file: String,
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ClipboardHistory {
    config: Config,
    entries: Vec<String>,
}

impl ClipboardHistory {
    /// Reads the saved values. A value that does not parse keeps the old config.
    fn reload(&mut self) {
        match serde_json::from_str::<Config>(&settings::get_json()) {
            Ok(config) => self.config = config,
            Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("settings not read: {error}")),
        }
    }

    fn trim_history(&mut self) {
        let limit = self.config.max_entries as usize;
        if self.entries.len() > limit {
            let excess = self.entries.len() - limit;
            self.entries.drain(..excess);
        }
    }
}

impl Lifecycle for ClipboardHistory {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        self.reload();
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for ClipboardHistory {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::SettingsChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            self.reload();
            if change.keys.iter().any(|key| key == "max_entries") {
                self.trim_history();
            }
            if change.keys.iter().any(|key| key == "per_project") {
                self.entries.clear(); // the project value picks another history
            }
            if change.origin == SettingsOrigin::Reset {
                log::log(Level::Info, "settings reset from the Settings screen");
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }

    /// Runs before a user or reset save is written. It has 100 ms, so it must
    /// stay pure: no file, network or clipboard access.
    fn settings_validate(&mut self, _patch: &str, merged: &str) -> Result<(), Vec<FieldError>> {
        let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_str::<Config>(merged) else {
            return Ok(()); // the schema check already passed; nothing to add
        };
        match regex_lite::Regex::new(&config.ignore_pattern) {
            Ok(_) => Ok(()),
            Err(_) => Err(vec![FieldError {
                key: "ignore_pattern".into(),
                message: format!("Not a valid pattern: {}", config.ignore_pattern),
            }]),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts. Client side of clipboard-history, 0.1.0.
import { definePlugin, type Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

type Config = {
  enabled: boolean;
  store: 'text' | 'rich';
  max_entries: number;
  hide_secrets: boolean;
  ignore_pattern: string;
  picker_key: string;
  per_project: boolean;
  sync_token: string;
  history_file: string;
};

let config: Config | undefined;
const entries: string[] = [];

/** Reads every key of the tab. get-json fills in the defaults. */
function reload(): void {
  config = JSON.parse(getJson()) as Config;
}

function trimHistory(): void {
  if (!config) return;
  const excess = entries.length - config.max_entries;
  if (excess > 0) entries.splice(0, excess);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {
    reload();
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'settings-changed') continue;
      reload();
      if (event.val.keys.includes('max_entries')) trimHistory();
      if (event.val.keys.includes('per_project')) entries.length = 0;
      if (event.val.origin === 'reset') log('info', 'settings reset from the Settings screen');
    }
    return [];
  },
  /** Runs before a user or reset save is written. 100 ms, no I/O. */
  settingsValidate(_patch: string, merged: string) {
    const next = JSON.parse(merged) as Config;
    try {
      new RegExp(next.ignore_pattern);
      return { ok: true as const };
    } catch {
      return {
        ok: false as const,
        errors: [{ key: 'ignore_pattern', message: `Not a valid pattern: ${next.ignore_pattern}` }],
      };
    }
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- The `Config` type has no optional fields, because the get call fills every default in. A missing key in the JSON is a bug in the host, so the parse fails and the old values stay.
- `reload` does not write anything. Reading is free, and the host never asks the plugin to validate a read.
- `enabled` is read by the capture code of the plugin. Clipboard reads that happen while it is `false` are skipped, so the toggle takes effect at once.

#### What you see

The page reads the same values the plugin reads. The Capture section lists its three rows, with the saved values.

│  Keep history ………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ On ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Record text copied in panes and the editor.        </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│

### Step 3: react to settings-changed

`settings-changed` arrives in the next event batch after a save. It is sent for every change to the plugin's own values, including the changes made by `set-json`, so the handler has one path for all of them. The handler in step 2 reloads the config, trims the history when the limit drops, clears it when the project switch moves, and logs a reset.

Points to notice:

- The handler checks the keys it needs, not the whole list. `keys` is a union of every change in the batch, so a single event can carry two changed keys.
- The `origin` tells the plugin why the value changed. A `plugin` change came from its own code, so the plugin should not write it back.
- Number steps are debounced. The host waits 600 ms after the last step, then writes once and sends one event. A dragged number therefore produces one event, not one per click.
- A value with `scope: "project"` changes when the user opens another project. The same event arrives with the new project value.

#### What you see

The number row is stepped with the arrow keys. The value on the screen changes at once. A dim mark shows that the write is still pending.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Clipboard history · plugin─────────────────────╮

│<span class="t-hi">CAPTURE                                                </span>│
│  Maximum entries ……………………………………………………… -  510  + * ◌  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Oldest entries are removed first.                  </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Number row after one step. The dim <code>◌</code> shows the write is pending. After 600 ms without another step it is written and the mark goes away.</figcaption>
</figure>

The Reset control sits on the section. It asks for confirmation, and the answer sends one merge patch that sets each key of the section to `null`, so the origin of the event is `reset`.

The plugin must not assume that a new `sync_token` is live. It reads the value at activation, so the new token takes effect when the plugin restarts. The marker tells the user the same thing.


### Step 5: validate the ignore pattern

The `text` row `ignore_pattern` holds a regular expression. The schema can check its length, but not whether it compiles. The plugin exports `settings-validate`, which the host calls before it saves a user or reset change. The export is listed in `client.exports`. In Rust it is the method `settings_validate` on the `Handler` impl, and in TypeScript it is the `settingsValidate` member of the `definePlugin` call. Both are in the files of step 2.

Points to notice:

- `merged` is the full value object after the patch, so the check sees the whole config. `patch` holds only what changed.
- The check runs for `user` and `reset` origins only. A `set-json` from the plugin's own code is not checked, because the plugin already knows its rules.
- A check that does not answer within 100 ms refuses the save. The rule is strict on purpose, so keep the function short and free of I/O.
- The field error replaces the row's description with the message, in the warning style, until the next change.

#### What you see

The user types `[a-z` in the Ignore pattern field and leaves the field. The save is refused, and the old value stays in place.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Clipboard history · plugin─────────────────────╮
│                                                       │
│<span class="t-hi">PICKER                                                 </span>│

│<span class="t-warn">    Not a valid pattern: [a-z                          </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>The save was refused by <code>settings-validate</code>. The error replaces the description in the warning style, and the old value is kept.</figcaption>

### Step 7: pack, install and see the tab

Build, pack and install the plugin as in [Tutorial 9](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/). The package is unsigned, so the install needs `--allow-unsigned`.

```bash
ilium plugin build
ilium plugin pack
ilium plugin install dist/example.clipboard-history-0.1.0.iliumpkg --allow-unsigned
ilium plugin logs example.clipboard-history --tail 3
```

The review dialog lists no settings line, because the tab needs no grant. It shows only the clipboard grants of the project. The tab appears in the rail as soon as the plugin is enabled. The plugin starts at `startup`, as the manifest says, so the validation of step 5 is ready before the user opens the page.

A plugin that fails three times in ten minutes is stopped. Its tab then stays in the rail, dimmed, and the page shows the disabled state:

<figure>

<div class="warn">
<p>A plugin that is disabled, or uninstalled, never loses its values. Only <code>ilium plugin uninstall --purge</code> or "Forget settings" on the recovery page deletes them. A reinstall reads the same values again.</p>
</div>

### Test it

Test the manifest first. Change one default on purpose, for example `"default": 0` on `max_entries`, and run `ilium plugin build`. The build reports `manifest.settings-default` with the JSON path of the row. Restore the value afterwards.

Then test the page in the app:

1. Step `Maximum entries` up and down, and check `ilium plugin logs example.clipboard-history --tail 5`. A burst of steps produces one write.
2. Type `[a-z` in Ignore pattern and leave the row. The error must show on the row, and the old value must stay.
3. Turn `Hide secrets` off. The Ignore pattern row must disappear. Turn it on again: the old pattern must come back.
4. Press Reset on the Picker section and answer Y. The log must show the reset line from step 3.
5. Type a token in `Sync token`. The value must show as `••••` and the last four characters, with the marker `↻`.
6. Press `/`, type `max`, and check that the rail and the content narrow to the matching row. Press Esc to clear it.

For unit tests, use the fixture format of the [Testing](/pages/testing/) page. Give each fixture a `settings` object and the events to deliver, and assert that `settings_validate` (Rust) or `settingsValidate` (TypeScript) returns the error on `ignore_pattern` for a bad pattern.

### Troubleshooting

| Code or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.settings-kind` | `kind` is missing or not `tab` or `section`. | Set `"kind": "tab"`. |
| `manifest.settings-id` | The id has a capital letter or starts with a digit. | Use `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}`. |
| `manifest.settings-title-clash` | The tab title equals a built-in tab name. | Choose another title. |
| `manifest.settings-key-clash` | Two rows use one key anywhere in the plugin. | Rename one key. |
| `manifest.settings-row-type`, `manifest.settings-row-field` | Misspelled row type, or a field the row does not take. | Fix the name, or remove the field. |
| `manifest.settings-default` | A default fails its own row. | Make the default pass the row. |
| `manifest.settings-command` | A `keybinding` or `button` names a command the plugin does not contribute. | Add the command to `contributes.commands`. |
| `manifest.settings-limit` | More than 24 rows in a section, or more than 8 sections. | Split the section. |
| `manifest.schema-keyword` | A keyword outside the settings subset. | Use only the keywords of the reference. |
| `invalid-argument` on save | A patch breaks a schema rule. The message names the JSON path. | Fix the value. |
| Could not check this value: did not answer | `settings-validate` took over 100 ms, or the instance is stopped. | Keep the check free of I/O. |
| A row is missing | Its `visible_when` is false. | Change the controlling row; the value is kept. |
| Rows dimmed and read-only | The plugin is disabled, or restarting with `settings-validate`. | Turn it on in Settings > Plugins. |
| `settings.value-ignored` warning | A stored value no longer fits its row. | The default applies. Set the value again. |
| Picker key inactive | Another binding of the same chord won. | Settings > Keys lists the conflict. |

# 11. Add settings to an existing tab

## 11. Add settings to an existing tab

Tutorial 10 gave a plugin a tab of its own. This tutorial covers the other case: a plugin adds one section to a tab that the kernel already draws. The example plugin, `example.clipboard-history` (named "Clipboard history"), adds a block titled "Terminal capture" to the Terminal tab of Settings. The built-in Terminal rows keep their positions and values. The plugin's block sits below them, under a divider that names the plugin.

The rules are strict on purpose. A plugin can add a section at an anchor. It cannot hide, relabel, reorder or restyle a built-in row, and it cannot write a built-in value. Each step below follows from those rules. The block uses a toggle stored per project, a number that hides itself, and a secret that applies after restart. Every row type is on the [row gallery](/pages/reference-settings-rows/).

### You will need

- [Tutorial 10](/pages/tutorial-10-settings-new-tab/) finished, or any plugin with a working manifest and a client build. This step does not need the tab that tutorial 10 adds. The keys here differ from those of tutorial 10, because keys are unique across the whole plugin.
- The grant `settings.contribute:terminal`, which step 1 adds. The plugin's own values need no grant.
- The [settings extension concept](/pages/settings-extension/) for the rail and the ordering rules, and the [settings schema reference](/pages/reference-settings-schema/) for every row field.

### Step 1: declare the section in the manifest

Add one entry to `contributes.settings` with `"kind": "section"`, and add the grant to `capabilities.client`. The `tab` field names the built-in Terminal tab by its frozen id, `terminal`. Settings labels and ids are different things: the label is "Terminal", and the manifest uses the id `terminal`, which never changes even if the label does.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.clipboard-history",
  "name": "Clipboard history",
  "version": "1.3.0",
  "publisher": "Example",
  "description": "Keeps a searchable history of copied text.",
  "icon": "clipboard-list",
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "client": ["settings.contribute:terminal"]
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "settings": [
      {
        "kind": "section",
        "id": "terminal-capture",
        "tab": "terminal",
        "placement": "after:main",
        "order": 500,
        "title": "Terminal capture",
        "scope": "client",
        "rows": [
          { "type": "toggle", "key": "record_panes", "title": "Record pane copies",
            "default": true, "scope": "project",
            "description": "Also store text copied from terminal panes." },
          { "type": "number", "key": "min_length", "title": "Ignore copies under",
            "minimum": 0, "maximum": 200, "unit": "chars", "default": 3,
            "visible_when": { "key": "record_panes", "equals": true },
            "description": "Short copies such as a single word are skipped." },
          { "type": "text", "key": "capture_token", "title": "Capture token",
            "secret": true, "reveal_last": 4, "max_length": 128, "default": "",
            "applies": "restart",
            "description": "Applies after restart." }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each field has one job:

- `kind` set to `"section"` adds rows to a tab that already exists. A `"tab"` entry would add a new rail entry instead.
- `tab` is `terminal`. The grant must name the same id. An unknown id fails with `manifest.settings-target-unknown`. A tab that accepts no plugin sections, such as `animations`, `debug`, `api`, `about` or `setup`, fails with `manifest.settings-target-closed`.
- `placement` chooses the anchor, explained below.
- `order` (0 to 1000, default 500) breaks ties with other plugins at the same anchor.
- `scope` `"client"` means every key in the section is stored on the client side. The values go to `[plugins."example.clipboard-history"]` in `config.toml`. They never go to the `[terminal]` table.
- `rows` holds up to 24 rows per section. This section has three.
- `scope: "project"` on `record_panes` stores that one value for the open project. The project value wins while that project is open.
- `visible_when` on `min_length` hides the row when `record_panes` is off. The hidden row keeps its value.
- `secret` with `reveal_last: 4` masks `capture_token` as `••••` and shows its last four characters. `applies: "restart"` adds `↻` and the note `Applies after restart.`

The first render shows the Terminal tab before the plugin is installed. Its kernel rows are the starting point that the section must leave unchanged.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Terminal───────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                       │
│  Smart Copy light key …………………………………… ← Control  +  →  │
│<span class="t-dim">    The modifier that starts Smart Copy light.         </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Parser pool ………………………………………………………………… -  0 MiB  + *  │
│<span class="t-dim">    No aggregate parser memory cap.                    </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Before: the end of the Terminal tab. The kernel rows are the starting point the section must leave unchanged.</figcaption>
</figure>

An anchor is a named point in a kernel tab. Every tab has `main`, the block of kernel rows. Terminal exposes only that one anchor, so the placements that work on Terminal are:

- `"after:main"` puts the block after the last kernel row. It is the form used above. Because the anchor is named, the position stays stable if the kernel later adds sections, since kernel anchors are never renamed or removed.
- `"end"`, the default, also puts the block after the last kernel row. On Terminal the two placements give the same result. They differ on a tab with several named anchors. The Remote compaction tab exposes `behaviour`, `technique-per-agent`, `custom-prompt`, `input-shaping` and `model`, so `after:input-shaping` places a block between two kernel sections. The diagram below shows that case.

`"before:main"` is refused at install. Kernel rows always come first, so a plugin cannot push the rows of a one-section tab down.

To use the second variant, change the placement line to `"placement": "end"`, or remove the line, since `end` is the default. The manifest is valid either way, and the Settings screen shows the same block on Terminal.

### Step 2: read the values and react to changes

Section values live in the plugin's own store, so the plugin reads them the same way as values of its own tab. The get call returns every own key of the calling side with defaults filled in, so one call gives the plugin `record_panes`, `min_length` and `capture_token` even before the user changes anything. The section grant gives no access to Terminal's own values, such as the scrollback budget (see "What you cannot do").

The event `settings-changed` carries the changed key names, the origin and the receiving side. Reload the values whenever a key of this section is listed. The token applies after restart, so the handler ignores a change of `capture_token` until the plugin restarts. The origin tells the plugin why the write happened: `user` means a row on the Settings screen changed, `reset` means the section's `[ Reset ]` control ran, `plugin` means the plugin's own `set-json` call, and `file` means `config.toml` was edited on disk and reloaded. A project value arrives as the same event when the user opens another project.

The complete client files follow. Parse the JSON with serde in Rust, and check its shape in TypeScript, because parsed JSON is untyped.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs. Client side of clipboard-history 1.3.0: the Terminal section.
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::{ilium_plugin, Event, Handler, SettingsOrigin, Submission};
use serde::Deserialize;

/// Values of the section `terminal-capture`, keyed as in the manifest.
#[derive(Deserialize, Default, Clone)]
pub struct TerminalCapture {
    pub record_panes: bool,
    pub min_length: u32,
    pub capture_token: String,
}

pub fn load_terminal_capture() -> Result<TerminalCapture, serde_json::Error> {
    serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json())
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ClipboardHistory {
    capture: TerminalCapture,
}

impl ClipboardHistory {
    fn reload(&mut self) {
        match load_terminal_capture() {
            Ok(capture) => self.capture = capture,
            Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &error.to_string()),
        }
    }

    /// Decides whether one copy from a terminal pane is stored.
    fn should_store(&self, text: &str) -> bool {
        self.capture.record_panes && text.chars().count() as u32 >= self.capture.min_length
    }
}

impl Handler for ClipboardHistory {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::SettingsChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            // capture_token applies after restart, so only the other keys reload.
            let live = change.keys.iter().any(|key| key == "record_panes" || key == "min_length");
            if live {
                self.reload();
            }
            if change.origin == SettingsOrigin::Reset {
                log::log(Level::Info, "terminal capture reset from the Settings screen");
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts. Client side of clipboard-history 1.3.0: the Terminal section.
import { definePlugin, type Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

export type TerminalCapture = {
  record_panes: boolean;
  min_length: number;
  capture_token: string;
};

function isTerminalCapture(value: unknown): value is TerminalCapture {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return false;
  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  return (
    typeof record.record_panes === 'boolean' &&
    typeof record.min_length === 'number' &&
    typeof record.capture_token === 'string'
  );
}

export function loadTerminalCapture(): TerminalCapture | null {
  const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(getJson());
  return isTerminalCapture(parsed) ? parsed : null;
}

let capture: TerminalCapture | null = null;

/** Decides whether one copy from a terminal pane is stored. */
export function shouldStore(text: string): boolean {
  if (!capture) return false;
  return capture.record_panes && [...text].length >= capture.min_length;
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {
    capture = loadTerminalCapture();
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'settings-changed') continue;
      // capture_token applies after restart, so only the other keys reload.
      const live = event.val.keys.some((key) => key === 'record_panes' || key === 'min_length');
      if (live) capture = loadTerminalCapture();
      if (event.val.origin === 'reset') log('info', 'terminal capture reset from the Settings screen');
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Step 3: two plugins on the same tab

Several plugins can add sections to one kernel tab. The kernel orders them by a fixed rule, and install order and enable order never change the result:

1. The anchor (kernel rows first, then `after:` blocks, then `end` blocks).
2. The `order` value, ascending.
3. The plugin id, compared bytewise.
4. The declaration order inside the plugin.

Each plugin's sections at one anchor sit next to each other under one divider. Suppose a second plugin, `example.terminal-bell`, adds a "Bell" section with `"placement": "after:main"` and `"order": 200`. Its block comes first, because 200 is lower than 500:

```json
{
  "kind": "section",
  "id": "bell",
  "tab": "terminal",
  "placement": "after:main",
  "order": 200,
  "title": "Bell",
  "scope": "client",
  "rows": [
    { "type": "toggle", "key": "ring_on_copy", "title": "Ring on copy", "default": false,
      "description": "Ring the terminal bell when a pane copy is stored." }
  ]
}
```

If both plugins used `order` 500, the clipboard block would come first, because `example.clipboard-history` sorts before `example.terminal-bell`.

Users cannot reorder plugin sections. The rule is the only order, so a plugin author controls its place only through `placement` and `order`, and a second plugin cannot push the first one's rows out of its place. Two machines with the same plugins show the same Terminal tab, whatever order the plugins were installed in.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Terminal───────────────────────────────────────╮
│<span class="t-hi">▏ ♪ TERMINAL BELL ──────────────────────────── plugin ─</span>│
│<span class="t-hi">▏ Bell                                                 </span>│
│▏  Ring on copy …………………………………………………………………………… ‹ Off ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">▏    Ring the terminal bell when a copy is stored.     </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">▏ ⎘ CLIPBOARD HISTORY ──────────────────────── plugin ─</span>│

│<span class="t-dim">▏    Also store text copied from terminal panes.       </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Two plugins at the same anchor. Each block has its own divider, and the lower <code>order</code> (200) comes first.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Step 4: limits

The kernel enforces these limits for sections in built-in tabs. Install refuses a manifest that exceeds a per-plugin limit with `manifest.settings-limit`:

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| Plugin sections per kernel tab, one plugin | 2 |
| Plugin sections per kernel tab, all plugins | 6 |
| Rows per section (a `group` counts its children) | 24 |
| Value keys per plugin | 128 |
| Choice options | 64 |
| Text value | 4,096 characters |

These limits keep the Terminal tab readable. A plugin that needs more than two sections in one tab merges its rows into fewer sections. A plugin that needs more room gives itself a tab of its own, as tutorial 10 shows.

A seventh plugin section on one tab is not drawn. The kernel drops the extra sections in ordering order and writes a load warning, so the plugin keeps running and the values stay stored. The render shows the warning as `ilium plugin list` prints it.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.clipboard-history
<span class="t-warn">2026-10-12 09:14:02 warn  host   example.clipboard-history</span>
    settings.section-dropped: section
    "example.clipboard-history/terminal-capture"
    in tab "terminal" is not shown: the tab
    already has 6 plugin sections
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The load warning in the log when a tab is full. Nothing is removed from the stored values.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Step 5: install and the permission prompt

Build the package, then install it with the package command. The install checks the manifest and its grants before it writes the plugin:

```bash
ilium plugin install ./example.clipboard-history.iliumpkg
```

The review dialog lists the grant in plain words. The grant `settings.contribute:terminal` appears as one line, low risk, and the always-granted settings of the plugin's own values need no line. Approving the install lets the plugin draw sections in the Terminal tab and nothing else. It gives no read or write access to Terminal values.

### Step 6: see it, search it, reset it

Open Settings, press Tab until the Terminal rail entry is selected, and scroll down past the Parser pool row. The block is drawn after the last kernel row. Press Up or Down to move between rows: the kernel handles those keys, so the plugin rows never see raw key events. A value changes at once for a toggle and after 600 ms for a number step.

Saving follows the Settings rules. A toggle or a choice writes at once. A number step writes 600 ms after the last step, so several quick presses become one write and one `settings-changed` event. Closing Settings with Esc or `✕ Close` flushes any pending write, so nothing is lost on the way out.

Press `/` and type part of a name to filter. A match inside a built-in tab shows the plugin divider above the matching row, so the owner stays visible. Esc clears the filter.

### Before and after

| Aspect | Before the plugin | After the plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal rows | The kernel rows | The same kernel rows, unchanged |
| Lines below Parser pool | None | A divider, a title and three plugin rows |
| Stored values | `[terminal]` only | Plugin values in `[plugins."example.clipboard-history"]`; `record_panes` also per project |
| Rail | The kernel tabs | The same tabs; no new entry |

The built-in rows are the same before and after, and the plugin adds a labelled block with no new rail entry. Users see the plugin's contribution in place, and a plugin cannot take over any part of the Terminal tab that belongs to the kernel.

### What you cannot do

The limits below follow directly from the rule that plugins add and never alter.

- **Change, hide, reorder or relabel a built-in row.** The kernel lays out the kernel rows first and splices plugin blocks in afterwards. There is no field that touches a kernel row.
- **Place a block before `main`.** `"before:main"` is refused, so kernel rows of a one-section tab always come first.
- **Write a built-in value.** The grant allows drawing sections only. A patch can only name keys of the plugin's own sections.
- **Read a built-in value without its own grant.** `settings.contribute` gives no read access. Reading needs `settings.read-kernel:terminal`, shown below. The read is one-way and secrets are redacted.
- **Add a section to a closed tab.** `animations`, `debug`, `api`, `about` and `setup` accept no plugin sections.

To read a Terminal value, add `settings.read-kernel:terminal` to `capabilities.client`. Changes arrive as the event `kernel-settings-changed`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;

// Needs the grant settings.read-kernel:terminal. Read-only, secrets are redacted.
fn scrollback_budget() -> Option<u64> {
    let json = kernel_settings::read("terminal").ok()?;
    let values: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&json).ok()?;
    values["scrollback_mib"].as_u64()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';

// Needs the grant settings.read-kernel:terminal. Read-only, secrets are redacted.
export function scrollbackBudget(): number | undefined {
  const values = JSON.parse(read('terminal')) as { scrollback_mib?: number };
  return values.scrollback_mib;
}
```

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom or code | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `manifest.settings-target-grant` | The section targets `terminal` but the manifest has no `settings.contribute:terminal` capability. Add the grant to `capabilities.client`. |
| `manifest.settings-target-unknown` | The `tab` value is not a kernel tab id. Use the lowercase id from the table in the concept page, such as `terminal`, not the label "Terminal". |
| `manifest.settings-target-closed` | The tab accepts no plugin sections, such as `debug`. Choose a tab that accepts sections. |
| `manifest.settings-anchor` | The placement names a section that the tab does not have, for example `after:output`. Use `main` on Terminal, or a named anchor of the tab. |
| `manifest.settings-limit` | A count is over its limit, such as a third section in one tab. Merge the rows into fewer sections. |
| `manifest.settings-key-clash` | Two rows in the plugin use the same `key`. Keys are unique across all tabs and sections of the plugin. |
| `manifest.settings-default` | A `default` does not match its row, for example a `min_length` default of 300 with a maximum of 200. Correct the default. |
| A row is missing | Its `visible_when` is false. Change the controlling row. |
| `settings.section-dropped` | The tab already has six plugin sections. This is a warning only. Remove a plugin or move a section to a tab with room. |
| `settings.value-ignored` | A stored value no longer matches its row, for example after the maximum was lowered. The default applies, and the stored text stays in the file. |

Kernel anchors are never removed, so a `after:main` placement keeps working through kernel updates. The `settings.anchor-missing` warning applies only to an anchor that the plugin itself declared in one of its own sections.
