# 17. A help topic and a custom sound

## 17. A help topic and a custom sound

This tutorial adds two small pieces of polish. The first is a **help topic**, a page of Markdown that ships inside the plugin and shows up in the Ilium help pane. The second is a **custom sound**, a short audio file that the plugin plays on request. The improvement adds a setting that lets the user mute the sound.

This tutorial is standalone. It starts a fresh plugin, so you do not need the earlier tutorials. You only need to have finished [Your first plugin in five minutes](/pages/getting-started-first-plugin/).

Some words first.

- A **help topic** is one Markdown file, listed in the manifest, that Ilium shows in its help pane.
- A **sound** is a short audio file in the package. The manifest gives it an id, such as `ding`.
- A **catalogue** is the list of sound ids that a plugin may play. It holds the bundled sound `chirping` and the sounds of the plugin itself.
- A **package** is the single file that holds the plugin: the manifest, the components and any asset files.
- A **command** is a named action that the user runs from the palette.
- An **intent** is a request the plugin hands back, such as "play this sound".
- A **grant** is a permission that the user allows at install.

Tutorial plugin: `example.chime`. Side: client, because sound and help belong to the client. Languages: Rust (target `wasm32-wasip2`) and TypeScript. Every listing is given in both.

### You will need

- [Your first plugin in five minutes](/pages/getting-started-first-plugin/) finished. Nothing else.
- Three grants, all on the client side:

| Grant | What the plugin may do with it |
|---|---|
| `sound.play` | Send the `play-sound` intent. |
| `help.read` | Read the text of a help topic with `help.topic`. |
| `notify.toast` | Show a toast. |

- One sound file. Any short WAV file with PCM samples, or OGG Vorbis file, works. Put it at `sounds/ding.ogg` in the project. Keep it under a second, because it plays on every command.
- Create the project:

```bash
ilium plugin new chime --id example.chime --lang rust --side client --name "Chime"
```

Use `--lang typescript` for the TypeScript version.

### What this plugin does

- The command `Play the chime` plays the sound `ding`.
- The command `Show the chime help` reads the help topic and shows its first line in a toast.
- The help topic is listed in the help pane, so the user can also open it there.

### The surface this step uses

| Name | Kind | Fields and types | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contributes.help` | manifest key | `id`, `file`, `title` | Declares a help topic. The file sits under `help/`. |
| `contributes.sounds` | manifest key | `id`, `file` | Declares a sound. The file sits under `sounds/`. |
| `help.topic` | host function | `topic(id) -> option<string>`, grant `help.read` | Returns the Markdown of a topic, or nothing. |
| `play-sound` | intent | the sound id, a string. Grant `sound.play`. | Asks the client to play a sound from the catalogue. |
| `sound.catalog` | host function | returns list of ids, always granted | The ids that this plugin may play. |
| `command-invoked` | event | `command`, `arguments-json`, `origin`, `context` | The user ran a command. |

### The files

Besides the manifest, this plugin has two asset files:

```text
help/chime.md
sounds/ding.ogg
```

The help file is plain Markdown. Start it with a heading, because the plugin shows the first line.

```markdown
# Chime

Chime plays a short sound when you run the command Play the chime.
Open Settings > Plugins to mute it.
```

### Manifest

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.chime",
  "name": "Chime",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "client": ["sound.play", "help.read", "notify.toast"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "play", "title": "Play the chime", "category": "Chime" },
      { "id": "help", "title": "Show the chime help", "category": "Chime" }
    ],
    "help": [
      { "id": "chime", "file": "help/chime.md", "title": "Chime" }
    ],
    "sounds": [
      { "id": "ding", "file": "sounds/ding.ogg" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The global id of the help topic is the plugin id, a slash and the local id: `example.chime/chime`. The sound id is only `ding`. Sound ids are plain, and each plugin sees only its own.

Two ids are protected. Ilium ships one bundled sound, `chirping`. A manifest may not reuse it, and may not repeat an id. Either mistake fails the package check with `manifest.sound-id-taken`.

### The smallest plugin

The handler waits for `command-invoked`. The first command returns a `play-sound` intent. The second reads the topic and returns a toast with its first line.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs. Play a sound and read a help topic.
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::help;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, ToastSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Tone;

const PLAY: &str = "example.chime/play";
const HELP: &str = "example.chime/help";
const TOPIC: &str = "example.chime/chime";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Chime;

impl Lifecycle for Chime {}

/// The first line of a Markdown text, without the leading marks.
pub fn first_line(markdown: &str) -> String {
    markdown
        .lines()
        .next()
        .unwrap_or("")
        .trim_start_matches('#')
        .trim()
        .to_string()
}

fn toast(title: String) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
        id: Some("chime".into()),
        tone: Tone::Info,
        title,
        body: None,
        actions: vec![],
        duration_ms: None,
    }))
}

impl Handler for Chime {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, .. }) = event else {
                continue;
            };
            if command == PLAY {
                submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::PlaySound("ding".into())));
            } else if command == HELP {
                let title = match help::topic(TOPIC) {
                    Some(markdown) => first_line(&markdown),
                    None => "The help topic is not installed".to_string(),
                };
                submissions.push(toast(title));
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/client.ts. Play a sound and read a help topic.
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { topic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/help';

const PLAY = 'example.chime/play';
const HELP = 'example.chime/help';
const TOPIC = 'example.chime/chime';
let nextCorrelation = 1n;

/** The first line of a Markdown text, without the leading marks. */
export function firstLine(markdown: string): string {
  const line = markdown.split('\n')[0] ?? '';
  return line.replace(/^#+/, '').trim();
}

function submission(intent: Submission['intent']): Submission {
  return { intent, correlation: nextCorrelation++, dedupKey: undefined };
}

function toast(title: string): Submission {
  return submission({
    tag: 'toast',
    val: { id: 'chime', tone: 'info', title, body: undefined, actions: [], durationMs: undefined },
  });
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command === PLAY) {
        submissions.push(submission({ tag: 'play-sound', val: 'ding' }));
      } else if (event.val.command === HELP) {
        const markdown = topic(TOPIC);
        submissions.push(toast(markdown === undefined
          ? 'The help topic is not installed' : firstLine(markdown)));
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

### Line by line

1. `Intent::PlaySound("ding".into())` names the sound by its id from `contributes.sounds`. The plugin never opens the audio device.
2. `help::topic` takes the global topic id and returns the Markdown, or nothing when no installed plugin declares the id.
3. `first_line` is a pure function. It strips the leading `#` marks, so the toast reads `Chime` and not `# Chime`.

Ilium has no call that opens the help pane from code. This tutorial shows the first line in a toast instead. The user opens the full topic in the help pane. A plugin with a settings page can also point a row at the topic with the row key `help`.

### One improvement: let the user mute the sound

A sound that cannot be turned off is rude. Add a settings toggle `sound_enabled`. The plugin reads it before it plays.

Add the setting to the manifest. It is a tab with one section and one toggle row, as in [Tutorial 10](/pages/tutorial-10-settings-new-tab/).

```json
"settings": [
  {
    "kind": "tab",
    "id": "chime",
    "title": "Chime",
    "render": "rows",
    "sections": [
      {
        "id": "sound",
        "title": "Sound",
        "scope": "client",
        "rows": [
          { "type": "toggle", "key": "sound_enabled", "title": "Play the sound",
            "default": true,
            "description": "Turn this off to keep the chime silent.",
            "help": "example.chime/chime" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

The row key `help` links the row to the topic. The topic id must be declared under `contributes.help`, or the install fails with `manifest.settings-help`.

Now read the setting. The function `settings::get_json` returns the plugin values as one JSON object. A missing key means the default, which is on.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;

/// True when the setting is on, or when it cannot be read.
pub fn sound_enabled(json: &str) -> bool {
    serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(json)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|values| values["sound_enabled"].as_bool())
        .unwrap_or(true)
}

// In on_events, replace the PLAY branch with:
//     if sound_enabled(&settings::get_json()) {
//         submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::PlaySound("ding".into())));
//     }
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

/** True when the setting is on, or when it cannot be read. */
export function soundEnabled(json: string): boolean {
  try {
    const values: Record<string, unknown> = JSON.parse(json);
    return typeof values['sound_enabled'] === 'boolean' ? values['sound_enabled'] : true;
  } catch {
    return true;
  }
}

// In onEvents, replace the PLAY branch with:
//     if (soundEnabled(getJson())) submissions.push(submission({ tag: 'play-sound', val: 'ding' }));
```

The user can also take away the grant. Settings > Plugins > Capabilities lists `sound.play`, and the command `ilium plugin grants example.chime --revoke sound.play` revokes it. After that, every `play-sound` is refused with `not-permitted`.

### What the package check does

`ilium plugin pack` builds the package and writes the `files` inventory: each file with its length and a hash. The check at install compares every listed file with its entry.

| Problem | Error code |
|---|---|
| A file is in the package but not in `files` | `manifest.file-unlisted` |
| A file in `files` is missing | `manifest.file-missing` |
| The length does not match | `manifest.file-length` |
| The hash does not match | `manifest.file-hash` |
| A sound file is not WAV PCM or OGG Vorbis | package check fails |

### Points to notice

- **Each plugin has its own sounds.** The catalogue holds `chirping` and your own ids. Another plugin's id is refused with `not-found`.
- **The grant is separate from the setting.** The user can mute in the settings or revoke the grant.

### Edge cases and errors

| Case | What happens | Code or result |
|---|---|---|
| Sound id not in the catalogue | Nothing plays | `refused(not-found)` |
| Grant `sound.play` declined | Nothing plays | `refused(not-permitted)` |
| More than 4 sounds in a second | The extra sounds are dropped | `refused(rate-limited)` with `retry-after-ms` |
| Topic id unknown | `help.topic` returns nothing | No error |
| `help.read` declined | `help.topic` returns nothing, with a warning in the log | No error |

### Common mistakes

| Mistake | What you see | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Used the id `chirping` in `sounds` | Install refused with `manifest.sound-id-taken` | Choose another id. |
| Pointed `file` at a path outside `sounds/` | The package check fails | Keep sound files under `sounds/`. |
| Played `example.chime/ding` | `refused(not-found)` | Use the plain id `ding`. |
| Read the topic with the plain id `chime` | `help.topic` returns nothing | Use the global id `example.chime/chime`. |

### Test it

The text functions are pure. Test them with plain tests. Test the sound command with the fake host.

mod tests {

**TypeScript**

# 18. Offer an extension point: a link preview plugin

## 18. Offer an extension point: a link preview plugin

This step makes your plugin the owner of an extension point. The plugin is `example.linkpreview`. When the user runs a command on a URL, the plugin builds a short preview. It does not know every site. It owns a **collect** point, `renderers`, where other packages list a URL pattern and the service that can render it. It also owns a **transform hook**, `before-preview`, where other packages can adjust the finished preview. A second package, `example.linkpreview-github`, fills the point for GitHub URLs. The step shows the dormant state of that package before the owner is installed.

You start a fresh plugin. You need tutorials 1 to 9, and you should have read [Services](/pages/services/) and [Architecture](/pages/architecture/). The full mechanism is in [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/). The points of the core plugins are in [Reference: core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/), and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) compares the five ways to work with a core feature. This page does not repeat those tables.

### You will need

- Rust: stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crates `ilium-plugin-sdk`, `serde_json` and `regex-lite`. TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. `RegExp` is built in.
- Grants for the owner: `extensions.provide:example.linkpreview/renderers`, `extensions.provide:example.linkpreview/before-preview`, `services.use:example.linkpreview-github/render` and `topics.subscribe:ilium.extensions/changed`. Nothing else.
- Grants for the contributor: `extensions.contribute:example.linkpreview/renderers` and `services.provide:example.linkpreview-github/render`.
- Both manifests set `"unstable": ["plugin-services"]` (dev mode, T2 and T3), because the renderer is a plugin-defined service.

### The surface this step uses

| Area | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest | `contributes.extension_points[]` | Declares `renderers` (collect, dynamic) and `before-preview` (hook, transform). The global ids are `example.linkpreview/renderers` and `example.linkpreview/before-preview`. |
| Manifest | `contributes.extensions[]` | The contributor writes `point`, `id`, `priority` and `entry`. |
| Grant | `extensions.provide:<point>` | Owner of one point. It may only own points that start with its own plugin id. |
| Grant | `extensions.contribute:<point>` | Contributor to one point. No wildcard. |
| Host | `extensions::list(point)` / `list(point)` | The active entries, in run order. |
| Host | `extensions::run_hook(point, payload).await` / `runHook(point, payload)` | Runs the chain and resolves with the final payload. |
| Host | `extensions::register` and `unregister` | Add or remove an entry of a `dynamic` point at run time. |
| Topic | `ilium.extensions/changed` | Tells the owner, and nobody else, that the list of a point changed. Payload `{ "point": "<id>" }`. |

### The flow

### Step 1: the owner manifest

The owner declares both points. `renderers` is a collect point, so it has an `entry_schema`. It is `dynamic`, so a contributor may also add entries at run time. `before-preview` is a hook with the mode `transform`, so a handler may replace the payload.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.linkpreview",
  "name": "Link preview",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "icon": "link",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "unstable": ["plugin-services"],
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "extensions.provide:example.linkpreview/renderers",
      "extensions.provide:example.linkpreview/before-preview",
      "services.use:example.linkpreview-github/render",
      "topics.subscribe:ilium.extensions/changed",
      "notify.toast"
    ]
  },
  "activation": ["command:example.linkpreview/preview"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "preview", "title": "Link preview: show preview of a URL" }
    ],
    "topics": { "subscribes": ["ilium.extensions/changed"] },
    "extension_points": [
      {
        "id": "renderers",
        "kind": "collect",
        "title": "Link renderers",
        "version": "1.0.0",
        "dynamic": true,
        "max_entries": 32,
        "entry_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["id", "regex", "service"],
          "properties": {
            "id": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 64 },
            "regex": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 256 },
            "service": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 128 }
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "before-preview",
        "kind": "hook",
        "mode": "transform",
        "title": "Before a preview is shown",
        "version": "1.0.0",
        "risk": "standard",
        "deadline_ms": 20,
        "max_handlers": 4,
        "payload_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["url", "title", "summary"],
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 2048 },
            "title": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 200 },
            "summary": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 600 }
          }
        },
        "reply_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["title", "summary"],
          "properties": {
            "title": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 200 },
            "summary": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 600 }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Points to notice:

- The global ids are the plugin id, a slash and the point id: `example.linkpreview/renderers`. Each `extensions.provide` grant names one of them. A grant for a point that starts with another plugin's id is refused at install with `manifest.grant-missing-extension`, and a point without a grant fails the same way.
- The owner does not list `hook-handler` in `exports`. It runs hooks and does not handle them.
- `version` is the version of the point's schema. Bump the minor number when you add an optional field. Bump the major number when you remove a field or make a field required. Contributors can ask for a minimum, as step 3 shows.
- `max_entries` caps the whole list at 32. A 33rd entry is refused with `cap-exceeded`. The default is 64 and the limit is 256.
- The owner grants itself `services.use` for exactly one renderer service. An entry that names another service is listed, but the call fails with `not-permitted`. Step 2 turns that into a plain preview.

### Step 2: the owner code

The owner has four jobs. It reads the list on start. It reads the list again when `ilium.extensions/changed` arrives for `renderers`. On the command it finds the first entry whose pattern matches, calls that entry's service, and runs the hook. If there is no match, no renderer or a failing renderer, it falls back to a plain preview from the URL. The preview never fails because a contributor is bad.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::task;
use regex_lite::Regex;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const RENDERERS: &str = "example.linkpreview/renderers";
const BEFORE_PREVIEW: &str = "example.linkpreview/before-preview";

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Renderer {
    extension: String,
    regex: Regex,
    service: String,
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct LinkPreview {
    renderers: Vec<Renderer>,
}

impl LinkPreview {
    fn reload(&mut self) {
        let entries = match extensions::list(RENDERERS) {
            Ok(entries) => entries,
            Err(error) => {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("list failed: {error:?}"));
                return;
            }
        };
        self.renderers = entries
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| {
                let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&entry.entry_json).ok()?;
                // A bad pattern drops this entry only. The others stay usable.
                let regex = Regex::new(value["regex"].as_str()?).ok()?;
                Some(Renderer {
                    extension: entry.extension,
                    regex,
                    service: value["service"].as_str()?.to_string(),
                })
            })
            .collect();
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{} renderers loaded", self.renderers.len()));
    }
}

impl Lifecycle for LinkPreview {
    fn activate(&mut self) {
        self.reload();
    }
}

impl Handler for LinkPreview {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::TopicPublished(published) if published.topic == "ilium.extensions/changed" => {
                    let changed: Value = serde_json::from_str(&published.payload_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                    if changed["point"] == RENDERERS {
                        self.reload();
                    }
                }
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command == "example.linkpreview/preview" => {
                    let arguments: Value = serde_json::from_str(&invoked.arguments_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                    let url = arguments["url"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
                    task::spawn(build_preview(url, self.renderers.clone()));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

async fn build_preview(url: String, renderers: Vec<Renderer>) {
    let mut preview = plain_preview(&url);
    if let Some(renderer) = renderers.iter().find(|renderer| renderer.regex.is_match(&url)) {
        match services::call(&renderer.service, "render", &json!({ "url": url }).to_string()).await {
            Ok(reply) => match parse_preview(&reply) {
                Some(rendered) => preview = rendered,
                None => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{} sent a bad reply", renderer.extension)),
            },
            Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{} failed: {}", renderer.extension, error.code)),
        }
    }
    let payload = json!({ "url": url, "title": preview.0, "summary": preview.1 }).to_string();
    match extensions::run_hook(BEFORE_PREVIEW, &payload).await {
        Ok(Some(changed)) => {
            if let Some(adjusted) = parse_preview(&changed) {
                preview = adjusted;
            }
        }
        Ok(None) => {}
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("hook failed: {}", error.code)),
    }
    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("preview ready: {}", preview.0));
    // The toast submission is returned by the next batch in a full plugin.
}

fn parse_preview(json_text: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(json_text).ok()?;
    Some((value["title"].as_str()?.to_string(), value["summary"].as_str()?.to_string()))
}

fn plain_preview(url: &str) -> (String, String) {
    let host = url.split('/').nth(2).unwrap_or(url);
    (host.to_string(), format!("No renderer for {host}."))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { list, runHook } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';
import { call } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const RENDERERS = 'example.linkpreview/renderers';
const BEFORE_PREVIEW = 'example.linkpreview/before-preview';

interface Renderer { extension: string; regex: RegExp; service: string }
type Preview = { title: string; summary: string };

let renderers: Renderer[] = [];

function reload(): void {
  try {
    renderers = list(RENDERERS).flatMap((entry) => {
      try {
        const value = JSON.parse(entry.entryJson) as { regex: string; service: string };
        // A bad pattern drops this entry only. The others stay usable.
        return [{ extension: entry.extension, regex: new RegExp(value.regex), service: value.service }];
      } catch {
        return [];
      }
    });
    log('info', `${renderers.length} renderers loaded`);
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `list failed: ${String(error)}`);
  }
}

function plainPreview(url: string): Preview {
  const host = url.split('/')[2] ?? url;
  return { title: host, summary: `No renderer for ${host}.` };
}

function parsePreview(text: string): Preview | undefined {
  try {
    const value = JSON.parse(text) as Partial<Preview>;
    if (typeof value.title !== 'string' || typeof value.summary !== 'string') return undefined;
    return { title: value.title, summary: value.summary };
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

async function buildPreview(url: string, active: Renderer[]): Promise<void> {
  let preview = plainPreview(url);
  const renderer = active.find((candidate) => candidate.regex.test(url));
  if (renderer) {
    try {
      const reply = await call(renderer.service, 'render', JSON.stringify({ url }));
      const rendered = parsePreview(reply);
      if (rendered) preview = rendered;
      else log('warn', `${renderer.extension} sent a bad reply`);
    } catch (error) {
      log('warn', `${renderer.extension} failed: ${String((error as { code?: string }).code)}`);
    }
  }
  try {
    const changed = await runHook(BEFORE_PREVIEW, JSON.stringify({ url, ...preview }));
    const adjusted = changed === undefined ? undefined : parsePreview(changed);
    if (adjusted) preview = adjusted;
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `hook failed: ${String((error as { code?: string }).code)}`);
  }
  log('info', `preview ready: ${preview.title}`);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    reload();
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'topic-published' && event.val.topic === 'ilium.extensions/changed') {
        const changed = JSON.parse(event.val.payloadJson) as { point?: string };
        if (changed.point === RENDERERS) reload();
      }
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'example.linkpreview/preview') {
        const args = JSON.parse(event.val.argumentsJson) as { url?: string };
        void buildPreview(args.url ?? '', renderers);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- `list` returns entries already sorted by the user's order, then priority, then plugin id. Take the first match.
- The owner keeps the compiled list and reloads on the topic. The topic carries only the point id, so the owner reloads the whole list.
- A contributor is untrusted input. The kernel checks `reply_schema` for the hook, but the owner parses the service reply itself.
- With no handler, `run_hook` returns nothing and the owner keeps its own preview. A full plugin returns an `Intent::Toast` from the next batch ([tutorial 4](/pages/tutorial-04-finished-notice/)).

### Step 3: the contributor package

The second package knows GitHub. It fills the point from its manifest, so it needs no code to register. Its service answers the `render` calls. It can also ask for a minimum version of the point: `example.linkpreview/renderers@1.0.0` means the same major version and a minor version of 0 or more.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.linkpreview-github",
  "name": "Link preview: GitHub",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "icon": "brand-github",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["service-provider"]
  },
  "unstable": ["plugin-services"],
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "extensions.contribute:example.linkpreview/renderers",
      "services.provide:example.linkpreview-github/render"
    ]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "services": {
      "provides": [
        {
          "name": "example.linkpreview-github/render",
          "version": "1.0.0",
          "schema": "schemas/render.json"
        }
      ]
    },
    "extensions": [
      {
        "point": "example.linkpreview/renderers@1.0.0",
        "id": "github",
        "priority": 40,
        "entry": {
          "id": "github",
          "regex": "^https://github\\.com/[^/]+/[^/]+",
          "service": "example.linkpreview-github/render"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`schemas/render.json` (params `{ "url": string }`, result `{ "title": string, "summary": string }`, each field with a `maxLength`):

```json
{ "methods": { "render": {
  "params": { "type": "object", "required": ["url"], "properties": { "url": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 2048 } } },
  "result": { "type": "object", "required": ["title", "summary"], "properties": {
    "title": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 200 }, "summary": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 600 } } }
} } }
```

The provider code reads the owner and the repository from the path. It does no network call, so it needs no `http` grant. A real renderer would add `http:api.github.com`, which is a separate grant that the user would see in the review dialog.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{ServiceCall, ServiceProvider, ServiceReply};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["service-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct GithubRenderer;

impl Lifecycle for GithubRenderer {}

impl Handler for GithubRenderer {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl ServiceProvider for GithubRenderer {
    fn handle(&mut self, call: ServiceCall) -> ServiceReply {
        if call.method != "render" {
            return ServiceReply::Done(json!({ "title": "", "summary": "" }).to_string());
        }
        let params: Value = serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        let url = params["url"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let mut parts = url.trim_start_matches("https://github.com/").split('/');
        let owner = parts.next().unwrap_or("");
        let repository = parts.next().unwrap_or("");
        ServiceReply::Done(
            json!({
                "title": format!("{owner}/{repository}"),
                "summary": format!("GitHub repository {repository} owned by {owner}."),
            })
            .to_string(),
        )
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { ServiceCall, ServiceReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export const { lifecycle, handler, serviceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents() {
    return [];
  },
  handle(call: ServiceCall): ServiceReply {
    if (call.method !== 'render') {
      return { tag: 'done', val: JSON.stringify({ title: '', summary: '' }) };
    }
    const params = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson) as { url?: string };
    const [owner = '', repository = ''] = (params.url ?? '')
      .replace('https://github.com/', '')
      .split('/');
    return {
      tag: 'done',
      val: JSON.stringify({
        title: `${owner}/${repository}`,
        summary: `GitHub repository ${repository} owned by ${owner}.`,
      }),
    };
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- The manifest is the whole contribution. The entry is checked against the owner's `entry_schema` when the package is installed. A missing `service` field fails with `manifest.extension-entry-invalid`, and a missing grant with `manifest.grant-missing-extension`.
- `priority` 40 puts GitHub before the default 50. Lower runs first, and the user can still move it on the owner's Extensions tab.
- A missing `service` field fails the install with `manifest.extension-entry-invalid`.

### Step 4: dormant until the owner is installed

Install the contributor first, with the owner missing. The install does not fail. The entry stays in the package and counts for nothing. The Plugins screen shows `waiting for example.linkpreview`. Install the owner second, and the entry becomes active. The kernel sends `ilium.extensions/changed` with `{ "point": "example.linkpreview/renderers" }` to the owner. The owner reloads and shows `1 renderers loaded` in its log.

The same happens when the owner is disabled: the entries go dormant at once and a preview falls back to plain text. An entry that asks for `renderers@1.2.0` from an owner at `1.0.0` is dormant too, and the Plugins screen names the version the owner must reach.

### Step 5: dynamic entries with register and unregister

Because `renderers` is `dynamic`, a contributor may add and remove entries while it runs. This is how a plugin offers a renderer for something it only learns at run time, such as the host name of a company wiki read from its settings. The contributor needs the same `extensions.contribute` grant. The entry is validated again against the schema.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;

fn add_wiki(host: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let regex = host.replace('.', "\\.");
    let entry = format!(
        r#"{{"id":"wiki","regex":"^https://{regex}/","service":"example.linkpreview-github/render"}}"#
    );
    extensions::register("example.linkpreview/renderers", "wiki", 60, &entry)
        .map_err(|error| format!("{error:?}"))
}

// Remove it later: extensions::unregister("example.linkpreview/renderers", "wiki")
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { register } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

export function addWiki(host: string): void {
  const regex = host.replace(/\./g, '\\.');
  const entry = JSON.stringify({
    id: 'wiki',
    regex: `^https://${regex}/`,
    service: 'example.linkpreview-github/render',
  });
  register('example.linkpreview/renderers', 'wiki', 60, entry);
}

// Remove it later: unregister('example.linkpreview/renderers', 'wiki')
```

Registering an id the plugin already used replaces that entry. A plugin can only remove entries it registered, and a call on a point that is not `dynamic` fails with `not-dynamic`. A registered entry does not survive a restart of the contributor, so register again in `activate`. A dynamic entry has the same cap, the same priority rules and the same toggles as a manifest entry.

### Step 6: change the schema without breaking contributors

Point versions let you grow the schema. Suppose you want to add an optional `icon` field to renderer entries.

1. Add `icon` to `properties`, not to `required`, and set `"version": "1.1.0"`. Contributors that wrote `renderers@1.0.0` stay active and the owner uses a default icon.
2. Contributors that need the field write `renderers@1.1.0`. On an owner still at `1.0.0` they are dormant, which is correct.
3. To remove a field or require one, bump to `2.0.0`. Every contributor that asked for `@1.0.0` goes dormant.

A contributor that does not write a version always matches. Tell contributors to write one.

### Security and consent

| Grant | Who | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extensions.provide:example.linkpreview/renderers` | Owner | normal | The plugin owns the point. |
| `extensions.provide:example.linkpreview/before-preview` | Owner | normal | The plugin owns the hook. The point has `risk: "standard"`. |
| `extensions.contribute:example.linkpreview/renderers` | GitHub package | normal | The package adds one entry. |
| `services.use:example.linkpreview-github/render` | Owner | normal | The owner calls one named service. |
| `services.provide:example.linkpreview-github/render` | GitHub package | normal | The package answers that service. |
| `topics.subscribe:ilium.extensions/changed` | Owner | normal | The owner hears about list changes. |

- A contributor is untrusted input. It can name any service in its entry. The owner can call only services it holds a `services.use` grant for, so an entry with a different service fails with `not-permitted` and the owner falls back.
- A contributor cannot see the owner's state. A handler sees the payload and nothing else.
- Mark a hook `high` only when a handler could do harm. A preview carries no secret, so `before-preview` stays standard.

### Test it

Test the manifests first. Remove `"service"` from the GitHub entry and run `ilium plugin build`. It reports `manifest.extension-entry-invalid`. Restore it, then remove the `extensions.contribute` grant to see `manifest.grant-missing-extension`.

Then run the unit tests. The [Testing](/pages/testing/) page documents the fake host. It delivers events and records the calls. Use `FakeSession` to run the owner and a stub contributor together, so the test covers the real `list` and `run-hook` path. Use a fixture for host data. Test the pure parts directly, as plain functions. See [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/).

**Rust**

```rust

    #[test]

        let preview = plain_preview("https://example.org/a/b");

    }

    #[test]

```

4. Disable the GitHub package. The owner log must show `0 renderers loaded`.

### What can go wrong

| Code or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.extension-point-invalid`, `manifest.extension-point-duplicate` | A bad id, kind, mode or schema keyword, or two points with one id. | Fix the point entry. |
| `manifest.grant-missing-extension`, `manifest.grant-wildcard` | A point or extension has no matching grant, or the grant ends in `*`. | Add the exact grant. |
| `manifest.extension-entry-invalid` | The entry fails the owner's `entry_schema`. | Match the schema. |
| `extension.schema-mismatch` on `run-hook` | The payload fails `payload_schema`. | Trim title and summary. |
| `extension.cap-exceeded`, `extension.not-dynamic` | Over `max_entries`, or `register` on a static point. | Raise the cap, or set `dynamic`. |
| The renderer never runs | The entry is dormant, disabled, or sorted below another match. | Check the Extensions tab. |
| `not-permitted` from the service | The owner has no `services.use` for the entry's service. | Add the grant, or ignore that renderer. |

# 19. Stop core actions with hooks: quiet hours

## 19. Stop core actions with hooks: quiet hours

This step writes the handler side of extension points. The plugin is `example.quiet-hours`. It adds three handlers to core plugins. A **veto** handler on `ilium.core.notifications/before-notify` refuses low-urgency notices between 22:00 and 07:00. A **veto** handler on `ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire` refuses office rules outside 09:00 to 18:00. A **transform** handler on `ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy` removes secret keys from copied text. The three handlers show what a hook can change, how a handler fails safely, and why one of the grants is high risk.

You start a fresh plugin. You have finished tutorials 1 to 9 and read [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/). The points of the core plugins are listed in [Reference: core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/), and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) compares the five ways to work with a core feature. [Tutorial 18](/pages/tutorial-18-add-an-extension-point/) shows the owner side. This page does not repeat the reference tables.

Tutorial plugin: `example.quiet-hours`, version 0.1.0, API `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Rust and TypeScript behave the same in every step.

### You will need

- Rust: stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crates `ilium-plugin-sdk`, `serde_json` and `regex-lite`. TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- Three grants: `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.notifications/before-notify`, `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy` and `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire`. The last one is high risk, because that point declares `risk: "high"`. A trigger sends text into a terminal, so a handler there can stop a command from reaching an agent.
- A scratch folder for package inspection: `/media/arthur/tmp/quiet-hours/` with a `.scratch-reaper` file in it.

### The surface this step uses

| Area | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest | `contributes.extensions[]` | Entries with `point`, `id`, `priority` and `handler`. |
| Manifest | `exports: ["handler", "hook-handler"]` | A package with a hook extension must list `hook-handler`, or the install fails with `manifest.exports-mismatch`. |
| Export | `hook-handler` | Rust: `HookHandler::handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply`. TypeScript: `handleHook(call)` in `definePlugin`. |
| Call | `HookCall` | `point`, `extension` (the `handler` name), `call` (a number for log lines) and `payload_json`. |
| Replies | `pass`, `replace(json)`, `refuse(reason)`, `answer(json)` | Allowed by mode: `transform` allows `replace`, `veto` allows `refuse`, `first` allows `answer`. |
| Core points | `before-notify` (veto), `before-fire` (veto, high), `after-copy` (transform) | Payload fields are in the reference page and in the code below. |

### The flow

The core plugin runs the chain. Your handler sees one payload and answers with one reply. The kernel stops the chain at the first refusal.

### Step 1: the manifest

The package has one server side, three extensions and the `hook-handler` export. All three handlers run on the server, because all three points belong to server-side core plugins. A handler on the other side fails the install with `manifest.extension-side`.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.quiet-hours",
  "name": "Quiet hours",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Mutes low notices at night, holds office rules after hours and removes keys from copies.",
  "icon": "moon",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["hook-handler"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.notifications/before-notify",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy"
    ]
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      { "point": "ilium.core.notifications/before-notify@0.1.0", "id": "quiet-night",
        "priority": 20, "handler": "quiet_night" },
      { "point": "ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire@0.1.0", "id": "office-hours",
        "priority": 50, "handler": "office_hours" },
      { "point": "ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy@0.1.0", "id": "strip-keys",
        "priority": 70, "handler": "strip_keys" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Points to notice:

- `exports` must list `hook-handler` next to `handler`. A package that lists hook extensions without it fails with `manifest.exports-mismatch`.
- `handler` is a name that your code dispatches on. It reaches you as `call.extension`. The `id` is for the user: it is shown on the Extensions tab and is unique per contributor and point.
- `priority` runs from 0 to 100. Lower runs first, and ties go in plugin id order. Quiet night runs at 20 so that it refuses before other handlers spend their time. The user can override the order, as step 5 shows.
- Each grant names one point. There is no wildcard, and no grant that covers every point. A wildcard fails with `manifest.grant-wildcard`.
- `@0.1.0` asks for a minimum version of the point. The core plugin's point is at that version or newer in the same major. Otherwise the extension is dormant.
- `activation: ["startup"]` keeps the plugin loaded so that the first call does not pay a start. A lazy plugin would start on the first hook call, and that call would count against its 20 ms.

### Step 2: the handlers

A hook handler is a plain function from one call to one reply. It runs synchronously on the contributor's own instance, within `deadline_ms` of the point (20 ms for these three). It may call other host functions that its grants allow, such as `clock`, but each call must finish inside the deadline. It cannot wait for a reply from another plugin.

Each handler does three things. It parses its payload and passes at once when the payload is not what it expected. It decides. It returns one reply. Parsing errors are `pass`, never `refuse`. A broken payload must not stop a notice.

The code keeps the time rules in two small pure functions, so the tests in step 6 can drive them with fixed times. Ilium gives plugins the clock in UTC. The sketch uses a fixed offset constant of 120 minutes. A real plugin reads the offset from a setting, as [tutorial 10](/pages/tutorial-10-settings-new-tab/) shows.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{HookCall, HookHandler, HookReply};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::clock;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use regex_lite::Regex;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const UTC_OFFSET_MINUTES: u64 = 120;
const NIGHT_START: u64 = 22 * 60;
const NIGHT_END: u64 = 7 * 60;
const OFFICE_START: u64 = 9 * 60;
const OFFICE_END: u64 = 18 * 60;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["hook-handler"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct QuietHours {
    refused: u32,
}

impl Lifecycle for QuietHours {}

impl Handler for QuietHours {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn minute_of_day(now_unix_millis: u64) -> u64 {
    (now_unix_millis / 60_000 + UTC_OFFSET_MINUTES) % 1440
}

fn is_night(minute: u64) -> bool {
    minute >= NIGHT_START || minute < NIGHT_END
}

fn is_office(minute: u64) -> bool {
    (OFFICE_START..OFFICE_END).contains(&minute)
}

fn pass() -> HookReply {
    HookReply::Pass
}

impl HookHandler for QuietHours {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        let payload: Value = match serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json) {
            Ok(value) => value,
            Err(_) => return pass(),
        };
        let reply = match call.extension.as_str() {
            "quiet_night" => quiet_night(&payload, clock::now_unix_millis()),
            "office_hours" => office_hours(&payload, clock::now_unix_millis()),
            "strip_keys" => strip_keys(&payload),
            _ => pass(),
        };
        if matches!(reply, HookReply::Refuse(_)) {
            self.refused += 1;
            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("call {} refused ({} so far)", call.call, self.refused));
        }
        reply
    }
}

fn quiet_night(payload: &Value, now: u64) -> HookReply {
    if payload["urgency"] != "low" || !is_night(minute_of_day(now)) {
        return pass();
    }
    HookReply::Refuse("quiet hours until 07:00".to_string())
}

fn office_hours(payload: &Value, now: u64) -> HookReply {
    let is_office_rule = payload["rule"].as_str().is_some_and(|rule| rule.starts_with("office-"));
    if !is_office_rule || is_office(minute_of_day(now)) {
        return pass();
    }
    HookReply::Refuse("office rule outside 09:00 to 18:00".to_string())
}

fn strip_keys(payload: &Value) -> HookReply {
    let Some(text) = payload["text"].as_str() else { return pass() };
    let Ok(pattern) = Regex::new(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}") else { return pass() };
    let cleaned = pattern.replace_all(text, "[removed]");
    if cleaned == text {
        return pass();
    }
    HookReply::Replace(json!({ "text": cleaned }).to_string())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { definePlugin, type HookCall, type HookReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const UTC_OFFSET_MINUTES = 120;
const NIGHT_START = 22 * 60;
const NIGHT_END = 7 * 60;
const OFFICE_START = 9 * 60;
const OFFICE_END = 18 * 60;

export function minuteOfDay(nowMillis: bigint): number {
  return (Number(nowMillis / 60000n) + UTC_OFFSET_MINUTES) % 1440;
}
const isNight = (minute: number): boolean => minute >= NIGHT_START || minute < NIGHT_END;
const isOffice = (minute: number): boolean => minute >= OFFICE_START && minute < OFFICE_END;

const pass = (): HookReply => ({ tag: 'pass' });
const refuse = (reason: string): HookReply => ({ tag: 'refuse', val: reason });
const replace = (payload: unknown): HookReply => ({ tag: 'replace', val: JSON.stringify(payload) });

function quietNight(payload: { urgency?: string }, now: bigint): HookReply {
  if (payload.urgency !== 'low' || !isNight(minuteOfDay(now))) return pass();
  return refuse('quiet hours until 07:00');
}

function officeHours(payload: { rule?: string }, now: bigint): HookReply {
  const isOfficeRule = typeof payload.rule === 'string' && payload.rule.startsWith('office-');
  if (!isOfficeRule || isOffice(minuteOfDay(now))) return pass();
  return refuse('office rule outside 09:00 to 18:00');
}

function stripKeys(payload: { text?: string }): HookReply {
  if (typeof payload.text !== 'string') return pass();
  const cleaned = payload.text.replace(/sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/g, '[removed]');
  return cleaned === payload.text ? pass() : replace({ text: cleaned });
}

let refused = 0;

export function onHook(call: HookCall): HookReply {
    let payload: Record<string, unknown>;
    try {
      payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson) as Record<string, unknown>;
    } catch {
      return pass();
    }
    const now = nowUnixMillis();
    let reply: HookReply;
    switch (call.extension) {
      case 'quiet_night': reply = quietNight(payload, now); break;
      case 'office_hours': reply = officeHours(payload, now); break;
      case 'strip_keys': reply = stripKeys(payload); break;
      default: reply = pass();
    }
    if (reply.tag === 'refuse') {
      refused += 1;
      log('info', `call ${call.call} refused (${refused} so far)`);
    }
    return reply;
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, hookHandler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents() {
    return [];
  },
  handleHook: onHook,
});
```

Points to notice:

- The reply constructors are tiny local functions. They keep the three handlers free of repeated enum syntax and make a wrong reply easy to see in review.
- `strip_keys` is a `transform` handler. It returns `Replace` with a complete payload that matches the point's `reply_schema` (an object with `text`). A reply that fails the schema counts as `pass` and is logged as `extension.schema-mismatch`.
- A reply that the mode does not allow also counts as `pass`. `Refuse` on `after-copy` would log `extension.reply-not-allowed` and change nothing.
- The handlers touch only their payload and the clock. They do no I/O, no file read and no service call. That keeps them far below 20 ms.
- The state is a counter. A handler keeps state only for its own use. It cannot see the owner's state or the other handlers.
- `refuse` carries a short reason. The owner sees it as `example.quiet-hours: quiet hours until 07:00`, and the user sees it in logs and notices. Do not put secrets in a reason.
- The regular expression is compiled for every call in the sketch. Compile it once in a `static` for a hot point. `after-copy` runs on every copy, so keep it cheap.

### Step 3: how a chain ends

The mode of the point decides what a chain does with your reply.

| Point | Mode | Your reply | Result for the core plugin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before-notify` | veto | `refuse(reason)` | The chain stops. The completion is `refused` with code `extension.vetoed`. The notice is dropped. |
| `before-notify` | veto | `pass` | The next handler runs. When all pass, the notice goes on. |
| `before-fire` | veto | `refuse(reason)` | The trigger does not send its reply. The rule is logged as vetoed. |
| `after-copy` | transform | `replace(json)` | The next handler gets your payload as its input. The last payload becomes the copied text. |
| `after-copy` | transform | `pass` | The payload goes on unchanged. |

Three rules limit the damage that a handler can do.

1. **Fail open.** A timeout, a trap or an error counts as `pass`. A slow handler never blocks a notice. It is logged as `extension.handler-timeout`.
2. **Three strikes.** Three breaches in a row disable that extension until the plugin restarts. The Plugins screen shows `stopped after 3 timeouts` and a Reset button. The other two extensions of the package keep running.
3. **A 100 ms chain.** The whole chain has a cap of 100 ms. Handlers after the cap are skipped and logged, so the action goes on.

A handler runs in the contributor's own instance. A T1 plugin shares the Ilium process, so a call is cheap. A T2 or T3 plugin costs one helper round trip per call, so do not use a hook on a path hotter than about 100 calls per second.

### Step 4: grants, risk and the review dialog

Two of the grants are normal risk and one is high.

| Grant | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.notifications/before-notify` | normal | A handler can only hide a notice. |
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy` | normal | A handler can change copied text. It cannot see more than the text, its kind and the pane. |
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire` | **high** | A handler can stop a trigger from sending text into a terminal. The point declares `risk: "high"`. |

The review dialog shows the high-risk grant unchecked. If the user leaves it unchecked, the package installs, but the `office-hours` extension is not granted and does nothing. The other two extensions work. Check `ilium plugin grants example.quiet-hours` to see the state. The user can revoke a grant later with `ilium plugin grants example.quiet-hours --revoke extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire`.

A veto hook is a power. Keep the reason honest, keep the rule narrow, and put the rule in the description so the user knows what the package does. A `high` risk point means that a bundled T1 plugin is also asked for the grant at its first activation.

### Step 5: priority and the user's order

Priority is the order you suggest. The user's order wins. On the owner's Extensions tab, each contributor has a toggle and a move up and down. If the user moves `quiet-night` below another veto handler, the new order applies from then on, and the priority in your manifest is ignored for that point. If the user turns a toggle off, the extension is not called, and its log line is `extension.disabled`.

Write handlers that work in any order. A veto handler is order-independent when each handler judges only its own rule. A transform handler is not: the output of one is the input of the next. Make a transform handler accept the payload shape of the point, not the shape of your own previous output, and always return a payload that fits `reply_schema`.

### Step 6: test the handlers

The fake host described in [Testing](/pages/testing/) delivers events and records submissions. `host.run_hook` drives a hook handler with a `HookCall` and returns the `HookReply`, and `FakeSession.install_core` adds a stub of the core plugin that owns the point. Test the pure time functions and the three handlers. The 20 ms deadline is enforced in component mode (`ilium plugin test --component`), not in native mode. Check it in the app with the log as well, as step 7 shows. See [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/).

**Rust**

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const NIGHT: u64 = 24 * 3_600_000 - UTC_OFFSET_MINUTES * 60_000; // 00:00 local
    const NOON: u64 = 12 * 3_600_000 - UTC_OFFSET_MINUTES * 60_000;

    fn call(extension: &str, payload: serde_json::Value) -> HookCall {
        HookCall {
            point: "test/point".to_string(),
            extension: extension.to_string(),
            call: 1,
            payload_json: payload.to_string(),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn low_notice_is_refused_at_night() {
        let payload = json!({ "urgency": "low" });
        assert!(matches!(quiet_night(&payload, NIGHT), HookReply::Refuse(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn high_notice_is_never_refused() {
        let payload = json!({ "urgency": "high" });
        assert!(matches!(quiet_night(&payload, NIGHT), HookReply::Pass));
    }

    #[test]
    fn low_notice_passes_at_noon() {
        let payload = json!({ "urgency": "low" });
        assert!(matches!(quiet_night(&payload, NOON), HookReply::Pass));
    }

    #[test]
    fn office_rule_is_held_at_night_only() {
        let payload = json!({ "rule": "office-standup" });
        assert!(matches!(office_hours(&payload, NIGHT), HookReply::Refuse(_)));
        assert!(matches!(office_hours(&payload, NOON), HookReply::Pass));
        assert!(matches!(office_hours(&json!({ "rule": "retry" }), NIGHT), HookReply::Pass));
    }

    #[test]
    fn copied_key_is_removed() {
        let mut plugin = QuietHours::default();
        let reply = plugin.handle_hook(call("strip_keys", json!({ "text": "key sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstu end" })));
        match reply {
            HookReply::Replace(text) => assert!(text.contains("[removed]")),
            _ => panic!("expected replace"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn garbage_payload_and_unknown_handler_pass() {
        let mut plugin = QuietHours::default();
        let mut bad = call("quiet_night", json!({}));
        bad.payload_json = "not json".to_string();
        assert!(matches!(plugin.handle_hook(bad), HookReply::Pass));
        assert!(matches!(plugin.handle_hook(call("nobody", json!({}))), HookReply::Pass));
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.test.ts
import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import type { HookCall } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { minuteOfDay, onHook } from './index';

const MIDNIGHT_LOCAL = BigInt((24 * 60 - 120) * 60000); // 00:00 at offset 120
const NOON_LOCAL = BigInt((12 * 60 - 120) * 60000);

function call(extension: string, payload: unknown): HookCall {
  return { point: 'test/point', extension, call: 1n, payloadJson: JSON.stringify(payload) };
}

test('time of day uses the offset', () => {
  expect(minuteOfDay(MIDNIGHT_LOCAL)).toBe(0);
  expect(minuteOfDay(NOON_LOCAL)).toBe(720);
});

test('copied key is removed', () => {
  const reply = onHook(call('strip_keys', { text: 'key sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstu end' }));
  expect(reply.tag).toBe('replace');
});

test('garbage payload and unknown handler pass', () => {
  const bad: HookCall = { ...call('quiet_night', {}), payloadJson: 'not json' };
  expect(onHook(bad).tag).toBe('pass');
  expect(onHook(call('nobody', {})).tag).toBe('pass');
});
```

Export `quietNight` and `officeHours` as well and add the same cases as in the Rust tests: a low notice at night is refused, a high notice never is, and an office rule is held at midnight but not at noon. Run `cargo test` or `bun test`. Then run the plugin against a fixture with `ilium plugin test . --fixture tests/fixtures/idle.json` to check that it activates and does nothing else.

The handler functions take the time as an argument for this reason. A test that reads the real clock would pass in the daytime and fail at night.

### Step 7: pack, install and see it work

Build and pack as in [tutorial 9](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/): `ilium plugin build`, `ilium plugin pack`, then `ilium plugin keygen`, `ilium plugin sign` and `ilium plugin trust add` once. Install `dist/example.quiet-hours-0.1.0.iliumpkg`. An unsigned package is T3 and needs `--allow-unsigned`.

### Security and consent

| Concern | What the plugin does |
|---|---|
| What the handlers see | The payload of one call. `before-notify` shows the title and the pane, so the plugin sees what a notice says. Say so in the description. |
| What the handlers can change | A veto can hide a notice or hold a trigger. A transform can edit copied text. Nothing else. |
| High-risk grant | `before-fire` is high risk. The user opts in. A refused grant leaves the other two handlers working. |
| Reasons | A refusal reason is shown in logs. It holds no secret and no text from the payload. |
| Fail open | A bug in the plugin cannot silence the product. It can only fail to help. |
| Copy edits | `strip_keys` removes text. It never adds text. Test it, because a bad pattern can corrupt a copy. |

### Edge cases and errors: what can go wrong

| Code or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.exports-mismatch` | Hook extensions without `hook-handler` in `exports`. | Add the export. |
| `manifest.extension-side` | The handler is declared on a different side from the point's calls. | Declare it on the side that owns the call. |
| `manifest.grant-missing-extension` | An extension has no matching `extensions.contribute` grant. | Add the exact grant. |
| `manifest.grant-wildcard` | A grant ends in `*`. | Name one point. |
| `manifest.extension-limit` | More than 64 extensions in one plugin. | Merge handlers. |
| Extension is dormant | The owner is missing, or the point version is older than `@0.1.0`. | Install the owner, or lower the version. |
| `extension.handler-timeout` | The handler took over 20 ms. It counts as pass. | Remove I/O. Precompile patterns. |
| `extension.disabled` | Three breaches, or the user turned it off. | Fix the cause, then Reset. |
| `extension.reply-not-allowed` | A reply that the mode does not allow, for example `refuse` on a transform. | Use the reply of the mode. |
| `extension.schema-mismatch` | A `replace` that fails the `reply_schema`. | Return a complete object. |
| `extension.vetoed` | Your own refusal, as the core plugin sees it. | Not an error of yours. |
| A refusal has no effect | Another handler runs first, or the extension is toggled off. | Check the Extensions tab. |
| Wrong hour | The clock is in UTC and the offset is wrong. | Fix the offset constant. |

- [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) for the quiet hours scenario and the other ways to extend.

# 20. Extend six core plugins from one package: a team pack

## 20. Extend six core plugins from one package: a team pack

This step is mostly manifest work. The plugin is `example.team-pack`, a package that a team installs once. It adds one entry to each of six core plugins: a recogniser for Smart Copy, a rule pack for Text Triggers, a price source for Cost, a palette for Ambient, a key hint for Keys and help, and an instruction block for Agent setup. Almost all of it is data in `contributes.extensions`, and it needs no code. One part needs code: the per-project rules. The team keeps a file `.ilium/team-rules.json` in each repository, and the plugin registers its rules at run time with `register`.

You start a fresh plugin. You have finished tutorials 1 to 9 and read [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/). The points of every core plugin are in [Reference: core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/). [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) compares the ways to extend a core feature. [Tutorial 18](/pages/tutorial-18-add-an-extension-point/) shows the owner side, and [tutorial 19](/pages/tutorial-19-stop-core-actions-with-hooks/) the hook side. This page does not repeat the reference tables.

Tutorial plugin: `example.team-pack`, version 0.1.0, API `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Rust and TypeScript behave the same in every step.

### You will need

- Rust: stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crates `ilium-plugin-sdk` and `serde_json`. TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- Seven grants: one `extensions.contribute:<point>` for each of the six points, and `fs.read:project` for the rules file. Step 1 lists them.
- A file `help/team-style.md` in the package. The instruction block points to it.
- A scratch folder for package inspection: `/media/arthur/tmp/team-pack/` with a `.scratch-reaper` file in it.

### The surface this step uses

| Core plugin | Point (global id) | Kind | Entry fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| Smart Copy | `ilium.core.smart-copy/recognisers` | collect | `id`, `kind`, `regex`, `multiline`, `label` |
| Text Triggers | `ilium.core.text-triggers/rule-packs` | collect | `id`, `title`, `rules` (a list of `pattern`, `reply`, `enabled`) |
| Cost | `ilium.core.cost/price-sources` | collect | `id`, `model_pattern`, `input_per_mtok`, `output_per_mtok`, `cache_read_per_mtok`, `currency` |
| Ambient | `ilium.core.ambient/palettes` | collect | `id`, `title`, `stops` |
| Keys and help | `ilium.core.keys-and-help/key-hints` | collect | `id`, `context`, `chord`, `label` |
| Agent setup | `ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks` | collect | `id`, `title`, `marker`, `file` |

The host calls are `extensions::register` and `unregister` (TypeScript `register` and `unregister`) for the run-time part, and `fs::read_all` for the rules file. The kernel topic `ilium.extensions/changed` goes to each owner when your entries change.

### The flow

Install does the six static contributions by itself. The code runs afterwards and adds the per-project rules.
