### Step 1: the manifest

The manifest is the larger part of the package. It has seven grants, six extensions and one export. It has a `server` side for the run-time part only. The extensions do not belong to a side: a collect entry is data.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.team-pack",
  "name": "Team pack",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Adds the team's patterns, prices, palette, hints and agent notes.",
  "icon": "package",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/recognisers",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.text-triggers/rule-packs",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.cost/price-sources",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.ambient/palettes",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.keys-and-help/key-hints",
      "extensions.contribute:ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks",
      "fs.read:project"
    ]
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "reload-rules", "title": "Team pack: reload project rules" }
    ],
    "extensions": [
      { "point": "ilium.core.smart-copy/recognisers@0.1.0", "id": "ticket",
        "entry": { "id": "ticket", "kind": "ticket", "regex": "TEAM-[0-9]{1,6}",
                   "multiline": false, "label": "Ticket key" } },
      { "point": "ilium.core.text-triggers/rule-packs@0.1.0", "id": "team-basics",
        "entry": { "id": "team-basics", "title": "Team basics",
                   "rules": [
                     { "pattern": "Run the tests\\? \\(y/n\\)", "reply": "y\n", "enabled": false }
                   ] } },
      { "point": "ilium.core.cost/price-sources@0.1.0", "id": "internal-model",
        "entry": { "id": "internal-model", "model_pattern": "^team-llm-.*",
                   "input_per_mtok": 1.5, "output_per_mtok": 6.0,
                   "cache_read_per_mtok": 0.15, "currency": "EUR" } },
      { "point": "ilium.core.ambient/palettes@0.1.0", "id": "harbour",
        "entry": { "id": "harbour", "title": "Harbour",
                   "stops": ["#0b1d2a", "#1f6f8b", "#99d5c9", "#f6f1d1"] } },
      { "point": "ilium.core.keys-and-help/key-hints@0.1.0", "id": "board-new",
        "entry": { "id": "board-new", "context": "pane:board", "chord": "n",
                   "label": "New card" } },
      { "point": "ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks@0.1.0", "id": "team-style",
        "entry": { "id": "team-style", "title": "Team style notes",
                   "marker": "team-style", "file": "help/team-style.md" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

Points to notice:

- Each extension needs its own grant, and each grant names one point. There is no "contribute to any" grant, and a wildcard fails with `manifest.grant-wildcard`. A missing grant fails with `manifest.grant-missing-extension`.
- `point` carries `@0.1.0`. The owner must offer that version or a newer minor in the same major. Otherwise the entry stays dormant.
- `priority` is left out. The default is 50. Collect entries are listed in priority order, so priority matters only when two entries compete, such as two recognisers that match the same text.
- Backslashes in a JSON string are doubled. The Text Triggers pattern `Run the tests\\? \\(y/n\\)` reaches the owner as `Run the tests\? \(y/n\)`.
- The trigger rule is `enabled: false`. A rule pack is a set the user turns on. It never starts sending text by itself.
- The price source is data. It makes Cost able to price a model the built-in table does not know. It does not change the prices of known models.
- `help/team-style.md` must exist in the package. A missing file fails with `manifest.extension-entry-invalid`, because the entry names a file the package does not hold.
- `reload-rules` is a command of the plugin, as in tutorial 3. It reads the file again without a restart.
- The plugin has no `hook-handler` export. It contributes no hook.

### Step 2: what the schema checks

The kernel checks each entry against the owner's `entry_schema` when the package is installed. It does not run any of your code for this. If one entry fails, the whole install fails, and no extension of the package is added.

Break the price source on purpose. Change `"input_per_mtok": 1.5` to `"input_per_mtok": "1.5"` and run `ilium plugin build`. The error names the entry and the field:

<figure>
<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin build
<span class="t-err">error manifest.extension-entry-invalid</span>
  contributes.extensions[2].entry.input_per_mtok
  expected number, found string
  point ilium.core.cost/price-sources
<span class="t-dim">1 error, 0 warnings</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The path counts extensions from 0, so index 2 is the third entry, the price source.</figcaption>
</figure>

Restore the number. The same code covers a missing required field, a string over its `maxLength`, a list over `maxItems`, an entry over 16 KiB and a field that is not in `properties` when the schema forbids extra fields. A palette with only one stop fails if the owner's schema requires at least two.

### Step 3: the run-time part

Teams keep different rules per repository. Build the rule pack from the file `.ilium/team-rules.json` of the open project, and register it with `register`. The file looks like this:

```json
{
  "packs": [
    { "id": "release", "title": "Release checks",
      "rules": [ { "pattern": "Publish\\? \\(y/n\\)", "reply": "n\n", "enabled": false } ] }
  ]
}
```

The code has three parts. A pure function turns the file text into entries. A function registers the entries through a callback, so a test can replace the host call. The handler runs both on start and on the command.

Two facts matter. First, `register` works only on a point that is `dynamic`. If the Text Triggers point is static, `register` returns `not-dynamic`. The plugin does not crash. It logs one line and keeps the static entries. Second, `register` validates the entry again, so a bad rule in the file gives `schema-mismatch` for that pack only, and the other packs still register.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs::{self, FsPath};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::task;
use serde_json::Value;

const RULE_PACKS: &str = "ilium.core.text-triggers/rule-packs";
const RULES_FILE: &str = ".ilium/team-rules.json";
const MAX_PACKS: usize = 16;

/// Turns the text of the rules file into (extension id, entry JSON) pairs.
/// A pack that is not an object with an id is skipped, and the pack count is capped.
pub fn packs_from_file(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let Ok(file) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(text) else { return Vec::new() };
    let Some(packs) = file["packs"].as_array() else { return Vec::new() };
    packs
        .iter()
        .take(MAX_PACKS)
        .filter_map(|pack| {
            let id = pack["id"].as_str()?;
            // The file is untrusted. Force every rule to disabled.
            let mut entry = pack.clone();
            for rule in entry["rules"].as_array_mut()? {
                rule["enabled"] = Value::Bool(false);
            }
            Some((format!("project-{id}"), entry.to_string()))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Registers every pack. Returns how many were accepted.
pub fn register_packs(
    packs: &[(String, String)],
    register: &mut dyn FnMut(&str, &str) -> Result<(), String>,
) -> usize {
    let mut accepted = 0;
    for (extension, entry_json) in packs {
        match register(extension, entry_json) {
            Ok(()) => accepted += 1,
            Err(reason) if reason.contains("NotDynamic") => {
                log::log(Level::Warn, "rule-packs is not dynamic; project rules skipped");
                break;
            }
            Err(reason) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{extension} refused: {reason}")),
        }
    }
    accepted
}

async fn load_project_rules() {
    let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: RULES_FILE.into() };
    let bytes = match fs::read_all(&path).await {
        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
        Err(code) => {
            // A project without the file is normal.
            log::log(Level::Debug, &format!("no team rules: {code}"));
            return;
        }
    };
    let packs = packs_from_file(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes));
    let mut register = |extension: &str, entry_json: &str| {
        extensions::register(RULE_PACKS, extension, 50, entry_json).map_err(|error| format!("{error:?}"))
    };
    let accepted = register_packs(&packs, &mut register);
    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{accepted} of {} project packs registered", packs.len()));
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct TeamPack;

impl Lifecycle for TeamPack {
    fn activate(&mut self) {
        task::spawn(load_project_rules());
    }
}

impl Handler for TeamPack {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event {
                if invoked.command == "example.team-pack/reload-rules" {
                    task::spawn(load_project_rules());
                }
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { register } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';
import { readAll } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const RULE_PACKS = 'ilium.core.text-triggers/rule-packs';
const RULES_FILE = '.ilium/team-rules.json';
const MAX_PACKS = 16;

type Pack = { extension: string; entryJson: string };

/** Turns the text of the rules file into extension ids and entry JSON. */
export function packsFromFile(text: string): Pack[] {
  let file: { packs?: Array<{ id?: unknown; rules?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }> };
  try {
    file = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(file.packs)) return [];
  return file.packs.slice(0, MAX_PACKS).flatMap((pack) => {
    if (typeof pack.id !== 'string' || !Array.isArray(pack.rules)) return [];
    // The file is untrusted. Force every rule to disabled.
    const rules = pack.rules.map((rule) => ({ ...rule, enabled: false }));
    return [{ extension: `project-${pack.id}`, entryJson: JSON.stringify({ ...pack, rules }) }];
  });
}

/** Registers every pack. Returns how many were accepted. */
export function registerPacks(packs: Pack[], put: (extension: string, entryJson: string) => void): number {
  let accepted = 0;
  for (const pack of packs) {
    try {
      put(pack.extension, pack.entryJson);
      accepted += 1;
    } catch (error) {
      const code = String((error as { code?: string }).code ?? error);
      if (code.includes('not-dynamic')) {
        log('warn', 'rule-packs is not dynamic; project rules skipped');
        break;
      }
      log('warn', `${pack.extension} refused: ${code}`);
    }
  }
  return accepted;
}

async function loadProjectRules(): Promise<void> {
  let bytes: Uint8Array;
  try {
    bytes = await readAll({ scope: 'project', path: RULES_FILE });
  } catch (error) {
    // A project without the file is normal.
    log('debug', `no team rules: ${String(error)}`);
    return;
  }
  const packs = packsFromFile(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes));
  const accepted = registerPacks(packs, (extension, entryJson) => register(RULE_PACKS, extension, 50, entryJson));
  log('info', `${accepted} of ${packs.length} project packs registered`);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    void loadProjectRules();
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'example.team-pack/reload-rules') {
        void loadProjectRules();
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- `fs.read:project` reads one file. The plugin has no write grant, so it cannot change the repository.
- The file belongs to the repository, so anyone who can commit to it can write rules. That is why `enabled` is forced to `false`. A cloned repository must not make an agent answer prompts by itself. The user enables a pack on the Text Triggers screen.
- The pack ids start with `project-`, so they never clash with the static `team-basics`. Registering an id again replaces that entry, so the command can be run any number of times.
- `register` is bounded. The point has `max_entries` and a pack has a size cap of 16 KiB. The plugin caps itself at 16 packs and stays inside both.
- `load_project_rules` is async because `read_all` is async. The activation returns at once, and the work finishes later. A hook does not wait for it.
- Entries registered at run time are not kept when the plugin restarts. `activate` registers them again.
- To drop a pack that has left the file, keep the ids of the previous load and call `unregister` for each id that is gone. A plugin can remove only entries it registered.

### Step 4: dormant, updated and disabled contributions

The package works only when the owners are present.

| Owner state | Your entry | What the Plugins screen shows |
|---|---|---|
| Installed and enabled | Active | The entry with its toggle on |
| Not installed | Dormant | `waiting for ilium.core.cost` |
| Disabled by the user | Dormant, toggle kept | `waiting for ilium.core.cost` |
| Installed, point version too old | Dormant | The version the owner must reach |
| Installed, point removed | Dormant | `waiting for ilium.core.cost` |

Install never fails because an owner is missing. All six owners are bundled core plugins, so in practice they are present.

When you ship the next version of the package, the kernel checks every entry again. Suppose the Cost owner releases a new major version of its point with a changed schema. Your entry, which asks for `@0.1.0`, no longer matches, and that entry goes dormant. The other five stay active, and the user sees a line for the entry. Raise your entry to the new version and change its fields.

When the package is updated, the owners hear `ilium.extensions/changed` once for each point whose entries changed. A point whose entries did not change hears nothing.

### Step 5: pack, review and install

Build and pack as in [tutorial 9](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/): `ilium plugin build`, `ilium plugin pack`, `ilium plugin keygen --publisher "Example Developer" --out <dir>`, `ilium plugin sign <file> --key <publisher.key>` and `ilium plugin trust add <publisher.pub>` once. Then `ilium plugin install dist/example.team-pack-0.1.0.iliumpkg`. An unsigned package is T3 and needs `--allow-unsigned`.

#### What you see

The review dialog lists the six contributions under **Adds to other plugins**, by owner. All six grants are normal risk, so all are checked. The file grant is listed with them.

### Step 6: test it

The fake host described in [Testing](/pages/testing/) has no registry, so it cannot run the owners. Test what you wrote. That is the manifest, the pure function that reads the file and the function that registers the packs.

1. **Manifest.** Run `ilium plugin build` with each entry broken in turn: a number as a string, a missing `file`, and a removed grant. Expect `manifest.extension-entry-invalid` and `manifest.grant-missing-extension`.
2. **File parser.** Feed `packs_from_file` or `packsFromFile` a good file, a file that is not JSON, a file without `packs`, a pack without an id and a pack with 20 entries.
3. **Registration.** Give `register_packs` or `registerPacks` a callback that fails with `NotDynamic`, one that fails with `SchemaMismatch` for the first pack only, and one that always succeeds.

**Rust**

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const GOOD: &str = r#"{"packs":[{"id":"release","title":"Release","rules":[{"pattern":"p","reply":"n\n","enabled":true}]}]}"#;

    #[test]
    fn every_rule_is_forced_to_disabled() {
        let packs = packs_from_file(GOOD);
        assert_eq!(packs.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(packs[0].0, "project-release");
        assert!(packs[0].1.contains(r#""enabled":false"#));
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_files_give_no_packs() {
        assert!(packs_from_file("not json").is_empty());
        assert!(packs_from_file("{}").is_empty());
        assert!(packs_from_file(r#"{"packs":[{"title":"no id","rules":[]}]}"#).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn pack_count_is_capped() {
        let many = (0..20).map(|n| format!(r#"{{"id":"p{n}","rules":[]}}"#)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",");
        assert_eq!(packs_from_file(&format!(r#"{{"packs":[{many}]}}"#)).len(), MAX_PACKS);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_static_point_stops_the_loop() {
        let packs = packs_from_file(GOOD);
        let mut calls = 0;
        let mut register = |_: &str, _: &str| {
            calls += 1;
            Err("NotDynamic".to_string())
        };
        assert_eq!(register_packs(&packs, &mut register), 0);
        assert_eq!(calls, 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn one_refused_pack_does_not_stop_the_others() {
        let two = r#"{"packs":[{"id":"a","rules":[]},{"id":"b","rules":[]}]}"#;
        let mut register = |extension: &str, _: &str| {
            if extension == "project-a" { Err("SchemaMismatch".to_string()) } else { Ok(()) }
        };
        assert_eq!(register_packs(&packs_from_file(two), &mut register), 1);
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.test.ts
import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { packsFromFile, registerPacks } from './index';

const GOOD = '{"packs":[{"id":"release","title":"Release","rules":[{"pattern":"p","reply":"n\\n","enabled":true}]}]}';

test('every rule is forced to disabled', () => {
  const packs = packsFromFile(GOOD);
  expect(packs.length).toBe(1);
  expect(packs[0].extension).toBe('project-release');
  expect(packs[0].entryJson).toContain('"enabled":false');
});

test('bad files give no packs', () => {
  expect(packsFromFile('not json')).toEqual([]);
  expect(packsFromFile('{}')).toEqual([]);
  expect(packsFromFile('{"packs":[{"title":"no id","rules":[]}]}')).toEqual([]);
});

test('pack count is capped', () => {
  const many = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, n) => ({ id: `p${n}`, rules: [] }));
  expect(packsFromFile(JSON.stringify({ packs: many })).length).toBe(16);
});

test('a static point stops the loop', () => {
  let calls = 0;
  const accepted = registerPacks(packsFromFile(GOOD), () => {
    calls += 1;
    throw Object.assign(new Error('x'), { code: 'extension.not-dynamic' });
  });
  expect(accepted).toBe(0);
  expect(calls).toBe(1);
});

test('one refused pack does not stop the others', () => {
  const two = JSON.stringify({ packs: [{ id: 'a', rules: [] }, { id: 'b', rules: [] }] });
  const accepted = registerPacks(packsFromFile(two), (extension) => {
    if (extension === 'project-a') throw Object.assign(new Error('x'), { code: 'extension.schema-mismatch' });
  });
  expect(accepted).toBe(1);
});
```

Run `cargo test` or `bun test`. Then check it in the app. Install the package, open Settings > Text triggers and look for `Team basics`. Put the sample file in a project, run `Team pack: reload project rules` and look for `Release checks` in the same list, switched off. Copy a line with `TEAM-123` and check that Smart Copy offers it as a ticket. Open Settings > Plugins, disable Cost, and check that `internal-model` says `waiting for ilium.core.cost`.

### Security and consent

| Grant | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions.contribute:` six points | normal | Each point is data. None is a hook. |
| `fs.read:project` | normal | The plugin reads one file, `.ilium/team-rules.json`. It cannot write. |

- A rule pack can make Text Triggers send text to a terminal once the user enables it. The package never enables a rule itself, and it forces every project rule to `enabled: false`.
- The instruction block is text that Agent setup writes into agent files between markers. The user runs Agent setup, and the block is shown before it is written. Keep the file free of secrets and of commands you do not want an agent to follow.
- A price source changes a number that the user reads. A wrong price misleads. Keep prices in the package, signed and reviewed.
- A recogniser can slow Smart Copy if its regex is expensive. Keep patterns anchored and short.

### What can go wrong

| Code or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.extension-entry-invalid` | An entry fails the owner's `entry_schema`, or names a file that the package does not hold. | Match the schema. Include the file. |
| `manifest.grant-missing-extension` | An extension has no `extensions.contribute` grant for its point. | Add the exact grant. |
| `manifest.grant-wildcard` | A grant ends in `*`. | Name one point. |
| `manifest.extension-limit` | More than 64 extensions in one plugin. | Merge entries, or split the package. |
| Entry shows `waiting for <owner>` | The owner is disabled, or the point version is too new. | Enable the owner, or lower `@version`. |
| `extension.not-dynamic` | `register` on a point that is static. | Put the entry in the manifest. |
| `extension.schema-mismatch` | A run-time entry fails the schema. | Fix the pack in the file. |
| `extension.cap-exceeded` | The point holds `max_entries`, or the entry is over 16 KiB. | Register fewer or smaller packs. |
| `not-permitted` on the file | No `fs.read:project`, or the path leaves the project. | Add the grant. Use a path inside the project. |
| `no team rules: not-found` | The project has no rules file. | Nothing. This is normal. |
| Project pack is off | The plugin forces `enabled: false`. | The user enables it. |

# 21. Replace a core plugin: Titles Lite

## 21. Replace a core plugin: Titles Lite

This step replaces a core plugin. The plugin is `example.titles-lite`. It takes the place of `ilium.core.titles`, the plugin that names panes from the prompts you send. The replacement is deliberately small. It names a pane once, from the first prompt, with four words or fewer. It keeps every item of the surface of the plugin it replaces, so the services, points and topics that other plugins use keep working. It drops the rest: the preview panel, the tree tidy and the settings tab.

Replacement is the heaviest of the five ways to work with a core plugin. The built-in plugin is turned off while yours is on, and you must keep up with it. Use it only when no extension point is enough. [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/) compares all five, and [Reference: core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/) lists the surface of each plugin. [Core plugin: titles](/pages/core-plugin-titles/) describes the plugin you replace. This page does not repeat those tables.

You start a fresh plugin. You have finished tutorials 1 to 9 and read [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/), [tutorial 18](/pages/tutorial-18-add-an-extension-point/) and [tutorial 19](/pages/tutorial-19-stop-core-actions-with-hooks/). Tutorial plugin: `example.titles-lite`, version 0.1.0, API `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Rust and TypeScript behave the same in every step.

### You will need

- Rust: stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crates `ilium-plugin-sdk` and `serde_json`. TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- Grants, with the reason for each in the table of step 5: `inference`, `agent.read-prompts`, `tree.read`, `tree.write`, `services.provide:ilium.core.titles/suggest`, `extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/before-apply-title` and `extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/title-styles`.
- `"unstable": ["plugin-services"]`, because `suggest` is a plugin-defined service (dev mode, T2 and T3).
- An AI provider that the user has set up. The titles come from [Inference providers](/pages/core-plugin-inference/).
- A scratch folder for package inspection: `/media/arthur/tmp/titles-lite/` with a `.scratch-reaper` file in it.

### The surface this step uses

`ilium.core.titles` is replaceable and lists four surface items. A replacement must provide all four.

| Surface item | What the replacement provides | Declared as |
|---|---|---|
| `services:suggest` | A service that returns a title for some text | `contributes.services.provides` and `services.provide:ilium.core.titles/suggest` |
| `points:before-apply-title` | A transform hook, run before a title is applied | `contributes.extension_points` and `extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/before-apply-title` |
| `points:title-styles` | A collect point of styles with an instruction text | `contributes.extension_points` and `extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/title-styles` |
| `topics:title-applied` | A topic with `{ node, title }` | `contributes.topics.publishes` |

The replacement uses the names of the plugin it replaces, such as `ilium.core.titles/suggest`. This is what lets every extension and every caller written for the core plugin go on working. It is allowed only for a plugin that lists the id in `replaces`. Any other plugin that uses a name with another plugin's id is refused.

Other parts of the surface of this step: the top-level key `"replaces": ["ilium.core.titles"]` (at most 4 ids), the host call `inference::complete_request` for the model, `extensions::run_hook_request` and `take_reply` for the hook, and `topics::publish`.

### The flow

One prompt becomes one title in four moves. The model proposes, the hook may adjust, the plugin applies and then tells the rest of the product.

### Step 1: the manifest

The manifest has the key `replaces`, the four surface items and the grants. The plugin has a server side only. The core plugin has a client side for its preview panel, and the replacement does not need one.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.titles-lite",
  "name": "Titles Lite",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Names a pane once, from its first prompt, in four words or fewer.",
  "icon": "tag",
  "replaces": ["ilium.core.titles"],
  "unstable": ["plugin-services"],
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["service-provider"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "inference",
      "agent.read-prompts",
      "tree.read",
      "tree.write",
      "services.provide:ilium.core.titles/suggest",
      "extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/before-apply-title",
      "extensions.provide:ilium.core.titles/title-styles",
      "topics.subscribe:ilium.extensions/changed"
    ]
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "topics": {
      "publishes": ["ilium.core.titles/title-applied"],
      "subscribes": ["ilium.extensions/changed"]
    },
    "services": {
      "provides": [
        { "name": "ilium.core.titles/suggest", "version": "0.1.0", "schema": "schemas/suggest.json" }
      ]
    },
    "extension_points": [
      {
        "id": "before-apply-title",
        "kind": "hook",
        "mode": "transform",
        "title": "Before a title is applied",
        "version": "0.1.0",
        "deadline_ms": 20,
        "payload_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["node", "proposed", "source"],
          "properties": {
            "node": { "type": "integer" },
            "proposed": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 120 },
            "source": { "type": "string", "enum": ["transcript", "process", "manual-trigger"] },
            "previous": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 120 }
          }
        },
        "reply_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["proposed"],
          "properties": { "proposed": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 120 } }
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "title-styles",
        "kind": "collect",
        "title": "Title styles",
        "version": "0.1.0",
        "max_entries": 16,
        "entry_schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["id", "title", "instruction"],
          "properties": {
            "id": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 64 },
            "title": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 60 },
            "instruction": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 400 }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`schemas/suggest.json` describes the `title` method: its params are `{ "text": string }` with a `maxLength` of 4000, and its result is `{ "title": string }`.

Points to notice:

- `replaces` takes ids. Install checks every one. An unknown id fails with `manifest.replaces-unknown`. A core plugin with `replaceable: false` fails with `manifest.replaces-not-replaceable`. Two packages that replace each other fail with `manifest.replaces-cycle`. No grant is needed for `replaces`. The consent is the user's, in the review dialog.
- The service, the points and the topic use the id `ilium.core.titles`, not `example.titles-lite`. A name with a foreign id is refused in any plugin that does not replace that id.
- The point schemas must be compatible with the core plugin's: the same field names and types, so a handler written for the core plugin sees what it expects. Copy the shape from [Reference: core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/) and the page [Core plugin: titles](/pages/core-plugin-titles/), and keep `version` at the same number.
- There is no `tree.restructure`. That high-risk grant belongs to the tree tidy, which the replacement drops. The review dialog is shorter for it.
- The plugin subscribes to `ilium.extensions/changed` because it owns `title-styles` and reloads the list when a contributor changes it. That topic goes to the owner only.

### Step 2: the logic

The plugin has four jobs. It names a pane from the first prompt. It answers the `suggest` service. It runs the hook before it applies a title. It publishes the topic. All four share one small state machine, because each step ends in a `request-completed` event.

The state is a map from request id to what the request was for.

| Pending kind | Started by | Ends with |
|---|---|---|
| `Inference` for a pane | `input-submitted` | Run the hook with the proposed title |
| `Inference` for a service call | A `suggest` call | Reply to the call with the title |
| `Hook` for a pane | End of the inference | Rename the pane, publish the topic |

Titles Lite keeps a set of panes it has already titled. It names a pane once. A title typed by hand is never replaced, because the host answers `refused(conflict)` to an inferred rename against a manual title, and the plugin only reads the outcome.

**Rust**

```rust
// src/lib.rs
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

use ilium_plugin_sdk::dedup;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::topics;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::RenameNodeSpec;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const BEFORE_APPLY: &str = "ilium.core.titles/before-apply-title";
const STYLES: &str = "ilium.core.titles/title-styles";
const APPLIED: &str = "ilium.core.titles/title-applied";
const DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION: &str = "Reply with a title of at most four words and nothing else.";

enum Pending {
    PaneTitle(NodeId),
    ServiceTitle(u64),
    Hook { node: NodeId, proposed: String },
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["service-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct TitlesLite {
    pending: HashMap<RequestId, Pending>,
    titled: HashSet<NodeId>,
    instruction: String,
}

/// Keeps a model reply to at most four plain words.
pub fn clean_title(raw: &str) -> String {
    let words: Vec<&str> = raw
        .trim()
        .trim_matches(|c: char| c == '"' || c == '\'' || c == '`' || c == '.')
        .split_whitespace()
        .take(4)
        .collect();
    words.join(" ")
}

/// The instruction of the first style in run order, or the default.
pub fn instruction_from(entries_json: &[String]) -> String {
    entries_json
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(entry).ok())
        .find_map(|entry| entry["instruction"].as_str().map(str::to_string))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION.to_string())
}

fn ask(instruction: &str, text: &str) -> Result<RequestId, PluginError> {
    inference::complete_request(CompletionRequest {
        messages: vec![
            ChatMessage { role: "system".into(), content: instruction.into() },
            ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: text.chars().take(4000).collect() },
        ],
        max_output_tokens: Some(24),
        json_schema: None,
        purpose: "pane-title".into(),
    })
}

impl TitlesLite {
    fn reload_styles(&mut self) {
        let entries = extensions::list(STYLES).unwrap_or_default();
        let json_entries: Vec<String> = entries.into_iter().map(|entry| entry.entry_json).collect();
        self.instruction = instruction_from(&json_entries);
    }
}

impl Lifecycle for TitlesLite {
    fn activate(&mut self) {
        self.reload_styles();
    }
}

impl Handler for TitlesLite {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::TopicPublished(published) if published.topic == "ilium.extensions/changed" => {
                    self.reload_styles();
                }
                Event::InputSubmitted(input) if self.titled.insert(input.node) => {
                    match ask(&self.instruction, &input.text) {
                        Ok(id) => {
                            self.pending.insert(id, Pending::PaneTitle(input.node));
                        }
                        Err(error) => {
                            self.titled.remove(&input.node);
                            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("no title: {}", error.code));
                        }
                    }
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(done) => {
                    let Some(pending) = self.pending.remove(&done.request) else { continue };
                    self.finish(pending, done.request, &mut submissions);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}

impl TitlesLite {
    fn finish(&mut self, pending: Pending, request: RequestId, submissions: &mut Vec<Submission>) {
        match pending {
            Pending::PaneTitle(node) => {
                let proposed = inference::take_completion(request).map(|c| clean_title(&c.text)).unwrap_or_default();
                if proposed.is_empty() {
                    self.titled.remove(&node);
                    return;
                }
                let payload = json!({ "node": node, "proposed": proposed, "source": "transcript" }).to_string();
                match extensions::run_hook_request(BEFORE_APPLY, &payload) {
                    Ok(id) => {
                        self.pending.insert(id, Pending::Hook { node, proposed });
                    }
                    Err(_) => apply(node, &proposed, submissions),
                }
            }
            Pending::ServiceTitle(call) => {
                let title = inference::take_completion(request).map(|c| clean_title(&c.text)).unwrap_or_default();
                let _ = services::reply(call, Ok(json!({ "title": title }).to_string()));
            }
            Pending::Hook { node, proposed } => {
                // No handler, or a refused chain, leaves the proposed title as it is.
                let adjusted = extensions::take_reply(request)
                    .and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text).ok())
                    .and_then(|value| value["proposed"].as_str().map(clean_title))
                    .filter(|title| !title.is_empty());
                apply(node, &adjusted.unwrap_or(proposed), submissions);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn apply(node: NodeId, title: &str, submissions: &mut Vec<Submission>) {
    let key = dedup::key_for(&["title", &node.to_string(), title]);
    submissions.push(Submission::keyed(
        Intent::RenameNode(RenameNodeSpec { node, title: title.to_string(), expected_revision: None }),
        key,
    ));
    let payload = json!({ "node": node, "title": title }).to_string();
    if let Err(error) = topics::publish(APPLIED, &payload) {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("publish failed: {error:?}"));
    }
}

impl ServiceProvider for TitlesLite {
    fn handle(&mut self, call: ServiceCall) -> ServiceReply {
        let params: Value = serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        let Some(text) = params["text"].as_str() else {
            return ServiceReply::Done(json!({ "title": "" }).to_string());
        };
        match ask(&self.instruction, text) {
            Ok(id) => {
                self.pending.insert(id, Pending::ServiceTitle(call.call));
                ServiceReply::Deferred
            }
            Err(_) => ServiceReply::Done(json!({ "title": "" }).to_string()),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { ServiceCall, ServiceReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { list, runHookRequest, takeReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';
import { completeRequest, takeCompletion } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { reply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';
import { publish } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/topics';

const BEFORE_APPLY = 'ilium.core.titles/before-apply-title';
const STYLES = 'ilium.core.titles/title-styles';
const APPLIED = 'ilium.core.titles/title-applied';
const DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION = 'Reply with a title of at most four words and nothing else.';

type Pending =
  | { kind: 'pane'; node: bigint }
  | { kind: 'service'; call: bigint }
  | { kind: 'hook'; node: bigint; proposed: string };

const pending = new Map<bigint, Pending>();
const titled = new Set<bigint>();
let instruction = DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION;
let correlation = 1n;

/** Keeps a model reply to at most four plain words. */
export function cleanTitle(raw: string): string {
  return raw.trim().replace(/^["'`.]+|["'`.]+$/g, '').split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 4).join(' ');
}

/** The instruction of the first style in run order, or the default. */
export function instructionFrom(entriesJson: string[]): string {
  for (const text of entriesJson) {
    try {
      const entry = JSON.parse(text) as { instruction?: unknown };
      if (typeof entry.instruction === 'string') return entry.instruction;
    } catch {
      // A broken entry is skipped.
    }
  }
  return DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION;
}

function ask(text: string): bigint {
  return completeRequest({
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: instruction },
      { role: 'user', content: text.slice(0, 4000) },
    ],
    maxOutputTokens: 24,
    jsonSchema: undefined,
    purpose: 'pane-title',
  });
}

function reloadStyles(): void {
  try {
    instruction = instructionFrom(list(STYLES).map((entry) => entry.entryJson));
  } catch {
    instruction = DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION;
  }
}

function apply(node: bigint, title: string, submissions: Submission[]): void {
  submissions.push({
    intent: { tag: 'rename-node', val: { node, title, source: 'inferred', expectedRevision: undefined } },
    correlation: correlation++,
    dedupKey: `title:${node}:${title}`.slice(0, 128).replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._:/-]/g, '-'),
  });
  try {
    publish(APPLIED, JSON.stringify({ node: Number(node), title }));
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `publish failed: ${String(error)}`);
  }
}

function finish(request: bigint, kind: Pending, submissions: Submission[]): void {
  if (kind.kind === 'pane') {
    const completion = takeCompletion(request);
    const proposed = completion ? cleanTitle(completion.text) : '';
    if (proposed === '') {
      titled.delete(kind.node);
      return;
    }
    try {
      const id = runHookRequest(BEFORE_APPLY, JSON.stringify({ node: Number(kind.node), proposed, source: 'transcript' }));
      pending.set(id, { kind: 'hook', node: kind.node, proposed });
    } catch {
      apply(kind.node, proposed, submissions);
    }
  } else if (kind.kind === 'service') {
    const completion = takeCompletion(request);
    const title = completion ? cleanTitle(completion.text) : '';
    reply(kind.call, { tag: 'ok', val: JSON.stringify({ title }) });
  } else {
    // No handler, or a refused chain, leaves the proposed title as it is.
    let adjusted = '';
    try {
      const text = takeReply(request);
      adjusted = text === undefined ? '' : cleanTitle((JSON.parse(text) as { proposed?: string }).proposed ?? '');
    } catch {
      adjusted = '';
    }
    apply(kind.node, adjusted || kind.proposed, submissions);
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, serviceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    reloadStyles();
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'topic-published' && event.val.topic === 'ilium.extensions/changed') {
        reloadStyles();
      } else if (event.tag === 'input-submitted' && !titled.has(event.val.node)) {
        titled.add(event.val.node);
        try {
          pending.set(ask(event.val.text), { kind: 'pane', node: event.val.node });
        } catch (error) {
          titled.delete(event.val.node);
          log('warn', `no title: ${String((error as { code?: string }).code)}`);
        }
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed') {
        const entry = pending.get(event.val.request);
        if (entry === undefined) continue;
        pending.delete(event.val.request);
        finish(event.val.request, entry, submissions);
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
  handle(call: ServiceCall): ServiceReply {
    const params = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson) as { text?: string };
    if (typeof params.text !== 'string') return { tag: 'done', val: JSON.stringify({ title: '' }) };
    try {
      pending.set(ask(params.text), { kind: 'service', call: call.call });
      return { tag: 'deferred' };
    } catch {
      return { tag: 'done', val: JSON.stringify({ title: '' }) };
    }
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- `clean_title` is pure. The model may answer with quotes, a full stop or a sentence. The function keeps at most four words, so the pane title never grows.
- The hook is run with `run_hook_request`, not `run_hook`, because the work happens inside `on_events`, which cannot wait. The completion arrives as a `request-completed` event, and `take_reply` returns the final payload. A chain with no handler gives no reply, and the plugin keeps its own proposal.
- The service reply is deferred. `suggest` returns at once with `Deferred`, and `reply` answers when the model has answered. A late `reply` after the caller's 30 second timeout gives `not-found`, and the plugin ignores the result. [Tutorial 22](/pages/tutorial-22-versioned-service-with-fallbacks/) covers deferred replies in detail.
- The dedup key joins the node and the title. A repeat of the same title for the same pane is a `duplicate`, not an error.
- `source: inferred` marks the rename. The host never lets an inferred title replace a title the user typed. The plugin does not need its own check.

### Step 3: what happens to the old plugin

When the user turns Titles Lite on, the built-in plugin is turned off. Only one of the two is enabled at a time. The change applies in this order.

1. The review dialog at install says what the replacement does. The user confirms.
2. The kernel turns `ilium.core.titles` off and turns `example.titles-lite` on.
3. The registry keeps every contribution that was made to `ilium.core.titles/title-styles` and `before-apply-title`. They apply to the replacement, because it provides the points of the same names.
4. The settings tab, the commands and the pane kinds of the built-in plugin disappear. The Titles settings tab is not in the rail while the replacement is on. The command `ilium.core.titles/tidy` and the preview panel are gone too.
5. Stored data stays on disk. The replacement does not read it. It cannot see the titles history, the style choice or the prompt text of the built-in plugin.

Turning Titles Lite off, or uninstalling it, turns the built-in plugin back on. It finds its data as it left it. Titles that the replacement applied to panes stay on the panes. A title is a property of the pane, not of the plugin.

Some parts of the product cannot be replaced.

| Plugin | Replaceable | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `ilium.core.titles` and the other feature plugins | yes | A feature may be swapped. |
| `ilium.core.sessions` | no | It owns saved sessions. A broken replacement could lose them. |
| `ilium.core.settings` | no | It hosts the Plugins screen. Without it the user could not turn a replacement off. |

A package that lists either of these in `replaces` fails with `manifest.replaces-not-replaceable`.

### Step 4: the install errors

The surface check is the main safety rule of replacement. Remove the service from the manifest, or leave out the topic, and run `ilium plugin build`:

<figure>
<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin build
<span class="t-err">error manifest.replaces-surface-incomplete</span>
  replaces ilium.core.titles
  missing topics:title-applied
<span class="t-dim">1 error, 0 warnings</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The error lists every missing item, so one run shows them all.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Step 5: grants, risk and consent

| Grant | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `inference` | normal | The titles come from the user's model. The user's AI admission settings apply to the purpose `pane-title`. |
| `agent.read-prompts` | normal | The plugin reads the prompt to name the pane. It does not store it. |
| `tree.read` | normal | The plugin reads the node it renames. |
| `tree.write` | normal | The plugin renames panes. |
| `services.provide:ilium.core.titles/suggest` | normal | The plugin answers one service. |
| `extensions.provide:` two points | normal | The plugin owns two points. |
| `topics.subscribe:ilium.extensions/changed` | normal | The plugin reloads its styles. |

- A replacement of a core plugin is a trust decision. The built-in plugin is reviewed with Ilium. Yours is reviewed by the user, once, in the dialog. A signed package from a publisher the user trusts is the right shape.

### Step 6: test it

The fake host described in [Testing](/pages/testing/) does not run the model. `FakeSession` runs the registry and a stub of the core plugin, so test the pure parts, the manifest and the service calls through the session. See [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/).

**Rust**

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn long_or_quoted_reply_is_shortened() {
        assert_eq!(clean_title("\"Fix the login redirect loop today\"."), "Fix the login redirect");
        assert_eq!(clean_title("  Refactor parser  "), "Refactor parser");
        assert_eq!(clean_title(""), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn first_style_wins_and_broken_entries_are_skipped() {
        let entries = vec!["not json".to_string(), r#"{"id":"a","title":"A","instruction":"Use verbs."}"#.to_string()];
        assert_eq!(instruction_from(&entries), "Use verbs.");
        assert_eq!(instruction_from(&[]), DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION);
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// src/index.test.ts
import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { cleanTitle, instructionFrom } from './index';

test('long or quoted reply is shortened', () => {
  expect(cleanTitle('"Fix the login redirect loop today".')).toBe('Fix the login redirect');
  expect(cleanTitle('  Refactor parser  ')).toBe('Refactor parser');
  expect(cleanTitle('')).toBe('');
});

test('first style wins and broken entries are skipped', () => {
  const entries = ['not json', '{"id":"a","title":"A","instruction":"Use verbs."}'];
  expect(instructionFrom(entries)).toBe('Use verbs.');
  expect(instructionFrom([])).toContain('four words');
});
```

Then check it in the app, with the steps from [Debugging](/pages/debugging/):

1. Pack and install as in [tutorial 9](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/). Read the dialog and confirm.
2. Open Settings. The Titles tab must be gone from the rail.
3. Send a prompt in an agent pane. The pane gets a title of four words or fewer. A second prompt does not rename it.
4. Run `ilium plugin logs example.titles-lite --tail 5`. A failed model call appears as `no title: <code>`.
5. Turn Titles Lite off in Settings > Plugins. The Titles tab returns and the older settings are still there.

### Edge cases and errors: what can go wrong

| Code or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.replaces-surface-incomplete` | A surface item is missing. The error lists them. | Provide each missing item. |
| `manifest.replaces-unknown` | The id is not an installed core plugin. | Check the id. |
| `manifest.replaces-not-replaceable` | The plugin is `ilium.core.sessions` or `ilium.core.settings`. | Extend it instead. |
| `manifest.replaces-cycle` | Two packages replace each other. | Replace one plugin with one package. |
| `timed-out` on `suggest` | The model took over 30 s. | The caller shows a plain fallback. |
| `not-found` on `reply` | The call already ended. | Ignore. The plugin drops the result. |
| `refused(conflict)` on rename | The user typed the title by hand. | None. This is the rule. |
| `extension.reply-not-allowed` | A handler used `refuse` on this transform point. | The handler must use `replace` or `pass`. |
| Title never appears | No model is set up, or the pane is already in `titled`. | Set up a provider. Check the log. |

A replacement inherits no grants and T3 cannot replace ([SEC-300], [SEC-301]). See [Extension security](/pages/reference-extension-security/).

# 22. A versioned service with fallbacks

## 22. A versioned service with fallbacks

This step builds two plugins that talk through a plugin-defined service. The provider is `example.glossary`. It offers `example.glossary/lookup`, first at version 1.0.0 and then at 1.1.0. The consumer is `example.glossary-hover`. It asks for a definition and keeps working when the provider is missing, too old, slow or wrong.

The service version here is plugin-defined semver. It is the version of the glossary service, not the contract version. The contract is `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` and does not change in this step. The page [Services](/pages/api-services/) lists the call API and the error codes. This page does not repeat that table. It shows how to design for each failure and how to test each one.

You have finished tutorials 1 to 9 and read [Services](/pages/api-services/). Rust and TypeScript behave the same in every step.

### You will need

- Rust: stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crates `ilium-plugin-sdk` and `serde_json`. TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- Two plugin folders: `example-glossary/` and `example-glossary-hover/`.
- `"unstable": ["plugin-services"]` in both manifests (dev mode, T2 and T3).
- Grants: the provider needs `services.provide:example.glossary/lookup`. The consumer needs `services.use:example.glossary/lookup`.
- A scratch folder for the packages: `/media/arthur/tmp/glossary/` with a `.scratch-reaper` file in it.

### The surface this step uses

| Surface | Used for |
|---|---|
| `contributes.services.provides` | The provider names the service, its version and a schema file. |
| `requires.services` | The consumer names the service and the lowest version it needs. |
| `ServiceProvider::handle` and `ServiceReply` | The provider answers at once with `Done`, or later with `Deferred`. |
| `services::call_request`, `take_reply` | The consumer calls without blocking, then reads the result. |
| `services::reply` | The provider sends a deferred answer. |
| Grants `services.provide` and `services.use` | The bare service name, never a version. |
| Errors `not-found`, `unsupported`, `timed-out`, `busy`, `invalid-argument` | The failures the consumer must handle. |

### The flow

The consumer calls. The provider answers at once, or later.

### Step 1: the provider at 1.0.0

Version 1.0.0 takes a term and returns a definition.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.glossary",
  "name": "Glossary",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Looks up a term in a small built-in glossary.",
  "icon": "book",
  "unstable": ["plugin-services"],
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["service-provider"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["services.provide:example.glossary/lookup"]
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "services": {
      "provides": [
        { "name": "example.glossary/lookup", "version": "1.0.0", "schema": "schemas/lookup.json" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

`schemas/lookup.json` describes one method, `lookup`. The schema uses only the allowed keywords: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `enum`, `title`, `description`, `default`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `pattern`, `maxLength` and `items`.

```json
{
  "methods": {
    "lookup": {
      "params": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["term"],
        "properties": { "term": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 80 } }
      },
      "result": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["found", "definition"],
        "properties": {
          "found": { "type": "boolean" },
          "definition": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 2000 }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
// example-glossary/src/lib.rs
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const TERMS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("latency", "The time between a request and its first answer."),
    ("throughput", "How much work is done in a span of time."),
];

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["service-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Glossary;

impl Lifecycle for Glossary {}

/// Pure lookup. Case is ignored. An unknown term is a normal answer, not an error.
pub fn define(term: &str) -> Value {
    let wanted = term.trim().to_lowercase();
    match TERMS.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == wanted) {
        Some((_, text)) => json!({ "found": true, "definition": text }),
        None => json!({ "found": false, "definition": "" }),
    }
}

impl ServiceProvider for Glossary {
    fn handle(&mut self, call: ServiceCall) -> ServiceReply {
        let params: Value = serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        let Some(term) = params["term"].as_str() else {
            // The host checks params against the schema first. This is a second guard.
            return ServiceReply::Done(define("").to_string());
        };
        ServiceReply::Done(define(term).to_string())
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// example-glossary/src/index.ts
import { definePlugin, type ServiceCall, type ServiceReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

const TERMS: Record<string, string> = {
  latency: 'The time between a request and its first answer.',
  throughput: 'How much work is done in a span of time.',
};

/** Pure lookup. Case is ignored. An unknown term is a normal answer, not an error. */
export function define(term: string): { found: boolean; definition: string } {
  const text = TERMS[term.trim().toLowerCase()];
  return text === undefined ? { found: false, definition: '' } : { found: true, definition: text };
}

export const { lifecycle, serviceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  handle(call: ServiceCall): ServiceReply {
    const params = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson) as { term?: string };
    return { tag: 'done', val: JSON.stringify(define(params.term ?? '')) };
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- The grant names the service without a version. The version lives in `provides`.
- The host validates params against the schema before `handle` runs. A wrong shape never reaches your code. The caller gets `invalid-argument`.

### Step 2: evolve to 1.1.0 without breaking anyone

Version 1.1.0 adds a language and a list of aliases. The change is additive. That is the rule that keeps a consumer of 1.0 working: add optional input, add output fields, never remove or rename either.

| Change | Allowed in a minor version? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| New optional param `lang` with a default | yes | An old caller does not send it, and the default applies. |
| New result field `aliases` | yes | An old caller ignores fields it does not know. |
| Remove or rename a field | no | An old caller reads a field that is gone. Make it a major version. |

Change the manifest version fields to 1.1.0 and add the optional pieces to the schema. The old fields stay as they were.

```json
"properties": {
  "term": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 80 },
  "lang": { "type": "string", "enum": ["en", "de"], "default": "en" }
}
```

Add `"aliases": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 80 } }` to the result and leave `required` as it was. A consumer that asked for 1.0 still gets a compatible answer, because the host matches on major version and a minor at least as high.

Now a slow case. Some lookups need work that cannot finish in one call, such as a model call. The provider returns `Deferred` and answers later with `reply`. The pending map is keyed by the call number that the host gave the provider.

**Rust**

```rust
// example-glossary/src/lib.rs, version 1.1.0
use std::collections::HashMap;

use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services;

/// Extra definitions for German, as plain data.
const GERMAN: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("latency", "Die Zeit zwischen einer Anfrage und der ersten Antwort.")];

pub fn define_in(term: &str, lang: &str) -> Value {
    if lang == "de" {
        let wanted = term.trim().to_lowercase();
        if let Some((_, text)) = GERMAN.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == wanted) {
            return json!({ "found": true, "definition": text, "aliases": [] });
        }
    }
    let mut base = define(term);
    base["aliases"] = json!([]);
    base
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["service-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct GlossaryV11 {
    /// Calls waiting for a slow source, keyed by the host's call number.
    waiting: HashMap<u64, String>,
}

impl ServiceProvider for GlossaryV11 {
    fn handle(&mut self, call: ServiceCall) -> ServiceReply {
        let params: Value = serde_json::from_str(&call.payload_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
        let term = params["term"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let lang = params["lang"].as_str().unwrap_or("en").to_string();
        if params["slow"].as_bool() == Some(true) {
            // Answer later. The caller keeps waiting, for at most 30 s.
            self.waiting.insert(call.call, term);
            return ServiceReply::Deferred;
        }
        ServiceReply::Done(define_in(&term, &lang).to_string())
    }
}

impl GlossaryV11 {
    /// Called when the slow source has an answer. A late call gets `not-found`, which is ignored.
    fn finish(&mut self, call: u64) {
        if let Some(term) = self.waiting.remove(&call) {
            let _ = services::reply(call, Ok(define_in(&term, "en").to_string()));
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// example-glossary/src/index.ts, version 1.1.0
import { reply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';

const GERMAN: Record<string, string> = {
  latency: 'Die Zeit zwischen einer Anfrage und der ersten Antwort.',
};

export function defineIn(term: string, lang: string) {
  const key = term.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (lang === 'de' && GERMAN[key] !== undefined) {
    return { found: true, definition: GERMAN[key], aliases: [] as string[] };
  }
  return { ...define(term), aliases: [] as string[] };
}

/** Calls waiting for a slow source, keyed by the host's call number. */
const waiting = new Map<bigint, string>();

export function handleCall(call: ServiceCall): ServiceReply {
  const params = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson) as { term?: string; lang?: string; slow?: boolean };
  if (params.slow === true) {
    waiting.set(call.call, params.term ?? '');
    return { tag: 'deferred' };
  }
  return { tag: 'done', val: JSON.stringify(defineIn(params.term ?? '', params.lang ?? 'en')) };
}

/** Called when the slow source has an answer. A late call gets `not-found`, which is ignored. */
export function finish(call: bigint): void {
  const term = waiting.get(call);
  if (term === undefined) return;
  waiting.delete(call);
  try {
    reply(call, { tag: 'ok', val: JSON.stringify(defineIn(term, 'en')) });
  } catch {
    // The caller has gone away. Nothing to do.
  }
}
```

Points to notice:

- A deferred call has an owner: the pending map. If the provider restarts, the host cancels every deferred call. The caller sees `cancelled`. Do not try to save the map.

### Step 3: the consumer

The consumer asks for the lowest version it can live with. It does not require 1.1.0, because it works without `lang` and `aliases`.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.glossary-hover",
  "name": "Glossary hover",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Developer",
  "description": "Defines a term. Falls back to plain text when the glossary is not usable.",
  "icon": "book",
  "unstable": ["plugin-services"],
  "requires": { "services": ["example.glossary/lookup@1.0.0"] },
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["services.use:example.glossary/lookup"]
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "example.glossary-hover/define", "title": "Define a term", "side": "server" }
    ],
    "topics": { "publishes": ["example.glossary-hover/definition"] }
  }
}
```

`requires.services` makes the host wait at activation. It waits for a compatible provider, 2 s by default and 5 s at most. If none shows up, the consumer still activates and its first call fails with `not-found`. Install never fails because a provider is missing.

The consumer must handle six outcomes. Write them as one pure function, so each can be tested alone.

| Outcome | Cause | What the consumer shows |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | Normal case | The definition |
| `found: false` | The term is not in the glossary | `No entry for "<term>".` |
| `not-found` | No provider, or it is off, or the call was late | `Glossary is not available.` |
| `unsupported` | The provider is older than the method needs | `Glossary is too old.` |
| `timed-out` | The provider took over 30 s | `Glossary did not answer.` |
| `invalid-argument` or garbage | A broken schema or a broken result | `Glossary gave an unusable answer.` |

Garbage matters most. A provider is a different author's code. Read the result like any untrusted input. Check the type of every field and cap the length before you show it.

**Rust**

```rust
// example-glossary-hover/src/lib.rs
use std::collections::HashMap;

use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::topics;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const SERVICE: &str = "example.glossary/lookup";
const MAX_SHOWN: usize = 400;

/// What the user sees for one lookup. A failure never panics and never goes blank.
pub fn describe(term: &str, outcome: Result<String, String>) -> String {
    let text = match outcome {
        Ok(text) => text,
        Err(code) => {
            return match code.as_str() {
                "not-found" => "Glossary is not available.".to_string(),
                "unsupported" => "Glossary is too old.".to_string(),
                "timed-out" => "Glossary did not answer.".to_string(),
                _ => "Glossary gave an unusable answer.".to_string(),
            };
        }
    };
    let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) else {
        return "Glossary gave an unusable answer.".to_string();
    };
    match (value["found"].as_bool(), value["definition"].as_str()) {
        (Some(true), Some(definition)) if !definition.is_empty() => {
            definition.chars().take(MAX_SHOWN).collect()
        }
        (Some(false), _) => format!("No entry for \"{term}\"."),
        _ => "Glossary gave an unusable answer.".to_string(),
    }
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["handler"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct GlossaryHover {
    asking: HashMap<RequestId, String>,
}

impl Lifecycle for GlossaryHover {}

impl Handler for GlossaryHover {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) => {
                    let args: Value = serde_json::from_str(&invoked.arguments_json).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                    let term = args["term"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
                    let payload = json!({ "term": term }).to_string();
                    match services::call_request(SERVICE, "lookup", &payload) {
                        Ok(id) => {
                            self.asking.insert(id, term);
                        }
                        // The call could not even start. Show the fallback now.
                        Err(error) => show(&term, Err(error.code)),
                    }
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(done) => {
                    let Some(term) = self.asking.remove(&done.request) else { continue };
                    let outcome = services::take_reply(done.request).map_err(|error| error.code);
                    show(&term, outcome);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn show(term: &str, outcome: Result<String, String>) {
    let text = describe(term, outcome);
    let payload = json!({ "term": term, "text": text }).to_string();
    let _ = topics::publish("example.glossary-hover/definition", &payload);
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// example-glossary-hover/src/index.ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { callRequest, takeReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';
import { publish } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/topics';

const SERVICE = 'example.glossary/lookup';
const MAX_SHOWN = 400;

type Outcome = { ok: string } | { error: string };

/** What the user sees for one lookup. A failure never throws and never goes blank. */
export function describe(term: string, outcome: Outcome): string {
  if ('error' in outcome) {
    switch (outcome.error) {
      case 'not-found': return 'Glossary is not available.';
      case 'unsupported': return 'Glossary is too old.';
      case 'timed-out': return 'Glossary did not answer.';
      default: return 'Glossary gave an unusable answer.';
    }
  }
  let value: { found?: unknown; definition?: unknown };
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(outcome.ok);
  } catch {
    return 'Glossary gave an unusable answer.';
  }
  if (value.found === true && typeof value.definition === 'string' && value.definition !== '') {
    return value.definition.slice(0, MAX_SHOWN);
  }
  if (value.found === false) return `No entry for "${term}".`;
  return 'Glossary gave an unusable answer.';
}

const asking = new Map<bigint, string>();

function show(term: string, outcome: Outcome): void {
  publish('example.glossary-hover/definition', JSON.stringify({ term, text: describe(term, outcome) }));
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked') {
        const args = JSON.parse(event.val.argumentsJson) as { term?: string };
        const term = args.term ?? '';
        try {
          asking.set(callRequest(SERVICE, 'lookup', JSON.stringify({ term })), term);
        } catch (error) {
          show(term, { error: (error as { code?: string }).code ?? 'failed' });
        }
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed') {
        const term = asking.get(event.val.request);
        if (term === undefined) continue;
        asking.delete(event.val.request);
        try {
          show(term, { ok: takeReply(event.val.request) });
        } catch (error) {
          show(term, { error: (error as { code?: string }).code ?? 'failed' });
        }
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Points to notice:

- `describe` is the whole degradation policy, in one pure function. Every row of the table above has a test.
- The call is non-blocking. A slow provider does not freeze the consumer. The 30 s timeout becomes `timed-out`, which the table covers.
- `found: false` is shown differently from an error. The user learns that the glossary works and the term is unknown.

### Step 4: one provider per name, and the user's choice

Two plugins may provide `example.glossary/lookup`. The host does not merge them. The first enabled provider owns the name. The second stays installed and idle.

- The Plugins screen shows both. The one that owns the name says `active`. The other says `waiting: example.glossary owns lookup`.
- The user can pick the owner on the Surface view of the service. The switch turns the other provider off. Consumers see no change except a brief `not-found` while the new provider starts.

The requirement `example.glossary/lookup@1.0.0` is satisfied by a provider at 1.0.0 or at 1.1.0. It is not satisfied by 2.0.0, because the major differs. 
### Step 5: security and limits

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Who may call | Only a plugin that holds `services.use:<name>`. The grant is standard risk. |
| Who may answer | Only a plugin that holds `services.provide:<name>`. |
| What the caller sends | Text. Do not send secrets to a service you do not own. A provider is another author's code. |
| What the provider returns | Untrusted. Check types and cap lengths before you use or show them. |
| Pending calls | At most 64 per provider. More give `busy`. |
| Time | 30 s from the call. Then `timed-out`. |

### Step 6: test each failure

`FakeSession` runs two plugins against one registry, so install the provider and the caller in one session and call across them. Test the pure policy directly as well. This follows [Testing](/pages/testing/) and [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/). Never test by sleeping 30 s.

**Rust**

```rust
// example-glossary-hover/src/lib.rs
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn ok(text: &str) -> Result<String, String> { Ok(text.to_string()) }
    fn err(code: &str) -> Result<String, String> { Err(code.to_string()) }

    #[test]
    fn normal_definition() {
        assert_eq!(describe("latency", ok(r#"{"found":true,"definition":"A wait."}"#)), "A wait.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_term() {
        assert_eq!(describe("zzz", ok(r#"{"found":false,"definition":""}"#)), "No entry for \"zzz\".");
    }

    #[test]
    fn provider_absent() {
        assert_eq!(describe("x", err("not-found")), "Glossary is not available.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn provider_too_old() {
        assert_eq!(describe("x", err("unsupported")), "Glossary is too old.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn provider_slow() {
        assert_eq!(describe("x", err("timed-out")), "Glossary did not answer.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn provider_returns_garbage() {
        assert_eq!(describe("x", ok("not json")), "Glossary gave an unusable answer.");
        assert_eq!(describe("x", ok(r#"{"found":"yes"}"#)), "Glossary gave an unusable answer.");
        assert_eq!(describe("x", err("invalid-argument")), "Glossary gave an unusable answer.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn long_definition_is_capped() {
        let long = format!(r#"{{"found":true,"definition":"{}"}}"#, "a".repeat(5000));
        assert_eq!(describe("x", ok(&long)).chars().count(), MAX_SHOWN);
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// example-glossary-hover/src/index.test.ts
import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { describe as describeOutcome } from './index';

const ok = (text: string) => ({ ok: text });
const err = (code: string) => ({ error: code });

test('normal definition', () => {
  expect(describeOutcome('latency', ok('{"found":true,"definition":"A wait."}'))).toBe('A wait.');
});
test('unknown term', () => {
  expect(describeOutcome('zzz', ok('{"found":false,"definition":""}'))).toBe('No entry for "zzz".');
});
test('provider absent, old and slow', () => {
  expect(describeOutcome('x', err('not-found'))).toBe('Glossary is not available.');
  expect(describeOutcome('x', err('unsupported'))).toBe('Glossary is too old.');
  expect(describeOutcome('x', err('timed-out'))).toBe('Glossary did not answer.');
});
test('provider returns garbage', () => {
  expect(describeOutcome('x', ok('not json'))).toBe('Glossary gave an unusable answer.');
  expect(describeOutcome('x', ok('{"found":"yes"}'))).toBe('Glossary gave an unusable answer.');
  expect(describeOutcome('x', err('invalid-argument'))).toBe('Glossary gave an unusable answer.');
});
test('long definition is capped', () => {
  const long = JSON.stringify({ found: true, definition: 'a'.repeat(5000) });
  expect(describeOutcome('x', ok(long)).length).toBe(400);
});
```

The provider has tests too: `define` and `define_in` for an unknown term, case and `de`, and `handle` with `slow` set, which must give `Deferred`.

Then check the live path, using the steps in [Debugging](/pages/debugging/).

1. Install the provider at 1.0.0 and then the consumer. Run the command with the term `latency`.
2. Turn the provider off. Run the command again. The text is `Glossary is not available.`
3. Install provider 1.1.0 over 1.0.0. Run the command again. The text is the same as step 1.

### What you see

With the provider on, the consumer publishes its topic, and the user sees the text in a message line.

</pre>

### Edge cases and errors: what can go wrong

| Code or symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `not-found` | No enabled provider, a late reply, or the name is wrong | Show the fallback. Check the name and the Plugins screen. |
| `not-permitted` | The consumer lacks `services.use:<name>` | Add the grant. A version in the grant is wrong. |
| `invalid-argument` | Params do not match the schema, or a `done` result does not match the result schema | Fix the payload. Fix the provider's result. |
| `unsupported` | The provider has no such method | Ask for a higher version, or fall back. |
| `busy` | The provider has 64 pending calls | Retry later. Cache answers. |
| `timed-out` | No reply in 30 s | Show the fallback. The provider should defer less. |
| `cancelled` | The provider restarted with a deferred call open | Show the fallback. Retry once if it is safe. |
| Second provider idle | One provider per name | Pick the owner on the Surface view. |

# 23. Drive the fleet: a review swarm

## 23. Drive the fleet: a review swarm

This step builds `example.swarm`, a plugin with a server side and a client side. One command starts a review swarm. The plugin creates N worktrees, starts one review agent in a new pane for each, sends them one shared instruction, shows progress, collects the diffs when the agents stop, and sends one notification with the result.

Core services are called as in [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/). Their names are in [Reference: core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/). Use them from here. This page does not repeat those tables. [Tutorial 22](/pages/tutorial-22-versioned-service-with-fallbacks/) covers the failure rules of service calls.

You have finished tutorials 1 to 9 and read [Services](/pages/api-services/). Rust and TypeScript behave the same in every step.

### You will need

- Rust: stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crates `ilium-plugin-sdk` and `serde_json`. TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- A Git repository with at least one commit, and an agent command on the path, such as `claude`.
- `"unstable": ["plugin-services"]`, because the plugin uses core services (dev mode, T2 and T3).

### The surface this step uses

| Surface | Used for |
|---|---|
| `ilium.core.worktrees/create` | One worktree per reviewer. |
| `Intent::CreatePane` and the grant `panes.create` | One terminal pane per reviewer. |
| `freeze-pane` and `terminate-pane-process` (grant `panes.lifecycle`) | Stop agents on cancel or at the deadline. |
| `ilium.core.fleet/broadcast` | One instruction to every reviewer. |
| `ilium.core.progress/report` | A progress bar for the run. |
| `ilium.core.notifications/notify` | The result. |
| Storage (always granted) | The run state, so a restart can resume. |
| `timers::at` and `timers::cancel_durable` | The deadline. |
| `jobs` (grant `jobs.run`) | Reading each diff off the main thread. |
| `dedup::key_for` and `Submission::keyed` | Each step happens once. |

### The permission summary

This plugin asks for a lot. Say so in its description and in this table. The user reads it in the review dialog.

| Grant | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `services.use` for four core services | normal | Worktrees, broadcast, progress, notifications. |
| `panes.create` | normal | Reviewer panes. |
| `fs.read:project` | normal | The pane's working folder is a worktree path. |
| `terminal.write` | high | The first instruction is typed into the agent's terminal at start. |
| `panes.lifecycle` | high | Stop agents on cancel and at the deadline. Server only. |
| `process.run:git` | high | The job runs `git diff` in a worktree. |
| `jobs.run` | normal | The diff job. |
| `panes.read` | normal | Learn that a reviewer pane has ended. |
