- **Granted.** The import works as its API page describes.
- **Declined.** The import links to a stub. Functions with a result return `not-permitted`, and
  the plugin keeps running. Some functions have no error result, so they return a value instead.
  `clipboard` `read-text` and `location` `current` return `none`. `plugins.list` returns an empty
  list. A declined `http-api.route` answers `404 Not Found`. A declined topic subscription delivers
  no events and returns no error. A refused call is written to the plugin log.
- **Not requested.** The manifest never asked for the capability, so the import traps. The
  manifest and the code disagree, which is a plugin bug. The trap ends the instance and the kernel
  logs it.

## Always granted

Every plugin has these without a request, and it need not list them: `log`, `clock`, `timers`,
`storage` for its own buckets, `settings` for its own values, `codec`, read access to its package,
read and write access to its own `data` and `cache` folders, messages between its own two sides,
and `ui.invalidate` for the views it contributes. A manifest without `capabilities` behaves exactly
like `"capabilities": {}`.

## Reading the granted list

The activation context carries `granted`, the list of capabilities that were actually granted. A
plugin should read it on every activation, because a revocation changes it. The example below
hides the file feature when the project grant is missing and keeps the rest of the plugin working.
The grant list is a hint, not a guarantee. A call can still return `not-permitted` or `revoked`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, log::{self, Level}};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notes;

impl Lifecycle for Notes {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if context.granted.iter().any(|grant| grant == "fs.read:project") {
            task::spawn(load_readme());
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn deactivate(&mut self, _reason: DeactivationReason) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        None
    }
}

impl Handler for Notes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

async fn load_readme() {
    let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: "README.md".into() };
    match fs::read_all(path).await {
        Ok(bytes) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("README has {} bytes", bytes.len())),
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::NotPermitted => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, "project files are not granted");
        }
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Error, &format!("README read failed: {}", error.message)),
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { readAll } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

async function loadReadme(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const bytes = await readAll({ scope: 'project', path: 'README.md' });
    log('info', `README has ${bytes.length} bytes`);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'not-permitted') {
      log('warn', 'project files are not granted');
      return;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    if (context.granted.includes('fs.read:project')) {
      loadReadme().catch((error) => log('error', `README read failed: ${String(error)}`));
    }
  },
  onEvents(): Submission[] {
    return [];
  },
});
```

## Changing grants

- **Revocation.** The user revokes a grant in Settings > Plugins > <plugin> > Capabilities, or with
  `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke <grant>`. The kernel bumps the authorization epoch. Calls in
  flight return `revoked`. Pending requests that need the grant complete as `failed(revoked)`.
  Contributions that need the grant are withdrawn, including decorations, grabs, routes and
  watches. The plugin receives `deactivate(revoked)` and is activated again with the reduced list.
  This re-activation is not counted as a failure.
- **Later grants.** A grant that the user adds, or one that a plugin upgrade requests and the user
  accepts, bumps the epoch too. The plugin receives `deactivate(granted)` and is activated again
  with the new list.
- **Disable.** A disabled plugin receives `deactivate(disabled)` and its contributions are
  withdrawn. See [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).

## What the user sees

- The review dialog at install, and the prompt for H capabilities at first activation of a T1
  plugin.
- Settings > Plugins > <plugin> > Capabilities, which lists each grant with its state.
- `ilium plugin grants <id>`, which also shows declined grants.
- `ilium plugin logs <id>`, which shows each refusal, each file write outside `data` and `cache`,
  each process run with its arguments, and each clipboard read by length only.

<figure>
<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.notes
server  tree.read          <span class="t-ok">granted</span>
server  fs.read:project    <span class="t-ok">granted</span>
server  process.run:git    <span class="t-dim">declined</span>
client  ui.panels          <span class="t-ok">granted</span>
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.notes \
    --revoke fs.read:project
<span class="t-ok">ok</span> revoked fs.read:project, plugin re-activated
</pre>
<figcaption>The grant commands for one plugin. The layout of the output is a sketch.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Errors

Manifest errors are reported as `error` lines by `ilium plugin install` and `ilium plugin build`,
one line per error.

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `manifest.grant-unknown` | The name is not a capability of this plugin API version. |
| `manifest.grant-argument` | The grant has an argument, but the name takes none. |
| `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | The name needs an argument and none was given. |
| `manifest.grant-wildcard` | A wildcard was used where the name does not accept one, such as `process.run:*`. |
| `manifest.grant-scope` | The file scope is unknown or does not accept that access. |
| `manifest.grant-side` | The capability is not available on the side that requests it. |
| `manifest.grant-tier` | The capability is for bundled plugins only. |
| `manifest.grant-dependency` | The capability also needs another capability. |
| `manifest.export-grant` | An export needs a capability that the manifest does not request. |

Runtime codes that relate to grants are `not-permitted` (the capability is declined, revoked in
flight, or the argument is outside the grant), `revoked` (the authorization epoch changed during the
call) and `failed(revoked)` (a pending request lost its grant).

Edge cases to design for:

- `fs.pick` needs `fs.read:picked` or `fs.write:picked`. Without either it fails with
  `manifest.grant-dependency`.
- `settings.write-all` needs `settings.read-all`, and the review dialog cannot grant write alone.
- `settings.contribute:<tab-id>` lets a plugin add sections to one built-in tab, such as `settings.contribute:terminal`. It is low risk and independent of `settings.read-all` and `settings.write-all`: it never implies them, and they never imply it. A plugin's own tabs need no grant. See [Plugin settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/).
- `fs.write:agent-sessions:<agent>` is refused at install with `manifest.grant-scope`. Transcripts
  are read only.
- An `inference-provider` export needs `inference.provide`. Without the grant the plugin installs
  but is never selected as a provider.
- A `process.run` call for a program outside its grant fails with `invalid-argument` before the
  process starts. A `cwd` that the plugin cannot read is `not-permitted`.
- A `http:*` grant, or any other bare wildcard, is refused. A redirect follows the same host rule
  on each hop.

## Migration of animation rights

Earlier animation packages used a separate set of rights. The new names replace them. `network.http`
becomes `http:<host>`, `audio.microphone` becomes `audio.capture`, `state.persist` becomes the
always-granted `storage`, and `input.pointer` becomes the scene's `wants-pointer`. Animation
packages must be rebuilt, because there is no compatibility layer.

# Debugging

## Overview

A plugin problem shows up in one of four places: the plugin log, a trap, a deadline breach or the disabled notice in the tree footer. This page explains the `log` import and its levels, how to read `ilium plugin logs`, what the host writes for traps and restarts, how a debug build maps trap frames to source lines, and how `ilium plugin dev` reloads a plugin while you edit it.

The plugin log holds one entry per line: the time, the level, the plugin id and the message. The host writes entries for your own log calls, for standard output and error, for calls refused by a missing or declined grant, and for every trap, deadline breach and restart.

## What you need

- A plugin package with a `server`, `client` or `scene` side. The `log` import needs no grant.
- Rust: the crate `ilium-plugin-sdk` (S1). TypeScript: `@ilium/plugin-sdk` with Bun 1.2 or later (S14).
- The `ilium` binary. The `plugin` subcommands are part of it (U5), so nothing else is installed.
- Background reading: [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the error codes and the restart rule, and [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) for `activate` and `deactivate`.

## The log import

The import is `ilium:host/log`. It has one function and one enum.

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `log(level, message)` | function, no result | Writes one entry. It never fails. |
| `level` | enum `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | Severity of the entry, from least to most serious. |
| Rust `log::log(Level, &str)` | SDK function | Rust path `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log`, enum `Level`. |
| TypeScript `log(level, message)` | SDK function | Import from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log`. Level is a string. |

Rules that apply to every entry:

- A message over 16 KiB is cut at the last whole UTF-8 character that keeps the entry at 16,384 bytes or less. The entry then ends with `…[truncated]`.
- A line break in the message is written as the two characters `\n`, so each entry stays on one line.
- An empty message is accepted and writes an entry with no text after the plugin id.
- The rate is 200 lines per second for an ordinary plugin and 1,000 for a trusted T1 plugin. Lines over the rate are dropped and counted. Once per second, with lines dropped, the host writes one `warn` entry, `<n> lines dropped in the last second`. That summary does not use the rate budget.
- WASI standard output is written at level `info` and standard error at level `error`. Both share the rate budget and the size cap.
- Log entries carry no source position. The Rust `log!` macros of the SDK add `file:line` to the message themselves.

Write each message as `operation: object`, for example `sync: 3 notes saved to data/notes.json`, so that the line can be read without the source code.

## Reading the plugin log

`ilium plugin logs <id>` prints the log of one plugin, oldest entry first. `--tail <n>` prints only the last `n` entries. Each line has this form:

```text
YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss level(5) side(6) plugin-id message
```

The level is padded to five characters and the side to six. The side is `server`, `client`, `scene` or `host` for entries the host wrote. The default threshold is `info`, so `debug` and `trace` entries are dropped unless the plugin runs under `ilium plugin dev` or you raise it with `ilium plugin log-level`. The full format, the storage and the rotation rules are in [Debugging tools](/pages/reference-debugging-tools/). The host writes these kinds of entry:

| Source | Level | Message |
|---|---|---|
| Your log call, stdout, stderr | as given, `info`, `error` | Your text. |
| Refused call | `warn` | Names the capability, the function and the reason, one word from the closed list in [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#refusal-reasons). A call the manifest never requested is a trap, `host.capability-not-requested`, not a refusal. |
| Grant-sensitive action | `info` | File writes outside `data` and `cache`, and every process run, with the scope or program and the arguments. |
| Trap | `error` | `trap in <export> (<view>): <reason>`, followed by frame entries (see Traps). |
| Deadline breach | `error` | `deadline breach in <export>: limit <n> ms`. |
| Restart | `warn` | `restarting in <1 or 5 or 30> s (failure <n> of 3 in 10 minutes)`. |
| Dropped lines | `warn` | `<n> lines dropped in the last second`. |

<figure>
<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs notes --tail 5
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:02:04</span> info  server notes
  activate: 14 notes opened before
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:02:09</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>
                    notes 12 lines dropped in the last second
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:02:11</span> <span class="t-err">error</span>
  server notes trap in views.render (sidebar): no child 7
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:02:11</span> <span class="t-err">error</span>
  server notes   at src/lib.rs:42:7
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:02:11</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>
                    notes restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3 in 10 minutes)
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. A trap in a view, the frame entry of a debug build and the first restart.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Traps

A trap ends the instance at once. The host drops the instance, withdraws its dynamic contributions, cancels its pending requests and starts a new instance after a delay. A trap is caused by one of these:

- A call to an import that the manifest never requested. A declined grant does not trap: the import returns `not-permitted`. A call without any request in the manifest does trap.
- An invalid `ui-tree`: a child index out of range, or two nodes with the same `key` in one tree (UI3). The SDK builder cannot produce a bad index, so this comes from hand-written `raw` code or a duplicate key.
- More than 256 submissions returned from one `on-events` call.
- A deadline breach on an export that traps (see the table below).
- Exceeding `memory_mib` or `table_elements`, or a Rust panic or a thrown TypeScript exception in an export that has no outcome.

The first entry names the export and, for `views.render`, the view. Each backtrace frame follows as its own `error` entry. The restart then follows the schedule in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart): 1 s after the first failure and 5 s after the second. The third failure inside the window disables the plugin on that side.

| Deadline | Default | T1 ceiling | Effect when passed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_deadline_ms` | 20 ms | 50 ms | Trap |
| `command_deadline_ms` | 50 ms | 100 ms | Trap |
| `render_deadline_ms` (`views.render`) | 10 ms | 20 ms | Trap |
| `annotate_deadline_ms` | 10 ms | 20 ms | Late result dropped; the third breach in a row traps |
| `frame_deadline_ms` (scene `render`) | the frame budget | 50 ms | Frame skipped; 30 breaches in a row trap |
| `activate_deadline_ms` | 2,000 ms | 5,000 ms | Trap |
| `deactivate_deadline_ms` | 500 ms | 1,000 ms | Instance dropped; no restore bytes kept |

A job that runs past its deadline does not trap the plugin. The job request fails with `timed-out`, and the failure does not count toward the restart rule (A22). Move slow work into a job, as described on the [background jobs page](/pages/background-jobs/).

### Stuck plugins

Each side has an event queue of 1,024 entries for events that are never dropped. When the queue overflows, the plugin is treated as stuck. The host writes `event queue full at 1,024 events; restarting` at level `error`, and restarts the plugin. The new instance gets a `tree-changed` event for every node and reads its state again. The restart counts as a failure.

### Failures that do not count

A revoked re-activation, a disable, an upgrade during development and a shutdown never count toward the restart rule. A trap in a job instance does not count either. An `activate` that returns an error does count.

## Source maps and debug builds

`ilium plugin build --debug` keeps the debug information in the component:

- Rust: DWARF information. Each trap frame is written as `at src/lib.rs:42:7`.
- TypeScript: the bundle's source map, written to `dist/<side>.wasm.map`. A package carries the map under `src/` only when it was packed with `--include-src`. The host maps each trap position through it, so frames read `at src/index.ts:18:5`.

Release builds strip the debug information. Their frames show function names only, as `at handle_batch`. The host reads the source map only to write frame entries. The sources under `src/` are never loaded or run, and log entries are never mapped.

## Development reload

`ilium plugin dev` watches the package directory. A plugin installed this way has tier T3 and shows a `dev` badge (U3). Each save follows these steps:

  </defs>

    <text x="150" y="265" font-size="10">tree and footer drawn by the new build</text>

  </g>
</svg>
<figcaption>A save triggers an upgrade. The new build receives the bytes that the old one returned on deactivate.</figcaption>
</figure>

A save starts a rebuild 300 ms after the last change in the directory. If the build fails, the running instance keeps running, the compiler error is printed in the terminal, and no deactivate happens. If the build succeeds, the old instance receives `deactivate(upgrade)` and returns its restore bytes, within the 500 ms deadline. The bytes are capped at 1 MiB. Bytes over the cap are dropped, and the new instance starts without a `restored` value.

Keep in the restore bytes only the state that the host does not keep. Settings, storage and node metadata already persist across the reload, so most plugins need a few bytes at most.

## Worked example: server-side plugin

**Rust**

The plugin logs each agent start, keeps a count across reloads and warns about a bad restore. The `log::log` calls use the SDK paths of S4 and S7.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notes {
    started_work: u32,
}

impl Lifecycle for Notes {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if let Some(bytes) = context.restored {
            match <[u8; 4]>::try_from(bytes.as_slice()) {
                Ok(array) => self.started_work = u32::from_le_bytes(array),
                Err(_) => log::log(Level::Warn, "restore: 4 bytes expected, count reset"),
            }
        }
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("activate: {} agent starts so far", self.started_work));
        Ok(())
    }

    fn deactivate(&mut self, _reason: DeactivationReason) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        log::log(Level::Debug, "deactivate: returning the start count");
        Some(self.started_work.to_le_bytes().to_vec())
    }
}

impl Handler for Notes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { current, .. }) = event
            else {
                continue;
            };
            if current != AgentActivity::Working {
                continue;
            }
            self.started_work += 1;
            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("agent started work, count {}", self.started_work));
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

`Handler` is required for a `server` plugin. `Lifecycle` has default methods, so you implement only the ones you need. Debug entries are written like any other entry, so use `Level::Debug` for detail that you need only while investigating.

**TypeScript**

The client plugin counts editor opens. It writes the count as restore bytes on `deactivate` and reads them on `activate`. It logs a warning, instead of failing, when the restored bytes are not valid JSON.

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

interface NotesState {
  openedCount: number;
}

const encoder = new TextEncoder();
const decoder = new TextDecoder();
let state: NotesState = { openedCount: 0 };

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate(context) {
    if (context.restored !== undefined) {
      try {
        state = JSON.parse(decoder.decode(context.restored)) as NotesState;
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `restore: ${String(error)}, count reset`);
      }
    }
    log('info', `activate: ${state.openedCount} editors opened before this start`);
  },
  deactivate(reason) {
    log('debug', 'deactivate: returning the open count');
    return encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(state));
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'editor-opened') continue;
      state.openedCount += 1;
      log('debug', `editor opened, count ${state.openedCount}`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Use `log('debug', ...)` for lines that repeat on every event. Keep `info` for lifecycle events, which the user reads while debugging.

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | What the host does | Entry in the plugin log |
|---|---|---|
| More lines than the rate allows | Drops the extra lines | `warn` summary, once per second |
| A message over 16 KiB | Cuts it, keeps the marker within the cap | Entry ends with `…[truncated]` |
| A call with a declined or revoked grant | Returns `not-permitted`, or `none` for calls with no error channel | `warn` refusal entry |
| A call to an import the manifest never requested | Traps the instance | `error` trap entry |
| A `deactivate` past 500 ms | Drops the instance without restore bytes | `warn`: `deactivate deadline passed; state not kept` |
| Restore bytes over 1 MiB | Drops them, starts without `restored` | `warn`: `restore bytes over 1 MiB dropped` |
| Three failures in 10 minutes | Disables the plugin on that side | Disable notice in the tree footer |

The disabled notice is the last step of the restart schedule. A disabled plugin keeps its `data` and storage. Enabling it again resets the failure count to zero. Check the plugin log for the first trap, because later restarts usually repeat it.

## Debugging the extended surfaces

The contract includes surfaces that fail in ways the earlier sections do not cover. The table lists the first thing to check for each.

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| The render traps, the previous view stays and the plugin log has `invalid-argument` | A tree or widget cap: 4,096 nodes, 1,024 KiB, 256 `check-list` items, 64 `list-editor` items, 4 popups | The log entry names the cap. Page the data with a virtual-row or catalogue provider. |
| `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms` | More than 10 widget updates per second, or 3 toasts in 10 s | Update when a value changes by a visible step. The entry shows the retry delay. |
| A menu or a token list shows static content | A `menu-items` or `tokens` provider missed its 10 or 20 ms deadline | Time the provider with `clock.monotonic-millis` and cache the result. |
| `quota-exceeded` on `http.stream`, `process.spawn` or `vector` | A requestable limit (`limits` in the manifest) is at its ceiling | Raise the key in the manifest within the tier ceiling, or close what you opened. |
| The manifest is refused with a `manifest.` code | A new manifest code, for example `manifest.asset-size` or `manifest.scene-prerender` | The code and the path are in the install error. See [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/). |
| A client request resolves with a timeout | `client-requests.request` timeout between 1 and 30,000 ms | Increase the timeout, and check that the target pane still exists. |
| A handler runs after a screen change but sees old rows | `screen-changed` is coalesced to 10 per second per pane | Read the rows in `first-row` to `last-row` of the newest event. |

Use `journal.log-event` for events that a user should see in the session journal, and `log` for the plugin log that only you read. Rows of the plugin log are 16 KiB at most, so log a count or an id, not a whole payload.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::clock;

fn timed_provider<T>(name: &str, work: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T {
    let started = clock::monotonic_millis();
    let result = work();
    let elapsed = clock::monotonic_millis() - started;
    if elapsed > 10 {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{name} took {elapsed} ms; the deadline is 10 to 20 ms"));
    }
    result
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { monotonicMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';

function timedProvider<T>(name: string, work: () => T): T {
  const started = monotonicMillis();
  const result = work();
  const elapsed = Number(monotonicMillis() - started);
  if (elapsed > 10) log('warn', `${name} took ${elapsed} ms; the deadline is 10 to 20 ms`);
  return result;
}
```

## Beyond the plugin log

The `log` import is one of several tools. The trace, the widget tree inspector, the profiler and the memory view are specified in [Debugging tools](/pages/reference-debugging-tools/). Symptoms from users, listed by phase with a fix for each, are in [Troubleshooting](/pages/guide-troubleshooting/). A plugin MUST NOT depend on `--unredacted` traces to diagnose a user's problem, because that flag works only for a plugin installed with `dev`. [AUT-804]

## What the user sees

When a plugin is disabled, the tree footer shows notice N14 with the plugin name and the failing export, and Settings > Plugins shows the same text. N14 is defined once, with its render, in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart).

<div class="warn">
<p>Disabling a plugin does not delete its data. Fix the first trap, re-enable the plugin, and check the plugin log for the first trap, because later restarts usually repeat it.</p>
</div>

### Reload and health while you develop

`ilium plugin dev` reloads each rebuilt side with the reason `upgrade` and keeps restore bytes up to 1 MiB ([Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#development-reload)). A trap during development follows the normal restart rule. Run `ilium plugin status <id>` to see health and near-misses ([Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/)), and `ilium plugin stats <id>` for resource use ([Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/)). A development install can be reset with `--purge-on-exit`.

- [Background jobs](/pages/background-jobs/)

### Security

Logs are redacted of secrets ([SEC-243]). If a plugin breaks the client, start with `ilium --safe-mode` ([Security response](/pages/reference-security-response/)).

# Errors and limits

## Errors and limits

A host call can fail in two ways. It can return a typed error that the plugin handles, or it can trap, which ends the plugin instance at once. A returned error is an ordinary result: `Result<T, PluginError>` in Rust, or a thrown `PluginError` in TypeScript. A trap is a plugin bug. The kernel restarts the instance under a fixed back-off, and the third failure inside 10 minutes disables the plugin.

## You will need

- The grants for the capabilities you use. A declined or revoked grant returns `not-permitted`. Calling an import the manifest never requested is a trap.
- Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- [Events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) and [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).

## Returned errors

Every function that can fail returns `result<T, plugin-error>`. The record has a `code`, a `message` and an optional `retry-after-ms`.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/errors in reference-wit
enum error-code {
  not-permitted, not-found, invalid-argument, conflict, quota-exceeded,
  rate-limited, busy, timed-out, cancelled, unsupported, pane-not-ready,
  revoked, io, network, internal,
}
record plugin-error { code: error-code, message: string, retry-after-ms: option<u32> }
```

In Rust the fields are `code`, `message` and `retry_after_ms`. In TypeScript they are `code`, `message` and `retryAfterMs`, and codes are strings such as `'rate-limited'`.

| Code | Meaning | Retry |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | The capability is missing, declined or revoked, the path leaves its scope, or a policy forbids it. | No. Hide the feature or ask for the grant. |
| `not-found` | The node, pane, buffer, file, command, plugin or provider does not exist. | No. |
| `invalid-argument` | The call breaks a rule the plugin can check first: syntax, range, size or corrupt input. | No. Fix the call. |
| `conflict` | A stale revision, a manual title, a lock, or an existing file for `create-new`. | Yes, after reading the state again. |
| `quota-exceeded` | A stored or held quota is full, or the CPU budget is spent. | After freeing resources, or after `retry-after-ms`. |
| `rate-limited` | A rate rule throttles the call. `retry-after-ms` is always set. | Yes, after `retry-after-ms`. |
| `busy` | Transient capacity is full: pending requests, the job queue, or a device in use. | Yes, later. |
| `timed-out` | A deadline passed: a lock wait, HTTP, a process, a job, or a reply. | Yes. |
| `cancelled` | The plugin, the user or a shutdown cancelled the request. | Maybe. |
| `unsupported` | The host or platform cannot do it, or the call is in the wrong instance kind. | No. |
| `pane-not-ready` | A restored terminal pane has not started its process yet. | Yes, after `pane-created` or `tree-changed`. |
| `revoked` | The authorization epoch changed during the call. | No. The plugin is re-activated. |
| `io` | An operating system I/O error other than a missing file. | Maybe. |
| `network` | DNS, connect, TLS or transport failure. | Yes. |
| `internal` | A host bug, or a trap inside a job instance. | No. |

Every function that returns a result may return `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`. A call that returns a request id checks its grant, scope, syntax and per-call caps at once, and returns those errors synchronously. Anything that needs the disk, the network, another process or the user is reported later as `failed(code)` in the completion.

A value over a per-call cap is refused with `invalid-argument` before anything is written. The host never truncates a value silently, except that log lines are cut and marked.

## Rate limits and retries

A `rate-limited` error is not a plugin bug. Wait for `retry-after-ms`, then try the same call again. A refused submission reports the same error in its outcome:

```json
{
  "type": "request-completed",
  "request": { "submission": 23 },
  "outcome": {
    "refused": {
      "code": "rate-limited",
      "message": "Too many send-input calls for this pane",
      "retry-after-ms": 2000
    }
  }
}
```

A refused submission does not reserve its `dedup-key`, so a retry with the same key is correct. A submission that was accepted and later failed keeps its key reserved. A retry of that action needs a new key.

A dedup key is 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:`, `/` and `-`. Keys are remembered for 10 minutes. A submission with a reserved key completes as `duplicate(original)` and has no effect. `send-input` and `agent-action` must carry a key.

## Worked examples

### Rust: handle the typed errors of a file read

This server plugin reads `NOTES.md`. A missing file is normal, an oversized file is skipped with a log line, and any other error is logged.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, log::{self, Level}};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::Activation;

async fn read_notes() -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
    let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: "NOTES.md".into() };
    match fs::read_all(&path).await {
        Ok(bytes) => Ok(bytes),
        Err(error) if matches!(error.code, ErrorCode::NotFound) => Ok(Vec::new()),
        Err(error) if matches!(error.code, ErrorCode::QuotaExceeded) => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, "NOTES.md is over the read-all limit; skipped");
            Ok(Vec::new())
        }
        Err(error) => Err(error),
    }
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesReader;

impl Lifecycle for NotesReader {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        ilium_plugin_sdk::task::spawn(async {
            match read_notes().await {
                Ok(bytes) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("read {} bytes", bytes.len())),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Error, &format!("read failed: {}", error.message)),
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for NotesReader {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

The read runs in `task::spawn`, so activation returns without waiting for the file.

### TypeScript: retry a rate-limited notice with the same key

When the command runs, this server sends a notice. If the host refuses it with `rate-limited`, the plugin waits `retryAfterMs` with a one-shot timer, then sends a notice again with the same dedup key. The plugin submits only notices, so every refused submission is one of them.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';

const SAVED_NOTICE_KEY = 'example.notes:saved:notes-md';
let nextCorrelation = 1n;
// Timer id to the submission it will send. Timers are not saved across a restart.
const pendingByTimer = new Map<bigint, Submission>();

function savedNotice(): Submission {
  nextCorrelation += 1n;
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'notify',
      val: { title: 'Notes', body: 'Notes saved', urgency: 'low', sound: undefined },
    },
    correlation: nextCorrelation,
    dedupKey: SAVED_NOTICE_KEY,
  };
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const out: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'example.notes/save') {
        out.push(savedNotice());
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && event.val.outcome.tag === 'refused') {
        const error = event.val.outcome.val;
        if (error.code === 'rate-limited' && error.retryAfterMs !== undefined) {
          pendingByTimer.set(timers.set(error.retryAfterMs, undefined), savedNotice());
        }
      } else if (event.tag === 'timer-fired') {
        const retry = pendingByTimer.get(event.val);
        pendingByTimer.delete(event.val);
        if (retry !== undefined) {
          out.push(retry);
        }
      }
    }
    return out;
  },
});
```

The retry gets a new correlation number and keeps the dedup key. The refused notice did not reserve its key, so the retry is accepted.

## Traps

A trap ends the instance at once, and the kernel restarts it under the rules below. These cases trap:

- The plugin calls an import that its manifest never requested.
- One `on-events` call returns more than 256 submissions.
- A `ui-tree` has a child index out of range, a graph that is not a tree, or a duplicate `key`.
- A call passes its deadline, or the instance exceeds its memory or table limit.
- The guest panics, or a TypeScript export with no result (`onEvents`, `render`, `deactivate`) throws.

A declined capability does not trap. The call returns `not-permitted`. A trap inside a job fails the job with `internal`, and the plugin keeps running.

<div class="warn">
<p>Do not use a trap as normal control flow. Each trap is a failure, and the third one inside 10 minutes disables the plugin until the user turns it on again.</p>
</div>

## Logged refusals and traps

Every `not-permitted` result and every trap is written to the plugin log, with the plugin id, the interface and the function. Each entry is one line: the time as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, the level padded to five characters, the plugin id and the message. Refusals are logged at `warn`, traps at `error` and restarts at `info`. Run `ilium plugin logs <id>`, or add `--tail <n>` for the last `n` lines.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.notes --tail 4
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:14:02</span> <span class="t-warn">warn </span> example.notes refused fs.read: not-permitted
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:14:03</span> <span class="t-err">error</span> example.notes trap in ui.set-widget-state: index 7
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:14:03</span> <span class="t-ok">info </span> example.notes restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3)
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:14:09</span> <span class="t-err">error</span> example.notes trap in ui.set-widget-state: index 7
</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The plugin log: one refusal, two traps and the restart between them.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Restart and disable

A trap or a deadline breach drops the instance, cancels its pending requests and restarts it. The count is kept per plugin on each side. A failing view counts for the plugin, not for the view.

- Back-off: the first failure in the window restarts the plugin after 1 s and the second after 5 s. The third failure in the window disables it; no 30 s step exists. A failure older than 10 minutes no longer counts, so the next failure restarts after 1 s again [API-040].
- Each failure counts for 10 minutes after it happens. The window slides, and a successful run does not reset it.
- Disable: the third failure inside the window disables the plugin on that side. A manual re-enable resets the count to zero.

A revoked re-activation, a disable, an upgrade or a shutdown never counts.

When a plugin is disabled, the tree footer shows a notice that names the export and the cause. The view is named only when the failing export was `views.render`.

Timers and watches end at a restart, so the plugin registers them again in `activate`.

## Resource limits

Each limit is a manifest key with a default and two ceilings. The T1 ceiling applies to bundled first-party plugins, and the T2/T3 ceiling to all others. A manifest may ask for any value up to the ceiling. A value above the ceiling is clamped and logged, never refused. The user sets each limit in `config.toml` under `[plugins.limits]`, or for one plugin under `[plugins."<id>".limits]`, with the same key. The effective value is the smallest of the tier ceiling and the first of the per-plugin user value, the all-plugins user value, the manifest value and the default; 0 or a missing value means not set. The user can raise a value up to the ceiling and can lower it. The default is the same for every tier; a T1 plugin may request up to the T1 ceiling in `limits`.

| Limit | Default | Ceiling T1 | Ceiling T2/T3 | Effect when reached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linear memory per instance | 32 MiB | 256 MiB | 128 MiB | trap |
| Table elements | 10,000 | 50,000 | 20,000 | trap |
| `on-events` deadline | 20 ms | 50 ms | 20 ms | trap |
| Command handling inside `on-events` | 50 ms | 100 ms | 50 ms | trap |
| `views.render` deadline | 10 ms | 20 ms | 10 ms | trap |
| `annotate` deadline | 10 ms | 20 ms | 10 ms | late result dropped; third miss in a row traps |
| Scene `render` deadline | the frame budget | 50 ms | 50 ms | frame skipped; 30 misses in a row traps |
| `activate` deadline (may yield) | 2,000 ms | 5,000 ms | 2,000 ms | trap |
| `deactivate` deadline | 500 ms | 1,000 ms | 500 ms | instance dropped without restore bytes |
| Job CPU deadline | 2,000 ms | 60,000 ms | 10,000 ms | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Job wall-clock deadline | 20,000 ms | 600,000 ms | 100,000 ms | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Job memory | 64 MiB | 512 MiB | 256 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| Job input or output, each | 16 MiB | 64 MiB | 16 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Concurrent jobs per plugin | 2 | 8 | 2 | queued |
| Job queue | 16 | 64 | 16 | `busy` |
| Event queue per plugin | 1,024 | 4,096 | 1,024 | stuck plugin: restart |
| Pending requests | 64 | 256 | 64 | `busy` |
| Timers | 64 | 256 | 64 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Output filters | 32 | 128 | 32 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Watches (a recursive watch counts once) | 64 | 256 | 64 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Key grabs | 8 | 32 | 8 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `ui-tree` nodes | 4,096 | 16,384 | 4,096 | trap |
| `ui-tree` size | 1 MiB | 4 MiB | 1 MiB | trap |
| Decorations | 4,096 | 16,384 | 4,096 | `refused(quota-exceeded)` |
| Node metadata per node | 64 KiB | 256 KiB | 64 KiB | `quota-exceeded` |
| Storage per bucket | 16 MiB | 256 MiB | 16 MiB | `quota-exceeded` |
| Disk for `data` plus `cache` | 256 MiB | 4 GiB | 256 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| `fs.read-all` per request | 64 MiB | 512 MiB | 64 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| `fs.write` per call | 16 MiB | 64 MiB | 16 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| HTTP response body | 8 MiB | 64 MiB | 8 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| Process output (stdout plus stderr) | 4 MiB | 32 MiB | 4 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| Log lines | 200 per second | 1,000 per second | 200 per second | dropped and counted |
| Open videos | 2 | 8 | 2 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Audio captures | 2 | 4 | 2 | `quota-exceeded` |

CPU time and bytes also draw on the plugin's execution quota group. When it is spent, submissions get `quota-exceeded` with `retry-after-ms`.

Per-call caps are fixed:

| Cap | Value | Error |
|---|---|---|
| Submissions per `on-events` return | 256 | trap |
| Events per `on-events` batch | 256 | the excess is split into later batches |
| Synchronous `fs.read` | 1 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Codec input | 16 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Storage key and value | 256 bytes and 1 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| `send-input` text or raw bytes per intent | 64 KiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `fs.scan` entries | 65,536 | results truncated, `truncated: true` |
| Journal payload | 4 KiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Message payload | 1 MiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| Topic payload | 64 KiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Command `arguments-json` | 64 KiB | `invalid-argument` |

Larger codec input belongs in a background job. See [Background jobs](/pages/background-jobs/).

Rate rules return `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms`, except where noted. `topics.publish` allows 100 per second per plugin. `notify` allows 6 per minute, and `play-sound` 4 per second, both refused with `refused(rate-limited)`. `send-input` allows 20 per second per pane. Log lines and output-filter matches over their rate are dropped and counted.

Events that drop under load (`output-matched`, `topic-published`, `audio-frames`) are counted. The next batch starts with one `events-dropped` event that lists each source and count.

There are five session keys in `[plugins.limits]`, which apply to all plugins in one process: `session_memory_mib`, `session_helpers`, `session_processes`, `session_http_streams` and `session_decorations`. The user may only lower them. Each instance reserves its configured linear memory limit against `session_memory_mib` at activation (a sandbox helper reserves its `memory_mib` plus 32 MiB). When the pool is full, a new instance is refused and the refusal is logged. It does not count as a failure. At most 16 children per session (`session_processes`) are shared by `process.run` (`busy`) and `process.spawn` (`quota-exceeded`). Fixed session caps are 4,096 pending requests (`busy`) and 32 key grabs (`quota-exceeded`).

Replies to slow calls wait 30 s for commands and services, 120 s for inference, and 30 s for HTTP API replies. These and the other fixed reply deadlines are in the [reply deadlines table](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#reply-deadlines).

## Settings limits

Settings rows have their own limits. A value that is stored but no longer valid is ignored, and the default applies. The limits fall into two groups, by the moment they are checked.

**Checked at install (`manifest.settings-limit` refusal; the message names the item and the limit).**

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| Tabs per plugin | 2 |
| Sections per plugin tab | 8 |
| Sections per plugin, per built-in tab | 2 |
| Plugin sections in one built-in tab, all plugins | 6; the extra ones are not drawn |
| Plugin tabs in the rail, all plugins | 16 |
| Rows per section, children per group | 24 (a `group` counts as one row plus its children), and 12 children in one group |
| Value keys per plugin | 128 |
| Choice options | 64 |
| List items | 64, each object at most 8 fields |

**Checked on save or at run time (`invalid-argument`, the value is not stored; a `settings-validate` timeout refuses the save).**

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| Text value | 4,096 characters; text area 65,536 |
| All values of one plugin, serialized | 256 KiB |
| `settings-validate` answer | 100 ms; a timeout refuses the save |

The full list of codes and warnings is in [Reference: errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/). A plugin's settings are explained in [Plugin settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/).

## Additional codes, limits and deadlines

The extended surface adds no runtime error code. The 15 codes stay, and the newer functions reuse them. The complete lists are in [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) and the [install error catalogue](/pages/reference-manifest-schema/#error-catalogue).

Four ideas explain most of the new rules.

- **Rate limits are per slot or per plugin.** A status segment accepts 10 updates per second, a toast 3 per 10 seconds, a geocode request 1 per second. An update over the rate is refused with `rate-limited`, and the previous content stays.
- **Quotas are counts of live things.** Streams, children, durable timers and vector entries count what is open or stored. Close or delete one, then retry.
- **Deadlines fall back.** A slow `menu-items` or `tokens` call does not fail the user action. The menu opens with its static entries, and the lines stay plain.
- **The first-party tier is not a way around limits.** `limits_tier: "first-party"` raises the settings caps for bundled plugins. A third-party package that sets it is refused at install.

**Rust**

```rust
// A toast is refused over 3 per 10 s. Coalesce instead of retrying in a loop.
fn show_progress(&mut self, text: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
    self.latest = text.to_string();
    if self.toast_in_flight { return vec![]; }   // the next event shows self.latest
    self.toast_in_flight = true;
    vec![Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
        id: Some("progress".into()), tone: Tone::Info, title: text.into(),
        body: None, actions: vec![], duration_ms: None,
    }))]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// A toast is refused over 3 per 10 s. Coalesce instead of retrying in a loop.
function showProgress(text: string) {
  latest = text;
  if (toastInFlight) return []; // the next event shows `latest`
  toastInFlight = true;
  return [{ intent: { tag: 'toast', val: { id: 'progress', tone: 'info', title: text,
    body: undefined, actions: [], durationMs: undefined } },
    correlation: nextCorrelation++, dedupKey: undefined }];
}
```

<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Settings─────────────────────────────────╮
│ Palette ………………………… ← Sunset … → +               │
│ ! Stars must be 10 to 2000. Value not saved.    │
│ ✕ Too many streams: close one first.            │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────── ╯
</pre>

A refused value and a refused call as the settings page shows them. Illustrative, not generated.

## Extension point codes and limits

Extension points add install codes and run codes, and no new `error-code` case. Each run code is carried by one of the 15 codes plus a message prefix; the mapping is in [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes). The tables are in [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#extension-point-codes). In short, a point owner may declare 16 points and a contributor may add 64 extensions. A hook handler has 5 to 50 ms (default 20 ms), and a whole chain has 100 ms. A payload or reply is at most 64 KiB, and a collect entry is at most 16 KiB. Hooks fail open: a timeout, trap or error counts as a pass, and `extension.vetoed` appears only when a veto handler refused on purpose.

## Install codes and budgets for authors

Errors in this page are returned to a running plugin. A package that fails to install gets a `manifest.` or `package.` code instead, and no plugin runs. The complete list of those codes is the install code index in [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/). The limits an author should keep a plugin well inside are collected in the budget table of [Performance](/pages/performance/). An author MUST treat a limit as a trap and not as a warning. [AUT-111]

## Edge cases

- Audio rates from 8,000 to 192,000 Hz are accepted. More than two channels is `unsupported`.
- A malformed submission, or a batch whose grant is missing, refuses the batch. The offending submission completes as `refused`, and every other submission of that batch completes as `refused(cancelled)` with the message `batch refused: submission <index>`. A batch of more than 256 submissions is a trap, not a refusal.

## Rules

- Handle `rate-limited`, `busy` and `pane-not-ready` by waiting and then retrying. Never loop without a delay.
- Fix the cause of every trap. The third trap inside 10 minutes disables the plugin.

- [Debugging](/pages/debugging/)
- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)

- [Background jobs](/pages/background-jobs/)
- [Reference: errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

Security codes and limits are listed in [Reference: errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) and defined in [Security and policy requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-security-policy/).

# Events and intents

## Events and intents

A plugin learns what happens through events and changes the world through intents. The kernel delivers events in batches of at most 256. The handler answers each batch with a list of submissions, each carrying one intent. The kernel checks the list against the plugin's grants, applies the accepted submissions in order, and reports each outcome as a `request-completed` event in a later batch.

## You will need

- The grants for each event and intent you use. The tables below name them. See [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/).
- A server or client side. In Rust, `#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]` or `side = "client"`. In TypeScript, `side: 'server'` or `side: 'client'` in `definePlugin`. A scene plugin exports `renderer` instead of `handler`.
- The `lifecycle` and `handler` exports. Both are required, so the manifest never lists them in `exports`.
- Rust stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, or Bun 1.2 or later for TypeScript.
- Background from [Worlds and sides](/pages/worlds-and-sides/).

## The handler

The handler is the `Handler` trait in Rust and the `onEvents` function in TypeScript. The kernel calls it with one batch, and it returns the submissions to apply.

| Language | Signature |
|---|---|
| WIT | `on-events: func(batch: list<event>) -> list<submission>;` |
| Rust | `fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission>` (required) |
| TypeScript | `onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[]` inside `definePlugin` |

An instance runs one call at a time, so a handler never re-enters itself.

The `on-events` deadline is 20 ms by default for every tier. A manifest may request up to 50 ms, and only a T1 plugin gets above 20 ms (T2 and T3 ceiling: 20 ms). A breach traps the instance, which follows the [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule): restart after 1 s, then 5 s, and disable at the third failure within 10 minutes, with a notice in the tree footer. See [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

## Event catalogue

An event reaches a plugin only when the plugin holds the listed grant. Lazily activated plugins receive events only after activation.

| Event | Payload | Grant | Delivery policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree-changed` | `list<node-id>` | `tree.read` | Coalesced; pending lists merge into one union |
| `node-removed` | `node-id` | `tree.read` | Never dropped |
| `pane-created` | `pane-info` | `panes.read` | Never dropped |
| `pane-exited` | `node`, `status: option<s32>`, `signal: option<string>` | `panes.read` | Never dropped |
| `pane-focused` | `option<node-id>` | `panes.read` | Coalesced |
| `pane-resized` | `node`, `columns`, `rows` | `panes.read` | Coalesced by node |
| `pane-title-changed` | `node`, `title`, `source` (osc, manual, inferred) | `panes.read` | Coalesced by node |
| `agent-identified` | `node`, `signature` | `agent.read` | Never dropped |
| `agent-activity-changed` | `node`, `previous`, `current`, `revision` | `agent.read` | Never dropped |
| `agent-goal-changed` | `node`, `goal: option<string>` | `agent.read` | Coalesced by node |
| `input-submitted` | `node`, `text`, `source` (user, plugin, scheduled, voice), `epoch: u64` | `agent.read-prompts` | Never dropped |
| `output-matched` | `node`, `filter-id`, `line`, `row` | `terminal.output-filter` | Drop oldest, counted |
| `link-activated` | `node`, `detector-id`, `text` | own `link_detectors` | Never dropped |
| `pointer` | `node`, `row`, `column`, `kind` (down, up, drag, wheel), `button` | `terminal.pointer`, while claimed | Coalesced (drag) |
| `editor-opened`, `editor-closed` | `buffer-ref` | `editor.read` | Never dropped |
| `editor-changed` | `buffer`, `revision`, `first-line`, `last-line` | `editor.read` | Coalesced by buffer, debounced 100 ms |
| `editor-saved` | `buffer`, `path` | `editor.read` | Never dropped |
| `settings-changed` | `settings-change { keys, origin, side }` | always (own) | Coalesced |
| `timer-fired` | `timer-id` | always (own) | Coalesced by timer |
| `request-completed` | `request-result` | always (own) | Never dropped |
| `job-progress` | `request-id`, `percent` | always (own) | Coalesced by job |
| `message` | `from`, `channel`, `payload` | own sides, or the sender's `messages.peer` | Never dropped |
| `topic-published` | `topic`, `from`, `payload-json` | `topics.subscribe` | Drop oldest, counted |
| `command-invoked` | `command`, `arguments-json`, `origin`, `context` | own commands | Never dropped |
| `ui-action` | `view`, `key`, `action-id`, `kind`, `value` | own views | Never dropped (`scrolled` coalesced) |
| `key-pressed`, `key-released` | `grab`, `pane`, `chord`, `repeat` | `keys.intercept` or `wants_keys` | Never dropped |
| `view-visibility` | `view`, `visible: bool` | own views | Coalesced |
| `fs-changed` | `watch`, `paths: list<string>` | `fs.watch` | Coalesced by watch |
| `audio-frames` | `capture`, `samples: list<s16>` | audio grant | Drop oldest, counted |
| `cli-invoked` | `invocation`, `name`, `argv`, `cwd` | `cli.contribute` | Never dropped |
| `cli-cancelled` | `invocation` | `cli.contribute` | Never dropped |
| `http-called` | `call`, `method`, `path`, `headers`, `body` | `http-api.route` | Never dropped |
| `client-attached`, `client-detached` | `client-id` | server side, always | Never dropped |
| `theme-changed` | none | client side, always | Coalesced |
| `events-dropped` | `list<dropped-count>` | always (own) | Coalesced by (event, source); never dropped |

In Rust the payload records live in `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events`. In TypeScript an event is a tagged value such as `{ tag: 'pane-exited', val: { node, status, signal } }`.

### Delivery policies

| Policy | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Coalesced | Pending events of one kind and key always merge into one, whatever the queue fill. The merged event keeps the newest payload at the position of its newest occurrence. |
| Never dropped | The event always arrives. |
| Drop oldest, counted | At a full queue the oldest pending drop-oldest event of any kind is removed and counted under its own event and source. If none is pending and the new event is drop-oldest, the new event is discarded and counted. |

When a never-dropped event cannot be queued, the plugin counts as stuck. The kernel restarts it, and the new instance receives a `tree-changed` for every node so that it can re-read its state.

Dropped events are counted. The next batch starts with one `events-dropped` event. At most one is pending: a second drop before the next batch adds to the matching (event, source) count or appends a record, and the event is never dropped. `source` is the filter id, the topic name or the decimal capture id, and none for every other kind. The full rules are in [Events](/pages/api-events/).

## Extended events

The contract adds 18 events after `events-dropped`, so the catalogue holds 56 events. A plugin that does not match them is unaffected. The `ui-action` event gains 6 kinds (17 in total), and `pointer` and `command-invoked` gain fields.

| Event | Payload | Grant | Delivery policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `screen-changed` | `pane`, `first-row`, `last-row`, `revision` | `terminal.read-cells` | Coalesced by pane, 10 per second |
| `user-line-submitted` | `pane`, `text`, `at` | `agent.read-prompts` | Never dropped |
| `signal-changed` | `pane`, `signal`, `value` | `agent.read` | Coalesced by pane and signal |
| `agent-model-changed` | `pane`, `model` | `agent.read` | Coalesced by pane |
| `editor-pointer` | `buffer`, `pane`, `position`, `pointer` | `editor.read` | Coalesced (move) |
| `editor-viewport-changed` | `editor-viewport` | `editor.read` | Coalesced by pane, 100 ms |
| `http-stream-data`, `http-stream-closed` | `stream`, `status`, `headers`, `chunk`, or `outcome` | the stream's `http` grant | Never dropped, with back-pressure |
| `child-output`, `child-exited` | `child`, `stream`, `bytes`, or `status`, `signal` | `process.long-lived` | Never dropped |
| `pane-lifecycle-changed` | `pane`, `state`, `by` | `panes.read` | Never dropped |
| `attention-changed` | `node`, `marked`, `reason`, `by` | `tree.attention` or `tree.read` | Coalesced by node |
| `client-request` | `call`, `kind`, `payload-json` | client side, own `client_requests` | Never dropped |
| `kernel-settings-changed` | `tab`, `keys` | `settings.read-kernel:<tab>` | Coalesced by tab |
| `keymap-changed` | none | `keymap.read` | Coalesced |
| `durable-timer-fired` | `timer`, `name`, `late-by-millis` | always (own) | Never dropped |
| `input-uncertain` | `pane`, `dedup-key` | the grant of the original `send-input` | Never dropped |
| `display-mode-changed` | `mode` | own `display_modes` | Coalesced |

**Rust**

```rust
for event in batch {
    match event {
        Event::DurableTimerFired(fired) if fired.name == "nightly-scan" => {
            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("scan is {} ms late", fired.late_by_millis));
        }
        Event::InputUncertain(uncertain) => {
            // The server restarted before the outcome of a send-input was recorded.
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("input to pane {} is uncertain", uncertain.pane));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
for (const event of batch) {
  if (event.tag === 'durable-timer-fired' && event.val.name === 'nightly-scan') {
    log('info', `scan is ${event.val.lateByMillis} ms late`);
  } else if (event.tag === 'input-uncertain') {
    // The server restarted before the outcome of a send-input was recorded.
    log('warn', `input to pane ${event.val.pane} is uncertain`);
  }
}
```

## Batches, order and queues

- A batch holds at most 256 events. The host splits larger backlogs.
- Each plugin has one queue. The queue holds 1,024 events by default. The ceiling of `event_queue` is 4,096 for T1 and 1,024 for T2 and T3. The host clamps a larger request to the ceiling and logs the clamp [API-043] [EVT-046]. The manifest key `event_queue` requests a value.
- Events arrive in kernel emission order across all kinds. For one node the order is `pane-created`, other pane events, `pane-exited`, then `node-removed`. `agent-identified` always precedes `agent-activity-changed` for the same pane.
- A handler may return at most 256 submissions. More than 256 traps the instance.

The log below shows one batch under load: a counted drop, a refused submission and a trap.

<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 12:04:01</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span> events-dropped: output-matched 2 (drop oldest)
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 12:04:02</span> <span class="t-err">err</span>  #2 refused(not-permitted): notify.desktop not granted

## Submissions and outcomes

A submission is `record submission { intent: intent, correlation: u64, dedup-key: option<string> }`.

- `intent` is the change to make, such as `set-decoration` or `send-input`.
- `correlation` matches the outcome with the plugin's request. Numbers below 2^63 belong to the plugin. The SDK allocates from 2^63 upward.
- `dedup-key` is the optional key described below.

Some intents are applied by the server and some by the client kernel. A client plugin's submission to the server is forwarded and its outcome comes back to that client only. The table is in [Intents](/pages/api-intents/#which-side-applies-an-intent).

In Rust, `Submission::new(intent)` sets no key and `Submission::keyed(intent, key)` sets one. In TypeScript, write `{ intent, correlation, dedupKey }`, with `correlation` as a `bigint`.

Every submission completes exactly once, as a `request-completed` event whose `request-ref` is `submission(<correlation>)`.

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok` | Applied. For calls, the typed result is ready to take with a `take-*` function. It is held for 30 s or until taken. |
| `ok-node(node-id)` | Applied. Returns the node the intent created. |
| `duplicate(request-ref)` | The dedup key was already reserved. Nothing happened. The ref names the submission that reserved it. |
| `refused(plugin-error)` | An acceptance check failed. Nothing was applied, and the key was not reserved. |
| `failed(plugin-error)` | The kernel accepted the submission but could not apply it. The key stays reserved. |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled by the plugin, the user or a shutdown. A sibling of a refused submission in the same batch completes as `refused(cancelled)`, not as `cancelled` [ABI-009]. Submissions accepted but not yet applied at shutdown complete as `cancelled`. |

A take of a slow-call result before completion, a second take, or a take of an unknown id returns `none` [ABI-014]. The table of every slow call and its take function is in [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#slow-calls). A result is held for 30 s [ABI-012]. Pending requests are limited to 64 per plugin by default and 4,096 per session, and a call over the limit fails with `busy` [ABI-013].

### Batch checks

The kernel runs two batch-level checks over the whole list, in index order, before any effect. Check 1 is shape: a valid variant tag, required fields present, string and list lengths within the ABI caps, a `dedup-key` present where the intent requires one, and every key 1 to 128 characters from the documented set. Check 2 is the grant: requested in the manifest and currently granted. The lowest-index submission that fails (shape before grant inside one submission) completes as `refused(invalid-argument)` for shape or `refused(not-permitted)` for grant. Every other submission completes as `refused(cancelled)`. All of them carry the message `batch refused: submission <index>`, where `<index>` is the 0-based index of that offender. No effect runs and no dedup key is reserved [ABI-009]. All other checks are per submission and affect only that submission: target exists, pane ready, payload value valid (for example a text node id where a pane is needed), rate, quota, conflict and `if-current` [ABI-032]. Accepted submissions are applied in order, so a node removed by an earlier one gives `failed(not-found)` to a later one.

## Dedup keys

There is one key, `dedup-key` on the submission. The older `idempotency-key` field no longer exists in any intent.

- Format: 1 to 128 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`. Other characters make the submission malformed.
- Scope: the pair of plugin id and key, at the kernel that applies the intent. The server and each client keep separate tables.
- Window: 10 minutes after reservation. For `send-input` and `agent-action` the journal keeps 24 hours or 4,096 entries per session, whichever is smaller, and is written to the snapshot before the input reaches the pane. A server restart does not repeat input.
- Reservation: a key is reserved only after every acceptance check passes. A refused submission keeps its key free for a retry. An accepted one keeps it even if it later fails, so a retry of a failed action needs a new key.

The SDK helper `dedup::key_for(parts: &[&str])` joins its parts with `:` and replaces disallowed characters with `-`. It returns a key such as `finish:42:7`.

For `send-input`, two checks run at batch level before this list (see Batch checks): shape (key present, total text across all stages at most 65,536 bytes, otherwise `refused(invalid-argument)`) and the grant `terminal.write` (otherwise `refused(not-permitted)`). The kernel then checks each submission in this order. The first failing check decides the outcome.

1. Dedup key already reserved. Then `duplicate(original)`.
2. Pane exists and is a terminal pane. Otherwise `refused(not-found)` or `refused(unsupported)`.
3. The pane is restored, which means its process has started. Otherwise `refused(pane-not-ready)`.
4. The rate limit has room. Otherwise `refused(rate-limited)`.
5. `prompt-epoch`, when given, equals the pane's current epoch. Otherwise `refused(conflict)`.
6. `if-current`, when given, matches the pane (activity, screen revision and foreground command). Otherwise `refused(conflict)` with the message `precondition: <field>`.
7. No other plugin holds the input lock of the pane. Otherwise `refused(conflict)` with the message `input-locked`.
8. The input is accepted: the key is reserved, the rate token is taken and the text is written. A refused attempt never takes a rate token [EVT-050].

## Intent catalogue

Every intent needs its grant. The outcome column lists the codes beyond `ok`.

| Intent | Payload | Grant | Outcomes beyond `ok` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rename-node` | `node`, `title` | `tree.write` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(conflict)` for a manually named node |
| `move-node` | `node`, `target`, `placement` (before, after, inside-first, inside-last) | `tree.write` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(invalid-argument)` for a target inside the node |
| `close-node` | `node` | `tree.write` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(conflict)` for a locked node |
| `set-node-locked` | `node`, `locked` | `tree.write` | `refused(not-found)` |
| `create-pane` | `parent`, `title`, `content-kind`, `cwd`, `command`, `initial-input` | `panes.create` (and `terminal.write` for `initial-input`) | `ok-node`; `refused(not-found)`, `failed(io)` |
| `signal-pane` | `pane`, `signal` (interrupt, terminate, kill, hangup) | `panes.signal` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(pane-not-ready)` |
| `send-input` | `pane`, `text`, `delivery` (Typed, Submitted, Pasted), `prompt-epoch` | `terminal.write` | `refused(pane-not-ready)`, `refused(rate-limited)`, `refused(conflict)` |
| `agent-action` | `pane`, `action-id` | `agent.control` | `refused(unsupported)`, `refused(conflict)` |
| `set-decoration` | `node`, `slot`, `content`, `icon`, `sort-key`, `persist` | `tree.decorate` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(invalid-argument)`, `refused(quota-exceeded)` |
| `clear-decoration` | `node`, `slot` | `tree.decorate` | As `set-decoration` |
| `set-virtual-rows` | `row-kind`, `rows` | `tree.decorate` | `refused(invalid-argument)` for an undeclared row kind |
| `play-sound` | sound id | `sound.play` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(rate-limited)` (4 per second) |
| `notify` | `title`, `body`, `urgency` (low, normal, high), `sound` | `notify.desktop` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(rate-limited)` (6 per minute) |
| `open-view`, `close-view` | `view-target`, `focus` | `ui.panels` | `refused(not-found)` |
| `invoke-command` | `command`, `arguments-json` | `commands.invoke` | `refused(not-found)`, `failed(timed-out)` after 30 s |
| `message` | `to`, `channel`, `payload` | `messages.peer:<plugin-id>` | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(invalid-argument)` over 1 MiB |
| `editor-apply-edits` | `buffer`, `base-revision`, `edits` | `editor.edit` | `refused(conflict)` for a stale revision, `refused(invalid-argument)` for overlapping edits |
| `editor-open` | `path`, `line`, `placement` (new pane, split, replace) | `editor.edit` | `ok-node`; `refused(not-permitted)`, `failed(not-found)`, `failed(io)` |

## Extended intents

The contract adds 23 intents, so the catalogue holds 42. `send-input` and the `ok-epoch` outcome are described in [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/). `restructure` is atomic: all operations apply or none does.

| Family | Intents | Grant |
|---|---|---|
| Pane lifecycle | `freeze-pane`, `unfreeze-pane`, `replace-pane-command`, `terminate-pane-process`, `resize-pane` | `panes.lifecycle` |
| Tree structure | `create-group`, `create-folder`, `create-project`, `create-split`, `restructure`, `revert-restructure` | `tree.restructure` |
| Tree state | `set-bookmarked`, `set-expanded` | `tree.write`, or own `virtual_rows` |
| Tree decoration | `set-inferred-icon` | `tree.decorate` |
| Attention | `mark-attention`, `ack-attention` | `tree.attention` |
| Chrome | `set-status-segment`, `clear-status-segment`, `set-frame-slot`, `clear-frame-slot` | `ui.chrome` |
| Notices | `toast`, `dismiss-toast` | `notify.toast` |
| Desktop | `open-external` | `open-external` |

Five intents carry optional fields: `send-input`, `set-decoration`, `rename-node`, `notify` and `set-virtual-rows`. A missing field keeps the plain behaviour.

**Rust**

```rust
let toast = ToastSpec {
    id: Some("scan-done".into()),
    tone: Tone::Success,
    title: "Scan finished".into(),
    ..Default::default()
};
Submission::keyed(Intent::Toast(toast), "toast:scan-done".to_string())
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const submission: Submission = {
  intent: { tag: 'toast', val: { id: 'scan-done', tone: 'success', title: 'Scan finished', actions: [] } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: 'toast:scan-done',
};
```

## Worked example: Rust

This server plugin puts a badge on each pane whose agent starts working. It needs the `agent.read` and `tree.decorate` grants and one decoration slot named `hello` in the manifest.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetDecorationSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Hello;

impl Lifecycle for Hello {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("hello from {}", context.plugin));
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for Hello {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. })
                = event else { continue };
            if current != AgentActivity::Working {
                continue;
            }
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
                node,
                slot: "hello".into(),
                content: vec![Span::plain("hi")],
                icon: None,
                sort_key: None,
                persist: false,
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

The next snippet keys a `send-input` so that a repeated finish event types the command only once. `pane` comes from an earlier event.

```rust
let key = dedup::key_for(&["finish", "42", "7"]); // "finish:42:7"
let submission = Submission::keyed(
    Intent::SendInput(SendInputSpec {
        pane,
        text: "/compact".into(),
        delivery: Delivery::Submitted,
        prompt_epoch: None,
    }),
    key,
);
```

## Worked example: TypeScript

This client plugin answers its own command with a desktop notice. It needs the `notify.desktop` grant. The `command-invoked` event is always delivered to the plugin's own commands.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate(context) {
    log('info', `hello from ${context.plugin}`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const out: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.hello/greet') {
        continue;
      }
      out.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'notify',
          val: { title: 'Hello', body: 'from a plugin', urgency: 'normal', sound: undefined },
        },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return out;
  },
});
```

The `correlation: 1n` value is below 2^63, so the plugin owns it. To suppress repeats for 10 minutes, set `dedupKey` to a string such as `'greet:1'`.

## Testing a handler

Rust `FakeHost` (feature `testing`) and TypeScript `createFakeHost()` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing` accept events with `deliver(events)` (a list of events in, `Vec<Submission>` out) and return the submissions. Outcomes come back as `request-completed` events when you call `settle()`. `ilium plugin test` runs every fixture against the built component, compares its expectation file, and exits 3 when one differs. Include a fixture that sends the same finish twice within the window. See [Testing](/pages/testing/) and [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/).

## Common mistakes

- Treating an event as a command. Events report what happened. Submit an intent to change something, and expect a refusal when a check fails.
- Keeping state in local variables. An instance can restart at any time, so keep durable state in storage, node metadata or settings.
- Relying on a dropped event. Drop-oldest events can be lost under load. `events-dropped` tells you the count, not the contents.
- Reusing a key after a failure. An accepted key stays reserved, so retry a failed action with a new key.
