│ <span class="t-hi">com.example.cursor 0.1.0</span>    T2  <span class="t-ok">On</span>                             │
│ com.example.notes 0.1.0     T2  <span class="t-dim">Off</span>                            │
│ vendor.ext 0.1.0            T3  <span class="t-warn">Refused: no sandbox</span>            │
│                                                                │

### Rules defined elsewhere on this page

- [LIF-271] On a trap or stop the host MUST release every effect listed in the stop-effects paragraph of this page, for the dead instance as well. Test: trap a plugin holding an input lock, a stream and a child process.
- [USR-173] An update MUST keep the grants the user already answered and MUST ask only for new ones. A failed update MUST roll back to the previous version. The user-facing rules are USR-123 and USR-124 in [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/#update-a-plugin). Test: update with one new grant and count the rows in the dialog.
- [LIF-275] An update MUST reset the "Not now" counter of a bundled plugin. Test: answer Not now twice, update, and count prompts.

# Packages and manifests

## Packages and manifests

A plugin ships as one `.iliumpkg` file. It is a ZIP archive with a fixed layout and a `manifest.json` at its root. The manifest names the plugin, lists its components, states the grants it needs and declares what it adds to Ilium. Ilium reads the manifest and the contributions before it runs any plugin code, so menus, help and settings work before the plugin starts.

This page covers the package layout, every manifest key, the contribution shapes, the `ilium plugin` commands, the install checks and their error codes.

## What you need

- A plugin id in reverse-DNS form, such as `example.notes`. The prefix `ilium.` is reserved for first-party plugins.
- The worlds and sides, from [Worlds and sides](/pages/worlds-and-sides/), and the grant strings, from [Capabilities and grants](/pages/capabilities/).
- The `ilium` binary, which includes the `ilium plugin` commands. Rust plugins need a Rust toolchain. TypeScript plugins need Bun 1.2 or later. See [Getting started toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/).

## Package layout

A `.iliumpkg` file is a deterministic ZIP32 archive. Entries are stored without compression, sorted by path, with fixed timestamps, so two builds of the same sources are byte-identical.

| Path | Required | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | yes | The manifest. |
| `server.wasm`, `client.wasm`, `scene.wasm` | if the side is declared | Components for the `server`, `client` or `scene` side. |
| `assets/**` | no | Read-only files, visible through the `package` file scope. |
| `help/*.md` | no | Help topics referenced by `contributes.help`. |
| `sounds/*` | no | Sound files referenced by `contributes.sounds`. |
| `src/**` | no | Sources and source maps, for review only. Never loaded. |
| `signature` | for tier T2 | Detached Ed25519 signature over the canonical bytes of `manifest.json`. |

Every entry except `manifest.json` and `signature` must appear in the `files` list with its length in bytes and its lowercase SHA-256. Each component also carries an `ilium:api-version` custom section (three big-endian `u16` values: major, minor, patch) that must equal the manifest `api`.

The install checks run in one fixed order of 11 stages, and each failure has an error code. The stages are defined once, in [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/#the-validation-order), and the codes in [Manifest schema and error catalogue](/pages/reference-manifest-schema/#error-catalogue). [Security](/pages/security/#verifying-a-package) and [Grant review and consent](/pages/reference-grant-review-and-consent/#the-install-pipeline) describe the same stages from the user's side. A failed check stops the install, no component is loaded, and no plugin code runs.

## Manifest keys

The manifest is JSON with snake_case keys. Unknown keys fail the install with `manifest.unknown-key`. A source manifest may omit `files`, because `ilium plugin pack` writes it. A packed manifest must contain it.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | string | yes | Contract version, `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. |
| `id` | string | yes | Matches `[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+`. |
| `name`, `version` | string | yes | Display name and semantic version. |
| `publisher` | string | yes | Must equal the publisher recorded for the signing key in a T2 package. |
| `description`, `license`, `icon` | string | no | One paragraph, an SPDX expression, and a Tabler icon name. |
| `server`, `client`, `scene` | object | at least one | `{ entry, world, exports }`. `exports` lists optional exports only. |
| `capabilities` | object | no | Grant strings per side: `server`, `client` or `scene`. |
| `activation` | list of strings | no | Triggers such as `startup` or `topic:<topic>`. Default: first use of a contribution. |
| `requires` | object | no | `{ "services": ["ilium:inference/provider@0.1.0"] }`. Activation waits for a provider. |
| `replaces` | list of strings | no | At most 4 ids of replaceable core plugins. The user confirms the replacement. |
| `replaceable`, `surface` | boolean, list | core plugins | `replaceable: true` plus the `kind:name` items a replacement must provide. |
| `contributes` | object | no | Static contributions, below. |
| `limits` | object | no | Requested limits. The host clamps each value to the tier ceiling. |
| `limits_tier` | string | no | `"standard"` (default) or `"first-party"`. Raises the settings caps. Accepted only for bundled T1 plugins whose id starts with `ilium.`, otherwise `manifest.limits-tier`. |
| `unstable` | list of strings | no | Opt-in names. Four exist in 0.1.0: `ui-calendar`, `plugin-services`, `gpu-kernels` and `websocket`. |
| `files` | list | packed only | `{ "path", "length", "sha256" }` for each entry. |

The `exports` list names only the optional exports: `views`, `detector`, `job-runner`, `service-provider`, `inference-provider` and `annotator`. Required exports (`lifecycle`, `handler`, `renderer`) are never listed. A component whose real exports differ from required plus listed fails with `manifest.exports-mismatch`.

## Contributions

`contributes` declares what Ilium shows without running plugin code. Ids are local. The host builds global ids as `<plugin-id>/<id>` for commands, settings pages and help topics, and `<plugin-id>.<id>` for pane kinds.

| Key | Entry shape |
|---|---|
| `commands` | `{ id, title, arguments_schema?, voice?, palette?, icon?, when? }`. `palette` defaults to `true`. `voice` is 1 to 8 phrases. |
| `keybindings` | `{ command, chord, mode }`. Mode is `prefix`, `global` or `pane:<kind>`. |
| `settings` | `{ page, section?, scope, schema }`. Scope is `server` or `client`. |
| `settings` | `kind` `tab` (with `"render": "view"` for a custom page) or `section`. See [Plugin settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/). |
| `help` | `{ id, file, title }`. The file is Markdown under `help/`. |
| `decoration_slots` | `{ id, placement, priority }`. Placement is `badge`, `icon`, `subtitle` or `footer`. |
| `virtual_rows` | `{ id, title, icon, parent }`. Parent is `project` or `session`. |
| `toolbar_buttons` | `{ id, icon, label, command, applies_to }`. |
| `context_menu` | `{ id, title, command, target }`. Target is `terminal`, `tree-node`, `editor` or `pane:<kind>`. |
| `panels` | `{ id, title, icon?, default_size?, modal }`. |
| `pane_kinds` | `{ id, title, icon, primitive, wants_keys, persist }`. Primitive is `basic`. Persist is `metadata` or `none`. |
| `scenes` | `{ id, title, family, modes, settings_schema, frame_rate_cap? }`. Needs a `scene` side. |
| `signatures` | `{ id, process_names, aliases, icon, resume?, actions?, session_scope? }`. |
| `output_filters` | `{ id, regex, panes, rate_per_second }`. Panes are `all`, `agents` or `terminals`. |
| `link_detectors` | `{ id, regex, command }`. |
| `editor_line_actions` | `{ id, title, regex?, command }`. |
| `sounds` | `{ id, file }`. |
| `cli` | `{ name, summary, arguments_schema, output }`. One subcommand, output `jsonl`. |
| `http_routes` | `{ method, path }`. Needs the matching `http-api.route:<path>` grant. |
| `services` | `{ provides }`. Interface names. |
| `topics` | `{ publishes, subscribes }`. Publishing stays under the plugin's id prefix. |
| `jobs` | `{ kind, deadline_ms?, memory_mib? }`. |
| `onboarding_steps` | `{ id, title, view, order }`. |
| `extension_points` | `{ id, kind, mode?, title, entry_schema?, payload_schema?, reply_schema?, risk?, deadline_ms?, max_handlers?, max_entries?, dynamic?, version }`. At most 16. |
| `extensions` | `{ point, id, priority?, entry?, handler? }`. At most 64. Needs `extensions.contribute`. |

The `themes` key is not part of the contract. Plugins ship no colour themes.

## Worked example: a Rust plugin

This plugin counts words in the current note. Its source manifest has no `files` list, and it needs no grants, because the always-granted set covers it.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.word-count",
  "name": "Word count",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Labs",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "activation": ["startup"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "count", "title": "Count words in note", "icon": "calculator" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`ilium plugin new ./word-count --id example.word-count --lang rust --side server` creates `manifest.json`, `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`. Then build and pack:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin build ./word-count
<span class="t-ok">ok</span>   server.wasm           component, 412 KiB
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin pack ./word-count
<span class="t-dim">step</span>   inventory            hashing 1 file
<span class="t-ok">ok</span>   artifact             dist/example.word-count-0.1.0.iliumpkg
<span class="t-hi">done</span> result               unsigned, tier T3
</pre>

Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The commands print JSON lines with `--json`. This render shows the same fields as plain text, with the hash omitted.

## Worked example: a TypeScript plugin with a notes pane

This manifest serves a notes plugin with a server and a client component. The same manifest works for Rust or TypeScript. `ilium plugin build` detects the toolchain from the project files: `Cargo.toml` means Rust, and `package.json` means TypeScript. A TypeScript project holds `manifest.json`, `package.json`, `src/server.ts` and `src/client.ts`.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.notes",
  "name": "Notes",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Labs",
  "description": "Keeps a notes pane for each project.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "icon": "notes",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["views"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["tree.read"],
    "client": ["ui.panels", "panes.read", "panes.provide-kind"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "new-note", "title": "New note", "icon": "plus" }
    ],
    "pane_kinds": [
      {
        "id": "notes",
        "title": "Notes",
        "icon": "notes",
        "primitive": "basic",
        "wants_keys": true,
        "persist": "metadata"
      }
    ],
    "help": [
      { "id": "overview", "file": "help/overview.md", "title": "Notes" }
    ]
  },
  "files": [
    { "path": "server.wasm", "length": 412390, "sha256": "<64 hex characters>" },
    { "path": "client.wasm", "length": 905112, "sha256": "<64 hex characters>" },
    { "path": "help/overview.md", "length": 1204, "sha256": "<64 hex characters>" }
  ]
}
```

The `pane_kinds` entry has the global id `example.notes.notes`. The `help` entry creates the topic `example.notes/overview`. The hashes and lengths above are placeholders that the packer replaces.

<div class="warn">
<p>A package that holds a file not listed in <code>files</code> is refused. So is a listed file whose length or hash differs from the file on disk. Run <code>ilium plugin pack</code> after every rebuild.</p>
</div>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin install dist/example.notes-0.1.0.iliumpkg
<span class="t-err">err</span>  manifest.file-length  client.wasm: 905120 bytes, inventory says 905112
<span class="t-err">err</span>  manifest.file-unlisted  src/notes.ts is not in the files list
<span class="t-warn">warn</span> no plugin code was loaded or run
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. An install that fails the inventory check. Nothing from the package runs.

## Commands

The build commands are defined in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/). The commands that install, update, search, publish and sign are in [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/), with one exit-code table for both. Commands that build, check, pack and sign print JSON lines when you pass `--json`. The commands that read a running plugin (`logs`, `list`, `trace`) print text by default. Registry commands such as `verify`, `publish` and `update` are in [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/). The ones you use for packages are `new`, `build`, `pack`, `check`, `lint`, `test`, `inspect --verify`, `keygen`, `sign`, `trust`, `install`, `dev` and `grants`.

## Install errors

The install runs the checks in the diagram order. Each failure prints one `error` line and stops the install. The grant checks use the `manifest.grant-*` family from [Capabilities and grants](/pages/capabilities/).

| Code | When it fires |
|---|---|
| `manifest.unknown-key` | A manifest key is not in the schema. |
| `manifest.key-missing` | A packed manifest has no `files` key. |
| `manifest.id-invalid` | The id does not match the pattern. |
| `manifest.id-reserved` | A third-party package uses an `ilium.` id. |
| `manifest.file-unlisted` | A package entry is missing from `files`. |
| `manifest.file-missing` | A listed file is absent from the package. |
| `manifest.file-length`, `manifest.file-hash` | A listed length or SHA-256 differs from the file. |
| `manifest.api-version` | A component's `ilium:api-version` differs from `api`. |
| `manifest.signature-invalid` | A T2 signature does not verify. |
| `manifest.publisher-mismatch` | `publisher` differs from the key's recorded publisher. |
| `manifest.exports-mismatch` | The component exports differ from the manifest list. |
| `manifest.export-grant` | An export needs a grant the manifest does not request. |
| `manifest.grant-wildcard` | A grant argument is `*` where no wildcard is allowed. |
| `manifest.grant-unknown`, `manifest.grant-tier`, `manifest.grant-dependency` | A grant is unknown, limited to bundled plugins, or missing a required companion grant. |
| `manifest.schema-keyword` | A settings schema uses a keyword outside the allowed subset. |
| `manifest.settings-key-clash`, `manifest.settings-id-clash` | A settings key or tab or section id is declared twice. |
| `manifest.cli-name-reserved` | The CLI name is a kernel command. |
| `manifest.cli-name-taken` | The CLI name belongs to another installed plugin. |
| `manifest.sound-id-taken` | A sound id repeats, or equals the bundled id `chirping`. |
| `manifest.catalog-unknown` | A row `source` names an unknown catalogue, or a `catalogs` entry has no `catalog-provider` export. |
| `manifest.contribution-limit` | More entries of a contribution key than its cap. |
| `manifest.contribution-target` | `applies_to` or `slot` names an unknown target or another plugin's slot. |
| `manifest.row-format` | An unknown `item_format`, a bad `steps` ladder or `special_values` out of bounds. |
| `manifest.limits-tier` | `limits_tier: "first-party"` on a package that is not a bundled T1 `ilium.*` plugin. |
| `manifest.when-key` | An unknown `when` context key. |
| `manifest.client-request-unknown` | A client-request export is inconsistent with the other side's manifest. |
| `manifest.asset-size` | Package assets over 64 MiB, or a font asset over 4 MiB. |
| `manifest.visible-when` | `visible_when` names another plugin's key, an unknown key, or forms a cycle with `depends_on`. |
| `manifest.menu-depth` | Menu items nested deeper than 2. |
| `manifest.settings-source` | A `choice` row `source` with both `options` and `source`, or neither. |
| `manifest.cli-field` | An invalid `output`, `stdin` or `argument_groups` value on a `cli` entry. |
| `manifest.scene-prerender` | `prerender` out of range, or on a scene that declares `wants-pointer`. |

This table lists the common codes. The complete list of `manifest.` and `package.` codes, with the page that defines each, is the install code index in [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).

## Tiers and the review dialog

| Tier | Who | Install behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Bundled first-party plugins | Grants up to the manifest ceiling. High-risk grants are asked once at first activation. |
| T2 | Signed by a publisher key the user trusts | The review dialog shows every grant. High-risk grants start unchecked. |
| T3 | Unsigned local packages | Needs `--allow-unsigned` or `ilium plugin dev`. Shows a `dev` badge and T2 ceilings. |

A package signed by an unknown key is offered for trust, with the key fingerprint. Declining refuses the install. A T2 or T3 install shows the review dialog. The plugin installs with the grants that stay checked:

<pre class="term">╭─ Install example.notes 0.1.0 ────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Example Labs · signed (T2) · fingerprint 3F2A…9C01               │
│ Keeps a notes pane for each project.                             │
│                                                                  │
│ Server                                                           │
│ [x] Read the workspace tree …………………………………………………………………… tree.read │
│ Client                                                           │
│ [x] Show panels and settings pages ………………………………………………… ui.panels │
│ [x] See pane sizes, titles and focus ………………………………………… panes.read │
│ [x] Provide its own kind of pane ……………………………… panes.provide-kind │
│                                                                  │
│              [ Install ]   [ Details ]   [ Cancel ]              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. Each row is one capability with its grant string. Rows marked `HIGH` start unchecked.

A package that fills other plugins' extension points shows them in a separate group, **Adds to other plugins**. Each line names the owner and the point, for example `Text triggers > Before fire: can stop a trigger from sending text (high risk)`. A package with `replaces` adds one more confirmation: `Replaces Titles and organisation. The built-in plugin is turned off while this one is on.` Turning the replacement off or uninstalling it turns the built-in plugin back on. Its stored data stays on disk and the replacement does not read it. See [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/).

## Updates, trust and keys

The rules for a person who installs packages are in [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/). The rules that a package and its publisher must meet are these. Key formats, the trust store and registry updates are defined in [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/) and [Install and update](/pages/reference-install-and-update/).

- [USR-126] An update MUST keep the plugin id and MUST have a higher version. The signature MUST come from the key that signed the installed version, or from a key that the user trusts after seeing both fingerprints. Test: offer an update signed by a second key and assert the prompt shows the old and the new fingerprint.
- [USR-127] Trust MUST be per key, MUST be stored in the user's trust list, and MUST NOT be created by installing a package without a prompt. Test: install with a new key in a script without `--yes` and assert the install is refused.
- [USR-128] A T2 package whose key was removed from the trust list MUST keep running and MUST show `untrusted` in `ilium plugin list`. A later update MUST ask for trust again. Test: remove the key, list, and offer an update.
- [USR-129] A publisher MUST keep the private key offline and MUST NOT put it in a package. A lost key means new packages need a new key and a new trust prompt. Test: review `ilium plugin keygen` output for the path of the private key and its mode `0600`.

## Edge cases

- **Clamped limits.** A limit above the tier ceiling is clamped and logged, never refused. The user can set limits in `config.toml` under `[plugins.limits]`.
- **Declined grants.** The plugin still installs. Imports for a declined capability return `not-permitted`.
- **Updates.** A newer version of an installed id is an update, and the dialog shows only new capabilities. A lower version needs `--allow-downgrade`.
- **Keybinding conflicts.** The user's remap wins, then kernel keys, then T1, then T2 and T3 plugins. The losing binding is inactive and listed in Settings > Keys.
- **Settings schema.** Allowed keywords are `type`, `properties`, `required`, `enum`, `title`, `description`, `default`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `pattern`, `maxLength`, `help`, `step`, `unit`, `secret`, `multiline`, `enum_titles` and `picker`.
- **Process grants.** `process.run:*` is refused with `manifest.grant-wildcard`. `process.run:sh` is valid only in T1 packages.

## What the user sees

After a successful install, the plugin appears in Settings > Plugins with its grants. Its commands appear in the command palette, and its help topic `example.notes/overview` is readable. Revoking a grant in Settings > Plugins, or with `ilium plugin grants`, withdraws the contributions that need it and restarts the plugin with the smaller grant set. A failed install prints its errors and runs no plugin code.

### After install

Install, update, rollback and uninstall follow [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/). Data layout changes use [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/). A development copy installed by `ilium plugin dev` reloads with the reason `upgrade`; see [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#development-reload).

# Pane primitives

## Pane primitives

A pane holds one piece of content: a shell, an agent session, a text buffer or a widget tree. A primitive is the host-provided kind of pane that a plugin builds on. Ilium has four primitives: `terminal`, `agent`, `editor` and `basic`. Each is a WIT interface in the package `ilium:primitives`. The kernel keeps the per-byte and per-keystroke work. A plugin reads state, adds rules and decorations, and, for a `basic` pane, supplies the whole pane body.

A plugin imports the interface, never the implementation behind it. The implementation can move later, for example the editor after version 1, without changing the plugin's imports.

## You will need

- Grants in the manifest `capabilities` block for each call you make (table below). A declined grant links the import to a stub, and calls through it return `not-permitted`.
- Rust 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, or Bun 1.2 or later for TypeScript. See [Toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/).
- The side that owns the call. The server world imports `terminal` and `agent`. The client world imports `editor` and `basic`. Terminal reads work on both sides.
- The model in [Architecture](/pages/architecture/) and [The UI model](/pages/ui-model/).

## The four primitives

In the tables below, S is the server side and C is the client side.

| Primitive | Interface | Sides | The kernel owns | Plugins add | Grants |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `terminal` | `ilium:primitives/terminal` | S and C (read), S (filters), C (pointer) | PTY, vt100 screen, scrollback, selection, paste, mouse | screen reads, output filters, highlight layers, input | `terminal.read-screen`, `terminal.output-filter`, `terminal.pointer`, `terminal.write` |
| `agent` | `ilium:primitives/agent` | S and C (read), S (signatures) | process-tree walk, poll schedule, signatures, activity state, toolbar strip | agent and prompt reads, signatures, toolbar buttons, actions | `agent.read`, `agent.read-prompts`, `agent.signatures`, `agent.control` |
| `editor` | `ilium:primitives/editor` | C | the native editor: buffers, undo, file custody, 1 s autosave, highlighting | buffer reads, decorations, gutter marks, edits, file loads and saves | `editor.read`, `editor.edit` |
| `basic` | `ilium:primitives/basic` | C | the generic frame: focus, scrollbars, split geometry, key and mouse routing | title, footer, focus, size, and the body from `views.render` | `panes.provide-kind` |

`pane-info` reports `primitive` as `terminal`, `editor` or `basic`. An agent pane is a terminal pane whose process a signature identifies, so the `agent` interface adds no pane type.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭──≡ ● · terminal───────────╮ ╭──≡ ● · agent──────────────╮
│<span class="t-prompt">$</span> cargo test               │ │🦀 <span class="t-hi">⠋</span> Fix auth              │
│running 14 tests           │ │goal: ship v0              │
│test result: ok            │ │                           │
╰───────────────────────────╯ ╰───────────────────────────╯
╭──≡ ● · editor─────────────╮ ╭──≡ ● · basic──────────────╮
│fn main() {                │ │Notes                      │
│    run();                 │ │Rows below come from the   │
│}                          │ │plugin view tree           │
╰───────────────────────────╯ ╰───────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The four primitives, each in a rounded Ilium panel with the chrome title. Every border in Ilium is rounded.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Further capabilities per primitive

Each primitive has further capabilities. Each has its own page with signatures, Rust and TypeScript examples, errors and limits.

| Primitive | Capability | Page | Grants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terminal` | cell attributes, frozen snapshot, history text and search, modes, foreground process, `screen-changed`, `user-line-submitted` | [Terminal reads](/pages/primitives-terminal-reads/) | `terminal.read-cells`, `terminal.history` |
| `terminal` | sub-cell pointer, `move`, modifier gestures, drag-over | [Terminal pointer](/pages/primitives-terminal-pointer/) | `terminal.pointer` |
| `terminal` | `send-input` stages, raw bytes, mouse, preconditions, input lock, journal, interactive `terminal-view` | [Terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/) | `terminal.raw-input`, `terminal.input-lock` |
| `agent` | model fact, prompt epoch, typed transcript, `signal-changed`, `agent-model-changed` | [Agent transcript and signals](/pages/primitives-agent-transcript/) | `agent.transcript` |
| `editor` | viewport, pointer, minimap marks, token provider | [Editor viewport and tokens](/pages/primitives-editor-viewport/) | none new |
| `basic` | `report-activity`, `set-dirty` | [Basic primitive](/pages/primitives-basic/) | none new |

## Basic: a pane kind on the basic primitive

A plugin declares a pane kind under `pane_kinds` in its manifest. Its body is the plugin's `views.render` export for that pane.

```json
"pane_kinds": [
  {
    "id": "notes",
    "title": "Notes",
    "icon": "notes",
    "primitive": "basic",
    "wants_keys": true,
    "persist": "metadata"
  }
]
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Local id. The content kind of its panes is `<plugin-id>/<id>`, here `com.example.notes/notes`. |
| `primitive` | Always `"basic"`. |
| `wants_keys` | When true, keys the focused widget does not use arrive as `key-pressed` for the pane. |
| `persist` | Required, no default. `metadata` keeps state in node metadata. `storage` keeps it in session-bucket keys under `pane/<node-id>/`, deleted when the pane closes. `none` recreates the pane empty after a restart. |

| Rust, `primitives::basic` | TypeScript, `/primitives/basic` | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set_title(pane, title)` | `setTitle` | `result<_, plugin-error>` | Title row. Over 256 characters: `invalid-argument`. |
| `set_status(pane, status)` | `setStatus` | `result<_, plugin-error>` | One-line footer, as `styled-text`. |
| `request_focus(pane)` | `requestFocus` | `result<_, plugin-error>` | Focuses the pane. |
| `size(pane)` | `size` | `option<tuple<u16, u16>>` | Inner columns and rows. `none` for a node that is not the plugin's kind. |

Basic panes have no process, so `pane-not-ready` never applies. The three functions that change the frame return `not-permitted` for any node that is not one of the plugin's kinds.

<div class="warn">
<p>Basic functions exist only in the client world. A server build that imports them fails to compile.</p>
</div>

### Example: a notes pane in Rust

This client plugin sets the title and footer of each notes pane when the pane is created. Its manifest needs `panes.read` (for `pane-created`) and `panes.provide-kind`.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::basic;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::PaneInfo;

const NOTES_KIND: &str = "com.example.notes/notes";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesPanes {
    created: u32,
}

impl Lifecycle for NotesPanes {}

impl Handler for NotesPanes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::PaneCreated(pane) = event else { continue };
            if pane.content_kind == NOTES_KIND {
                self.decorate(pane);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl NotesPanes {
    fn decorate(&mut self, pane: PaneInfo) {
        self.created += 1;
        if let Err(error) = basic::set_title(pane.node, "Notes") {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("set_title refused: {}", error.message));
            return;
        }
        let footer = format!("{} notes open in this session", self.created);
        let status = vec![Span::plain(footer.as_str())];
        if let Err(error) = basic::set_status(pane.node, status) {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("set_status refused: {}", error.message));
        }
    }
}
```

## Terminal: screen, filters, highlights and input

| Rust / TypeScript | Grant | Returns and rules |
|---|---|---|
| `read_screen(pane, part, max_rows)` / `readScreen` | `terminal.read-screen` | `option<Screen>`. `part` is `visible` or `scrollback`. `max_rows` above 10,000 is clamped. |
| `selection(pane)` / `selection` | `terminal.read-screen` | `option<Selection>`: text, first and last row and column. |
| `add_output_filter(pane, filter)` / `addOutputFilter` | `terminal.output-filter` (S) | `result`. Regex at most 1 KiB, rate 1 to 100 per second. An existing id on the pane is replaced. |
| `remove_output_filter(pane, id)` / `removeOutputFilter` | `terminal.output-filter` (S) | No result. |
| `claim_pointer(pane)` / `claimPointer` | `terminal.pointer` (C) | `result`. `conflict` when another plugin holds the claim. |
| `release_pointer(pane)` / `releasePointer` | `terminal.pointer` (C) | No result. |
| `set_highlights(pane, layer, regions)` / `setHighlights` | `terminal.pointer` (C) | `result`. Layer names match `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`. At most 4,096 regions per layer, 16 layers per pane. |
| `clear_highlights(pane, layer)` / `clearHighlights` | `terminal.pointer` (C) | No result. |
| `prompt_epoch(pane)` / `promptEpoch` | `terminal.write` | `option<u64>`: the count of submitted prompts. |

A `Screen` holds `columns`, `rows` (one string per row), `cursor-row`, `cursor-column`, `title` and a `revision`. Filter matches arrive as `output-matched` events with `node`, `filter-id`, `line` and `row`. Surplus matches above a filter's rate are dropped and counted in one `events-dropped` event. A highlight region outside the screen is clipped silently. A region whose first position comes after its last is `invalid-argument`.

Input is the intent `send-input`: `pane`, `text` (at most 64 KiB), `delivery` (`typed`, `submitted` or `pasted`), an optional `prompt-epoch` and a mandatory `dedup-key`. The kernel checks in this order and stops at the first failure:

1. Shape, key and text size. Failure refuses the batch with `invalid-argument`.
2. The `terminal.write` grant. Failure refuses the batch with `not-permitted`.
3. The dedup key. A reserved key completes as `duplicate(original)`.
4. The pane exists and is a terminal pane. Failure is `not-found` or `unsupported`.
5. The pane is restored. A restored pane still waiting for its process gives `pane-not-ready`.
6. The rate. Failure is `rate-limited`.
7. The prompt epoch, if given, matches the pane. Otherwise `conflict`.
8. The key is reserved and the text is written.

A refused submission does not reserve its key, so a retry with the same key after fixing the cause is valid.

### Example: a build-error filter in TypeScript

This server plugin adds an output filter to each new terminal pane and reads the visible screen on a match. Its manifest needs `panes.read`, `terminal.output-filter` and `terminal.read-screen`.

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { addOutputFilter, readScreen } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const FILTER_ID = 'build-errors';
const ERROR_PATTERN = 'error(\\[E[0-9]+\\])?:';

function installFilter(pane: bigint): void {
  try {
    addOutputFilter(pane, { id: FILTER_ID, regex: ERROR_PATTERN, ratePerSecond: 5 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError) {
      log('warn', `filter refused for pane ${pane}: ${error.code}, ${error.message}`);
    }
  }
}

function reportErrorTail(pane: bigint): void {
  const screen = readScreen(pane, 'visible', 40);
  if (screen === undefined) return;
  const lastRow = screen.rows[screen.rows.length - 1] ?? '';
  log('info', `pane ${pane} shows an error at screen revision ${screen.revision}: ${lastRow}`);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'pane-created' && event.val.primitive === 'terminal') {
        installFilter(event.val.node);
      }
      if (event.tag === 'output-matched' && event.val.filterId === FILTER_ID) {
        reportErrorTail(event.val.node);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Adding a filter with an id the pane already has replaces it, so the handler is safe to run again after a restart.

## Agent: agents, signatures and actions

| Rust / TypeScript | Grant | Returns and rules |
|---|---|---|
| `agents()` / `agents` | `agent.read` | One `{ pane, view }` per identified agent. An empty list when declined. |
| `view(pane)` / `view` | `agent.read` | `option<AgentView>`: `signature`, `activity`, `objective`, `goal`. |
| `session(pane)` / `session` | `agent.read` | `option<SessionRef>`: `scope`, `path`, `session-id`, inside `agent-sessions:<agent>`. |
| `last_prompt(pane)` / `lastPrompt` | `agent.read-prompts` | `option<string>`. Synchronous. |
| `register_signature(spec)` / `registerSignature` | `agent.signatures` (S) | `result`. Same validation as manifest signatures. |
| `set_toolbar_state(button, pane, enabled, label)` / `setToolbarState` | `agent.control` | `result`. A button that is not the plugin's gives `not-found`. A label over 32 cells gives `invalid-argument`. |

Activity values are `none`, `working`, `idle`, `awaiting-approval`, `done` and `menu`. In Rust they are `AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval` and so on. In TypeScript they are strings such as `'awaiting-approval'`.

A signature names an agent CLI. It has `id` (1 to 64 characters from `[a-z0-9-]`), `process-names` (1 to 32), `aliases` (at most 32), `icon` (a Tabler icon name), `resume` (an argv template with `{session}`), `actions` (at most 32), `session-scope` and `submit-keys`. A plugin signature has the global id `<plugin-id>.<id>`. When two origins match one process name, a user signature wins over a plugin signature, which wins over a built-in one (`claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`).

An action is the intent `agent-action`. It sends the key sequence the signature declares for the action id and needs a `dedup-key`. By default an action runs only in the states `idle`, `done`, `awaiting-approval` or `menu`. A `compact` action sent while the agent is `working` completes as `refused(conflict)` with `agent is working`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">▼ 📂 Ilium
›   🦀 <span class="t-hi">⠋</span> Fix auth      <span class="t-dim">(agent pane, working)</span>
›   🖥️    Shell
</pre>
<figcaption>How an agent pane appears in the tree while it works: the identity icon, then the spinner in the activity slot, then the title.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Editor: buffers, decorations and edits

The editor is native. Plugins reach it through the interface that a later editor plugin will also provide.

| Rust / TypeScript | Grant | Returns and rules |
|---|---|---|
| `buffers()` / `buffers` | `editor.read` | `list<BufferRef>`: `buffer`, `pane`, `path`, `language`, `revision`, `line-count`, `dirty`. |
| `buffer_for_pane(pane)` / `bufferForPane` | `editor.read` | `option<BufferRef>`. |
| `read_lines(buffer, first_line, count)` / `readLines` | `editor.read` | `result<list<string>>`. `count` over 10,000 or a line past the end: `invalid-argument`. |
| `selections(buffer)` / `selections` | `editor.read` | `list<TextRange>`, columns in Unicode scalar values. |
| `set_decorations(buffer, layer, items)` / `setDecorations` | `editor.read` | `result`. Items hold a `range`, a `style` and an optional `hover`. |
| `set_gutter(buffer, layer, marks)` / `setGutter` | `editor.read` | `result`. Marks hold a `line`, an `icon`, a `tooltip` and a `command`. |
| `create_buffer(initial, language)` / `createBuffer` | `editor.edit` | `result<buffer-id>`. Up to 16 MiB, 64 buffers per plugin. |
| `load_file(path)` / `loadFile` | `editor.edit`, `fs.read` | Request id, then `take_buffer(request)` gives the buffer id. |
| `save_buffer(buffer, path)` / `saveBuffer` | `editor.edit`, `fs.write` | Request id. `conflict` when the file changed on disk since load. |
| `close_buffer(buffer)` / `closeBuffer` | `editor.read` (the spec lists no other grant) | No result. |

Edits go through the intent `editor-apply-edits` with a base revision. A stale revision gives `conflict`. Decorations and gutter layers belong to the plugin that set them and are cleared when it stops.

<div class="note">
<p>The editor provider is reserved and is not part of <code>ilium:plugin@0.1.0</code>. The editor is a built-in pane kind, the grant <code>editor.provide</code> is refused with <code>manifest.grant-unknown</code>, and no <code>editor-provider</code> interface exists in the WIT reference. After the freeze only additive changes are allowed. See <a href="/pages/versioning/">Versioning</a>.</p>
</div>

The editor stays native because every keystroke passes through it, and it keeps the undo history, file custody and autosave. A plugin call per keystroke would cross the plugin boundary every time. The `code-view` widget therefore edits buffers natively.

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Basic frame call on a node that is not the plugin's kind | `not-permitted`. `size` returns `none`. |
| Undeclared pane kind in `create-pane` | `invalid-argument`. |
| Restored terminal or agent pane still waiting for its process | `pane-not-ready`. Retry after `pane-created` or `tree-changed` for it. |
| Pane, node or buffer closed during a call | `not-found`. |
| Invalid filter regex, rate 0 or over 100 | `invalid-argument`. |
| Layers, filters or buffers over quota | `quota-exceeded`. |
| `send-input` with a reserved key | `duplicate(original)`. No second write. |
| `send-input` with a stale prompt epoch | `conflict`. Read `prompt_epoch` again. |
| `agent-action` while working | `refused(conflict)`, `agent is working`. |
| Edit on a stale revision, or save after an outside change | `conflict`. Read the state again. |
| Filter matches above the rate | Dropped and counted in `events-dropped`. |

Every function that returns a result can also return `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`. See [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

## What the user sees

- A basic pane shows the title in its title row, the footer from `set_status`, and the body from `views.render`.
- Highlight layers paint their regions over the terminal rows. Output filters have no visible effect; they only feed the plugin.
- An agent pane shows its toolbar buttons. `set_toolbar_state` turns each button on or off.
- Editor decorations and gutter marks appear at once and disappear when the plugin stops.
- A refused call returns an error to the plugin. The user sees a message only when the plugin shows one.

# Requests and outcomes

## Requests and outcomes

Some host calls take longer than a handler can wait. A handler has a deadline of 20 ms by default, so an HTTP request, a whole-file read or a process run cannot finish inside one `on-events` call. For those calls the host returns a `request-id` at once. The typed result arrives later, as a `request-completed` event that carries the id, and the plugin takes it with a `take-*` function.

Submissions follow the same pattern. Every submission that a handler returns completes exactly once with an outcome, delivered as a `request-completed` event too.

## You will need

- [Events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) for the event batch and for the submissions that a handler returns.
- The grant for the call. `http.fetch` needs `http:<host-pattern>`, for example `http:api.example.com`. `fs.read-all` needs `fs.read:<path>`. Without the grant the call returns `not-permitted` at once.
- The grant for the intent of a submission. The `notify` intent needs `notify.desktop`. Without it the submission completes as `refused(not-permitted)`.
- The Rust SDK (`ilium-plugin-sdk`) or the TypeScript SDK (`@ilium/plugin-sdk`).

## Two kinds of identifier

| Identifier | Type | Chosen by | Names | Appears in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `correlation` | `u64` | The plugin | One submission | `submission.correlation`, and `request-ref` `submission(n)` |
| `request-id` | `u64` | The host | One slow host call | The raw call's return value, `request-ref` `call(id)`, and every `take-*` function. Unique per plugin side for the whole server run, starts at 1 at server start and is never reused, also across instance restarts [ABI-040] |

The plugin picks correlation numbers below 2^63. The SDK allocates its own numbers from 2^63 upward.

## The surface

### Types

The WIT shapes are `submission { intent, correlation, dedup-key }`, `request-ref { submission(u64), call(request-id) }`, `outcome { ok, ok-node, duplicate, refused, failed, cancelled, ok-epoch }` and `request-result { request, outcome }`. Each shape maps to the SDK forms below.

| WIT | Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|
| `submission` | `Submission { intent, correlation, dedup_key }` | `{ intent, correlation: bigint, dedupKey: string \| undefined }` |
| `request-ref` `call(id)` | `RequestRef::Call(id)` | `{ tag: 'call', val: id }` |
| `request-ref` `submission(n)` | `RequestRef::Submission(n)` | `{ tag: 'submission', val: n }` |
| `outcome` `ok` | `Outcome::Ok` | `{ tag: 'ok' }` |
| `outcome` `ok-node(id)` | `Outcome::OkNode(id)` | `{ tag: 'ok-node', val: id }` |
| `outcome` `duplicate(r)` | `Outcome::Duplicate(r)` | `{ tag: 'duplicate', val: r }` |
| `outcome` `refused(e)` | `Outcome::Refused(e)` | `{ tag: 'refused', val: e }` |
| `outcome` `failed(e)` | `Outcome::Failed(e)` | `{ tag: 'failed', val: e }` |
| `outcome` `cancelled` | `Outcome::Cancelled` | `{ tag: 'cancelled' }` |

`plugin-error` has a `code`, a `message` and an optional `retry-after-ms`. Its codes are listed in [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

### Slow calls

Each slow call exists in two forms. The async wrapper is the normal form. The raw form returns the `request-id` and leaves the completion to `on-events`.

| Interface | Raw function | Take function | Typed result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fs` | `read-all`, `scan`, `lock`, `pick`, `read-with-revision`, `write-atomic` | `take-bytes`, `take-entries`, `take-lock`, `take-picked`, `take-revisioned`, `take-written` | Bytes, entries, lock id, path, bytes with a revision, revision token |
| `fs` | `write`, `remove`, `rename` | None | `ok` or `failed` only |
| `http` | `fetch` | `take-response` | `http-response` |
| `jobs` | `start` | `take-output` | Output bytes |
| `process` | `run` | `take-exit` | `process-exit` |
| `inference` | `complete`, `models` | `take-completion`, `take-models` | Completion, model names |
| `vector` | `embed` | `take-vectors` | One vector of `f32` per input |
| `services` | `call` | `take-reply` | JSON text |
| `editor` | `load-file` | `take-buffer` | Buffer id |
| `editor` | `save-buffer` | None | `ok` or `failed` only |
| `catalogs` | `query-async` | `take-page` | `catalog-page` |
| `geocode` | `search`, `reverse` | `take-places` | List of `geo-place` |
| `sessions` | `send` | `take-reply` | JSON text |
| `client-requests` | `request` | `take-answer` | JSON text |
| `extensions` | `run-hook` | `take-reply` | JSON text |
| `terminal` | `history-text`, `search-history` | `take-history`, `take-matches` | Text, list of `history-match` |
| `agent` | `transcript` | `take-transcript` | List of `transcript-turn` |
| `cli` | `read-stdin` | `take-stdin` | Bytes |
| `commands` | `invoke` | None | `ok` or `failed` only |
| `audio` | `play` | None | `ok` or `failed` only |
| `intents-host` | `submit` | None | The outcome of the submission |

Every row follows the take rules [ABI-014]: a result is held for 30 seconds, counted from the end of the `on-events` call that delivered the completion [ABI-012], and a take before completion, a second take or a take of an unknown id returns `none` (the wrapper returns `not-found`). The same rows are in the [host conformance matrix](/pages/reference-host-conformance/#2-import-matrix).

In Rust the wrapper is named after the WIT function, for example `http::fetch(request).await`. The raw form has the suffix `_request`, for example `http::fetch_request(request)`, and the take function keeps its name, `http::take_response(id)`. In TypeScript the same names appear in camelCase: `fetchRequest(request)` and `takeResponse(id)`.

## Slow call: fetch, complete, take

A plugin fetches a page from a host it is granted. The flow has three steps.

1. The plugin calls `http.fetch` with an `http-request`. The call returns a `request-id` at once, for example 5001.
2. The kernel completes the request later and delivers a `request-completed` event in a batch.
3. The plugin calls `take-response` with the request id and receives the typed result.

The completion event carries `request: call(5001)` and `outcome: ok`. The outcome `ok` means that the result is ready for `take-response`. It does not mean that the HTTP status was 200. The status is in the `http-response` that the take returns. The result is held for 30 seconds, or until it is taken once. The hold starts when `on-events` returns for the batch that delivered the `request-completed` event, not when the host emitted the event [ABI-037]. After the hold, `take-response` returns `none` and the request no longer counts toward `pending_requests`.

The sequence below shows the three steps with the kernel between the plugin and the HTTP service.

    </marker>
  </defs>

  <text x="265" y="110" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">request</text>
  <line x1="330" y1="146" x2="200" y2="146" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#req-arrow)"/>
  <text x="265" y="140" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">reply</text>
  <line x1="200" y1="176" x2="70" y2="176" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#req-arrow)"/>
  <text x="135" y="170" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">request-completed ok</text>
  <line x1="70" y1="206" x2="200" y2="206" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#req-arrow)"/>
  <text x="135" y="200" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">take-response 5001</text>
  <line x1="200" y1="236" x2="70" y2="236" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#req-arrow)"/>
  <text x="135" y="230" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">http-response</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Time runs downwards. The plugin receives a request id at once, and the typed response only after the completion event and a take call.</figcaption>
</figure>

Take the result once. A second take returns `none`, as the replay below shows.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin test ./fetcher --fixture fetch.json
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:14</span>  <span class="t-hi">call</span>      http.fetch -> request 5001
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:14</span>  <span class="t-dim">batch</span>     on-events, completion pending
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:15</span>  <span class="t-ok">complete</span>  request 5001 outcome ok
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:15</span>  <span class="t-ok">take</span>      take-response 5001 -> http-response 200
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:16</span>  <span class="t-warn">take</span>      take-response 5001 -> none, already taken
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The second take returns none. An async wrapper turns that same none into `not-found`.

## The outcomes

Every submission completes exactly once. The table lists the outcomes and what each one means for the plugin.

| Outcome | When it happens | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | The intent was applied. For a call, the result is ready to take. | Take the result within 30 seconds. |
| `ok-node(node-id)` | The intent was applied and created a node. | Keep the node id if the plugin needs the node later. |
| `ok-epoch(u64)` | `send-input` on an agent pane applied. The value is the new prompt epoch. | Keep it to pass as `if-current` or `prompt-epoch` in a later input. |
| `duplicate(original)` | The dedup key was already taken within the dedup window. Nothing was applied. | The outcome says nothing about the result of the first submission, which may still be running or may have failed. Read the completion of the first submission when the result matters. |
| `refused(plugin-error)` | The submission failed a check at acceptance, so nothing was applied, for example `not-found` or `conflict`. | Read the code. `busy`, `rate-limited` and `conflict` can succeed later. |
| `failed(plugin-error)` | The submission was accepted, but applying it or running it failed, for example `io`, `timed-out` or `network`. | Read the code. A retry of an accepted submission needs a new dedup key. |
| `cancelled` | The request stopped before it finished, because the plugin stopped, the user cancelled, or the host shut down. A sibling of a refused submission is not `cancelled`: it completes as `refused(cancelled)` with the message `batch refused: submission <index>` [ABI-009]. | Do nothing, or start the work again on the next trigger. |

Submissions of one batch are applied in order. If an earlier submission removes a node, a later submission for that node completes as `failed(not-found)`.

A batch of more than 256 submissions traps the call [ABI-008]. A batch is refused as a whole only by the two batch-level checks, which run over the whole list in index order before any effect. Check 1 is shape (a valid variant tag, required fields, lengths within the ABI caps, a dedup key where the intent requires one, and a key of 1 to 128 characters from the documented set). Check 2 is the grant (requested in the manifest and currently granted). The lowest-index submission that fails completes as `refused(invalid-argument)` for shape or `refused(not-permitted)` for grant. Inside one submission shape is checked before grant, so a submission with both defects is reported as malformed [RQO-009]. Every other submission in the batch completes as `refused(cancelled)`. The offender and its siblings carry the message `batch refused: submission <index>` with the 0-based index of the offender, and the log line has the same text. Nothing in a refused batch is applied, and no dedup key of the batch is reserved [RQO-011]. Every other check (target exists, pane ready, payload value valid, rate, quota, conflict, `if-current`) is per submission and affects only that submission. A batch of more than 256 submissions is not a refusal: it is a trap that counts as one failure, no submission is applied, and none completes [RQO-010]. A missing grant on `intents-host.submit`, which carries a single submission, is reported as `err(not-permitted)` at once.

## Hook runs

`extensions.run-hook` is a request like a service call. It returns a request id at once. The result arrives as the usual `request-completed` event, with no new event type.

| Outcome | Meaning for the owner |
|---|---|
| `ok` | The chain finished. Call `take-reply` for the final payload (`transform`) or the answer (`first`). `observe` and `veto` give none |
| `refused(conflict)` with message prefix `extension.vetoed` | A `veto` handler refused. The message is `extension.vetoed: <contributor>: <reason>`. Do not perform the action |
| `failed(...)` with an `extension.*` message prefix | The call itself failed, for example `failed(invalid-argument)` with prefix `extension.schema-mismatch` |

A timeout in a handler is never a veto. The chain treats it as a pass. See [extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/).

## Uncertain input after a restart

`send-input` with `journal: true` writes a journal entry before the keys reach the pane. If the server restarts before the outcome is recorded, the plugin cannot know whether the keys arrived. After activation the plugin receives `input-uncertain` with the pane and the dedup key. The plugin decides: retry with a new key, or ask the user.

**Rust**

```rust
if let Event::InputUncertain(uncertain) = event {
    log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("check pane {} before resending", uncertain.pane));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
if (event.tag === 'input-uncertain') {
  log('warn', `check pane ${event.val.pane} before resending`);
}
```

## Duplicate submissions and dedup keys

A submission carries an optional `dedup-key`. It has 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:`, `/` and `-`. The key is scoped to the plugin id, and it stays reserved for 10 minutes from the moment the kernel accepts the submission. A refused submission does not reserve its key, so a retry with the same key after fixing the cause is valid. An accepted submission keeps its key even if it later fails or is cancelled. A key is reserved while `now_wall_ms - accepted_wall_ms < 600,000`. The accepted time is persisted in the journal on the wall clock, so it survives a server restart, and at exactly 600,000 ms the key is free [ABI-034].

A submission that a client plugin half forwards to the server has a wider scope: the pair (plugin id, client id), held by the server for the same 10 minutes. Two clients that send the same key for the same plugin are two submissions. See [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/).

A repeated key completes as `duplicate`, and the outcome names the first submission by the ref it was first submitted with, even across instances, server restarts and re-attach resends. If submission 17 repeats the key of submission 16, the event for 17 carries `duplicate(submission 16)`, and the kernel applies only the first one. `duplicate` means only that the key was taken within the window. It makes no claim about the result of the original. The host does not check that correlation numbers are unique: completions carry the number as given, and the plugin owns uniqueness [ABI-035].

`send-input` and `agent-action` must carry a key, and a submission of either without one refuses its batch. The kernel journals these keys before it writes to the terminal, so a duplicate is caught after a server restart. The journal keeps 24 hours or 4,096 entries per session, whichever is smaller. The journal and the dedup window are separate rules. The dedup window is always 10 minutes from reservation, also across a server restart: a repeat of a journaled key within 10 minutes completes as `duplicate`, and a repeat after 10 minutes is a new submission and is applied. The journal only lets the plugin learn, through `input-uncertain`, that a submission was in flight at a restart; it never makes a key unusable for longer than 10 minutes and never replays input [RQO-030].

The Rust helper `dedup::key_for(&["finish", "node-12"])` returns `finish:node-12`. TypeScript writes the key string directly.

## Limits

| Limit | Value | Result when exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Pending requests per plugin (`pending_requests`) | 64 by default; ceiling 256 for tier T1, 64 for T2 and T3 | `busy`, synchronously |
| Pending requests per session | 4,096 | `busy`, synchronously |
| Hold of a completed result | 30 seconds, or until the first take | Take returns `none`; wrapper returns `not-found` |
| Command or service reply | 30 seconds | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Inference provider reply | 120 seconds | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Dedup window | 10 minutes | Duplicate outcome |
| Submissions per batch | 256 | Trap (counts as a failure, nothing applied, nothing completes) |

Per-tier ceilings are set by the manifest and clamped by the host. See [Security](/pages/security/) for the tiers.

## Worked example in Rust

This client-side plugin fetches release notes once, when it activates. The wrapper returns a response or an error, so the code reads as ordinary sequential code.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, Header, HttpRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ReleaseNotes;

impl Lifecycle for ReleaseNotes {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        task::spawn(fetch_release_notes());
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for ReleaseNotes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

async fn fetch_release_notes() {
    let request = HttpRequest {
        method: "GET".to_string(),
        url: "https://api.example.com/v1/release-notes".to_string(),
        headers: vec![Header {
            name: "accept".to_string(),
            value: "application/json".to_string(),
        }],
        body: None,
        timeout_millis: 5_000,
    };
    match http::fetch(request).await {
        Ok(response) if response.status == 200 => {
            let text = format!("release notes: {} bytes", response.body.len());
            log::log(Level::Info, &text);
        }
        Ok(response) => {
            let text = format!("feed returned status {}", response.status);
            log::log(Level::Warn, &text);
        }
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Busy => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, "too many pending requests; try again later");
        }
        Err(error) => {
            log::log(Level::Error, &format!("feed failed: {}", error.message));
        }
    }
}
```

The `Busy` arm handles a full pending queue. Any other error, such as `revoked` or `timed-out`, reaches the last arm.

## Worked example in TypeScript

This example uses the raw form. `activate` starts the request and keeps its id. `onEvents` matches each completion with the id, takes the response, and submits a notification with a dedup key. The key is `feed:<name>:<day>`, so a second completion on the same day does not notify twice.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { fetchRequest, takeResponse, type HttpRequest } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

// Request ids of the calls this plugin started, mapped to a feed name.
const feedByRequest = new Map<bigint, string>();

function startFeedFetch(): void {
  const request: HttpRequest = {
    method: 'GET',
    url: 'https://api.example.com/v1/release-notes',
    headers: [{ name: 'accept', value: 'application/json' }],
    body: undefined,
    timeoutMillis: 5000,
  };
  try {
    const requestId = fetchRequest(request);
    feedByRequest.set(requestId, 'release-notes');
  } catch (error) {
    log('error', `feed request refused: ${String(error)}`);
  }
}

function submissionsForCompletions(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  const submissions: Submission[] = [];
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag !== 'request-completed') continue;
    const { request, outcome } = event.val;
    if (request.tag !== 'call') continue;
    const feedName = feedByRequest.get(request.val);
    if (feedName === undefined) continue;
    feedByRequest.delete(request.val);
    if (outcome.tag !== 'ok') {
      log('warn', `feed ${feedName} did not complete: ${outcome.tag}`);
      continue;
    }
    const response = takeResponse(request.val);
    if (response === undefined || response.status !== 200) {
      log('warn', `feed ${feedName} gave no usable response`);
      continue;
    }
    const day = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
    submissions.push({
      intent: {
        tag: 'notify',
        val: {
          title: 'Release notes updated',
          body: feedName,
          urgency: 'normal',
          sound: undefined,
        },
      },
      correlation: BigInt(submissions.length + 1),
      dedupKey: `feed:${feedName}:${day}`,
    });
  }
  return submissions;
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {
    startFeedFetch();
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    return submissionsForCompletions(batch);
  },
});
```

`fetchRequest` throws a `PluginError` when the call is refused at once. Raw completions reach `onEvents` unchanged, so the plugin matches ids itself.

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result | Retry |
|---|---|---|
| No grant for the host | `not-permitted`, at once | No |
| Pending requests full | `busy`, at once | Yes, later |
| CPU budget spent | `quota-exceeded` with `retry-after-ms`, at once | Yes, after the delay |
| Timeout passed before the response | `failed(timed-out)` | Yes |
| More than 5 redirects | `failed(network)` | Yes |
| Response body too large to hold | `failed(quota-exceeded)` | No |
| Grant withdrawn during the call | `failed(revoked)`; the plugin is re-activated | No |
| Plugin stopped, restarted or disabled | Pending requests are cancelled; a restarted instance does not receive their completions | Start the work again |
| Take after the 30-second hold, second take, or unknown id | `none`; wrapper returns `not-found` | Start the call again |
| Refused submission retried with the same key | Valid; the refusal did not reserve the key | Yes |
| Accepted submission retried with the same key | `duplicate`, no effect | Use a new key |
| User cancels `fs.pick` | `cancelled`; the wrapper fails with `cancelled` | Yes, if the user wants |

## What the user sees

Most requests run without visible UI. A few do:

- A file picker (`fs.pick`) shows a modal dialog. Cancelling it completes the request as `cancelled`.
- A `notify` intent shows a desktop notification, limited to 6 per minute.
- If a plugin fails three times within 10 minutes, the host disables it on that side and shows a notice in the tree footer and in Settings:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-warn">warn</span> Plugin demo-fetcher stopped after 3 failures in 10
     minutes: handler.on-events trap. Turn it on again in
     Settings &gt; Plugins.
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The notice shows the export that failed. It names a view only when the failing export is `views.render`.

## Rules

- Treat `ok` as "ready to take", not as "done with the result". Take it within 30 seconds.
- Handle `duplicate` as success. Use a new dedup key for each new attempt of an accepted action.
- Expect `cancelled` when the plugin stops. Pending host requests are cancelled at shutdown and at disable.

Requirement ids for this page: [EVT-021], [EVT-022], [RQO-001], [RQO-002], [RQO-003], [RQO-004], [RQO-005], [RQO-006], [RQO-007], [RQO-008], [RQO-009], [RQO-010], [RQO-011], [RQO-020], [RQO-021], [RQO-022], [RQO-030], [RQO-031], [RQO-040]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

# Retained mode

## Retained mode

Plugins do not draw on every frame. A plugin describes the state it wants, such as a badge on a tree row, a virtual row in the tree or the enabled state of an agent toolbar button. The kernel stores that state, draws it on every frame and sends it to every attached client. A plugin changes the state only when its meaning changes.

Views work differently. A panel, a pane body or a popup is a widget tree that the plugin returns from `views.render`. The kernel calls that export when the view first opens, after `ui.invalidate` and on resize. It never calls it per frame. This page covers the three kinds of retained output, the intents and calls that set them, how long each one lives and what happens when a plugin fails.

## You will need

- The grants `tree.decorate` (decorations and virtual rows) and `agent.control` (toolbar state). Reading agent activity, as the examples do, needs `agent.read`.
- Declarations in the manifest `contributes` block: `decoration_slots` for each slot, `virtual_rows` for each row kind, `toolbar_buttons` for each button and `commands` for each command a row invokes. The kernel rejects an undeclared slot or row kind.
- The Rust SDK (`ilium_plugin_sdk`) or the TypeScript SDK (`@ilium/plugin-sdk`). The examples run on the server side.
- A working knowledge of [events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) and [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/). Each intent completes exactly once, with one outcome.

## What is retained

| Output | Set by | Cleared or replaced by | Grant | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Decoration | `set-decoration` intent | `clear-decoration` intent, removal of the node, disable | `tree.decorate` | A declared slot on a tree row |
| Virtual rows | `set-virtual-rows` intent | Another `set-virtual-rows` call with the same row kind; an empty `rows` list | `tree.decorate` | Rows under the project or session, named by `virtual_rows` |
| Toolbar state | `set-toolbar-state` function of the agent primitive | Another call; a plugin restart resets it to the manifest state | `agent.control` | The toolbar of an agent pane |

Views are not retained. A plugin that changes a view calls `ui.invalidate` and the kernel asks it for a new tree on its next render.

## Surface

### Intents

| Intent | Fields | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `set-decoration` | `node: node-id`, `slot: string`, `content: styled-text`, `icon: option<string>`, `sort-key: option<s64>`, `persist: bool` | `ok` |
| `clear-decoration` | `node: node-id`, `slot: string` | `ok`, also on an empty slot |
| `set-virtual-rows` | `row-kind: string`, `rows: list<virtual-row>` | `ok` |

A `virtual-row` has `id: string`, `label: string` (plain text), `icon: option<string>` and `command: option<string>`. The `command` is the global id `<plugin-id>/<id>` of a command the plugin declares. An `icon` is a Tabler icon name, not a file path. An unknown name draws no icon.

`content` is a `styled-text`: a list of `span` records. Each span has `text` and a `style` with `fg`, `bg`, `add` and `remove`. Colours can be theme roles (`foreground`, `muted`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `selection`, `border`), so a decoration follows the theme.

In Rust the payloads are `SetDecorationSpec`, `DecorationKey` and `SetVirtualRowsSpec` (with `VirtualRow`) in `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents`. In TypeScript the same objects use camelCase fields, such as `sortKey` and `rowKind`.

### Extended decoration

`set-decoration` has optional fields: `spans` (rich text), `tooltip` (`{ lines, delay-ms }`), `frames` (2 to 16 frames) with `frame-ms` (at least 90), `trailing` and `visibility` (`always` or `on-hover`). A decoration with `frames` animates in the host with no plugin call. `set-virtual-rows` rows gain `parent`, `expandable`, `accepts-drop`, `tooltip`, `label` and `trailing`. The intents `set-expanded`, `set-bookmarked` and `set-inferred-icon` change retained node state in the same way. [Tutorial 1](/pages/tutorial-01-agent-badge/) shows the record in Rust and TypeScript.

### Calls

| Call | Rust | TypeScript | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Set the state of a toolbar button | `primitives::agent::set_toolbar_state(button, pane, enabled, label)` | `setToolbarState(button, pane, enabled, label)` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent` | `Result<(), PluginError>` |

`button` is the local id from `toolbar_buttons`. `pane` is `None` (or `none`) for every agent pane that shows the button, or a node id for one pane. `label` is `None` (or `none`) to keep the current label.

### Placements

| Placement | Position on the row | Size limit |
|---|---|---|
| `icon` | Before the title | 2 cells |
| `badge` | Right of the title | 12 cells |
| `subtitle` | Under the title | Width of the row |
| `footer` | Bottom line of the row | Width of the row |

Text wider than the limit is cut and ends with `…`. Widths use the host's display-width rules, so a wide glyph counts as two cells. The `priority` in the manifest orders slots of one placement; a lower number is drawn first. Give each kind of information its own slot, so that two badges do not replace each other.

## Setting a decoration in Rust

The manifest declares the slot and the capability:

```json
{
  "capabilities": { "server": ["agent.read", "tree.decorate"] },
  "contributes": {
    "decoration_slots": [{ "id": "review-count", "placement": "badge", "priority": 10 }]
  }
}
```

The plugin shows a badge while an agent works and clears it when the agent leaves that state:

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{DecorationKey, SetDecorationSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

const SLOT: &str = "review-count";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ReviewBadge;

impl Lifecycle for ReviewBadge {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let message = format!("review badge active in {}", context.plugin);
        log::log(Level::Info, &message);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for ReviewBadge {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            let intent = if change.current == AgentActivity::Working {
                Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
                    node: change.node,
                    slot: SLOT.into(),
                    content: vec![Span::plain("reviewing")],
                    icon: Some("checks".into()),
                    sort_key: None,
                    persist: false,
                })
            } else {
                Intent::ClearDecoration(DecorationKey { node: change.node, slot: SLOT.into() })
            };
            submissions.push(Submission::new(intent));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

`Submission::new` takes the next correlation number and no dedup key. `Submission::keyed(intent, key)` adds a key. The handler sends one submission per event, and the kernel checks the batch as a whole.

## Virtual rows in TypeScript

The manifest declares the row kind and the command that the row invokes:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "virtual_rows": [{ "id": "review-queue", "title": "Reviews", "icon": "checks", "parent": "project" }],
    "commands": [{ "id": "open-review", "title": "Open review" }]
  }
}
```

The plugin keeps the finished panes in memory and sends the whole list each time it changes. Each `set-virtual-rows` call replaces every row of that kind:

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const ROW_KIND = 'review-queue';
const OPEN_REVIEW = 'com.example.review-tools/open-review';
const finishedPanes = new Map<bigint, string>();
let nextCorrelation = 1n;

function rowsSubmission(): Submission {
  const rows = [...finishedPanes].map(([node, label]) => ({
    id: String(node), label, icon: 'checks', command: OPEN_REVIEW,
  }));
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'set-virtual-rows', val: { rowKind: ROW_KIND, rows } },
    correlation: nextCorrelation++,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    log('info', `review queue active for ${context.plugin}`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    let changed = false;
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'agent-activity-changed') {
        const { node, current } = event.val;
        if (current === 'done') finishedPanes.set(node, `Review ready in pane ${node}`);
        else finishedPanes.delete(node);
        changed = true;
      } else if (event.tag === 'node-removed' && finishedPanes.delete(event.val)) {
        changed = true;
      }
    }
    return changed ? [rowsSubmission()] : [];
  },
});
```

The `node-removed` branch matters. Without it the row would keep pointing at a pane that no longer exists.

## Toolbar state

Toolbar state is a direct call, not an intent. The SDK returns its result at once, because the function has no request id. This sketch disables a button named `review` on one pane while that pane has no review to run:

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent;

fn set_review_button(pane: u64, has_review: bool) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    agent::set_toolbar_state("review", Some(pane), has_review, Some("Review now".into()))
}
```

The state lasts until the plugin changes it. A label over 32 cells is refused.

## Edge cases and errors

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `set-decoration` or `clear-decoration` on a node that does not exist | `refused(not-found)` |
| Slot not declared in `decoration_slots` | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| More than 4,096 decorations for one plugin at the default limit | `refused(quota-exceeded)` |
| `set-virtual-rows` with a row kind not declared in `virtual_rows` | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `clear-decoration` on an empty slot | `ok` |
| `set-decoration` on a slot that already holds a decoration | Replaces it; the slot never holds two |
| Toolbar call for a button that is not the plugin's own, or for a missing pane | `not-found` |
| Toolbar label over 32 cells | `invalid-argument` |
| A malformed submission in a batch | The whole batch is refused, so nothing is half-applied |
| Repeat of a submission with the same `dedup-key` within 10 minutes | `duplicate(original)`, with no effect |
| Node removed | Its decorations and its rows are removed with it |

Wide content is cut, as described under placements. Limits apply per plugin, and the host limit for all plugins together is 65,536 decorations.

## Lifetime and failure

- `persist: true` stores the decoration in the snapshot. After a server restart it is shown in the muted colour, and it stays that way until the plugin sets or clears it after its activation.
- `persist: false` decorations are dropped at server shutdown.
- A trap, a deadline breach or a crash keeps the plugin's decorations, marked stale in the muted colour. The plugin's virtual rows are withdrawn until it sets them again. The toolbar state returns to the manifest state on restart.
- Disable and uninstall remove all of the plugin's retained state.
- A revoked `tree.decorate` or `agent.control` grant withdraws the matching output.

A plugin that fails three times in 10 minutes is disabled, and the tree footer shows a notice. See [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).

## Rules for retained state

- Set a decoration when its meaning changes, not on every event. A repeated intent costs one submission each time and changes nothing on screen.
- Keep slot ids, row kinds and row ids stable across plugin versions. The kernel stores them as strings in the snapshot.
- Give an intent a `dedup-key` when a repeat would be harmful, for example a notice that must not appear twice.
- Send the complete row list on every `set-virtual-rows` call. The call replaces the rows of its kind; it does not add to them.

- [Capability: tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/)

# Services

## Services

A service is a named interface that one plugin provides and other plugins call. The caller sends a method name and a JSON payload. The provider answers with a JSON reply, at once or later. The plugins never link to each other. The kernel checks both grants and the payload, and it routes the call to the provider the user has enabled. A consumer can also declare that it needs a provider, so the kernel starts that provider first.

Version 0.1 has two kinds of service. Kernel-known interfaces, such as `ilium:inference/provider`, have typed WIT signatures. Plugin-defined services use the generic `services.call` form, which is unstable in 0.1. The call-side reference is [services API](/pages/api-services/).

## What you need

- **Grants.** A caller needs `services.use:<name>`. A provider needs `services.provide:<name>`. The inference provider needs `inference.provide` instead.
- **Manifest.** The provider lists `service-provider` in `exports` and its services in `contributes.services.provides`. The caller lists the services it needs in `requires.services`. Both plugins set `"unstable": ["plugin-services"]`, which is accepted only in dev mode for T2 and T3 plugins (see [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/)).
- **SDK.** The [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) provides `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services`. The [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/) provides `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services`.

## Names, versions and grants

| Item | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel-known service | `ilium:<package>/<interface>` | `ilium:inference/provider` |
| Plugin-defined service | `<plugin-id>/<name>`; `<name>` is 1 to 64 characters from `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` | `com.example.titles/suggest` |
| Caller grant | `services.use:<name>` | `services.use:com.example.titles/suggest` |
| Provider grant | `services.provide:<name>` | `services.provide:com.example.titles/suggest` |
| Provider manifest entry | object with `name`, `version`, `schema` | see below |
| Caller manifest entry | string with a version, in `requires.services` | `com.example.titles/suggest@0.1.0` |

A grant carries the bare name, with no version and no wildcard. The first colon in a grant separates the grant from its argument, so `services.use:ilium:inference/provider` names `ilium:inference/provider`. A version appears only in `requires` and `provides`, always written `@0.1.0`.

## The registry

The kernel keeps one service registry, keyed by name. A provider enters it when it is installed, enabled and granted `services.provide`. A name has one provider. If a second enabled plugin declares a registered name, the registry keeps the first and never calls the second.
