# The UI model

## The UI model

A plugin describes its interface as a flat list of widgets. The kernel lays the list out, draws it with the Ilium theme, keeps the state of each widget and reports what the user did. The plugin never draws, and it never stores a scroll position, a selection, a hover state or a focus. Each render call returns a fresh description, and the host merges it with the state it holds under each widget key.

This page covers the render function, the flat tree and its flags, the fields a node can carry (tooltip, tab index and disabled reason), host-owned state, the 17 action kinds and 12 value cases, the pointer model, hover and tooltips, popups and their anchors, focus order, drag and drop, the widened widget set of settings views and the theme extras. Every code example is given in Rust and in TypeScript.

## What you need

- A client-side component. The `views` export exists only on the client side.
- The `ui.panels` grant, or `panes.provide-kind` for pane views. See [UI panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/).
- The `views` export in the manifest. Every component also has a `handler` export.
- Rust: the `ilium-plugin-sdk` crate. TypeScript: `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.

Read [Retained mode](/pages/retained-mode/) and [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/) before you build a view.

## The render function

| Language | Signature |
|---|---|
| WIT | `render: func(view: view-target, area: area) -> ui-tree;` |
| Rust | `fn render(&mut self, view: ViewTarget, area: Area) -> UiTree` |
| TypeScript | `render(view: ViewTarget, area: Area): UiTree` inside `definePlugin` |

The kernel calls `render` when the view first opens, after `ui.invalidate` for that view, and when the view's area changes. It never runs on every frame. Every change of the view's area triggers one render with the new area, coalesced to at most one per 16 ms; until it returns, the host lays out the previous tree in the new area through the same constraint solver. `area` gives the `columns` and `rows` the view may use. The host clips every widget to that area. [Layout constraints](/pages/layout/) shows how a plugin uses `area`.

### View targets

| Case | Payload | Where the view appears |
|---|---|---|
| `panel` | `string`, the panel id | A workspace panel |
| `pane` | `node-id` | The body of a pane whose kind the plugin provides |
| `popup` | `string`, the popup id | A popup opened with `open-popup` |
| `settings-page` | `string`, the page id | A Settings page |
| `onboarding-step` | `string`, the step id | A first-run onboarding step |

In Rust these are `ViewTarget::Panel(String)`, `ViewTarget::Pane(NodeId)`, `ViewTarget::Popup(String)`, `ViewTarget::SettingsPage(String)` and `ViewTarget::OnboardingStep(String)`. In TypeScript they are tagged objects such as `{ tag: 'panel', val: 'notes' }`.

## The ui-tree

WIT has no recursive types, so a tree is a flat list of nodes, and each node names its children by index.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/ui in reference-wit
record ui-node {
  key: option<string>, widget: widget, children: list<u32>, %flags: node-flags,
  tooltip: option<tooltip>,          // hover help
  tab-index: option<s16>,            // focus order
  disabled-reason: option<string>,   // at most 40 characters
}
flags node-flags { focusable, draggable, drop-target, hidden, hover-events, pointer-events }
record ui-tree { version: u32, nodes: list<ui-node>, root: u32 }
```

- `root` must be 0. The field stays for the shape of later versions and must equal 0. Every child index must be greater than its parent's index and less than `nodes.len()`. Every node except the root must appear exactly once, in exactly one `children` list. A nonzero root, an out-of-range index, an unreachable node, a node with two parents or a backward index traps the instance with `ui.invalid-tree`.
- Each `key` must be unique across the whole view, not only among siblings. A duplicate key anywhere in one `ui-tree` traps with `ui.duplicate-key`. The host matches nodes by key across the whole view, so a keyed node that moves to another parent keeps its host-owned state.
- The depth is at most 32, and the root is depth 1. A node at depth 33 traps with `ui.too-deep`.
- A `layout` needs one child per constraint, and a `ratio` with denominator 0 is invalid (`ui.invalid-tree`).
- `views.render` returns a `ui-tree`, not a `result`, so it cannot return `invalid-argument`. There is one outcome for every invalid tree: the host keeps the previous tree (marked stale), logs one error, and the instance traps with a `ui.*` code. The trap counts as one failure under the restart rule (see [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/)). The codes are `ui.invalid-tree` (structure, duplicate item ids, a prop out of range, more than 256 check-list items, more items than `max-items`, a bad validation regex), `ui.duplicate-key`, `ui.too-deep`, `ui.too-large` (more than 4,096 nodes or 1 MiB) and `ui.widget-not-allowed` (a `menu`, `list-editor` or other input widget in a settings page). A render over its deadline traps with `ui.render-timeout`.

The Rust and TypeScript builders fill `version`, the widget defaults and the child indices. A wrong layout stops the render before the tree leaves the plugin, and the message names the layout key.

| Limit | Default, every tier | T1 ceiling (requested in `limits`) |
|---|---|---|
| Nodes in one tree | 4,096 | 16,384 |
| Encoded size | 1 MiB | 4 MiB |

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `focusable` | The node can take keyboard focus. Widgets in [Inherently focusable widgets](#inherently-focusable-widgets) take it without the flag; every other widget, such as a `surface` that reports clicks, needs it. |
| `draggable` | The node can be dragged onto a `drop-target`. |
| `drop-target` | The node accepts a drop and receives one `dropped` action. |
| `hidden` | The node is not drawn. Its state is kept. |
| `hover-events` | The node sends `hover-enter` and `hover-leave`. |
| `pointer-events` | The node sends `pointer` actions. It also needs `focusable`. |

| Node field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tooltip` | `option<tooltip>` | Help shown after a delay on hover, or on focus with F1. It needs no flag. |
| `tab-index` | `option<s16>` | Focus order, see [Focus order](#focus-order). Values from 1 come first, in ascending order. None and 0 follow in tree order. A negative value is skipped by Tab. |
| `disabled-reason` | `option<string>` | The node is drawn muted and ignores input. It stays in the focus order. The reason, at most 40 characters, shows as its tooltip. |

**Rust**

```rust
let search = tree
    .text_input("Search")
    .key("search")
    .tab_index(1)
    .tooltip("Filters the list as you type")
    .hover_events(true);
let export = tree
    .button("Export")
    .key("export")
    .disabled_reason("No sessions selected");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const search = textInput('Search', {
  key: 'search',
  tabIndex: 1,
  tooltip: 'Filters the list as you type',
  flags: { hoverEvents: true },
});
const exportButton = button('Export', {
  key: 'export',
  disabledReason: 'No sessions selected',
});
```

## Widgets

Each node carries one `widget` variant. There are 51 widgets in seven families. The [widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/) lists all of them with their pages. The table lists what each family sends back; a blank cell means it sends nothing.

| Family | Widgets | Sends to the plugin | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layout and containers | `layout`, `block`, `clear`, `separator` | nothing | [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) |
| Layout and containers | `tabs` | `selected` with `index(u32)` | [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) |
| Layout and containers | `popup` | `closed` with `none` | [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) |
| Layout and containers | `split` | `resized` with `number(f64)` | [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) |
| Layout and containers | `dialog` | `activated` with `text(button id)`, `closed` | [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) |
| Layout and containers | `scroll-view`, `scrollbar` | `scrolled` with `index(u32)` | [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/) |
| Text | `paragraph` | `scrolled` when scrollable; `activated` for clickable spans | [Text](/pages/widgets-text/) |
| Text | `markdown` | `activated` with `text(target)` without `link-command` | [Text](/pages/widgets-text/) |
| Text | `leader-row`, `key-hints`, `diff-view` | nothing; `key-hints` runs its command on the host | [Text](/pages/widgets-text/) |
| Collections | `%list`, `table`, `tree-list`, `menu`, `check-list`, `list-editor` | `selected`, `activated`, `toggled`, `changed`, `context-requested`, `closed` | [Collections](/pages/widgets-collections/) |
| Data display | `gauge`, `line-gauge`, `sparkline`, `bar-chart`, `canvas`, `calendar`, `minimap` | nothing | [Data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/) |
| Data display | `chart`, `progress-row`, `meter` | `selected` (focusable chart), `activated` (progress row) | [Data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/) |
| Input | `button`, `toggle`, `choice`, `number`, `text-input`, `text-area`, `schema-form`, `key-capture`, `color-picker`, `path-field`, `location-picker` | `activated`, `changed`, `submitted`, `filter-changed` | [Input](/pages/widgets-input/) |
| Status and feedback | `badge`, `spinner`, `notice`, `icon` | nothing; `notice` may send `closed` | [Widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/) |
| Media and embedded | `surface`, `terminal-view`, `code-view` | `activated` with `cell`, `pointer`, `changed` | [Media and embedded](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) |
| Media and embedded | `image`, `video` | nothing | [Media and embedded](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) |

The [widget input map](/pages/reference-widget-input-map/) gives the exact focus behaviour, keys, mouse actions, events, colour roles and stable-glyph substitutes of every widget. The family pages repeat it for their widgets.

## Keys and host-owned state

The host keeps each widget's state under its key. A key must stay the same across renders. Without one, a widget loses its state on every render: a text cursor jumps to the start and a list drops its selection.

| Widget | Host-owned state | `widget-state` case |
|---|---|---|
| `%list`, `table` | selected row, scroll offset | `selected(option<u32>)`, `offset(u32)` |
| `%list`, `table`, `tree-list` | multi-selection | `ids(list<string>)` |
| `tree-list` | selected item | read as `ids(list<string>)` with one id; set with `ids([id])` |
| `choice` | selected option | `selected(option<u32>)`; a catalogue choice is set with `text(item id)` and `selected(n)` on it returns `invalid-argument` |
| `tabs` | active tab | `tab(u32)` |
| `text-input`, `text-area` | text and cursor | `text(string)` |
| `tree-list` | expanded items | `expanded(list<string>)` (read and set) |
| `toggle` | on or off | `checked(bool)` |
| `check-list`, tri-state `toggle` | the state of each item | `tri(list<tuple<string, tri-state>>)` |
| `location-picker` | the chosen point | `geo(option<geo-point>)` |
| `number` (also the slider) | the value | `number(f64)` |
| `split` | the divider position in per mille | `split(u16)` |

Read the state with `ui.widget-state(view, key)` when `render` needs it, and change it with `ui.set-widget-state(view, key, state)`. Setting state for an unknown key returns `not-found`. A state kind that does not fit the widget returns `invalid-argument`.

**Rust**

```rust
// Select the third row of a list and open the second tab.
ui::set_widget_state(view.clone(), "notes-list", WidgetState::Selected(Some(2)))?;
ui::set_widget_state(view, "views", WidgetState::Tab(1))?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
ui.setWidgetState(view, 'notes-list', { tag: 'selected', val: 2 });
ui.setWidgetState(view, 'views', { tag: 'tab', val: 1 });
```

## Actions back to the plugin

When the user acts on a widget, the kernel sends one `ui-action` event with the payload `UiAction { view, key, action-id, kind, value }`. In 0.1.0 `action-id` is always a copy of `key`; no widget has a separate action id prop. The `key` is the widget that sent it, and for a drop it is the drop target. A widget without a key sends nothing.

There are 17 kinds: `activated`, `changed`, `submitted`, `selected`, `toggled`, `scrolled`, `dropped`, `context-requested`, `closed`, `focus-gained`, `focus-lost`, `hover-enter`, `hover-leave`, `pointer`, `drag-over`, `resized` and `filter-changed`. The last six (`hover-enter`, `hover-leave`, `pointer`, `drag-over`, `resized`, `filter-changed`) report hover, pointer, drag, resize and filter changes. Every focusable widget also sends `focus-gained` and `focus-lost`.

| `action-value` case | Used by |
|---|---|
| `none` | `button` (`activated`), `popup`, `dialog`, `menu` and `key-capture` (`closed`), hover and focus kinds. The docs write `none` for the option case `none` of `value: option<action-value>` |
| `text(string)` | `text-input`, `text-area`, `markdown`, `tree-list` (item id), a catalogue `choice` (item id), `menu`, `dialog` (button id), `filter-changed` |
| `index(u32)` | `%list`, `table`, `tabs`, `choice`, `scrolled` of every scrolling widget (always the first visible row) |
| `number(f64)` | `number`, `split` (`resized`) |
| `flag(bool)` | `toggle` |
| `cell(cell-position)` | `surface` (column and row, relative to the surface) |
| `drop(drop-value)` | `drop-target` nodes (`dropped`) |
| `pointer(view-pointer)` | nodes with `pointer-events` |
| `drag-over(drag-over-value)` | `drop-target` nodes during a drag |
| `item-state(tuple<string, tri-state>)` | `check-list`, tri-state `toggle` (state read with the `tri` case) |
| `geo(geo-point)` | `location-picker` |
| `ids(list<string>)` | multi-selection in `%list`, `table`, `tree-list` |

The host coalesces `scrolled`, `pointer` and `drag-over`. The others are never dropped.

Typing never reaches the plugin key by key. A `text-input` sends `changed` after 600 ms. A `text-area` with `debounce-ms` unset waits 600 ms while its current text is at most 10,000 bytes (UTF-8) and 1,000 ms above that, re-evaluated at each keystroke; an explicit `debounce-ms` (0 to 2,000) always wins. 64 KiB stays only as the `text-input` `max-length` cap. A `text-input` with `submit-on-enter` sends `submitted` on Enter. A `toggle` and a `choice` send `changed` at once. `filter-changed` is debounced by 150 ms.

The handler changes its own state and calls `ui.invalidate` for the view. The next `render` reads the new state.

### Context requests

`context-requested` is sent for a right click on any node that has a key, and for Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the focused node. The node does not need `pointer-events`. A mouse trigger carries `pointer` data with the cell relative to the node, button `right` and `clicks` 1. A keyboard trigger carries `pointer` data with column 0, row 0, button `none` and `clicks` 0. In a collection the item under the pointer (or the selected item, for the keyboard) is selected first, and the `selected` event is delivered before `context-requested` in the same batch.

## The pointer model

By default the host turns mouse input into the widget's own actions: a click on a button sends `activated`, a click on a tab sends `selected`. A plugin that draws its own surface can ask for raw pointer input. Set the `pointer-events` and `focusable` flags on the node. The node then sends `pointer` actions whose value is a `view-pointer`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `down`, `up`, `move`, `drag`, `wheel-up`, `wheel-down`, `wheel-left` or `wheel-right` |
| `button` | `none`, `left`, `middle` or `right` |
| `modifiers` | flags `shift`, `control`, `alt` |
| `column`, `row` | The cell inside the widget's area, 0-based |
| `sub-x`, `sub-y` | The position inside the cell, 0 to 255, from left and top to right and bottom. The value is 128 when the terminal reports cells only |
| `clicks` | 1, 2 or 3 for `down` events; 0 for the others |

`move` is sent only while a button is held, and the host coalesces it to the frame rate. A plain hover does not produce `move`; use `hover-events` for that.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 190" role="img" aria-label="A pointer position inside a cell: column, row and the sub-cell offset from 0 to 255">

  <desc>A grid of cells. The pointer is in column 3, row 1, at sub-x 192 and sub-y 64, that is three quarters from the left and a quarter from the top of the cell.</desc>

  </g>

**Rust**

```rust
// ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, PointerKind}
for event in batch {
    let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
    if action.key != "plot" || action.kind != ActionKind::Pointer {
        continue;
    }
    let ActionValue::Pointer(pointer) = action.value else { continue };
    if pointer.kind == PointerKind::Down && pointer.clicks == 2 {
        // Double click: zoom to the cell, using the sub-cell offset for half-cell accuracy.
        let x = f64::from(pointer.column) + f64::from(pointer.sub_x) / 255.0;
        let y = f64::from(pointer.row) + f64::from(pointer.sub_y) / 255.0;
        self.zoom_to(x, y);
        ui::invalidate(view.clone());
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
for (const event of batch) {
  if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
  const action = event.val;
  if (action.key !== 'plot' || action.kind !== 'pointer') continue;
  if (action.value.tag !== 'pointer') continue;
  const pointer = action.value.val;
  if (pointer.kind === 'down' && pointer.clicks === 2) {
    // Double click: zoom to the cell, using the sub-cell offset for half-cell accuracy.
    const x = pointer.column + pointer.subX / 255;
    const y = pointer.row + pointer.subY / 255;
    zoomTo(x, y);
    ui.invalidate(view);
  }
}
```

The node that draws the plot sets the flags: `focusable` and `pointer-events` (`flags: { focusable: true, pointerEvents: true }` in TypeScript, `.focusable(true).pointer_events(true)` in Rust).

## Hover and tooltips

Hover tracking belongs to the host. A node with `hover-events` sends `hover-enter` and `hover-leave`. Tooltips need no flag: any node with a `tooltip` field shows it.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 130" role="img" aria-label="Hover timeline: enter, 500 milliseconds to the tooltip, leave, 150 milliseconds grace">
  <title>The hover timeline</title>
  <desc>The pointer enters a node and hover-enter is sent. After 500 ms the tooltip appears. When the pointer leaves, hover-leave is sent and a popup with dismiss-on-leave closes after a 150 ms grace time.</desc>
  <defs>
    <marker id="hover-arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker>
  </defs>
  <line x1="20" y1="70" x2="400" y2="70" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#hover-arrow)"/>
  <circle cx="40" cy="70" r="4" fill="currentColor"/><text x="40" y="52" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">enter</text><text x="40" y="95" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">hover-enter</text>
  <circle cx="190" cy="70" r="4" fill="currentColor"/><text x="190" y="52" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">500 ms</text><text x="190" y="95" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">tooltip shows</text>
  <circle cx="290" cy="70" r="4" fill="currentColor"/><text x="290" y="52" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">leave</text><text x="290" y="95" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">hover-leave</text>
  <circle cx="365" cy="70" r="4" fill="currentColor"/><text x="365" y="52" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">150 ms</text><text x="365" y="95" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">popup closes</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The host owns the timing. A tooltip delay of 500 ms is the default and a plugin may choose 0 to 2000 ms. The 150 ms leave grace applies to a popup with dismiss-on-leave.</figcaption>
</figure>

A tooltip is text of at most 200 Unicode scalar values in total, given as `styled-lines`. Beyond that the host cuts it to 199 plus `…`. The box is a rounded border with an inner width of min(40, view width - 4) cells, word-wrapped, and at most 8 inner lines (the 8th line is cut with `…`). On hover its top-left corner sits one row below the pointer cell. For F1 it sits one row below the node's top-left cell. It flips above when it does not fit below, then shifts left to stay inside the view. The text uses the foreground role on the info background role. It shows after the tooltip delay (default 500 ms, 0 to 2,000 ms) and hides when the pointer leaves the node or on any key. Keyboard users get the same text with F1 while the node has focus. A disabled node shows its `disabled-reason` as the tooltip.

            ╭──────────────────────────────╮
            │ Writes the recommended       │
            │ threshold                    │
            ╰──────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered below the hovered span after 500 ms. A tooltip is a rounded block with one cell of horizontal padding, placed one row below the pointer cell, or above it when there is no room.</figcaption>
</figure>

    .button("Apply 180k")

**Rust**

```rust
match (action.kind, action.key.as_str()) {
    (ActionKind::HoverEnter, "session-row") => self.preview_open = true,
    (ActionKind::HoverLeave, "session-row") => self.preview_open = false,
    _ => {}
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
if (action.key === 'session-row') {
  if (action.kind === 'hover-enter') previewOpen = true;
  if (action.kind === 'hover-leave') previewOpen = false;
}
```

## Popups and anchors

A `popup` node is drawn only while `ui.open-popup` or `ui.open-popup-with` has it open. The popup id is the `key` of the popup or dialog node. Popup ids must be unique across all open views of one plugin instance. `open-popup` searches the last committed tree of each open view. It returns `not-found` when it finds no match and `invalid-argument` when it finds two. A view may have at most 4 popups open (`quota-exceeded` for a fifth). `close-popup` on an id that is not open is a no-op that returns `ok`, and a popup whose node disappears from the next tree closes and sends `closed`. Open popups form a stack: the topmost takes input first, Escape closes it and sends `closed`, and focus moves into an opened popup and returns to the anchor on close.

| Anchor | Placement |
|---|---|
| `centered((width, height))` | In the middle of the view. Its size overrides the spec width and height. |
| `at-cell((column, row))` | Top-left corner on that cell. |
| `below-key("key")` | Under the widget with that key. |
| `at-key({ key, side })` | Next to a widget, on the `below`, `above`, `right` or `left` side. |
| `at-tree-node(node)` | Next to a tree row. Used for toolbar popovers and row actions. |
| `at-pointer` | At the last pointer position. Used for context menus in own views. |

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `modal` | true | Input stays in the popup, and the view behind takes none. Options passed to `open-popup-with` override the spec fields `modal` and `close-on-escape`. |
| `pinnable` | false | Adds a pin glyph to the title. A pinned popup stays open until Escape or a click on the pin. |
| `dismiss-on-leave` | false | The popup closes when the pointer leaves both the popup and its anchor for longer than 150 ms. |
| `close-on-escape` | true | Escape closes the popup. |

Size and placement follow the rules in [Popup size and placement](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/#popup-size-and-placement).

**Rust**

```rust
// ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{PopupAnchor, PopupOptions, KeyAnchor, AnchorSide}; host::log::{self, Level}
let anchor = PopupAnchor::AtKey(KeyAnchor { key: "stats-button".into(), side: AnchorSide::Below });
let options = PopupOptions { modal: false, pinnable: true, dismiss_on_leave: true, close_on_escape: true };
if let Err(error) = ui::open_popup_with("session-stats", anchor, options) {
    log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("open_popup_with failed: {error:?}"));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
try {
  ui.openPopupWith(
    'session-stats',
    { tag: 'at-key', val: { key: 'stats-button', side: 'below' } },
    { modal: false, pinnable: true, dismissOnLeave: true, closeOnEscape: true },
  );
} catch (error) {
  log('warn', String(error));
}
```

## Focus

Left and Right, Up and Down and the other keys belong to the focused widget. Focus moves into an opened popup and returns to the anchor when it closes.

### Focus order

Tab order works as follows.

1. First come the focusable nodes with `tab-index` of 1 or more, in ascending value. Ties are broken by pre-order position.
2. Then come the nodes with `tab-index` none or 0, in pre-order.
3. Nodes with a negative `tab-index` take focus by click and by `set-focus` but are skipped by Tab and Shift+Tab.
4. Tab wraps from the last node to the first within the view, and Shift+Tab wraps the other way.
5. Hidden nodes are skipped. A disabled node (`disabled-reason` set) stays in the focus order but ignores input.

### Inherently focusable widgets

These widgets take focus without the `focusable` flag.

| Widget | Condition |
|---|---|
| `button`, `toggle`, `choice`, `number`, `text-input`, `text-area`, `key-capture`, `color-picker`, `path-field`, `location-picker` | always |
| `%list`, `table`, `tree-list`, `menu`, `check-list`, `list-editor`, `tabs`, `scroll-view` | always |
| `split` divider | `resizable` is true |
| `paragraph` | `scroll` is set |
| `markdown` | the text contains a link or a task item |
| `diff-view`, `code-view` | always |
| `terminal-view` | `interactive` is set |
| `schema-form` | one stop per row |

Every other widget is focusable only with `flags.focusable`.

### Escape

Escape is resolved in this order, and the first step that applies consumes it.

1. A focused `key-capture` that is capturing cancels the capture and sends `closed`.
2. A focused text widget with a non-empty selection clears the selection.
3. The topmost open popup or dialog in the view closes (`close-on-escape` true), sending `closed` or the cancel activation of a dialog.
4. A modal panel closes.
5. A non-modal panel or pane view returns focus to the session tree.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭────────────────╮  ╭────────────────╮  ╭────────────────╮
│<span class="t-hi"> Search  [1]    </span>│  │ Filter  [2]    │  │ List  [3]      │
╰────────────────╯  ╰────────────────╯  ╰────────────────╯
<span class="t-dim">Tab moves 1, 2, 3 and back. Shift+Tab goes the other way.</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Focus order with <code>tab-index</code> 1, 2 and 3. The focused widget is drawn in the highlight colours; the numbers are shown only to explain the order.</figcaption>
</figure>

The host draws focus on the widget: a focused frame is cyan and bold, a focused row uses the selection colours. The plugin hears `focus-gained` and `focus-lost`.

**Rust**

```rust
let search = tree.text_input("Search").key("search").tab_index(1);
let filter = tree.choice(["All", "Running", "Done"]).key("filter").tab_index(2);
let list = tree.list(items).key("list").tab_index(3);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const search = textInput('Search', { key: 'search', tabIndex: 1 });
const filter = choice(['All', 'Running', 'Done'], { key: 'filter', tabIndex: 2 });

```

## Drag and drop

A `draggable` node dropped on a `drop-target` node produces one `dropped` action. Its value is `drop(drop-value)` (a record with `source-key`, `target-key` and `index`), with `index` as the insertion position. The event `key` is the target key. The host does not move data; the plugin moves its own.

While a drag hovers a drop target, the host sends `drag-over` with `drag-over-value { source-key, target-key, index, accept }` once each time the target changes. The host decides the position from the pointer row inside the target's area, and `accept` carries the result: `before`, `after`, `inside` or `none`. For a `tree-item` with `expandable` set, the top third is `before`, the middle third is `inside` and the bottom third is `after`, with rows rounded down. For any other target, the top half is `before` and the bottom half is `after`. A target with `drop-target` unset accepts nothing. A drop sends `dropped` to the target key with the position in the `drop` value, and for a `tree-list` the source item id as `text`. The host draws the insertion line or the inside highlight, and scrolls the list when the pointer is near an edge.

## Settings views

A `settings-page` tree uses a subset of the widgets. The subset is: `block`, `paragraph`, `tabs`, `separator`, `leader-row`, `%list`, `table`, `button` and `schema-form`, and also `layout`, `split`, `scroll-view`, `markdown`, `key-hints`, `diff-view`, `tree-list`, `check-list`, `gauge`, `line-gauge`, `sparkline`, `bar-chart`, `chart`, `canvas`, `progress-row`, `meter`, `minimap`, `badge`, `spinner`, `notice`, `icon`, `image`, `surface`, `location-picker` and `code-view` with `read-only: true`.

These trap the instance in a settings page with `ui.widget-not-allowed`, and the host keeps the previous tree and logs one error: `popup`, `dialog`, `menu`, `video`, `terminal-view`, an editable `code-view`, and the input widgets other than `button`, `schema-form` and `location-picker`. Values are still edited through `schema-form`, and the host validates and saves them.

## Theme extras

`ui.theme-extras()` returns the motion, density and icon settings that a view should respect, next to the colours of `ui.theme()`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reduced-motion` | When true, a view should avoid animation. The host also stops its own spinners. |
| `density` | `compact`, `normal` or `comfortable`. Use it to choose margins and spacing. |
| `icon-mode` | `normal` or `stable`. Stable icons are used only when the user opted in. |
| `info`, `selection`, `border` | RGB colours for the roles that `theme-tokens` lacks. |

**Rust**

```rust
let extras = ui::theme_extras();
let margin = match extras.density {
    Density::Compact => 0,
    Density::Normal => 1,
    Density::Comfortable => 2,
};
let animate = !extras.reduced_motion;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const extras = ui.themeExtras();
const margin = { compact: 0, normal: 1, comfortable: 2 }[extras.density];
const animate = !extras.reducedMotion;
```

## Worked example in Rust: a filtered notes panel

This component renders a panel with a filter field and a list. It filters the rows when the filter text changes. The host keeps the text, the cursor and the selected row.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::{ListItem, Tree};

const PANEL: &str = "notes";
const FILTER_KEY: &str = "filter";
const LIST_KEY: &str = "notes-list";
const NOTES: [&str; 3] = ["Meeting notes", "Shopping list", "Release checklist"];

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesPanel {
    filter: String,
}

impl Handler for NotesPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if action.key != FILTER_KEY {
                continue;
            }
            if let (ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(text)) = (action.kind, action.value) {
                self.filter = text;
                ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Panel(PANEL.to_string()));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for NotesPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let needle = self.filter.to_lowercase();
        let items: Vec<ListItem> = NOTES
            .iter()
            .filter(|name| name.to_lowercase().contains(&needle))
            .map(|name| ListItem::plain(*name))
            .collect();

        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let filter = tree.text_input("Filter").key(FILTER_KEY).tab_index(1);
        let notes = tree.list(items).key(LIST_KEY).tab_index(2);
        let body = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Min(1)])
            .child(filter)
            .child(notes);
        let root = tree.block().title("Notes").child(body);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

The panel id `notes` must be declared in the manifest. The plugin keeps the filter text only because it needs that text to filter.

│ Filter                                     │
│<span class="t-hi">› Meeting notes                             </span>│
│  Shopping list                             │
│  Release checklist                         │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
<span class="t-dim">Enter opens a note. Esc closes the panel.</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>The notes panel before a filter is typed. The host selects the first row and draws the selected row in the selection colours.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Worked example in TypeScript: reordering rows

Each note is a draggable row. A drop moves the dragged row to the insertion index, and `drag-over` tells the host where the row would land.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import * as ui from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { block, layout, paragraph, span, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const PANEL = 'notes';
const ROW_PREFIX = 'row:';
let order = ['Meeting notes', 'Shopping list', 'Release checklist'];

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  deactivate() { return undefined; },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
      const action = event.val;
      if (action.kind !== 'dropped' || action.value.tag !== 'drop') continue;
      const { sourceKey, index } = action.value.val;
      const moved = sourceKey.slice(ROW_PREFIX.length);
      order = order.filter((name) => name !== moved);
      order.splice(index, 0, moved);
      ui.invalidate({ tag: 'panel', val: PANEL });
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    const rows = order.map((name) =>
      paragraph([[span(name)]], {
        key: ROW_PREFIX + name,
        flags: { draggable: true, dropTarget: true },
      }),
    );
    const body = layout(
      { direction: 'vertical', constraints: rows.map(() => ({ tag: 'length', val: 1 })) },
      rows,
    );
    return tree(block({ titles: [{ text: 'Notes', position: 'top', alignment: 'left' }] }, [body]));
  },
});
```

The row keys carry the note name, so the drop handler reads the source from `sourceKey` without a lookup.

The same example in Rust marks the row as `draggable` and `drop_target`:

**Rust**

```rust
let row = tree
    .paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain(name)]])
    .key(format!("row:{name}"))
    .draggable(true)
    .drop_target(true);
```

## Cell width

The host measures every plugin string in cells, and plugins never pass widths. The width is the sum, over extended grapheme clusters (UAX #29, Unicode 15.1), of these values.

- 2 when the base of the cluster has East Asian Width W or F, when the cluster contains U+FE0F, or when it is an emoji ZWJ sequence.
- 0 for a cluster made only of controls, ZWJ or default-ignorable code points.
- 1 otherwise. This includes East Asian Ambiguous characters.

Nerd Font private-use glyphs count as 1. Text that overflows a cell boundary at the right edge is replaced by spaces, never by half of a wide glyph. `ui.display-width` returns this value.

## Text sanitising

Before layout, the host removes the following from every plugin string. It applies to labels, spans, titles, tooltips and items alike.

1. The complete ECMA-48 sequences: `ESC [` up to its final byte, `ESC ]`, `ESC P`, `ESC X`, `ESC ^` and `ESC _` up to a terminating BEL or `ESC \` (or the end of the string), and two-byte `ESC Fe` sequences.
2. The remaining C0 controls except TAB and LF, DEL, and the C1 controls U+0080 to U+009F.

TAB expands to spaces up to the next multiple of 4 cells. LF splits lines in multi-line widgets. In single-line fields (labels, titles, items and the first line of a tooltip) CR, LF and CRLF each become one space. Each view logs at most one warn line per render with the code `ui.text-sanitized`. [RND-019]

## Host functions

These live in `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui` (Rust) and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui` (TypeScript).

| Function | Signature (WIT) | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `invalidate` | `(view: view-target)` | none; a view the plugin does not declare is ignored with one warn line |
| `open-panel` | `(panel: string) -> result` | `not-found` (panel not declared) |
| `close-panel` | `(panel: string)` | none |
| `open-popup` | `(popup: string, anchor: popup-anchor) -> result` | `not-found` (no such `popup` in the last committed tree of any open view), `invalid-argument` (two matches), `quota-exceeded` |
| `open-popup-with` | `(popup: string, anchor: popup-anchor, options: popup-options) -> result` | as `open-popup` |
| `close-popup` | `(popup: string)` | none; an id that is not open is a no-op |
| `widget-state` | `(view, key: string) -> option<widget-state>` | none; `none` for an unknown key |
| `set-widget-state` | `(view, key, state) -> result` | `not-found`, `invalid-argument` |
| `display-width` | `(text: string) -> u16` | none |
| `theme` | `() -> theme-tokens` | none |
| `theme-extras` | `() -> theme-extras` | none |
| `write-surface` | `(view, key, first-row: u32, format, data: list<u8>) -> result` | `not-found`, `invalid-argument` (format mismatch, partial row, over 16 MiB) |

## Edge cases and errors

- **Escape** is reserved by the host and follows the order in [Escape](#escape). A modal popup cannot refuse the close, and the plugin receives `closed`.
- **Popups** draw only while an `open-popup` call has them open. A fifth open popup in one view fails with `quota-exceeded`.
- **Traps.** A duplicate key, a bad child index, a broken layout, a tree over a limit or a widget outside the allowed subset traps the instance with a `ui.*` code (see [The ui-tree](#the-ui-tree)).
- **Permissions.** A `code-view` on a buffer the plugin did not create needs `editor.read`. A `terminal-view` needs `terminal.read-screen`. Without the grant the widget draws an empty frame with the text `not permitted`.
- **Pointer without focusable.** A node with `pointer-events` but not `focusable` sends no pointer actions.
- **Render-time caps.** `views.render` has no result type, so a widget outside the allowed subset, or a `check-list` or `list-editor` over its item cap, cannot return `invalid-argument`. The host traps the instance (one failure under the restart rule) with `ui.invalid-tree` or `ui.widget-not-allowed` and logs the widget key [WID-014].
- **Tooltip length.** A tooltip is limited to 200 Unicode scalar values. A longer text is cut at 199 characters and ends with `…`; it is not an error.
- **Settings views.** A widget outside the allowed subset traps with `ui.widget-not-allowed`.

## What the user sees

The user sees the widgets drawn by the host. The plugin sees the filtered list only after the debounce, when the host asks for a new render. The two panels above show the notes panel before and after a filter is typed. ## Common mistakes

- **Colour as the only signal.** Add a word or glyph to every status. See [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/). A view MUST show state in text as well as in colour. [AUT-507]
- **Missing keys on interactive widgets.** State is lost on every render, and actions cannot be matched.
- **Expecting a per-key event.** A text input sends `changed` after the debounce, not once per key press.
- **Forgetting `ui.invalidate`.** The host does not render again after a state change. Call `invalidate` for every view whose content changed.
- **Pointer events without focus.** Set both `pointer-events` and `focusable`.
- **Storing hover state in the tree.** Hover belongs to the host. Keep only what the plugin needs to react to.

Requirement ids for this page: [WID-002], [WID-003], [WID-017], [WID-018], [WID-019], [WID-008], [WID-009], [WID-010], [WID-011], [WID-012], [WID-013], [WID-014], [WID-015], [WID-016]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

# Versioning

## Versioning

The plugin contract has a version. The host and each plugin declare the version they use, and the host decides at install whether it can load a package. This page explains the version identity of a package, the markers on each item of the contract, the unstable features a plugin must opt into, the frozen snapshots the host keeps, the window of versions it loads, and the rule that governs changes after version 0.1.0.

## You will need

- A package whose `api` value matches the SDK it was built with, for example `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
- [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/) for the manifest layout and the install checks.
- For an unstable feature, either a T2 or T3 package installed in development mode with `ilium plugin dev`, or a T1 bundled plugin.

## The version identity

The `api` key in the manifest names the contract version. Each component also carries an `ilium:api-version` custom section with the same version as three big-endian `u16` values: major, minor and patch. The host compares the two at install. They must match exactly, patch number included. A mismatch fails with `manifest.api-version` before any code loads.

```json
{
  "id": "com.example.notes-caller",
  "name": "Notes caller",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Corp",
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "unstable": ["plugin-services"],
  "requires": { "services": ["com.example.titles/suggest@0.1.0"] }
}
```

The example shows only the keys that this page discusses. A real manifest also carries the keys described in [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/).

The `version` key is the version of the plugin itself. The `api` key is the version of the contract the plugin was built for. The two are independent: a plugin at version 0.3.0 may target `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

## The markers on each item

Every item in the contract carries one of two markers:

| Marker | Meaning | Who can use it |
|---|---|---|
| `@since(version = 0.1.0)` | The item first appears in that version and keeps its shape in later minor versions. | Every plugin built for that version or later. |
| `@unstable(feature = <name>)` | The item may change or disappear inside 0.x. | Only plugins whose `unstable` key lists `<name>`. |

Version 0.1.0 has four unstable features. The manifest `unstable` key accepts only these names:

| Feature name | What it opens | Why it is unstable |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-calendar` | The `calendar` widget, which mirrors the monthly calendar of ratatui. | No first-party plugin needed it for 0.1, so its shape is still open. |
| `plugin-services` | Plugin-defined services: `services.call`, and the `services.use` and `services.provide` grants for names such as `com.example.titles/suggest`. | The payload contract between two plugins is new. |
| `gpu-kernels` | The `gpu.kernels` grant and the `gpu.run` function. See [More unstable features](#more-unstable-features). | The kernel interface depends on graphics hardware that varies. |
| `websocket` | WebSocket connections. See [More unstable features](#more-unstable-features). | The streaming contract may change. |

The `chart` widget is stable in 0.1.0. Kernel-known typed services, such as `ilium:inference/provider`, are stable too.

## Frozen snapshots and the window

Each released minor version is kept as a frozen snapshot of the contract, in a folder named after it, for example `wit/since_v0_1/`. The host loads the current minor version and the previous one through small adapters written by hand. A plugin built for the previous minor keeps working until the window moves past it. Version 0.1.0 is the first release, so it has no previous minor, and a host at 0.1.0 loads only `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

The window is the current minor version and the previous one, counted by minor number. A package whose `api` falls outside the window is refused at install with `package.api-unsupported`. The message names both ends of the window:

<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin install demo-plugin-0.3.0.iliumpkg
<span class="t-err">error</span> package.api-unsupported
<span class="t-dim">      Plugin demo-plugin 0.3.0 needs a plugin API</span>
<span class="t-dim">      that this Ilium does not support.</span>
<span class="t-dim">      This Ilium supports</span>
<span class="t-dim">      ilium:plugin@0.1.0.</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. A host with a previous minor version names both versions it supports.

<div class="note">
<p>The window is a rule about minor numbers only. The exact match between the `api` value and the `ilium:api-version` section still applies inside the window.</p>
</div>

## Unstable opt-in checks

The install checks for the `unstable` key run before any code loads:

| Code | When it fails | What the message says |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.unstable-unknown` | A name in `unstable` is not an unstable feature of this host. | The name and the plugin API. |
| `manifest.unstable-tier` | A T2 or T3 package lists a feature outside development mode. | That the feature needs `ilium plugin dev`. |
| `manifest.unstable-missing` | The component imports an unstable item, but its manifest does not list the feature. | The feature name and the item that uses it. |

Development mode is the only way to install a T2 or T3 package that uses an unstable feature. Such a package is shown with a `dev` badge. A T1 bundled plugin may list unstable features in any build.

<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin install notes-caller-0.1.0.iliumpkg
<span class="t-err">error</span> manifest.unstable-tier
<span class="t-dim">      notes-caller 0.1.0 lists plugin-services,</span>
<span class="t-dim">      which is unstable.</span>
<span class="t-dim">      Unstable features need development mode:</span>
<span class="t-dim">      ilium plugin dev.</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The same package installs in development mode with `ilium plugin dev`.

When a later version removes or renames an unstable feature, a package that still lists the old name fails with `manifest.unstable-unknown` after the upgrade. Read the changelog before you upgrade Ilium with a plugin that uses an unstable feature.

## Worked example: a caller of an unstable service

The manifest above lists `plugin-services` and requires `com.example.titles/suggest@0.1.0`. The code below makes one call. It needs the `services.use:com.example.titles/suggest` grant on the caller side.

Rust, in a crate that depends on `ilium-plugin-sdk = "0.1"`:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::services;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::PluginError;

/// Asks the titles provider for a title. Unstable in 0.1: `plugin-services` must be listed.
pub async fn suggest_title(note: &str) -> Result<String, PluginError> {
    // Escape the note with a JSON library before you format it in a real plugin.
    let payload = format!(r#"{{"text":"{note}"}}"#);
    services::call("com.example.titles/suggest", "suggest", &payload).await
}
```

TypeScript, in a package that depends on `@ilium/plugin-sdk` at its pinned version:

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { call } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/services';

/** Asks the titles provider for a title. Unstable in 0.1: `plugin-services` must be listed. */
export async function suggestTitle(note: string): Promise<string> {
  const payloadJson = JSON.stringify({ text: note });
  return call('com.example.titles/suggest', 'suggest', payloadJson);
}
```

Both functions return the reply string. If the provider is missing, the call fails with `not-found`, as it does for any service call.

## What the contract contains

The contract is one unit, `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, and its items fall into three kinds.

| Kind | What it contains | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| New | Interfaces, functions, export fragments, and cases appended at the end of variants and enums | the host interfaces `catalogs`, `geocode`, `sessions`, `kernel-settings`, `keymap`, `client-requests` and `extensions`, the exports `catalog-provider`, `menu-provider`, `virtual-rows-provider` and `token-provider`, 18 events, 23 intents, 23 grants |
| Manifest | Keys and fields on manifest entries | nine `contributes` keys, `limits_tier`, six settings row types, 13 `manifest.*` codes |
| Shape | Fields of records, fixed by the first freeze | See [ABI evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/#2-what-may-change). After the freeze a record never gains a field |

The widget catalogue has 51 widgets in seven families, there are 18 settings row types, 17 ui-action kinds and 12 action-value cases, and the outcome case `ok-epoch(u64)` is part of the outcome variant. A plugin that matches only `ok` still works, because `is_ok()` in Rust and `isOk()` in TypeScript cover both.

The render shows how plugins look in the install check.

<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Install check─────────────────────────────╮
│ old-titler 1.2.0 ……… api ilium:plugin@0.1.0  ✓   │
│ future-x 1.0.0 …… api ilium:plugin@0.3.0  ✕      │
│   built for a newer minor than this host (0.1.0) │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

The first loads. The second is refused with `package.api-unsupported`, naming both versions. Illustrative, not generated.

### Which `api` string a plugin declares

The manifest key `api` must equal the version in the component's `ilium:api-version` section. A plugin declares `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` in both places. A plugin built for a newer minor than the host is refused. The SDKs write the version into the component for you.

The package manifest carries the string in the `api` key, shown here for both SDKs because the manifest is JSON:

```json
{ "id": "com.example.guard", "version": "0.4.0", "publisher": "Example Labs", "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0" }
```

Each SDK project file takes the contract version from the SDK dependency: `ilium-plugin-sdk = "0.1"` in Rust and `@ilium/plugin-sdk` at its pinned version in TypeScript.

### More unstable features

Two of the four unstable features (see [ABI evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/#3-markers-and-unstable-features) for the one list) are described in this section: `gpu-kernels` (the `gpu.kernels` grant and the `gpu.run` function) and `websocket`. They are visible only to a plugin that opts in, and T2 and T3 plugins need developer mode for them. They may change in any release.

The manifest lists the opt-in, so the line is the same for Rust and TypeScript plugins:

```json
"unstable": ["gpu-kernels"]
```

## Stable public names

Some names are part of a plugin's public surface, and they keep their spelling across plugin versions. These are:

- pane kind ids,
- command ids,
- settings keys,
- decoration slots, and
- topic names.

The kernel stores them as strings in the snapshot of each user. A rename breaks the saved state of that user, so treat each name as permanent once a release has used it. To change a name, add the new name, keep the old one working and document both. Removing the old name is a change that is not allowed after version 0.1.0.

## The rule after version 0.1.0

Moving the editor and the boards into plugins after the first freeze may only add items marked `@since`. Shape items change the record layout, so they belong to the first freeze, and every later release only adds. Nothing that version 0.1.0 exports is removed or changed. The editor interface, the basic interface, the cases of the widget variant, and the events and intents keep their shape. New widget cases are appended at the end of the variant. See [Pane primitives](/pages/primitives/).

A later addition looks like this. Suppose a future minor adds a grant marked `@since(version = 0.4.0)`. A package built for `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` that names that grant fails at install with `manifest.grant-unknown`, because the grant is not known to its API.

## Versions of extension points

The contract version `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` is one thing. Each extension point has its own `version`, the semver of its payload, reply or entry schema. A contributor may write `"point": "<plugin-id>/<id>@<minimum-version>"`. The point satisfies it when the major version is the same and the minor version is at least as high. An owner that changes a schema incompatibly raises the major version, and contributions that name the old major version become dormant. See [extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/).

## Practical advice

- Set the manifest `api` value to the version your SDK was built for, and rebuild the package whenever you update the SDK.
- Use unstable features only in development. A feature may change or disappear inside 0.x.
- Do not rename a pane kind, command, setting or topic in a later release. Add the new name and leave the old one working.
- Expect a refusal for a package whose `api` is outside the window. Rebuild it with an SDK for a version the host supports.
- Read [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) before you rename anything, change a data layout or raise a version. The plugin MUST keep every name of the stable public list across its own releases. [AUT-214]

## See also

- [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) for the author side of versions
- [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/)
- [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/)

- [Widgets: data display](/pages/widgets-data-display/)

# Worlds and sides

## Worlds and sides

A plugin package holds up to three components, one for each side of Ilium: `server`, `client` and `scene`. The server component runs in one host for each session server. The client component runs in one host for each attached client, so two attached clients mean two instances with separate state. The scene component runs the background animation of one client.

Each component targets a world. The world decides which host imports the component may call and which exports it must provide. The host checks both when it installs the package, and it refuses a package that breaks either rule.

The two halves of a package exchange messages. They never share memory, and each side has its own instance, its own memory and its own limits.

## You will need

- **Grants.** Each side declares the capabilities it needs in the manifest `capabilities` object, with one list per side. The host records the grants per plugin, per side and per user configuration. See [Capabilities and grants](/pages/capabilities/).
- **A toolchain.** Rust stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, or Bun 1.2 or later for TypeScript. The SDK pins the remaining tools, and `bun install` installs them inside the plugin folder. Nothing is installed globally.
- **The SDK.** The crate `ilium-plugin-sdk` for Rust, or the npm package `@ilium/plugin-sdk` for TypeScript.
- **Background reading.** [Architecture](/pages/architecture/) explains the kernel, and [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/) explains the package layout.

## The three worlds

| Side | Manifest key | World | Required exports | Optional exports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Server | `server` | `ilium:server/base@0.1.0` | `lifecycle`, `handler` | `detector`, `job-runner`, `service-provider`, `inference-provider` |
| Client | `client` | `ilium:client/base@0.1.0` | `lifecycle`, `handler` | `views`, `annotator`, `job-runner`, `service-provider`, `inference-provider` |
| Scene | `scene` | `ilium:anim/base@0.1.0` | `lifecycle`, `renderer` | `job-runner` |

The server world runs once per session server and has the widest set of imports. The client world reaches almost the same list, except the CLI, the HTTP API, workspaces and sessions, and it adds the UI, keys, clipboard, help, plugins, keymap and the editor and basic primitives. The scene world is the smallest. It draws through its own surface, and it has no intents, topics or messages.

The table below is generated from section 9 of [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/#9-worlds). It shows which world may call each import. Interfaces of `ilium:host` and `ilium:primitives` are named without the package; the two scene-only interfaces are in `ilium:anim`. "Yes" means the world imports it; "no" means the host rejects a component that uses it.

| Imports | Server | Client | Scene |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log`, `clock`, `storage`, `codec`, `fs`, `http`, `jobs`, `geocode` | yes | yes | yes |
| `timers`, `journal`, `tree`, `panes`, `intents-host`, `settings`, `process`, `inference`, `vector`, `sounds`, `topics`, `commands`, `services`, `catalogs`, `kernel-settings`, `client-requests`, `extensions`, `terminal`, `agent` | yes | yes | no |
| `cli`, `http-api`, `workspace`, `sessions` | yes | no | no |
| `audio`, `media`, `location`, `gpu` | no | yes | yes |
| `ui-host`, `keys`, `clipboard`, `help`, `plugins`, `keymap`, `editor`, `basic` | no | yes | no |
| `anim/surface`, `anim/fonts` | no | no | yes |

The `ilium:host/messages` interface no longer exists. Sending a message is the `message` intent, and receiving one is the `message` event.

WASI imports are allowed at their Preview 2 versions for `wasi:cli`, `wasi:io`, `wasi:clocks`, `wasi:random` and `wasi:filesystem`. Standard output and error go to the plugin log. A component that imports `wasi:sockets` or `wasi:http` is refused at install.

## Exports each side provides

Each world requires two or three exports. The SDK generates the export glue from the `#[ilium_plugin]` attribute in Rust or from `definePlugin` in TypeScript.

| Export | Side | Rust trait | Required methods |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lifecycle` | all | `Lifecycle` | `activate`, `deactivate` (both have defaults) |
| `handler` | server, client | `Handler` | `on_events(batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission>` |
| `views` | client | `Views` | `render(view: ViewTarget, area: Area) -> UiTree` |
| `renderer` | scene | `anim::renderer::Renderer` | `new(spec: SceneSpec)`; the rest have defaults |

The `activate` call receives an `Activation` record. Its fields are `plugin`, `api`, `instance` (a `u64` that rises for each new instance), `side`, `settings-json`, `granted` (the list of capabilities actually granted, so a plugin can hide features it cannot use) and `restored` (bytes that `deactivate` returned in an earlier run).

`deactivate` receives one of five delivered reasons: `shutdown`, `disabled`, `upgrade`, `revoked` or `granted` (listed with their effects in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)). The enum has six cases in a fixed order. The `crash-restart` case is reserved and never delivered [ABI-028], because a trap drops the instance without a call. Bytes returned from `deactivate` come back as `restored` on the next activation.

## Optional exports

The manifest `exports` list names only the optional exports, by interface name. Required exports such as `handler` or `renderer` are never listed. The host reads the component's real export list and compares it with the required exports plus the listed ones. A difference refuses the package with `manifest.exports-mismatch`.

The contract also defines optional exports (`catalog-provider`, the provider form of virtual rows, and others). The list is in [Getting started: overview](/pages/getting-started-overview/). The rule is the same: list each one in the manifest.

In Rust, the same names go into the attribute: `#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["detector"])]`.

### Optional exports by side and world variant

A **world variant** is a base world plus the export fragments that a plugin implements. The fragment name is `with-<export>`. The table lists what each fragment adds and where it exists.

| Fragment | Adds the export | Server | Client | Scene |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `with-detector` | `detector` | yes | no | no |
| `with-views` | `views` | no | yes | no |
| `with-annotator` | `annotator` | no | yes | no |
| `with-jobs` | `job-runner` | yes | yes | yes |
| `with-service` | `service-provider` | yes | yes | no |
| `with-inference-provider` | `inference-provider` | yes | yes | no |
| `with-settings-validate` | `settings-validate` | yes | yes | no |
| `with-catalog` | `catalog-provider` | yes | yes | no |
| `with-menus` | `menu-provider` | no | yes | no |
| `with-virtual-rows` | `virtual-rows-provider` | yes | yes | no |
| `with-tokens` | `token-provider` | no | yes | no |
| `with-hook-handler` | `hook-handler`, which dispatches the hook extensions of the plugin on this side | yes | yes | no |
| `with-migrator` | `migrator`, which converts stored data when `data_version` rose | yes | yes | no |

The `hook-handler` export is listed in the manifest `exports` of every side that has hook extensions. The `collect` kind of extension point needs no export, because entries are data. A plugin that owns a point and runs hooks does not export `hook-handler` (see [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/)).

### Where each side runs

Each side runs in the process that hosts it: the `server` side in the session server, the `client` and `scene` sides in each attached client, and a CLI entry with `requires_server: false` in the short-lived CLI process. A T2 or T3 side also has a sandbox helper process. The side's instance, its failure count and its restart timer belong to that process, so a client and the server count failures separately. The full process map is in [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/).

## Splitting a plugin across sides

Put a feature on the server side when it must keep working while no client is attached, or when it must survive a client detach. Agent signatures, scheduled input, text triggers, the prompt queue, progress monitors and chatroom routing belong there.

Put a feature on the client side when it draws to this user's screen or uses this user's devices. Settings pages, panels, dialogs, pane bodies, scenes, voice and smart copy belong there.

A scene gets its data only from its constructor argument, which carries its settings and the current palette. It cannot read the server side or send to it.

## Messages between sides

The server side and the client side talk through the `message` intent and the `message` event.

| Type | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| intent `message(message-spec)` | `to` | `message-target` | The receiving plugin, side and client |
| | `channel` | `string` | 1 to 64 characters from `[a-z0-9.-]` |
| | `payload` | `list<u8>` | Up to 1 MiB |
| event `message(message-event)` | `from`, `from-side` | `plugin-id`, `plugin-side` | The sending plugin and side |
| | `from-client` | `option<client-id>` | The sending client, if the sender was a client |
| | `channel`, `payload` | as above | As sent |
| record `message-target` | `plugin`, `side`, `client` | `plugin-id`, `plugin-side`, `option<client-id>` | `client: none` from the server reaches every attached client |

A plugin always reaches its own other side without a grant. A message to another plugin needs the grant `messages.peer:<plugin-id>`, with the exact id and no wildcard. A message to an installed plugin that is not active activates it, and the message is delivered after `activate` returns.

Rust names are `Event::Message(MessageEvent)` and `Intent::Message(MessageSpec)`, with `MessageTarget` and `PluginSide` from `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents`. TypeScript uses `{ tag: 'message', val: {...} }` for the event. Its `fromClient` and `client` fields are `bigint`, and its `payload` is a `Uint8Array`.

## Worked example in Rust: the server side

The server keeps the notes. When the client sends a note on the channel `notes.add`, the server stores it and sends the count back on `notes.summary` to the same client.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

const ADD_CHANNEL: &str = "notes.add";
const SUMMARY_CHANNEL: &str = "notes.summary";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesServer {
    notes: Vec<String>,
}

// The default methods accept activation and deactivation without state to restore.
impl Lifecycle for NotesServer {}

impl Handler for NotesServer {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::Message(message) = event else { continue };
            if message.channel != ADD_CHANNEL {
                continue;
            }
            let Ok(text) = String::from_utf8(message.payload) else { continue };
            self.notes.push(text);
            let summary = format!("{} notes", self.notes.len());
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
                to: MessageTarget {
                    plugin: "example.notes".into(),
                    side: PluginSide::Client,
                    client: message.from_client,
                },
                channel: SUMMARY_CHANNEL.into(),
                payload: summary.into_bytes(),
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

The server needs no grant for this, because it only messages its own client side. `Submission::new` takes the next correlation number and sets no dedup key.

## Worked example in TypeScript: the client side and manifest

The client shows the summary in a panel. When the summary arrives, it stores the text and asks the host to render the panel again.

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { invalidate } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { block, paragraph, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const SUMMARY_CHANNEL = 'notes.summary';
const PANEL_VIEW = 'example.notes.notes';
let summaryText = 'No notes yet';

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'message' || event.val.channel !== SUMMARY_CHANNEL) continue;
      summaryText = new TextDecoder().decode(event.val.payload);
      invalidate({ tag: 'panel', val: PANEL_VIEW });
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    return tree(block(paragraph([summaryText])));
  },
});
```

The manifest declares both sides, the client export and the grant the panel needs:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.notes",
  "name": "Notes",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Labs",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["views"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "client": ["ui.panels"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "panels": [{ "id": "notes", "title": "Notes", "modal": false }]
  },
  "files": []
}
```

The `files` list is empty only for this sketch. A real package lists both components with their length and SHA-256, as described on the [packages page](/pages/packages/). The panel id `notes` is global as `example.notes.notes`.

To send a note, the client submits a `message` intent with `to` set to `{ plugin: 'example.notes', side: 'server', client: undefined }` and `channel` set to `notes.add`. The server side then answers as shown above.

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Channel empty, longer than 64 characters or outside `[a-z0-9.-]` | `refused(invalid-argument)` for that submission |
| Payload over 1 MiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` for that submission |
| Target plugin not installed or not enabled | `refused(not-found)` |
| Message to another plugin without `messages.peer:<plugin-id>` | `refused(not-permitted)`, logged at level warn |
| Message to the plugin's own other side | Always allowed, no grant needed |
| Target plugin not active, and its `activate` fails | The message is discarded and logged at level error under the receiver. The sender is not told |
| Component exports differ from the manifest | Package refused with `manifest.exports-mismatch` |
| Component imports outside its world, or `wasi:sockets` or `wasi:http` | Package refused at install; the installer names the import and the world |
| Trap or deadline breach in an export | The instance is dropped without `deactivate`, and restarts after 1 s, then 5 s |
| Third failure within 10 minutes | The plugin is disabled on that side. On the client side the count is kept per client |
| `ui.invalidate` for a view the plugin does not declare | Ignored; the host logs one warn line that names the view |

A `refused` result applies to one submission. A batch of more than 256 submissions traps the call, and nothing in it is applied [ABI-008]. A malformed submission (for example a missing mandatory dedup key) or a missing grant refuses the whole batch, and the other submissions then complete as `refused(cancelled)` with the message `batch refused: submission <index>` [ABI-009].

## What the user sees

The server side has no screen. The client side shows the Notes panel, which reads `No notes yet` until the first summary arrives, and then `3 notes` after the third note. Errors reach the user through the plugin log, which the command `ilium plugin logs` prints. Each line holds the date and time, the level padded to five characters, the plugin id and the message.

<pre class="term">$ ilium plugin logs example.notes --tail 3
2026-10-11 09:14:02 warn  example.notes refused submit: not-permitted
2026-10-11 09:14:04 error example.notes trap in on-events: index out of bounds
2026-10-11 09:14:04 info  example.notes restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3)
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The first line is a refused peer message; the last two show a trap and the restart that follows it.

# Extending Settings

## Extending Settings

A plugin can put its own settings into Ilium's Settings screen. It can do that in two ways:

- **A. A new tab.** The plugin adds one or two tabs of its own to the rail, next to the built-in tabs. The plugin decides what the tab holds.
- **B. Sections in an existing tab.** The plugin adds a group of rows to a built-in tab, such as Terminal, Editor or Sound. The rows sit under a divider that names the plugin, so the user always sees where they came from.

Most plugins need only A. Use B when a setting belongs beside related built-in settings. Both ways use the same 18 row types, save rules and storage. Step-by-step guides are [tutorial 10, a new tab](/pages/tutorial-10-settings-new-tab/) and [tutorial 11, a section in an existing tab](/pages/tutorial-11-settings-extend-tab/). Exact field tables and error codes are in the [settings schema reference](/pages/reference-settings-schema/), the calls a plugin uses to read and write values are in [settings API](/pages/api-settings/), and the screen itself is described in [building settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/).

### The model

Every settings tab has a stable id. Built-in tabs use kebab-case ids such as `terminal`, `editor` or `user-interface`. These ids never change, even when the label on screen changes. A plugin's own tab has a global id made of the plugin id and its local id, for example `example.clipboard-history/main`.

A plugin declares its settings in `contributes.settings`. Each entry has a `kind`:

- `kind: "tab"` creates a new tab in the rail.
- `kind: "section"` adds a group of rows. Its `tab` field names either a built-in tab id (for example `terminal`) or one of the plugin's own tabs, written `self:<tab-id>`.

A section is placed at an **anchor**. An anchor is a named point in a tab:

- `end` (the default) puts the section after the last built-in row.
- `before:<section>` puts it directly before a named section.
- `after:<section>` puts it directly after a named section.

Most built-in tabs have one unnamed section called `main`, so `before:main` is refused. Tabs with headings, such as Remote compaction, expose named anchors: `behaviour`, `technique-per-agent`, `custom-prompt`, `input-shaping` and `model`. Kernel anchors are never renamed or removed.

A new tab is placed in the rail with `after`, which names the tab it follows. The default is `text-triggers`. The tail of the rail (`debug`, `api`, `about`, `setup`) is pinned, so a plugin tab never appears after `debug`.

### Ordering

The order of plugin content inside one tab is fixed by three keys, applied in turn:

1. The anchor. Built-in rows come first. A `before:` block sits directly before its named section, an `after:` block sits directly after it, and `end` blocks follow the last built-in row.
2. The `order` number, from 0 to 1000 (default 500). Lower numbers come first.
3. The plugin id, compared as bytes, then the order of declaration inside the plugin.

All sections of one plugin at one anchor sit together under one divider. The installation order and the enable order never change the result, so two machines with the same plugins show the same page.

    </marker>
  </defs>
