### Example 2: inflate a saved file and hash the result

The plugin reads a zlib-compressed file that the user picked, inflates it with a hard output cap, and computes the SHA-256 of the plain data. The cap guards against a small file that expands to a very large output.

**Grants:** `fs.read:picked`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::codec::{self, Compression};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

const MAX_INFLATED: u32 = 16_777_216;

/// Returns the inflated bytes and their 32-byte SHA-256 digest.
fn inflate_and_hash(path: FsPath) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), PluginError> {
    let packed = fs::read(&path, 0, 1_048_576)?;
    let plain = codec::inflate(Compression::Zlib, &packed, MAX_INFLATED)?;
    let digest = codec::sha256(&plain);
    Ok((plain, digest))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as codec from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/codec';
import * as fs from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import type { FsPath } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const MAX_INFLATED = 16_777_216;

export function inflateAndHash(path: FsPath): { plain: Uint8Array; digest: Uint8Array } {
  const packed = fs.read(path, 0n, 1_048_576);
  const plain = codec.inflate('zlib', packed, MAX_INFLATED);
  const digest = codec.sha256(plain); // always 32 bytes
  return { plain, digest };
}
```

### Where codec output goes

The `codec` interface (`ilium:host/codec@0.1.0`) has several consumers of its output. A decoded image can be written to a `surface` widget with `write-surface`, drawn in a scene, or kept as a frame of a pre-rendered loop. `rasterize-text` returns a decoded image whose alpha channel holds the ink tone, ready for `write-surface`. A font that ships in the package is rasterized by the scene's `font` resource instead (see [scenes](/pages/api-scenes/)); `rasterize-text` is for text drawn with the host's default font. Video frames come from [media](/pages/api-media/), not from `codec`.

### Errors

`codec` raises only the codes below. Every function may also return `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`, which apply to all host calls.

| Code | Raised by | When |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid-argument` | every function | Input over 16 MiB. |
| `invalid-argument` | `inflate` | `max-output` over 64 MiB, output longer than `max-output`, or corrupt data. |
| `invalid-argument` | `deflate` | `level` over 9. |
| `invalid-argument` | `image-info`, `decode-image` | Corrupt data, `frame` out of range, or more pixels than `max-pixels` or 67,108,864. |
| `invalid-argument` | `rasterize-text` | Text over 64 KiB, `size-px` of 0 or over 512, or `max-width-px` of 0 or over 16,384. |
| `unsupported` | `image-info`, `decode-image` | The format is not PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP. |

Corrupt compressed or image data is always `invalid-argument`. The code `io` never comes from `codec`, because `io` is reserved for operating system I/O. `sha256` has no codec-specific error.

<div class="warn">
<p>Call <code>image_info</code> before <code>decode_image</code>. The header check costs almost nothing, and it refuses an oversized picture before the decoder allocates its pixel buffer.</p>
</div>

### Decode path

The plugin supplies bytes and receives pixels. Every step between those two points runs in host code.

### Edge cases

- **Animated formats.** `image-info` reports every frame. `decode-image` decodes one frame at a time, so a plugin that plays an animation calls it once per frame and never asks for all frames in one call.
- **Frame index.** Frames are counted from 0. A `frame` at or above `frames` returns `invalid-argument`.
- **Pixel budget.** `max-pixels` is an upper bound that the plugin chooses. The host never allows more than 67,108,864 pixels, whatever value the plugin passes.
- **Size of the output.** A decoded picture is `width × height × 4` bytes. Check the product before you write it to a surface, because `ui.write-surface` accepts at most 16 MiB per call.
- **Jobs.** A job instance calls the same functions with the same results. Jobs are the right place for work near the 16 MiB input limit.

### What the user sees

`codec` has no screen output of its own. The user sees a result only through what the plugin shows: the decoded picture in its surface, or the message the plugin writes when a call fails. The host does not display a codec error by itself.

### Used by

- Saved-world scenes use `inflate` to read compressed chunks. See [scenes](/pages/api-scenes/).
- Map and Wikipedia scenes use `decode-image` for the image tiles they fetch. See [http](/pages/api-http/).
- Media scenes use `decode-image` for picture files. See [media](/pages/api-media/).

### See also

- [fs](/pages/api-fs/) for reading the bytes.
- [ui](/pages/api-ui/) for `write-surface`.
- [background jobs](/pages/background-jobs/) for work near the input limit.
- [always-granted capabilities](/pages/capability-always-granted/) for the grant rules.
- [errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the error codes.
- [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) and [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/) for project setup.

# commands

## commands

A command is a named action that a plugin contributes, such as "New note" or "Save note". The user runs a command from the command palette, a keybinding, a toolbar button, a context menu, a tree row action, a status bar segment, a voice phrase or the `ilium` CLI. The client side of the plugin receives every invocation of its own commands as a `command-invoked` event. Any plugin that holds the matching grant can invoke a command, including commands that other plugins contribute.

Commands connect the parts of a plugin that the user touches with the parts that do the work. A plugin declares a command in its manifest, handles the event in its client handler, and can grey the command out while its work runs. A command also carries a palette category and search keywords, and the menus that start commands can be static or filled by the plugin each time they open.

**You will need:**

- No grant to contribute a command, handle its `command-invoked` events, or change its state with `set-state`.
- `commands.invoke:<pattern>` to invoke any command, including your own. The pattern is an exact global id such as `ilium.git/status`, a plugin prefix such as `ilium.git/*`, or a bare `*` for every command. The bare `*` is high risk: the review dialog leaves it unchecked by default. See [Capability: commands.invoke](/pages/capability-commands-invoke/).
- `ui.chrome` for the contributions that put a button, a row action, a status segment or a frame slot in the kernel's chrome (`tree_toolbar`, `row_actions`, `status_segments`, `pane_frame_slots`). Menus and toolbar buttons of the agent primitive need no grant.
- The client side for `set-state` and for handling events. A server instance can call `invoke` but not `set-state`.
- The command's provider installed and enabled. An invocation of a command that no installed plugin contributes fails with `not-found`.

### Interface

```wit
// commands (C, plus S for invoke)
set-state: func(command: string, enabled: bool, checked: option<bool>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;   // own commands
invoke: func(command: string, arguments-json: string) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;          // commands.invoke:<pattern>

// event command-invoked (own commands, never dropped)
//   command, arguments-json, origin, context { pane, view, buffer, line, virtual-row, menu-item }

// menu-provider (export of C, fragment with-menus)
menu-items: func(context: menu-context) -> list<menu-entry>;      // <= 64 entries, deadline 20 ms
```

### Command ids and manifest entries

A command is declared in the `contributes` section of the manifest. Its local id is written in the manifest, and its global id is the plugin id, a slash and the local id. So `example.notes` with the local id `new-note` becomes `example.notes/new-note`. Every function in this page takes the global id.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | Local id, lower case, hyphens allowed |
| `title` | string | required | Text shown in the palette and menus |
| `palette` | boolean | `true` | Lists the command in the command palette |
| `icon` | string | none | Tabler icon name |
| `voice` | list of 1 to 8 strings | none | Phrases of 1 to 64 characters that invoke the command by voice |
| `arguments_schema` | JSON Schema subset | none | Validates `arguments-json` (see [errors](#errors)) |
| `when` | context expression | none | Shows the command only when the expression holds |
| `category` | string, at most 32 characters | none | The group the palette lists the command under |
| `keywords` | list of at most 8 strings of at most 24 characters | none | Extra search terms that the palette matches besides the title |

The command palette is a kernel surface: it ranks, groups and draws the commands, and a plugin only supplies the entries. A plugin cannot open the palette, add a mode to it, or read what the user typed. `category` and `keywords` are the whole contract. A `category` or `keywords` value above its limit is refused at install.

Keybindings name a command and a chord. The `mode` key is `global`, `prefix` (the chord is the key after the prefix) or `pane:<kind>` (active only in one pane kind). Chords use the grammar of [keys](/pages/api-keys/). When two plugins bind the same chord, the user's remap wins, then built-in bindings, then the earlier installed plugin (the rule of [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/)). A plugin can read the user's current bindings with [keymap.bindings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/).

### Context expressions

The `when` value is a context expression. It is a key compared with a string, combined with `&&`, `||`, `!` and parentheses:

```
pane.primitive == "agent" && agent.activity != "working"
```

| Key | Values |
|---|---|
| `pane.primitive` | `basic`, `terminal`, `agent`, `editor`, `none` |
| `pane.kind` | the global id of a pane kind, such as `example.notes.note` (the content kind) |
| `agent.activity` | the `agent-activity` values: `idle`, `working`, `awaiting-approval`, `menu`, `done` |
| `node.kind` | `pane`, `group`, `folder`, `project` |
| `node.file_extension` | the extension of the node's file, without the dot |
| `agent.signature` | the id of the detected agent signature |
| `view.focused` | `true` or `false` |
| `display_mode` | the active tree display mode: `normal`, `attention` or a plugin mode id |

A key that refers to no pane is false when no pane is in scope. An expression with an unknown key, an unknown value or bad syntax is refused at install: bad syntax with `manifest.when-syntax`, an unknown key with `manifest.when-key`. The keys `node.kind`, `node.file_extension`, `agent.signature`, `view.focused` and `display_mode` can be used in the `when` of `commands`, `toolbar_buttons`, `context_menu`, `row_actions` and `tree_toolbar`. The expression controls only whether the command is shown in the palette, a menu or a keybinding. It never blocks `commands.invoke`.

### Functions

| Function | Grant | Sides | Rust | TypeScript | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `set-state` | none (own commands) | client | `commands::set_state(command, enabled, checked)` | `setState(command, enabled, checked)` | `Result<(), PluginError>`; throws in TypeScript |
| `invoke` | `commands.invoke:<pattern>` | server, client | `commands::invoke(command, arguments_json).await` | `await invoke(command, argumentsJson)` | `Result<(), PluginError>`; `Promise<void>` |
| `invoke` request form | as `invoke` | server, client | `commands::invoke_request(...)` | `invokeRequest(...)` | `Result<RequestId, PluginError>`; `bigint` |

`set-state` takes `enabled: bool` and `checked: Option<bool>` (`undefined` in TypeScript). A `None` leaves the checked mark as it is. A `Some(true)` or `Some(false)` sets the check mark that the palette and menus draw for the command.

The async `invoke` resolves when the command has run. Use `invoke_request` only when you need the `request-id` yourself, for example to match the completion in `on-events`.

### Events

| Event | Field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command-invoked` | `command` | `String` | `string` | Global id of the command |
| | `arguments-json` | `String` | `string` | One JSON object, `{}` when none was given |
| | `origin` | `InvocationOrigin` | string union | How the user started it: `keybinding`, `palette`, `toolbar`, `menu`, `voice`, `cli`, `toast`, `row-action`, `status-segment`, `tree-toolbar`, `frame-slot`, `virtual-row-drop` or `text`. |
| | `context` | `CommandContext` | `{ pane, view, buffer, line, virtualRow, menuItem }` | Pane node, view, buffer and line, each optional. Also `virtual-row` (the row id) and `menu-item` (the id of the clicked menu entry). |

The event is never dropped. It is delivered to the client handler of the plugin that owns the command, and it needs no grant. The types are in `ilium:types/events`, so Rust code imports them from `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events`.

### Example 1: set-state and invoke

This plugin handles its own two commands. Saving disables the "Save note" command while the git status is refreshed, so the user cannot start a second save. It needs `commands.invoke:ilium.git/status` for the invoke. The manifest declares the commands, a palette category with keywords, and the grant:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.notes",
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "new-note", "title": "New note", "icon": "notes",
        "category": "Notes", "keywords": ["create", "write", "jot"],
        "when": "pane.primitive == \"basic\"" },
      { "id": "save-note", "title": "Save note", "icon": "device-floppy",
        "category": "Notes", "keywords": ["store", "write"] }
    ],
    "keybindings": [{ "command": "new-note", "chord": "ctrl+alt+n", "mode": "global" }]
  },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["commands.invoke:ilium.git/status"] }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::commands;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::task;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;

const NEW_NOTE: &str = "example.notes/new-note";
const SAVE_NOTE: &str = "example.notes/save-note";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notes;

impl Lifecycle for Notes {}

impl Handler for Notes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event {
                handle_invocation(invoked);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn handle_invocation(invoked: CommandInvokedEvent) {
    match invoked.command.as_str() {
        NEW_NOTE => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("new note from {:?}", invoked.origin)),
        SAVE_NOTE => refresh_status(),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn refresh_status() {
    if let Err(error) = commands::set_state(SAVE_NOTE, false, None) {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("cannot disable save: {}", error.message));
    }
    task::spawn(async {
        match commands::invoke("ilium.git/status", "{}").await {
            Ok(()) => log::log(Level::Info, "git status refreshed"),
            Err(error) => {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("git status failed: {}", error.message));
            }
        }
        if let Err(error) = commands::set_state(SAVE_NOTE, true, None) {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("cannot enable save: {}", error.message));
        }
    });
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { invoke, setState } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/commands';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const NEW_NOTE = 'example.notes/new-note';
const SAVE_NOTE = 'example.notes/save-note';

async function refreshStatus(): Promise<void> {
  setState(SAVE_NOTE, false, undefined);
  try {
    await invoke('ilium.git/status', '{}');
    log('info', 'git status refreshed');
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `git status failed: ${String(error)}`);
  } finally {
    setState(SAVE_NOTE, true, undefined);
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      const { command, origin } = event.val;
      if (command === NEW_NOTE) log('info', `new note from ${origin}`);
      if (command === SAVE_NOTE) void refreshStatus();
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Menus: context menus, toolbar buttons and row actions

Four contribution points start a command from a click. They share the `when` grammar above, an icon, and the origin of the resulting `command-invoked`. Counts and grants are in the table.

| Key | Fields | Grant | Cap | Origin of the invocation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `context_menu` | `id`, `title`, `command`, `target` (`terminal`, `tree-node`, `editor`, `pane:<kind>`), and `icon`, `when`, `dynamic`, `items` | none | none | `menu` |
| `toolbar_buttons` | `id`, `icon`, `label`, `command`, `applies_to` (signature ids or `all`), and `submenu`, `right_click_command` | none | none | `toolbar` |
| `row_actions` | `id`, `icon`, `label`, `command`, `applies_to`, `when`, `order` (0 to 1000, default 500) | `ui.chrome` | 4 | `row-action`, arguments `{"node": <id>}` or `{"row": "<virtual row id>"}` |
| `tree_toolbar` | `id`, `icon`, `label` (at most 24 characters), `command`, `caption` (at most 12 cells), `popup_view`, `when` | `ui.chrome` | 4 | `tree-toolbar` |

A `context_menu` entry with `dynamic: true` makes the host ask the plugin for its entries each time the menu opens. A static menu lists `items` in the manifest. An item is a `menu-entry` with a `parent` reference; the depth is at most 2, and a deeper tree is refused at install with `manifest.menu-depth`. A `toolbar_buttons` entry with `submenu` opens the submenu on a left click instead of running its `command`; the value is a static `items` list or the string `"dynamic"`, served by the same export with the menu id `<button id>`. `right_click_command` runs on a right click. The client draws the menu: placement, the stack of submenus and the keyboard handling are the host's, and the plugin supplies entries only.

#### The `menu-provider` export

A dynamic menu needs the client side to list `menu-provider` in its `exports`.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/menu-provider in reference-wit
record menu-context { menu: string, node: option<node-id>, pane: option<node-id>, view: option<view-target>,
                      key: option<string>, buffer: option<buffer-id>, line: option<u32>, selection: option<string> }
record menu-entry {
  id: string, label: string, icon: option<string>, shortcut: option<string>,
  parent: option<string>,                 // id of a submenu entry; depth <= 2
  is-submenu: bool, separator-before: bool,
  checked: option<tri-state>, disabled-reason: option<string>,   // <= 40 characters
  tooltip: option<tooltip>, danger: bool,
}
menu-items: func(context: menu-context) -> list<menu-entry>;      // <= 64 entries
```

| `menu-entry` field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `String` | `string` | Id of the entry, returned in `menu-item` of the click context |
| `label` | `String` | `string` | Text of the row |
| `icon` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | Catalogue id or glyph |
| `shortcut` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | Text shown at the right edge, informational only |
| `parent` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | Id of the submenu entry this entry belongs to |
| `is_submenu` | `bool` | `isSubmenu` | The entry opens the entries that name it as `parent` |
| `separator_before` | `bool` | `separatorBefore` | A rule is drawn above the entry |
| `checked` | `Option<TriState>` | `'off' \| 'on' \| 'mixed' \| undefined` | A check mark; `off` is an empty mark, `undefined` has no mark |
| `disabled_reason` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | When set, the entry is dimmed and cannot be chosen; at most 40 characters |
| `tooltip` | `Option<Tooltip>` | `Tooltip \| undefined` | Hover help, at most 200 characters |
| `danger` | `bool` | `boolean` | Draws the entry in the warning style |

The host calls `menu-items` with the deadline of 20 ms. On a timeout the menu opens with the static entries only, and the breach counts toward the plugin's deadline record. The export is activated by the trigger `menu:<id>`; until the instance answers, the host shows the static entries. A click arrives as `command-invoked` with `command` set to the menu's command and `arguments-json` `{"item": "<id>", ...context}`, and `context.menu-item` carries the entry id. At most 64 entries are shown; further ones are cut with a `… N more` row.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::menu_provider::MenuContext;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::MenuEntry;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::TriState;

fn entry(id: &str, label: &str) -> MenuEntry {
    MenuEntry {
        id: id.into(), label: label.into(), icon: None, shortcut: None, parent: None,
        is_submenu: false, separator_before: false, checked: None,
        disabled_reason: None, tooltip: None, danger: false,
    }
}

impl MenuProvider for NoteMenus {
    fn menu_items(&mut self, context: MenuContext) -> Vec<MenuEntry> {
        let mut order = MenuEntry { is_submenu: true, ..entry("order", "Order notes by") };
        order.separator_before = true;
        let mut by_title = entry("order-title", "Title");
        by_title.parent = Some("order".into());
        by_title.checked = Some(if self.order == "title" { TriState::On } else { TriState::Off });
        let mut by_date = entry("order-date", "Date");
        by_date.parent = Some("order".into());
        by_date.checked = Some(if self.order == "date" { TriState::On } else { TriState::Off });
        let mut delete = entry("delete", "Delete note");
        delete.danger = true;
        if context.node.is_none() {
            delete.disabled_reason = Some("select a note first".into());
        }
        vec![entry("open", "Open note"), order, by_title, by_date, delete]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { MenuContext, MenuEntry } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types/menus';

function entry(id: string, label: string): MenuEntry {
  return {
    id, label, icon: undefined, shortcut: undefined, parent: undefined,
    isSubmenu: false, separatorBefore: false, checked: undefined,
    disabledReason: undefined, tooltip: undefined, danger: false,
  };
}

// the `menuItems` member of definePlugin
export function menuItems(context: MenuContext): MenuEntry[] {
  const order = { ...entry('order', 'Order notes by'), isSubmenu: true, separatorBefore: true };
  const byTitle = { ...entry('order-title', 'Title'), parent: 'order',
    checked: currentOrder === 'title' ? 'on' as const : 'off' as const };
  const byDate = { ...entry('order-date', 'Date'), parent: 'order',
    checked: currentOrder === 'date' ? 'on' as const : 'off' as const };
  const remove = { ...entry('delete', 'Delete note'), danger: true,
    disabledReason: context.node === undefined ? 'select a note first' : undefined };
  return [entry('open', 'Open note'), order, byTitle, byDate, remove];
}
```

The manifest entry that uses it:

```json
{
  "client": { "exports": ["menu-provider"] },
  "contributes": {
    "context_menu": [
      { "id": "note-actions", "title": "Note actions", "command": "example.notes/menu-click",
        "target": "tree-node", "icon": "notes", "dynamic": true,
        "when": "node.kind == \"pane\" && pane.kind == \"example.notes.note\"" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The client's own context menus show how such a menu looks: a rounded block with the chrome title, a blank row at top and bottom, rows with two cells of padding, `✓` marking the checked entry in a submenu, `▸` at the right edge of an entry that opens a submenu, and a `─` rule above entries with `separator_before`. The two frames below follow that row layout, with the example plugin's entries in place of the client's own and the icons switched off.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Note actions──────────────╮
│                                  │
│  Open note                       │
│  ──────────────────────────────  │
│  Order notes by                ▸ │
│  <span class="t-dim">Delete note</span>                     │
│  <span class="t-dim">  select a note first</span>           │
│                                  │
╰──────────────────────────────────╯
╭  ≡ ● · Order notes by────────────╮
│                                  │
│    Title                         │

│                                  │
╰──────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The menu of the example, composed by hand from the client's popup layout (ui.rs <code>popup_action_line</code>, <code>popup_rows</code>): the row prefix, the <code>▸</code> and <code>✓</code> markers and the separator are the client's. Where the menu shows the disabled reason, the client's own submenu model appends it to the label; its exact placement is the host's choice, so the second dimmed line shows one possible placement.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Palette, keywords and categories

The palette lists a command under its `category` and finds it by title, id and `keywords`. The host does the matching, case-insensitively and ranked by prefix first, the same way as for catalogues. A command with `palette: false` is not listed, but it still runs from keybindings, menus and `invoke`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Commands───────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-prompt">&gt;</span> note                                            │
│                                                   │
│   Notes                                           │
│ <span class="t-hi">  New note                         ctrl+alt+n    </span> │
│   Open notes panel                                │
│ <span class="t-dim">  Save note                         disabled      </span>│
│                                                   │
│ <span class="t-dim">Enter run · Esc close · 3 commands match</span>          │
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The command palette as the specification describes it: a kernel surface, grouped by category, with disabled commands dimmed. The client build in this tree has no command palette yet, so the frame is composed by hand from the client's chrome and hint-bar conventions and is not a capture.</figcaption>
</figure>

A command disabled by `set-state` stays listed, dimmed. Pressing its keybinding does nothing. When the command runs, the user sees its effect: a new pane, a panel or a notice. The palette shows no status for an invocation. A refused invocation is written to the plugin log as a refusal line, the same way as a refused HTTP call.

### Errors

Synchronous errors come back from the call itself. Errors in the completion come back later as `request-completed`, with the outcome `failed` or `cancelled`.

| Call | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `set-state` | `not-found` | The command is not one of the plugin's own commands |
| `set-state` | `unsupported` | Called from a server instance |
| `invoke` | `not-found` | No installed plugin contributes that global id |
| `invoke` | `not-permitted` | The id is outside the granted pattern |
| `invoke` | `invalid-argument` | `arguments-json` is not one JSON object, is over 64 KiB, or fails `arguments_schema` |
| `invoke` | `conflict` | The command is disabled with `set-state` |
| `invoke` | `busy`, `quota-exceeded` | Pending requests are full, or the CPU budget is spent |
| completion | `ok` | The command ran |
| completion | `failed(code)` | The command returned its own error code |
| completion | `failed(timed-out)` | The command did not reply within 30 seconds |
| completion | `cancelled` | The plugin cancelled the request, the application shut down, or the owning plugin was disabled while the command ran |

A command that is disabled and then invoked by the user through a keybinding or the palette gives the intent `refused(conflict)`, with the same meaning.

Manifest errors (the install is refused with the key path):

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `manifest.when-syntax` | A `when` value with bad syntax or an unknown value |
| `manifest.when-key` | An unknown `when` key |
| `manifest.menu-depth` | Static `context_menu` or `toolbar_buttons.submenu` items nested deeper than 2 |
| `manifest.contribution-limit` | More `row_actions`, `tree_toolbar` entries and so on than the cap of 4 |
| `manifest.contribution-target` | `row_actions.applies_to` names an unknown target |

### Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| `arguments-json` | 64 KiB, one JSON object |
| Command completion | 30 s, then `failed(timed-out)` |
| `category` | 32 characters |
| `keywords` | 8 entries of at most 24 characters |
| `voice` phrases | 1 to 8, each 1 to 64 characters |
| Menu entries per menu | 64, then `… N more` |
| Submenu depth | 2 |
| `disabled-reason` | 40 characters |
| Tooltip | 200 characters |
| `menu-items` deadline | 20 ms, static entries on a breach |
| `tree_toolbar`, `row_actions` | 4 each, per plugin |
| `tree_toolbar` `label`, `caption` | 24 characters, 12 cells |

### Edge cases

- Own commands need no grant, both for `set-state` and for `invoke`. A plugin can invoke its own command without holding any `commands.invoke` grant.
- `when` is not checked by `invoke`. A plugin can run a command that is hidden from the palette.
- A command returns no data. The completion carries an outcome only. To send data back, use [services](/pages/api-services/) or a [topic](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).
- The `*` pattern never crosses a slash. `*/status` and `ilium.git/prefix*` are rejected at install.
- `set-state` changes the state until the next call or until the plugin restarts. A restart resets every command to its manifest state.
- A dynamic menu whose provider is slow shows the static entries for that opening only; the next opening asks again.

Checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Events

## Events

Events are what the kernel tells a plugin. The kernel queues them for each plugin and hands them over in batches to the `handler` export. Each call to `on-events` returns the submissions the plugin wants the kernel to apply. Each event has a payload, needs a capability, and has a delivery policy that says what happens when the plugin is slow: the event is kept, merged with newer ones, or dropped and counted.

### What you need

- **Grants.** Each catalogue entry names the capability it needs. Entries marked "always" need no grant. Request the grants per side in the manifest:

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["panes.read", "sound.play"] }
```

- **Language.** Rust plugins use the `ilium-plugin-sdk` crate. TypeScript plugins use `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both generate their types from the WIT interfaces. See the [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) and [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/) pages.
- **Export.** A `server` or `client` plugin exports `handler`. The export is required and is never listed in the manifest `exports` key.
- **Activation.** Events for an inactive plugin are not queued. Events produced while the plugin activates are queued and arrive in the first batch after `activate` returns `ok`. Add a trigger such as `"activation": ["event:pane-exited"]` to start the plugin when that event happens. Without an `activation` key the plugin starts on first use of any of its contributions.

### Handler surface

| Language | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| WIT | `on-events: func(batch: list<event>) -> list<submission>;` | The `handler` export |
| Rust | `fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission>` | Method of the `Handler` trait, required |
| TypeScript | `onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[]` | Member of the object passed to `definePlugin` |

Every event is one case of the WIT variant `event`. Names follow the SDK naming rules:

- Rust: `Event::PaneExited(PaneExitedEvent { node, status, signal })`. Import the types with `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event`, which the prelude also brings in.
- TypeScript: `{ tag: 'pane-exited', val: { node, status, signal } }`. Import the type with `Event` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types`.

Every `u64`, including a node id, is a `bigint` in TypeScript.

### Batch and delivery rules

- A batch holds at most 256 events. The host splits a longer backlog into several batches.
- Each plugin has one queue, filled in kernel emission order across all event kinds. The queue holds 1,024 events by default. The ceiling of `event_queue` is 4,096 for T1 and 1,024 for T2 and T3. The host clamps a larger request to the ceiling and logs the clamp [API-043] [EVT-046]. The manifest key `event_queue` requests a value. The user can set it in `[plugins.limits]` in `config.toml`.
- Order is kept per node: `pane-created`, then the other pane events, then `pane-exited`, then `node-removed`. `agent-identified` always precedes `agent-activity-changed`.
- **Coalesced** events are merged with the pending, undelivered event of the same kind and key (node, buffer, timer, job, watch, pane or signal), whatever the queue fill. The merged event keeps the newest payload at the position of the newest occurrence, so a coalesced kind occupies at most one slot per key [EVT-043]. Pending `tree-changed` events merge into one event whose list is the union of the node ids in first-seen order. When `node-removed` for a node is queued, the host removes that node id from a pending `tree-changed` list and discards every pending coalesced event keyed by that node [EVT-041].
- **Drop oldest, counted** events can be evicted. When an event arrives at a full queue, the host first removes the oldest pending drop-oldest event of any kind and counts it under its own event and source. If no drop-oldest event is pending and the incoming event is drop-oldest, the incoming event is discarded and counted. A coalesced event whose key is already pending never causes an eviction [EVT-004]. The next batch after a drop starts with one `events-dropped` event. `events-dropped` is itself never dropped. At most one is pending: a new drop adds to the count of the matching (event, source) record or appends a new record, and the event always sits at the head of the next batch [EVT-045]. In a record, `event` is the kebab-case case name as in the WIT (for example `"output-matched"`). `source` is `some(filter id)` for `output-matched`, `some(topic name)` for topic events, `some(decimal capture id)` for capture events, and `none` for every other kind. There is one record per (event, source) pair, in order of first drop.
- **Never dropped** events are never lost. If the queue is full, no drop-oldest event is pending and a never-dropped event other than `message` (or a coalesced event with a new key) arrives, the plugin is treated as stuck. A `message` is checked when it is submitted: the sender gets `refused(busy)` instead [SVC-030]. Its instance is restarted, and the new instance receives `tree-changed` for every node so it can read its state again [EVT-004].

### Event catalogue

Payloads use WIT types. Capabilities are the grant strings from the manifest.

| Event | Payload | Capability | Delivery policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree-changed` | `list<node-id>` | `tree.read` | coalesced; pending lists merge into one union |
| `node-removed` | `node-id` | `tree.read` | never dropped |
| `pane-created` | `pane-info` | `panes.read` | never dropped |
| `pane-exited` | `node`, `status: option<s32>`, `signal: option<string>` | `panes.read` | never dropped |
| `pane-focused` | `option<node-id>` | `panes.read` | coalesced |
| `pane-resized` | `node`, `columns`, `rows` | `panes.read` | coalesced by node |
| `pane-title-changed` | `node`, `title`, `source` (osc, manual, inferred) | `panes.read` | coalesced by node |
| `agent-identified` | `node`, `signature` | `agent.read` | never dropped |
| `agent-activity-changed` | `node`, `previous`, `current`, `revision` | `agent.read` | never dropped |
| `agent-goal-changed` | `node`, `goal: option<string>` | `agent.read` | coalesced by node |
| `input-submitted` | `node`, `text`, `source` (user, plugin, scheduled, voice), `epoch` | `agent.read-prompts` | never dropped |
| `output-matched` | `node`, `filter-id`, `line`, `row` | `terminal.output-filter` | drop oldest, counted |
| `link-activated` | `node`, `detector-id`, `text` | own `link_detectors` | never dropped |
| `pointer` | `node`, `row`, `column`, `kind` (down, up, drag, wheel, move), `button`, plus `sub-x`, `sub-y`, `modifiers` | `terminal.pointer` while claimed | coalesced (drag) |
| `editor-opened`, `editor-closed` | `buffer-ref` | `editor.read` | never dropped |
| `editor-changed` | `buffer`, `revision`, `first-line`, `last-line` | `editor.read` | coalesced by buffer, debounced 100 ms |
| `editor-saved` | `buffer`, `path` | `editor.read` | never dropped |
| `settings-changed` | `settings-change { keys, origin, side }` | always (own) | coalesced |
| `timer-fired` | `timer-id` | always (own) | coalesced by timer |
| `request-completed` | `request-result` | always (own) | never dropped |
| `job-progress` | `job: request-id`, `percent: f32` | always (own) | coalesced by job |
| `message` | `message-event` (`from`, `from-side`, `from-client`, `channel`, `payload: list<u8>`) | always (own sides) or the sender's `messages.peer` | never dropped |
| `topic-published` | `topic`, `from`, `payload-json` | `topics.subscribe:<pattern>` | drop oldest, counted |
| `command-invoked` | `command`, `arguments-json`, `origin` (keybinding, palette, toolbar, menu, voice, cli, toast, row-action, status-segment, tree-toolbar, frame-slot, virtual-row-drop, text), `context` | own commands | never dropped |
| `ui-action` | `view`, `key`, `action-id`, `kind`, `value` | own views | never dropped (`scrolled` coalesced) |
| `key-pressed`, `key-released` | `grab: option<u64>`, `pane: option<node-id>`, `chord`, `repeat` | `keys.intercept` or `wants_keys` | never dropped |
| `view-visibility` | `view`, `visible: bool` | own views | coalesced |
| `fs-changed` | `watch`, `paths: list<string>` | `fs.watch` | coalesced by watch |
| `audio-frames` | `capture`, `samples: list<s16>` | audio grant | drop oldest, counted |
| `cli-invoked` | `invocation`, `name`, `argv`, `cwd` | `cli.contribute` | never dropped |
| `cli-cancelled` | `invocation: u64` | `cli.contribute` | never dropped |
| `http-called` | `call`, `method`, `path`, `headers`, `body` | `http-api.route` | never dropped |
| `client-attached`, `client-detached` | `client-id` | server side, always | never dropped |
| `theme-changed` | none | client side, always | coalesced |
| `events-dropped` | `list<dropped-count>` (`event`, `source: option<string>`, `count: u32`) | always (own) | coalesced by (event, source); never dropped |

### Request results

`request-completed` is the only way a plugin learns the outcome of a submission or a slow host call. Its payload is `request-result`, which holds the `request` (`submission(u64)` with the correlation number, or `call(request-id)`) and the `outcome`:

- `ok`: the submission was applied. For a call, the typed result is ready to take.
- `ok-node(node-id)`: the submission created that node.
- `duplicate(request-ref)`: the `dedup-key` was already used. Nothing happened.
- `refused(plugin-error)`: the kernel refused the submission before applying it.
- `failed(plugin-error)`: the kernel accepted it but could not apply it.
- `cancelled`: the request was cancelled by the plugin, the user or a shutdown. A sibling of a refused submission completes as `refused(cancelled)`, not as `cancelled`.

In Rust and TypeScript, the SDK removes the completions that a future or promise awaits from the batch. Only unawaited completions reach `on-events`.

The `ui-action` kinds and values are listed below.

#### ui-action kinds and values

A plugin view reports user actions as `ui-action { view, key, action-id, kind, value }`, where `action-id` is a copy of `key` in 0.1.0 and `value` is an option. There are 17 kinds. The value variant has 12 cases in total.

| Kind | Value | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| `activated` | `none`, or `text(<target>)` for a clickable span with an `action` target | never dropped |
| `changed` | `text`, `index`, `number`, `flag`, `item-state`, `geo` or `ids`, by widget; text inputs arrive after 600 ms (a text-area above 10,000 bytes waits 1 s; `debounce-ms` overrides both) | never dropped |
| `submitted` | `text` | never dropped |
| `selected` | `index`, or `ids` for multi-selection | never dropped |
| `toggled` | `flag`, or `item-state` for `check-list` items and tri-state toggles | never dropped |
| `scrolled` | `number` | coalesced |
| `dropped` | `drop(drop-value)` with `source-key`, `target-key` and `index` | never dropped |
| `context-requested` | `none` | never dropped |
| `closed` | `none` | never dropped |
| `focus-gained`, `focus-lost` | `none` | never dropped |
| `hover-enter`, `hover-leave` | `none`; only for nodes with `hover-events` | never dropped |
| `pointer` | `pointer(view-pointer)`; only for nodes with `pointer-events` | coalesced |
| `drag-over` | `drag-over(drag-over-value)`; drop targets during a drag | coalesced per target |
| `resized` | `number`; the `split` widget | never dropped |
| `filter-changed` | `text`; `%list` and `choice` | never dropped, debounced 150 ms |

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/ui in reference-wit
variant action-value {
  none, text(string), index(u32), number(f64), flag(bool),
  drop(drop-value),
  cell(cell-position),
  pointer(view-pointer),
  drag-over(drag-over-value),
  /// Check-list item id, or "" for a tri-state toggle.
  item-state(tuple<string, tri-state>),
  /// location-picker.
  geo(geo-point),
  /// Multi-selection in the list, table and tree-list.
  ids(list<string>),
}
```

`view-pointer` is `{ kind: pointer-kind, button: pointer-button, modifiers: pointer-modifiers, column: u16, row: u16, sub-x: u8, sub-y: u8, clicks: u8 }`. The column and row are 0-based inside the widget's area. `sub-x` and `sub-y` are 0 to 255 within the cell and read 128 when the terminal reports whole cells only. `clicks` is 1, 2 or 3 for `down` and 0 otherwise.

**Rust**

```rust
Event::UiAction(UiAction { view, key, kind, value, .. }) => match (kind, value) {
    (UiActionKind::Pointer, ActionValue::Pointer(pointer)) if pointer.clicks == 2 => {
        self.open_cell(&key, pointer.column, pointer.row);
    }
    (UiActionKind::DragOver, ActionValue::DragOver(over)) => {
        self.hint = Some((over.target_key, over.accept));   // coalesced per target
    }
    (UiActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Geo(GeoPoint { lat, lon })) => {
        self.home = (lat, lon);
    }
    (UiActionKind::FilterChanged, ActionValue::Text(query)) => self.filter = query,
    _ => {}
},
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
if (event.tag === 'ui-action') {
  const { kind, value, key } = event.val;
  if (kind === 'pointer' && value.tag === 'pointer' && value.val.clicks === 2) {
    openCell(key, value.val.column, value.val.row);
  } else if (kind === 'drag-over' && value.tag === 'drag-over') {
    hint = { target: value.val.targetKey, accept: value.val.accept };
  } else if (kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'geo') {
    home = [value.val.lat, value.val.lon];
  } else if (kind === 'filter-changed' && value.tag === 'text') {
    filter = value.val;
  }
}
```

### Further events

The contract appends 18 more event cases after `events-dropped`. Each payload is a record named `<case>-event`, for example `ScreenChangedEvent` in Rust. Fields use kebab-case in WIT, `snake_case` in Rust and `camelCase` in TypeScript.

| Event | Payload | Capability | Delivery policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `screen-changed` | `pane`, `first-row`, `last-row`, `revision` | `terminal.read-cells` | coalesced by pane, at most 10 per second |
| `user-line-submitted` | `pane`, `text`, `at: epoch-ms` | `agent.read-prompts` | never dropped |
| `signal-changed` | `pane`, `signal`, `value: string` | `agent.read` | coalesced by pane and signal |
| `agent-model-changed` | `pane`, `model: agent-model` | `agent.read` | coalesced by pane |
| `editor-pointer` | `buffer`, `pane`, `position: text-position`, `pointer: view-pointer` | `editor.read` | coalesced (move) |
| `editor-viewport-changed` | `editor-viewport` | `editor.read` | coalesced by pane, 100 ms |
| `http-stream-data` | `stream`, `status: option<u16>`, `headers: option<list<header>>` (`some` on the first chunk only), `chunk: list<u8>` | the `http` grant of the stream | never dropped; the host stops reading the socket while the queue is full |
| `http-stream-closed` | `stream`, `outcome: stream-outcome` (`ended`, `cancelled` or `failed(plugin-error)`) | the `http` grant of the stream | never dropped |
| `child-output` | `child`, `stream` (stdout, stderr), `bytes` | `process.long-lived` | never dropped; same back-pressure |
| `child-exited` | `child`, `status: option<s32>`, `signal: option<string>` | `process.long-lived` | never dropped |
| `pane-lifecycle-changed` | `pane`, `state` (`running`, `frozen`, `restarting`, `exited`), `by: option<plugin-id>` | `panes.read` | never dropped |
| `attention-changed` | `node`, `marked: bool`, `reason: option<string>`, `by: option<plugin-id>` | `tree.attention` or `tree.read` | coalesced by node |
| `client-request` | `call`, `kind`, `payload-json` | client side, own `client_requests` | never dropped |
| `kernel-settings-changed` | `tab`, `keys: list<string>` | `settings.read-kernel:<tab>` | coalesced by tab; keys unioned |
| `keymap-changed` | none | `keymap.read` | coalesced |
| `durable-timer-fired` | `timer`, `name`, `late-by-millis: u64` | always (own) | never dropped |
| `input-uncertain` | `pane`, `dedup-key` | the grant of the original `send-input` | never dropped |
| `display-mode-changed` | `mode: option<string>` (global id; none for Normal) | own `display_modes` | coalesced |

The never-dropped rule is as follows: a full queue marks the plugin as stuck and restarts it. `http-stream-data` and `child-output` add back-pressure first, so a fast network peer or a chatty child slows down before that point. `events-dropped` still counts the drop-oldest events only.

Extended payloads of existing events (shape changes):

- `pointer` gains `sub-x`, `sub-y`, `modifiers` and the kind `move`. A `move` is reported only while the plugin claims the pointer and the pointer is over the pane. A claim may ask for a modifier gesture, so plain clicks keep going to the program.
- `command-invoked` `origin` gains `toast`, `row-action`, `status-segment`, `tree-toolbar`, `frame-slot`, `virtual-row-drop` and `text` (a clickable span). Its `context` gains `virtual-row: option<string>` and `menu-item: option<string>`.
- `input-submitted` is joined by `user-line-submitted`, which also covers plain terminal panes. It needs the same `agent.read-prompts` grant.

#### Pane and attention events

`pane-lifecycle-changed` is the confirmation of the lifecycle intents in the [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-intent-pane-lifecycle/) page, and it also reports changes made by the user or by another plugin, with `by` naming the plugin. `attention-changed` does the same for `mark-attention` and `ack-attention` (see [chrome intents](/pages/api-intent-chrome/)). `input-uncertain` follows a crash during a journaled `send-input` (see [send-input stages](/pages/api-intent-send-input/)).

**Rust**

```rust
Event::PaneLifecycleChanged(PaneLifecycleChangedEvent { pane, state, by }) => {
    self.states.insert(pane, state);
    if state == PaneLifecycleState::Frozen && by.is_none() {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("pane {pane} frozen by the user"));
    }
}
Event::AttentionChanged(AttentionChangedEvent { node, marked, reason, .. }) => {
    if !marked { self.pending.remove(&node); } else if let Some(r) = reason { self.pending.insert(node, r); }
}
Event::InputUncertain(InputUncertainEvent { pane, dedup_key }) => {
    // read the screen, decide, then resend with a NEW key
    self.needs_review.push((pane, dedup_key));
}
Event::DurableTimerFired(DurableTimerFiredEvent { name, late_by_millis, .. }) => {
    if late_by_millis > 60_000 { self.catch_up(&name); }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
switch (event.tag) {
  case 'pane-lifecycle-changed':
    states.set(event.val.pane, event.val.state);
    if (event.val.state === 'frozen' && event.val.by === undefined) {
      log('info', `pane ${event.val.pane} frozen by the user`);
    }
    break;
  case 'attention-changed':
    if (!event.val.marked) pending.delete(event.val.node);
    else if (event.val.reason !== undefined) pending.set(event.val.node, event.val.reason);
    break;
  case 'input-uncertain':
    needsReview.push([event.val.pane, event.val.dedupKey]);   // resend with a NEW key
    break;
  case 'durable-timer-fired':
    if (event.val.lateByMillis > 60_000n) catchUp(event.val.name);
    break;
}
```

<text x="16" y="105" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">audio-frames, output-matched, topic-published</text>
<text x="8" y="138" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Coalesced by key</text>
<rect x="8" y="146" width="324" height="20" rx="5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
<text x="16" y="160" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">tree-changed, editor-changed, timer-fired</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Each event kind has one policy. Check the policy before you rely on an event for state.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Example 1: sound on pane exit, with a settings check

The handler plays a sound when a pane exits, unless the user muted it. It logs timers and request results, and it re-reads the setting when `sound-enabled` changes.

**Grants:** `panes.read`, `sound.play`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notices {
    sound_muted: bool,
}

impl Lifecycle for Notices {}

impl Handler for Notices {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::PaneExited(exited) => {
                    let line = format!("pane {} exited: {:?}", exited.node, exited.status);
                    log::log(Level::Info, &line);
                    if !self.sound_muted {
                        submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::PlaySound("ding".to_string())));
                    }
                }
                Event::TimerFired(timer_id) => {
                    log::log(Level::Debug, &format!("timer {timer_id} fired"));
                }
                Event::SettingsChanged(keys) => {
                    if keys.iter().any(|key| key == "sound-enabled") {
                        self.sound_muted = !read_sound_enabled(); // see api-settings
                    }
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(result) => {
                    log::log(Level::Debug, &format!("request result: {:?}", result.outcome));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let soundMuted = false;
let nextCorrelation = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {},
  deactivate() { return undefined; },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      switch (event.tag) {
        case 'pane-exited':
          log('info', `pane ${event.val.node} exited: ${event.val.status}`);
          if (!soundMuted) {
            submissions.push({
              intent: { tag: 'play-sound', val: 'ding' },
              correlation: nextCorrelation++,
              dedupKey: undefined,
            });
          }
          break;
        case 'timer-fired':
          log('debug', `timer ${event.val} fired`);
          break;
        case 'settings-changed':
          if (event.val.includes('sound-enabled')) {
            soundMuted = !readSoundEnabled(); // see api-settings
          }
          break;
        case 'request-completed':
          log('debug', `request result: ${event.val.outcome.tag}`);
          break;
        default:
          break;
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

Outcome: when a pane exits and sound is on, the batch returns one `play-sound` submission. The kernel applies it and sends `request-completed` in a later batch. Its `request` field is `submission(<correlation>)` with the same number, and its `outcome` is `ok`. The sound id `ding` must be in the catalogue from `sound.catalog()`. An unknown id refuses only that submission.

<figure>
<pre class="term">$ ilium plugin test ./notices --fixture pane-exit.json
<span class="t-dim">{"type":"log","message":"pane 14 exited"}</span>
<span class="t-hi">{"type":"submission","index":0,"intent":"play-sound"}</span>
<span class="t-ok">{"type":"outcome","index":0,"outcome":"ok"}</span>
<span class="t-dim">1 batch, 1 submission, 0 refused</span>
</pre>

</figure>

### Example 2: track changed nodes and count dropped events

This server handler keeps the set of nodes that changed since it last read the tree. Because `tree-changed` is coalesced, the set holds one entry per node, however often the node changed. When the kernel reports dropped events, the handler logs the counts.

**Grants:** `tree.read`

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct TreeWatch {
    dirty_nodes: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
}

impl Lifecycle for TreeWatch {}

impl Handler for TreeWatch {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::TreeChanged(nodes) => self.dirty_nodes.extend(nodes),
                Event::NodeRemoved(node) => {
                    self.dirty_nodes.remove(&node);
                }
                Event::EventsDropped(counts) => {
                    for count in counts {
                        let line = format!("{} {} events dropped", count.count, count.event);
                        log::log(Level::Warn, &line);
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const dirtyNodes = new Set<bigint>();

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {},
  deactivate() { return undefined; },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      switch (event.tag) {
        case 'tree-changed':
          event.val.forEach((node) => dirtyNodes.add(node));
          break;
        case 'node-removed':
          dirtyNodes.delete(event.val);
          break;
        case 'events-dropped':
          for (const count of event.val) {
            log('warn', `${count.count} ${count.event} events dropped`);
          }
          break;
        default:
          break;
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Outcome: a batch with three `tree-changed` events for node 7 leaves one entry for node 7 in `dirtyNodes`. If the queue dropped 12 `output-matched` events, the next batch starts with `events-dropped`, and the handler logs `12 output-matched events dropped` at level warn.

### Errors and limits

| Condition | Effect |
|---|---|
| Malformed submission in a batch | The batch is refused. The lowest-index bad submission completes as `refused(invalid-argument)`, the others as `refused(cancelled)` |
| Submission without the grant it needs | The batch is refused. That submission completes as `refused(not-permitted)`; the rest of the batch is `refused(cancelled)` |
| More than 256 submissions returned | Trap. The instance restarts |
| Handler exceeds its deadline (20 ms by default, 50 ms at the tier 1 ceiling) | Trap. The instance restarts after 1 s |
| Never-dropped event with a full queue | The plugin is treated as stuck and restarted. The new instance receives `tree-changed` for all nodes |
| Restart failures | Restart after 1 s on the first failure in the window and 5 s on the second. The third failure within 10 minutes disables the plugin on that side |
| Event for a capability that was not granted | Not delivered. The plugin never sees it |

Events themselves do not fail. Keep the handler short. Move slow work to a job (see [Jobs](/pages/api-jobs/)) or to a submission whose outcome arrives later.

<div class="warn">
<p>A trap or a deadline breach ends the instance and cancels its pending requests. The new instance starts with empty state, so re-read any state it needs from the tree or from storage.</p>
</div>

### What the user sees

Events are not shown directly. The user sees their effects: a sound plays, a decoration appears, and the plugin's log lines appear in `ilium plugin logs`. A refused submission and every trap are written to the log with the plugin id, the interface and the function. When a plugin is disabled after repeated failures, the tree footer shows a notice, and the user re-enables the plugin from settings or the kernel recovery page.

Requirement ids for this page: [EVT-030]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

# Plugin exports

## Plugin exports

A plugin imports host functions and also exports functions that the host calls. Each export belongs to one side of the plugin: `server`, `client` or `scene`. The host calls an export only when the feature it serves is present, so a plugin never receives calls for features it did not declare.

Every server and client plugin implements `lifecycle` and `handler`. A scene plugin implements `lifecycle` and `renderer`. Optional exports are named in the `exports` list of the side in the manifest. The component must export exactly the required set plus the listed optional exports. If it does not, install refuses the package with `manifest.exports-mismatch`.

### What you need

- **A manifest entry.** Add each optional export to `exports`, for example `"exports": ["detector"]`. Never list a required export.
- **The grant in the catalogue table.** Only the exports with a grant in that table need one. Your plugin's own host calls need their grants as usual.
- **A toolchain.** Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, where the export traits live in `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports`. Or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk` and `definePlugin`.

### The export catalogue

| Export | Side | Required | Manifest name | Grant | The host calls it to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lifecycle` | all | yes | none | none | activate, and deactivate with a reason |
| `handler` | server, client | yes | none | none | deliver a batch of events, and take submissions back |
| `views` | client | no | `views` | none; `ui.invalidate` is always granted for own views | render a view tree when it opens, is invalidated or resizes |
| `detector` | server | no | `detector` | `agent.read` | identify an agent from a pane's processes, and classify its screen |
| `job-runner` | server, client, scene | no | `job-runner` | none; the job kind must be in `contributes.jobs` | run a declared job with input bytes, and return output bytes |
| `service-provider` | server, client | no | `service-provider` | `services.provide:<name>` (name without version) | answer a call to a service it provides |
| `inference-provider` | server, client | no | `inference-provider` | `inference.provide` | complete a model request, and list its models |
| `annotator` | client | no | `annotator` | `editor.read` | annotate the visible lines of an editor buffer |
| `settings-validate` | server, client | no | `settings-validate` | none | check a pending settings change before it is saved (100 ms) |
| `hook-handler` | server, client | no | `hook-handler` | `extensions.contribute` | run one hook extension of another plugin's extension point (WIT fragment `with-hook-handler`); the handler lives on the side that owns the point |
| `renderer` | scene | yes | none | none | draw frames of a background scene |
| `catalog-provider` | server, client | no | `catalog-provider` | none; ids must be in `contributes.catalogs` | serve a page of an option catalogue |
| `menu-provider` | client | no | `menu-provider` | none | build a dynamic context menu or toolbar submenu |
| `virtual-rows-provider` | server, client | no | `virtual-rows-provider` | `tree.decorate` for the rows themselves | return a page of children of a virtual tree row |
| `token-provider` | client | no | `token-provider` | `editor.read` | return syntax tokens for lines of a language the host does not know |
| `migrator` | server, client | no | `migrator` | none | convert stored data once before `activate` when `data_version` rose (WIT fragment `with-migrator`) |

The `handler` export receives events in batches of at most 256, and returns at most 256 submissions per call. The host applies the submissions in order. A malformed submission, or one without its grant, refuses the whole batch. See [Events](/pages/api-events/) for the event catalogue and [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) for the submission outcomes.

### Worlds and export fragments

A plugin's world is one base world plus the fragments it implements. The manifest `exports` list must match the component's exports.

| World | Required exports | Optional fragments |
|---|---|---|
| `ilium:server/base` | `lifecycle`, `handler` | `with-detector`, `with-jobs`, `with-service`, `with-inference-provider`, `with-settings-validate`, `with-catalog`, `with-virtual-rows`, `with-hook-handler`, `with-migrator` |
| `ilium:client/base` | `lifecycle`, `handler` | `with-views`, `with-annotator`, `with-jobs`, `with-service`, `with-inference-provider`, `with-settings-validate`, `with-catalog`, `with-menus`, `with-virtual-rows`, `with-tokens`, `with-hook-handler`, `with-migrator` |
| `ilium:anim/base` | `lifecycle`, `renderer` | `with-jobs` |

### The four provider exports

Each has its own page with the full records, a Rust and a TypeScript example, and the render the user sees.

| Export | Called when | Deadline | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog-provider` | a row or widget opens a plugin catalogue | 20 ms | [catalogs](/pages/api-catalogs/) |
| `menu-provider` | a dynamic menu or toolbar submenu opens | 20 ms | [menu provider](/pages/api-menu-provider/) |
| `virtual-rows-provider` | a provider virtual row is expanded | 20 ms | [virtual rows provider](/pages/api-virtual-rows-provider/) |
| `token-provider` | a buffer of a declared language is visible | 10 ms per call | [token provider](/pages/api-token-provider/) |

Further activation triggers: `catalog:<id>`, `menu:<id>`, `virtual-rows:<row-kind>`, `language:<id>`, `client-request:<kind>` and `durable-timer`. Until the instance answers, the host shows the static menu entries, a spinner row, or plain text.

Further stop rules: on deactivate, trap or revocation the host closes the plugin's HTTP streams, terminates its spawned children, releases its input locks, withdraws its status segments, frame slots, toasts and row actions, and fails its open client requests with `cancelled`. Durable timers and journal entries survive.

### Lifecycle

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/lifecycle in reference-wit
enum deactivation-reason { shutdown, disabled, upgrade, crash-restart, revoked, granted }
```

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/lifecycle in reference-wit
activate: func(context: activation) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
deactivate: func(reason: deactivation-reason) -> option<list<u8>>;
```

The record `activation` is defined once in the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/#413-lifecycle). It has the fields `plugin`, `api`, `instance`, `side`, `settings-json`, `granted` and `restored`.

`granted` lists the capabilities actually granted, so a plugin can hide features it cannot use. The bytes that `deactivate` returns come back as `restored` on the next activation. Use them to keep state across a restart.

| Reason | When the host sends it |
|---|---|
| `shutdown` | The server or client stops. |
| `disabled` | The user turns the plugin off, or calls `plugins.set-enabled(id, false)`. |
| `upgrade` | An update, a rollback or a dev reload replaces this version. |
| `crash-restart` | Reserved. In the enum but never sent [ABI-028]: a trap drops the instance without a call (see the restart rule below). |
| `revoked` | The user removes a capability. The plugin is activated again with the smaller `granted` list. |
| `granted` | The user adds a capability. The plugin is activated again with the larger `granted` list. |

A client that detaches has no reason of its own. A client instance that loses its connection is deactivated with `shutdown`, and the returned bytes are stored for the next attach.

The time limits are fixed per call. `activate` has 2,000 ms, or 5,000 ms for a bundled plugin (tier T1). `deactivate` has 500 ms, or 1,000 ms for a bundled plugin. If `deactivate` runs past its limit, the host drops the instance and keeps no restore bytes.

### Example 1: lifecycle and handler on the server

This plugin counts the events it receives. It keeps the count across restarts by returning it from `deactivate`. It makes no host calls except `log`, which every plugin may use.

**Grants:** none.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{Activation, DeactivationReason, Handler, Lifecycle};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{log, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Plugin {
    events_seen: u64,
}

impl Lifecycle for Plugin {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if let Some(bytes) = &context.restored {
            if let Ok(array) = <[u8; 8]>::try_from(bytes.as_slice()) {
                self.events_seen = u64::from_le_bytes(array);
            }
        }
        let message = format!("activated {} with {} grants", context.plugin, context.granted.len());
        log(Level::Info, &message);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn deactivate(&mut self, reason: DeactivationReason) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        log(Level::Info, &format!("deactivating: {reason:?}"));
        Some(self.events_seen.to_le_bytes().to_vec())
    }
}

impl Handler for Plugin {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        self.events_seen += batch.len() as u64;
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let eventsSeen = 0;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    if (context.restored) {
      eventsSeen = Number(new TextDecoder().decode(context.restored));
    }
    log('info', `activated ${context.plugin} with ${context.granted.length} grants`);
  },
  deactivate(reason) {
    log('info', `deactivating: ${reason}`);
    return new TextEncoder().encode(String(eventsSeen));
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    eventsSeen += batch.length;
    return [];
  },
});
```

The host calls `activate` first, then `on-events` with the first batch. A `deactivate` with `shutdown` returns the count, and the next `activate` receives those bytes as `restored`.

<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.skeleton --tail 3
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 08:31:02</span> <span class="t-ok">info </span> activated example.skeleton with 2 grants
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 08:31:02</span> <span class="t-dim">debug</span> on-events batch: 3 events, 1 submission
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:45:19</span> <span class="t-ok">info </span> deactivating: shutdown, 0 bytes returned
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> <span class="t-dim">3 lines shown</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The log lines a skeleton plugin writes during one session.

### Example 2: a detector on the server

A detector identifies an agent in a pane's process list, then classifies the pane's screen. This example recognises Codex by its process name. It reports the agent as working while the screen shows the interrupt hint, and as idle otherwise.

**Grants:** `agent.read`, the grant for agent state.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{
    Activation, Classification, Detector, DetectorProcess, DetectorScreen,
    DeactivationReason, Handler, Lifecycle,
};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent::AgentActivity;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["detector"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Plugin;

impl Lifecycle for Plugin {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn deactivate(&mut self, _reason: DeactivationReason) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        None
    }
}

impl Handler for Plugin {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Detector for Plugin {
    fn identify(&mut self, processes: Vec<DetectorProcess>) -> Option<String> {
        processes
            .iter()
            .find(|process| process.name == "codex")
            .map(|_| "codex".to_string())
    }

    fn classify(&mut self, _signature: String, screen: DetectorScreen) -> Classification {
        let working = screen.rows.iter().any(|row| row.contains("esc to interrupt"));
        let activity = if working { AgentActivity::Working } else { AgentActivity::Idle };
        Classification { activity, objective: None, goal: None }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Classification, DetectorProcess, DetectorScreen } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export const { lifecycle, handler, detector } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {},
  deactivate(reason) { return undefined; },
  onEvents(batch) { return []; },
  identify(processes: DetectorProcess[]): string | undefined {
    return processes.some((process) => process.name === 'codex') ? 'codex' : undefined;
  },
  classify(signature: string, screen: DetectorScreen): Classification {
    const working = screen.rows.some((row) => row.includes('esc to interrupt'));
    return { activity: working ? 'working' : 'idle', objective: undefined, goal: undefined };
  },
});
```

A detector has to export `lifecycle` and `handler` as well, because they are required in every server plugin. The `activity` values are the `agent-activity` cases: `none`, `working`, `idle`, `awaiting-approval`, `done` and `menu`. Rust writes them as `AgentActivity::Working`. TypeScript writes the kebab-case string.

<figcaption>Each host trigger calls one export. A trigger for an export the plugin did not declare calls nothing.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Deadlines per export

Each export runs under a deadline. The default is the same for every tier. The value in brackets is the **T1 ceiling**: the most that a bundled plugin may ask for in its manifest `limits`. T2 and T3 ceilings are in [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/), which holds the single call-class table with the breach effect and the failure counting of each row. A batch that contains a `command-invoked` event runs under `command_deadline_ms` (50 ms, T1 ceiling 100 ms) instead of the event deadline.

| Export | Deadline | Breach result |
|---|---|---|
| `lifecycle.activate` | 2,000 ms (5,000 ms) | trap |
| `lifecycle.deactivate` | 500 ms (1,000 ms) | instance dropped, no restore bytes |
| `handler.on-events` | 20 ms (50 ms) | trap |
| `views.render` | 10 ms (20 ms) | trap |
| `annotator.annotate` | 10 ms (20 ms) | late result dropped; the third breach in a row traps |
| `renderer` frame | the frame budget (1,000 ms divided by the effective frame rate, rounded down; 33 ms at 30 fps; `frame_deadline_ms` may raise it to at most 50 ms) | frame skipped; 30 breaches in a row trap |
| `detector.identify` and `detector.classify` | 20 ms (50 ms), key `detector_deadline_ms` | previous classification kept; the third breach in a row traps |
| `lifecycle.migrate` | 30,000 ms (60,000 ms), key `migrate_deadline_ms` | the migration fails, the backup is restored; not a failure |
| `hook-handler.handle-hook` | 20 ms by default, 5 to 50 ms by the manifest `deadline_ms` | counts as `pass`; the third breach in a row disables that extension |
| `service-provider` call | 50 ms (100 ms), key `command_deadline_ms` | trap; the caller's request fails with `internal` |
| `inference-provider.complete` and `models` | 50 ms (100 ms), key `command_deadline_ms` | trap; the request fails with `internal` |
| client-request answer | 5,000 ms request timeout (30,000 ms) | the request completes `failed(timed-out)` |
| `settings-validate` | 100 ms | the save is refused and the previous value kept |
| `catalog-provider.query-catalog` | 20 ms | cached page used, breach counted |
| `menu-provider.menu-items` | 20 ms | static entries only, breach counted |
| `virtual-rows-provider.list-virtual-children` | 20 ms | spinner row stays, breach counted |
| `token-provider.tokens` | 10 ms per call | lines stay plain, host retries |
| `job-runner.run` | 2,000 ms CPU (60,000 ms), 20,000 ms wall (600,000 ms) | `failed(timed-out)` |

<div class="warn">
<p>A Rust panic or a thrown TypeScript exception in on-events or views.render is a trap, and a trap restarts the plugin. In deactivate it drops the instance without counting as a failure. Handle every expected error inside the export and return a value.</p>
</div>

### Errors and restarts

An export can return `plugin-error` only when a caller is waiting for its result. The host passes the error on in these cases:

- `job-runner.run` fails the job request with that error.
- `inference-provider.complete` fails the inference request.
- A deferred `service-provider` reply fails the service call.

Exports with no outcome, such as `handler.on-events`, `views.render` and `deactivate`, cannot return an error. The table shows each failure and whether it counts toward the restart rule.

| Situation | Result | Counts as a failure |
|---|---|---|
| `activate` returns an error | logged at level error with the code and message | yes |
| Trap or deadline breach in `on-events` or `views.render` | the plugin is restarted | yes |
| Trap or deadline breach in `deactivate` | the instance is dropped and no restore bytes are kept | no |
| Restart of a stuck event queue, or death of the sandbox helper during a call | the plugin is restarted | yes |
| Trap in a job instance | `failed(internal)` with the trap text | no |
| Job CPU or wall deadline | `failed(timed-out)` | no |
| Job memory limit | `failed(quota-exceeded)` | no |
| Re-activation for `revoked` or `granted` | the plugin runs with the new grants | no |
| `disabled`, `upgrade` or `shutdown` | the plugin stops | no |

Restart back-off is 1 s after the first failure and 5 s after the second. The third failure inside a sliding window of 10 minutes disables the plugin on that side. The rules are defined once in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart). On the client side each client counts separately, and a failing view counts for the plugin, not for the view.

Two more results apply to a batch. A malformed submission completes as `refused(invalid-argument)`, or `refused(not-permitted)` when its grant is missing. Every other submission in that batch completes as `refused(cancelled)` with the message `batch refused: submission <index>`. A return of more than 256 submissions is a trap.

### What the user sees

<pre class="term">
<span class="t-warn">warn</span> Plugin example.detector stopped after 3 failures in 10 minutes:
      detector.identify trap. Turn it on again in Settings &gt; Plugins.
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The notice shown in the tree footer and in Settings > Plugins after the third failure. The text names the view only when the failing export was `views.render`.

- The plugin's log lines appear in `ilium plugin logs`.
- A disabled plugin stays disabled until the user turns it on in Settings > Plugins. Its contributions are withdrawn and its pending requests are cancelled.
- Turning it on again resets the failure count to zero.

Requirement ids for this page: [RND-001]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).
