### Example 1: suggest tags for a note

A command arrives with the note text in its `arguments-json`, as `{"note": "..."}`. The plugin asks for tags as JSON that matches a small schema, then logs them. The command `com.example.notes/tag-note` is declared in the manifest (see [commands](/pages/api-commands/)).

**Grants:** `inference` on the server side.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;
use serde::Deserialize;

const TAG_SCHEMA: &str = r#"{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": { "tags": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } } },
  "required": ["tags"]
}"#;

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct TagArguments {
    note: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct TagReply {
    tags: Vec<String>,
}

async fn suggest_tags(note: String) -> Vec<String> {
    let request = CompletionRequest {
        messages: vec![
            ChatMessage { role: "system".into(), content: "Reply with tags only.".into() },
            ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: note },
        ],
        max_output_tokens: None,
        json_schema: Some(TAG_SCHEMA.into()),
        purpose: "note-tags".into(),
    };
    match inference::complete(request).await {
        Ok(completion) => serde_json::from_str::<TagReply>(&completion.text)
            .map(|reply| reply.tags)
            .unwrap_or_default(),
        Err(error) => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("note tags failed: {:?}", error.code));
            Vec::new()
        }
    }
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NoteTags;

impl Handler for NoteTags {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, arguments_json, .. }) = event
            else { continue };
            if command != "com.example.notes/tag-note" {
                continue;
            }
            let Ok(arguments) = serde_json::from_str::<TagArguments>(&arguments_json)
            else { continue };
            task::spawn(async move {
                let tags = suggest_tags(arguments.note).await;
                log::log(Level::Info, &format!("note tags: {}", tags.join(", ")));
            });
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type PluginError, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { complete, type CompletionRequest } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const TAG_SCHEMA = JSON.stringify({
  type: 'object',
  properties: { tags: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } },
  required: ['tags'],
});

async function suggestTags(note: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const request: CompletionRequest = {
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: 'Reply with tags only.' },
      { role: 'user', content: note },
    ],
    maxOutputTokens: undefined,
    jsonSchema: TAG_SCHEMA,
    purpose: 'note-tags',
  };
  try {
    const completion = await complete(request);
    return (JSON.parse(completion.text) as { tags: string[] }).tags;
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `note tags failed: ${(error as PluginError).code}`);
    return [];
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.notes/tag-note') {
        continue;
      }
      const { note } = JSON.parse(event.val.argumentsJson) as { note: string };
      void suggestTags(note).then((tags) => log('info', `note tags: ${tags.join(', ')}`));
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The `take_completion` outcome for the example's reply looks like this:

```text
text: {"tags": ["plugins", "api"]}
model: claude-haiku-5-5
input-tokens: 118, output-tokens: 14
```

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs com.example.notes --tail 2
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-12 09:30:12</span> info  note tags: plugins, api
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-12 09:31:40</span> warn  note tags failed: RateLimited
</pre>

The plugin log after one successful tag request and one throttled request. The lines are written by the plugin, so the text is an illustration of the form, not captured output.

### Example 2: list the models and offer them in a picker

The settings page of a plugin shows the models that the provider offers. An empty list means that no provider is selected or that the call failed, so the picker can still open.

**Grants:** `inference` on the client side.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Model names for a settings picker. An empty list means that no provider is selected
/// or that the call failed.
async fn available_models() -> Vec<String> {
    match inference::models().await {
        Ok(models) => models,
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::NotFound => Vec::new(),
        Err(error) => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("model list failed: {:?}", error.code));
            Vec::new()
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { models } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export async function availableModels(): Promise<string[]> {
  try {
    return await models();
  } catch (error) {
    const code = (error as PluginError).code;
    if (code !== 'not-found') {
      log('warn', `model list failed: ${code}`);
    }
    return [];
  }
}
```

### Models as a catalogue

A settings row or a `choice` widget does not need the code above. The host catalogue `ilium.models` lists the configured inference models, and a `choice` takes it as its source with `source: catalog("ilium.models")` (see [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/)). The catalogue needs the `inference` grant, which is the only host catalogue with a grant. A plugin that wants the entries in code reads them with `catalogs.query`, a synchronous call for host catalogues:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::catalogs::{self, CatalogQuery};

fn model_titles() -> Vec<String> {
    let query = CatalogQuery {
        catalog: "ilium.models".into(),
        filter: String::new(),
        cursor: None,
        limit: 64,
    };
    match catalogs::query(&query) {
        Ok(page) => page.items.into_iter().map(|item| item.title).collect(),
        Err(_) => Vec::new(), // not-permitted without `inference`, not-found if absent
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { query } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/catalogs';

export function modelTitles(): string[] {
  try {
    const page = query({ catalog: 'ilium.models', filter: '', cursor: undefined, limit: 64 });
    return page.items.map((item) => item.title);
  } catch {
    return []; // not-permitted without `inference`
  }
}
```

An item whose provider is unavailable carries a `disabled-reason` of at most 40 characters, and the choice dialog shows it. The dialog is the client's value dialog: `●` marks the current option and a disabled option gets the suffix `[unavailable]` with its reason beneath.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Model─────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">● claude-haiku-5-5</span>                       │
│   claude-sonnet-5-5                      │
│   local-qwen [unavailable]               │
│     Unavailable: server offline          │
│ 2 of 3 options · Current: claude-haiku-… │
│ Enter applies · Esc cancels              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A choice dialog over the <code>ilium.models</code> catalogue. The row format, the <code>●</code> marker, the <code>[unavailable]</code> suffix and the two footer lines follow the client's choice dialog (value_dialog.rs). The model names are made up.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Providing models (`inference.provide`)

A plugin that supplies the model answers the calls that the host routes to it. It needs the `inference.provide` grant (without it, install refuses the package, and a declined grant makes the plugin unavailable in Settings). Its manifest lists `inference-provider` in `exports`, not the WIT fragment name. The grant page is [Capability: inference.provide](/pages/capability-inference-provide/).

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inference-provider.complete` (export) | `fn complete(&mut self, call: ProviderCall) -> Result<(), PluginError>` | `complete(call)` | The host asks for one completion. The provider answers later with `provider_reply`. An `Err` fails the caller's request. |
| `inference-provider.models` (export) | `fn models(&mut self) -> Vec<String>` | `models()` | The model names that the provider offers. |
| `inference.provider-reply` (import) | `inference::provider_reply(call, outcome)` | `providerReply(call, outcome)` | Answers one call with a `Completion` or a `PluginError`. |

`ProviderCall` holds `call: u64` (a `bigint` in TypeScript) and the `request: CompletionRequest`. Keep the `call` number and pass it back unchanged.

A provider that also offers embeddings serves them through the same selection; a provider without them makes `vector.embed` fail with `unsupported` (see [vector and embeddings](/pages/api-vector/)).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, Completion, ProviderCall};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["inference-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct LocalModel;

impl InferenceProvider for LocalModel {
    fn complete(&mut self, call: ProviderCall) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let number = call.call;
        let prompt = call.request.messages.last().map(|m| m.content.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
        task::spawn(async move {
            // `run_local_model` is the plugin's own code, for example an http call
            // to a server on the user's machine.
            let outcome = run_local_model(&prompt).await.map(|text| Completion {
                text,
                model: "local-qwen".into(),
                input_tokens: 0,
                output_tokens: 0,
            });
            inference::provider_reply(number, outcome);
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    fn models(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        vec!["local-qwen".into()]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { providerReply, type ProviderCall } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';

export const { lifecycle, handler, inferenceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  complete(call: ProviderCall): void {
    const prompt = call.request.messages.at(-1)?.content ?? '';
    // `runLocalModel` is the plugin's own code.
    void runLocalModel(prompt).then(
      (text) => providerReply(call.call, {
        tag: 'ok',
        val: { text, model: 'local-qwen', inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0 },
      }),
      (error: { code: string; message: string }) => providerReply(call.call, {
        tag: 'err',
        val: { code: error.code, message: error.message, retryAfterMs: undefined },
      }),
    );
  },
  models(): string[] {
    return ['local-qwen'];
  },
});
```

### Errors

Every error is a `plugin-error` with a `code`, a `message` and an optional `retry-after-ms`. Errors from a call that returns a request id are of two kinds. Synchronous errors are returned at once, and nothing is sent. Completion errors arrive later, through the request.

| Code | Returned when | Retry |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | The `inference` grant is declined, the admission policy refuses the `purpose` or the provider, or `provider-reply` runs without `inference.provide`. | No |
| `not-found` | No provider is selected. The call returns at once. For `provider-reply`, the call is unknown, answered or expired. | No |
| `invalid-argument` | No messages, input over 4 MiB, a schema over 64 KiB or not valid JSON, or a reply text over 4 MiB. | No, fix the call |
| `rate-limited` | The admission gate throttles the request to the provider. `retry-after-ms` is set. | Yes, after the delay |
| `timed-out` | The provider does not answer within 120 s. | Yes |
| `network` | The provider cannot be reached, or the connection fails. | Yes |
| `busy` | The plugin already has 64 pending requests. | Yes, later |
| `quota-exceeded` | The CPU budget of the execution group is spent. `retry-after-ms` is set. | Yes, after the delay |
| `cancelled` | The plugin or the host cancelled the request. | No |
| `revoked` | The authorization changed during the call. The plugin is activated again. | No |
| `internal` | A host bug. | No |

A provider's own failure, for example an HTTP error from its service, passes through with the provider's code. Related interfaces use the same codes: `catalogs.query` returns `not-found` for an unknown catalogue and `not-permitted` for `ilium.models` without `inference`, and `vector.embed` returns `unsupported` when the provider has no embeddings.

### Limits

| Limit | Value | Result when exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Messages, all together | 4 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| `json_schema` text | 64 KiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Time to a completion | 120 s | `timed-out` |
| Reply text in `provider-reply` | 4 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Pending requests per plugin (`pending_requests`) | 64 by default | `busy` |
| Catalogue page (`ilium.models`) | 256 items | clamped |

A plugin can raise `pending_requests` in its manifest `limits`. The ceiling is 256 for T1 plugins and 64 for T2 and T3 plugins. The host clamps a higher request to the ceiling and logs it.

### What the user sees

- **Install review.** The review dialog shows the grant as a row of the side that asks. The user can decline it, and a plugin without the grant still installs.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Install com.example.notes 0.1.0───────────────────────────────────╮
│ Example Corp · signed (T2)                                               │
│                                                                          │
│ Client                                                                   │
│ [x] Use your AI model provider ……………………………………………………………… inference        │
│     Requests go to the provider you selected in Settings.                │
│                                                                          │
│   Esc Cancel                                          Enter Install      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The review row for <code>inference</code> in the install dialog, composed by hand from the client's glyphs: rounded border, chrome title, the <code>[x]</code> checkbox and the grey <code>…</code> leader. The wording is the manual's illustration, not a capture.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **Provider choice.** Requests go to the provider that the user selected in Settings (the Inference tab). The plugin cannot choose another one.
- **Privacy log.** Each request that the gate admits adds one line to the privacy log, with the plugin id, the `purpose`, the provider, the model and the token counts. Settings > Privacy shows that log.
- **Plugin log.** The lines that the plugin writes appear in `ilium plugin logs`, as in Example 1.

### Edge cases

- **Declined grant.** `complete` and `models` return `not-permitted`. Keep the feature working without AI, for example by using the first line of a note as its title.
- **Reply that is not JSON.** The host returns the text as the provider sent it. A parse error is the plugin's own problem, so the plugin handles it.
- **Second read.** `take_completion` and `take_models` return the value once.
- **Jobs.** A job instance calls `complete` with the same grant. It waits for the reply with `jobs.wait-request` (see [jobs](/pages/api-jobs/)).
- **Provider grant declined.** A provider plugin whose `inference.provide` grant is declined is never selected, and Settings shows it as unavailable.
- **Provider that never replies.** The caller's request fails with `timed-out` after 120 s. A late `provider-reply` then returns `not-found`.

### Used by

- Automatic pane titles (feature 41) and session naming (feature 42) ask for a short title.
- Smart Copy AI (feature 66) asks for a `json-schema` answer that picks text on screen.
- Tree organisation (feature 43) uses structured output for its suggested moves and names.
- AI triggers (feature 44) run completions on command events.
- The icon picker (feature 20) ranks glyphs by meaning through the embeddings of the same provider.

### See also

- [vector and embeddings](/pages/api-vector/) for `inference.embed` and the host-held index.
- [http](/pages/api-http/) for calls to a provider that a plugin reaches directly. Those calls also pass the admission gate.
- [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/) for the `inference-provider` export that a provider plugin implements.
- [Services](/pages/api-services/) for the `requires.services` rule that makes a plugin wait for a provider.
- [jobs](/pages/api-jobs/) for waiting on a completion inside a job.
- [Capability: inference](/pages/capability-inference/) and [Capability: inference.provide](/pages/capability-inference-provide/) for grant rules.

### Security

Every request is recorded in the privacy log; see [User security and privacy](/pages/user-plugin-security-and-privacy/) ([SEC-264]).

# intents

## intents

An intent is a request that asks the kernel to change something: rename a node, close a pane, type into a terminal, show a notice. A plugin never changes the tree, a pane or a window itself. It returns submissions from `on-events`, or calls `intents.submit` from a timer or request callback. The kernel checks each batch against the plugin's grants, applies the accepted submissions in order, and gives every submission exactly one outcome.

**You need:** the grant listed for each intent in the catalogue below, declared in the manifest for the side that submits it (see [capabilities](/pages/capabilities/)). Results that arrive later come as `request-completed` in [events](/pages/api-events/). In Rust, add the `ilium_plugin` attribute to a struct and implement `Handler` (see [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/)). In TypeScript, export the object from `definePlugin` (see [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/)).

### Interface

The records, the outcome and the submit function, as declared in WIT:

```wit
record submission { intent: intent, correlation: u64, dedup-key: option<string> }
variant request-ref { submission(u64), call(request-id) }
variant outcome {
  ok, ok-node(node-id), duplicate(request-ref), refused(plugin-error),
  failed(plugin-error), cancelled,
  ok-epoch(u64),   // send-input on an agent pane, the new prompt epoch
}
record request-result { request: request-ref, outcome: outcome }

submit: func(submission: submission) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
```

The intent variant has one case per catalogue row. A case with one value carries that value. A case with several fields carries a record named `<case>-spec`:

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/intents in reference-wit
variant intent {
  rename-node(rename-node-spec),
  move-node(move-node-spec),
  close-node(node-id),
  set-node-locked(set-node-locked-spec),
  create-pane(create-pane-spec),
  signal-pane(signal-pane-spec),
  send-input(send-input-spec),
  agent-action(agent-action-spec),
  set-decoration(set-decoration-spec),
  clear-decoration(decoration-key),
  set-virtual-rows(set-virtual-rows-spec),
  play-sound(string),
  notify(notify-spec),
  open-view(open-view-spec),
  close-view(view-target),
  invoke-command(invoke-command-spec),
  message(message-spec),
  editor-apply-edits(editor-apply-edits-spec),
  editor-open(editor-open-spec),
  // appended in this order
  freeze-pane(freeze-pane-spec),
  unfreeze-pane(freeze-pane-spec),
  replace-pane-command(replace-pane-command-spec),
  terminate-pane-process(terminate-pane-process-spec),
  resize-pane(resize-pane-spec),
  create-group(create-group-spec),
  create-folder(create-folder-spec),
  create-project(create-project-spec),
  create-split(create-split-spec),
  set-bookmarked(set-bookmarked-spec),
  set-expanded(set-expanded-spec),
  restructure(restructure-spec),
  revert-restructure(u64),
  set-inferred-icon(set-inferred-icon-spec),
  mark-attention(mark-attention-spec),
  ack-attention(node-id),
  open-external(open-external-spec),
  set-status-segment(set-status-segment-spec),
  clear-status-segment(string),
  set-frame-slot(set-frame-slot-spec),
  clear-frame-slot(clear-frame-slot-spec),
  toast(toast-spec),
  dismiss-toast(string),
}
```

New cases are only ever appended, so existing plugins keep decoding. The record names follow the same `<case>-spec` rule; the fields of each record are the payload columns of the tables below. A case with exactly one value carries that value, (`revert-restructure` carries the token, `dismiss-toast` the toast id).

Import paths:

- Rust: `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission}` and `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::intents::submit`. The prelude (`use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;`) also brings in `Intent`, `Submission`, `Outcome` and `RequestRef`.
- TypeScript: `Submission` and `Intent` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types`, and `submit` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/intents`.

`submit` returns a `request-id` at once. Its completion arrives later as `request-completed`, with `request-ref` set to `call(<request-id>)`. Use it only from timers and request callbacks. Inside `on-events`, return submissions instead.

### Batches

- `on-events` returns a list of `Submission` values. The kernel checks the batch against the grants and applies the submissions in order.
- A node removed by an earlier submission in the same batch makes a later submission on that node fail with `failed(not-found)`.
- A return of more than 256 submissions traps the plugin. None of them is applied.
- A batch is refused as a whole in two cases, both checked over the whole list in index order before any effect: a malformed submission (shape, then a missing or malformed dedup key), and a missing grant. The lowest-index offender gets `refused(invalid-argument)` or `refused(not-permitted)` (shape before grant inside one submission). Every other submission gets `refused(cancelled)`. All carry the message `batch refused: submission <index>`, with the 0-based index of the offender. Nothing is half applied and no dedup key is reserved.
- Every other check is per submission. A missing target, a payload value that is well formed but invalid (for example a text node id), a stale revision or a rate limit affects only its own submission.
- `correlation` is a number the plugin chooses. It is returned as `request-ref` `submission(<correlation>)` in `request-completed`. Plugin numbers stay below 2^63. `Submission::new` in Rust takes the next SDK number, which starts at 2^63.

### Functions

| Function | Signature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `intents.submit` | `submit(submission) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>` | Queues one submission from a timer or request callback. Errors: `invalid-argument` for a malformed submission or a missing mandatory key, `not-permitted` at once when the grant is missing, `rate-limited`. The completion carries `submission(correlation)` from the submission passed in. The returned request id is informational and never appears in a completion. |

Rust: `host::intents::submit(submission)` returns `Result<RequestId, PluginError>`. TypeScript: `submit(submission)` returns the request id as `bigint` and throws `PluginError`.

### Dedup keys

A submission may carry a `dedup-key`. The rules:

- Format: 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:`, `/` and `-`. Any other character makes the submission malformed.
- Scope: the pair (plugin id, key), at the kernel that applies the intent. The server and each client keep separate tables.
- Window: 10 minutes from the moment the key is reserved.
- Duplicate: a submission with a reserved key completes as `duplicate(<original>)` and has no effect. `original` is the `request-ref` of the submission that reserved the key.
- A key is reserved only after every acceptance check passes. A refused submission keeps its key free, so a retry with the same key after fixing the cause is valid. A submission that was accepted keeps its key even if it later fails. Retry a failed action with a new key.
- `send-input` and `agent-action` require a key. Without one, the batch is refused. The kernel journals these keys before the write, for 24 hours or 4,096 entries per session, whichever is smaller. A restart therefore does not repeat the input.

The SDK helper `dedup::key_for(&["finish", &node.to_string()])` joins its parts with `:` and replaces disallowed characters with `-`. TypeScript plugins write the key string directly.

### Intent catalogue

| Intent | Payload | Grant | Outcome, beyond `ok` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rename-node` | `node: node-id`, `title: string` | `tree.write` | `refused(conflict)` when the user named the node by hand and the plugin is a titler; `refused(not-found)` |
| `move-node` | `node`, `target: node-id`, `placement` (before, after, inside-first, inside-last) | `tree.write` | `refused(invalid-argument)` when the target is inside the moved node |
| `close-node` | `node` | `tree.write` | `refused(conflict)` on a locked node |
| `set-node-locked` | `node`, `locked: bool` | `tree.write` | `refused(not-found)` |
| `create-pane` | `parent: option<node-id>`, `title`, `content-kind: string`, `cwd: option<fs-path>`, `command: option<list<string>>`, `initial-input: option<string>` | `panes.create`, plus `terminal.write` when `initial-input` is set | `ok-node(node-id)`; `refused(not-found)` for a missing parent or `cwd`; `failed(not-found)` for a missing program; `failed(io)` on spawn failure |
| `signal-pane` | `pane: node-id`, `signal` (interrupt, terminate, kill, hangup) | `panes.signal` | `refused(not-found)` with no running process; `refused(pane-not-ready)` on a restored pane |
| `send-input` | `pane: node-id`, `text: string`, `delivery` (typed, submitted, pasted), `prompt-epoch: option<u64>`, key required | `terminal.write` | `refused(pane-not-ready)`; `refused(conflict)` on a stale epoch; `refused(rate-limited)` |
| `agent-action` | `pane: node-id`, `action-id: string`, key required | `agent.control` | `refused(unsupported)` when the signature has no such action; `refused(conflict)` when the activity is not allowed |
| `set-decoration` | `node`, `slot: string`, `content: styled-text`, `icon: option<string>`, `sort-key: option<s64>`, `persist: bool` | `tree.decorate` | `refused(invalid-argument)` for an undeclared slot; `refused(quota-exceeded)` |
| `clear-decoration` | `node`, `slot` | `tree.decorate` | `refused(invalid-argument)` for an undeclared slot |
| `set-virtual-rows` | `row-kind: string`, `rows: list<virtual-row>` (id, label, icon, command) | `tree.decorate` | `refused(invalid-argument)` for an undeclared row kind |
| `play-sound` | sound id: `string` | `sound.play` | `refused(not-found)` for an id outside the catalogue; `refused(rate-limited)` |
| `notify` | `title`, `body`, `urgency` (low, normal, high), `sound: option<string>` | `notify.desktop` | `refused(rate-limited)` |
| `open-view` | `view-target`, `focus: bool` | `ui.panels` | `refused(not-found)` for an undeclared view |
| `close-view` | `view-target` | `ui.panels` | none beyond the universal codes |
| `invoke-command` | `command: string`, `arguments-json: string` | `commands.invoke:<pattern>` | `ok` once the command has run; `refused(not-found)`; the command's own `failed` code; `failed(timed-out)` after 30 s |
| `message` | `to: string` (plugin id), `channel: string`, `payload: list<u8>` | `messages.peer:<plugin-id>` | `ok` when queued; `refused(not-found)` when the target is not installed; `refused(invalid-argument)` over 1 MiB |
| `editor-apply-edits` | `buffer`, `base-revision: u64`, `edits: list<text-edit>` | `editor.edit` | `refused(conflict)` on a stale revision; `refused(invalid-argument)` for overlapping edits |
| `editor-open` | `path: fs-path`, `line: option<u32>`, `placement` (new-pane, split, replace) | `editor.edit` and `fs.read` for the path | `ok-node(node-id)`; `failed(not-found)`; `failed(io)` |

`send-input` and `set-decoration` also accept the optional fields listed under "Further intents and extended intents" below.

Every intent can also return `refused(not-permitted)` when its grant is missing. Its submission gets that code, and the other submissions in the batch get `refused(cancelled)`.

### Which side applies an intent

The tree, the panes and the terminals live in the session server. A plugin half in a client therefore cannot apply most intents itself. The client forwards them to the server and the outcome returns to the client that submitted them.

| Intents | Applied by | Path from a client plugin |
|---|---|---|
| `rename-node`, `move-node`, `close-node`, `set-node-locked`, `set-bookmarked`, `set-expanded` | Server | Forwarded |
| `create-pane`, `signal-pane`, `freeze-pane`, `unfreeze-pane`, `replace-pane-command`, `terminate-pane-process`, `resize-pane` | Server | Forwarded |
| `create-group`, `create-folder`, `create-project`, `create-split`, `restructure`, `revert-restructure` | Server | Forwarded |
| `send-input`, `agent-action` | Server | Forwarded; a dedup key is required |
| `set-decoration`, `clear-decoration`, `set-virtual-rows`, `set-inferred-icon`, `mark-attention`, `ack-attention` | Server | Forwarded; the server replicates the result to every client |
| `notify`, `play-sound` | Server (desktop and sound queue) | Forwarded |
| `message` | Server routes it to the peer side | Forwarded |
| `invoke-command` | The side that registered the command | Forwarded when the command is a server command |
| `open-view`, `close-view`, `toast`, `dismiss-toast`, `set-status-segment`, `clear-status-segment`, `set-frame-slot`, `clear-frame-slot`, `open-external` | The client kernel of the submitting plugin half | Applied locally; nothing is forwarded |
| `editor-apply-edits`, `editor-open` | The client kernel that holds the buffer | Applied locally |

A server plugin submits all of these to the server directly. The chrome intents of a server plugin are applied by the server and replicated to every client as retained contributions. A client plugin's chrome intents change only that client.

For a forwarded intent:

- The outcome returns only to the client that submitted it, as `request-completed`.
- The tree change that the intent caused reaches that client before the outcome (see [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/)).
- The added latency is 3 ms at the 99th percentile on a local connection (benchmark B15).
- If the client is detached, the submission waits in a queue of 256. The 257th queued submission completes as `refused(busy)` at once, and submissions still queued when the client exits complete as `cancelled`.

- **[HST-490]** Every intent MUST be applied by exactly one side as listed above, and an intent applied by the server MUST be forwarded when the submitter is a client plugin half.
- **[HST-491]** The outcome of a forwarded submission MUST be delivered only to the submitting client.
- **[HST-492]** The added latency of a forwarded submission MUST be at most 3 ms at the 99th percentile on an idle local connection (B15).

### Send-input check order

For `send-input`, two checks run at batch level before the list below, over the whole batch: shape (key present, total text across all stages at most 65,536 bytes, otherwise `invalid-argument`) and the grant `terminal.write` (otherwise `not-permitted`). The kernel then checks each submission in this order. `agent-action` uses the same order, with its own grant. The first failing check decides the outcome.

1. Dedup key. A reserved key gives `duplicate(<original>)`.
2. The pane exists and is a terminal pane. Otherwise `not-found` or `unsupported`.
3. The pane is restored, which means its process has started. Otherwise `pane-not-ready`.
4. The rate limit has room: 20 per second per pane and plugin. Otherwise `rate-limited`.
5. The epoch, if given, equals the pane's current prompt epoch. Otherwise `conflict`.
6. The `if-current` precondition, if given, matches the pane. Otherwise `conflict` with the message `precondition: <field>`.
7. No other plugin holds the input lock of the pane. Otherwise `conflict` with the message `input-locked`.
8. The input is accepted: the key is reserved, the rate token is taken and the text is written. A refused attempt never takes a rate token.

`agent-action` is refused with `conflict` and the message `agent is working` while the agent is working. By default an action is allowed in the `idle`, `done`, `awaiting-approval` and `menu` states, unless its signature says otherwise.

### Limits

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Submissions per `on-events` return | 256; more traps |
| `send-input` text | 64 KiB |
| `message` payload | 1 MiB |
| `invoke-command` `arguments-json` | one JSON object, at most 64 KiB |
| `notify` rate | 6 per minute per plugin |
| `toast` rate | 3 per 10 s per plugin (`rate-limited`) |
| `set-status-segment`, `set-frame-slot` rate | 10 per second per slot |
| `restructure` operations | 256 |
| `send-input` stages and total stage delay | 16 and 10 s |
| `send-input` `raw` bytes | 64 KiB |
| Input lock | 2 s; one lock per pane |
| `terminate-pane-process` `grace-ms` | at most 10,000 |
| Decoration frames, frame time | 2 to 16, at least 90 ms |
| `toast` title, body, actions | 60, 200 characters, 2 |
| `mark-attention` reason | 80 characters |
| `play-sound` rate | 4 per second per plugin |
| `send-input` rate | 20 per second per pane and plugin |
| Dedup window | 10 minutes |

### Example: rename a pane when its agent finishes (Rust)

This server-side plugin renames the pane when its agent reaches `done`. The key stops a repeated `done` from renaming the pane again within 10 minutes. The plugin logs any refused outcome from the next batch. The manifest grants `tree.write` to the server side.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::dedup;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::RenameNodeSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct FinishTitler;

impl Handler for FinishTitler {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. })
                    if current == AgentActivity::Done =>
                {
                    let spec = RenameNodeSpec { node, title: "Agent finished".to_string() };
                    let key = dedup::key_for(&["finished", &node.to_string()]);
                    submissions.push(Submission::keyed(Intent::RenameNode(spec), key));
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(result) => {
                    if let Outcome::Refused(error) = result.outcome {
                        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("rename refused: {}", error.message));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

### Example: open a panel and notify once (TypeScript)

This client-side plugin opens its status panel when the user runs its command. It sends a notice with a key, so a second run within 10 minutes opens the panel again but shows no second notice. The manifest grants `ui.panels` and `notify.desktop` on the client side.

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const STATUS_COMMAND = 'com.example.notes/open-status';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate(context) {
    log('info', `ready in ${context.plugin}`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === STATUS_COMMAND) {
        submissions.push({
          intent: { tag: 'open-view', val: { view: { tag: 'panel', val: 'status' }, focus: true } },
          correlation: 1n,
          dedupKey: undefined,
        });
        submissions.push({
          intent: {
            tag: 'notify',
            val: { title: 'Status', body: 'Panel opened', urgency: 'low', sound: undefined },
          },
          correlation: 2n,
          dedupKey: 'status:opened',
        });
      }
      if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && event.val.outcome.tag === 'refused') {
        log('warn', 'an intent was refused; the outcome names the reason');
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

### Further intents and extended intents

The contract has 23 further intent cases and extends 5 existing ones. The batch rule, the dedup rule and the outcome rules above apply unchanged. `restructure` is atomic inside the batch. Four deep pages cover the groups: [send-input stages](/pages/api-intent-send-input/), [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-intent-pane-lifecycle/), [tree structure and restructure](/pages/api-intent-tree-structure/) and [toast, status segments and open-external](/pages/api-intent-chrome/).

The new outcome case is `ok-epoch(u64)`. `send-input` returns it on an agent pane, carrying the pane's new prompt epoch. A plugin that tests only for `ok` still works through the SDK: `is_ok()` in Rust and `isOk()` in TypeScript are true for both `ok` and `ok-epoch`.

**Rust**

```rust
match result.outcome {
    Outcome::OkEpoch(epoch) => self.prompt_epoch.insert(pane, epoch),
    outcome if outcome.is_ok() => None,
    Outcome::Refused(error) | Outcome::Failed(error) => {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{}: {}", error.code, error.message));
        None
    }
    _ => None,
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const { outcome } = event.val;
if (outcome.tag === 'ok-epoch') {
  promptEpochs.set(pane, outcome.val);           // bigint
} else if (outcome.tag === 'refused' || outcome.tag === 'failed') {
  log('warn', `${outcome.val.code}: ${outcome.val.message}`);
}
```

#### Pane lifecycle (grant `panes.lifecycle`, high risk, server only)

| Intent | Payload | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `freeze-pane` | `pane` | `ok`; the process is stopped (SIGSTOP on Unix), output stops, the pane shows the frozen mark; `refused(unsupported)` on Windows |
| `unfreeze-pane` | `pane` | `ok`; `refused(conflict)` when the pane is not frozen |
| `replace-pane-command` | `pane`, `command: list<string>`, `cwd: option<fs-path>`, `keep-scrollback: bool` | `ok` once the new process runs; the durable resume binding stays with the kernel |
| `terminate-pane-process` | `pane`, `grace-ms: u32` (at most 10,000) | `ok` when the process has exited; the pane stays open with its exit status |
| `resize-pane` | `pane`, `columns: option<u16>`, `rows: option<u16>` | `ok`; `refused(conflict)` when the layout cannot give the size, and the message names the limiting neighbour |

#### Tree structure and attention (grants `tree.restructure`, `tree.write`, `tree.decorate`, `tree.attention`)

| Intent | Payload | Grant | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create-group` | `parent`, `title`, `placement`, `children: list<node-id>` | `tree.restructure` | `ok-node` |
| `create-folder` | `parent`, `title`, `path: option<fs-path>` | `tree.restructure` | `ok-node` |
| `create-project` | `title`, `root: fs-path` | `tree.restructure` | `ok-node` |
| `create-split` | `panes: list<node-id>` (2 to 4), `direction` | `tree.restructure` | `ok-node` (the split container) |
| `set-bookmarked` | `node`, `bookmarked: bool` | `tree.write` | `ok` |
| `set-expanded` | `node` or `virtual-row: string`, `expanded: bool` | `tree.write` for nodes, own `virtual_rows` for rows | `ok` |
| `restructure` | `operations: list<restructure-op>` (move, create-group, ungroup, rename; at most 256), `label: string` | `tree.restructure` | `ok-node` carrying an undo token (0 when none); all or nothing: one failing operation refuses the whole intent with `refused(conflict)` and the operation index in the message |
| `revert-restructure` | `token: u64` | `tree.restructure` | `ok`; `refused(conflict)` when a later change touched the same nodes |
| `set-inferred-icon` | `node`, `icon: option<string>` (catalogue id or glyph), `source: string` | `tree.decorate` | `ok`; a manual icon wins (`refused(conflict)`) |
| `mark-attention` | `node`, `reason: string` (at most 80) | `tree.attention` | `ok`; the attention policy (done prefix, sound) stays with the kernel |
| `ack-attention` | `node` | `tree.attention` | `ok` |

#### Chrome and feedback (grants `open-external`, `ui.chrome`, `notify.toast`)

| Intent | Payload | Grant | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open-external` | `target`: `url(string)`, `file(fs-path)` or `settings(string)` for `ilium://settings/...` | `open-external` | `ok` after the desktop handler started; `refused(not-permitted)` when the user declines; only `http`, `https` and `mailto` URLs |
| `set-status-segment` | `segment` (own `status_segments` id), `content: rich-text`, `tooltip: option<tooltip>`, `tone: option<tone>` | `ui.chrome` | `ok`; at most 10 per second per segment |
| `clear-status-segment` | `segment` | `ui.chrome` | `ok` |
| `set-frame-slot` | `pane`, `slot` (own `pane_frame_slots` id), `content: rich-text`, `icon: option<string>`, `tooltip` | `ui.chrome` | `ok`; `refused(invalid-argument)` when the pane does not match the slot's `applies_to` |
| `clear-frame-slot` | `pane`, `slot` | `ui.chrome` | `ok` |
| `toast` | `id: option<string>`, `tone`, `title` (60), `body: option<rich-text>` (200 characters), `actions: list<toast-action>` (2), `duration-ms: option<u32>` | `notify.toast` | `ok`; 3 per 10 s per plugin (`rate-limited`); a shown `id` is replaced |
| `dismiss-toast` | `id` | `notify.toast` | `ok` |

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/intents in reference-wit
record toast-action { label: string, command: string }
```

#### Extended intents

The extended intents add optional fields. A submission that leaves them out behaves as it does without them.

| Intent | New fields | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `send-input` | `stages`, `raw`, `mouse`, `if-current`, `lock-user-input`, `journal` | The check order is the one above. `refused(conflict)` names the failed precondition. See [send-input stages](/pages/api-intent-send-input/). |
| `set-decoration` | `spans: option<rich-text>`, `tooltip: option<tooltip>`, `frames: list<styled-text>` (2 to 16), `frame-ms: u16` (at least 90), `trailing: bool`, `visibility` (`always`, `on-hover`), `tone` | The host steps the frames with no plugin call. Reduced motion shows the first frame. See [toast, status segments and open-external](/pages/api-intent-chrome/). |
| `rename-node` | `source` (`plugin`, `inferred`), `expected-revision: option<u64>` | A stale revision is `refused(conflict)`. An `inferred` title never replaces a manual one. |
| `notify` | `coalesce-key: option<string>`, `coalesce-window-ms: u32` (at most 60,000) | Notifications with the same key inside the window replace each other. |
| `set-virtual-rows` | rows gain `parent: option<string>`, `expandable`, `accepts-drop`, `tooltip`, `label: rich-text`, `trailing` | Kinds declared with `children: "provider"` ask the provider export instead (see [plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/)). |

#### Error codes of the further intents

No error code was added: the intents reuse the 15 codes of the error model. Beyond the universal codes (`not-permitted`, `invalid-argument`, `cancelled`), these arise:

| Code | Intents and cause |
|---|---|
| `unsupported` | `freeze-pane` on Windows; `send-input` `mouse` while mouse reporting is off |
| `conflict` | `unfreeze-pane` on a pane that is not frozen; `resize-pane` the layout cannot satisfy; `restructure` with a failing operation (index in the message); `revert-restructure` after a later change; `set-inferred-icon` and `rename-node` against a manual value or a stale revision; `send-input` with a failed `if-current` or a held input lock |
| `invalid-argument` | more than 16 stages, more than 10 s of delay, more than 64 KiB of `raw`, a lock over 2 s, more than 256 operations, frames outside 2 to 16 or under 90 ms, a slot whose `applies_to` does not match |
| `rate-limited` | `toast`, `set-status-segment`, `set-frame-slot`, with `retry-after-ms` |
| `not-permitted` | a missing grant, or `open-external` declined by the user |
| `pane-not-ready` | `send-input` and the lifecycle intents on a restored pane that has not started |
| `not-found` | a node, pane, slot or segment that does not exist or is not the plugin's own |

#### Example: freeze a pane, then show a toast (Rust and TypeScript)

This server-side plugin freezes a runaway terminal and tells the user how to resume it. It holds `panes.lifecycle` on the server side and `notify.toast` where the toast is shown. The freeze carries a key, so a repeated command does not freeze twice. The toast `id` makes a second toast replace the first.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{FreezePaneSpec, ToastSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Tone;

fn freeze_and_tell(pane: NodeId) -> Vec<Submission> {
    vec![
        Submission::keyed(Intent::FreezePane(FreezePaneSpec { pane }), format!("freeze-{pane}")),
        Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
            id: Some("frozen".into()),
            tone: Tone::Warning,
            title: "Pane frozen".into(),
            body: None,
            actions: vec![],
            duration_ms: Some(5_000),
        })),
    ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function freezeAndTell(pane: bigint): Submission[] {
  return [
    { intent: { tag: 'freeze-pane', val: { pane } }, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: `freeze-${pane}` },
    {
      intent: {
        tag: 'toast',
        val: { id: 'frozen', tone: 'warning', title: 'Pane frozen', body: undefined, actions: [], durationMs: 5000 },
      },
      correlation: 2n,
      dedupKey: undefined,
    },
  ];
}
```

The log of the test harness for this batch, when the pane is already frozen:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin test ./freezer --fixture freeze-twice.json
<span class="t-ok">{"type":"outcome","i":0,"intent":"freeze-pane","outcome":"ok"}</span>
<span class="t-ok">{"type":"outcome","i":1,"intent":"toast","outcome":"ok"}</span>
{"type":"outcome","i":2,"intent":"freeze-pane","outcome":"duplicate(0)"}
<span class="t-ok">{"type":"outcome","i":3,"intent":"toast","outcome":"ok"}</span>
<span class="t-dim">{"type":"summary","ok":3,"duplicate":1,"refused":0}</span>

Illustrative, not generated: the JSONL form follows the harness output of the example earlier on this page; the fixture delivers the command twice.

### Edge cases and errors

- `refused(pane-not-ready)` means a restored pane has not started its process yet. Retry after `pane-created` or `tree-changed` for that pane.
- `refused(rate-limited)` always carries `retry-after-ms`. Wait that long before retrying.
- `refused(conflict)` means the state changed. Read the current state, then submit again. A refused submission keeps its key free, so the same key is valid for the retry.
- `failed(timed-out)` on `invoke-command` means the command did not reply within 30 seconds. The command may still finish later, so check its effect before a retry.
- `cancelled` means another submission in the same batch was refused. Fix the refused one, then resubmit the whole group.
- `duplicate(<original>)` is not an error. It confirms that an earlier submission with the same key already took effect.
- A trap ends the plugin instance. The kernel restarts it under the restart rule in [errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

### What the user sees

- A rename, a decoration or a closed node changes the tree at once. A badge is at most 12 cells wide. Longer text is cut and ends with `…`.
- `send-input` types into the pane as if the user typed the text. `submitted` also presses the submit keys of the pane's signature, which default to a carriage return. `pasted` uses bracketed paste when the program enables it.
- `notify` shows a desktop notification. When an attached client reports that the pane the notice is about has focus, the notice appears in the client footer instead.
- A refused outcome is silent to the user. Only the plugin sees it, in its log or in its own state. Use the test harness in [testing](/pages/testing/) to see outcomes before you ship.

<pre class="term">$ ilium plugin test ./titler --fixture done.json
<span class="t-hi">{"type":"submission","i":0,"intent":"rename-node"}</span>
<span class="t-ok">{"type":"outcome","i":0,"outcome":"ok"}</span>
<span class="t-hi">{"type":"submission","i":1,"intent":"rename-node"}</span>
{"type":"outcome","i":1,"outcome":"duplicate(submission(0))"}
<span class="t-dim">{"type":"summary","ok":1,"duplicate":1,"refused":0}</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated: the JSONL that `ilium plugin test` prints for the Rust example when its fixture delivers the same `done` event twice.

### Units and conventions

Times are `epoch-ms` (`u64`, milliseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC) and durations are milliseconds. Correlation numbers below 2^63 belong to the plugin and the rest to the SDK. A limit in characters counts Unicode scalar values. The rules are stated once in the [conventions of the WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/#2-conventions).

# jobs

## jobs

A job is work that runs in the background, away from the plugin's event handler. The plugin starts a job with a kind and an input of bytes. The host runs the plugin's `job-runner` export in a second instance of the same component, in its own memory, under a CPU deadline, a wall-clock deadline and a memory limit. The plugin then reads the output, watches the progress, or cancels the job.

Use a job for work that takes longer than the event deadline of 20 ms: parsing a large file, searching a workspace, calling a model and waiting for its answer, or building an export. Short work that finishes in a few milliseconds needs no job.

**You will need:** the `jobs.run` grant, one `contributes.jobs` entry for each job kind, and `job-runner` in the `exports` list of the side that runs the job (see [exports](/pages/api-exports/)). The `job-runner` export exists in the server world, the client world and the animation world, so a job can belong to any side. Any import the job calls, such as `fs.read` or `inference`, needs its grant on that same side. The grant page is [Capability: jobs.run](/pages/capability-jobs-run/).

### Interface

```wit
// jobs (S C A, grant jobs.run)
start: func(kind: string, input: list<u8>) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
cancel: func(job: request-id);
take-output: func(job: request-id) -> option<list<u8>>;
// callable only inside job-runner.run:
report-progress: func(percent: f32);
is-cancelled: func() -> bool;
wait-request: func(request: request-id, timeout-millis: u32) -> result<_, plugin-error>;

// job-runner (export of S C A, fragment with-jobs)
run: func(kind: string, input: list<u8>) -> result<list<u8>, plugin-error>;
```

The SDK imports are `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::jobs` in Rust and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs` in TypeScript (see [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) and [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/)).

The SDK names of the calls on this page, including the `_request` / `Request` starting forms and the `_json` / `Json` names, follow [Wrapper names in the SDKs](/pages/reference-wit/#wrapper-names-in-the-sdks).

### Surface

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Grant | Call | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | `jobs::start(kind, input).await` returns `Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError>`. The raw form `jobs::start_request` returns `Result<RequestId, PluginError>`. | `await start(kind, input)` returns `Promise<Uint8Array>`. The raw form `startRequest` returns `bigint`. | `jobs.run` | async | Starts a job of a declared kind. The awaited form resolves with the output. |
| `cancel` | `jobs::cancel(job)` | `cancel(job)` | `jobs.run` | sync | Asks the job to stop. See cancellation below. |
| `take-output` | `jobs::take_output(job)` returns `Option<Vec<u8>>` | `takeOutput(job)` returns `Uint8Array \| undefined` | `jobs.run` | sync | Returns the output bytes once. |
| `report-progress` | `jobs::report_progress(percent)` takes `f32` | `reportProgress(percent)` | inside `run` only | sync | Reports a percentage from 0 to 100. |
| `is-cancelled` | `jobs::is_cancelled()` returns `bool` | `isCancelled()` | inside `run` only | sync | Returns true after a cancel. |
| `wait-request` | `jobs::wait_request(request, timeout_millis)` returns `Result<(), PluginError>` | `waitRequest(request, timeoutMillis)` | inside `run` only | blocks | Waits until a slow call completes, so the job can start a call and then take its result. |

The `job-runner` export has one function, `run(kind, input)`. In Rust it is `JobRunner::run(&mut self, kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError>`. In TypeScript it is the `run` member of `definePlugin`. It returns a `Uint8Array` or throws a `PluginError`.

The JSON helpers `jobs::start_json(kind, &value)` in Rust and `startJson(kind, value)` in TypeScript encode a value as JSON bytes. The job decodes the bytes itself.

### What a job instance can call

A job instance is not activated. Its `activate` never runs and it has no event handler. It may call `log`, `clock`, `codec`, `fs`, `http`, `process`, `inference`, `storage.get`, `storage.keys`, `report-progress`, `is-cancelled` and `wait-request`, with the grants of its side. Every other import, including `jobs.start`, returns `unsupported`. Imports without a result do nothing.

The host keeps a pool of job instances for each plugin, at most `concurrent_jobs`, and reuses them between jobs. A job never shares memory with the instance that started it, so the only data that cross are the input bytes, the output bytes and the progress value.

### Manifest and limits

Declare each kind in `contributes.jobs`. `deadline_ms` is the CPU deadline and `memory_mib` the memory limit. Both are optional.

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "jobs": [{ "kind": "export-pdf", "deadline_ms": 60000, "memory_mib": 256 }]
  }
}
```

A value above the tier ceiling is clamped and logged. The CPU deadline counts CPU time only, so time spent in `wait-request` counts only against the wall-clock limit.

| Limit | Default | Ceiling T1 | Ceiling T2 and T3 | Over the limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPU deadline (`deadline_ms`) | 2,000 ms | 60,000 ms | 10,000 ms | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Wall-clock deadline | 20,000 ms | 600,000 ms | 100,000 ms | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Memory (`memory_mib`) | 64 MiB | 512 MiB | 256 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| Input, and output, each | 16 MiB | 64 MiB | 16 MiB | Input: `invalid-argument` at the call. Output: `failed(invalid-argument)`. |
| Concurrent jobs | 2 | 8 | 2 | Extra jobs wait in the queue. |
| Queued jobs | 16 | 64 | 16 | `busy` |
| Finished result held | 30 s | 30 s | 30 s | `take-output` returns `none` |

<figcaption>Solid arrows are calls, dashed arrows are returns and events. A cancel is optional; when it comes, the outcome is cancelled whatever the job returns.</figcaption>
</figure>

- `start` returns a request id at once. A job waits in the queue while the concurrency limit is full.
- While the job runs, `job-progress` events arrive with the request id (`job`) and the `percent` (`f32`). Delivery is coalesced by job: only the newest value per job reaches the plugin in one batch. The event needs no grant beyond `jobs.run`.
- When the job ends, `request-completed` arrives with an outcome: `ok`, `cancelled` or `failed(code)`.
- `take-output` returns the bytes once. The kernel holds a finished result for 30 s or until it is taken. A later take returns `none`, which the SDK reports as `not-found`.

`report-progress` clamps a value below 0 to 0 and a value above 100 to 100. A NaN value is ignored.

**Cancellation.** `cancel` sets a flag and returns at once. It returns nothing: cancelling a completed, unknown or already cancelled job is a silent no-op and produces no further completion. The job sees the flag through `is-cancelled` and should return early. Once a cancel is requested, the outcome is `cancelled`, whatever the job returns or whichever deadline it reaches, and the output is dropped. A queued job that is cancelled never starts. Cancelling a finished job does nothing. When the plugin is disabled, its pending jobs are cancelled. When a plugin restarts after a trap, jobs started by the earlier instance are cancelled as well.

### Example 1: a cancellable PDF export

The example exports one cancellable PDF job on the server side. The command `com.example.notes/export-pdf` starts the job, `com.example.notes/cancel-export` stops it, and a desktop notice reports the result. Both command ids are declared under `contributes.commands`. The helpers `read_notebook`, `split_pages` and `render_page` are the plugin's own code.

Manifest excerpt:

```json
{
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["job-runner"]
  },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["jobs.run", "notify.desktop"] },
  "contributes": { "jobs": [{ "kind": "export-pdf", "deadline_ms": 60000, "memory_mib": 256 }] }
}
```

**Grants:** `jobs.run`, `notify.desktop`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::jobs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{NotifySpec, Urgency};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::requests::RequestResult;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["job-runner"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesExport {
    job: Option<RequestId>,
}

impl Lifecycle for NotesExport {} // the default methods are enough

impl Handler for NotesExport {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, .. }) => {
                    if command == "com.example.notes/export-pdf" && self.job.is_none() {
                        match jobs::start_request("export-pdf", &read_notebook()) {
                            Ok(job) => self.job = Some(job),
                            Err(error) => submissions.push(notice(&error.message)),
                        }
                    } else if command == "com.example.notes/cancel-export" {
                        if let Some(job) = self.job {
                            jobs::cancel(job);
                        }
                    }
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(RequestResult { request: RequestRef::Call(job), outcome })
                    if self.job == Some(job) =>
                {
                    self.job = None;
                    let body = match outcome {
                        Outcome::Ok => {
                            let size = jobs::take_output(job).map_or(0, |pdf| pdf.len());
                            format!("PDF ready, {size} bytes")
                        }
                        Outcome::Cancelled => "Export cancelled".to_string(),
                        Outcome::Failed(error) => format!("Export failed: {}", error.message),
                        _ => "Export ended".to_string(),
                    };
                    submissions.push(notice(&body));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}

impl JobRunner for NotesExport {
    // Runs in the job instance, so `self.job` is not visible here.
    fn run(&mut self, _kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
        let pages = split_pages(&input);
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        for (index, page) in pages.iter().enumerate() {
            if jobs::is_cancelled() {
                return Err(PluginError {
                    code: ErrorCode::Cancelled,
                    message: "export stopped".into(),
                    retry_after_ms: None,
                });
            }
            output.extend(render_page(page));
            jobs::report_progress(100.0 * (index + 1) as f32 / pages.len() as f32);
        }
        Ok(output)
    }
}

fn notice(body: &str) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Notify(NotifySpec {
        title: "Notes export".into(),
        body: body.into(),
        urgency: Urgency::Normal,
        sound: None,
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { cancel, isCancelled, reportProgress, startRequest, takeOutput } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';

let activeJob: bigint | undefined;

function notice(body: string): Submission {
  // Only one notice per batch, so the fixed correlation number cannot clash.
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'notify',
      val: { title: 'Notes export', body, urgency: 'normal', sound: undefined },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, jobRunner } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const out: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked') {
        const { command } = event.val;
        if (command === 'com.example.notes/export-pdf' && activeJob === undefined) {
          activeJob = startRequest('export-pdf', readNotebook());
        } else if (command === 'com.example.notes/cancel-export' && activeJob !== undefined) {
          cancel(activeJob);
        }
      } else if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && activeJob !== undefined) {
        const { request, outcome } = event.val;
        if (request.tag !== 'call' || request.val !== activeJob) continue;
        const finishedJob = activeJob;
        activeJob = undefined;
        const body = outcome.tag === 'ok'
          ? `PDF ready, ${takeOutput(finishedJob)?.byteLength ?? 0} bytes`
          : `Export ${outcome.tag}`;
        out.push(notice(body));
      }
    }
    return out;
  },
  run(_kind: string, input: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
    const pages = splitPages(input);
    const parts: Uint8Array[] = [];
    pages.forEach((page, index) => {
      if (isCancelled()) throw new PluginError('cancelled', 'export stopped');
      parts.push(renderPage(page));
      reportProgress((100 * (index + 1)) / pages.length);
    });
    return concatBytes(parts);
  },
});
```

### Example 2: wait for a slow call inside a job

A job runs on its own instance and has no event loop, so it cannot wait for `request-completed`. It starts the slow call in its raw request form, calls `wait-request` to block until the call completes, and then takes the result. This job asks the selected model for a summary and returns the text. It needs `jobs.run` on the side that starts it and `inference` on the side that runs the job. The manifest declares the kind `summarise` with `deadline_ms` 2,000 (the CPU deadline) and relies on the 20 s wall-clock default, so the wait is limited to 15,000 ms.

**Grants:** `jobs.run`, `inference`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{inference, jobs};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl JobRunner for Summariser {
    fn run(&mut self, _kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
        let text = String::from_utf8(input).map_err(|_| PluginError {
            code: ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
            message: "the input is not UTF-8 text".into(),
            retry_after_ms: None,
        })?;
        let request = inference::complete_request(CompletionRequest {
            messages: vec![ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: text }],
            max_output_tokens: None,
            json_schema: None,
            purpose: "note-summary".into(),
        })?;
        jobs::report_progress(10.0);
        // Waiting counts against the wall-clock limit, not against the CPU deadline.
        jobs::wait_request(request, 15_000)?;
        match inference::take_completion(request) {
            Some(completion) => Ok(completion.text.into_bytes()),
            None => Err(PluginError {
                code: ErrorCode::NotFound,
                message: "the completion was already taken".into(),
                retry_after_ms: None,
            }),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { completeRequest, takeCompletion } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { reportProgress, waitRequest } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';

export function run(_kind: string, input: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
  const text = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(input);
  const request = completeRequest({
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: text }],
    maxOutputTokens: undefined,
    jsonSchema: undefined,
    purpose: 'note-summary',
  });
  reportProgress(10);
  // Waiting counts against the wall-clock limit, not against the CPU deadline.
  waitRequest(request, 15_000);
  const completion = takeCompletion(request);
  if (completion === undefined) {
    throw new PluginError('not-found', 'the completion was already taken');
  }
  return new TextEncoder().encode(completion.text);
}
```

### What the user sees

A job has no view and no handler, so it draws nothing by itself. The user sees what the plugin shows: a desktop notice when the export ends (limited to 6 notices per minute), a `progress-row` or `gauge` widget in a pane or panel, updated from `job-progress` (see [ui](/pages/api-ui/)), and the lines in `ilium plugin logs`. Refused calls and traps are logged there as well.

A progress row built from the `percent` of `job-progress` is drawn by the client's progress widgets. The status prefix glyphs (`▶` running, `✓` done, `✕` error) and the bar characters (`█` filled, `░` unfilled) are those of the client progress bar.

╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

The border, the title chrome, the status glyph and the bar characters are those that the client draws; the text inside is the plugin's own. This frame is composed by hand from the client's glyph table, not captured from a running build.</figcaption>
</figure>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs com.example.notes --tail 4
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-12 09:30:05</span> info  job export-pdf started (input 412 KiB)
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-12 09:30:09</span> info  job export-pdf progress 64
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-12 09:30:12</span> info  job export-pdf done (output 1.2 MiB)
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-12 09:30:12</span> info  notice sent: PDF ready, 1258291 bytes
</pre>

The log lines are written by the plugin through the `log` import; the exact text is the plugin's choice. They are an illustration of the form, not captured output.

### Errors

| Where it appears | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Call to `start` | `invalid-argument` | The kind is not declared in `contributes.jobs`, or the input is over the job input limit. |
| Call to `start` | `busy` | The job queue is full. |
| Call to `start` | `not-permitted` | `jobs.run` is not granted. |
| Call to `start` | `quota-exceeded` | The CPU budget of the execution group is spent. `retry-after-ms` is set. |
| Completion | `failed(timed-out)` | The CPU or wall-clock deadline passed. |
| Completion | `failed(quota-exceeded)` | The job reached its memory limit. |
| Completion | `failed(invalid-argument)` | The output is over the job output limit. |
| Completion | `failed(internal)` | A trap in the job instance. The trap text is in `message`. |
| Completion | `failed(<code>)` | `run` returned an error with that code. |
| Completion | `cancelled` | A cancel was requested. |
| Call to `wait-request` | `not-found` | The request id is unknown. |
| Call to `wait-request` | `timed-out` | The call did not complete within `timeout-millis`. The request keeps running. |
| Call to `wait-request` | `unsupported` | `wait-request` was called outside `run`. |
| `take-output` | `not-found` in the SDK wrappers | The output was already taken or held longer than 30 s. |

Concurrency is not an error: a job past `concurrent_jobs` waits in the queue. A job failure never counts toward the plugin's restart rule, so a failing job cannot disable the plugin.

### Edge cases

- A kind that is declared but whose side lacks `job-runner` in `exports` fails the install review, not the call.
- A job that returns normally after `cancel` still ends as `cancelled`, and its output is dropped.
- Two handlers that start jobs of the same kind get separate request ids; the input is copied at the call.
- The job instance may be reused for the next job, so keep no state in it across jobs.
- `report-progress` outside `run` is ignored. It has no result to carry an error.

### Used by

- Workspace search (feature 9), session stats (feature 31) and the compaction optimiser (feature 82) run long reads as jobs.
- Convert a session between Claude and Codex (feature 77) starts its conversion with `jobs.start`.
