# tree

## tree

The `tree` interface reads the project tree: the containers, folders and panes, with their titles, parents, working directories, agent state and lock flags. Every node has a `node-id`, a number that stays the same for the life of the node, including across moves and server restarts. A plugin can also keep its own small byte map on any node, for example a bookmark flag or the id of a note. No other plugin can read that map.

All reads are synchronous. They answer at once from the copy of the tree that the plugin's side holds, so a plugin does not await them. Changes to the tree go through intents, not through this interface: see [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

**You will need:**

- `tree.read` for `get`, `children`, `roots` and `find`, and for the `tree-changed` and `node-removed` events.
- `tree.metadata` for `metadata` and `set-metadata`.
- `agent.read` if the `agent` field of a node must be filled in. Without it, `agent` is always none for this plugin.
- Language: Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both are available on the server and client sides. The two sides of one plugin share one metadata map per node.
- Writes to the tree need `tree.write` (rename, move, lock, close) or `tree.decorate` (badges and rows). Those are intents, not calls on this interface.

### Surface

Functions, all in the `tree` interface. Every function is synchronous and returns no request id.

| Rust (`host::tree`) | TypeScript (`host/tree`) | Grant | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get(node)` | `get(node)` | `tree.read` | `Option<NodeView>`, `NodeView` or `undefined` | The view of one node, or none when it does not exist. |
| `children(node)` | `children(node)` | `tree.read` | `Vec<NodeId>`, `bigint[]` | The child ids in tree order. Empty for a pane or an unknown node. |
| `roots()` | `roots()` | `tree.read` | `Vec<NodeId>`, `bigint[]` | The top-level node ids in tree order. |
| `find(query)` | `find(query)` | `tree.read` | `Vec<NodeId>`, `bigint[]` | The ids of nodes that match every field set in the query. |
| `metadata(node)` | `metadata(node)` | `tree.metadata` | `Option<Vec<u8>>`, `Uint8Array` or `undefined` | The plugin's own bytes on that node, or none. |
| `set_metadata(node, bytes)` | `setMetadata(node, bytes)` | `tree.metadata` | `Result<(), PluginError>`, `void` (throws) | Replaces the plugin's own bytes on that node. |

The records and their fields:

| Record | Field | Rust type | TypeScript type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NodeView` | `id` | `NodeId` (`u64`) | `bigint` | The node id. |
| `NodeView` | `parent` | `Option<NodeId>` | `bigint \| undefined` | The parent node. None for a top-level node. |
| `NodeView` | `class` | `NodeClass` | `'container' \| 'folder' \| 'pane'` | The kind of node. |
| `NodeView` | `content_kind` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | Such as `ilium.terminal`, `ilium.editor`, `ilium.board` or `<plugin-id>.<kind>`. |
| `NodeView` | `title` | `String` | `string` | The title the user sees. |
| `NodeView` | `cwd` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | A display string. It grants no file access. |
| `NodeView` | `agent` | `Option<AgentView>` | `AgentView \| undefined` | Present only for a pane that runs an agent, and only with `agent.read`. |
| `NodeView` | `locked` | `bool` | `boolean` | True when the user or a plugin locked the node. |
| `NodeView` | `revision` | `u64` | `bigint` | Rises whenever a field above changes. Compare it to detect a change cheaply. |
| `NodeQuery` | `content_kind` | `Option<String>` | `contentKind?: string` | Match nodes of this content kind. |
| `NodeQuery` | `signature` | `Option<String>` | `signature?: string` | Match panes whose agent has this signature, such as `claude`. |
| `NodeQuery` | `under` | `Option<NodeId>` | `under?: bigint` | Match strict descendants of this node, at any depth. |
| `AgentView` | `signature` | `String` | `string` | The detected agent, such as `claude` or `codex`. |
| `AgentView` | `activity` | `AgentActivity` | `AgentActivity` | The current activity, see below. |
| `AgentView` | `objective` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | The objective the agent reports, when it reports one. |
| `AgentView` | `goal` | `Option<String>` | `string \| undefined` | The active goal, when one is set. |

`AgentActivity` has six values: `none`, `working`, `idle`, `awaiting-approval`, `done` and `menu`. In Rust they are `AgentActivity::Working` and so on. In TypeScript they are the strings `'working'` and `'awaiting-approval'`.

Events that concern the tree, delivered in batches to `on-events`:

| Event | Payload | Grant | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree-changed` | list of node ids | `tree.read` | Coalesced: pending events merge into one event whose list is the union of node ids in first-seen order. |
| `node-removed` | node id | `tree.read` | Never dropped. |
| `agent-identified`, `agent-activity-changed` | node and agent details | `agent.read` | Never dropped. |

The WIT declaration of the interface, for reference:

```wit
enum node-class { container, pane, folder }
record node-view {
  id: node-id, parent: option<node-id>, class: node-class,
  content-kind: option<string>, title: string, cwd: option<string>,
  agent: option<agent-view>, locked: bool, revision: u64,
}
record node-query {
  content-kind: option<string>, signature: option<string>, under: option<node-id>,
}
get: func(node: node-id) -> option<node-view>;                       // tree.read
children: func(node: node-id) -> list<node-id>;                      // tree.read
roots: func() -> list<node-id>;                                      // tree.read
find: func(query: node-query) -> list<node-id>;                      // tree.read
metadata: func(node: node-id) -> option<list<u8>>;                   // tree.metadata
set-metadata: func(node: node-id, bytes: list<u8>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
```

### Import paths

Rust:

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;                 // NodeId, PluginError
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::tree::{self, NodeQuery};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::{NodeView, AgentActivity};
```

TypeScript:

```ts
import * as tree from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';
import type { NodeView, AgentActivity } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
```

### Example 1: find Claude panes and bookmark them

The plugin finds every terminal pane that runs the `claude` agent. It keeps a bookmark flag in its own metadata: the byte `1` means on, and an empty list means off.

**Grants:** `tree.read` `tree.metadata`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::tree::{self, NodeQuery};

const BOOKMARK_ON: u8 = 1;

fn claude_panes() -> Vec<NodeId> {
    tree::find(NodeQuery {
        content_kind: Some("ilium.terminal".to_string()),
        signature: Some("claude".to_string()),
        under: None,
    })
}

fn set_bookmark(node: NodeId, on: bool) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let bytes = if on { vec![BOOKMARK_ON] } else { Vec::new() };
    tree::set_metadata(node, bytes)
}

fn is_bookmarked(node: NodeId) -> bool {
    tree::metadata(node).is_some_and(|bytes| bytes == [BOOKMARK_ON])
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as tree from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';

const BOOKMARK_ON = 1;

export function claudePanes(): bigint[] {
  return tree.find({
    contentKind: 'ilium.terminal',
    signature: 'claude',
    under: undefined,
  });
}

export function setBookmark(node: bigint, on: boolean): void {
  tree.setMetadata(node, new Uint8Array(on ? [BOOKMARK_ON] : []));
}

export function isBookmarked(node: bigint): boolean {
  const bytes = tree.metadata(node);
  return bytes !== undefined && bytes.length === 1 && bytes[0] === BOOKMARK_ON;
}
```

For the tree in the render below, `claude_panes()` returns:

```text
[ 14 ]
```

Pane 22 runs `codex`, so the signature filter leaves it out.

### Example 2: breadcrumb from the parent links

The plugin builds a path such as `project / backend / claude: api fix` by following `parent` from a node up to its top-level ancestor. The walk stops when a node has no parent.

**Grants:** `tree.read`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::tree;

/// Titles from the top-level node down to `node`, joined with " / ".
/// Returns None when `node` or one of its ancestors does not exist.
fn breadcrumb(node: NodeId) -> Option<String> {
    let mut titles = Vec::new();
    let mut current = Some(node);
    while let Some(node_id) = current {
        let view = tree::get(node_id)?;
        titles.push(view.title);
        current = view.parent;
    }
    titles.reverse();
    Some(titles.join(" / "))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as tree from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';

/** Titles from the top-level node down to `node`, joined with " / ". */
export function breadcrumb(node: bigint): string | undefined {
  const titles: string[] = [];
  let current: bigint | undefined = node;
  while (current !== undefined) {
    const view = tree.get(current);
    if (view === undefined) {
      return undefined;
    }
    titles.unshift(view.title);
    current = view.parent;
  }
  return titles.join(' / ');
}
```

`breadcrumb(14)` returns `Some("project / backend / claude: api fix")` for the tree below. Pane 14 has parent 4, and folder 4 has parent 1.

### Reading the tree on the client

A plugin half on a client reads the tree from the **client mirror**, not from the server. The mirror holds every node with its kind, title, status, attention and the metadata keys that a plugin may read. The server sends changes as `tree-changed` events and the client applies them to the mirror before it delivers the event to the plugin. The read functions are synchronous and answer from the mirror, so they never wait for the server.

- **Staleness.** The mirror lags the server by the delivery time of one delta, 5 ms at the 99th percentile on a local connection. A read right after a submission can still show the old tree. Wait for the `request-completed` of your own submission: the server sends the tree change before that outcome, so the mirror already shows the effect when you hear it.
- **After a reconnect.** A client that attaches again receives a full snapshot of the tree, and then a `tree-changed` event for every node.
- **Detached.** While the connection is down the mirror is frozen. Reads succeed on the old data, and submissions are queued.
- **Servers.** A server plugin half reads the tree itself and always sees the current state.

- **[HST-493]** A client plugin half MUST read the tree from the client mirror, and the mirror MUST be updated before the matching `tree-changed` event is delivered.
- **[HST-494]** The tree change caused by a forwarded submission MUST reach the client mirror before the `request-completed` of that submission.

### Intents and events around the read functions

Intents and events surround the six read functions. Nothing in this section is a new call on the `tree` interface.

| Addition | Where | Grant |
|---|---|---|
| `create-group`, `create-folder`, `create-project`, `create-split` | [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/) | `tree.restructure` |
| `restructure` and `revert-restructure` (batches with undo) | [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/) | `tree.restructure` |
| `set-bookmarked`, `set-expanded` | below | `tree.write` |
| `rename-node` with `source` and `expected-revision`, `set-inferred-icon` | [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/) | `tree.write`, `tree.decorate` |
| `mark-attention`, `ack-attention`, event `attention-changed` | [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/) | `tree.attention` |
| Decorations with spans, tooltips, frames, trailing and hover-only slots | [tree chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/) | `tree.decorate` |
| `tree_toolbar`, `row_actions`, `tree_orderings`, `display_modes`, virtual rows with children and drops | [tree chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/) | `ui.chrome`, `tree.decorate` |
| Event `display-mode-changed` | [tree chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/) | own `display_modes` |

`set-bookmarked { node, bookmarked }` sets or clears the star that the user sees on a row; the outcome is `ok`. `set-expanded { node, expanded }` folds or unfolds a real node and needs `tree.write`; for a plugin's own virtual row, pass `virtual-row` instead of `node`. A plugin that wants its own flag, not the user's star, still keeps it in `tree.metadata` as in Example 1.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, SetBookmarkedSpec, SetExpandedSpec, ExpandTarget};

/// Star every Claude pane and fold the group that holds them.
fn star_and_fold(panes: &[NodeId], group: NodeId) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let mut submissions: Vec<Submission> = panes.iter().map(|&node| {
        Submission::new(Intent::SetBookmarked(SetBookmarkedSpec { node, bookmarked: true }))
    }).collect();
    submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetExpanded(SetExpandedSpec {
        target: ExpandTarget::Node(group),
        expanded: false,
    })));
    submissions
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

/** Star every Claude pane and fold the group that holds them. */
export function starAndFold(panes: bigint[], group: bigint): Submission[] {
  const stars: Submission[] = panes.map((node, index) => ({
    intent: { tag: 'set-bookmarked', val: { node, bookmarked: true } },
    correlation: BigInt(index + 1),
    dedupKey: undefined,
  }));
  stars.push({
    intent: { tag: 'set-expanded', val: { target: { tag: 'node', val: group }, expanded: false } },
    correlation: BigInt(panes.length + 1),
    dedupKey: undefined,
  });
  return stars;
}
```

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">before</span>                          <span class="t-dim">after star_and_fold</span>
▼ Ilium                      ▶ Ilium
›   ⠋ Fix auth               <span class="t-dim">(group folded; the stars are inside)</span>
›   ● Review
</pre>
<figcaption>Folding hides the starred rows but does not remove them. A <code>find</code> still returns them, because the plugin reads the tree, not the screen.</figcaption>
</figure>

The new intents are refused with `not-permitted` without their grant and with `not-found` for a node that is gone. Batch limits and the full error table of these intents are on [pane lifecycle](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits).

### What the user sees

Reading the tree shows nothing on its own. The user sees what the plugin does with the data: a decoration, a sorted list, a notice or a log line. Metadata is never shown unless the plugin shows it. A bookmark flag from Example 1 appears only if the plugin draws it, for example as a badge with `tree.decorate`. Log lines from a refused read appear in `ilium plugin logs <plugin-id>`.

### Errors and limits

Reads never fail. A missing node gives none or an empty list. The error cases are these:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `get`, `metadata` for a node that does not exist | `None` or `undefined` |
| `children`, `roots`, `find` with no match, or `under` naming an unknown node | Empty list |
| `tree.read` or `tree.metadata` not granted, or declined by the user | `not-permitted`, written to the plugin log |
| `set-metadata` for a node that is absent or removed during the call | `not-found` |
| `set-metadata` past the per-node limit | `quota-exceeded` |
| Call while the authorization changed | `revoked`; the plugin is re-activated |

Limit: the key `node_metadata_kib` sets the metadata that one plugin may keep on one node. The default is 64 KiB. The T1 ceiling is 256 KiB. A manifest request above the ceiling is clamped and logged, and the user can lower the value in `config.toml` under `[plugins.limits]`.

<div class="warn">
<p>A write that passes the limit is refused whole. The old bytes stay in place, so store a version number in the first byte if the format may change.</p>
</div>

<div class="note">
<p>Metadata survives restarts because it is saved in the session snapshot. It is removed when its node is closed. It is not removed when the node is only moved or renamed.</p>
</div>

### Used by

- Tree ordering reads the tree and sets a `sort-key` on decorations; see [tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/).
- Bookmark and lock plugins store their flags in `tree.metadata`, as in Example 1.
- Workspace search and session statistics read the tree and the agent state.
- Tree toolbar, hover actions, orderings and virtual rows build on this interface; see [tree chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/).

# ui

## Overview

The `ui` import controls the views that a client-side plugin shows: panels, popups, the state of the
widgets inside them, the theme and the width of text. A plugin never draws cells. It describes each
view as a tree of widgets, returned from its `views.render` export. The host lays the tree out with
the constraint solver described in [layout](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/), paints it with the
user's theme and keeps the state of every widget (selection, scroll offset, text) between renders.

A view renders in four cases only: when it first opens, after the plugin calls `invalidate`, when its
area changes (a resize), and after a theme change. Views never render per frame. When the user acts on a widget, the host sends a `ui-action`
event back to the plugin's `handler`, and the plugin decides whether to change the view.

## What you need

- **Grants.** `ui.panels` gives panels, settings pages, onboarding steps, popups and the state calls.
  `panes.provide-kind` gives the same calls for the view of a basic pane. `ui.invalidate` needs no
  grant for views the plugin contributes.
- **Side.** Client only. The plugin declares the `client` side and exports `views` (`exports = ["views"]`
  in Rust, a `render` function in TypeScript). The `ui` imports do not exist on the server.
- **Manifest.** Panels go in `contributes.panels`, custom settings pages as `settings` tabs with `"render": "view"`, and
  guided steps in `onboarding_steps`. Each entry names a local `id`, which becomes the view target.
- **Language.** Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both use the
  same names, spelled per the naming rule of the SDK.

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "panels": [{ "id": "notes", "title": "Notes", "modal": false }]
  },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] }
}
```

## Functions

Rust imports these from `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui`. TypeScript imports them from
`@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui`. Every call that returns `Result` throws `PluginError` in TypeScript.

| Rust and TypeScript | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalidate(view)` | nothing | Queues a new render of the view. |
| `open_panel(panel)` | `Result` | Shows a panel declared in the manifest. |
| `close_panel(panel)` | nothing | Hides a panel. |
| `open_popup(popup, anchor)` | `Result` | Shows the `popup` or `dialog` node whose key is `popup`. It searches the last committed tree of each open view. No match returns `not-found`, two matches `invalid-argument`, and a fifth open popup in one view `quota-exceeded`. Popup ids are unique across all open views of the plugin. |
| `close_popup(popup)` | nothing | Hides that popup. An id that is not open is a no-op that returns `ok`. A popup whose node disappears from the next tree closes and sends `closed`. |
| `widget_state(view, key)` | `Option` | Reads the host-owned state of a widget: selection, offset, tab, text, expansion or check. |
| `set_widget_state(view, key, state)` | `Result` | Changes that state, for example to select row 0 of a list. |
| `display_width(text)` | `u16` | Width in cells of a text, using the host's rules for icons and wide glyphs. |
| `theme()` | `ThemeTokens` | The theme colours, whether the theme is dark, and whether stable glyphs are on. |
| `write_surface(view, key, first_row, format, data)` | `Result` | Writes pixels into a `surface` widget, starting at `first_row`. |

`display_width`, `theme` and `invalidate` never return an error code.

## Types

| Type | Cases | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ViewTarget` | `panel(string)`, `pane(node-id)`, `popup(string)`, `settings-page(string)`, `onboarding-step(string)` | The view that a call or event refers to. |
| `PopupAnchor` | `centered(tuple<constraint, constraint>)`, `at-cell(tuple<u16, u16>)`, `below-key(string)` | Where `open_popup` places the popup. |
| `WidgetState` | `none`, `selected(option<u32>)`, `offset(u32)`, `tab(u32)`, `text(string)`, `expanded(list<string>)`, `checked(bool)` | Host-owned state of one widget. |
| `Constraint` | `length(u16)`, `min(u16)`, `max(u16)`, `percentage(u16)`, `ratio(tuple<u32, u32>)`, `fill(u16)` | A size rule for layouts, popups and panels. |
| `PixelFormat` | `mask8`, `mono1`, `gray8`, `rgb8`, `rgba8` | The pixel format of a `surface` widget. |
| `ThemeTokens` | `foreground`, `background`, `accent`, `muted`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` (each `u32` as `0x00RRGGBB`), `is-dark`, `stable-glyphs` | The theme returned by `theme()`. |

Rust names are `ViewTarget::Panel`, `PopupAnchor::BelowKey` and `WidgetState::Selected`. In TypeScript
a variant is `{ tag, val }` with a kebab-case tag, so `below-key` becomes `{ tag: 'below-key', val: 'help' }`.
A `u64` node id is a `bigint` in TypeScript.

## Events and actions

The host sends these events to `handler.on-events` for the plugin's own views.

| Event | Payload | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-action` | `view`, `key`, `action-id`, `kind`, `value` | Never dropped; `scrolled` is coalesced. |
| `view-visibility` | `view`, `visible` | Coalesced. |
| `theme-changed` | none | Sent when the user changes the theme, after the host has repainted the last tree. One `views.render` per open view follows. |

The `key` is the widget's key. In 0.1.0 `action-id` is always a copy of `key`. The `kind` is one of `activated`, `changed`, `submitted`, `selected`,
`toggled`, `scrolled`, `dropped`, `context-requested`, `closed`, `focus-gained` or `focus-lost`. The
`value` is an option: `none` for a button `activated`, a menu or key-capture `closed`, and the hover and focus kinds; otherwise `text(string)`, `index(u32)`, `number(f64)`, `flag(bool)` or `drop(source, target, index)`.
Which kind each widget sends is listed on the widget pages, starting with [widgets index](/pages/widgets-index/).

## Rules for trees

- **Keys.** Every interactive widget needs a `key` that stays the same from one render to the next,
  and keys must be unique across the whole view, not only among siblings. A duplicate key anywhere traps with `ui.duplicate-key`. The host keeps widget state by key, so a widget without
  a key loses its state on every render.
- **Size.** A tree is a flat list of nodes with child indices. It holds at most 4,096 nodes and 1 MiB
  by default. A manifest `limits` entry can raise both to 16,384 nodes and 4 MiB.
- **Render time.** `views.render` has a deadline of 10 ms by default (`render_deadline_ms`, ceiling 20 ms).
- **Pure call.** `views.render` is a pure call, like `annotate` and `settings-validate`. An effectful import called inside it (an intent submission, a request, a storage write or a timer) returns `err(not-permitted)` with the message `effectful import in a pure call` and the call continues [ABI-048]. Read-only imports stay allowed.
- **Popups.** A `popup` widget in a tree is drawn only while an `open_popup` call has opened it. A popup or dialog node takes no space in its parent's layout. Its size and placement follow [Popup size and placement](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/#popup-size-and-placement).
- **Theme.** A tree stores colour roles such as `accent` and `muted`, not colours. The host resolves
  roles when it paints. On a theme change the host repaints the last tree of every open view at once, delivers `theme-changed`, and triggers exactly one `views.render` per open view, coalesced with any other trigger in the same 16 ms window. A plugin need not call `invalidate`. Plugins cannot ship themes.

<div class="warn">
<p>An invalid tree traps the plugin with a <code>ui.*</code> code: <code>ui.invalid-tree</code>, <code>ui.duplicate-key</code>, <code>ui.too-deep</code>, <code>ui.too-large</code>, <code>ui.widget-not-allowed</code> or <code>ui.render-timeout</code>. The host keeps the previous tree, marked stale, and logs one error. <code>views.render</code> returns a tree, not a result, so it never returns <code>invalid-argument</code>.
A trap counts as a failure for the restart rule: the third failure in ten minutes disables the plugin on
that side.</p>
</div>

## Example 1: a help popup below a button

The panel shows a `Keys` button. When the user activates it, the plugin opens a popup below the
button. The popup is part of the view's tree, so `views.render` declares it. The popup needs
`ui.panels`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{log::{self, Level}, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, PopupAnchor, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct RenameHelp;

impl Lifecycle for RenameHelp {}

impl Handler for RenameHelp {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if action.key != "help" || action.kind != ActionKind::Activated { continue; }
            let anchor = PopupAnchor::BelowKey("help".to_string());
            if let Err(error) = ui::open_popup("keys-help", anchor) {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &error.message);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for RenameHelp {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let help = tree.button("Keys").key("help");
        let text = tree.paragraph(["Enter saves the name.", "Esc cancels."]);
        let popup = tree.popup("keys-help", text).title("Keys")
            .width(Constraint::Length(40)).height(Constraint::Length(4));
        let root = tree.layout(Direction::Vertical,
            vec![Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(0)], vec![help, popup]);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { openPopup } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { button, layout, paragraph, popup, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
      if (event.val.key !== 'help' || event.val.kind !== 'activated') continue;
      try {
        openPopup('keys-help', { tag: 'below-key', val: 'help' });
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', String(error));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    return tree(layout({ direction: 'vertical',
      constraints: [{ tag: 'length', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 0 }] }, [
      button('Keys', { key: 'help' }),
      popup('keys-help', { title: 'Keys', modal: false,
        width: { tag: 'length', val: 40 }, height: { tag: 'length', val: 4 } }, [
        paragraph(['Enter saves the name.', 'Esc cancels.']),
      ]),
    ]));
  },
});
```

The popup node sits in a `length(0)` slot, because a popup takes no space in the layout. The call returns `ok`, and the popup appears directly below the `help` button, with its left edge aligned to the button. If no popup with id
`keys-help` is in the last committed tree of any open view, the call returns `not-found`. Escape closes the popup. The plugin
then receives a `ui-action` with kind `closed`.

## Example 2: a notes panel with a list and a delete button

This panel lists note titles in a `%list` widget keyed `notes-list`, with a `Delete` button keyed
`delete`. The plugin tracks the selected row from `selected` actions. After a delete, it moves the
selection to row 0 and invalidates the view. The host keeps the list's offset; the plugin owns the
titles.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{log::{self, Level}, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, UiTree, ViewTarget, WidgetState};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notes { titles: Vec<String>, selected: usize }

fn notes_view() -> ViewTarget { ViewTarget::Panel("notes".to_string()) }

impl Lifecycle for Notes {}

impl Handler for Notes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if action.view != notes_view() { continue; }
            match (action.key.as_str(), action.kind, action.value) {
                ("notes-list", ActionKind::Selected, ActionValue::Index(index)) => {
                    self.selected = index as usize;
                }
                ("delete", ActionKind::Activated, _) if self.selected < self.titles.len() => {
                    self.titles.remove(self.selected);
                    self.selected = 0;
                    let state = WidgetState::Selected(Some(0));
                    if let Err(error) = ui::set_widget_state(notes_view(), "notes-list", state) {
                        log::log(Level::Warn, &error.message);
                    }
                    ui::invalidate(notes_view());
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for Notes {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let list = tree.list(self.titles.clone()).key("notes-list");
        let delete = tree.button("Delete").key("delete");
        let root = tree.layout(Direction::Vertical,
            vec![Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(3)], vec![list, delete]);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import type { ViewTarget } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { invalidate, setWidgetState } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { button, layout, list, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const NOTES_VIEW: ViewTarget = { tag: 'panel', val: 'notes' };
let titles: string[] = [];
let selected = 0;

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
      const { view, key, kind, value } = event.val;
      if (view.tag !== 'panel' || view.val !== 'notes') continue;
      if (key === 'notes-list' && kind === 'selected' && value.tag === 'index') {
        selected = value.val;
      }
      if (key === 'delete' && kind === 'activated' && selected < titles.length) {
        titles.splice(selected, 1);
        selected = 0;
        try {
          setWidgetState(NOTES_VIEW, 'notes-list', { tag: 'selected', val: 0 });
        } catch (error) {
          log('warn', String(error));
        }
        invalidate(NOTES_VIEW);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    return tree(layout({ direction: 'vertical',
      constraints: [{ tag: 'fill', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 3 }] }, [
      list(titles, { key: 'notes-list' }),
      button('Delete', { key: 'delete' }),
    ]));
  },
});
```

## Errors and limits

| Call or case | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Any `ui` call | `not-permitted` | The grant is missing or the user declined it. |
| `open_panel`, `close_panel` | `not-found` | The panel id is not declared in the manifest. |
| `open_popup` | `not-found` | No popup or dialog node with that key is in the last committed tree of any open view. |
| `open_popup` | `invalid-argument` | Two open nodes have that key. |
| `open_popup` | `quota-exceeded` | A fifth popup would be open in one view. |
| `set_widget_state` | `not-found` | The key is unknown in that view. |
| `set_widget_state` | `invalid-argument` | The state kind does not fit the widget, for example `offset` on a button. |
| `write_surface` | `not-found` | No `surface` widget has that key. |
| `write_surface` | `invalid-argument` | The format differs from the widget, the data is not a whole number of rows, or it is over 16 MiB. |
| Any call | `revoked` | The authorization changed during the call; the plugin is re-activated. |

A `secret` text input sends its value in `changed` and `submitted`, because the plugin needs it. The
host redacts that value in logs and never stores it in the snapshot. Text that contains escape
sequences has them removed, and the host logs one warning per view.

## What the user sees

- A non-modal panel takes the whole content area. A modal panel is centred at 80 percent by 80 percent by default.
- Escape follows the order in [Escape](/pages/ui-model/#escape): a capturing key-capture, a text selection, the topmost popup, then a modal panel.
- Popups and panels are painted with the user's theme. The user alone chooses the theme and the
  `ui.stable_glyphs` setting, which the plugin reads from `theme()`.

## Used by

- Workspace search and the help reference open panels with `text-input` and list widgets.
- Chatroom and session stats show a panel or a popup.
- Voice confirmations open a popup with buttons.
- The settings screens render custom pages with `tabs`, `schema-form` and `leader-row`.

### Further fields and flags

The UI tree has optional fields and flags.

| Addition | Where | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `tooltip`, `tab-index`, `disabled-reason` on `ui-node` | node fields | [popovers](/pages/api-popovers/) |
| `hover-events`, `pointer-events` node flags | `node-flags` | [pointer](/pages/api-pointer/) |
| `open-popup-with` and the new `popup-anchor` cases (`at-key`, `at-tree-node`, `at-pointer`) | `ui` | [popovers](/pages/api-popovers/) |
| `menu-entry` and the `menu-provider` export | menus | [menus](/pages/api-menus/) |
| `theme-extras`: reduced motion, density, icon mode | `ui` | below |
| `widget-state` cases `geo`, `number`, `split`, `ids`, `tri` | state | below |
| `ui-action` kinds `hover-enter`, `hover-leave`, `pointer`, `drag-over`, `resized`, `filter-changed` | actions | [pointer](/pages/api-pointer/) |
| Settings views may embed display widgets | settings pages | below |

**Theme extras.** `theme-extras()` returns `{ reduced-motion, density, info, selection, border, icon-mode }`. Honour `reduced-motion` by drawing one static frame; `icon-mode` is `stable` only when the user opted in, and normal icons stay the default. `theme().stable-glyphs` is a derived convenience field: it always equals `icon-mode == stable`, and widgets follow `icon-mode`.

**Rust**

```rust
let extras = ui::theme_extras();
let frames = if extras.reduced_motion { 1 } else { 8 };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { themeExtras } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
const frames = themeExtras().reducedMotion ? 1 : 8;
```

**Focus and popups.** Tab and Shift+Tab follow the [focus order](/pages/ui-model/#focus-order). At most 4 popups per view are open (`quota-exceeded`). A node with `disabled-reason` is muted and shows the reason as its tooltip.

**Settings views.** A `settings-page` tree may now use layout, `split`, `scroll-view`, `markdown`, `diff-view`, `check-list`, the data-display widgets, `progress-row`, `meter`, `minimap`, `badge`, `spinner`, `notice`, `icon`, `image`, `surface`, `location-picker` and a read-only `code-view`. Still refused there: `popup`, `dialog`, `menu`, `video`, `terminal-view` and the input widgets other than `button`, `schema-form` and `location-picker`; they fail with `invalid-argument` on render and are logged.

### WIT

The contract below is an excerpt. The owner is the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/), and that page wins if the two differ.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/ui-host in reference-wit
/// Marks the view as stale. The host calls views.render before the next frame. Always granted for own views.
invalidate: func(view: view-target);
/// Errors: not-found when the panel is not declared.
open-panel: func(panel: string) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
close-panel: func(panel: string);
/// Errors: not-found when no popup or dialog node with that key is in the last committed tree of any
/// open view, invalid-argument when two match, quota-exceeded for a fifth open popup in one view.
open-popup: func(popup: string, anchor: popup-anchor) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
open-popup-with: func(popup: string, anchor: popup-anchor, options: popup-options) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
close-popup: func(popup: string);
widget-state: func(view: view-target, key: string) -> option<widget-state>;
/// Errors: not-found for an unknown key, invalid-argument when the case does not fit the widget.
set-widget-state: func(view: view-target, key: string, state: widget-state) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
/// Width in cells by the cell width rule of the UI model page.
display-width: func(text: string) -> u16;
theme: func() -> theme-tokens;
theme-extras: func() -> theme-extras;
/// Rows are top to bottom. first-row plus the rows written must be within the surface height.
/// Errors: not-found for a key with no surface, invalid-argument for a bad length.
write-surface: func(view: view-target, key: string, first-row: u32, format: pixel-format, data: list<u8>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
```

# workspace

## workspace

The `workspace` import records which pane owns which Git worktree. A worktree is a second checkout of a repository in its own folder, so one project can have several branches checked out at the same time. An agent pane often works in a worktree of its own.

The kernel keeps one custody record for each registered worktree. The record holds the id, the folder, the branch, the owning pane and whether a process is running in it. The snapshot, the close policy and the worktree list all read these records, so they agree on who owns what.

The kernel never runs Git. A plugin creates the worktree with `git worktree add` through [process control](/pages/api-process-control/), then registers it here. Release removes the record only. The folder stays on disk until the plugin runs `git worktree remove`.

<div class="note">
<p>Register and release change custody records only. Creating and removing the folder are Git commands that the plugin runs itself.</p>
</div>

### What you need

- **Grant `workspace.manage`** (high risk). It lets the plugin register worktrees and release them. A registered worktree can be owned by a pane.
- **Grant `process.run:git`** (high risk). It lets the plugin run `git worktree add` and `git worktree remove`.
- **Grant `fs.read:project`** for the repository folder that `register` names.
- **Grant `fs.write:worktrees`** (high risk) for the worktree folder. The `worktrees` scope is rooted at the setting `workspace.worktree_root`. Its default is `<project name>.worktrees/` in the parent folder of the project.
- **Side and language.** Server side only, in Rust or TypeScript. The client world has no `workspace` import.

### Surface

The interface as the kernel declares it (WIT, `ilium:host/workspace@0.1.0`). The name `%list` escapes a keyword in WIT. In code the function is `list`.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/workspace in reference-wit
record workspace-spec {
  repository: fs-path, path: fs-path, branch: string, base: option<string>, owner: option<node-id>,
}
record workspace-info {
  id: u64, path: fs-path, branch: string, owner: option<node-id>, in-use: bool,
}
register: func(spec: workspace-spec) -> result<u64, plugin-error>;
release: func(workspace: u64) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
%list: func() -> list<workspace-info>;
```

All three functions are synchronous. There is no request id and nothing to await.

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Grant | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `register` | `workspace::register(spec)` | `register(spec)` | `workspace.manage` | Records a worktree and its owner. Returns the new id. |
| `release` | `workspace::release(id)` | `release(id)` | `workspace.manage` | Removes the custody record. The folder and branch stay. |
| `%list` | `workspace::list()` | `list()` | `workspace.manage` | Returns every record, ordered by id. |

The fields of the two records:

| Field | Rust type | TypeScript type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WorkspaceSpec.repository` | `FsPath` | `FsPath` | Git repository folder. The plugin must hold `fs.read` for its scope. |
| `WorkspaceSpec.path` | `FsPath` | `FsPath` | Worktree folder, normally in the `worktrees` scope. |
| `WorkspaceSpec.branch` | `String` | `string` | Branch that the worktree checks out. |
| `WorkspaceSpec.base` | `Option<String>` | optional `string` | Commit or branch the branch starts from. Recorded for display only. |
| `WorkspaceSpec.owner` | `Option<NodeId>` | optional `bigint` | Pane or tree node that owns the worktree. |
| `WorkspaceInfo.id` | `u64` | `bigint` | Id returned by `register`. |
| `WorkspaceInfo.owner` | `Option<NodeId>` | optional `bigint` | Owner. It becomes `None` when the owner pane closes. |
| `WorkspaceInfo.in_use` | `bool` | `inUse: boolean` | True while a process runs in the worktree (see below). |

`in_use` is true while the owner pane is open with a running process. It is also true while any pane with a running process has a working directory inside the worktree path. A worktree with an idle shell is not in use.

### Example 1: create a worktree and register it (Rust)

The plugin runs `git worktree add` for a new branch, then records the worktree as owned by an agent pane. The caller passes the absolute host path of the new folder as a string, because git needs a host path and the SDK does not give one for a scope.

**Grants:** `workspace.manage`, `process.run:git`, `fs.read:project`, `fs.write:worktrees`

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::process::{self, ProcessSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::workspace::{self, WorkspaceSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Creates a worktree for `branch` and records it as owned by `pane`.
async fn create_agent_worktree(
    repository: FsPath,
    worktree: FsPath,
    worktree_host_path: String,
    branch: String,
    pane: NodeId,
) -> Result<u64, PluginError> {
    let git = ProcessSpec {
        program: "git".to_string(),
        arguments: vec![
            "worktree".to_string(),
            "add".to_string(),
            "-b".to_string(),
            branch.clone(),
            worktree_host_path,
            "HEAD".to_string(),
        ],
        cwd: Some(repository.clone()),
        stdin: None,
        environment: Vec::new(),
        timeout_millis: 60_000,
    };
    let exit = process::run(git).await?;
    if exit.status != Some(0) {
        return Err(PluginError {
            code: ErrorCode::Io,
            message: "git worktree add exited with a non-zero status".into(),
            retry_after_ms: None,
        });
    }
    workspace::register(WorkspaceSpec {
        repository,
        path: worktree,
        branch,
        base: Some("HEAD".to_string()),
        owner: Some(pane),
    })
}
```

### Example 1: create a worktree and register it (TypeScript)

**Grants:** `workspace.manage`, `process.run:git`, `fs.read:project`, `fs.write:worktrees`

```ts
import { run } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';
import { register } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/workspace';
import type { FsPath, NodeId } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

/** Creates a worktree for `branch` and records it as owned by `pane`. */
export async function createAgentWorktree(
  repository: FsPath,
  worktree: FsPath,
  worktreeHostPath: string,
  branch: string,
  pane: NodeId,
): Promise<bigint> {
  const exit = await run({
    program: 'git',
    arguments: ['worktree', 'add', '-b', branch, worktreeHostPath, 'HEAD'],
    cwd: repository,
    stdin: undefined,
    environment: [],
    timeoutMillis: 60_000,
  });
  if (exit.status !== 0) {
    throw new Error(`git worktree add exited with status ${exit.status}`);
  }
  // register is synchronous: it returns the id or throws a PluginError.
  return register({ repository, path: worktree, branch, base: 'HEAD', owner: pane });
}
```

### Example 2: release a worktree after its pane closed (Rust and TypeScript)

When the owner pane closes, the kernel sets `owner` to `None`, and the record stays. The plugin keeps the id it received from `register` in its own [storage](/pages/api-storage/). It releases the record once no process uses the folder. A release that hits a running process returns `conflict`, so the plugin tries again later.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::workspace;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Returns true when the record is gone, false when it must be tried again later.
fn release_after_close(workspace_id: u64) -> Result<bool, PluginError> {
    let Some(info) = workspace::list().into_iter().find(|record| record.id == workspace_id) else {
        return Ok(true);
    };
    if info.in_use {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("worktree {workspace_id} is in use, trying later"));
        return Ok(false);
    }
    match workspace::release(workspace_id) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(true),
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Conflict => Ok(false),
        Err(error) => Err(error),
    }
}
```

```ts
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { list, release } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/workspace';
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

/** Returns true when the record is gone, false when it must be tried again later. */
export function releaseAfterClose(workspaceId: bigint): boolean {
  const info = list().find((record) => record.id === workspaceId);
  if (info === undefined) {
    return true;
  }
  if (info.inUse) {
    log('info', `worktree ${workspaceId} is in use, trying later`);
    return false;
  }
  try {
    release(workspaceId);
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'conflict') {
      return false;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

After `release` succeeds, the folder is still on disk. To remove it, the plugin runs `git worktree remove <path>` through `process.run:git`, as a separate step. The release record and the folder are two separate things.

### Live sessions across projects

One Ilium server runs per project session. A workspace plugin often needs to see the others: which sessions are running, and how busy they are. The `sessions` interface (server side, grant `sessions.cross`, medium to high risk) lists the user's live sessions and runs one command of the same plugin in another session.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/sessions in reference-wit
// ilium:host/sessions
record live-session { name: string, project: string, socket-id: string, panes: u32, attached-clients: u32, is-self: bool }
list-live: func() -> list<live-session>;
record cross-request { session: string, command: string, arguments-json: string }
send: func(request: cross-request) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
take-reply: func(request: request-id) -> option<string>;
```

| Function | Rust (`host::sessions`) | TypeScript (`host/sessions`) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list-live` | `list_live()` | `listLive()` | The user's running Ilium sessions on this machine. Another user's sockets are never visible. |
| `send` | `send(request)` | `send(request)` | Runs one command of this same plugin in the named session. Returns a request id. |
| `take-reply` | `take_reply(id)` | `takeReply(id)` | The reply text once the request completed, else none. |

Rules. The target session must have the same plugin installed and enabled, with `sessions.cross` granted there. The command must be one that the plugin declares. Kernel commands of another session cannot be reached. The request carries the caller's plugin id and session name, so the receiving command can tell who asked. A target that is not found is `not-found`; a target without the plugin or grant is `not-permitted`. A completion can fail with `timed-out` or `network`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::sessions::{self, CrossRequest};

/// Asks every other live session to report its busy agents.
fn ask_all() -> Vec<(String, Result<RequestId, PluginError>)> {
    sessions::list_live().into_iter()
        .filter(|session| !session.is_self)
        .map(|session| {
            let request = CrossRequest {
                session: session.name.clone(),
                command: "report-busy".into(),
                arguments_json: "{}".into(),
            };
            (session.name, sessions::send(&request))
        })
        .collect()
}

fn reply_for(request: RequestId) -> Option<String> {
    sessions::take_reply(request)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as sessions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions';

/** Asks every other live session to report its busy agents. */
export function askAll(): Array<{ session: string; request: bigint | Error }> {
  return sessions.listLive()
    .filter((session) => !session.isSelf)
    .map((session) => {
      try {
        const request = sessions.send({ session: session.name, command: 'report-busy', argumentsJson: '{}' });
        return { session: session.name, request };
      } catch (error) {
        return { session: session.name, request: error as Error };
      }
    });
}

export function replyFor(request: bigint): string | undefined {
  return sessions.takeReply(request);
}
```

### What the user sees

Pane 14 owns worktree 7. The plugin logs each step in `ilium plugin logs`.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs demo-worktrees
2026-10-11 12:04:11 <span class="t-ok">ok</span>   registered worktree 7 for pane 14
2026-10-11 12:09:40 <span class="t-warn">warn</span> worktree 7 is in use, trying later
2026-10-11 12:09:52 <span class="t-ok">ok</span>   released worktree 7, folder kept
2026-10-11 12:12:03 <span class="t-err">error</span> release 9: not-found, no such id
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. Each line is a plugin log entry. The retry in the second line is the plugin's own decision, based on `in_use`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Call | Code | When it happens |
|---|---|---|
| any | `not-permitted` | The `workspace.manage` grant is missing, or the folder is outside the granted scope. |
| `register` | `not-permitted` | The `path` lies outside `fs.write:worktrees`, or `repository` lies outside a read grant. |
| `register` | `not-found` | The repository is not a Git repository, or the `owner` node does not exist. |
| `register` | `conflict` | The `path` is already registered. |
| `register` | `invalid-argument` | The branch name is empty or not a valid Git branch name. |
| `release` | `not-found` | The id is not registered. A second release of the same id gives this too. |
| `release` | `conflict` | The worktree is in use (see `in_use`). Try again after the process ends. |

Edge cases:

- If `register` fails after git has created the folder, the folder stays on disk with no record. Remove it with `git worktree remove`, then try again.
- If the owner pane closes while a process still runs, `owner` becomes `None` and `release` returns `conflict` until the process ends.
- `base` is written to the record and shown in the list. The kernel does not use it. The plugin passes the same `base` it gave `git worktree add`.
- The records are the kernel's view. A plugin that has forgotten a worktree id can find the record again with `list`, matching on `path`.
- Every refusal is logged with the plugin id and function, and shows in `ilium plugin logs`.

### Used by

- Agent in a new Git worktree: calls `register` after `process.run` creates the worktree.
- Agent in an existing worktree: lists worktrees with `list`.
- Worktree cleanup and prune: calls `release` after `process.run` removes the worktree, behind a confirmation `popup`.

### See also

- Live sessions use the grant `sessions.cross`; see the [capability reference](/pages/reference-capabilities/).
- [Process control](/pages/api-process-control/) for the git commands and their grants.
- [Capability: workspace.manage](/pages/capability-workspace-manage/) for the grant and its risk.
- [File access](/pages/api-fs/) for the `worktrees` and `project` scopes.
- [Settings](/pages/api-settings/) for `workspace.worktree_root`.
- [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/) for the server side world that holds this import.

Matches `ilium:host/workspace@0.1.0`.

# toast

## toast

A toast is a short message that Ilium draws inside its own window, over the workspace, for a few seconds. It is the in-app counterpart of the desktop notice that the `notify` intent shows (see [Notifications and sounds](/pages/api-notifications/)). Use a toast when the user is looking at Ilium and the news is small: a copy finished, a scan found three items, a quota is nearly used. A toast carries a title, an optional body of rich text, a tone and at most two buttons. Each button runs one of the plugin's own commands.

Two intents control toasts: `toast` shows or replaces one, and `dismiss-toast` removes one. Both are submissions returned from the `handler` export. There is no read function: a plugin learns that the user pressed a button because its command is invoked, and it learns nothing else about the toast.

### What you need

- **Grant.** `notify.toast`. It is a normal-risk grant, available on the server and client sides. Request it per side in the manifest.
- **Commands.** Every toast button names a command that the plugin declares in `contributes.commands`. A button that names an unknown command refuses the whole intent with `invalid-argument`.
- **Language.** Rust with the crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with the package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both build the same intent record.

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["notify.toast"] },
"contributes": { "commands": [{ "id": "open-report", "title": "Open the scan report" }] }
```

See [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/) for how grants are requested and shown to the user. The desktop counterpart is [notify.desktop](/pages/capability-notify-desktop/).

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/text in reference-wit
enum tone { info, success, warning, danger, muted }
```

The `toast-spec` record below belongs to `ilium:types/intents`.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/intents in reference-wit
record toast-action { label: string, command: string }       // label <= 24 characters

record toast-spec {
  id: option<string>,                 // a toast with the same id is replaced in place
  tone: tone,
  title: string,                      // at most 60 characters
  body: option<rich-text>,            // at most 200 characters of text
  actions: list<toast-action>,        // at most 2
  duration-ms: option<u32>,           // 1,000 to 30,000
}

// intent cases
toast(toast-spec),
dismiss-toast(string),                // the id
```

| Intent | Rust | TypeScript | Grant | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toast` | `Intent::Toast(ToastSpec)` | `{ tag: 'toast', val: ToastSpec }` | `notify.toast` | `ok` once queued; `refused(rate-limited)`; `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `dismiss-toast` | `Intent::DismissToast(String)` | `{ tag: 'dismiss-toast', val: string }` | `notify.toast` | `ok`, also when the id is not on screen |

When `duration-ms` is none, a toast of tone `danger` stays until the user dismisses it, and any other tone stays 5,000 ms. A value outside 1,000 to 30,000 ms is refused with `invalid-argument`. The countdown is drawn by the host; the plugin is not called while it runs.

### How a toast looks

The host draws a toast as a small rounded panel with the usual Ilium title notch, the body, a dim line for the buttons, and a gauge that shrinks until the toast closes. The gauge uses `━` for the time left and `─` for the time spent, as the preview dialogs of the client do. The tone sets the border colour and the title colour; the glyphs are the same for every tone.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Copied 3 regions ──────────╮
│ Smart Copy kept the last 3 blocks │
│ of the output of pane Shell.      │
│ Open report · Dismiss             │
│ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━───────────────│
╰───────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A toast of tone success with one button, about 60 percent through its 5,000 ms. Drawn from the preview dialog of the real client: rounded border, chrome title, dim hint line, gauge of heavy and light horizontal bars.</figcaption>
</figure>

At most `toasts_pending` (3, the same for every tier) toasts are alive at once; a fourth replaces the oldest. A toast never takes keyboard focus away from the pane the user is typing in. The buttons answer to a click.

<svg viewBox="0 0 440 150" role="img" aria-label="Toast intent flow">

### Rules

- **Replace by id.** A toast whose `id` equals one already on screen replaces it in place and restarts its countdown. Use a stable id for progress-like news ("scan", "copied") so the stack does not fill with copies. A toast without an id is always new.
- **Rate.** 3 toasts per 10 seconds per plugin. The fourth within the window completes as `refused(rate-limited)`. Replacing by id counts as a toast.
- **Length.** The title is cut by the plugin: over 60 characters is `invalid-argument`, not a silent cut. The body is rich text with at most 200 characters in total; over that is `invalid-argument`. Button labels are at most 24 characters.
- **Buttons.** At most two. A button runs the named command with `origin: toast` and `context` set to the toast `id`. The toast closes when a button is pressed.
- **Accessibility.** With reduced motion the gauge is drawn as a fixed text `5 s left` that updates once per second, not as a shrinking bar. A `danger` toast never closes by itself.
- **Not a log.** A toast is gone when it closes. Put the permanent record in the plugin [log](/pages/api-log/), or in a pane.

### Examples

#### Example 1: a success toast with one button

Grants: `notify.toast`. Commands: `open-report`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, ToastAction, ToastSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::{RichSpan, Tone};

fn copied_toast(regions: usize) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
        id: Some("copied".into()),
        tone: Tone::Success,
        title: format!("Copied {regions} regions"),
        body: Some(vec![vec![RichSpan::plain("Smart Copy kept the last blocks.")]]),
        actions: vec![ToastAction { label: "Open report".into(), command: "open-report".into() }],
        duration_ms: None,
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { richSpan } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export function copiedToast(regions: number): Submission {
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'toast',
      val: {
        id: 'copied',
        tone: 'success',
        title: `Copied ${regions} regions`,
        body: [[richSpan('Smart Copy kept the last blocks.')]],
        actions: [{ label: 'Open report', command: 'open-report' }],
        durationMs: undefined,
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

#### Example 2: a danger toast, then dismiss it when the problem is gone

A `danger` toast has no timeout. The plugin removes it by id when the cause ends.

**Rust**

```rust
fn quota_alert(used_percent: u8) -> Vec<Submission> {
    if used_percent >= 95 {
        vec![Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
            id: Some("quota".into()),
            tone: Tone::Danger,
            title: "Quota almost used".into(),
            body: None,
            actions: vec![],
            duration_ms: None,
        }))]
    } else {
        vec![Submission::new(Intent::DismissToast("quota".into()))]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function quotaAlert(usedPercent: number): Submission[] {
  if (usedPercent >= 95) {
    return [{
      intent: { tag: 'toast', val: { id: 'quota', tone: 'danger', title: 'Quota almost used',
        body: undefined, actions: [], durationMs: undefined } },
      correlation: 1n, dedupKey: undefined,
    }];
  }
  return [{ intent: { tag: 'dismiss-toast', val: 'quota' }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined }];
}
```

### Errors and limits

| Case | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Grant `notify.toast` missing | `refused(not-permitted)` |
| 4th toast of the plugin within 10 s | `refused(rate-limited)` |
| Title over 60 characters, body over 200, more than 2 buttons, duration outside 1,000 to 30,000 ms | `refused(invalid-argument)` with the field in the message |
| Button names an unknown command | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `dismiss-toast` of an id not on screen | `ok` |

Limits: `toasts_pending` 3 (fixed), toast actions 2, body 200 characters, title 60 characters. See [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).

### See also

- [Notifications and sounds](/pages/api-notifications/) for desktop notices and the `coalesce-key` field.
- [Commands](/pages/api-commands/) for the commands that toast buttons run.
- [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for the outcome cases.
- [Command palette](/pages/api-command-palette/) for the other in-app surface that runs commands.

### Security

Toast text is sanitised and prefixed with the plugin name ([SEC-378], [SEC-380]).

# catalogs

## catalogs

A catalogue is a named list of options that a `choice` row or widget can read instead of carrying the options itself. Ilium owns seven catalogues of its own data: palettes, dithers, colour filters, style presets, icons, sounds and models. A plugin may read them, and may declare catalogues of its own that it serves with the `catalog-provider` export. The `catalogs` import is the way to query both. The host does the filtering and the ranking, so every catalogue filters the same way.

### You will need

| Need | Value |
|---|---|
| Side | Server, client and scene. The import is in all three base worlds. |
| Grant | None for `ilium.*` catalogues, except `ilium.models`, which needs `inference`. Reading another plugin's catalogue needs `services.use:catalog/<plugin-id>`. |
| Manifest (own catalogue) | `contributes.catalogs`: `{ id, title, item_kind }`, plus `"exports": ["catalog-provider"]`. At most 8 catalogues per plugin. |
| Rust | Crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, module `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::catalogs`; trait `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::CatalogProvider`. |
| TypeScript | Package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, module `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/catalogs`; member `queryCatalog` of `definePlugin`. |

### Interface

```wit
record catalog-item {
  id: string, title: string,
  description: option<string>,          // at most 120 characters
  preview: option<preview>,             // glyph, swatch or pattern
  group: option<string>,                // heading in the choice dialog, at most 32 characters
  keywords: list<string>,               // at most 8, matched by the filter
  disabled-reason: option<string>,      // at most 40 characters
}
record catalog-page { items: list<catalog-item>, next: option<string>, total: option<u32> }
record catalog-query { catalog: string, filter: string, cursor: option<string>, limit: u16 }   // limit 1..256

query: func(q: catalog-query) -> result<catalog-page, plugin-error>;       // synchronous for host catalogues
query-async: func(q: catalog-query) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;   // plugin catalogues
take-page: func(request: request-id) -> option<catalog-page>;
lookup: func(catalog: string, id: string) -> option<catalog-item>;

// export (with-catalog)
query-catalog: func(q: catalog-query) -> result<catalog-page, plugin-error>;
```

`preview` is one of `glyph(string)` (one grapheme), `swatch(list<u32>)` (1 to 16 RGB colours drawn as a strip of half blocks) or `pattern(list<string>)` (1 to 4 lines of at most 8 cells, drawn in the muted colour).

### Functions

| WIT function | Rust | TypeScript | Result | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `catalogs::query(&CatalogQuery) -> Result<CatalogPage, PluginError>` | `query(q: CatalogQuery): CatalogPage` | page | Returns a page of a host catalogue now. |
| `query-async` | `catalogs::query_async(&CatalogQuery) -> Result<RequestId, PluginError>` | `queryAsync(q): bigint` | `request-id` | Starts a query to a plugin catalogue. The page arrives as a request completion; read it with `take-page`. |
| `take-page` | `catalogs::take_page(RequestId) -> Option<CatalogPage>` | `takePage(request): CatalogPage \| undefined` | page | Takes the finished page once. |
| `lookup` | `catalogs::lookup(&str, &str) -> Option<CatalogItem>` | `lookup(catalog, id): CatalogItem \| undefined` | item | Returns one item by id, for example to show the title of a stored choice. |
| `query-catalog` (export) | `CatalogProvider::query_catalog(&mut self, q: CatalogQuery) -> Result<CatalogPage, PluginError>` | `queryCatalog(q): CatalogPage` | page | Serves a catalogue the plugin declared. |

### The host catalogues

| Id | Content | Preview | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ilium.palettes` | The 38 and more palette presets of the shared look | `swatch` | Read-only kernel data. |
| `ilium.dithers` | Every dither mode | `pattern` | |
| `ilium.filters` | The 46 colour filters | `swatch` | |
| `ilium.style-presets` | The 50 and more style presets | none | |
| `ilium.icons` | The icon catalogue, grouped by set | `glyph` | The glyphs are not copied into the manual; the catalogue is the source. |
| `ilium.sounds` | Bundled and contributed sounds | none | |
| `ilium.models` | Configured inference models | none | Needs the `inference` grant. |

Plugin catalogues have the global id `<plugin-id>/<id>`. An unknown catalogue returns `not-found`.

### How queries behave

- **Filter.** Case-insensitive substring over title, id and keywords. Entries whose title starts with the filter rank first. A plugin catalogue does not implement filtering: the host applies it to the items the provider returns, except that a provider may narrow its work using `filter`.
- **Paging.** `limit` is 1 to 256. `next` holds the cursor for the following page, `total` the full count when known.
- **Deadline.** The export has 20 ms. A slow source returns the page it has cached and calls `ui.invalidate` (or `settings.set-choice-items`) when fresh data arrives.
- **Use in rows and widgets.** A `choice` row names a catalogue with `"source": { "catalog": "ilium.palettes" }`, and the widget uses `source: "ilium.palettes"`. A source that names neither a host catalogue nor one of the plugin's own fails the install with `manifest.catalog-unknown`.
- **Activation.** The trigger `catalog:<id>` starts a stopped instance when a row or widget opens one of its catalogues.

### Example 1: read a host catalogue

List the first 20 icons that match a word.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::catalogs::{self, CatalogQuery};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{log, Level};

fn find_icons(word: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let page = catalogs::query(&CatalogQuery {
        catalog: "ilium.icons".into(),
        filter: word.into(),
        cursor: None,
        limit: 20,
    })?;
    for item in page.items {
        log(Level::Debug, &format!("{} {}", item.id, item.title));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { query } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/catalogs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export function findIcons(word: string): void {
  const page = query({ catalog: 'ilium.icons', filter: word, cursor: undefined, limit: 20 });
  for (const item of page.items) log('debug', `${item.id} ${item.title}`);
}
```

### Example 2: serve a catalogue of themes

The manifest declares `{ "id": "themes", "title": "Themes", "item_kind": "swatch" }`. A choice row uses `{ "source": { "catalog": "mythemes/themes" } }`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::CatalogProvider;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::CatalogItem;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::catalogs::{CatalogPage, CatalogQuery};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Preview;

impl CatalogProvider for Plugin {
    fn query_catalog(&mut self, _q: CatalogQuery) -> Result<CatalogPage, PluginError> {
        let items = self.themes.iter().map(|theme| {
            CatalogItem::new(&theme.id, &theme.name)
                .preview(Preview::Swatch(theme.colors.clone()))
                .group("Dark")
                .keywords(["night"])
        }).collect();
        Ok(CatalogPage { items, next: None, total: Some(self.themes.len() as u32) })
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { CatalogPage } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export const { catalogProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  queryCatalog(_q): CatalogPage {
    return {
      items: themes.map((theme) => ({
        id: theme.id, title: theme.name, description: undefined,
        preview: { tag: 'swatch', val: theme.colors },
        group: 'Dark', keywords: ['night'], disabledReason: undefined,
      })),
      next: undefined,
      total: themes.length,
    };
  },
});
```

### What the user sees

A `choice` with `style: "dialog"` opens the filterable choice dialog of the client: a rounded block with the options, `●` before the current option, a status line with the count and the current value, and the thumb `┃` on the scrollbar track when the list is longer than the dialog. A disabled option shows its reason in brackets.

<pre class="term">
╭  ≡ ● · Palette─────────────────────────╮
│ su                                     │
│   Sunset                              ││
│ ● Sunrise                             ┃│
│   Subtle grey [unavailable]           ││
│ 3 of 38 options · Current: Sunrise     │
│ Enter applies · Esc cancels            │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

The text lines are those of the client's choice dialog (`value_dialog.rs`). Swatch previews are drawn as a strip of half blocks next to the title and are not reproducible in plain text.

### Errors and limits

| Function | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| `query`, `query-async` | `not-found` | The catalogue does not exist. |
| `query`, `query-async` | `invalid-argument` | `limit` is 0 or above 256. |
| `query-async`, export | `timed-out` | The provider missed its 20 ms deadline. |
| `query`, `query-async` | `not-permitted` | `ilium.models` without `inference`, or another plugin's catalogue without `services.use`. |
| any | `internal` | A host bug. |

Caps: 8 catalogues per plugin, 256 items per page, `description` 120 characters, `group` 32, `disabled-reason` 40, 8 keywords per item. Install errors: `manifest.catalog-unknown`, `manifest.contribution-limit`.

- [Settings](/pages/api-settings/) for `choice` rows and `set-choice-items`.
- [Widgets: input](/pages/widgets-input/) for the `choice` widget.
- [Inference](/pages/api-inference/) for the model catalogue.
- [Services](/pages/api-services/) for `services.use`.

Contract: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, import `catalogs`, export fragment `with-catalog`.

# client requests

## client requests

A plugin has up to two sides that run in different processes: the server side, which lives with the session, and the client side, which lives in the terminal window the user attached. Some facts exist only in the client: the size of its terminal, its theme, the contents of its clipboard. The server side cannot read them. Without this interface a plugin would have to build a question and answer from two `messages` and a hand-made correlation id. The `client-requests` interface gives the server side a typed question and the client side a typed answer.

Use it when the server side needs one answer from one client now. Use [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/) for news that nobody has to answer. Client routing stays in the kernel.

    </marker>
  </defs>
  <text x="70" y="16" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">Server side</text>

<figcaption>The server side asks, the kernel delivers the question to the named client, the client answers once, and the server side takes the answer after the completion event.</figcaption>
