# menus

## menus

A menu is a list of entries the user picks from: a context menu opened by a right click, a submenu of a toolbar button, or the `menu` widget in a view. The menu model gives every entry an icon, a shortcut label, a checked state, a disabled reason, a tooltip and a danger flag, allows submenus two levels deep, and lets a plugin compute the entries when the menu opens through the `menu-provider` export.

### What you need

- **Grant.** `ui.panels` for menus in the plugin's own views; `ui.chrome` for menus attached to kernel surfaces (see [tree chrome](/pages/api-tree-chrome/)). The commands behind the entries need no extra grant.
- **Manifest.** Static entries in `contributes.context_menu` or `toolbar_buttons.submenu`; `dynamic: true` plus the export `menu-provider` for computed entries.

```json
"exports": ["menu-provider"],
"contributes": { "context_menu": [{ "id": "pane-actions", "applies_to": ["pane"], "dynamic": true, "command": "run-action" }] }
```

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/menu-provider in reference-wit
record menu-context { menu: string, node: option<node-id>, pane: option<node-id>, view: option<view-target>,
                      key: option<string>, buffer: option<buffer-id>, line: option<u32>, selection: option<string> }
record menu-entry {
  id: string, label: string, icon: option<string>, shortcut: option<string>,
  parent: option<string>,                 // id of a submenu entry; depth <= 2
  is-submenu: bool, separator-before: bool,
  checked: option<tri-state>, disabled-reason: option<string>,   // <= 40 characters
  tooltip: option<tooltip>, danger: bool,
}
// export menu-provider
menu-items: func(context: menu-context) -> list<menu-entry>;      // <= 64 entries
```

The host calls `menu-items` when a `dynamic` menu opens. The deadline is 20 ms; on a timeout the menu opens with its static entries only and the breach is counted. A click arrives as `command-invoked` with the menu's command and `arguments-json` `{"item": "<id>", ...context}`.

### Rules

- A menu has at most 64 entries; more are cut with `… N more`. Submenus nest at most 2 deep; static menus nested deeper fail the install with `manifest.menu-depth`.
- `disabled-reason` greys the entry, takes no click, and shows the reason as its tooltip (at most 40 characters).
- `icon` is a catalogue id or one glyph; normal icons are the default, a stable glyph only when the user opted in.
- `danger` draws the entry in the warning style.
- Placement, the submenu delay and the submenu stack belong to the host.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Pane ───────────────────╮
│ 🔎 Find in output     Ctrl+F   │
│ ✓ Follow output                │
│ 📋 Copy                      › │
│ ───────────────────────────────│
│ ❄ Freeze (no process)          │
│ 🚫 Close pane                  │
╰────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A context menu with an icon, shortcut label, check mark, submenu arrow (the client uses the single right angle quotation mark for it), separator and a dangerous entry. Rounded border and chrome title as in the client's panels; the exact row layout is the host's.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Examples

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

impl MenuProvider for Actions {
    fn menu_items(&mut self, context: MenuContext) -> Vec<MenuEntry> {
        let frozen = context.pane.map_or(false, |pane| self.is_frozen(pane));
        vec![
            MenuEntry::new("freeze", if frozen { "Unfreeze" } else { "Freeze" }).icon("❄"),
            MenuEntry::new("copy", "Copy").submenu(),
            MenuEntry::new("copy-last", "Last answer").parent("copy"),
            MenuEntry::new("close", "Close pane").danger().separator_before()
                .disabled_reason_if(context.pane.is_none(), "No pane here"),
        ]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type MenuContext, type MenuEntry } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export const { menuProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  menuItems(context: MenuContext): MenuEntry[] {
    const frozen = context.pane !== undefined && isFrozen(context.pane);
    return [
      { id: 'freeze', label: frozen ? 'Unfreeze' : 'Freeze', icon: '❄', isSubmenu: false, separatorBefore: false, danger: false },
      { id: 'copy', label: 'Copy', isSubmenu: true, separatorBefore: false, danger: false },
      { id: 'copy-last', label: 'Last answer', parent: 'copy', isSubmenu: false, separatorBefore: false, danger: false },
      { id: 'close', label: 'Close pane', danger: true, separatorBefore: true, isSubmenu: false,
        disabledReason: context.pane === undefined ? 'No pane here' : undefined },
    ];
  },
});
```

### Menus in own views

A `menu` widget inside a popup anchored `at-pointer` is a context menu for a view; open it on the `context-requested` action (see [popovers](/pages/api-popovers/)). The widget takes the same `menu-entry` list.

### Errors and limits

| Case | Effect |
|---|---|
| Provider over 20 ms | static entries only |
| Over 64 entries | cut with `… N more` |
| Submenu depth over 2 | `manifest.menu-depth` (static) or truncated (dynamic) |
| Entry command unknown | install refused or entry disabled |

- [commands](/pages/api-commands/), [command palette](/pages/api-command-palette/), [popovers](/pages/api-popovers/), [ui](/pages/api-ui/), [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/).

# geocode and location picker

## geocode and location picker

Geocoding turns a place name into coordinates and back. The host provides it as a service, so a plugin never needs the `http` grant for it: the host owns the provider (Photon, with Nominatim as fallback), the user agent, the attribution string and the rate limit. The same service feeds the `location-picker` widget, a world map the user clicks, and `location` settings rows.

### What you need

- **Grant.** `location.geocode` on the client side. The first call asks the user once for consent to send place names to the provider; without it calls return `not-permitted`.
- **Language.** Rust `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::geocode`, TypeScript `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/geocode`.

```json
"capabilities": { "client": ["location.geocode"] }
```

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/geocode in reference-wit
record geocode-query { text: string, near: option<geo-point>, limit: u8, language: option<string> }   // text 2..200; limit 1..8
search: func(q: geocode-query) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
reverse: func(point: geo-point) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;        // at most 1 result
take-places: func(request: request-id) -> option<list<geo-place>>;
```

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `geocode::search(&GeocodeQuery)` | `search(q)` | request id; places arrive with `take_places` |
| `reverse` | `geocode::reverse(GeoPoint)` | `reverse(point)` | request id |
| `take-places` | `geocode::take_places(request)` | `takePlaces(request)` | `Option<Vec<GeoPlace>>` |

Results are cached for 24 hours by query text. Up to 8 places are returned. An empty list is a valid answer, not an error. Rate: 1 request per second per plugin.

### The picker and the row

The `location-picker` widget draws the world as a Braille map (each cell holds a 2 by 4 dot pattern) and returns a `geo(geo-point)` value when the user clicks or searches. A `location` settings row embeds the same picker in a dialog and stores the point; the plugin may show it without ever seeing the coordinates as text.

<figure>

│ ⠀⠙⠿⣿⣿⠿⠋⠀⠀⠀⠀⠛⠿⣿⣿⠿⠛⠀⠀⠀⠈⠻⣿⣿⠟⠁⠀⠀⠀⠀             │

### Examples

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::geocode::{self, GeocodeQuery};

fn find(text: &str) -> Result<RequestId, PluginError> {
    geocode::search(&GeocodeQuery { text: text.into(), near: None, limit: 5, language: Some("en".into()) })
}
fn on_completed(request: RequestId) -> Vec<String> {
    geocode::take_places(request).unwrap_or_default().into_iter().map(|place| place.name).collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { search, takePlaces } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/geocode';

export const find = (text: string) => search({ text, near: undefined, limit: 5, language: 'en' });
export const onCompleted = (request: bigint): string[] => (takePlaces(request) ?? []).map((place) => place.name);
```

### Errors

| Case | Error |
|---|---|
| No consent | `not-permitted` |
| Over 1 request per second | `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms` |
| Text outside 2 to 200 characters, limit outside 1 to 8 | `invalid-argument` |
| Provider failure, or 10 s without answer | `network`, `timed-out` |

The privacy notice about sending place names to the provider is shown by the host, not the plugin. See [location](/pages/api-location/).

### See also

- [location](/pages/api-location/), [catalogs](/pages/api-catalogs/), [Settings](/pages/api-settings/), [Capabilities reference](/pages/reference-capabilities/).

# sessions

## sessions

The `sessions` import lets a server-side plugin see the other Ilium sessions that run on the same machine and run one command of its own in another session. Ilium keeps one server per project session, so a plugin in one session knows nothing about the others by default. This import closes that gap for commands such as a message to every agent in every session.

The import is deliberately narrow. A plugin can talk only to the same plugin in another session, and only to a command that plugin declared. It can never reach a kernel command of another session. The grant is high risk.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 440 250" role="img" aria-label="A plugin sends a command to the same plugin in another session">
  <defs>
    <marker id="api-sessions-arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="10" y="10" width="200" height="140" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="110" y="28" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">Session work (this one)</text>
  <rect x="30" y="44" width="160" height="34" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="110" y="65" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">Plugin sync, caller</text>
  <rect x="30" y="98" width="160" height="34" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>

  <text x="10" y="212" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">3. The target runs it. The caller takes the reply text later.</text>

<figcaption>The caller and the target run the same plugin. The kernel routes the request between the two session servers and delivers the reply as a completion.</figcaption>
</figure>

### What you need

- **Grant:** `sessions.cross`, server side only, no argument. High risk (see [capabilities](/pages/capabilities/)). The grant dialog shows it in the warning style, even for a bundled tier 1 plugin.
- **Both sessions:** the same plugin must be installed and enabled in the target session, with `sessions.cross` granted there too.
- **Tier:** the grant is limited to tier 1 and signed tier 2 plugins. An unsigned tier 3 plugin cannot hold it.
- **Language:** Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Imports: `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::sessions` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions`.

### Surface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/sessions in reference-wit
// ilium:host/sessions  (sessions.cross, server side)
record live-session {
  name: string,            // the session name, "default" for a bare ilium
  project: string,         // the canonical project directory
  socket-id: string,       // the kernel's identity of the session socket
  panes: u32,
  attached-clients: u32,
  is-self: bool,           // true for the session that runs this plugin instance
}
list-live: func() -> list<live-session>;

record cross-request { session: string, command: string, arguments-json: string }
send: func(request: cross-request) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
take-reply: func(request: request-id) -> option<string>;
```

| WIT function | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list-live` | `sessions::list_live() -> Vec<LiveSession>` | `listLive(): LiveSession[]` | The user's running Ilium sessions on this machine. Other users' sockets are never visible. Synchronous. |
| `send` | `sessions::send(request: CrossRequest) -> Result<RequestId, PluginError>` | `send(request: CrossRequest): bigint` | Runs one command of the same plugin in another session. Asynchronous. The reply arrives as `request-completed`. |
| `take-reply` | `sessions::take_reply(request: RequestId) -> Option<String>` | `takeReply(request: bigint): string \| undefined` | Takes the reply text, once. The reply is whatever the target command returned. |

#### Records

| Record | Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|
| `live-session` | `LiveSession { name: String, project: String, socket_id: String, panes: u32, attached_clients: u32, is_self: bool }` | `{ name: string; project: string; socketId: string; panes: number; attachedClients: number; isSelf: boolean }` |
| `cross-request` | `CrossRequest { session: String, command: String, arguments_json: String }` | `{ session: string; command: string; argumentsJson: string }` |

`session` in a `cross-request` is the `name` of a `live-session`. `command` is the id of a command the plugin declared in `contributes.commands`. `arguments-json` is a JSON text passed to that command as its arguments. The request carries the caller's plugin id and the caller's session name, so the target command can tell where a call came from.

### How a call runs

1. The caller calls `list-live` and picks a session whose `is-self` is `false`.
2. The caller calls `send`. The kernel checks the grant, finds the session, and checks the target.
3. The target kernel runs the command in its copy of the same plugin. The request carries the caller's plugin id and session name.
4. The target returns a reply text. The caller's kernel completes the request, and the caller takes the reply with `take-reply`.

The target must have the plugin installed and enabled with `sessions.cross` granted, and the command must be declared by that plugin. If any of these fail, `send` returns `not-permitted`. Kernel commands are never reachable (D16).

### Worked example: ask every other session for its pane count

A plugin declares a command `pane-count` that returns the number of panes in its session as JSON. A second command, `count-everywhere`, asks all other sessions and sums the replies. This is the pattern of a message to all agents in all sessions, reduced to a count.

Manifest:

```json
{
  "capabilities": { "server": ["sessions.cross", "cli.contribute"] },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [{ "id": "pane-count", "title": "Count panes" }],
    "cli": { "name": "count-everywhere", "summary": "Count panes in every session" }
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;

use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{cli, sessions};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::sessions::CrossRequest;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct CountEverywhere {
    /// Request id to (invocation, session name).
    waiting: HashMap<RequestId, (u64, String)>,
    /// Invocation to the number of replies still expected and the sum so far.
    totals: HashMap<u64, (usize, u64)>,
}

impl Lifecycle for CountEverywhere {}

impl CountEverywhere {
    fn start(&mut self, invocation: u64) {
        let others: Vec<_> = sessions::list_live().into_iter().filter(|s| !s.is_self).collect();
        if others.is_empty() {
            let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, r#"{"type":"summary","sessions":0,"panes":0}"#);
            cli::finish(invocation, 0);
            return;
        }
        let mut sent = 0;
        for session in &others {
            let request = CrossRequest {
                session: session.name.clone(),
                command: "pane-count".into(),
                arguments_json: "{}".into(),
            };
            match sessions::send(request) {
                Ok(id) => {
                    self.waiting.insert(id, (invocation, session.name.clone()));
                    sent += 1;
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    let line = format!(
                        r#"{{"type":"warning","session":"{}","code":"{:?}"}}"#,
                        session.name, error.code
                    );
                    let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
                }
            }
        }
        self.totals.insert(invocation, (sent, 0));
        if sent == 0 {
            cli::finish(invocation, 1);
        }
    }

    fn on_reply(&mut self, id: RequestId, is_ok: bool) {
        let Some((invocation, name)) = self.waiting.remove(&id) else { return };
        let panes = sessions::take_reply(id)
            .filter(|_| is_ok)
            .and_then(|text| text.trim().parse::<u64>().ok());
        let Some((remaining, sum)) = self.totals.get_mut(&invocation) else { return };
        *remaining -= 1;
        match panes {
            Some(count) => {
                *sum += count;
                let line = format!(r#"{{"type":"session","name":"{name}","panes":{count}}}"#);
                let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
            }
            None => {
                let line = format!(r#"{{"type":"warning","session":"{name}","code":"no-reply"}}"#);
                let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
            }
        }
        if *remaining == 0 {
            let line = format!(r#"{{"type":"summary","panes":{}}}"#, *sum);
            let _ = cli::write_line(invocation, &line);
            cli::finish(invocation, 0);
            self.totals.remove(&invocation);
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as cli from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/cli';
import * as sessions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions';

const waiting = new Map<bigint, { invocation: bigint; name: string }>();
const totals = new Map<bigint, { remaining: number; sum: number }>();

function start(invocation: bigint): void {
  const others = sessions.listLive().filter((session) => !session.isSelf);
  if (others.length === 0) {
    cli.writeLine(invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'summary', sessions: 0, panes: 0 }));
    cli.finish(invocation, 0);
    return;
  }
  let sent = 0;
  for (const session of others) {
    try {
      const id = sessions.send({ session: session.name, command: 'pane-count', argumentsJson: '{}' });
      waiting.set(id, { invocation, name: session.name });
      sent += 1;
    } catch (error) {
      const code = error instanceof Error ? error.name : 'error';
      cli.writeLine(invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'warning', session: session.name, code }));
    }
  }
  totals.set(invocation, { remaining: sent, sum: 0 });
  if (sent === 0) cli.finish(invocation, 1);
}

function onReply(id: bigint, isOk: boolean): void {
  const entry = waiting.get(id);
  if (entry === undefined) return;
  waiting.delete(id);
  const total = totals.get(entry.invocation);
  if (total === undefined) return;
  total.remaining -= 1;
  const text = isOk ? sessions.takeReply(id) : undefined;
  const panes = text === undefined ? Number.NaN : Number.parseInt(text.trim(), 10);
  if (Number.isNaN(panes)) {
    cli.writeLine(entry.invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'warning', session: entry.name, code: 'no-reply' }));
  } else {
    total.sum += panes;
    cli.writeLine(entry.invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'session', name: entry.name, panes }));
  }
  if (total.remaining === 0) {
    cli.writeLine(entry.invocation, JSON.stringify({ type: 'summary', panes: total.sum }));
    cli.finish(entry.invocation, 0);
    totals.delete(entry.invocation);
  }
}

export const { handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'cli-invoked' && event.val.name === 'count-everywhere') start(event.val.invocation);
      else if (event.tag === 'request-completed') onReply(event.val.request, event.val.outcome.tag === 'ok');
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The `pane-count` command in the target session answers from its own tree and returns the number as text. Its handler is an ordinary command handler and needs no special code to be reachable from another session, because the request carries the caller's plugin id and session name.

### What the user sees

The user runs the plugin's own CLI command. The plugin writes one JSON line per session and a summary. This is the same line shape that `ilium broadcast` prints in the repository (types `progress`, `result`, `warning` and `summary`).

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium count-everywhere
<span class="t-dim">{"type":"session","name":"default","panes":5}</span>
<span class="t-dim">{"type":"session","name":"docs","panes":3}</span>
<span class="t-warn">{"type":"warning","session":"build","code":"NotPermitted"}</span>
<span class="t-dim">{"type":"summary","panes":8}</span>
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> echo $?
0
</pre>
<figcaption>The plugin asks three other sessions. The session named build has no matching plugin enabled, so the send is refused with not-permitted (the Rust example prints the code with its debug name). Illustrative, not generated.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Error codes

| Function | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| `list-live` | none | Returns an empty list when only this session runs. |
| `send` | `not-permitted` | The grant is missing here, the target lacks the plugin or the grant, the target plugin is disabled, or the command is not declared by the plugin. |
| `send` | `not-found` | No live session has the given name. |
| completion | `timed-out` | The target did not answer in time. |
| completion | `network` | The target session's socket closed before the reply. |
| `take-reply` | none | Returns `none` when the reply was already taken, or when the request failed. |

### Limits

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Reply hold time | 30 s, or until taken once, as for every `take-*` function |
| Sessions visible | Only the sessions of the current user on this machine |
| Reach | The same plugin id, commands declared in `contributes.commands` only |
| Tier | Tier 1 and signed tier 2 |

### Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The target session stops while the request runs | The request completes as `failed(network)`. |
| The target does not declare the command | `send` returns `not-permitted`. |
| A plugin lists a session it cannot reach | The session is listed. Only `send` reveals whether the plugin is enabled there. |
| Many `send` calls in one batch | Each gets its own request id. Replies can arrive in any order. |

<div class="warn">
<p>A plugin that holds <code>sessions.cross</code> can run its own commands in every session of the user. Declare only commands that are safe to run from another session, and validate <code>arguments-json</code> in the target as for any untrusted input.</p>
</div>

### See also

- [cli](/pages/api-cli/) for the commands that usually start a cross-session call.
- [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for `request-completed` and the `take-*` pattern.
- [commands](/pages/api-commands/) for declaring the command that the target runs.
- [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/) for risk levels and the grant dialog.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the common error codes.

Interface version: `ilium:host/sessions`, version 0.1.

# fs: atomic write, revisions, tail, agent homes

## fs: atomic write, revisions, tail, agent homes

The `fs` import also offers four things for plugins that share files with other programs: a read that returns a revision token, a write that succeeds only when the file is still at that revision, a cursor-based `tail` for growing files, and three more agent home scopes. They are specified in section 6.29. The base functions (`read`, `write`, `lock`, `watch` and the scopes) are on the [fs](/pages/api-fs/) page; read that first.

### What you need

| Function | Grant | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `read-with-revision` | `fs.read:<scope>` | async, completes with `take-revisioned` |
| `write-atomic` | `fs.write:<scope>` | async, completes with `take-written` |
| `tail` | `fs.read:<scope>` | sync |

No new grant exists. The grant of the scope is the grant of the call. Available on the server, client and scene sides.

The additional scopes:

| Scope (grant argument) | Preopen | Root | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-sessions:gemini` | `/agent-sessions/gemini` | the Gemini CLI transcripts, `~/.gemini/tmp/*/chats` | high for read; a write grant is refused at install, as for every `agent-sessions` scope |
| `agent-config:gemini` | `/agent-config/gemini` | the Gemini CLI configuration, `~/.gemini/settings.json` | normal for read, high for write |
| `agent-config:antigravity` | `/agent-config/antigravity` | the Antigravity configuration directory | normal for read, high for write |

The kernel resolves each root per platform, so a plugin never builds the home path itself. A scope whose directory does not exist is still granted; the calls then return `not-found`.

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["fs.read:agent-sessions:gemini", "fs.read:agent-config:gemini", "fs.write:agent-config:gemini"] }
```

### Signatures

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/fs in reference-wit
type revision-token = string;     // opaque; equal tokens mean equal content
record revisioned { bytes: list<u8>, revision: revision-token }
record tail-chunk { bytes: list<u8>, cursor: u64, truncated: bool }

read-with-revision: func(path: fs-path) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
take-revisioned: func(request: request-id) -> option<revisioned>;
write-atomic: func(path: fs-path, data: list<u8>, expected: option<revision-token>) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
take-written: func(request: request-id) -> option<revision-token>;
tail: func(path: fs-path, cursor: u64, max-bytes: u32) -> result<tail-chunk, plugin-error>;
```

| Rust | TypeScript | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `fs::read_with_revision(&path).await` | `await readWithRevision(path)` | `Revisioned { bytes, revision }` |
| `fs::write_atomic(&path, data, expected).await` | `await writeAtomic(path, data, expected)` | the new `RevisionToken` (`string`) |
| `fs::tail(&path, cursor, max_bytes)` | `tail(path, cursor, maxBytes)` | `TailChunk { bytes, cursor, truncated }` (`cursor` is `bigint` in TypeScript) |

A revision token is opaque. It is a hash of the content plus the size and the modification time, and two equal tokens mean equal content. A plugin stores it and passes it back; it never parses it.

### Atomic write and the expected revision

`write-atomic` writes to a temporary file in the directory of the target and renames it over the target, so a reader never sees a half-written file. The `expected` argument decides when the rename is allowed:

| `expected` | The write succeeds when | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | the file does not exist | completion `failed(conflict)` |
| `some(token)` | the file still has that revision | completion `failed(conflict)` |

On success the completion carries the revision of the new content, which is the `expected` value for the next write. The check and the rename are one step in the host, so two plugins that read the same revision cannot both win.

### Example: update a board file without losing another writer's change

A kanban plugin reads its board file with a revision, changes one card and writes it back. On `conflict` it rereads and applies the change again, at most three times. `move_card` is the plugin's own pure function.

**Grants:** `fs.read:project`, `fs.write:project`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;

const BOARD: &str = ".kanban/board.json";
const MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 3;

async fn move_card_on_disk(card: String, column: String) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: BOARD.into() };
    for _attempt in 0..MAX_ATTEMPTS {
        let current = fs::read_with_revision(&path).await?;
        let updated = move_card(&current.bytes, &card, &column)?;
        match fs::write_atomic(&path, updated, Some(current.revision)).await {
            Ok(_new_revision) => return Ok(()),
            Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Conflict => continue,
            Err(error) => return Err(error),
        }
    }
    Err(PluginError {
        code: ErrorCode::Conflict,
        message: "the board kept changing; gave up after 3 attempts".to_string(),
        retry_after_ms: None,
    })
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { readWithRevision, writeAtomic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { moveCard } from './board';

const BOARD = { scope: 'project', path: '.kanban/board.json' };
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;

export async function moveCardOnDisk(card: string, column: string): Promise<void> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
    const current = await readWithRevision(BOARD);
    const updated = moveCard(current.bytes, card, column);
    try {
      await writeAtomic(BOARD, updated, current.revision);
      return;
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'conflict') {
        continue;
      }
      throw error;
    }
  }
  throw new PluginError('conflict', 'the board kept changing; gave up after 3 attempts');
}
```

To create a file that must not exist yet, pass `None` (`undefined` in TypeScript) as `expected`. Combine `write-atomic` with `lock` when several plugins must also serialize longer read-modify-write sequences; the revision alone detects a lost update but does not queue writers.

### Tail: read what was appended

`tail(path, cursor, max-bytes)` returns the bytes after `cursor` and the cursor to use next. Start with cursor 0. It never blocks and returns at most 1 MiB per call.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bytes` | New bytes since the cursor, possibly empty. |
| `cursor` | Offset to pass to the next call. |
| `truncated` | `true` when the file became shorter than the cursor or was replaced. The read then restarted at 0 and `bytes` is the new start of the file. Drop any partial line you kept. |

A cursor may end in the middle of a line, because a writer can be between two `write` calls. Keep the incomplete tail of the last chunk in the plugin and prepend it to the next one.

### Example: follow a log and react to each complete line

The plugin follows a log file when `fs-changed` arrives. It keeps the cursor and the unfinished last line.

**Grants:** `fs.read:project`, `fs.watch:project`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::FsChangedEvent;

const LOG: &str = ".ilium/agent.log";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct LogFollower {
    watch: Option<u64>,
    cursor: u64,
    partial: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Lifecycle for LogFollower {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: LOG.into() };
        self.watch = Some(fs::watch(&path, false)?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for LogFollower {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::FsChanged(FsChangedEvent { watch, .. }) = event else { continue };
            if self.watch != Some(watch) {
                continue;
            }
            self.drain();
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl LogFollower {
    fn drain(&mut self) {
        let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: LOG.into() };
        loop {
            let Ok(chunk) = fs::tail(&path, self.cursor, 65_536) else { return };
            if chunk.truncated {
                self.partial.clear();
            }
            self.cursor = chunk.cursor;
            let empty = chunk.bytes.is_empty();
            self.partial.extend_from_slice(&chunk.bytes);
            while let Some(end) = self.partial.iter().position(|byte| *byte == b'\n') {
                let line: Vec<u8> = self.partial.drain(..=end).collect();
                handle_line(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&line));
            }
            if empty {
                return;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { tail, watch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';

const LOG = { scope: 'project', path: '.ilium/agent.log' };
let logWatch: bigint | undefined;
let cursor = 0n;
let partial = '';
const decoder = new TextDecoder();

function drain(): void {
  for (;;) {
    const chunk = tail(LOG, cursor, 65536);
    if (chunk.truncated) {
      partial = '';
    }
    cursor = chunk.cursor;
    partial += decoder.decode(chunk.bytes, { stream: true });
    let end = partial.indexOf('\n');
    while (end >= 0) {
      handleLine(partial.slice(0, end));
      partial = partial.slice(end + 1);
      end = partial.indexOf('\n');
    }
    if (chunk.bytes.length === 0) {
      return;
    }
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    logWatch = watch(LOG, false);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'fs-changed' && event.val.watch === logWatch) {
        drain();
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

`handle_line` and `handleLine` are the plugin's own code. A watch event says that something changed; it does not carry bytes, so `tail` is how the plugin gets them.

### Agent homes

The three scopes above let a plugin read what the Gemini CLI and Antigravity store, in the same way the Claude and Codex scopes work. Typical uses: list Gemini chats for a transcript view, read the auto-compact setting of an agent, or write a hook entry into an agent configuration. A write to a configuration file should use `write-atomic` with the revision read just before, so an edit by the agent itself is never overwritten.

**Rust**

```rust
let settings = FsPath { scope: "agent-config:gemini".into(), path: "settings.json".into() };
let current = fs::read_with_revision(&settings).await?;
let updated = add_hook(&current.bytes)?;
fs::write_atomic(&settings, updated, Some(current.revision)).await?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const settings = { scope: 'agent-config:gemini', path: 'settings.json' };
const current = await readWithRevision(settings);
await writeAtomic(settings, addHook(current.bytes), current.revision);
```

Paths inside an agent scope are relative to the root the kernel resolved, so a Gemini chat is addressed as `<project-hash>/chats/<file>` under `agent-sessions:gemini`. Use `list-dir` or `scan` with a glob to find them.

### What the user sees

The grant dialog shows the new scopes in plain words. A high-risk grant is drawn in the warning style, and a write to an agent configuration is logged at info level like every write outside `data` and `cache`.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.kanban --tail 4
<span class="t-dim">10:02:11</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  fs.write project .kanban/board.json replace
<span class="t-dim">10:02:13</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>  fs.write-atomic .kanban/board.json: conflict
<span class="t-dim">10:02:13</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  fs.write project .kanban/board.json replace
<span class="t-dim">10:02:40</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  fs.write agent-config:gemini settings.json
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> <span class="t-dim">4 lines shown, 0 dropped</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The log of a plugin that lost one write race, retried on the new revision and then edited the Gemini configuration.

### Errors and limits

| Function | Sync codes | Completion codes |
|---|---|---|
| `read-with-revision` | `not-permitted`, `invalid-argument` | `not-found`, `quota-exceeded` (over `fs_read_all_mib`), `io` |
| `write-atomic` | `not-permitted`, `invalid-argument` (over `fs_write_mib`, read-only scope) | `conflict` (revision differs, or the file exists and `expected` is `none`), `not-found` (parent folder missing), `io` |
| `tail` | `not-permitted`, `not-found`, `invalid-argument` (`max-bytes` over 1 MiB), `io` | none, the call is sync |

Limits: `tail` returns at most 1 MiB per call; `read-with-revision` is bounded by `fs_read_all_mib`; `write-atomic` by `fs_write_mib` (16 MiB by default). The temporary file counts against `disk_mib` for `data` and `cache` until the rename.

# http streams

## http streams

A stream is an HTTP response that the plugin reads piece by piece while it is still arriving. Use it for server-sent events, newline-delimited JSON, long downloads and live feeds, where `fetch` (which waits for the whole body) does not fit. Streams are specified in section 6.30. They use the same `http:<host-pattern>` grant as [http](/pages/api-http/), so read that page for request, header and host-pattern rules.

### What you need

- The grant `http:<host-pattern>` of the target host, on the side that opens the stream. There is no separate stream grant.
- Optionally `http:setting:<key>`, when the host comes from a setting the user edits. See [Hosts from a setting](#hosts-from-a-setting).
- Room under the `http_streams` limit: 4 open streams per plugin by default, 16 at the T1 ceiling, 4 at the T2 and T3 ceiling, and 64 for the whole session.
- Sides: server, client and scene (animation) worlds.

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["http:stream.example.com"], "client": ["http:setting:feed_host"] }
```

### Signatures

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/http in reference-wit
enum stream-framing { raw, lines, server-sent-events, ndjson }
record stream-request { request: http-request, framing: stream-framing, max-chunk-bytes: u32 }   // <= 1 MiB
type stream-id = u64;
open-stream: func(request: stream-request) -> result<stream-id, plugin-error>;
close-stream: func(stream: stream-id);
// @unstable(feature = websocket)
open-websocket: func(url: string, protocols: list<string>) -> result<stream-id, plugin-error>;
send-websocket: func(stream: stream-id, text: string) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
```

Events (section 12.1):

| Event | Payload | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| `http-stream-data` | `stream: stream-id`, `status: option<u16>`, `headers: option<list<header>>` (`some` on the first chunk only), `chunk: list<u8>` | Never dropped. The host stops reading the socket while the queue is full. |
| `http-stream-closed` | `stream: stream-id`, `outcome: stream-outcome` (`ended`, `cancelled`, `failed(plugin-error)`) | Never dropped. |

| Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|
| `http::open_stream(StreamRequest { request, framing, max_chunk_bytes })?` returns `StreamId` | `openStream({ request, framing, maxChunkBytes })` returns `bigint` |
| `http::close_stream(stream)` | `closeStream(stream)` |
| `Event::HttpStreamData(HttpStreamDataEvent)`, `Event::HttpStreamClosed(HttpStreamClosedEvent)` | `{ tag: 'http-stream-data', val }`, `{ tag: 'http-stream-closed', val }` |
| `http::open_websocket(&url, &protocols)?` (unstable) | `openWebsocket(url, protocols)` (unstable) |
| `http::send_websocket(stream, &text)?` (unstable) | `sendWebsocket(stream, text)` (unstable) |

`open-stream` returns at once with the id; connecting, status and data all arrive as events. A stream is owned by the plugin that opened it. It closes when the server ends the body, when the plugin calls `close-stream`, when the connection fails, or when the plugin deactivates, traps or loses the grant. On those last three the host does not deliver `http-stream-closed` to the dead instance.

### Framing

Framing decides what one `http-stream-data` chunk contains. With every framing except `raw`, the host splits the body, so a chunk is one complete record and the plugin never reassembles lines.

| Framing | One chunk is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `raw` | Whatever bytes arrived, at most `max-chunk-bytes` | Larger network reads are split. Use it for downloads and binary data. |
| `lines` | One line without its terminator | `\n` and `\r\n` both end a line. |
| `server-sent-events` | The payload of one event | The host does the SSE parsing, so the plugin sees records, not `data:` prefixes. |
| `ndjson` | One JSON text line | The host does not parse the JSON. A blank line is skipped. |

`max-chunk-bytes` is at most 1 MiB. A record longer than that is delivered in several chunks.

<title>HTTP stream sequence</title>
<desc>The plugin calls open-stream and receives a stream id. The host connects, the first http-stream-data event carries the status and headers, later events carry chunks, and http-stream-closed ends the stream. The plugin may close earlier.</desc>

<figcaption>The first data event carries the status and headers. The closed event always ends a stream that the server or the network ends.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Example: follow a server-sent event feed

The plugin opens one feed when it activates, keeps the stream id, and handles each event as one chunk. When the stream closes with a retryable error, it reopens after the delay in `retry-after-ms`. `apply_update` and `applyUpdate` are the plugin's own code.

**Grants:** `http:feed.example.com`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, Header, HttpRequest, StreamFraming, StreamRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::{HttpStreamClosedEvent, HttpStreamDataEvent};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct FeedReader {
    stream: Option<u64>,
}

impl FeedReader {
    fn open(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let request = HttpRequest {
            method: "GET".to_string(),
            url: "https://feed.example.com/v1/events".to_string(),
            headers: vec![Header { name: "accept".into(), value: "text/event-stream".into() }],
            body: None,
            timeout_millis: 300_000,
        };
        self.stream = Some(http::open_stream(StreamRequest {
            request,
            framing: StreamFraming::ServerSentEvents,
            max_chunk_bytes: 65_536,
        })?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Lifecycle for FeedReader {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        self.open()
    }
    fn deactivate(&mut self, _reason: DeactivationReason) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        if let Some(stream) = self.stream.take() {
            http::close_stream(stream);
        }
        None
    }
}

impl Handler for FeedReader {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::HttpStreamData(HttpStreamDataEvent { stream, chunk, .. })
                    if self.stream == Some(stream) =>
                {
                    apply_update(&chunk);
                }
                Event::HttpStreamClosed(HttpStreamClosedEvent { stream, outcome })
                    if self.stream == Some(stream) =>
                {
                    self.stream = None;
                    if let Err(error) = outcome {
                        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("feed closed: {:?}", error.code));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { closeStream, openStream } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { applyUpdate } from './feed';

let stream: bigint | undefined;

function open(): void {
  stream = openStream({
    request: {
      method: 'GET',
      url: 'https://feed.example.com/v1/events',
      headers: [{ name: 'accept', value: 'text/event-stream' }],
      body: undefined,
      timeoutMillis: 300000,
    },
    framing: 'server-sent-events',
    maxChunkBytes: 65536,
  });
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    open();
  },
  deactivate() {
    if (stream !== undefined) {
      closeStream(stream);
      stream = undefined;
    }
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'http-stream-data' && event.val.stream === stream) {
        applyUpdate(event.val.chunk);
      } else if (event.tag === 'http-stream-closed' && event.val.stream === stream) {
        stream = undefined;
        if (event.val.outcome.tag === 'err') {
          log('warn', `feed closed: ${event.val.outcome.val.code}`);
        }
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Example: NDJSON progress lines

The same code with `framing: NDJSON` (`'ndjson'` in TypeScript) delivers one JSON object per chunk. Parse inside the handler and ignore a line that does not parse; a server may interleave comments or keep-alive text.

**Rust**

```rust
if let Ok(update) = serde_json::from_slice::<Update>(&chunk) {
    self.progress = update.percent;
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
try {
  const update = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(chunk)) as { percent: number };
  progress = update.percent;
} catch {
  // ignore a line that is not JSON
}
```

For an unbounded download, use `raw` and write each chunk with `fs.write` in `append` mode; the host's back-pressure then paces the socket to the disk.

### Politeness

The host, not the plugin, keeps requests polite, so several plugins cannot flood one server.

| Mechanism | Effect |
|---|---|
| Per-host rate limiter | Requests to one host are spaced by the host. A request over the allowance fails with `rate-limited`. |
| `Retry-After` | A server `Retry-After` makes the call, or the stream, fail with `rate-limited` and `retry-after-ms` set. Wait that long before the next open. |
| ETag cache for `fetch` | The host sends `If-None-Match` for a URL it has seen and returns a cached `304` as the cached `200`. The plugin always sees a `200` with the full body. |
| Back-pressure | While the plugin's event queue is full, the host stops reading the socket instead of dropping data. |
| Session cap | At most 64 open streams for the whole session and 32 connections. |

### Hosts from a setting

When the user chooses the server, as with an Overpass or tile mirror, the manifest declares `http:setting:<key>` instead of a fixed host. `<key>` must be one of the plugin's own setting keys (otherwise `manifest.grant-argument`). The setting is a `text` row with `item_format: "url"` or `"host"`, or a `list` of them. Wildcards in a stored value are refused.

```json
{
  "contributes": { "settings": { "sections": [ { "id": "feed", "rows": [
    { "key": "feed_host", "type": "text", "label": "Feed server", "item_format": "host", "default": "feed.example.com" }
  ] } ] } },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["http:setting:feed_host"] }
}
```

The host checks the current value at `open-stream` and at `fetch`. When the value changes to a host the user has not confirmed, the user is asked once, before the first request. Until the answer, calls to that host fail with `not-permitted`.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">╭  ≡ ● · Allow new host──────────────────────────╮</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> example.map wants to connect to:               <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>   <span class="t-hi">overpass.local.example:8443</span>                  <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> This host comes from its setting "Feed server".<span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>                                                <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>        Esc Deny              Enter Allow       <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> Esc cancel · Enter allow                       <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The confirmation after the user edits a host setting, drawn in the style of the client's confirm dialogs: rounded border, chrome title, key hints and a dim hint line. The exact wording is the host's.

The setting row itself looks like any text row, with leaders:

<pre class="term">Feed server …………………………………… [ overpass.local.example:8443 ]
</pre>

### WebSocket (unstable)

`open-websocket` and `send-websocket` exist only when the feature `websocket` is enabled for development builds (`@unstable(feature = websocket)`). The functions are absent from stable builds. Server frames arrive as `http-stream-data` events and the end as `http-stream-closed`. Send text with `send-websocket`. The grant is the same `http:<host-pattern>`, for a `wss://` URL.

### Errors and limits

| Code | Where | When |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | `open-stream`, at once | Host not granted, not yet confirmed (setting host), or a redirect led to an ungranted host. |
| `quota-exceeded` | `open-stream`, at once | `http_streams` reached for the plugin or the session. |
| `invalid-argument` | `open-stream`, at once | `max-chunk-bytes` over 1 MiB, or the request rules of [http](/pages/api-http/) are broken. |
| `unsupported` | `open-websocket` | The feature `websocket` is off. |
| `network` | `http-stream-closed` | DNS, TLS or connect failure, or a dropped connection. |
| `timed-out` | `http-stream-closed` | No byte arrived before `timeout_millis`. |
| `rate-limited` | `http-stream-closed` or at once | The per-host limiter or a `Retry-After`; `retry-after-ms` is set. |
| `revoked` | `http-stream-closed` | The grant changed while the stream was open. |

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| `http_streams` per plugin | 4 default, 16 T1 ceiling, 4 T2 and T3 ceiling |
| Streams per session | 64 |
| Chunk | at most 1 MiB; larger records are split |

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.feed --tail 4
<span class="t-dim">09:30:00</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  http.open-stream feed.example.com sse
<span class="t-dim">09:30:00</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  stream 7 opened: status 200
<span class="t-dim">09:41:12</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>  stream 7 closed: rate-limited, retry in 30000 ms
<span class="t-dim">09:41:42</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  http.open-stream feed.example.com sse
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. A plugin log of a stream that the server closed with a `Retry-After`.

# gpu

## gpu

<div class="warn">

This interface is `@unstable(feature = gpu-kernels)`. It exists only in development builds, the grant `gpu.kernels` appears only there, and its shape can change before it is stable (D18).

</div>

The `gpu` import lets a scene run a small fixed set of image kernels on the graphics card: blur, threshold, palette mapping, ordered dithering and scaling. The kernels belong to the host. A plugin never ships shader code, and it never sees a graphics device; it hands over pixels and gets pixels back. Without a graphics card, every kernel runs on a CPU fallback and returns the same result, only slower. The specification is section 6.35. It exists so animation scenes such as clouds, dithered waves and pattern fields can offload their heaviest per-pixel step.

### What you need

- The grant `gpu.kernels`, in the `capabilities.scene` list of a scene plugin. The scene world (`ilium:anim`) is the only world that has this import.
- A host build with the feature `gpu-kernels` enabled. A package that asks for the grant installs on such a build only.
- Nothing else: the call needs no filesystem or network access.

```json
"capabilities": { "scene": ["gpu.kernels"] }
```

### Signatures

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/gpu in reference-wit
enum gpu-kernel { blur, threshold, palette-map, dither-ordered, scale }
run: func(kernel: gpu-kernel, input: list<u8>, width: u32, height: u32, params-json: string) -> result<list<u8>, plugin-error>;
available: func() -> bool;
```

| Rust (`ilium_plugin_sdk::host::gpu`) | TypeScript (`@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/gpu`) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `gpu::available()` | `available()` | `true` when a graphics device runs the kernels. `false` means the CPU fallback is used; calls still work. |
| `gpu::run(kernel, &input, width, height, &params_json)?` | `run(kernel, input, width, height, paramsJson)` | Runs one kernel and returns the output bytes. Synchronous. |
| `GpuKernel::{Blur, Threshold, PaletteMap, DitherOrdered, Scale}` | `'blur' \| 'threshold' \| 'palette-map' \| 'dither-ordered' \| 'scale'` | The kernels the host offers. |

The call is synchronous and runs inside the frame budget of the scene's `renderer` export, so it should be used for a frame step, not for batch work. For heavy offline work, use a [job](/pages/api-jobs/).

### Kernels

| Kernel | What it does | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `blur` | Softens the image. | Cloud edges, glow. |
| `threshold` | Turns tone into two levels. | Masks, coastlines from a height field. |
| `palette-map` | Maps tone onto a palette. | Colouring a field by the shared palette. |
| `dither-ordered` | Ordered (matrix) dithering. | Preparing a tone raster for cells. |
| `scale` | Resamples to another size. | Fitting a pre-rendered field to the surface. |

The kernel parameters travel in `params-json`, a JSON object whose keys depend on the kernel. A kernel the host does not offer returns `unsupported`. Bad dimensions or malformed parameters return `invalid-argument`.

The shared look, dithering and frame pacing of the surface stay in the kernel and apply to whatever the scene draws, so a scene should use `dither-ordered` only for its own intermediate step, not to replace the global dither setting.

<title>gpu.run path</title>
<desc>The scene calls run with pixels and parameters. The host picks the GPU when available, else the CPU fallback, and returns pixels. The scene writes them to its surface.</desc>

### Example: blur a cloud field when a GPU is present

The scene builds a tone field on the CPU, blurs it with the host kernel and draws the result. When `available` is false it still calls `run`, because the CPU fallback gives the same pixels; it only lowers the field size to keep the frame time. `field_to_surface` and `build_params` are the scene's own code.

**Grants:** `gpu.kernels`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::gpu::{self, GpuKernel};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

struct CloudScene {
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    field: Vec<u8>,
    params_json: String,
}

impl CloudScene {
    fn soften(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
        let (width, height) = if gpu::available() {
            (self.width, self.height)
        } else {
            (self.width / 2, self.height / 2)
        };
        let input = self.field_at(width, height);
        match gpu::run(GpuKernel::Blur, &input, width, height, &self.params_json) {
            Ok(output) => Ok(output),
            Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Unsupported => Ok(input),
            Err(error) => Err(error),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { available, run } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/gpu';

export function soften(
  field: (width: number, height: number) => Uint8Array,
  width: number,
  height: number,
  paramsJson: string,
): Uint8Array {
  const [w, h] = available() ? [width, height] : [width >> 1, height >> 1];
  const input = field(w, h);
  try {
    return run('blur', input, w, h, paramsJson);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'unsupported') {
      return input;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

### What the user sees

Nothing separate. The scene looks the same with or without a graphics card; only the frame rate differs. The user can tell a development build apart in the plugin list, where the review dialog shows the grant in plain words.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin list
<span class="t-ok">ok</span>   example.clouds 0.1.0   scene  gpu.kernels
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.clouds --tail 2
<span class="t-dim">11:20:04</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  gpu.available false, cpu fallback, field 160x45
<span class="t-dim">11:20:04</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  gpu.run blur 160x45 in 3 ms
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. A scene on a host without a graphics device: the call works and the plugin lowers its field size.

### Errors and limits

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | The grant `gpu.kernels` is missing, declined or revoked. |
| `unsupported` | The kernel is not one the host offers. |
| `invalid-argument` | `width` or `height` is zero, `input` does not match the size, or `params-json` is not valid for the kernel. |

`available` never fails. There is no new requestable limit; the call counts against the scene's frame budget and the usual CPU budget of the plugin.

- [Scenes](/pages/api-scenes/) for the `renderer` export and the surface the result is drawn on.
- [media](/pages/api-media/) for decoded video frames, another source of pixels.
- [codec](/pages/api-codec/) for decoding images before a kernel runs on them.
- [jobs](/pages/api-jobs/) for work that is too heavy for a frame.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the shared codes.

# vector and embeddings

## vector and embeddings

The `vector` import turns text into embeddings and searches them. An embedding is a list of numbers (a vector) that places a piece of text in a space where similar meanings sit close together. Cosine similarity measures how close two vectors point: 1.0 means the same direction, 0 means unrelated. A plugin can embed its notes once, store the vectors in an index, and later find the notes nearest to a question.

Two parts make up the import. `embed` sends texts through the inference provider that the user selected and returns one vector per text. The index functions keep vectors in a host-held index and answer nearest-neighbour queries. The host does the maths, so the plugin ships no search code and the query stays fast up to the entry limit.

**You will need:**

- The `inference.embed` grant, on the server or the client side that calls the import. The grant takes no argument and has ordinary risk. The user reviews it at install. See [Capability: inference.embed](/pages/capability-inference/) for the related `inference` grant; there is no separate page for `inference.embed`.
- A selected inference provider that offers embeddings. Without one, `embed` fails with `unsupported`. The index functions work without a provider, because they only store and compare vectors the plugin already holds.
- Your own data scope. Indexes are persisted per plugin and are never shared with other plugins.

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/vector in reference-wit
// vector (S C, grant inference.embed)
embed: func(texts: list<string>, purpose: string) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;   // <= 256 texts of <= 8 KiB
take-vectors: func(request: request-id) -> option<list<list<f32>>>;

type index-id = u32;
create-index: func(name: string, dimensions: u16) -> result<index-id, plugin-error>;    // persisted in the data scope
upsert: func(index: index-id, entries: list<tuple<string, list<f32>>>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
remove-entries: func(index: index-id, ids: list<string>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
top-k: func(index: index-id, query: list<f32>, k: u16) -> result<list<tuple<string, f32>>, plugin-error>;   // cosine; k <= 100
drop-index: func(index: index-id);
```

The SDK imports are `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::vector` in Rust and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/vector` in TypeScript. Both ship an awaited wrapper for `embed` and a raw `embed_request` / `embedRequest` form that returns the `request-id`. The awaited wrapper does the `request-completed` and `take-vectors` steps for you. See [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for the pattern.

### Functions

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embed` | `vector::embed(texts, purpose).await` | `await embed(texts, purpose)` | `Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>, PluginError>`; `Promise<number[][]>` |
| `embed` request form | `vector::embed_request(texts, purpose)` | `embedRequest(texts, purpose)` | `Result<RequestId, PluginError>`; `bigint` |
| `take-vectors` | `vector::take_vectors(id)` | `takeVectors(id)` | `Option<Vec<Vec<f32>>>`; once only |
| `create-index` | `vector::create_index(name, dimensions)` | `createIndex(name, dimensions)` | `Result<IndexId, PluginError>`; `number` |
| `upsert` | `vector::upsert(index, entries)` | `upsert(index, entries)` | `Result<(), PluginError>`; `void` |
| `remove-entries` | `vector::remove_entries(index, ids)` | `removeEntries(index, ids)` | `Result<(), PluginError>`; `void` |
| `top-k` | `vector::top_k(index, query, k)` | `topK(index, query, k)` | `Result<Vec<(String, f32)>, PluginError>`; `Array<[string, number]>` |
| `drop-index` | `vector::drop_index(index)` | `dropIndex(index)` | nothing |

`purpose` names the feature that asks. It reaches the admission gate and the privacy log, the same way as the `purpose` of a [completion](/pages/api-inference/). Write a short noun phrase such as `note search`.

`embed` returns the vectors in the order of the texts. All vectors of one call have the same length, which is set by the embedding model. Create an index with exactly that length as `dimensions`; a mismatch fails `upsert` with `invalid-argument`. The score that `top-k` returns is the cosine similarity of the query and the entry, highest first.

The index persists in the plugin's data scope. The interface has no call that looks an index up by name, so keep the `index-id` with the plugin's own state next to the index name.

<text x="56" y="200" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">top-k(index, query, 5)</text>
<line x1="210" y1="232" x2="52" y2="232" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#vec-arrow)"/>
<text x="62" y="226" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">ids with cosine scores</text>
<text x="216" y="254" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">index lives in the host</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Only embed reaches the provider. The index calls are answered by the host at once, and the query itself needs a vector, so a question is embedded first.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Example 1: index notes and search them

The plugin embeds each note body and stores the vectors in an index named `notes`. To search, it embeds the question and asks the index for the five nearest notes. The manifest asks for the grant:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.notes",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["inference.embed"] }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::vector;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::errors::PluginError;

const PURPOSE: &str = "note search";
const NOTES_INDEX: &str = "notes";

pub struct NoteIndex {
    index: u32,
}

impl NoteIndex {
    /// Embeds one batch of notes and stores them. `notes` holds (id, body).
    pub async fn build(notes: &[(String, String)]) -> Result<NoteIndex, PluginError> {
        let texts: Vec<String> = notes.iter().map(|(_, body)| body.clone()).collect();
        let vectors = vector::embed(&texts, PURPOSE).await?;
        let dimensions = vectors.first().map(|vector| vector.len()).unwrap_or(0);
        let index = vector::create_index(NOTES_INDEX, dimensions as u16)?;
        let entries: Vec<(String, Vec<f32>)> = notes
            .iter()
            .map(|(id, _)| id.clone())
            .zip(vectors)
            .collect();
        vector::upsert(index, &entries)?;
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("indexed {} notes", entries.len()));
        Ok(NoteIndex { index })
    }

    /// Returns the ids of the five nearest notes with their cosine scores.
    pub async fn search(&self, question: &str) -> Result<Vec<(String, f32)>, PluginError> {
        let query = vector::embed(&[question.to_string()], PURPOSE).await?;
        let Some(first) = query.into_iter().next() else {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
        vector::top_k(self.index, &first, 5)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { embed, createIndex, upsert, topK } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/vector';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const PURPOSE = 'note search';
const NOTES_INDEX = 'notes';

export async function buildIndex(notes: Array<[string, string]>): Promise<number> {
  const vectors = await embed(notes.map(([, body]) => body), PURPOSE);
  const dimensions = vectors[0]?.length ?? 0;
  const index = createIndex(NOTES_INDEX, dimensions);
  const entries: Array<[string, number[]]> = notes.map(([id], position) => [id, vectors[position]]);
  upsert(index, entries);
  log('info', `indexed ${entries.length} notes`);
  return index;
}

export async function search(index: number, question: string): Promise<Array<[string, number]>> {
  const [query] = await embed([question], PURPOSE);
  return query === undefined ? [] : topK(index, query, 5);
}
```

An `embed` call takes at most 256 texts of at most 8 KiB each. Split a larger corpus into batches of 256 and call `upsert` for each batch. Calling `upsert` again with an id that exists replaces that entry, so a changed note is handled by embedding it once more.

### Example 2: remove entries and drop an index

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::vector;

fn forget_note(index: u32, note_id: &str) {
    if let Err(error) = vector::remove_entries(index, &[note_id.to_string()]) {
        log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("cannot forget {note_id}: {}", error.message));
    }
}

fn reset_notes(index: u32) {
    vector::drop_index(index);
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { removeEntries, dropIndex } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/vector';

export function forgetNote(index: number, noteId: string): void {
  removeEntries(index, [noteId]);
}

export function resetNotes(index: number): void {
  dropIndex(index);
}
```

`drop-index` deletes the index and its entries and frees their quota. Do not use the `index-id` after a drop.

### What the user sees

The import has no screen of its own. The user sees the effect in the plugin's panel, such as a list of notes ordered by relevance, and in the admission gate and privacy log, which receive the `purpose` of each `embed` call. The plugin log shows the calls the plugin writes:

<pre class="term">2026-10-12 09:41:03 example.notes info  indexed 212 notes
2026-10-12 09:41:03 example.notes info  vector.embed 212 texts, 2 batches
2026-10-12 09:44:19 example.notes info  vector.top_k notes k=5 best=0.83
2026-10-12 09:44:51 example.notes warn  embed failed: unsupported
</pre>

The capture is hand-composed to show the format of the plugin log lines. The `embed failed: unsupported` line is what a plugin writes when the user has selected a provider that offers no embeddings; the plugin then falls back to a plain text filter.

### Errors

| Call | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `embed` | `unsupported` | The selected provider offers no embeddings, or none is selected |
| `embed` | `invalid-argument` | More than 256 texts, a text over 8 KiB, or an empty list |
| `embed` | `not-permitted` | The `inference.embed` grant is not held or was revoked |
| `embed` completion | `network`, `rate-limited`, `timed-out` | The provider failed. Retry later |
| `embed` completion | `cancelled` | The plugin cancelled the request, or the application shut down |
| `create-index` | `quota-exceeded` | The plugin already holds the maximum number of indexes (`vector_indexes`) |
| `create-index` | `invalid-argument` | `dimensions` is 0 |
| `upsert` | `quota-exceeded` | The entry count over all indexes reaches `vector_entries` |
| `upsert` | `invalid-argument` | A vector length differs from the dimensions of the index |
| `top-k` | `invalid-argument` | The query length differs from the dimensions, or `k` is 0 or above 100 |

### Limits

| Limit | Default | Ceiling T1 | Ceiling T2 and T3 | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vector_indexes` | 4 | 16 | 4 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `vector_entries` (all indexes together) | 10,000 | 200,000 | 50,000 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Texts per `embed` | 256 | | | `invalid-argument` |
| Size of one text | 8 KiB | | | `invalid-argument` |
| `k` of `top-k` | 100 | | | `invalid-argument` |

The default applies unless the manifest asks for more, up to the ceiling of the tier. A plugin with `limits_tier: first-party` follows the T1 column.

### Edge cases

- Switching the embedding model changes the vector length. Existing indexes keep their old dimensions, so create a new index, re-embed, and drop the old one. A plugin should store the name of the model in the index name, such as `notes-v2`.
- An index is exact, not approximate: the answer is the true nearest set. It stays fast up to the entry limit only because the host holds the data.
- Embeddings leave the machine when the provider is remote. Treat `embed` like a completion for privacy.

### See also

- [inference](/pages/api-inference/) for completions and for routing to the selected provider.
- [Capability: inference](/pages/capability-inference/) for the related grant and review text.
- [requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for the `request-id` pattern.
- [storage](/pages/api-storage/) for the plugin data scope that holds the indexes.
- [errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) for the full tables.

Checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# kernel settings and keymap reads

## kernel settings and keymap reads

Two read-only imports let a plugin look at the configuration the user made in Ilium itself. `kernel-settings` returns the values of one built-in Settings tab, such as Terminal or Keyboard, as a JSON object. `keymap` returns the key bindings that are active now, and the display form of a chord such as `ctrl+shift+k`.

A plugin uses them to adapt. A plugin that draws a hint bar can show the user's real chord for a command instead of a default. A plugin that sizes its panel can read the terminal tab. Reading changes nothing. Only the one plugin that owns a tab may write that tab, with the grant `settings.write-kernel:<tab-id>` (D13, see "Writing a kernel tab"). No plugin writes a binding. Every other plugin links to the setting row.

**You will need:**

- For `kernel-settings`: the grant `settings.read-kernel:<tab-id>`, on the server or the client side. The argument is one kernel tab id such as `terminal`. It is required, and `*` is refused with `manifest.grant-wildcard`. A missing argument is refused with `manifest.grant-argument-missing`. The grant for the `api` tab is high risk (H). See [Capability: settings.read-kernel](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/).
- For `keymap`: the grant `keymap.read`, client side only. It takes no argument and has ordinary risk.
- The `open-external` grant for the link to a settings row.

### Interface

```wit
// kernel-settings (S C, grant settings.read-kernel:<tab-id>)
read: func(tab: string) -> result<string, plugin-error>;          // JSON object of that tab's values; secrets as "<redacted>"

// keymap (C, grant keymap.read)
record binding { command: string, chords: list<string>, context: string, is-default: bool }
bindings: func() -> list<binding>;
chord-label: func(chord: string) -> string;                         // the user-visible form, "Ctrl+Shift+K"

// events
//   kernel-settings-changed { tab: string, keys: list<string> }   (grant settings.read-kernel:<tab>; coalesced by tab, keys unioned)
//   keymap-changed                                                   (grant keymap.read; coalesced)
```

The SDK imports are `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::kernel_settings` and `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::keymap` in Rust, and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keymap` in TypeScript.

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel-settings.read` | `kernel_settings::read(tab)` | `read(tab)` | `Result<String, PluginError>`; `string`, throws `PluginError` |
| `keymap.bindings` | `keymap::bindings()` | `bindings()` | `Vec<Binding>`; `Binding[]` |
| `keymap.chord-label` | `keymap::chord_label(chord)` | `chordLabel(chord)` | `String`; `string` |

All calls are synchronous. They read a snapshot and return at once, so no `request-id` is involved.

| `binding` field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | `String` | `string` | Global command id, such as `example.notes/new-note`, or a kernel command name |
| `chords` | `Vec<String>` | `string[]` | Every chord bound to the command, in the chord syntax of [keys](/pages/api-keys/) |
| `context` | `String` | `string` | The context in which the binding applies |
| `is_default` | `bool` | `isDefault` | `true` when the user has not remapped the binding |

### The kernel tab ids

`read` takes the frozen kebab-case id of a built-in Settings tab. The ids follow the label as it stood on 2026-10-11 and never change when a label changes.

| Id | Label in Settings | Id | Label in Settings |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user-interface` | User Interface | `sound` | Sound |
| `icons` | Icons | `voice-control` | Voice control |
| `agent-monitoring` | Agent Monitoring | `reset-planning` | Reset planning |
| `agent-cost` | Agent Cost | `inference` | Inference |
| `optimization` | Optimization | `llm-instructions` | LLM Instructions |
| `remote-compaction` | Remote compaction | `titles` | Titles |
| `keyboard` | Keyboard | `triggers` | Triggers |
| `terminal` | Terminal | `text-triggers` | Text Triggers |
| `editor` | Editor | `debug` | Debug |
| `session` | Session | `api` | API |
| `git` | Git | `about` | About |
| `kanban-board` | Kanban Board | `setup` | Setup |
| `animations` | Animations | | |

An unknown id fails with `not-found`. The labels are for the reader of this table; the plugin passes the id.

### What `read` returns

The result is one JSON object of the tab's values. The keys are the kernel's stable configuration keys of that tab. A key that the kernel removes in a later release disappears from the object, so read keys defensively and give each a default. Every secret value, such as an API key, is the string `"<redacted>"` and never the secret. The object has the shape of the tab at the moment of the call, and a later change does not alter an object already returned.
