### Example 1: read a kernel tab

The plugin reads the Terminal tab at activation and again when the kernel reports a change in it. It needs `settings.read-kernel:terminal`.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "example.hints",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["settings.read-kernel:terminal", "keymap.read"] }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::kernel_settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use serde_json::Value;

fn read_terminal_tab() -> Option<Value> {
    match kernel_settings::read("terminal") {
        Ok(text) => serde_json::from_str(&text).ok(),
        Err(error) => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("cannot read terminal tab: {}", error.message));
            None
        }
    }
}

fn on_kernel_settings_changed(tab: &str, keys: &[String]) {
    if tab != "terminal" {
        return;
    }
    if let Some(values) = read_terminal_tab() {
        let count = values.as_object().map(|object| object.len()).unwrap_or(0);
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("terminal tab: {count} keys, changed {keys:?}"));
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

function readTerminalTab(): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(read('terminal')) as Record<string, unknown>;
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `cannot read terminal tab: ${String(error)}`);
    return undefined;
  }
}

export function onKernelSettingsChanged(tab: string, keys: string[]): void {
  if (tab !== 'terminal') return;
  const values = readTerminalTab();
  if (values) log('info', `terminal tab: ${Object.keys(values).length} keys, changed ${keys.join(',')}`);
}
```

The `kernel-settings-changed` event carries `tab` and `keys`, coalesced by tab. If several changes arrive before the plugin runs, the keys are joined into one set. The event is delivered only for tabs the plugin holds a grant for.

### Example 2: show the user's chord for a command

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::keymap;

/// Returns the first chord of a command in display form, or None when unbound.
fn hint_for(command: &str) -> Option<String> {
    keymap::bindings()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|binding| binding.command == command)
        .and_then(|binding| binding.chords.first().map(|chord| keymap::chord_label(chord)))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { bindings, chordLabel } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keymap';

export function hintFor(command: string): string | undefined {
  const found = bindings().find((binding) => binding.command === command);
  const chord = found?.chords[0];
  return chord === undefined ? undefined : chordLabel(chord);
}
```

Call `hint_for` again when `keymap-changed` arrives, and redraw the hint. `chord-label` gives the form the client shows to the user, such as `Ctrl+Shift+K`, so a hint matches what the user sees in Settings and in the help screens.

### Writing a kernel tab

The core plugin that owns a tab writes it with `kernel-settings.write`. The write goes through the same validation and auto-save path as a row edit in Settings, and the file on disk is the same `config.toml` key, so the kernel and the plugin never disagree. The owner of each of the 25 tabs is listed in [who owns each tab](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/#who-owns-each-tab).

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/fs in reference-wit
// kernel-settings (S C, grant settings.write-kernel:<tab-id>, T1 only)
write: func(tab: string, key: string, value: string) -> result<_, plugin-error>;   // value is JSON; one key per call
```

| Function | Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|
| `kernel-settings.write` | `kernel_settings::write(tab, key, json)` | `write(tab, key, json)` |

A write sends `kernel-settings-changed` to every reader of the tab, including the writer. A secret key cannot be written through this call; the owner uses the secrets import. Tabs with no owner plugin have no writer: the kernel row is the only editor.

### Link to a setting

A plugin that does not own the tab cannot write it. It links to the row with `ilium://settings/<tab-id>#<key>`, through the `open-external` intent. Ilium opens Settings at that row.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{ExternalTarget, OpenExternalSpec};

fn open_terminal_setting(key: &str) -> Submission {
    Submission {
        intent: Intent::OpenExternal(OpenExternalSpec {
            target: ExternalTarget::Settings(format!("ilium://settings/terminal#{key}")),
        }),
        correlation: 1,
        dedup_key: None,
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export function openTerminalSetting(key: string): Submission {
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'open-external', val: { target: { tag: 'settings', val: `ilium://settings/terminal#${key}` } } },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

Return the submission from `on_events` (or `onEvents`). The intent needs the `open-external` grant. See [intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [Capability: open-external](/pages/capability-open-external/).

### What the user sees

Neither import draws anything. The user sees the plugin adapt, and a log line when the plugin writes one. This capture is hand-composed to show the log format:

<pre class="term">2026-10-12 10:02:11 example.hints info  terminal tab: 31 keys, changed []
2026-10-12 10:03:40 example.hints info  keymap: new-note is Ctrl+Alt+N
2026-10-12 10:04:02 example.hints info  keymap-changed: new-note is Ctrl+Shift+N
2026-10-12 10:04:20 example.hints warn  cannot read git tab: not-permitted
</pre>

### Errors

| Call | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `kernel-settings.read` | `not-permitted` | No `settings.read-kernel:<tab>` grant for that tab, or the user revoked it |
| `kernel-settings.read` | `not-found` | The tab id is unknown |
| manifest | `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | `settings.read-kernel` without a tab id |
| manifest | `manifest.grant-wildcard` | `settings.read-kernel:*` |
| manifest | `manifest.grant-tier` | `settings.read-kernel:api` in a package that may not hold high-risk grants, or `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` in any package that is not first-party (T1) |
| manifest | `manifest.settings-owner` | A second plugin declares `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for a tab that already has an owner |
| `kernel-settings.write` | `not-permitted` | No `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` grant for that tab, or the user revoked it |
| `kernel-settings.write` | `not-found` | The tab id or the key is unknown |
| `kernel-settings.write` | `invalid-argument` | The value does not match the key's type or range |

### Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Writes to a kernel setting | only with `settings.write-kernel:<tab-id>`, T1, one holder per tab; none for a binding |
| Secrets in a returned object | always `"<redacted>"` |
| Wildcard tab argument | refused |
| `keymap` side | client only |
| Events | coalesced: one `kernel-settings-changed` per tab, one `keymap-changed` |

### Edge cases

- The read value is a snapshot. Read again after the event; do not cache for long.
- A key can disappear in a release. Treat a missing key as the default, not as an error.
- A chord from `bindings` may be bound to a kernel command and not to a plugin command. Check `command` before showing it.
- The server side has no `keymap`, because keys belong to the client. A server that needs a chord asks its client with [client requests](/pages/api-client-requests/).

### See also

- [Capability: settings.read-kernel](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/) for the grant review.
- [keys](/pages/api-keys/) for chord syntax, grabs and the `key-capture` widget.
- [commands](/pages/api-commands/) for command ids and keybinding contributions.
- [settings](/pages/api-settings/) for the plugin's own settings.
- [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) for the kernel tab ids and anchors in full.
- [events](/pages/api-events/) for `kernel-settings-changed` and `keymap-changed`.

# intent: send-input stages

## The send-input intent in depth

`send-input` writes text, bytes or mouse events into a terminal pane as if the user had typed them. Besides a single piece of text with a delivery mode, it supports staged sends with delays, raw bytes, mouse events, a precondition, an input lock and a crash-safe journal. The kernel still owns the parts that are easy to get wrong: the two-stage submit of each agent signature, bracketed paste, and the prompt journal.

**You need:** `terminal.write` for any `send-input`. Raw bytes and mouse events also need `terminal.raw-input` (high risk). `lock-user-input` needs `terminal.input-lock` (high risk). `agent.read` is needed to read the activity that a precondition compares with. The grants belong in the manifest of the side that submits. The base grant is described in [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/); the general rules for intents are in [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

### Records

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/intents in reference-wit
variant delivery { typed, submitted, pasted }
record input-stage { text: string, delay-ms: u16, delivery: delivery }
record terminal-mouse { kind: pointer-kind, button: pointer-button, column: u16, row: u16, modifiers: pointer-modifiers }
record input-precondition { activity: option<agent-activity>, screen-revision: option<u64>, foreground: option<string> }

record send-input-spec {
  pane: node-id,
  text: string,                               // ignored when stages is not empty
  delivery: delivery,
  prompt-epoch: option<u64>,                  // refused(conflict) when stale
  // all optional
  stages: list<input-stage>,                  // at most 16, total delay at most 10 s
  raw: option<list<u8>>,                      // at most 64 KiB, needs terminal.raw-input
  mouse: option<list<terminal-mouse>>,        // needs terminal.raw-input
  if-current: option<input-precondition>,
  lock-user-input: bool,                      // at most 2 s, needs terminal.input-lock
  journal: bool,                              // write a journal entry before the PTY write
}
```

The mandatory key is the `dedup-key` of the submission (the field is called `idempotency-key` in the intent table). It follows the format and window rules in [intents](/pages/api-intents/). `pointer-kind`, `pointer-button` and `pointer-modifiers` are the shared types also used by the `pointer` event: kinds `down`, `up`, `move`, `drag`, `wheel-up`, `wheel-down`, `wheel-left` and `wheel-right`; buttons `none`, `left`, `middle` and `right`; modifiers `shift`, `control` and `alt`.

### Fields and rules

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `stages` | Replaces `text` when present. The host sends the stages in order and waits `delay-ms` before each. A stage uses its own `delivery`. The two-stage submit rule of the pane's signature still applies to a `submitted` stage. At most 16 stages and a total delay of at most 10 s, otherwise `invalid-argument` for the batch. |
| `raw` | Bytes written as they are, with no encoding, no bracketed paste and no submit keys. At most 64 KiB. Needs `terminal.raw-input`. |
| `mouse` | The host encodes each event in the protocol the program enabled (for example SGR 1006). `refused(unsupported)` when mouse reporting is off. Needs `terminal.raw-input`. |
| `if-current` | A precondition. Every field that is set must match, otherwise `refused(conflict)` before any byte is written. The message names the failed field: `activity`, `screen-revision` or `foreground`. |
| `lock-user-input` | Hold the user's keys for the duration of the stages, at most 2 s. Keys the user types meanwhile are queued, not lost. |
| `journal` | Write the journal entry before the PTY write. See "Crash safety" below. |

The text of a stage, and `text` itself, is at most 64 KiB.

### Check order

The kernel runs these checks in order. Steps 1 and 2 run at batch level over the whole list. The others are per submission. The same order, without the `mouse` step, is in [intents](/pages/api-intents/#send-input-check-order).

1. Shape, key present, sizes, stage count, total delay, `raw` size and the total text across all stages (at most 65,536 bytes). Otherwise the batch is refused with `invalid-argument`.
2. Grants: `terminal.write`, then `terminal.raw-input` if `raw` or `mouse` is set, then `terminal.input-lock` if `lock-user-input` is set. Otherwise the batch is refused with `not-permitted`.
3. Dedup key. A reserved key completes as `duplicate`.
4. The pane exists and is a terminal pane (`not-found`, `unsupported`).
5. The pane is restored (`pane-not-ready`).
6. The rate limit has room: 20 per second per pane and plugin (`rate-limited`).
7. `prompt-epoch`, if given, equals the pane's epoch (`conflict`).
8. `mouse`: reporting is enabled (`unsupported`).
9. `if-current` matches (`conflict`, message `precondition: <field>`).
10. The lock is free: another plugin holding the input lock of the pane gives `conflict` with the message `input-locked`.
11. The input is accepted: the key is reserved, the rate token is taken, the journal entry is written when requested, and the stages are sent. A refused attempt never takes a rate token.

### Example: compact an agent, only when it is idle

The plugin sends a slash command in two stages, waits for the agent to be idle, and holds the user's keys while the stages run. The `if-current` precondition prevents the text from landing in a running turn.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{InputPrecondition, InputStage, SendInputSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::Delivery;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

fn compact(pane: NodeId) -> Submission {
    let spec = SendInputSpec {
        pane,
        text: String::new(),
        delivery: Delivery::Typed,
        prompt_epoch: None,
        stages: vec![
            InputStage { text: "/compact".into(), delay_ms: 0, delivery: Delivery::Typed },
            InputStage { text: String::new(), delay_ms: 120, delivery: Delivery::Submitted },
        ],
        raw: None,
        mouse: None,
        if_current: Some(InputPrecondition {
            activity: Some(AgentActivity::Idle),
            screen_revision: None,
            foreground: None,
        }),
        lock_user_input: true,
        journal: true,
    };
    Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(spec), format!("compact-{pane}"))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

function compact(pane: bigint): Submission {
  return {
    intent: {
      tag: 'send-input',
      val: {
        pane, text: '', delivery: 'typed', promptEpoch: undefined,
        stages: [
          { text: '/compact', delayMs: 0, delivery: 'typed' },
          { text: '', delayMs: 120, delivery: 'submitted' },
        ],
        raw: undefined, mouse: undefined,
        ifCurrent: { activity: 'idle', screenRevision: undefined, foreground: undefined },
        lockUserInput: true,
        journal: true,
      },
    },
    correlation: 1n,
    dedupKey: `compact-${pane}`,
  };
}
```

### Example: raw bytes and a mouse click

Send the escape sequence for "cursor up", then click at column 12, row 3. The program must have mouse reporting on, or the click is refused with `unsupported`. The check of the modes uses the `terminal.modes` read of the [terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/).

**Rust**

```rust
let spec = SendInputSpec {
    pane,
    text: String::new(),
    delivery: Delivery::Typed,
    prompt_epoch: None,
    stages: vec![],
    if_current: None,
    lock_user_input: false,
    journal: false,
    raw: Some(vec![0x1b, b'[', b'A']),
    mouse: Some(vec![
        TerminalMouse { kind: PointerKind::Down, button: PointerButton::Left, column: 12, row: 3, modifiers: PointerModifiers::empty() },
        TerminalMouse { kind: PointerKind::Up,   button: PointerButton::Left, column: 12, row: 3, modifiers: PointerModifiers::empty() },
    ]),
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const val = {
  pane, text: '', delivery: 'typed' as const, promptEpoch: undefined, stages: [],
  raw: new Uint8Array([0x1b, 0x5b, 0x41]),
  mouse: [
    { kind: 'down', button: 'left', column: 12, row: 3, modifiers: [] },
    { kind: 'up', button: 'left', column: 12, row: 3, modifiers: [] },
  ],
  ifCurrent: undefined, lockUserInput: false, journal: false,
};
```

### Input lock

`terminal.lock-input(pane, millis)` and `unlock-input(pane)` (see [terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/)) hold the user's keys on their own. `lock-user-input` on `send-input` does the same for exactly the duration of the stages and releases the lock when the last stage is sent or the intent fails. Only one lock exists per pane. A second plugin asking for it gets `conflict`. A requested duration over 2,000 ms is `invalid-argument`. Queued keys are delivered to the program in order after the unlock, so nothing the user typed is lost.

### Crash safety: journal and input-uncertain

With `journal: true` the kernel writes a pane journal entry (kind `input-sent`, with the dedup key and the delivery result) before the PTY write. A `send-input` on an agent pane and `agent-action` always journal their keys, from Phase 5. If the server stops between the write and the recorded outcome, the restarted plugin receives `input-uncertain { pane, dedup-key }` once, and the kernel never resends silently. The plugin reads the screen, decides whether the text arrived, and resends under a new key if it did not. In the sketches below, `screen_shows` and `screenShows` stand for the plugin's own helper that reads cells and looks for the text.

**Rust**

```rust
Event::InputUncertain(InputUncertainEvent { pane, dedup_key }) => {
    // read the visible rows with terminal::read_cells (terminal.read-cells), decide, then:
    if !self.screen_shows(pane, "/compact") {
        out.push(compact(pane));   // build it with a new key suffix: the old key is reserved
    }
    log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("input {dedup_key} on {pane} was uncertain"));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
if (event.tag === 'input-uncertain') {
  // read the visible rows with readCells (terminal.read-cells), decide, then:
  if (!screenShows(event.val.pane, '/compact')) out.push(compact(event.val.pane));   // with a new key suffix
  log('warn', `input ${event.val.dedupKey} on ${event.val.pane} was uncertain`);
}
```

### The ok-epoch outcome

On an agent pane the outcome is `ok-epoch(n)`, where `n` is the new prompt epoch. Store it, and pass it later as `prompt-epoch` to refuse a send that raced with another prompt. A plugin that tests for `ok` only keeps working through `is_ok()` or `isOk()`.

### Staged signature actions

An agent signature in the manifest may declare an action as stages with the same rules, so `agent-action` uses them too:

```json
{ "actions": { "compact": { "stages": [
  { "keys": "/compact", "delay_ms": 0 },
  { "keys": "\r", "delay_ms": 120 } ] } } }
```

### Errors and limits

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| More than 16 stages, total delay over 10 s, `raw` over 64 KiB, lock over 2 s | batch refused, `invalid-argument` |
| `raw`, `mouse` or lock without its grant | batch refused, `not-permitted` |
| Restored pane that has not started | `refused(pane-not-ready)` |
| Mouse reporting off | `refused(unsupported)` |
| `if-current` mismatch, stale epoch or held lock | `refused(conflict)`; the message names the failed precondition |
| More than 20 sends per second per pane and plugin | `refused(rate-limited)` with `retry-after-ms` |
| Server stops during a journaled send | `input-uncertain` after restart, no replay |

### What the user sees

While the lock is held the user's keys wait, and a typed line appears after the stages finish. The stages appear in the terminal as typing, with the pauses of `delay-ms`. The tree shows the lock glyph from the client icon set on the pane for the duration.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">▼ 📂 Ilium</span>
<span class="t-hi">›   🦀 🔒 ⠋ Fix auth</span>
<span class="t-dim">›   🖥️    Shell</span>

<span class="t-dim">pane 7 (claude)  send-input  compact-7</span>
<span class="t-ok">0 ms     stage 1 typed   "/compact"</span>
<span class="t-ok">120 ms   stage 2 submit  CR</span>
<span class="t-ok">121 ms   outcome         ok-epoch(5)</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated: the tree row uses glyphs from the client icon inventory (agent, lock, working spinner); the log lines are an example of the layout, not a capture.

- [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) for batches, dedup keys and the other intents.
- [Events](/pages/api-events/) for `input-uncertain` and `request-completed`.
- [Terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/) and [agent primitives](/pages/primitives-agent/) for `modes`, `read-cells`, `lock-input` and the activity states.
- [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/) and [agent.control](/pages/capability-agent-control/).

# intents: pane lifecycle

## Pane lifecycle intents

Five intents let a server-side plugin control the process of a terminal pane: stop it without killing it, restart it with another command, terminate it politely, and ask for a size. All five need the grant `panes.lifecycle`, which is high risk and offered to the server side only. A high-risk grant needs an explicit user grant even for a bundled first-party plugin. The kernel keeps what stays kernel: PTY spawn, the resize itself, and the durable resume binding of agent sessions.

**You need:** `panes.lifecycle` in the `server` capability list of the manifest. To observe results you also want `panes.read`, which delivers `pane-lifecycle-changed`. See [panes](/pages/api-panes/) for the read side and [intents](/pages/api-intents/) for batches and keys.

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["panes.read", "panes.lifecycle"] }
```

### Records

```wit
record freeze-pane-spec { pane: node-id }
record unfreeze-pane-spec { pane: node-id }
record replace-pane-command-spec {
  pane: node-id, command: list<string>, cwd: option<fs-path>, keep-scrollback: bool,
}
record terminate-pane-process-spec { pane: node-id, grace-ms: u32 }       // at most 10,000
record resize-pane-spec { pane: node-id, columns: option<u16>, rows: option<u16> }

enum pane-lifecycle-state { running, frozen, restarting, exited }
// event: pane-lifecycle-changed { pane: node-id, state: pane-lifecycle-state, by: option<plugin-id> }
```

### Intents

| Intent | Effect | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `freeze-pane` | The process is stopped with SIGSTOP on Unix. Output stops and the pane shows the frozen mark. | `ok`; `refused(unsupported)` on Windows |
| `unfreeze-pane` | The process continues. | `ok`; `refused(conflict)` when the pane is not frozen |
| `replace-pane-command` | The current process ends and the new `command` runs in the same pane, with `cwd` if given. `keep-scrollback` keeps the history above the new output. | `ok` once the new process runs. The durable resume binding stays with the kernel. |
| `terminate-pane-process` | Sends a terminate request, waits `grace-ms`, then kills. At most 10,000 ms. | `ok` when the process has exited. The pane stays open and shows its exit status. |
| `resize-pane` | Asks the layout for `columns` and `rows`. A field left unset keeps its size. | `ok`; `refused(conflict)` when the layout cannot give the size. The message names the limiting neighbour. |

Common refusals: `refused(not-permitted)` without the grant, `refused(not-found)` for a missing pane, `refused(pane-not-ready)` on a restored pane that has not started, `refused(invalid-argument)` for an empty command or a `grace-ms` over 10,000.

### Example: freeze on a lock-up, unfreeze after a pause

This plugin freezes a pane whose agent has been working too long, and unfreezes it again on a timer. The freeze key stops a repeated event from freezing twice. A timer comes from the [clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/) interface.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{FreezePaneSpec, TerminatePaneProcessSpec, UnfreezePaneSpec};

fn on_runaway(pane: NodeId) -> Vec<Submission> {
    vec![Submission::keyed(Intent::FreezePane(FreezePaneSpec { pane }), format!("freeze-{pane}"))]
}

fn on_timer(pane: NodeId) -> Vec<Submission> {
    vec![Submission::keyed(Intent::UnfreezePane(UnfreezePaneSpec { pane }), format!("thaw-{pane}"))]
}

fn stop_hard(pane: NodeId) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::TerminatePaneProcess(TerminatePaneProcessSpec { pane, grace_ms: 3_000 }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const freeze = (pane: bigint): Submission =>
  ({ intent: { tag: 'freeze-pane', val: { pane } }, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: `freeze-${pane}` });
const thaw = (pane: bigint): Submission =>
  ({ intent: { tag: 'unfreeze-pane', val: { pane } }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: `thaw-${pane}` });
const stopHard = (pane: bigint): Submission =>
  ({ intent: { tag: 'terminate-pane-process', val: { pane, graceMs: 3000 } }, correlation: 3n, dedupKey: undefined });
```

### Example: replace the command and ask for a size

**Rust**

```rust
let replace = Intent::ReplacePaneCommand(ReplacePaneCommandSpec {
    pane,
    command: vec!["bash".into(), "-lc".into(), "make watch".into()],
    cwd: Some("/work/app".into()),
    keep_scrollback: true,
});
let resize = Intent::ResizePane(ResizePaneSpec { pane, columns: Some(100), rows: None });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const replace = { tag: 'replace-pane-command', val: {
  pane, command: ['bash', '-lc', 'make watch'], cwd: '/work/app', keepScrollback: true } } as const;
const resize = { tag: 'resize-pane', val: { pane, columns: 100, rows: undefined } } as const;
```

When the layout cannot give 100 columns, the outcome is `refused(conflict)` and the message names the neighbour that limits the pane, for example `cannot widen: pane 9 is at its minimum width`. The exact wording is up to the kernel.

### Handling the confirmations

**Rust**

```rust
Event::PaneLifecycleChanged(PaneLifecycleChangedEvent { pane, state, by }) => match state {
    PaneLifecycleState::Frozen => self.frozen.insert(pane),
    PaneLifecycleState::Running | PaneLifecycleState::Exited => self.frozen.remove(&pane),
    PaneLifecycleState::Restarting => false,
},
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
if (event.tag === 'pane-lifecycle-changed') {
  const { pane, state } = event.val;
  if (state === 'frozen') frozen.add(pane); else if (state !== 'restarting') frozen.delete(pane);
}
```

### Errors and limits

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| `freeze-pane` on Windows | `refused(unsupported)` |
| `unfreeze-pane` on a running pane | `refused(conflict)` |
| `grace-ms` over 10,000 | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| Layout cannot satisfy `resize-pane` | `refused(conflict)`, message names the neighbour |
| Pane not started after a restore | `refused(pane-not-ready)` |
| Pane missing | `refused(not-found)` |

### What the user sees

A frozen pane shows the frozen mark in its tree row and its frame, and its output stops. The tree row uses the glyph of the frozen slot from the client's icon set.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">▼ 📂 Ilium</span>
<span class="t-hi">›   🖥️ ❄ build-watch</span>
<span class="t-dim">›   🖥️    logs</span>
<span class="t-dim">pane 5  freeze-pane   outcome ok</span>
<span class="t-dim">pane 5  state: running -> frozen  by com.example.guard</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated: glyphs come from the client icon inventory; the two log lines are an example layout.

- [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [events](/pages/api-events/) for batches and `pane-lifecycle-changed`.
- [Panes](/pages/api-panes/), [terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/) and [panes.signal](/pages/capability-panes-signal/), the lighter signal intent.
- [send-input stages](/pages/api-intent-send-input/) to type into a pane after `replace-pane-command`.

**[SEC-041]** Pane lifecycle intents from a plugin are checked against its grants like host calls. See [Sandbox reference](/pages/reference-sandbox/).

# intents: tree structure and restructure

## Tree structure intents

The session tree is made of groups, folders, projects, splits and panes. A plugin can build and reorganise it with intents: create the container kinds, bookmark and expand nodes, and apply a whole reorganisation as one atomic, undoable batch. The tree model, the layout solver and the drawing of splits stay in the kernel, so a plugin only asks and the kernel checks.

**You need:** `tree.restructure` (high risk) for `create-group`, `create-folder`, `create-project`, `create-split`, `restructure` and `revert-restructure`. `tree.write` for `set-bookmarked` and `set-expanded` on nodes. `tree.read` to learn node ids and to receive `tree-changed`. A plugin that expands its own virtual rows needs the `virtual_rows` entry in its manifest instead. See [tree](/pages/api-tree/) for the read side, [tree.write](/pages/capability-tree-write/) and [tree.read](/pages/capability-tree-read/) for the grants, and [intents](/pages/api-intents/) for batches.

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["tree.read", "tree.write", "tree.restructure"] }
```

### Records

```wit
variant placement { before, after, inside-first, inside-last }           // as for move-node

record create-group-spec   { parent: node-id, title: string, placement: placement, children: list<node-id> }
record create-folder-spec  { parent: node-id, title: string, path: option<fs-path> }
record create-project-spec { title: string, root: fs-path }
record create-split-spec   { panes: list<node-id>, direction: split-direction }   // 2 to 4 panes
record set-bookmarked-spec { node: node-id, bookmarked: bool }
variant expand-target { node(node-id), virtual-row(string) }
record set-expanded-spec   { target: expand-target, expanded: bool }
record restructure-spec    { operations: list<restructure-op>, label: string }    // at most 256 operations
// restructure-op is a variant with the cases move, create-group, ungroup and rename
// revert-restructure carries the undo token (u64)
```

### Intents

| Intent | Effect | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `create-group` | Creates a group under `parent` at `placement` and moves `children` into it. | `ok-node` with the new group |
| `create-folder` | Creates a folder node, optionally bound to a directory `path`. | `ok-node` |
| `create-project` | Creates a project node rooted at `root`. | `ok-node` |
| `create-split` | Joins 2 to 4 panes into one split container. | `ok-node` with the split container |
| `set-bookmarked` | Sets or clears the bookmark star on a node. | `ok` |
| `set-expanded` | Expands or collapses a node, or one of the plugin's own virtual rows. | `ok` |
| `restructure` | Applies up to 256 operations (move, create-group, ungroup, rename) as one change with a `label` for the undo. | `ok-node` carrying an undo token node id (0 when nothing changed) |
| `revert-restructure` | Undoes the restructure with that token. | `ok`; `refused(conflict)` when a later change touched the same nodes |

`restructure` is all or nothing. One failing operation refuses the whole intent with `refused(conflict)` and the index of that operation in the message, and the tree is unchanged. An undo token does not survive a server restart.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 150" role="img" aria-label="A restructure batch is applied atomically and can be reverted">
  <defs>
    <marker id="treestruct-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="6" y="50" width="110" height="46" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="61" y="70" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">restructure</text>

  <text x="220" y="108" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">one fails: refused(conflict)</text>
  <text x="220" y="122" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">index in message, no change</text>
  <rect x="320" y="14" width="94" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>

### Example: group two panes and bookmark the group

The first submission creates the group and its result `ok-node` gives the new node id. A later batch uses that id, because a node created in a batch is not yet known to the plugin when it builds the batch.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{CreateGroupSpec, SetBookmarkedSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::Placement;

fn group_panes(parent: NodeId, panes: Vec<NodeId>) -> Submission {
    Submission::keyed(
        Intent::CreateGroup(CreateGroupSpec {
            parent,
            title: "Deploy".into(),
            placement: Placement::InsideLast,
            children: panes,
        }),
        format!("group-deploy-{parent}"),
    )
}

// in on_events: Event::RequestCompleted with Outcome::OkNode(group)
fn bookmark(group: NodeId) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::SetBookmarked(SetBookmarkedSpec { node: group, bookmarked: true }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const groupPanes = (parent: bigint, panes: bigint[]): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'create-group', val: { parent, title: 'Deploy', placement: 'inside-last', children: panes } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: `group-deploy-${parent}`,
});

// in onEvents: event.tag === 'request-completed' && outcome.tag === 'ok-node'
const bookmark = (group: bigint): Submission => ({
  intent: { tag: 'set-bookmarked', val: { node: group, bookmarked: true } },
  correlation: 2n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
});
```

### Example: a split, a project and an expanded virtual row

**Rust**

```rust
let split = Intent::CreateSplit(CreateSplitSpec { panes: vec![left, right], direction: SplitDirection::Vertical });
let project = Intent::CreateProject(CreateProjectSpec { title: "api".into(), root: "/work/api".into() });
let expand = Intent::SetExpanded(SetExpandedSpec { target: ExpandTarget::VirtualRow("builds".into()), expanded: true });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const split = { tag: 'create-split', val: { panes: [left, right], direction: 'vertical' } } as const;
const project = { tag: 'create-project', val: { title: 'api', root: '/work/api' } } as const;
const expand = { tag: 'set-expanded', val: { target: { tag: 'virtual-row', val: 'builds' }, expanded: true } } as const;
```

### Example: apply a restructure and keep the undo token

The operations list is built by the plugin's own code (move, create-group, ungroup and rename operations). The token arrives as the node id of `ok-node`; 0 means that nothing changed and there is nothing to undo.

**Rust**

```rust
let submission = Submission::new(Intent::Restructure(RestructureSpec {
    operations: self.plan_operations(),          // at most 256
    label: "Group panes by project".into(),
}));

// later, on Event::RequestCompleted
if let Outcome::OkNode(token) = result.outcome {
    if token != 0 { self.undo_token = Some(token); }
}
// to undo: Intent::RevertRestructure(token)
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const submission: Submission = {
  intent: { tag: 'restructure', val: { operations: planOperations(), label: 'Group panes by project' } },
  correlation: 5n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
};
// on request-completed: if (outcome.tag === 'ok-node' && outcome.val !== 0n) undoToken = outcome.val;
// to undo: { tag: 'revert-restructure', val: undoToken }
```

### Errors and limits

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Missing `tree.restructure` or `tree.write` | batch refused, `not-permitted` |
| More than 256 operations, a split with fewer than 2 or more than 4 panes | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| One operation of a restructure fails | whole intent `refused(conflict)`, index in the message |
| Revert after a later change touched the same nodes | `refused(conflict)` |
| Token from before a server restart | `refused(not-found)` or `refused(conflict)`; tokens do not survive restarts |
| A node that does not exist or a locked node that must move | `refused(not-found)`, `refused(conflict)` |

### What the user sees

The tree changes at once. A group shows as an expanded node, a split as the split glyph of the client, a bookmark as the star. The restructure appears as one entry in the kernel's undo, labelled with `label`.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">▼ 📂 Ilium</span>
<span class="t-dim">› ▼ 📂 Deploy</span>
<span class="t-hi">› ›   🖥️ ★ api-deploy</span>
<span class="t-dim">› ›   🖥️    web-deploy</span>
<span class="t-dim">› ▶ ▥ left | right</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated: composed from the glyph inventory of the client tree (expand arrows, folder, bookmark star, split glyph, indent marks per depth); the split row label is invented.

- [Tree](/pages/api-tree/), [intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [events](/pages/api-events/) (`tree-changed`, `node-removed`).
- [tree.write](/pages/capability-tree-write/), [tree.read](/pages/capability-tree-read/) and [tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/).
- [Chrome intents](/pages/api-intent-chrome/) for titles, icons and attention marks.

# intents: toast, status segments, open-external

## Toast, status segments, frame slots, open-external, titles and decorations

These intents change the kernel's own chrome without letting a plugin draw it. A plugin sends a toast, writes a segment in the status bar, fills a slot in a pane frame, opens a link in the desktop handler, marks a node as needing attention, and decorates tree rows with rich, animated content. The kernel decides placement, timing, colour mapping and policy.

**You need:** `notify.toast` for `toast` and `dismiss-toast`; `ui.chrome` for the status segment and frame slot intents, together with the matching `status_segments` and `pane_frame_slots` manifest entries; `open-external` for `open-external`; `tree.attention` for the attention marks; `tree.decorate` for `set-decoration`, `clear-decoration` and `set-inferred-icon`; `tree.write` for `rename-node`. See [intents](/pages/api-intents/) for batches and keys, [notifications](/pages/api-notifications/) for desktop notices, [tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/) and [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/).

```json
"capabilities": { "client": ["notify.toast", "ui.chrome", "open-external"] },
"status_segments": [{ "id": "quota" }]
```

### Records

```wit
enum tone { info, success, warning, danger, muted }
record toast-action { label: string, command: string }
record toast-spec {
  id: option<string>, tone: tone, title: string,                    // title at most 60 characters
  body: option<rich-text>,                                          // at most 200 characters
  actions: list<toast-action>,                                      // at most 2
  duration-ms: option<u32>,                                         // 1,000 to 30,000
}
variant external-target { url(string), file(fs-path), settings(string) }
record open-external-spec { target: external-target }
record set-status-segment-spec { segment: string, content: rich-text, tooltip: option<tooltip>, tone: option<tone> }
record set-frame-slot-spec { pane: node-id, slot: string, content: rich-text, icon: option<string>, tooltip: option<tooltip> }
record clear-frame-slot-spec { pane: node-id, slot: string }
record mark-attention-spec { node: node-id, reason: string }        // at most 80 characters
record set-inferred-icon-spec { node: node-id, icon: option<string>, source: string }
enum title-source { plugin, inferred }
enum decoration-visibility { always, on-hover }
```

### Toast

A toast is a short message that the kernel draws near the corner of the client and removes by itself. `duration-ms` of none means until dismissed for the `danger` tone and 5,000 ms for the others. A toast with an `id` that is already shown replaces it. The action buttons run a command: its arrival is a `command-invoked` event with the origin `toast`. At most 3 toasts per 10 s per plugin (`rate-limited`, with `retry-after-ms`) and `toasts_pending` is 3, replacing the oldest.

**Rust**

```rust
let toast = Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
    id: Some("deploy".into()),
    tone: Tone::Danger,
    title: "Deploy failed".into(),
    body: Some(RichText::plain("exit status 2 on api-deploy")),
    actions: vec![ToastAction { label: "Open log".into(), command: "com.example.deploy/open-log".into() }],
    duration_ms: None,
});
let dismiss = Intent::DismissToast("deploy".into());
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const toast = { tag: 'toast', val: {
  id: 'deploy', tone: 'danger', title: 'Deploy failed',
  body: [{ text: 'exit status 2 on api-deploy', style: {}, target: { tag: 'none' }, tooltip: undefined }],
  actions: [{ label: 'Open log', command: 'com.example.deploy/open-log' }],
  durationMs: undefined,
} } as const;
const dismiss = { tag: 'dismiss-toast', val: 'deploy' } as const;
```

### Status segments and frame slots

`set-status-segment` writes one of the plugin's declared `status_segments` (at most 2 per plugin). `set-frame-slot` fills one of its `pane_frame_slots` (at most 4) on a pane: the slot's `placement` is `header-icon`, `header-text`, `footer-row` or `banner`, and `applies_to` limits the panes. Both are limited to 10 per second per slot. A pane that does not match `applies_to` gives `refused(invalid-argument)`. The `clear-` intents remove the content. A click on a rich span with a `command` target arrives as `command-invoked` with the origin `status-segment` or `frame-slot`.

**Rust**

```rust
let segment = Intent::SetStatusSegment(SetStatusSegmentSpec {
    segment: "quota".into(),
    content: RichText::plain("quota 82%"),
    tooltip: None,
    tone: Some(Tone::Warning),
});
let slot = Intent::SetFrameSlot(SetFrameSlotSpec {
    pane, slot: "branch".into(), content: RichText::plain("main"), icon: Some("🌿".into()), tooltip: None,
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const segment = { tag: 'set-status-segment', val: {
  segment: 'quota', content: richText('quota 82%'), tooltip: undefined, tone: 'warning' } } as const;
const slot = { tag: 'set-frame-slot', val: {
  pane, slot: 'branch', content: richText('main'), icon: '🌿', tooltip: undefined } } as const;
```

### open-external

`open-external` hands a target to the desktop. `url` accepts `http`, `https` and `mailto` only. `file` opens a path with the desktop handler. `settings` takes an `ilium://settings/<tab-id>#<key>` link and opens the Settings screen at that row, which is how a plugin points at a kernel setting it may not write. The first time a plugin opens a target origin the user is asked, and the answer is remembered for that plugin. A declined request is `refused(not-permitted)`. The `open_target` allowlist stays in the kernel.

**Rust**

```rust
let url = Intent::OpenExternal(OpenExternalSpec { target: ExternalTarget::Url("https://status.example.com".into()) });
let settings = Intent::OpenExternal(OpenExternalSpec { target: ExternalTarget::Settings("ilium://settings/keyboard#chords".into()) });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const url = { tag: 'open-external', val: { target: { tag: 'url', val: 'https://status.example.com' } } } as const;
const settings = { tag: 'open-external', val: { target: { tag: 'settings', val: 'ilium://settings/keyboard#chords' } } } as const;
```

### Titles and icons: rename-node source and inferred icons

`rename-node` gains `source` (`plugin` or `inferred`) and `expected-revision`. A stale `expected-revision` is `refused(conflict)`. A title with the source `inferred` never replaces a title the user set by hand, so an automatic titler cannot overwrite a manual name. `set-inferred-icon` follows the same rule for icons: a manual icon wins and the intent is `refused(conflict)`. `icon` is a catalogue id or a glyph, and none clears the inferred icon. `source` names the origin of the inference.

**Rust**

```rust
let rename = Intent::RenameNode(RenameNodeSpec {
    node, title: "Fix auth".into(), source: TitleOrigin::Inferred, expected_revision: Some(view.revision),
});
let icon = Intent::SetInferredIcon(SetInferredIconSpec { node, icon: Some("🔧".into()), source: "titler".into() });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const rename = { tag: 'rename-node', val: {
  node, title: 'Fix auth', source: 'inferred', expectedRevision: view.revision } } as const;
const icon = { tag: 'set-inferred-icon', val: { node, icon: '🔧', source: 'titler' } } as const;
```

### Attention marks

`mark-attention` flags a node with a `reason` of at most 80 characters. `ack-attention` clears it. The kernel keeps the attention policy: the done prefix and the sound are not plugin controls. Every change produces `attention-changed { node, marked, reason, by }` for plugins with `tree.attention` or `tree.read`, coalesced by node.

**Rust**

```rust
let mark = Intent::MarkAttention(MarkAttentionSpec { node, reason: "build needs review".into() });
let ack = Intent::AckAttention(node);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const mark = { tag: 'mark-attention', val: { node, reason: 'build needs review' } } as const;
const ack = { tag: 'ack-attention', val: node } as const;
```

### Rich decorations

`set-decoration` also takes these optional fields: `spans: option<rich-text>` (clickable styled text), `tooltip`, `frames: list<styled-text>` (2 to 16 frames), `frame-ms: u16` (at least 90), `trailing: bool` (placed after the title), `visibility` (`always` or `on-hover`) and `tone`. The host steps the frames with no plugin call per frame. With reduced motion the first frame is shown. Frames outside 2 to 16 or a `frame-ms` under 90 is `invalid-argument`.

**Rust**

```rust
let deco = Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
    node, slot: "build".into(), content: styled("building"), icon: None, sort_key: None, persist: false,
    spans: None,
    tooltip: Some(Tooltip::text("Build running")),
    frames: vec![styled("⠋"), styled("⠙"), styled("⠹"), styled("⠸")],
    frame_ms: 100,
    trailing: true,
    visibility: DecorationVisibility::Always,
    tone: Some(Tone::Info),
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const deco = { tag: 'set-decoration', val: {
  node, slot: 'build', content: styled('building'), icon: undefined, sortKey: undefined, persist: false,
  spans: undefined,
  tooltip: tooltip('Build running'),
  frames: ['⠋', '⠙', '⠹', '⠸'].map(styled), frameMs: 100,
  trailing: true, visibility: 'always', tone: 'info',
} } as const;
```

### Errors and limits

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| 4th toast in 10 s | `refused(rate-limited)` with `retry-after-ms` |
| Title over 60 characters, body over 200, more than 2 actions, duration outside 1,000 to 30,000 ms | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| More than 10 `set-status-segment` or `set-frame-slot` per second per slot | `refused(rate-limited)` |
| Segment or slot id not declared by the plugin | `refused(not-found)` |
| Pane does not match `applies_to` | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `open-external` declined, or a scheme other than `http`, `https`, `mailto` | `refused(not-permitted)` or `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `mark-attention` reason over 80 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| Manual title or icon in place | `refused(conflict)` |
| Frames outside 2 to 16, `frame-ms` under 90 | `refused(invalid-argument)` |

### What the user sees

The toast shows as a rounded panel in the corner with a countdown line that uses the filled and unfilled bar glyphs of the client. A status segment is part of the status bar pill. A frame slot sits in the pane header or footer. An attention mark changes the tree row.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-err">╭  ≡ ● · Deploy failed───────────────────╮</span>
<span class="t-err">│ exit status 2 on api-deploy            │</span>
<span class="t-err">│ Open log                               │</span>
<span class="t-err">│ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━───────────────────│</span>
<span class="t-err">╰────────────────────────────────────────╯</span>

<span class="t-hi">ℹ NORMAL  -  quota 82%  -  3 panes</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated: the border is the client's rounded panel, the countdown uses the toast gauge glyphs of the client, and the status line uses the segment separator. The toast layout and the colour mapping are the kernel's, and this composition is not a capture.

# menu provider

## menu provider

The `menu-provider` export lets a client plugin build a context menu or a toolbar submenu at the moment it opens. A static menu is a list in the manifest. A dynamic menu is built from what the user clicked: the node, the pane, the editor line, the selected text. The host calls the export, draws the returned entries with its own menu painter, and delivers the click as a `command-invoked` event. The plugin never draws the menu and never decides where it appears.

### You will need

| Need | Value |
|---|---|
| Side | Client only. The export fragment is `with-menus` in the world `ilium:client/base`. |
| Manifest | `"exports": ["menu-provider"]` on the client side, plus a `context_menu` entry with `"dynamic": true` or a `toolbar_buttons` entry with `"submenu": "dynamic"`. |
| Grant | None for the export. The menu target decides what the click handler may do: its own host calls need their own grants. |
| Rust | Crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, trait `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::MenuProvider`. |
| TypeScript | Package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, optional member `menuItems` of `definePlugin`. |
| Activation | The trigger `menu:<id>` starts a stopped client instance when a dynamic menu opens. Until the instance answers, the host shows the static entries. |

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/menu-provider in reference-wit
record menu-context {
  menu: string,                      // the menu id: a context_menu id, or a toolbar button id
  node: option<node-id>,             // tree node under the click
  pane: option<node-id>,             // pane that owns the click
  view: option<view-target>,         // plugin view, when the click was inside one
  key: option<string>,               // widget key inside that view
  buffer: option<buffer-id>,         // editor buffer, for target "editor"
  line: option<u32>,                 // editor line, 0 based
  selection: option<string>,         // selected text, at most 64 KiB
}

record menu-entry {
  id: string,                        // stable within the menu
  label: string,
  icon: option<string>,              // catalogue id or glyph
  shortcut: option<string>,          // display only, for example "ctrl+shift+c"
  parent: option<string>,            // id of a submenu entry; depth at most 2
  is-submenu: bool,
  separator-before: bool,
  checked: option<tri-state>,        // off, on or mixed
  disabled-reason: option<string>,   // at most 40 characters; a disabled entry shows it
  tooltip: option<tooltip>,
  danger: bool,
}

menu-items: func(context: menu-context) -> list<menu-entry>;   // at most 64 entries
```

`menu-entry` is also the item record of the `menu` widget, so the same value describes a menu inside a plugin view.

### Functions

| WIT function | Rust | TypeScript | Result | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `menu-items` | `MenuProvider::menu_items(&mut self, context: MenuContext) -> Vec<MenuEntry>` | `menuItems(context: MenuContext): MenuEntry[]` | `list<menu-entry>` | Returns the entries for the menu that is opening. |

### How the call behaves

- **When.** The host calls `menu-items` each time a dynamic menu opens, with the click context. A menu opened twice calls the export twice. The plugin may cache nothing across calls except what it keeps itself.
- **Deadline.** 20 ms, soft. On a timeout the menu opens with the static `items` only, and the breach counts toward the streak rule of the plugin (the third in a row traps; see [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/)).
- **Open latency.** The client calls all providers of the menu at once, one call per plugin side. It opens the menu when every provider has answered or after 25 ms, whichever comes first. The static entries are always in the first frame; entries of a provider that answered in time are in it too, and entries of a late provider are dropped for that opening. With three providers that answer in under 1 ms the menu is on screen within 5 ms of the click (benchmark B11).
- **What the user sees while waiting.** Nothing is drawn until the menu opens, so the user never sees a menu that fills in after it appeared. The wait is at most 25 ms.
- **T2 and T3.** A provider in a helper pays one round trip of about 0.5 ms at the 99th percentile inside the 20 ms. Keep the work small. A provider that is not running is activated by the trigger `menu:<id>`, and the first opening shows the static entries only because activation takes longer than the 25 ms wait. The menu does not wait for an activation.
- **[HST-476]** The client MUST call all menu providers of one opening at once, MUST open the menu when all have answered or after 25 ms, and MUST drop the entries of a late provider for that opening.
- **[HST-477]** The static entries MUST be in the first frame of the menu, and a menu MUST NOT change after its first frame is drawn.
- **[HST-478]** An opening MUST NOT wait for the activation of a provider that is not running.
- **Size.** At most 64 entries. Extra entries are cut and the host appends a last row `… N more`.
- **Depth.** A submenu entry has `is-submenu: true`. Its children name it in `parent`. Depth is at most 2. A static list nested deeper is refused at install with `manifest.menu-depth`. 
- **Click.** Choosing an entry arrives as `command-invoked` with `command` set to the command of the menu, `origin` set to `menu`, and the `context` field carrying `menu-item` with the chosen id, and `arguments-json` equal to `{"item": "<id>"}` merged with the click context fields that are present, for example `{"item":"open-in-editor","node":42,"line":17}`. A disabled entry cannot be chosen.
- **Placement.** The host places the menu, clamps it to the screen, and opens a submenu to the right of its parent entry. A submenu opens on hover after a short delay or on Right. The plugin cannot influence either.

### Example: a line menu for an editor

A plugin offers three entries for an editor line: open the path on the line, copy it, and a submenu with two refactor actions. The entries depend on whether the line holds a path, which is why the menu is dynamic. The manifest entry is `{ "id": "line-actions", "target": "editor", "dynamic": true, "command": "my.plugin/line-action" }` under `contributes.context_menu`.

**Grants:** `editor.read` (to read the line text for the path test).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::MenuProvider;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::menu_provider::MenuContext;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::MenuEntry;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::TriState;

impl MenuProvider for Plugin {
    fn menu_items(&mut self, context: MenuContext) -> Vec<MenuEntry> {
        let (Some(buffer), Some(line)) = (context.buffer, context.line) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        let text = editor::read_lines(buffer, line).unwrap_or_default();
        let has_path = looks_like_path(&text);
        vec![
            MenuEntry::new("open", "Open referenced path")
                .icon("file")
                .disabled_reason(if has_path { None } else { Some("no path on this line") }),
            MenuEntry::new("copy", "Copy line").shortcut("ctrl+shift+c"),
            MenuEntry::new("refactor", "Refactor").submenu().separator_before(true),
            MenuEntry::new("rename", "Rename symbol").parent("refactor"),
            MenuEntry::new("extract", "Extract function").parent("refactor")
                .checked(TriState::Off),
        ]
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as editor from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor';
import type { MenuContext, MenuEntry } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export const { menuProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  menuItems(context: MenuContext): MenuEntry[] {
    if (context.buffer === undefined || context.line === undefined) return [];
    const text = editor.lineText(context.buffer, context.line) ?? '';
    const hasPath = looksLikePath(text);
    return [
      { id: 'open', label: 'Open referenced path', icon: 'file',
        disabledReason: hasPath ? undefined : 'no path on this line' },
      { id: 'copy', label: 'Copy line', shortcut: 'ctrl+shift+c' },
      { id: 'refactor', label: 'Refactor', isSubmenu: true, separatorBefore: true },
      { id: 'rename', label: 'Rename symbol', parent: 'refactor' },
      { id: 'extract', label: 'Extract function', parent: 'refactor', checked: 'off' },
    ];
  },
});
```

Fields not set take the defaults: `icon`, `shortcut`, `parent`, `checked`, `disabled-reason` and `tooltip` are absent, and `is-submenu`, `separator-before` and `danger` are false.

Handling the click:

**Rust**

```rust
fn on_command(&mut self, event: CommandInvokedEvent) {
    let args: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&event.arguments_json).unwrap_or_default();
    match args["item"].as_str() {
        Some("open") => self.open_path(args["line"].as_u64()),
        Some("copy") => self.copy_line(args["line"].as_u64()),
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
function onCommand(event: CommandInvokedEvent): void {
  const args = JSON.parse(event.argumentsJson) as { item?: string; line?: number };
  if (args.item === 'open') openPath(args.line);
  else if (args.item === 'copy') copyLine(args.line);
}
```

### What the user sees

The host draws the menu with its rounded block, a two-space inset on every row, the check marker, the icon, and `▸` at the right of a submenu entry. The selected row is reversed. A disabled entry is dimmed and its reason is shown as a tooltip.

<pre class="term">
╭──────────────────────────────╮
│   Open referenced path       │
│   Copy line                  │
│                              │
│   Refactor                 ▸ │
╰──────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

The submenu opens beside the parent with its parent label as title:

<pre class="term">
╭──────────────────────────────╮╭──Refactor─────────────────╮
│   Open referenced path       ││   Rename symbol           │
│   Copy line                  ││   Extract function        │
│                              │╰───────────────────────────╯
│   Refactor                 ▸                              │
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

A checked entry draws `✓ ` before its icon; an unchecked tri-state entry keeps two blank cells so labels stay aligned. This is the layout of the host function `popup_action_line` of the client, and the glyph table in the manual's glyph reference.

### Errors and limits

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Deadline of 20 ms exceeded | Static `items` shown, breach counted. |
| More than 64 entries | Cut to 64, last row `… N more`. |
| Depth above 2 in a static list | Install refused with `manifest.menu-depth`. |
| `disabled-reason` longer than 40 characters | Truncated with `…`. |
| Trap inside `menu-items` | The menu opens with static items only and the plugin restarts under the usual rule. |

### See also

- [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/) for the export list and the deadline table.
- [Commands](/pages/api-commands/) for `command-invoked`, `context_menu` and `toolbar_buttons`.
- [Events](/pages/api-events/) for the click event.
- [Widgets: collections](/pages/widgets-collections/) for the `menu` widget that uses the same record.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) for `manifest.menu-depth`.

Return unique entry ids and valid parents; the result of an unknown `parent` or a duplicate entry `id` is undefined. Contract: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, export fragment `with-menus`.

# virtual rows provider

## virtual rows provider

A virtual row is a row in the project tree that does not belong to a pane or a group. The Chatroom row is one: it has a title, an icon, and it opens a panel when activated. A plugin declares a kind of virtual row in `contributes.virtual_rows` and fills it with the intent `set-virtual-rows`. The `virtual-rows-provider` export adds the missing piece: rows that have children, loaded when the user expands the row, a page at a time. A plugin that shows a folder explorer, a list of remote sessions or a mailbox in the tree uses it.

### You will need

| Need | Value |
|---|---|
| Side | Server and client. The export fragment is `with-virtual-rows`, in `ilium:server/base` and `ilium:client/base`. The row is owned by the side that sends `set-virtual-rows`. |
| Manifest | `"exports": ["virtual-rows-provider"]` and a `virtual_rows` entry with `"expandable": true` and `"children": "provider"`. |
| Grant | `tree.decorate` for `set-virtual-rows`. The export itself needs no grant. |
| Rust | Crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, trait `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::VirtualRowsProvider`. |
| TypeScript | Package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, member `listVirtualChildren` of `definePlugin`. |
| Activation | The trigger `virtual-rows:<row-kind>` starts a stopped instance when a provider row expands. |

### Manifest

```json
{ "contributes": { "virtual_rows": [
  { "id": "inbox", "expandable": true, "children": "provider",
    "accepts_drop": ["file", "text"], "drop_command": "mail/drop-on-folder" }
] } }
```

`children` is `"static"` when the child rows come from `set-virtual-rows` with a `parent`, and `"provider"` when the export supplies them. `accepts_drop` lists what the row accepts from a drag: `pane`, `file` or `text`. A drop runs `drop_command` with the origin `virtual-row-drop`, and the `context` of the event carries `virtual-row` with the id of the row that received it.

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/virtual-rows-provider in reference-wit
record virtual-row-child {
  id: string,                         // stable within the row kind; also used as the parent of deeper rows
  label: rich-text,                   // clickable spans allowed
  icon: option<string>,               // catalogue id or glyph
  expandable: bool,                   // true when the child can itself be expanded
  command: option<string>,            // global command id run on activation
  tooltip: option<tooltip>,
  accepts-drop: bool,
}

list-virtual-children: func(row-kind: string, parent: string, cursor: option<string>)
    -> result<tuple<list<virtual-row-child>, option<string>>, plugin-error>;
```

The result holds one page of children and the cursor of the next page. A `none` cursor means the last page.

### Functions and related intents

| Item | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list-virtual-children` | `VirtualRowsProvider::list_virtual_children(&mut self, row_kind: &str, parent: &str, cursor: Option<String>) -> Result<(Vec<VirtualRowChild>, Option<String>), PluginError>` | `listVirtualChildren(rowKind: string, parent: string, cursor?: string): [VirtualRowChild[], string \| undefined]`, throws `PluginError` | Returns one page of children of `parent`. |
| `set-virtual-rows` | `Intent::SetVirtualRows(SetVirtualRowsSpec)` | `{ tag: 'set-virtual-rows', val: ... }` | Sets the top-level rows of a kind. Rows gain `parent`, `expandable`, `accepts-drop`, `tooltip`, a `rich-text` label and `trailing`. |
| `set-expanded` | `Intent::SetExpanded(SetExpandedSpec)` | `{ tag: 'set-expanded', val: ... }` | Expands or collapses a row from the plugin. Needs `tree.write` for nodes; own virtual rows need no extra grant. |

### How the call behaves

- **When.** The host calls the export when the user expands a row of a kind declared with `children: "provider"`. `parent` is the id of the expanded row, and the first call has `cursor` unset. The host asks again with the returned cursor when the user chooses the row `Load more`.
- **Deadline.** 20 ms per call. A page that is not ready in time is shown as a row `…` with a spinner. A plugin that needs longer returns what it has cached and sends a fresh `set-virtual-rows` when the data arrives.
- **Page size.** At most 256 children per page.
- **Expansion state.** The host keeps which rows are expanded. The plugin may change it with `set-expanded`.
- **Cancel.** Collapsing a row discards its pending page. A late result for a collapsed row is dropped.
- **Errors.** The contract does not define how a failed page is drawn. Return a page whose first child explains the problem when the user must see it.

### Example: a mailbox with folders

The plugin keeps a list of folders on the server side and returns them page by page. The messages of a folder are children of the folder row.

**Grants:** `tree.decorate`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::VirtualRowsProvider;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{SetVirtualRowsSpec, VirtualRow};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::virtual_rows_provider::VirtualRowChild;

const PAGE: usize = 50;

impl VirtualRowsProvider for Plugin {
    fn list_virtual_children(
        &mut self,
        row_kind: &str,
        parent: &str,
        cursor: Option<String>,
    ) -> Result<(Vec<VirtualRowChild>, Option<String>), PluginError> {
        if row_kind != "inbox" {
            return Err(PluginError::not_found("unknown row kind"));
        }
        let start: usize = cursor.as_deref().and_then(|c| c.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
        let all = self.messages_of(parent);
        let page = all.iter().skip(start).take(PAGE).map(|message| {
            VirtualRowChild::new(&message.id, &message.subject)
                .icon("mail")
                .command("mail/open")
        });
        let next = (start + PAGE < all.len()).then(|| (start + PAGE).to_string());
        Ok((page.collect(), next))
    }
}

// top level rows, sent from on_events
fn top_rows(&self) -> Submission {
    Submission::new(Intent::SetVirtualRows(SetVirtualRowsSpec {
        row_kind: "inbox".into(),
        rows: self.folders().iter()
            .map(|f| VirtualRow::new(&f.id, &f.name).expandable(true))
            .collect(),
    }))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { VirtualRowChild, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const PAGE = 50;

export const { virtualRowsProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  listVirtualChildren(rowKind, parent, cursor): [VirtualRowChild[], string | undefined] {
    if (rowKind !== 'inbox') throw { code: 'not-found', message: 'unknown row kind' };
    const start = cursor === undefined ? 0 : Number(cursor);
    const all = messagesOf(parent);
    const page = all.slice(start, start + PAGE).map((message) => ({
      id: message.id,
      label: [{ text: message.subject, style: {}, target: { tag: 'none' } }],
      icon: 'mail',
      expandable: false,
      command: 'mail/open',
      acceptsDrop: false,
    }));
    return [page, start + PAGE < all.length ? String(start + PAGE) : undefined];
  },
});

function topRows(): Submission {
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'set-virtual-rows', val: {
      rowKind: 'inbox',
      rows: folders().map((f) => ({ id: f.id, label: f.name, expandable: true })),
    } },
    correlation: 0n, dedupKey: undefined,
  };
}
```

### What the user sees

The expanded row loads its children; the first page ends with a row `Load more` when a cursor was returned. While a page is pending the child area shows `…` and a spinner. Rows follow the tree layout of the client: an indent marker `›` per depth, an expand symbol, the icon, the title.

<pre class="term">
▼ 📂 Ilium
›   🦀 ⠋ Fix auth
›   🖥️    Shell
▼ 📬 Inbox
› ▶ 📁 Work
› ▼ 📁 Reviews
›   ›   ✉ Review request: tree rows
›   ›   ✉ Re: provider paging
›   ›   Load more
</pre>

The glyph set for the group and agent rows is the one the real client draws (see the glyph reference); the mailbox icons are examples of what a plugin may pass as `icon`.

### Errors and limits

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Row kind not declared | `set-virtual-rows` completes as `refused(invalid-argument)`. |
| More than 256 children in a page | The page is cut to 256. |
| Deadline of 20 ms exceeded | The breach is counted; the host shows `…` with a spinner while the page is pending. |
| Trap in the provider | The plugin restarts under the usual rule. |

### See also

- [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/) for the export list and deadlines.
- [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) for `set-virtual-rows` and `set-expanded`.
- [Events](/pages/api-events/) for `command-invoked` with the `virtual-row-drop` origin.
- [capability: tree decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/) for `tree.decorate`.
- [Tree](/pages/api-tree/) for reading the real tree.

Contract: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, export fragment `with-virtual-rows`.

# token provider

## token provider

The `token-provider` export teaches the editor a language the host does not know. The host calls it with lines of text, and the plugin answers with tokens: a line, a start column, a length and a kind. The host then draws the tokens with its theme colours. The plugin never chooses a colour. The syntax engine, its caches and its size budget stay a host service; the provider only supplies tokens for the languages the plugin declares.

### You will need

| Need | Value |
|---|---|
| Side | Client only. The export fragment is `with-tokens` in `ilium:client/base`. |
| Grant | `editor.read`, for both the export and the `languages` contribution. |
| Manifest | `"exports": ["token-provider"]` and one or more `contributes.languages` entries. |
| Rust | Crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, trait `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::TokenProvider`. |
| TypeScript | Package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, member `tokens` of `definePlugin`. |
| Activation | The trigger `language:<id>` starts a stopped instance when a buffer of that language becomes visible. |

### Manifest

```json
{ "contributes": { "languages": [
  { "id": "ilium-log", "title": "Ilium log", "extensions": ["ilog"], "file_names": ["progress.log"] }
] } }
```

`extensions` are written without the dot. At most 8 languages per plugin; more is refused with `manifest.contribution-limit`.

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/token-provider in reference-wit
enum token-kind { keyword, string, number, comment, type-name, function, variable,
                  operator, punctuation, constant, tag, attribute, plain }
record token { line: u32, start: u32, length: u32, kind: token-kind }

tokens: func(buffer: buffer-id, first-line: u32, lines: list<string>, state-in: option<list<u8>>)
    -> tuple<list<token>, option<list<u8>>>;
```

`line` is an absolute buffer line (0 based), `start` and `length` count characters of that line. The second tuple element is the lexer state at the end of the block. The host hands it back as `state-in` for the next block, so a construct that spans lines, such as a block comment, continues correctly.

### Functions

| WIT function | Rust | TypeScript | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `TokenProvider::tokens(&mut self, buffer: BufferId, first_line: u32, lines: Vec<String>, state_in: Option<Vec<u8>>) -> (Vec<Token>, Option<Vec<u8>>)` | `tokens(buffer: bigint, firstLine: number, lines: string[], stateIn?: Uint8Array): [Token[], Uint8Array \| undefined]` | tokens of the block and the carried state |

### How the call behaves

- **Which lines.** The host calls for the visible lines plus a margin, not for the whole file. It passes the carried state of the previous block, so the plugin keeps no cursor of its own.
- **Deadline.** 10 ms per call. On a timeout the lines stay plain and the host retries later. The breach counts toward the deadline rule.
- **Colours.** Colours come from the theme by `token-kind`. `plain` draws in the normal text colour. A plugin cannot pick a colour, so a theme change recolours every language at once.

<defs>
<marker id="tok-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto">
<path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/>
</marker>
</defs>
<title>Token blocks and carried state</title>
<desc>The host sends block one with no state, receives tokens and a state, then sends block two with that state.</desc>

<text x="168" y="130" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">tokens + state-out</text>
<line x1="130" y1="145" x2="300" y2="117" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#tok-arrow)"/>
<text x="160" y="170" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">state-in: the bytes returned above</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The state returned for one block is the input of the next, so a multi-line comment keeps its colour across the seam.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Example: a log language

The plugin colours a time stamp, a level word and the rest of a line. It keeps no state, so the second tuple element is unset.

**Grants:** `editor.read`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::TokenProvider;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor::BufferId;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::token_provider::{Token, TokenKind};

impl TokenProvider for Plugin {
    fn tokens(
        &mut self,
        _buffer: BufferId,
        first_line: u32,
        lines: Vec<String>,
        _state_in: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    ) -> (Vec<Token>, Option<Vec<u8>>) {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (offset, text) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            let line = first_line + offset as u32;
            // "2026-10-12 09:15:03 warn message"
            if text.len() >= 19 {
                out.push(Token { line, start: 0, length: 19, kind: TokenKind::Number });
            }
            for (word, kind) in [("warn", TokenKind::Keyword), ("error", TokenKind::Constant)] {
                if let Some(at) = text.find(word) {
                    out.push(Token { line, start: at as u32, length: word.len() as u32, kind });
                }
            }
        }
        (out, None)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Token } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export const { tokenProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  tokens(_buffer, firstLine, lines): [Token[], Uint8Array | undefined] {
    const out: Token[] = [];
    lines.forEach((text, offset) => {
      const line = firstLine + offset;
      if (text.length >= 19) out.push({ line, start: 0, length: 19, kind: 'number' });
      for (const [word, kind] of [['warn', 'keyword'], ['error', 'constant']] as const) {
        const at = text.indexOf(word);
        if (at >= 0) out.push({ line, start: at, length: word.length, kind });
      }
    });
    return [out, undefined];
  },
});
```

Byte offsets and character offsets differ for non-ASCII text. The contract counts characters of the line, so a Rust plugin converts `str::find` byte positions with `chars().count()` when a line is not ASCII.

### What the user sees

The editor draws the tokens with the theme colours of each kind. A line with a warning keeps the time stamp in the number colour and the word `warn` in the keyword colour:

<pre class="term">
 41 │ 2026-10-12 09:15:03 info  server started
 42 │ 2026-10-12 09:15:07 warn  config key ignored
 43 │ 2026-10-12 09:15:09 error plugin stopped
</pre>

The render shows the layout only. Colours are not shown here because they come from the user's theme and the plugin never sets them.

### Errors and limits

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Deadline of 10 ms exceeded | Lines stay plain, host retries, breach counted. |
| More than 8 languages | `manifest.contribution-limit`. |
| Trap in `tokens` | The lines stay plain and the plugin restarts under the usual rule. |

### See also

- [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/) for the export list and deadlines.
- [Primitives: editor](/pages/primitives-editor/) for the `annotator` path and `editor.viewport`.
- [capability: editor read](/pages/capability-editor-read/) for `editor.read`.
- [Widgets: media and embedded](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) for `code-view`, which uses the same tokens.

Contract: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, export fragment `with-tokens`.
