# Glyph plane and frame receipts

## Glyph plane and frame receipts

The glyph plane and frame receipts are part of the surface of the single contract `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. There is no second contract version. The surface is the extended pixel surface that ambient scenes draw into (see [scenes](/pages/api-scenes/)). It adds a glyph plane for text over the pixels, owner ids so a scene can learn which of its objects is under the pointer, a receipt for every presented frame, fonts rasterized by the host, pre-rendered loops, and larger package assets. It does not change the rule that the shared look, dithering and the palette are applied by the host: glyph colours go through the shared look too, so a scene never escapes the global appearance.

### What you need

- **Grant.** None for the surface. Video from bytes needs `media.video` (see [media](/pages/api-media/)).
- **Manifest.** In `contributes.scenes`: `glyph_plane: true` for the glyph plane, and `prerender: { frames, fps, cache_mib }` for a looped scene. `prerender` and `wants-pointer` exclude each other (`manifest.scene-prerender`).
- **Sides.** The scene (A) world. Fonts are always available there.

```json
"contributes": { "scenes": [{ "id": "lanes", "title": "Lanes", "glyph_plane": true }] }
```

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:anim/surface in reference-wit
record glyph-cell { column: u16, row: u16, text: string, fg: option<u32>, bg: option<u32>, add: modifiers }
write-glyphs: func(cells: list<glyph-cell>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;       // glyph_plane: true; <= 131,072 cells per frame
clear-glyphs: func();
set-owner-ids: func(first-row: u32, ids: list<u16>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;   // one id per pixel, 0 = none
record frame-receipt { frame: u64, presented-at-millis: u64, dropped-before: u32, pointer-owner: option<u16> }
last-receipt: func() -> option<frame-receipt>;
```

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:anim/fonts in reference-wit
resource font {
  constructor(asset: string);
  rasterize: func(text: string, size-px: u16) -> result<tuple<u32, u32, list<u8>>, plugin-error>;
}
```

| Method | Rust (`Surface`) | TypeScript | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `write-glyphs` | `write_glyphs(&[GlyphCell])` | `writeGlyphs(cells)` | Text cells drawn over the pixels after dithering. Icon widths apply. |
| `clear-glyphs` | `clear_glyphs()` | `clearGlyphs()` | Removes every glyph cell. |
| `set-owner-ids` | `set_owner_ids(first_row, &[u16])` | `setOwnerIds(firstRow, ids)` | One id per pixel from `first_row`, 0 means none. |
| `last-receipt` | `last_receipt()` | `lastReceipt()` | None before the first frame is presented. |
| `font` | `Font::new(asset)`, `.rasterize(text, size_px)` | `new Font(asset)`, `.rasterize(text, sizePx)` | Returns width, height and `gray8` bytes. |

### The glyph plane

A glyph cell is one terminal cell of text with optional foreground, background (RGB `0xRRGGBB`) and modifiers. The host draws it over the dithered pixels with the same glyph widths the tree uses, so a wide icon takes two cells. Glyph colours are recoloured by the shared look, brightness, contrast and palette included. Use the plane for labels, scores and axes; keep pictures in the pixels.

<figure>
<pre class="term">⠀⠀⣀⣤⣶⣿⣿⣶⣤⣀⠀⠀⠀⠀⣀⣤⣶⣿⣿⣶⣤⣀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⣴⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣦⠀⣴⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣦⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠻⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⠟⠀⠻⣿⣿⣿ Lane 2 ⣿⣿⠟⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠈⠛⠿⣿⣿⠿⠛⠁⠀⠀⠀⠈⠛⠿⣿⣿⠿⠛⠁⠀⠀⠀⠀
</pre>
<figcaption>Pixels shown as Braille cells (two columns by four rows of dots per cell, as the client draws scenes). The words "Lane 2" are glyph cells over them.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

fn label(surface: &mut Surface, column: u16, row: u16) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    surface.clear_glyphs();
    let cells: Vec<GlyphCell> = "Lane 2".chars().enumerate().map(|(index, ch)| GlyphCell {
        column: column + index as u16, row, text: ch.to_string(),
        fg: Some(0xffffff), bg: None, add: Modifiers::BOLD,
    }).collect();
    surface.write_glyphs(&cells)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Surface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export function label(surface: Surface, column: number, row: number): void {
  surface.clearGlyphs();
  const cells = [...'Lane 2'].map((text, index) => ({
    column: column + index, row, text, fg: 0xffffff, bg: undefined, add: { bold: true },
  }));
  surface.writeGlyphs(cells);
}
```

### Owner ids and receipts

`set-owner-ids` tells the host which logical object each pixel belongs to (a lane, a ship, a button). The receipt of the last presented frame names `pointer-owner`, the owner under the pointer, so a scene with `wants-pointer` hit-tests without keeping its own copy of the frame. `dropped-before` counts frames the host skipped to keep pace, which lets a scene advance its clock by real time.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 440 130" role="img" aria-label="Owner ids and the frame receipt">
<title>Owner ids</title>
<desc>The scene writes pixels and owner ids. The host presents the frame, finds the owner under the pointer and returns it in the receipt.</desc>
<defs><marker id="s2" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
<rect x="8" y="14" width="130" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/><text x="73" y="38" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">render: pixels + ids</text>
<line x1="138" y1="34" x2="180" y2="34" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#s2)"/>
<rect x="180" y="14" width="120" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/><text x="240" y="38" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">host presents</text>
<line x1="300" y1="34" x2="340" y2="34" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#s2)"/>
<rect x="340" y="14" width="92" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/><text x="386" y="38" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">receipt</text>

</svg>
<figcaption>The pointer is resolved by the host against the ids the scene wrote.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
fn hover_lane(surface: &Surface) -> Option<u16> {
    surface.last_receipt().and_then(|receipt| receipt.pointer_owner)
}
fn mark_lanes(surface: &mut Surface, width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let ids: Vec<u16> = (0..width * height).map(|i| 1 + ((i % width) * 4 / width) as u16).collect();
    surface.set_owner_ids(0, &ids)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export const hoverLane = (surface: Surface): number | undefined => surface.lastReceipt()?.pointerOwner;
export function markLanes(surface: Surface, width: number, height: number): void {
  const ids = Array.from({ length: width * height }, (_, i) => 1 + Math.floor(((i % width) * 4) / width));
  surface.setOwnerIds(0, ids);
}
```

### Fonts

Fonts are package assets (TTF or OTF, at most 4 MiB each; `manifest.asset-size` otherwise). `rasterize` returns `(width, height, gray8)`, which a scene blends into its raster with its own colour. Package assets as a whole may be up to 64 MiB.

### Pre-rendered loops

With `prerender: { frames, fps, cache_mib }` the host calls `render` for the declared frame count once, caches the frames (at most 3,600 frames, 30 fps, 128 MiB) and plays them in a loop with no further plugin calls. A change to the scene's settings or palette invalidates the cache and the host renders again.

### Errors and limits

| Case | Error |
|---|---|
| Cell outside the surface, id rows outside | `invalid-argument` |
| More than 131,072 glyph cells per frame | `quota-exceeded` |
| `write-glyphs` without `glyph_plane` | `unsupported` |
| Font asset over 4 MiB | `manifest.asset-size` |
| `prerender` out of range or with `wants-pointer` | `manifest.scene-prerender` |

### See also

- [scenes](/pages/api-scenes/), [media](/pages/api-media/), [pointer](/pages/api-pointer/), [Capabilities reference](/pages/reference-capabilities/) and [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).

<!-- source: http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/primitives-agent.md -->
# Agent primitive

## Agent primitive

An agent pane runs an agent CLI such as Claude Code or Codex. The agent primitive lets a plugin find
the agent in a pane, read its activity and session, read the last prompt the user submitted, add
toolbar buttons, send actions that the agent understands, and register signatures for agents the host
does not know.

The kernel owns the process walk, the screen snapshot and every key write. The plugin owns the
signature (how to recognise the agent) and the classifier (what the agent is doing now).

### What you need

| Grant | Needed for |
|---|---|
| `agent.read` | `agents`, `view`, `session`; the events `agent-identified`, `agent-activity-changed` and `agent-goal-changed` |
| `agent.signatures` | The `signatures` manifest entry, the `detector` export and `register-signature` |
| `agent.control` | `set-toolbar-state` and the intent `agent-action` |
| `agent.read-prompts` | The event `input-submitted` and `last-prompt`. High risk: it exposes what the user typed. |
| `fs.read:agent-sessions:<agent>` | Reading the transcript file that `session` points to |

`agent-action` needs only `agent.control`. The kernel checks the activity itself, so the plugin does
not need `agent.read` to send an action.

The detector and runtime signatures run on the server side. Toolbar state and agent actions also work
from the client side. Plugins are written in Rust (stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2`
target) or TypeScript (Bun 1.2 or later). See [toolchain setup](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/).

### Interface

```wit
// ilium:types/tree
enum agent-activity { none, working, idle, awaiting-approval, done, menu }
record agent-view {
    signature: string, activity: agent-activity, objective: option<string>, goal: option<string>,
}

// ilium:primitives/agent
record agent-pane { pane: node-id, view: agent-view }
record session-ref { scope: string, path: string, session-id: string }
record signature-action { id: string, keys: string, allowed-when: option<list<agent-activity>> }
record signature-spec {
    id: string, process-names: list<string>, aliases: list<string>, icon: option<string>,
    resume: option<list<string>>, actions: list<signature-action>,
    session-scope: option<string>, submit-keys: option<string>,
}
agents: func() -> list<agent-pane>;
view: func(pane: node-id) -> option<agent-view>;
session: func(pane: node-id) -> option<session-ref>;
last-prompt: func(pane: node-id) -> option<string>;
register-signature: func(spec: signature-spec) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
set-toolbar-state: func(button: string, pane: option<node-id>, enabled: bool,
    label: option<string>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
```

The `detector` export is a separate contract, so a plugin can implement it without registering
signatures at run time:

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/detector in reference-wit
// ilium:server/detector
record detector-process { name: string, argv: list<string> }
record detector-screen {
    columns: u16, rows: list<string>, cursor-row: u16, title: option<string>, revision: u64,
}
record classification { activity: agent-activity, objective: option<string>, goal: option<string> }
identify: func(processes: list<detector-process>) -> option<string>;
classify: func(signature: string, screen: detector-screen) -> classification;
```

### Functions

| Function (Rust / TypeScript) | Grant | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agents()` / `agents()` | `agent.read` | `list<agent-pane>` | One entry per identified agent pane. Empty when the grant is declined. |
| `view(pane)` / `view(pane)` | `agent.read` | `option<agent-view>` | Signature and activity of one pane. None when the pane is not identified or the grant is declined. |
| `session(pane)` / `session(pane)` | `agent.read` | `option<session-ref>` | Transcript reference. Only a signature with `session_scope` yields one. |
| `last_prompt(pane)` / `lastPrompt(pane)` | `agent.read-prompts` | `option<string>` | Last prompt submitted to the pane. None when the grant is declined. |
| `register_signature(spec)` / `registerSignature(spec)` | `agent.signatures` | `result<_, plugin-error>` | Adds a signature, or replaces one the same plugin added at run time. |
| `set_toolbar_state(...)` / `setToolbarState(...)` | `agent.control` | `result<_, plugin-error>` | Enables or relabels a toolbar button. |

All of them are synchronous and take no request id. The Rust module is
`ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent`; the TypeScript import is `@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent`.
Types follow the SDK naming rules: `AgentPane`, `SessionRef`,
`SignatureSpec` and `SignatureAction` in Rust, with the same fields in camelCase in TypeScript.
`AgentActivity` and `AgentView` come from `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree`.

`set_toolbar_state` with `pane: None` sets the state for every agent pane that shows the button. With a
pane id it sets that pane only, overrides the all-pane state, and is dropped when the pane closes. A
`label` of `None` keeps the current label. A label over 32 cells is `invalid-argument`.

Activity values are `none` (not identified yet), `working`, `idle`, `awaiting-approval`, `done` and
`menu`. In Rust they are `AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval` and so on; in TypeScript they are the
strings `'awaiting-approval'` and so on.

### Signatures

A signature describes one agent program. Plugin signatures from the manifest and from
`register-signature` share one set of rules:

| Manifest key | Field | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `id` | required | 1 to 64 characters from `[a-z0-9-]`. The global id is `<plugin-id>.<id>`. |
| `process_names` | `process-names` | required | 1 to 32 names, each non-empty, at most 255 bytes, with no `/` unless absolute. |
| `aliases` | `aliases` | none | At most 32 entries. |
| `icon` | `icon` | none | A Tabler icon name. |
| `resume` | `resume` | none | An argv template. `{session}` is replaced by the session id. |
| `actions` | `actions` | none | At most 32 actions. Each `keys` value is at most 1 KiB. |
| `session_scope` | `session-scope` | none | A scope such as `agent-sessions:claude`. |
| `submit_keys` | `submit-keys` | `"\r"` | Keys that submit a prompt in this agent. |

Each action may set `allowed_when`, a list of activities in which the action is allowed. The default is
`["idle", "done", "awaiting-approval", "menu"]`, so a compact action is refused while the agent works.
Built-in signatures keep bare ids (`claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`). A signature from `register-signature`
replaces an earlier one with the same id from the same plugin. A signature id that the manifest already
contributes returns `conflict`.

Settings can also supply signatures as plain JSON. They go through the same validation, and an error
names the field path, for example `process_names[2]: empty name`.

### Contributions

```json
{
  "id": "example.agent-tools",
  "signatures": [{
    "id": "example-agent",
    "process_names": ["example-agent"],
    "aliases": ["ea"],
    "icon": "robot",
    "actions": { "compact": { "keys": "/compact\r", "allowed_when": ["idle", "done"] } },
    "resume": ["example-agent", "--resume", "{session}"],
    "session_scope": "agent-sessions:claude"
  }],
  "commands": [{ "id": "compact", "title": "Compact agent context" }],
  "toolbar_buttons": [{
    "id": "compact", "icon": "compress", "label": "Compact",
    "command": "example.agent-tools/compact",
    "applies_to": ["example-agent"], "requires_action": "compact"
  }],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["agent.read", "agent.control", "agent.signatures"] }
}
```

A toolbar button has `applies_to`, either `"all"` or a list of signature ids. Use the local id for the
plugin's own signatures and the bare id for built-in ones. `requires_action` shows the button only on
panes whose signature declares that action. The button's `command` is a global command id.

### Detector rules

- `identify` runs on every detection tick for each pane that has no signature. It returns the local
  signature id, and the kernel adds the plugin prefix. An id the plugin did not register is ignored, the
  pane stays unidentified, and the kernel logs a warning.
- `classify` runs for an identified pane whenever its screen revision changes.
- Each call has a 20 ms deadline. A missed deadline keeps the previous classification, emits nothing and
  logs a warning.
- A trap counts as a failure and follows the [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule): restart after 1 s, then 5 s, and disable
  on the third failure within 10 minutes.
- Without the `detector` export a pane is identified by `process_names` and `aliases` alone. Its
  activity stays `none`, but `resume`, `actions` and `submit_keys` still apply.

<svg viewBox="0 0 400 190" role="img" aria-label="Agent detection loop between kernel and plugin">
  <defs>

      markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <text x="10" y="160" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">The plugin never polls. The kernel calls it on each tick.</text>
  <text x="10" y="176" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">classify runs only when the screen revision changes.</text>

<figcaption>The kernel owns the timing and the stored state. The plugin answers identify and classify
calls only.</figcaption>

### Example 1: classifier and compact button (Rust)

This server plugin identifies `example-agent`, classifies its screen, and enables the Compact button
only while the agent is idle. When the user presses the button, the plugin submits the `compact` action,
which the kernel sends as `/compact` followed by Enter. The manifest above is the matching manifest.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{Classification, DetectorProcess, DetectorScreen};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::{AgentActivityEvent, CommandInvokedEvent};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::AgentActionSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

const SIGNATURE: &str = "example-agent";
const COMPACT_COMMAND: &str = "example.agent-tools/compact";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["detector"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct AgentTools;

impl Detector for AgentTools {
    fn identify(&mut self, processes: Vec<DetectorProcess>) -> Option<String> {
        let found = processes.iter().any(|process| process.name == "example-agent");
        found.then(|| SIGNATURE.to_string())
    }

    fn classify(&mut self, _signature: String, screen: DetectorScreen) -> Classification {
        let shows = |text: &str| screen.rows.iter().any(|row| row.contains(text));
        let activity = if shows("Do you want to proceed?") {
            AgentActivity::AwaitingApproval
        } else if shows("esc to interrupt") {
            AgentActivity::Working
        } else {
            AgentActivity::Idle
        };
        Classification { activity, objective: None, goal: None }
    }
}

impl Handler for AgentTools {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. }) => {
                    let enabled = current == AgentActivity::Idle;
                    // A pane that closed meanwhile returns not-found; nothing else depends on it.
                    let _ = agent::set_toolbar_state("compact", Some(node), enabled, None);
                }
                Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, context, .. })
                    if command == COMPACT_COMMAND =>
                {
                    let Some(pane) = context.pane else { continue };
                    let spec = AgentActionSpec { pane, action_id: "compact".into() };
                    let key = format!("compact:{pane}");
                    submissions.push(Submission::keyed(Intent::AgentAction(spec), key));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

Grants: `agent.read` for the activity event, `agent.control` for the toolbar state and the action, and
`agent.signatures` for the manifest signature and the detector export.

Outcome: on a permission prompt the pane shows `awaiting-approval` and Compact is disabled. A press
sends `compact` once; a second press with the same key within 10 minutes completes as `duplicate`.

### Example 2: runtime signature and session (TypeScript)

This server plugin registers a second agent, `example-agent-beta`, when it activates. A command reads the
session reference and the last prompt of the focused pane and writes them to the plugin log.

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { lastPrompt, registerSignature, session } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent';

const SHOW_SESSION_COMMAND = 'example.beta-agent/show-session';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    // Throws PluginError (invalid-argument) when validation fails; activation then fails.
    registerSignature({
      id: 'example-agent-beta',
      processNames: ['example-agent-beta'],
      aliases: [],
      icon: 'robot',
      resume: ['example-agent-beta', '--resume', '{session}'],
      actions: [],
      sessionScope: 'agent-sessions:codex',
      submitKeys: undefined,
    });
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== SHOW_SESSION_COMMAND) continue;
      const pane = event.val.context.pane;
      if (pane === undefined) continue;
      const reference = session(pane);
      const prompt = lastPrompt(pane);
      log('info', `session ${reference?.path ?? 'none'}; last prompt ${prompt ?? 'none'}`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Grants: `agent.signatures`, `agent.read` and `agent.read-prompts`. The manifest also needs a `commands` entry with id `show-session`. Reading the transcript behind
`reference.path` would also need `fs.read:agent-sessions:codex`, which this example does not use.

### Intent and events

`agent-action` is an intent, `Intent::AgentAction(AgentActionSpec { pane, action_id })` in Rust and
`{ tag: 'agent-action', val: { pane, actionId } }` in TypeScript. Its submission must carry a
`dedup-key`. The kernel checks the steps below in order. A refused submission does not reserve its
key, so a retry with the same key after fixing the cause is valid.

| Step | Outcome when it fails |
|---|---|
| Well formed, key present | `refused(invalid-argument)`; the whole batch is refused |
| Grant `agent.control` | `refused(not-permitted)` |
| Key reserved already | `duplicate(original)` |
| Pane exists and is an agent pane | `refused(not-found)` |
| Pane restored and process started | `refused(pane-not-ready)` |
| Action id in the signature | `refused(unsupported)` |
| Activity allowed by `allowed_when` | `refused(conflict)` with the message `agent is working` |
| Rate: 20 per second per pane per plugin | `refused(rate-limited)` with `retry-after-ms` |
| Write | `failed(code)`; the key stays reserved, so a retry needs a new key |

Events:

| Event | Payload | Grant | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-identified` | `node`, `signature` | `agent.read` | Never dropped. Always before the first activity event of the pane. |
| `agent-activity-changed` | `node`, `previous`, `current`, `revision` | `agent.read` | Never dropped. |
| `agent-goal-changed` | `node`, `goal` | `agent.read` | Coalesced per node. |
| `input-submitted` | `node`, `text`, `source`, `epoch` | `agent.read-prompts` | Never dropped. Without the grant, nothing derived from the text is sent. |

`source` is one of `user`, `plugin`, `scheduled` or `voice`. `epoch` is the prompt counter of the pane, and it increases with each submitted prompt.

### Errors and edge cases

- `register-signature` returns `invalid-argument` for a rule that breaks the signature limits (id, process names, aliases, icon,
  action count or key size). The message names the field path. It returns `conflict` for an id the
  manifest already contributes.
- Two signatures from different origins that match one process name do not fail. The user's signature
  wins over a plugin signature, which wins over a built-in one, and the overlap is logged as a warning.
- `set-toolbar-state` returns `not-found` for a button that is not the plugin's own or a pane that does
  not exist, and `not-permitted` when the grant is missing. Its state lasts until the plugin changes it.
  A plugin restart resets each button to its manifest state, and a revoked grant withdraws the state.
- `agents()` returns an empty list when `agent.read` is declined. `view`, `session` and `last_prompt`
  return none, because these functions have no error channel.
- A grant revoked at run time takes effect on the next call.
- A pane has no activity before its `agent-identified` event. Restored panes return none for
  `last_prompt` until a new prompt is submitted, because the text is not in the snapshot.

### What the user sees

The toolbar of an agent pane shows each button that matches `applies_to` and `requires_action`. A
disabled button is greyed out and does not respond. The tree shows each identified pane's activity
through `node-view.agent`.

╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
<span class="t-dim">🗜️ Compact  disabled while the agent awaits approval</span>

# Basic primitive

## Basic primitive

A basic pane is a pane whose body the plugin draws. The kernel draws everything around the body: the frame, the title in the top edge and a one-line status in the footer. The plugin declares a pane kind in its manifest, opens panes of that kind, and draws each pane's body from the `views` export. The plugin keeps its state in node metadata or in storage, so a restored pane shows the same content after a restart.

A basic pane has no process. The `pane-not-ready` error never applies to it, and the pane is usable as soon as the kernel creates it.

### What you need

**Grants.** The plugin needs `panes.provide-kind` to contribute a pane kind and to call the four `basic` functions for panes of that kind. The same grant lets the plugin draw the body through `ui`, so no separate `ui.panels` grant is needed. Add `tree.metadata` when the plugin keeps its state in node metadata.

**Language and side.** A basic pane runs in the client instance of the plugin. Its `handler` and its `views` export both run there. Rust and TypeScript both work; the examples below show each.

**Manifest.** Each pane kind is one entry in `pane_kinds`. The `persist` field has no default, so every entry must set it.

```json
{
  "pane_kinds": [{
    "id": "notes",
    "title": "Notes",
    "icon": "notebook",
    "primitive": "basic",
    "wants_keys": true,
    "persist": "metadata"
  }]
}
```

The global kind id is the plugin id, a dot and the local id. The plugin `example.scratchpad` with the local id `notes` gives the kind `example.scratchpad.notes`. The pane's content kind has the same string, so the plugin compares against it when a pane is created.

| Manifest field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `primitive` | `basic` | Selects this primitive. |
| `wants_keys` | `true` or `false` | With `true`, keys that the focused widget does not consume arrive as `key-pressed` for the pane. |
| `persist` | `metadata`, `storage` or `none` | Decides what survives a restart (see below). |

With `persist: "metadata"`, the kernel saves the node's metadata, up to 64 KiB per node per plugin, and gives it back on restore. With `persist: "storage"`, the kernel recreates the node empty and deletes the plugin's storage keys under `pane/<node-id>/` when the pane closes; the plugin reads its own buckets. With `persist: "none"`, the pane starts empty after a restart.

### Interface

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:primitives/basic in reference-wit
interface basic {
  set-title: func(pane: node-id, title: string) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
  set-status: func(pane: node-id, status: styled-text) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
  request-focus: func(pane: node-id) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
  size: func(pane: node-id) -> option<tuple<u16, u16>>;
}
```

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `set-title` | `basic::set_title(pane, &str)` | `basic.setTitle(pane, title)` | `Result<(), PluginError>` | Sets the title in the top edge of the frame. At most 256 characters. |
| `set-status` | `basic::set_status(pane, StyledText)` | `basic.setStatus(pane, status)` | `Result<(), PluginError>` | Sets the one-line footer. Styled text, at most 256 characters, no line break. |
| `request-focus` | `basic::request_focus(pane)` | `basic.requestFocus(pane)` | `Result<(), PluginError>` | Asks the kernel to focus the pane. |
| `size` | `basic::size(pane)` | `basic.size(pane)` | `Option<(u16, u16)>` | Columns and rows of the body. `None` for a node that is not a pane of the plugin's kinds. |

The TypeScript functions come from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/basic`, imported as
`import * as basic from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/basic';`. Rust uses
`use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::basic;`. A status is a list of spans. `Span::plain("Saved")` in
Rust and `span('Saved')` in TypeScript build a span with the default style.

`size` gives the same numbers as the `area` argument of `render` for that pane. Use either one to
lay out the body.

### Body and lifecycle

The body is the `views` export. Rust implements `fn render(&mut self, view: ViewTarget, area: Area)
-> UiTree`, and TypeScript exports `render(view, area)`. For a basic pane, `view` is
`ViewTarget::Pane(node)`, or `{ tag: 'pane', val: node }` in TypeScript.

The host calls `render` in four cases: when the pane's view first opens, after the plugin calls
`ui::invalidate` for that pane, on a resize, and after a restore. It never calls `render` for each
frame. The render deadline is 10 ms by default. A render that runs longer traps the plugin instance.

The pane's life follows this order:

1. The kernel creates the pane node and emits `pane-created` with a `pane-info` record. The record
   holds `node`, `content-kind`, `primitive`, `columns`, `rows`, `focused`, `title` and `is-restored`.
2. The plugin sets the title and the status for its own panes.
3. The kernel renders the body. Widget events arrive as `ui-action` events, and keys arrive as
   `key-pressed` when `wants_keys` is set.
4. After a change, the plugin writes its state and calls `ui::invalidate` so the body is drawn again.

### Events the plugin receives

| Event | Payload | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| `pane-created` | `pane-info` | Never dropped. |
| `pane-resized` | `node`, `columns`, `rows` | Coalesced by node. |
| `pane-title-changed` | `node`, `title`, `source` | Coalesced by node. `source` is `osc`, `manual` or `inferred`. |
| `ui-action` | `view`, `key`, `kind`, `value` | Never dropped. `kind` is `submitted` on Enter in a `text-input`. |
| `key-pressed` | `grab`, `pane`, `chord`, `repeat` | Only when `wants_keys` is `true`. Never dropped. |

The widget `key` is the action id that the plugin matches on, so give every interactive widget a
unique key.

### Example: a notes pane in Rust

The plugin `example.scratchpad` opens a pane kind for notes. The title shows the note count, the
footer shows the save state, and the body lists the notes above a text input. The notes are kept in
the node's metadata as UTF-8 bytes, one note per line, so the pane restores with its notes.

**Grants:** `panes.provide-kind`, `tree.metadata`

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{tree, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::basic;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::ColorRole;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

const PANE_KIND: &str = "example.scratchpad.notes";
const NEW_NOTE_KEY: &str = "new-note";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Scratchpad;

impl Lifecycle for Scratchpad {}

impl Handler for Scratchpad {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::PaneCreated(pane) if pane.content_kind == PANE_KIND => {
                    // Errors are not reported from here; see the edge cases below.
                    let _ = refresh_pane(pane.node, &load_notes(pane.node));
                }
                Event::UiAction(action) if action.key == NEW_NOTE_KEY => {
                    if let ViewTarget::Pane(node) = action.view {
                        if let (ActionKind::Submitted, ActionValue::Text(text)) =
                            (action.kind, action.value)
                        {
                            let _ = add_note(node, &text);
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for Scratchpad {
    fn render(&mut self, view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let notes = match view {
            ViewTarget::Pane(node) => load_notes(node),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        };
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let note_lines = tree.paragraph(notes).key("notes");
        let input = tree.text_input("New note").key(NEW_NOTE_KEY);
        let body = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(3)])
            .child(note_lines)
            .child(input);
        tree.finish(body)
    }
}

fn load_notes(node: NodeId) -> Vec<String> {
    tree::metadata(node)
        .map(|bytes| String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes).lines().map(str::to_owned).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

fn save_notes(node: NodeId, notes: &[String]) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    tree::set_metadata(node, notes.join("\n").into_bytes())
}

fn refresh_pane(node: NodeId, notes: &[String]) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    basic::set_title(node, &format!("Notes ({})", notes.len()))?;
    basic::set_status(node, vec![Span::plain("Saved")])
}

fn add_note(node: NodeId, text: &str) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let note = text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    if note.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let mut notes = load_notes(node);
    notes.push(note);
    basic::set_status(node, vec![Span::plain("Saving")])?;
    if let Err(error) = save_notes(node, &notes) {
        basic::set_status(node, vec![Span::styled("Not saved", Style::role(ColorRole::Danger))])?;
        return Err(error);
    }
    refresh_pane(node, &notes)?;
    ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Pane(node));
    Ok(())
}
```

`ui::invalidate` returns nothing, so it is not wrapped in `?`. The handler discards errors with
`let _ =` only where the state is already shown in the footer.

### Example: the same pane in TypeScript

The TypeScript entry module uses `definePlugin`. It exports the same three objects as the Rust
version: `lifecycle`, `handler` and `views`.

**Grants:** `panes.provide-kind`, `tree.metadata`

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { role, type Area, type Event, type Submission, type ViewTarget }
  from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import * as basic from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/basic';
import * as treeHost from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/tree';
import { invalidate } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { layout, paragraph, span, textInput, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const PANE_KIND = 'example.scratchpad.notes';
const NEW_NOTE_KEY = 'new-note';

function loadNotes(node: bigint): string[] {
  const bytes = treeHost.metadata(node);
  if (bytes === undefined) return [];
  return new TextDecoder().decode(bytes).split('\n').filter((line) => line.length > 0);
}

function saveNotes(node: bigint, notes: string[]): void {
  treeHost.setMetadata(node, new TextEncoder().encode(notes.join('\n')));
}

function refreshPane(node: bigint, notes: string[]): void {
  basic.setTitle(node, `Notes (${notes.length})`);
  basic.setStatus(node, [span('Saved')]);
}

function addNote(node: bigint, rawText: string): void {
  const note = rawText.split(/\s+/).filter((word) => word !== '').join(' ');
  if (note === '') return;
  const notes = [...loadNotes(node), note];
  basic.setStatus(node, [span('Saving')]);
  try {
    saveNotes(node, notes);
  } catch (error) {
    basic.setStatus(node, [span('Not saved', { fg: role('danger') })]);
    return;
  }
  refreshPane(node, notes);
  invalidate({ tag: 'pane', val: node });
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'pane-created' && event.val.contentKind === PANE_KIND) {
        refreshPane(event.val.node, loadNotes(event.val.node));
      }
      if (event.tag === 'ui-action' && event.val.key === NEW_NOTE_KEY
          && event.val.kind === 'submitted' && event.val.view.tag === 'pane'
          && event.val.value.tag === 'text') {
        addNote(event.val.view.val, event.val.value.val);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render(view: ViewTarget, area: Area) {
    const notes = view.tag === 'pane' ? loadNotes(view.val) : [];
    return tree(layout({
      direction: 'vertical',
      constraints: [{ tag: 'fill', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 3 }],
    }, paragraph(notes, { key: 'notes' }), textInput('New note', { key: NEW_NOTE_KEY })));
  },
});
```

The notes are passed through `tree.metadata` as bytes in both versions. A note with a line break
cannot be stored, so both versions join the words of the input with single spaces first.

### What the user sees

- When the pane opens, the title shows the number of stored notes and the footer shows `Saved`.
- The user types into the input and presses Enter. The footer changes to `Saving`, then back to
  `Saved`, and the title count goes up by one.

  colour, and the note is not kept.
- After a restart the pane restores its notes, because `persist` is `metadata`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Code | When it happens on a basic pane | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | The node is not a pane of one of the plugin's kinds, or `panes.provide-kind` or `tree.metadata` is missing. | Stop calling for that node. The host logs `refused basic.set-title: not-permitted` at level warn. |
| `invalid-argument` | A title over 256 characters, or a status over 256 characters or with a line break. | Fix the argument. Nothing is changed. |
| `conflict` | The user has set a manual title on the pane. The title is not changed. | Show the user's title. The plugin title appears again after the user clears the manual title. |
| `quota-exceeded` | The metadata would be over 64 KiB. `set-metadata` writes nothing. | Keep the older notes, show `Not saved`, and ask the user to delete notes. |
| `not-found` | The node was removed during `set-metadata`. | Drop the node from the plugin's state. |
| `revoked`, `internal` | The authorization epoch changed, or the kernel failed. | Retry later or wait for the next event. |

Other rules:

- `pane-not-ready` never applies to basic panes.
- `size` returns `none`, with no error code, for a node that is not one of the plugin's panes.
- `metadata` returns `none` when `tree.metadata` is declined or revoked, so an empty list is shown
  instead of an error.
- A render that returns a layout whose child count differs from its constraint count traps the
  instance. A zero-size area draws nothing and is not an error.
- With `persist: "none"` or `"storage"`, notes kept only in metadata are lost on restart. Pick the
  persist mode that matches where the state lives.

### Pane activity and dirty state

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:primitives/basic in reference-wit
report-activity: func(pane: node-id, activity: agent-activity) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
set-dirty: func(pane: node-id, dirty: bool) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
```

| Rust (`primitives::basic`) | TypeScript | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `report_activity(pane, activity)` | `reportActivity` | Drives the activity icon of the pane's tree row, as an agent pane does. |
| `set_dirty(pane, dirty)` | `setDirty` | Marks the pane as holding unsaved work; closing it asks before discarding. |

Both need `panes.provide-kind` and return `not-permitted` for a node that is not the plugin's kind. A pane that reports `working` shows the spinner in the now slot of its tree row.

**Rust**

```rust
basic::report_activity(pane, AgentActivity::Working)?;
basic::set_dirty(pane, true)?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
reportActivity(pane, 'working');
setDirty(pane, true);
```

<pre class="term">▼ 📂 Ilium
›   📝 <span class="t-hi">⠋</span> Notes (3)
</pre>

- Boards created from Markdown files are native in version 1 and become part of the board plugin in

# Editor primitive

## Editor primitive

The editor primitive gives a client plugin access to the Ilium editor. A plugin can list the open buffers, read lines and selections, draw decorations and gutter marks, create and load buffers, save them, and change their text. It can also export an `annotator` that highlights text in the visible lines of a buffer. Only client-side plugins can use the primitive.

The native editor provides this interface. The editor is a built-in pane kind, and no grant lets a plugin replace it in 0.1.0. A later version may let an editor plugin provide it under the `editor.provide` grant. That provider is post-v1 and high risk, and a package that names `editor.provide` fails with `manifest.grant-unknown`. See [Editor provider](/pages/capability-editor-provide/).

### What you need

| Grant | What it allows |
|---|---|
| `editor.read` | List buffers, read lines and selections, set decorations and gutter marks, receive editor events, and export an `annotator`. |
| `editor.edit` | Create, load, save and close buffers, apply edits, and open files in the editor. It also reads buffers, so most edit plugins hold both grants. |
| `fs.read` | Load a file with `load-file`, or open a path with `editor-open`. The grant applies to the file's scope. |
| `fs.write` | Save a buffer with `save-buffer`. The grant applies to the file's scope. |

The grants take no argument. `editor.read` and `editor.edit` are valid, and `editor.read:project` is invalid. Files are reached through their scope, for example `project`. See [File access](/pages/file-access/).

The SDK for your language exposes the functions under `primitives/editor`. Rust uses `ilium-plugin-sdk` and TypeScript uses `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both need the manifest to list the grants above. The annotator also needs an entry in the manifest `exports` list. See [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/).

### Interface

```wit
record buffer-ref {
    buffer: buffer-id, pane: option<node-id>, path: option<fs-path>,
    language: option<string>, revision: u64, line-count: u32, dirty: bool,
}
record text-position { line: u32, column: u32 }
record text-range { start: text-position, end: text-position }
buffers: func() -> list<buffer-ref>;
buffer-for-pane: func(pane: node-id) -> option<buffer-ref>;
read-lines: func(buffer: buffer-id, first-line: u32, count: u32)
    -> result<list<string>, plugin-error>;
selections: func(buffer: buffer-id) -> list<text-range>;
record range-decoration { range: text-range, style: style, hover: option<string> }
set-decorations: func(buffer: buffer-id, layer: string, items: list<range-decoration>)
    -> result<_, plugin-error>;
record gutter-mark {
    line: u32, icon: string, tooltip: option<string>, command: option<string>,
}
set-gutter: func(buffer: buffer-id, layer: string, marks: list<gutter-mark>)
    -> result<_, plugin-error>;
create-buffer: func(initial: string, language: option<string>)
    -> result<buffer-id, plugin-error>;
load-file: func(path: fs-path) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
take-buffer: func(request: request-id) -> option<buffer-id>;
save-buffer: func(buffer: buffer-id, path: option<fs-path>)
    -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
close-buffer: func(buffer: buffer-id);
record line-annotation {
    line: u32, first-column: u32, last-column: u32, style: style,
}
annotate: func(buffer: buffer-id, revision: u64, first-line: u32, lines: list<string>)
    -> list<line-annotation>;
```

Lines count from zero, and columns count Unicode scalar values, not bytes. A `text-range` is half open: its end is not part of the range. The `style` record is the shared one from the text model, and its colour roles are listed in [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/).

### Functions

| Function | Rust (`primitives::editor`) | TypeScript (`primitives/editor`) | Grant | Sync or async | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `buffers` | `buffers()` | `buffers()` | `editor.read` | sync | Lists the open buffers with their revisions and line counts. |
| `buffer-for-pane` | `buffer_for_pane(pane)` | `bufferForPane(pane)` | `editor.read` | sync | Returns the buffer shown in one pane, or none. |
| `read-lines` | `read_lines(buffer, first_line, count)` | `readLines(buffer, firstLine, count)` | `editor.read` | sync | Returns up to `count` lines from `first_line`. |
| `selections` | `selections(buffer)` | `selections(buffer)` | `editor.read` | sync | Returns the selections as text ranges. |
| `set-decorations` | `set_decorations(buffer, layer, &[..])` | `setDecorations(buffer, layer, [..])` | `editor.read` | sync | Replaces every decoration of one layer on a buffer. |
| `set-gutter` | `set_gutter(buffer, layer, &[..])` | `setGutter(buffer, layer, [..])` | `editor.read` | sync | Replaces every gutter mark of one layer on a buffer. |
| `create-buffer` | `create_buffer(initial, language)` | `createBuffer(initial, language?)` | `editor.edit` | sync | Creates a buffer with initial text and returns its id. |
| `load-file` | `load_file(path).await` | `loadFile(path)` | `editor.edit`, `fs.read` | async | Loads a file. The completion carries the buffer id. |
| `take-buffer` | `take_buffer(request)` | `takeBuffer(request)` | none | sync | Reads the buffer id of a finished `load-file`. |
| `save-buffer` | `save_buffer(buffer, path).await` | `saveBuffer(buffer, path?)` | `editor.edit`, `fs.write` | async | Writes a buffer to its path, or to a new path. |
| `close-buffer` | `close_buffer(buffer)` | `closeBuffer(buffer)` | `editor.edit` | sync | Closes a buffer and frees its slot in the quota. |

Sync functions return `Result<T, PluginError>` in Rust. In TypeScript they return the value or throw a `PluginError`. The async functions return a request in the raw form, and the wrappers take the buffer at once.

Decorations and gutter marks belong to the plugin. Each layer is named by the plugin, and a call on one layer never touches another layer or another plugin's marks. The host clears every layer of a plugin when the plugin stops.

### Events and intents

| Item | Payload | Grant | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor-opened`, `editor-closed` | `buffer-ref` | `editor.read` | Never dropped. |
| `editor-changed` | `buffer`, `revision`, `first-line`, `last-line` | `editor.read` | Coalesced per buffer, debounced 100 ms. |
| `editor-saved` | `buffer`, `path` | `editor.read` | Never dropped. |
| `editor-apply-edits` intent | `buffer`, `base-revision`, `edits` (`range`, `replacement`) | `editor.edit` | Outcome `ok`, or `refused(conflict)` when the revision is stale. |
| `editor-open` intent | `path`, `line`, `placement` (`new-pane`, `split`, `replace`) | `editor.edit`, `fs.read` | Outcome `ok-node`, the pane that opened. |

An edit names the revision that the plugin read. The kernel applies all edits of one submission as one change, and the revision rises by one. Edits in one submission must not overlap. Read the buffer again after a `conflict`, decide whether the change is still needed, and submit again. See [Editor edit](/pages/capability-editor-edit/) for the full rules.

### Annotator export

The annotator is an optional export of the client side. It has one method, `annotate`, which the kernel calls for the visible lines of a buffer. It runs at most once every 100 ms per buffer, and a late result for an old revision is dropped. It needs `editor.read`. A call that breaches its time budget is dropped, and three breaches in a row trap the plugin. See [Plugin exports](/pages/api-exports/).

### Worked example in Rust

This client plugin highlights every `TODO` word in the visible lines through its annotator. It also puts a gutter mark on each line that contains `TODO`. The mark runs `example.todo/open` when clicked. The plugin needs the grant `editor.read` and the manifest entries `exports = ["annotator"]` and a command with the id `example.todo/open`.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor::{self, GutterMark, LineAnnotation};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ids::BufferId;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::ColorRole;

const TODO_LAYER: &str = "todo-marks";
const OPEN_COMMAND: &str = "example.todo/open";
const MAX_LINES: u32 = 10_000;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["annotator"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct TodoMarks;

impl Lifecycle for TodoMarks {}

impl Handler for TodoMarks {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::EditorChanged(change) = event else { continue };
            let Some(buffer) = editor::buffers()
                .into_iter()
                .find(|candidate| candidate.buffer == change.buffer)
            else {
                continue;
            };
            // set-gutter replaces the whole layer, so every mark of the buffer is sent.
            let count = buffer.line_count.min(MAX_LINES);
            let Ok(lines) = editor::read_lines(change.buffer, 0, count) else { continue };
            let marks = todo_marks(&lines);
            let _ = editor::set_gutter(change.buffer, TODO_LAYER, &marks);
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn todo_marks(lines: &[String]) -> Vec<GutterMark> {
    lines
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, text)| text.contains("TODO"))
        .map(|(index, _)| GutterMark {
            line: index as u32,
            icon: "list-check".into(),
            tooltip: Some("Open the TODO issue".into()),
            command: Some(OPEN_COMMAND.into()),
        })
        .collect()
}

impl Annotator for TodoMarks {
    fn annotate(
        &mut self,
        _buffer: BufferId,
        _revision: u64,
        first_line: u32,
        lines: Vec<String>,
    ) -> Vec<LineAnnotation> {
        lines
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(index, text)| {
                let byte_index = text.find("TODO")?;
                let column = text[..byte_index].chars().count() as u32;
                Some(LineAnnotation {
                    line: first_line + index as u32,
                    first_column: column,
                    last_column: column + "TODO".chars().count() as u32,
                    style: Style::role(ColorRole::Accent),
                })
            })
            .collect()
    }
}
```

### Worked example in TypeScript

This client plugin handles a command that summarises the selections of the buffer where it ran. It writes the summary into a new buffer and highlights the selected ranges in the source buffer. The plugin needs `editor.read` and `editor.edit`, and the command `example.selections/summarise` in its manifest.

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import {
  createBuffer, readLines, selections, setDecorations, type RangeDecoration,
} from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor';
import { role, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const SUMMARY_COMMAND = 'example.selections/summarise';
const SELECTION_LAYER = 'selection-summary';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== SUMMARY_COMMAND) continue;
      const buffer = event.val.context.buffer;
      if (buffer !== undefined) summarise(buffer);
    }
    return [];
  },
});

function summarise(buffer: bigint): void {
  const ranges = selections(buffer);
  if (ranges.length === 0) return;
  try {
    const summaryLines = ranges.map((range) => {
      const [text = ''] = readLines(buffer, range.start.line, 1);
      return `line ${range.start.line + 1}: ${text.trim()}`;
    });
    createBuffer(`${summaryLines.join('\n')}\n`);
    const decorations: RangeDecoration[] = ranges.map((range) => ({
      range,
      style: { fg: role('accent') },
      hover: 'Included in the selection summary',
    }));
    setDecorations(buffer, SELECTION_LAYER, decorations);
  } catch (error) {
    // not-found means the buffer closed during the call. Other errors are not handled here.
    if (!(error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'not-found')) throw error;
  }
}
```

### Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A sync call without its grant | `not-permitted` at once. |
| `buffers()`, `buffer-for-pane()` or `selections()` with `editor.read` declined or revoked | An empty list or none, and one refusal line in the plugin log. These calls have no result. |
| `read-lines`, `set-decorations` or `set-gutter` with the grant declined or revoked | `not-permitted`. |
| `read-lines` with a first line past the end of the buffer | `invalid-argument`. |
| `read-lines` with a count past the last line | The lines that exist, with no error. |
| `read-lines` with a count over 10,000 | `invalid-argument`. |
| `set-decorations` or `set-gutter` with over 10,000 items in one layer | `invalid-argument`. |
| A buffer id that does not exist or has closed | `not-found`. |
| `create-buffer` with more than 16 MiB of text | `invalid-argument`. |
| The 65th buffer held by one plugin | `quota-exceeded`. Closing a buffer frees its slot. |
| `load-file` with a binary file or a file over 16 MiB | `failed(invalid-argument)` in the completion. |
| `load-file` with a missing file | `failed(not-found)` in the completion. |
| `save-buffer` with `path: none` on a buffer without a path | `invalid-argument` at once. |
| `save-buffer` when the file changed on disk after loading | `failed(conflict)` in the completion. |
| `editor-apply-edits` with a stale base revision | `refused(conflict)`. No edit is applied. |
| `editor-apply-edits` with overlapping or out-of-range edits | `refused(invalid-argument)`. |

A `load-file` completes once the buffer is open. If the plugin does not call `take-buffer` within 30 seconds, the buffer stays open and the plugin finds it again with `buffers()`. Buffers stay open when a plugin stops, is disabled or is restarted. The editor keeps their text.

### Limits

| Limit | Value | Error |
|---|---|---|
| Lines per `read-lines` call | 10,000 | `invalid-argument` |
| Decorations or gutter marks per layer | 10,000 | `invalid-argument` |
| Buffers created or held per plugin | 64 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Text in `create-buffer` | 16 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Edits in one `editor-apply-edits` | 10,000 | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| Annotator calls per buffer | once per 100 ms | Extra calls are not made. |

# Terminal primitive

## Terminal primitive

A terminal pane shows the output of a program in a pseudo-terminal, usually a shell or an agent CLI. The terminal primitive lets a server-side plugin read the screen and selection, watch output for text, draw highlights, claim the mouse for one pane, and type input. The kernel parses every output byte. The plugin receives only matches of its output filters, and it reads the screen only when it asks.

### What you need

Declare the grants you use in `capabilities.server` of the manifest. Each grant unlocks a group of calls:

| Grant | Unlocks |
|---|---|
| `terminal.read-screen` | `read_screen`, `selection` |
| `terminal.output-filter` | `add_output_filter`, `remove_output_filter`, `output-matched` events, and manifest `output_filters` |
| `terminal.pointer` | `claim_pointer`, `release_pointer`, `set_highlights`, `clear_highlights`, `pointer` events while a claim is held |
| `terminal.write` | the `send-input` intent and `prompt_epoch` |

The primitive is available to the server side only, through the `ilium:server/base` world. Import it from `ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal` in Rust, or from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal` in TypeScript. Agent identification is a separate contract, described in [primitives-agent](/pages/primitives-agent/).

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["terminal.read-screen", "terminal.output-filter", "terminal.pointer",
               "notify.desktop"]
  },
  "output_filters": [{
    "id": "rate-limit", "regex": "rate limit exceeded", "panes": "agents", "rate_per_second": 1
  }],
  "link_detectors": [{ "id": "issue-ref", "regex": "#[0-9]+", "command": "example.issues/open" }],
  "context_menu": [{
    "id": "copy-block", "title": "Copy block", "command": "example.copy/block", "target": "terminal"
  }]
}
```

### Functions

Every function is synchronous. The Rust name is shown first, then the TypeScript name.

| Function | Grant | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `read_screen(pane, part, max_rows)` / `readScreen` | `terminal.read-screen` | `Option<Screen>`, `none` for an unknown pane |
| `selection(pane)` / `selection` | `terminal.read-screen` | `Option<Selection>` |
| `add_output_filter(pane, filter)` / `addOutputFilter` | `terminal.output-filter` | `Result<(), PluginError>` |
| `remove_output_filter(pane, filter_id)` / `removeOutputFilter` | `terminal.output-filter` | nothing |
| `claim_pointer(pane)` / `claimPointer` | `terminal.pointer` | `Result<(), PluginError>` |
| `release_pointer(pane)` / `releasePointer` | `terminal.pointer` | nothing |
| `set_highlights(pane, layer, regions)` / `setHighlights` | `terminal.pointer` | `Result<(), PluginError>` |
| `clear_highlights(pane, layer)` / `clearHighlights` | `terminal.pointer` | nothing |
| `prompt_epoch(pane)` / `promptEpoch` | `terminal.write` | `Option<u64>` |

In TypeScript, a `result` that fails throws a `PluginError`. The functions that return nothing never fail.

### Types

| Type | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Screen` | `columns`, `rows`, `cursor_row`, `cursor_column`, `title`, `revision` | Text of one part of the pane, with the cursor. |
| `ScreenPart` | `Visible`, `Scrollback` | Which part `read_screen` returns. |
| `Selection` | `first_row`, `first_column`, `last_row`, `last_column`, `text` | The current mouse selection. |
| `OutputFilter` | `id`, `regex`, `rate_per_second` (`u16`) | A runtime rule for one pane. |
| `CellRegion` | `first_row`, `first_column`, `last_row`, `last_column`, `style`, `label` | One highlighted rectangle of cells. |
| `OutputMatchedEvent` | `node`, `filter_id`, `line`, `row` (`u32`) | A completed line matched a filter. |
| `LinkActivatedEvent` | `node`, `detector_id`, `text` | The user activated a link match. |
| `PointerEvent` | `node`, `row`, `column`, `kind`, `button` | Mouse input while a claim is held. |

`kind` is `down`, `up`, `drag` or `wheel`. `button` is `left`, `middle`, `right`, or `none` for a wheel event. `row` and `column` count from the top visible row and the left column of the pane. The scrollback offset is not applied.

### Reading the screen

`read_screen` with `Visible` returns the bottom `max_rows` rows of the visible area, top to bottom. `cursor_row` counts from the first returned row. A cursor above the returned rows gives the number of returned rows and column 0. With `Scrollback`, it returns the rows directly above the visible area, oldest first. Each row holds the characters of its cells, with escape sequences and trailing blanks removed. A wide character appears once.

`max_rows` of 0 returns an empty list. A value above 10,000 is clamped to 10,000 without an error. `revision` is per pane. It starts at 0 when the host starts the pane, rises when either part changes, and is not saved in the snapshot. Compare it with the last revision you saw to skip unchanged work.

`selection` counts coordinates from the top of the visible area. Its text covers only the visible part, with lines joined by a newline. A selection that lies wholly in the scrollback returns `none`.

### Output filters

A filter is a regular expression in the dialect of the Rust `regex` crate. It has no look-around and no back-references. Each completed line is matched after escape sequences are removed. A pattern is at most 1 KiB, and the compiled program at most 1 MiB. `rate_per_second` is 1 to 100.

Manifest entries need `panes`: `all` (every terminal pane), `agents` (panes whose agent is identified) or `terminals` (terminal panes with no identified agent). A missing or unknown value makes the package fail to install. A runtime filter applies to the one pane named in the call, and an existing id on that pane is replaced. The host removes runtime filters when the plugin deactivates or the pane closes, without an event.

The `row` of a match is the zero-based number of the line since the pane started printing. It does not change when the pane scrolls. A match above the rate is dropped and counted in `events-dropped`, with the filter id as `source`.

### Highlights and the pointer claim

A highlight layer has a name of 1 to 32 characters from `[a-z0-9-]`. Layer names are scoped to the calling plugin, so two plugins can both use `search`. Regions of one layer are painted in list order. Where two regions overlap, the later region sets the foreground and background, and the modifiers of all overlapping regions are combined. A region outside the screen is clipped without an error. A region whose first position is after its last is `invalid-argument`.

A `label` is not drawn in the pane. It appears as a tooltip after the pointer rests on the region for 500 ms. A label over 128 characters is `invalid-argument`. Highlights survive `release_pointer`. They are withdrawn when the plugin is disabled, its grant is revoked, or the pane is removed.

A claim gives the plugin the pointer of one pane. While it holds the claim, the host stops forwarding mouse events to the program in the pane, and its own selection and wheel scrollback are off there. Wheel events reach the plugin as `pointer` events with kind `wheel`. Typing is not affected, because typing needs `terminal.write`, not a claim. The plugin that already holds a claim can call `claim_pointer` again and gets `ok`. `release_pointer` without a claim does nothing.

### Input: the send-input intent

Input is an intent, not a function. The plugin submits `send-input` with these fields:

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `pane` | A terminal pane. |
| `text` | At most 64 KiB. |
| `delivery` | `typed` writes keystrokes. `submitted` writes the text, then the submit keys of the pane's signature (`"\r"` by default). `pasted` uses bracketed paste when the program enabled it (DEC mode 2004), and otherwise works like `typed`. |
| `prompt_epoch` | Optional. Refuses with `conflict` when the pane's epoch has moved on. |
| `dedup_key` | Mandatory, from 1 to 128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`. The key is reserved for 10 minutes once the submission is accepted. |

The rate is 20 submissions per second per pane per plugin. The checks run in this order: shape and key, grant, duplicate key, pane exists and is a terminal, pane restored, rate, prompt epoch, then the write. A refusal does not reserve the key, so a retry with the same key is valid after the cause is fixed.

The pane's `prompt_epoch` is a counter that the kernel raises each time it records a submitted prompt. Read it when the agent is idle, and submit with it. If the agent has moved to a newer prompt in the meantime, the input is refused, and nothing is typed into the wrong prompt.

### Reads, pointer and input

The terminal primitive has three further areas. Each has a page of its own.

| Need | Calls and events | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Styled cells, snapshot, history, modes, foreground process | `read-cells`, `freeze-snapshot`, `history-text`, `search-history`, `modes`, `foreground-process`, `screen-changed`, `user-line-submitted` | [Terminal reads](/pages/primitives-terminal-reads/) |
| Sub-cell pointer, move, modifier gestures | `claim-pointer-gesture`, extended `pointer` event | [Terminal pointer](/pages/primitives-terminal-pointer/) |
| Staged, raw, mouse and conditional input, lock, journal | extended `send-input`, `lock-input`, `unlock-input` | [Terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/) |

The grants `terminal.read-cells`, `terminal.history`, `terminal.raw-input` and `terminal.input-lock` are listed in [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/). The `pointer` event gains `sub-x`, `sub-y`, `modifiers` and the kind `move`; the `wheel` kind is split into `wheel-up`, `wheel-down`, `wheel-left` and `wheel-right` in `view-pointer`. The new fields are optional.

### Manifest contributions

| Key | Shape | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `output_filters` | `{ id, regex, panes, rate_per_second }` | 32 per plugin, 128 for bundled plugins |
| `link_detectors` | `{ id, regex, command }` | with the same regex limits |
| `context_menu` | `{ id, title, command, target }` | `target` is `terminal` for this primitive |

A link detector sends `link-activated` to its plugin when the user activates a match. The command named in `command` runs with the detector id and the matched text as its arguments. Output filters and link detectors are installed by the kernel and run natively on the output.

### Examples

#### Example 1: a rate-limit filter with a notice and a highlight

The manifest above installs the `rate-limit` filter on agent panes, at most once per second. When it matches, the plugin highlights the row in a `warning` layer and sends a desktop notice.

**Grants:** `terminal.output-filter`, `terminal.pointer`, `terminal.read-screen`, `notify.desktop`

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, CellRegion};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::OutputMatchedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{NotifySpec, Urgency};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct RateLimitWatch;

impl Handler for RateLimitWatch {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::OutputMatched(OutputMatchedEvent { node, filter_id, line, row }) = event
            else { continue };
            if filter_id != "rate-limit" { continue; }
            let region = CellRegion {
                first_row: row, first_column: 0, last_row: row, last_column: 79,
                style: Style::role(ColorRole::Warning), label: Some("rate limit".into()),
            };
            // A failed highlight, such as a pane that just closed, must not block the notice.
            let _ = terminal::set_highlights(node, "warning", vec![region]);
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::Notify(NotifySpec {
                title: "Rate limit".into(),
                body: line.chars().take(2048).collect(),
                urgency: Urgency::High,
                sound: None,
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { role } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { setHighlights } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';

let nextCorrelation = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'output-matched' || event.val.filterId !== 'rate-limit') {
        continue;
      }
      const { node, line, row } = event.val;
      try {
        setHighlights(node, 'warning', [{
          firstRow: row, firstColumn: 0, lastRow: row, lastColumn: 79,
          style: { fg: role('warning'), bg: undefined, add: undefined, remove: undefined },
          label: 'rate limit',
        }]);
      } catch {
        // A failed highlight must not block the notice.
      }
      submissions.push({
        intent: { tag: 'notify', val: {
          title: 'Rate limit', body: Array.from(line).slice(0, 2048).join(''),
          urgency: 'high', sound: undefined,
        } },
        correlation: nextCorrelation++,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

Outcome: the matched row shows the `warning` role with the tooltip `rate limit`, and a desktop notice appears. The filter fires at most once per second, because of `rate_per_second: 1`.

#### Example 2: continue an agent only if its prompt has not changed

An agent stops at a prompt and waits. The plugin reads the prompt epoch when it sees the agent go idle, and sends `continue` only if the epoch is still the same when it acts. The Rust form follows.

**Grants:** `terminal.write`

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Delivery, SendInputSpec};

/// Returns the submission only while the prompt is still the one seen at idle time.
fn continue_if_unchanged(pane: NodeId, epoch_at_idle: u64) -> Option<Submission> {
    if terminal::prompt_epoch(pane)? != epoch_at_idle {
        return None;
    }
    let spec = SendInputSpec {
        pane,
        text: "continue".into(),
        delivery: Delivery::Submitted,
        prompt_epoch: Some(epoch_at_idle),
    };
    let dedup_key = format!("continue:{pane}:{epoch_at_idle}");
    Some(Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(spec), dedup_key))
}
```

Store `epoch_at_idle` when the agent becomes idle, and return the submission from `on_events`. A `refused(conflict)` outcome means the agent moved on. In TypeScript the fields are `promptEpoch` and `dedupKey`.

### Edge cases and errors

| Call | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| any function with a pane | `not-permitted` | The grant is missing or was declined. |
| any function with a pane | `not-found` | The pane does not exist or has closed. |
| `read_screen`, `selection`, `prompt_epoch` | none | Unknown pane, declined or revoked grant. A refusal line goes to the plugin log. |
| `add_output_filter` | `invalid-argument` | Empty id, invalid regex, pattern over 1 KiB, compiled program over 1 MiB, rate 0 or above 100. |
| `add_output_filter` | `quota-exceeded` | The plugin has its limit of filters, or the session has 512 runtime filters. |
| `claim_pointer` | `conflict` | Another plugin holds the claim. |
| `claim_pointer`, `set_highlights` | `unsupported` | The node exists but is not a terminal pane. |
| `set_highlights` | `invalid-argument` | Layer name not `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, over 4,096 regions, a region with first after last, or a label over 128 characters. |
| `set_highlights` | `quota-exceeded` | The plugin already has 16 layers on this pane. |
| `send-input` | `refused(pane-not-ready)` | The pane is restored but its process has not started. Retry after `pane-created` or `tree-changed` for the pane. Check the pane's `is-restored` flag before each write. |
| `send-input` | `refused(conflict)` | The prompt epoch is stale. Do not retry with the same epoch. |
| `send-input` | `refused(rate-limited)` | More than 20 per second. Retry after `retry-after-ms`. |
| `send-input` | `duplicate(original)` | The dedup key was reserved in the last 10 minutes. The input was not sent twice. |

### What the user sees

- The matched row takes the theme's warning colour. The label appears as a tooltip after the pointer rests on the row for 500 ms.
- A desktop notice appears. When an attached client shows the pane and reports focus, the notice appears in the client footer instead (see [notify](/pages/capability-notify-desktop/)).
- While a claim is held, clicks no longer select text in that pane, and the wheel goes to the plugin. Typing still reaches the program.
- A highlight stays after `release_pointer`, and disappears when the plugin is disabled, loses the grant, or the pane closes.

### Used by

- Screen transfer between panes: `read_screen`, then `send-input` with delivery `pasted`.
- Pane titles: `pane-title-changed`, raised from terminal title sequences.
- Clickable links: `link_detectors` and `link-activated`.
- Text selection and the right-click menu: `selection` and a `context_menu` item.
- Smart Copy: `read_screen` and `set_highlights`.
- Text triggers: `add_output_filter` and `output-matched`.

Requirement ids for this page: [PRI-001]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

# Terminal reads

## Terminal reads

The base terminal primitive returns plain text rows. This page covers the reads a plugin needs to reimplement Smart Copy, link detection, screen scraping and history search: styled cells, a frozen snapshot, the terminal modes, the foreground process, scrollback text and a regex search over it, plus two events, `screen-changed` and `user-line-submitted`. The kernel keeps the vt100 emulation and the scrollback store. The plugin never sees a byte stream; it asks for rows when it needs them.

This page extends [Terminal primitive](/pages/primitives-terminal/). Writing to the terminal is in [Terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/), and the mouse is in [Terminal pointer](/pages/primitives-terminal-pointer/).

### You will need

| Grant | Risk | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.read-cells` | normal | `read-cells`, `modes`, `foreground-process`, `freeze-snapshot`, `read-snapshot-cells`, `drop-snapshot`, the `screen-changed` event |
| `terminal.history` | high | `history-text`, `take-history`, `search-history`, `take-matches` |
| `agent.read-prompts` | high | the `user-line-submitted` event, for every terminal pane |

The grants are listed in [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/). `terminal.read-screen` stays the grant for the older text-only `read-screen`; see [terminal.read-screen](/pages/capability-terminal-read-screen/). A high-risk grant needs the user's explicit approval at install, and a bundled first-party plugin gets it through its tier. Both sides can import the interface: the server side reads the authoritative screen, and the client side reads the client's mirror.

### Signatures

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:primitives/terminal in reference-wit
interface terminal {
  // terminal.read-cells
  record cell { text: string, fg: option<color>, bg: option<color>, add: modifiers, wide: bool }
  record cell-rows { first-row: u32, columns: u16, rows: list<list<cell>>, revision: u64 }
  read-cells: func(pane: node-id, part: screen-part, first-row: u32, count: u32) -> option<cell-rows>;

  flags terminal-mode { alternate-screen, mouse-reporting, bracketed-paste,
                        application-cursor, focus-reporting, synchronized-output }
  modes: func(pane: node-id) -> option<terminal-mode>;

  record foreground-process { name: string, command-line: list<string>, cwd: option<string> }
  foreground-process: func(pane: node-id) -> option<foreground-process>;

  freeze-snapshot: func(pane: node-id) -> result<u64, plugin-error>;
  read-snapshot-cells: func(snapshot: u64, first-row: u32, count: u32) -> option<cell-rows>;
  drop-snapshot: func(snapshot: u64);

  // terminal.history
  history-text: func(pane: node-id, max-bytes: u32) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
  take-history: func(request: request-id) -> option<string>;
  record history-match { row: u32, column: u16, length: u16 }
  search-history: func(pane: node-id, regex: string, max-matches: u16) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
  take-matches: func(request: request-id) -> option<list<history-match>>;
}
```

| Rust (`primitives::terminal`) | TypeScript (`primitives/terminal`) | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `read_cells(pane, part, first_row, count)` | `readCells` | `Option<CellRows>` |
| `modes(pane)` | `modes` | `Option<TerminalMode>`; a flag set in Rust, a string array in TypeScript |
| `foreground_process(pane)` | `foregroundProcess` | `Option<ForegroundProcess>` |
| `freeze_snapshot(pane)` | `freezeSnapshot` | `Result<u64, PluginError>` (throws) |
| `read_snapshot_cells(snapshot, first_row, count)` | `readSnapshotCells` | `Option<CellRows>` |
| `drop_snapshot(snapshot)` | `dropSnapshot` | nothing |
| `history_text(pane, max_bytes)` | `historyText` | `Result<RequestId, PluginError>`; the text arrives through `take_history` |
| `search_history(pane, regex, max_matches)` | `searchHistory` | `Result<RequestId, PluginError>`; the matches arrive through `take_matches` |

The two history functions are requests: they return a request id at once, the host works off the main path, and `request-completed` tells the plugin to call `take-history` or `take-matches`. See [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

### Cells

A `cell` holds the grapheme cluster at that position in `text`, the resolved foreground and background colours (`none` means the terminal default), the modifier flags `add` (bold, dim, italic, underline, reverse, strike) and `wide`. A wide character occupies two columns: the first cell has `wide: true` and the text, and the second cell has an empty `text`. Row `first-row` counts from the top of the part you asked for. For `visible` it is the top visible row; for `scrollback` it is the oldest retained row.

`columns` is the width of every row at the time of the read. A row that is shorter than the pane is padded with default cells, so `rows[i].len() == columns` always holds. `revision` is the screen revision of the pane, the same counter that `read-screen` returns. A read never blocks the PTY reader: the host copies the requested rows under a short lock.

<svg viewBox="0 0 420 170" role="img" aria-label="read-cells returns styled cells from the vt100 grid">
  <rect x="10" y="20" width="120" height="120" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="70" y="42" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">kernel</text>
