  <text x="70" y="104" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">scrollback store</text>
  <rect x="290" y="20" width="120" height="120" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="350" y="42" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">plugin</text>
  <text x="350" y="64" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">read-cells</text>
  <text x="350" y="84" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">freeze-snapshot</text>
  <text x="350" y="104" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">search-history</text>
  <path d="M290 60 H135" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" marker-end="url(#a)"/>
  <path d="M135 100 H285" stroke="currentColor" fill="none"/>
  <text x="212" y="54" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ask for rows</text>
  <text x="212" y="116" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">copy of cells</text>
  <text x="210" y="160" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">screen-changed: at most 10 per second per pane</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The plugin pulls rows; the kernel pushes only the coalesced screen-changed event.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Modes and the foreground process

`modes` returns the flags the running program set. `alternate-screen` is on for full-screen programs such as an editor or a pager, `mouse-reporting` for programs that asked for mouse input, `bracketed-paste` for DEC mode 2004, `application-cursor` for DECCKM, `focus-reporting` for focus events and `synchronized-output` for DEC mode 2026. A plugin that scrapes text should check `alternate-screen` first, because the scrollback holds nothing of a full-screen program.

`foreground-process` reports the process group that currently owns the terminal: its name, its command line and its working directory. The `cwd` is a display string and grants no file access. It is `none` for a pane that was restored and has not started yet.

### Frozen snapshots

`freeze-snapshot` copies the visible screen and the scrollback into a stable object and returns its id. Reads through `read-snapshot-cells` see exactly that copy while the program keeps printing. This is what Smart Copy needs: the user selects, the plugin freezes, analyses at leisure, and writes the result to the clipboard. A snapshot is held by the host until `drop-snapshot`, until the plugin stops, or until the pane is removed. A plugin holds at most 4 snapshots per pane; the fifth call returns `quota-exceeded`. The copy shares storage with the live grid until a row changes, so a snapshot of an idle pane costs almost nothing.

### History text and search

`history-text` returns the scrollback and the visible screen as one string, newest text kept when the pane holds more than `max-bytes`. The limit is 4 MiB per call. Lines are joined with a newline and trailing blanks are removed. `search-history` runs a regular expression of the Rust `regex` dialect over the same text and returns at most `max-matches` positions, each as row, column and length in cells, counted from the oldest retained row. Both are high risk because scrollback can hold secrets the user typed or pasted long ago. The host removes the regions that a program marked as a hidden password prompt.

### Events

| Event | Payload | Grant | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| `screen-changed` | `pane`, `first-row`, `last-row`, `revision` | `terminal.read-cells` | coalesced per pane, at most 10 per second |
| `user-line-submitted` | `pane`, `text`, `at` (`epoch-ms`) | `agent.read-prompts` | never dropped |

`screen-changed` tells the plugin which rows changed between its last event and this one. Rows scrolled out of the visible part do not widen the range; the range is in visible coordinates and the revision tells the plugin it missed a scroll. `user-line-submitted` fires when the user presses Enter on a line in any terminal pane, not only agent panes. The text is the line as the program received it, with the prompt removed when the kernel can tell where the prompt ends.

### Rust and TypeScript

This example scans the visible screen after each change and underlines every URL, then keeps a frozen copy for later.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, ScreenPart};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct UrlScan { last_revision: u64 }

impl Handler for UrlScan {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::ScreenChanged(changed) = event else { continue };
            if changed.revision == self.last_revision { continue; }
            self.last_revision = changed.revision;
            let flags = terminal::modes(changed.pane).unwrap_or_default();
            if flags.contains(TerminalMode::ALTERNATE_SCREEN) { continue; }
            let count = changed.last_row - changed.first_row + 1;
            let Some(rows) = terminal::read_cells(
                changed.pane, ScreenPart::Visible, changed.first_row, count) else { continue };
            for (offset, row) in rows.rows.iter().enumerate() {
                let line: String = row.iter().map(|cell| cell.text.as_str()).collect();
                if line.contains("https://") {
                    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("url on row {}", rows.first_row + offset as u32));
                }
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { readCells, modes } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

let lastRevision = 0n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'screen-changed') continue;
      const { pane, firstRow, lastRow, revision } = event.val;
      if (revision === lastRevision) continue;
      lastRevision = revision;
      if (modes(pane)?.includes('alternate-screen')) continue;
      const rows = readCells(pane, 'visible', firstRow, lastRow - firstRow + 1);
      if (!rows) continue;
      rows.rows.forEach((row, offset) => {
        const line = row.map((cell) => cell.text).join('');
        if (line.includes('https://')) log('info', `url on row ${rows.firstRow + offset}`);
      });
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The history search follows the request pattern. Submit it, return, and read the result when the completion arrives.

**Rust**

```rust
let request = terminal::search_history(pane, r"error\[E\d{4}\]", 200)?;
self.pending.insert(request, pane);
// later, in on_events, for Event::RequestCompleted with a matching id:
if let Some(matches) = terminal::take_matches(request) {
    for found in matches { /* found.row, found.column, found.length */ }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const request = searchHistory(pane, 'error\\[E\\d{4}\\]', 200);
pending.set(request, pane);
// later, in onEvents, for a request-completed event with a matching id:
const found = takeMatches(request);
for (const match of found ?? []) { /* match.row, match.column, match.length */ }
```

### Outcomes, errors and limits

| Call | Error | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `read-cells`, `freeze-snapshot` | `pane-not-ready` | the pane has no process yet |
| `read-cells`, `freeze-snapshot` | `not-found` | no such pane or snapshot |
| `read-cells` | `quota-exceeded` | `count` above 1,000 rows |
| `freeze-snapshot` | `quota-exceeded` | more than 4 live snapshots on this pane |
| `search-history` | `invalid-argument` | the regex does not compile in the `regex` dialect, or is over 1 KiB |
| `history-text`, `search-history` | completion `timed-out` | the host gave up after its deadline |
| any call | `not-permitted` | the grant is missing or revoked |

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Rows per `read-cells` | 1,000 |
| `history-text` | 4 MiB, newest kept |
| Matches per search | the `max-matches` you pass, at most 10,000 |
| Live snapshots per pane and plugin | 4 |
| `screen-changed` | 10 per second per pane |

### What the user sees

Nothing changes in the pane while a plugin reads it. A plugin that uses the reads typically draws with highlights or the status bar. This render shows a terminal pane after a build, with a plugin highlight on the error row (the row is drawn in the warning colour of the theme).

<pre class="term">╭──≡ ● · Shell────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮

│   Compiling demo v0.1.0                                             │
│<span class="t-err">error[E0308]: mismatched types</span>                                       │
│ <span class="t-dim">--&gt;</span> src/main.rs:12:5                                                │
│<span class="t-prompt">$</span>                                                                    │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

# Terminal pointer

## Terminal pointer

A plugin can take the mouse of one terminal pane to implement selection helpers, link clicks, drag-and-drop of files onto a prompt, or a modifier gesture such as Ctrl+click to open. The pointer has a common model for terminal panes, plugin views and editors: whole-cell coordinates plus a position inside the cell, modifier keys, the click count and a `move` kind for hover. The kernel keeps the mouse protocol encodings (X10, SGR, UTF-8) and the auto-scroll at the edges.

### You will need

| Grant | Unlocks |
|---|---|
| `terminal.pointer` | `claim-pointer`, `claim-pointer-gesture`, `release-pointer`, highlights, the `pointer` event of a claimed pane |

See [terminal.pointer](/pages/capability-terminal-pointer/). The calls are synchronous. The base claim and highlight rules are in [Terminal primitive](/pages/primitives-terminal/).

### Signatures

```wit
claim-pointer: func(pane: node-id) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
claim-pointer-gesture: func(pane: node-id, modifiers: pointer-modifiers) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
release-pointer: func(pane: node-id);

enum pointer-kind { down, up, move, drag, wheel-up, wheel-down, wheel-left, wheel-right }
enum pointer-button { none, left, middle, right }
flags pointer-modifiers { shift, control, alt }
record view-pointer {
  kind: pointer-kind, button: pointer-button, modifiers: pointer-modifiers,
  column: u16, row: u16,    // cell inside the area, 0-based
  sub-x: u8, sub-y: u8,     // 0..255 inside the cell; 128 when the terminal reports cells only
  clicks: u8,               // 1, 2 or 3 for down events; 0 otherwise
}
```

The terminal `pointer` event carries the same fields: `node`, `row`, `column`, `kind`, `button`, plus the shape fields `sub-x`, `sub-y` and `modifiers`.

| Rust (`primitives::terminal`) | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_pointer(pane)` | `claimPointer` | Take every mouse event of the pane. |
| `claim_pointer_gesture(pane, modifiers)` | `claimPointerGesture` | Take the mouse only while those modifiers are held. |
| `release_pointer(pane)` | `releasePointer` | Give it back. |

### The pointer model

A pointer event has a kind and a button. `down` and `up` mark a press and a release. `drag` repeats while a button is held and the pointer moves. `move` is new and reports a pointer with no button held; it is sent only while a claim is held and the pointer is over the pane. The four wheel kinds replace the older single `wheel` kind in `view-pointer`.

The position is `column` and `row` of the cell, counted from 0 in the area of the widget or pane, and `sub-x`, `sub-y` for the place inside the cell, from 0 at the left or top edge to 255 at the right or bottom edge. Terminals that report only whole cells give 128 for both. A drawing plugin can use the sub-cell position to choose a half block or a Braille dot. `clicks` is 1, 2 or 3 for a `down` event, and is counted by the host with the user's double-click interval.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 150" role="img" aria-label="Pointer position: cell coordinates plus a position inside the cell">
  <rect x="20" y="20" width="240" height="110" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <g stroke="currentColor" opacity="0.4">
    <path d="M60 20 V130 M100 20 V130 M140 20 V130 M180 20 V130 M220 20 V130"/>
    <path d="M20 47 H260 M20 75 H260 M20 102 H260"/>
  </g>
  <rect x="140" y="47" width="40" height="28" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <circle cx="165" cy="55" r="3" fill="currentColor"/>
  <text x="270" y="50" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">column 3, row 1</text>
  <text x="270" y="70" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">sub-x 160, sub-y 60</text>
  <text x="270" y="90" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">kind move, button none</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>One cell is highlighted. The dot is the pointer; sub-x and sub-y locate it inside the cell.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Claims, gestures and drag-over

A whole claim stops the host from forwarding the mouse to the program and switches off its own selection and wheel scrollback on that pane. A gesture claim is gentler. It applies only while the listed modifiers are held when the button goes down. A plain click still reaches the program, so an editor in the pane keeps working, and Ctrl+click goes to the plugin. When a gesture claim is held, the plugin gets events only for presses that match, and for the drags and the release that follow them.

Only one plugin holds the claim of a pane at a time. If another plugin claims a pane that already has a whole claim, the call returns `conflict`. Two plugins may hold gesture claims with different modifier sets on the same pane. The same modifier set is `conflict`.

A drag that carries data, such as a file dragged from a tree list, produces `drag-over` actions on plugin view nodes that declare drop targets, with a `drag-over-value` of source key, target key, index and acceptance (`none`, `before`, `after`, `inside`). A terminal pane does not take drops itself; a plugin that wants a file dropped on a prompt claims the pointer and watches for `up` after a `drag`.

### Rust and TypeScript

This plugin claims Ctrl+click on terminal panes and sends the path under the pointer to its own command.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, PointerModifiers};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::PointerKind;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct CtrlOpen;

impl Handler for CtrlOpen {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::PaneCreated(pane) => {
                    let _ = terminal::claim_pointer_gesture(pane.node, PointerModifiers::CONTROL);
                }
                Event::Pointer(pointer) if pointer.kind == PointerKind::Down => {
                    let hot = pointer.sub_x > 128; // right half of the cell
                    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("ctrl-click {}:{} right={}",
                        pointer.row, pointer.column, hot));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { claimPointerGesture } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'pane-created') {
        try { claimPointerGesture(event.val.node, ['control']); } catch { /* conflict */ }
      } else if (event.tag === 'pointer' && event.val.kind === 'down') {
        const hot = event.val.subX > 128;
        log('info', `ctrl-click ${event.val.row}:${event.val.column} right=${hot}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Outcomes, errors and limits

| Call | Error | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `claim-pointer`, `claim-pointer-gesture` | `not-found` | no such pane |
| `claim-pointer`, `claim-pointer-gesture` | `conflict` | another plugin holds an overlapping claim |
| `claim-pointer-gesture` | `invalid-argument` | the modifier set is empty |
| any | `not-permitted` | `terminal.pointer` is missing or revoked |

The host releases every claim of a plugin when the plugin stops, is disabled or loses the grant. `move` events are coalesced per pane; the plugin sees the latest position, not every cell crossed.

### What the user sees

While a whole claim is held, Ilium shows the pane title with the claim marker of the plugin in the status bar. Under a gesture claim nothing changes until the user holds the modifier. The render below is a terminal pane whose path under the pointer is highlighted by a plugin layer.

│main.rs   <span class="t-hi">lib.rs</span>   util.rs                                           │
│<span class="t-prompt">$</span>                                                                    │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

# Terminal input

## Terminal input

Input to a terminal pane is an intent, `send-input`, not a function. The intent lets a plugin reproduce what the built-in features do: send a command in stages with delays, write raw bytes, send mouse events in the protocol the program enabled, refuse to write when the pane changed, hold the user's keys while it types, and journal the write so a restart cannot lose track of it. A `terminal-view` widget can also forward the user's keys to a pane directly.

### You will need

| Grant | Risk | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.write` | normal | `send-input` with `text` and `stages`, `prompt_epoch` |
| `terminal.raw-input` | high | `raw` bytes, `mouse` events, `interactive: true` on `terminal-view` |
| `terminal.input-lock` | high | `lock-input`, `unlock-input`, `lock-user-input` |

See [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/) and [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/). The journal needs no grant for the plugin's own entries.

### Signatures

```wit
lock-input: func(pane: node-id, millis: u16) -> result<_, plugin-error>;   // at most 2,000 ms
unlock-input: func(pane: node-id);

record input-stage { text: string, delay-ms: u16, delivery: input-delivery }
record terminal-mouse { kind: pointer-kind, button: pointer-button, column: u16, row: u16, modifiers: pointer-modifiers }
record input-precondition { activity: option<agent-activity>, screen-revision: option<u64>, foreground: option<string> }
```

The `send-input` intent takes these optional fields. Without them it sends plain text as described in [Terminal](/pages/primitives-terminal/).

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `stages` | `list<input-stage>` | At most 16 stages, total delay at most 10 s. Replaces `text`. Sent in order, each after its `delay-ms`. |
| `raw` | `option<list<u8>>` | Written as given. At most 64 KiB. Needs `terminal.raw-input`. |
| `mouse` | `option<list<terminal-mouse>>` | Encoded by the host in the protocol the program enabled. `unsupported` when `mouse-reporting` is off. |
| `if-current` | `option<input-precondition>` | A mismatch is `refused(conflict)` before any byte is written. |
| `lock-user-input` | `bool` | Hold the user's keys during the stages, at most 2 s. |
| `journal` | `bool` | Write a journal entry before the PTY write. |

The outcome of a successful write to an agent pane is `ok-epoch(n)`, the new prompt epoch. A plugin that matches only `ok` receives it through the SDK as `ok`.

### Stages and the two-stage submit

Some agent programs lose text that arrives in the same read as the submit key. A signature can declare a two-stage submit, and `stages` lets any plugin do the same by hand: first stage `typed` with the text, a delay of 80 ms, second stage with the submit key. Each stage has its own `delivery`: `typed`, `submitted` or `pasted`. The host sends stages from one queue per pane, so two intents to the same pane never interleave their stages.

### Preconditions

`if-current` makes a write conditional. `activity` must equal the agent activity the host detects, `screen-revision` must equal the revision from `read-cells` or `read-screen`, and `foreground` must equal the name of the foreground process. The check order is the base checks (shape, grant, duplicate key, pane, rate, prompt epoch), then `if-current`, then the lock. The refusal is `refused(conflict)` and names the failed condition, and no key is reserved, so the plugin can retry after reading again.

### Input lock

`lock-input` holds the user's keys in a queue for up to 2,000 ms. The keys are not lost: they are delivered after `unlock-input` or when the time runs out, in order. Only one lock per pane exists; a second `lock-input` from another plugin returns `conflict`. The `lock-user-input` field of `send-input` takes the lock for exactly the duration of its stages.

### Journaled writes

With `journal: true`, the host writes a journal entry (kind `input-sent`, with the dedup key) before the PTY write, and completes it with the delivery result. If the server stops between the write and the outcome, the restarted plugin receives `input-uncertain { pane, dedup-key }` instead of a silent loss, and decides whether to send again. Durable timers and the journal are described in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 440 150" role="img" aria-label="send-input checks, lock, stages and journal order">
  <rect x="6" y="50" width="70" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="41" y="74" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">intent</text>

  <text x="136" y="74" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">K checks</text>
  <rect x="196" y="50" width="80" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="236" y="74" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">if-current</text>
  <rect x="296" y="50" width="60" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="326" y="74" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">lock</text>
  <rect x="376" y="50" width="60" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="406" y="74" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">stages</text>
  <path d="M76 70 H96 M176 70 H196 M276 70 H296 M356 70 H376" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="236" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">journal entry is written before the first PTY write</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>A refusal at any step writes nothing and reserves no dedup key.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Interactive terminal view

The `terminal-view` widget embeds a live pane in a plugin view. With `interactive: true` and `terminal.raw-input`, the view forwards keys and mouse to the pane's program while it has focus; pressing Escape twice leaves it. `scrollback: true` lets the user scroll, and `highlights` names a layer of the plugin that is drawn over the view. See [Media and embedded widgets](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/).

### Rust and TypeScript

This example waits for the agent to be idle, types a command in two stages, locks the keyboard for the duration and journals it.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Delivery, InputStage, Intent, SendInputSpec, InputPrecondition};

let spec = SendInputSpec {
    pane,
    stages: Some(vec![
        InputStage { text: "/compact".into(), delay_ms: 0, delivery: Delivery::Typed },
        InputStage { text: "\r".into(), delay_ms: 80, delivery: Delivery::Typed },
    ]),
    if_current: Some(InputPrecondition {
        activity: Some(AgentActivity::Idle), screen_revision: None, foreground: None }),
    lock_user_input: true,
    journal: true,
    ..SendInputSpec::default()
};
Submission::keyed(Intent::SendInput(spec), format!("compact-{pane}"))
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const submission: Submission = {
  intent: { tag: 'send-input', val: {
    pane,
    stages: [
      { text: '/compact', delayMs: 0, delivery: 'typed' },
      { text: '\r', delayMs: 80, delivery: 'typed' },
    ],
    ifCurrent: { activity: 'idle', screenRevision: undefined, foreground: undefined },
    lockUserInput: true,
    journal: true,
  } },
  correlation: 1n,
  dedupKey: `compact-${pane}`,
};
```

A mouse click sent as input, for a program that enabled mouse reporting:

**Rust**

```rust
let click = [PointerKind::Down, PointerKind::Up].map(|kind| TerminalMouse {
    kind, button: PointerButton::Left, column: 12, row: 4, modifiers: PointerModifiers::empty() });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const click = (['down', 'up'] as const).map((kind) => ({
  kind, button: 'left', column: 12, row: 4, modifiers: [],
}));
```

### Outcomes, errors and limits

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Precondition mismatch | `refused(conflict)`, nothing written |
| Mouse reporting off | `refused(unsupported)` |
| More than 16 stages, delay over 10 s, `raw` over 64 KiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `lock-input` over 2,000 ms | `invalid-argument` |
| Lock held by another plugin | `conflict` |
| Server stopped mid-write with `journal` | `input-uncertain` after restart |
| Grant missing | `not-permitted` |

The rate of 20 submissions per second per pane per plugin still applies, and so do the dedup key rules.

### What the user sees

While a lock is held, the user's keystrokes in that pane are held back and appear after the write. A staged command appears as it is typed:

<pre class="term">╭──≡ ● · Claude─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│<span class="t-dim">&gt;</span> /compact                                                             │
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

# Agent transcript and signals

## Agent transcript and signals

The base agent primitive tells a plugin which agent runs in a pane and what it is doing. The primitive also gives the facts a cost meter, a context gauge or a handoff tool needs: the model in use, the prompt epoch, the typed transcript of the conversation, and two events, `signal-changed` and `agent-model-changed`. The host parses the agent's session file. The plugin never receives a file path to read.

This page extends [Agent primitive](/pages/primitives-agent/).

### You will need

| Grant | Risk | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `agent.read` | normal | `model`, `prompt-epoch`, `signal-changed`, `agent-model-changed` |
| `agent.transcript` | high | `transcript`, `take-transcript` |
| `agent.read-prompts` | high | `last-prompt`, `user-line-submitted` |

See [agent.read](/pages/capability-agent-read/), [agent.read-prompts](/pages/capability-agent-read-prompts/) and [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/). Both sides can import the interface.

### Signatures

```wit
record agent-model { model: string, provider: option<string>, context-window: option<u32>, source: string }
model: func(pane: node-id) -> option<agent-model>;       // source: statusline, transcript or signature
prompt-epoch: func(pane: node-id) -> option<u64>;

enum turn-role { user, assistant, tool, system }
record transcript-turn { role: turn-role, text: string, tool: option<string>, at: option<epoch-ms>, tokens: option<u32> }
record transcript-query { pane: node-id, last-turns: u32, max-bytes: u32 }
transcript: func(q: transcript-query) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>;
take-transcript: func(request: request-id) -> option<list<transcript-turn>>;
```

| Rust (`primitives::agent`) | TypeScript | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `model(pane)` | `model` | `Option<AgentModel>` |
| `prompt_epoch(pane)` | `promptEpoch` | `Option<u64>` |
| `transcript(query)` | `transcript` | `Result<RequestId, PluginError>` |
| `take_transcript(request)` | `takeTranscript` | `Option<Vec<TranscriptTurn>>` |

### Model and epoch

`model` returns the name the agent reports, the provider when known, the context window in tokens when known, and `source`, which says where the host found it: the agent's status line, its transcript, or the signature's default. A model change fires `agent-model-changed { pane, model }`, coalesced per pane. The prompt epoch is the counter that `send-input` compares against (see [Terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/)); the call replaces a read-and-guess pattern. A successful `send-input` on an agent pane returns the new epoch in its outcome.

### Signals

A signature can declare named signals that the host extracts from the agent's status line or screen: context percentage, session cost, the rate-limit reset time. `signal-changed { pane, signal, value }` carries the signal name and its value as a string. The event is coalesced by pane and signal, so a rapidly changing percentage arrives as its latest value. Signal names come from the signature, so a plugin lists the names it cares about in its own configuration.

### The transcript

`transcript` is a request. The host reads the session file in the background, parses it into turns, and answers through `request-completed`; then `take-transcript` returns the turns, oldest first. `last-turns` is at most 512 and `max-bytes` at most 4 MiB. When the result is larger, the oldest turns are dropped. A turn has a role, its text, the tool name for a tool turn, the time when the file records one, and the token count when the file records one. A signature without a known file format returns `unsupported`; a pane with no session yet returns `not-found`.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 140" role="img" aria-label="Host parses session file into typed turns">
  <rect x="10" y="40" width="110" height="50" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="65" y="62" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">session file</text>
  <text x="65" y="78" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">path stays in kernel</text>
  <rect x="150" y="40" width="110" height="50" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="205" y="70" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">host parser</text>
  <rect x="290" y="40" width="120" height="50" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="350" y="70" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">list of turns</text>
  <path d="M120 65 H150 M260 65 H290" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">request-completed, then take-transcript</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The plugin receives typed turns, never the file or its path.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Rust and TypeScript

This example keeps the latest model per pane and, when an agent goes idle, requests the last 20 turns.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent::{self, TranscriptQuery};

for event in batch {
    match event {
        Event::AgentModelChanged(changed) => {
            self.models.insert(changed.pane, changed.model.model);
        }
        Event::SignalChanged(signal) if signal.signal == "context-percent" => {
            self.context.insert(signal.pane, signal.value);
        }
        Event::AgentActivityChanged(change) if change.activity == AgentActivity::Idle => {
            match agent::transcript(TranscriptQuery {
                pane: change.pane, last_turns: 20, max_bytes: 256 * 1024 }) {
                Ok(request) => { self.pending.insert(request, change.pane); }
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &error.message),
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
for (const event of batch) {
  if (event.tag === 'agent-model-changed') {
    models.set(event.val.pane, event.val.model.model);
  } else if (event.tag === 'signal-changed' && event.val.signal === 'context-percent') {
    context.set(event.val.pane, event.val.value);
  } else if (event.tag === 'agent-activity-changed' && event.val.current === 'idle') {
    try {
      const request = transcript({ pane: event.val.node, lastTurns: 20, maxBytes: 256 * 1024 });
      pending.set(request, event.val.node);
    } catch (error) {
      log('warn', String(error));
    }
  }
}
```

Reading the result when the request completes:

**Rust**

```rust
if let Some(turns) = agent::take_transcript(request) {
    let tokens: u32 = turns.iter().filter_map(|turn| turn.tokens).sum();
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const turns = takeTranscript(request) ?? [];
const tokens = turns.reduce((sum, turn) => sum + (turn.tokens ?? 0), 0);
```

### Outcomes, errors and limits

| Call | Error | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `transcript` | `unsupported` | the signature has no known session file format |
| `transcript` | `not-found` | no session yet for the pane |
| `transcript` | `invalid-argument` | `last-turns` over 512 or `max-bytes` over 4 MiB |
| completion | `io`, `quota-exceeded` | the file could not be read, or the result was too large to hold |
| any | `not-permitted` | the grant is missing |

### What the user sees

Nothing in the pane changes. A plugin typically shows the facts in the tree row or the status bar. The tree row of an agent pane, drawn by the host from the activity, shows the working spinner:

<pre class="term">▼ 📂 Ilium
›   🦀 <span class="t-hi">⠋</span> Fix auth
›   🐢 ● Refactor parser
</pre>

- [Terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/)
- [Events](/pages/api-events/)

# Editor viewport and tokens

## Editor viewport and tokens

The editor primitive lets a plugin read buffers and add decorations and gutter marks. This page covers what a minimap, a scroll-sync tool, a hover provider or a language plugin needs: the visible range of an editor pane, pointer events over text, marks on the minimap, and a `token-provider` export that supplies syntax tokens for languages the plugin declares. The syntax engine of the built-in editor stays a host service.

This page extends [Editor primitive](/pages/primitives-editor/). The editor lives on the client side.

### You will need

| Grant | Unlocks |
|---|---|
| `editor.read` | `viewport`, `set-minimap-marks`, `editor-pointer`, `editor-viewport-changed`, the `token-provider` export, the `languages` manifest key |

See [editor.read](/pages/capability-editor-read/). A manifest that exports `token-provider` also needs `contributes.languages`, at most 8 entries, each with `id`, `title`, `extensions` and optional `file_names`.

### Signatures

```wit
record editor-viewport { buffer: buffer-id, pane: node-id, first-line: u32, last-line: u32, columns: u16, rows: u16 }
viewport: func(pane: node-id) -> option<editor-viewport>;
record minimap-mark { line: u32, color: color, lane: u8 }      // lane 0..2
set-minimap-marks: func(buffer: buffer-id, layer: string, marks: list<minimap-mark>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;

// export, with-tokens
enum token-kind { keyword, string, number, comment, type-name, function, variable,
                  operator, punctuation, constant, tag, attribute, plain }
record token { line: u32, start: u32, length: u32, kind: token-kind }
tokens: func(buffer: buffer-id, first-line: u32, lines: list<string>, state-in: option<list<u8>>)
  -> tuple<list<token>, option<list<u8>>>;
```

| Rust (`primitives::editor`) | TypeScript | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `viewport(pane)` | `viewport` | `Option<EditorViewport>` |
| `set_minimap_marks(buffer, layer, marks)` | `setMinimapMarks` | `Result<(), PluginError>` |

Events: `editor-viewport-changed(editor-viewport)`, coalesced per pane at 100 ms, and `editor-pointer { buffer, pane, position, pointer }`, where `position` is a `text-position` (line and column in Unicode scalar values) and `pointer` is the `view-pointer` of [Terminal pointer](/pages/primitives-terminal-pointer/). Hover, click and drag over text produce it; `move` events are coalesced.

### Viewport

`first-line` and `last-line` are the first and last buffer lines that are at least partly visible; `columns` and `rows` are the size of the text area. Wrapped lines count once. The event arrives after scrolling, resizing or switching the buffer in the pane. A plugin that mirrors a second view, such as a preview, follows `first-line` and answers with its own scroll.

### Minimap marks

The minimap is the narrow strip at the right of an editor pane; the host draws it from the text density with the ramp `·`, `-`, `=`, `≡`, `≣`, `█`. A plugin adds marks to three lanes (0 to 2) to show diagnostics, search hits or changes. A mark has a line and a colour; the layer name scopes the set to the plugin, and each call replaces the layer. At most 4,096 marks per layer. Marks are removed when the plugin stops.

<pre class="term">╭──≡ ● · main.rs───────────────────────────────────────╮
│fn main() {                                       <span class="t-dim">·</span>   │
│    <span class="t-hi">let</span> total = add(1, 2);                      <span class="t-dim">-</span>     │
│    <span class="t-err">oops();</span>                                     <span class="t-err">≡</span>     │
│    println!("{total}");                          <span class="t-dim">-</span>   │
│}                                                 <span class="t-dim">·</span>   │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

### Token provider

A language plugin implements `tokens`. The host calls it for the visible lines plus a margin, with `state-in` from the previous block so multi-line constructs such as block comments work, and stores the returned state for the next call. The deadline is 10 ms per call. After a timeout the lines stay plain and the host retries later. The plugin chooses a `token-kind`; it never picks colours, because the theme maps kinds to colours.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 140" role="img" aria-label="Host asks token-provider for visible lines with carried state">
  <rect x="10" y="30" width="120" height="70" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="70" y="55" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">editor (host)</text>
  <text x="70" y="75" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">visible lines + margin</text>
  <rect x="290" y="30" width="120" height="70" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="350" y="55" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">token-provider</text>
  <text x="350" y="75" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">10 ms per call</text>
  <path d="M130 50 H290" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <path d="M290 80 H130" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="44" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">lines, state-in</text>
  <text x="210" y="96" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">tokens, state-out</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The carried state lets a block comment span calls.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Rust and TypeScript

A minimal provider for a language whose comments start with `#`, plus a viewport follower:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{TokenProvider, Token, TokenKind};

impl TokenProvider for HashLang {
    fn tokens(&mut self, _buffer: BufferId, first_line: u32, lines: Vec<String>,
              state_in: Option<Vec<u8>>) -> (Vec<Token>, Option<Vec<u8>>) {
        let mut found = Vec::new();
        for (offset, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Some(start) = line.find('#') {
                found.push(Token {
                    line: first_line + offset as u32,
                    start: line[..start].chars().count() as u32,
                    length: line[start..].chars().count() as u32,
                    kind: TokenKind::Comment,
                });
            }
        }
        (found, state_in)
    }
}

// follow the viewport
if let Event::EditorViewportChanged(view) = event {
    editor::set_minimap_marks(view.buffer, "marks", vec![
        MinimapMark { line: view.first_line, color: Color::role(ColorRole::Accent), lane: 0 }])?;
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { setMinimapMarks } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor';

export const { lifecycle, handler, tokenProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  tokens(buffer, firstLine, lines, stateIn) {
    const found = [];
    lines.forEach((line, offset) => {
      const start = line.indexOf('#');
      if (start >= 0) {
        found.push({ line: firstLine + offset, start: [...line.slice(0, start)].length,
                     length: [...line.slice(start)].length, kind: 'comment' });
      }
    });
    return [found, stateIn];
  },
  onEvents(batch) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'editor-viewport-changed') {
        setMinimapMarks(event.val.buffer, 'marks',
          [{ line: event.val.firstLine, color: { tag: 'role', val: 'accent' }, lane: 0 }]);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Outcomes, errors and limits

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `viewport` for a pane that is not an editor | `none` |
| `set-minimap-marks` over 4,096 marks, or lane over 2 | `invalid-argument` |
| `set-minimap-marks` for an unknown buffer | `not-found` |
| `tokens` over 10 ms | lines stay plain, retried later |
| Missing grant | `not-permitted` |

# Collections

## Collections

Collections draw many items and let the user pick, toggle or edit them. The family has six widgets: `%list`, `table`, `tree-list`, `menu`, `check-list` and `list-editor`. The host owns the state of every collection: selection, scroll offset, expansion, filter text and the text being edited. The plugin sends items and hears about changes.

| Widget | Shows | Main event | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `%list` | rows of styled lines | `selected`, `activated` | `index`, or `ids` with `multi-select` |
| `table` | rows and columns with a header | `selected`, `activated` | `index`, `ids`, or `text(column id)` for a header click |
| `tree-list` | an expandable tree | `selected`, `activated`, `toggled` | `text(item id)` |
| `menu` | commands with submenus | `activated`, `closed` | `text(item id)` |
| `check-list` | boxes with a tri-state | `changed` | `item-state(id, state)` |
| `list-editor` | an editable list of strings or objects | `changed`, `selected` | `text(json array)`, `index` |

### You will need

- A view that can hold the widget: a panel, popup, dialog, pane view or settings page. A `menu` is refused in a settings page, and so is `list-editor` (use a `list` row with `schema-form` there). See [UI model](/pages/ui-model/).
- The `ui.panels` grant for panels and popups. See [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/).
- Items with stable ids. A collection that sends `ids` or `text(id)` needs an `id` on every item.

### Host-owned state

| Widget | State the host keeps | Read with `widget-state` | Set with `set-widget-state` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `%list` | selected index, scroll offset, filter text, multi-selection | `selected`, `offset`, `text`, `ids` | `selected`, `offset`, `text`, `ids` |
| `table` | selected row, scroll offset, sort, multi-selection | `selected`, `offset`, `ids` | `selected`, `offset`, `ids` |
| `tree-list` | selected item, expansion, scroll offset | `selected`, `ids` | `selected`, `expanded`, `ids` |
| `check-list` | the state of each item | `tri` | `tri` |
| `list-editor` | the item being edited and its draft text | `selected` | `selected` |

When the plugin renders a new tree, the host keeps this state by key. A selection of an item that is no longer present moves to the nearest row. A widget without a `key` loses its state on every render.

### Props every collection accepts

`key`, `tooltip`, `disabled-reason`, `tab-index` and `hover-events` work as for every input widget, see [Input](/pages/widgets-input/). `item-tooltip` on `%list` shows each item's `tooltip`.

#### %list

**Purpose.** A scrolling list of items, each made of one or more styled lines. It is the list of the Agents panel and of the choice dialog. The selected row carries the highlight symbol. The filter row narrows the list while the user types, and `follow-tail` keeps the newest row visible for logs.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `list<list-item>` | required | The rows. Item fields: `lines`, `style`, `id`, `icon`, `trailing`, `tooltip`, `disabled-reason`. |
| `highlight-symbol` | `string` | `▶ ` | Drawn before the selected row (`> ` in stable glyph mode). |
| `highlight-style` | `style` | selection | The style of the selected row. |
| `highlight-spacing` | `highlight-spacing` | `when-selected` | `always`, `when-selected` or `never`. |
| `repeat-highlight-symbol` | `bool` | `false` | Draws the symbol on each line of a multi-line item. |
| `direction` | `list-direction` | `top-to-bottom` | Or `bottom-to-top`. |
| `filter` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the `Filter:` row above the list. |
| `filter-placeholder` | `option<string>` | none | Hint text of the filter row. |
| `multi-select` | `bool` | `false` | Space toggles the row. The value becomes `ids`. |
| `follow-tail` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the last item visible until the user scrolls up. |
| `empty` | `option<styled-lines>` | none | Shown when there are no items. |
| `item-tooltip` | `bool` | `false` | Shows each item's tooltip on hover. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `selected` | `index(u32)` | The highlight moves. |
| `activated` | `index(u32)` | Enter or double click. |
| `changed` | `ids(list<string>)` | The multi-selection changes. |
| `filter-changed` | `text(string)` | The filter text changes, after 150 ms. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | Move the highlight. A disabled item is skipped. |
| Enter | Activates the selected item. |
| Space | Toggles the item in `multi-select`. |
| Typing | Filters, when `filter` is true. |
| Left click, double click | Select, activate. |
| Mouse wheel | Scrolls three rows per notch. |

Theme roles: `selection` for the highlighted row, `accent` for the highlight symbol, `muted` for disabled items and trailing text.

#### table

**Purpose.** Rows and columns with a header. Columns have an id, a title, a width, a minimum width and a priority. When the area is too narrow the host drops the columns with the lowest priority first and never shrinks one below its minimum width. A sortable column shows `▲` or `▼`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | `list<table-column>` | required | `id`, `title`, `width` (a constraint), `min-width`, `priority`, `align`, `sortable`. |
| `rows` | `list<table-row>` | required | `cells`, `height`, `style`, and an optional `id`. |
| `sort` | `option<tuple<string, bool>>` | none | The sort column id and whether it is ascending. |
| `multi-select` | `bool` | `false` | Space toggles a row. |
| `follow-tail` | `bool` | `false` | Keeps the last row visible. |
| `column-spacing` | `u16` | `2` | Cells between columns. |
| `highlight-symbol` | `string` | `▶ ` | Before the selected row. |
| `highlight-spacing` | `highlight-spacing` | `when-selected` | As for `%list`. |
| `widths`, `header` | | | Prefer `columns`. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `selected` | `index(u32)` | The highlight moves. |
| `activated` | `index(u32)` | Enter or double click. |
| `activated` | `text(column id)` | A click on a sortable header. The plugin sorts and sets `sort`. |
| `changed` | `ids(list<string>)` | The multi-selection changes. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | Move the highlight. |
| Left, Right | Scroll hidden columns. |
| Enter | Activates the row. |
| Left click on a row, on a header | Select, sort. |

Theme roles: `selection`, `muted` for the header and the rule, `border` for the rule.


#### tree-list

**Purpose.** An expandable tree, with the glyphs of the session tree: `▼` expanded, `▶` collapsed, two blank cells for a leaf and one dim `›` per depth level. Items can carry an icon, a trailing text and a badge, and can be dragged onto each other.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `list<tree-item>` | required | `id`, `label`, `depth`, `expandable`, `expanded`, `icon`, `trailing`, `badge`, `tooltip`, `draggable`, `drop-target`. |
| `multi-select` | `bool` | `false` | Space toggles an item. |

The items form a flat list in display order. `depth` places an item, and `expandable` says whether it has children. The plugin sends only the visible items. The host keeps `expanded` per item id and sends `toggled` when it changes.

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `selected` | `text(id)` | The highlight moves. |
| `activated` | `text(id)` | Enter or double click. |
| `toggled` | `text(id)` | An item is expanded or collapsed. |
| `changed` | `ids(list<string>)` | The multi-selection changes. |
| `dropped` | `text(target id)` | A draggable item is dropped on a drop target. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Up, Down | Move the highlight. |
| Right | Expands, or goes to the first child. |
| Left | Collapses, or goes to the parent. |
| Enter | Activates. |
| Click on `▶` or `▼`, click on the label | Toggles, selects. |
| Drag | Moves a draggable item. |

Theme roles: `selection`, `muted` for the guides and for trailing text.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Project───────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">▼ 📂 src</span>                                     │
│ <span class="t-dim">›</span>   ▶ 📁 ui                                  │
│ <span class="t-dim">›</span>   ▼ 📂 app                                 │
│ <span class="t-dim">››</span>    📄 main.rs                             │
│ <span class="t-dim">››</span>    📄 lib.rs                              │
│ ▶ 📁 docs                                    │
│   📄 README.md                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A tree-list with the glyphs of the session tree: ▼ expanded, ▶ collapsed, two blank cells for a leaf, and one dim › per depth level as indentation. The selected row is reversed. Icons come from the item icon field.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let items = vec![
    TreeItem::new("src", "src").depth(0).expandable(true).icon("📂"),
    TreeItem::new("main", "main.rs").depth(2).icon("📄"),
];
let tree_list = tree.tree_list(items).key("files");
// ("files", ActionKind::Toggled, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.reload_children(&id),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const files = treeList([
  { id: 'src', label: 'src', depth: 0, expandable: true, icon: '📂' },
  { id: 'main', label: 'main.rs', depth: 2, icon: '📄' },
], { key: 'files' });
// if (kind === 'toggled' && value.tag === 'text') reloadChildren(value.val);
```

#### menu

**Purpose.** A list of commands in a popup, the same widget as the terminal context menu. Use it inside a `popup` anchored `at-pointer` and open it when the host sends `context-requested`. Entries can have an icon, a shortcut, a check, a submenu, a disabled reason and a danger flag.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entries` | `list<menu-entry>` | required | `id`, `label`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `parent`, `is-submenu`, `separator-before`, `checked`, `disabled-reason` (up to 40 characters), `tooltip`, `danger`. |
| `items` | `list<menu-item>` | none | `entries` replaces it when present. |

A menu has at most 64 entries and two levels of submenu. An entry names its submenu with `parent`.

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `activated` | `text(id)` | An entry runs. The popup then closes. |
| `closed` | `none` | The user leaves with Escape or a click outside. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Up, Down | Move the highlight. A disabled entry is skipped. |
| Right | Opens a submenu. |
| Left | Closes the submenu. |
| Enter | Runs the entry. |
| Escape | Closes. |
| Click, hover | Runs, or opens a submenu after 200 ms. |

Theme roles: `selection`, `muted` for shortcuts and disabled entries, `danger` for danger entries.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · File────────────────────────╮
│ 📂 Open file                 <span class="t-dim">Enter</span> │
│ <span class="t-hi">✎ Rename                        F2 </span>│
│ ✓ Show hidden                      │
│ 🔀 Open with                     › │
│ <span class="t-dim">⛔ Delete  (read-only volume)</span>      │
│ <span class="t-err">🚫 Move to trash</span>                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A menu in a popup. The selected row is reversed and bold, a check is ✓ (– for mixed), a submenu is marked ›, a disabled entry is dim with its reason, and a danger entry uses the danger colour. The block title uses the chrome icons.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let entries = vec![
    MenuEntry::new("open", "Open file").shortcut("Enter"),
    MenuEntry::new("hidden", "Show hidden").checked(TriState::On),
    MenuEntry::new("with", "Open with").submenu(true),
    MenuEntry::new("delete", "Delete").disabled_reason("read-only volume"),
    MenuEntry::new("trash", "Move to trash").danger(true),
];
let menu = tree.menu(entries).key("file-menu");
// ("file-menu", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.run(&id),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const fileMenu = menu([
  { id: 'open', label: 'Open file', shortcut: 'Enter' },
  { id: 'hidden', label: 'Show hidden', checked: 'on' },
  { id: 'with', label: 'Open with', isSubmenu: true },
  { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete', disabledReason: 'read-only volume' },
  { id: 'trash', label: 'Move to trash', danger: true },
], { key: 'file-menu' });
// if (kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'text') run(value.val);
```

#### check-list

**Purpose.** A list of boxes. Each item is `[x]`, `[ ]` or `[-]`. A parent item names its `children`. Its box is `[-]` when the children differ, and toggling it sets all of them. With `all-toggle` the key `a` toggles every item. The host owns the states and reports them through `widget-state::tri`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `list<check-item>` | required | `id`, `label`, `state` (`on`, `off`, `mixed`), `disabled-reason`, `children`. At most 256 items. |
| `all-toggle` | `bool` | `false` | The `a` key toggles all items. |
| `max-height` | `u16` | none | Rows shown before the list scrolls. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `item-state(id, state)` | An item changes. A parent sends one event per child that changed. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Up, Down | Move the highlight. |
| Space | Toggles the item. |
| `a` | Toggles all items, with `all-toggle`. |
| Click on the box or label | Toggles. |

Theme roles: `accent` for a checked box, `muted` for a disabled item.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Group members─────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">[-] All agents</span>                                       │
│     [x] claude: refactor                             │
│     [ ] codex: tests                                 │
│     <span class="t-dim">[ ] gemini: docs  (frozen)</span>                       │
│ [x] Shell                                            │
│                                                      │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggles · a toggles all · Enter applies</span>        │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A check-list with a parent row. The parent shows [-] because its children differ and toggles all of them. A disabled child is dim and carries its reason. The key line below is a key-hints widget, not part of the check-list.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let items = vec![
    CheckItem::new("all", "All agents").children(vec!["claude", "codex", "gemini"]),
    CheckItem::new("claude", "claude: refactor").state(TriState::On),
    CheckItem::new("codex", "codex: tests"),
    CheckItem::new("gemini", "gemini: docs").disabled_reason("frozen"),
];
let list = tree.check_list(items).key("members").all_toggle(true);
// ("members", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::ItemState(id, state)) => self.set(&id, state),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const members = checkList([
  { id: 'all', label: 'All agents', children: ['claude', 'codex', 'gemini'] },
  { id: 'claude', label: 'claude: refactor', state: 'on' },
  { id: 'codex', label: 'codex: tests' },
  { id: 'gemini', label: 'gemini: docs', disabledReason: 'frozen' },

// if (value.tag === 'item-state') set(value.val[0], value.val[1]);
```

#### list-editor

**Purpose.** Edits a list of strings, for example globs, URLs, hosts or chords, or a list of objects with up to eight fields. It is the widget behind the `list` rows of Settings. A checked format (`glob`, `url`, `host`, `path`, `regex`, `chord`) draws an invalid item with `✗` and the reason, and the item is not written.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `list<string>` | required | The values. |
| `item-format` | `option<item-format>` | none | `glob`, `url`, `host`, `path`, `regex` or `chord`. Checked on commit. |
| `object-fields` | `list<list-field>` | empty | `id`, `title`, `kind`, `width`. Up to 8. The items are then objects. |
| `reorderable` | `bool` | `true` | Shows the `⠿` grip and allows Alt+Up and Alt+Down. |
| `max-items` | `u32` | `64` | 1,024 with the first-party tier. |
| `item-states` | `list<row-state>` | empty | A status per item: `checking`, `ok` or `error`, with a message. |
| `placeholder` | `option<string>` | none | Shown in an empty new item. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `text(json array)` | An edit is committed. The whole array is sent. |
| `selected` | `index(u32)` | The highlight moves. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Up, Down | Move the highlight. |
| Enter | Edits the item. |
| Insert or `+` | Adds an item. |
| Delete | Removes the item. |
| Alt+Up, Alt+Down | Reorders. |
| Click on `+`, `✗`; drag the `⠿` grip | Add, remove, reorder. |

Theme roles: `foreground` for the items, `danger` for an invalid item and its message, `muted` for the grip and the placeholder.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Ignore globs──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ⠿  node_modules/**                                               │
│ ⠿  <span class="t-hi">target/**/*.rlib</span>                                        ✗     │
│ ⠿  <span class="t-err">[unclosed</span>                                              <span class="t-err">✗</span>      │
│ ⠿  <span class="t-dim">add a pattern…</span>                                                │
│ +                                                                │
│ <span class="t-err">✗ Invalid glob: unclosed [</span>                                       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A list-editor for glob patterns. Each row has a grip ⠿ for dragging, the inline editable text, and ✗ to remove it. The second row is being edited. An invalid item (third row) is drawn in the danger colour and the message is on the last line. The + at the bottom adds an item.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Image URLs────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ⠿  https://example.org/a.jpg                  <span class="t-ok">✓</span>                  │
│ ⠿  https://example.org/b.jpg                  <span class="t-dim">…</span>                  │
│ ⠿  ftp://example.org/c.jpg                    <span class="t-err">✗</span>                  │
│ +                                                                │

╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

With `object-fields` each item is one row with a column per field. The commit sends the whole array of objects as JSON.

**Rust**

```rust
    ListField::new("name", "Name", FieldKind::Text).width(12),
    ListField::new("host", "Host", FieldKind::Text).width(20),
    ListField::new("port", "Port", FieldKind::Number).width(6),

```

```ts
  key: 'providers',
  objectFields: [
    { id: 'name', title: 'Name', kind: 'text', width: 12 },
    { id: 'host', title: 'Host', kind: 'text', width: 20 },
```

### Worked example: an agents table

The plugin shows every session in a table, sorts it by the column the user clicks and opens the selected one on Enter.

**Rust**

```rust
impl Views for Agents {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let columns = vec![
            TableColumn::new("name", "Name").width(Constraint::Length(18)).priority(9).sortable(true),
            TableColumn::new("state", "State").width(Constraint::Length(10)).priority(5),
        ];
        let rows = self.rows.iter().map(|row| TableRow::new(vec![row.name.clone(), row.state.clone()]).id(&row.id)).collect();
        let table = tree.table(columns, rows).key("agents").sort(Some((self.sort.clone(), self.ascending)));
        tree.finish(table)
    }
}

impl Handler for Agents {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            match (action.key.as_str(), action.kind, action.value) {
                ("agents", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(column)) => {
                    self.ascending = self.sort == column && !self.ascending;
                    self.sort = column;
                }
                ("agents", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Index(row)) => self.open(row as usize),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export const { handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  render() {
    const columns = [
      { id: 'name', title: 'Name', width: { tag: 'length', val: 18 }, priority: 9, sortable: true },
      { id: 'state', title: 'State', width: { tag: 'length', val: 10 }, priority: 5 },
    ];
    const rows = state.rows.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, cells: [row.name, row.state] }));
    return tree(table(columns, rows, { key: 'agents', sort: [state.sort, state.ascending] }));
  },
  onEvents(batch) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || event.val.key !== 'agents') continue;
      const { kind, value } = event.val;
      if (kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'text') {
        state.ascending = state.sort === value.val ? !state.ascending : true;
        state.sort = value.val;
      } else if (kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'index') open(value.val);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Edge cases and errors

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| More than 256 `check-list` items, or more than `max-items` in a `list-editor` | `invalid-argument` on render. |
| More than 64 menu entries, or a submenu deeper than two levels | The menu is truncated with `… N more`. |
| Two items with the same `id` | The tree is invalid and the instance traps. |
| An invalid item in a `list-editor` | Drawn with `✗` and the reason. It is not written and `changed` is not sent for it. |
| A selected item removed by the next render | The selection moves to the nearest row. |
| `menu` or `list-editor` in a settings page | `invalid-argument` on render. |
| `set-widget-state` with a case the widget does not take | `invalid-argument`. |

# Data display

## Data display

Data widgets turn numbers into pictures. This family has ten widgets. `gauge` and `line-gauge` show one ratio. `sparkline` shows a short series in one row. `bar-chart` shows bars. `chart` plots datasets with axes, in a high resolution Braille render or as a text line. `canvas` draws shapes in a coordinate space. `calendar` shows a month. `progress-row` shows the state of one job. `meter` shows a segmented bar for costs and quotas. `minimap` shows the shape of a long text.

The plugin computes the numbers and the host draws them. Most data widgets are one way: they send nothing back unless the plugin sets the `focusable` flag or the widget has an action of its own, such as a click on a progress row.

## You need

- A grant to show the view: `ui.panels` for a panel ([UI panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/)), or `panes.provide-kind` for a pane kind. `ui.invalidate` is always granted for views the plugin contributes.
- Rust with the `ilium-plugin-sdk` crate, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both target API `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
- The [widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/) for the common props, the widget keys, and the rule that a plugin renders only when it calls `ui.invalidate` or the view area changes.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 340 130" role="img" aria-label="A plugin sends numbers to the host, and the host draws them without sending actions back">
  <title>Data widgets are one way</title>
  <desc>The plugin computes numbers and sends a new tree after ui.invalidate. The host draws the widget and sends no action back.</desc>
  <defs>
    <marker id="dd-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

<figcaption>Data widgets are mostly one way. The plugin computes the numbers and returns a new tree when they change.</figcaption>
</figure>

## How a data view updates

The host calls the plugin's `render` function when the view first opens, after `ui.invalidate` for that view, and when the area changes. The plugin answers with a full `ui-tree`. The host diffs the new tree against the last one by node `key`, and repaints the nodes that changed. Give a node a `key` that stays the same across renders, so that the diff can match it.

## The widgets

| Widget | Shows | Sends |
|---|---|---|
| `gauge` | One ratio as a bar with a centred label | nothing |
| `line-gauge` | One ratio as a single line | nothing |
| `sparkline` | A series in one row | nothing |
| `bar-chart` | Bars in groups | `selected` (a bar) when focusable |
| `chart` | Datasets on axes | `selected` (a point) when focusable |
| `canvas` | Shapes in a coordinate space | `activated` with a cell when focusable |
| `calendar` | One month (unstable) | `selected` (a day) |
| `progress-row` | The state of one job | `activated` |
| `meter` | A segmented bar | `selected` (a segment) when focusable |
| `minimap` | The shape of a long text | `activated`, `scrolled` |

Every widget has a builder. The required prop is the constructor argument, and the other props are setters. In Rust the setters are snake_case and chain on the node handle. In TypeScript they go in the props object in camelCase. A prop that is not set takes the default in the last column of its table.

## gauge

Mirrors `ratatui::widgets::Gauge`. It fills a bar with a ratio and draws a label over it.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ratio` | `f64` (0 to 1) | required | The fraction of the bar that is filled. |
| `label` | `option<styled-text>` | none | Text centred over the bar. |
| `use-unicode` | `bool` | `true` | Whether partial cells use block characters. |
| `gauge-style` | `style` | empty | Colours of the filled and unfilled parts. |

Keys, mouse and actions: none. Roles: `accent` for the filled part and `muted` for the rest.
