### Widget surface

Each table lists the props with their type, default and meaning. A required prop is a constructor argument of the builder. Other props are chained setters in Rust (`Tree` in `ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build`) or fields of a props object in TypeScript (`@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build`). Rust setters are snake_case and TypeScript fields are camelCase.

#### button

**Purpose.** Starts an action: save, run, delete. It is a copy of the dialog buttons of the client. The `role` sets the look and the host never confirms anything for the plugin, so a destructive action needs a `dialog` of its own.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | The text of the button. |
| `icon` | `option<string>` | none | A host icon name drawn before the label. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | When false, the button cannot be pressed. |
| `role` | `button-role` | `secondary` | `primary`, `secondary` or `danger`. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `activated` | `none` | Enter or Space with focus, or a left click. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Enter or Space | Presses the focused button. |
| Left click | Focuses the button and presses it. |
| Tab | Moves focus to the next focusable widget. |

**Drawing.** A button whose area height is 1 or 2 draws `[ label ]` on the first row, left-aligned. With an icon it draws `[ icon label ]`. A button with height 3 or more draws a rounded box filling its area, with the label centred on the middle row and the odd cell going right. A label wider than the space is cut with `…`. The focused button draws bold, with its label in the `selection` role.

Theme roles: `accent` for a primary button, `danger` for a danger button, `foreground` for a secondary button and `muted` for a disabled one.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Buttons───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                          │
│  <span class="t-hi">[ Save ]</span>   [ Cancel ]   [ Delete ]   <span class="t-dim">[ Apply ]</span>                          │
│                                                                          │
│  primary (focused)  secondary  danger        disabled                    │
│                                                                          │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The four button states in a one-row area. The first button holds focus and uses the accent colours, the last one is disabled and dimmed. The second line is a note and not part of the render.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭───────╮
│ Save  │
╰───────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The same button in an area of height 3 and width 9. The label is centred, and the odd cell goes right.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let save = tree.button("Save").key("save").role(ButtonRole::Primary);
// in on_events: ("save", ActionKind::Activated, _) => self.save(),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const save = button('Save', { key: 'save', role: 'primary' });
// in onEvents: if (key === 'save' && kind === 'activated') save();
```

#### toggle

**Purpose.** Switches a flag. It is the toggle row of the Settings screen. Three styles cover three uses: `switch` for a row with leaders, `checkbox` for a list of flags, and `icon` for a toolbar. With `tri-state` the toggle also has a mixed state for a flag that is true for some members of a group.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | The text of the row. |
| `value` | `bool` | required | The state the row shows. |
| `style` | `toggle-style` | `switch` | `switch` draws `[ On ]` and `[ Off ]`, `checkbox` draws `[x]` and `[ ]`, `icon` draws one glyph. |
| `tri-state` | `bool` | `false` | Adds the mixed state `[-]`. The event value is then an `item-state`. |
| `icon-on`, `icon-off` | `option<string>` | none | The glyphs of the `icon` style, for example `★` and `☆`. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `flag(bool)` | The user flips the toggle. |
| `changed` | `item-state("", tri-state)` | The user cycles a `tri-state` toggle. The id is the empty string. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Space or Enter | Flips the focused toggle. A tri-state toggle cycles off, on, mixed. |
| Left click | Focuses and flips. |

Theme roles: `success` for on, `muted` for off, `accent` for the focused row.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Toggles───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Show background</span> <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">[ On ]</span> │
│ Reverse colours <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ Off ] │
│ <span class="t-dim">Natural placement</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">[ On ]</span> │
│ [x] Enabled                                                              │
│ [ ] Dry run                                                              │
│ [-] Some agents selected                                                 │
│ Bookmark <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> ★ │
│ Bookmark <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> ☆ │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rows of the toggle widget. Switch style on rows one to three (focused, idle, disabled), checkbox style and tri-state on rows four to six, icon style with the icon-on and icon-off glyphs at the end.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let dry = tree.toggle("Dry run", self.dry_run).key("dry-run");
let agents = tree.toggle("All agents", false).key("all").style(ToggleStyle::Checkbox).tri_state(true);
let star = tree.toggle("Bookmark", self.starred).key("star")
    .style(ToggleStyle::Icon).icon_on("★").icon_off("☆");
// ("dry-run", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Flag(on)) => self.dry_run = on,
// ("all", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::ItemState(_, state)) => self.all = state,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const dry = toggle('Dry run', state.dryRun, { key: 'dry-run' });
const agents = toggle('All agents', false, { key: 'all', style: 'checkbox', triState: true });
const star = toggle('Bookmark', state.starred, { key: 'star', style: 'icon', iconOn: '★', iconOff: '☆' });
// if (value.tag === 'flag') state.dryRun = value.val;
// if (value.tag === 'item-state') state.all = value.val[1];
```

#### choice

**Purpose.** Picks one option out of a fixed list or out of a catalogue. This is the widget behind most rows of the Settings screen: palette, dither, colour filter, theme, model. It has three styles. `stepper` is the compact row with the `←` `→` `+` buttons and fits a handful of options. `list` draws every option as its own row. `dialog` shows the current value and opens the filterable choice dialog, which suits long lists such as the 38 palettes or about 12,000 icons.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | The text of the row. |
| `options` | `list<string>` | required | The options in order. Ignored when `items` or `source` is set. |
| `selected` | `u32` | required | The index of the option shown. 0 is the first option. |
| `style` | `choice-style` | `stepper` | `stepper`, `list` or `dialog`. |
| `items` | `list<catalog-item>` | empty | Option records. Replaces `options` when not empty. |
| `source` | `option<string>` | none | A catalogue id such as `ilium.palettes`. Items page in as the user scrolls. |
| `selected-id` | `option<string>` | none | The current item id for `items` and `source`. |
| `filter` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the Search line in the dialog. |
| `view-modes` | `list<view-mode>` | none | `list` and `grid`, adds the View switch of the icon picker. |
| `disabled-marker` | `disabled-marker` | `reason` | `reason` draws `(reason)`, `cross` draws `✗`. |
| `allow-custom` | `bool` | `false` | Lets the user type a value that is not in the list. |

A `catalog-item` has `id`, `title`, `description` (up to 120 characters), `preview`, `group` (a heading in the dialog), `keywords` (up to 8, matched by the filter) and `disabled-reason` (up to 40 characters). A `preview` is one of `glyph(string)`, `swatch(list<u32>)` (1 to 16 colours, drawn as half blocks) or `pattern(list<string>)` (1 to 4 lines of at most 8 cells).

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `index(u32)` | A fixed list changes. |
| `changed` | `text(item id)` | A catalogue or `items` choice changes. |
| `filter-changed` | `text(string)` | The dialog filter text changes, debounced 150 ms. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Left or Right | Steps to the previous or next option. It never wraps and skips disabled options. |
| Enter, or a click on `+` or on the value | Opens the dialog (`dialog` style, or the full list from a stepper). |
| Mouse wheel | Steps, like the arrow keys. |
| In the dialog | Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown move the highlight. Typing filters. Enter applies. Escape cancels. A click on a row applies it, a click outside cancels. |
| Click on a disabled option | Nothing changes. The reason stays on screen. |

Theme roles: `accent` for the value, `muted` for disabled options.

**Stepper.** The stepper is the row `Label …… ← value → +`. A click on the value or on `→` goes forward, a right click on the value goes back, a click on `+` opens the list. A disabled button is dimmed and inert.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Choice rows───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Palette</span> <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">← Sunset → +</span> │
│ Dither <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> ← Bayer 4x4 → + │
│ <span class="t-dim">Colour filter</span> <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">← Sepia → +</span> │
│ Colour source <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-err">← Banana → +</span> │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Stepper style. Left and right step through the options, the value and the arrow to its right go forward, and the plus opens the full list. Row one has focus, row three is disabled, row four shows an invalid stored value in the error colour.</figcaption>
</figure>

**List.** The list style draws one row per option and marks the current one with the same `●` as the dialog.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Choice list───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Theme                                                                    │
│   ● Dark                                                                 │
│     Light                                                                │
│     Auto                                                                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>List style: every option is a row and the current one carries the same ● marker as the choice dialog.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Dialog.** The dialog is the choice popover of the Settings screen, drawn by the host. Its parts, from the top, are the title, the `Search:` line, the option rows, the status line and the `Enter applies · Esc cancels` hint. The status line reads `N of M options · Current: X`, where N counts the options left by the filter. A disabled option keeps its place, carries the suffix `[unavailable]` and shows `Unavailable: <reason>` under it, and typing a word of the reason finds it. The host revalidates the chosen id on commit, so a stale id cannot be applied.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Palette───────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Search: sun_                                         │
│   Sunburst                                           │
│ <span class="t-hi">● Sunset</span>                                             │
│   Sunrise                                            │
│   Sunken garden <span class="t-dim">[unavailable]</span>                        │
│ <span class="t-dim">    Unavailable: needs Color mode</span>                    │
│                                                      │
│ 4 of 38 options · Current: Sunset                    │
│ Enter applies · Esc cancels                          │
│                                                      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The choice dialog as the Settings screen draws it. The Search line filters while the user types. The highlighted row is drawn in the selection colours, ● marks the current value, a disabled option carries the [unavailable] suffix and an indented reason line. The status line counts the filtered options. With more rows than fit, the last column of the list's area becomes a scrollbar with the ┃ thumb on the │ track.</figcaption>
</figure>

With more rows than the dialog can show, the last column of the list's area becomes a scrollbar, drawn by the [scrollbar rule](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/#scrollbar): `│` is the track and `┃` is the thumb. A catalogue source is read in pages of up to 256 items as the user scrolls, so a list of 12,000 icons opens at once.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Icon─────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Search: _                                               │
│<span class="t-hi"> ● Rocket</span>                                              ┃ │
│   Satellite                                           │ │
│   Saturn                                              │ │
│   Scroll                                              │ │
│   Seedling                                            │ │
│ 6 of 12041 options · Current: Rocket                    │
│ Enter applies · Esc cancels                             │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A long catalogue. The track is the last column of the list's area. The list holds 12,041 rows and shows 5, so the thumb is the minimum length of one row. Further pages load as the user scrolls.</figcaption>
</figure>

The same dialog serves the palette, dither and icon pickers, which differ only in their previews. They are shown in [Pickers](/pages/widgets-pickers/).

**Rust**

```rust
// types::ui::{ChoiceStyle, ViewMode, DisabledMarker, CatalogItem}; types::text::Preview
let theme = tree.choice("Theme", vec!["Light", "Dark", "Auto"], 1).key("theme");

// A catalogue with a filter: items page in from the host.
let palette = tree.choice("Palette", Vec::<String>::new(), 0)
    .source("ilium.palettes").style(ChoiceStyle::Dialog).filter(true).key("palette");

// Own options with previews and a disabled option.
let items = vec![
    CatalogItem::new("slow", "Slow").description("Every 10 s"),
    CatalogItem::new("live", "Live").preview(Preview::Glyph("●".into())).disabled_reason("needs a key"),
];
let rate = tree.choice("Refresh", Vec::<String>::new(), 0)
    .items(items).selected_id("slow").style(ChoiceStyle::Dialog).key("refresh");

// ("theme", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Index(i)) => self.theme = i,
// ("palette", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.palette = id,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const theme = choice('Theme', ['Light', 'Dark', 'Auto'], 1, { key: 'theme' });

const palette = choice('Palette', [], 0, {
  key: 'palette', source: 'ilium.palettes', style: 'dialog', filter: true,
});

const rate = choice('Refresh', [], 0, {
  key: 'refresh', style: 'dialog', selectedId: 'slow',
  items: [
    { id: 'slow', title: 'Slow', description: 'Every 10 s', keywords: [] },
    { id: 'live', title: 'Live', preview: { tag: 'glyph', val: '●' }, disabledReason: 'needs a key', keywords: [] },
  ],
});

// if (value.tag === 'index') state.theme = value.val;
// if (value.tag === 'text') state.palette = value.val;
```

#### number

**Purpose.** Edits a bounded number. It is the number row of the Settings screen, with two styles. The `stepper` style is `- 42 cm + *`: minus and plus step the value and the star opens the entry dialog. The `slider` style adds a track `─` with a thumb `●` in front of the same buttons.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | The text of the row. |
| `value` | `f64` | required | The current value. |
| `minimum` | `f64` | `0` | The lower bound. A typed value below it is clamped to it. |
| `maximum` | `f64` | `100` | The upper bound. A typed value above it is clamped to it. |
| `step` | `f64` | `1` | The change per step. |
| `unit` | `option<string>` | none | A unit shown after the value. |
| `style` | `number-style` | `stepper` | `stepper` or `slider`. |
| `steps` | `list<f64>` | none | A ladder of values. A step moves to the next rung instead of adding `step`. |
| `special-values` | `list<tuple<f64, string>>` | none | A value drawn as a word, for example `0` as `Off`. |
| `scale` | `u32` | `1` | Typed digits are divided by it, so `1.7` entered with scale 10 means 17 in the stored unit. |
| `debounce-ms` | `u32` | `600` | The delay for typed digits. Steps and drags are not debounced. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `number(f64)` | A step, a drag, a wheel turn, or a valid typed value. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Left or Right, `-` or `+` | Steps by `step`, or to the next rung of `steps`. A value never wraps. |
| Home or End | Goes to the minimum or the maximum. |
| Enter or `*` | Opens the entry dialog. |
| Left click on `-` or `+` | Steps. |
| Click or drag on the slider track | Sets the value at the pointer, see the slider rule below. |
| Mouse wheel | Steps. |

**Slider rule.** The track is the area width minus the label column, minus the stepper part (`- value unit + *`), minus 2 gap cells. When the track is narrower than 12 cells, the slider falls back to the stepper style. Let W be the track width. The thumb cell is `round((value-minimum)/(maximum-minimum)*(W-1))`. A click at track cell x sets `value = minimum + x/(W-1)*(maximum-minimum)`, snapped to the nearest step and clamped. Track cells are `─` (`muted`) and the thumb is `●` (`accent`). In stable-glyph mode they are `-` and `o`.

Theme roles: `accent` for the value and the thumb, `muted` for the track and for a disabled step button.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Number rows───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Scroll speed</span> <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">- 3 + *</span> │
│ Width <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> - 42 cm + * │
│ Retention <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> - 30 days + * │
│ Timeout <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> Off │
│ <span class="t-dim">Port</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">- 8080 + *</span> │
│ Port <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-err">- 99999 + *</span> │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Stepper style. The minus and plus buttons step, the star opens the entry dialog. A special value (row four, zero shown as Off) replaces the number. The error row shows a stored value outside the bounds.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Slider rows───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Density</span>         <span class="t-dim">────────</span><span class="t-hi">●</span><span class="t-dim">────────────</span>  - 60 % + *                        │
│ Speed           <span class="t-dim">───</span><span class="t-hi">●</span><span class="t-dim">─────────────────</span>  - 25 % + *                        │
│ Frame rate cap  <span class="t-dim">────────────────────</span><span class="t-hi">●</span>  - 30 fps + *                      │
│ <span class="t-dim">Hue shift</span>       <span class="t-dim">──────────</span><span class="t-hi">●</span><span class="t-dim">──────────</span>  - 0 deg + *                       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Slider style. The track is a row of ─ and the thumb is ●. The same row carries the stepper buttons, so keyboard users can step and mouse users can drag the thumb. Below 12 cells the host falls back to the stepper.</figcaption>
</figure>

The entry dialog opens on Enter or `*`. It is the number dialog of the client: a `Value:` line, an error line and the `Enter applies · Esc cancels` hint. The host parses the exact draft against the bounds and shows its own message, so the plugin only ever receives a valid number. A step button stops at the bound and is drawn dimmed there. Areas narrower than 12 cells fall back from the slider to the stepper, and the stepper keeps single-cell `-` and `+` targets so the unit stays visible at 80 columns.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Speed───────────────────────────────╮
│ Value: 4x_                                 │
│ <span class="t-err">Enter a number between 25 and 300</span>          │
│                                            │
│ Enter applies · Esc cancels                │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The number entry dialog opened by Enter or the star. The host parses the exact draft and shows its message on the error line. Nothing reaches the plugin until the draft is valid.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let density = tree.number("Density", self.density).key("density")
    .style(NumberStyle::Slider).minimum(25.0).maximum(100.0).step(5.0).unit("%");
let timeout = tree.number("Timeout", self.timeout).key("timeout")
    .minimum(0.0).maximum(300.0).special_values(vec![(0.0, "Off".into())]);
// ("density", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Number(v)) => self.density = v,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const density = number('Density', state.density, {
  key: 'density', style: 'slider', minimum: 25, maximum: 100, step: 5, unit: '%',
});
const timeout = number('Timeout', state.timeout, {
  key: 'timeout', minimum: 0, maximum: 300, specialValues: [[0, 'Off']],
});
// if (value.tag === 'number') state.density = value.val;
```

#### text-input

**Purpose.** Edits one line of text. It is the text row of the Settings screen, drawn as `Label …… [ value ]`. The host owns the contents and the cursor after the first render, so `initial` sets only the starting text. The terminal cursor is the real cursor and no cursor glyph is drawn. A secret field shows one `•` per hidden character and can keep the last characters visible, like the API key rows (`••••a1b2`).

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | required | The text before the field. |
| `initial` | `string` | required | The starting text. An empty string gives an empty field. |
| `placeholder` | `option<string>` | none | Text shown while the field is empty. |
| `secret` | `bool` | `false` | Hides the text. |
| `reveal-last` | `u8` | `0` | With `secret`, how many trailing characters stay visible (0 to 8). |
| `reveal` | `bool` | `false` | Lets the user hold Ctrl+R to show a secret. |
| `max-length` | `u32` | `0` | The longest allowed value in characters. `0` means the 64 KiB cap. |
| `submit-on-enter` | `bool` | `true` | Whether Enter sends `submitted`. |
| `debounce-ms` | `u32` | `600` | Delay of `changed`, from 0 to 2,000. |
| `validation` | `option<string>` | none | A regular expression. A value that does not match is drawn in the error colour. |
| `suggestions` | `option<string>` | none | A catalogue id that offers completions while typing. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `text(string)` | After the debounce. |
| `submitted` | `text(string)` | On Enter, when `submit-on-enter` is true. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Typing, Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home, End | Edit the text natively, with paste support. |
| Enter | Sends `submitted`. |
| Ctrl+R held | Shows a secret while `reveal` is true. |
| Left click | Places the cursor. Dragging selects. |

Theme roles: `foreground` for the text, `muted` for the placeholder and for the leaders, `danger` for an invalid value.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Text rows─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Title</span> <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">[ My session ]</span> │
│ Folders <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………</span> [ ~/Pictures;/data/*/wallpapers/**/*.jpg ] │
│ <span class="t-dim">Name</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">[ Type a name… ]</span> │
│ Host <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-err">[ photon..komoot ]</span> │
│ API key <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ ••••a1b2 ] │
│ API key (revealed) <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ sk-live-9f3a1b2 ] │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Single-line text. The focused field uses the real terminal cursor, no cursor glyph is drawn. An empty field shows its placeholder, an invalid value uses the error colour, a secret shows one dot per hidden character and keeps the last characters selected by reveal-last. Holding the reveal key shows the full value.</figcaption>
</figure>

A longer prompt, for example the rename dialog, is the same field inside a `dialog`. Put the field in a nested block with the title `Value`, or `Protected value` with the hint `The stored value remains hidden` for a secret.

**Rust**

```rust
let name = tree.text_input("Name", self.name.clone()).key("name")
    .placeholder("Type a name…").submit_on_enter(true);
let key = tree.text_input("API key", String::new()).key("api-key")
    .secret(true).reveal_last(4).reveal(true).validation("^sk-[a-z0-9-]+$");
// ("name", ActionKind::Submitted, ActionValue::Text(t)) => self.rename(t),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const name = textInput('Name', state.name, { key: 'name', placeholder: 'Type a name…', submitOnEnter: true });
const apiKey = textInput('API key', '', {
  key: 'api-key', secret: true, revealLast: 4, reveal: true, validation: '^sk-[a-z0-9-]+$',
});
// if (kind === 'submitted' && value.tag === 'text') rename(value.val);
```

#### text-area

**Purpose.** Edits several lines of text, for example a note, a prompt or a list of commands. Enter adds a line. The `max-bytes` cap counts bytes, not characters, so a multi-byte character uses more of the cap.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initial` | `string` | required | The starting text. |
| `placeholder` | `option<string>` | none | Text shown while the area is empty. |
| `wrap` | `bool` | `true` | Whether long lines wrap. |
| `line-numbers` | `bool` | `false` | Whether line numbers are shown. |
| `max-bytes` | `u32` | `0` | The largest allowed value in bytes. `0` means 1 MiB. |
| `debounce-ms` | `u32` | unset | Delay of `changed`, from 0 to 2,000. Unset means 600 ms while the text is at most 10,000 bytes and 1,000 ms above that, re-evaluated at each keystroke. An explicit value always wins. |
| `tab-moves-focus` | `bool` | `false` | When true, Tab leaves the area. Otherwise Tab inserts a tab. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `text(string)` | After the debounce. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Typing, Enter, arrows, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown | Edit natively. |
| Left click, drag | Place the cursor, select. |
| Mouse wheel | Scrolls the area. |

Theme roles: `foreground` for the text, `muted` for line numbers and for the placeholder.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Notes─────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ 1  Fix the tree crash                                │
│ 2  Add the chatroom pane                             │
│ 3                                                    │
│ <span class="t-dim">Enter adds a line · Tab inserts a tab</span>                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A multi-line text area with line numbers. The cursor is the real terminal cursor on line three.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let notes = tree.text_area(self.notes.clone()).key("notes").line_numbers(true).max_bytes(4096);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const notes = textArea(state.notes, { key: 'notes', lineNumbers: true, maxBytes: 4096 });
```

#### schema-form

**Purpose.** Draws the rows of one settings section from the manifest. The host validates each change and saves it, and the plugin only names the section. It is the generic settings renderer of the client, so the rows, the leaders, the keys and the help anchors are exactly those of the Settings screen. All 18 row types work, including the rows documented in [Settings rows](/pages/settings-screens/).

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin` | `plugin-id` | required | The plugin that owns the settings: its own id. |
| `section` | `string` | required | The id of one of the plugin's own sections, or of its own tab, from `contributes.settings`. |

A `schema-form` sends no `ui-action`. The host saves each change, and the owning plugin receives `settings-changed` with the changed keys. Read the values through the [settings API](/pages/api-settings/). Keyboard and mouse follow the rows: each row behaves like the control it shows (a `choice` row steps with Left and Right, a `number` row steps with `-` and `+`). A `schema-form` for a section of another plugin is drawn only when the rendering plugin holds `settings.write-all`. See [Plugin settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/).

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Cleanup settings──────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Enabled <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ On ] │
│ <span class="t-hi">Port</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">- 8080 + *</span> │
│ Mode <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> ← Dry run → + │
│ Token <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ ••••a1b2 ] │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A schema form built from four settings rows. It uses the same rows, leaders and keys as the Settings screen.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let form = tree.schema_form("com.example.demo", "badges").key("settings");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const form = schemaForm('com.example.demo', 'badges', { key: 'settings' });
```

#### key-capture

**Purpose.** Records one key chord, for example a shortcut for a plugin command. The user presses Enter on the field, then presses the chord, and the field takes it. The chord is a string such as `Ctrl+Shift+K`. The field looks up the chord in the kernel keymap when `reserved-check` is on, and shows `! used by <command>` for a chord that the kernel already binds. The kernel's own prefix chooser, which offers only the 26 `Ctrl+letter` choices, is not this widget. The global chord registry stays with the kernel, so a captured chord is a value that the plugin stores and applies itself, for example through `contributes.commands`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chord` | `option<string>` | none | The current chord. None shows `not set`. |
| `allow-modifier-only` | `bool` | `false` | Accepts a chord that is only a modifier, such as `Shift`. |
| `reserved-check` | `bool` | `true` | Warns about chords the kernel binds (needs `keymap.read`). |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `text(chord)` | A chord is taken, or cleared with an empty string. |
| `closed` | `none` | The user cancels a capture with Escape. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Enter | Starts a capture. The field shows `⌨ press keys…`. |
| Any chord during a capture | Takes the chord as the value and ends the capture. |
| Escape during a capture | Cancels and sends `closed`. |
| Backspace on the field | Clears the chord. |
| Left click | Starts a capture. |

Theme roles: `accent` while capturing, `warning` for a conflict, `muted` when disabled.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Shortcuts─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Split pane</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">[ Ctrl+Shift+K ]</span> │
│ Rename pane <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ ⌨ press keys… ] │
│ Toggle tree <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………</span> [ Ctrl+B ]  <span class="t-warn">! used by tree.toggle</span> │
│ <span class="t-dim">Zoom</span> <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">[ not set ]</span> │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The key-capture widget in four states: a bound chord with focus, capturing, a chord that the kernel keymap already uses, and a disabled field. While capturing, the next chord is taken as the value.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let chord = tree.key_capture().chord(self.chord.clone()).reserved_check(true).key("chord");
// ("chord", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(c)) => self.chord = Some(c).filter(|c| !c.is_empty()),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const chordField = keyCapture({ key: 'chord', chord: state.chord, reservedCheck: true });
// if (key === 'chord' && value.tag === 'text') state.chord = value.val || undefined;
```

### Changing a widget from the plugin

The host applies a user's change at once. To set a value from the plugin, call `set-widget-state(view, key, state)` with the state case that matches the widget. In Rust that is `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui::set_widget_state`, in TypeScript `setWidgetState` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui`.

| Widget | State case | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `toggle` | `checked(bool)` | The flag. |
| `toggle` with `tri-state` | `tri(list<tuple<string, tri-state>>)` | One entry under the id `""`. |
| `choice` | `selected(option<u32>)` | The index. On a catalogue choice use `text(item id)`; `selected(n)` returns `invalid-argument`. |
| `text-input`, `text-area` | `text(string)` | The text. |
| `number` | `number(f64)` | The value. |
| `location-picker` | `geo(option<geo-point>)` | The point. See [Pickers](/pages/widgets-pickers/). |

**Rust**

```rust
ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui::set_widget_state(ViewTarget::Panel("cleanup".into()), "dry-run", WidgetState::Checked(true))?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
setWidgetState({ tag: 'panel', val: 'cleanup' }, 'dry-run', { tag: 'checked', val: true });
```

### Worked example: a cleanup panel

The manifest declares the panel. The `views` export draws it, and the handler stores each change.

```json
{
  "id": "com.example.cleanup",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] },
  "exports": ["views"],
  "contributes": {
    "panels": [{ "id": "cleanup", "title": "Clean up", "modal": true }]
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, ButtonRole, NumberStyle, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Cleanup {
    target_name: String,
    dry_run: bool,
    keep_days: f64,
    shortcut: Option<String>,
}

impl Lifecycle for Cleanup {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        self.keep_days = 30.0;
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for Cleanup {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            match (action.key.as_str(), action.kind, action.value) {
                ("target-name", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(name)) => self.target_name = name,
                ("dry-run", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Flag(on)) => self.dry_run = on,
                ("keep-days", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Number(days)) => self.keep_days = days,
                ("shortcut", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(chord)) => {
                    self.shortcut = Some(chord).filter(|chord| !chord.is_empty());
                }
                ("run", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::None) => {
                    let mode = if self.dry_run { "dry run" } else { "real run" };
                    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("cleanup of {} as {mode}", self.target_name));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for Cleanup {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let name = tree.text_input("Name", self.target_name.clone()).key("target-name");
        let dry_run = tree.toggle("Dry run", self.dry_run).key("dry-run");
        let keep = tree.number("Keep days", self.keep_days).key("keep-days")
            .style(NumberStyle::Slider).minimum(1.0).maximum(365.0).unit("days");
        let shortcut = tree.key_capture().chord(self.shortcut.clone()).key("shortcut");
        let run = tree.button("Run cleanup").key("run").role(ButtonRole::Primary);
        let rows = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical)
            .constraints(vec![Constraint::Length(3), Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(1),
                              Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(3)])
            .child(name).child(dry_run).child(keep).child(shortcut).child(run);
        tree.finish(rows)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { button, keyCapture, layout, number, textInput, toggle, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const state = { targetName: '', dryRun: false, keepDays: 30, shortcut: undefined as string | undefined };

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
      const { key, kind, value } = event.val;
      if (key === 'target-name' && kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'text') state.targetName = value.val;
      else if (key === 'dry-run' && kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'flag') state.dryRun = value.val;
      else if (key === 'keep-days' && kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'number') state.keepDays = value.val;
      else if (key === 'shortcut' && kind === 'changed' && value.tag === 'text') state.shortcut = value.val || undefined;
      else if (key === 'run' && kind === 'activated') {
        log('info', `cleanup of ${state.targetName} as ${state.dryRun ? 'dry run' : 'real run'}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    return tree(
      layout(
        { direction: 'vertical', constraints: [
          { tag: 'length', val: 3 }, { tag: 'length', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 1 },
          { tag: 'length', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 3 } ] },
        [
          textInput('Name', state.targetName, { key: 'target-name' }),
          toggle('Dry run', state.dryRun, { key: 'dry-run' }),
          number('Keep days', state.keepDays, { key: 'keep-days', style: 'slider', minimum: 1, maximum: 365, unit: 'days' }),
          keyCapture({ key: 'shortcut', chord: state.shortcut }),
          button('Run cleanup', { key: 'run', role: 'primary' }),
        ],
      ),
    );
  },
});
```

### What the user sees

- The widgets appear in tree order, top to bottom. Focusable widgets take focus in the [focus order](/pages/ui-model/#focus-order).
- The focused widget uses the accent colour. A text field shows the terminal cursor.
- Typing changes the text on screen at once. The plugin hears nothing until the user pauses for the debounce time.
- A secret field shows dots in place of its text, and the last characters when `reveal-last` is set.
- A disabled widget is dimmed, ignores input and shows its reason as a tooltip.

### Edge cases and errors

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Typed text longer than `max-length` | The host refuses the extra characters. No event is sent. |
| Typed number outside `minimum` and `maximum` | The entry dialog shows its error line and nothing is sent. A step stops at the bound. |
| A `validation` pattern that is not a valid regular expression | `ui.invalid-tree`. The instance traps, the previous tree stays (stale) and one error is logged. |
| Two widgets with the same key anywhere in one view | `ui.duplicate-key`. The instance traps. |
| A tree with more than 4,096 nodes or 1 MiB | `ui.too-large`. The instance traps. |
| `choice` with `selected-id` that is not in `items` | The first option is shown and nothing is sent. |
| `set-widget-state` with a key the view does not have | `not-found` |
| `set-widget-state` with a state the widget does not take | `invalid-argument` |
| An input widget in a settings page | `ui.widget-not-allowed`. The instance traps and the previous tree stays. Use `schema-form`, and `location-picker` with `bind`. |
| The `ui.panels` grant is declined | Every `ui` import returns `not-permitted`, and the panel is not registered. |
| The grant changes during a call | `revoked`. The plugin is activated again. |

Requirement ids for this page: [WID-026], [WID-027]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

# Layout and containers

## Layout and containers

Containers decide where their children go and draw the frames around them. This family has ten widgets. `layout` splits an area into segments, `block` frames one child, `tabs` shows one child per tab, `popup` and `dialog` float above the view, `clear` erases an area, `scrollbar` shows the offset of another widget, `split` divides an area with a draggable divider, `separator` draws a rule, and `scroll-view` scrolls one tall child.

The plugin never sees screen rectangles. It declares the tree, and the host runs the constraint solver, draws the frames and paints them with the user's theme. `views.render` runs when a view opens, after `ui.invalidate`, when the view's area changes and when the theme changes. It does not run on every frame.

## You need

- The `ui.panels` grant ([Panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/)), or `panes.provide-kind` for a pane kind ([Basic panes](/pages/capability-panes-provide-kind/)). Both are client-side (`side = "client"`).
- Rust with the `ilium-plugin-sdk` crate, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. The builders fill every default listed on this page.
- The layout types `Area`, `Constraint`, `Direction`, `Flex`, `Spacing` and `Margin`. [Layout constraints](/pages/layout/) explains them.
- The [widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/) for the rules that all widgets share: keys, host-owned state and `ui-action` events.

Text values in the examples are plain strings. In WIT they are `styled-text`. Use `span()` in TypeScript or `Span::styled` in Rust for a fragment with its own colour.

## The shape of a block

## The ten widgets

| Widget | Mirrors | Children | Sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layout` | `ratatui::layout::Layout` | one per constraint, in order | nothing |
| `block` | `ratatui::widgets::Block` | zero or one | nothing |
| `tabs` | `ratatui::widgets::Tabs` | one per title; only the selected one draws | `selected` |
| `popup` | `Clear` plus `Block` | one | `closed` |
| `clear` | `ratatui::widgets::Clear` | none | nothing |
| `scrollbar` | `ratatui::widgets::Scrollbar` | none | `scrolled` |
| `split` | Ilium pane split geometry | exactly two | `resized` |
| `separator` | Ilium `─` rule | none | nothing |
| `dialog` | Ilium dialog frame and button row | zero or one (the body) | `activated`, `closed` |
| `scroll-view` | Ilium scroll regions | one | `scrolled` |

Keys, mouse input and theme roles follow the [widget input map](/pages/reference-widget-input-map/). Each widget below lists them again.

## layout

`layout` runs the constraint solver. It takes one child per constraint, in order. [Layout constraints](/pages/layout/) shows six renders and the rules of the solver.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `horizontal` or `vertical` | The axis of the split. |
| `constraints` | `list<constraint>` | One entry per child. |
| `flex` | `legacy`, `start`, `end`, `center`, `space-between`, `space-around` or `space-evenly` | Where leftover cells go. Default `start`. |
| `spacing` | `space(u16)` or `overlap(u16)` | The gap, or the overlap, between segments. Default `space(0)`. |
| `margin` | `horizontal`, `vertical` (both `u16`) | Cells removed from the area before the split. Default 0 by 0. |

Actions: none. Keys: none. Theme roles: none. It draws nothing itself. A `popup` or `dialog` child occupies its slot as empty space; give it `length(0)` to take none.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">0         1         2         3         4         5
012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789</span>
╭─ Sidebar ────────╮╭─ Body ───────────────────────────────╮
│Agents            ││Select a session to read it.          │
│Sessions          ││                                      │
│                  ││                                      │
╰──────────────────╯╰──────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 60 columns. A horizontal layout with <code>length(20)</code> and <code>fill(1)</code>. The sidebar keeps 20 cells and the body takes the other 40.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let root = tree
    .layout(Direction::Horizontal, [Constraint::Length(20), Constraint::Fill(1)])
    .child(sidebar)
    .child(body);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const root = layout({
  direction: 'horizontal',
  constraints: [length(20), fill(1)],
}, [sidebar, body]);
```

## block

`block` draws its border and titles around one child. A title sits on the top or bottom line and aligns left, centre or right.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `borders` | flags `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` | Edges that draw a line. Default: all four. |
| `border-type` | `plain`, `rounded`, `double`, `thick`, `quadrant-inside` or `quadrant-outside` | The line set. Default `rounded`. |
| `titles` | `list<block-title>` | Each title has `text`, `position` (`top` or `bottom`) and `alignment`. Default: none. |
| `padding` | `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` (all `u16`) | Cells between the border and the child. Default 0. |
| `style`, `border-style` | `style` record | Colours and modifiers. An empty style inherits the theme. |

The border uses the `border` role. The focused block is the innermost block whose area contains the focused node. Its border and title use the `accent` role, and its title is also bold. Actions: none.

### Block titles

- A left-aligned title draws starting at x+1 as `─`, a space, the title, a space.
- A right-aligned title ends at the last cell before the corner, mirrored: the title, a space, then `─` against the corner.
- A centred title is centred on the inner width, with an odd remainder going right.
- A title wider than the inner width minus 4 is cut to that width minus 1, plus `…`.
- Several titles at the same position are joined by one `─`.

### Border sets

The host frame is always rounded. A plugin `block` defaults to rounded and may use any of the six `border-type` cases. Each case draws these corners and edges.

| `border-type` | Top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right | Horizontal edge (top, bottom) | Vertical edge (left, right) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plain` | `┌ ┐ └ ┘` | `─` `─` | `│` `│` |
| `rounded` | `╭ ╮ ╰ ╯` | `─` `─` | `│` `│` |
| `double` | `╔ ╗ ╚ ╝` | `═` `═` | `║` `║` |
| `thick` | `┏ ┓ ┗ ┛` | `━` `━` | `┃` `┃` |
| `quadrant-inside` | `▗ ▖ ▝ ▘` | `▄` `▀` | `▐` `▌` |
| `quadrant-outside` | `▛ ▜ ▙ ▟` | `▀` `▄` | `▌` `▐` |

<figure>
<pre class="term">┌────┐ ╭────╮ ╔════╗
│    │ │    │ ║    ║
└────┘ ╰────╯ ╚════╝
┏━━━━┓ ▗▄▄▄▄▖ ▛▀▀▀▀▜
┃    ┃ ▐    ▌ ▌    ▐
┗━━━━┛ ▝▀▀▀▀▘ ▙▄▄▄▄▟
</pre>
<figcaption>The six border types at 6 by 3 cells: plain, rounded, double, thick, quadrant-inside and quadrant-outside.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Host frame

The host draws a frame around every panel, popup and dialog. It is not a plugin `block`. The top edge is, from the left: `╭`, two spaces, `≡` (the frame menu, a click target, `accent` role), one space, `●` (the view state: `success` role when live, `warning` role when stale), one space, `·` (`muted`), one space, the title (`foreground`, bold when focused), then `─` up to the corner `╮`. In stable-glyph mode `≡` becomes `=`, `●` becomes `*` and `·` becomes `-`. The title is cut with `…` so the edge keeps at least one `─`. A plugin `block` title instead draws as `╭─ Title ─…╮`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                          │
│  Compiled 14 crates                                      │
│  Warnings are listed below                               │
│                                                          │
╰───────────────────────────────────────────── 3 warnings ─╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 60 columns. A rounded block with padding 1 by 2, a top title at the left and a bottom title at the right. The border uses the <code>border</code> role, or <code>accent</code> and bold while the block has focus.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let frame = tree
    .block()
    .title("Build")
    .padding(Padding { left: 2, right: 2, top: 1, bottom: 1 })
    .child(report);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const frame = block({
  titles: [
    { text: 'Build', position: 'top', alignment: 'left' },
    { text: '3 warnings', position: 'bottom', alignment: 'right' },
  ],
  padding: { left: 2, right: 2, top: 1, bottom: 1 },
}, [report]);
```

## tabs

`tabs` shows every title in a strip. The host keeps the selected index as the widget state `tab(u32)`. Give each tab one child, in title order; only the selected child draws. The number of titles MUST equal the number of children, otherwise the instance traps with `ui.invalid-tree`. There is no action-id prop: the widget's `key` names the tabs in `ui-action` events.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `titles` | `list<styled-text>` | One title per tab. |
| `divider` | string | The text between titles. Default `│`. |
| `padding-left`, `padding-right` | `u16` | Cells around each title. Default 1 and 1. |
| `highlight-style` | `style` | The style of the selected title. Default: the selection colours. |

The strip takes row 0 of the area, and the selected child gets rows 1 to the end. The strip draws, for each tab, the left padding, the title and the right padding, with the divider (`│`, `muted`) between tabs only. Titles that overflow are cut from the right, with `…` as the last cell. The selected title uses `highlight-style` (default: the `selection` role).

Actions: `selected` with `index(u32)`, the newly selected tab. Keys: Left and Right step tabs without wrapping, Home and End, and Ctrl+PageUp and Ctrl+PageDown from inside a child. Mouse: a click on a title selects it. Roles: `muted` for other titles, `selection` for the selected one, `border` for the divider.

<figure>
<pre class="term"> Agents <span class="t-dim">│</span><span class="t-hi"> Sessions </span><span class="t-dim">│</span> Costs
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  12 sessions in this project                             │
│  Sorted by last activity                                 │
│                                                          │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 60 columns. The selected title is drawn with the selection colours (lavender background in the dark theme). Only the child of the selected tab is drawn.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let root = tree
    .tabs(["Agents", "Sessions", "Costs"])
    .key("views")
    .child(agents)
    .child(sessions)
    .child(costs);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const root = tabs(['Agents', 'Sessions', 'Costs'], { key: 'views' }, [agents, sessions, costs]);
```

To pick the tab from code, call `ui.set-widget-state` with `tab(1)` on the key `views`. The tab count must match the child count.

## popup

`popup` is drawn only while `ui.open-popup` has it open, and `ui.close-popup` hides it again. Open popups form a stack, and the topmost one takes input first. The `id` is the name both calls use. It is the `key` of the popup node and is unique across the open views of one plugin instance. A view may have at most 4 popups open.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Names the popup. It equals the node key. Unique across the open views of the plugin. |
| `title` | `option<styled-text>` | Text on the top border. Default: none. |
| `modal` | `bool` | When true, input stays in the popup. Default: true. |
| `width`, `height` | `constraint` | The size, see [Popup size and placement](#popup-size-and-placement). Default: 60% each. |

`open-popup-with` takes an anchor and options. The anchors are `centered((width, height))`, `at-cell((column, row))`, `below-key("key")`, `at-key("key")`, `at-tree-node(node)` and `at-pointer`. The options are `modal`, `pinnable`, `dismiss-on-leave` and `close-on-escape`. [The UI model](/pages/ui-model/) explains each anchor.

Actions: `closed` with `none` when the host closes the popup, for example after Escape. Escape follows the order in [Escape](/pages/ui-model/#escape), and a modal popup cannot refuse the close. A click outside closes a non-modal popup. `close-popup` sends nothing. Roles: `border`, and `accent` for the title.

### Popup size and placement

- **Size.** `centered(w, h)` overrides the spec width and height. Every other anchor uses the spec width and height. A percentage is relative to the view area. The default is `percentage(60)` by `percentage(60)`. The result is clamped to [3, view width] by [3, view height] cells.
- **Placement.** `below-key` places the popup at the row under the key's area, with the left edge aligned. `at-key`, `at-cell`, `at-tree-node` and `at-pointer` place its top-left corner at the anchor cell.
- **Fit.** If the popup does not fit below, it flips to above. It then shifts left or up to stay inside the view.
- **Options.** Options passed to `open-popup-with` override the spec fields `modal` and `close-on-escape`.
- **Layout.** A popup or dialog child takes no space in its parent's layout. The slot still gets its constraint's cells and is drawn blank. The popup draws only while open, at its anchor, above all content.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Build output ───────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│compiling ilium-core                                          │
│compiling ilium-detect                                        │
│linking ilium╭  ≡ ● · Delete 3 files?───────────╮             │
│running 14 te│                                  │             │
│finished in 4│  <span class="t-dim">Esc Cancel</span>   <span class="t-err">Enter Delete</span>       │             │
│             │                                  │             │
│Build finishe╰──────────────────────────────────╯             │
│                                                              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 64 columns. A modal popup centred over a view. The popup clears its cells first, so no text of the view shows inside it. The danger button uses the <code>danger</code> role.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
// Declare the popup in the tree, then open it from an event handler.
let confirm = tree.popup("confirm-delete").title("Delete 3 files?").modal(true).child(buttons);
ui::open_popup("confirm-delete", PopupAnchor::Centered((Constraint::Length(36), Constraint::Length(5))))?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const confirm = popup('confirm-delete', { title: 'Delete 3 files?', modal: true }, [buttons]);
openPopup('confirm-delete', { tag: 'centered', val: [length(36), length(5)] });
```

A non-modal popup anchored to a hovered row is the usual way to show details:

<figure>
<pre class="term">▼ Ilium
›   ⠋ Fix auth
›     Shell
    ╭─ Session stats ──────────────────╮

## clear

`clear` erases every cell of its area. It has no props and no children. Use it when a notice must hide content drawn earlier in the same view.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog 0123456789        │
│Second row of bac╭─ Notice ─────────────────╮to the right     │
│Third row of back│  Saved                   │o the right      │
│Fourth row of bac╰──────────────────────────╯to the right     │
│Fifth row of background text that continues to the right      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 64 columns. The notice draws a <code>clear</code> first, so the text behind it is erased inside the frame and stays visible outside it.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let erase = tree.clear();
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const erase = clear();
```

Actions: none. Keys and mouse: none.

## scrollbar

`scrollbar` has no content of its own. It draws the scroll offset of the widget named by `target-key`, so the thumb always shows where that widget is.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `orientation` | `vertical-right`, `vertical-left`, `horizontal-bottom` or `horizontal-top` | Where the bar draws. Default `vertical-right`. |
| `target-key` | string | The key of a scrollable widget in the same view. |

The track is the last column of the scrolling node's own area (the first column with position left) and spans the node's full height. Let T be the track length, V the viewport rows and C the content rows. When C <= V, no bar is drawn and the column belongs to the content. Otherwise `thumb_len = max(1, floor(T*V/C))` and `thumb_start = round((T-thumb_len)*offset/(C-V))`. The track draws `│` (`muted`) and the thumb draws `┃` (`accent` when the node is focused, else `foreground`). There are no arrows. In stable-glyph mode the track is `|` and the thumb is `#`. While the user drags the thumb it uses `accent`. A drag moves the target; a click on the track pages. The scrollable widget sends `scrolled` with `index(u32)`, the new top row offset. The host coalesces bursts of wheel events.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Log ────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│Line 03: compiling ilium-core                            <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│Line 04: compiling ilium-detect                          <span class="t-hi">┃</span>│
│Line 05: compiling ilium-server                          <span class="t-hi">┃</span>│
│Line 06: compiling ilium-client                          <span class="t-hi">┃</span>│
│Line 07: compiling ilium-ipc                             <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│Line 08: compiling ilium-pty                             <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│Line 09: linking                                         <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│Line 10: done                                            <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 60 columns. A <code>vertical-right</code> scrollbar drawn inside the border. The thumb <code>┃</code> sits on the track <code>│</code>; the log holds 20 rows and 8 are visible, scrolled to offset 2. With T=8, V=8 and C=20, `thumb_len` is 3 and `thumb_start` is 1.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let bar = tree.scrollbar(ScrollbarOrientation::VerticalRight, "log").key("log-bar");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const bar = scrollbar('log', { orientation: 'vertical-right', key: 'log-bar' });
```

## split

`split` divides its area between exactly two children and lets the user move the divider. It mirrors the pane split of the Ilium tree. The divider position is host state `widget-state::split(u16)`, in per mille; the host keeps it under the key, so it survives a re-render.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `horizontal` or `vertical` | `horizontal` puts the children side by side. |
| `position` | `u16` | The initial divider position in per mille, 50 to 950. Default 500. |
| `min-first`, `min-second` | `u16` | Minimum size of each child, in cells. |
| `resizable` | `bool` | Whether the user can move the divider. Default true. |

Let A be the area length along the split axis. `first = floor((A-1)*position/1000)`, the divider takes 1 cell, and `second = A-1-first`. Then `first` is clamped to [`min-first`, A-1-`min-second`]; if both minimums cannot fit, `first` gets `min-first` and `second` gets the rest. The divider draws `│` for a horizontal split and `─` for a vertical one (`muted`; `accent` when focused or dragged). It is focusable and draggable only when `resizable` is true. During a drag the grip `┃` or `━` shows.

Actions: `resized` with `number(f64)`, the new position in per mille (the value is `split(position)` as host state), sent when a drag or a key press ends. Keys: with the divider focused, Left and Right (or Up and Down) move `position` by 50, and Home or End move it to the minimum bounds. Mouse: drag the divider.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭──────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────╮
│Explorer                          <span class="t-hi">┃</span>Preview                │
│src/                              <span class="t-hi">┃</span>fn main() {            │
│  main.rs                         <span class="t-hi">┃</span>  run();               │
│  lib.rs                          <span class="t-hi">┃</span>}                      │
│tests/                            <span class="t-hi">┃</span>                       │
╰──────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 60 columns. A horizontal <code>split</code> at position 600 per mille. The divider is <code>│</code> at rest; while it is hovered or dragged the host draws the grip <code>┃</code> in the accent colour (shown here). The two panels share the divider column.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let root = tree
    .split(Direction::Horizontal)
    .key("main-split")
    .position(600)
    .min_first(20)
    .min_second(16)
    .child(explorer)
    .child(preview);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const root = split({
  direction: 'horizontal',
  key: 'main-split',
  position: 600,
  minFirst: 20,
  minSecond: 16,
}, [explorer, preview]);
```

## separator

`separator` draws a one-cell rule, with an optional label.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `horizontal` or `vertical` | A horizontal rule is `─`, a vertical rule is `│`. |
| `label` | `option<styled-text>` | Text centred on a horizontal rule. |
| `style` | `style` | Overrides the `border` role. |

Actions, keys and mouse: none. It is allowed in settings views.

<figure>
<pre class="term">  src/main.rs
<span class="t-dim">── Selected file ─────────────────────────────────────────</span>
  fn main() {}
<span class="t-dim">──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 58 columns. A horizontal <code>separator</code> with a label, and one without. A vertical separator is one column of <code>│</code>.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let rule = tree.separator(Direction::Horizontal).label("Selected file");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const rule = separator({ direction: 'horizontal', label: 'Selected file' });
```

## dialog

`dialog` is a modal frame with a title, an optional body and a button row. It is opened like a popup, with `open-popup` and its key as popup id, and it is always modal.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `styled-text` | Text on the top border. |
| `kind` | `plain`, `confirm` or `danger-confirm` | `confirm` and `danger-confirm` add two buttons: `cancel` (`is-cancel`, label Cancel) and `ok` (primary, label OK, or Delete for `danger-confirm`). `danger-confirm` styles the frame and `ok` with the `danger` role and focuses Cancel first. |
| `buttons` | `list<dialog-button>` | Each has `id`, `label`, `role` (`primary`, `secondary` or `danger`) and `is-cancel`. |
| `width`, `height` | `constraint` | The size of the frame. |
| `message` | `option<styled-lines>` | Text above the buttons. |

The body is zero or one child. The dialog's action key is its node key. Actions: `activated` with `text(button id)` when a button runs, and `closed` with `none` when the dialog closes without a button. Keys: Escape sends `activated` with `text(id of the is-cancel button)`, or `closed` when there is no `is-cancel` button. Enter on a focused button activates that button, and Enter while focus is in the body activates the primary button. Left and Right move between buttons. Mouse: click a button. Roles: `border`, `accent` for the primary button, and `danger` for a danger button and for a `danger-confirm` frame.

The host draws the hint line `Esc cancel · Enter <primary label>` in the `muted` role on the last inner row. The buttons draw on the row above it, centred, as their labels separated by three spaces.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Delete file?──────────────────────────────╮
│  notes-2026-10.md will be removed.               │
│  This cannot be undone.                          │
│                                                  │
│                 <span class="t-dim">Cancel</span>   <span class="t-err">Delete</span>                  │
│<span class="t-dim"> Esc cancel · Enter Delete                        </span>│
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 52 columns. A <code>danger-confirm</code> dialog. The frame is drawn with the <code>danger</code> role, the Cancel button is neutral, the Delete button uses the <code>danger</code> role, and the dim hint line repeats the keys. Cancel has focus first.</figcaption>
</figure>

A `plain` dialog can hold a body widget such as a `text-input`:

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · New session───────────────────────────────╮
│ ╭  ≡ ● · Name──────────────────────────────╮     │
│ │Fix auth                                      │ │
│ ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯ │
│                 <span class="t-dim">Cancel</span>   <span class="t-hi">Create</span>                  │
│<span class="t-dim"> Esc cancel · Enter Create                        </span>│
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 52 columns. A <code>plain</code> dialog with a <code>text-input</code> as its body and two buttons. The primary button uses the <code>accent</code> role, and Enter in the text field activates it.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let dialog = tree
    .dialog("delete-file", "Delete file?")
    .kind(DialogKind::DangerConfirm)
    .message("notes-2026-10.md will be removed.\nThis cannot be undone.")
    .width(Constraint::Length(52))
    .height(Constraint::Length(7));
ui::open_popup("delete-file", PopupAnchor::Centered((Constraint::Length(52), Constraint::Length(7))))?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts

  title: 'Delete file?',
  kind: 'danger-confirm',

  height: length(7),

openPopup('delete-file', { tag: 'centered', val: [length(52), length(7)] });
```

## scroll-view

`scroll-view` lays out its one child at `content-rows` height and clips it to its area. The child can be taller than the view. The host keeps the first visible row as `widget-state::offset(u32)`.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `content-rows` | `u32` | The height at which the child is laid out. |
| `show-scrollbar` | `bool` | Draw the scrollbar. Default true. |
| `follow-tail` | `bool` | Keep the last row visible while the user is at the bottom. |

Keys go to the focused node first. Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home and End that the focused node does not consume bubble to the nearest ancestor `scroll-view`. Up and Down scroll 1 row, the Page keys scroll V-1 rows, and the mouse wheel scrolls 3 rows. When focus moves to a descendant, the `scroll-view` adjusts `offset` so that the descendant's area is fully visible, aligning to its top. The child is laid out at width A-1 when the scrollbar is visible and at width A otherwise; its height is `content-rows`. The scrollbar follows the [scrollbar drawing rule](#scrollbar).

Actions: `scrolled` with `index(u32)`, the first visible row. Keys: Up and Down, PageUp and PageDown, Home and End. Mouse: the wheel, and a drag of the scrollbar. Roles: `border` and `muted`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Job log, following the tail ────────────────────────────╮
│ 07 12:01:44 indexed 412 sessions                        <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│ 08 12:01:45 wrote cost table                            <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│ 09 12:01:45 wrote token table                           <span class="t-dim">│</span>│
│ 10 12:01:46 checking quotas                             <span class="t-hi">┃</span>│
│ 11 12:01:47 quota ok                                    <span class="t-hi">┃</span>│
│ 12 12:01:47 done                                        <span class="t-hi">┃</span>│
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 60 columns. A <code>scroll-view</code> with <code>follow-tail</code>. With V=6 and C=12 the thumb has length 3 and sits at the bottom, so the newest rows are visible. If the user scrolls up, following stops until the thumb returns to the bottom.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let log = tree.scroll_view(240).key("job-log").follow_tail(true).child(log_lines);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const log = scrollView({ contentRows: 240, key: 'job-log', followTail: true }, [logLines]);
```

## Hover and tooltips on containers

Any node can carry a `tooltip` of at most 200 Unicode scalar values, and the `hover-events` and `pointer-events` flags. Containers are no exception: a `block` with a tooltip shows it when the pointer rests on the block for 500 ms. The tooltip box, its size and its placement follow [Hover and tooltips](/pages/ui-model/#hover-and-tooltips).

<figure>
<pre class="term">Threshold too low. <span class="t-hi">Apply 180k</span><span class="t-dim">  (hover)</span>
            ╭──────────────────────────────╮
            │ Writes the recommended       │
            │ threshold                    │
            ╰──────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered below the hovered span after 500 ms. A tooltip is a rounded block with one cell of horizontal padding. It is placed one row below the pointer cell, or above it when there is no room.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Paint order and overlap

Nodes paint in pre-order, so a later sibling overdraws an earlier one cell by cell. With `overlap(n)` between bordered blocks, shared cells use the box-drawing merge rule. In a horizontal layout the shared vertical edge becomes `┬` at the top and `┴` at the bottom. In a vertical layout the shared horizontal edge becomes `├` at the left and `┤` at the right. Rounded corners that become joints use the plain joints. When the two border types differ, the later sibling's glyph wins. Popups, then tooltips, paint after all content.

## Builder defaults

The WIT records have no defaults. The SDK builders fill these, so a plugin sets only what differs.

| Widget | Defaults |
|---|---|
| `layout` | `flex` start, `spacing` `space(0)`, `margin` 0 by 0 |
| `block` | all four borders, `border-type` rounded, no titles, padding 0, empty styles |
| `tabs` | divider `│`, padding 1 and 1, highlight style = selection colours |
| `popup` | no title, `modal` true, width and height 60% |
| `scrollbar` | `orientation` vertical-right |
| `split` | `position` 500, `resizable` true |
| `dialog` | `kind` plain, no message |
| `scroll-view` | `show-scrollbar` true, `follow-tail` false |

## Worked example in Rust

A client view with a split between a list and a log, the log in a scroll view, under a two-tab strip. A Delete button opens a danger dialog.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{DialogKind, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct BuildPanel;

impl Lifecycle for BuildPanel {}

impl Handler for BuildPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if action.key == "delete" {
                let anchor = PopupAnchor::Centered((Constraint::Length(52), Constraint::Length(7)));
                if let Err(error) = ui::open_popup("delete-file", anchor) {
                    log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("open_popup failed: {error:?}"));
                }
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for BuildPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let files = tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("src/")]]).key("files");
        let log_text = tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("Line 01: starting the build")]]);
        let log = tree.scroll_view(240).key("log").follow_tail(true).child(log_text);
        let split = tree.split(Direction::Horizontal).key("main-split").position(400).child(files).child(log);
        let costs = tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("Costs this week")]]);
        let tabs = tree.tabs(["Log", "Costs"]).key("views").child(split).child(costs);
        let delete = tree.button("Delete").key("delete");
        let dialog = tree
            .dialog("delete-file", "Delete file?")
            .kind(DialogKind::DangerConfirm)
            .message("This cannot be undone.");
        let root = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(0)])
            .child(delete)
            .child(tabs)
            .child(dialog);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

The dialog sits in a `length(0)` slot, so it takes no space until `open-popup` shows it.

## Worked example in TypeScript

The same view.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { openPopup } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import {
  button, dialog, fill, layout, length, paragraph, scrollView, span, split, tabs, tree,
} from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || event.val.key !== 'delete') continue;
      try {
        openPopup('delete-file', { tag: 'centered', val: [length(52), length(7)] });
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', String(error));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    const files = paragraph([[span('src/')]], { key: 'files' });
    const logText = paragraph([[span('Line 01: starting the build')]]);
    const logView = scrollView({ contentRows: 240, key: 'log', followTail: true }, [logText]);
    const main = split({ direction: 'horizontal', key: 'main-split', position: 400 }, [files, logView]);
    const costs = paragraph([[span('Costs this week')]]);
    const views = tabs(['Log', 'Costs'], { key: 'views' }, [main, costs]);
    const confirm = dialog('delete-file', {
      title: 'Delete file?',
      kind: 'danger-confirm',
      message: 'This cannot be undone.',
    });
    return tree(layout({
      direction: 'vertical',
      constraints: [length(1), fill(1), length(0)],
    }, [button('Delete', { key: 'delete' }), views, confirm]));
  },
});
```

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A `layout` has a different number of children from constraints | `ui.invalid-tree`. The instance traps. The builders stop the render first and name the layout key. |
| A `ratio` has denominator 0 | `ui.invalid-tree`. The instance traps. |
| The tree has more than 4,096 nodes or 1 MiB | `ui.too-large`. The instance traps. |
| Two nodes anywhere in one tree share a `key` | `ui.duplicate-key`. The instance traps. |
| A `split` has a number of children other than two | `ui.invalid-tree`. The instance traps. |
| A `tabs` has a different number of titles and children | `ui.invalid-tree`. The instance traps. |
| A `split` position outside 50 to 950 | The host clamps it. |
| `min-first` and `min-second` need more cells than the area has | The host shrinks both, and the divider cannot move. |
| A constraint asks for more cells than the area has, or the area has zero columns or rows | The solver clips it, or nothing is drawn. No error. |
| `ui.open-popup` names an id missing from the view's last tree | `not-found`. |
| A fifth popup is opened in one view | `quota-exceeded`. The limit is 4 popups per view. |
| Two open views of the plugin hold a popup with the same key | `invalid-argument` from `open-popup`. |
| `ui.close-popup` names a popup that is not open | Nothing happens. No error. |
| `ui.set-widget-state` names an unknown key | `not-found`. |
| `ui.set-widget-state` gives a state the widget does not take, such as `tab(1)` on a `paragraph` | `invalid-argument`. |
| A `scrollbar` names a `target-key` that is not in the view | Nothing is drawn. No error. |
| A `popup` or `dialog` sits in a `layout` | The slot gets its constraint's cells and is drawn blank. Use `length(0)` to take none. |
| A `popup` or `dialog` in a settings page | `ui.widget-not-allowed`. The instance traps and the previous tree stays. |

## What the user sees

- Host frames are always rounded. A plugin `block` is rounded unless `border-type` says otherwise. The focused frame is cyan and bold in the default theme.
- A popup draws over the view, which stays visible behind it. A modal popup blocks input to that view.
- A resize triggers one new `render` with the new area, at most one per 16 ms. Until it returns, the host lays out the previous tree in the new area, so the screen never shows a stale size. The scrollbar thumb follows the target's offset.
- The divider of a `split` highlights when the pointer is on it, and keeps its position when the plugin redraws.
