# Media and embedded views

## Media and embedded views

Five widgets show things that text and tables cannot. `image` shows a picture from the package, a file or encoded bytes. `surface` shows pixels that the plugin draws itself, with an optional glyph plane and owner ids. `code-view` shows a text buffer with the native editor, read-only or editable. `terminal-view` shows an existing pane, read-only or interactive. `video` plays a clip from the package, a file or a range of a file.

| Widget | Shows | The plugin supplies |
|---|---|---|
| `image` | A picture | An asset path, an `fs-path`, decoded pixels or encoded bytes |
| `surface` | Pixels the plugin writes | Rows of pixels with `ui.write-surface`, glyph cells, owner ids |
| `code-view` | A text buffer | A buffer id |
| `terminal-view` | A live view of a pane | A pane node id |
| `video` | A clip | An asset, a file or a file range |

`image` mirrors ratatui-image's `StatefulImage`, and `surface` mirrors the Ilium frame surface. The editing and terminal widgets mirror the native views, so a plugin sees keystrokes only through the events of the grants it holds.

## You need

- The `ui.panels` grant for a panel, settings page or onboarding step. A pane kind that shows these widgets needs `panes.provide-kind` instead. Both are client-side grants.
- `fs.read` for the scope of an `fs-path` image or video source. Package assets need no grant, because `fs.read:package` is always granted.
- For `code-view`: `editor.edit` to show a buffer that the plugin created with `create-buffer`, and `editor.read` to show any other buffer or to receive `editor-changed` events.
- For `terminal-view`: `terminal.read-screen`, and `terminal.raw-input` for `interactive`.
- For `video`: `media.video`. Without `audio.playback` the video is always muted.
- The SDK for Rust (`ilium-plugin-sdk`) or TypeScript (`@ilium/plugin-sdk`). The worked examples use the builders from `ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build`.

Without a grant, the widget draws an empty frame with the text `not permitted`.

## Properties

Every widget takes an optional `key`. The host keeps widget state by key, and actions name the key. Set the `focusable` flag on a `surface` or `image` that sends clicks.

| Widget | Property | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `source` | `image-source` | required | `asset(string)`, `fs-path(fs-path)`, `rgba(decoded-image)` or `bytes(list<u8>, string)`. |
| `image` | `fit` | `contain`, `cover` or `fill` | `contain` | How the picture meets the area. |
| `surface` | `format` | `pixel-format` | required | `mask8`, `mono1`, `gray8`, `rgb8` or `rgba8`. |
| `surface` | `min-columns`, `min-rows` | `u16` | 1 | Size in cells. |
| `surface` | `glyph-plane` | `bool` | `false` | Allow `write-glyphs`. |
| `surface` | `owner-ids` | `bool` | `false` | Allow `set-owner-ids` and pointer hit tests. |
| `code-view` | `buffer` | `buffer-id` | required | The buffer to show. |
| `code-view` | `read-only` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the user can type. |
| `code-view` | `line-numbers` | `bool` | `true` | Whether line numbers are shown. |
| `code-view` | `wrap` | `bool` | `false` | Whether long lines wrap. |
| `code-view` | `minimap` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a minimap is drawn at the right edge. |
| `terminal-view` | `pane` | `node-id` | required | The existing pane to show. |
| `terminal-view` | `rows` | `option<u16>` | none | Height in rows. Without it the view fills the area. |
| `terminal-view` | `interactive` | `bool` | `false` | Forward keys and mouse to the program. Needs `terminal.raw-input`. |
| `terminal-view` | `scrollback` | `bool` | `false` | Allow scrolling the history. |
| `terminal-view` | `highlights` | `option<string>` | none | Name of an own highlight layer. |
| `video` | `source` | `video-source` | required | `asset(string)`, `fs(fs-path)` or `range(fs-path, u64, option<u64>)`. |
| `video` | `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `controls` | `bool` | `false` | Playback options. Rust spells `loop` as `looped`. |
| `video` | `fit` | `contain`, `cover` or `fill` | `contain` | How the frame meets the area. |

The pixel size of a surface is `min-columns` and `min-rows` multiplied by the sub-cell factor of the user's active dither mode, so it depends on that setting. The plugin asks for the size with `ui::surface_size` and does not compute it.

## Actions and events

| Widget | Sends | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `activated` when focusable | `cell(cell-position)` | Pictures are otherwise not interactive. |
| `surface` | `activated` on a click | `cell(cell-position)`, relative to the surface | Needs `focusable`. |
| `surface` | `pointer` | `pointer(view-pointer)` | With the `pointer-events` flag. The receipt names the owner id under the pointer. |
| `surface` | `scrolled` on the wheel | `number(f64)`, notches since the last action | Negative up, positive down. Coalesced. |
| `code-view` | no `ui-action` | none | Changes arrive as `editor-changed` events, debounced by 100 ms. |
| `terminal-view` | `activated` | `none` | A request to focus the view. |
| `video` | `changed` on seek | `number(f64)`, the position in ms | |
| `video` | `activated` | `none` | Play or pause. |

## Keys, mouse and roles

| Widget | Keys | Mouse | Theme |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image`, `surface` | none | click | The shared look and dithering apply. |
| `code-view` | The editor's keys. | The editor's mouse rules. | The `syntax-*` roles and the gutter in `muted`. |
| `terminal-view` | None, or all keys when `interactive`. | Click focuses. With `interactive` the mouse goes to the program. | The terminal colours of the pane. |
| `video` | Space play or pause, Left and Right seek 5 s. | Click toggles play. | The shared look. The progress line is `━` and `─`. |

An interactive `terminal-view` forwards keys and mouse to the pane's program while it has focus. Press Escape twice to leave it.

## image

An asset is a path relative to the package's `assets/` folder, for example `asset("icons/logo.png")`, and the file must be listed in the package `files` inventory. An `fs-path` names a file under a file scope and needs the `fs.read` grant. `rgba` carries decoded pixels, and `bytes` carries an encoded PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP up to 16 MiB with its MIME type.

The host decodes the first frame with the limits of `codec.decode-image`: input up to 16 MiB and up to 67,108,864 pixels. The decoded picture is kept until the source changes. Supported formats are PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and BMP.

- `contain` keeps the aspect ratio. Unused cells keep the cell background.
- `cover` keeps the aspect ratio and crops the overflow equally at both ends.
- `fill` stretches the picture to the area.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Logo ─────────────────────────────────╮
│          <span class="t-hi">      ▄▄▄▄▄▄      </span>            │
│          <span class="t-hi">   ▄██▀▀▀▀▀▀██▄   </span>            │
│          <span class="t-hi">  ██▀  ▄▄▄▄  ▀██  </span>            │
│          <span class="t-hi">  ██   ▀██▀   ██  </span>            │
│          <span class="t-hi">  ▀██▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄██▀  </span>            │
│          <span class="t-hi">     ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀     </span>            │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 42 columns. An <code>image</code> fitted with <code>contain</code>. The host draws the picture with half blocks when the terminal has no graphics protocol, and the empty margin keeps the cell background.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
// types::ui::{ImageSource, MediaFit}
let logo = tree
    .image(ImageSource::Asset("icons/logo.png".into()))
    .fit(MediaFit::Contain)
    .key("logo");
let avatar = tree.image(ImageSource::Bytes(png_bytes, "image/png".into())).key("avatar");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const logo = image({ tag: 'asset', val: 'icons/logo.png' }, { key: 'logo', fit: 'contain' });
const avatar = image({ tag: 'bytes', val: [pngBytes, 'image/png'] }, { key: 'avatar' });
```

## surface

A `surface` has a fixed pixel format. The plugin writes rows of pixels into it with `ui::write_surface(view, key, first_row, format, data)` in Rust, or `writeSurface(view, key, firstRow, format, data)` in TypeScript. The host converts those pixels to cells with the shared look and dithering.

| Format | Bytes per pixel | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `mask8` | 1 | Coverage from 0 to 255. 255 is fully on. |
| `mono1` | 1 bit | One bit per pixel, most significant bit first. Each row is padded to a whole byte, so a row is `ceil(width / 8)` bytes. |
| `gray8` | 1 | One tone per pixel. |
| `rgb8` | 3 | Red, green, blue. |
| `rgba8` | 4 | Red, green, blue, alpha. |

A row holds `width` pixels, where `width` is the pixel width from `ui::surface_size(view, key)`. The `data` must hold whole rows, and `first-row` plus the number of rows written must stay inside `height`.

A click on a focusable surface arrives as `activated` with `cell(cell-position)`, the column and row relative to the surface. A wheel movement arrives as `scrolled`.

### Glyph plane and owner ids

A surface created with `glyph-plane: true` accepts glyph cells. `write-glyphs` takes a list of `glyph-cell` records (`column`, `row`, `text`, `fg`, `bg`, `add`) with at most 131,072 cells per frame, and `clear-glyphs` removes them. The cells are drawn over the pixel layer after dithering and the shared look, with icon widths, and their colours go through the shared look too. Without `glyph-plane`, `write-glyphs` returns `unsupported`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Board ────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-dim">░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░</span> │
│ <span class="t-hi">      ♜ ♞ ♝ ♛ ♚ ♝ ♞ ♜             </span> │
│ <span class="t-hi">      ♟ ♟ ♟ ♟ ♟ ♟ ♟ ♟             </span> │
│ <span class="t-dim">░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░</span> │
│ <span class="t-dim">░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░</span> │
╰────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 38 columns. A <code>surface</code> with <code>glyph-plane</code>. The pixel layer is the background, and the glyph cells are drawn over it after dithering. Glyph colours go through the shared look.</figcaption>
</figure>

A surface created with `owner-ids: true` accepts `set-owner-ids(first-row, ids)`, one `u16` per pixel, where 0 means none. After a frame, `last-receipt` returns a `frame-receipt` with `frame`, `presented-at-millis`, `dropped-before` and `pointer-owner`. A plugin that sets the `pointer-events` flag can hit-test a click on a logical object without keeping a copy of the frame. The same calls exist on scene surfaces, described in [Primitives](/pages/primitives/).

**Rust**

```rust
// host::ui, types::ui::{GlyphCell, PixelFormat}
let board = tree
    .surface(PixelFormat::Rgb8)
    .min_columns(40)
    .min_rows(12)
    .glyph_plane(true)
    .owner_ids(true)
    .key("board")
    .flags(NodeFlags::FOCUSABLE | NodeFlags::POINTER_EVENTS);

// After render, in an event handler:
ui::write_glyphs(panel_view(), "board", &[GlyphCell {
    column: 3, row: 1, text: "N".into(), fg: Some(0xffffff), bg: None, add: Modifiers::BOLD,
}])?;
ui::set_owner_ids(panel_view(), "board", 0, &owner_ids)?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const board = surface({
  key: 'board',
  format: 'rgb8',
  minColumns: 40,
  minRows: 12,
  glyphPlane: true,
  ownerIds: true,
  flags: { focusable: true, pointerEvents: true },
});

// After render, in an event handler:
writeGlyphs(panelView(), 'board', [
  { column: 3, row: 1, text: 'N', fg: 0xffffff, bg: undefined, add: { bold: true } },
]);
setOwnerIds(panelView(), 'board', 0, ownerIds);
```

## code-view

A `code-view` shows the buffer as the native editor does. The user types, moves the cursor, selects and undoes natively. Set `read-only: false` and hold `editor.edit` to make it a text editor. The plugin learns about changes through `editor-changed`, which carries `buffer`, `revision`, `first-line` and `last-line` but not the text. The plugin reads the lines it needs with the editor primitive ([Editor primitive](/pages/primitives-editor/)). Syntax colours come from the `token-provider` exports of languages that plugins declare.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ notes.md ─────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-dim">  1 </span># Plugin notes                         │
│ <span class="t-dim">  2 </span>                                       │
│ <span class="t-dim">  3 </span>The build uses the release profile.    │
│ <span class="t-dim">  4 </span>The cursor sits on line four.▏         │
│ <span class="t-dim">  5 </span>                                       │
│ <span class="t-dim">  6 </span>- check the grant list                 │
│ <span class="t-dim">  7 </span>- run the probe                        │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 46 columns. A <code>code-view</code> with line numbers. The gutter uses <code>muted</code>. Syntax colours come from the <code>syntax-*</code> theme roles.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let buffer = editor::create_buffer("# Plugin notes\n", Some("markdown"))?;
let notes = tree
    .code_view(buffer)
    .read_only(false)
    .line_numbers(true)
    .wrap(true)
    .minimap(true)
    .key("notes");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const buffer = createBuffer('# Plugin notes\n', 'markdown');
const notes = codeView(buffer, {
  key: 'notes',
  readOnly: false,
  lineNumbers: true,
  wrap: true,
  minimap: true,
});
```

## terminal-view

A `terminal-view` embeds a pane that already exists. It shows the bottom rows of the pane's visible area. With `rows` set, the view is that many rows tall at the top of its area. The view never resizes the pane. By default the view is read-only. With `interactive: true` the view forwards keys and mouse to the pane's program while it has focus, and the plugin needs `terminal.raw-input`. Press Escape twice to leave an interactive view.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Pane: build ──────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-prompt">$ </span>cargo test                                           │
│    Compiling ilium-core v0.1.0                         │
│     Running unittests src/lib.rs                       │
│ <span class="t-ok">test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed</span>                   │
│                                                        │
│ <span class="t-dim">Keys go to the pane owner, not to the plugin.</span>          │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 58 columns. A read-only <code>terminal-view</code>. The cells use the terminal colours of the pane, not the theme.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let build = tree.terminal_view(self.build_pane).rows(8).key("build");
let shell = tree
    .terminal_view(self.shell_pane)
    .interactive(true)   // needs terminal.raw-input
    .scrollback(true)
    .key("shell");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const build = terminalView(buildPane, { key: 'build', rows: 8 });
const shell = terminalView(shellPane, {
  key: 'shell',
  interactive: true,   // needs terminal.raw-input
  scrollback: true,
});
```

## video

A `video` is decoded natively, and the shared look and dithering apply to its frames. The source is a package asset, a file under a granted scope, or a range of a file given as a start and an optional end in milliseconds. Video bytes up to 16 MiB can also be opened from memory with `media.open-video-bytes`. Playback is always muted unless the plugin holds `audio.playback`. With `controls` the widget draws a progress line of `━` and `─`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Shore ────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-dim">▒▒▒▒▓▓▓▓████▓▓▒▒░░░░▒▒▓▓████▓▓▒▒░░░░▒▒▒▒</span>   │

## Worked example in Rust

The example is a panel with five widgets. It creates a notes buffer on activation and repaints the surface on scroll.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{editor, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ids::BufferId;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{
    ActionKind, ActionValue, MediaFit, ImageSource, PixelFormat, UiTree, VideoSource, ViewTarget,
};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::{NodeFlags, Tree};

const PANEL: &str = "media-demo";
const SCOPE_KEY: &str = "scope";
const SCOPE_COLUMNS: u16 = 40;
const SCOPE_ROWS: u16 = 6;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["lifecycle", "handler", "views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct MediaDemo {
    notes: Option<BufferId>,
    // Set by on_events when the build pane is known, for example from a PaneCreated event.
    build_pane: Option<NodeId>,
    scroll: u32,
}

impl Lifecycle for MediaDemo {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        self.notes = Some(editor::create_buffer("# Plugin notes\n", Some("markdown"))?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for MediaDemo {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            if action.key != SCOPE_KEY {
                continue;
            }
            let (ActionKind::Scrolled, ActionValue::Number(notches)) = (action.kind, action.value)
            else {
                continue;
            };
            // Wheel notches are negative for up and positive for down.
            self.scroll = self.scroll.wrapping_add(notches as i32 as u32);
            self.paint_scope();
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl MediaDemo {
    fn paint_scope(&self) {
        // None until the panel has rendered once.
        let Some((width, height)) = ui::surface_size(panel_view(), SCOPE_KEY) else {
            return;
        };
        let mut tones = Vec::with_capacity((width * height) as usize);
        for row in 0..height {
            for column in 0..width {
                tones.push((column + row + self.scroll) as u8);
            }
        }
        // gray8 is one byte per pixel; the rows start at the top of the surface.
        let _ = ui::write_surface(panel_view(), SCOPE_KEY, 0, PixelFormat::Gray8, &tones);
    }
}

fn panel_view() -> ViewTarget {
    ViewTarget::Panel(PANEL.to_string())
}

impl Views for MediaDemo {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let logo = tree
            .image(ImageSource::Asset("icons/logo.png".to_string()))
            .fit(MediaFit::Contain)
            .key("logo");
        let scope = tree
            .surface(PixelFormat::Gray8)
            .min_columns(SCOPE_COLUMNS)
            .min_rows(SCOPE_ROWS)
            .key(SCOPE_KEY)
            .flags(NodeFlags::FOCUSABLE);
        let clip = tree
            .video(VideoSource::Asset("loops/shore.webm".to_string()))
            .autoplay(true)
            .looped(true)
            .key("clip");
        let notes = match self.notes {
            Some(buffer) => tree.code_view(buffer).read_only(true).key("notes"),
            None => tree
                .paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("Notes are not open yet.")]])
                .key("notes"),
        };
        let build = match self.build_pane {
            Some(pane) => tree.terminal_view(pane).rows(8).key("build-view"),
            None => tree
                .paragraph(vec![vec![Span::plain("No build pane.")]])
                .key("build-view"),
        };
        let top = tree
            .layout(Direction::Horizontal, [Constraint::Length(20), Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(24)])
            .child(logo)
            .child(scope)
            .child(clip);
        let body = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(12), Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(8)])
            .child(top)
            .child(notes)
            .child(build);
        tree.finish(body)
    }
}
```

## Worked example in TypeScript

The TypeScript version builds the same panel with the camelCase builders.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { createBuffer } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/editor';
import { surfaceSize, writeSurface } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { codeView, image, layout, paragraph, surface, terminalView, tree, video }
  from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import { span, type Event, type Submission, type ViewTarget } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const PANEL = 'media-demo';
const SCOPE_KEY = 'scope';
const SCOPE_COLUMNS = 40;
const SCOPE_ROWS = 6;

const state = {
  notes: undefined as bigint | undefined,
  buildPane: undefined as bigint | undefined,
  scroll: 0,
};

function panelView(): ViewTarget {
  return { tag: 'panel', val: PANEL };
}

function paintScope(): void {
  // Undefined until the panel has rendered once.
  const size = surfaceSize(panelView(), SCOPE_KEY);
  if (size === undefined) return;
  const [width, height] = size;
  const tones = new Uint8Array(width * height);
  for (let row = 0; row < height; row += 1) {
    for (let column = 0; column < width; column += 1) {
      tones[row * width + column] = (column + row + state.scroll) & 0xff;
    }
  }
  // gray8 is one byte per pixel; the rows start at the top of the surface.
  writeSurface(panelView(), SCOPE_KEY, 0, 'gray8', tones);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {
    state.notes = createBuffer('# Plugin notes\n', 'markdown');
  },
  deactivate() {
    return undefined;
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action' || event.val.key !== SCOPE_KEY) continue;
      const { kind, value } = event.val;
      if (kind === 'scrolled' && value.tag === 'number') {
        // Wheel notches are negative for up and positive for down.
        state.scroll = (state.scroll + Math.trunc(value.val)) >>> 0;
        paintScope();
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  render(_view: ViewTarget) {
    const logo = image({ tag: 'asset', val: 'icons/logo.png' }, { key: 'logo', fit: 'contain' });
    const scope = surface({
      key: SCOPE_KEY,
      format: 'gray8',
      minColumns: SCOPE_COLUMNS,
      minRows: SCOPE_ROWS,
      flags: { focusable: true },
    });
    const clip = video({ tag: 'asset', val: 'loops/shore.webm' }, {
      key: 'clip', autoplay: true, loop: true,
    });
    const notes = state.notes !== undefined
      ? codeView(state.notes, { key: 'notes', readOnly: true })
      : paragraph([[span('Notes are not open yet.')]], { key: 'notes' });
    const build = state.buildPane !== undefined
      ? terminalView(state.buildPane, { key: 'build-view', rows: 8 })
      : paragraph([[span('No build pane.')]], { key: 'build-view' });
    const top = layout(
      {
        direction: 'horizontal',
        constraints: [
          { tag: 'length', val: 20 }, { tag: 'fill', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 24 },
        ],
      },
      [logo, scope, clip],
    );
    const body = layout(
      {
        direction: 'vertical',
        constraints: [
          { tag: 'length', val: 12 }, { tag: 'fill', val: 1 }, { tag: 'length', val: 8 },
        ],
      },
      [top, notes, build],
    );
    return tree(body);
  },
});
```

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A grant is missing or declined | The widget draws an empty frame with the text `not permitted`. |
| An image asset or file is missing, or its data is corrupt, unsupported or over 16 MiB | The widget draws an empty frame with the text `image not available`. The plugin log gets one warn line that names the source. |
| An `rgba` picture has a length other than `width x height x 4` | The same as a corrupt image. |
| A video source is missing, not decodable or over 16 MiB from bytes | An empty frame, and `invalid-argument` or `quota-exceeded` from the open call. |
| A `code-view` names a buffer that does not exist | Empty frame with the text `not found`. |
| A `terminal-view` names a pane that is closed or was never created | Empty frame with the text `not found`. |
| `interactive` without `terminal.raw-input` | The view stays read-only. |
| `ui.write-surface` names a key with no surface | `not-found`. |
| The format differs from the widget's `format` | `invalid-argument`, nothing written. |
| The data is not a whole number of rows, or is over 16 MiB | `invalid-argument`, nothing written. |
| `first-row` plus the rows written goes past `height` | `invalid-argument`, nothing written. The host never truncates a write silently. |
| `write-glyphs` without `glyph-plane`, or outside the surface | `unsupported` or `invalid-argument`. More than 131,072 cells in a frame gives `quota-exceeded`. |
| The area is smaller than the surface | The surface is clipped at the right and bottom. |
| The area is larger than the surface | The surface is drawn from the top-left corner, and the extra cells keep the cell background. |
| A surface has received no rows | It draws the cell background. |

The `not-found`, `invalid-argument`, `unsupported` and `quota-exceeded` codes are described in [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/). A missing grant or bad source never fails the render, so check the plugin log when a widget stays empty.

## What the user sees

- An image keeps its proportions in `contain` and `cover` modes.
- A surface shows the plugin's picture, recoloured by the user's shared look. The user cannot edit its pixels.
- A code view behaves like the native editor, with typing, selection and undo, unless `read-only` is true.
- A terminal view looks like the pane itself. Its keys go to the pane owner unless the view is interactive.
- A video plays muted in a loop, dithered with the user's settings.

API version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

Requirement ids for this page: [WID-028]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

# Text

## Text

Text widgets show words. Five widgets make up this family. `paragraph` wraps and aligns styled lines, and its spans can be clickable. `markdown` renders a Markdown source with Ilium's own renderer, the same one the help pages use. `leader-row` puts a label and a value on one line with dotted leaders. `key-hints` draws a line of key chords. `diff-view` shows a diff that the plugin supplies.

The plugin describes the text as data inside a UI tree. The host measures the text, wraps it, aligns it and paints it with the active theme. The plugin never computes a line break or a column position.

## You need

- The `ui.panels` grant on the client side, to show a view. A basic pane uses `panes.provide-kind` for its view instead. See [UI panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/).
- The `commands.invoke` grant only when a link, span or key hint runs a command that the plugin does not own. A plugin's own commands need no grant. See [Commands invoke](/pages/capability-commands-invoke/).
- Rust with the `ilium-plugin-sdk` crate, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both build the tree with the same widget names.
- The [widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/) for keys and host-owned state.

Text values are `styled-text`: a list of spans, and each span holds a string and a style. A `styled-lines` value is a list of `styled-text` values, one per line. In Rust, `Span::plain("x")` builds an unstyled span and `Span::styled("x", Style::role(ColorRole::Warning))` builds a coloured one. In TypeScript, `span('x')` and `span('x', { role: 'warning' })` do the same.

A `rich-span` adds two fields to a span: a `target` that makes the span clickable, and a `tooltip`. A `rich-text` is a list of rich spans and a `rich-lines` is a list of those.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/text in reference-wit
record rich-span { text: string, style: style, target: span-target, tooltip: option<string> }
```

The `span-target` cases are `none`, `action(string)`, `command(string)` and `link(string)`. A link opens only through the open-external rules.

## Overview

| Widget | Use it for | Action sent to the plugin |
|---|---|---|
| `paragraph` | Several styled lines in a block, with clickable spans | `scrolled` when `scrollable`; `activated` for an `action` span |
| `markdown` | Help text and rich notes | `activated` for a link with no `link-command`; `toggled` with `task-click` |
| `leader-row` | A label and a read-only value | None |
| `key-hints` | One line of key chords | None. A chord runs its command on the host |
| `diff-view` | A diff that the plugin supplies | `selected` and `activated` with the hunk or line index |

Use a `toggle`, `choice` or `number` widget, not a `leader-row`, when the user must change a value. See [Input](/pages/widgets-input/).

## paragraph

`paragraph` mirrors `ratatui::widgets::Paragraph`. Each entry of `lines` is one line. Set `wrap` when long lines must break at the edge of the widget. Set `scrollable` when the text can be taller than the area. The host then owns the scroll offset.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lines` | `styled-lines` | Required | The lines to show, one entry per line. |
| `rich` | `rich-lines` | none | Lines with clickable spans. When set it replaces `lines`. |
| `wrap` | `option<bool>` | `none` | `none` cuts long lines at the right edge. `some(false)` wraps. `some(true)` wraps and removes leading spaces of wrapped lines. |
| `alignment` | `left`, `center` or `right` | `left` | Horizontal alignment of every line. |
| `style` | `style` | Empty, so the theme applies | Default colours and modifiers. |
| `scrollable` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the host keeps a scroll offset for the widget. |

Keys: Up and Down scroll a scrollable paragraph. Mouse: the wheel scrolls it, and a click on a clickable span activates it. Roles: as styled; a clickable span uses `accent` and an underline.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Server ───────────────────────────────╮
│ Connected to the server.               │
│ Last sync 2026-10-11 14:02:07.         │
│ <span class="t-warn">2 plugins wait for a grant.</span>            │
│ Lines longer than the block wrap to    │
│ the next row.                          │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 42 columns. A <code>paragraph</code> with <code>wrap</code> set inside a block. The warning line uses the <code>warning</code> role.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let status = tree
    .paragraph(vec![
        vec![Span::plain("Connected to the server.")],
        vec![Span::styled("2 plugins wait for a grant.", Style::role(ColorRole::Warning))],
    ])
    .key("status")
    .wrap(Some(true));
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const status = paragraph([
  [span('Connected to the server.')],
  [span('2 plugins wait for a grant.', { role: 'warning' })],
], { key: 'status', wrap: true });
```

### Clickable spans

A span with a `target` becomes clickable. The host draws it in the accent colour with an underline and shows its `tooltip` after 500 ms. Each target behaves in one way.

| Target | A click does |
|---|---|
| `action(id)` | Sends `ui-action` with kind `activated` and the value `text(id)` to the paragraph's key. |
| `command(name)` | Runs the command through the command registry. The plugin receives `command-invoked` with the origin `text`. It needs `commands.invoke` for commands the plugin does not own. |
| `link(url)` | Opens the URL through the open-external rules. |
| `none` | Nothing. |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Advice ───────────────────────────────────╮
│ Threshold too low. <span class="t-hi">Apply 180k</span>              │
│ <span class="t-dim">Hover for details, click to apply.</span>         │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 46 columns. A <code>paragraph</code> with a clickable <code>rich-span</code>. The span is drawn in the accent colour and underlined (shown here as the highlight). A click sends <code>activated</code> with <code>text("apply-180k")</code>.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
// types::text::{RichSpan, SpanTarget}
let advice = vec![vec![
    RichSpan::plain("Threshold too low. "),
    RichSpan::new("Apply 180k", Style::default())
        .target(SpanTarget::Action("apply-180k".into()))
        .tooltip("Writes the recommended threshold and keeps a revert point"),
]];
let text = tree.paragraph(Vec::new()).rich(advice).key("advice");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { paragraph, richSpan } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const text = paragraph([], {
  key: 'advice',
  rich: [[
    richSpan('Threshold too low. '),
    richSpan('Apply 180k', {
      target: { tag: 'action', val: 'apply-180k' },
      tooltip: 'Writes the recommended threshold and keeps a revert point',
    }),
  ]],
});
```

A click arrives as `ui-action { key: "advice", kind: activated, value: text("apply-180k") }`.

When `scrollable` is true, every change of the top row sends a `ui-action` of kind `scrolled` with `index(u32)`, the new top row offset. The host coalesces these events, so a fast wheel sends one event with the latest offset. The plugin reads the offset with `ui::widget_state(view, key)`, which returns `offset(n)`. It moves the view with `ui::set_widget_state(view, key, offset(n))`.

<div class="warn">
<p>A scrollable paragraph without a <code>key</code> loses its offset on every render. Give each scrollable widget a key that is unique across the whole view.</p>
</div>

## markdown

`markdown` mirrors the Ilium Markdown renderer that the help pages use. The host renders `source` with the shared theme, so headings, emphasis and links take their colours from the theme. The plugin never styles the Markdown itself.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string` | Required | The Markdown text to render. |
| `link-command` | `option<string>` | `none` | The command that runs when the user activates a link. |
| `task-click` | `bool` | `false` | Task list items can be clicked. |
| `images` | `bool` | `false` | Images render as pictures instead of their alt text. |
| `base` | `option<fs-path>` | `none` | The folder against which relative image paths are resolved. |

Keys: Up and Down scroll, Tab walks the links and Enter follows one. Mouse: a click on a link or a task box. Roles: the theme's Markdown roles. Bullets are `•` and task boxes are `☐` and `☑`.

A link behaves in one of two ways.

- With `link-command` set, the host runs that command through the command registry on activation. It passes the arguments `{"target": "<link target>"}`. The command must be one of the plugin's own commands or covered by its `commands.invoke` grant. The plugin then receives `command-invoked`.
- Without `link-command`, the plugin receives a `ui-action` of kind `activated` whose value is `text(<link target>)`. The host never opens a browser itself.

With `task-click`, a click on a task item sends `toggled` with `text("<line>")`, the line number of the item. The plugin rewrites its source, for example `- [ ]` to `- [x]`, and renders again. With `images`, an image written as `![alt](asset:path)`, or a file inside a granted `fs` scope, renders through the rules of the `image` widget. Any other image shows its alt text.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Help: keys ─────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Keys</span>                                                 │
│                                                      │
│ Ctrl+B is the prefix key.                            │
│ • Tab moves focus between panes                      │
│ ☑ Read the key list                                  │
│ ☐ Remap one key                                      │
│ See the <span class="t-hi">command list</span>.                                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 56 columns. A <code>markdown</code> view with <code>task-click</code>. The heading and the link text use the theme. Bullets are <code>•</code> and task boxes are <code>☐</code> and <code>☑</code>.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let notes = tree
    .markdown(self.source.clone())
    .key("notes")
    .task_click(true)
    .images(true);

// In on_events:
if let (ActionKind::Toggled, ActionValue::Text(line)) = (action.kind, action.value) {
    if let Ok(line_number) = line.parse::<usize>() {
        self.toggle_task(line_number);
        ui::invalidate(view.clone());
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const notes = markdown(source, { key: 'notes', taskClick: true, images: true });

// In onEvents:
if (action.key === 'notes' && action.kind === 'toggled' && action.value.tag === 'text') {
  toggleTask(Number(action.value.val));
  ui.invalidate(view);
}
```

The props table has no scroll setting for a source taller than the area, so the host scrolls it with the keys above.

## leader-row

`leader-row` mirrors the `leader_span` helper that every settings row uses. The label sits at the left, the value at the right, and grey dotted leaders (the `…` character) fill the gap between them. The rule has four parts.

- One blank cell is left on each side of the dots.
- A gap shorter than five cells stays blank, with no dots.
- Leaders are never part of a hit target.
- Leaders never overwrite label text, glyphs or the value.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `styled-text` | The text at the left. |
| `value` | `styled-text` | The text at the right. |

Roles: `foreground` for the label, `muted` for the leaders, and the value as styled. The widget sends no actions and takes no keys.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Settings ───────────────────────────╮
│ Font size <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………</span> 14 │
│ Restore previous sessions on boot on │
│ Save every <span class="t-dim">………………………………………</span> 5 minutes │
╰──────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 40 columns. Three <code>leader-row</code> widgets. The first and third gaps are five cells or more, so they draw grey <code>…</code> leaders with one blank cell on each side. The second gap is shorter than five cells and stays blank.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let font = tree
    .leader_row(vec![Span::plain("Font size")], vec![Span::plain("14")])
    .key("font-size");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const font = leaderRow([span('Font size')], [span('14')], { key: 'font-size' });
```

When the label and the value together are wider than the row, the label is cut at its right edge first. The value is cut only when it does not fit on its own.

## key-hints

`key-hints` mirrors the status-line hints of the Ilium client. Each hint is a record with three fields: `keys` (the chord text), `label` (the short description) and `command` (an optional command name). The host draws the chords in the accent colour and keeps the whole list on one line, joined by the separator ` · `.

```text
record key-hint { keys: string, label: string, command: option<string> }
```

Pressing a hint's chord while the view has focus runs its `command` through the command registry, and so does a click on the hint. The same grant rule as a markdown link applies. No `ui-action` is sent. A hint with no `command`, or with an empty string, is a label only, and the host draws it in the muted colour. Arrow keys appear as `↑ ↓ ← →` and the page keys as `Pg↑ Pg↓`.

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `hints` | `list<key-hint>` | The hints to show, in display order. |

Roles: `accent` for the keys and `muted` for the labels.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">Enter</span> open · <span class="t-hi">q</span> close · <span class="t-dim">? keys</span>

<span class="t-hi">Enter</span> open · <span class="t-hi">q</span> close · <span class="t-hi">/</span> filter · <span class="t-dim">… 3 more</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Two <code>key-hints</code> lines. The chords use the <code>accent</code> role and the labels use <code>muted</code>. When the row is too narrow the host cuts the list and appends <code>… N more</code>, as in the second line. The last hint of the first line has no command and is a label only.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let hints = tree
    .key_hints(vec![
        KeyHint::new("Enter", "open").command("my.plugin/open"),
        KeyHint::new("q", "close").command("my.plugin/close"),
        KeyHint::new("?", "keys"),
    ])
    .key("hints");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const hints = keyHints([
  { keys: 'Enter', label: 'open', command: 'my.plugin/open' },
  { keys: 'q', label: 'close', command: 'my.plugin/close' },
  { keys: '?', label: 'keys' },
], { key: 'hints' });
```

## diff-view

`diff-view` shows a diff that the plugin supplies. The plugin builds the hunks and the host colours the lines, highlights changed words and draws the tokens of a language.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/ui in reference-wit
record diff-hunk { header: string, lines: list<diff-line> }
record diff-line { kind: diff-line-kind, old-line: option<u32>, new-line: option<u32>, text: string }
enum diff-line-kind { added, removed, context }
```

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `hunks` | `list<diff-hunk>` | The hunks to show. |
| `layout` | `unified` or `split` | One column, or old and new side by side. |
| `language` | `option<string>` | The language whose tokens the host highlights. |
| `word-diff` | `bool` | Highlight the changed words inside a changed line. |

Actions: `selected` with `index(u32)` (the hunk) and `activated` with `index(u32)`. Keys: Up and Down move by line, `n` and `p` jump to the next and the previous hunk, and Enter activates. Mouse: a click on a line. Roles: `success` for added lines, `danger` for removed lines, and `muted` for context and the gutter. The gutter shows `+`, `-` or a blank.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Config diff ──────────────────────────────╮
│<span class="t-dim">@@ -11,3 +11,3 @@ [budget]</span>                  │
│<span class="t-dim"> 11  11   [budget]</span>                          │
│<span class="t-err"> 12     - threshold = 150000</span>                │
│<span class="t-ok">     12 + threshold = 180000</span>                │
│<span class="t-dim"> 13  13   unit = "tokens"</span>                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 46 columns. A unified <code>diff-view</code>. Added lines use <code>success</code>, removed lines use <code>danger</code>, and context and the gutter use <code>muted</code>. The gutter shows the old and new line numbers and the mark <code>+</code>, <code>-</code> or a blank.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─ Config diff ───────────────────────────────────────╮
│<span class="t-dim">@@ -11,3 +11,3 @@                                    </span>│
│<span class="t-dim"> 11   [budget]            </span>│<span class="t-dim"> 11   [budget]            </span>│
│<span class="t-err"> 12 - threshold = 150000  </span>│<span class="t-ok"> 12 + threshold = 180000  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim"> 13   unit = "tokens"     </span>│<span class="t-dim"> 13   unit = "tokens"     </span>│
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 55 columns. The same diff with <code>layout: split</code>. The old text is on the left and the new text on the right, with one <code>│</code> divider between them.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
// types::ui::{DiffHunk, DiffLine, DiffLineKind, DiffLayout}
let hunk = DiffHunk {
    header: "@@ -11,3 +11,3 @@ [budget]".into(),
    lines: vec![
        DiffLine::context(11, 11, "[budget]"),
        DiffLine::removed(12, "threshold = 150000"),
        DiffLine::added(12, "threshold = 180000"),
        DiffLine::context(13, 13, "unit = \"tokens\""),
    ],
};
let diff = tree
    .diff_view(vec![hunk])
    .layout(DiffLayout::Split)
    .language("toml")
    .word_diff(true)
    .key("diff");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { diffView } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const hunk = {
  header: '@@ -11,3 +11,3 @@ [budget]',
  lines: [
    { kind: 'context', oldLine: 11, newLine: 11, text: '[budget]' },
    { kind: 'removed', oldLine: 12, text: 'threshold = 150000' },
    { kind: 'added', newLine: 12, text: 'threshold = 180000' },
    { kind: 'context', oldLine: 13, newLine: 13, text: 'unit = "tokens"' },
  ],
};
const diff = diffView([hunk], { key: 'diff', layout: 'split', language: 'toml', wordDiff: true });
```

## Worked example in Rust: a server status panel

A client view with a status paragraph, a clickable fix, a settings-style row and a hint line.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::{RichSpan, SpanTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, ActionValue, UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::{KeyHint, Tree};

const PANEL: &str = "server-status";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ServerStatus {
    threshold: u32,
}

impl Handler for ServerStatus {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::UiAction(action) = event else { continue };
            let (ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(id)) = (action.kind, action.value) else { continue };
            if action.key == "advice" && id == "apply-180k" {
                self.threshold = 180_000;
                ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Panel(PANEL.to_string()));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for ServerStatus {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let advice = vec![vec![
            RichSpan::plain("Threshold too low. "),
            RichSpan::new("Apply 180k", Style::default())
                .target(SpanTarget::Action("apply-180k".into()))
                .tooltip("Writes the recommended threshold"),
        ]];
        let text = tree.paragraph(Vec::new()).rich(advice).key("advice");
        let value = format!("{}", self.threshold);
        let row = tree.leader_row(vec![Span::plain("Threshold")], vec![Span::plain(value)]).key("threshold");
        let hints = tree
            .key_hints(vec![KeyHint::new("Enter", "apply").command("server-status/apply")])
            .key("hints");
        let body = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical, [Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(1)])
            .child(text)
            .child(row)
            .child(hints);
        let root = tree.block().title("Server").child(body);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

## Worked example in TypeScript: a help view with tasks

A help view that renders a Markdown checklist and rewrites the source when a task is clicked.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import * as ui from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { block, keyHints, layout, markdown, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import { fill, length } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const PANEL = 'help';
let source = ['# Keys', '', 'Ctrl+B is the prefix key.', '- [x] Read the key list', '- [ ] Remap one key'].join('\n');

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
      const action = event.val;
      if (action.key !== 'help-text' || action.kind !== 'toggled' || action.value.tag !== 'text') continue;
      const lines = source.split('\n');
      const index = Number(action.value.val);
      lines[index] = lines[index].includes('[ ]')
        ? lines[index].replace('[ ]', '[x]')
        : lines[index].replace('[x]', '[ ]');
      source = lines.join('\n');
      ui.invalidate({ tag: 'panel', val: PANEL });
    }
    return [];
  },
  render() {
    const body = markdown(source, { key: 'help-text', taskClick: true });
    const hints = keyHints([{ keys: 'Esc', label: 'close' }], { key: 'hints' });
    const page = layout({ direction: 'vertical', constraints: [fill(1), length(1)] }, [body, hints]);
    return tree(block({ titles: [{ text: 'Help: keys', position: 'top', alignment: 'left' }] }, [page]));
  },
});
```

The `toggled` value is the zero-based or one-based line number as the host counts it; check it against your own source on the first run, because the specification names it only as the line of the task item.

## Width and language

Every text widget lays out text by cell width, and a wide character takes two cells. A plugin MUST measure text with `display-width` and MUST NOT size a column by character count. [AUT-617] See [Internationalisation](/pages/guide-internationalisation/).

## Edge cases and errors

The text widgets return no error codes of their own. The errors below come from the state calls, the command registry and the tree validator.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Two widgets with the same `key` in one view | The tree is invalid and the instance traps. |
| A tree with more than 4,096 nodes, or a child index out of range | The tree is invalid and the instance traps. |
| A scrollable paragraph with no `key` | Its offset resets on every render. |
| A tooltip longer than 200 characters | Not allowed. The limit is 200 characters. |
| `set-widget-state` with an unknown key | `not-found`. |
| `set-widget-state` with `offset` on a `leader-row` | `invalid-argument`, because the state kind does not fit the widget. |
| A link, span or hint whose command the plugin may not invoke | `not-permitted`. The command does not run. |
| A hint with an empty `command` | A label only, drawn muted, with no action. |
| `rich` and `lines` both set on a paragraph | `rich` is used. |
| Wrap off, and a line wider than the area | The line is cut at the right edge. |
| A paragraph line below the area, and `scrollable` false | The line is not drawn. |
| A leader row with a gap under five cells | The gap is blank and no dots are drawn. |
| Key hints wider than the row | The list is cut and ends with `… N more`. |
| A markdown image outside a granted scope | The alt text shows. |

The limits of the whole tree are in [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/). Trap behaviour is in the [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) and [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/) pages.

## What the user sees

Text takes its colours from the active theme. A clickable span or link is accent coloured and underlined, so it reads as a target; a task box toggles under the pointer; key hints look the same as the hints in the status bar; and a diff is coloured red and green on a muted gutter, like the diff views of the client.

Requirement ids for this page: [WID-025]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

- [Widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/)
- [Layout and containers](/pages/widgets-layout-and-containers/)
- [Media and embedded](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) for `code-view`, the text editor
- [Input](/pages/widgets-input/) for editable values
- [Commands invoke](/pages/capability-commands-invoke/)
- [The UI model](/pages/ui-model/)

API version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Status and feedback

## Status and feedback

Status widgets tell the user that something is happening, that something changed, or that something needs attention. The family has four widgets: `badge`, `spinner`, `notice` and `icon`. They draw small, quiet signs and never take focus unless they have an action.

| Widget | Shows | Event |
|---|---|---|
| `badge` | A dot, a label or a count | `activated` when focusable |
| `spinner` | A moving frame set with an optional label | none |
| `notice` | An inline banner with a tone, text and actions | `activated`, `closed` |
| `icon` | One glyph from a slot or a literal | none |

### You will need

- A view that can hold the widget. All four work in panels, popups, dialogs, pane views and settings pages. See [UI model](/pages/ui-model/).
- For the look in the tree, tabs and toolbars: a badge in a tree row is a decoration, see [Tree decorations](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/).
- A short-lived message that is not part of a view is a toast, see [Toasts](/pages/api-toast/).

### Tone

A tone is one of `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` or `muted`. It sets the colour of a `badge` and the colour, icon and border of a `notice`. The tones map to theme roles, so a plugin never picks a colour.

| Tone | Notice icon | Stable glyph | Theme role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `info` | `ℹ` | `i` | `accent` |
| `success` | `✓` | `+` | `success` |
| `warning` | `!` | `!` | `warning` |
| `danger` | `✗` | `x` | `danger` |
| `muted` | none | none | `muted` |

#### badge

**Purpose.** A small sign next to a name: an unread dot, a count, a short label. A dot is the smallest form. A count above 99 is drawn `99+`. A label is at most 12 cells. A badge with a `key` can take focus and send `activated`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `option<string>` | none | Text of up to 12 cells, drawn in brackets. |
| `count` | `option<u32>` | none | A number. Above 99 it shows `99+`. |
| `dot` | `bool` | `false` | Draws `●` and ignores `label` and `count`. |
| `tone` | `tone` | `info` | The colour. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `activated` | `none` | Enter or a click, when the badge has a `key`. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Enter | Activates a focusable badge. |
| Left click | Focuses and activates. |

Theme roles: the `tone` role.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Badges────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Unread <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">●</span>                             │
│ Messages <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-ok">[ 3 ]</span>                         │
│ Errors <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-err">[ 99+ ]</span>                       │
│ Mode <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………</span> [ new ]                        │
│ Tabs: Agents <span class="t-warn">●</span> │ Notes │ Log <span class="t-ok">[ 2 ]</span>                           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Badges. A dot (first row) is the smallest form. A count is drawn in brackets and shows 99+ above 99. A label of up to 12 cells is drawn the same way. The tone sets the colour: info, success, warning, danger or muted.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let unread = tree.badge().dot(true).tone(Tone::Info);
let errors = tree.badge().count(142).tone(Tone::Danger).key("errors");
let mode = tree.badge().label("new");
// ("errors", ActionKind::Activated, _) => self.show_errors(),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const unread = badge({ dot: true, tone: 'info' });
const errors = badge({ count: 142, tone: 'danger', key: 'errors' });
const mode = badge({ label: 'new' });
// if (key === 'errors' && kind === 'activated') showErrors();
```

#### spinner

**Purpose.** Shows that work is running. The host steps the frames and the plugin makes no calls while it spins. Reduced motion shows one static frame `⠿`, so the spinner stays readable and costs nothing.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | `spinner-frames` | `braille` | `braille`, `blocks`, `moons`, `quarters`, or `custom(list<string>)` of 2 to 16 frames. |
| `interval-ms` | `u16` | `100` | Time per frame, 80 to 1,000. |
| `label` | `option<styled-text>` | none | Text after the frame. |

A spinner has no event, no keyboard input and no mouse input. Theme role: `accent`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Spinner frame sets────────────────────────────────────╮
│ braille    ⠋ ⠙ ⠹ ⠸ ⠼ ⠴ ⠦ ⠧ ⠇ ⠏                               │
│ blocks     ▁ ▂ ▃ ▄ ▅ ▆ ▇ █                                   │
│ moons      🌑 🌒 🌓 🌔 🌕                                    │
│ quarters   ○ ◔ ◑ ◕ ●                                         │
│ reduced    ⠿                                                 │
│                                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi">⠹</span> Indexing 412 sessions                                      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The four built-in frame sets of the spinner, each shown frame by frame, and the single static frame ⠿ that appears when the user prefers reduced motion. The last line shows the spinner in use, frozen on its third frame, followed by its label.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let busy = tree.spinner().frames(SpinnerFrames::Braille).label("Indexing 412 sessions");
let custom = tree.spinner().frames(SpinnerFrames::Custom(vec!["-".into(), "\\".into(), "|".into(), "/".into()]));
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const busy = spinner({ frames: { tag: 'braille' }, label: 'Indexing 412 sessions' });
const custom = spinner({ frames: { tag: 'custom', val: ['-', '\\', '|', '/'] }, intervalMs: 120 });
```

#### notice

**Purpose.** An inline banner inside a view. It has a tone, an optional title, rich text, up to three action buttons and an optional dismiss `✗`. The `notice` row of the Settings screen is the same widget. A dismissal is stored per `id` when the notice is a settings row.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | `tone` | `info` | The colour and the icon. |
| `title` | `option<string>` | none | Bold first line next to the icon. |
| `text` | `rich-lines` | required | The body. Spans can be styled or clickable. |
| `actions` | `list<tuple<string, string>>` | empty | Pairs of id and label. At most 3. |
| `dismissible` | `bool` | `false` | Shows `✗` at the top right. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `activated` | `text(action id)` | An action button is pressed. |
| `closed` | `none` | The user dismisses the notice. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves between the actions. |
| Enter | Presses the focused action. |
| Escape | Dismisses, when `dismissible`. |
| Left click on an action or on `✗` | Presses, dismisses. |

Theme roles: the `tone` role for the icon, the title and the `border`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Notices─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-info">╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮</span> │
│ <span class="t-info">│</span> <span class="t-info">ℹ Update available</span>                                         <span class="t-info">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-info">│</span> Version 0.9.4 is ready.                                    <span class="t-info">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-info">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span> │
│ <span class="t-ok">╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮</span> │
│ <span class="t-ok">│</span> <span class="t-ok">✓ Saved</span>                                                    <span class="t-ok">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-ok">│</span> The settings were written.                                 <span class="t-ok">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-ok">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">│</span> <span class="t-warn">! Privacy</span>                                                  <span class="t-warn">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">│</span> The provider sends place names to photon.komoot.io.        <span class="t-warn">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span> │
│ <span class="t-err">╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮</span> │
│ <span class="t-err">│</span> <span class="t-err">✗ Failed</span>                                                   <span class="t-err">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-err">│</span> The key was rejected by the server.                        <span class="t-err">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-err">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span> │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Four notices in the info, success, warning and danger tones, with the tone icons ℹ ✓ ! ✗ and a border in the tone colour. The title takes the tone colour, the text is plain.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Notice with actions─────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-warn">╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">│</span> <span class="t-warn">! Privacy</span>                                               <span class="t-warn">✗</span>  <span class="t-warn">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">│</span> The provider sends place names to photon.komoot.io.        <span class="t-warn">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">│</span> <span class="t-hi">[ Understood ]</span>  [ Open settings ]                          <span class="t-warn">│</span> │
│ <span class="t-warn">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span> │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A dismissible notice with two actions. The ✗ at the top right closes it and sends closed; each action button sends activated with its id. The first action has focus.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let notice = tree.notice(vec!["The provider sends place names to photon.komoot.io.".into()])
    .tone(Tone::Warning).title("Privacy").dismissible(true).key("privacy")
    .actions(vec![("ok".into(), "Understood".into()), ("settings".into(), "Open settings".into())]);
// ("privacy", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(id)) => self.on_privacy(&id),
// ("privacy", ActionKind::Closed, _) => self.privacy_hidden = true,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const privacyNotice = notice(['The provider sends place names to photon.komoot.io.'], {
  key: 'privacy', tone: 'warning', title: 'Privacy', dismissible: true,
  actions: [['ok', 'Understood'], ['settings', 'Open settings']],
});
// if (kind === 'activated' && value.tag === 'text') onPrivacy(value.val);
// if (kind === 'closed') state.privacyHidden = true;
```

#### icon

**Purpose.** One glyph. It takes a slot name from the user's icon preset, or a literal glyph. A slot follows the preset, so the same slot can show an emoji or a Nerd Font glyph. The host knows the cell width of the glyph and reserves it, so a width-2 emoji does not push the next widget.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required | A slot such as `model.claude`, or a literal glyph. |
| `tone` | `option<tone>` | none | Colours the glyph. |

An icon has no event, no keyboard input and no mouse input. Theme role: the `tone` role, or `foreground`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Icons─────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Slot model.claude <span class="t-dim">……………………</span> 🦀  Claude                        │
│ Slot model.codex <span class="t-dim">………………………</span> 🐢  Codex                         │
│ Slot status.done <span class="t-dim">………………………</span> 🔔  Done                          │
│ Slot status.idle <span class="t-dim">………………………</span> ●  Idle                           │
│ Glyph "★" <span class="t-dim">………………………………………</span> ★  Bookmark                        │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The icon widget. A slot glyph follows the user icon preset, so the same slot can show an emoji or a Nerd Font glyph. Widths follow the host icon width rules: the emoji take two cells and the label starts after them.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let claude = tree.icon("model.claude");
let star = tree.icon("★").tone(Tone::Warning);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const claude = icon('model.claude');
const star = icon('★', { tone: 'warning' });
```

### Worked example: a progress notice

The plugin shows a spinner while it indexes and a notice when it ends. The failure case has a retry action.

**Rust**

```rust
impl Views for Indexer {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let body = match &self.state {
            State::Running(count) => tree.spinner().label(format!("Indexing {count} sessions")).into_node(),
            State::Failed(reason) => tree.notice(vec![reason.clone()]).tone(Tone::Danger)
                .title("Indexing failed").actions(vec![("retry".into(), "Retry".into())]).key("failed").into_node(),
            State::Done(count) => tree.notice(vec![format!("{count} sessions indexed")])
                .tone(Tone::Success).dismissible(true).key("done").into_node(),
        };
        tree.finish(body)
    }
}
// ("failed", ActionKind::Activated, ActionValue::Text(id)) if id == "retry" => self.start(),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
render() {
  const body =
    state.kind === 'running' ? spinner({ label: `Indexing ${state.count} sessions` })
    : state.kind === 'failed'
      ? notice([state.reason], { key: 'failed', tone: 'danger', title: 'Indexing failed', actions: [['retry', 'Retry']] })
      : notice([`${state.count} sessions indexed`], { key: 'done', tone: 'success', dismissible: true });
  return tree(body);
}
// if (key === 'failed' && kind === 'activated' && value.val === 'retry') start();
```

### Edge cases and errors

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| A badge label longer than 12 cells | Truncated with `…`. |
| A notice with more than 3 actions | `invalid-argument` on render. |
| A spinner with fewer than 2 or more than 16 custom frames | `invalid-argument` on render. |
| A spinner `interval-ms` outside 80 to 1,000 | Clamped. |
| Reduced motion | A spinner shows `⠿`. A tone keeps its colour. |
| An icon slot that does not exist | The slot name is drawn as text. |

# Pickers

## Pickers

A picker is an input that opens a dialog drawn by the host. The plugin shows a closed field and hears only the result. This page documents three widgets, `color-picker`, `path-field` and `location-picker`, and three uses of `choice` that the Settings screen shows as pickers: the palette picker, the dither picker and the icon picker. Their dialogs are kernel code, so the look, the keys and the network rules are the same as in the Settings screen, and a plugin cannot change them.

| Picker | Widget | Dialog | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colour | `color-picker` | hue strip, shade strip, swatches, hex field | `text(#rrggbb)` |
| Path | `path-field` | the kernel file picker | `text(display path)` |
| World map | `location-picker` | Braille map, address search, coordinates | `geo(geo-point)` |
| Palette | `choice` over `ilium.palettes` | choice dialog with swatches | `text(palette id)` |
| Dither | `choice` over `ilium.dithers` | choice dialog with patterns | `text(dither id)` |
| Icon | `choice` over `ilium.icons` | choice dialog with a List and Grid switch | `text(icon id)` |

### You will need

- The `ui.panels` grant for a view that holds the picker. See [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/).
- `fs.pick` for the file picker of a `path-field`. See [fs.pick](/pages/capability-fs-pick/).
- `location.geocode` for the address search of a `location-picker`, and `location.observer` for its `Use current location` button. See [location.geocode](/pages/capability-location-geocode/) and [location.observer](/pages/capability-location-observer/).
- Catalogue ids for the choice pickers. The host publishes `ilium.palettes`, `ilium.dithers` and `ilium.icons`. A plugin can add its own catalogue, see [Catalogues](/pages/api-catalogs/).

### Settings pages

A settings page accepts `location-picker`, and no other picker. Its value is written only through the `bind` prop to an own `location` key, and the host validates and saves it as it does for a row. For the other pickers use the matching settings row: `color`, `path`, `choice` with a catalogue source. See [Settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/).

#### color-picker

**Purpose.** Edits a colour as `#rrggbb`. The closed field shows a swatch `██` and the hex text. Enter opens the host colour dialog with a hue strip, a shade strip, a row of swatches and a hex field. The dialog is true colour, so the capture shows only its glyphs. The Ilium client has no colour dialog of its own yet, so the render follows the specification on this page.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | required | The colour as `#rrggbb`. |
| `palette` | `option<string>` | none | A catalogue id of preset swatches. |
| `allow-theme-roles` | `bool` | `false` | Adds the theme roles (`accent`, `border`) to the swatches. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `text(#rrggbb)` | The user applies a colour in the dialog. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Enter | Opens the dialog. |
| Tab | Cycles the dialog fields: hue, shade, swatches, hex. |
| Left, Right, Up, Down | Move the hue, shade or swatch. |
| Typing in the hex field | Sets the colour. A value that is not `#rrggbb` is refused. |
| Enter in the dialog | Applies. |
| Escape | Cancels. |
| Click on a swatch, drag in a strip | Pick. |

Theme roles: the picked colour for the swatch, `border` for the dialog frame, `danger` for an invalid value.

<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Colour rows───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Accent</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">[ ██ #7aa2f7 ]</span> │
│ Border <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ ██ #4a4a4a ] │
│ Marker <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-err">[ ██ #zzzzzz ]</span> │
│ <span class="t-dim">Background</span> <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">[ ██ #1a1b26 ]</span> │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

**Rust**

```rust
let accent = tree.color_picker("#7aa2f7").key("accent").palette("ilium.palettes").allow_theme_roles(true);
// ("accent", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(hex)) => self.accent = hex,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const accent = colorPicker('#7aa2f7', { key: 'accent', palette: 'ilium.palettes', allowThemeRoles: true });
// if (key === 'accent' && value.tag === 'text') state.accent = value.val;
```

#### path-field

**Purpose.** Chooses a file or a folder. The field shows a display text and a `…` button. The text is only a label: the plugin never sees the raw path, only a picked scope that `fs.pick` created. This keeps a plugin from reading outside the paths the user chose.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `path-kind` | required | `open-file`, `open-directory` or `save-file`. |
| `value` | `option<fs-path>` | none | The picked scope. |
| `display` | `string` | empty | The text shown. |
| `extensions` | `list<string>` | empty | File extensions the picker offers. |
| `editable` | `bool` | `false` | Lets the user type a path. The host resolves it. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `text(display path)` | The user picks a path. |
| `submitted` | `text(display path)` | Enter in an editable field. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Enter on the button | Opens the host file picker. |
| Typing | Edits the text when `editable`. |
| Click on `…` | Opens the file picker. |

Theme roles: `foreground` for the text, `danger` for a path the plugin reports as missing.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Path rows─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">Project folder</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-hi">[ ~/dev/ilium ] [ … ]</span> │
│ Export file <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> [ report.html ] [ … ] │
│ Backup folder <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-err">[ /data/old-backups ] [ … ]</span> │
│ <span class="t-dim">Cache folder</span> <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-dim">[ ~/.cache/demo ] [ … ]</span> │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The path-field widget. The text is the display string and the … button opens the host file picker. The error row names a path the plugin has reported missing. The plugin never sees the raw path: the picked scope is what it receives.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
let export = tree.path_field(PathKind::SaveFile).key("export").display(&self.export_name).extensions(vec!["html"]);
// ("export", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Text(name)) => self.export_name = name,
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const exportField = pathField('save-file', { key: 'export', display: state.exportName, extensions: ['html'] });
// if (key === 'export' && value.tag === 'text') state.exportName = value.val;
```

#### location-picker

**Purpose.** Picks a point on the world. The host draws the real Ilium world map in Braille dots, a crosshair `┼`, an address search and a coordinates mode. The plugin receives only the point. Geocoding runs in the host with Photon and falls back to Nominatim. The user agrees once to send place names to that provider.

**The map.** The land is a Braille mask of 360 by 180 samples, one per degree, taken from the same data as the ambient world map scene. Each Braille cell holds 2 by 4 dots, and a dot is set when land covers at least half of its area. The equator and the prime meridian are drawn as `─` and `│` lines. The crosshair `┼` is drawn in the accent colour at the selected point. Land is `muted` and the sea is the background. The Selected row names the place and shows the point.

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `option<geo-point>` | none | The point: `latitude` and `longitude` in degrees. |
| `label` | `option<string>` | none | The place name shown in the Selected row. |
| `search` | `bool` | `false` | Shows the Address search. Needs `location.geocode`. |
| `allow-current` | `bool` | `false` | Adds `Use current location`. Needs `location.observer`. |
| `zoom` | `bool` | `false` | Lets the wheel zoom the map. |
| `bind` | `option<string>` | none | An own `location` key. Used in settings pages only. |

| Event | Value | Sent when |
|---|---|---|
| `changed` | `geo(geo-point)` | The crosshair moves to a new point. |
| `submitted` | `geo(geo-point)` | The user presses `Use location`. |

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Arrows | Move the crosshair by one Braille dot. Shift moves by 10 dots. |
| Tab | Switches between Address and Coordinates. |
| Typing in Address | Searches after 300 ms and lists up to 5 results. |
| Up, Down in the results | Choose a result. |
| Enter | Uses the highlighted result, or confirms the point (`Use location`). |
| Escape | Cancels. |
| Left click on the map | Sets the point. |
| Mouse wheel | Zooms, when `zoom` is true. |

Theme roles: `muted` for land, `background` for the sea, `accent` for the crosshair, `danger` for an error message.

Inside a settings page the picker is smaller and writes through `bind`, so the plugin receives `settings-changed` and reads the point from its own `location` key.

Geocoding limits: 1 request per second per plugin, a 24 hour cache by query text, a 10 s timeout. Without consent the search returns `not-permitted`. Errors appear in the status line under the buttons: `network`, `rate-limited` with the wait time, `timed-out`.

**Rust**

```rust
let place = tree.location_picker().key("place").value(self.point).label("Paris, France")
    .search(true).allow_current(true).zoom(true);
// ("place", ActionKind::Changed, ActionValue::Geo(point)) => self.point = Some(point),
// ("place", ActionKind::Submitted, ActionValue::Geo(point)) => self.apply(point),
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const place = locationPicker({
  key: 'place', value: state.point, label: 'Paris, France', search: true, allowCurrent: true, zoom: true,
});
// if (value.tag === 'geo') { if (kind === 'changed') state.point = value.val; else apply(value.val); }
```

For a settings page the same widget binds to a key:

**Rust**

```rust
let place = tree.location_picker().key("place").bind("home_location");
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const place = locationPicker({ key: 'place', bind: 'home_location' });
```

### Choice pickers

The palette, dither and icon pickers are not separate widgets. They are a `choice` with `style: "dialog"`, a catalogue `source` and a `preview` on each item, see [Input](/pages/widgets-input/) for the full prop list. The host reads the items in pages as the user scrolls. The dialog filters with the `Search:` line, marks the current item with `●`, and shows the status line `N of M options · Current: X`.

#### Palette picker

The palette catalogue `ilium.palettes` holds 38 presets. Each item has a `swatch` preview of 1 to 16 colours, drawn as a strip of half blocks coloured with the stops of the palette. A scene or widget that uses colour reads the chosen palette and recolours itself. The first item keeps the scene colours.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Palette───────────────────────────────────────────╮

│   Pastel rainbow   ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀                          │
│   Cotton candy     ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀                          │
│   Sea glass        ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀                          │
│   Sunset           ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀                          │
│ 38 of 38 options · Current: Scene colors                 │
│ Enter applies · Esc cancels                              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>A choice over the ilium.palettes catalogue with swatch previews. The names are the first entries of the real list; each swatch is a strip of half blocks coloured with the stops of the palette (1 to 16 colours). The first entry keeps the scene colours and has no swatch.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

let palette = tree.choice("Palette", Vec::<String>::new(), 0).key("palette")
    .source("ilium.palettes").style(ChoiceStyle::Dialog).filter(true).selected_id(&self.palette);

#### Dither picker

The dither catalogue `ilium.dithers` lists every matrix and error-diffusion mode. Each item has a `pattern` preview of 1 to 4 lines of at most 8 cells, drawn by the host from the algorithm. Dithering is global in Ilium, so a plugin never implements it. It only offers the choice.

#### Icon picker

The icon catalogue `ilium.icons` holds about 12,000 glyphs. Each item has a `glyph` preview. With `view-modes` the dialog gets the `View` row `← List → +` that switches between a list and a grid. The glyphs are normal UTF-8 icons. The stable alternative appears only when the user has chosen it.
