## You will need

- The grant `editor.read` in `capabilities.client`. It is a client-side grant only. A server-side plugin that asks for it fails with `manifest.grant-side`.
- Rust 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, or Bun 1.2 or later for TypeScript. The SDK pins the rest of the toolchain.
- The SDK module `ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor` in Rust, or `@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor` in TypeScript.
- [panes.read](/pages/capability-panes-read/) if the plugin needs to know which pane a buffer belongs to.
- `editor.edit` only when the plugin also changes text.

## Grant syntax

`editor.read` takes no argument. The valid form is:

- `editor.read`

The invalid form `editor.read:project` fails the build with this text:

`capability "editor.read" takes no argument (got "editor.read:project")`

Buffers are chosen by id or by pane, not by a grant argument. A file in the project is read through a file scope such as `fs.read:project`, which is a different grant.

## The surface

The `editor` primitive offers these functions on the client side. Every function is synchronous. The functions with a result return an error code. The others return a plain value.

| Rust | TypeScript | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor::buffers()` | `buffers()` | `Vec<BufferRef>` / `BufferRef[]` | Every open buffer. |
| `editor::buffer_for_pane(pane)` | `bufferForPane(pane)` | `Option<BufferRef>` / `BufferRef \| undefined` | The buffer shown in one pane. |
| `editor::read_lines(buffer, first_line, count)` | `readLines(buffer, firstLine, count)` | `Result<Vec<String>, PluginError>` / `string[]`, throws | Up to `count` lines from `first_line`. |
| `editor::selections(buffer)` | `selections(buffer)` | `Vec<TextRange>` / `TextRange[]` | The selected ranges of the buffer. |
| `editor::set_decorations(buffer, layer, items)` | `setDecorations(buffer, layer, items)` | `Result<(), PluginError>` / `void`, throws | Styled ranges with optional hover text. |
| `editor::set_gutter(buffer, layer, marks)` | `setGutter(buffer, layer, marks)` | `Result<(), PluginError>` / `void`, throws | Icons in the gutter, each with an optional tooltip and command. |

The records used by these functions are:

| Record | Fields (Rust, TypeScript) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `BufferRef` | `buffer` (u64, bigint), `pane` (option of node id), `path` (option of path), `language` (option of string), `revision` (u64), `line_count` / `lineCount` (u32), `dirty` (bool) | The description of one buffer. `revision` rises with every change. |
| `TextPosition` | `line`, `column` (u32) | A position. Columns count Unicode scalar values. |
| `TextRange` | `start`, `end` (`TextPosition`) | A range in one buffer. |
| `RangeDecoration` | `range` (`TextRange`), `style` (`Style`), `hover` (option of string) | A styled range. |
| `GutterMark` | `line` (u32), `icon` (Tabler icon name), `tooltip` (option of string), `command` (option of command id) | One icon in the gutter of a line. |

### Events

The grant opens four events, delivered to the `on-events` export of the `handler` trait:

| Event | Rust variant | TypeScript tag and payload | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor-opened` | `Event::EditorOpened(BufferRef)` | `'editor-opened'`, `BufferRef` | Never dropped. |
| `editor-closed` | `Event::EditorClosed(BufferRef)` | `'editor-closed'`, `BufferRef` | Never dropped. |
| `editor-changed` | `Event::EditorChanged(EditorChangedEvent)` | `'editor-changed'`, `buffer`, `revision`, `firstLine`, `lastLine` | Coalesced by buffer, debounced by 100 ms. |
| `editor-saved` | `Event::EditorSaved(EditorSavedEvent)` | `'editor-saved'`, `buffer`, `path` | Never dropped. |

`first_line` and `last_line` of `editor-changed` are both inside the changed range.

A plugin that offers the `annotator` export also needs this grant. The kernel calls the annotator for the visible lines of a buffer at most once every 100 ms. Without the grant the manifest fails with `manifest.export-grant`.

## Limits

- `read_lines` takes at most 10,000 lines per call. A larger `count` is `invalid-argument`.
- `set_decorations` and `set_gutter` take at most 10,000 items per layer. A larger list is `invalid-argument`.
- Each plugin owns its layers. A layer name is any string the plugin chooses. The decorations and marks of a layer are cleared when the plugin stops.

## Worked example: marking error lines in Rust

This client plugin reads the lines of every changed range and puts a gutter icon on each line that
contains ` ERROR `. The manifest requests the grant and exports nothing optional.

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "client": ["editor.read"]
  },
  "client": {
    "entry": "client.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::editor::{self, GutterMark};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::EditorChangedEvent;

const LOG_LAYER: &str = "log-levels";
const MAX_LINES_PER_READ: u32 = 10_000;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct LogLevels;

impl Lifecycle for LogLevels {}

impl Handler for LogLevels {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::EditorChanged(EditorChangedEvent { buffer, first_line, last_line, .. })
                = event
            else {
                continue;
            };
            let count = (last_line - first_line + 1).min(MAX_LINES_PER_READ);
            let Ok(lines) = editor::read_lines(buffer, first_line, count) else {
                continue;
            };
            let marks: Vec<GutterMark> = lines
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .filter(|(_, text)| text.contains(" ERROR "))
                .map(|(offset, _)| GutterMark {
                    line: first_line + offset as u32,
                    icon: "alert-triangle".into(),
                    tooltip: Some("Error line".into()),
                    command: None,
                })
                .collect();
            let _ = editor::set_gutter(buffer, LOG_LAYER, marks);
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

## Worked example: the same plugin in TypeScript

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { readLines, setGutter, type GutterMark } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/editor';

const LOG_LAYER = 'log-levels';
const MAX_LINES_PER_READ = 10_000;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'editor-changed') continue;
      const { buffer, firstLine, lastLine } = event.val;
      const count = Math.min(lastLine - firstLine + 1, MAX_LINES_PER_READ);
      let lines: string[];
      try {
        lines = readLines(buffer, firstLine, count);
      } catch {
        continue; // The buffer closed before the call, or the grant was revoked.
      }
      const marks: GutterMark[] = [];
      lines.forEach((text, offset) => {
        if (!text.includes(' ERROR ')) return;
        marks.push({
          line: firstLine + offset,
          icon: 'alert-triangle',
          tooltip: 'Error line',
          command: undefined,
        });
      });
      try {
        setGutter(buffer, LOG_LAYER, marks);
      } catch {
        // The buffer closed between the two calls, so there is nothing left to mark.
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The buffer id and the revision are `bigint` values in TypeScript. Line numbers are plain `number`
values. A failing call throws a `PluginError` that carries its code, so the `try` blocks are the
place where a closed buffer or a revoked grant is handled.

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `read_lines`, `set_decorations` or `set_gutter` with the grant declined or revoked | `not-permitted` |
| `buffers()`, `buffer_for_pane()` or `selections()` with the grant declined or revoked | An empty list, none, an empty list. One refusal line is written to the plugin log. |
| The buffer no longer exists | `not-found` |
| `first_line` at or past the last line of the buffer | `invalid-argument` |
| `count` over 10,000 | `invalid-argument` |
| `count` runs past the last line | The lines that exist are returned, without an error. |
| More than 10,000 items for one layer | `invalid-argument` |
| The grant is revoked during a call | `revoked`. The plugin is re-activated with the reduced set. |
| Any call fails inside the host | `internal` |

The grant is revoked from Settings > Plugins > the plugin > Capabilities, or with
`ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke editor.read`. The kernel then withdraws the plugin's decorations
and gutter marks, sends `deactivate(revoked)`, and re-activates the plugin without the grant. A
revocation never counts as a failure. A disabled plugin loses its marks in the same way.

## Risk and tier rules

- This grant has the normal risk tier. It is not marked high risk.
- A T1 bundled plugin receives it automatically up to its manifest ceiling.
- A T2 or T3 plugin lists it in the review dialog, checked by default. The user can uncheck it
  before the install completes. The grant is remembered for that plugin on the client side.
- The native editor serves every call. The text is the user's work, so a plugin should read only
  the lines it needs.

## What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant for a T2 plugin on the client side:

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.editor 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                    │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Reads open files and buffers <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………</span> editor.read │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests editor.read, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

When the plugin marks a line, the gutter shows the icon and its tooltip appears on hover. A click
runs the command named in the mark, if the mark has one. Decorations appear as styled ranges with
their hover text. A plugin whose grant is declined still loads, but its marks and extra lines are
missing. The editor itself works without any plugin.

If the grant is requested on the wrong side, the build stops and names the side:

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin build
<span class="t-err">error</span> manifest.grant-side
      capability "editor.read" is not available on the server side
</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The build output for a manifest that lists editor.read under the server side.</figcaption>
</figure>

## First-party features that request it

- Feature 20, syntax highlighting and source windows, through the annotator in Phase 7.
- Feature 21, Markdown source and rendered views, through the annotator in Phase 7.
- Feature 23, create an agent from an editor line, which reads the line under the cursor.

# Capability: fs.pick

## fs.pick

The `fs.pick` capability lets a client-side plugin open the file picker. The picker is a modal panel that the kernel draws and owns. The plugin never sees the folders the user did not choose. It receives only the path the user confirmed, as a `picked/<n>` scope.

A plugin cannot choose a file by itself. It asks for a picker, the user decides, and the plugin gets one path back. Reading or writing that path needs a second grant, `fs.read:picked` or `fs.write:picked`.

### What you need

- **Grants.** `fs.pick` in `capabilities.client`, plus `fs.read:picked` for an `open-file` or `open-directory` pick, or `fs.write:picked` for a `save-file` pick. `fs.pick` without either of them fails the install with `manifest.grant-dependency`.
- **Language.** Rust with the `ilium_plugin_sdk` crate, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both wrappers are `async`.
- **Event handling.** A pick completes later as a `request-completed` event. The SDK wrapper hides this, but the plugin must run inside `definePlugin` or an async task so the completion can arrive. See [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

### Grant syntax

The grant takes no argument.

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `fs.pick` | yes | the only form |
| `fs.pick:project` | no | the grant takes no argument |
| `fs.picker` | no | the name is `fs.pick` |

Manifest excerpt for a plugin that opens a picker and then reads the chosen file:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["fs.pick", "fs.read:picked"] }
}
```

### Surface

| Name | Kind | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pick(spec)` | function | `pick-spec` to `result<request-id, plugin-error>` | Opens the picker. Needs `fs.pick`. Take the result with `take-picked`. |
| `take-picked(request)` | function | `request-id` to `option<fs-path>` | The chosen path, once the completion arrives. |
| `pick-spec` | record | `kind`, `title: string`, `extensions: list<string>` | Picker mode, title line and extension filter. |
| `pick-kind` | enum | `open-file`, `open-directory`, `save-file` | The mode of the picker and the button it shows. |
| `fs-path` | record | `scope: string`, `path: string` | The result. `scope` is `picked/<n>`, and `path` is empty. |
| `picked/<n>` | scope | grant per pick | Reading and writing needs `fs.read:picked` or `fs.write:picked`. |

Rust names: `fs::pick(spec).await`, `PickSpec`, `PickKind::OpenFile`, `PickKind::OpenDirectory`
and `PickKind::SaveFile`, all from `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs`. TypeScript names: `pick(spec)`
from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs`, with `kind` set to the strings `'open-file'`, `'open-directory'`
or `'save-file'`.

The `extensions` filter takes lower-case names without a leading dot, such as `png`. It matches
case-insensitively. An empty list allows every file. The filter applies only to file modes, not to
`open-directory`.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant in plain words when the package is installed. Tier T1 bundled plugins
receive `fs.pick` without a prompt. Tier T2 and T3 packages show it in the review dialog.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">Review permissions: com.example.notes 0.1.0</span>
     Opens the file picker: fs.pick
     Lets you choose a file or folder. The plugin sees only your choice.
<span class="t-dim">[allow]  [decline]</span>

</figure>

The picker itself has a title line, a path input, the entry list, the extension filter and two buttons.
The button label depends on the mode. Keys: Enter opens a folder or confirms, Backspace goes to the
parent folder, Tab moves between the input, the list and the buttons, Ctrl+H shows hidden files, and
Escape cancels.

The button reads `Open` for `open-file`, `Save` for `save-file` and `Choose` for `open-directory`.
`Cancel` is always present.

### Worked example: Rust

This example asks for an image and reads it. It treats a cancelled pick as a normal outcome.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs::{self, PickKind, PickSpec};

/// Asks the user for a background image. Needs fs.pick, fs.read:picked.
async fn choose_background() -> Result<FsPath, PluginError> {
    let spec = PickSpec {
        kind: PickKind::OpenFile,
        title: "Choose a background image".to_string(),
        extensions: vec!["png".to_string(), "jpg".to_string()],
    };
    fs::pick(spec).await
}

/// Returns the image bytes, or None when the user cancelled the picker.
async fn load_background() -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, PluginError> {
    let picked_path = match choose_background().await {
        Ok(picked_path) => picked_path,
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::Cancelled => return Ok(None),
        Err(error) => return Err(error),
    };
    let bytes = fs::read_all(&picked_path).await?;
    Ok(Some(bytes))
}
```

The picked path has an empty `path`, so `read_all` with `picked_path` reads the chosen file itself.

### Worked example: TypeScript

The same flow in TypeScript. A cancelled pick rejects with a `PluginError`, which the function turns
into `undefined`.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { pick, readAll } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';

/** Asks the user for a background image and returns its bytes, or undefined on cancel. */
export async function loadBackground(): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined> {
  try {
    const pickedPath = await pick({
      kind: 'open-file',
      title: 'Choose a background image',
      extensions: ['png', 'jpg'],
    });
    return await readAll(pickedPath);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'cancelled') {
      return undefined;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

### Save-file example

A `save-file` pick returns a scope whose path is empty and names the file the user typed. The file may
not exist yet. Write it with `write` and a `create-new` mode to avoid overwriting an existing file:

**Rust**

```rust
let target = fs::pick(PickSpec {
    kind: PickKind::SaveFile,
    title: "Save the export".to_string(),
    extensions: vec!["json".to_string()],
}).await?;
fs::write(&target, export_bytes, WriteMode::CreateNew).await?;
```

This needs `fs.write:picked` in the manifest. Without it, `write` returns `not-permitted`.

### Limits and rules

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Pickers open at once per plugin | 1. A second `pick` returns `busy`. |
| Picked paths kept per plugin | 64. The oldest is forgotten when a 65th is added. |
| `<n>` in `picked/<n>` | A per-plugin counter that never repeats. |
| Lifetime of a picked path | Survives restarts until its grant is revoked. |
| Watching a picked scope | Allowed for folders only. |

Paths inside a picked folder are relative to it, as for every scope. A path that leaves the folder
through `..` or a symbolic link returns `not-permitted`.

### Errors

Every error code of `plugin-error` can occur. These are the ones that matter for a picker:

| Code | When | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | `fs.pick` declined or revoked. No dialog opens. | Returned by `pick`. |
| `busy` | This plugin already shows a picker. | Returned by `pick`, before any dialog opens. |
| `cancelled` | The user pressed Cancel or Escape. | Completion; the SDK wrapper fails with it. |
| `not-found` | The completion succeeded but has no picked path. | SDK wrapper. |
| `revoked` | The grant changed during the call. The plugin is reactivated with the reduced grant set. | Returned or completion. |
| `not-permitted` on read or write | The plugin lacks `fs.read:picked` or `fs.write:picked`. | `read_all`, `write`, and so on. |

When the grant is declined, the plugin should tell the user that the feature needs the picker
permission. It should not retry in a loop.

### Who requests it

No first-party plugin in the feature mapping lists `fs.pick` in its capability column. Feature 22
(File explorer and picker) keeps the picker dialog in the kernel. Feature 101 (Media scenes) reads
paths that the user picked, under the `picked` scope. A scene gets its path from a settings field with
the `picker` keyword, so it declares `fs.read:picked` without `fs.pick`.

### See also

- [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/) for the read functions that work on a picked path.
- [fs.write](/pages/capability-fs-write/) for writing to a path the user saved.
- [fs.watch](/pages/capability-fs-watch/) for watching a picked folder.
- [File access](/pages/file-access/) for scopes, grants and preopened folders.
- [Filesystem API](/pages/api-fs/) for every `fs` function, type and limit.
- [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for how completions reach the plugin.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) for the full error code list.

# fs.read:<scope>

## Overview

The `fs.read:<scope>` grant lets a plugin read files and list directories inside one named scope. A scope is a directory the host has chosen for the plugin: the session's project, a folder or file the user picked, the Minecraft saves folder, or the transcript or configuration folder of an agent.

The plugin never names a path on the disk. It names a scope and a path relative to that scope, and the host refuses any path that leaves the scope. The grant is checked on every call, so a revoked grant stops reads at once.

Each scope is mounted for the plugin as a preopen, a directory the sandbox can see. Standard synchronous file code in a Rust or TypeScript plugin also works against these preopens, but the SDK functions below are the supported route.

## What you need

- A grant `fs.read:<scope>` in the manifest for every side that reads the scope. Use `server`, `client` or `scene`, as the scope applies:

  ```json
  {
    "capabilities": {
      "server": ["fs.read:project"]
    }
  }
  ```

- Rust with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, or TypeScript with Bun 1.2 or later and `@ilium/plugin-sdk`.
- Nothing extra for the always-granted scopes. The set in [always-granted](/pages/capability-always-granted/) already covers reads of `package`, `data` and `cache`.
- A separate `fs.write:<scope>` grant for any write to the same scope. See [fs.write](/pages/capability-fs-write/).

## Scopes and grant syntax

The scope is the text after the colon. Valid grants:

| Grant | Preopen | Root and meaning | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fs.read:project` | `/project` | The session's canonical project directory. Excludes its `.ilium` folder. | normal |
| `fs.read:worktrees` | `/worktrees` | The project's worktree folder from `workspace.worktree_root`. | normal |
| `fs.read:picked` | `/picked/<n>` | Each path the user chose in a picker. Granted per pick. | normal |
| `fs.read:minecraft-saves` | `/minecraft-saves` | The platform's Minecraft saves directory. | normal |
| `fs.read:agent-config:claude` | `/agent-config/claude` | The Claude configuration directory. Also `codex`. | normal |
| `fs.read:agent-sessions:claude` | `/agent-sessions/claude` | Claude transcript directory. Also `codex` and `antigravity`. | high |
| `fs.read:path:<template>` | `/paths/<n>` | A path template, see below. | normal, high if literal |

A path template starts with a placeholder or a literal absolute path, and ends with a name or with `/**`:

- Placeholders: `{home}`, `{config}`, `{data}`, `{cache}`, `{project}`, `{worktrees}`.
- `fs.read:path:{config}/ilium/themes/**` grants the whole theme subtree.
- `fs.read:path:{home}/.gitconfig` grants that one file.
- `fs.read:path:/srv/logs/**` uses a literal absolute path. Such a grant is always high risk.

Invalid grants are refused at install with `manifest.grant-scope`:

- `fs.read` with no scope.
- `fs.read:agent-sessions` with no agent name. The agent is part of the scope.
- `fs.read:*`, or a wildcard anywhere except the trailing `/**` of a template.
- `fs.write:agent-sessions:claude`. Transcript scopes are read only.

## Risk and review

- Most scopes are normal risk. The three `agent-sessions` scopes are high risk, because they hold the user's private conversations.
- A T1 bundled plugin receives normal scopes automatically, up to its manifest ceiling. High-risk scopes are asked for once, at first activation.
- A T2 or T3 plugin needs an explicit grant in the review dialog for each scope. The grant is remembered until it is revoked.

## Surface

The `fs` interface offers these read functions. Rust names are in `snake_case` and TypeScript names in `camelCase`.

| Function | Rust (`ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs`) | TypeScript (`@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs`) | Kind | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roots` | `roots() -> Vec<(String, bool)>` | `roots(): [string, boolean][]` | sync | Each granted scope and whether it is writable |
| `metadata` | `metadata(path) -> Result<FsMetadata, PluginError>` | `metadata(path): FsMetadata` | sync | Kind, length, modified time, read-only flag |
| `list_dir` | `list_dir(path, max_entries)` returns `Result<Vec<DirEntry>, PluginError>` | `listDir(path, maxEntries): DirEntry[]` | sync | Entries of one folder, at most 4,096 |
| `read` | `read(path, offset, max_bytes)` returns `Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError>` | `read(path, offset, maxBytes): Uint8Array` | sync | At most 1 MiB from `offset` |
| `read_all` | `read_all(path).await` returns `Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError>` | `readAll(path): Promise<Uint8Array>` | async | Whole file, up to the read-all limit |
| `scan` | `scan(path, glob, max_entries).await` | `scan(path, glob, maxEntries): Promise<[string, DirEntry][]>` | async | Matching entries, sorted by path bytes |

The WIT functions `take-bytes` and `take-entries` are used only through the wrappers above. The raw request forms, such as `read_all_request`, are for code that needs them.

Records, from `ilium:host/fs`:

```wit
record fs-path { scope: string, path: string }
enum entry-kind { file, directory, symlink, other }
record fs-metadata {
  kind: entry-kind, length: u64, modified-unix-millis: option<u64>, read-only: bool,
}
record dir-entry { name: string, metadata: fs-metadata }
```

The `path` is relative to the scope root and uses `/` as the separator. An empty `path` names the root itself. For a `picked/<n>` scope, an empty `path` names the picked file or folder.

Limits:

| Limit | Value | Over the limit |
|---|---|---|
| `read` `max-bytes` | 1 MiB per call | `invalid-argument` |
| `list-dir` `max-entries` | 1 to 4,096 | `invalid-argument` |
| `scan` `max-entries` | 1 to 65,536 | `invalid-argument`; more matches complete as `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| `read-all` file size | 64 MiB by default (`fs_read_all_mib`) | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |

See [errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the full table.

Glob grammar for `scan`: `*` matches any run of characters inside one segment. A whole `**` segment matches zero or more folders. `?` matches one character inside a segment. Braces, character classes and escapes are not supported. A leading `/`, a `..` segment or a backslash is `invalid-argument`.

## Worked example: Rust

This server-side plugin reads the first kilobyte of one file, and lists the Rust sources of the project from a task.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Returns the first `max_bytes` bytes of a file in the project scope.
fn read_head(relative_path: &str, max_bytes: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
    let path = FsPath {
        scope: "project".into(),
        path: relative_path.into(),
    };
    fs::read(path, 0, max_bytes)
}

/// Lists the Rust sources under src/, sorted by path.
async fn rust_sources() -> Result<Vec<String>, PluginError> {
    let root = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: String::new() };
    let entries = fs::scan(root, "src/**/*.rs", 500).await?;
    Ok(entries.into_iter().map(|(relative_path, _entry)| relative_path).collect())
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Scanner;

impl Handler for Scanner {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        match read_head("src/lib.rs", 1024) {
            Ok(bytes) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("read {} bytes", bytes.len())),
            Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::NotPermitted => {
                // The grant is missing or declined: the scope is simply absent.
            }
            Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("read failed: {}", error.message)),
        }
        task::spawn(async {
            // A real plugin turns the list into an intent or a tree update.
            let _sources = rust_sources().await;
        });
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

## Worked example: TypeScript

This server-side plugin checks which scopes it holds, reads a file, handles a refused escape, and counts the newlines of a README through the async call.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { listDir, read, readAll, roots } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

async function countReadmeLines(): Promise<number> {
  const bytes = await readAll({ scope: 'project', path: 'README.md' });
  return bytes.filter((byte) => byte === 10).length;
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(_batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const hasProject = roots().some(([scope]) => scope === 'project');
    if (!hasProject) return [];

    const head = read({ scope: 'project', path: 'src/lib.rs' }, 0n, 1024);
    log('info', `read ${head.length} bytes`);

    const sources = listDir({ scope: 'project', path: 'src' }, 200);
    log('info', `src holds ${sources.length} entries`);

    try {
      read({ scope: 'project', path: '../.ssh/id_ed25519' }, 0n, 1024);
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'not-permitted') {
        log('warn', 'escape refused, as expected');
      }
    }

    countReadmeLines()
      .then((lines) => log('info', `README has ${lines} lines`))
      .catch((error) => log('warn', `README read failed: ${String(error)}`));
    return [];
  },
});
```

`offset` is a `u64`, so it is a `bigint` (`0n`) in TypeScript. `max-bytes` is a `u32` and stays a plain number.

## Edge cases and errors

| Code | When it happens for a read |
|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | The grant is missing or declined, the path leaves the scope through `..`, or a symbolic link points outside the scope root. |
| `not-found` | No entry exists at the path, or the picked file was removed. |
| `invalid-argument` | A bad path, `max-entries` of 0 or above the cap, `max-bytes` above 1 MiB, or the wrong kind, such as `list-dir` on a file. |
| `revoked` | The grant was revoked while the call was in flight. The plugin is reactivated. |
| `io` | An operating system error other than a missing file. A retry may succeed. |
| `busy` | Too many requests are pending. Only the async calls return this. |
| `quota-exceeded` | `read-all` finished with a file over the limit, or `scan` found more matches than `max-entries`. |

Behaviour the plugin can rely on:

- **Symbolic links.** `metadata` and `list-dir` report a link as kind `symlink` and do not follow it. `read` and `read-all` follow it only when the target stays inside the same scope root.
- **Hidden folder.** The project's `.ilium` folder is missing from listings, and access to it returns `not-permitted`.
- **Offset past the end.** A `read` at or beyond the end of a file returns an empty list. A read that reaches the end returns fewer bytes than `max-bytes`.
- **Dotfiles.** `scan` and `list-dir` return dotfiles too.
- **Declined scope.** The scope is absent from `roots()`, and calls on it return `not-permitted`. Other scopes keep working. A workspace search that loses its project scope should say that it needs project access, not show zero results.
- **Revocation.** Revoking the grant bumps the authorization epoch, so reads in flight fail with `revoked`.

The review dialog names every scope, so the user can tell a project request from a picked file or a transcript folder. Illustrative, not generated.

## Declined and revoked grants

When the user declines a scope, or the grant is revoked, the scope is removed from `roots()` and every call on it returns `not-permitted`. Each refused call writes one refusal line to the plugin log, which `ilium plugin logs` shows. The line names the scope and the function, and gives the reason: `declined`, or `not-requested` when the manifest never asked for that scope.

# Capability: fs.watch

## fs.watch:&lt;scope&gt;

The `fs.watch:<scope>` grant lets a plugin ask the host to watch a folder inside one file scope and to tell it when files in that folder change. The host sends the changes as `fs-changed` events, one per watch and batch, so the plugin never has to poll the disk.

A watch names a scope and a path relative to that scope. It never names a path on the disk. A watch reads no file contents: to read a changed file, the plugin also needs `fs.read` for the same scope.

**You will need:**

- A manifest grant `fs.watch:<scope>` on the side that calls `watch`. Grants are recorded per side.
- The `fs.read:<scope>` grant, when the plugin reads the changed files. See [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/).
- The SDK for your language: `ilium-plugin-sdk` for Rust, or `@ilium/plugin-sdk` for TypeScript. Both sides can watch.
- An active plugin instance. A watch belongs to the instance that started it.

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `fs.watch:project` | yes | watches the session's project folder |
| `fs.watch:data` | yes | watches the plugin's own data folder |
| `fs.watch:path:{project}/**` | yes | a path template; `path:` must come first |
| `fs.watch:path:/srv/notes` | yes, high risk | a literal absolute path after `path:` |
| `fs.watch` | no | the scope argument is missing (`manifest.grant-argument-missing`) |
| `fs.watch:/srv/notes` | no | a bare absolute path is not a scope; write `path:/srv/notes` |
| `fs.watch:package` | no | `package` is not watchable, because it never changes |
| `fs.read:project` | no | a read grant does not allow a watch |

A grant that breaks these rules stops the install. Each error is one JSONL `error` line of `ilium plugin install` and `ilium plugin build`, with the code shown in the table above.

### Surface

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `watch(path, recursive)` | `fs::watch(&FsPath, bool) -> Result<u64, PluginError>` | `watch(path: FsPath, recursive: boolean): bigint` | Starts a watch on a folder and returns its id. Synchronous. |
| `unwatch(watch)` | `fs::unwatch(u64)` | `unwatch(watch: bigint): void` | Stops a watch. Synchronous. An unknown id is ignored. |
| `fs-changed` event | `Event::FsChanged(FsChangedEvent { watch, paths })` | `{ tag: 'fs-changed', val: { watch, paths } }` | The changed paths of one watch. |

The WIT declarations, from which the SDK bindings are generated, are:

```wit
type watch-id = u64;
watch: func(path: fs-path, recursive: bool) -> result<watch-id, plugin-error>;  // fs.watch
unwatch: func(watch: watch-id);
record fs-changed-event { watch: watch-id, paths: list<string> }               // fs-changed
```

Every `u64` is a `bigint` in TypeScript. The `path` argument is an `fs-path` record with a `scope` and a `path` field in both languages.

### Watchable scopes

| Scope | Grant example | Watchable |
|---|---|---|
| Project folder | `fs.watch:project` | yes; the `.ilium` folder never appears |
| Worktrees | `fs.watch:worktrees` | yes |
| Plugin data and cache | `fs.watch:data`, `fs.watch:cache` | yes |
| Picked folder | `fs.watch:picked` with `picked/<n>` | yes, folders only |
| Agent transcripts and configuration | `fs.watch:agent-sessions:claude` | yes |
| Minecraft saves | `fs.watch:minecraft-saves` | yes |
| Literal or template path | `fs.watch:path:{home}/notes/**` | yes |
| Plugin package | `fs.watch:package` | no |

### How a watch behaves

- **Window.** After the first change, the host waits 200 ms and sends one `fs-changed` event with every path changed in that time. A watch sends at most five events per second.
- **Paths.** Paths are relative to the scope root and use `/` separators, so `FsPath { scope, path }` can be built from them directly. Each path appears once per event.
- **Reach.** A non-recursive watch reports only the direct children of the folder. A recursive watch reports every changed path below it. A rename lists the old and the new path.
- **Symbolic links.** A link is reported by its own name. The host never follows it, so a change inside its target is not reported.
- **Large bursts.** An event lists at most 1,024 paths. A larger burst becomes one event whose `paths` holds only the watched path. The plugin must then read that folder again.
- **Removed folder.** When the watched folder is removed or renamed, one event lists the watched path, and the watch ends.
- **Quota.** `watches` defaults to 64 per plugin. A recursive watch counts once, however many folders it covers. The manifest may request another value under `limits`, clamped to 256 for a T1 bundled plugin and 64 for T2 and T3. A `watch` beyond the quota returns `quota-exceeded`.
- **Duplicates.** A second `watch` on the same folder returns a new id and counts separately. Each id sends its own event.
- **Lifetime.** A watch ends on `unwatch`, when its instance deactivates, restarts or is disabled, or when the plugin loses the grant. Ids do not survive a restart, so the plugin starts its watches again in `activate`.
- **Delivery.** `fs-changed` reaches only the instance that called `watch`. Events of one watch keep their order, and `fs-changed` is never dropped under the drop policy.

### Risk and tier rules

- `fs.watch:<scope>` is a normal-risk grant. The API permission table does not mark it as high risk.
- `fs.watch:path:` with a literal absolute path is high risk. The user checks it by hand.
- A T1 bundled plugin receives a normal grant up to its manifest ceiling. A T2 or T3 package lists the grant in the install dialog, checked by default.
- Revoking the grant withdraws every watch of the plugin. Calls in flight return `revoked`. The plugin receives `deactivate(revoked)` and is activated again with the reduced grant set. A later `watch` returns `not-permitted`.

### What the user sees

The install and permission dialog shows one row for the grant. The row text is "Watch files in the project folder for changes", followed by the grant string. The row is grey-dotted, as every row of that dialog is.

The client never shows a prompt for a watch or for an event. A grant is a standing permission until it is revoked. To revoke it, open Settings > Plugins > <plugin> > Capabilities, or run `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke fs.watch:project`.

### Errors

| Call | Code | When |
|---|---|---|
| `watch` | `not-permitted` | the grant is missing or declined, the path leaves the scope, or it is a symbolic link |
| `watch` | `not-found` | the folder does not exist |
| `watch` | `invalid-argument` | the scope is not watchable, or the path names a file |
| `watch` | `quota-exceeded` | the plugin already holds its `watches` limit |
| `watch` | `revoked` | the authorization changed during the call |
| `watch` | `internal` | a host bug |
| `unwatch` | none | an unknown id is ignored |

A `watch` call that fails inside `activate` makes the activation fail. The host counts it as a failure under the restart rule, and repeated failures disable the plugin.

When the grant is declined, `watch` returns `not-permitted`. The plugin keeps running without change notifications and must read the folder on demand.

### Example: a docs watcher in Rust

The manifest requests the grants and a lower watch limit:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.docs-watch",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["fs.read:project", "fs.watch:project"] },
  "limits": { "watches": 8 }
}
```

The plugin starts the watch in `activate`, reads each changed file, and logs its size.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::FsChangedEvent;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct DocsWatcher {
    watch: Option<u64>,
}

impl Lifecycle for DocsWatcher {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let docs = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: "docs".into() };
        self.watch = Some(fs::watch(&docs, true)?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for DocsWatcher {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::FsChanged(FsChangedEvent { watch, paths }) = event else { continue };
            if self.watch != Some(watch) {
                continue;
            }
            for path in paths {
                let target = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: path.clone() };
                task::spawn(async move {
                    match fs::read_all(&target).await {
                        Ok(bytes) => {
                            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{path}: {} bytes", bytes.len()));
                        }
                        Err(error) => {
                            log::log(Level::Error, &format!("{path}: {}", error.message));
                        }
                    }
                });
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

### Example: the same watch in TypeScript

The TypeScript version runs on the server side. It keeps the watch id as a `bigint`, because every `u64` is a `bigint` in TypeScript.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { readAll, watch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const DOCS_FOLDER = { scope: 'project', path: 'docs' };
let docsWatch: bigint | undefined;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    docsWatch = watch(DOCS_FOLDER, true);
    log('info', `${context.plugin} watches the docs folder`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'fs-changed' || event.val.watch !== docsWatch) continue;
      for (const path of event.val.paths) {
        readAll({ scope: 'project', path })
          .then((bytes: Uint8Array) => log('info', `${path}: ${bytes.length} bytes`))
          .catch(() => log('warn', `${path} could not be read`));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

<!-- source: http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/capability-fs-write.md -->
# Capability: fs.write

## fs.write:&lt;scope&gt;

The `fs.write:<scope>` capability lets a plugin create, replace and append files, create folders, remove entries and rename files inside one file scope. A scope is a named root that the host hands to the plugin, such as the project folder, the plugin's private `data` folder or a path the user picked. Every write path is resolved inside that root. A path that tries to leave the root through `..` or a symbolic link is refused.

Writes are asynchronous. A call checks the grant, the scope, the path syntax and the size cap at once, then returns a `request-id`. The disk result arrives later as a `request-completed` event.

<div class="note">
<p>Grants are per side. A plugin that writes from its server side needs the grant in <code>capabilities.server</code>. A client-side write needs it in <code>capabilities.client</code>. A scene can write its <code>data</code> and <code>cache</code> scopes without a grant; any other scope is declared in <code>capabilities.scene</code>.</p>
</div>

**You will need:** a manifest grant `fs.write:<scope>`, or no grant for the always-granted `data` and `cache` scopes. Read [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/) first, because every write path is resolved the same way as a read path. The calls themselves are documented on [fs](/pages/api-fs/).

SDK paths: Rust `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs`, TypeScript `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs`. Paths use the `FsPath` type: a struct in Rust, and a `{ scope, path }` object in TypeScript.

### Grant syntax

The grant is `fs.write:<scope>`. The argument is one scope name from the table in the next section, or `path:<template>`. The manifest checks the grant when the package is installed.

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `fs.write:project` | yes | the session's project folder, high risk |
| `fs.write:path:{project}/**` | yes | a template with the `{project}` placeholder and a trailing `/**`, high risk |
| `fs.write:worktrees` | yes | the worktree folder, high risk; `{worktrees}` names the same root |
| `fs.write:agent-config:claude` | yes | the Claude configuration folder, high risk |
| `fs.write:data` | yes | always granted, so no manifest entry is needed; not logged |
| `fs.write` | no | `manifest.grant-argument-missing`: needs an argument, for example `fs.write:project` |
| `fs.write:/home/me/notes` | no | `manifest.grant-scope`; an absolute path needs `path:<template>` |
| `fs.write:package` | no | `manifest.grant-scope`; the `package` scope is read only |
| `fs.write:agent-sessions:claude` | no | `manifest.grant-scope`; agent transcripts are read only |
| `fs.read:project` | no | a read grant does not allow writes |

A literal absolute path inside `path:` (for example `fs.write:path:/srv/logs/**`) is high risk and is available to bundled T1 plugins only.

### Scopes

| Scope | Root on disk | Grant to write | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | the session's project folder, without the `.ilium` folder | `fs.write:project` | H |
| `worktrees` | the worktree folder from `workspace.worktree_root` | `fs.write:worktrees` | H |
| `path:<template>` | the folders a template names | `fs.write:path:<template>` | H |
| `agent-config:claude`, `agent-config:codex` | each agent's configuration folder | one grant per agent | H |
| `picked/<n>` | the file or folder the user chose | `fs.write:picked` for a save pick | normal |
| `data` | the plugin's private data folder | always granted | none |
| `cache` | the plugin's private cache folder, which the host may evict | always granted | none |
| `package`, `agent-sessions:*` | read only | not writable | refused at install |

The placeholders for `path:<template>` are `{home}`, `{config}`, `{data}`, `{cache}`, `{project}` and `{worktrees}`. A template ends with a name, which covers that file or folder, or with `/**`, which covers the whole subtree. The wildcard `*` is refused in every position, so a manifest that needs both agent configuration folders lists both grants.

### Functions

| Function | Rust (`fs::`) | TypeScript | Kind | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `write(path, data, mode)` | `write(&FsPath, Vec<u8>, WriteMode)` | `write(path, Uint8Array, mode)` | async | `ok`, or `failed(code)` |
| `create-dir(path)` | `create_dir(&FsPath)` | `createDir(path)` | sync | `Result<(), PluginError>` |
| `remove(path)` | `remove(&FsPath)` | `remove(path)` | async | `ok`, or `failed(code)` |
| `rename(source, target)` | `rename(&FsPath, &FsPath)` | `rename(source, target)` | async | `ok`, or `failed(code)` |

The Rust and TypeScript async wrappers return `()` or `void` on `ok`, and an error on `failed(code)`. The raw calls that return a request id stay available as `write_request`, `remove_request` and `rename_request`.

`create-dir` is synchronous and not recursive. It creates one folder. An existing folder counts as success, so a call can be repeated safely.

### Write modes

The `write-mode` enum has three cases. In Rust they are `WriteMode::CreateNew`, `WriteMode::Replace` and `WriteMode::Append`. In TypeScript they are the strings `'create-new'`, `'replace'` and `'append'`.

- `create-new` creates the file. When the file already exists the completion is `failed(conflict)`, and the file is not changed.
- `replace` writes a temporary sibling file and renames it over the target. A reader sees either the old content or the new content, never a partial file. It also creates the file when it is absent.
- `append` adds bytes to the end of the file and creates the file when it is absent.

One `write` call takes at most `fs_write_mib` (16 MiB by default). Write a larger file with several `append` calls, or produce it in a job.

### Completion

A finished write arrives in a batch as a `request-completed` event. Its `request-result` names the call and gives the outcome:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok` | The file, folder or entry was changed as requested. |
| `failed(code)` | The disk or the current state refused the call. The code is in the errors table. |
| `cancelled` | The plugin stopped, the user cancelled, or the host shut down. |

```
request-result { request: call(41), outcome: ok }
```

The SDK turns this event into the result of the async wrapper, so most plugins never read it directly.

### Errors

Every write function may also return `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`. Synchronous errors come back from the call. Errors that need the disk or the user arrive in the completion.

| Code | Where | When |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | call | No grant, the grant was declined, or the path escapes the scope root or a symbolic link leaves it. |
| `invalid-argument` | call | A bad path, data over `fs_write_mib`, an empty `path` outside a `picked/<n>` scope, a rename across two scopes, or `remove` on a scope root. |
| `busy` | call | The plugin already has `pending_requests` (64 by default) open. |
| `quota-exceeded` | call | The CPU budget is spent; `retry-after-ms` is set. |
| `revoked` | call | The grant was revoked while the call was running. |
| `conflict` | completion | `create-new` found a file, a folder has the target name, another holder has a lock on the path, or a rename targets a non-empty folder. |
| `not-found` | completion | The parent folder is missing, or the source of a rename or remove does not exist. |
| `quota-exceeded` | completion | The `data` plus `cache` disk limit (`disk_mib`, 256 MiB by default) is full. |
| `io` | completion | An operating system error other than a missing file. |
| `revoked` | completion | A write still pending when its grant is revoked completes as `failed(revoked)`. |

`create-dir` is the exception. It is synchronous, so `conflict` (a file has that name), `not-found` (the parent is missing) and `io` come back from the call.

### Limits

| Key | Default | T1 ceiling | T2 and T3 ceiling | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fs_write_mib` (one call) | 16 | 64 | 16 | `invalid-argument` above the limit |
| `disk_mib` (`data` plus `cache`) | 256 | 4,096 | 256 | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| `pending_requests` | 64 | 256 | 64 | `busy` above the limit |

A plugin asks for a higher value in its manifest. The host clamps the request to the ceiling and writes a log line, so a T2 plugin cannot write more than 16 MiB in one call:

```json
"limits": { "fs_write_mib": 32 }
```

### Risk, review and logging

- Writes outside the `data` and `cache` scopes are high risk (H). A bundled T1 plugin with an H grant is first activated without it. The user then sees one prompt per plugin, `Plugin <name> asks for: <list>`, with the buttons `Allow selected` and `Not now`.
- A T2 or T3 package shows every requested grant in the review dialog. H rows start unchecked, and the user checks each one by hand. The dialog is 70 columns wide and each row shows its wording and its grant string.
- A grant is a standing permission. There is no prompt per call.
- Revoking the grant in Settings > Plugins, or with `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke <grant>`, fails calls in flight with `revoked`. The plugin then restarts with the reduced grant set.
- Every `write`, `remove`, `rename` and `create-dir` outside `data` and `cache` is written to the plugin log at level info, with the scope, the path, the operation and the byte count. `ilium plugin logs <id>` shows them.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │

</figure>

### When the grant is declined

A declined grant links the write imports to stubs that return `not-permitted` at once. The plugin keeps running and can show the error to the user. A write call whose capability the manifest never requested traps the instance instead, because that is a plugin bug.

### Examples

Both examples assume this manifest, with the grant on the server side:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "capabilities": { "server": ["fs.write:project"] }
}
```

**Example 1: replace a note atomically (Rust).** The `replace` mode means that a reader never sees a half-written note. A failed write comes back in `Err`, and the plugin logs its `code`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs::{self, WriteMode};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::Activation;

const NOTE_PATH: &str = "notes/today.md";

// Replaces the note in one step. A reader sees either the old or the new file.
async fn save_note(body: String) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let target = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: NOTE_PATH.into() };
    fs::write(&target, body.into_bytes(), WriteMode::Replace).await
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NoteSaver;

impl Lifecycle for NoteSaver {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let body = format!("# Notes\n\nPlugin {} started.\n", context.plugin);
        task::spawn(async move {
            if let Err(error) = save_note(body).await {
                log::log(Level::Error, &format!("save failed: {:?}", error.code));
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for NoteSaver {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**Example 2: create an export without overwriting it (TypeScript).** `create-new` fails with `conflict` when the file exists. The plugin treats that as a normal result and leaves the existing file alone.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { createDir, write } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';

const encoder = new TextEncoder();

// Creates exports/<name> and never overwrites an existing file.
async function createExport(name: string, body: string): Promise<'created' | 'exists'> {
  createDir({ scope: 'project', path: 'exports' });
  try {
    const target = { scope: 'project', path: `exports/${name}` };
    await write(target, encoder.encode(body), 'create-new');
    return 'created';
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'conflict') {
      return 'exists';
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    const body = `# Summary\n\nFrom ${context.plugin}.\n`;
    createExport('summary.md', body).catch((error: unknown) => {
      console.error('export failed', error);
    });
  },
  onEvents: () => [],
});
```

### What the user sees

Writes outside `data` and `cache` appear in the plugin log. The user reads them with the plugin's logs:

<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:09</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  write project exports/summary.md create-new 96 bytes
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:09</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>  create-new conflict on exports/summary.md, file kept
</pre>

</figure>

# Capability: help.read

## help.read

The `help.read` grant lets a client-side plugin read the Markdown help topics of every installed plugin, and the kernel's own topics. A plugin can show a reference page inside its own panel instead of shipping a copy of that page. Any plugin can read any installed topic, so one plugin can show another plugin's help next to its own.

The grant covers reading only. Declaring a topic in a package needs no grant.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 230" role="img" aria-label="A reading plugin calls topic with a global id. The kernel looks the id up in the help folders of installed packages and returns Markdown or none.">

      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>

  </defs>

  <text x="140" y="74" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">topic(id)</text>

  <line x1="340" y1="92" x2="340" y2="52" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr-help)"/>
  <text x="332" y="76" text-anchor="end" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">Markdown or none</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The topic call reads one Markdown file from an installed package. The kernel returns none when no installed plugin declares the id.</figcaption>

### What you need

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Grant `help.read` | Reads any installed help topic. The grant takes no argument. Its risk is ordinary, not high (H). |
| Side | `client`. The `help` import is part of `ilium:client/base`. A server-side plugin cannot call it. |
| Language | Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. |
| Topic files | Each topic you offer is declared under `contributes.help`, with its Markdown file in the `help/` folder. |

### Grant syntax

The grant takes no argument. The kernel checks the form when the package is installed.

| Grant | Valid | Result at install |
|---|---|---|
| `help.read` | yes | the only form |
| `help.read:com.example.notes` | no | `manifest.grant-argument`: `capability "help.read" takes no argument (got "help.read:com.example.notes")` |
| `help` | no | `manifest.grant-unknown`, because `help` is not a grant name |

### The surface

Rust paths start at `ilium_plugin_sdk::host`. TypeScript paths start at `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host`.

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | WIT | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `topic(id)` | `help::topic(id: &str) -> Option<String>` | `topic(id: string): string \| undefined` | `topic: func(id: string) -> option<string>` | Returns the Markdown text of the topic with that global id, or none. |

The function is synchronous. It reads the topic from the installed package, so it needs no request and no completion. Its WIT signature returns `option`, not `result`, so it has no error channel and never returns a `PluginError`. A missing topic, a declined grant and an unknown id all produce `none`.

The `id` argument is a global topic id, written `<plugin-id>/<local-id>`:

- `<plugin-id>` is the id of the plugin that declares the topic, such as `com.example.notes`.
- `<local-id>` is the `id` the manifest gives the topic, such as `notes.search`.
- The kernel's own topics use the prefix `ilium/`.

A local id on its own (`notes.search`) matches nothing and returns `none`.

### Manifest contribution

A plugin that offers help topics lists each one under `contributes.help`:

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Local id. The global id is `<plugin-id>/<id>`. |
| `file` | string | Path of the Markdown file inside the package, under `help/`, such as `help/search.md`. |
| `title` | string | Name shown in the help index. |

```json
"contributes": {
  "help": [ { "id": "notes.search", "file": "help/search.md", "title": "Searching notes" } ]
}
```

The topic file is plain Markdown. Its first heading is conventionally the topic title. The host returns the file text unchanged.

### Worked example in Rust

This client plugin shows the search topic of a notes plugin in its own panel. When the topic cannot be read, the panel shows one fallback line that points to the manual. The plugin declares `help.read` in `capabilities.client`.

Manifest:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.help",
  "name": "Help panel",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Example Labs",
  "client": { "entry": "client.wasm", "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["help.read"] }
}
```

Source, `src/lib.rs`:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::help;

const SEARCH_TOPIC_ID: &str = "com.example.notes/notes.search";
const FALLBACK_TEXT: &str =
    "Search help is not available. Open the plugin manual for the full reference.";

/// Markdown for the search help panel. The kernel returns none when the
/// grant is declined or the topic is missing, so the fallback line is shown.
fn search_help_markdown() -> String {
    help::topic(SEARCH_TOPIC_ID).unwrap_or_else(|| FALLBACK_TEXT.to_string())
}

/// First heading of the topic, used as the panel title.
fn search_help_title() -> String {
    search_help_markdown()
        .lines()
        .find(|line| line.starts_with('#'))
        .map(|line| line.trim_start_matches('#').trim().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "Help".to_string())
}
```

The view code calls `search_help_title()` for the panel heading and `search_help_markdown()`
for the body.

### Worked example in TypeScript

The same panel in TypeScript. The topic file ships in the notes plugin, not in this plugin.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { topic } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/help';

const SEARCH_TOPIC_ID = 'com.example.notes/notes.search';
const FALLBACK_TEXT =
  'Search help is not available. Open the plugin manual for the full reference.';

/** Markdown for the search help panel, or one fallback line. */
export function searchHelpMarkdown(): string {
  return topic(SEARCH_TOPIC_ID) ?? FALLBACK_TEXT;
}

/** Heading of the topic, used as the panel title. */
export function searchHelpTitle(): string {
  const firstHeading = searchHelpMarkdown()
    .split('\n')
    .find((line) => line.startsWith('#'));
  return firstHeading ? firstHeading.replace(/^#+\s*/, '').trim() : 'Help';
}
```

The notes plugin ships the topic file `help/search.md` with this text:

```markdown
# Searching notes

Type a word in the search box to find it in every note.
```

With the grant allowed, `searchHelpTitle()` returns `Searching notes`, and `searchHelpMarkdown()`
returns the whole file text.

### Edge cases and errors

The function has no error codes. The universal codes of the plugin API do not apply to it, because
a missing answer is `none`, not an error.

| Situation | Result | Log line |
|---|---|---|
| Id declared by an installed, enabled plugin | the Markdown text | none |
| Id declared by a disabled plugin | the Markdown text; topics of a disabled plugin stay readable | none |
| Kernel topic with the `ilium/` prefix | the Markdown text | none |
| Id not declared, misspelt, or a local id without the plugin prefix | `none` | none |
| `help.read` declined by the user | `none` | one warn line in the plugin log |
| `help.read` revoked while the plugin runs | `none` | one warn line in the plugin log |
| `help` import used from server code | not available: the import is not in `ilium:server/base` | build error |
| `contributes.help` entry whose `file` is missing or outside `help/` | package check fails | install error |

The function never throws. Code that needs the topic text must handle `none` in every case. A
declined grant and a missing topic look the same to the caller, so the warn line in the log is the
only way to tell them apart.

### What the user sees

When the user installs a T2 or T3 package that asks for `help.read`, the review dialog shows the
grant as an ordinary row. The row is checked by default, because the grant is not high risk. A T1
bundled plugin receives the grant up to its manifest ceiling without a dialog.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.help 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                      │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Reads help topics <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> help.read │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests help.read, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>

</figure>

When the user declines the grant, the plugin keeps running. Its panel shows the fallback line, and
the plugin log gets a warn line. The developer can check the state from the terminal:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.help
<span class="t-err">declined</span>  client  help.read
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs com.example.help
<span class="t-warn">warn</span>  help.topic returned none: help.read is declined
</pre>

<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. A declined grant shows in <code>grants</code>, and the warn line shows in <code>logs</code>.</figcaption>

### Risk and tier rules

- `help.read` has ordinary risk. It is not in the high-risk set, so the review dialog checks it by default.
- T1 bundled plugins receive the grant automatically, up to their manifest ceiling.
- T2 and T3 packages show the grant in the review dialog. The user can clear it there or later in Settings.
- Topic text comes only from the `help/` folder of an installed package. The kernel never fetches help over the network.

### Who requests it

First-party plugins from `feature-mapping.md`:

- 10 Help and key reference, which shows the topics of every installed plugin.
- 90 Settings UI, which links each settings page to its help topic.

### See also

# Capability: http

## http:&lt;host-pattern&gt;

The `http:<host-pattern>` grant lets a plugin send HTTP requests to the hosts that match the pattern. Each host needs its own grant. The host checks the grant before a request leaves the machine, so a request to any other host returns `not-permitted` at once and nothing is sent.

Use this grant for remote APIs, data feeds, map tiles and article sources. For large transfers, run the download in a job with [`jobs.run`](/pages/capability-jobs-run/). A job can call `http.fetch` with the same grants as its side, and the job's memory and wall-clock limits apply.

### What you need

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Grant | One `http:<host-pattern>` per host, on the side that sends the request: `client`, `server` or `scene` in the manifest. A job needs the grant on the side that runs it. |
| Rust | `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http` |
| TypeScript | `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http` |
| Protocol | HTTPS only. Plain HTTP works only for loopback hosts (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`) when the grant names them. |
| Tier | T1 bundled plugins receive the grant up to the manifest ceiling. T2 and T3 packages must be approved in the review dialog. |

Declare grants in the manifest under the side that makes the request:

```json
"capabilities": { "server": ["http:api.example.com", "http:*.openstreetmap.org"] }
```

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `http:api.example.com` | yes | one exact host |
| `http:api.example.com:8443` | yes | one exact host and port |
| `http:*.openstreetmap.org` | yes | any subdomain at any depth; not the bare domain |
| `http:localhost` | yes | loopback; plain HTTP allowed |
| `http:*` | no | a bare `*` is refused |
| `http:tile.*.org` | no | a wildcard in any position other than the leftmost label |
| `http` | no | the host pattern is missing |
| `http:https://api.example.com/v1` | no | a scheme or path; keep only the host |

A grant without a port matches the default port of the scheme only (443 for HTTPS, 80 for plain HTTP on loopback). A grant with `:<port>` matches that port alone.

`http:*.openstreetmap.org` covers `a.openstreetmap.org` and `a.b.openstreetmap.org`, but not `openstreetmap.org`. Declare the bare domain as its own grant when you need it.

### Surface

The `http` module has three calls: one that waits for the response, one that starts a request and returns its id, and one that reads a stored response.

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Send and wait | `http::fetch(request).await` | `await http.fetch(request)` | `Result<HttpResponse, PluginError>` / `Promise<HttpResponse>` | Sends the request and resolves with the full response. |
| Start | `http::fetch_request(request)` | `http.fetchRequest(request)` | `Result<RequestId, PluginError>` / `bigint` | Starts the request and returns its id. Use it when you need the id first. |
| Read result | `http::take_response(id)` | `http.takeResponse(id)` | `Option<HttpResponse>` / `HttpResponse \| undefined` | Returns the response once it is available. Nothing is returned before the request completes. |

Failed requests do not appear as a response. A transport failure, timeout or limit breach completes the request with an error code. The async wrapper turns that completion into a `PluginError`. The raw form delivers it in a `request-completed` event.

The types are the same in both languages:

| Type | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HttpRequest` | `method` | string | `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` or `OPTIONS`, in upper case. Any other value is `invalid-argument`. |
| `HttpRequest` | `url` | string | Absolute `https://` URL, at most 8 KiB. |
| `HttpRequest` | `headers` | `Header` list | At most 64 entries. |
| `HttpRequest` | `body` | bytes, optional | At most 8 MiB. `None` or `undefined` sends no body. |
| `HttpRequest` | `timeout_millis` | `u32` | 1 to 300,000. Covers connect, redirects and reading the body. |
| `Header` | `name`, `value` | string | One header. |
| `HttpResponse` | `status` | `u16` | The HTTP status code. A 404 or a 503 is a normal response. |
| `HttpResponse` | `headers` | `Header` list | The response headers. |
| `HttpResponse` | `body` | bytes | The response body. Default cap 8 MiB for every tier; a T1 plugin may request up to 64 MiB in `limits`. |

Each plugin may hold 64 pending requests by default (`pending_requests`); a T1 plugin may request up to 256. A call over that limit returns `busy`.

### Worked example: Rust, server side

This plugin fetches a notes feed when it activates. The request runs on the server side, so the manifest grants `http:api.example.com` under `server`.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "server": { "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["http:api.example.com"] }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, Header, HttpRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};

const NOTES_URL: &str = "https://api.example.com/v1/notes?since=2026-10-01";

async fn sync_notes() -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let request = HttpRequest {
        method: "GET".into(),
        url: NOTES_URL.into(),
        headers: vec![Header { name: "accept".into(), value: "application/json".into() }],
        body: None,
        timeout_millis: 5_000,
    };
    let response = http::fetch(request).await?;
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&response.body);
    log::log(
        Level::Info,
        &format!("notes sync: status {}, {} bytes", response.status, text.len()),
    );
    Ok(())
}

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesSync;

impl Lifecycle for NotesSync {
    fn activate(&mut self, _context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        task::spawn(async {
            if let Err(error) = sync_notes().await {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("notes sync failed: {:?}", error.code));
            }
        });
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for NotesSync {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

The `?` operator works because `http::fetch` returns `Result<_, PluginError>`. The `task::spawn` block keeps the request running after `activate` returns, and its error is logged rather than dropped.

### Worked example: TypeScript, client side

The same request from a client plugin. The manifest grants the host under `client`.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "client": { "entry": "client.wasm", "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["http:api.example.com"] }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as http from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const NOTES_URL = 'https://api.example.com/v1/notes?since=2026-10-01';

async function syncNotes(): Promise<void> {
  const response = await http.fetch({
    method: 'GET',
    url: NOTES_URL,
    headers: [{ name: 'accept', value: 'application/json' }],
    body: undefined,
    timeoutMillis: 5000,
  });
  const text = new TextDecoder().decode(response.body);
  log('info', `notes sync: status ${response.status}, ${text.length} characters`);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {
    syncNotes().catch((error: PluginError) => {
      log('warn', `notes sync failed: ${error.code}`);
    });
  },
  onEvents() {
    return [];
  },
});
```

`import * as http` keeps the SDK call apart from the global `fetch`. The promise is handled in `activate`, so a failure is logged and never becomes an unhandled rejection.

### Rules for every request

- Only HTTPS is accepted, except loopback when the grant names `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`.
- A request follows at most 5 redirects, and each hop must match a grant. A redirect to an ungranted host completes as `failed(not-permitted)`. A sixth redirect completes as `failed(network)`.
- A request to the host of a configured inference provider passes the AI admission gate first. The gate can refuse it by the user's policy (`not-permitted`) or throttle it (`rate-limited`, with `retry-after-ms`). Each admitted request adds one line to the privacy log. A refused request writes none.
- A non-2xx status is a normal response. Check `status` yourself; only transport failures are errors.
- The response body is capped at 8 MiB by default for every tier; a T1 plugin may request up to 64 MiB in `limits`. A larger body completes as `failed(quota-exceeded)`.
- `timeout_millis` covers the whole exchange. Passing it completes as `failed(timed-out)`.
- The kernel never forwards a request from one side to another. The side that calls `fetch` needs the grant.

### Review dialog and tiers

The install review dialog shows one row per capability. An `http` row reads `Connect to <host>` and shows the grant string at the right edge. Rows that are not `HIGH` start checked. `http` is not a `HIGH` capability, so it does not need a separate opt-in.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.http 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                      │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Connects to api.example.com <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………</span> http:api.example.com │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests http:api.example.com, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

A declined grant shows as unchecked and dimmed. The plugin's `granted` list in the activation context leaves it out, so a plugin can check its own status at start and tell the user what is missing.

### When a grant is missing or declined

A request to a host without a grant returns `not-permitted` at once. The host also writes one refusal line to the plugin log. The `reason` field is `declined` when the user unticked the row, and `not-granted` when the manifest asked for other hosts but not this one:

```json
{"type":"refusal","capability":"http:api.example.com","function":"http.fetch","reason":"declined"}
```

A request that matches a granted host still works. A granted host that is down or unreachable returns `network`, not `not-permitted`.

### Errors

| Code | When it happens | Where it appears | Retry |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invalid-argument` | URL not HTTPS outside loopback, unparsable or over 8 KiB; body over 8 MiB; timeout outside 1 to 300,000 ms; over 64 headers; method not in the list | at the call | no, fix the call |
| `not-permitted` | no grant for the host; the admission policy refused an AI provider call; a redirect to an ungranted host | at the call, or in the completion for redirects and policy | no |
| `busy` | 256 pending requests (1,024 at T1) | at the call | yes, later |
| `quota-exceeded` | response body over the cap; CPU budget of the quota group spent | in the completion, or at the call with `retry-after-ms` | after freeing resources or after `retry-after-ms` |
| `rate-limited` | the admission gate throttled a provider host | in the completion, with `retry-after-ms` | yes, after `retry-after-ms` |
| `network` | DNS, connect or TLS failure; more than 5 redirects | in the completion | yes |
| `timed-out` | the exchange did not finish within `timeout_millis` | in the completion | yes |
| `revoked`, `internal` | the grant changed during the call; a host bug | at the call or in the completion | `revoked`: the plugin is re-activated |

### Edge cases

- A `404` or a `503` from the server is an `ok` response with that status. Only transport failures are errors.
- A wildcard grant does not cover the bare domain, and a grant without a port does not cover other ports.
- A redirect chain is checked hop by hop. A granted first host that redirects to an ungranted second host fails with `failed(not-permitted)`.
- `timeout_millis` includes redirects and the body download. A slow body fails with `failed(timed-out)` even when the headers arrived in time.
- A request from a job uses the job's side. Declare the grant on the side that runs the job.
- A scene declares its host grants under `capabilities.scene`.

### Who requests it

First-party plugins that use this grant:

- 50 Voice session: `http:<provider-host>`.
- 84 AI providers: one `http:<provider-host>` grant for each provider.
- 88 Reset planning: `http:<feed-host>`.
- 99 Live-data scenes: one `http:<data-host>` grant for each source.
- 100 Maps, space, Wikipedia and voxel saved worlds: `http:*.openstreetmap.org` and `http:*.wikipedia.org`.

- [inference](/pages/capability-inference/) for requests that go through the AI admission gate.
- [jobs.run](/pages/capability-jobs-run/) for long downloads.
- [api-http](/pages/api-http/) for the full function reference.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the error code table and every size limit.
- [capability-http-api-route](/pages/capability-http-api-route/) for the opposite direction: local requests that reach your plugin.

Checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` (API draft of 2026-10-11).

Address checks, redirects, TLS and the offline switch are defined in [Network egress](/pages/reference-network-egress/). Extra `not-permitted` reasons: `private-address`, `downgrade`, `reserved`, `offline`, `policy`.
