# Capability: http-api.route

## http-api.route:&lt;path&gt;

The `http-api.route:<path>` capability lets a server-side plugin answer requests on one path of the Ilium loopback HTTP API. The kernel owns the listener. It listens on the local machine only, checks each request, and sends every request for a granted route to the plugin as an `http-called` event. The plugin answers with one `respond` call. A request that matches no granted route never reaches the plugin.

Use a route when a program that the user runs on this computer needs an endpoint that the plugin serves. A route cannot be reached from the network, and a web page in a browser cannot call it.

**You will need:**

- One `http-api.route:<path>` grant per route, in `capabilities.server`. The grant is valid on the server side only.
- One `http_routes` entry per route under `contributes`, with the same path and method as the grant.
- The SDK for your language: `ilium_plugin_sdk` for Rust, or `@ilium/plugin-sdk` for TypeScript. Both expose the same surface. See the [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) and [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/) pages.
- The local bearer token, which the caller must send with every request. See [Authentication](#authentication).

### Grant syntax

The argument is the route path. It starts with `/`, may contain `{name}` segments, and is required.

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `http-api.route:/notes/search` | yes | one literal path |
| `http-api.route:/notes/{id}` | yes | `{id}` matches one non-empty path segment |
| `http-api.route` | no | the argument is required |
| `http-api.route:*` | no | a wildcard is not accepted |
| `http-api.route:notes/search` | no | the path must start with `/` |
| `http-api.route:https://example.com/notes` | no | a URL is not a route path; the listener is loopback only |

### Manifest entry

Each route needs one `http_routes` entry and one grant. The manifest must contain both. Install refuses a manifest where they do not match (`manifest.grant-argument`).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["http-api.route:/notes/search", "http-api.route:/notes/{id}"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "http_routes": [
      { "method": "GET", "path": "/notes/search" },
      { "method": "GET", "path": "/notes/{id}" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The method is an upper-case HTTP method name. Each route is served at `/plugins/<plugin-id>/<path>`, so `/notes/{id}` of `com.example.notes` is served at `/plugins/com.example.notes/notes/{id}`. Two plugins cannot collide, because each plugin owns its own prefix.

### Surface

The capability adds one import and one event. Each `respond` call answers exactly one `http-called` event.

```wit
respond: func(call: u64, status: u16, headers: list<tuple<string, string>>,
              body: list<u8>) -> result<_, plugin-error>;

record http-called-event { call: u64, method: string, path: string,
                           headers: list<tuple<string, string>>, body: list<u8> }
```

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `respond` (import) | `http_api::respond(call, status, &headers, &body)` returns `Result<(), PluginError>` | `respond(call, status, headers, body)` returns `void` and throws `PluginError` | Sends the response for one open call. Import path: `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http_api` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http-api`. |
| `http-called` (event) | `Event::HttpCalled(HttpCalledEvent)` | `{ tag: 'http-called', val: HttpCalledEvent }` | A request matched a granted route. Delivered in `on_events`. Never dropped. |
| `call` | `u64` | `bigint` | Identifies one open request. Pass it back unchanged to `respond`. |
| `method` | `String` | `string` | The request method in upper case. |
| `path` | `String` | `string` | The concrete path with `{name}` values in place, and the query string kept. |
| `headers` | `Vec<(String, String)>` | `[string, string][]` | The request headers. |
| `body` | `Vec<u8>` | `Uint8Array` | The request body, at most 1 MiB. |
| `status` (argument) | `u16` | `number` | 100 to 599. |
| `headers` (argument) | `&[(String, String)]` | `[string, string][]` | Response headers. No hop-by-hop headers. |
| `body` (argument) | `&[u8]` | `Uint8Array` | Response body, at most 8 MiB. |

The listener does not parse `{name}` values or the query string. The plugin reads them from `path`.

### Matching rules

- The listener matches the method and the path without the query string. `GET /notes/42?full=1` matches `GET /notes/{id}`.
- `{name}` matches exactly one non-empty segment. `/notes/{id}` matches `/notes/42` but not `/notes/` or `/notes/42/tags`.
- A method must be declared. A `POST` to a path that only declares `GET` gets `405 Method Not Allowed` with an `Allow` header.
- The plugin receives `path` with the query string, so it must strip the query string before comparing routes.

### Limits and timing

| Limit | Value | Result when exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Request body | 1 MiB | The listener answers `413 Content Too Large`. The plugin never sees the request. |
| Response body (`respond`) | 8 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Response status (`respond`) | 100 to 599 | `invalid-argument` |
| Response headers (`respond`) | No hop-by-hop header | `invalid-argument` |
| Time to answer | 30 s | The listener answers `504 Gateway Timeout` and closes the call. |

The hop-by-hop headers are `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding` and `Upgrade`. The check ignores case.

### Authentication

The route is protected by a bearer token. The listener checks, in this order:

1. The `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`. Anything else gets `403 Forbidden`.
2. A request with an `Origin` header gets `403 Forbidden`. This blocks web pages in the user's browser.
3. The request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing or wrong token gets `401 Unauthorized`.
4. The route and method must match a granted route. Otherwise the listener answers `404` or `405`.
5. The body must be at most 1 MiB. Otherwise `413`.

Only then does the plugin receive `http-called`. The server writes a fresh token at each start to `http-api.token`, and the port to `http-api.port`. Both files are owner-only and sit beside the session socket in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ilium/`. When no runtime directory exists, the OS temporary directory is used. A program run by the same user can read these files. A program run by another user cannot.

### Risk, review and tiers

- The grant has normal risk. It is not marked high risk (H), so a T2 or T3 package lists it checked by default in the install review. A T1 bundled plugin gets it up to its manifest ceiling.
- The grant is server side only. The review dialog shows one row per route, with the grant string on the right.
- A declined route is not served. A revoked grant withdraws the route, so later requests get `404 Not Found`. This is the same answer a path that does not exist gets, so a caller cannot tell a declined route from a missing one.

│ com.example.http 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                      │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Serves local API routes <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………</span> http-api.route:/notes/* │

### Routing flow

  <rect x="10" y="188" width="340" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="180" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">4. Plugin calls respond(call, status, headers, body)</text>
  <text x="180" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor">Dashed box: kernel policy, not plugin code.</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The listener rejects a request before the plugin sees it. The plugin answers each call once.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Responses from the listener

The listener answers these cases itself. The plugin does not run for them.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401 Unauthorized` | The bearer token is missing or wrong. |
| `403 Forbidden` | The `Host` header is not loopback for this port, or the request has an `Origin` header. |
| `404 Not Found` | No granted route covers the path, or the route was declined or revoked. |
| `405 Method Not Allowed` | The path is known, but the method is not declared. The `Allow` header lists the declared methods. |
| `413 Content Too Large` | The request body is over 1 MiB. |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | The plugin is stopped, failed or disabled, or the call was open when the plugin stopped or the grant was revoked. |
| `504 Gateway Timeout` | The plugin did not call `respond` within 30 s. |

### Errors from respond

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `not-found` | The call was already answered, timed out or lost its caller. A second `respond` for the same call gets this code. |
| `invalid-argument` | The status is outside 100 to 599, the body is over 8 MiB, or a header is hop-by-hop. |

A `not-found` error means no response is needed, because the caller has already gone or been answered. Do not retry it.

### Worked example: GET /notes/{id} in Rust

The route returns one note as JSON. An unknown id gets `404` with a JSON error body. `find_note_json` is the plugin's own code and is not part of the SDK. It returns `Option<String>`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http_api;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::HttpCalledEvent;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NoteLookup;

impl Handler for NoteLookup {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            if let Event::HttpCalled(request) = event {
                answer_note_lookup(&request);
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

fn answer_note_lookup(request: &HttpCalledEvent) {
    // The path keeps its query string. Only the part before "?" is the route.
    let route_path = request.path.split('?').next().unwrap_or("");
    let Some(note_id) = route_path.strip_prefix("/notes/") else {
        // The listener only sends granted paths, so this is a defensive answer.
        let _ = http_api::respond(request.call, 404, &[], &[]);
        return;
    };
    let Some(note_json) = find_note_json(note_id) else {
        let body = br#"{"error":"note not found"}"#;
        let _ = http_api::respond(request.call, 404, &json_headers(), body);
        return;
    };
    // An Err here means the call already closed. Nothing is left to send.
    let _ = http_api::respond(request.call, 200, &json_headers(), note_json.as_bytes());
}

fn json_headers() -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    vec![("content-type".to_string(), "application/json".to_string())]
}
```

### Worked example: GET /notes/{id} in TypeScript

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { respond } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http-api';
import type { Event, HttpCalledEvent } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { findNoteJson } from './notes';

const JSON_HEADERS: [string, string][] = [['content-type', 'application/json']];

export const { handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'http-called') {
        answerNoteLookup(event.val);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});

function answerNoteLookup(request: HttpCalledEvent): void {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const routePath = request.path.split('?')[0];
  const noteId = routePath.startsWith('/notes/') ? routePath.slice('/notes/'.length) : '';
  const noteJson = noteId === '' ? undefined : findNoteJson(noteId);
  if (noteJson === undefined) {
    reply(request.call, 404, JSON_HEADERS, encoder.encode('{"error":"note not found"}'));
    return;
  }
  reply(request.call, 200, JSON_HEADERS, encoder.encode(noteJson));
}

// respond throws PluginError when the call already closed. Nothing is left to send.
function reply(
  call: bigint,
  status: number,
  headers: [string, string][],
  body: Uint8Array,
): void {
  try {
    respond(call, status, headers, body);
  } catch {
    // The caller left, or the 30 s reply limit passed.
  }
}
```

### What the caller sees

Run the plugin, then call the route from a terminal. The token and port come from the two owner-only files.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> TOKEN=$(cat "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ilium/http-api.token")
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> PORT=$(cat "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ilium/http-api.port")
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> BASE="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/plugins/com.example.notes"
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$BASE/notes/42"
{"id":"42","title":"Weekly plan"}
<span class="t-ok">200</span>
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "$BASE/notes/42"
<span class="t-err">401</span>
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$BASE/notes/7/tags"
<span class="t-warn">404</span>
</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. A request with the token, one without it, and a path that no route covers.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Edge cases

- **Query strings.** `path` keeps the query string. Route matching ignores it, so `/notes/42?full=1` reaches the same route.
- **Several parameters.** A route may declare more than one segment, such as `/notes/{id}/tags/{tag}`. Each segment matches one non-empty value.
- **Empty bodies.** A reply with no body is valid: `respond(call, 204, [], [])` in Rust takes `&[]` for the body.
- **Stopped plugin.** If the plugin stops while a call is open, the caller gets `503`. Any later `respond` for that call returns `not-found`.
- **Slow handlers.** The 30 s limit covers the whole time from the event to `respond`. Start slow work in a task or a job, and answer when it completes.
- **Kernel routes.** The kernel's own API routes, such as the agent creation route, are served under `/api/` with the same token. They do not use this grant.

### See also

- [http-api](/pages/api-http-api/) for the `http-api` import and its event, with the full SDK examples.
- [capabilities](/pages/capabilities/) for how grants are requested, reviewed and revoked.
- [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) for the `http_routes` field.
- [cli.contribute](/pages/capability-cli-contribute/) for a subcommand that gives the same kind of output on the command line.
- [http](/pages/capability-http/) for requests that go out from the plugin instead of in.

Checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` (API draft of 2026-10-11).

### Security

Listener rules and token handling are in [Network egress](/pages/reference-network-egress/) ([SEC-097] to [SEC-099]).

# Capability: inference

## inference

The `inference` capability lets a plugin ask the language model provider that the user selected for a completion, and ask which models that provider offers. The plugin never names a provider. The kernel routes each request to the chosen provider, and the AI admission gate checks every request before it leaves the machine. A request that the gate refuses never reaches the provider.

Use this capability for features that need a model's answer, such as a generated note title or a tag suggestion. Keep every feature working without it. A user who has no provider, or who declined the grant, must still get the plain, non-AI result.

**You need:**

- an `inference` grant on the server or client side. Scenes cannot request it. A background job runs with the grants of its plugin side and may call `inference` as well (see [jobs](/pages/capability-jobs-run/)).
- a provider selected by the user in Settings. Without one, every call returns `not-found` at once.
- no language runtime beyond the SDK for your language. The examples below use Rust and TypeScript.

A plugin that supplies a model is covered on the [inference.provide](/pages/capability-inference-provide/) page.

### Grant syntax

The grant takes no argument.

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `inference` | yes | the only form |
| `inference:anthropic` | no | the grant takes no argument; the user picks the provider |
| `inference.provide` | no | a different grant, for plugins that supply a provider |

### Surface

Every call that returns a `request-id` is a slow call. It returns at once and completes later as a `request-completed` event. The SDK wraps each one in an `async` function, so most plugins never see the raw form.

| WIT function | Rust (`host::inference`) | TypeScript (`host/inference`) | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `complete(request)` | `complete(request).await` | `await complete(request)` | `Completion` |
| `take-completion(id)` | `take_completion(id)` | `takeCompletion(id)` | `Option<Completion>` |
| `models()` | `models().await` | `await models()` | `Vec<String>` |
| `take-models(id)` | `take_models(id)` | `takeModels(id)` | `Option<Vec<String>>` |

The raw `complete` and `models` functions, which return a request id, are available as `complete_request` and `models_request` in Rust.

| WIT record | Fields | Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat-message` | `role: string`, `content: string` | `ChatMessage` | `{ role, content }` |
| `completion-request` | `messages: list<chat-message>`, `max-output-tokens: option<u32>`, `json-schema: option<string>`, `purpose: string` | `CompletionRequest` | `CompletionRequest` with `maxOutputTokens`, `jsonSchema` |
| `completion` | `text: string`, `model: string`, `input-tokens: u32`, `output-tokens: u32` | `Completion` | `{ text, model, inputTokens, outputTokens }` |

The Rust `Option` fields map to `undefined` in TypeScript when unset.

### Request fields

- `messages` must hold at least one message. Each `role` is `system`, `user` or `assistant`. Any other value is `invalid-argument`.
- `max-output-tokens: none` asks for the model's maximum output. Set a value only when the feature needs a shorter answer. The value `0` is `invalid-argument`.
- `json-schema` asks the provider for output that matches the schema. The schema is at most 64 KiB and must be valid JSON Schema. The provider can still return text that does not match, so parse and check the result in your code.
- `purpose` names the feature that makes the request. It is 1 to 64 bytes from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`. The admission gate and the privacy log both use it, so name the feature honestly. Do not reuse one purpose for two features.

### How a call flows

<figure>

    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="10" y="8" width="300" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>

  <rect x="10" y="66" width="300" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="160" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Admission gate: kernel policy for AI requests</text>

  <rect x="10" y="240" width="300" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="160" y="264" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Event request-completed, then take-completion</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The dashed step is kernel policy. The plugin does not choose the provider or bypass the gate.</figcaption>

</figure>

The kernel answers a call in one of three ways. A refusal by policy returns `not-permitted` and writes no privacy line. A throttle returns `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms`. An admitted request adds one line to the privacy log with the plugin id, the `purpose`, the provider id, the model and the token counts. Settings > Privacy lists that log.

A completed result stays available for 30 s or until you take it, whichever comes first. A take is one-shot: a second `take-completion` for the same id returns `none`.

### Worked example: a note title in Rust

This example starts a request from a handler without blocking it. The title arrives in the log.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, ChatMessage, CompletionRequest};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Asks the user's chosen provider for a five-word title for a note.
async fn suggest_note_title(note_text: String) -> Result<String, PluginError> {
    let request = CompletionRequest {
        messages: vec![
            ChatMessage {
                role: "system".into(),
                content: "Reply with a title of five words.".into(),
            },
            ChatMessage { role: "user".into(), content: note_text },
        ],
        max_output_tokens: Some(32),
        json_schema: None,
        purpose: "note-title".into(),
    };
    let completion = inference::complete(request).await?;
    Ok(completion.text)
}

/// Starts the request and returns at once, so the event handler is not held up.
fn on_note_saved(note_text: String) {
    task::spawn(async move {
        match suggest_note_title(note_text).await {
            Ok(title) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("note title: {title}")),
            Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("no title: {:?}", error.code)),
        }
    });
}
```

The `?` operator returns the error to the caller. `Err` holds a `PluginError` with a `code`, a `message` and an optional `retry_after_ms`.

### Worked example: tags with a JSON schema in TypeScript

This example asks for structured output and handles the codes that matter for it.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { complete } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import type { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

const TAG_SCHEMA = JSON.stringify({
  type: 'object',
  properties: { tags: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } },
  required: ['tags'],
});

/** Returns up to three tags for a note. An empty list means no tags, not a failure. */
export async function suggestTags(noteText: string): Promise<string[]> {
  try {
    const completion = await complete({
      messages: [
        { role: 'system', content: 'Return up to three lowercase tags for the note.' },
        { role: 'user', content: noteText },
      ],
      maxOutputTokens: 64,
      jsonSchema: TAG_SCHEMA,
      purpose: 'tree-organisation',
    });
    const parsed = JSON.parse(completion.text) as { tags?: string[] };
    return parsed.tags ?? [];
  } catch (error) {
    const failure = error as PluginError;
    if (failure.code === 'not-found') {
      log('info', 'no AI provider selected; skipping tags');
      return [];
    }
    if (failure.code === 'rate-limited') {
      log('warn', `tags throttled, retry after ${failure.retryAfterMs ?? 0} ms`);
      return [];
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

The function returns an empty list for the two codes that mean "no tags right now". Every other code is a bug or an outage, so it is thrown to the caller.

Use `models()` to show the user which models the provider offers, for example in a picker. The list is empty when the provider offers no models. That is not an error.

### Errors and edge cases

| Code | When it happens | Retry |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | the grant is missing or declined; the gate refuses the request by policy, for example a purpose or provider the user blocked | no |
| `not-found` | no provider is selected; the call does not wait for one | after the user selects a provider |
| `invalid-argument` | no messages, a bad role, an empty or malformed `purpose`, `max-output-tokens: 0`, input over 4 MiB, or a schema over 64 KiB or invalid | no, fix the call |
| `rate-limited` | the gate throttles the request; `retry-after-ms` is set | yes, after the delay |
| `timed-out` | the provider does not answer within 120 s | yes |
| `network` | the provider cannot be reached | yes |
| `busy` | the pending request list of the plugin is full | yes, later |
| `quota-exceeded` | the CPU budget of the execution quota group is spent; `retry-after-ms` is set | yes, after the delay |
| `revoked` | the user revoked the grant during the call; the pending request completes as failed | no; the plugin is re-activated |

The provider can also return its own error code, which the kernel passes on unchanged.

If your feature must wait for a provider, declare the service requirement in the manifest. The plugin then activates only when a compatible provider runs:

```json
{
  "requires": { "services": ["ilium:inference/provider@0.1.0"] }
}
```

### What the user sees

The install dialog shows one row for the grant, in the server or client group. The row wording is fixed by the platform:

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.inference 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                 │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Asks the selected language model <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………</span> inference │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests inference, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>

</figure>

- A T1 bundled plugin receives the grant automatically, up to its manifest ceiling.
- The grant is normal risk, not high risk. A T2 or T3 package lists it checked by default. The user can uncheck it, and the plugin then sees the grant missing in its `granted` list.
- A grant declined at install is shown dimmed and unchecked. Your feature must keep working without it.
- The user can revoke the grant later in Settings > Plugins > Capabilities. Calls in flight return `revoked`.

### Risk and privacy rules

- Requests send the user's project content to the chosen provider. Send only the text the feature needs, and never a whole project when a note is enough.
- Every admitted request is recorded in the privacy log. Use a `purpose` that the user can recognise in that log.
- The grant does not let the plugin pick a provider or bypass the gate.

- 43 Tree organisation, which also uses `json-schema`.
- 46 Inferred-title icons.
- 66 Smart Copy AI, which also uses `json-schema`.
- 77 Convert a session between Claude and Codex.
- 80 Remote compaction.

# Capability: inference.provide

## inference.provide

The `inference.provide` grant lets a plugin act as the AI model provider that the user selects in Settings. Features in other plugins call `inference.complete` (see [inference](/pages/capability-inference/)). The kernel routes each call to the selected provider by calling its `complete` export. The provider does its work and answers later through the `inference.provider-reply` import, with the same call number. The kernel never waits inside `complete`, so a slow network request does not block anything.

A provider receives every prompt that the user's features send to it. Say where the prompts go in the plugin description and on its settings page.

### What you need

- **The grant `inference.provide`.** It takes no argument and has normal risk, so the install dialog checks it by default.
- **One grant `http:<provider-host>` per host** the provider calls, for example `http:api.provider.example`. Requests to those hosts also pass the AI admission gate.
- **The export `inference-provider`** in the manifest `exports` list, for the side that implements it (`server` or `client`). The component also exports `lifecycle` and `handler`. Those two are required and are never listed (N9).
- **A toolchain.** Rust stable 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, plus `ilium-plugin-sdk` and `serde_json` (the Rust example uses it). Or Bun 1.2 or later with `@ilium/plugin-sdk` (S14).
- **A settings field for the API key**, declared with `"secret": true` in the settings schema. Settings masks the value, the host redacts it from logs, and only the owning plugin can read it (P3).

### Grant syntax

The grant takes no argument.

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `inference.provide` | yes | the only form |
| `inference.provide:example` | no | the grant takes no argument |
| `inference-provider` | no | that is the export name, not a grant |

### Surface

The provider implements two exports. Both are required when the manifest lists `inference-provider`.

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inference-provider.complete` (export) | `fn complete(&mut self, call: ProviderCall) -> Result<(), PluginError>` | `complete(call)` | Accepts one request. `Ok` accepts it; an `Err` fails the caller's request with that error. The reply comes later. |
| `inference-provider.models` (export) | `fn models(&mut self) -> Vec<String>` | `models()` | The model names the provider offers. Consumers read them with `inference.models`. |
| `inference.provider-reply` (import) | `inference::provider_reply(call, outcome)` | `providerReply(call, outcome)` | Answers one call with `Ok(Completion)` or `Err(PluginError)`. It returns nothing and never blocks. |

The Rust names come from `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports` (the export traits and records) and `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference` (the import and the records). The TypeScript names come from `@ilium/plugin-sdk` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference`.

| Record | Field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `provider-call` | `call` | `u64` | `bigint` | The kernel's call number. Pass it back unchanged. |
| | `request` | `CompletionRequest` | `CompletionRequest` | The request, as below. |
| `completion-request` | `messages` | `Vec<ChatMessage>` | `ChatMessage[]` | The conversation in order. Never empty. |
| | `max_output_tokens` | `Option<u32>` | `number` or `undefined` | `None` asks for the model's maximum output. |
| | `json_schema` | `Option<String>` | `string` or `undefined` | A JSON Schema document as text. The reply is still plain text. |
| | `purpose` | `String` | `string` | The feature name, for example `note-tags`. The gate and the privacy log use it. |
| `chat-message` | `role` | `String` | `string` | `system`, `user` or `assistant`, as sent. |
| | `content` | `String` | `string` | The text of the message. |
| `completion` | `text` | `String` | `string` | The reply exactly as the provider wrote it. Up to 4 MiB. |
| | `model` | `String` | `string` | The model that answered. |
| | `input_tokens` | `u32` | `number` | Tokens in the request. |
| | `output_tokens` | `u32` | `number` | Tokens in the reply. |

TypeScript passes a WIT `result` as a tagged object: `{ tag: 'ok', val: completion }` or `{ tag: 'err', val: pluginError }`.

### How a request flows

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 190" role="img" aria-label="Provider call flow: the kernel calls complete, the provider makes an HTTP request, the provider calls provider-reply, and the caller receives the completion">
<defs>
<marker id="ipv-arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto">
<path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>
</marker>
</defs>
<rect x="20" y="10" width="380" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
<text x="210" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">1. Kernel calls complete(call) on the provider</text>
<line x1="210" y1="40" x2="210" y2="56" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#ipv-arrow)"/>
<rect x="20" y="56" width="380" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
<text x="210" y="75" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">2. Provider calls its own service over HTTP</text>
<line x1="210" y1="86" x2="210" y2="102" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#ipv-arrow)"/>
<rect x="20" y="102" width="380" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
<text x="210" y="121" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">3. Provider calls provider-reply(call, outcome)</text>
<line x1="210" y1="132" x2="210" y2="148" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#ipv-arrow)"/>
<rect x="20" y="148" width="380" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
<text x="210" y="167" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">4. The caller receives the completion or the error</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The provider answers asynchronously. The call number ties the reply to the request that the kernel sent.</figcaption>
</figure>

The `complete` export must return at once. Work that needs the network runs in a task (`task::spawn` in Rust, a promise in TypeScript), and the task answers through `provider_reply`. The kernel drops a reply whose call number is unknown, answered or expired.

### Worked example 1: a Rust provider

The manifest lists only the optional export. `lifecycle` and `handler` are required, so the component implements them and the manifest does not name them.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.provider",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["inference-provider"]
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["inference.provide", "http:api.provider.example"]
  }
}
```

The provider reads its API key from its settings, sends the conversation to the provider's HTTP API, and answers the call:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{InferenceProvider, ProviderCall};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, Header, HttpRequest, HttpResponse};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::inference::{self, Completion};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::task;

const PROVIDER_URL: &str = "https://api.provider.example/v1/chat";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["inference-provider"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ExampleProvider;

impl Lifecycle for ExampleProvider {}

impl Handler for ExampleProvider {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl InferenceProvider for ExampleProvider {
    fn complete(&mut self, call: ProviderCall) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let settings: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or_default();
        let api_key = settings["apiKey"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
        let messages: Vec<serde_json::Value> = call
            .request
            .messages
            .iter()
            .map(|message| {
                serde_json::json!({ "role": message.role, "content": message.content })
            })
            .collect();
        let body = serde_json::json!({
            "messages": messages,
            "max_tokens": call.request.max_output_tokens,
        });
        let request = HttpRequest {
            method: "POST".into(),
            url: PROVIDER_URL.into(),
            headers: vec![
                Header { name: "authorization".into(), value: format!("Bearer {api_key}") },
                Header { name: "content-type".into(), value: "application/json".into() },
            ],
            body: Some(body.to_string().into_bytes()),
            timeout_millis: 60_000,
        };
        let call_number = call.call;
        task::spawn(async move {
            let outcome = match http::fetch(request).await {
                Ok(response) => parse_reply(response),
                Err(error) => Err(error),
            };
            inference::provider_reply(call_number, outcome);
        });
        Ok(())
    }

    fn models(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {
        vec!["example-model-1".to_owned()]
    }
}

fn parse_reply(response: HttpResponse) -> Result<Completion, PluginError> {
    let failure = |message: String| PluginError {
        code: ErrorCode::Network,
        message,
        retry_after_ms: None,
    };
    if response.status != 200 {
        return Err(failure(format!("provider answered HTTP {}", response.status)));
    }
    let reply: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(&response.body).map_err(|error| failure(error.to_string()))?;
    Ok(Completion {
        text: reply["text"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(),
        model: reply["model"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(),
        input_tokens: u32::try_from(reply["input_tokens"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0)).unwrap_or(0),
        output_tokens: u32::try_from(reply["output_tokens"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0)).unwrap_or(0),
    })
}
```

The settings schema declares the key as `"apiKey": { "type": "string", "secret": true }`.

### Worked example 2: a TypeScript provider

The same manifest applies. The TypeScript entry module exports the same three names: `lifecycle`, `handler` and `inferenceProvider`.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { fetch as httpFetch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import { providerReply, type Completion } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/inference';
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

const PROVIDER_URL = 'https://api.provider.example/v1/chat';

function networkFailure(message: string) {
  return {
    tag: 'err' as const,
    val: { code: 'network' as const, message, retryAfterMs: undefined },
  };
}

// The SDK's fetch is renamed on import so it does not shadow the global fetch.
async function answer(callNumber: bigint, apiKey: string, body: string): Promise<void> {
  let outcome;
  try {
    const response = await httpFetch({
      method: 'POST',
      url: PROVIDER_URL,
      headers: [
        { name: 'authorization', value: `Bearer ${apiKey}` },
        { name: 'content-type', value: 'application/json' },
      ],
      body: new TextEncoder().encode(body),
      timeoutMillis: 60_000,
    });
    if (response.status !== 200) {
      outcome = networkFailure(`provider answered HTTP ${response.status}`);
    } else {
      const reply = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(response.body));
      const completion: Completion = {
        text: reply.text,
        model: reply.model,
        inputTokens: reply.input_tokens,
        outputTokens: reply.output_tokens,
      };
      outcome = { tag: 'ok' as const, val: completion };
    }
  } catch (error) {
    outcome = networkFailure(String(error));
  }
  providerReply(callNumber, outcome);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, inferenceProvider } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(): Submission[] {
    return [];
  },
  complete(call) {
    const settings = JSON.parse(getJson()) as { apiKey?: string };
    const messages = call.request.messages.map((message) => ({
      role: message.role,
      content: message.content,
    }));
    const body = JSON.stringify({ messages, max_tokens: call.request.maxOutputTokens ?? null });
    // answer() catches every failure itself, so the promise never rejects.
    void answer(call.call, settings.apiKey ?? '', body);
  },
  models: () => ['example-model-1'],
});
```

### Edge cases and errors

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| No provider selected | The caller's `inference.complete` returns `not-found` at once. It does not wait. |
| Selected provider installed but not running | The call starts it and waits up to its activation deadline (2,000 ms by default). If it does not start in time, the caller's request fails with `timed-out`. |
| Grant declined at install | The plugin installs, is never selected, and Settings shows it as unavailable. |
| Export listed without the grant | Install refuses the package with `manifest.export-grant`. |
| Grant revoked while installed | The plugin is deactivated and re-activated with the reduced grant set. It is no longer selected. |
| `complete` returns `Err` | The caller's request fails with that error. |
| Reply after the caller's 120 s deadline | The caller already has `failed(timed-out)`. The late `provider-reply` returns `not-found` to the provider. |
| Second reply for one call | The second call returns `not-found`. |
| Reply text over 4 MiB | `provider-reply` returns `invalid-argument`. |
| Reply sent without the grant | The reply is dropped and the host writes a refusal line to the plugin log. The caller times out. |
| Gate refuses the purpose or provider | The caller gets `not-permitted`. The same gate applies to the provider's own HTTP calls to its host. |
| Gate throttles the call | The caller gets `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms` (A16, A17). |
| HTTP to a host without a grant | `http.fetch` returns `not-permitted` and the plugin log records the refusal. |
| Trap or deadline breach in `complete` | A failure under the restart rule. It follows the [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule): restart after 1 s, then 5 s, and disable at the third failure inside 10 minutes. |
| Empty `messages` or input over 4 MiB | The caller's `inference.complete` returns `invalid-argument` before the provider sees it. |

Codes a provider can return from `complete` are the plugin's own: use `invalid-argument` when the request breaks a rule the provider checks (for example, no messages), and `unsupported` when the provider does not offer the requested model.

### Limits

| Limit | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Request input, one call | 4 MiB | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) |
| `json_schema` | 64 KiB | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) |
| Reply text | 4 MiB | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) |
| Caller's deadline | 120 s | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) |
| `complete` and `models` deadline | `command_deadline_ms`, 50 ms by default | [Resource limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) |
| Activation deadline of a stopped provider | 2,000 ms by default | [Resource limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) |
| Memory of the provider instance | 32 MiB by default | [Resource limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) |

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests inference.provide, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>

- **Install review.** The dialog shows one row per grant, and the rows use the wording of G9. Both grants are checked by default because they have normal risk.
- **Settings.** Settings > Plugins lists the provider with its capability list. Settings > Plugins > (provider) shows it as unavailable if the grant was declined. Requests go to the provider that the user selected in Settings, and the plugin cannot choose another one.
- **Secret field.** The API key appears masked. The host never stores it in the snapshot (P3).
- **Privacy log.** Each request that the gate admits adds one line to the privacy log: the consumer's plugin id, the `purpose`, the provider, the model and the token counts. Settings > Privacy shows that log (api-inference).
- **Revocation.** `ilium plugin grants com.example.provider --revoke inference.provide` takes the grant away. The plugin is re-activated without it and is no longer selected.

### Security

`inference.provide` is high risk: the provider sees every prompt other plugins send. See [Threat model](/pages/reference-threat-model/) ([SEC-007]) and [User security and privacy](/pages/user-plugin-security-and-privacy/).

# Capability: jobs.run

## jobs.run

The `jobs.run` grant lets a plugin start background jobs. A job runs the plugin's `job-runner.run` export on a separate worker instance, with its own CPU deadline, wall-clock deadline and memory limit. The job never shares memory with the code that started it.

Use a job for work that is too long for an event handler, such as scanning a large folder, parsing a long transcript or building an export. Work that finishes in a few milliseconds needs no job. The starting side uses three calls (`start`, `cancel` and `take-output`), and the job side uses three more (`report-progress`, `is-cancelled` and `wait-request`). This page covers the grant, the limits, the failure rules and the review dialog. The full function reference is on the [jobs](/pages/api-jobs/) page.

### What you need

- The `jobs.run` grant. It takes no argument.
- A `job-runner` export. Add `"job-runner"` to the manifest `exports` list of the side that runs the job, and implement it: the `JobRunner` trait in Rust, or the `run` member of `definePlugin` in TypeScript. The `with-jobs` world fragment adds the import and export (section 8.5 of the API). See [exports](/pages/api-exports/).
- One `contributes.jobs` entry for every job kind the plugin starts.
- A side that supports jobs: `server`, `client` or `scene`. A scene declares the grant in `capabilities.scene`.

Manifest for the worked examples below:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.logs",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": ["job-runner"]
  },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["jobs.run", "fs.read:project", "agent.read"] },
  "contributes": {
    "jobs": [ { "kind": "count-errors", "deadline_ms": 5000, "memory_mib": 64 } ]
  }
}
```

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `jobs.run` | yes | the only form |
| `jobs.run:any` | no | the grant takes no argument (`manifest.grant-argument`) |
| `jobs` | no | the grant name is incomplete (`manifest.grant-unknown`) |

### Risk and install

- The grant has the `normal` risk level. A T1 bundled plugin receives it at activation, up to the manifest ceiling in the table below.
- A T2 or T3 package lists the grant in the review dialog, checked by default. The user can uncheck it. A declined grant is shown dimmed, and the plugin's `granted` list omits it.
- The host refuses a package whose component exports differ from its manifest `exports` list, with `manifest.exports-mismatch`. A `contributes.jobs` entry without a `job-runner` export fails for that reason.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.jobs 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                      │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Runs background work <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> jobs.run │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests jobs.run, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Surface

| Name | Rust | TypeScript | Runs in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | `jobs::start(kind, &input).await` returns `Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError>`; `jobs::start_request` returns the request id | `await start(kind, input)` returns `Promise<Uint8Array>`; `startRequest` returns the request id | server, client, scene | Starts a declared kind. The async form resolves to the output bytes. |
| `start_json` | `jobs::start_json(kind, &value)` | `startJson(kind, value)` | starting side | Encodes the value as JSON bytes. The job decodes it. |
| `cancel` | `jobs::cancel(job)` | `cancel(job)` | starting side | Sets the cancel flag and returns at once. |
| `take-output` | `jobs::take_output(job)` returns `Option<Vec<u8>>` | `takeOutput(job)` returns `Uint8Array \| undefined` | starting side | Returns the output once, after an `ok` completion. |
| `report-progress` | `jobs::report_progress(percent)`, `f32` | `reportProgress(percent)` | job only | Reports a value from 0 to 100. |
| `is-cancelled` | `jobs::is_cancelled()` returns `bool` | `isCancelled()` | job only | Returns true after a cancel. |
| `wait-request` | `jobs::wait_request(request, timeout_millis)` | `waitRequest(request, timeoutMillis)` | job only | Blocks until a slow call completes, such as `fs.read-all`. |
| `run` | `JobRunner::run(&mut self, kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError>` | `run(kind, input)` member of `definePlugin` | job instance | Does the work and returns the output bytes, or fails with a `PluginError`. |

Two events report the job to the starting side. `job-progress` carries the `request-id` and the `percent`; only the newest value per job reaches the plugin in one batch. `request-completed` carries the outcome: `ok`, `cancelled` or `failed(code)`.

A job instance has no `activate` and no event handler. It may call `log`, `clock`, `codec`, `fs`, `http`, `process`, `inference`, `storage.get` and `storage.keys`, with the grants of its side. Every other import returns `unsupported`.

### Limits

Each limit has a default, a ceiling for the plugin's tier, and an effect when it is reached. The manifest may ask for more than the default, up to the ceiling. A request above the ceiling is clamped and logged, never refused. The user can change the host-side values under `[plugins.limits]` in `config.toml`.

| Limit | Default | T1 ceiling | T2 and T3 ceiling | Over the limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPU deadline (`deadline_ms`) | 2 s | 60 s | 10 s | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Wall-clock deadline | 20 s | 600 s | 100 s | `failed(timed-out)` |
| Memory (`memory_mib`) | 64 MiB | 512 MiB | 256 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| Input, and output, each | 16 MiB | 64 MiB | 16 MiB | input: `invalid-argument` at the call; output: `failed(invalid-argument)` |
| Concurrent jobs per plugin | 2 | 8 | 2 | extra jobs wait in the queue |
| Queued jobs | 16 | 64 | 16 | `busy` |
| Pending requests per plugin | 64 | 256 | 64 | `busy` |

The per-kind values in `contributes.jobs` override the CPU and memory defaults for that kind, within the same ceilings. Time spent in `wait-request` counts against the wall-clock deadline only. All plugins in one server or client share `session_job_workers`, which defaults to `min(4, cores / 2)` with a minimum of 1. Jobs queue when those workers are busy.

### How a job runs

<figure>

  <text x="160" y="218" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">request-completed; take-output reads bytes</text>

<figcaption>The job runs apart from the event handler, and its result comes back as a completed request.</figcaption>
</figure>

The starting side gets a request id at once. A job waits in the queue while the concurrency limit is full. Later jobs of the same plugin reuse the job instance. A finished result stays available to `take-output` for 30 s or until it is taken. A second take, or a take after the 30 s, returns `none`, which the async wrapper reports as `not-found`.

### Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Grant declined, or revoked while the plugin runs | `start` returns `not-permitted`, and `run` is never called. Pending jobs that need the grant complete as `failed(revoked)`. |
| Kind not listed in `contributes.jobs` | `start` returns `invalid-argument`. |
| Input over the input limit | `start` returns `invalid-argument` at once. Nothing is queued. |
| Job queue full | `start` returns `busy`. Jobs within the queue limit wait without an error. |
| Output over the output limit | The job completes as `failed(invalid-argument)`. |
| CPU or wall-clock deadline passed | `failed(timed-out)`. |
| Memory limit reached | `failed(quota-exceeded)`. |
| Trap inside `run` | `failed(internal)`, with the trap text. The failure does not count toward the plugin restart rule. |
| `run` returns a `plugin-error` | The job fails with that error code and message. |
| `cancel` called | The outcome is `cancelled`, whatever the job returns, and its output is dropped. A queued job never starts. |
| `cancel` on a finished job | No effect. |
| `start` called from inside a job | `unsupported`. |
| `wait-request` called outside `run` | `unsupported`. |
| Plugin disabled while jobs run | Pending jobs are cancelled. |

`report-progress` clamps a value below 0 to 0 and a value above 100 to 100. A NaN value is ignored.

### Example in Rust

The plugin counts error lines in a log file each time an agent goes idle. The handler reads the file, starts the job and logs the result. The job counts the lines and reports progress.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, jobs, log::{self, Level}};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::task;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

const COUNT_KIND: &str = "count-errors";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["job-runner"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ErrorCounter;

impl Lifecycle for ErrorCounter {}

impl Handler for ErrorCounter {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { current, .. }) = event
            else { continue; };
            if current == AgentActivity::Idle {
                task::spawn(count_errors_after_idle());
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

async fn count_errors_after_idle() {
    let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: "logs/session.log".into() };
    let transcript = match fs::read_all(path).await {
        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
        Err(error) => {
            log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("read failed: {}", error.message));
            return;
        }
    };
    match jobs::start(COUNT_KIND, &transcript).await {
        Ok(output) => {
            let errors = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output);
            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("errors: {errors}"));
        }
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("count failed: {}", error.message)),
    }
}

impl JobRunner for ErrorCounter {
    // Only kinds declared in contributes.jobs reach this function.
    fn run(&mut self, _kind: String, input: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PluginError> {
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&input);
        let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
        let mut count = 0u32;
        for (index, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
            if jobs::is_cancelled() {
                break; // the outcome is already cancelled, so the output is dropped
            }
            if line.contains("error") {
                count += 1;
            }
            if index % 1000 == 0 {
                jobs::report_progress(100.0 * index as f32 / lines.len() as f32);
            }
        }
        jobs::report_progress(100.0);
        Ok(count.to_string().into_bytes())
    }
}
```

### Example in TypeScript

The same plugin in TypeScript. It uses the same manifest, with the TypeScript build as the `server` entry.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type PluginError, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { readAll } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { start, isCancelled, reportProgress } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/jobs';

const COUNT_KIND = 'count-errors';

async function countErrorsAfterIdle(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const transcript = await readAll({ scope: 'project', path: 'logs/session.log' });
    const output = await start(COUNT_KIND, transcript);
    log('info', `errors: ${new TextDecoder().decode(output)}`);
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `count failed: ${(error as PluginError).message}`);
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, jobRunner } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'agent-activity-changed' && event.val.current === 'idle') {
        void countErrorsAfterIdle();
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
  run(_kind: string, input: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
    const lines = new TextDecoder().decode(input).split('\n');
    let count = 0;
    for (let index = 0; index < lines.length; index++) {
      if (isCancelled()) break;
      if (lines[index].includes('error')) count++;
      if (index % 1000 === 0) reportProgress((100 * index) / lines.length);
    }
    reportProgress(100);
    return new TextEncoder().encode(String(count));
  },
});
```

### What the user sees

The host draws no progress bar or status for a job. The plugin draws progress with its own widgets. A failed job reaches the user only when the plugin reports it, for example through a log line, a notice or a status row. The plugin log of the example above looks like this:

<figure>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs com.example.logs
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:02</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span>  errors: 37
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 09:14:09</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>  count failed: job deadline passed
</pre>

<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The plugin log after two idle transitions.</figcaption>
</figure>

# keys.intercept

## Overview

The `keys.intercept` grant lets a client-side plugin take chosen key chords before the focused pane sees them. While a grab is active, a key that matches one of its chords arrives at the plugin as a `key-pressed` event, and the pane does not receive that key. A key that matches no grab takes the normal path to the pane.

The grant is high risk (H). A grab that hides keys from a shell or an editor breaks the program the user is typing into, so Ilium never grants it by default. Hold a grab only while its feature is active, and release it as soon as the feature ends.

<div class="warn">

While a grab is active, its chords never reach the pane. A plugin that grabs a common chord, or never releases its grab, can make a terminal or an editor look broken. Grab only the chords a feature needs, release them as soon as the feature ends, and list the chords in the plugin's description.

</div>

## You need

| Need | Value |
|---|---|
| Side | Client only. Declare the grant under `capabilities.client`. A server plugin cannot call `keys`. |
| Grant | `keys.intercept`. The grant takes no argument. |
| Language | Rust, through `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::keys`, or TypeScript, through `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keys`. |
| Companion grant | `terminal.pointer` when the same feature also selects text with the mouse. |
| Manifest entry | Optional. A `keybindings` contribution starts the feature from a chord the user can rebind. The user's remap wins over the plugin's default. |

Grant syntax is strict. `keys.intercept` is valid. `keys.intercept:ctrl-c` is refused at build time with `manifest.grant-argument`:

```text
$ ilium plugin build
error  manifest.grant-argument
       capability "keys.intercept" takes no argument
       (got "keys.intercept:ctrl-c")
```

The chords belong to the `grab` call, not to the grant. Chord strings follow the grammar of [keys](/pages/api-keys/): lower case, zero or more of `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift` and `super` joined with `+`, then one key. Examples are `alt+s`, `up` and `shift+tab`.

## Surface

The grant opens two functions and four event fields from the `keys` interface:

| Name | Kind | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grab` | function | `keys::grab(&GrabSpec) -> Result<u64, PluginError>` | `grab(spec: GrabSpec): bigint` | Starts a grab and returns its id. TypeScript throws `PluginError`. |
| `release` | function | `keys::release(grab: u64)` | `release(grab: bigint): void` | Ends a grab. An unknown or ended id does nothing. |
| `GrabSpec.chords` | field | `Vec<String>` | `string[]` | One to 32 chords. |
| `GrabSpec.pane` | field | `Option<NodeId>` | `bigint \| undefined` | With a pane, the grab follows that pane's focus. With `none`, it is active whatever has focus. |
| `GrabSpec.until_release` | field | `bool` | `boolean` | The grab ends when the matched key is released. |
| `key-pressed` | event | `Event::KeyPressed(KeyEvent)` | `{ tag: 'key-pressed', val }` | A grabbed chord was pressed. Never dropped. |
| `key-released` | event | `Event::KeyReleased(KeyEvent)` | `{ tag: 'key-released', val }` | A grabbed key was released. Arrives only with release reports. |
| `KeyEvent.grab` | field | `Option<u64>` | `bigint \| undefined` | The grab that matched the key. |
| `KeyEvent.pane` | field | `Option<NodeId>` | `bigint \| undefined` | The focused pane when the key arrived. |
| `KeyEvent.chord` | field | `String` | `string` | The matched chord, as written in the grab. |
| `KeyEvent.repeat` | field | `bool` | `boolean` | `true` for an auto-repeat while the key is held. |

The WIT form, from `ilium:host/keys`:

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/keys in reference-wit
record grab-spec { chords: list<string>, pane: option<node-id>, until-release: bool }
type grab-id = u64;
grab: func(spec: grab-spec) -> result<grab-id, plugin-error>;
release: func(grab: grab-id);
```

Key release reports need the kitty keyboard protocol. The client enables it when the outer terminal supports it. Without it, only `key-pressed` arrives, and an `until-release` grab ends at the next key that does not match.

## How a grab routes keys

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 210" role="img" aria-label="A key press goes to the plugin when a grab matches, and to the pane otherwise">

<path d="M0 0 L10 5 L0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/>
</marker>
</defs>
<rect x="110" y="10" width="180" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="200" y="29" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">Key press</text>

<rect x="110" y="64" width="180" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>

<text x="305" y="159" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">Focused pane</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>A matching chord stops at the plugin and never reaches the pane. A key that no grab matches goes to the pane as usual.</figcaption>
</figure>

A grab with `pane: none` is active on that client whatever has focus, except while a kernel modal dialog is open. A grab with a pane is active only while that pane has focus. It is suspended while another pane has focus and resumes when focus returns. An `until-release` grab ends when focus changes.

A grab ends with no event to the plugin when its pane closes, when its plugin stops, or when its grant is revoked. A revocation also withdraws every grab and sends `deactivate(revoked)`. A later `release` of an ended id does nothing, so the plugin can call it without checking.

## Risk and tier rules

- `keys.intercept` is high risk (H). A T1 bundled plugin is activated first without it. At first activation the user sees one prompt, "Plugin <name> asks for: <list>", with the buttons `Allow selected` and `Not now`. `Not now` asks again at the next server start, at most three times, and then never again. Settings > Plugins can grant it at any time.
- A T2 or T3 plugin shows the review dialog at install. The grant is listed with the H mark and is unchecked by default.
- A grant is a standing permission. Nothing asks the user again on each call.
- Revoke it in Settings > Plugins > <plugin> > Capabilities, or with `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke keys.intercept`.

## What the user sees

At install of a T2 plugin, the review dialog shows one row for the grant:

<figure>

│ <span class="t-warn">! [ ] Grabs keys before Ilium sees them</span> <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-warn">keys.intercept</span> │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-warn">! marks a high-risk grant. It starts unchecked and is</span>                      │
│ <span class="t-warn">always asked for, even for bundled plugins.</span>                                │

While a grab holds a chord, pressing that chord does nothing in the pane, and the grab itself shows no indicator. Put the chords in the plugin's description. If the feature needs on-screen help, show the chord in the plugin's own view.

## Worked example 1: hold to select (Rust)

The Smart Copy light feature starts with a command and holds `alt+s` while the user selects output. The command starts from the `alt+g` keybinding. The grab is `until-release`, so it ends when the user lets go of `alt+s`.

Manifest:

```json
{
  "capabilities": { "client": ["keys.intercept", "terminal.pointer"] },
  "contributes": {
    "keybindings": [
      { "command": "com.example.smart-copy/start", "chord": "alt+g", "mode": "global" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Plugin code:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::keys::{self, GrabSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

const START_COMMAND: &str = "com.example.smart-copy/start";
const HOLD_CHORD: &str = "alt+s";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct SmartCopy {
    hold_grab: Option<u64>,
}

impl Lifecycle for SmartCopy {
    fn deactivate(&mut self, _reason: DeactivationReason) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        if let Some(grab) = self.hold_grab.take() {
            keys::release(grab);
        }
        None
    }
}

impl Handler for SmartCopy {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command == START_COMMAND => {
                    self.arm(invoked.context.pane);
                }
                Event::KeyReleased(key) if key.grab.is_some() && key.grab == self.hold_grab => {
                    // The until-release grab ended with the key. The copy itself is
                    // written from the rows that terminal.pointer highlighted.
                    self.hold_grab = None;
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl SmartCopy {
    fn arm(&mut self, pane: Option<NodeId>) {
        let Some(pane) = pane else { return };
        if self.hold_grab.is_some() {
            return;
        }
        let spec = GrabSpec {
            chords: vec![HOLD_CHORD.to_string()],
            pane: Some(pane),
            until_release: true,
        };
        match keys::grab(&spec) {
            Ok(grab) => self.hold_grab = Some(grab),
            Err(error) => {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("hold grab refused: {:?}", error.code));
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`arm` returns at once when the command has no pane or a grab is already held, so only one selection runs at a time. The `KeyReleased` arm matches only the grab that this plugin holds.

## Worked example 2: declined grant and cleanup (TypeScript)

The same feature in TypeScript shows the declined path. A `not-permitted` error means the user declined the grant. The feature logs the reason and leaves the mouse path to work. The plugin also releases its grab when it deactivates.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError, type Event } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as keys from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keys';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const START_COMMAND = 'com.example.smart-copy/start';
const HOLD_CHORD = 'alt+s';

let holdGrab: bigint | undefined;

function arm(pane: bigint | undefined): void {
  if (pane === undefined || holdGrab !== undefined) {
    return;
  }
  try {
    holdGrab = keys.grab({ chords: [HOLD_CHORD], pane, untilRelease: true });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError && error.code === 'not-permitted') {
      log('info', 'keys.intercept not granted: select with the mouse instead');
      return;
    }
    const code = error instanceof PluginError ? error.code : 'unknown';
    log('warn', `hold grab refused: ${code}`);
  }
}

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  deactivate() {
    if (holdGrab !== undefined) {
      keys.release(holdGrab);
    }
    holdGrab = undefined;
    return undefined;
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]) {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === START_COMMAND) {
        arm(event.val.context.pane);
      } else if (event.tag === 'key-released' && event.val.grab !== undefined) {
        if (event.val.grab === holdGrab) {
          holdGrab = undefined;
        }
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Every `u64` is a `bigint` in TypeScript, so the grab id and the pane id are `bigint` values. Compare them with `===`, never with a number.

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Grant declined or revoked | `grab` returns `not-permitted`. The keys go to the pane as usual. |
| Chord outside the grammar, or more than 32 chords | `invalid-argument`. |
| Chord the client cannot report | `invalid-argument`. With the legacy keyboard protocol, `ctrl` with `shift` on a letter, `super`, and `ctrl` on digits and most punctuation cannot be reported. |
| `pane` names a node that is not a pane | `not-found`. |
| Another plugin holds the same chord in the same scope | `conflict`. |
| 8 active grabs for one plugin side, or 32 for the session | `quota-exceeded`. |
| Pane closes, plugin stops, or grant revoked | The grab ends. A revocation sends `deactivate(revoked)`. No event reports the end. |
| Focus moves away from a pane grab | The grab is suspended until focus returns. An `until-release` grab ends. |
| Kernel modal dialog open | A `pane: none` grab is inactive until the dialog closes. |
| No release reports | `key-released` never arrives. An `until-release` grab ends at the next key that does not match, and that key goes to the pane. The end sends no event. |
| Key held down | `key-pressed` arrives again with `repeat: true`. Ignore repeats when counting presses. |
| `release` of an unknown or ended id | Nothing happens. |

A plugin must not retry a `grab` that returned `not-permitted`. It should fall back to its mouse path or tell the user that the feature is unavailable.

## See also

- [keys](/pages/api-keys/) for the full `keys` interface, the chord grammar and a copy-mode example.
- [terminal.pointer](/pages/capability-terminal-pointer/) for the mouse half of the Smart Copy feature.
- [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/) for the input that a grab takes away from the pane.
- [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/) for the grant model and the review dialog.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) for the error codes and the grab quotas.

Checked against the API version `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Capability: location.observer

## location.observer

The `location.observer` grant lets a client-side or scene plugin read the observer position. The observer position is the latitude and longitude that the user sets in Settings > Location. The host does not use GPS, an operating system location service or IP geolocation, so the value is the user's own setting and not a live reading of where the computer is.

The grant is high risk (H), because a position is personal data. It always needs an explicit user grant, including for a bundled plugin.

The grant covers one function, `current`. It returns the position, or `none` when there is no position to give.

**You will need:**

- A plugin built against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, with a client world (`ilium:client/base`) or a scene world (`ilium:anim/base`). The server side cannot hold this grant.
- The grant in the capability list of that side: `capabilities.client` for a client plugin, or `capabilities.scene` for a scene.
- The Rust SDK (`ilium-plugin-sdk`) or the TypeScript SDK (`@ilium/plugin-sdk`). Both expose the same function.
- Nothing else. A plugin cannot set the position. Only the user can, in Settings > Location.

<div class="warn">
<p>A position reveals where the user is. Grant it only to a plugin whose visible feature needs it. The grant does not allow network traffic: a plugin that sends the value to a host also needs an <code>http:&lt;host&gt;</code> grant, and the user should know that the value leaves the computer.</p>
</div>

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 200" role="img" aria-label="A scene calls current, the host checks the grant and reads the observer position set in Settings > Location, then returns a tuple or none">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arr-loc" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="8" y="40" width="124" height="56" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="70" y="62" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Scene plugin</text>
  <text x="70" y="80" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">location.observer</text>
  <rect x="268" y="40" width="124" height="56" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="330" y="62" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host grant check</text>
  <text x="330" y="80" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">returns option</text>
  <line x1="134" y1="60" x2="264" y2="60" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr-loc)"/>
  <text x="199" y="50" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">current()</text>
  <line x1="264" y1="84" x2="134" y2="84" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr-loc)"/>

  <line x1="330" y1="126" x2="330" y2="98" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr-loc)"/>

  <text x="330" y="162" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">Settings &gt; Location</text>
  <text x="199" y="190" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">A declined or revoked grant also returns none.</text>
