<figcaption>The host checks the grant before it reads the observer position. A declined or revoked grant gives the same none as an unset position, so the scene shows its default view.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

The grant string is the name alone. The grant takes no argument.

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `location.observer` | yes | the only form |
| `location.observer:city` | no | install fails with `manifest.grant-argument` |
| `location.current` | no | `current` is the function name, not the grant; install fails with `manifest.grant-unknown` |

### Surface

The grant adds one host function, from the WIT interface `ilium:host/location`. The Rust import is `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::location` and the TypeScript import is `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/location`.

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | WIT signature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `current` | `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::location::current()` | `current()` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/location` | `func() -> option<tuple<f64, f64>>` | The observer position, or none |

The WIT form is:

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/location in reference-wit
current: func() -> option<tuple<f64, f64>>;
```

The return value maps to these types:

| Part | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | `Option<(f64, f64)>` | `[number, number] \| undefined` | `None` or `undefined` when there is no position |
| first value | `f64` | `number` | latitude, in decimal degrees on WGS 84 |
| second value | `f64` | `number` | longitude, in decimal degrees on WGS 84 |

The call is synchronous. It has no `async` form and returns at once, so Rust code does not use `.await` and TypeScript code does not use `await`.

The value behaves as follows:

- **No accuracy.** The host returns no accuracy value, because the position is the user's own setting.
- **No staleness.** The value is as old as the setting and never goes stale. A plugin that needs the value calls `current` when it needs it. A change in Settings > Location takes effect at the next call.
- **No position.** When the user has not set a position, the call returns none.

### Worked example 1: Rust scene

The scene declares the grant in `capabilities.scene`:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.scenes",
  "scene": { "entry": "scene.wasm", "world": "ilium:anim/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "capabilities": { "scene": ["location.observer"] }
}
```

The scene chooses the centre of its map. It uses its own default when the call returns none:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::location;

/// Centre of the map view. Falls back to `default_centre` when the grant is
/// declined or the user has not set a position.
pub fn map_centre(default_centre: (f64, f64)) -> (f64, f64) {
    match location::current() {
        Some((latitude, longitude)) => (latitude, longitude),
        None => default_centre,
    }
}
```

Call it from the scene constructor with a fixed fallback, for example `map_centre((52.52, 13.405))`.

### Worked example 2: TypeScript client plugin

The client plugin declares the grant in `capabilities.client`:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.weather-panel",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["location.observer"] }
}
```

The panel label reads the position through a named import, and it destructures the tuple in the order latitude, then longitude:

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as location from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/location';

/** Short label for the weather panel. Never throws when the grant is missing. */
export function observerLabel(): string {
  const position = location.current();
  if (position === undefined) {
    return 'Set your position in Settings > Location to see local weather.';
  }
  const [latitude, longitude] = position;
  return `Observer at ${latitude.toFixed(2)}, ${longitude.toFixed(2)}`;
}
```

A plugin that does not want the coordinates on screen can drop the second branch and show only the set or unset state. The value stays inside the plugin until the plugin sends it somewhere.

### What the user sees

When a T2 or T3 package is installed, the review dialog lists the grant in the Scene group. The row shows the label, a `HIGH` mark in the danger colour, and the grant string. High risk rows start unchecked.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.location 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                  │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ <span class="t-warn">! [ ] Reads your location</span> <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-warn">location.observer</span> │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-warn">! marks a high-risk grant. It starts unchecked and is</span>                      │
│ <span class="t-warn">always asked for, even for bundled plugins.</span>                                │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests location.observer, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

A bundled T1 plugin is not shown the review dialog. It is activated first without the grant. On its first activation the host asks once:

<figure>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">Plugin com.example.scenes asks for:</span>
  <span class="t-err">HIGH</span> [ ] Know your configured location  location.observer
<span class="t-dim">[Allow selected]  [Not now]</span></pre>

<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The first-activation prompt for a bundled plugin. Choosing Not now asks again at the next server start, up to three times in total.</figcaption>
</figure>

The user can change a grant at any time in Settings > Plugins > <plugin> > Capabilities, or with `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke location.observer`.

When the host refuses a call, it writes a refusal line to the plugin log. Run `ilium plugin logs <id>` to see it. A declined grant writes this line:

```json
{
  "type": "refusal",
  "capability": "location.observer",
  "function": "location.current",
  "reason": "declined"
}
```

### Risk and tier rules

- `location.observer` is high risk (H). It always needs an explicit grant, even for a T1 bundled plugin.
- **T1 bundled plugins** show one prompt per plugin at first activation: `Plugin <name> asks for: <list>`, with the buttons `Allow selected` and `Not now`.
- **T2 and T3 packages** show the grant in the review dialog. The user checks each high risk row.
- **Client and scene worlds only.** The grant is available on the client side (`C`) and the animation world (`A`). It is not available on the server side.
- **Per side and per plugin.** The grant is recorded per plugin, per side and per user configuration, not per project.

### Declined, revoked and unset positions

These three situations return `none`. A call when the manifest never asked for the grant is not one of them: it traps with `host.capability-not-requested`. The plugin cannot tell them apart from the value alone, which is why the scene shows its default view.

| Situation | `current` returns | Plugin log |
|---|---|---|
| Grant declined at install or at the prompt | `none` | refusal line, reason `declined` |
| Grant revoked while the plugin runs | `none` at the next call | refusal line, reason `revoked` |
| User has not set a position | `none` | no refusal line |

A revocation first withdraws the grant for in-flight work. The plugin then receives `deactivate(revoked)` and is re-activated with the reduced grant set. That restart does not count as a failure of the plugin.

### Edge cases and errors

- **No error codes.** `current` returns an option, not a result, so no error code exists for it. The universal codes of the error table do not apply.
- **Refusal is not an error.** A plugin should show its default view and should not show a message that suggests the location failed. A message such as "No observer position. Set one in Settings > Location." is correct when the user has not set a position, but it is misleading for a declined grant.
- **Install errors.** `location.observer:city` fails with `manifest.grant-argument`, with the text `capability "location.observer" takes no argument (got "location.observer:city")`. A grant on the server side fails with `manifest.grant-side`, with the text `capability "location.observer" is not available on the server side`.
- **Tuple order.** The first value is always the latitude. Swapping the two values puts the position in the wrong place without any error.
- **Network use.** The value never leaves the plugin on its own. Sending it to a host also needs the `http:<host>` grant.

### Who requests it

The first-party live-data scenes request this grant, together with `http:<data-host>` for each data source and `jobs.run`. The live-data scenes use the observer position to choose which local data to fetch.

### See also

- [api-location](/pages/api-location/) for the import and its value behaviour in full.
- [capability-http](/pages/capability-http/) for the network request that a location might feed.
- [capability-jobs-run](/pages/capability-jobs-run/) for work that reads the location on a schedule.
- [api-scenes](/pages/api-scenes/) for the scene world and its manifest.
- [reference-capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/) for every grant in one table.

Checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` (API draft of 2026-10-11).

# Capability: media.video

## media.video

The `media.video` grant lets a client-side plugin or a scene open a video file and read its frames as pixels. The host decodes the file natively, using the `ffmpeg` program that it finds on `PATH`. The plugin therefore ships no decoder and never parses a container format. It asks for one frame at a time, at the size it needs, and draws the result, usually into a `surface` widget with `ui.write-surface`.

The grant has normal risk. It is not a high-risk capability. Bundled T1 plugins receive it automatically up to their ceiling. T2 and T3 packages list it checked by default in the review dialog.

### What you need

- **Grant.** `media.video` in `capabilities.client` or in `capabilities.scene`. The server side cannot import `media`. The grant takes no argument:

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `media.video` | yes | the only form |
| `media.video:h264` | no | the grant takes no argument; the host chooses the decoder |
| `media.decode` | no | the grant name is `media.video` |

- **A readable path.** `open-video` takes an `fs-path` and needs `fs.read` for that path's scope. A file the user chose arrives in a `picked/<n>` scope. A client plugin therefore also needs `fs.pick` and `fs.read:picked` ([fs.pick](/pages/capability-fs-pick/)). A scene does not declare `fs.pick`. It declares `fs.read:picked` and takes its path from a settings field that uses the `picker` keyword ([settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/)).
- **A view.** Drawing frames needs the `ui` import, which requires `ui.panels` or `panes.provide-kind`, and a `surface` widget in the view's tree.
- **The `ffmpeg` program on `PATH`.** Without it, `open-video` returns `unsupported` and names the missing program in the message.
- **Language.** Rust with the `ilium_plugin_sdk` crate, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. The import paths are `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::media` and `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/media`.

### Full surface

#### Functions

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open-video` | `media::open_video(path: FsPath) -> Result<(u64, VideoInfo), PluginError>` | `openVideo(path: FsPath): [bigint, VideoInfo]` | Opens the file and returns its video id and description. Synchronous. Throws in TypeScript. |
| `next-frame` | `media::next_frame(video: u64, width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, PluginError>` | `nextFrame(video: bigint, width: number, height: number): Uint8Array \| undefined` | Returns the next frame as `rgb8`, scaled to exactly `width` by `height`. `None` (`undefined`) at the end of the video. Synchronous. |
| `close-video` | `media::close_video(video: u64)` | `closeVideo(video: bigint): void` | Releases the decoder and its frame buffer. The id is invalid afterwards. |

#### Types

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/media in reference-wit
record video-info {
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    frames-per-second: f32,
    duration-millis: option<u64>,
}
open-video: func(path: fs-path) -> result<tuple<u64, video-info>, plugin-error>;
next-frame: func(video: u64, width: u32, height: u32) -> result<option<list<u8>>, plugin-error>;
close-video: func(video: u64);
```

| Field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width`, `height` | `u32` | `number` | Size of the video in pixels. |
| `frames-per-second` | `frames_per_second: f32` | `framesPerSecond: number` | Frame rate that the container states. |
| `duration-millis` | `duration_millis: Option<u64>` | `durationMillis: bigint \| undefined` | Length in milliseconds, or none when the container does not state one. |
| video id | `u64` | `bigint` | Identifies one open video. Every `u64` is a `bigint` in TypeScript. |

The host does not pace frames. The plugin decides how often it calls `next-frame`, usually from a timer ([timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/)).

### Frame format and limits

- **Layout.** Each frame is packed `rgb8`: three bytes per pixel, row by row, top row first. The byte count is `width * height * 3`. A 320 by 180 frame is 172 800 bytes, and a 640 by 360 frame is 691 200 bytes.
- **Size.** Each dimension must be at least 1. A frame larger than 3,840 by 2,160 pixels is refused with `invalid-argument`. The frame size should match the pixel size of the receiving `surface`. The host derives that size from the widget's `min-columns` and `min-rows` and from the sub-cell factor of the dither mode.
- **Buffer.** The host decodes frames ahead, as many as fit in the buffer of each open video, and always at least one. A call that finds a buffered frame returns at once.
- **Open videos.** A plugin may hold open videos up to a count (below). A further `open-video` returns `quota-exceeded` until one is closed.

| Limit (manifest key) | Default | Ceiling T1 | Ceiling T2 and T3 | Effect when reached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open videos (`open_videos`) | 2 | 8 | 2 | `quota-exceeded` from `open-video` |
| Frame buffer per video (`video_buffer_mib`) | 64 MiB | 256 MiB | 64 MiB | Decode-ahead shortens, to a minimum of one frame |

A manifest may request other values under `limits`. The host clamps each request to the ceiling of the tier and logs the clamp.

### Worked example: Rust

The plugin plays one picked video at a time. A 100 ms timer shows 10 frames per second in a surface with the key `frame`, inside the panel `preview`. At the end of the file, the plugin stops the timer and closes the decoder. The `start` method receives the path that `fs::pick` returns. Run `choose_video` in a task that the plugin spawns with `task::spawn`, then call `start` with its result.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs::{self, PickKind, PickSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{media, timers, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ids::TimerId;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{PixelFormat, ViewTarget};

const WIDTH: u32 = 320;
const HEIGHT: u32 = 180;
const FRAME_MILLIS: u32 = 100; // 10 frames per second

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Preview {
    video: Option<u64>,
    timer: Option<TimerId>,
}

/// Asks the user for a video file. Resolves to a picked/<n> path with an empty path field.
async fn choose_video() -> Result<FsPath, PluginError> {
    fs::pick(PickSpec {
        kind: PickKind::OpenFile,
        title: "Choose a video".to_string(),
        extensions: vec!["mp4".to_string(), "mkv".to_string(), "webm".to_string()],
    })
    .await
}

impl Preview {
    /// Starts playback of a path that the picker returned.
    fn start(&mut self, picked: FsPath) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        self.stop();
        let (video, info) = media::open_video(picked)?;
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("opened {}x{}", info.width, info.height));
        self.video = Some(video);
        self.timer = Some(timers::set(FRAME_MILLIS, Some(FRAME_MILLIS))?);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Draws one frame. `None` from the decoder means the end of the video.
    fn show_next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let Some(video) = self.video else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        match media::next_frame(video, WIDTH, HEIGHT)? {
            Some(pixels) => ui::write_surface(
                ViewTarget::Panel("preview".into()),
                "frame",
                0,
                PixelFormat::Rgb8,
                &pixels,
            ),
            None => {
                log::log(Level::Info, "end of video, decoder closed");
                self.stop();
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }

    fn stop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(timer) = self.timer.take() {
            timers::cancel(timer);
        }
        if let Some(video) = self.video.take() {
            media::close_video(video);
        }
    }
}

impl Handler for Preview {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::TimerFired(timer) = event else {
                continue;
            };
            if Some(timer) != self.timer {
                continue;
            }
            if let Err(error) = self.show_next_frame() {
                log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("preview stopped: {}", error.message));
                self.stop();
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

### Worked example: TypeScript

The TypeScript version behaves the same way. `definePlugin` returns the `handler` export that the manifest lists. The picker call returns a promise.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, FsPath, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import * as fs from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import * as media from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/media';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';
import * as ui from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';

const WIDTH = 320;
const HEIGHT = 180;
const FRAME_MILLIS = 100; // 10 frames per second

let video: bigint | undefined;
let timer: bigint | undefined;

/** Asks the user for a video file and resolves to the picked scope path. */
export function chooseVideo(): Promise<FsPath> {
  return fs.pick({
    kind: 'open-file',
    title: 'Choose a video',
    extensions: ['mp4', 'mkv', 'webm'],
  });
}

/** Starts playback of a path that the picker returned. Throws PluginError on failure. */
export function start(picked: FsPath): void {
  stop();
  const [id, info] = media.openVideo(picked);
  log('info', `opened ${info.width}x${info.height} at ${info.framesPerSecond.toFixed(1)} fps`);
  video = id;
  timer = timers.set(FRAME_MILLIS, FRAME_MILLIS);
}

function showNextFrame(): void {
  if (video === undefined) {
    return;
  }
  const pixels = media.nextFrame(video, WIDTH, HEIGHT);
  if (pixels === undefined) {
    log('info', 'end of video, decoder closed');
    stop();
    return;
  }
  ui.writeSurface({ tag: 'panel', val: 'preview' }, 'frame', 0, 'rgb8', pixels);
}

function stop(): void {
  if (timer !== undefined) {
    timers.cancel(timer);
    timer = undefined;
  }
  if (video !== undefined) {
    media.closeVideo(video);
    video = undefined;
  }
}

export const { handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'timer-fired' || event.timerId !== timer) {
        continue;
      }
      try {
        showNextFrame();
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `preview stopped: ${String(error)}`);
        stop();
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

### Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result | What the plugin should do |
|---|---|---|
| Grant declined or revoked | `open-video` returns `not-permitted` | Draw the fallback image. |
| Path outside the granted scopes | `not-permitted` | Ask the user again through the picker. |
| No `ffmpeg` on `PATH` | `unsupported`, message names `ffmpeg` | Show the message in the view. |
| Extension or codec that `ffmpeg` cannot decode | `unsupported` | Choose another file. |
| File does not exist | `not-found` from `open-video` | Re-pick the file. |
| Third open video (default limit 2) | `quota-exceeded` | Close a video first. |
| Zero width or height, or over 3,840 by 2,160 | `invalid-argument` from `next-frame` | Fix the size in the call. |
| Video id that is closed or was never opened | `not-found` from `next-frame` | Stop calling it. |
| Decoder fails in the middle of a file | `io` from `next-frame`; the video stays open | Close the video and report the message. |
| Plugin restarts, is disabled or loses the grant | Open video ids end; later calls return `not-found` | Open the video again after activation. |

Keep each `on-events` call short. One `next-frame` call per timer event normally fits the handler deadline, because the host decodes ahead.

### Who requests it

The native video scene becomes the bundled scene plugin `ilium.video` in Phase 4d. It is the first first-party user of this capability ([api-media](/pages/api-media/)).

# Capability: messages.peer

## messages.peer:&lt;plugin-id&gt;

The `messages.peer:<plugin-id>` capability lets a plugin send a one-way message to one other plugin. The sender submits the intent `message` with a channel name and a payload of bytes. The receiving plugin gets a `message` event that names the sender, the side it came from, the channel and the payload. The receiver cannot answer through this capability. A request that expects a reply uses [services.use](/pages/capability-services/). A message that many listeners receive without naming a receiver uses [topics.subscribe](/pages/capability-topics-subscribe/).

A plugin reaches its own other side without any grant. A server half sends to its client half, and a client half sends to its server half, by naming its own plugin id in the intent.

### What you need

- A grant `messages.peer:<plugin-id>` for each other plugin that the sending side messages. Grants are per side, so the grant goes in `capabilities.server` or `capabilities.client`, whichever side sends.
- The id of the receiving plugin, exactly as its manifest `id` writes it.
- The Rust crate `ilium-plugin-sdk` or the npm package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, both for `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
- Nothing extra on the receiver. A `message` event from another plugin needs no grant on the receiving side.

The receiver must be installed and enabled. If it is installed but not active, the host activates it first and delivers the message after `activate` returns.

### Grant syntax

The argument is the exact id of the receiving plugin. The host checks the grant string at install.

| Grant | Result at install | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `messages.peer:com.example.other` | valid | one exact receiver |
| `messages.peer` | refused, `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | the argument is required |
| `messages.peer:*` | refused, `manifest.grant-wildcard` | wildcards are not accepted |
| `messages.peer:com.example.*` | refused, `manifest.grant-wildcard` | a wildcard is not accepted in any position |

### Surface

The intent `message` sends. The event `message` receives.

**Intent `message` (sender):**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `to` | `message-target` | the receiver, described by the three fields below |
| `to.plugin` | `plugin-id` | the receiving plugin id |
| `to.side` | `plugin-side` | `server` or `client` |
| `to.client` | `option<client-id>` | one attached client; `none` from the server reaches every attached client |
| `channel` | `string` | 1 to 64 characters from `a-z`, `0-9`, `.` and `-` |
| `payload` | `list<u8>` | the message bytes, at most 1 MiB |

The submission also carries `correlation` and an optional `dedup-key`. A `message` does not need a dedup key. A key that the same plugin already used within 10 minutes completes as `duplicate(original)` with no effect.

**Event `message` (receiver):**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `plugin-id` | the sending plugin |
| `from-side` | `plugin-side` | the side that sent the message |
| `from-client` | `option<client-id>` | the client that sent it, when the sending side had one |
| `channel` | `string` | the channel name, as sent |
| `payload` | `list<u8>` | the bytes, unchanged |

Message events are never dropped by the host.

**Binding names:**

| WIT | Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|
| intent `message(message-spec)` | `Intent::Message(MessageSpec { to, channel, payload })` | `{ tag: 'message', val: { to, channel, payload } }` |
| `message-target` | `MessageTarget { plugin, side, client }` in `types::intents` | `{ plugin, side, client }` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types` |
| `plugin-side` | `PluginSide::Server`, `PluginSide::Client` | `'server'`, `'client'` |
| event `message(message-event)` | `Event::Message(MessageEvent { from, from_side, from_client, channel, payload })` in `types::events` | `{ tag: 'message', val: { from, fromSide, fromClient, channel, payload } }` |
| `list<u8>` | `Vec<u8>` | `Uint8Array` |

### Outcomes

The sender gets a `request-completed` event for each `message` submission.

| Outcome | When |
|---|---|
| `ok` | the message is queued for the receiver. The receiver may not have handled it yet. |
| `refused(not-permitted)` | no grant for that receiver, or the grant was declined or revoked before the call |
| `refused(not-found)` | the receiver is not installed or is disabled |
| `refused(invalid-argument)` | channel outside the allowed form, payload over 1 MiB, or a malformed submission |
| `duplicate(original)` | the same `dedup-key` was used within 10 minutes |

A missing grant refuses the whole batch. The offending submission completes as `refused(not-permitted)`, and every other submission of that batch completes as `refused(cancelled)` with the message `batch refused: submission <index>`.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 280" role="img" aria-label="Message flow from sender intent through grant check to the receiver's message event">
  <defs>
    <marker id="mp-arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="10" y="8" width="300" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="160" y="32" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">Sender submits intent message</text>
  <line x1="160" y1="48" x2="160" y2="70" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#mp-arrow)"/>

  <text x="160" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">Own-side messages skip the grant check.</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Sending to another plugin needs the grant. Sending to a plugin's own other side does not.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Review and risk

- Section 3 of the API does not mark `messages.peer` as high risk. A plugin with this grant is installed with it checked by default in the review dialog.
- The grant names the receiver, so a sender cannot reach a plugin that was not granted. The review dialog shows each receiver id before the user allows it.
- A T2 or T3 package shows every receiver id in the review dialog. T1 bundled plugins take the grant from their manifest ceiling.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.messages 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                  │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Sends messages to com.example.peer <span class="t-dim">…………</span> messages.peer:com.example.peer │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests messages.peer:com.example.peer, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

A declined grant appears unchecked and dimmed. The plugin then sees no `messages.peer` entry in its granted list, and every message to that receiver completes as `refused(not-permitted)`.

### What the user sees

- During install, the review row above, with the receiver id in the grant string.
- Each refused message is logged at level `warn`, with the sending plugin id, the import `ilium:host/intents` and the function `submit`. The line appears in `ilium plugin logs <id>`:

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs com.example.notes --tail 1
2026-10-11 09:14:02 warn  com.example.notes not-permitted: messages.peer
</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The log line for a refused message. The text after the plugin id is an example.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Worked example in Rust

The server half of `com.example.notes` sends `export-done` to `com.example.other` when the user runs its `export` command. The manifest grants `messages.peer:com.example.other` under `capabilities.server`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::Activation;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::CommandInvokedEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{MessageSpec, MessageTarget, PluginSide};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notes;

impl Lifecycle for Notes {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("started as {}", context.plugin));
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for Notes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(CommandInvokedEvent { command, .. }) = event else {
                continue;
            };
            if command != "com.example.notes/export" {
                continue;
            }
            // Submission::new uses the next correlation number and no dedup key.
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::Message(MessageSpec {
                to: MessageTarget {
                    plugin: "com.example.other".into(),
                    side: PluginSide::Server,
                    client: None,
                },
                channel: "status".into(),
                payload: b"export-done".to_vec(),
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

### Worked example in TypeScript

The receiver is `com.example.other`, a server half that logs each status message from `com.example.notes`. The handler needs no grant of its own.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    log('info', `started as ${context.plugin}`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'message') continue;
      const { from, channel, payload } = event.val;
      if (from !== 'com.example.notes' || channel !== 'status') continue;
      // The payload is ASCII in this example, so a char-code decode is enough.
      const text = String.fromCharCode(...payload);
      log('info', `status from ${from}: ${text}`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The matching send from a TypeScript sender is one literal submission. The intent `to` takes `client: undefined` to reach the receiver's server half:

**TypeScript**

```ts
{
  intent: {
    tag: 'message',
    val: {
      to: { plugin: 'com.example.other', side: 'server', client: undefined },
      channel: 'status',
      payload: new TextEncoder().encode('export-done'),
    },
  },
  correlation: 3n,
  dedupKey: undefined,
}
```

### Edge cases and errors

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Grant missing, declined or revoked during a call | `refused(not-permitted)` for that submission, batch refused (see Outcomes) |
| Receiver not installed or disabled | `refused(not-found)` |
| Receiver installed but not active | the host activates it; the message is delivered after `activate` |
| Receiver's `activate` returns an error | the message is discarded, the error is logged at level `error` under the receiver, and the sender is not told |
| Channel empty, longer than 64 characters, or with other characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| Payload over 1 MiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| Batch with more than 256 submissions | the whole batch is refused as malformed |
| Same `dedup-key` within 10 minutes | `duplicate(original)`, no second delivery |
| Message to the plugin's own other side | allowed with no grant; `from` is the plugin's own id |

A `message` is not a request. An `ok` outcome means the host queued the message, so the receiver's handler must decide what to do with it.

### Who requests it

No first-party plugin in `feature-mapping.md` lists `messages.peer` in its capability column. Feature 52 (`ilium voice say`) sends an intent `message` to the plugin's own client side, which needs no grant.

### See also

- [topics.subscribe](/pages/capability-topics-subscribe/) for one-to-many messages that do not name a receiver.
- [services.use](/pages/capability-services/) for a request that expects a reply.
- [API: messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/) for the full messages and topics API.
- [Events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) for how submissions and outcomes work.

### Security

A receiver MAY restrict senders with `accepts_messages_from` ([SEC-050]). Cross-plugin data flows are discussed in [Threat model](/pages/reference-threat-model/).

# Capability: extensions.provide

## extensions.provide:&lt;plugin-id&gt;/&lt;point&gt;

The `extensions.provide:<plugin-id>/<point>` capability lets a plugin own an extension point. An extension point is a named slot that other plugins fill with data (a collect point) or with code (a hook point). The owner reads the data with `list` and runs the code with `run-hook`. The owner decides when each happens. The pair of this grant is [extensions.contribute](/pages/capability-extensions-contribute/), which lets a plugin fill a slot. The full interface is in [extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/).

A plugin may own only points whose name starts with its own plugin id. The grant string must match a point that the plugin declares in `contributes.extension_points`.

### What you need

- **One grant for each point.** The grant goes in `capabilities.server` or `capabilities.client`, on the side that calls `list` or `run-hook`.
- **A declaration.** The point is listed in `contributes.extension_points` with its id, kind and schemas. A grant without a declaration, or a declaration without a grant, is refused at install with `manifest.grant-missing-extension`.
- **A language SDK.** Rust: crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, module `ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions`. TypeScript: `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions`.
- **Nothing on the contributors.** The owner does not need to know who the contributors are. The kernel orders them.

### Grant syntax

The argument is the global point name: the plugin id, a slash, and the point id. The point id is 1 to 64 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`.

| Grant | Result at install | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions.provide:com.example.notes/before-export` | valid | one point of the plugin `com.example.notes` |
| `extensions.provide:com.example.notes` | refused, `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | the point id is required |
| `extensions.provide:com.example.notes/*` | refused, `manifest.grant-wildcard` | wildcards are refused |
| `extensions.provide:com.example.other/before-export` | refused, `manifest.extension-point-invalid` | the prefix is not this plugin's id |
| `extensions.provide:com.example.notes/missing` | refused, `manifest.grant-missing-extension` | no declared point has that id |
| `extensions.provide:com.example.notes/before-export@0.1.0` | refused, `manifest.grant-unknown` | a version is never part of a grant |

### What it allows

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `list(point)` | Read the active entries of a point. Dormant and disabled entries are left out. |
| `run-hook(point, payload)` | Run the handlers of a hook point and wait for the outcome. |
| `take-reply(request)` | Take the final payload or the answer of a finished chain. |
| the topic `ilium.extensions/changed` | Learn that contributions to the point changed. Delivered only to the owner. |

It does not allow anything on other plugins' points. It does not allow reading a contributor's code or state. A contributor sees only the payload of the owner's `payload_schema`.

### Risk

The grant is normal risk (S). It is checked by default in the review dialog. Owning a point gives a plugin no power over the user's machine. It gives other plugins a way to run code at a place in the owner's flow, so the owner is responsible for what it puts in the payload. The owner sets `risk: "high"` on a point whose handlers can see or change sensitive data, such as text that goes to a terminal. A high-risk point makes the contributor's grant a high-risk (H) grant.

### Manifest

```json
{
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["extensions.provide:com.example.notes/before-export"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "extension_points": [
      { "id": "before-export", "kind": "hook", "mode": "transform",
        "title": "Before export",
        "payload_schema": { "type": "object",
          "properties": { "text": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 65536 } } },
        "reply_schema": { "type": "object",
          "properties": { "text": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 65536 } } },
        "risk": "standard", "deadline_ms": 20, "max_handlers": 8, "version": "0.1.0" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Example: run a hook

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};

// manifest: "extensions.provide:com.example.notes/before-export"
async fn export_note(text: &str) {
    let payload = format!(r#"{{"text":{}}}"#, serde_json::to_string(text).unwrap_or_default());
    match extensions::run_hook("com.example.notes/before-export", &payload).await {
        Ok(Some(final_payload)) => log::log(Level::Info, &final_payload),
        Ok(None) => log::log(Level::Info, "no handler changed the text"),
        Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{}: {}", error.code, error.message)),
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { runHook } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

// manifest: "extensions.provide:com.example.notes/before-export"
export async function exportNote(text: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const finalPayload = await runHook('com.example.notes/before-export', JSON.stringify({ text }));
    log('info', finalPayload ?? 'no handler changed the text');
  } catch (error) {
    log('warn', `hook failed: ${String(error)}`);
  }
}
```

### Errors

| Code | When | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| `extension.not-granted` | The plugin lacks the grant for that point, or the user declined it. | synchronous |
| `extension.unknown-point` | The point is not declared by an installed and enabled plugin. | synchronous |
| `extension.schema-mismatch` | The payload fits the size cap but fails `payload_schema`. Base code `invalid-argument`. | synchronous |
| `extension.cap-exceeded` | The payload is over 64 KiB. Base code `invalid-argument`. | synchronous |
| `extension.reentrant` | A handler called `run-hook` on the point that is running it. | synchronous |
| `extension.vetoed` | A `veto` handler refused. Base code `conflict`. | completion, outcome `refused(conflict)` |

Every extension code travels as a base `plugin-error` code plus a message prefix; see [the code mapping](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes).

### Edge cases

- **No contributors.** `list` returns an empty list. `run-hook` resolves with outcome `ok` and no reply. The owner carries on with its original data.
- **Grant declined.** Every call returns `extension.not-granted`. Contributions to the point go dormant because the point has no active owner.
- **Owner disabled.** Its contributions go dormant at once. When the user enables the owner again, they become active and the owner receives `ilium.extensions/changed`.
- **Replaced owner.** A plugin that replaces a core plugin takes over its points. The replacement must declare them all. See [extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replace).
- **Limits.** 16 points per plugin, up to 256 entries per collect point, up to 8 handlers per hook point, a chain of 100 ms.

### Review dialog

The install dialog lists one row for each owned point.

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Review permissions: com.example.notes 0.1.0  │
│                                              │
│ [x] Offer the point Before export            │
│     extensions.provide:                      │
│     com.example.notes/before-export          │
│                                              │
│   [allow]  [decline]                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The review row for an owned point.</figcaption>
</figure>

Owners declare risk and `on_failure` per [SEC-280] and [SEC-287]. See [Extension security](/pages/reference-extension-security/).

# Capability: extensions.contribute

## extensions.contribute:&lt;plugin-id&gt;/&lt;point&gt;

The `extensions.contribute:<plugin-id>/<point>` capability lets a plugin fill an extension point that another plugin owns. A collect point takes an entry: a piece of data the owner reads. A hook point takes a handler: code that the owner runs at a fixed place in its flow. Core plugins own many such points, so this grant is how a third-party plugin extends a core feature. The pair of this grant is [extensions.provide](/pages/capability-extensions-provide/). The full interface is in [extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/).

There is no grant that covers every point. Each point needs its own grant.

### What you need

- **One grant for each point you fill.** The grant goes in `capabilities.server` or `capabilities.client`, on the side that owns the call (see below).
- **A declaration.** Each entry or handler is listed in `contributes.extensions`. A grant without a declaration, or a declaration without a grant, is refused at install with `manifest.grant-missing-extension`.
- **The `hook-handler` export** on any side that has hook extensions. Without it install fails with `manifest.exports-mismatch`.
- **A language SDK.** Rust: crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`, trait `ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::HookHandler`. TypeScript: `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, member `handleHook` of `definePlugin`.

The owner does not have to be installed. A contribution to a point whose owner is missing or disabled is dormant. It stays in the package and counts for nothing until the owner appears.

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Result at install | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy` | valid | one point of a core plugin |
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy` | refused, `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | the point id is required |
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/*` | refused, `manifest.grant-wildcard` | wildcards are refused |
| `extensions.contribute:*` | refused, `manifest.grant-wildcard` | wildcards are refused in any position |
| `extensions.contribute-any` | refused, `manifest.grant-unknown` | this grant does not exist; list each point |
| `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy@0.1.0` | refused, `manifest.grant-unknown` | a version is never part of a grant |

A version can appear in the `point` field of a `contributes.extensions` entry, for example `ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy@0.1.0`. It means "same major, minor at least this". See [versioning](/pages/versioning/).

### Side

A handler runs on the side that owns the call. A server-owned point calls the server half of the contributor. A client-owned point calls the client half. A contributor declares its handler and its grant on that side. A handler declared on the wrong side is refused at install with `manifest.extension-side`.

### What it allows

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| An entry in `contributes.extensions` | Adds data to a collect point. Validated against `entry_schema` at install, on update and on `register`. |
| A handler in `contributes.extensions` | Adds code to a hook point. The `hook-handler` export receives the calls. |
| `register(point, extension, priority, entry)` | Adds or replaces an entry at run time. Only for collect points with `dynamic: true`. |
| `unregister(point, extension)` | Removes an entry this plugin registered. |

A handler gets only the payload of the owner's `payload_schema`. It may call other host functions its own grants allow, synchronously, within its deadline.

### Risk

The grant is normal risk (S) for a point with `risk: "standard"`. It is high risk (H) for a point with `risk: "high"`. The owner sets the risk, because the owner knows what its payload holds. A high-risk grant starts unchecked in the review dialog, and the line carries a warning. Examples are the `before-send-input` point of the terminal, `before-fire` of text triggers, and `before-broadcast` of fleet.

A handler on a `veto` point can stop an action. A handler on a `transform` point can change data in flight. Both are limited. A handler that is slow, traps or errors counts as `pass`, so a broken contributor never blocks the owner. Three breaches in a row stop that extension until the plugin restarts.

### Manifest

```json
{
  "id": "com.example.quiet-hours",
  "exports": ["hook-handler"],
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.notifications/before-notify"]
  },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      { "point": "ilium.core.notifications/before-notify@0.1.0", "id": "quiet-hours",
        "priority": 40, "handler": "quiet_hours" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Example: a handler

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::{HookCall, HookHandler, HookReply};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server", exports = ["hook-handler"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct QuietHours;

impl Lifecycle for QuietHours {}

impl Handler for QuietHours {
    fn on_events(&mut self, _batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl HookHandler for QuietHours {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        if call.extension != "quiet_hours" {
            return HookReply::Pass;
        }
        // Parse call.payload_json with a JSON library and read the hour in a real plugin.
        if call.payload_json.contains(r#""urgency":"low""#) && is_night() {
            return HookReply::Refuse("quiet hours".to_string());
        }
        HookReply::Pass
    }
}

fn is_night() -> bool {
    false // stand-in for a clock read
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type HookCall, type HookReply } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

function isNight(): boolean {
  const hour = new Date().getHours();
  return hour >= 22 || hour < 7;
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, hookHandler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents() {
    return [];
  },
  handleHook(call: HookCall): HookReply {
    if (call.extension !== 'quiet_hours') {
      return { tag: 'pass' };
    }
    const payload = JSON.parse(call.payloadJson) as { urgency?: string };
    if (payload.urgency === 'low' && isNight()) {
      return { tag: 'refuse', val: 'quiet hours' };
    }
    return { tag: 'pass' };
  },
});
```

### Errors

| Code | When | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.grant-missing-extension` | An extension has no matching grant. | install |
| `manifest.extension-entry-invalid` | An entry fails the owner's `entry_schema`. | install, update |
| `manifest.extension-side` | The handler is on the wrong side. | install |
| `manifest.extension-limit` | More than 64 extensions in one plugin. | install |
| `extension.not-granted` | `register` without the grant, or the user declined it. | synchronous |
| `extension.not-dynamic` | `register` on a point that is not dynamic. | synchronous |
| `extension.cap-exceeded` | The point already holds `max_entries` entries or `max_handlers` handlers. | synchronous, or the extension stays dormant |
| `extension.handler-timeout` | The handler passed its deadline. Counts as `pass`. | log |
| `extension.reply-not-allowed` | The reply does not fit the mode. Counts as `pass`. | log |
| `extension.disabled` | Stopped after three breaches, or turned off by the user. | log, Plugins screen |

### Edge cases

- **Owner missing.** The contribution is dormant. The Plugins screen shows `waiting for <owner>`. Install succeeds.
- **Grant declined.** The extension is not added. Other extensions of the same package still work.
- **Point full.** If the owner's point already holds its maximum, the new extension stays dormant and the log gets `extension.cap-exceeded`.
- **Replaced owner.** If the user replaces the owner by another plugin that declares the same point, contributions move to the replacement. A replacement that lacks the point leaves them dormant.
- **User order.** The user can move or turn off your extension on the owner's Extensions tab. Your priority is a default.

### Review dialog

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Review: com.example.quiet-hours 0.1.0        │
│                                              │
│ Adds to other plugins                        │
│ [x] Notifications > Before notify            │
│     can stop a notice from being shown       │
│                                              │
│   [allow]  [decline]                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. A standard-risk contribution is checked by default. A high-risk one starts unchecked and carries a warning.</figcaption>
</figure>

# Capability: notify.desktop

## notify.desktop

The `notify.desktop` capability lets a plugin show a desktop notification. The plugin submits the intent `notify` with a title, a body, an urgency and an optional sound. The host turns the intent into a notice, picks the desktop form that matches the urgency, and reports `ok` once the notice is queued. The host does not wait for the user to read it.

A notice is an optional extra. A plugin should keep its own in-app status line working, because the user can decline the grant at any time.

**You will need:**

- A `notify.desktop` grant in the manifest of the plugin. The grant takes no argument.
- An SDK that exposes the `notify` intent. The Rust path is `ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents`, and the TypeScript import is `@ilium/plugin-sdk/types`.
- A sound id from `sound.catalog()` if you want a sound. See [sound.play](/pages/capability-sound-play/).
- A `dedup-key` if the same notice could be submitted twice, as described in the section on duplicates below.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 400 260" role="img" aria-label="A notify intent passes the batch checks, then becomes a desktop notice or a footer notice, and the plugin receives ok or a refusal">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arr-notify" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="360" height="36" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>

</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `notify.desktop` | yes | the only form |
| `notify.desktop:all` | no | the grant takes no argument; the manifest fails with `manifest.grant-argument` |
| `notify` | no | `notify` is the intent name, not the grant |

The grant is a normal risk capability. It is not marked high risk.

### Surface

The grant unlocks one intent and one related host function from the sound module.

| Name | Kind | Type and meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `notify` | intent | Submits a notice. Payload is `notify-spec`. Rust: `Intent::Notify(NotifySpec)`. |
| `notify-spec.title` | field | `string`, 1 to 256 characters. The first line of the notice. |
| `notify-spec.body` | field | `string`, 0 to 2,048 characters. The text below the title. |
| `notify-spec.urgency` | field | `enum urgency`: `low`, `normal` or `high`. Rust: `Urgency::Low` and so on. TypeScript: `'low'`, `'normal'`, `'high'`. |
| `notify-spec.sound` | field | `option<string>`, a sound id, or none. Rust: `Option<String>`. TypeScript: `string \| undefined`. |
| `sound.catalog` | host function | `func() -> list<string>`. Returns the bundled and contributed sound ids. |
| `ok` | outcome | The notice is queued. |

The payload is a record with these four fields and no others. The WIT form is `record notify-spec { title: string, body: string, urgency: urgency, sound: option<string> }`.

### Urgency

The urgency sets the form that the desktop uses for the notice. The host does not change the text.

| Urgency | Linux (freedesktop) | Windows (toast) | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `low` | urgency 0 | silent | passive |
| `normal` | urgency 1 | default toast | active |
| `high` | urgency 2 (critical) | `urgent` scenario | time-sensitive |

Use `high` only for something the user must see soon, such as a failed export that blocks further work. Overusing `high` makes the desktop treat every notice as urgent.

### Focus and visibility

A notice is shown in one of two places:

- The desktop notification, when no attached client reports terminal focus.
- The client footer, when an attached client reports terminal focus (focus reporting, DEC mode 1004). The desktop notification is then replaced by a footer notice in the Ilium client.

`notify-spec` has no pane field, so the host cannot tell which pane a notice concerns. The rule therefore applies to every notice. A plugin cannot choose the place.

The host passes `title` and `body` to the desktop unchanged. How a desktop shortens a long line is up to that desktop.

### Sound

The `sound` field names a sound id. The id must be in the catalogue, which is the set returned by `sound.catalog()`. The sound plays with the notice in either place, and it needs only `notify.desktop`. A plugin does not also need `sound.play` for a sound inside a notice. An unknown id refuses the whole submission with `refused(not-found)`, so no notice is shown.

### Duplicates and dedup keys

The submission carries a `dedup-key`. The key is optional for `notify`, but a plugin that can submit the same notice twice should set one.

- Format: 1 to 128 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`. Any other character makes the submission malformed.
- Scope: the pair of plugin id and key, in the kernel that applies the intent.
- Window: 10 minutes from the moment the key is reserved.
- Duplicate: a submission whose key is reserved completes as `duplicate(original)` and shows nothing. `original` is the `request-ref` of the submission that reserved the key.
- A refused submission does not reserve its key, so a retry with the same key is correct after the cause is fixed.

In Rust, `dedup::key_for(&["notes-export", "2026-10-11"])` joins the parts with `:` and returns `notes-export:2026-10-11`. TypeScript has no helper, so write the string.

### Worked example: manifest

The manifest grants the capability to the client side. Notifications come from the client.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["notify.desktop"] }
}
```

### Worked example: Rust

This client plugin shows a notice when its export command runs. The example fixes the date in the key. A real plugin uses an id for each export run.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::dedup;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, NotifySpec, Submission, Urgency};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesNotifier;

impl Handler for NotesNotifier {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.notes/export" { continue; }
            submissions.push(Submission::keyed(
                Intent::Notify(NotifySpec {
                    title: "Export finished".into(),
                    body: "12 notes written to the archive folder.".into(),
                    urgency: Urgency::Normal,
                    sound: Some("done".into()),
                }),
                dedup::key_for(&["notes-export", "2026-10-11"]),
            ));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

### Worked example: TypeScript

The same behaviour in TypeScript. The sound is used only when the catalogue contains it.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { catalog } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sounds';

const EXPORT_COMMAND = 'com.example.notes/export';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    const soundIds = catalog();
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== EXPORT_COMMAND) continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'notify',
          val: {
            title: 'Export finished',
            body: '12 notes written to the archive folder.',
            urgency: 'normal',
            sound: soundIds.includes('done') ? 'done' : undefined,
          },
        },
        correlation: 2n,
        dedupKey: 'notes-export:2026-10-11',
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

The `correlation` value is a `bigint` in TypeScript. It names the submission, so the plugin can match the outcome to the batch that caused it.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing, or declined by the user | `refused(not-permitted)`; the rest of the batch is `refused(cancelled)` | Keep the in-app status line. Do not retry. |
| Sound id not in the catalogue | `refused(not-found)`; no notice is shown | Call `sound.catalog()` first, or omit the sound. |
| `title` empty or over 256 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Fix the text. |
| `body` over 2,048 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Shorten the text. |
| `dedup-key` with a disallowed character or over 128 characters | The batch is refused as malformed (`invalid-argument`) | Fix the key. |
| Same key within 10 minutes | `duplicate(original)`; no second notice | Nothing. The first notice stands. |
| More than 6 notices per minute | `refused(rate-limited)` for the extra ones | Wait a minute, or merge the notices. |
| Grant revoked later | Later submissions are `refused(not-permitted)`; queued notices stay | Re-read the grant on activation. |

A notice already queued is not recalled if the grant is revoked afterwards. The desktop may also hide a notice under its own focus or do-not-disturb rules. The plugin receives `ok` in both cases, because `ok` means the notice was queued, not that the user saw it.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a T2 or T3 package is installed. The T1 bundled plugins receive the grant automatically up to their ceiling.

│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

A revocation re-activates the plugin with the reduced grant set. The plugin receives `deactivate(revoked)` and its activation does not count as a failure.

### Risk and tier rules

- The grant has the normal risk. The review dialog lists it, and it is checked by default.
- A notice is visible to anyone who looks at the screen. Do not put private transcript text, file paths with personal names or secrets into the title or body.
- T1 bundled plugins receive the grant automatically up to their manifest ceiling. T2 and T3 packages show it in the review dialog, and the user keeps or removes it there.

### Who requests it

First-party plugins from `feature-mapping.md` use the grant for:

- 48: desktop notifications.
- 56: text triggers, which often finish with a notice. See [the terminal output filter](/pages/capability-terminal-output-filter/).
- 59: the progress monitor, which notifies when a job finishes.

# panes.create

## Overview

The `panes.create` grant lets a plugin open a new pane in the tree. A pane is either a terminal that runs a command, or a pane of a kind that the plugin or the kernel provides. The plugin asks for the pane with the `create-pane` intent. It never starts a process itself: the kernel creates the node, starts any command inside it, and reports the result.

The request is asynchronous. A plugin returns the submission from `on-events`, or calls `intents.submit` from a timer or request callback. The kernel answers later with a `request-completed` event that carries `ok-node(<id>)`. A `pane-created` event for the same node follows. A plugin that needs the new id must wait for the completion and must not assume the pane exists when the submission is returned.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 340 140" role="img" aria-label="A plugin sends create-pane to the kernel pane tree, which adds the node and returns ok-node with its id">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arr-pane" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="8" y="8" width="324" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="170" y="32" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin (server or client side)</text>
  <line x1="130" y1="48" x2="130" y2="76" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr-pane)"/>
  <text x="138" y="66" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">create-pane</text>
  <rect x="8" y="76" width="324" height="50" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="170" y="98" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Pane tree (kernel)</text>
  <text x="170" y="116" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">adds the node and starts the command</text>
  <line x1="250" y1="76" x2="250" y2="48" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr-pane)"/>
  <text x="258" y="66" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">ok-node(id)</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The plugin asks the kernel for a pane with create-pane. The kernel makes the node, starts any command, and returns ok-node with the new id.</figcaption>
</figure>

## You will need

- The grant `panes.create` in the manifest, under the side that submits the intent (`server` or `client`).
- `fs.read:<scope>` for every file scope that `cwd` uses, for example `fs.read:project`. See [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/).
- [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/) when the plugin sets `initial-input`, because that text is typed into the new pane.
- [tree.read](/pages/capability-tree-read/) or [panes.read](/pages/capability-panes-read/) when the plugin must find or watch the new pane afterwards.
- Rust with the `ilium-plugin-sdk` crate, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both forms are shown below. Submissions are described in [intents](/pages/api-intents/).

## Grant syntax

- Valid: `panes.create`
- Invalid: `panes.create:terminal`. The grant takes no argument (`manifest.grant-argument`). The kind of pane is an intent field, not part of the grant.

## Surface

The grant opens one intent, `create-pane`. Its payload is a record named `create-pane-spec`.

| Field (WIT) | Rust (`CreatePaneSpec`) | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parent: option<node-id>` | `parent: Option<NodeId>` | `parent: bigint \| undefined` | The node that holds the new pane. `none` places it after the focused pane in its group, or at the end of the session's root group when nothing has focus. |
| `title: string` | `title: String` | `title: string` | The title shown in the tree. |
| `content-kind: string` | `content_kind: String` | `contentKind: string` | `ilium.terminal` for a terminal, or a plugin pane kind (see the rules below). |
| `cwd: option<fs-path>` | `cwd: Option<FsPath>` | `cwd: FsPath \| undefined` | The start folder, as a scope and a relative path. |
| `command: option<list<string>>` | `command: Option<Vec<String>>` | `command: string[] \| undefined` | The program and its arguments. The first item is the program. |
| `initial-input: option<string>` | `initial_input: Option<String>` | `initialInput: string \| undefined` | Text typed into the pane after it starts. Needs `terminal.write`. |

`FsPath` is a record with `scope` and `path`. The path is relative to the scope root and uses `/` as separator. A path is never absolute.

The outcome arrives in a `request-completed` event. The `request` field is `submission(<correlation>)` for the submission that asked for the pane:

| Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok-node(node-id)` | The pane exists. Rust `Outcome::OkNode(node)`; TypeScript `{ tag: 'ok-node', val: 58n }`. |
| `duplicate(request-ref)` | The dedup key was reserved by an earlier accepted submission. Nothing was created. |
| `refused(plugin-error)` | A check failed before anything was created. The submission can be retried after the cause is fixed. |
| `failed(plugin-error)` | The kernel accepted the request but could not finish it, for example the program did not start. |
| `cancelled` | The batch was refused, or the request was cancelled. |

Keep the `node-id` from `ok-node`. Later reads and intents refer to the pane by that id.

## Field rules

| Rule | Limit | Result when broken |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | 256 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `command` | 1,024 arguments | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `command` program | resolved through `PATH`, or an absolute path | `failed(io)` when the program cannot start |
| `initial-input` | 64 KiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `cwd` | scope must be granted with `fs.read`; the folder must exist | `refused(not-permitted)` or `refused(not-found)` |
| `parent` | the node must exist | `refused(not-found)` |
| `content-kind` | `ilium.terminal`, or a kind the plugin declares | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `dedup-key` | optional for this intent, 1 to 128 characters | retries without a key open a second pane |

With `command: none` and `content-kind: "ilium.terminal"`, the pane runs the user's login shell from the `SHELL` variable, or `/bin/sh` when `SHELL` is unset. With `cwd: none`, the pane starts in the root of the `project` scope.

A plugin's own pane kind has the content kind `<plugin-id>/<kind>`, where `<kind>` is declared in the `pane_kinds` entry of its manifest. See [panes.provide-kind](/pages/capability-panes-provide-kind/).

## Worked example: Rust, server side

This server plugin opens a review pane each time an agent finishes. It keeps the correlation numbers of its own submissions and logs the node id when the pane exists. The manifest requests `agent.read` for the activity event and `panes.create` for the new pane.

```json
{
  "capabilities": { "server": ["panes.create", "agent.read"] }
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::dedup;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::CreatePaneSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::requests::RequestResult;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ReviewPane {
    /// Correlation numbers of create-pane submissions still waiting for a result.
    pending: Vec<u64>,
}

impl Handler for ReviewPane {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. })
                    if current == AgentActivity::Done =>
                {
                    let spec = CreatePaneSpec {
                        parent: None,
                        title: "Review of agent work".into(),
                        content_kind: "ilium.terminal".into(),
                        cwd: None,
                        command: Some(vec!["git".into(), "diff".into(), "--stat".into()]),
                        initial_input: None,
                    };
                    let key = dedup::key_for(&["review", &node.to_string()]);
                    let submission = Submission::keyed(Intent::CreatePane(spec), key);
                    self.pending.push(submission.correlation);
                    submissions.push(submission);
                }
                Event::RequestCompleted(RequestResult {
                    request: RequestRef::Submission(correlation),
                    outcome: Outcome::OkNode(new_node),
                }) => {
                    if let Some(index) = self.pending.iter().position(|&c| c == correlation) {
                        self.pending.swap_remove(index);
                        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("review pane is node {new_node}"));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

`Submission::keyed` sets the dedup key, so an agent that reports `done` twice in the same window does not open two panes. `Submission::new` would take the next correlation number without a key. Use `intents::submit` from a timer or request callback, where no batch is being returned.

## Worked example: TypeScript, client side

This client plugin opens a pane that tails a build log when a command is invoked. It reads the completion and logs the node id. The command must be declared in the manifest and be one of the plugin's own commands.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

const OPEN_LOG_COMMAND = 'com.example.build/open-log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate(context) {
    log('info', `ready in ${context.plugin}`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === OPEN_LOG_COMMAND) {
        submissions.push({
          intent: {
            tag: 'create-pane',
            val: {
              parent: undefined,
              title: 'Build log',
              contentKind: 'ilium.terminal',
              cwd: { scope: 'project', path: 'logs' },
              command: ['tail', '-n', '200', 'build.log'],
              initialInput: undefined,
            },
          },
          correlation: 1n, // chosen by the plugin, unique per plugin, below 2^63
          dedupKey: 'open-log-build',
        });
      }
      if (event.tag === 'request-completed' && event.val.request.tag === 'submission') {
        if (event.val.outcome.tag === 'ok-node') {
          log('info', `build log pane is node ${event.val.outcome.val}`);
        }
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

The manifest for this plugin requests `panes.create` on the client side and `fs.read:project` for the `cwd` scope:

```json
{
  "capabilities": { "client": ["panes.create", "fs.read:project"] }
}
```

In TypeScript, every `u64` is a `bigint`, so `correlation` is written `1n`. The `dedupKey` is written as a plain string.

## Risk tier

- The grant is `normal` risk, not marked high.
- A T1 bundled plugin receives it automatically up to its manifest ceiling.
- A T2 or T3 plugin lists it in the review dialog, checked by default. The user can uncheck it.
- `initial-input` needs `terminal.write`, which is high risk. The user must turn that row on separately.

The grant is recorded per plugin and per side. A revoked grant withdraws any pane creation still pending and completes it as `failed(revoked)`, and the plugin is re-activated with the reduced set.

## Review dialog

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.panes 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                     │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Creates panes <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………</span> panes.create │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests panes.create, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| The grant is not granted or the user declined it | `refused(not-permitted)`. No pane is created and no process starts. |
| The grant is revoked while the request is pending | `failed(revoked)` for the request. The plugin is re-activated. |
| `cwd` names a scope without `fs.read` | `refused(not-permitted)` |
| `cwd` names a folder that does not exist | `refused(not-found)` |
| `cwd` names a file | `refused(not-found)` |
| `parent` names a node that was removed | `refused(not-found)` |
| `content-kind` is not declared | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `title` longer than 256 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` |
| `initial-input` without `terminal.write` | The whole batch is refused as `refused(not-permitted)`. |
| The program in `command` cannot start | `failed(io)`. |
| A key was accepted within the last 10 minutes | `duplicate(<original>)`. Nothing is created. |
| The batch holds more than 256 submissions | The plugin traps. |

A refused submission does not reserve its dedup key, so a retry with the same key after fixing the cause is valid. A key that was accepted stays reserved even if the pane later fails. Retry a failed creation with a new key.

## When the grant is declined

`create-pane` completes with `refused(not-permitted)`. No pane is created, and no process starts. The plugin can still run its other features. A plugin that offers "start an agent in a new pane" should hide that action when the grant is missing. Check the grant list at activation, so the menu item is never shown for a pane that cannot open.

## What the user sees

After the kernel accepts the request, the new pane appears in the tree under its parent, with its title and status line. The command runs at once. With `parent: none`, the pane is placed after the focused pane in its group, the same place a user-created pane gets (U33).

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">session default</span>
├─ Group
│  ├─ <span class="t-dim">codex-1</span>      working
│  ├─ <span class="t-hi">Review of agent work</span>  running
│  ╰─ shell              idle
</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The new pane sits in the same group as the agent that finished. Its command output is shown in the pane itself.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Minimal example

The intent payload as the kernel sees it, written as a value (not WIT), and the outcome:

```text
create-pane { parent: some(7), title: "Test run", content-kind: "ilium.terminal",
              cwd: none, command: some(["cargo", "test"]), initial-input: none }
```

```text
request-completed: request submission(1) -> ok-node(58)
```

## First-party features that request it

- Feature 23, create an agent from an editor line.
- Feature 67, agent in a new Git worktree.
- Feature 68, agent in an existing worktree.
- Feature 80, remote compaction, which creates a pane with the resume template.

Requirement ids for this page: [PAN-030], [PAN-031]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

### Security

**[SEC-040]** A plugin MAY create a pane that runs a program only with `panes.create-command:<program>` (high risk). The grant is defined in the [Capability table](/pages/reference-capabilities/) (it requires `panes.create` in the same side, else the install fails with `manifest.grant-dependency`). A `command` whose program matches no such grant completes `refused(not-permitted)` with reason `not-granted`, or `declined` when the grant was requested but unchecked. The program is not confined ([Sandbox reference](/pages/reference-sandbox/)).
