## You will need

- The grant `ui.panels` on the client side. The `ui` import is not available on the server side.
- A `panels` or `onboarding_steps` entry in the manifest for each view, or a `settings` tab with `"render": "view"`, and `"views"` in the manifest `exports` list.
- A `views` export that returns a UI tree for each view target.
- The grant [help.read](/pages/capability-help-read/) if the panel links to help topics.
- A Rust crate built with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or a TypeScript entry module that imports `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both SDKs expose the same `ui` functions under the names in the tables below.

## Grant syntax

- Valid: `ui.panels`
- Invalid: `ui.panels:settings`. A custom settings page is a `settings` tab with `"render": "view"` in the manifest.

## Manifest contributions

| Contribution | Fields | View target | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `panels` | `id`, `title`, `icon?`, `default_size?`, `modal` | `panel("<id>")` | A full-screen or overlay view. |
| `settings` tab with `"render": "view"` | `id`, `title`, `icon?` | `settings-page("<id>")` | A custom page in Settings, listed under the plugin. |
| `onboarding_steps` | `id`, `title`, `order` | `onboarding-step("<id>")` | A guided setup step, shown in the given order. |

`settings` tabs with `"render": "view"` and `onboarding_steps` no longer carry a `view` key. The host finds the view through the view target. The `id` of a settings tab must differ from every other settings tab and section id of the same plugin, or the manifest is refused with `manifest.settings-id-clash`.

## The host imports

All functions are in the `ui` interface. Each one needs `ui.panels` or the `panes.provide-kind` grant, except `invalidate`, which the plugin may call for its own views at any time.

| WIT function | Rust | TypeScript | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `open-panel(panel)` | `ui::open_panel` | `openPanel` | `result` | Shows a declared panel. |
| `close-panel(panel)` | `ui::close_panel` | `closePanel` | none | Hides a panel. |
| `open-popup(popup, anchor)` | `ui::open_popup` | `openPopup` | `result` | Shows a `popup` widget of the last rendered tree. |
| `close-popup(popup)` | `ui::close_popup` | `closePopup` | none | Hides a popup. |
| `invalidate(view)` | `ui::invalidate` | `invalidate` | none | Asks the host to call `render` again. |
| `widget-state(view, key)` | `ui::widget_state` | `widgetState` | `option` | Reads the host-owned state of a keyed widget. |
| `set-widget-state(view, key, state)` | `ui::set_widget_state` | `setWidgetState` | `result` | Changes that state, for example the selected row. |
| `write-surface(view, key, first-row, format, data)` | `ui::write_surface` | `writeSurface` | `result` | Writes whole rows of pixels into a `surface`. |
| `display-width(text)` | `ui::display_width` | `displayWidth` | `u16` | Width of a string in cells, with the host's rules for icons and wide glyphs. |
| `theme()` | `ui::theme` | `theme` | `theme-tokens` | The current colour roles, dark or light flag and glyph preference. |

`open-view` and `close-view` intents do the same as `open-panel` and `close-panel` when a command or the server submits them. The `open-view` intent takes a view target and a `focus` flag.

## Types

| Type | Cases or fields |
|---|---|
| `view-target` | `panel(string)`, `pane(node-id)`, `popup(string)`, `settings-page(string)`, `onboarding-step(string)` |
| `popup-anchor` | `centered((constraint, constraint))`, `at-cell((u16, u16))`, `below-key(string)` |
| `widget-state` | `none`, `selected(option<u32>)`, `offset(u32)`, `tab(u32)`, `text(string)`, `expanded(list<string>)`, `checked(bool)` |
| `area` | `columns: u16`, `rows: u16` |
| `pixel-format` | `mask8`, `mono1`, `gray8`, `rgb8`, `rgba8` |
| `theme-tokens` | colour roles `foreground`, `background`, `accent`, `muted`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` as `u32`, plus `is-dark: bool` and `stable-glyphs: bool` |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When it arrives |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-action` | `view`, `key`, `kind`, `value` | The user acts on a widget of the plugin's own view. Never dropped. |
| `view-visibility` | `view`, `visible` | A view opens or closes. Coalesced. |
| `theme-changed` | none | The user changes the theme. The host repaints the colour roles itself, so no new render is needed. |

The `kind` of a `ui-action` is one of `activated`, `changed`, `submitted`, `selected`, `toggled`, `scrolled`, `dropped`, `context-requested`, `closed`, `focus-gained` or `focus-lost`. The `value` is one of `none`, `text(string)`, `index(u32)`, `number(f64)`, `flag(bool)`, `drop(source-key, target-key, index)` or `cell(cell-position)`. The widget `key` is the action id: the plugin matches on it.

The host sends `changed` for a text widget 600 ms after the last keystroke, 1 s for a large editor, and immediately for a toggle or a choice. A `tabs` widget sends `selected` with the new index. A `schema-form` sends no `ui-action`: the host saves each change and the owning plugin receives `settings-changed`.

## The UI tree

A view returns a flat `ui-tree`: a list of nodes with child indices, and a root index. Each node has an optional `key`, a `widget`, its `children` and flags (`focusable`, `draggable`, `drop-target`, `hidden`).

- Keys are unique across the whole view and stable across renders. The host keeps widget state by key, so a widget without a key loses its selection, scroll offset and typed text on every render.
- The host owns list and table selection, tab index, scroll offsets, text contents and cursor, tree expansion, the popup stack and focus.
- A tree holds at most 4,096 nodes and 1,024 KiB by default. Each limit is a trap when exceeded.
- Layout uses the ratatui solver. The constraints are `length(u16)`, `min(u16)`, `max(u16)`, `percentage(u16)`, `ratio((u32, u32))` and `fill(u16)`. The plugin never sees a `Rect`. It reads `area` in `render` when it needs geometry.

Every widget is listed in [widgets-index](/pages/widgets-index/). A settings page built from `schema-form` and `tabs` uses those entries unchanged.

## Panel size

A panel's `default_size` is `{ "width": <constraint>, "height": <constraint> }`. A constraint is a string: `"80%"` for a share of the content area, `"60"` for a number of cells, or `"fill"` for the remaining space.

- Without `default_size`, a modal panel is centred at 80% by 80%.
- Without `default_size`, a non-modal panel takes the whole content area.

## Popups and Escape

A `popup` widget is drawn only while an `open-popup` call has it open. The popup has a `modal` flag and a title. `close-popup` or Escape hides it, and the plugin then receives `closed` with `none`. A modal popup cannot refuse the close.

Escape is reserved by the host. It closes the topmost popup first, then the topmost panel. A focused text widget consumes the first Escape, so the second Escape closes the panel. The plugin can also submit `close-view` for its own panel.

## Risk and tier rules

- This grant is not marked high risk.
- A T1 bundled plugin receives it automatically up to its manifest ceiling.
- A T2 or T3 plugin needs an explicit grant in the review dialog, and the grant is remembered.
- A view shows only what the plugin renders. Any data a view reads needs its own grant, such as `fs.read:project`.

## What the review dialog says

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.ui 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                        │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Shows panels and settings pages <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………</span> ui.panels │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests ui.panels, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar. Checked rows are granted; a high-risk row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

## When the grant is declined

- Every `ui` import returns `not-permitted`.
- The `panels`, `settings` tabs with `"render": "view"` and `onboarding_steps` contributions are not registered.
- The `open-view` intent is refused with `not-permitted`.
- A settings page that is not registered does not appear in the Settings screen.
- The rest of the plugin, such as its commands and its server logic, is unaffected.

## Worked example in Rust: a run log panel

The manifest declares the panel, a command that opens it, and the `views` export.

```json
{
  "id": "example-plugin",
  "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] },
  "exports": ["views"],
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [{ "id": "open-run-log", "title": "Open run log" }],
    "panels": [
      { "id": "run-log", "title": "Run log", "icon": "list",
        "default_size": { "width": "80%", "height": "60%" }, "modal": false }
    ]
  }
}
```

The command id is `example-plugin/open-run-log`, because the local id gets the plugin id as prefix.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{log, ui};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::Level;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::{Area, Constraint, Direction};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{ActionKind, UiTree, ViewTarget};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct RunLog {
    lines: Vec<String>,
}

impl Lifecycle for RunLog {}

impl Handler for RunLog {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(command)
                    if command.command == "example-plugin/open-run-log" =>
                {
                    if ui::open_panel("run-log").is_err() {
                        log::log(Level::Warn, "the run log panel could not be opened");
                    }
                }
                Event::UiAction(action) if action.key == "refresh" => {
                    if action.kind == ActionKind::Activated {
                        self.lines.push(format!("refresh {}", self.lines.len() + 1));
                        ui::invalidate(ViewTarget::Panel("run-log".into()));
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for RunLog {
    fn render(&mut self, _view: ViewTarget, area: Area) -> UiTree {
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let visible: Vec<String> =
            self.lines.iter().rev().take(area.rows as usize).cloned().collect();
        let log_view = tree.paragraph(visible).key("log").scrollable(true);
        let refresh = tree.button("Refresh").key("refresh");
        let body = tree
            .layout(Direction::Vertical)
            .constraints([Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(3)])
            .child(log_view)
            .child(refresh);
        let root = tree.block().title("Run log").child(body);
        tree.finish(root)
    }
}
```

The `Tree` type comes from `ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build`. The example omits that import for brevity.

## Worked example in TypeScript: a settings page with tabs

The manifest declares the settings page. The view target is `settings-page("display")`.

```json
{
  "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] },
  "exports": ["views"],
  "contributes": {
    "settings": [{ "kind": "tab", "id": "display", "title": "Display", "icon": "sliders", "render": "view" }]
  }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { invalidate } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { block, paragraph, span, tabs, toggle, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const preferences = { showHints: true };
const DISPLAY_PAGE = { tag: 'settings-page', val: 'display' } as const;

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  deactivate() { return undefined; },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') continue;
      const action = event.val;
      if (action.key !== 'show-hints' || action.kind !== 'toggled') continue;
      preferences.showHints = action.value.tag === 'flag' && action.value.val;
      invalidate(DISPLAY_PAGE);
    }
    return [];
  },
  render(_view, _area) {
    return tree(
      block({ title: 'Display' }, [
        tabs({ titles: [span('General'), span('Advanced')] }, [
          toggle({ key: 'show-hints', label: 'Show hints', value: preferences.showHints }),
          paragraph(['Advanced options are listed here.']),
        ]),
      ]),
    );
  },
});
```

The `tabs` widget renders only its selected child, and the host keeps the tab index. A real plugin stores its preferences with `settings`, not in a module variable.

## Limits, errors and edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `open-panel` for a panel that is not declared | `not-found` |
| `open-popup` when no `popup` widget with that id is in the last rendered trees | `not-found` |
| `set-widget-state` with a key unknown in that view | `not-found` |
| `set-widget-state` with a state kind that does not fit the widget | `invalid-argument` |
| `write-surface` with no `surface` of that key | `not-found` |
| `write-surface` with a format that differs from the widget, data that is not whole rows, or data over 16 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| `invalidate`, `close-panel`, `close-popup`, `widget-state`, `display-width`, `theme` | no error code |
| Two nodes with the same `key` in one tree | trap; the plugin is restarted |
| A child index out of range, or a tree that is not a tree | trap |
| More than 4,096 nodes, or more than 1,024 KiB of tree | trap |
| `views.render` runs past its deadline (10 ms by default, up to 20 ms for a T1 plugin) | trap |
| Three failures in 10 minutes | the plugin stops, and Settings > Plugins offers to turn it on again |

## What the user sees

The run log panel from the Rust example, after two presses of Refresh, looks like this in an 80-column terminal:

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭─ Run log ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ refresh 1                                                │
│ refresh 2                                                │
│ refresh 3                                                │
│                                                          │
│                                                          │
│                       [ Refresh ]                        │
│                                                          │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  Enter: press the button   Esc: close the panel
</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The host paints the run log view from the tree in the Rust example.</figcaption>
</figure>

- A panel opens at its `default_size` and closes with Escape.
- A settings page is listed under the plugin in Settings.
- An onboarding step appears in the setup flow, in the order the manifest gives.
- Widgets that have a key keep their selection, scroll offset and typed text across renders.
- Colours follow the theme. The host applies the leader-row and icon rules to every view without extra code.

# Capability: workspace.manage

## workspace.manage

The `workspace.manage` capability lets a server-side plugin record Git worktrees in the kernel and release them again. A worktree is a second checkout of a repository in its own folder, so one project can have several branches checked out at the same time. An agent pane often works in a worktree of its own.

The kernel keeps a custody record for each registered worktree. The record holds the id, the folder, the branch, the owning pane or tree node, and whether a process is running in the worktree. The snapshot, the close policy and the list all read these records, so they agree on who owns what.

The kernel never runs Git. The plugin creates the branch and the folder with `git worktree add`, through [process control](/pages/api-process-control/) and the `process.run:git` grant, and then registers the result. Release removes the custody record only. The folder and the branch stay on disk until the plugin removes them itself. The host functions are listed on the [workspace](/pages/api-workspace/) page. This page covers the grant, its rules, its errors and what the user sees.

<div class="warn">
<p>Register writes a custody record that the snapshot and the close policy depend on. Release the record when the worktree is no longer needed. Grant this capability only to a plugin whose purpose is managing worktrees.</p>
</div>

### What you need

- **Grant `workspace.manage`** (risk H, no argument). It covers `register`, `release` and `list`.
- **Grant `process.run:git`** (risk H). The plugin needs it to run `git worktree add` and `git worktree remove`. `workspace.manage` does not imply it, and the kernel checks the two separately.
- **Grant `fs.read:project`** for the folder passed as `repository`.
- **Grant `fs.write:worktrees`** (risk H) for the folder passed as `path`. The `worktrees` scope is rooted at the setting `workspace.worktree_root`. Its default is `<parent of the project>/<project name>.worktrees/`.
- **Side and language.** Server side only, in Rust or TypeScript. The client world has no `workspace` import.
- **Tier.** The grant is H for every tier. A T1 bundled plugin is asked once, at its first activation. A T2 or T3 plugin shows it in the install review dialog, unchecked.

### Grant syntax

The grant takes no argument. The install check rejects the other forms with these errors:

| Grant | Result | Install error |
|---|---|---|
| `workspace.manage` | valid | none; the only form |
| `workspace.manage:git` | rejected | `manifest.grant-argument`: `capability "workspace.manage" takes no argument (got "workspace.manage:git")` |
| `workspace` | rejected | `manifest.grant-unknown`: `capability "workspace" is not known to plugin API ilium:plugin@0.1.0` |

### Surface

The interface as the kernel declares it (WIT, `ilium:host/workspace@0.1.0`). The name `%list` escapes a keyword in WIT. In code the function is `list`.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:host/workspace in reference-wit
record workspace-spec {
  repository: fs-path, path: fs-path, branch: string,
  base: option<string>, owner: option<node-id>,
}
record workspace-info {
  id: u64, path: fs-path, branch: string, owner: option<node-id>, in-use: bool,
}
register: func(spec: workspace-spec) -> result<u64, plugin-error>;
release: func(workspace: u64) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
%list: func() -> list<workspace-info>;
```

All three functions are synchronous. They return at once, have no request id and never return `busy`.

| Function | Rust | TypeScript | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `register` | `workspace::register(spec)` | `register(spec)` | `Result<u64, PluginError>`, `bigint` | Records a worktree and its owner. Returns the new record id. |
| `release` | `workspace::release(id)` | `release(id)` | `Result<(), PluginError>`, `void` | Removes the custody record. The folder and the branch stay. |
| `%list` | `workspace::list()` | `list()` | `Vec<WorkspaceInfo>`, `WorkspaceInfo[]` | Returns every record in ascending id order. |

The fields of the two records:

| Record | Field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WorkspaceSpec` | `repository` | `FsPath` | `FsPath` | The Git repository folder. The plugin needs `fs.read` for its scope. |
| `WorkspaceSpec` | `path` | `FsPath` | `FsPath` | The worktree folder. Normally in scope `worktrees`. |
| `WorkspaceSpec` | `branch` | `String` | `string` | The branch that the worktree checks out. |
| `WorkspaceSpec` | `base` | `Option<String>` | `base?: string` | The commit or branch the branch started from. Stored and shown by `list`. The kernel does not apply it. |
| `WorkspaceSpec` | `owner` | `Option<NodeId>` | `owner?: bigint` | The pane or tree node that owns the worktree. |
| `WorkspaceInfo` | `id` | `u64` | `bigint` | The record id that `register` returned. |
| `WorkspaceInfo` | `in-use` | `in_use: bool` | `inUse: boolean` | Whether the worktree is in use now (see below). |

Node ids are `u64` in WIT, so they are `u64` in Rust and `bigint` in TypeScript. Write them with a trailing `n` in TypeScript literals, for example `41n`.

### The custody record and in-use

`register` creates a custody record. The owner pane may close while the record lives. `release` ends it.

- **Owner.** The `owner` field names a pane or tree node. When the owner pane closes, the kernel sets `owner` to `none`. The record stays, so the plugin still sees the worktree in `list` and can release it.
- **In use.** A worktree is in use while its owner pane is open with a running process, or while any pane with a running process has a working directory inside the worktree path. An open owner pane that is idle does not make the worktree in use. The kernel evaluates this when a call runs. It is not stored.
- **Close policy.** The kernel never deletes a worktree. Closing a pane changes the record, not the folder. The plugin removes the folder with `git worktree remove` after `release`.

<figure>

<svg viewBox="0 0 360 280" role="img" aria-label="Worktree custody: the plugin calls the kernel custody record, the snapshot reads it, and Git runs through process.run:git">

### Checks and errors

`register` checks the call before it writes anything. The checks run in this order:

1. The grant is held, and `path` sits inside a write scope the plugin holds (`fs.write:worktrees` normally). Otherwise `not-permitted`.
2. The branch name has valid Git syntax. Otherwise `invalid-argument`.
3. `repository` and `path` are existing folders with a `.git` entry. The `.git` entry is the marker that `git worktree add` writes. Otherwise `not-found`.
4. `owner`, when set, names a node that exists. Otherwise `not-found`.
5. `path` is not registered already. Otherwise `conflict`.

The kernel does not check that the branch exists, because the plugin creates it before it registers. It does not apply `base` either.

| Function | Code | Cause | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `register` | `not-permitted` | Grant missing or declined, or `path` outside a write scope the plugin holds | Offer the user a manual route. Do not retry. |
| `register` | `invalid-argument` | Branch name breaks Git's syntax rules | Fix the name and call again. |
| `register` | `not-found` | `repository` or `path` is not a Git folder or does not exist, or `owner` is gone | Create the worktree, or fix the call. |
| `register` | `conflict` | `path` is already registered | Call `list` and reuse the existing id. |
| `release` | `not-found` | Unknown id, or the record was already released | Nothing to do. |
| `release` | `conflict` | The worktree is in use (see above) | Wait for the process to end, read `list` again, then release. |

Every function may also return the universal codes `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`. `revoked` means the grant changed during the call. The plugin is then reactivated with its reduced grant set.

<div class="note">
<p>Read `list` before `release` when the plugin is unsure whether a worktree is still in use. Its `in-use` field is the same value that `release` checks.</p>
</div>

### Review dialog and what the user sees

For a T2 or T3 package, the install review dialog lists the grant in the server block. The dialog marks it as high risk and leaves it unchecked by default. The user checks it, or the plugin installs without it. The `worktrees` scope is described as "this project's worktrees".

A T1 bundled plugin is activated first without its high-risk grants. The first activation shows one prompt, "Plugin <name> asks for:", with a checkbox for `workspace.manage` and the buttons `Allow selected` and `Not now`. `Not now` asks again at the next server start, at most three times. After that the user grants it from Settings > Plugins.

The user can also inspect and revoke the grant from the command line:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.worktrees

  <span class="t-err">HIGH</span>  workspace.manage    Create and track Git worktrees  <span class="t-ok">granted</span>

</pre>

Revoking the grant takes effect at once. The plugin then runs with the reduced grant set. The render above is illustrative, not generated.

### Example: register and release in Rust

The plugin first runs `git worktree add -b` through process control, which creates the branch and the folder. The functions below run from a `Lifecycle` or `Handler` implementation of a server plugin.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::workspace::{self, WorkspaceSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Records a worktree that the plugin already created with `git worktree add -b`.
pub fn register_worktree(folder: &str, branch: &str, owner: NodeId) -> Result<u64, PluginError> {
    let spec = WorkspaceSpec {
        repository: FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: String::new() },
        path: FsPath { scope: "worktrees".into(), path: folder.into() },
        branch: branch.into(),
        base: Some("master".into()),
        owner: Some(owner),
    };
    workspace::register(spec)
}

/// Removes the custody record only. The folder and the branch stay on disk.
pub fn release_worktree(workspace_id: u64) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    workspace::release(workspace_id).map_err(|error| {
        let message = format!("release of worktree {workspace_id} failed: {:?}", error.code);
        log::log(Level::Warn, &message);
        error
    })
}
```

The manifest declares the server grants `workspace.manage`, `process.run:git`, `fs.read:project` and `fs.write:worktrees`.

### Example: register, list and release in TypeScript

The same flow in TypeScript. `owner` is a `bigint`, and a failed call throws `PluginError`, whose `code` field holds the error code.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { list, register, release } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/workspace';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {
    for (const record of list()) {
      log('info', `worktree ${record.id} on ${record.branch}, in use: ${record.inUse}`);
    }
  },
});

/** Records a worktree that the plugin already created with `git worktree add -b`. */
export function registerWorktree(folder: string, branch: string, owner: bigint): bigint {
  return register({
    repository: { scope: 'project', path: '' },
    path: { scope: 'worktrees', path: folder },
    branch,
    base: 'master',
    owner,
  });
}

/** Removes the custody record only. The folder and the branch stay on disk. */
export function releaseWorktree(workspaceId: bigint): void {
  try {
    release(workspaceId);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError) {
      log('warn', `release of worktree ${workspaceId} failed: ${error.code}`);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

### Edge cases

- **Owner pane closes.** The record survives with `owner` set to `none`. Release it when the plugin finishes with the worktree.
- **Process running in the worktree after the owner closed.** `release` returns `conflict`, because another pane with a running process has the worktree path as its working directory.
- **Grant revoked.** Calls in flight return `revoked`. Later calls return `not-permitted`. The plugin is reactivated without the grant.
- **Declined grant.** `register`, `release` and `list` return `not-permitted`. The plugin should tell the user what it cannot do and offer a manual way to create the worktree.
- **Deleting the folder by hand.** The kernel does not notice. The record stays until the plugin releases it.

### Who requests it

First-party plugins from `feature-mapping.md` use this capability:

- 67 Agent in a new Git worktree: `workspace.manage`, `process.run:git`, `fs.write:worktrees`.
- 68 Agent in an existing worktree: `workspace.manage`, `process.run:git`.
- 70 Worktree cleanup and prune: `workspace.manage`, `process.run:git`.

- [workspace](/pages/api-workspace/) for the host functions and their records.
- [process.run](/pages/capability-process-run/) for the Git commands the plugin runs.
- [process control](/pages/api-process-control/) for starting the Git commands and reading their exit status.
- [fs.write](/pages/capability-fs-write/) for the `worktrees` scope the worktree is written to.
- [fs.read](/pages/capability-fs-read/) for the `project` scope that holds the repository.
- [settings](/pages/api-settings/) for reading `workspace.worktree_root`.

# Capability: terminal.read-cells

## terminal.read-cells

The `terminal.read-cells` capability lets a plugin read the cells of a terminal pane, not only its text. A cell carries its text, foreground and background colour, text modifiers and a wide-character flag. The plugin also reads the terminal modes that the running program enabled, the foreground process, and takes a frozen snapshot of screen plus scrollback that stays stable while the program keeps writing.

The grant is the colour-aware sibling of [terminal.read-screen](/pages/capability-terminal-read-screen/), which returns plain text only. It does not read history above the scrollback window of the visible screen request; for the full scrollback as text use [terminal.history](/pages/capability-terminal-history/).

**You will need:**

- A `terminal.read-cells` grant on the side that reads. The grant takes no argument.
- A pane id from the tree or from a [pane event](/pages/api-events/).
- Optional: the `screen-changed` event, which this grant also enables, to know when to read again.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A read-cells call is checked and answered with cell rows and a revision">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls read-cells(pane, part, first_row, count)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">count is at most 1,000 rows</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant, the pane and the range</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">unknown pane returns none</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>

<figcaption>A read of cells is a copy. The revision lets the plugin tell whether the screen changed between two reads.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.read-cells` | yes | the only form |
| `terminal.read-cells:*` | no | the grant takes no argument (`manifest.grant-argument`) |
| `terminal.cells` | no | unknown grant name (`manifest.grant-unknown`) |

The grant is a normal-risk capability. Screen contents can still hold secrets, so the review dialog states that the plugin reads what is on the screen. It is granted automatically to bundled T1 plugins up to their manifest ceiling.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.read-cells` | function | `read-cells(pane, part, first-row, count) -> option<cell-rows>`. `part` is a `screen-part`. `count` is at most 1,000. |
| `terminal.modes` | function | Returns the `terminal-mode` flags: alternate screen, mouse reporting, bracketed paste, application cursor, focus reporting, synchronized output. |
| `terminal.foreground-process` | function | Returns `foreground-process { name, command-line, cwd }`. The `cwd` is for display only. |
| `terminal.freeze-snapshot` | function | Returns a snapshot id: a stable copy of screen and scrollback. Read it with `read-snapshot-cells`, release it with `drop-snapshot`. |
| `screen-changed` | event | `{ pane, first-row, last-row, revision }`, coalesced to at most 10 per second per pane. |

The interface is described on [Terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/) and the events on [Events](/pages/api-events/). Pane lookups go through [Panes](/pages/api-panes/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.cellview",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "panes.read",
      "terminal.read-cells"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin copies the first 40 visible rows when the command `com.example.cellview/snapshot` runs. The snapshot keeps the copy stable while the program continues to write.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal::{self, ScreenPart};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct CellView;

impl Handler for CellView {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.cellview/snapshot" { continue; }
            let Some(pane) = invoked.pane else { continue };
            match terminal::freeze_snapshot(pane) {
                Ok(snapshot) => {
                    if let Some(rows) = terminal::read_snapshot_cells(snapshot, 0, 40) {
                        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{} rows, revision {}", rows.rows.len(), rows.revision));
                    }
                    terminal::drop_snapshot(snapshot);
                }
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("freeze failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { freezeSnapshot, readSnapshotCells, dropSnapshot } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== 'com.example.cellview/snapshot' || event.val.pane === undefined) continue;
      try {
        const snapshot = freezeSnapshot(event.val.pane);
        const rows = readSnapshotCells(snapshot, 0, 40);
        if (rows) log('info', `${rows.rows.length} rows, revision ${rows.revision}`);
        dropSnapshot(snapshot);
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `freeze failed: ${String(error)}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The snapshot is released in every path. A plugin that forgets `drop-snapshot` keeps the copy until deactivation, and the host counts snapshots against the plugin memory quota.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `not-permitted` | Fall back to [terminal.read-screen](/pages/capability-terminal-read-screen/) if that is granted. |
| Unknown pane or pane closed | `none`, or `not-found` for `freeze-snapshot` | Drop the cached pane id. |
| `count` above 1,000 | `invalid-argument` | Read in chunks and compare the `revision` of each chunk. |
| Pane has no screen yet | `pane-not-ready` | Wait for the next `screen-changed` event. |
| Snapshot id already dropped | `none` | Do not reuse a dropped snapshot. |
| Grant revoked later | `revoked`, then `not-permitted` | Stop reading; the plugin is re-activated with the reduced set. |

Reading cells does not wake an idle terminal. A read of a pane that the user closed during the call returns none, not an error.

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states the colour-aware reading of the screen.

# Capability: terminal.history

## terminal.history

The `terminal.history` capability lets a plugin read the scrollback above the visible screen, as text, and search it with a regular expression. Scrollback holds everything the program printed, including commands, tokens and passwords that scrolled off screen, so the grant is high risk (**H**).

Both calls are asynchronous: they return a request id and the result is picked up with a `take-` call once it is ready.

**You will need:**

- A `terminal.history` grant. It takes no argument and always needs an explicit grant, even for a bundled T1 plugin.
- A pane id and a plan for how much text to ask for: the answer is capped at 4 MiB, newest text kept.
- The request id pattern: see [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A history request is checked and later answered with text or matches">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls history-text or search-history</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">returns a request id</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the explicit grant and the size caps</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">max-bytes at most 4 MiB</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host reads the scrollback off the UI thread</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">newest text is kept when truncated</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">take-history or take-matches</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">not-permitted, invalid-argument</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>History reads are two steps: submit the request, then take the result when it is ready.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.history` | yes | the only form |
| `terminal.history:visible` | no | no argument is accepted (`manifest.grant-argument`) |
| `terminal.read-history` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk. A bundled T1 plugin still needs the explicit grant, and the review dialog shows the line in the warning style with `!`, unchecked by default. The grant does not include the live screen; that is [terminal.read-screen](/pages/capability-terminal-read-screen/).

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.history-text` | function | `history-text(pane, max-bytes) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>`. At most 4 MiB, newest text kept. Pick up with `take-history`. |
| `terminal.take-history` | function | Returns `option<string>`: none until ready. |
| `terminal.search-history` | function | `search-history(pane, regex, max-matches)`. `max-matches` is a `u16`. Pick up with `take-matches`. |
| `history-match` | record | `{ row: u32, column: u16, length: u16 }` in scrollback coordinates. |

See [Terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/) and [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.scrollsearch",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "panes.read",
      "terminal.history"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin searches the scrollback of a pane for the text `error:` when the command `com.example.scrollsearch/errors` runs, and logs how many lines matched.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::terminal;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ScrollSearch;

impl Handler for ScrollSearch {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.scrollsearch/errors" { continue; }
            let Some(pane) = invoked.pane else { continue };
            // Async wrapper: submits search-history, then take-matches when ready.
            match terminal::search_history(pane, "error:", 200).block_on() {
                Ok(matches) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{} matches", matches.len())),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("search failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { searchHistory } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/terminal';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  async onEvents(batch: Event[]): Promise<Submission[]> {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== 'com.example.scrollsearch/errors' || event.val.pane === undefined) continue;
      try {
        const matches = await searchHistory(event.val.pane, 'error:', 200);
        log('info', `${matches.length} matches`);
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `search failed: ${String(error)}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The regular expression runs in the host, so the plugin never receives the whole scrollback when it only needs positions. Ask for text with `history-text` only when the plugin must show or store it.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing, declined or not explicit | `not-permitted` | Explain in the UI that history needs the grant. |
| `max-bytes` above 4 MiB | `invalid-argument` | Ask for less. |
| Invalid regular expression | `invalid-argument` with the position in the message | Fix the pattern. |
| Pane closed while the request runs | `take-` returns none, then `not-found` | Drop the request. |
| Too many open requests | `busy` | Retry after the previous request finished. |
| Grant revoked later | `revoked` | Discard results already taken if they were secret-bearing. |

The text is cut at a line boundary when it is truncated to `max-bytes`, newest lines kept. Plugins should not write history text to their own storage unless the user asked for it.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

# Capability: terminal.input-lock

## terminal.input-lock

The `terminal.input-lock` capability lets a plugin hold the user's own keystrokes for a very short time so that a multi-stage input from the plugin cannot interleave with typing. Held keys are queued, not lost, and are delivered when the lock ends. The lock is high risk (**H**) because a plugin that holds input can make a pane unresponsive.

The lock has a hard ceiling of 2,000 ms, and only one lock exists per pane at a time.

**You will need:**

- A `terminal.input-lock` grant (explicit, high risk). It usually goes together with [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/), which sends the input.
- A staged `send-input` or another reason to hold the keys for less than 2 s.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A lock holds user keys, then releases them in order">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls lock-input(pane, millis) or sends lock-user-input</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">at most 2,000 ms</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant and that no other lock holds the pane</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">one lock per pane</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">User keys are queued until unlock or timeout</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">nothing is dropped</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok, keys delivered at unlock</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">conflict or not-permitted</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The lock ends on unlock-input, on the timeout, or when the plugin stops. Queued keys are then delivered in order.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.input-lock` | yes | the only form |
| `terminal.input-lock:5000` | no | a duration is not a grant argument; the ceiling is fixed at 2,000 ms |
| `terminal.lock` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk. The grant needs an explicit user decision even for a bundled plugin. The host also enforces the ceiling, so a plugin cannot extend a lock by calling `lock-input` again before the first lock ended: the second call is `conflict`.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.lock-input` | function | `lock-input(pane, millis) -> result<_, plugin-error>`. `millis` at most 2,000. |
| `terminal.unlock-input` | function | `unlock-input(pane)`. Releases the lock and delivers the queue. |
| `send-input.lock-user-input` | field | `bool` on the intent `send-input`: hold the keys for the duration of the stages, at most 2 s. See [Intents](/pages/api-intents/). |

Staged input is described on [Terminal primitives](/pages/primitives-terminal/). The input rules of the intent are on [Intents](/pages/api-intents/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.stagedinput",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "panes.read",
      "terminal.write",
      "terminal.input-lock"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin sends a slash command in two stages and holds the user keys for the duration, so typing cannot land between the two stages.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{InputStage, SendInputSpec};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct StagedInput;

impl Handler for StagedInput {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.stagedinput/compact" { continue; }
            let Some(pane) = invoked.pane else { continue };
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SendInput(SendInputSpec {
                pane,
                stages: vec![
                    InputStage::keys("/compact", 0),
                    InputStage::keys("\r", 120),
                ],
                lock_user_input: true,
                ..SendInputSpec::default()
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== 'com.example.stagedinput/compact' || event.val.pane === undefined) continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'send-input',
          val: {
            pane: event.val.pane,
            stages: [
              { text: '/compact', delayMs: 0 },
              { text: '\r', delayMs: 120 },
            ],
            lockUserInput: true,
          },
        },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

Without the grant the whole `send-input` is refused with `not-permitted`; a plugin that only wants staged input without the lock leaves `lock-user-input` out.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` on the intent, `not-permitted` on the function | Send the stages without `lock-user-input`. |
| `millis` above 2,000 | `invalid-argument` | Use a shorter lock. |
| Pane already locked | `conflict` | Wait for the unlock; one lock per pane at a time. |
| Plugin stops while locked | lock released, queue delivered | Nothing. |
| Pane closed while locked | lock dropped with the pane | Nothing. |
| Session limit on locks | `busy` | Retry later. |

Check order for `send-input` is: capability, stage and size rules, `if-current` precondition, then the lock. A failed precondition refuses the intent before any lock is taken.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

# Capability: terminal.raw-input

## terminal.raw-input

The `terminal.raw-input` capability lets a plugin send bytes to a terminal exactly as they are, send mouse events that the host encodes for the program, and ask a `terminal-view` widget to be interactive. Ordinary [terminal.write](/pages/capability-terminal-write/) sends text; raw input can send any byte sequence, so it can drive any program that reads the terminal, which is why the grant is high risk (**H**).

**You will need:**

- A `terminal.raw-input` grant (explicit, high risk).
- A pane id and the bytes or mouse events to send.
- Knowledge of the modes of the target pane: read them with [terminal.read-cells](/pages/capability-terminal-read-cells/) if mouse reporting matters.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A raw send-input is checked and written to the pty">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits send-input with raw bytes or mouse events</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">raw at most 64 KiB</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant, the stage and size rules and mouse reporting</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">mouse needs the program to enable it</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host writes the bytes to the PTY</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">mouse is encoded in the protocol the program asked for</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">refused(not-permitted or unsupported)</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Raw bytes go to the PTY unchanged. Mouse events are encoded by the host, so the plugin never writes escape sequences for them.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `terminal.raw-input` | yes | the only form |
| `terminal.raw-input:mouse` | no | no argument; raw bytes and mouse events share one grant |
| `terminal.raw` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk. A bundled T1 plugin still needs an explicit grant. The host does not inspect raw bytes, so the grant is as strong as keyboard access to the pane. Prefer plain text through `terminal.write` whenever the plugin can.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `send-input.raw` | field | `option<list<u8>>`, written as they are, at most 64 KiB. |
| `send-input.mouse` | field | `option<list<terminal-mouse>>`; `terminal-mouse { kind, button, column, row, modifiers }`. `unsupported` when mouse reporting is off. |
| `terminal-view.interactive` | widget field | `interactive: true` on the `terminal-view` widget forwards the user's input in the view to the pane. |

The widget is described on [Media and embedded widgets](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/). The intent is on [Intents](/pages/api-intents/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.rawkeys",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "panes.read",
      "terminal.write",
      "terminal.raw-input"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin sends a mouse click at column 10, row 5 to a pane when the command `com.example.rawkeys/click` runs. If the program has not enabled mouse reporting, the outcome is `refused(unsupported)`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{SendInputSpec, TerminalMouse};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Modifiers;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::PointerKind;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct RawKeys;

impl Handler for RawKeys {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.rawkeys/click" { continue; }
            let Some(pane) = invoked.pane else { continue };
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SendInput(SendInputSpec {
                pane,
                mouse: Some(vec![TerminalMouse {
                    kind: PointerKind::Press, button: 0, column: 10, row: 5, modifiers: Modifiers::empty(),
                }]),
                ..SendInputSpec::default()
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== 'com.example.rawkeys/click' || event.val.pane === undefined) continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'send-input',
          val: {
            pane: event.val.pane,
            mouse: [{ kind: 'press', button: 0, column: 10, row: 5, modifiers: [] }],
          },
        },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

To send bytes instead, set `raw` (Rust `raw: Some(vec![0x1b, b'[', b'A'])`, TypeScript `raw: new Uint8Array([0x1b, 0x5b, 0x41])`). A submission cannot mix `raw` and `text` or `stages` in one `send-input`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` | Send plain text through `terminal.write` instead. |
| Mouse events while mouse reporting is off | `refused(unsupported)` | Read `terminal.modes` first. |
| `raw` above 64 KiB | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Split into several sends. |
| `if-current` precondition fails | `refused(conflict)` | Re-read the pane state and retry. |
| Pane exited | `refused(not-found)` | Drop the pane id. |
| Rate limit | `refused(rate-limited)` | Coalesce events. |

The precondition `if-current` is checked before any byte is written, so a stale click never lands on a changed screen.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

│ <span class="t-warn">! marks a high-risk grant. It starts unchecked and is</span>                      │

# Capability: panes.lifecycle

## panes.lifecycle

The `panes.lifecycle` capability lets a plugin control the process inside a pane: freeze and unfreeze it, replace its command, terminate it and resize the pane. It also delivers `pane-lifecycle-changed` events. Because a plugin that can stop or replace a process can destroy the user's work, the grant is high risk (**H**) and is server-side only.

**You will need:**

- A `panes.lifecycle` grant on the server side (explicit, high risk).
- A pane id from [panes.read](/pages/capability-panes-read/).
- A way to show the user that a pane is frozen: the host draws the frozen mark itself.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="Lifecycle intents pass checks and act on the pane process">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits freeze-pane, replace-pane-command, terminate-pane-process or resize-pane</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">one intent per action</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant, the pane and the platform</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">freeze is refused on Windows</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host acts on the pane process</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">durable resume bindings stay with the kernel</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">refused(conflict, unsupported, not-permitted)</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Each lifecycle action is one intent with its own outcome. The kernel keeps ownership of the durable session resume binding.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `panes.lifecycle` | yes | the only form |
| `panes.lifecycle:freeze` | no | no argument; all five actions share one grant |
| `panes.control` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk and server-side only; the client side cannot request it. A bundled plugin still needs an explicit grant.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `freeze-pane` | intent | `pane`. Stops the process (SIGSTOP on Unix). `refused(unsupported)` on Windows. |
| `unfreeze-pane` | intent | `pane`. `refused(conflict)` when the pane is not frozen. |
| `replace-pane-command` | intent | `pane`, `command: list<string>`, `cwd`, `keep-scrollback: bool`. `ok` once the new process runs. |
| `terminate-pane-process` | intent | `pane`, `grace-ms` at most 10,000. `ok` when the process has exited; the pane stays open with its exit status. |
| `resize-pane` | intent | `pane`, optional `columns` and `rows`. `refused(conflict)` when the layout cannot give the size. |
| `pane-lifecycle-changed` | event | Reports freeze, exit and replace transitions. |

Intents are described on [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) and pane state on [Panes](/pages/api-panes/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server only).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.panecontrol",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "panes.read",
      "panes.lifecycle"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin freezes a pane when the command `com.example.panecontrol/freeze` runs. The dedup key stops a double click from submitting twice.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::FreezePaneSpec;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct PaneControl;

impl Handler for PaneControl {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.panecontrol/freeze" { continue; }
            let Some(pane) = invoked.pane else { continue };
            submissions.push(Submission::keyed(
                Intent::FreezePane(FreezePaneSpec { pane }),
                format!("freeze-{pane}"),
            ));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== 'com.example.panecontrol/freeze' || event.val.pane === undefined) continue;
      const pane = event.val.pane;
      submissions.push({
        intent: { tag: 'freeze-pane', val: { pane } },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: `freeze-${pane}`,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

Pair every freeze with a visible way to unfreeze. A frozen pane shows the frozen mark in the tree and the pane frame, and the user can unfreeze it by hand.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` | Hide the feature. |
| Freeze on Windows | `refused(unsupported)` | Check the platform before offering the action. |
| Unfreeze of a running pane | `refused(conflict)` | Ignore. |
| Resize that the layout cannot give | `refused(conflict)`, the limiting neighbour in the message | Ask for a smaller size. |
| `grace-ms` above 10,000 | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Use a shorter grace period. |
| Pane not found | `refused(not-found)` | Drop the pane id. |

A process frozen when the plugin stops stays frozen: the pane keeps the frozen mark so the user can resume it. Plugins should unfreeze on deactivation.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

# Capability: tree.restructure

## tree.restructure

The `tree.restructure` capability lets a plugin create groups, folders, projects and splits, and reorganise many nodes in one atomic step that the user can revert. It is high risk (**H**) because it changes how the user's whole workspace is arranged.

**You will need:**

- A `tree.restructure` grant (explicit, high risk).
- Node ids from [tree.read](/pages/capability-tree-read/).
- A label for the undo entry: `restructure` takes a human-readable `label`.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A restructure intent is validated as a whole and applied as one undoable step">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits restructure with up to 256 operations</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">move, create-group, ungroup, rename</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host validates every operation first</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">all or nothing</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>

  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host applies them as one undoable step</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">an undo token is returned</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `tree.restructure` | yes | the only form |
| `tree.restructure:groups` | no | no argument is accepted |
| `tree.reorganize` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk. Even a bundled T1 plugin needs an explicit grant. Simple renames, locks and moves of single nodes need only [tree.write](/pages/capability-tree-write/).

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `create-group` | intent | `parent`, `title`, `placement`, `children`. Outcome `ok-node`. |
| `create-folder` | intent | `parent`, `title`, optional `path`. Outcome `ok-node`. |
| `create-project` | intent | `title`, `root`. Outcome `ok-node`. |
| `create-split` | intent | `panes` (2 to 4), `direction`. Outcome `ok-node` for the split container. |
| `restructure` | intent | `operations` (at most 256), `label`. Outcome `ok-node` carrying an undo token (0 when none). |
| `revert-restructure` | intent | `token`. `refused(conflict)` when a later change touched the same nodes. |

See [Tree](/pages/api-tree/) and [Intents](/pages/api-intents/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.organizer",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "tree.read",
      "tree.restructure"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin groups two panes into a new group called Review when the command `com.example.organizer/group` runs, and keeps the undo token for a later revert.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::CreateGroupSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::Placement;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Organizer;

impl Handler for Organizer {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.organizer/group" { continue; }
            let Some(parent) = invoked.parent else { continue };
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::CreateGroup(CreateGroupSpec {
                parent,
                title: "Review".into(),
                placement: Placement::End,
                children: invoked.selection.clone(),
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked') continue;
      if (event.val.command !== 'com.example.organizer/group' || event.val.parent === undefined) continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'create-group',
          val: { parent: event.val.parent, title: 'Review', placement: 'end', children: event.val.selection },
        },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

The outcome `ok-node` carries the new node id. For `restructure` it carries the undo token as a node id, which a later `revert-restructure` takes.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` | Fall back to single moves with `tree.write` if granted. |
| One of many operations fails | `refused(conflict)` with the operation index | Fix that operation and resubmit the batch. |
| More than 256 operations | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Split into several restructures. |
| Revert after a later change | `refused(conflict)` | Tell the user that the layout changed since. |
| Locked node in the batch | `refused(conflict)` | Skip locked nodes. |
| Unknown node | `refused(not-found)` | Re-read the tree. |

The attention policy and the user's manual order are kernel concerns. A restructure never changes a title that the user set by hand.

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

# Capability: tree.attention

## tree.attention

The `tree.attention` capability lets a plugin mark a node as needing the user's attention and acknowledge that mark, and receive `attention-changed` events. The mark appears in the tree and in the Attention display mode. The policy for the done prefix and the sound stays with the kernel; the plugin only supplies the node and a short reason.

**You will need:**

- A `tree.attention` grant. No argument.
- A node id from [tree.read](/pages/capability-tree-read/) or an event.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="mark-attention shows a mark in the tree and ack-attention clears it">

  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits mark-attention(node, reason)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">reason at most 80 characters</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant and the node</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">the kernel owns sound and prefix</text>

  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">ack-attention clears it</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>

<figcaption>The plugin supplies the node and the reason. The kernel decides how the mark looks and whether a sound plays.</figcaption>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `tree.attention` | yes | the only form |
| `tree.attention:pane` | no | no argument |
| `attention` | no | unknown grant name |

Normal risk. A plugin can only add a mark and a reason of at most 80 characters, so the grant cannot hide or change anything else in the tree.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mark-attention` | intent | `node`, `reason` (at most 80 characters). Outcome `ok`. |
| `ack-attention` | intent | `node`. Outcome `ok`. |
| `attention-changed` | event | Reports a node whose attention state changed, from any source. |

See [Tree](/pages/api-tree/) and [Events](/pages/api-events/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.attention",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "tree.read",
      "tree.attention"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin marks the pane of a finished build and clears the mark when the user acknowledges it elsewhere.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::MarkAttentionSpec;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Attention;

impl Handler for Attention {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command == "com.example.attention/build-done" => {
                    if let Some(node) = invoked.pane {
                        submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::MarkAttention(MarkAttentionSpec {
                            node, reason: "Build finished".into(),
                        })));
                    }
                }
                Event::AttentionChanged(changed) if !changed.marked => {
                    log::log(Level::Debug, &format!("node {} acknowledged", changed.node));
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'com.example.attention/build-done' && event.val.pane !== undefined) {
        submissions.push({
          intent: { tag: 'mark-attention', val: { node: event.val.pane, reason: 'Build finished' } },
          correlation: 1n,
          dedupKey: undefined,
        });
      } else if (event.tag === 'attention-changed' && !event.val.isMarked) {
        log('debug', `node ${event.val.node} acknowledged`);
      }
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

A plugin never needs to clear a mark that the user acknowledged: the kernel clears it and sends `attention-changed`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` | Show the status in the plugin's own panel. |
| `reason` above 80 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Shorten the reason. |
| Node not found | `refused(not-found)` | Re-read the tree. |
| Marking too often | `refused(rate-limited)` | Coalesce marks per node. |
| Ack of an unmarked node | `ok` (no change) | Nothing. |
| Grant revoked later | later submissions `refused(not-permitted)`; existing marks stay | Nothing. |

Marks set by a plugin are removed when the plugin is disabled, so a disabled plugin cannot leave stale marks.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is a normal-risk grant and starts checked.
