# Capability: ui.chrome

## ui.chrome

The `ui.chrome` capability lets a plugin put its own controls into the frame of the client: a button in the tree toolbar, an icon in the hover strip of tree rows, a segment of the status bar, and a slot in pane frames (header icon, header text, footer row or banner). The plugin declares each place in its manifest and fills it at run time with intents.

The grant covers decoration of the chrome only. Whole panels need [ui.panels](/pages/capability-ui-panels/), and tree decorations need [tree.decorate](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/).

**You will need:**

- A `ui.chrome` grant. No argument.
- The matching `contributes` keys: `tree_toolbar` (cap 4), `row_actions` (cap 4), `status_segments` (cap 2) and `pane_frame_slots` (cap 4).
- Commands for the buttons to run: see [Commands](/pages/api-commands/).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="Chrome contributions are declared in the manifest and filled by intents">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Manifest declares a status segment, toolbar button, row action or frame slot</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">above the cap: manifest.contribution-limit</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits set-status-segment or set-frame-slot</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">at most 10 per second per slot</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Client draws the content in the declared place</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">clicks arrive as command-invoked</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok, drawn in the chrome</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">refused(invalid-argument, rate-limited)</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The place is declared once in the manifest. The content changes at run time through intents. A click on a toolbar button or row action runs the declared command.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `ui.chrome` | yes | the only form |
| `ui.chrome:status` | no | no argument; all four places share one grant |
| `ui.frame` | no | unknown grant name |

Normal risk. The host owns the layout: content is rich text of bounded length, a segment is at most 40 cells wide, and a plugin cannot hide or restyle kernel chrome.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tree_toolbar` | contribution | `{ id, icon, label, command, caption?, popup_view?, when? }`. `label` at most 24 characters. |
| `row_actions` | contribution | `{ id, icon, label, command, applies_to, when?, order? }`. The click arrives as `command-invoked` with origin `row-action`. |
| `status_segments` | contribution | `{ id, priority, max_width? }`. `priority` 0 to 100, `max_width` 4 to 40 cells. |
| `pane_frame_slots` | contribution | `{ id, placement, applies_to }`. Placement `header-icon`, `header-text`, `footer-row` or `banner`. |
| `set-status-segment`, `clear-status-segment` | intents | Fill or clear an own segment: `content: rich-text`, `tooltip`, `tone`. |
| `set-frame-slot`, `clear-frame-slot` | intents | Fill or clear an own slot for one pane. |

Contribution keys are in [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/); the intents are on [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [UI](/pages/api-ui/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.quota",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "ui.chrome"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin declares a status bar segment `quota` in its manifest (`"status_segments": [{ "id": "quota", "priority": 60 }]`) and fills it with a warning text when the command `com.example.quota/update` runs.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetStatusSegmentSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::{RichText, Tone};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Quota;

impl Handler for Quota {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.quota/update" { continue; }
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetStatusSegment(SetStatusSegmentSpec {
                segment: "quota".into(),
                content: RichText::plain("Quota 82%"),
                tooltip: None,
                tone: Some(Tone::Warning),
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { richText } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.quota/update') continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'set-status-segment',
          val: { segment: 'quota', content: richText('Quota 82%'), tooltip: undefined, tone: 'warning' },
        },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

The client draws the segment with the real status bar separators, and drops the lowest-priority segments first when the terminal is narrow.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)`; declared contributions are not drawn | Keep the information in an own panel. |
| Segment or slot id not declared | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Declare it in the manifest. |
| Pane does not match `applies_to` | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Check the pane kind first. |
| More than 10 updates per second | `refused(rate-limited)` | Coalesce updates. |
| Contribution cap exceeded | install refused with `manifest.contribution-limit` | Declare fewer places. |
| Unknown `when` key | install refused with `manifest.when-key` | Use a key from the context grammar. |

When a plugin is disabled, its segments, slots, buttons and row actions disappear at once.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states that the plugin adds controls to the client frame.

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests ui.chrome, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>

# Capability: open-external

## open-external

The `open-external` capability lets a plugin ask the host to open something outside Ilium: a web address in the default browser, a file with its desktop handler, a mail link, or an Ilium settings page with an `ilium://settings/...` link. The plugin never starts the handler itself. The host checks the target, and it asks the user to confirm the first open for each target origin (decision D25).

**You will need:**

- An `open-external` grant. No argument.
- A target: `url(string)` for `http`, `https` or `mailto`, `file(fs-path)`, or `settings(string)`.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="An open-external intent is checked, may ask the user once per origin, then starts the desktop handler">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits open-external(target)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">http, https, mailto, file or settings</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the scheme and the origin</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">first open per origin asks the user</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Desktop handler starts</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">ok means the handler started</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">refused(not-permitted, invalid-argument)</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The user confirms the first open for each origin. Later opens to the same origin run without a prompt.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `open-external` | yes | the only form |
| `open-external:https` | no | no argument; the schemes are fixed by the host |
| `open.external` | no | unknown grant name |

Normal risk, because the host confirms the first open per origin and restricts the schemes. A `file` target opens with the desktop default handler only and never executes it.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `open-external` | intent | `target`: `url(string)` (`http`, `https`, `mailto` only), `file(fs-path)` or `settings(string)` for `ilium://settings/<tab-id>#<key>`. Outcome `ok` after the handler started. |

The settings link form is the supported way to point a user at a kernel setting; see [settings.read-kernel](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/). See [Intents](/pages/api-intents/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.links",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "open-external"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin opens a status page when the command `com.example.links/status` runs, and a kernel setting when `com.example.links/scrollback` runs.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{ExternalTarget, OpenExternalSpec};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Links;

impl Handler for Links {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.links/status" { continue; }
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::OpenExternal(OpenExternalSpec {
                target: ExternalTarget::Url("https://status.example.com".into()),
            })));
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::OpenExternal(OpenExternalSpec {
                target: ExternalTarget::Settings("ilium://settings/terminal#scrollback".into()),
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.links/status') continue;
      submissions.push(
        { intent: { tag: 'open-external', val: { target: { tag: 'url', val: 'https://status.example.com' } } }, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: undefined },
        { intent: { tag: 'open-external', val: { target: { tag: 'settings', val: 'ilium://settings/terminal#scrollback' } } }, correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined },
      );
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

Both submissions are independent. If the user declines the first open of `status.example.com`, only that one is `refused(not-permitted)`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` | Show the address as text the user can copy. |
| User declines the origin confirmation | `refused(not-permitted)` | Do not ask again in a loop. |
| Scheme other than http, https or mailto in a `url` | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Use `file` or `settings` targets for those. |
| Settings link to an unknown tab | `refused(not-found)` | Use a tab id from the settings reference. |
| No desktop handler | `refused(unsupported)` | Show the target as text. |
| Rate limit | `refused(rate-limited)` | Open once per user action. |

`ok` means that the handler started, not that the page loaded.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line says that the plugin can open links and files outside Ilium.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Opens links and files outside Ilium <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………</span> open-external │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests open-external, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>

Listing the grants of an installed plugin from the terminal:

<figure>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.links
<span class="t-dim">Grant                             Risk     State</span>
open-external                     normal   <span class="t-ok">granted</span>
</pre>

<figcaption>Output of the grant listing for this plugin. A high-risk grant that the user left unchecked shows as declined.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Security

**[SEC-043]** `open-external` accepts only `https`, `http`, `mailto` and file paths inside granted scopes; each origin needs consent (D25). See [Network egress](/pages/reference-network-egress/).

# Capability: sessions.cross

## sessions.cross

The `sessions.cross` capability lets a server-side plugin list the user's other running Ilium sessions on the same machine and run one declared command of the same plugin in another session. The target session must also have the plugin installed and enabled with `sessions.cross` granted. It is high risk (**H**) because it lets a plugin act across project boundaries.

**You will need:**

- A `sessions.cross` grant on the server side (explicit, high risk).
- The same plugin installed and enabled in the target session, with the grant.
- A command declared by the plugin in `contributes.commands`: kernel commands of another session are never reachable (D16).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A plugin lists live sessions and sends one declared command to another session">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls sessions.list-live()</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">only the user's own sockets are visible</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls sessions.send(session, command, arguments)</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">same plugin, declared command</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Target session runs the command and replies</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">take-reply returns the reply string</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">reply string</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">not-permitted, not-found</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Both sessions must run the same plugin with the grant. The request carries the plugin id and the caller session name.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.cross` | yes | the only form |
| `sessions.cross:*` | no | no argument; the target is chosen per call |
| `sessions.all` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk and server-side only. A bundled plugin still needs the explicit grant, in both sessions.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.list-live` | function | Returns `list<live-session>`: `{ name, project, socket-id, panes, attached-clients, is-self }`. |
| `sessions.send` | function | `send(cross-request { session, command, arguments-json }) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>`. |
| `sessions.take-reply` | function | Returns `option<string>` once the target replied. |

See the host interface list in [Commands](/pages/api-commands/) and [Messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/) for same-session messaging.

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server only).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.sessionbridge",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "sessions.cross"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin sends the command `com.example.sessionbridge/ping` to every other live session and logs the replies.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::sessions::{self, CrossRequest};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct SessionBridge;

impl Handler for SessionBridge {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.sessionbridge/ping" { continue; }
            for session in sessions::list_live().into_iter().filter(|s| !s.is_self) {
                let request = CrossRequest {
                    session: session.name.clone(),
                    command: "com.example.sessionbridge/pong".into(),
                    arguments_json: "{}".into(),
                };
                match sessions::send(request).block_on() {
                    Ok(reply) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{}: {reply}", session.name)),
                    Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("{}: {error:?}", session.name)),
                }
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { listLive, send } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  async onEvents(batch: Event[]): Promise<Submission[]> {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.sessionbridge/ping') continue;
      for (const session of listLive().filter((s) => !s.isSelf)) {
        try {
          const reply = await send({ session: session.name, command: 'com.example.sessionbridge/pong', argumentsJson: '{}' });
          log('info', `${session.name}: ${reply}`);
        } catch (error) {
          log('warn', `${session.name}: ${String(error)}`);
        }
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

A reply is a string chosen by the target command. Treat it as untrusted input: it comes from another session, possibly of another project.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing in this session | `not-permitted` | Hide the feature. |
| Target session lacks the plugin or the grant | `not-permitted` | Tell the user to enable it there. |
| Command not declared by the plugin | `not-permitted` | Declare it in `contributes.commands`. |
| Session closed meanwhile | `not-found` | Call `list-live` again. |
| No reply within the deadline | `timed-out` | Retry once; do not loop. |
| Other user's socket | never listed | Nothing. |

The target session sees the caller's plugin id and session name, so the command can refuse unknown callers.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

# Capability: process.long-lived

## process.long-lived

The `process.long-lived` capability lets a plugin start a helper program that keeps running, feed it through standard input, and receive its output line by line. A one-shot run with [process.run](/pages/capability-process-run/) waits for the program to end; a spawned child stays alive until it exits, the plugin drops it, or the plugin stops. The program must also match a `process.run:<program>` grant. Long-lived children are high risk (**H**).

**You will need:**

- Two grants: `process.long-lived` and `process.run:<program>` for the same program.
- A plan for the child's lifetime: dropping the handle or stopping the plugin ends it (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A child process is spawned, streams lines to the plugin and ends on exit or when the plugin drops it">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls process.spawn(spawn-spec)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">program must match process.run</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host starts the child at low priority</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">counts against the 16 per session (session_processes)</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Output arrives as child-output events</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">whole lines with line-mode; child-exited at the end</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>

</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `process.long-lived` | yes | no argument; the program is named by `process.run:<program>` |
| `process.long-lived:tail` | no | no argument (`manifest.grant-argument`) |
| `process.spawn` | no | unknown grant name |

High risk. Without a matching `process.run:<program>` grant, `spawn` fails with `not-permitted`. Children run at low priority under the plugin CPU quota.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `process.spawn` | function | `spawn(spawn-spec { process, stdin-open, line-mode }) -> result<child, plugin-error>`. |
| `child` | resource | `pid-hint()` (display only), `write-stdin(bytes)`, `close-stdin()`, `signal(one of interrupt, terminate, kill, hangup)`. |
| `child-output` | event | `{ child, stream, bytes }`; whole lines with `line-mode`. |
| `child-exited` | event | `{ child, status, signal }`. |

One-shot runs are on [Process control](/pages/api-process-control/). The `timeout-millis` of a one-shot spec is ignored for children.

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.watcher",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "process.run:tail",
      "process.long-lived"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin starts `tail -f` on a log file, receives each line as an event, and stops the child when the command `com.example.watcher/stop` runs.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::process::{self, Child, ProcessSpec, SpawnSpec};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Watcher { child: Option<Child> }

impl Handler for Watcher {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            match event {
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command == "com.example.watcher/start" => {
                    let spec = SpawnSpec {
                        process: ProcessSpec::new("tail", &["-f", "/var/log/syslog"]),
                        stdin_open: false,
                        line_mode: true,
                    };
                    self.child = process::spawn(spec).ok();
                }
                Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) if invoked.command == "com.example.watcher/stop" => {
                    if let Some(child) = self.child.take() { let _ = child.signal("terminate"); }
                }
                Event::ChildOutput(output) => log::log(Level::Info, &String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.bytes)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { spawn, type Child } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

let child: Child | undefined;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'com.example.watcher/start') {
        child = spawn({ process: { program: 'tail', args: ['-f', '/var/log/syslog'] }, stdinOpen: false, lineMode: true });
      } else if (event.tag === 'command-invoked' && event.val.command === 'com.example.watcher/stop') {
        child?.signal('terminate');
        child = undefined;
      } else if (event.tag === 'child-output') {
        log('info', new TextDecoder().decode(event.val.bytes));
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Keep the handle in plugin state. Dropping it ends the child, which is also the clean-up path when the plugin deactivates.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `not-permitted` | Use a one-shot `process.run` if granted. |
| Program not covered by `process.run:<program>` | `not-permitted` | Add the matching grant. |
| More than 16 per session (`session_processes`), shared by `process.run` (`busy`) and `process.spawn` (`quota-exceeded`) | `quota-exceeded` | Reuse one child. |
| Program not found | `not-found` | Check the path or tell the user. |
| Child exits on its own | `child-exited` event | Restart only on user action. |
| Plugin stops | child gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s | Nothing. |

Output of a child can carry secrets from the environment. The host passes a minimal environment unless the spec names variables.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked. The matching program grant is listed on the next line.

# Capability: settings.read-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>

## settings.read-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>

The `settings.read-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>` capability lets a plugin read the values of one built-in Settings tab, for example the scrollback budget of the Terminal tab. The read is read-only (decision D13), secrets are always returned as `<redacted>`, and the plugin is told when a value changes. The argument is required and names exactly one kernel tab; there is no wildcard. The grant is normal risk for most tabs and high risk (**H**) for the `api` tab.

**You will need:**

- A `settings.read-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>` grant with one tab id from the settings reference (for example `terminal`).
- To change a value, link the user to it with [open-external](/pages/capability-open-external/): only the single owner plugin of a tab writes it, with `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` (see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/#writing-a-kernel-tab)).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A kernel tab is read as JSON with secrets redacted, and changes are reported as events">

  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls kernel-settings.read("terminal")</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">argument must match the grant</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host returns a JSON object of the tab values</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">secrets are "&lt;redacted&gt;"</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host sends kernel-settings-changed on edits</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">tab and changed keys</text>

<figcaption>The read is one-way. A plugin that does not own the tab never writes a kernel value.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `settings.read-kernel:terminal` | yes | one kernel tab id |
| `settings.read-kernel` | no | argument required (`manifest.grant-argument-missing`) |
| `settings.read-kernel:*` | no | no wildcard (`manifest.grant-wildcard`) |
| `settings.read-kernel:api` | yes, high risk | the api tab holds credentials |

Normal risk for ordinary tabs and high risk for `api`. The grant is independent of `settings.contribute:<tab>` (which adds sections) and of `settings.read-all` (which reads other plugins' values).

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kernel-settings.read` | function | `read(tab) -> result<string, plugin-error>`. JSON object of that tab; secrets are `"<redacted>"`. |
| `kernel-settings-changed` | event | `{ tab, keys }`. |

The tab ids are listed in [Settings](/pages/api-settings/) and [Settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.scrollinfo",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "settings.read-kernel:terminal"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin reads the Terminal tab when the command `com.example.scrollinfo/show` runs and logs the scrollback value. The key name is illustrative; read the keys from the tab reference.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::kernel_settings;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ScrollInfo;

impl Handler for ScrollInfo {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.scrollinfo/show" { continue; }
            match kernel_settings::read("terminal") {
                Ok(json) => log::log(Level::Info, &json),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("read failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.scrollinfo/show') continue;
      try {
        log('info', read('terminal'));
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `read failed: ${String(error)}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Parse the JSON defensively: a key that the kernel removes disappears from the object.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Tab not granted | `not-permitted` | Request only the tabs you need. |
| Unknown tab id | install refused, or `not-found` at run time | Use an id from the reference. |
| Missing argument in the manifest | `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | Add the tab id. |
| Wildcard argument | `manifest.grant-wildcard` | Name one tab. |
| Secret value | returned as `"<redacted>"` | Never prompt for the real value. |
| Grant revoked later | `revoked`, then `not-permitted` | Stop reading. |

To let the user change a value, submit `open-external` with `ilium://settings/<tab-id>#<key>`.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line names the tab. For the api tab it is high risk and unchecked.

# Capability: settings.contribute:<kernel-tab-id>

## settings.contribute:<kernel-tab-id>

The `settings.contribute:<kernel-tab-id>` capability lets a plugin add a section with rows to a built-in Settings tab, for example the Terminal tab. The section is always labelled with the plugin name, so the user can tell plugin rows from kernel rows. The grant gives permission to draw the section and nothing else: it does not read kernel values, and it does not write them. A plugin's own Settings tab needs no grant.

**You will need:**

- A `settings.contribute:<kernel-tab-id>` grant with one tab id, for example `terminal`.
- A `contributes.settings` entry with `kind: "section"` whose `tab` is that kernel tab id.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A section for a kernel tab is declared, checked against the grant and drawn with a plugin label">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Manifest declares a section for a kernel tab</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">kind section, tab terminal</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant at install</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">manifest.settings-target-grant otherwise</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Settings shows the labelled section</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">values live under the plugin id</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">section drawn</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">install refused</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The kernel rows stay untouched. Plugin values are stored under the plugin id and never in a kernel table.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `settings.contribute:terminal` | yes | one kernel tab id |
| `settings.contribute` | no | argument required |
| `settings.contribute:*` | no | no wildcard |
| `settings.contribute:self:main` | no | an own tab needs no grant |

Normal risk. The grant is independent of `settings.read-all`, `settings.write-all` and `settings.read-kernel`, in both directions.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `contributes.settings` section | contribution | `{ kind: "section", tab: "terminal", id, title, scope, placement, rows }` with at most 24 rows. Limits: 2 sections per plugin per kernel tab, 6 plugin sections per kernel tab. |
| `settings-changed` | event | Reports edits of the plugin's own values. |

Rows, row types and validation are on [Settings](/pages/api-settings/) and [Settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/). The tutorial is [Extend a built-in settings tab](/pages/tutorial-11-settings-extend-tab/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (the side of the section's scope).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.clipboardhistory",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "settings.contribute:terminal"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

The section itself is declared in the manifest. The plugin code only reacts to the user's edits. This plugin logs the value of the `max_entries` row when it changes.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ClipboardHistory;

impl Handler for ClipboardHistory {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::SettingsChanged(changed) = event else { continue };
            if changed.keys.iter().any(|key| key == "max_entries") {
                log::log(Level::Info, &format!("settings changed: {:?}", changed.keys));
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'settings-changed') continue;
      if (event.val.keys.includes('max_entries')) log('info', `settings changed: ${event.val.keys.join(', ')}`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

The manifest entry for the section: `{ "kind": "section", "tab": "terminal", "id": "capture", "title": "Capture", "scope": "client", "rows": [ { "type": "number", "key": "max_entries", "title": "Maximum entries", "default": 500 } ] }`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Section without the grant | install refused, `manifest.settings-target-grant` | Add `settings.contribute:<tab>`. |
| Unknown tab id | `manifest.settings-target-unknown` | Use a tab id from the reference. |
| Closed kernel tab | `manifest.settings-target-closed` | The tab does not accept sections. |
| Too many sections or rows | `manifest.settings-limit` | Reduce rows or sections. |
| Plugin disabled | rows dimmed and read-only, values kept | Nothing. |
| Grant declined by the user | section not drawn | Nothing. |

The values of a section are stored in `[plugins."<plugin-id>"]` and survive disabling and uninstalling until the user purges them.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The review dialog uses the wording `Adds settings to the <Tab label> tab`.

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# Capability: keymap.read

## keymap.read

The `keymap.read` capability lets a client plugin read the user's key bindings and turn a chord into the label the user sees, such as `Ctrl+Shift+K`. It is read-only: a plugin never changes a binding (decision D13). It also delivers `keymap-changed` events, so hints stay correct after a remap.

**You will need:**

- A `keymap.read` grant on the client side. No argument.
- Command ids to look up, as in [Commands](/pages/api-commands/).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A plugin reads bindings, formats chords and refreshes on keymap-changed">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls keymap.bindings()</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">returns every binding</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls chord-label(chord)</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">user-visible form</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host sends keymap-changed after a remap</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">re-read the bindings</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">list of bindings</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">not-permitted</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Hints are built from live bindings, so they follow the user's remaps.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `keymap.read` | yes | the only form |
| `keymap.write` | no | does not exist; bindings are never writable by plugins |
| `keymap.read:global` | no | no argument |

Normal risk. Bindings reveal which keys the user uses, not what the user types.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `keymap.bindings` | function | Returns `list<binding>`: `{ command, chords, context, is-default }`. |
| `keymap.chord-label` | function | `chord-label(chord) -> string`, for example `Ctrl+Shift+K`. |
| `keymap-changed` | event | Sent when the user changes the keymap. |

Intercepting keys is a different grant: see [keys.intercept](/pages/capability-keys-intercept/) and [Keys](/pages/api-keys/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (client only).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.keyhints",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "keymap.read"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin looks up the first chord for its own command and logs the user-visible label.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::keymap;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct KeyHints;

impl Handler for KeyHints {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.keyhints/show" { continue; }
            let label = keymap::bindings()
                .into_iter()
                .find(|binding| binding.command == "com.example.keyhints/show")
                .and_then(|binding| binding.chords.first().map(|chord| keymap::chord_label(chord)));
            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("shortcut: {}", label.unwrap_or_else(|| "none".into())));
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { bindings, chordLabel } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keymap';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.keyhints/show') continue;
      const binding = bindings().find((b) => b.command === 'com.example.keyhints/show');
      const chord = binding?.chords[0];
      log('info', `shortcut: ${chord ? chordLabel(chord) : 'none'}`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Call `bindings()` again on every `keymap-changed` event instead of caching labels for a long time.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `not-permitted` | Show no shortcut hint. |
| Command has no binding | empty chord list | Show no hint. |
| Server side requests the grant | install refused, the grant is client-only | Move the code to the client side. |
| Unknown chord string | `invalid-argument` | Use chords taken from `bindings()`. |
| Grant revoked later | `revoked` | Drop cached labels. |
| Keymap changes while reading | a `keymap-changed` event follows | Re-read. |

Bindings that conflict with another plugin's chord follow the keymap conflict rule; the user's remap always wins.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states that the plugin reads key bindings.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.keyhints 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                  │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Reads your key bindings <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………………………………</span> keymap.read │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests keymap.read, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>

Listing the grants of an installed plugin from the terminal:

<figure>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.keyhints
<span class="t-dim">Grant                             Risk     State</span>
keymap.read                       normal   <span class="t-ok">granted</span>
</pre>

# Capability: agent.transcript

## agent.transcript

The `agent.transcript` capability lets a plugin read the conversation of an agent pane as typed turns: role, text, tool name, time and token count. The host parses the agent's own session file; the path stays resolved by the kernel and is never shown to the plugin. A transcript contains everything the user and the agent said, including pasted secrets, so the grant is high risk (**H**).

**You will need:**

- An `agent.transcript` grant (explicit, high risk).
- An agent pane id from [agent.read](/pages/capability-agent-read/).
- An agent signature with a known transcript format: otherwise the call returns `unsupported`.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A transcript query is parsed by the host from the agent session file and returned as typed turns">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls agent.transcript(pane, last-turns, max-bytes)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">at most 512 turns and 4 MiB</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host parses the session file of the agent</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">path stays in the kernel</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls take-transcript</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">returns the typed turns</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">list of transcript-turn</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">unsupported, not-permitted</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The plugin sees turns, never the path of the session file.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `agent.transcript` | yes | the only form |
| `agent.transcript:claude` | no | no argument; support depends on the signature |
| `fs.read:agent-sessions:*` | separate | file access to session folders is a different, high-risk grant |

High risk. A bundled T1 plugin still needs an explicit grant. Prefer [agent.read](/pages/capability-agent-read/) when the plugin only needs the activity or the model.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agent.transcript` | function | `transcript(transcript-query { pane, last-turns, max-bytes }) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>`. |
| `agent.take-transcript` | function | Returns `option<list<transcript-turn>>`. |
| `transcript-turn` | record | `{ role, text, tool?, at?, tokens? }`; `role` is `user`, `assistant`, `tool` or `system`. |

See [Agent primitives](/pages/primitives-agent/) and [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.recap",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "agent.read",
      "agent.transcript"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin counts the assistant turns among the last 20 turns of an agent pane when the command `com.example.recap/count` runs.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::primitives::agent::{self, TranscriptQuery, TurnRole};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Recap;

impl Handler for Recap {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.recap/count" { continue; }
            let Some(pane) = invoked.pane else { continue };
            let query = TranscriptQuery { pane, last_turns: 20, max_bytes: 262_144 };
            match agent::transcript(query).block_on() {
                Ok(turns) => {
                    let replies = turns.iter().filter(|turn| turn.role == TurnRole::Assistant).count();
                    log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{replies} assistant turns"));
                }
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("transcript failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { transcript } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/primitives/agent';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  async onEvents(batch: Event[]): Promise<Submission[]> {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.recap/count' || event.val.pane === undefined) continue;
      try {
        const turns = await transcript({ pane: event.val.pane, lastTurns: 20, maxBytes: 262144 });
        log('info', `${turns.filter((turn) => turn.role === 'assistant').length} assistant turns`);
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `transcript failed: ${String(error)}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Do not copy transcript text into the plugin's storage unless the user asked for it.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `not-permitted` | Use `agent.read` data only. |
| Signature has no known transcript format | `unsupported` | Hide the feature for that agent. |
| `last-turns` above 512 or `max-bytes` above 4 MiB | `invalid-argument` | Ask for less. |
| Pane is not an agent pane | `not-found` | Check the pane kind. |
| Session file not written yet | empty list | Try again after the first turn. |
| Grant revoked later | `revoked` | Discard cached turns. |

Turns come from the agent's file, so they can lag the screen by a moment.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line is high risk and starts unchecked.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.recap 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                     │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ <span class="t-warn">! [ ] Reads agent conversations</span> <span class="t-dim">…………………………………………………………………</span> <span class="t-warn">agent.transcript</span> │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-warn">! marks a high-risk grant. It starts unchecked and is</span>                      │
│ <span class="t-warn">always asked for, even for bundled plugins.</span>                                │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests agent.transcript, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>

Listing the grants of an installed plugin from the terminal:

<figure>

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.recap
<span class="t-dim">Grant                             Risk     State</span>
agent.transcript                  high     <span class="t-warn">declined</span>
</pre>

<figcaption>Output of the grant listing for this plugin. A high-risk grant that the user left unchecked shows as declined.</figcaption>
</figure>

The user can change the grant at any time in Settings > Plugins > com.example.recap > Capabilities. A revocation re-activates the plugin with the reduced grant set, and the stubs of the declined imports return `not-permitted`.

# Capability: location.geocode

## location.geocode

The `location.geocode` capability lets a plugin turn a place name into coordinates and coordinates into a place name. The host owns the provider (Photon, with Nominatim as fallback), the user agent, the attribution and the rate limit. The first use asks the user once for consent to send place names to the provider; without it the calls return `not-permitted`. The same service backs the `location-picker` widget and `location` rows, so a plugin does not need an [http](/pages/capability-http/) grant for geocoding.

**You will need:**

- A `location.geocode` grant on the client or scene side.
- The user's one-time consent to send place names to the provider.

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `location.geocode` | yes | the only form |
| `location.geocode:photon` | no | the provider is chosen by the host |
| `location.observer` | separate | reads the device location; high risk |

Normal risk. Place names leave the machine only after the user's consent. The grant does not give the user's own position; that is [location.observer](/pages/capability-location-observer/). Kernel settings tabs never need this grant.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `geocode.search` | function | `search(geocode-query { text, near?, limit, language? }) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>`. |
| `geocode.reverse` | function | `reverse(point) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>`; at most one result. |
| `geocode.take-places` | function | Returns `option<list<geo-place>>`. |
| `location-picker` search | widget field | The search field of the widget and of `location` rows in own tabs. |

See [Location](/pages/api-location/) and [Media and embedded widgets](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (client or scene).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.places",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "location.geocode"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin searches for Lyon, limited to five results, in French.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::geocode;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::geocode::GeocodeQuery;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Places;

impl Handler for Places {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.places/lookup" { continue; }
            let query = GeocodeQuery { text: "Lyon".into(), near: None, limit: 5, language: Some("fr".into()) };
            match geocode::search(query).block_on() {
                Ok(places) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{} places", places.len())),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("geocode failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { search } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/geocode';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  async onEvents(batch: Event[]): Promise<Submission[]> {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.places/lookup') continue;
      try {
        const places = await search({ text: 'Lyon', near: undefined, limit: 5, language: 'fr' });
        log('info', `${places.length} places`);
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `geocode failed: ${String(error)}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Show the provider attribution that the host supplies next to results, as the provider terms require.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `not-permitted` | Let the user type coordinates instead. |
| User refused the one-time consent | `not-permitted` | Do not ask again in a loop. |
| More than 1 request per second | `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms` | Wait for the delay. |
| Provider unreachable | `network` | Retry later. |
| Provider slower than 10 s | `timed-out` | Retry later. |
| `limit` above 8 | clamped to 8 | Nothing. |

Results are cached for 24 hours by query text, so repeating a search is free.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states that place names are sent to a lookup service.

# Capability: inference.embed

## inference.embed

The `inference.embed` capability lets a plugin turn text into embedding vectors and keep a small vector index inside the host. The host runs the embeddings through the selected inference provider and holds the exact cosine search, so the plugin does no maths. The index is persisted in the plugin's data scope.

**You will need:**

- An `inference.embed` grant. No argument.
- A selected inference provider that offers embeddings; otherwise the calls return `unsupported`.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="Texts become vectors, vectors go into a host-held index and queries return the closest ids">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls vector.embed(texts, purpose)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">at most 256 texts of 8 KiB</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host asks the selected inference provider</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">unsupported when it has no embeddings</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin upserts vectors and queries top-k</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">cosine, k at most 100</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">vectors, then (id, score) list</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">unsupported, quota-exceeded</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The index lives in the host, so a query does not copy the vectors into the plugin.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `inference.embed` | yes | the only form |
| `inference.embed:local` | no | the provider is the user's choice |
| `inference` | separate | completions and model lists |

Normal risk. The text goes to the provider the user selected, as with [inference](/pages/capability-inference/).

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `vector.embed` | function | `embed(texts, purpose) -> result<request-id, plugin-error>`; pick up with `take-vectors`. |
| `vector.create-index` | function | `create-index(name, dimensions) -> result<index-id, plugin-error>`. |
| `vector.upsert`, `remove-entries` | functions | Add or replace `(id, vector)` pairs; remove ids. |
| `vector.top-k` | function | `top-k(index, query, k) -> result<list<tuple<string, f32>>, plugin-error>`; `k` at most 100. |
| `vector.drop-index` | function | Delete an index. |

See [Inference](/pages/api-inference/) and the entry limits in [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.semsearch",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "inference.embed",
      "fs.write:data"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin embeds two notes, stores them in an index and asks for the closest note to a query.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::vector;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct SemSearch;

impl Handler for SemSearch {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.semsearch/demo" { continue; }
            let result = (|| -> Result<Vec<(String, f32)>, PluginError> {
                let notes = vec!["buy milk".to_string(), "plan the release".to_string()];
                let vectors = vector::embed(&notes, "notes").block_on()?;
                let index = vector::create_index("notes", vectors[0].len() as u16)?;
                let entries = notes.iter().cloned().zip(vectors.into_iter()).collect();
                vector::upsert(index, entries)?;
                let query = vector::embed(&["release plan".to_string()], "query").block_on()?;
                vector::top_k(index, &query[0], 1)
            })();
            match result {
                Ok(hits) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("closest: {:?}", hits)),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("vector failed: {error:?}")),
            }
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { embed, createIndex, upsert, topK } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/vector';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  async onEvents(batch: Event[]): Promise<Submission[]> {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.semsearch/demo') continue;
      try {
        const notes = ['buy milk', 'plan the release'];
        const vectors = await embed(notes, 'notes');
        const index = createIndex('notes', vectors[0].length);
        upsert(index, notes.map((id, i) => [id, vectors[i]] as [string, number[]]));
        const [query] = await embed(['release plan'], 'query');
        log('info', `closest: ${JSON.stringify(topK(index, query, 1))}`);
      } catch (error) {
        log('warn', `vector failed: ${String(error)}`);
      }
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Use the same model and dimension for the index and the queries. Changing the provider changes the vectors, so rebuild the index after the user switches models.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `not-permitted` | Fall back to keyword search. |
| Provider without embeddings | `unsupported` | Tell the user which provider to select. |
| More than 256 texts or a text above 8 KiB | `invalid-argument` | Split the batch. |
| Wrong vector dimension for the index | `invalid-argument` | Create a new index. |
| Index over the entry limit | `quota-exceeded` | Remove old entries. |
| Provider unreachable | `network` | Retry later. |

Index files count against the plugin storage quota.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states that text is sent to the selected inference provider.

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Computes text embeddings <span class="t-dim">……………………………………………………………………………</span> inference.embed │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests inference.embed, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>
