# Capability: notify.toast

## notify.toast

The `notify.toast` capability lets a plugin show a short in-app notice in the client, called a toast, with a tone, a title, an optional body and up to two action buttons. A toast stays inside Ilium and disappears by itself, unlike a desktop notice from [notify.desktop](/pages/capability-notify-desktop/). A plugin can replace a toast by reusing its `id` and remove it with `dismiss-toast`.

**You will need:**

- A `notify.toast` grant. No argument.
- Commands for the action buttons, if any (declared in `contributes.commands`).

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A toast intent is rate limited, shown with a countdown and removed by timeout, action or dismiss">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin submits toast(id, tone, title, body, actions)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">title at most 60 characters</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host checks the grant and the rate</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">3 per 10 s per plugin</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Client shows the toast with a countdown bar</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">an action runs its command</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">ok</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">refused(rate-limited, invalid-argument)</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>A toast with an id that is already shown replaces that toast.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `notify.toast` | yes | the only form |
| `notify.toast:danger` | no | no argument; the tone is a field |
| `notify.desktop` | separate | desktop notices |

Normal risk. Toasts have fixed size limits, at most two actions, and a rate limit of 3 per 10 s per plugin, so a plugin cannot flood the screen.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `toast` | intent | `id?`, `tone`, `title` (at most 60), `body?` (at most 200 characters), `actions` (at most 2; `{ label, command }`), `duration-ms?` (1,000 to 30,000). |
| `dismiss-toast` | intent | `id`. Outcome `ok`. |

The default duration is 5,000 ms, and a `danger` toast stays until dismissed. See [Notifications](/pages/api-notifications/) and [Intents](/pages/api-intents/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.exporter",
  "capabilities": {
    "client": [
      "notify.toast"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin shows a success toast with one action button when the command `com.example.exporter/done` runs.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{ToastAction, ToastSpec};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::{RichText, Tone};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Exporter;

impl Handler for Exporter {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.exporter/done" { continue; }
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::Toast(ToastSpec {
                id: Some("export-done".into()),
                tone: Tone::Success,
                title: "Export finished".into(),
                body: Some(RichText::plain("12 notes written.")),
                actions: vec![ToastAction { label: "Open".into(), command: "com.example.exporter/open".into() }],
                duration_ms: None,
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { richText } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.exporter/done') continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'toast',
          val: {
            id: 'export-done',
            tone: 'success',
            title: 'Export finished',
            body: richText('12 notes written.'),
            actions: [{ label: 'Open', command: 'com.example.exporter/open' }],
            durationMs: undefined,
          },
        },
        correlation: 1n,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

The toast uses the client's real toast stack, with a countdown bar drawn with `━` and `─`.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing or declined | `refused(not-permitted)` | Use the plugin's own panel. |
| More than 3 toasts in 10 s | `refused(rate-limited)` | Merge messages or reuse the same `id`. |
| Title above 60 or body above 200 characters | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Shorten the text. |
| More than 2 actions | `refused(invalid-argument)` | Keep two. |
| Action command not declared | `refused(not-found)` | Declare it in the manifest. |
| No client attached | `ok`; the toast is shown when a client attaches only if its duration allows | Use desktop notices for important news. |

Toast text goes through the same rich text rules as other labels. Reduced motion shows no animation.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states that the plugin shows notices inside Ilium.

<figure>

<pre class="term">╭─<span class="t-hi"> Review permissions </span>───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ com.example.exporter 0.1.0 by Example Ltd                                  │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-hi">Client side</span>                                                                │
│ [x] Shows short notices inside Ilium <span class="t-dim">………………………………………………………………</span> notify.toast │
│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

# Capability: journal.read

## journal.read

The pane journal records what happened to a pane: plugin entries written with `journal.log-event` and host entries such as `pane-created`, `pane-exited` and `input-sent` (with the dedup key and the delivery result). A plugin always reads its own entries. The `journal.read` capability extends reading to the host entries and to the entries of other plugins. Entries survive restarts and are trimmed oldest first.

**You will need:**

- A `journal.read` grant. No argument.
- Optional: `journal: true` on `send-input`, which writes an entry before the PTY write.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="Journal reads return own entries always and host and foreign entries when the grant is held">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin calls journal.read(pane, since, limit)</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">own entries need no grant</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host adds host and foreign entries when granted</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">ordered by time</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin receives journal-entry records</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">source tells who wrote it</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">list of journal-entry</text>

  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">not-permitted for foreign sources</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Without the grant the result holds only the plugin's own entries.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `journal.read` | yes | the only form |
| `journal.write` | no | does not exist; writing own entries is always granted |
| `journal.read:pane` | no | no argument |

Normal risk. Journal entries record events and delivery results, not screen contents. Payloads are at most 4 KiB.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `journal.read` | function | `read(pane?, since, limit) -> list<journal-entry>`; with the grant the list includes host entries and other plugins' entries. |
| `journal-entry` | record | `{ at, pane?, source, kind, payload-json }`. |
| `journal.log-event` | function | Always granted: `log-event(pane?, kind, payload-json)`; payload at most 4 KiB. |

See [Clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/) and [Storage](/pages/api-storage/).

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (server or client).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.audit",
  "capabilities": {
    "server": [
      "journal.read"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This plugin reads the last 50 journal entries of a pane from the last hour and counts the host entries of kind `input-sent`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::Event;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::{Intent, Submission};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, journal};

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Audit;

impl Handler for Audit {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        for event in batch {
            let Event::CommandInvoked(invoked) = event else { continue };
            if invoked.command != "com.example.audit/count" { continue; }
            let since = clock::now_unix_millis() - 3_600_000;
            let entries = journal::read(invoked.pane, since, 50);
            let sent = entries.iter().filter(|entry| entry.kind == "input-sent").count();
            log::log(Level::Info, &format!("{sent} inputs sent in the last hour"));
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { read } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/journal';
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'command-invoked' || event.val.command !== 'com.example.audit/count') continue;
      const entries = read(event.val.pane, nowUnixMillis() - 3_600_000n, 50);
      const sent = entries.filter((entry) => entry.kind === 'input-sent').length;
      log('info', `${sent} inputs sent in the last hour`);
    }
    return [];
  },
});
```

Entries from other sources can be absent when the grant is missing; the call does not fail, it returns fewer entries.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Grant missing | only own entries are returned | Do not treat an empty result as proof that nothing happened. |
| `limit` above the cap | clamped | Page with `since`. |
| Payload above 4 KiB when logging | `invalid-argument` | Store a reference instead. |
| Pane closed | entries remain until trimmed | Nothing. |
| Journal full | oldest entries trimmed | Nothing. |
| Grant revoked later | `revoked` | Stop reading foreign entries. |

Journal entries are part of the session snapshot, so they survive a restart of the server.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The line states that the plugin reads pane history records.

│ <span class="t-hi">Server side</span>                                                                │

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests journal.read, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>

Listing the grants of an installed plugin from the terminal:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin grants com.example.audit
<span class="t-dim">Grant                             Risk     State</span>

# Capability: gpu.kernels

## gpu.kernels

The `gpu.kernels` capability lets an animation scene run the host's own image kernels on pixel data: blur, threshold, palette map, ordered dither and scale. A plugin never ships shader code (decision D18). Without a GPU every kernel runs on the CPU with the same result. The capability is unstable: it is marked `@unstable(feature = gpu-kernels)` and appears only in development builds.

**You will need:**

- A development build of Ilium with the `gpu-kernels` feature.
- A scene-side component (world `ilium:anim/base`).
- A `gpu.kernels` grant on the `scene` side.

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 252" role="img" aria-label="A scene sends pixels to a host kernel and receives processed pixels">
  <defs><marker id="arr" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="7" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
  <rect x="20" y="8" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="210" y="27" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Scene calls gpu.available()</text>
  <text x="210" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">tells whether a GPU is used</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="52" x2="210" y2="72" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="72" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="210" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Scene calls gpu.run(kernel, pixels, width, height, params)</text>
  <text x="210" y="107" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">host kernels only</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="116" x2="210" y2="136" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="136" width="380" height="44" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="210" y="155" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Host returns the processed pixels</text>
  <text x="210" y="171" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">CPU fallback gives the same result</text>
  <line x1="210" y1="180" x2="210" y2="200" stroke="currentColor" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="20" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">pixel bytes</text>
  <rect x="220" y="200" width="180" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="310" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">unsupported in release builds</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Only kernels from the host list run. The scene passes parameters as JSON.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Grant syntax

| Grant | Valid | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `gpu.kernels` | yes | the only form, development builds only |
| `gpu.kernels:blur` | no | no argument |
| `device.gpu` | no | a name that never existed; see the animation migration notes |

Normal risk, unstable. In release builds the grant is unknown and the manifest is refused with `manifest.grant-unknown`.

### What it unlocks

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `gpu.run` | function | `run(kernel, input, width, height, params-json) -> result<list<u8>, plugin-error>`. |
| `gpu.available` | function | `available() -> bool`. |
| `gpu-kernel` | enum | `blur`, `threshold`, `palette-map`, `dither-ordered`, `scale`. |

See [Scenes](/pages/api-scenes/). Colour and dithering stay global in the shared look: a scene does not add its own palette controls.

### Manifest

The grant goes into `manifest.json` under `capabilities`, in the list of the side that uses it (scene only).

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "com.example.glowscene",
  "capabilities": {
    "scene": [
      "gpu.kernels"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Worked example

This scene blurs a frame buffer with a radius of 2 cells.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::gpu::{self, GpuKernel};

fn blur_frame(pixels: &[u8], width: u32, height: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    if !gpu::available() { log::log(Level::Debug, "gpu: cpu fallback"); }
    gpu::run(GpuKernel::Blur, pixels, width, height, r#"{"radius":2}"#)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| pixels.to_vec())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { run, available } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/gpu';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export function blurFrame(pixels: Uint8Array, width: number, height: number): Uint8Array {
  if (!available()) log('debug', 'gpu: cpu fallback');
  try {
    return run('blur', pixels, width, height, '{"radius":2}');
  } catch {
    return pixels;
  }
}
```

Call the helper from the scene's frame function. Keep the original buffer: a failed kernel must not blank the animation.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Outcome | What the plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Release build | grant unknown, manifest refused | Gate the feature behind a development build. |
| Grant declined | `not-permitted` | Draw without the effect. |
| Unknown kernel name | `invalid-argument` | Use the enum. |
| Pixel buffer size mismatch | `invalid-argument` | Match width, height and format. |
| Buffer too large | `quota-exceeded` | Process tiles. |
| No GPU | CPU fallback with the same result | Nothing. |

Because the feature is unstable, kernels and parameters may change between development builds.

### What the user sees

The review dialog lists the grant when a package is installed or first activated. The grant appears only in development builds.

│ <span class="t-hi">Scene side</span>                                                                 │

│                                                                            │
│ <span class="t-dim">Space toggle · Enter allow · Esc decline</span>                                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>

<figcaption>The review dialog for a package that requests gpu.kernels, drawn with the client's dialog characters: rounded corners, dotted leaders and the hint bar.</figcaption>
</figure>

# Capability: settings.write-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>

## settings.write-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>

The `settings.write-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>` capability lets one first-party plugin write the values of one built-in Settings tab, for example the Terminal tab. It is how a core plugin such as the settings owner of that tab keeps the tab editable after the tab moved out of the kernel. It is high risk, T1 only, and always needs an explicit grant.

**You will need:**

- A `settings.write-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>` grant with exactly one tab id from the settings reference. A wildcard is refused with `manifest.grant-argument`.
- A first-party (T1) package. A T2 or T3 package that declares the grant is refused with `manifest.grant-tier`.
- To be the only installed plugin that holds the grant for that tab. A second holder is refused with `manifest.settings-owner`.

### Rules

- The host MUST accept `kernel-settings.write` for tab `T` only from the plugin that holds `settings.write-kernel:T`.
- A write without the grant, or after the user revoked it, MUST fail with `not-permitted`.
- A write to an unknown tab or key MUST fail with `not-found` and change nothing.
- A value that fails the tab schema MUST fail with `invalid-argument` and change nothing. A write is all or nothing.
- A successful write MUST be persisted before the call returns and MUST produce one `kernel-settings-changed` event naming the tab and the changed keys.
- Keybindings are not part of any kernel tab. No grant writes a binding.
- A secret key MUST NOT be written through this call. The owner uses the secrets import.

### Errors

| Call | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `kernel-settings.write` | `not-permitted` | no grant for that tab, or revoked |
| `kernel-settings.write` | `not-found` | unknown tab or key |
| `kernel-settings.write` | `invalid-argument` | value fails the tab schema |
| manifest | `manifest.grant-argument` | wildcard or missing tab id |
| manifest | `manifest.grant-tier` | package is not T1 |
| manifest | `manifest.settings-owner` | another plugin already owns the tab |

See [Kernel settings and keymap](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/) for the host interface and [settings.read-kernel](/pages/capability-settings-read-kernel/) for the read side.

# Providing the docs to agents

## Providing the docs to agents

A coding agent that builds an Ilium plugin needs two things: the contract (this manual) and a short set of project rules. This chapter covers how the manual reaches an agent, which instruction file each tool reads, and how the files stay in step with the contract. The site serves the manual for machines as well as for people. It publishes an `llms.txt` index, one `llms-full.txt` file with every page, a plain Markdown copy of each page, and a kit of ready-made instruction files under `/agent-kit/`.

## You will need

- A plugin project, or the wish to create one with `ilium plugin new`. See [Set up a toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/).
- The address of this manual. The examples use `http://127.0.0.1:4327`, the address the build records in `_config.yml`. Replace it with the address where you read this page.
- Any coding agent. The kit covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and any tool that reads `AGENTS.md`.

## How an agent finds the docs

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 190" role="img" aria-label="An agent reads a project instruction file, which points to llms.txt, which links to Markdown pages">
  <rect x="8" y="20" width="110" height="56" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="63" y="44" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Plugin project</text>
  <text x="63" y="62" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">AGENTS.md</text>
  <rect x="205" y="20" width="110" height="56" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="260" y="44" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">Docs site</text>
  <text x="260" y="62" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">/llms.txt</text>
  <rect x="402" y="20" width="110" height="56" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="457" y="44" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">One page</text>
  <text x="457" y="62" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">/pages/x.md</text>
  <line x1="118" y1="48" x2="205" y2="48" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <line x1="315" y1="48" x2="402" y2="48" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="161" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">URL</text>
  <text x="358" y="40" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">link</text>
  <rect x="205" y="120" width="110" height="46" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <text x="260" y="140" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">/llms-full.txt</text>
  <text x="260" y="156" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="10">every page</text>
  <line x1="260" y1="76" x2="260" y2="120" stroke="currentColor" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
</svg>
<figcaption>The project file holds the address. The index links each page as Markdown. The full file is the one-request alternative.</figcaption>
</figure>

The loop has three steps. The agent starts a session and loads the instruction file of the project automatically. The file names the index URL. When the agent needs a fact, it fetches `llms.txt`, picks a page, and fetches that page as Markdown. An agent that can hold a large context may fetch `llms-full.txt` once instead.

## Which file for which tool

| Tool | File and location | Read automatically |
|---|---|---|
| Codex, Jules, Gemini CLI, Zed, Warp, Devin, Amp and others | `AGENTS.md` at the repository root; the nearest file up the tree wins | Yes (agents.md lists the tools; Gemini CLI and Aider need a setting) |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` in the project or a parent folder; imports with `@path` | Yes. It reads `AGENTS.md` only when no `CLAUDE.md` exists, so a thin `CLAUDE.md` imports it |
| Claude Code skills | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | The name and description load at start; the body loads when the skill applies |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` with `description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply` front matter; also reads `AGENTS.md` | Yes, by rule type |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md`; path rules in `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`; also reads `AGENTS.md` | Yes |
| Any tool with a fetch or browse tool | `llms.txt` | No. The project file must give the URL |

The sources are the pages at agents.md, code.claude.com (memory and skills), cursor.com (rules), docs.github.com (Copilot repository instructions) and llmstxt.org. The details are on [the project files page](/pages/agent-docs-project-files/).

<div class="note">
<p>An instruction file is context, not enforcement. The host enforces grants, limits and deadlines whatever an agent writes. The file helps an agent get it right the first time.</p>
</div>

## In this chapter

- [llms.txt and Markdown pages](/pages/agent-docs-llms-txt/): how this site publishes the index, the full file and the per-page Markdown.
- [Project instruction files](/pages/agent-docs-project-files/): the AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor and Copilot templates.
- [The Ilium plugin skill](/pages/agent-docs-skill/): an Agent Skill for Claude Code.
- [Keeping the kit current](/pages/agent-docs-maintenance/): what is generated, what is maintained by hand, and the release checklist.

# llms.txt and Markdown pages

## llms.txt and Markdown pages

The llms.txt proposal (llmstxt.org) gives a site a Markdown file at a known address that an agent reads to find the pages worth fetching. This site follows it. The build writes `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, a `.md` copy of every page, and the folder `/agent-kit/`, all from the page sources. Nobody edits those outputs by hand.

## You will need

- The built site, or the running copy. The files are static and need no server feature.
- For adding a page: the page conventions in the manual folder (`CONVENTIONS.md`) and an entry in `_data/nav.yml`.

## The standard

The llmstxt.org format is a Markdown file in this order. The H1 with the site name is the only required part.

| Part | Rule |
|---|---|
| H1 | The project or site name. Required. |
| Blockquote | A short summary with the context needed to read the rest. Optional. |
| Free text | Paragraphs or lists without headings. Optional. |
| H2 sections | Each holds a list of `[name](url)` links, each optionally followed by `: notes`. Optional. |
| H2 named `Optional` | Secondary links an agent can skip when it needs a shorter context. |

The file lives at the site root, or at a subpath that it covers; the most specific file wins. A page can also be served as Markdown at the same address with `.md` appended or substituted. `llms-full.txt` is a common extension, not part of the proposal: the whole documentation in one file.

## What this site publishes

| Address | Content | Made by |
|---|---|---|
| `/llms.txt` | The index: H1, summary, one H2 per navigation group, one link per page with a description | `write_llms_files` in the build |
| `/llms-full.txt` | Every page body in navigation order, each after a `<!-- source: URL -->` line | the same function |
| `/pages/<slug>.md` | The page body as Markdown under an H1 title, for every page | the build, one per page |
| `/agent-kit/` | The files in `_agent-kit/`, copied unchanged | the build |

This is the start of the real index, as the build produced it:

<pre class="term"># Ilium Plugin Developer Manual

&gt; Developer manual for Ilium plugins: WebAssembly components (wasm32-wasip2)
&gt; written in Rust or TypeScript that add tree decorations, commands, ...

Every page below is also served as plain Markdown at the same address with
`.md` instead of the trailing slash. `llms-full.txt` holds the whole manual
in one file. Ready-made agent instruction files for plugin projects are
under `agent-kit/`.

## Start here

- [Plugin manual](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/landing.md): A plugin adds
  features to Ilium. It can decorate tree rows with badges, add commands ...
- [What a plugin is](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/getting-started-overview.md):
  Ilium splits its work into two parts. The kernel ...
</pre>

The excerpt is wrapped and shortened for this page; in the file each link entry is one line. The link host comes from `url` in `_config.yml`. The index follows the standard: H1, blockquote, a free-text paragraph, then H2 sections of links. The H2 names are the navigation groups, so the order of the index is the order of the navigation.

## Add a page so it appears

1. Create `pages/<slug>.md` with `layout`, `title` and `permalink` front matter.
2. Add an entry with the page title and permalink to `_data/nav.yml`. A page that is not in the navigation is not in the index.
3. Choose the slug prefix of its group (`api-`, `capability-`, `widgets-`, `agent-docs` and so on). The build groups pages by prefix.
4. Make the first body paragraph a plain sentence. The index description is the first prose paragraph, shortened to 220 characters; it skips headings, tables, lists, quotes and HTML.
5. Run `bash build.sh` and check the `result` line. Then open `/llms.txt` and find the page.

## Point an agent at the manual

Put the index address in the instruction file of the plugin project; the kit templates already do. For a one-off session, give the agent the address in the prompt.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4327/llms.txt | head -3
# Ilium Plugin Developer Manual

&gt; Developer manual for Ilium plugins: WebAssembly components (wasm32-wasip2)
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/events-and-intents.md | head -3
# Events and intents

## Events and intents
</pre>

<div class="note">
<p>The twin is the page body without front matter, with the page title added as an H1. Raw HTML blocks such as diagrams and terminal captures stay in the text.</p>
</div>

# Project instruction files

## Project instruction files

Each coding agent reads one or two files from the repository without being asked. The kit holds a version of those files for an Ilium plugin project. This page shows what each tool reads, what is in the kit, how to install it and how to keep it current.

## You will need

- A plugin project from `ilium plugin new`. See [Set up a toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/).
- The kit at `/agent-kit/` on this site, or the folder `_agent-kit/` in the manual sources. The [kit README](/agent-kit/README.md) lists every file.

## What each tool reads

| Tool | File | Facts that matter |
|---|---|---|
| AGENTS.md tools | `AGENTS.md` at the root | Plain Markdown, no required headings. The nearest file up the tree wins, and a prompt from the user overrides it. Monorepos may add nested files. |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` in the working folder or a parent | Target under 200 lines. `@path` imports are expanded at launch, up to four hops deep, relative to the importing file. With only an `AGENTS.md` and no `CLAUDE.md`, Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md`; once a `CLAUDE.md` exists it reads that file only, so the kit file imports `@AGENTS.md`. |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | Front matter `description`, `globs` and `alwaysApply`. A plain `.md` file in that folder is ignored. Cursor also reads `AGENTS.md` in the root and nested folders. |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Repository-wide. Path rules go in `.github/instructions/NAME.instructions.md` with `applyTo`. Copilot also reads `AGENTS.md`. |

## What the kit contains

| Kit file | Content |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | The full rules: documentation URLs, toolchain, the `ilium plugin` commands, eight contract rules, Rust and TypeScript idioms, testing, and a list of things never to do. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | An import of `@AGENTS.md` and two Claude-specific lines. |
| `.cursor/rules/ilium-plugin.mdc` | A short rule that attaches to `manifest.json`, Rust and TypeScript sources. |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | A short summary that points at `AGENTS.md`. |

The long rules live in one place, `AGENTS.md`. The tool files repeat only the essentials, so a change has few places to land.

## Install

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4327/agent-kit
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -fsSO $BASE/AGENTS.md -O $BASE/CLAUDE.md
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> mkdir -p .cursor/rules .github
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -fs $BASE/.cursor/rules/ilium-plugin.mdc \
    -o .cursor/rules/ilium-plugin.mdc
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -fs $BASE/.github/copilot-instructions.md \
    -o .github/copilot-instructions.md
</pre>

Then replace the host `http://127.0.0.1:4327` in each file with the address of the manual you use, and commit the files. The skill has its own install step on [the skill page](/pages/agent-docs-skill/).

## Excerpt: what the agent is told

This is the core of the kit `AGENTS.md`, the part that matters most for a first change.

**Rust**

```rust
// Rule 1: events in, intents out. Return quickly; never block.
fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
    batch.into_iter().filter_map(|event| self.handle(event)).collect()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// Rule 1: events in, intents out. Return quickly; never block.
onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  return batch.flatMap((event) => this.handle(event));
}
```

The bodies of `handle` depend on the plugin; the tutorials show complete ones. See [Events and intents](/pages/events-and-intents/).

## Keep the files in step with the contract

Every kit file starts with a stamp. In Markdown it is an HTML comment; in the Cursor rule and the skill it is a comment after the front matter.

```text
contract: 0.1
generated-with: manual
```

`contract` is the version of the plugin contract the facts were checked against. `generated-with: manual` marks a file that people maintain. When the contract changes, compare the stamp of the installed files with the stamp on the site, and fetch the files again if they differ. The release checklist is on [Keeping the kit current](/pages/agent-docs-maintenance/).

# The Ilium plugin skill

## The Ilium plugin skill

An Agent Skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file that Claude Code loads on demand. The kit holds a skill, `ilium-plugin-sdk`, that carries the plugin workflow without filling the context of every session. This page shows its layout, front matter and content, and how to install it.

## You will need

- Claude Code. Skills in this layout are read from `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in a project, from `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for all projects of one user, and from a nested `.claude/skills` folder for a subfolder.
- The kit folder `skills/ilium-plugin/` from `/agent-kit/`.

## Layout

## The front matter

```yaml
---
name: ilium-plugin-sdk
description: Build, change, test and package Ilium plugins (WebAssembly components in Rust or TypeScript). Use when the project has an Ilium manifest.json, when the user asks for an Ilium plugin, ...
---
```

`name` defaults to the folder name and sets the slash command. `description` is what Claude reads to decide whether to load the skill, so it says what the skill does and when to use it; the first 1,536 characters of the description are kept. Other fields, such as `allowed-tools`, are optional and the kit does not use them. Claude Code ignores field names it does not know, so spelling mistakes fail silently.

## What the skill contains

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Find the facts first | Fetch `llms.txt`, then only the pages for the task as Markdown; say so when the manual lacks a fact. |
| Workflow | Seven steps from `ilium plugin new` to `ilium plugin pack`, including the fake-host test. |
| Both languages | The Rust and TypeScript names to use in every answer. |
| Hard rules | Never block, smallest grants, handle every outcome, no invented glyphs. |
| `reference.md` | Package layout, sides and worlds, deadlines and limits, error codes, test harness table. |

## Install

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4327/agent-kit/skills/ilium-plugin
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> mkdir -p .claude/skills/ilium-plugin

<span class="t-prompt">$</span> curl -fs $BASE/reference.md -o .claude/skills/ilium-plugin/reference.md
</pre>

Commit the folder to share it with the team. Use `~/.claude/skills/ilium-plugin/` instead to have it in every project.

# Keeping the kit current

## Keeping the kit current

An agent file that states an old fact does more harm than none. This page separates what the build generates from what people maintain, and gives the checklist to run for every release of the manual or the plugin contract.

## You will need

- The manual sources and the command `bash build.sh` in the manual folder.
- The version of the plugin contract being released.

## Generated and maintained

| Item | Origin | Action on release |
|---|---|---|
| `/llms.txt` | generated from page front matter, navigation and first paragraphs | rebuild |
| `/llms-full.txt` | generated from page bodies | rebuild |
| `/pages/<slug>.md` | generated, one per page | rebuild |
| `/agent-kit/` | copied unchanged from `_agent-kit/` | edit the sources, rebuild |
| Files in `_agent-kit/` | written by hand, stamped `generated-with: manual` | review against the contract |
| Page text and navigation | written by hand | update with the change |

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 120" role="img" aria-label="Pages and agent kit sources go through build.sh into llms files and the agent-kit folder">
  <rect x="8" y="20" width="120" height="36" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="68" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">pages/*.md, nav</text>
  <rect x="8" y="68" width="120" height="36" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="68" y="91" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">_agent-kit/</text>
  <rect x="200" y="40" width="110" height="40" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="255" y="64" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="12">bash build.sh</text>
  <rect x="380" y="10" width="132" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="446" y="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">llms.txt, llms-full.txt</text>
  <rect x="380" y="45" width="132" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="446" y="65" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">pages/*.md twins</text>
  <rect x="380" y="80" width="132" height="30" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="446" y="100" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-size="11">agent-kit/</text>
  <line x1="128" y1="38" x2="200" y2="55" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <line x1="128" y1="86" x2="200" y2="68" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <line x1="310" y1="60" x2="380" y2="25" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <line x1="310" y1="60" x2="380" y2="60" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <line x1="310" y1="60" x2="380" y2="95" stroke="currentColor"/>

<figcaption>Sources on the left are edited. Everything on the right is output and is never edited.</figcaption>

## Release checklist

1. Update the pages that the change touches, and add new pages to `_data/nav.yml`.
2. Update the kit files under `_agent-kit/`. Check each fact against [the manual pages](/pages/landing/): command names and flags ([Set up a toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/)), deadlines and limits ([Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/)), SDK names ([Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/), [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/)), manifest keys ([Manifest keys](/pages/reference-manifest/)).
3. Set the `contract:` stamp in every kit file to the released contract version. Search for stale stamps:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> rg -L "contract: 0.1" _agent-kit
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> rg -n "contract:" _agent-kit
</pre>

   The first command lists files that lack the current stamp. Every file must carry one.
4. Run the build and read the `result` line. The command exits with a non-zero status on any error.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> bash build.sh
</pre>

5. Check the outputs: `llms.txt` lists every new page, `llms-full.txt` ends with the last page, `agent-kit/` holds all files.
6. Check links. Every `/pages/<slug>/` target in the new pages must have a source file `pages/<slug>.md`, and every `.md` address in `llms.txt` must exist under `_site/pages/`.
7. Check the host in the kit files. The files carry the address `http://127.0.0.1:4327`; for a published manual replace it with the public address.
8. Install the kit in a scratch plugin project and ask an agent to add a command. Confirm that it fetches the index and uses the right commands.

## Version stamps

The stamp `contract: 0.1` says the facts were checked against contract 0.1. The manifest `api` key of a package names the exact WIT package version, see [Versioning](/pages/versioning/). Keep both in step: when the manifest version a template generates changes, update the stamps in the same commit.

## See also

- [llms.txt and Markdown pages](/pages/agent-docs-llms-txt/)
- [Project instruction files](/pages/agent-docs-project-files/)

# Capability table

## Capability table

A capability is a permission that unlocks one group of host functions or events. Every import a plugin can call, and every event it can receive, belongs to exactly one capability. The plugin lists the capabilities it needs in the `capabilities` object of its manifest, with one list per side. At install time the user grants them. First-party bundled (T1) plugins receive every capability up to the manifest ceiling automatically, except the high-risk ones marked H, which always need an explicit grant.

A declined capability does not stop the plugin. Its imports return `not-permitted`, its events are never sent, and the plugin keeps running. A call to a function whose grant the manifest never requested for that side is different: it is a trap `host.capability-not-requested`, which counts as a plugin failure.

### You will need

- A manifest with a `capabilities` object. Its keys are `server`, `client` and `scene`, and each value is a list of grant strings. The full manifest layout is in the [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/).
- For Rust: stable Rust 1.90 or later with the `wasm32-wasip2` target, and the crate `ilium-plugin-sdk`. For TypeScript: Bun 1.2 or later and the package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both SDKs pin their binding generators, so nothing is installed globally.
- A working scaffold. The [first plugin guide](/pages/getting-started-first-plugin/) builds one step by step.

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "server": ["fs.read:project", "http:api.example.com"],
    "client": ["ui.panels"]
  }
}
```

The example omits the other manifest keys. Grants are per side, so a `server` grant never applies to `client`.

## Grant syntax

A grant is a name, optionally followed by a colon and an argument. The first colon separates the name from the argument, and later colons belong to the argument. So `services.use:ilium:inference/provider` has the name `services.use` and the argument `ilium:inference/provider`.

| Argument form | Grant | Example | Rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact global command id | `commands.invoke:<pattern>` | `commands.invoke:ilium.git/status` | `*/status` |
| All commands of one plugin | `commands.invoke:<plugin-id>/*` | `commands.invoke:ilium.git/*` | `ilium.git/prefix*` |
| Exact host, or any subdomain | `http:<host-pattern>` | `http:api.example.com`, `http:*.openstreetmap.org` | a bare `*`, a path |
| Loopback host with a port, plain HTTP allowed (H) | `http:localhost:<port>`, `http:127.0.0.1:<port>` | `http:localhost:8080` | `http:localhost` without a port (`manifest.grant-argument`) |
| Program name or absolute path | `process.run:<program>` | `process.run:git` | any wildcard, whitespace, an empty value, a relative path with `/`, or `..` (`manifest.grant-program`) |
| Program name or absolute path, same validation as `process.run` (H) | `panes.create-command:<program>` | `panes.create-command:htop` | the same values as `process.run` (`manifest.grant-program`) |
| Exact topic, prefix or all topics (H) | `topics.subscribe:<pattern>` | `topics.subscribe:ilium.progress/*` | `*` in another position |
| Exact peer plugin id | `messages.peer:<plugin-id>` | `messages.peer:com.example.logger` | any wildcard |
| Service name without version | `services.use:<name>` | `services.use:com.example.git/status` | a version suffix |
| Route path with `{name}` segments | `http-api.route:<path>` | `http-api.route:/notes/{id}` | `*` |

A wildcard in a position that the table does not allow is refused at install. A `*` never crosses a `/` in a command id, except the bare `*`, which means every command.

### File scopes

The `fs` grants take a scope argument. Each scope has a fixed preopen name in the plugin's file view and a root on disk.

| Scope | Preopen | Root | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package` | `/package` | the unpacked package `assets/` folder | always, read only |
| `data` | `/data` | the plugin's private data folder | always, read and write |
| `cache` | `/cache` | the plugin's private cache folder, evictable | always, read and write |
| `project` | `/project` | the session's canonical project folder | grant |
| `worktrees` | `/worktrees` | the workspace worktree root | grant, H for write |
| `picked` | `/picked/<n>` | each path the user chose in `fs.pick` | grant per pick |
| `agent-sessions:<agent>` | `/agent-sessions/<agent>` | the agent's transcript folder, read only | grant, H, read and watch only |
| `agent-config:<agent>` | `/agent-config/<agent>` | the agent's configuration folder, read only | grant, H, read only |
| `minecraft-saves` | `/minecraft-saves` | the Minecraft saves folder | grant |
| `path:<template>` | `/paths/<n>` | a template with `{home}`, `{config}`, `{data}`, `{cache}`, `{project}` or `{worktrees}` | grant |

A `path:` template ends either with a name (that file or folder, plus the direct children of a folder) or with `/**` (the whole subtree). A literal absolute path such as `path:/srv/logs/**` is always H. A path that escapes its scope root with `..`, or through a symbolic link, is refused with `not-permitted`.

<div class="note">

Scope examples: `fs.read:project` reads the project folder. It is a normal-risk grant and starts checked. `fs.read:path:{home}/Pictures/**` reads a subtree of the user's Pictures folder.

</div>

## Always granted

These need no manifest entry and no user grant:

- `log`, `clock`, `timers`, `storage` (the plugin's own buckets), `settings` (the plugin's own values) and `codec`.
- `fs.read:package`, `fs.read:data`, `fs.write:data`, `fs.read:cache` and `fs.write:cache`, and `fs.watch:package`, `fs.watch:data` and `fs.watch:cache`. `fs.watch:<scope>` has the same risk as `fs.read:<scope>`. A watch on a scope without a grant returns `not-permitted` with the reason `not-granted`.
- The plugin's own-side `messages`, and `ui.invalidate` for the views the plugin contributes.

## Table

Sides: S is the server world, C is the client world and A is the animation (scene) world. Risk H means the capability always needs an explicit grant. The last column names what the grant unlocks.

Every grant is listed once. Capabilities with several grants share one row.

| Grant | Argument form | Sides | Risk | Page | API pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tree.read` | none | S C | normal | [page](/pages/capability-tree-read/) | [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/) |
| `tree.write` | none | S C | normal | [page](/pages/capability-tree-write/) | [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/), [api-intents](/pages/api-intents/) |
| `tree.metadata` | none | S C | normal | [page](/pages/capability-tree-metadata/) | [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/) |
| `tree.decorate` | none | S C | normal | [page](/pages/capability-tree-decorate/) | [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/) |
| `tree.restructure` | none | S C | **H** | [page](/pages/capability-tree-restructure/) | [api-tree](/pages/api-tree/), [api-intents](/pages/api-intents/) |

### Newer grants

The grants below extend the base set. Ten of them are high risk and always need an explicit grant, even for a T1 bundled plugin: `terminal.history`, `terminal.input-lock`, `terminal.raw-input`, `panes.lifecycle`, `tree.restructure`, `sessions.cross`, `process.long-lived`, `agent.transcript`, `settings.read-kernel:api` and `settings.write-kernel:<tab-id>` (T1 only). The grant `gpu.kernels` is unstable and exists only in development builds. Both `extensions.*` grants take exactly one global point id and refuse wildcards (`manifest.grant-wildcard`). `extensions.contribute` is high risk only for a point that declares `risk: "high"`; the review dialog then shows a warning. Four argument forms are less common: `http:setting:<key>` (the host comes from one of the plugin's own settings, and the user confirms a changed host before the first request), `fs.read:agent-sessions:gemini` with `fs.read:agent-config:gemini`, `fs.read:agent-config:antigravity`, and `settings.read-kernel:<kernel-tab-id>` (argument required, no wildcard).

## Who grants what

The risk tier decides how the user sees a capability.

- **Normal.** Listed in the review dialog and checked by default. A T2 or T3 package installs with the grants the user leaves checked.
- **High (H).** Listed but unchecked, so the user must tick each one. A T1 bundled plugin starts without its H capabilities. At its first activation the user sees one prompt, "Plugin <name> asks for: <list>", with the buttons `Allow selected` and `Not now`. `Not now` asks again at the next server start, at most three times, and the user can grant later from Settings > Plugins.

There is no prompt for each call. A grant is a standing permission until it is revoked. The review dialog shows one row per capability, grouped by side, with the grant string at the end of the row:

<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">╭─ Install com.example.notes 1.2.0 ──────────────────────────────────╮</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> Example Corp · signed (T2) · fingerprint 3F2A…9C01                 <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>                                                                    <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> <span class="t-hi">Server</span>                                                             <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> <span class="t-ok">[x]</span> Read the workspace tree ………………………………………………………………………… tree.read <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> <span class="t-ok">[x]</span> Read files in this project ………………………………………………… fs.read:project <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> <span class="t-dim">[ ]</span> Connect to api.example.com …………………………………… http:api.example.com <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>                                                                    <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span> Unchecked capabilities are not granted. Turn on the ones you need. <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">│</span>               [ Install ]   [ Details ]   <span class="t-hi">[ Cancel ]</span>               <span class="t-dim">│</span>
<span class="t-dim">╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</span>
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The user left the HTTP grant unchecked, so the plugin's `granted` list omits it. Focus starts on Cancel ([SEC-103]). Up and Down move, Space toggles, Enter activates and Escape cancels.

## Changing grants while the plugin runs

A grant change never restarts a plugin silently. The rules are:

- **Grant added.** An added grant bumps the authorization epoch. The plugin receives `deactivate(granted)` and is re-activated with the new set.
- **Grant revoked.** Revoke in Settings > Plugins > <plugin> > Capabilities, or with `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke <grant>`. A host call records the epoch at entry. If the epoch changes before the call returns and the change removed a grant the call needs, the call returns `revoked` (an intent completes `failed(revoked)`); otherwise it completes normally. A call that enters after the bump is checked against the new set and returns `not-permitted` with a message starting `revoked: `, until re-activation and after it. The plugin receives `deactivate(revoked)` and is re-activated with the reduced set and its restore bytes. Contributions that need the grant (decorations, grabs, claims, filters, watches, routes) are withdrawn at once.
- **Failure counting.** A grant change never counts as a plugin failure.

The activation context carries `granted: list<string>`. Each entry is the grant string exactly as the manifest spells it, such as `http:api.example.com`, so a plugin can test for it directly. Declined grants are absent from the list.

## Worked example in Rust

This server-side plugin reads a project file and calls one HTTP host. It starts the HTTP call only when the user granted that host. The example uses the manifest from the top of this page.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{fs, http, log::{self, Level}};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::Activation;

const FETCH_GRANT: &str = "http:api.example.com";

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct NotesReader;

impl Lifecycle for NotesReader {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // fs.read:project is in the manifest, so this read is granted unless declined.
        task::spawn(async {
            let path = FsPath { scope: "project".into(), path: "NOTES.md".into() };
            match fs::read_all(path).await {
                Ok(bytes) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("read {} bytes", bytes.len())),
                Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("read failed: {:?}", error.code)),
            }
        });
        // A declined grant is missing from `granted`, so the feature is skipped, not called.
        if context.granted.iter().any(|grant| grant == FETCH_GRANT) {
            task::spawn(async {
                let request = http::HttpRequest {
                    method: "GET".into(),
                    url: "https://api.example.com/v1/status".into(),
                    headers: Vec::new(),
                    body: None,
                    timeout_millis: 5_000,
                };
                match http::fetch(request).await {
                    Ok(response) => log::log(Level::Info, &format!("status {}", response.status)),
                    Err(error) => log::log(Level::Warn, &format!("fetch failed: {:?}", error.code)),
                }
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

Each `async` wrapper resolves when its `request-completed` event arrives.

## Worked example in TypeScript

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { readAll } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import { fetch as httpFetch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';

const FETCH_GRANT = 'http:api.example.com';

async function readNotes(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const bytes = await readAll({ scope: 'project', path: 'NOTES.md' });
    log('info', `read ${bytes.length} bytes`);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError) log('warn', `read failed: ${error.code}`);
  }
}

async function fetchStatus(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const response = await httpFetch({
      method: 'GET',
      url: 'https://api.example.com/v1/status',
      headers: [],
      body: undefined,
      timeoutMillis: 5000,
    });
    log('info', `status ${response.status}`);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof PluginError) log('warn', `fetch failed: ${error.code}`);
  }
}

export const { lifecycle } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    void readNotes();
    if (context.granted.includes(FETCH_GRANT)) void fetchStatus();
  },
});
```

The `granted` check only saves a refused call. A call without a grant returns `not-permitted` anyway.

## Errors and edge cases

Every function that returns a result can also return `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`. The table shows what each capability situation looks like to the plugin.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Import of an interface that no requested capability on that side unlocks | The install fails with `manifest.import-not-requested`. |
| Call of a function whose grant the manifest never requested for that side (also when it is requested only for the other side) | Trap `host.capability-not-requested`, counted as a plugin failure. |
| User left the grant unchecked or declined it | `not-permitted` at once, synchronously, with a message starting `declined: `. The plugin keeps running. |
| Argument outside the grant (host, scope, program, command) | `not-permitted` at once, with the reason `not-granted` (`scope` for a path outside the granted scope). |
| `create-pane` with a command whose program matches no `panes.create-command` grant | `refused(not-permitted)` with the reason `not-granted` (`declined` when the grant was requested but unchecked). A command-less `create-pane` needs only `panes.create`. |
| Path escapes the scope with `..` or a symbolic link | `not-permitted`. |
| Redirect to a host without a grant | Completion `failed(not-permitted)`. |
| Grant revoked while a call is in flight | `revoked`. The plugin is re-activated. |
| Declined CLI subcommand | Hidden from help. `ilium <name>` fails with `unknown command`. |
| Declined HTTP API route | `404 Not Found`, the same as an unknown path. |
| Declined command invocation | `not-permitted`, and the command does not run. |

Manifest mistakes stop the install. Each one is reported as a JSONL `error` line by `ilium plugin install` and `ilium plugin build`:

| Code | Text |
|---|---|
| `manifest.grant-unknown` | `capability "<grant>" is not known to plugin API <api>`. Also used for a reserved grant (`editor.provide`), an alias (the message names the right grant, for example `use terminal.raw-input`) and `gpu.kernels` in a release build |
| `manifest.grant-argument` | `capability "<name>" takes no argument (got "<grant>")` |
| `manifest.grant-argument-missing` | `capability "<name>" needs an argument, for example "<name>:<example>"` |
| `manifest.grant-wildcard` | `capability "<grant>" uses a wildcard that "<name>" does not accept` |
| `manifest.grant-scope` | `file scope "<scope>" is not known or does not accept "<access>"` |
| `manifest.grant-side` | `capability "<name>" is not available on the <side> side` |
| `manifest.grant-tier` | `capability "<name>" is available to bundled plugins only` |
| `manifest.grant-dependency` | `capability "<grant>" also needs "<other>"` |
| `manifest.grant-program` | `capability "<name>" takes a program name or an absolute path (got "<value>")` |
| `manifest.import-not-requested` | `import "<interface>" is not unlocked by any capability requested on the <side> side` |
| `manifest.settings-owner` | `kernel tab "<tab>" is already owned by "<plugin>"` |
| `manifest.export-grant` | `export "<export>" needs capability "<grant>"` |

`settings.write-all` without `settings.read-all` fails with `manifest.grant-dependency`, and so does `fs.pick` without `fs.read:picked` or `fs.write:picked`.

<div class="warn">

A misspelled host such as `http:api.example.co` is valid syntax. It installs, and every call to the real host returns `not-permitted`.

</div>

## What the user sees

Each refused call is logged. The text form of a refusal is `refused <grant> by <function> (<reason>)`. The log file holds the same refusal as one JSON line, `{"type":"refusal","grant":"<grant>","function":"<function>","reason":"<reason>"}`, and `ilium plugin logs <id>` shows it in plain text. The reason is one of the closed list in [Refusal reasons](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#refusal-reasons). Writes outside `data` and `cache` are logged at info level.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs com.example.notes
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:20:33</span> <span class="t-ok">info</span> read 1842 bytes
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:20:35</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span> refused http:api.example.com by http.fetch (declined)
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 14:20:35</span> <span class="t-err">err</span>  fetch failed: not-permitted
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The plugin keeps running after the refusal. The HTTP call is skipped on the next activation because the grant is still declined.

Clipboard reads also show in the client footer as `clipboard read by <plugin name>` for 3 seconds after each read.

# Error codes and limits

## Error codes and limits

A plugin calls host functions, and some of those calls fail. A failed call returns a `plugin-error` record to the caller, and the plugin keeps running. A contract violation is different: it traps the plugin instance, which the host then ends and restarts. Resource limits bound how much CPU time, memory, storage, I/O and queue space a plugin can use. Each limit has a default. A manifest may ask for a lower value or a higher one, up to the ceiling for the plugin's tier.

Tiers decide the ceilings. T1 is first-party bundled plugins. T2 is a third-party package signed by a publisher key the user trusts. T3 is an unsigned local package, installed with `--allow-unsigned` or `ilium plugin dev` and shown with a `dev` badge. T2 and T3 share the same ceilings.

### What you need

- **Grants:** none for this page. Each call needs the grant of its own capability. A declined or revoked grant returns `not-permitted`. Storage is always granted.
- **Language:** Rust with `ilium_plugin_sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both SDKs expose the same record and codes.
- **Prerequisites:** the [Rust SDK reference](/pages/rust-sdk/) or the [TypeScript SDK reference](/pages/typescript-sdk/) for handler rules, and the [Performance guide](/pages/performance/) for how deadlines are charged.

### The plugin error record

Every fallible host function returns `result<T, plugin-error>`. The record has three fields.

| Field | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | `error.code` (`ErrorCode`) | `error.code` (string) | One of the codes in the table below |
| `message` | `error.message` (`String`) | `error.message` | Text for logs. Do not match on it |
| `retry-after-ms` | `error.retry_after_ms` (`Option<u32>`) | `error.retryAfterMs` | Set for `rate-limited`; the CPU budget case also sets it |

The SDKs map the result to `Result<T, PluginError>` in Rust and to a return value or a thrown `PluginError` in TypeScript. The WIT surface itself has only results and traps.

| Code | Meaning | Retry |
|---|---|---|
| `not-permitted` | The capability is missing, declined or revoked, the argument is outside the grant, a path escapes its scope, or a policy forbids the action | No |
| `not-found` | The node, pane, buffer, file, command, plugin, provider, call or device does not exist any more | No |
| `invalid-argument` | The argument breaks a rule the plugin can check before the call: syntax, range, a per-call cap | No, fix the call |
| `conflict` | State changed or is held: a stale revision, a manual title, a held lock, an existing file for `create-new` | Yes, after reading the state again |
| `quota-exceeded` | A stored or held quota is full, or the CPU budget of the execution quota group is spent | After freeing resources, or after `retry-after-ms` |
| `rate-limited` | A rate rule throttles the call | Yes, after `retry-after-ms` |
| `busy` | Transient capacity is full: pending requests, the job queue, an open picker, a device in use | Yes, later |
| `timed-out` | A deadline passed: lock wait, HTTP, process, job time or a reply from a service or command | Yes |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled by the plugin, the user, a shutdown, or a refused batch | Maybe |
| `unsupported` | The host or platform cannot do it, such as a codec, a channel count or an unknown action, or the call is made in the wrong instance kind | No |
| `pane-not-ready` | A restored terminal pane has not started its process yet | Yes, after `pane-created` or `tree-changed` |
| `revoked` | The authorization epoch changed during the call. The plugin is re-activated | No |
| `io` | An operating system I/O error other than a missing file | Maybe |
| `network` | DNS, connect, TLS or transport failure | Yes |
| `internal` | A host bug, or a trap inside a job instance | No |

Every function that returns a result can return `not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal`. A function that returns a `request-id` can also return `busy`, and `quota-exceeded` when the CPU budget is spent. Other codes are listed per function. For example, `storage.put` returns `invalid-argument` for an empty key, a key over 256 bytes or a value over 1 MiB, and `quota-exceeded` when the bucket or the disk is full.

Calls that return a `request-id` split their errors in two. Grant, scope, syntax and per-call cap checks fail at once, in the call. Disk, network, process and user failures arrive later in the completion as `failed(code)`. Check the completion, not only the call.

### Handling errors in Rust

The example stores a cursor in the session bucket. A full bucket skips the save. A busy host asks the caller to retry. Any other error is passed up, because it means a bug in the plugin or a missing grant.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::{self, Bucket};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

const CURSOR_KEY: &str = "cursor";

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SaveOutcome {
    Saved,
    SkippedFull,
    RetryLater,
}

pub fn save_cursor(cursor: &[u8]) -> Result<SaveOutcome, PluginError> {
    match storage::put(Bucket::Session, CURSOR_KEY, cursor) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(SaveOutcome::Saved),
        Err(error) => match error.code {
            ErrorCode::QuotaExceeded => Ok(SaveOutcome::SkippedFull),
            ErrorCode::Busy => Ok(SaveOutcome::RetryLater),
            _ => Err(error),
        },
    }
}
```

### Handling errors in TypeScript

The TypeScript version applies the same rules. A thrown `PluginError` is checked with `instanceof`, and `error.code` is a string union of the kebab-case codes. Errors that the plugin cannot fix are rethrown, so the restart rule sees them.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';

const CURSOR_KEY = 'cursor';

export type SaveOutcome = 'saved' | 'skipped-full' | 'retry-later';

export function saveCursor(cursor: Uint8Array): SaveOutcome {
  try {
    storage.put('session', CURSOR_KEY, cursor);
    return 'saved';
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof PluginError)) {
      throw error;
    }
    switch (error.code) {
      case 'quota-exceeded':
        return 'skipped-full';
      case 'busy':
        return 'retry-later';
      default:
        // invalid-argument, not-permitted and the rest are plugin bugs or missing grants.
        throw error;
    }
  }
}
```

### Traps

A trap ends the instance. The plugin is restarted under the restart rule below. The plugin cannot catch a trap. A trap is raised for these cases, because each one is a plugin bug:

- Calling a function of a capability the manifest never requested, in an interface that the plugin linked because it requested another capability of it. An interface that no requested capability unlocks is refused at install with `manifest.import-not-requested` and never links. A function of a requested capability that the user declined is not a trap: it returns `not-permitted`. See [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/).
- An invalid `ui-tree`: an index out of range, a graph that is not a tree, a duplicate `key` in one tree, more nodes than the effective `ui_tree_nodes` limit (4,096 by default), or a `layout` whose child count differs from its constraint count.
- Returning more than 256 submissions from one `on-events` call.
- A hard deadline breach in `activate`, `on-events` or `views.render`. A breach in `deactivate` is not a trap: the instance is dropped and no restore bytes are kept. A soft deadline breach traps and counts as a failure when it reaches the streak limit of its call class (3 consecutive, or 30 consecutive for scene frames) or when the call runs 100 ms past its deadline (grace). A hook-handler breach never counts as a failure; it disables that extension handler. The call classes are in [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/).
- Exceeding the linear memory or table limits.
- A Rust panic or an uncaught TypeScript exception in such an export.

### Trap codes

A trap carries one code. The codes are diagnostics of the host, the harness and `ilium plugin logs`. They are never a value of `plugin-error.code`, which is always one of the 15 values of the error-code enum above.

| Code | Raised when |
|---|---|
| `trap.deadline` | A hard deadline breach in `activate`, `on-events` or `views.render`, or a soft breach on the streak limit |
| `trap.memory` | Linear memory grows past the effective `memory_mib` limit |
| `trap.table` | A table grows past the effective table limit |
| `trap.submission-batch` | One `on-events` call returns more than 256 submissions |
| `trap.invalid-ui-tree` | A `ui-tree` is invalid: an index out of range, a graph that is not a tree, a duplicate `key`, more nodes than `ui_tree_nodes`, or a `layout` whose child count differs from its constraint count |
| `trap.import-not-requested` | A function of a capability the manifest never requested is called |
| `trap.abi` | An ABI fault: the bytes cannot be a value of the type |
| `trap.panic` | A Rust panic or an uncaught TypeScript exception in an export |

- **[API-081]** A trap MUST carry exactly one of the eight codes `trap.deadline`, `trap.memory`, `trap.table`, `trap.submission-batch`, `trap.invalid-ui-tree`, `trap.import-not-requested`, `trap.abi` and `trap.panic`, and the log line of the trap MUST name it.

Every `not-permitted` result and every trap is logged with the plugin id, the interface and the function, and shown in `ilium plugin logs`. Release builds show function names in trap backtraces only. Build with `ilium plugin build --debug` to see `file:line` for each frame.

<pre class="term">
<span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin logs example.notes --tail 4
16:02:10 <span class="t-err">err</span>  on-events 34 ms (limit 20 ms)
16:02:12 <span class="t-err">err</span>  on-events 41 ms (limit 20 ms)
16:02:20 <span class="t-err">err</span>  on-events 38 ms (limit 20 ms)
16:02:20 <span class="t-hi">note</span> 3 failures in 10 minutes: disabled
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. A plugin that breaches its event deadline three times is restarted after the first two traps, then disabled.
