### Common row keys

| Key | Rows | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | value rows | `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}`, unique in the plugin |
| `id` | button, info, group | Same grammar and namespace as `key` |
| `title` | all but unlabelled info | 1 to 48 characters. The label column |
| `description` | all | At most 200 characters |
| `default` | value rows | Required. Must pass the compiled schema |
| `help` | all | An id from `contributes.help`. Adds a `?` |
| `depends_on` | all | `{ "key", "equals" }`, `{ "key", "in" }` or `{ "key", "not" }`. Own keys only |
| `keywords` | all | At most 4 terms |
| `reset` | value rows | Default `true`. `false` keeps the row out of a section reset |
| `visible_when` | value rows | The `depends_on` shape on one own key. A false condition hides the row |
| `scope` | value rows | `"project"` stores the value in the project's `.ilium/` settings under `[plugins."<plugin-id>"]`. The project value wins while that project is open |
| `applies` | value rows | `"restart"` draws `↻` after the value and the note `Applies after restart.` |

A false `depends_on` leaves the row on the screen, read-only, with the description `Unavailable: <title> is <value>.` A false `visible_when` hides the row instead: it keeps its value and search skips it. The `label` key belongs to `button` only. The row `preview`, `notice` and `meter` take only the common keys that apply to a row with no value.

### Validation and saving

- **Install.** Every default and option is checked.
- **Load.** A stored value that no longer matches its row is ignored, and the default applies. The host never clamps a stored value. A number typed in the editor that is outside `min` and `max` is refused with the row note, and the stored value stays; the number stepper stops at the bounds [SET-020].
- **Save.** Schema check, then `settings-validate`, then the write, then `settings-changed`.

| Change | Shown | Written |
|---|---|---|
| Toggle, choice, dialog confirm | at once | at once |
| Number step | at once | 600 ms after the last step |
| Number or text typed | as typed | 600 ms after the last keystroke, or `debounce_ms` |
| Text-area | as typed | 1 s after the last keystroke |
| `set-json` from the plugin | at once | at once |

While a write is pending, the control shows a dim `◌` after the value. A failed change keeps the old value, and the message replaces the description line in the warning style. Closing Settings writes every pending change first.

### Keys on a plugin row

The kernel handles these keys before any plugin row sees them.

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| Up, Down | Move between rows |
| Left, Right | Step a number or choice, or flip a toggle |
| Enter, Space | Open the row's editor, or invoke a button |
| `*` | Type a value into a number row |
| `r` | Reset the focused value row |
| `?` | Open the row's help topic |
| `/` or Ctrl+F | Open the search filter. Esc clears it |
| Esc, `q` | Close Settings |

### Events and callbacks

**`settings-changed`** receives one record.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/events in reference-wit
enum settings-origin { user, plugin, reset, other-plugin, file }
record settings-change { keys: list<string>, origin: settings-origin, side: string }
```

- `keys`: changed keys, sorted, without duplicates.
- `origin`: `user`, `plugin`, `reset`, `other-plugin` or `file`.
- `side`: `"client"` or `"server"`, the receiving side. The field is named `side` so it is not confused with a row's `scope`, which is a storage scope (`"project"`). A section's `scope` key (`"client"` or `"server"`) names the side that hosts the section.

Coalesced writes send one event with the last origin and the union of keys.

**`settings-validate`** is an optional export on the side that owns the scope.

```wit
record field-error { key: string, message: string }
settings-validate: func(patch: string, merged: string) -> result<_, list<field-error>>;
```

It runs only for `user` and `reset` origins, after the schema check. Its deadline is 100 ms. A timeout, trap or stopped plugin refuses the save with `Could not check this value: <plugin name> did not answer.`

### Limits

An excess is refused with `manifest.settings-limit` unless the row says otherwise.

| Item | Limit |
|---|---|
| Tabs per plugin | 2 |
| Sections per plugin tab | 8 |
| Sections per plugin, per built-in tab | 2 |
| Plugin sections in one built-in tab | 6, extra ones are dropped with `settings.section-dropped` |
| Plugin tabs in the rail | 16, extra ones are dropped with `settings.tab-dropped` |
| Rows per section, children per group | 24 (a `group` counts as one row plus its children), and 12 |
| Value keys per plugin | 128 |
| Object item fields in a list | 8 |
| Segments in a meter | 8 |
| Notice text | 200 characters |
| Map entries | 64 |
| Choice options, list items | 64 |
| Tab, section and row titles | 32, 40 and 48 characters |
| Description, info text, button label | 200, 120 and 20 characters |
| Text value, text-area value | 4,096 and 65,536 characters, `invalid-argument` on save |
| All values of one plugin | 256 KiB, `invalid-argument` on save |
| `set-info`, `set-row-note` text | 120 characters, `invalid-argument` |
| `set-info`, `set-choices`, `set-row-note`, `set-row-state`, `set-item-states`, `set-choice-items`, `set-info-rich` and `set-meter` calls | 10 per second per plugin, all these calls together. A call over the rate is refused with `rate-limited` and the previous state stays [SET-050] |
| `settings-validate` answer | 100 ms, save refused on timeout |

### Error codes

Install errors refuse the package and name the JSON path of the entry.

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `manifest.settings-kind` | Unknown `kind` |
| `manifest.settings-id` | Bad tab, section or row id |
| `manifest.settings-key` | Bad value key |
| `manifest.settings-key-clash` | Duplicate key |
| `manifest.settings-id-clash` | Duplicate tab or section id |
| `manifest.settings-title-clash` | Tab title is a built-in label |
| `manifest.settings-target-unknown` | Missing target tab |
| `manifest.settings-target-closed` | Target tab takes no sections |
| `manifest.settings-target-grant` | Grant missing |
| `manifest.settings-anchor` | Unknown anchor, or `before:main` |
| `manifest.settings-tab-anchor` | Bad `after` |
| `manifest.settings-row-type` | Unknown row type |
| `manifest.settings-row-field` | Field not allowed for type |
| `manifest.settings-default` | Default fails its row |
| `manifest.settings-depends` | Unknown key or cycle |
| `manifest.settings-help` | Help id not in `contributes.help` |
| `manifest.settings-command` | Command not contributed |
| `manifest.settings-glyph` | Glyph not one 1 or 2 cell grapheme |
| `manifest.settings-limit` | Limit exceeded |
| `manifest.catalog-unknown` | A `source` names an unknown catalogue |
| `manifest.settings-source` | `source` together with `options` |
| `manifest.schema-keyword` | Keyword outside the subset |

Runtime and load codes:

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `invalid-argument` | A value is over its length limit, or `settings.open` names another plugin's target |
| `invalid-argument` | A `set-info`, `set-choices` or `set-row-note` call breaks a rule the plugin can check, such as text over 120 characters |
| `not-found` | A row-update call names an unknown key or id |
| `rate-limited` | More than 10 row-update calls per second per plugin, all kinds together |
| `settings.value-ignored` | A stored value no longer matches its row (warning) |
| `settings.anchor-missing` | An own-section anchor is gone, so the section moves to `end` (warning) |

### Reading the values in both languages

The rows of every type are read with one call and written with a merge patch. The plugin needs no grant for its own values.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;

let values: serde_json::Value =
    serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or_default();
let keep = values["enabled"].as_bool().unwrap_or(true);
settings::set_json(r#"{"max_entries": 800, "label": null}"#)?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { getJson, setJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

const values = JSON.parse(getJson()) as Record<string, unknown>;
const keep = typeof values['enabled'] === 'boolean' ? values['enabled'] : true;
setJson(JSON.stringify({ max_entries: 800, label: null }));
```

A `null` resets the key to its default. Per-type declarations are on the [row gallery](/pages/reference-settings-rows/).

### Versioning

- The `page` entries and `settings_pages` are removed, and `settings-changed` sends the record above.
- Built-in tab ids and anchors are frozen. Rows are closed, so an unknown row type or field refuses the package.

Requirement ids for this page: [SET-001], [SET-002], [SET-003], [SET-004], [SET-005], [SET-010], [SET-011], [SET-020], [SET-021], [SET-022], [SET-023], [SET-024], [SET-031], [SET-050], [SET-051], [SET-060], [SET-061], [SET-062], [SET-063], [SET-064]. See the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/).

### Security

Regex `pattern` values are limited per [SEC-046]; `secret` rows follow [SEC-242]. See [Secrets](/pages/reference-secrets/).

# Settings row gallery

## Settings row gallery

This page shows every row type of the Settings screen, as the kernel draws it. There are 18 row types: the first 12 are the base rows and the last 6 are `location`, `preview`, `notice`, `map`, `multi-choice` and `meter`. Each entry has the value type, the fields, the validation, how the value is written, a render in each state, a manifest example, and the declaration in Rust and in TypeScript. A row is declared in the manifest, so both SDKs share one JSON declaration. The two languages differ only in how the plugin reads the value and calls the row-update functions.

The field tables of the manifest are in the [settings schema reference](/pages/reference-settings-schema/). The calls that update rows at run time are in [settings](/pages/api-settings/). Tabs, sections and anchors are in the [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/), and custom pages are in [Building settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/).

### How to read the renders

Every render uses the glyphs that the real client draws. The panel is the content frame of a plugin tab, 59 columns wide. The rail and the header are shown on the [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) page.

- The label sits at the left and the control at the right. Between them are grey dotted leaders made of `…`, with one blank cell on each side. A gap shorter than five cells stays blank.
- The description is the dim line under the label, with a rule of `─` under the row.
- The selected row is drawn in the accent colours, lavender with a near-black foreground. There is no marker glyph.
- A dim `•` after the label means the value differs from the default. The `r` key resets the focused row.
- A dim `◌` after the value means a write is pending or the validate callback is running.
- `↻` after the value marks `applies: "restart"`, and the description reads `Applies after restart.`
- A failed change keeps the old value and replaces the description with the message of the failure, in the warning style.
- A row with a false `depends_on` stays visible and focusable, but is read-only: the control is dim and the description reads `Unavailable: <title> is <value>.`
- A row with a false `visible_when` is not drawn at all. It keeps its value, and search skips it. Nothing of a hidden row can be rendered, so the gallery shows the rows before and after instead.

The controls use these shapes:

| Control | Shape |
|---|---|
| Toggle, `switch` style | `‹ On ›` and `‹ Off ›` |
| Toggle, `checkbox` style | `[x]` and `[ ]` |
| Choice, `stepper` style | `← value → +` |
| Choice, `list` style and `dialog` style | `‹ value ›` |
| Number, `stepper` style | `- 42 + *` |
| Number, `slider` style | a `─` track with a `●` thumb, then the number control |
| Text, path, colour, key chord, list, map | `‹ value ›` |
| Secret text | `••••` plus the last characters |
| Button | `[ Label ]` |
| Scrollbar | `│` track with a `┃` thumb |

### Declaring and reading values

Every value row has a `key` of the form `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}`, a `title` of at most 48 characters and a `default`. These fields are common to all value rows: `description` (at most 200 characters, wrapped to 2 lines), `help` (a `contributes.help` id), `depends_on`, `visible_when`, `scope`, `applies`, `keywords` (at most 4) and `reset`.

The plugin reads all its values with one call and deserialises them into one type. The examples below show only the fields of the row that is being described. All of them belong to the same struct or interface.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
struct Config {
    // one field per value row, named by the row key
}

fn load_config() -> Config {
    serde_json::from_str(&settings::get_json()).unwrap_or_default()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { getJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

interface Config {
  // one property per value row, named by the row key
}

export function loadConfig(): Config {
  return JSON.parse(getJson()) as Config;
}
```

Every write is a merge patch (RFC 7396). A key set to `null` resets to the default. `set-json` writes at once and does not call `settings-validate`.

### 1. toggle

A boolean. The `switch` style is the default and the `checkbox` style suits a list of related flags.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | boolean |
| Fields | `on_label`, `off_label` (the text of the two states), `style`: `"switch"` or `"checkbox"` |
| Validation | `type: boolean`; a non-boolean in `set-json` is `invalid-argument` |
| Written | at once |

│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Sync ………………………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ On › ◌  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Pending: the write has not finished yet.           </span>│

**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "toggle", "key": "keep_history", "title": "Keep history",
  "description": "Record text copied in panes and the editor.",
  "default": true }
{ "type": "toggle", "key": "notify", "title": "Notify", "style": "checkbox",
  "default": false, "on_label": "Yes", "off_label": "No" }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    keep_history: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    notify: bool,
}

fn default_true() -> bool { true }

fn disable_history() -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    settings::set_json(r#"{"keep_history": false}"#)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { setJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

interface Config {
  keep_history: boolean;
  notify: boolean;
}

export function disableHistory(): void {
  setJson(JSON.stringify({ keep_history: false }));
}
```

### 2. choice

One value out of a list of options. The `stepper` style shows `← value → +`, the `list` style opens a list, and the `dialog` style opens the filterable choice dialog on Enter.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | string or integer |
| Fields | `options`: `[{ value, title }]` (2 to 64), `style`: `"stepper"`, `"list"` or `"dialog"`, `dynamic` |
| Option fields | `description` (120), `disabled_reason` (40), `preview`, `help` |
| Catalogue and filter | `source: { "catalog": "<id>" }`, `filter`, `allow_custom`, `custom_pattern`, `view_modes` |
| Validation | `enum` with `enum_titles`; a value that is not an option is `invalid-argument`; `source` together with `options` is `manifest.settings-source`; an unknown catalogue is `manifest.catalog-unknown` |
| Written | at once |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Choice states──────────────────────────────────╮
│  Store …………………………………………………………………………… ← Text only → +  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Stepper style: arrows step, + opens the list.      </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Density ……………………………………………………………………… ‹ Comfortable ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    List style and dialog style show the value.        </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Region • …………………………………… ‹ Frankfurt (unavailable) ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    The stored value is no longer offered.             </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Choice rows in the three styles. The last row shows a stored value that a <code>set-choices</code> call no longer offers.</figcaption>
</figure>
The dialog style opens the choice dialog of the kernel. The current option is marked with `●`. A disabled option carries `[unavailable]` and its reason on the line under it, and it cannot be chosen. The thumb of the scrollbar is `┃`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Region──────────────────────────────╮
│ Filter: fra                                │
│                                            │
│ ● Frankfurt                                │
│   Europe, Germany                          │
│   Frankfurt [unavailable]                  │
│   Unavailable: no capacity left            │
│   Paris                                    │
│ Esc cancel · Enter apply                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>The choice dialog of a <code>dialog</code> style row, with a filter, the current option, and a disabled option with its reason.</figcaption>
</figure>
Previews decorate options in the dialog. A `preview` is one of `{ "glyph": "x" }`, `{ "swatch": ["#rrggbb", ...] }` (at most 16 colours) or `{ "pattern": ["line", ...] }` (at most 4 lines of 8 cells). A catalogue source supplies them: `ilium.palettes` has swatch previews and `ilium.dithers` has pattern previews. The dither picker and the palette picker of the animation settings are these two catalogues.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Dither──────────────────────────────╮
│ Filter:                                    │
│ ● Bayer 4x4           █░█░                 │
│   Blue noise          ░█░░                 │
│   Scan lines          ████                 │
│ Esc cancel · Enter apply                   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>A catalogue choice with pattern previews, as in the dither row of <code>ilium.dithers</code>. The pattern cells come from the catalogue.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "choice", "key": "store", "title": "Store", "default": "text",
  "options": [
    { "value": "text", "title": "Text only" },
    { "value": "all", "title": "Everything",
      "description": "Images are kept as thumbnails." },
    { "value": "images", "title": "Images", "disabled_reason": "Needs 2 GiB" }
  ] }
{ "type": "choice", "key": "palette", "title": "Palette", "style": "dialog",
  "source": { "catalog": "ilium.palettes" }, "default": "sunset" }
{ "type": "choice", "key": "region", "title": "Region", "dynamic": true,
  "default": "fra", "options": [ { "value": "fra", "title": "Frankfurt" },
                                  { "value": "par", "title": "Paris" } ] }
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::CatalogItem;

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    store: String,
    palette: String,
    region: String,
}

fn offer_regions(names: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let items: Vec<CatalogItem> = names
        .iter()
        .map(|(id, title)| CatalogItem::new(id, title))
        .collect();
    settings::set_choice_items("region", &items)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { setChoiceItems } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

interface Config {
  store: 'text' | 'all' | 'images';
  palette: string;
  region: string;
}

export function offerRegions(names: Array<[string, string]>): void {
  setChoiceItems('region', names.map(([id, title]) => ({
    id, title, keywords: [],
  })));
}
```

`set-choices` replaces the options of a `dynamic` row with `value` and `title` pairs. `set-choice-items` replaces them with full catalogue records, so a dynamic row can carry descriptions, previews and disabled reasons.

### 3. number

An integer or a number with a range. The `stepper` style is `- 42 + *` and the `slider` style adds a `─` track with a `●` thumb. In an area narrower than 12 cells the slider falls back to the stepper.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | integer or number |
| Fields | `minimum`, `maximum` (required), `step` (default 1), `unit` (at most 8), `integer` (default true) |
| Fields | `style`: `"stepper"` or `"slider"`, `steps` (2 to 64 ascending numbers inside the range, replaces `step`), `special_values` (at most 8 `{ value, title }` pairs), `debounce_ms` (300 to 2,000) |
| Validation | `minimum`, `maximum`, `step`; `integer: true` rejects `4.5`; `steps` compile to `x-steps` and `special_values` to `x-special-values`, which are UI annotations only |
| Written | 600 ms after the last step, or `debounce_ms`; Enter writes at once |

The `*` button opens the entry dialog, in which the user types the number. The dialog also opens on Enter.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Number stepper states──────────────────────────╮
│  Maximum entries …………………………………………………………… -  500  + *  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Oldest entries are removed first.                  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Zoom • …………………………………………………………………………………… -  1.0  + *  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Selected, differs from the default.                </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Sync interval ………………………………………………………………… -  5 s  + *  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Unavailable: Sync is Off.                          </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Retention ……………………………………………………………………………… - Off  + *  │
│<span class="t-dim">    A special value is drawn instead of the number.    </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Speed ………………………………………………………………………………… -  1.5  + * ◌  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Pending: a step was made 200 ms ago.               </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Stepper rows. The last row waits for the 600 ms debounce before it is written. A special value (<code>0</code> as <em>Off</em>) replaces the number in the control.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Number slider──────────────────────────────────╮

**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "number", "key": "max_entries", "title": "Maximum entries",
  "minimum": 10, "maximum": 5000, "step": 10, "default": 500 }
{ "type": "number", "key": "speed", "title": "Speed", "style": "slider",
  "integer": false, "minimum": 0, "maximum": 4, "default": 1,
  "steps": [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4],
  "special_values": [ { "value": 0, "title": "Paused" } ] }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    max_entries: u32,
    speed: f64,
}

fn slow_down(config: &Config) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let patch = serde_json::json!({ "speed": config.speed / 2.0 });
    settings::set_json(&patch.to_string())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { setJson } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

interface Config {
  max_entries: number;
  speed: number;
}

export function slowDown(config: Config): void {
  setJson(JSON.stringify({ speed: config.speed / 2 }));
}
```

### 4. text

A single-line string. With `secret: true` the row shows `••••`, and with `reveal_last` it also shows the last characters.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | string |
| Fields | `max_length` (at most 4,096, default 256), `pattern`, `placeholder`, `secret` |
| Fields | `reveal_last` (0 to 8, only with `secret`), `debounce_ms` (300 to 2,000) |
| Validation | `maxLength`, `pattern`, and the optional `settings-validate` export |
| Written | 600 ms after the last keystroke, or at once on Enter or when the row loses focus |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Text states────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Label ……………………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ work ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Shown in the picker title; 40 characters.          </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Ignore regex …………………………………………………………………… ‹ ^\d{4}$ ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Selected.                                          </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Token • …………………………………………………………………………… ‹ •••• a1b2 ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Secret, reveal_last 4: last characters show.       </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Webhook ………………………………………………………………… ‹ ••••••••••••• ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Secret without reveal_last: dots only.             </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Pattern ………………………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ ( ›  │
│<span class="t-warn">    That is not a valid regular expression.            </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Text rows: plain, selected, two secrets, and a value that <code>settings-validate</code> refused. The refused value is reverted and the message replaces the description.</figcaption>
</figure>
A secret value is redacted in logs and in the snapshot. Other plugins that read the values with `get-plugin-json` see an empty string.

**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "text", "key": "label", "title": "Label", "default": "",
  "max_length": 40, "placeholder": "work" }
{ "type": "text", "key": "token", "title": "Token", "secret": true,
  "reveal_last": 4, "default": "" }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    label: String,
    token: String,
}

fn authorised(config: &Config) -> bool {
    !config.token.is_empty()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
interface Config {
  label: string;
  token: string;
}

export function authorised(config: Config): boolean {
  return config.token.length > 0;
}
```

### 5. text-area

A multi-line string. Enter opens an editor dialog, and the row shows the number of lines.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | string |
| Fields | `max_length` (at most 65,536, default 16,384), `language` |
| Fields | `debounce_ms` (300 to 2,000) |
| Validation | `maxLength`; compiles to `type: string` with `multiline: true` |
| Written | 1 s after the last keystroke, and at once when the editor closes |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Text area states───────────────────────────────╮
│  Paste template ……………………………………………………………… ‹ 3 lines ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Enter opens the editor; saved after 1 s.           </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Header ………………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ empty ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Selected.                                          </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Text-area rows. The value is the line count; the text is edited in the dialog.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Paste template──────────────────────╮
│ {{ text }}                                 │
│ Copied at {{ time }}                       │
│                                            │
│ Esc cancel · Enter newline · Ctrl+S save   │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>The editor dialog of a text area. Closing it writes the value at once.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "text-area", "key": "template", "title": "Paste template",
  "max_length": 2000, "language": "markdown", "default": "{{ text }}" }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    template: String,
}

fn render_entry(config: &Config, text: &str) -> String {
    config.template.replace("{{ text }}", text)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
interface Config {
  template: string;
}

export function renderEntry(config: Config, text: string): string {
  return config.template.replace('{{ text }}', text);
}
```

### 6. path

A file or a directory chosen with the kernel file picker.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | string |
| Fields | `picker`: `"file"` or `"directory"`, `extensions` |
| Validation | `type: string`; the extension list is checked on confirm |
| Written | on confirm |

The row stores the path as text. It grants no file access: the plugin needs its own `fs` grant to open the path, and the path must lie inside a scope it holds.

<figure>

│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Export folder ………………………………………………………………………… ‹ none ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    No value yet.                                      </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Path rows. Enter opens the file picker of the kernel.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "path", "key": "history_file", "title": "History file",
  "picker": "file", "extensions": ["db"], "default": "" }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    history_file: String,
}

fn history_path(config: &Config) -> Option<&str> {
    (!config.history_file.is_empty()).then_some(config.history_file.as_str())
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
interface Config {
  history_file: string;
}

export function historyPath(config: Config): string | undefined {
  return config.history_file === '' ? undefined : config.history_file;
}
```

### 7. color

A colour as `#rrggbb`. Enter opens the colour dialog with a hue strip, swatches and a hex field.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | string `#rrggbb` |
| Fields | `swatches`: `"theme"` or up to 16 colours |
| Validation | `pattern: ^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` |
| Written | on confirm |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Colour states──────────────────────────────────╮
│  Highlight colour ………………………………………………… ‹ ██ #4a9eff ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Colour of the newest entry in the picker.          </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Border colour • …………………………………………………… ‹ ██ #9d7cd8 ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Selected.                                          </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Colour rows. The block before the hex value is drawn in the chosen colour.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "color", "key": "highlight", "title": "Highlight colour",
  "swatches": "theme", "default": "#4a9eff" }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    highlight: String,
}

fn rgb(config: &Config) -> Option<(u8, u8, u8)> {
    let hex = config.highlight.strip_prefix('#')?;
    let value = u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok()?;
    Some(((value >> 16) as u8, (value >> 8) as u8, value as u8))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
interface Config {
  highlight: string;
}

export function rgb(config: Config): [number, number, number] {
  const value = parseInt(config.highlight.slice(1), 16);
  return [(value >> 16) & 255, (value >> 8) & 255, value & 255];
}
```

### 9. button

Runs one of the plugin's own commands on its declared side. The row holds no value.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | none |
| Fields | `label` (at most 20), `command` (own command id), `confirm` |
| Validation | the command must exist in `contributes.commands` (`manifest.settings-command`) |
| Written | nothing is written; the command runs |

With `confirm` set, the kernel asks first. The question uses the confirm dialog of the kernel, with the buttons ` N ` and ` Y ` and the hint `Y/N answer · Enter confirm · Esc cancel`.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Button states──────────────────────────────────╮
│  Clear history …………………………………………………………… [ Clear now ]  │

│<span class="t-hi">  Export ……………………………………………………………………………………… [ Export ]  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Selected.                                          </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Button rows. A read-only button (false <code>depends_on</code>) is dim and does not run.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Clear history───────────────────────╮
│ Delete every stored entry?                 │
│                                            │
│      N No          Y Yes                   │
│ Y/N answer · Enter confirm · Esc cancel    │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>The confirmation of a button with <code>confirm</code>. The buttons are drawn as filled colour blocks in the real client.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "button", "id": "clear_now", "title": "Clear history",
  "label": "Clear now", "command": "clear-history",
  "confirm": "Delete every stored entry?",
  "description": "Deletes every stored entry at once." }
```

A button has an `id` instead of a `key`, because it stores no value.

**Rust**

```rust
fn on_command(&mut self, command: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
    if command == "clear-history" {
        self.entries.clear();
    }
    Vec::new()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
onCommand(command: string): Submission[] {
  if (command === 'clear-history') entries.length = 0;
  return [];
}
```

### 10. info

A read-only text line. With `live: true` the plugin updates it while Settings is open. With `rich` spans it can carry tones, bold text and clickable commands.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | none |
| Fields | `text` (at most 120), `live` |
| Fields | `rich`: spans `{ text, tone?, bold?, command? }`, at most 120 characters in total, replacing `text`; a span with `command` (an own command id) is clickable |
| Validation | the 120 character limit; an unknown `command` is `manifest.settings-command` |
| Written | nothing |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Info states────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Stored entries ……………………………………………………………… 312 entries  │

│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Account …………………………………………………………………… Signed in as ada  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Rich spans: a tone, bold and a command.            </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Quota ……………………………………………………………………………………… ! 90 % used  │
│<span class="t-warn">    Warning tone from set-info-rich.                   </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Info rows. The first is a live row set by <code>set-info</code>. In the second, <em>Signed in as ada</em> is a clickable span. The third uses the warning tone.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "info", "id": "stored", "title": "Stored entries",
  "text": "0 entries", "live": true }
{ "type": "info", "id": "account", "title": "Account",

```

**Rust**

`set-info-rich(key, text)` takes a rich-text value instead of a string, for an `info` row with `live: true`. Calls to the `set-info` family are limited to 10 per second per plugin.

A titled group of rows, with an optional fold. The group holds no value, and it cannot contain another group.

### 12. list

An array of primitive items or of small objects. The `rows` style opens the list editor, and the `inline` style is one text field joined by a separator.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | array |
| Fields | `item` (one primitive type, or an object of primitive fields), `max_items` (at most 64) |
| Fields | `item_format`: `glob`, `url`, `host`, `path`, `regex` or `chord`; `style`: `"rows"` or `"inline"`; `separator` (default `;`); `reorderable` (default true); `remote`; `item_status`; object items with up to 8 fields (was 4) |
| Validation | `type: array`, `items`, `maxItems`; an item is checked on commit against its type and `item_format`; an invalid item is shown with `✗` and the reason and is not written |
| Written | on each committed item |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · List states────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Ignore patterns …………………………………………………………… ‹ 3 items ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Copies that match are never stored.                </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│<span class="t-hi">  Allowed hosts ……………………………………………… ‹ a.test; b.test ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Inline style, joined with ;.                       </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>List rows in the rows style and in the inline style.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Ignore patterns───────────────────────╮
│   *.log                                      │
│   secret-*                                   │
│ ✗ [a-z  Not a valid glob: unclosed class     │
│   *.tmp ◌                                    │
│                                              │
│ Enter edit · a add · d delete · Esc close    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>The list editor with <code>item_format: glob</code>. The third item failed its check and is not written. The last item is pending (<code>remote</code> rows wait for <code>set-item-states</code>).</figcaption>
</figure>
Object items are edited as one row of fields. The fields are primitive types, and an object has at most 8 of them.

**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "list", "key": "ignore", "title": "Ignore patterns",
  "item": { "type": "string" }, "item_format": "glob",
  "max_items": 32, "default": ["*.log"] }
{ "type": "list", "key": "hosts", "title": "Allowed hosts", "style": "inline",
  "separator": ";", "item": { "type": "string" }, "item_format": "host",
  "default": [] }
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::{RowState, RowStateKind, ItemState};

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    ignore: Vec<String>,
    hosts: Vec<String>,
}

fn confirm_item(index: u32) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let state = RowState { kind: RowStateKind::Idle, message: None };
    settings::set_item_states("ignore", &[ItemState { index, state }])
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { setItemStates } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

interface Config {
  ignore: string[];
  hosts: string[];
}

export function confirmItem(index: number): void {
  setItemStates('ignore', [{ index, state: { kind: 'idle' } }]);
}
```

### 13. location

A place on Earth. Enter opens the world-map picker of the kernel.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | object `{ lat, lon, label? }` |
| Fields | `search` (default true), `allow_current` (default false, needs `location.observer` on the client side), `precision` (decimals 0 to 6, default 4) |
| Validation | `lat` from -90 to 90, `lon` from -180 to 180, `label` at most 120 characters; both `lat` and `lon` are required |
| Written | when the user confirms `Use location` |

The address search needs `location.geocode`. The host owns the geocoding provider and asks the user once for consent to send place names. Without consent the search returns `not-permitted`.

### 14. preview

A live area that the plugin draws with one of its own `panels` views. It is for the effect of a setting, such as a colour scheme or a sound. It exists only in the plugin's own tabs (SE10).

| Item | Value |
|---|---|

| Validation | the view must exist; a `preview` row in a built-in tab is `manifest.settings-row-type` |
| Written | nothing |

The view may use display widgets, `schema-form`, `button` and `location-picker`. It may not embed other input widgets.

A banner inside a section. It tells the user something that is not a value, such as a privacy note.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|

| Validation | the text limit; `id` is unique in the plugin (`manifest.settings-id`) |
| Written | a dismissal is stored per `id` in the plugin's settings table and survives restarts |

<figure>

### 17. multi-choice

A set of options out of a list. The `checklist` style draws the options inline, and the `dialog` style opens the choice dialog with check marks.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | array of option values |
| Fields | `options` (2 to 64, the `choice` option shape) or `source`, `min_items` (default 0), `max_items` (default the option count), `style`: `"checklist"` (default) or `"dialog"` |
| Validation | `items: { enum }`, `uniqueItems: true`, `minItems`, `maxItems` |
| Written | at once on each toggle |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Multi-choice───────────────────────────────────╮
│  Capture kinds                                        │
│    [x] Text                                           │
│    [x] Images                                         │
│    [ ] Files                                          │
│<span class="t-dim">    Pick at least one.                                 </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Targets …………………………………………………………………… ‹ Text, Images ›  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Dialog style: Enter opens the list.                </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>A checklist and a dialog style row. The rule of <code>min_items</code> shows as the note under the list.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "multi-choice", "key": "kinds", "title": "Capture kinds",
  "min_items": 1, "default": ["text", "images"],
  "options": [ { "value": "text", "title": "Text" },
               { "value": "images", "title": "Images" },
               { "value": "files", "title": "Files" } ] }
```

**Rust**

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Config {
    kinds: Vec<String>,
}

fn captures_images(config: &Config) -> bool {
    config.kinds.iter().any(|kind| kind == "images")
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
interface Config {
  kinds: Array<'text' | 'images' | 'files'>;
}

export function capturesImages(config: Config): boolean {
  return config.kinds.includes('images');
}
```

### 18. meter

A segmented bar for a cost or a quota. The plugin updates it while Settings is open.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Value | none |
| Fields | `id` (required), `title`, `segments` (initial, at most 8), `max` (default 1), `show_values` (default false) |
| Validation | at most 8 segments; a segment is `{ label, value, tone }` |
| Written | nothing; updated with `set-meter` |

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Meter──────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Budget used …………………………………………………… ██████░░░░ 3.1 / 5  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Updated by the plugin.                             </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Quota ………………………………………………………………………………………… ████░░░░░░  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Segments differ by colour, not by glyph.           </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Meter rows. The filled part is drawn with <code>█</code> and the empty part with <code>░</code>, both from the progress bars of the real client.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "meter", "id": "budget", "title": "Budget used", "max": 5,
  "show_values": true,
  "segments": [ { "label": "used", "value": 0, "tone": "info" } ] }
```

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::settings;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::{MeterSegment, Tone};

fn show_budget(used: f64) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    settings::set_meter("budget", &[MeterSegment {
        label: "used".into(), value: used, tone: Tone::Info,
    }])
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { setMeter } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/settings';

export function showBudget(used: number): void {
  setMeter('budget', [{ label: 'used', value: used, tone: 'info' }]);
}
```

### Fields every value row shares

`visible_when`, `scope` and `applies` work on all value rows. They compile to the UI annotations `x-visible-when`, `x-scope` and `x-applies`, which never take part in validation.

#### visible_when

`visible_when` uses the `depends_on` shape, `{ key, equals | in | not }`, on one own key. The difference is what the user sees. A false `depends_on` leaves the row on the screen and makes it read-only. A false `visible_when` removes the row, keeps its value, and skips it in search.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Stars on───────────────────────────────────────╮
│<span class="t-hi">  Stars …………………………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ On ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Show stars in the background.                      </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">  ──────────────────────                               </span>│
│  Star count …………………………………………………………………… -  300  + * ↻  │
│<span class="t-dim">    Applies after restart.                             </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption><code>stars</code> is On, so <code>star_count</code> is drawn. It also has <code>applies: "restart"</code>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Stars off──────────────────────────────────────╮
│<span class="t-hi">  Stars • …………………………………………………………………………………………… ‹ Off ›  </span>│
│<span class="t-dim">    Show stars in the background.                      </span>│
╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption><code>stars</code> is Off. The row <code>star_count</code> is gone, and the rows below it move up. Its value of 300 is kept.</figcaption>
</figure>
**Manifest**

```json
{ "type": "number", "key": "star_count", "title": "Stars", "minimum": 10,
  "maximum": 2000, "default": 300, "applies": "restart",
  "visible_when": { "key": "stars", "equals": true } }
```

Hidden rows make the row positions jump under the cursor. Use `depends_on` when the user should see where a setting lives, and `visible_when` when the row would only confuse.

#### scope and applies

`scope: "project"` stores the value in the project's `.ilium/` settings under `[plugins."<plugin-id>"]` instead of the user configuration. The project value wins while that project is open. A `settings-changed` event carries the scope of the change in its `scope` field. `applies: "restart"` draws `↻` after the value and the note `Applies after restart.` The plugin reads the new value only after it restarts.

**Rust**

```rust
fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
    for event in batch {
        let Event::SettingsChanged(change) = event else { continue };
        // change.scope tells which side owns the keys; change.origin says who wrote them
        self.reload(&change.keys);
    }
    Vec::new()
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
  for (const event of batch) {
    if (event.tag !== 'settings-changed') continue;
    reload(event.val.keys);
  }
  return [];
}
```

### The controls of the Settings screen, by row type

The Settings screen draws these controls. Each is a style or a variant of one of the 18 row types, and no control has a row type of its own.

| Control | Row type and field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Toggle | `toggle` | `‹ On ›`; `style: "checkbox"` draws `[x]` |
| Stepper | `number`, `style: "stepper"` | `- 42 + *` |
| Slider | `number`, `style: "slider"` | `─` track with a `●` thumb plus the stepper |
| Number | `number` | the entry dialog opens on `*` or Enter |
| Choice | `choice` | `← value → +`, with the dialog on `+` |
| Dither | `choice` with `source: { "catalog": "ilium.dithers" }` | 15 algorithms with pattern previews |
| Palette | `choice` with `source: { "catalog": "ilium.palettes" }` | 38 presets with swatch previews |
| Colour | `color` | hex field, swatches and a hue strip |
| Key chord | `keybinding`, `list` with `item_format: "chord"` | the capture dialog |
| Glob list and URL list | `list` with `item_format: "glob"` or `"url"` | invalid items show `✗` and the reason |
| Masked secret | `text` with `secret: true` | `••••` plus `reveal_last` characters |
| Path | `path` | the kernel file picker |
| Text | `text`, `text-area` | one line or an editor dialog |
| Button | `button` | runs an own command |
| Info | `info` | live text, rich spans |
| Location | `location` | the world-map picker |

### Row calls at run time

These calls need no grant. They cover only the plugin's own rows. They are limited to 10 calls per second per plugin, all kinds together. A call over the rate is refused with `rate-limited`; nothing is coalesced.

| Call | Rust | TypeScript | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set-info` | `settings::set_info(key, text)` | `setInfo(key, text)` | `info` with `live: true` |
| `set-info-rich` | `settings::set_info_rich(key, text)` | `setInfoRich(key, text)` | `info` with `live: true` |
| `set-choices` | `settings::set_choices(key, options)` | `setChoices(key, options)` | `choice` with `dynamic: true` |
| `set-choice-items` | `settings::set_choice_items(key, items)` | `setChoiceItems(key, items)` | `choice` and `multi-choice` with a dynamic source |
| `set-row-note` | `settings::set_row_note(key, note)` | `setRowNote(key, note)` | any row, at most 120 characters |
| `set-row-state` | `settings::set_row_state(key, state)` | `setRowState(key, state)` | any value row; `idle`, `loading`, `pending`, `error`, message at most 80 characters |
| `set-item-states` | `settings::set_item_states(key, items)` | `setItemStates(key, items)` | `list` items |
| `set-meter` | `settings::set_meter(id, segments)` | `setMeter(id, segments)` | `meter`, at most 8 segments |

A call with an unknown key or id is `not-found`. A call for the wrong row type is `invalid-argument`.

### Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Tabs per plugin | 2 |
| Sections per plugin tab | 8 |
| Rows per section | 24 |
| Rows per group | 12 |
| Value keys per plugin | 128 |
| Choice options, list items | 64 |
| Text value, text-area value | 4,096 and 65,536 characters |
| Object item fields | 8 |
| All values of one plugin | 256 KiB |

The full table, with the error codes, is in [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).

## Pages

| Page | Lists | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Manifest keys](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Every key in `manifest.json`, its type, its default and the value it accepts. | You write or check the manifest. |
| [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/) | Every grant string, its argument form and its risk tier. | You add a grant to `capabilities`. |
| [Events and intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/) | Every event case and intent case, its payload and its outcomes. | You write `on-events` or build submissions. |
| [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) | The error codes, the default resource limits, the per-call caps and the rate rules. | You handle a failed call or size a value. |

## What you need

- The plugin API version `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. The manifest key `api` must name the version the plugin was built against, and the component must export the same version. See [Versioning](/pages/versioning/).
- The Rust crate `ilium-plugin-sdk` or the npm package `@ilium/plugin-sdk`, at the versions pinned by the SDK release. Rust stable 1.90 or later and Bun 1.2 or later are required for the build.
- The `ilium plugin` subcommand of the `ilium` binary. It runs every check named on these pages. No other tool is needed.

## Quick lookup

| Need | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grant string | `name` or `name:argument`. The first colon splits them; later colons belong to the argument. | [Capability table](/pages/reference-capabilities/) |
| Grant risk tiers | `always`, `normal` and `high`. A `high` grant is unchecked by default at install. | [Capability table](/pages/reference-capabilities/) |
| Memory limit | Default 32 MiB. Ceiling 256 MiB for a bundled plugin, 128 MiB for other tiers. | [Resource limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) |
| Restart back-off | 1 s after the first failure, 5 s after the second, disabled at the third within 10 minutes. | [Restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule) |
| Disable rule | The third failure inside 10 minutes disables the plugin on that side. | [Restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule) |
| Submission dedup key | 1 to 128 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`. Window of 10 minutes. | [Dedup keys](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#dedup-keys) |
| Submissions per return | 256 per `on-events` call. | [Fixed caps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Pending requests | 64 per plugin by default. Over that, `busy`. | [Resource limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) |
| Storage | Key up to 256 bytes. Value up to 1 MiB. Bucket 16 MiB by default. | [Resource limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) and L3 |
| Log line | Up to 16 KiB; longer lines are cut and end with `…[truncated]`. | [Fixed caps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Command reply | 30 s. Inference reply: 120 s. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Rate of `notify` | 6 per minute per plugin. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Rate of `play-sound` | 4 per second per plugin. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Rate of `topics.publish` | 100 per second per plugin. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Rate of `toast` | 3 per 10 s per plugin. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Rate of `geocode` | 1 per second per plugin. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Status segment and frame slot update | 10 per second per slot. | [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) |
| Contribution caps | `tree_toolbar` 4, `row_actions` 4, `tree_orderings` 4, `status_segments` 2, `pane_frame_slots` 4, `display_modes` 2, `catalogs` 8, `client_requests` 16, `languages` 8. | Manifest keys |
| Events and intents | 18 extended events, 23 extended intents, `ok-epoch`, 17 ui-action kinds, 12 action-value cases. | Events and intents |
| Settings rows | 18 row types. Six new: `location`, `preview`, `notice`, `map`, `multi-choice`, `meter`. | Manifest keys |
| Manifest error codes | 13 new codes, `manifest.catalog-unknown` to `manifest.scene-prerender`. | Errors and limits |

## Error codes

Every host call that can fail returns `plugin-error { code, message, retry-after-ms }`. The table lists the 15 codes.

| Code | Meaning | Retry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not-permitted` | The grant is missing, the user declined it, the argument is outside the grant, the path escapes its scope, or a policy forbids the action. | No |
| `not-found` | The named node, pane, buffer, file, command, plugin, provider, call, sound or device does not exist. | No |
| `invalid-argument` | The argument breaks a rule the plugin can check before the call: syntax, range, a size cap or an undeclared id. | No; fix the call |
| `conflict` | State changed or is held: a stale revision or epoch, a manual title, a held lock, or an existing file for `create-new`. | Yes, after reading state again |
| `quota-exceeded` | A stored or held quota is full: storage, disk, metadata, timers, watches, grabs, filters, captures or the CPU budget. | After freeing a resource, or after `retry-after-ms` for the CPU budget |
| `rate-limited` | A rate rule throttles the call. `retry-after-ms` is always set. | Yes, after `retry-after-ms` |
| `busy` | Transient capacity is full: pending requests, the job queue, an open picker or an exclusive device. | Yes, later |
| `timed-out` | A deadline passed: a lock wait, HTTP, a process, job time, or a service or command reply. | Yes |
| `cancelled` | The plugin, the user or a shutdown cancelled the request, or another submission of the batch was refused. | Maybe |
| `unsupported` | The host or platform cannot do it: a format, codec, channel count or missing action, or no clipboard. | No |
| `pane-not-ready` | A restored terminal pane has not started its process yet. | Yes, after `pane-created` or `tree-changed` |
| `revoked` | The authorization epoch changed during the call. The plugin is re-activated. | No |
| `io` | An operating system I/O error other than a missing file. | Maybe |
| `network` | DNS, connect, TLS or transport failure. | Yes |
| `internal` | A host bug, or a trap inside a job instance. | No |

`not-permitted`, `revoked` and `internal` can come back from every fallible function. Each function's own list of further codes is on the errors and limits page.

## Names in each SDK

The WIT name is the source. The SDKs derive the other spellings by fixed rules.

| WIT form | Rust | TypeScript |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Error code `rate-limited` | `ErrorCode::RateLimited` | `'rate-limited'` |
| Field `retry-after-ms` | `retry_after_ms` | `retryAfterMs` |
| Function `read-all` in `fs` | `fs::read_all(path).await` | `readAll(path)` from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs` |
| `u64` or `s64` | `u64` or `i64` | `bigint`, always |
| `option<T>` | `Option<T>` | `T` or `undefined` |
| Errors from a fallible call | `Result<T, PluginError>` | returns `T`; throws `PluginError` |

## Worked example: Rust

This function reads a notes file. A file that does not exist yet counts as empty. Every other error goes to the caller. The code uses the `not-found` completion of `fs.read-all`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::fs;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

/// Reads a notes file. A file that does not exist yet counts as empty.
async fn read_notes(path: FsPath) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, PluginError> {
    match fs::read_all(&path).await {
        Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(bytes)),
        Err(error) if error.code == ErrorCode::NotFound => Ok(None),
        Err(error) => Err(error),
    }
}
```

The prelude brings in `FsPath`, `PluginError` and `ErrorCode`. The caller decides what `None` means. A notes plugin, for example, writes an empty document on its first save.

## Worked example: TypeScript

This module turns a `rate-limited` error into a wait time. Any call that the host may throttle can use it, such as `topics.publish`. The caller schedules the next attempt with a one-shot timer from `@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers`.

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { PluginError } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

/**
 * Returns how many milliseconds to wait before retrying a failed call,
 * or undefined when waiting cannot help.
 */
export function delayBeforeRetry(error: unknown): number | undefined {
  if (!(error instanceof PluginError)) return undefined;
  if (error.code !== 'rate-limited') return undefined;
  return error.retryAfterMs;
}
```

A `PluginError` carries `code`, `message` and `retryAfterMs`. The function returns `undefined` for every other code, so the caller rethrows it.

Twenty-three grants are listed there, and ten of them are high risk. The settings row table lives in the [settings schema reference](/pages/reference-settings-schema/).

## Edge cases and errors

- A grant with a wildcard in the wrong place is refused at install with `manifest.grant-wildcard`. `commands.invoke:com.example.notes/*` is valid. `commands.invoke:*/notes` is not.
- A manifest limit above the tier ceiling is clamped and logged. It is never refused.
- A trap ends the plugin instance and is not an error code. Deadline breaches, memory over the limit and more than 256 submissions are traps.
- A dedup key with a character outside the allowed set is a malformed submission. It refuses the whole batch.
- A duplicate submission completes as `duplicate(original)`. It is not an error and has no effect.
- A value over a per-call cap that the plugin can know in advance returns `invalid-argument` at once, and nothing is written. Two exceptions do not fail: `log.log` cuts the line and `terminal.read-screen` clamps its row count.

## What the user sees

- The install dialog lists the grants by risk tier. A `high` grant is listed and unchecked; the user must check it.
- Refusals and traps are logged with the plugin id, the interface and the function. `ilium plugin logs` shows them (see [Debugging](/pages/debugging/)).
- A keybinding conflict makes the losing binding inactive and lists it in Settings > Keys (N25).
- A plugin disabled by the third failure stays disabled until the user enables it again. A manual enable resets the failure count.

## Check output

Run `ilium plugin check` on a package before you install it. The check names the key, the problem and the page that lists the correct value.

1 error, 0 warnings
</pre>

# Admin policy reference

## Admin policy reference

An administrator of a shared machine, a team or a company needs to decide which plugins people may run, without editing each person's settings. The **admin policy** is a file that the administrator owns. It limits what users and plugins can do. This page defines its locations, its schema, how it combines with user choices, and what users see when it blocks something.

The broker rule in the design is: a plugin may do something only if the tier ceiling, the install plan, the user's grants **and** the policy all allow it. The **install plan** is the ordered list of package id, version, tier, publisher fingerprint and requested grants that step 6 of the install pipeline evaluates. The broker evaluates the policy against this list and returns the first failing key's code, in the order of [USR-217](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/#how-the-keys-combine). This page defines the policy part. For deployment recipes see [Enterprise deployment](/pages/guide-enterprise-deployment/).

### You will need

- A system where you can write a root-owned file (administrator rights).
- The install pipeline in [Grant review and consent](/pages/reference-grant-review-and-consent/).
- The grant names in the [Capability table](/pages/reference-capabilities/).

## Locations and precedence

**[SEC-180]** The server reads these files at start, in this order, and merges them:

| Order | Platform | Path |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Linux | `/etc/ilium/policy.toml` |
| 1 | macOS | `/Library/Application Support/Ilium/policy.toml` |
| 1 | Windows | `%ProgramData%\Ilium\policy.toml` |
| 2 | All | `<user config dir>/policy.toml` (optional user file) |

**[SEC-181]** Merge rules. The user file can only make the policy stricter. For a list of allowed values the effective list is the intersection; for a list of denied values it is the union; for a boolean `allow_*` the effective value is the logical AND; for a boolean `*_only` or `offline` the effective value is the logical OR. A user file can never lift a restriction of the system file. **Deny wins over allow.** Policy wins over user choices and over the manifest.

**[SEC-182]** The system file MUST be owned by root (or by the Administrators group on Windows) and not writable by group or others. If it is not, it is **ignored** and the audit log records `policy-violation` with reason `policy-file-writable`. Because a policy that is silently ignored would be a security loss, the server also shows a persistent notice `Admin policy ignored: file is writable by non-administrators`.

## Schema

All keys are optional. A missing section means no restriction from that section. Types: `string`, `[string]` (list), `bool`, `int`.

```toml
version = 1

[packages]
allow_third_party = true           # default: true; false refuses every T2 and T3 install
allowed_tiers   = ["t1", "t2"]        # default: ["t1","t2","t3"]
allow_unsigned  = false               # default: true (T3 allowed)
allow_dev_mode  = false               # default: true
allowed_sources = ["file:///opt/ilium-plugins/", "/srv/plugins/"]  # default: any
blocklist_file  = "/etc/ilium/blocklist.json"
precompiled_cache = true
allow_url_installs = false          # default: true; false refuses a bare URL or file path source
allowed_channels = ["stable"]       # default: ["stable","beta"]
block_vulnerable_runtime = false

[publishers]
trusted_keys = ["3f2a91c07b6d1e44a1b20c9e55d3f7a8b6c102e94d7798af13c56e0bd2f48a19"]
allow        = ["3f2a91c0…"]          # when set, only these keys may sign T2 packages
deny         = ["a1b20c9e…"]

[plugins]
allow_ids      = ["example.*", "ilium.*"]    # glob on ids; default: all
deny_ids       = ["example.experimental.*"]
force_enabled  = ["example.compliance"]      # cannot be disabled by the user
force_disabled = ["example.fun"]             # cannot be enabled by the user

[grants]
deny              = ["http:*.pastebin.example", "process.run:sh", "terminal.history"]
max_risk          = "high"            # "normal" refuses every high-risk grant
deny_combinations = true              # refuse plugins that read data and send it out
[grants.preapproved]
"example.compliance" = ["fs.read:project", "process.run:git"]

[extensions]
allow_replacement = false
deny_points       = ["ilium.core.terminal/before-send-input"]

[network]
allow_hosts = ["*.example.com"]
deny_hosts  = ["*.pastebin.example"]
ca_bundle   = "/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem"
proxy       = "http://proxy.example.com:3128"
offline     = false

[processes]
deny_env = ["EXAMPLE_INTERNAL_TOKEN"]

[settings]
locked = { "terminal.scrollback" = 20000, "plugins.example.compliance.endpoint" = "https://c.example.com" }

[inference]
allowed_providers = ["local", "corp-gateway"]

[projects]
allow_project_values = false          # plugin values in .ilium/ are always ignored

[audit]
sink      = "file"                    # "file", "syslog" or "journald"
max_mib   = 64
keep_days = 365
```

| Key | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages.allow_third_party` | bool | true | `false` refuses to install, enable or run T2 and T3 plugins with the detail code `policy.third-party-denied`. Core and bundled plugins are not affected |
| `packages.allow_url_installs` | bool | true | `false` refuses `install` from a bare URL or file path with `policy.source-denied`; registry ids and bundles still work |
| `packages.allowed_channels` | list of `stable`, `beta` | both | Channels a user may select |
| `packages.allowed_tiers` | list | all | Install of another tier fails with `policy.tier-denied`; an installed one is disabled |
| `packages.allow_unsigned` | bool | true | `false` refuses `--allow-unsigned` and `ilium plugin dev` for T3 |
| `packages.allow_dev_mode` | bool | true | `false` refuses `ilium plugin dev` |
| `packages.allowed_sources` | list | any | Install files must lie below a listed path, file URL or `https://` registry prefix (scheme, host and path prefix are compared; a trailing slash does not matter); else `policy.source-denied`. This is the "managed registry" of 0.1.0: a managed folder, not a server |
| `packages.blocklist_file` | path | none | Extra blocklist ([SEC-147]) |
| `publishers.trusted_keys` | list | none | Keys that count as trusted without a user prompt |
| `publishers.allow` / `deny` | list | none | Fingerprints allowed or refused as signers; refusal code `policy.publisher-denied` |
| `plugins.allow_ids` / `deny_ids` | list | none | Glob on ids; refusal code `policy.id-denied` |
| `plugins.force_enabled` / `force_disabled` | list | none | See [SEC-189] |
| `grants.deny` | list | none | Grant patterns ([SEC-193]). A matching grant is locked off and refused at run time with reason `policy`; the install still succeeds ([SEC-198]) |
| `grants.max_risk` | string | high | `normal` locks off every high-risk grant like a denied grant ([SEC-198]) |
| `grants.deny_combinations` | bool | false | Refuses the toxic combination ([SEC-004]) |
| `grants.preapproved` | table | none | Grants given without a dialog ([SEC-117]) |
| `extensions.allow_replacement` | bool | true | `false` refuses `replaces` with `policy.replacement` |
| `extensions.deny_points` | list | none | Contributions to the listed points are dropped and the grant row is locked off ([SEC-382]) |
| `network.*` | | | See [Network egress](/pages/reference-network-egress/) |
| `processes.deny_env` | list | none | Added to the environment denylist ([SEC-033]) |
| `settings.locked` | table | none | Setting key to value; the key is read-only for the user and plugins |
| `inference.allowed_providers` | list | all | Other providers are refused with reason `policy` |
| `projects.allow_project_values` | bool | true | `false` ignores all plugin values in `.ilium/` |
| `audit.sink`, `max_mib`, `keep_days` | | file, 64, 365 | See [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/) |

## Evaluation

**[SEC-184]** The install pipeline applies the policy at the steps marked in [Grant review and consent](/pages/reference-grant-review-and-consent/): `policy.tier-denied`, `policy.id-denied`, `policy.publisher-denied` and `policy.source-denied` at step 6; `policy.replacement` at step 9. A grant that matches `grants.deny` is not an install failure ([SEC-198]). At run time, a host call that the policy forbids returns `not-permitted` with reason `policy`. The user and the plugin see reason `policy`, never the policy text.

**[SEC-185]** In the review dialog a policy-denied row is locked off and reads `Blocked by your administrator`:

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Install example.pane-tools 2.0.0 ───────────╮</span>
│ [ ] <span class="t-warn">HIGH</span> Run rg ………………………………… process.run:rg │
│ <span class="t-dim">    Blocked by your administrator</span>            │
│ [x] Show toasts ……………………………………… notify.toast │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Cancel                                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. A policy-denied row is locked off and cannot be checked.</figcaption>
</figure>

**[SEC-186]** An installed plugin that violates a new policy is disabled at the next start, with a notice `Disabled by your administrator`, and the audit log records `policy-violation`. Its data is kept.

**[SEC-187]** A malformed policy file (TOML error, unknown key, wrong type, `version` not 1) fails **closed** for third parties: T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load with `policy.invalid`, and T1 plugins run normally. The server shows `Admin policy is invalid: <line and message>` and keeps running. A policy file that is missing is not an error (no policy). An unreadable one (permission error) counts as malformed.

**[SEC-188]** The policy is read at server start only. A change takes effect at the next start. `ilium plugin policy reload` is not part of version 0.1.0.

**[SEC-189]** Forced states. `plugins.manage` and the Plugins screen MUST NOT enable a plugin in `force_disabled` or disable one in `force_enabled`. The call returns `not-permitted` with reason `policy`, and the screen shows a lock mark. A `force_enabled` plugin that is not installed is reported in `policy show` as `missing` and in the audit log; the server does not install it.

**[SEC-190]** Locked settings. A key in `settings.locked` is shown with a lock mark and its policy value. A write by the user, by `ilium config set`, or by a plugin with `settings.write-all` is refused with `settings.locked`. A plugin reads the policy value.

**[SEC-191]** `ilium plugin policy show` prints the effective policy as JSONL: one `policy-source` line per file read (path, owner, hash, used or ignored), one `policy` line with the merged values, and one `summary` line.

**[SEC-192]** `[projects] allow_project_values = false` makes every plugin value in a project folder ignored, regardless of project trust ([SEC-310]).

**[SEC-193]** Grant patterns. An entry of `grants.deny` has one of these forms and no other: `<name>` matches the bare grant and every argument form of that name; `<name>:<arg>` matches exactly that argument; `<name>:*` matches any argument; `<prefix>.*` matches every grant name that starts with `<prefix>.`, such as `clipboard.*`; and for http, `http:*.<domain>` matches any host grant whose host ends in `.<domain>`, including a `*.<sub>.<domain>` grant, so `http:*.pastebin.example` matches `http:a.pastebin.example`. `*` is valid only in these positions. A policy with any other pattern is rejected with `policy.invalid` ([SEC-187]). Test: deny `clipboard.*` and assert `clipboard.read` is locked; deny `http:*.pastebin.example` and assert `http:a.pastebin.example` is locked and `http:pastebin.example` is not; deny `net.*` and assert `policy.invalid`.

**[SEC-198]** Denied grants. A grant that matches `grants.deny` MUST NOT fail the install and MUST NOT disable the plugin. The review dialog shows the row locked off with `Blocked by your administrator`, and a call returns `not-permitted` with the message starting `policy: `. When the server reads a policy that denies a grant a plugin already holds, it removes the grant through the normal revocation path (authorization epoch bump, audit event `grant-revoked`, and `deactivate(revoked)` when the plugin was running). Only `plugins.deny_ids`, `packages.allowed_tiers`, `packages.allow_third_party` and the publisher rules disable a plugin. Test: deny `clipboard.read`, install a plugin that requests it, and assert state `enabled`, a locked row and a refused call; restart with the grant newly denied and assert the grant is gone from the plugin's granted list.

**[SEC-382]** Denied extension points. A contribution grant to a point in `extensions.deny_points` is treated as a denied grant ([SEC-198]): the install succeeds, the grant row is locked off, the contribution is not registered, and the owner never calls it. A plugin that owns a denied point (`extensions.provide`) still runs, and contributions from other plugins to it are dropped. The audit log records `policy-violation` with the point id. Test: deny a point, install a plugin that contributes to it, and assert the install succeeds, the row is locked, the owner's callback is never invoked and the audit record exists.

**[SEC-199]** Multi-user machines: see [Enterprise deployment](/pages/guide-enterprise-deployment/). Each user has their own stores and runtime directory. The system policy applies to all users. No store is shared between users.

## Examples

Lock the machine to one publisher and block all high-risk grants:

```toml
version = 1
[packages]
allowed_tiers  = ["t1", "t2"]
allow_unsigned = false
[publishers]
allow = ["3f2a91c07b6d1e44a1b20c9e55d3f7a8b6c102e94d7798af13c56e0bd2f48a19"]
[grants]
max_risk = "normal"
```

A package signed by another key fails with `policy.publisher-denied`. A package asking for `terminal.history` still installs. The review dialog shows the `terminal.history` row locked off, and a call returns `not-permitted` with the reason `policy`.

An offline site:

```toml
version = 1
[network]
offline = true
[packages]
allowed_sources = ["/srv/ilium-plugins/"]
```

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Both files set `offline`; user file sets `false` | Effective `true` (OR) |
| System allow list `["a"]` and user allow list `["a","b"]` | Effective `["a"]` |
| `force_enabled` plugin is blocked by `deny_ids` | Deny wins; reported in `policy show` as `conflict` |
| Policy denies a grant a bundled T1 plugin needs | The grant stays off; the plugin runs without it |
| `preapproved` grant not listed in the manifest | Ignored |
| Policy file replaced while the server runs | Not read until restart; audit line at next start |

- [Security model](/pages/security/)
- [Enterprise deployment](/pages/guide-enterprise-deployment/)

- [Capability: plugins.manage](/pages/capability-plugins-manage/)
