# Audit log

## Audit log

The audit log is one tamper-evident record of security decisions: installs, grants, consents, trust, policy and sandbox events. It is not the plugin log. The plugin log mixes lines the plugin wrote with host lines, is rate limited and is trimmed. The pane journal records pane input and output for plugins that hold `journal.read`, and it is trimmed oldest first. Neither is fit to answer "who allowed what, and when". The audit log is.

A **hash chain** links each record to the one before it by including the previous record's SHA-256, so removing or changing a record breaks every later link.

### You will need

- The CLI: `ilium plugin audit`.
- Access to the user's state directory for the file itself.
- The stores described in [Grant review and consent](/pages/reference-grant-review-and-consent/).

## Location and access

**[SEC-220]** The log is written only by the kernel to `audit.jsonl` in the audit directory: Linux `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/audit/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/Ilium/audit/`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ilium\audit\`. The file has mode 0600 in a 0700 directory. It is in the deny set ([SEC-060]): no plugin scope reaches it, and `journal.read` does not expose it.

## Record schema

**[SEC-221]** Each line is one JSON object:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ts` | string | UTC ISO 8601 with milliseconds, for example `2026-10-12T08:14:02.114Z` |
| `seq` | int | Starts at 1, increases by 1; a gap is a defect |
| `prev_hash` | string | SHA-256 (hex) of the previous line's bytes without the trailing newline; the first record uses 64 zeros |
| `session` | string | Session name |
| `actor` | object | `{ "kind": "user-tui" or "cli" or "policy" or "kernel" or "plugin", "pane": "<pane id>"?, "plugin": "<id>"? }` |
| `event` | string | See the catalogue |
| `plugin_id`, `version`, `tier` | string | When the event concerns a plugin |
| `publisher_fingerprint`, `package_sha256` | string | When known |
| `grant`, `target` | string | Grant string or consent target |
| `result` | string | `ok`, `refused`, `cancelled`, `failed` |
| `reason` | string | Short code |

**[SEC-222]** Event catalogue. Each of these events MUST be written exactly once per occurrence, except the rate-limited ones.

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `install`, `update`, `downgrade`, `uninstall` | End of the install pipeline, including cancelled and refused attempts |
| `enable`, `disable`, `failure-disable` | State change, with the actor |
| `grant-given`, `grant-revoked` | Each grant change |
| `consent-given`, `consent-withdrawn` | Each consent change |
| `trust-add`, `trust-remove` | Trust store change |
| `replacement-on`, `replacement-off` | A core plugin replacement is turned on or off |
| `policy-loaded`, `policy-violation` | Policy read at start; a plugin or file violates it |
| `sandbox-unavailable`, `sandbox-degraded` | Once per start and prerequisite |
| `signature-failure`, `integrity-failure`, `blocklist-hit` | Package or load checks fail |
| `process-run` | A T2 or T3 plugin runs a program, or a pane command starts unconfined ([SEC-066]) |
| `write-outside-data` | A write outside `data` and `cache` by a plugin |
| `egress-host-first-use` | First request of a plugin to a host ([SEC-087]) |
| `extension-disabled-after-breaches` | A contribution is stopped after repeated breaches |
| `store-external-edit` | A store changed outside the server ([SEC-113]) |
| `h-grant-refused` | Summary of refused H calls, at most one record per plugin and kind per minute, with a count |
| `project-trust` | A project is trusted or untrusted |
| `safe-mode` | The server started in safe mode |

**[SEC-223]** Redaction. A record never contains terminal text, prompts, transcripts, file contents or request bodies. Argument values equal to a current plugin secret (and its base64 and percent-encoded forms) are replaced with `<redacted>` ([SEC-243]). Process arguments are logged in full otherwise.

## Retention and failure

**[SEC-224]** Rotation. The log rotates at `audit.max_mib` (default 64 MiB) or when the oldest record is older than `audit.keep_days` (default 365). The new file starts with a record whose `prev_hash` is the hash of the last line of the rotated file, and the old file is renamed `audit-<first seq>.jsonl` and kept until its age exceeds `keep_days`. Policy may change both values.

**[SEC-225]** Disk full. If a record cannot be written, the server keeps running, keeps the record in memory (up to 1,000 records), retries every 10 s, and shows a notice. Security events have priority over the rest: when the in-memory queue is full, the oldest `h-grant-refused` and `egress-host-first-use` records are dropped first, and a `audit-dropped` record with the count is written when space returns.

**[SEC-226]** Verification. `ilium plugin audit --verify` re-computes the chain and prints `ok` or the first broken `seq`. The chain detects edits by someone who cannot also rewrite the whole file; an attacker with write access to the file can rebuild it. For stronger assurance the policy can set `[audit] sink` to `syslog` or `journald` ([SEC-228]).

## Viewing and export

**[SEC-227]** `ilium plugin audit [--plugin <id>] [--since <time>] [--event <name>] [--limit <n>]` prints matching records as JSONL (one `audit` object per line, then one `summary`). `--since` accepts an ISO 8601 time or a duration such as `24h`. Settings > Plugins > Activity shows the same records in a list.

**[SEC-228]** With `[audit] sink = "syslog"` or `"journald"` the server also sends each record to the system log with the identifier `ilium-audit`, one JSON object per message. The local file is still written.

## Example

```text
{"ts":"2026-10-12T08:14:02.114Z","seq":412,"prev_hash":"9c1f…","session":"default","actor":{"kind":"user-tui"},"event":"grant-given","plugin_id":"example.notes","version":"1.2.0","tier":"t2","grant":"fs.read:project","result":"ok"}
{"ts":"2026-10-12T08:14:02.240Z","seq":413,"prev_hash":"4ab7…","session":"default","actor":{"kind":"cli","pane":"shell-3"},"event":"install","plugin_id":"example.notes","version":"1.2.0","tier":"t2","package_sha256":"d5e0…","result":"ok"}
```

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The file is deleted while the server runs | The server recreates it with a record `audit-reset` and `prev_hash` of zeros; the loss is shown in a notice |
| Two servers (two sessions of one user) write | There is one file per user. Writers take a file lock, read the last `seq` and hash under the lock, and append. The `session` field tells them apart |
| Clock goes backwards | `ts` may decrease; `seq` stays the ordering |
| A plugin tries to read the file | `not-permitted`; the deny set applies |

### See also

- [Debugging](/pages/debugging/)
- [Capability: journal.read](/pages/capability-journal-read/)
- [Admin policy](/pages/reference-admin-policy/)
- [Secrets](/pages/reference-secrets/)

Contract: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Check and lint rules

## Check and lint rules

`ilium plugin check` finds mistakes that would stop an install or trap at run time. `ilium plugin lint` finds mistakes and weak spots that do not stop anything but make a plugin worse for its users. Both read files only and run offline. This page defines the rules, their codes, their severity, the input each one reads, the record each one prints, how to fix each one and how to suppress a lint rule.

Every rule has a stable code. A test or a CI job cites the code. The codes of `check` are the codes the install path uses, so a package that passes `check` passes the install checks (it can still fail trust or the review dialog, which need a person). Command flags and exit codes are in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/).

Terms:

- **Finding**: one problem reported by a rule.
- **Severity**: `error` stops a build gate, `warn` is advisory, `info` is a hint.
- **Key path**: a JSON Pointer into `manifest.json`, for example `/capabilities/client/2`. A finding about the manifest carries one.

## You will need

- A project folder with `manifest.json`. For the component rules, a built `dist/` folder.
- No toolchain for `check` on a package file. A built `dist/` for the rules that read components.
- Background: [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/), [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/) and [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/).

## What check does

- **[DEV-200]** `check` MUST run exactly the install checks of [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/), in the same order, with the same codes, and MUST NOT run any plugin code. It reports the install codes `manifest.*`. The install path uses no `package.*` codes, so `check` has none either. The rules of DEV-201 add further codes.
- **[DEV-201]** `check` MUST add the component rules below, which report `component.*` and `signature.*` codes and two further `manifest.*` codes. They need built components and are skipped, with one `component.missing` finding per absent side, when `dist/` has no component for a declared side.
- **[DEV-202]** Every `check` finding is an `error`, except `signature.absent`, `component.size-warning` and `check.stale-build`, which are `warn`, and `signature.fingerprint`, which is `info`. The severity column of the rule tables is normative.
- **[DEV-203]** `check` MUST NOT check trust. Whether a signing key is trusted depends on the user's machine. `check` verifies that a signature is valid for the manifest bytes and states the fingerprint in an `info` finding named `signature.fingerprint`.

### Component rules

| Code | Severity | Reads | Fires when | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `component.missing` | error | `dist/` | A declared side has no component | Run `ilium plugin build` |
| `component.invalid` | error | the component | The file is not a valid WebAssembly component | Rebuild |
| `component.world-mismatch` | error | component, manifest | The world of the component differs from `world` in the manifest | Fix the world in the manifest or the entry |
| `manifest.api-version` | error | component | The `ilium:api-version` section is absent, malformed or differs from `api` | Rebuild with the current SDK |
| `manifest.exports-mismatch` | error | component, manifest | The exports differ from the required set plus the listed optional exports | Fix the `exports` list |
| `component.import-ungranted` | error | component, manifest | The component imports a host function whose grant the side does not request | Add the grant, or remove the call |
| `component.import-unknown` | error | component | The component imports an interface that is not in the contract | Use the SDK imports only |
| `component.size-warning` | warn | component | A component is larger than 8 MiB | Strip dependencies |
| `signature.absent` | warn | package | A `.iliumpkg` has no `signature` entry | Sign it, or accept tier T3 |
| `check.stale-build` | warn | `dist/build.json`, sources | The input hash in `dist/build.json` differs from the current sources | Run `ilium plugin build` |
| `signature.fingerprint` | info | package | A valid signature exists | none |

- **[DEV-204]** `component.import-ungranted` MUST fire for each imported function whose required grant is missing from the `capabilities` list of the side that the component serves. A function of an always-granted interface MUST NOT fire. This is the static form of the trap that [Debugging](/pages/debugging/) describes for a call to an import that the manifest never requested.
- **[DEV-205]** `component.world-mismatch` and `manifest.api-version` MUST be reported from the component's own embedded data, never from the file name.
- **[DEV-206]** `component.size-warning` MUST fire above 8 MiB. Above 32 MiB the finding MUST be an `error` with the same code.

A finding record:

```json
{"type":"check","rule":"component.import-ungranted","severity":"error","message":"server.wasm imports ilium:host/fs.read-all but the server side does not request fs.read","file":"dist/server.wasm","key_path":"/capabilities/server"}
```

## What lint does

- **[DEV-210]** `lint` MUST run only `lint.*` rules. It reads the manifest, the files listed by the manifest, `dist/` when present, and the fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` when present.
- **[DEV-211]** A rule that needs an input that is absent MUST be skipped without a finding. `lint` MUST print one `info` finding named `lint.skipped` for each rule it skipped, with the missing input in the message.
- **[DEV-212]** Rules that render a view or replay a fixture MUST do so in the embedded test host and MUST NOT contact a session.

### Lint rule catalogue

| Code | Severity | Reads | Fires when | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lint.grant-unused` | warn | manifest, component | A requested grant has no import or contribution that needs it | Remove the grant |
| `lint.widget-missing-key` | warn | rendered views | An interactive widget has no `key` | Give every interactive widget a `key` |
| `lint.render-trap` | error | rendered views | A declared view traps in the test host with an empty fixture | Fix the render |
| `lint.help-topic-missing` | warn | manifest | The plugin contributes commands, pane kinds, panels or settings pages and `contributes.help` is empty | Add a help topic |
| `lint.settings-help-missing` | warn | manifest | A settings row has no `help` id | Add a topic id, see [guide](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/) |
| `lint.limit-above-ceiling` | warn | manifest | A `limits` value is above the ceiling of the tier, so the host clamps it | Lower the value |
| `lint.debug-info-in-release` | warn | `dist/`, `build.json` | A release build carries DWARF or a source map | Rebuild with `--release` |
| `lint.package-size-near-cap` | warn | files | The files sum to more than 100 MiB | Reduce assets |
| `lint.unstable-feature` | warn | manifest | `unstable` lists a name | Expect change before 1.0 |
| `lint.dedup-key-charset` | warn | replayed fixtures | A submission carries a dedup key with a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]` or longer than 128 characters | Fix the key |
| `lint.icon-name-unknown` | warn | manifest | An `icon` is not a Tabler icon name that the host ships | Choose a listed name |
| `lint.extension-schema` | warn | manifest | An extension point has a schema outside the allowed subset, no `version`, or `max_handlers` of 0 | Fix the declaration |
| `lint.description-missing` | warn | manifest | `description` is empty or longer than 280 characters | Write one short paragraph |
| `lint.license-missing` | info | manifest | `license` is empty | Add an SPDX expression |
| `lint.grant-unexplained` | warn | docs | A requested grant name does not appear in `README.md` | Explain the grant in the README |
| `lint.help-title-mismatch` | warn | docs | The first heading of a help topic differs from its manifest `title` | Make them equal |
| `lint.help-link-broken` | warn | docs | A `help:<id>` link names a topic the plugin does not ship | Fix the id or add the topic |
| `lint.help-topic-too-large` | warn | docs | A help topic is over 20 KiB | Split the topic |
| `lint.extension-point-undocumented` | warn | docs | A declared extension point id is in neither `README.md` nor `docs/EXTENDING.md` | Document the point |
| `lint.license-file-missing` | info | docs | `license` is set and no `LICENSE` file exists | Add the license text |
| `lint.activation-startup` | warn | manifest | `activation` lists `startup` and the plugin has no event handler that needs it | Use lazy activation |
| `lint.high-risk-grants` | info | manifest | A high-risk grant is requested | Confirm it is needed |
| `lint.src-in-package` | info | files | The package holds `src/**` entries, which reviewers can read but the host never loads | Pack without `--include-src` unless wanted |
| `lint.contribution-near-cap` | info | manifest | A contribution list is at 90 percent of its cap | Plan for the cap |
| `lint.readme-missing` | info | project | No `README.md` in the project folder | Add one |
| `lint.changelog-missing` | info | project | No `CHANGELOG.md` in the project folder | Add one |
| `lint.suppression-reason-missing` | error | `lint.toml` | A suppression has no reason | Add a reason |
| `lint.suppression-unknown` | error | `lint.toml` | A suppression names an unknown rule | Fix the rule id |
| `lint.suppression-unused` | warn | `lint.toml` | A suppression matched no finding | Remove it |
| `lint.skipped` | info | none | A rule was skipped for a missing input | none |

The check `manifest.when-key` already catches an unknown `when` key at install time, so lint has no second rule for it.

- **[DEV-213]** `lint.grant-unused` MUST consider a grant used when a component import needs it, a contribution needs it, or an `extensions` entry needs it. It MUST skip a grant that is named only in a feature that loads later through `requires`. It MUST read the component imports, so it is skipped when `dist/` is absent.
- **[DEV-214]** `lint.widget-missing-key` MUST render each declared view with an empty fixture at 40 columns by 12 rows and report each interactive node without a `key`. Interactive widgets are those with actions, such as buttons, inputs, lists and toggles.
- **[DEV-215]** `lint.limit-above-ceiling` MUST use the ceilings of tier T2 and T3 from [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) for any package that is not a bundled T1 plugin.
- **[DEV-216]** `lint.package-size-near-cap` MUST fire at 100 MiB total and MUST match the `pack.size-cap` warning, so `pack` and `lint` agree.
- **[DEV-217]** `lint.icon-name-unknown` MUST compare against the Tabler icon names built into the host version, and the finding MUST name the closest known name when one is within an edit distance of 2.
- **[DEV-218]** `lint.dedup-key-charset` MUST replay each fixture of `tests/fixtures/` through the test host and inspect the submissions. Without fixtures it is skipped.
- **[DEV-219]** `lint.high-risk-grants` MUST list the grants by name in `message`, so a reviewer sees the risk summary at a glance.
- **[DEV-220]** Rules with scope `docs` MUST read `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `docs/` and the help files named by the manifest. A missing file is a finding of the rule for that file, not a crash. The rules are defined in [Plugin documentation guide](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/).

A lint finding record:

```json
{"type":"lint","rule":"lint.settings-help-missing","severity":"warn","message":"settings row 'refresh_seconds' has no help id","file":"manifest.json","key_path":"/contributes/settings/0/schema/properties/refresh_seconds","fix":"add \"help\": \"<topic id from contributes.help>\" to the row","suppressed":false}
```

## Severity, deny and exit codes

- **[DEV-225]** Plain `lint` MUST exit with 0 when only `warn` and `info` findings exist, and with 3 when an `error` finding exists.
- **[DEV-226]** `lint --deny warnings` MUST exit with 3 when any unsuppressed `warn` or `error` finding exists. `info` findings never affect the exit code.
- **[DEV-227]** `check` MUST exit with 3 when any `error` finding exists, and `check` has no deny flag, because its two `warn` findings (an unsigned package and a large component) are normal during development.

## Suppression

A project suppresses a lint rule in a file named `lint.toml` in the project folder. Suppression is a per-project decision that a reviewer can read, so it carries a reason.

```toml
[[suppress]]
rule = "lint.grant-unused"
key_path = "/capabilities/client/2"
reason = "the optional exporter that needs this grant loads only after the first run"

[[suppress]]
rule = "lint.activation-startup"
reason = "scans the project once at startup to fill the tree decorations"
```

- **[DEV-230]** `lint.toml` MUST be the only place that suppresses a lint rule. The manifest MUST NOT carry a suppression key, because unknown manifest keys fail the install.
- **[DEV-231]** A `[[suppress]]` table MUST have `rule` and `reason`. `key_path` is optional and, when given, limits the suppression to findings with the same key path. A table without `reason` MUST produce `lint.suppression-reason-missing`.
- **[DEV-232]** `check` rules MUST NOT be suppressible. A `rule` that names a `manifest.*`, `component.*` or `signature.*` code MUST produce `lint.suppression-unknown`.
- **[DEV-233]** A suppressed finding MUST still be printed, with `suppressed` true, so a reviewer sees it. Suppressed findings do not count toward the exit code.

## Worked example

A TypeScript plugin requests `fs.read:project` but never calls a file function. The text form of `lint` prints:

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin lint
<span class="t-warn">warn</span> lint.grant-unused
     /capabilities/server/1 fs.read:project
     fix: remove the grant
<span class="t-warn">warn</span> lint.settings-help-missing
     row refresh_seconds has no help id
<span class="t-dim">info</span> lint.readme-missing
2 warnings, 0 errors, 1 hint
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The text form of lint. The exit code is 0, or 3 with --deny warnings.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Edge cases

- **Component older than the manifest.** A rule that reads the component can report a finding about a grant that was removed from the manifest after the build. `lint` and `check` MUST first compare `dist/build.json` with the sources and report a finding with rule `check.stale-build` and severity `warn` when they differ, and still run. `pack` fails on the same condition with `pack.stale-build`.
- **Two sides.** Every rule runs per side. A finding carries the side in its `file` path, such as `dist/client.wasm`.
- **Empty project.** A project with no `contributes` key passes every rule except `lint.description-missing` if the description is empty.
- **A TypeScript project with no `dist/`.** `check` reports `component.missing` for each side. `lint` skips the component rules and prints `lint.skipped`.

## See also

- [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/)

- [Plugin documentation guide](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/)

API checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# CLI compatibility

## CLI compatibility

Today every `ilium` subcommand is built into the binary. After the move to plugins, the rest are owned by core plugins. A user, a script or an agent that runs `ilium chat send` or `ilium progress set --wait` MUST see the same arguments, the same output records and the same exit codes. This page lists every command, who owns it, and the changes to the `cli` contract that make this possible.

Related pages: [cli](/pages/api-cli/), [capability cli.contribute](/pages/capability-cli-contribute/), [manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/), [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/), [feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/), [core parity requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-core-parity/).

### Command ownership

#### Kernel commands

The kernel parses these commands before any plugin runs. A plugin MUST NOT declare them. They work with `--no-plugins` and in safe start.

| Command | Why it stays in the kernel |
|---|---|
| `ilium` (attach) | Starts the server and the client. |
| `ilium new-session <name>` | Creates the session and its socket. |
| `ilium ls` | Reads the session sockets. |
| `ilium kill-session <name>` | Ends a session. |
| `ilium plugin ...` | Installs, enables and removes plugins. See [plugin commands](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/). |
| `ilium --help`, `ilium --version` | Help must work with no plugin. |
| `kernel.open-recovery` | The recovery page needs no plugin. |
| `--cwd`, `--session-name`, `--safe-plugins`, `--no-plugins` | Global options read before plugins load. |

#### Commands owned by core plugins

| Command | Owner plugin | Page | Needs a server | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ilium new-pane` | fleet | [fleet](/pages/core-plugin-fleet/) | yes | text for plain panes, JSONL for `--worktree` | Worktree creation calls the worktrees service. |
| `ilium panes` | fleet | [fleet](/pages/core-plugin-fleet/) | no | JSONL | Visits every running session. |
| `ilium broadcast` | fleet | [fleet](/pages/core-plugin-fleet/) | no | JSONL | Uses the pane selector. |
| `ilium chat init`, `send`, `context`, `tail` | chatroom | [chatroom](/pages/core-plugin-chatroom/) | no | text | Works on `CHATROOM.md` directly. |
| `ilium progress check`, `set`, `wait`, `status`, `clear` | progress | [progress](/pages/core-plugin-progress/) | yes | JSONL | `ilium wait` is a second declared name. |
| `ilium wait` | progress | [progress](/pages/core-plugin-progress/) | yes | JSONL | Alias of `ilium progress wait`. |
| `ilium voice say` | voice | [voice](/pages/core-plugin-voice/) | yes | JSONL | Asks the plugin's client side. |
| `ilium recap` | recap | [recap](/pages/core-plugin-recap/) | yes | JSONL or Markdown | Uses the pane selector. |

The chat hooks that `ilium chat init` installs call `ilium chat context --since-last-read`. These calls MUST keep working when the chatroom plugin is the owner.

### Contract changes

The current `cli` contract allows one subcommand per plugin and one output form per command. Core plugins need more. These changes apply to `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` and are already reflected in [cli](/pages/api-cli/) and [capability cli.contribute](/pages/capability-cli-contribute/).

| Change | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Several commands per plugin | `cli` is one object | `cli` is an object or a list of at most 8 objects. Names MUST be unique inside the plugin. |
| Aliases | none | Each entry MAY set `aliases`, a list of names that follow the same name rule. `ilium wait` is an alias of `progress wait`. |
| Mixed output | `jsonl` or `text` | `output` MAY also be `"mixed"`. Both `write-line` and `write-text` are allowed. `new-pane` uses it. |
| Reserved names | none | The kernel names above are reserved. A manifest that uses one fails with `manifest.cli-name-reserved`. |
| Startup meaning | one meaning | `startup` runs per side. The command table is read when the server side loads. |

[COR-040] A plugin MUST declare every `ilium` subcommand it owns in the `cli` key. A built-in command that has no declared owner MUST NOT exist after the move.

[COR-041] The arguments, option names, defaults, output records, exit codes and error codes of every command in the table MUST equal those in the CLI reference of the user documentation (`src/docs/cli-reference.md`) at the baseline commit.

### Disabled owner

When the owner plugin is disabled, the kernel keeps the command name but answers it.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `ilium chat send ...` and chatroom is disabled | One JSON record `{"type":"error","code":"cli.owner-disabled","plugin":"ilium.core.chatroom","message":"..."}` on standard output, a hint on standard error, exit code 1. |
| The owner failed to load | Same record with `cli.owner-failed`. |
| The command is not installed at all | `unknown command`, exit code 2, as today. |
| `ilium --help` | Lists the command with the mark `(disabled)`. |

[COR-042] A disabled or failed owner MUST give exit code 1 and an error record with the code `cli.owner-disabled` or `cli.owner-failed`. The record MUST name the plugin id and MUST NOT be a parse error.

### Sample fixes

The core-plugin pages had samples that broke the contract. They are corrected as follows.

| Page | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| fleet | `cli` was a list while the contract allowed one object; world `ilium:client/views@0.1.0` does not exist. | List allowed; world is `ilium:client/base@0.1.0`. |
| progress | Declared `progress` only; `wait` is a second name. | `aliases` or a second entry. |
| recap | `argument_groups` existed but the group was not defined. | Group `pane-selector` documented in [cli](/pages/api-cli/). |
| chatroom | Needed no server but did not say so. | `requires_server: false`. |

### Environment variables the plugins rely on

The kernel sets these inside every terminal pane. Plugins read them through the host, not through the process environment.

| Variable | Set by | Read by | Host function |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ILIUM_PANE_ID` | kernel | progress, chatroom (reader key), recap | `caller-pane` |
| `ILIUM_SESSION_NAME` | kernel | fleet, voice | `cli-invoked` payload `cwd` plus session lookup |
| `ILIUM_SESSION_SOCKET` | kernel | progress, voice | resolved by the kernel |
| `ILIUM_WORKTREE`, `ILIUM_BRANCH` | worktrees | agent setup scripts | none; set at pane spawn |
| `ILIUM_CHATROOM_AUTHOR`, `AGENT_NAME` | user | chatroom | listed in the `cli-invoked` environment subset |
| `ILIUM_CONFIG_DIR`, `ILIUM_SOCKET_DIR`, `ILIUM_DEBUG_LOG_DIR` | user | kernel | none |
| `ILIUM_SAFE_PLUGINS`, `ILIUM_NO_PLUGINS` | user | kernel | none |

The kernel MUST pass only the listed variables to a plugin. A plugin cannot read other variables of the caller.

### Requirements

[COR-040] and [COR-041] and [COR-042] above are collected, with their tests, in [core parity requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-core-parity/).

# Config and data migration

## Config and data migration

Ilium already stores user data: a global `config.toml`, a project `.ilium/config.yaml`, session snapshots, rolling backups, agent instruction files and a chatroom file. Core plugins must read and write the same files, with the same key names, so that a user who installs the plugin build loses nothing and can read every file with the old tools. This page states the migration rules, lists every key and file with its owner, and defines the one mechanism that plugins use to store state in a session snapshot.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. The platform is not implemented. Requirement ids have the form `[COR-nnn]` and are collected in [Core plugin parity requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-core-parity/).

### Contents

- Migration rules
- Settings ownership: kernel tables and plugin tables
- Who owns each tab
- `config.toml`, key by key
- Plugin tables in `config.toml`
- Project YAML
- Session snapshots
- Snapshot sections
- Data files
- Agent configuration files that Ilium writes
- A worked migration
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### Migration rules

1. **No key is renamed or moved.** Every key in `config.toml` and `.ilium/config.yaml` keeps its table and name. A feature that becomes a plugin keeps reading the kernel key through `settings.read-kernel:<tab>`. It does not copy the value to `[plugins."ilium.core.<name>"]`.
2. **The plugin tables are additive.** The platform adds `[plugins]`, `[plugins.limits]` and `[plugins."<id>"]`. A build that does not know them MUST ignore and preserve them.
3. **Unknown keys are preserved.** The kernel keeps every key it does not know when it rewrites a file, as it does today for the project YAML.
4. **A value that fails validation fails its table, not the file.** The message names the key. The other tables still load.
5. **A format that changes gets a version.** `config.toml` carries an integer `config_version`. Absent means 0, the format of the build before plugins. The snapshot carries `version`. Each plugin section in a snapshot carries `schema_version`.
6. **Migrations run once, on read, and are idempotent.** A migration reads the old shape, writes the new one to a temporary file in the same folder and renames it. Running it twice gives the same file.
7. **A migration keeps a copy.** Before the first write of a new `version`, the kernel keeps the old file next to it as `<stem>.pre-migration.<old-version><ext>`, where the file name splits into stem and extension at the last dot and `<old-version>` is the old `version` number. For example `main.json` at version 3 is kept as `main.pre-migration.3.json`. Snapshots also keep the existing `.pre-restore.json` copies (see Session recovery in the user documentation).
8. **No downgrade promise for snapshots.** A snapshot written by the plugin build has `version` 4. A build that only knows version 3 reads it without the plugin sections and without error (unknown fields are ignored), but the plugin state is not restored.
9. **Seeds are not re-run.** Default values are applied only for missing keys. A default never overwrites a stored value.

### Settings ownership: kernel tables and plugin tables

Two stores exist and they do not overlap.

| Store | Where | Who writes | Who reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kernel tables | `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, `[inference]` and the other 25 tab tables of `config.toml`, plus the project YAML | The kernel when the user edits a row. The one owner plugin of the tab, with `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` | Any plugin with `settings.read-kernel:<tab>` |
| Plugin tables | `[plugins."<id>"]` and `.ilium/config.yaml` key `plugins.<id>` | The plugin, through the always-granted `settings.set-json` | The plugin. Other plugins with `settings.read-all` (T1 only) |

The rules for the kernel tables, which close the question of "who may write a kernel value" (this replaces the read-only wording of D13, see [design decisions](/pages/design-decisions/#d13-kernel-settings-are-readable-and-the-tab-owner-may-write)):

- **[COR-030]** A kernel tab MUST have exactly one owner plugin when its feature is a core plugin. Only that plugin MAY hold `settings.write-kernel:<tab>`. A second plugin that declares the same grant fails to install with `manifest.settings-owner`.
- **[COR-031]** `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` is a T1-only, high-risk grant. A T2 or T3 package that declares it fails with `manifest.grant-tier`. Any plugin, of any tier, MAY hold `settings.read-kernel:<tab>`.
- The write goes through the same validator as the Settings screen. A value outside its range fails with `settings.invalid-value` and nothing is written. A write is atomic for the whole tab object: all keys in the call apply or none do.
- The rows of a kernel tab stay drawn by the kernel from the [settings schema](/pages/reference-settings-schema/). The owner plugin does not draw them again. The owner uses the write grant for changes the user did not type on the row: an import, a migration, a price update, a reset to defaults.
- A tab with no core plugin owner (a feature that stays native, such as the Editor and Kanban Board tabs in v1) has no owner. The kernel writes it.

### Who owns each tab

The 25 frozen tab ids and their owners. The owner is the only plugin that may hold `settings.write-kernel:<tab>`. The last column lists plugins that read the tab.

| Tab id | Label | `config.toml` table | Owner | Readers | Keys written |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user-interface` | User Interface | `[ui]`, `[theme]` | Settings | Tree, Agent toolbar, Titles, Diagnostics, Terminal | Every `[ui]` key except the ten listed under `agent-monitoring`, plus `[theme]` |
| `icons` | Icons | `[ui.icons]` | Settings | Tree, Agent toolbar | `[ui.icons]` |
| `agent-monitoring` | Agent Monitoring | `[ui]`, `[detection]` | Agent detect | Progress, Agent toolbar, Notifications | `[ui]` `agent_identifier_mode`, `agent_monitoring_mode`, `attention_running_indicator`, `claude_agent_icon`, `codex_agent_icon`, `antigravity_agent_icon`, `progress_monitor_enabled`, `progress_max_lines`, `completed_progress_hide_after_seconds`, `task_progress_frames`; all of `[detection]` |
| `agent-cost` | Agent Cost | `[cost]` | Cost | Fleet, Tree | `[cost]` |
| `optimization` | Optimization | none (writes the agent's own config) | Compaction | none | none |
| `remote-compaction` | Remote compaction | `[remote_compaction]` | Compaction | none | `[remote_compaction]` |
| `keyboard` | Keyboard | `[keyboard]`, `[keybindings]` | Keys and help | none | `[keyboard]`, `[keybindings]` |
| `terminal` | Terminal | `[terminal]` | Terminal | Smart copy | `[terminal]` |
| `editor` | Editor | `[editor]` | Editor (kernel while native) | Terminal | `[editor]` |
| `session` | Session | `[session]` | Sessions | none | `[session]` |
| `git` | Git | `[git]` | Worktrees | Fleet | `[git]` |
| `kanban-board` | Kanban Board | `[kanban_board]` | Kanban (kernel while native) | none | `[kanban_board]` |
| `animations` | Animations | project YAML `animation` | Ambient look | Scenes | project YAML `animation` |
| `sound` | Sound | `[sound]`, `[notifications]` | Notifications | none | `[sound]`, `[notifications]` |
| `voice-control` | Voice control | `[voice]` | Voice | none | Every `[voice]` key except `custom_prompt` |
| `reset-planning` | Reset planning | `[reset_planning]` | Cost | Notifications | `[reset_planning]` |
| `inference` | Inference | `[inference]` | Inference | Titles, Recap, Search, Smart copy, Compaction, Voice | Every `[inference]` key except `title_style` and `instructions` |
| `llm-instructions` | LLM Instructions | `[inference.instructions]`, `[voice]` | Inference | Titles, Recap, Smart copy, Voice | `[inference.instructions]` and `[voice] custom_prompt` |
| `titles` | Titles | `[inference]` | Titles | none | `[inference] title_style` only |
| `triggers` | Triggers | `[triggers]` | Titles | none | `[triggers]` |
| `text-triggers` | Text Triggers | `[text_triggers]` | Text triggers | none | `[text_triggers]` |
| `debug` | Debug | `[debug]` | Settings | Diagnostics | `[debug]` |
| `api` | API | `[api]` | Fleet | none | `[api]` |
| `about` | About | none | Settings | none | none |
| `setup` | Setup | `[agent_setup]` | Agent setup | none | `[agent_setup]` |

The table order is the rail order, equal to `src/docs/settings.md`: User Interface, Icons, Agent Monitoring, Agent Cost, Optimization, Remote compaction, Keyboard, Terminal, Editor, Session, Git, Kanban Board, Animations, Sound, Voice control, Reset planning, Inference, LLM Instructions, Titles, Triggers, Text Triggers, Debug, API, About, Setup. Plugin tabs follow after About and Setup. The labels are the baseline labels. The high-risk marking of the API tab is a notice row inside the tab, not part of the label.

**[COR-034]** The "Keys written" column is enforced by the host. A write through `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` that names a key outside the column fails with `settings.key-not-owned` and nothing is written, even when another tab of the same table holds that key. Several tabs share the `[ui]`, `[inference]` and `[voice]` tables; each tab rewrites only its own keys, as the baseline Settings screen does.

Twelve core plugins do not own a tab: Agent toolbar, Chatroom, Diagnostics, Layout, Progress, Recap, Scenes, Scheduler, Search, Session convert, Smart copy and Tree. They read the tabs of the plugins whose feature they depend on. Tree options such as tree order and project separators live on the User Interface tab and are written by the kernel when the user edits a row.

The tab `agent-cost` is also the id of the Cost plugin's earlier plugin tab. A plugin tab id is local to its plugin (`self:<tab-id>`) and never collides with a kernel id, but the two names must not both appear in one rail. The Cost plugin therefore declares no tab of its own. It adds sections to the kernel tab with `settings.contribute:agent-cost`. See [Plugin settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/).

### `config.toml`, key by key

The tables below are the complete list of keys the kernel knows today (see the [Settings page](/pages/settings-screens/) for values and defaults). The column **Consumer** names the core plugin whose behaviour the key changes. **Live** says whether a running side sees the change without a restart.

| Table | Keys | Consumer | Live |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[ui]` panel sizing | `left_panel_sizing_mode`, `left_panel_fixed_width`, `left_panel_unfocused_width`, `left_panel_focused_width`, `left_panel_minimum_terminal_width` | Kernel layout | yes |
| `[ui]` tree | `tree_order`, `show_tree_row_management_controls`, `show_project_separators`, `lock_closed_enabled`, `auto_remove_empty_groups` | Tree | yes |
| `[ui]` agents | `agent_identifier_mode`, `agent_monitoring_mode`, `attention_running_indicator`, `claude_agent_icon`, `codex_agent_icon`, `antigravity_agent_icon`, `show_inferred_title_icons` | Agent detect, Titles | yes |
| `[ui]` look | `color_scheme`, `motion_level`, `sidebar_density`, `use_stable_glyphs`, `show_context_menu_icons` | Kernel theme and menus | yes |
| `[ui]` toolbar | `agent_toolbar_enabled`, `show_toolbar_labels`, `last_prompt_enabled`, `last_prompt_max_lines` | Agent toolbar | yes |
| `[ui]` other | `agent_debug_menu_enabled`, `terminal_text_selection_enabled` | Diagnostics, Terminal | yes |
| `[ui]` progress | `progress_monitor_enabled`, `progress_max_lines`, `completed_progress_hide_after_seconds`, `task_progress_frames` | Progress | yes (server-owned) |
| `[ui.icons]` | one key per icon role | Tree, Agent toolbar | yes |
| `[theme]` | `accent_bg`, `accent_fg`, `border_focused`, `border_unfocused` | Kernel theme | yes |
| `[detection]` | `working_poll_seconds`, `idle_poll_seconds`, `auto_answer_interstitial_prompts`, `[[detection.custom_signatures]]` | Agent detect | yes (server-owned) |
| `[cost]` | `metric`, `quota_window`, `calibration`, `fixed_cuts`, `burn_cuts`, `budget_usd`, `quota_fixed_cuts`, `quota_burn_cuts`, `quota_budget_percent`, `history_days`, `sparkline_window_minutes`, `sparkline_cells`, `level_glyph`, `level_dollars`, `meter`, `sparkline`, `group_totals`, `detail_card`, `header_total`, `burn_marker`, `sort_by_cost`, `prices` | Cost | yes |
| `[remote_compaction]` | `enabled`, `automatic`, `threshold_percent`, `claude_technique`, `codex_technique`, `other_technique`, `custom_prompt`, `tail_tokens`, `protected_recent_tool_tokens`, `tool_result_chars`, `redact_secrets`, `summarizer_context_tokens`, `pause_timeout_seconds`, `cooldown_minutes`, `keep_backups`, `privacy_banner_dismissed` | Compaction | yes |
| `[keyboard]`, `[keybindings]` | `[keyboard]` holds the prefix keys and the preset; `[keybindings]` holds one key per action id, named by the action id in the key reference | Kernel keymap, Keys and help | yes |
| `[terminal]` | `scrollback_budget_mib`, `engine_memory_budget_mib`, `new_pane_directory`, `smart_copy_light`, `smart_copy_light_key` | Terminal, Smart copy | yes (`engine_memory_budget_mib` for new panes) |
| `[editor]` | `line_display`, `show_line_numbers`, `show_minimap`, `autosave_enabled`, `autosave_delay_ms`, `markdown_rendered_by_default` | Editor | yes |
| `[session]` | `recovery_policy`, `backups_enabled` | Sessions, kernel snapshot writer | yes (server-owned) |
| `[git]` | `default_where`, `branch_prefix`, `worktree_location_template`, `default_base`, `branch_line`, `setup_command`, `default_close_policy` | Worktrees | yes |
| `[kanban_board]` | `card_preview_lines`, `minimum_column_width` | Kanban | yes |
| `[sound]`: `source`, `file`, `design`, `events`. `[notifications]`: `enabled`, `agent_finished`, `approval_required`, `task_succeeded`, `task_failed`, `suppress_redundant_task_outcomes`, `task_coalesce_seconds` | Notifications | yes (server-owned) |
| `[voice]` | `enabled`, `api_key`, `model`, `voice`, `reasoning_effort`, `input_mode`, `vad_eagerness`, `input_device_name`, `output_device_name`, `output_volume_percent`, `confirm_terminal_submissions`, `pause_media_while_active`, `custom_prompt` | Voice | yes |
| `[reset_planning]` | `monitor_claude`, `monitor_codex`, `time_style` | Cost | yes |
| `[inference]` | `selected_provider`, `title_style`, `restructure_prompt_token_limit`, `instructions`, and the provider tables `kilo_gateway`, `ollama`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `openrouter` | Inference, Titles | yes |
| `[inference.instructions]` | seven instruction inputs | Inference, Titles, Recap, Smart copy | yes |
| `[triggers]` | eight event keys, each with an action list; the key names are the event names in the Triggers tab of `src/docs/settings.md` | Titles | yes |
| `[text_triggers]` | rule list | Text triggers | yes (server-owned) |
| `[agent_setup]` | the global instruction file paths and the never-ask choices; the field names are those of the Setup tab in `src/docs/settings.md` | Agent setup | yes |
| `[debug]` | `file_logging_enabled` | Kernel logger, Diagnostics | yes |
| `[api]` | `port` | Kernel HTTP listener | at next server start |
| `[onboarding]` | guided-setup progress, no credentials | Settings | yes |

Credentials: keys with secrets (API keys) keep their present storage. A plugin that reads a tab sees `"<redacted>"` in place of every secret (see [kernel settings](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/)). A plugin that must send a credential does so through a service that the owner provides (for example the Inference plugin calls the provider itself), never by reading the secret.

### Plugin tables in `config.toml`

```toml
# config.toml
config_version = 1

[plugins]
auto_update = "notify"          # off, notify, install
auto_update_interval_hours = 24
channel = "stable"
metered = false

[plugins.limits]
event_queue = 2048

[plugins."com.example.notes"]
density = "compact"

[plugins."com.example.notes".limits]
memory_mib = 64
```

- `[plugins]` keys are owned by the plugin host. Other keys are refused with `config.unknown-key`.
- `[plugins.limits]` sets a limit for every plugin. `[plugins."<id>".limits]` sets it for one plugin and wins. The effective value is `min(ceiling, first set of [plugins."<id>".limits] value, [plugins.limits] value, manifest value, default)` (LIF-143).
- `[plugins."<id>"]` holds the plugin's own settings. The reserved key `limits` is the only sub-table the host reads there.
- A core plugin keeps its values in the kernel tables listed above, not in `[plugins."ilium.core.<name>"]`. A core plugin MAY have a plugin table for values that are new in the plugin build, and each such key is listed on its page.
- The always-granted `settings` import reads and writes only the plugin's own table. It never sees `[plugins.limits]` of another plugin.

### Project YAML

`<project>/.ilium/config.yaml` keeps its four keys. Unknown keys are preserved.

| Key | Owner | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `project name` | Titles (project naming) | Tree |
| `project icon` | Titles | Tree |
| `show project separators` | Tree | Tree |
| `animation` | Ambient look | Scenes, kernel painter |
| `plugins.<id>` | the plugin | the plugin (project scope of its settings) |

The `animation` key holds the scene `kind`, the shared look and the per-scene controls. A scene control is stored under `animation.scene.<scene-id>`. The shared look is stored once, under `animation.look`, and is never repeated per scene. The file is written under an exclusive lock, and a plugin write goes through the same lock, so the kernel and a plugin never write at the same moment.

### Session snapshots

The snapshot is `<project>/.ilium/sessions/<session name>.json`. It is written by the kernel, atomically, 750 ms after the last change at most. At the baseline commit the file has `version` 3 and these fields.

| Field | Meaning | Owner in the plugin build |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | Format version of the whole file | Kernel |
| `tree` | Nodes, groups, titles, order | Kernel |
| `panes` | One entry per pane: `node_id` and `kind` (shell, agent with its resume command, editor, board) | Kernel |
| `agent_debug_logs` | Pane histories for the agent debug menu | Diagnostics section |
| `progress_monitors` | Durable monitor registrations and result delivery state | Progress section |
| `workspace_close_preferences` | Close policy of a worktree workspace | Worktrees section |
| `tree` pane fields `scheduled_input`, `prompt_queue` | Pending scheduled input and prompt queue | Scheduler section |

Version 4 adds one field:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin_sections` | object, key is plugin id | One entry per plugin that offered a section. Each entry is `{ "schema_version": <int>, "data": <json> }` |

The migration from 3 to 4 moves the three top-level fields and the two pane fields into `plugin_sections` under the ids of their owners (`ilium.core.diagnostics`, `ilium.core.progress`, `ilium.core.worktrees`, `ilium.core.scheduler`). The scheduler section is `plugin_sections["ilium.core.scheduler"] = {"schema_version":1,"data":{"panes":[{"pane_id":<n>,"scheduled_input":<v3 value or null>,"prompt_queue":<v3 value>}]}}`. The kernel keeps publishing the objective signal "scheduled input pending" from that section while the scheduler is disabled. It runs once, in the kernel, while no plugin exists. The old fields are removed from the file after the old file is kept as `<name>.pre-migration.3`. If the owner plugin is not installed, the section is kept as stored JSON and written back unchanged for 30 days of server time, then dropped with a warning in the lifecycle log (see Snapshot sections).

### Snapshot sections

One mechanism stores plugin state in a session snapshot: the extension point `ilium.core.sessions/snapshot-sections`. The earlier idea of storing opaque bytes at `deactivate` is not a persistence path. The bytes returned by `deactivate(restore)` live in the host's memory, are handed to the new instance on an update or a restart of the same session, and are lost when the server stops (see [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/)). The rules:

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Entry | `{ "id": "<section id>", "title": "...", "max_bytes": <n> }` contributed to `snapshot-sections`. `max_bytes` is at most 262144. The owner is the contributing plugin. One section per plugin in v1 |
| Write | The plugin implements the request `snapshot-section` in its handler and returns JSON. It is asked at every snapshot, at most once per 750 ms |
| Size | At most `max_bytes` per section, and never more than 256 KiB (262144 bytes). A larger value is dropped with `snapshot.section-too-large` and the previous stored value is kept |
| Version | The plugin returns `schema_version`. The host stores it with the data |
| Read | At boot step 7 the host sends `restore-section { schema_version, data }` to the plugin before any other event |
| Unknown version | If the plugin does not accept the `schema_version`, it answers `section-unsupported`. The section stays unchanged in the file |
| Missing plugin | A section of an uninstalled plugin, including one created by the 3 to 4 migration, is written back unchanged for 30 days of server time, then dropped with a warning in the lifecycle log |
| Crash safety | The kernel writes the last stored data of a failed plugin unchanged. A failed plugin never blocks the snapshot |

[COR-032] covers this. The session storage bucket of the `storage` import is a second, separate mechanism: key-value data that a plugin owns and the host copies into the snapshot as the bucket `session`. A core plugin uses snapshot sections for state that other parts of Ilium must see at restore time, such as scheduled sends (snapshot section `ilium.core.scheduler`) and progress monitors, and the bucket for its private state.

### Data files

| File | Location | Format | Written by | Plugin owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config.toml` | `<config>/config.toml` | TOML | Kernel, tab owners | per tab | `ILIUM_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the folder |
| `.ilium/config.yaml` | `<project>/.ilium/config.yaml` | YAML | Kernel, Ambient look, Titles | per key | Unknown keys preserved |
| Session snapshot | `<project>/.ilium/sessions/<name>.json` | JSON | Kernel | Sessions offers sections | Atomic |
| Pre-restore copies | `<project>/.ilium/sessions/<name>.pre-restore.json` and `.pre-restore.1.json` | JSON | Kernel | none | Last two starts |
| Rolling backups | `<project>/.ilium/backups/<name>/<ms>-<uuid>.json` | JSON | Kernel | Sessions (policy) | When `backups_enabled` |
| Lifecycle log | `<project>/.ilium/logs/<name>.lifecycle.jsonl` | JSONL | Kernel | Sessions | Rotated once at 8 MiB |
| Worktrees | `<repo parent>/<main checkout name>.worktrees/<branch slug>` | Git worktree | Worktrees | Worktrees | From the template `{repo_parent}/{repo_name}.worktrees/{branch_slug}`; created by `new-pane --worktree` |
| Chatroom | `<project>/CHATROOM.md` and `CHATROOM.archive.md` | Markdown | Chatroom | Chatroom | `/CHATROOM.md` and `/CHATROOM.archive.md` are added to `.gitignore` |
| Boards | any `.md` path the user picks | Markdown | Kanban | Kanban | Every change is saved to the file |
| Debug logs | `$ILIUM_DEBUG_LOG_DIR/…` | text | Kernel | Diagnostics | Five newest per session |
| Plugin storage | `<data>/plugins/storage/<id>.db`, `<project>/.ilium/plugins/<id>.db` | key-value | the plugin | the plugin | See [Plugin files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| Claude statusline registry | `<data>/claude-model-statusline-projects.json` | JSON | Agent detect (client side) | Agent detect | Holds session id, project path, model id |

All paths follow the folder rules of [Plugin files on disk](/pages/reference-plugin-files/). A core plugin never writes to a path outside this table without a grant (`fs.write:<scope>`).

### Agent configuration files that Ilium writes

These files belong to the agent tools, not to Ilium. Ilium edits only its own marked block, or its own entry, and leaves the rest of the file unchanged. Agent setup owns all of them, except where noted.

| File | Scope | What Ilium writes | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | global | Marked Chatroom and Progress instruction blocks | Agent setup |
| `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | global | The same blocks. Paths come from `[agent_setup]` | Agent setup |
| `<project>/CLAUDE.md`, `<project>/AGENTS.md` | project | The same blocks. A symlink is followed and written once | Agent setup |
| `<project>/.claude/settings.local.json` | project | Chatroom hook entries. A temporary `statusLine` entry that captures the model, restored on exit | Agent setup (hooks), Agent detect (statusLine) |
| `<project>/.codex/hooks.json` | project | Chatroom hook entries | Agent setup |
| `<project>/.gitignore` | project | `/CHATROOM.md` and `/CHATROOM.archive.md` lines | Chatroom |
| Agent session files (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity) | global | Written only by Session convert (new files) and Compaction (resume files). Existing files are never edited | Session convert, Compaction |

A write to any of these files uses `fs.write` with the scope `agent-config:<agent>` or `project`, with a revision check, so a change made by another process in the meantime is detected and the write is refused with `fs.conflict`. See [fs atomic writes](/pages/api-fs-atomic-and-tail/).

### A worked migration

A user has a build before plugins with this `config.toml` and snapshot, and installs the plugin build.

```toml
[terminal]
scrollback_budget_mib = 16

[detection]
working_poll_seconds = 1
```

1. The server starts. It reads `config.toml`. No `config_version`, so it is 0. No key changes. The server adds nothing until the user changes a setting.
2. The server reads the snapshot with `version` 3 and 2 progress monitors. The kernel keeps `main.pre-migration.3.json`, then writes version 4 with `plugin_sections["ilium.core.progress"] = { "schema_version": 1, "data": { "monitors": [ … ] } }`.
3. The host starts. Progress is a startup plugin. At step 7 it receives `restore-section`. It runs one probe per monitor before it reinstalls it (the same rule as today).
4. The user opens Settings. The Terminal tab shows 16 for the scrollback. The Terminal plugin reads `[terminal]` through `settings.read-kernel:terminal` and has the same value. No copy exists in `[plugins."ilium.core.terminal"]`.
5. The user changes the value to 32. The kernel writes `[terminal] scrollback_budget_mib = 32`, sends `kernel-settings-changed` and the plugin reads again.

A short sample of the plugin side of step 3:

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

const SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1;

impl Handler for ProgressPlugin {
    fn on_request(&mut self, request: Request) -> Response {
        match request.kind.as_str() {
            "snapshot-section" => Response::json(json!({
                "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
                "data": { "monitors": self.monitors_as_json() }
            })),
            "restore-section" => {
                let schema_version = request.field_u64("schema_version").unwrap_or(0);
                if schema_version != u64::from(SCHEMA_VERSION) {
                    return Response::error("section-unsupported");
                }
                let data: Value = request.field_json("data").unwrap_or(Value::Null);
                self.restore_monitors(&data);
                Response::ok()
            }
            _ => Response::error("unknown-request"),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Request, type Response } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

const SCHEMA_VERSION = 1;
let monitors: unknown[] = [];

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate() {},
  onRequest(request: Request): Response {
    if (request.kind === 'snapshot-section') {
      return { tag: 'json', val: { schema_version: SCHEMA_VERSION, data: { monitors } } };
    }
    if (request.kind === 'restore-section') {
      const body = request.body as { schema_version?: number; data?: { monitors?: unknown[] } };
      if (body.schema_version !== SCHEMA_VERSION) return { tag: 'error', val: 'section-unsupported' };
      monitors = body.data?.monitors ?? [];
      return { tag: 'ok' };
    }
    return { tag: 'error', val: 'unknown-request' };
  },
});
```

The request names are the only contract here. The SDK helper names follow [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Result | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Two plugins declare `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for one tab | The second install is refused | `manifest.settings-owner` |
| A T2 package declares `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` | Install refused | `manifest.grant-tier` |
| A write is outside the range of a row | Nothing is written | `settings.invalid-value` |
| A write names a key that belongs to another tab of the same table | Nothing is written | `settings.key-not-owned` |
| A write names a key the kernel does not know in that tab | Nothing is written | `settings.unknown-key` |
| `config.toml` has a table the build does not know | Preserved | none |
| The migration from 3 to 4 is interrupted | The next start reads the old file and runs it again | none |
| A snapshot section is larger than its `max_bytes` (at most 256 KiB) | The section is dropped, the old value is kept | `snapshot.section-too-large` |
| A section's plugin rejects its `schema_version` | The section is kept unchanged | `section-unsupported` |
| The `.ilium/config.yaml` lock is held by another process | The write waits up to 2 s, then fails | `fs.locked` |
| An agent file changed during a write | The write is refused, the user is told | `fs.conflict` |

### Requirements

- [COR-030] A kernel tab MUST have at most one plugin that holds `settings.write-kernel:<tab>`, and a second declaration MUST fail with `manifest.settings-owner`. Test: install two fixture T1 plugins that ask for `settings.write-kernel:terminal`; the second install fails.
- [COR-031] `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` MUST be T1 only and high risk, and `settings.read-kernel:<tab>` MUST be available to every tier. Test: a T2 package with the write grant fails with `manifest.grant-tier`; a T3 package with the read grant installs.
- [COR-032] Plugin state in a snapshot MUST be stored only through `snapshot-sections` with a `schema_version`, a section larger than its `max_bytes` (at most 256 KiB) MUST be dropped without losing the previous value, and a failed plugin MUST NOT block the snapshot. Test: write a 300 KiB section, check the old value stays; crash the plugin, check that the file still has the last value.
- [COR-033] No key in `config.toml` or `.ilium/config.yaml` MAY be renamed or moved by the plugin build, and the plugin build MUST preserve unknown keys and tables. Test: run the plugin build on a fixture config with an unknown key, change one setting, compare the files with a diff that must show only that change.

# Conformance suite

## Conformance suite

The conformance suite is a fixed list of cases that check one claim each about the contract `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. It has two uses. A plugin author runs it to learn that a built plugin follows the contract. A maintainer of Ilium or of an SDK runs it to learn that a host or an SDK still follows the contract after a change.

Terms:

- **Case**: one check with an id, a setup, a stimulus and an expected result.
- **Subject**: the thing under test. It is a plugin component, an SDK, or the host.
- **Verdict**: `pass`, `fail` or `skip` for one case.

## You will need

- A built component in `dist/` for plugin subjects. See [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/).
- The harness from [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/). The suite runs on `FakeHost` in component mode.

## Running the suite

`ilium plugin test --conformance [--subject <plugin|sdk|host>] [--case <id>]`

| Subject | Needs | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin` (default) | `dist/*.wasm` | That the component behaves within the contract limits |
| `sdk` | The SDK source tree | That the SDK maps every contract rule to its API |
| `host` | A running session | That the host enforces every contract rule |

- **[DEV-600]** `--subject plugin` MUST run only the cases marked `plugin` in the catalogue below. It MUST skip cases that need a grant the plugin does not request, with the reason `grant-not-requested`.
- **[DEV-601]** `--subject sdk` and `--subject host` MUST be refused with exit 2 and `usage.subject-unavailable` in a normal install. They are available only in the Ilium source tree, where the maintainer enables them with `ILIUM_CONFORMANCE_MAINTAINER=1`.
- **[DEV-602]** The suite MUST print one `conformance` record per case, then a `summary` record. A `fail` verdict makes the exit code 3. A suite with only `pass` and `skip` exits 0.
- **[DEV-603]** `--case <id>` MUST run one case. An unknown id MUST fail with exit 2 and `usage.invalid-value`.
- **[DEV-604]** The case ids MUST be stable. A case MUST NOT change meaning. A changed rule gets a new case id, and the old id is retired in the retired list at the end of this page.
- **[DEV-605]** Every case MUST be deterministic. It MUST use the fake clock and the default seed.
- **[DEV-606]** One case MUST finish within 10,000 ms of wall time. A longer case is a `fail` with the message `case exceeded 10000 ms`.
- **[DEV-607]** Durations in case expectations are fake-clock milliseconds, except the call time measured in fuel. A case that needs a deadline breach MUST use the built-in probe plugin `conformance-probe.wasm` with its fuel-burn import, never the plugin under test.

A record:

```json
{"type":"conformance","case":"CONF-LIFE-02","title":"activate stays under its deadline","subject":"plugin","verdict":"pass","duration_ms":41}
{"type":"summary","passed":31,"failed":0,"skipped":5,"duration_ms":18420}
```

## Case catalogue

Case ids have the form `CONF-<AREA>-<nn>`. The tables list the id, the claim, the stimulus and the expected result. The subject column says who can run the case: `P` plugin, `S` SDK, `H` host.

### Lifecycle

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-LIFE-01 | `activate` runs once before any event | Activate, then deliver one event | `activate` call precedes `on-events` | P S H |
| CONF-LIFE-02 | `activate` stays under its deadline | Subject P: activate the subject plugin and measure the fuel time. Subject H: the probe plugin burns fuel for 2,100 ms in `activate`. | P: fuel time under the effective deadline. H: `trap.deadline`. | P H |
| CONF-LIFE-03 | `deactivate` over 500 ms is cut | The probe plugin burns fuel for 600 ms in `deactivate` | Instance dropped, restore bytes discarded, not counted as a failure (`failures()` unchanged) | H |
| CONF-LIFE-04 | An error from `activate` fails the start | `activate` returns an error | Plugin not active, error code logged | P S H |
| CONF-LIFE-05 | Deactivate reason is one of the five delivered reasons | Deactivate with each of `shutdown`, `disabled`, `upgrade`, `revoked` and `granted` | The plugin sees that reason. `crash-restart` is reserved and never delivered. | S H |

### Events and submissions

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-EVT-01 | A batch holds at most 256 events | Queue 600 events | Batches of at most 256 | H |
| CONF-EVT-02 | A batch of events stays under its deadline | Subject P: deliver `sample_batch(256)` and measure the fuel time. Subject H: the probe plugin burns fuel for 25 ms in `on-events`. | P: fuel time under 20 ms. H: `trap.deadline`. | P H |
| CONF-EVT-03 | Coalesced events keep the newest state | Send three renames for one node | One event with the last name | H |
| CONF-EVT-04 | `events-dropped` follows a full queue | Fill the queue past 1,024 | Next batch starts with `events-dropped` | H |
| CONF-EVT-05 | Ungranted events are not delivered | Remove the grant, send the event | No delivery | P H |
| CONF-EVT-06 | More than 256 submissions trap | Return 257 submissions | `trap.submission-batch` | P S H |
| CONF-EVT-07 | Batch refusal cancels the rest | Third submission is invalid | Others `refused(cancelled)` with `batch refused: submission 2` | S H |
| CONF-EVT-08 | Dedup key repeats are duplicates | Same key twice in 10 minutes | Second is `duplicate` | S H |
| CONF-EVT-09 | A dedup key outside the charset is refused | Key with a space | `refused(plugin-error{code: invalid-argument, message starting "dedup-key-invalid:"})` | S H |
| CONF-EVT-10 | Outcomes arrive as `request-completed` | Submit one intent | One event with the same correlation | P S H |

### Grants

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-GRANT-01 | An import whose grant the user declined is refused | The manifest requests `fs.read:project`, the test declines it, the plugin calls `fs.read` | `Err(not-permitted)` | P S H |
| CONF-GRANT-02 | Revocation takes effect at once | Revoke, then call | `Err(not-permitted)` for an import, `refused(plugin-error{code: not-permitted})` for an intent | H |
| CONF-GRANT-03 | Grant arguments are matched exactly | Grant `fs.read:project`, read `FsPath{scope: "data"}` | `Err(not-permitted)` | H |
| CONF-GRANT-04 | A grant absent from the manifest cannot be gained | `host.grant_now` of a grant not in the manifest | `harness.grant-not-declared` | H |
| CONF-GRANT-05 | A function of a capability never requested traps | Call a function of a capability the manifest never requested | `trap.import-not-requested` | H |

### Views

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-VIEW-01 | A render stays under its deadline | Subject P: render each declared view at 80x24 and measure the fuel time. Subject H: the probe plugin burns fuel for 15 ms in `render`. | P: fuel time under 10 ms. H: last good render stays, `trap.deadline` counted. | P H |
| CONF-VIEW-02 | A view is pure | Render twice | Equal screens | P S |
| CONF-VIEW-03 | Node limits are enforced | Return a tree of 4,097 nodes, then one of 4,096 | `trap.invalid-ui-tree` at 4,097 nodes; 4,096 renders | H |
| CONF-VIEW-04 | An action with an unknown key is dropped | Click an action key the view never set | Not delivered | H |

### Storage, memory and state

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-STORE-01 | Storage survives a restart | Put, trap, restart, get | Value present | H |
| CONF-STORE-02 | A value over 1 MiB is refused | Put a value of 1,048,577 bytes | `Err(quota-exceeded)` | S H |
| CONF-STORE-03 | A bucket over 16 MiB is refused | Fill a bucket to 16 MiB plus 1 byte | `Err(quota-exceeded)` | S H |
| CONF-MEM-01 | Memory over `memory_mib` traps | The probe plugin allocates 40 MiB with the default 32 | `trap.memory` (see the trap code table of [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#trap-codes)) | H |
| CONF-MEM-02 | The ceiling is 128 MiB for T2 and T3 | Request 256 in the manifest | Install succeeds; the value is clamped to 128 MiB and the clamp is logged | H |

### Restart rule

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-RESTART-01 | First failure restarts after 1 s | Trap once | Restart at 1 s | H |
| CONF-RESTART-02 | Second failure restarts after 5 s | Trap twice in 10 minutes | Restart at 5 s | H |
| CONF-RESTART-03 | Third failure in 10 minutes disables | Trap three times | Plugin disabled | H |
| CONF-RESTART-04 | Old failures expire | Traps at 0, 6 and 11 minutes of fake time | Restarts after 1 s, 5 s and 5 s; never disabled | H |
| CONF-RESTART-05 | A lone old failure does not count | Traps at 0 and 11 minutes of fake time | Both restart after 1 s | H |

### Package and manifest

| Id | Claim | Stimulus | Expected | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONF-PKG-01 | A package is deterministic | Pack twice from one build | Equal bytes | P |
| CONF-PKG-02 | The api-version section matches the manifest | Read the custom section | `0.1.0` as three u16 big-endian | P |
| CONF-PKG-03 | A hash mismatch is refused at install | Change one byte of a file | `manifest.file-hash` | H |
| CONF-PKG-04 | An unsigned package installs only as T3 | Install without a signature | Tier T3 with the dev badge | H |
| CONF-PKG-05 | A manifest with an unknown key is refused | Add `colour` at top level | `manifest.unknown-key` | H |

- **[DEV-610]** The catalogue above MUST be the minimum. A release of the suite MAY add cases and MUST NOT remove a case without a retirement note.
- **[DEV-611]** Cases for the restart rule MUST use fake time. No case waits for real seconds.
- **[DEV-612]** A case for a limit MUST test the value just under the limit (pass) and the value just over (fail), unless the table says otherwise.
- **[DEV-613]** A `skip` MUST carry a reason: `grant-not-requested`, `side-not-built`, `subject-mismatch` or `needs-session`.

## Writing a plugin-specific conformance case

A plugin author can add cases to the project. A case is a test function that uses `conformance::case`.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::testing::{conformance, FakeHost};

#[test]
fn event_budget_holds() {
    conformance::case("PROJ-EVT-01", "handler stays under 20 ms", |host: &mut FakeHost| {
        host.activate::<Plugin>();
        host.deliver(conformance::sample_batch(256));
        conformance::assert_within_budget(host, "event", 20);
    });
}
```

```ts
import { test } from 'bun:test';
import { conformance, type FakeHost } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing';

test('event budget holds', async () => {
  await conformance.case('PROJ-EVT-01', 'handler stays under 20 ms', async (host: FakeHost) => {
    await host.activateModule('../src/server');
    host.deliver(conformance.sampleBatch(256));
    conformance.assertWithinBudget(host, 'event', 20);
  });
});
```

`conformance::case(id: &str, title: &str, body: impl FnOnce(&mut FakeHost))` in Rust and `conformance.case(id, title, async (host: FakeHost) => ...)` in TypeScript build the host the same way: `FakeHost::for_manifest("manifest.json")` in component mode with the default seed. The case receives the host as its argument and never builds one.

- **[DEV-624]** `conformance::case` and `conformance.case` MUST pass a `FakeHost` for `manifest.json` in component mode with the default seed to the body. The body MUST NOT build its own host.
- **[DEV-620]** A project case id MUST start with `PROJ-` so it can never clash with a suite case id.
- **[DEV-621]** `sample_batch(n)` MUST return `n` valid events for the grants of the host, using the fuzz generator with the host seed.
- **[DEV-622]** `assert_within_budget(host, kind, millis)` MUST compare the recorded time of the last call of that kind with `millis`. `kind` is one of `'event'`, `'render'`, `'activate'` and `'deactivate'`, and `millis` is an integer in milliseconds (Rust `u32`, TypeScript `number`). It MUST be skipped in native mode with the reason `needs-component`.

## Record fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | Always `conformance` for a case record |
| `case` | string | Case id |
| `title` | string | The claim, as in the catalogue |
| `subject` | string | `plugin`, `sdk` or `host` |
| `verdict` | string | `pass`, `fail` or `skip` |
| `reason` | string | For `skip`, one of the reasons in DEV-613. For `fail`, the message. |
| `duration_ms` | integer | Time the case took |

- **[DEV-640]** A `fail` record MUST carry `expected` and `actual` fields that describe the difference, as strings of at most 200 characters.
- **[DEV-641]** The `summary` record MUST list `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` and `duration_ms`. `passed` plus `failed` plus `skipped` MUST equal the number of case records.
- **[DEV-642]** Case order in the output MUST be the order of the catalogue on this page, area by area.

## Worked example: one case end to end

Case `CONF-EVT-06` checks that 257 submissions trap. The suite builds a probe batch of 257 submissions, delivers it to the component and expects `trap.submission-batch`.

```json
{"type":"conformance","case":"CONF-EVT-06","title":"more than 256 submissions trap","subject":"plugin","verdict":"pass","duration_ms":41}
```

For a plugin that returns at most 10 submissions per batch, the case drives the probe plugin, because the plugin itself never returns 257. The case therefore checks the host guard, and a plugin result `skip` with the reason `subject-mismatch` applies when the plugin world has no way to run the probe.

- **[DEV-643]** A case that cannot drive the plugin to the claimed state MUST be a `skip` with the reason `subject-mismatch`, never a `pass`.

## The edge of the suite

The suite checks the contract. It does not check:

- the look of a view on a real terminal;
- the speed on a given machine, except through the budgets above;
- the behaviour of a core plugin, which has its own tests.

## Using the suite in CI

Add `ilium plugin test --conformance --json` to the pipeline. A fail verdict exits 3. See [CI recipes](/pages/guide-ci-recipes/).

## Retired case ids

None. The first release of the suite is ids as listed.

## Edge cases

- A plugin with only a scene side skips all event and grant cases that need a server or client side, with `side-not-built`.
- A debug build runs slower than a release build and can fail a budget case. Use the release build for conformance. `--conformance` MUST refuse a debug build with exit 2 and `usage.release-build-required`, unless `--allow-debug` is given.
- **[DEV-630]** `--conformance` MUST run in component mode only. It MUST NOT run in native mode, because the limits are not enforced there.

## See also

- [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/)
- [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)
- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)
- [Debugging tools](/pages/reference-debugging-tools/)

API checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
