# Debugging tools

## Debugging tools

This page defines the tools that show what a plugin did: the log, the trace, the widget tree inspector, the profiler and the memory view. It also defines the log line format, where logs are stored and how they rotate. The task guide is [Debugging plugins](/pages/debugging/). The commands are in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/).

Terms:

- **Log**: text lines that the plugin and the host write about a plugin.
- **Trace**: a record of what crossed the boundary between the host and one plugin instance: events in, submissions out, host calls, outcomes.
- **Inspector**: a view of the widget tree a plugin returned.
- **Profile**: the time each export spent over a period.

## You will need

- A running session for every tool on this page except the log files, which can be read after the session ends.
- A plugin installed with `ilium plugin dev` to see debug-level lines and unredacted traces.

## The log

### Line format

A log line is plain text, one line per entry.

`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss level(5) side(6) plugin-id message`

| Part | Width | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Date and time | 19 | Local time of the machine, European order. |
| level | 5, left aligned | `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. Padded with spaces. |
| side | 6, left aligned | `server`, `client`, `scene` or `host` for lines the host wrote about the plugin. |
| plugin-id | variable | The plugin id. |
| message | rest | One line. A newline in a message is written as `\n`. |

One space separates the parts. Example:

```text
2030-01-01 09:14:02 info  server example.notes activate: ready
2030-01-01 09:14:09 warn  server example.notes storage near quota: 912 KiB of 1 MiB
2030-01-01 09:15:40 error host   example.notes restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3 in 10 minutes)
```

- **[DEV-650]** Every log line MUST follow the format above. A host line MUST use the side `host`.
- **[DEV-651]** A message longer than 16 KiB (16,384 bytes) MUST be cut at the last whole UTF-8 character that keeps the entry within the limit, and the entry MUST end with `…[truncated]`.
- **[DEV-652]** The thresholds in order are `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. A line is written when its level is at or above the threshold.
- **[DEV-653]** The default threshold MUST be `info`. A plugin installed with `dev` has the default `debug`. `debug` and `trace` lines at a threshold of `info` are dropped, not stored.
- **[DEV-654]** `ilium plugin log-level` and the environment variable `ILIUM_PLUGIN_LOG_LEVEL` MUST set the threshold. The command wins over the variable.
- **[DEV-655]** The restart message MUST be `restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3 in 10 minutes)` at level `warn`, with the delay and the failure count of that restart. The last failure MUST log `disabled after 3 failures in 10 minutes`.
- **[DEV-656]** The log rate limit is 200 lines per second for an ordinary plugin and 1,000 for a trusted T1 plugin. Lines over the limit MUST be dropped and counted. Once per second, when lines were dropped, the host MUST write one `warn` line `<n> lines dropped in the last second`. That line does not use the rate budget.
- **[DEV-657]** When the host event queue of a plugin is full, the host MUST write one line with level `error` and the message `event queue full: dropped N events`.
- **[DEV-658]** A plugin MUST NOT be able to write a line with the side `host`.

### Storage and rotation

Logs live at `<ilium-state>/plugins/logs/<session-slug>/<plugin-id>.log`. `<ilium-state>` is the Ilium state folder, shown by `ilium plugin doctor`.

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| File size before rotation | 4 MiB |
| Files kept | 5: `<plugin-id>.log` and `.log.1` to `.log.4` |
| Retention after uninstall | 7 days |
| `uninstall --purge` | Deletes the logs at once |
| Permissions | Owner only |

- **[DEV-660]** When the active file reaches 4 MiB, the host MUST rename `.log.3` to `.log.4`, `.log.2` to `.log.3`, `.log.1` to `.log.2`, the active file to `.log.1`, and start a new file. The oldest file is deleted.
- **[DEV-661]** The host MUST delete the logs of an uninstalled plugin 7 days after the uninstall, unless the plugin is installed again.
- **[DEV-662]** `ilium plugin logs` MUST read the files oldest first across rotation, so the output is in time order.
- **[DEV-663]** The log folder MUST be created with owner-only access.
- **[DEV-664]** Logs MUST NOT contain granted data such as file contents or storage values unless the plugin wrote them on purpose. The host lines never include payloads.

### Reading the log

`ilium plugin logs <id> [--level <level>] [--since <time>] [--side <side>] [--follow] [--tail <n>] [--json]`

- **[DEV-665]** `--level` MUST show lines at or above that level. `--since` MUST take `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` or a duration such as `10m`.
- **[DEV-666]** `--tail <n>` MUST show the last n lines and default to 200.
- **[DEV-667]** With `--json` each line becomes `{"type":"log","time":"...","level":"...","side":"...","plugin":"...","message":"..."}` followed by one `summary` record.

## The trace

The trace is a ring buffer per plugin instance. It is on by default.

| Kind | Content |
|---|---|
| `event` | An event batch delivered to the plugin: count and event tags |
| `submission` | A submission the plugin returned: intent name, correlation, dedup key |
| `outcome` | An outcome: correlation and outcome tag |
| `host-call` | An import call: name, duration, result tag |
| `render` | A render: target, size, duration, node count |
| `trap` | A trap: code and export |
| `lifecycle` | Activate, deactivate, restart, disable |

- **[DEV-670]** The ring buffer MUST hold 1,024 records per instance. When full, the oldest record is dropped.
- **[DEV-671]** Tracing MUST be on for every instance. It MUST add no more than 5 percent to the time of an event batch.
- **[DEV-672]** Payloads MUST be redacted in a normal trace. A redacted payload prints as `<redacted N bytes>`. Tags, names, counts and durations are never redacted.
- **[DEV-673]** `--unredacted` MUST work only for a plugin installed with `dev`. It MUST be refused with `trace.unredacted-denied` for all others.
- **[DEV-674]** A trace record MUST carry a sequence number that increases by one per record per instance, and the fake or real time in milliseconds.
- **[DEV-675]** `ilium plugin trace --record <file>` MUST write the recorded inputs as a replay file in the format of [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/).
- **[DEV-676]** The trace of an instance that restarted MUST keep the records of earlier instances, marked with the instance number.

A trace in text form:

<figure>
<pre class="term">
seq  time(ms)  kind        detail
 41  000120    event       batch 2: pane-created, node-renamed
 42  000121    submission  set-decoration corr=17
 43  000122    outcome     corr=17 ok
 44  000900    host-call   storage.put 0.2 ms ok
 45  001004    render      panel main 62x12 3.1 ms 8 nodes
 46  001510    trap        trap.deadline in on-events
 47  001511    lifecycle   restart 1 of 3, delay 1 s
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. Output of ilium plugin trace example.notes --last 7.</figcaption>
</figure>

## The widget tree inspector

`ilium plugin inspect <id> --view <target>` prints the tree the plugin returned for a target, with keys and styles.

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭ Widget tree: panel main ─────────────────────╮
│ stack  vertical                              │
│   text  "Open notes: 3"        style=title   │
│   list  rows=3 selected=1                    │
│     row  key=n1  "Inbox"                     │
│     row  key=n2  "Plans"       <- selected   │
│   button  key=add  "Add note"                │
│ nodes 8 of 2000   depth 3 of 16              │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The inspector view of panel main.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **[DEV-680]** The inspector MUST print the last tree the plugin returned for the target, not a new render. If the plugin never rendered the target, it MUST fail with `inspect.no-render`.
- **[DEV-681]** Each node MUST show its kind, its key when it has one, its main text and its style name. Selected rows MUST be marked.
- **[DEV-682]** The footer MUST show the node count against the node limit and the depth against the depth limit of [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).
- **[DEV-683]** `--json` MUST print the tree as one `tree` record with nested `children`.
- **[DEV-684]** The inspector MUST read the tree without changing focus or selection.

## The profiler

`ilium plugin profile <id> --duration <seconds>` measures the time each export spent over the period.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `export` | `on-events`, `render`, `activate`, `deactivate`, `handle-hook`, `frame` |
| `calls` | Number of calls in the period |
| `total_ms` | Sum of call time |
| `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `max_ms` | Percentiles of call time |
| `over_budget` | Calls over the deadline of that export |

- **[DEV-690]** `profile` MUST sample every call. It MUST NOT sample by chance.
- **[DEV-691]** `over_budget` MUST count calls over 20 ms for `on-events` and 10 ms for `render`, the limits in [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).
- **[DEV-692]** A period with no calls MUST print a `timing` record with `calls` 0 for the export and no percentiles.
- **[DEV-693]** Profiling MUST NOT change the time of calls by more than 5 percent.

## The memory view

`ilium plugin inspect <id> --memory` prints the memory a plugin uses.

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭ Memory: example.notes (server) ──────────────╮
│ linear memory   6.2 MiB of 32 MiB            │
│ peak            9.8 MiB                      │
│ storage         14 KiB of 1 MiB              │
│ instances       1   restarts 0               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The memory view of one plugin side.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **[DEV-700]** The memory view MUST show linear memory now, the peak since the instance started, the limit, storage used against the 1 MiB quota, the instance count and the restart count.
- **[DEV-701]** A peak of more than 80 percent of the limit MUST add the line `warning: peak above 80 percent of memory_mib`.
- **[DEV-702]** Values MUST use binary units (KiB, MiB).

## Dev loop contract

`ilium plugin dev` installs the build as a T3 plugin and keeps it fresh.

- **[DEV-710]** A dev install MUST show the dev badge in Settings > Plugins and in the plugin list, so nobody mistakes it for a signed package.
- **[DEV-711]** A dev install MUST use its own data folder, separate from an installed release of the same id. Two installs of one id cannot exist: `dev` MUST refuse when the release is installed, with `dev.id-installed`, unless `--replace-installed` is given.
- **[DEV-712]** After a rebuild, `dev` MUST reload the plugin: deactivate with reason `upgrade`, load the new component, activate. Storage is kept.
- **[DEV-713]** A failed rebuild MUST leave the running version in place and print the build errors.

## Source maps

- **[DEV-715]** A TypeScript build MUST write the source map at `dist/<side>.wasm.map`. A package contains the map under `src/` only when `pack --include-src` is used. A trap trace shows file and line when the map is present.
- **[DEV-716]** A Rust build MUST keep the `name` section of the component in debug builds and strip it in release builds. `inspect --verify` MUST report which it found.

## Record catalogue for --json

Each tool prints JSONL with `--json`. `type` is the first key. A `summary` record and then a `result` record end every run.

| Command | Record `type` | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `logs` | `log` | `time`, `level`, `side`, `plugin`, `message` |
| `trace` | `trace` | `seq`, `time_ms`, `kind`, `instance`, `detail` (object, redacted unless allowed) |
| `profile` | `timing` | `export`, `calls`, `total_ms`, `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `max_ms`, `over_budget` |
| `inspect --view` | `tree` | `target`, `nodes`, `depth`, `root` (nested `children`) |
| `inspect --memory` | `memory` | `side`, `linear_bytes`, `peak_bytes`, `limit_bytes`, `storage_bytes`, `instances`, `restarts` |

- **[DEV-720]** Field names in `--json` records MUST use `snake_case` and MUST match the table. A new field MAY be added. A field MUST NOT be removed or renamed within contract `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
- **[DEV-721]** Durations MUST be numbers in milliseconds with up to three decimals. Sizes MUST be integers in bytes.
- **[DEV-722]** Records of one run MUST appear in time order, except `summary` and `result`, which come last.

A `trace` record in JSON:

```json
{"type":"trace","seq":46,"time_ms":1510,"kind":"trap","instance":2,"detail":{"code":"trap.deadline","export":"on-events"}}
```

## Worked example: find why a plugin restarts

A plugin `example.notes` restarts every few minutes. The steps use only the tools on this page.

1. Read the log: `ilium plugin logs example.notes --level warn`. It shows `restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3 in 10 minutes)` and an `error` line `trap in on-events: deadline 20 ms`.
2. Read the trace: `ilium plugin trace example.notes --last 20 --kinds event,trap`. The trap follows a batch that holds 256 `node-renamed` events.
3. Profile: `ilium plugin profile example.notes --duration 30`. `on-events` shows `p95_ms` 14.8 and `max_ms` 31.2 with `over_budget` 2.
4. Inspect memory: `ilium plugin inspect example.notes --memory`. The peak is 9.8 MiB of 32 MiB, so memory is not the cause.
5. Reproduce: `ilium plugin trace example.notes --record rename-burst.jsonl`, then `ilium plugin test --replay rename-burst.jsonl`. The test traps the same way.
6. Fix the handler to coalesce renames, and run the replay again. It now exits 0.

- **[DEV-725]** A recorded trace replayed with `ilium plugin test --replay` MUST reproduce a deadline trap in component mode when the original call exceeded the deadline, as the recorded host call times are replayed with the fake clock.

## Problems and fixes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Check | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| No `debug` lines in the log | Threshold is `info` | `ilium plugin log-level <id>` | Run `log-level <id> debug` |
| `trace.unredacted-denied` | Not a dev install | `ilium plugin list` shows no `[dev]` | Install with `ilium plugin dev` |
| Trace shows fewer than 1,024 records | The instance is new | `seq` starts low | Wait for activity |
| Log folder missing | Plugin never logged | Look in `ilium plugin doctor` state path | Log one line on activation |
| `inspect.no-render` | View never rendered | Open the panel once | Open the target, then inspect |

- **[DEV-730]** `inspect --view` for a plugin that is disabled MUST fail with `inspect.no-render` and exit 1.
- **[DEV-731]** `profile` of a plugin that is disabled MUST fail with `plugin.not-running` and exit 1.

## Edge cases

- A plugin with several sides writes all its lines to one file. The `side` column tells them apart.
- Time moves back when the machine clock changes. The host MUST NOT reorder lines.
- Logs for a disabled plugin stay readable.
- A plugin that logs 200 lines per second at 80 bytes per line fills five files of 4 MiB in about 20 minutes. Old lines are then lost. Use the trace for short windows.

- [Debugging plugins](/pages/debugging/)

# Versions and dependencies reference

## Versions and dependencies reference

This page defines how plugin versions are written and compared, how a plugin states what it needs, how the host chooses versions, and how update channels work. It settles three older statements that disagreed: the "same major, minor at least as high" rule, the cycle rule in the lifecycle page, and the two forms of a service version.

A **version** is a number such as `1.4.2` that names one release of a plugin. A **range** is a rule that accepts some versions, such as `^1.4`. A **dependency** is something a plugin needs: another plugin, a service, an extension point or a minimum Ilium release. **Resolution** is the choice of one version for every plugin so that all ranges hold. A **channel** is a named stream of releases, such as `stable` or `beta`.

Requirement ids such as `PKG-310` can be cited by tests. See [Requirements: manifest and package](/pages/reference-requirements-manifest-package/).

### You will need

- The manifest keys: [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/).
- How the contract version differs from the plugin version: [Versioning](/pages/versioning/).
- How activation waits for services: [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).

## Plugin versions

A plugin version is a Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 string.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-310] | A version matches `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional `-prerelease`, as SemVer 2.0.0 defines. MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH are integers from 0 to 2,147,483,647 without leading zeros. |
| [PKG-311] | A prerelease is dot-separated identifiers of `[0-9A-Za-z-]`. Numeric identifiers have no leading zeros. The whole version is at most 64 characters. |
| [PKG-312] | A leading `v` is not part of a version. `v1.2.3` is refused with `manifest.version-invalid`. |
| [PKG-313] | Build metadata (`+build.5`) is allowed in a source manifest. It is ignored in every comparison and two versions that differ only in build metadata are equal. A registry refuses a version that has build metadata (`registry.version-invalid`), so each registry version has one meaning. |
| [PKG-314] | Precedence follows SemVer 2.0.0 section 11. A prerelease is lower than the release with the same numbers: `1.0.0-beta.2` is lower than `1.0.0`. Numeric identifiers compare as numbers. Alphanumeric identifiers compare in ASCII order. A numeric identifier is lower than an alphanumeric one. A shorter list is lower when all earlier identifiers are equal. |

Precedence examples, from lowest to highest: `0.9.0`, `1.0.0-alpha`, `1.0.0-alpha.1`, `1.0.0-alpha.beta`, `1.0.0-beta`, `1.0.0-beta.2`, `1.0.0-beta.11`, `1.0.0-rc.1`, `1.0.0`, `1.0.1`, `1.1.0`.

The plugin version is not the contract version. The contract is `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, which the `api` key states. A plugin may be at version `7.3.0` and still use contract `0.1.0`.

## Ranges

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-315] | A range is one or more comparators separated by single spaces. A version satisfies the range when it satisfies all comparators (logical AND). The operator `\|\|` is not supported and is refused with `manifest.requires-invalid`. |
| [PKG-316] | A comparator is one of: an exact version `=1.2.3` or `1.2.3`, `>1.2.3`, `>=1.2.3`, `<1.2.3`, `<=1.2.3`, a caret range `^1.2.3`, a tilde range `~1.2.3`, or the star `*`. |
| [PKG-317] | A bare version with no operator (`1.2.3`, `1.2`, `1`) means a caret range. This is the Cargo rule. It makes `@0.1.0` and `@^0.1.0` the same. |
| [PKG-318] | A caret range `^M.m.p` accepts versions that do not change the left-most non-zero part: `^1.2.3` is `>=1.2.3 <2.0.0`. `^0.2.3` is `>=0.2.3 <0.3.0`. `^0.0.3` is `>=0.0.3 <0.0.4`. `^0.0` is `>=0.0.0 <0.1.0`. `^0` is `>=0.0.0 <1.0.0`. |
| [PKG-319] | A tilde range `~M.m.p` accepts patch changes: `~1.2.3` is `>=1.2.3 <1.3.0`. `~1.2` is `>=1.2.0 <1.3.0`. `~1` is `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`. |
| [PKG-320] | `*` accepts every release version. |
| [PKG-321] | A prerelease version satisfies a range only if some comparator of the range has the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and itself carries a prerelease (the npm rule), or when the resolver runs on the `beta` channel for that plugin (see Channels). `1.3.0-beta.1` does not satisfy `^1.2.0` on the `stable` channel. |
| [PKG-322] | A range is at most 128 characters. An invalid range is refused with `manifest.requires-invalid`. |

This rule replaces the rule "same major, minor at least as high" that three pages stated. That rule is wrong for versions that start with `0`, because under SemVer every `0.x` minor may break the interface. The caret rule gives the right answer for both cases.

| Required range | Provider `0.1.0` | Provider `0.1.4` | Provider `0.2.0` | Provider `1.0.0` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.1.0` (caret) | yes | yes | no | no |
| `^0.2` | no | no | yes | no |
| `>=0.1.0 <1.0.0` | yes | yes | yes | no |
| `~0.1.2` | no | yes | no | no |
| `*` | yes | yes | yes | yes |

## The `requires` object

```json
"requires": {
  "host": ">=0.1.0",
  "services": ["ilium:inference/provider@0.1.0", "com.example.git/status@^1.2"],
  "plugins": [
    { "id": "com.example.git", "version": "^1.2", "optional": false },
    { "id": "com.example.theme-pack", "version": "*", "optional": true }
  ],
  "wait_ms": 2000
}
```

| Key | Type | Default | Constraint | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | string | none | A range over Ilium release versions. The host version is a SemVer string such as `0.1.0` | `manifest.requires-invalid`, `dependency.host-version` |
| `services` | list of string | `[]` | At most 32. Each is `<interface>@<range>`. The interface name follows the grant argument rule for `services.use`. The `@<range>` part is optional and defaults to `*` | `manifest.requires-invalid` |
| `plugins` | list of object | `[]` | At most 32. Keys `id` (a plugin id), `version` (a range, default `*`) and `optional` (boolean, default `false`) | `manifest.requires-invalid`, `manifest.requires-self` |
| `wait_ms` | integer | 2000 | 0 to 5000 | `manifest.requires-invalid` |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-323] | A plugin MUST NOT list its own id in `requires.plugins`. It is refused with `manifest.requires-self`. |
| [PKG-324] | `requires.plugins` MUST NOT name an id twice. Duplicates are refused with `manifest.requires-invalid`. |
| [PKG-325] | `requires.host` is checked against the version of the running Ilium release. A release that does not satisfy it is refused with `dependency.host-version` at install and keeps the plugin `disabled` with a reason at load time. |
| [PKG-326] | `wait_ms` replaces the fixed 2 s activation wait of the lifecycle page. It is the time a plugin's activation waits for each required service provider. A value above 5000 is refused. The older fixed values 2 s default and 5 s maximum remain the default and the ceiling. |
| [PKG-327] | The service form in `requires.services` is `interface@range` with the range grammar of this page. The form `ilium:inference/provider@0.1.0` stays valid and means `^0.1.0`. The older forms `@0.1` and `@0.1.0` are therefore the same. |
| [PKG-328] | An extension point reference `<plugin-id>/<point>@<minimum>` in `contributes.extensions.point` uses the same grammar: the part after `@` is a range, and a bare version is a caret range. `requires.points` does not exist. The point reference is the dependency. |

## What blocks an install and what does not

| Dependency | At install | At activation |
|---|---|---|
| `requires.host` | Refuses if not satisfied | Plugin stays disabled with a reason |
| `requires.plugins` (not optional) | Resolves from installed plugins and configured sources, or refuses with `dependency.unresolved` | Plugin does not activate until the required plugin is active |
| `requires.plugins` (optional) | Never blocks | Plugin activates without it |
| `requires.services` | A missing provider never blocks. A cycle is refused with `manifest.service-cycle` | Activation waits up to `wait_ms` per provider in the instance state `waiting-dependency`, then the side returns to `inactive` and shows "waiting for" |
| Extension point owner | Never blocks | The contribution is dormant until the owner is active |

[PKG-329] A missing service provider and a missing extension point owner MUST NOT block an install. This keeps the rule of the versioned-service tutorial: a missing provider never makes install fail. Only `requires.host`, non-optional `requires.plugins` and a service cycle block.

## Resolution

The resolver chooses one version per plugin id for the whole installation. Two versions of one id never run side by side.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-330] | The inputs are: the plugin being installed, the installed plugins with their current versions, the pins (see below), the available sources, and the user's channel settings. |
| [PKG-331] | For each required plugin id, the resolver collects every range from every installed or incoming plugin that requires it. The chosen version is the highest version that satisfies all ranges, is permitted by the channel and is not yanked. |
| [PKG-332] | A version that is already installed is preferred over a higher one when it satisfies all ranges and the command is not an update. The resolver does not upgrade a dependency during an install of another plugin unless the range forces it. |
| [PKG-333] | When no version satisfies all ranges, the resolver refuses with `dependency.conflict`. The message lists each constraint with its source plugin, and the versions that were available. |
| [PKG-334] | When a required id has no installed copy and no source has it, the resolver refuses with `dependency.unresolved` and lists every missing id with its range. |
| [PKG-335] | The resolver builds a graph from `requires.plugins` edges that are not optional. A cycle is refused with `dependency.cycle`, naming the cycle in order. Cycles through optional edges never block install. |
| [PKG-654] | A cycle in the graph whose edges are the non-optional `requires.services` entries, resolved against the installed set plus the package, is refused at stage 10 with `manifest.service-cycle`, listing the service names in cycle order starting with the smallest. Activation order is therefore always a directed acyclic graph. |
| [PKG-336] | The tie-break between equal candidates is the order: highest version, then the source order in the configuration, then the lowest `sha256` of the package. The result is deterministic. |
| [PKG-337] | `ilium plugin install --dry-run` prints the resolution plan without changing anything. |

The cycle rule covers hard plugin requirements and non-optional service requirements, as PKG-335 and PKG-654 say. A cycle through an optional edge is not an error.

### Resolution test table

| Id | Installed | Install | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| [PKG-338] | none | A needs B `^1.0`, source has B 1.0.0, 1.2.0, 2.0.0 | B 1.2.0 installed, then A |
| [PKG-339] | B 1.0.0 | A needs B `^1.0` | B 1.0.0 kept. No dependency change |
| [PKG-340] | B 1.0.0 | A needs B `^1.1`, source has B 1.2.0 | B updated to 1.2.0, then A. The user sees both in the review |
| [PKG-341] | C needs B `^1.0` | A needs B `^2.0` | `dependency.conflict` naming C and A |
| [PKG-342] | none | A needs B, no source has B | `dependency.unresolved` |
| [PKG-343] | none | A needs B, B needs A (hard) | `dependency.cycle` |
| [PKG-344] | none | A needs B optional, no B | A installed. B is not required |
| [PKG-345] | none | A needs service S, no provider | A installed. Instance state `waiting-dependency` for S |
| [PKG-346] | none | A needs host `>=9.0.0`, running release 0.1.0 | `dependency.host-version` |
| [PKG-347] | none | A needs B `^1.0`, only B 1.3.0-beta.1 exists, channel stable | `dependency.unresolved` |

## Effects on update and uninstall

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-348] | Updating plugin B is refused with `dependency.conflict` when the new version would leave an installed dependant outside its range. The message offers `ilium plugin update --all` or `update B A` to update both together when a satisfying version of A exists. |
| [PKG-349] | `ilium plugin uninstall B` is refused with `dependency.in-use` when an installed, enabled plugin requires B (not optional). `--force` removes B anyway. The dependants are then disabled with the reason `requires B` and are re-enabled when B is installed again. |

## Activation order

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-350] | The start order is Kahn's algorithm over the edges of the non-optional `requires.plugins` entries and of the `requires.services` entries to their providers. At each step the host takes the ready node with the smallest key: the tier number (T1 first), then the plugin id in byte order. Up to 4 activations run at once, started in that order (LIF-045 to LIF-047). |
| [PKG-351] | Shutdown runs the exact reverse of the start order, not the reverse of the order in which activations finished. Stops run one at a time (LIF-050). |
| [PKG-352] | A plugin with `replaces: ["id"]` satisfies a `requires.plugins` entry for the replaced id when the replacement is enabled and its version satisfies the range. The replacement is a different plugin, so its own version is compared with the range. A consumer that needs the replaced plugin's version series MUST name a range that the replacement also satisfies, or declare the dependency optional. |

The last rule is deliberately narrow. A replacement states which surface it provides, but it does not claim the version history of the plugin it replaces.

## Channels

A channel is a stream of releases. There are three.

| Channel | Meaning | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| `stable` | Releases meant for everyone. Version numbers have no prerelease part | Registry, files |
| `beta` | Releases for testers. Version numbers may carry a prerelease part | Registry, files |
| `dev` | Local builds from `ilium plugin dev` | Local only, never in a registry |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-353] | Each registry version belongs to exactly one channel. A version with a prerelease part belongs to `beta`. A version without one belongs to `stable` or `beta`, and the publisher chooses at publish time. |
| [PKG-354] | A user sets the default channel in `[plugins] channel = "stable"` (default `stable`) and can set a channel for one plugin with `ilium plugin channel <id> <stable\|beta>`. A plugin on `beta` is offered both `beta` and `stable` versions. A plugin on `stable` is offered only `stable` versions. |
| [PKG-355] | A switch from `beta` to `stable` never installs a lower version by itself. The plugin stays at its version until a `stable` version with a higher precedence appears. `ilium plugin install <id>@<version> --allow-downgrade` is the explicit way back. |
| [PKG-356] | A file install ignores channels. The version is whatever the file holds. The record keeps `channel: dev` for `ilium plugin dev` and `channel: file` for other files. |
| [PKG-357] | Administrators can limit the allowed channels with the policy key `packages.allowed_channels`. See [Administrator guide](/pages/guide-plugin-administration/). |

## Pins and lock files

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-358] | `ilium plugin pin <id>@<version>` records an exact version. Update commands skip pinned plugins, and the resolver treats a pin as the only allowed version of that id. `ilium plugin unpin <id>` removes it. |
| [PKG-359] | The lock file `plugins.lock` is JSON: `{ "format": "ilium-lock/1", "plugins": [ { "id", "version", "sha256", "source" } ] }`, sorted by id. `ilium plugin lock` writes it from the installed set. `ilium plugin install --locked <file>` installs exactly those versions. A locked version that no source offers fails with `dependency.unresolved`. A resolution that differs from the lock fails with `dependency.lock-mismatch`. |
| [PKG-360] | A lock file entry whose `sha256` differs from the SHA-256 of the downloaded package is refused with `registry.hash-mismatch`. |

Use a lock file when the same plugin set must run on many machines. See [Administrator guide](/pages/guide-plugin-administration/).

## Worked example

Plugin `com.example.reviews` needs the plugin `com.example.git` at `^1.2` and an inference service. The user has `com.example.git 1.1.0` and no other plugin.

1. The resolver reads the requirement `com.example.git ^1.2`.
2. `1.1.0` does not satisfy it. The sources list `1.2.0`, `1.3.1` and `2.0.0`.
3. It chooses `1.3.1`, the highest version below `2.0.0`.
4. The review dialog shows two packages: `com.example.git 1.3.1` (update) and `com.example.reviews` (new).
5. After approval the host installs `git`, then `reviews`. At start `git` activates first.
6. The inference provider is missing, so `reviews` activates after the 2 s wait in state `waiting-dependency` and shows "waiting for ilium:inference/provider".

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin install reviews.pkg --dry-run
<span class="t-dim">plan</span> update  com.example.git 1.1.0 > 1.3.1
<span class="t-dim">plan</span> install com.example.reviews 0.4.0
<span class="t-warn">note</span> waits for ilium:inference/provider
<span class="t-hi">dry-run</span> nothing was changed
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. A resolution plan.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A range with a space inside a comparator (`>= 1.0`) | Refused with `manifest.requires-invalid` |
| Same version, different hash | Refused with `package.version-reused` |
| A yanked version is already installed | It stays installed and works. It is never chosen for a new install |
| Required plugin disabled by the user | The dependant stays enabled but in state `waiting-dependency` until the required plugin is on |
| `requires.host` is a prerelease range | Supported with the prerelease rule of [PKG-321] |

## What the user sees

The review dialog lists plugins that will be installed or updated because of a dependency, under **Also installs**. A plugin that waits shows `waiting for <name>` in Settings > Plugins. See [Finding and installing plugins](/pages/user-plugin-store/).

# Extension security

## Extension security

Extension points let one plugin add data or code to another plugin's flow ([Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/)). They are the largest new attack surface of the platform, because they connect plugins to each other and to the core plugins that carry Ilium's features. This page sets the security rules for hooks, collect points, replacement of core plugins and project values. It is the source of the risk marks of the core points listed in [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/).

Terms. A **point** is a named place where a plugin accepts contributions. The **owner** provides the point; a **contributor** adds to it. A **hook** is a point where contributors' code runs (modes `observe`, `transform`, `veto`, `first`). A **collect** point gathers entries (data). A **data class** is a label for the kind of information in a payload field.

### You will need

- [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) and [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/).
- The attacker classes A4, A5, A6 and A7 in the [Threat model](/pages/reference-threat-model/).

## Risk of a point

**[SEC-280]** A point is **high** risk when any of these is true:

1. its payload (or an entry's field) carries data covered by an H grant, or terminal, agent, clipboard, file-content or secret data;
2. a transform reply, a first reply or a collect entry determines text sent to a terminal or an agent, a file written, a program run, a network destination, or instructions given to an agent;
3. a veto of the point blocks input to a terminal or an agent, or a message to many agents.

A third-party owner cannot choose `standard` for a point that meets these criteria: the host raises the risk to `high` at install and refuses a manifest that declares `risk: "standard"` for such a point with `manifest.point-risk`.

**[SEC-281]** Data classes. Each field of `payload_schema` and `entry_schema` MAY carry an annotation `x-ilium-data` with one of: `terminal-text`, `agent-prompt`, `file-content`, `path`, `secret`, `user-text`. A point with any field of class `terminal-text`, `agent-prompt`, `file-content` or `secret` is `high`. The review dialog lists the classes in the contributor's **Adds to other plugins** row.

**[SEC-282]** A contributor to a point with a sensitive data class MUST also hold the grant that would let it read the same data directly: `terminal.read-screen` or `terminal.history` for `terminal-text`, `agent.read-prompts` for `agent-prompt`, a matching `fs.read` for `file-content`. A contributor that lacks the grant is refused at install with `manifest.grant-dependency`. This closes data laundering through an owner (class A5).

**[SEC-283]** An entry that drives a privileged action of a T1 owner (a post-create step, an instruction block, a target file, a rule pack that sends text, a provider profile that redirects inference) MUST be validated by the owner with an explicit allowlist of what an entry can make it do. The review dialog shows a line `Can make <owner> <action>` per such entry type. The owner rejects any entry outside the allowlist with `extension.entry-rejected`.

## Fail-open and veto points

**[SEC-287]** Policy for failure. A handler that times out, traps or errors normally counts as a pass (fail open), so a slow handler cannot block the user. This is a deliberate trade between availability and safety. Hooks are **not a security boundary** on standard points; an administrator who needs enforcement uses the admin policy (`extensions.deny_points`), which the kernel enforces without handler code.

For `high` veto and transform points the owner declares `on_failure`: `"pass"` or `"refuse"`. It is allowed only when `risk` is `high` and `mode` is `veto` or `transform`; elsewhere the manifest fails with `manifest.extension-point-invalid`. The default for a high-risk point is `"refuse"`. With `refuse`, a handler failure refuses a plugin-initiated action with `extension.vetoed` (reason `guard-failed`). For an action the user started (the definition in [SEC-291]), the kernel shows a prompt `A guard did not answer. Continue anyway?` and proceeds only if the user agrees; the answer is audited.

**[SEC-288]** Order key. The run order is: user order first, then tier band (T1 before T2 and T3), then priority, then plugin id, then extension id. Declared priorities are kept and `ExtensionEntry.priority` returns the declared value. A T2 or T3 contributor therefore never runs before a T1 contributor of the same point unless the user moves it, and its priority orders it only among its own tier band.

**[SEC-284]** A transform handler's output is validated against `payload_schema` before the next handler runs, and every field not listed in `reply_schema.properties` must equal its input value. A failing output is treated as a pass and logged `extension.schema-mismatch`. For a point of mode `transform` whose result drives a privileged action, the owner MAY set `final_check: true`: after all transform handlers have run, the host calls once each contributor entry that declared `guard: true` on the final payload; any `refuse(reason)` refuses the action (`refused(conflict)`, `extension.vetoed`). This makes sure a guard sees the data the action will use.

**[SEC-286]** On `veto` points the handler sees the final payload (veto points have no transforms). On a point with `final_check` the guard sees the output of the transform chain, not the original.

**[SEC-285]** Withdrawn, see [HST-472]. The chain cap is a hard 100 ms: a handler that starts before 100 ms runs until its own `deadline_ms`, and handlers not started at 100 ms are skipped as `pass`.

**[SEC-289]** Nesting. A handler can start another hook chain with `run-hook`. The outermost chain is depth 1. A `run-hook` from a handler at depth 3 fails at once with `extension-error` `reentrant`, base code `conflict` and a message that starts with `extension.depth-exceeded`. It counts as a pass for the handler that caused it and not as a breach. A `run-hook` on any point already on the current chain stack, directly or indirectly, fails with `extension.reentrant`. The inner chain runs after the handler returns and its time does not count toward the outer deadline.

**[SEC-290]** Budgets. Per point the owner may call `run-hook` at most 200 times per second; further calls return `rate-limited`. Per handler, CPU time is limited to 50 ms per second; above it, calls to that handler are skipped for the rest of the second and count as a breach. A **breach** is defined in [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure): a timeout, a trap, an error return, a reply over 64 KiB, a schema failure, a CPU budget overrun, or a skip because the contributor's instance was busy. Three consecutive breaches stop the extension until the contributor's instance restarts or the user presses Reset. The notice that announces the stop is drawn by the kernel and lists the plugin, the point and the cause. The audit log records `extension-disabled-after-breaches`.

**[SEC-291]** Vetoes of user actions. A chain is **user-started** when the payload field `source` is `user`, `paste`, `mouse`, `keys` or `manual-trigger`, or, for points without `source`, when the action came from a key, a click or a command the user invoked. A veto on a user-started action can be overridden by the user on these points: `ilium.core.tree/before-close`, `ilium.core.tree/before-move`, `ilium.core.worktrees/before-remove`, `ilium.core.layout/before-split`, `ilium.core.compaction/before-compact` and `ilium.core.terminal/before-send-input` (sources `user` and `paste` only). The kernel shows `<plugin> refused: <reason>. Continue anyway?` with default focus on **No**. An override is audited with the plugin and point. After an override the chain completes `ok` with no reply, and the owner's log gets `extension.veto-overridden` with the contributor and the point. The **User override** column of [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/) marks these points.

**[SEC-292]** Reasons and labels. Text that a contributor supplies (reasons, labels, titles, error text) is plain text of at most 120 characters, with control characters and bidirectional overrides removed ([SEC-380]). In the user interface it is always prefixed by the host with the contributor's display name, so a reason cannot imitate a kernel message. The message of the `extension.vetoed` error itself carries the contributor's plugin id.

## Risk marks of core points

The review of every core point against [SEC-280] gives 19 high-risk points. The [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/) table and each core page carry the same marks. Points not listed here are `standard`.

| Point | New risk | Reason | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ilium.core.terminal/before-send-input` | high | Input to terminals | `on_failure: refuse`; user prompt on guard failure |
| `ilium.core.terminal/open-link` | high | Decides how a link opens (a program or a URL target) | First-handler answer validated against the allowlist of open targets |
| `ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy` | high | Sees copied secrets; rewrites clipboard text | Class `secret`, `terminal-text` |
| `ilium.core.editor/before-save` | high | Rewrites any saved file | Class `file-content` |
| `ilium.core.voice/transcript` | high | Changes which command runs | Class `user-text`; entries validated by the owner |
| `ilium.core.agent-detect/classify` | high | Can make a working agent look idle, so actions fire | Output limited to the activity enum |
| `ilium.core.fleet/before-broadcast` | high | Text to many agents | Existing |
| `ilium.core.inference/before-request` | high | Sees and rewrites every prompt | Class `agent-prompt` |
| `ilium.core.inference/provider-profiles` | high | Redirects inference to another endpoint | Endpoint checked by [Network egress](/pages/reference-network-egress/); owner confirms with the user |
| `ilium.core.notifications/channels` | high | Sends notification bodies to webhooks | Webhook host checked as egress |
| `ilium.core.scheduler/before-send-scheduled` | high | Existing | Existing |
| `ilium.core.text-triggers/before-fire` | high | Existing | Existing |
| `ilium.core.text-triggers/rule-packs` | high | Rules send text to terminals | Rules validated by the owner; see [Project values](#project-values) |
| `ilium.core.chatroom/before-post` | high | Rewrites messages that agents read | Class `agent-prompt` |
| `ilium.core.agent-setup/instruction-blocks` | high | Injects instructions into agent configuration files | Class `agent-prompt` |
| `ilium.core.agent-setup/targets` | high | Adds files that setup edits | Path must lie in `agent-config` scopes |
| `ilium.core.agent-setup/before-install` | high | Existing | Existing |
| `ilium.core.worktrees/post-create-steps` | high | Steps run programs | Each step's program needs a `process.run` grant of the contributor |
| `ilium.core.diagnostics/log-sinks` | high | Receives every log record | Records pass through redaction ([SEC-249]) |
| `ilium.core.tree/before-close`, `ilium.core.worktrees/before-remove` | standard | User-overridable ([SEC-291]) | |

**[SEC-293]** The core plugin pages for Smart copy, Editor, Voice, Agent detect, Chatroom, Agent setup, Worktrees, Diagnostics, Notifications, Text triggers, Inference, Terminal and Tree repeat the marks of their own points. A mismatch between a core page and this table is a defect.

## Replacement of core plugins

A plugin with `replaces` takes over a core plugin's surface ([Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/)). Twenty-eight core plugins can be replaced; `ilium.core.sessions` and `ilium.core.settings` cannot.

**[SEC-300]** A replacement has only the grants its own review dialog gave it. It never inherits the grants, consents, data or the replaced plugin's own contributions to other points. Contributions of other plugins to the replaced points are handled by [SEC-304].

**[SEC-301]** A T3 package cannot replace a core plugin (`manifest.replaces-tier`). A T2 replacement requires a confirmation that names the core plugin and lists every H grant the replaced surface needs. Policy `extensions.allow_replacement = false` refuses all replacements with `policy.replacement`.

**[SEC-302]** If the replaced surface needs grants that only T1 can hold (`process.run:sh`, `settings.read-all`, `plugins.manage`), a T2 package that claims the surface fails at install with `manifest.replaces-tier`, in addition to `manifest.replaces-surface-incomplete` for missing items.

**[SEC-303]** Namespace. A replacement serves the `ilium.core.<name>` surface ids, but its commands carry the replacement's display name and a `T2` badge in the palette and in help, and its keybindings rank as T2 (below T1 and user bindings). The ids `ilium.` stay reserved for bundled packages ([Packages](/pages/packages/)); a replacement keeps its own plugin id.

**[SEC-304]** Contributors. Plugins that contributed to points of the replaced core plugin are listed on the Plugins screen as **Now sending to <replacement>**. Their high-risk contributions are suspended until the user confirms them again for the new owner; standard contributions continue after a notice.

**[SEC-305]** Kernel-owned security functions never move to a replacement. They are: the grant check and the admission gate for host calls, the inference privacy log, consent prompts, the review dialog, breach notices, the recovery page, the audit log, safe mode, and the policy.

**[SEC-306]** Turning a replacement on or off writes `replacement-on` or `replacement-off` to the audit log. The replaced plugin's data folder stays on disk and is inaccessible to the replacement and to every other plugin.

## Project values

A **project value** is a setting stored in a repository's `.ilium/` folder. A cloned repository is attacker-controlled input (class A7). Plugin rows with `scope: "project"` and files such as `.ilium/team-rules.json` read by plugins would otherwise take effect when the user opens the folder.

**[SEC-310]** A project folder is **untrusted** until the user trusts it. When the user opens a project whose `.ilium/` holds plugin values, rules or sessions, the kernel asks once: `Trust this project? It contains plugin settings that could change how plugins behave.` The answer is stored per canonical path in the project trust store ([SEC-112]) and can be revoked in Settings > Plugins > Projects.

**[SEC-311]** In an untrusted project, project-scope plugin values are ignored: plugins read their defaults or user values. The `get` call reports `source: "default"` or `"user"`. A notice on the Plugins screen shows how many values were ignored.

**[SEC-312]** Even in a trusted project, rows whose type is `path`, `url`, `host` or command-like text, and any row marked `trust_sensitive: true`, take project values only with the extra step that the first use of each value is shown to the user (the same consent as `http:setting`, D23).

**[SEC-313]** Secrets never come from project files ([SEC-242]).

**[SEC-314]** The policy `[projects] allow_project_values = false` ignores all project values regardless of trust.

**[SEC-315]** Plugins that read files under `.ilium/` themselves, such as the rule file of tutorial 20, MUST ask the host for the project trust state (`project.trusted()` in the SDK) and MUST ignore the file when it is false. They validate the file: at most 64 KiB, at most 200 rules, schema checked, each rule's fields length-capped, and no regex outside the limits of [SEC-046].

## UI integrity

A plugin that can draw text on screen can try to look like the kernel. The rules below keep kernel security UI recognisable.

**[SEC-377]** Kernel security UI (review dialog, trust dialog, consent prompts, breach notices, recovery page, safe-mode badge) is always drawn on top of plugin UI. No kernel dialog opens, and none is imitated, while the user types in a terminal pane: the kernel queues the dialog until the user leaves the pane or presses the dialog key. Keystrokes typed before a dialog appears never reach it ([SEC-103]).

**[SEC-378]** Plugin toasts, tree chrome, palette entries, help pages and intent chrome are drawn in the plugin style. They carry the plugin display name as a prefix that the plugin cannot remove. Only the kernel uses the rounded border of security dialogs.

**[SEC-379]** A plugin cannot read or draw over the cells of a kernel dialog. Screen contents of kernel dialogs are not delivered by `screen-changed` or any capture call.

**[SEC-380]** Every plugin-supplied text shown by the client (labels, titles, toast text, reasons, status segments, help text) is sanitised: C0 and C1 control characters, escape sequences, bidirectional override characters (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069), zero-width characters and box-drawing characters in sequences of three or more are removed or replaced with a space. Text is clipped to its field limit with an ellipsis.

**[SEC-381]** Display names are 3 to 40 characters, must not equal or start with `Ilium` or `Kernel` unless the plugin id starts with `ilium.`, and are checked at install (`manifest.display-name`).

## Worked example: a guard that times out

A T2 plugin contributes a veto handler to `ilium.core.terminal/before-send-input`, sleeping for its whole deadline on each call. With `on_failure: refuse` (the default for the point), every plugin-initiated send is refused with `guard-failed` after 20 ms; the user's own paste shows `A guard did not answer. Continue anyway?` once, and the user can say yes. After three consecutive breaches the extension is stopped, the kernel draws the notice, and the audit log records it. With the previous fail-open rule, the handler would have been a free way to disable a guard. The test cases are in [Security testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/).

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Two handlers both rewrite and each exceed their deadline | Both are cut at their deadline; the chain keeps the last valid payload |
| A guard handler uses a nested hook that nests three deep | A `run-hook` from depth 3 returns `extension.depth-exceeded` and counts as a pass for that call |
| The user moves a T2 handler above a T1 handler | The user's order wins; priority is ignored |
| Project becomes trusted and then the repository is updated | Values read now come from the new files; the trust stays by path |
| Owner declares `risk: "standard"` for a point with a `terminal-text` field | Manifest refused with `manifest.point-risk` |

# Feature traceability

## Feature traceability

This page maps every user-visible Ilium feature to its owner after the move to plugins. The ids F-001 to F-111 are the feature numbers of the feature inventory (`docs/research/plugin-platform/feature-inventory.md`, features 1 to 111). F-112 to F-116 are features the inventory folds into other rows; they get their own rows so each has its own parity test. The "User doc" column names the page in `src/docs/` that describes the feature today. The "Kind" column uses the inventory classification: native-kernel, plugin-wasm, primitive-extended and plugin-js. The "Wave" column uses the phases and waves of the [roadmap](/pages/roadmap/). The COR ids point to [core parity requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-core-parity/).

[COR-003] Two checks run over this table. A row whose Kind is `native-kernel` names `kernel` first in its Owner cell. Every table named in the Config keys column appears in the key-by-key table of [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/). [COR-001] Every feature in this table MUST keep working with the same behaviour when its owner plugin is enabled. [COR-002] Every row MUST have exactly one owner. A feature that two pages claim is listed once, under "Resolved duplicates".

Related pages: [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/), [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/), [CLI compatibility](/pages/reference-cli-compatibility/), [core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/).

### Reconciliation with the feature inventory

- The inventory has 111 features. This table has 116 rows: the 111 inventory features plus F-112 to F-116, which the inventory folds into other features. No feature is dropped.
- Feature 108 (`ilium wait`) is native-kernel in the inventory. The manual makes it an alias of `ilium progress wait`, so the progress plugin owns it and the Kind is `plugin-wasm`. The kernel keeps no `wait` command.
- Features 19, 20, 21, 24 and 25 (editors and boards) are native-kernel in the inventory. They become plugins in phase 7, so the table names the editor and kanban plugins as the final owners and gives rows owned only by a plugin (F-020, F-021, F-025, F-107) the Kind `plugin-wasm` (see [roadmap](/pages/roadmap/)).
- Features 93 and 94 (shared look, dithering and display) stay in the kernel painter. The [ambient look](/pages/core-plugin-ambient/) plugin owns only the controls.
- Feature 58 (HTTP API) stays in the kernel as the listener. The fleet plugin registers `POST /create_agent` through `http-api.route`.
- Feature 102 (packaged JavaScript animations) is plugin-js in the inventory. The roadmap retires the V8 runtime at the end of wave 4c. Scenes become wasm packages.
- Features 72, 77 and 88 have no source path in the inventory; their owners follow the user documentation.

# Grant review and consent

## Grant review and consent

This page defines how a user decides what a plugin may do, how those decisions are stored, and how they are withdrawn. It replaces the three slightly different install descriptions in earlier pages with one pipeline. Mechanisms for enforcement are in the [Security model](/pages/security/). The attacker classes this page defends against are A1, A2 and A8 in the [Threat model](/pages/reference-threat-model/).

A **grant** is a standing permission that the user gives a plugin at install, for example `fs.read:project`. A **consent** is a one-off answer to a question asked at first use, for example whether a plugin may open `https://status.example.com`. The **review dialog** is the kernel-drawn screen that lists the grants a package asks for. The **authorization epoch** is the counter that changes when a grant changes ([Security model](/pages/security/)).

### You will need

- A package, local or signed. See [Packages](/pages/packages/).
- An attached Ilium client (the TUI). Decisions about grants and trust need one ([SEC-116]).
- The capability table in [Capability table](/pages/reference-capabilities/).

## The install pipeline

**[SEC-100]** `ilium plugin install`, the Plugins screen and `ilium plugin update` MUST run this one pipeline, in this order. The first failing step stops the install and writes one JSONL `error` line with the code. Nothing is written to the install directory before step 11.

| Step | Check | Failure code |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Open the archive with the hardened reader | `package.path-invalid`, `package.path-duplicate`, `package.entry-symlink` or `package.entry-directory`, `package.zip-invalid` |
| 2 | Layout and API version; unknown manifest keys | `manifest.api-version`, `manifest.unknown-key` |
| 3 | Inventory: every file listed with length and SHA-256; asset size | `manifest.file-unlisted`, `manifest.file-missing`, `manifest.file-length`, `manifest.file-hash`, `manifest.asset-size` |
| 4 | Signature (T2) verifies; publisher name matches the key's record | `manifest.signature-invalid`, `manifest.publisher-mismatch` |
| 5 | Blocklist (release and policy) | `package.blocked` |
| 6 | Policy: tier, id, publisher, source | `policy.tier-denied`, `policy.id-denied`, `policy.publisher-denied`, `policy.source-denied` |
| 7 | Key trust and key pinning: an untrusted key is offered for trust; an installed id signed by another key is refused | `trust.declined`, `package.publisher-key-changed` |
| 8 | Grant strings parse and fit the tier; dependencies between grants | `manifest.grant-tier`, `manifest.grant-argument`, `manifest.grant-argument-missing`, `manifest.grant-wildcard`, `manifest.grant-scope`, `manifest.grant-dependency`, `manifest.limits-tier`, `manifest.secret-scope`, `manifest.replaces-tier` |
| 9 | Policy: replacement. A grant denied by `grants.deny` is not checked here and does not fail the install; step 10 shows it locked off | `policy.replacement` |
| 10 | Review dialog (see below) | user cancels: exit code 1, audit `install` with result `cancelled` |
| 11 | Commit: unpack into the install directory, write the grants, bump the epoch, write the audit line | `install.write-failed` |

**[SEC-123]** Declining to trust a key at step 7 refuses the install with `trust.declined`. The package is never downgraded to T3 silently. A user who wants it as a local package passes `--allow-unsigned` explicitly, which strips the signature view and gives a T3 install with the `dev` badge.

**[SEC-124]** `sessions.cross` in a T3 package is refused at step 8 with `manifest.grant-tier`. `sessions.cross` is for T1 and T2 only.

## The review dialog

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Install example.pane-tools 2.0.0 ───────────╮</span>
│ Name (self-declared): Example Corp           │
│ Signed T2 · key 3F2A91C0 · Tab for Details   │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-dim">Server</span>                                       │
│ [x] Read terminal text   terminal.read-cells │
│ [ ] <span class="t-warn">HIGH</span> Read scrollback    terminal.history │
│ [ ] <span class="t-warn">HIGH</span> Run rg ………………………………… process.run:rg │
│ [x] Send data to api.example.com ……………… http │
│ <span class="t-dim">Client</span>                                       │
│ [x] Show toasts ……………………………………… notify.toast │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-warn">This plugin can read your data and send</span>      │
│ <span class="t-warn">data out.</span>                                    │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Cancel   <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Install               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The review dialog of a signed plugin. Focus starts on Cancel.</figcaption>
</figure>

**[SEC-102]** The review dialog MUST be drawn by the kernel (the client) only. It is modal over every plugin widget. No plugin widget can draw inside, over or in the reserved dialog border. No plugin input event reaches the dialog. The same holds for the consent prompts, breach notices, the recovery page and policy lock marks.

**[SEC-106]** Rows. Sections by side (Server, Client, Scene). A high-risk grant row starts unchecked and carries the text `HIGH` (not a symbol). Normal rows start checked. A row for a grant that the policy denies (`grants.deny`, see [SEC-198]) is locked off and reads `Blocked by your administrator`. Each row names the grant in the right column. The dialog also shows, as separate groups: **Adds to other plugins** (extension contributions), **Replaces** (a core plugin), **Receives data from other plugins**, and the **toxic combination** row ([SEC-004]) when the requested set holds, in the same side, at least one grant of the data-read set and at least one grant of the egress set, both enumerated in [SEC-006]. The toxic row is informational and has no checkbox of its own: it cannot be unchecked, and it disappears when the user unchecks either member grant.

**[SEC-103]** Protection against accidental approval. The default focus is on **Cancel**. The dialog ignores `Enter` and `Space` for 500 ms after it opens and while a key is auto-repeating (a second press of the same key within 80 ms of the previous one, without release). The dialog ignores input that arrived before it was drawn. A plugin cannot open the dialog while the user types in a terminal (see [SEC-377]). At most one review dialog is open at a time; others queue.

**[SEC-104]** Names. The publisher is shown as `Name (self-declared)` next to the verified fingerprint. Display names, plugin titles and publisher names shown in the dialog have control characters, bidirectional overrides and isolates, and zero-width joiners removed; they are limited to 64 characters; and they are refused (the install fails with `manifest.display-name`) when they equal or are confusable with a kernel name (`Ilium`, `Settings`, `Plugins`, `Security`, `Kernel`, `Ilium Team`) after case-folding and removal of spaces and punctuation.

**[SEC-107]** Details (reachable with Tab) shows: full SHA-256 fingerprint in groups of 4 hex digits, package SHA-256, the tier, `security_contact` if present, `data_use` if present, each grant with its risk, each file's size, and the optional provenance entries ([Trust and supply chain](/pages/reference-trust-and-supply-chain/)).

**[SEC-121]** Accessibility. Every row has a text label that a screen reader announces as `<state>, <risk>, <title>, <grant name>`. The dialog never relies on colour alone.

**[SEC-122]** If rows exceed the height of the terminal, the list scrolls. A scroll indicator shows `n of m`. The footer stays visible.

### Trust dialog

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Trust this publisher? ──────────────────────╮</span>
│ Self-declared name: Example Corp             │
│ Key fingerprint (SHA-256):                   │
│ 3F2A 91C0 7B6D 1E44 A1B2 0C9E 55D3 F7A8      │
│ B6C1 02E9 4D77 98AF 13C5 6E0B D2F4 8A19      │
│                                              │
│ Compare this with the publisher over a       │
│ channel you trust before you continue.       │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Do not trust   <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Trust           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. Full fingerprint, two groups of 8 hex digits per line pair.</figcaption>
</figure>

The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the raw public key, shown as 64 hex digits in 16 groups of 4. The short form `3F2A91C0` is the first 8 hex digits and appears only next to the full form or in `trust list`.

## Updates

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Update example.pane-tools 2.1.0 ────────────╮</span>
│ Same signing key as 2.0.0.                   │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-dim">New</span>                                          │
│ [ ] <span class="t-warn">HIGH</span> Read scrollback    terminal.history │
│ <span class="t-dim">Widened</span>                                      │
│ [ ] Send data to *.example.com …………………… http │
│ <span class="t-dim">Removed</span>                                      │
│ Show toasts ………………………………………………… notify.toast │
│                                              │
│ Unchanged grants keep their answers.         │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Cancel   <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Update                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The update dialog lists only what changed.</figcaption>
</figure>

**[SEC-108]** An update dialog MUST show three groups. **New**: grants not held before; a new high-risk grant is unchecked and a new normal grant is checked. **Wider**: a grant whose argument now covers more than before; always unchecked. **Removed**: grants the new version no longer lists, shown for information. A widened grant replaces the old one, so the old grant string also appears under Removed. Unchanged grants keep their state and are not shown. Always-granted entries are never shown. Test: update from {`fs.read:data`, `http:a.example`} to {`fs.read:project`, `http:*.example`}; assert New=[`fs.read:project`], Wider=[`http:*.example`], Removed=[`http:a.example`].

Widening is defined for these real argument forms only. Any other argument change is Removed plus New.

| Family | Widened when |
|---|---|
| `commands.invoke:<arg>` | an exact id becomes `<plugin-id>/*`, or `<plugin-id>/*` becomes `*` |
| `http:<host>` | an exact host becomes `*.<domain>` that covers it. Adding a port is a new grant. `http:setting:<key>` is never widened |
| `fs.*:path:<template>` | the template is replaced by an ancestor template (`path:{home}/a/b` to `path:{home}/a`) |
| `fs.*:<scope>` | the scope becomes a broader named scope (`project` to `path:{home}/**`), or read becomes write |
| `process.run:<program>` | a program name becomes an absolute path: a new grant, not widening |
| `extensions.*:<point>` | a different point: Removed plus New |
| risk | a normal grant becomes high: New |

An answer the user gave to an unchanged grant is kept. New and widened grants start in their default state (widened: unchecked). A removed grant is dropped.

**[SEC-109]** A change of the publisher key, or of the tier (T2 to T3 or T3 to T2), resets all grants and consents of the plugin and shows the full dialog as for a first install. A key change that is endorsed by a rotation statement ([SEC-143]) shows the update dialog and a line `Signing key rotated`.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Publisher key changed ──────────────────────╮</span>
│ example.pane-tools 2.2.0 is signed by a      │
│ different key than the installed 2.1.0.      │
│                                              │
│ Installed key  3F2A91C0 7B6D1E44             │
│ New key        A1B20C9E 55D3F7A8             │
│                                              │
│ The update is refused. To use this package,  │
│ uninstall the plugin first. Its grants and   │
│ data settings will be asked for again.       │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Close                                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The kernel refuses an update that changes the signing key without an endorsement.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Consent prompts

**[SEC-105]** Consent prompts (origin for `open-external`, host from a setting, geocoding, bundled first start) are limited. At most one prompt is pending per plugin. At most 6 prompts are shown per plugin in a rolling hour. The call that triggers a prompt waits for the answer, up to 120 s; then it returns `timeout`, the prompt is closed and nothing is stored. A second consent-gated call from the same plugin while one prompt is pending returns `busy` with `retry-after-ms` = 1000 and shows no prompt. The 7th prompt in a rolling hour returns `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms` = the time until the oldest prompt leaves the window. Test: trigger two consent calls at once and assert one prompt and one `busy`; trigger seven in an hour and assert `rate-limited` on the 7th. A prompt is a kernel dialog and cannot be answered by any event a plugin can cause.

**[SEC-110]** After a user declines the same target three times, the plugin gets `not-permitted` with reason `declined` for that target without a prompt, until the user resets it in Settings > Plugins > Consents or with `ilium plugin consents <id> --withdraw <target>`.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Allow once more? ───────────────────────────╮</span>
│ Notes Panel wants to open this site again:   │
│                                              │
│ https://status.example.com                   │
│                                              │
│ You declined this site twice before.         │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Decline        <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Allow           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. After three declines the prompt stops until the user resets it.</figcaption>
</figure>

**[SEC-111]** Bundled first start. A T1 plugin with H grants is activated without them. The kernel asks at first activation. Every row of the prompt starts unchecked, and focus starts on **Not now**. Enter with no row checked equals **Not now** and counts as one of the three asks. If the user answers **Not now**, the question comes back at the next server start. After three **Not now** answers (counted per plugin) the prompt stops and the grants stay off until the user enables them in Settings > Plugins > Capabilities.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Bundled plugin, first start ────────────────╮</span>
│ ilium.pane-tools asks for:                   │
│                                              │
│ [ ] Read scrollback ………………… terminal.history │
│ [ ] Hold the keyboard    terminal.input-lock │
│ [ ] Read agent transcripts  agent.transcript │
│                                              │
│ Asked 1 of 3 times.                          │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi"> Enter </span> Allow selected   <span class="t-hi"> Esc </span> Not now       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. Bundled plugins start without their high-risk grants, and every row starts unchecked.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Where decisions are stored

**[SEC-112]** The grant store, consent store, trust store and project trust store are separate files in the Ilium user state directory (Linux `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/Ilium/state/`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ilium\state\`). Each file is created with mode 0600 in a directory with mode 0700 and is owned by the user. No store lives in a project folder, and none is reachable by any plugin scope ([SEC-060]).

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `grants.json` | `{ "version": 1, "plugins": { "<id>": { "epoch": n, "tier": "t2", "key": "<fingerprint>", "grants": { "server": [...], "client": [...] }, "installed": "<ISO 8601>" } } }` |
| `consents.json` | `{ "version": 1, "plugins": { "<id>": { "open-external": { "<origin>": "allow" or "deny:<count>" }, "http-hosts": {...}, "geocode": "allow" } } }` |
| `trust.json` | `{ "version": 1, "keys": [ { "fingerprint", "publisher", "added", "public_key" } ] }` |
| `project-trust.json` | `{ "version": 1, "projects": { "<canonical path>": { "trusted": true, "added": "<ISO 8601>" } } }` |

**[SEC-114]** Stores are written atomically (temporary sibling, fsync, rename) and carry a `version`. A file with a newer version than the server knows is not modified and the server reports `store.version`. A file that cannot be parsed is renamed to `<name>.corrupt-<YYYYMMDD-HHmmss>`, the server logs `grants.unreadable` (`trust.unreadable` for the trust store), starts with no entries from it, and draws a notice. T2 and T3 plugins then start as not installed with no grants, and T1 plugins start with only their normal grants; grants and consents are asked again (fail closed).

**[SEC-113]** The server re-reads a store file only at start. External edits made while the server runs are ignored until the next start. At start, entries that appear in a store but were not written by the server (the file hash differs from the hash the server recorded in the audit log at its last write) are audited as `store-external-edit`. External edits MUST NOT add a high-risk grant: an H grant found in a store without an audit record of a user decision is dropped. An administrator uses the policy file `preapproved` list instead ([Admin policy](/pages/reference-admin-policy/)).

## Who may approve

**[SEC-116]** A decision that adds a grant, trusts a key, installs a package with `--allow-unsigned` or marks a project trusted MUST be confirmed in a dialog in an attached TUI client of the same session. When `ilium plugin install` runs in a shell pane (the `ILIUM_PANE_ID` variable is set), the CLI asks the server to open the dialog in the client, and the dialog names the requesting pane: `Requested from pane "shell 3"`. If no client is attached, the CLI waits up to 60 s, prints `waiting for a client to approve`, and then fails with `approval.no-client`.

**[SEC-117]** No command-line flag grants a high-risk capability, trusts a key or approves a project without that confirmation. The only exception is a grant that the admin policy lists in `preapproved` for that plugin id, which requires no dialog. A prompt-injected agent that runs `ilium plugin install pkg --yes` still reaches the dialog, and the dialog shows what is installed.

## Revocation and uninstall

**[SEC-118]** The user can withdraw a decision at any time: one grant, one consent, one picked path, or all of a plugin's grants and consents (**Revoke all**). Effects are those in the [Security model](/pages/security/): in-flight calls return `revoked`, the epoch bumps, contributions are withdrawn.

**[SEC-120]** CLI. `ilium plugin consents <id>` prints consents as JSONL. `ilium plugin consents <id> --withdraw <target>` withdraws one. `ilium plugin grants <id> --revoke <grant>` revokes one grant. Granting never happens from the CLI ([SEC-116]).

**[SEC-119]** Uninstall forgets the plugin's grants, consents and picked paths. Its data and cache are removed unless `--keep-data` is passed. A reinstall starts with a fresh review dialog.

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The user holds Enter while the dialog opens | Ignored for 500 ms and while repeating; the dialog stays open |
| A plugin tries to open a second review dialog | Queued; the first stays on top |
| The terminal is smaller than the dialog minimum (40 by 12) | The dialog shows `Terminal too small` and Cancel only |
| Two clients attached | The dialog opens in the client that most recently had input; the other shows `Waiting for approval` |
| Grants store missing | All third-party plugins are treated as not installed and the user is told |
| Package re-signed with the same key, same version | `install` refuses with `install.same-version` |

- [Trust and supply chain](/pages/reference-trust-and-supply-chain/)
- [Admin policy](/pages/reference-admin-policy/)
- [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/)
