# Reference, health and watchdog

## Reference, health and watchdog

A plugin can fail loudly, with a trap, or quietly, by being slow. This page defines the health states that Ilium shows for a plugin, the watchdog that enforces deadlines, how accurate that enforcement is, what happens to a stuck call, a stuck sandbox helper or a task that never ends, and which metrics the host keeps. A test author can use the tolerances here to assert bounds instead of exact times.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Failure counting and restart delays are in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart). Resource budgets are in [Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/).

### Health states

The health of a plugin is one value of the enum `health-state`. It is computed from the package state, the instance states of all sides and a few counters. The host evaluates the list below from the top and takes the first state that matches.

| Order | Health | Matches when | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `refused` | the package state is `refused-at-load` | load checks, policy |
| 2 | `disabled` | the package state is `installed-disabled-by-user` or `disabled-by-policy`, or safe mode is on | user, administrator |
| 3 | `failed` | any side is `stopped-by-failure` | the third counted failure in a window |
| 4 | `restarting` | any side is `restart-scheduled`, or `activating` after a failure | a counted failure |
| 5 | `degraded` | any degraded condition below holds | the counters below |
| 6 | `dormant` | the plugin is enabled and every side is `inactive`, and no side waits for host capacity | no trigger has fired |
| 7 | `healthy` | none of the above | |

A plugin that waits for host capacity (`host-capacity`) is `degraded`, not `dormant`.

Degraded conditions. A condition holds while the counter inside its time span meets the threshold.

| Condition | Threshold | Time span |
|---|---|---|
| Near-misses | 5 or more calls that ended within their deadline but took at least 80% of it | the last 5 minutes |
| Event queue | the queue held more than 75% of `event_queue` (768 of 1,024 by default) at any sample | the last 1 minute |
| Rate limits | 1 or more results of `rate-limited` returned to the plugin | the last 5 minutes |
| Quota hits | 1 or more results of `quota-exceeded` returned to the plugin | the last 5 minutes |
| Failures in the window | 1 or more counted failures, and the instance is active again | the failure window |
| Waiting for memory | the side is `inactive` with the reason `host-capacity` | until it activates |

- [LIF-122] The host MUST compute `health` from the first matching row of the first table, and MUST report it in `plugin-info`, in `ilium plugin status` and on the Plugins screen. Test: drive a plugin into each state and read the value.
- [LIF-123] The host MUST use the thresholds and time spans in the second table. Test: with `advance_clock`, produce 4 and then 5 near-misses and assert the change, and wait 5 minutes and assert the return to `healthy`.
- [LIF-124] A plugin that is stopped, disabled or dormant MUST NOT be reported `degraded`. Test: disable a degraded plugin.

### The watchdog

Every export call and every instance start runs under a deadline. The host enforces deadlines with Wasmtime epoch interruption.

- A background thread increments the engine epoch every tick: 10 ms in every process. Ticks come from a monotonic clock.
- Before an export call the host sets the epoch deadline to `ceil(D / 10) + 1` ticks after the call starts, where `D` is the deadline in milliseconds. When the epoch passes the deadline, the running Wasm code traps at its next safe point.
- Fuel metering is not used. Epoch interruption costs less, and the CPU budget is measured by thread time instead (see [Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/)).

Accuracy. An epoch tick is not a precise timer. A call that spins is interrupted no earlier than `D` and no later than `D + 20` ms of wall time on a host that is not overloaded.

| Side | Tick | A deadline of `D` traps between |
|---|---|---|
| Server | 10 ms | `D` and `D` plus 20 ms |
| Client and scene | 10 ms | `D` and `D` plus 20 ms |

For example, `render_deadline_ms` of 10 ms on the client traps a slow render between 10 ms and 30 ms after it began. A plugin must not depend on a deadline being exact. A call that ends before `D` never traps.

- [LIF-125] The host MUST interrupt a call that runs longer than its deadline `D` at a time `t` with `D <= t <= D + 20 ms` of wall time measured from the start of the call, on a host that is not overloaded. Test: a plugin that loops forever; assert the trap time is in [D, D + 20] ms, and that a call that returns at D - 1 ms never traps.
- [LIF-126] The host MUST NOT interrupt a call before its deadline. Test: a call that takes 0.9 times `D` completes.
- [LIF-127] The host MUST NOT use fuel to enforce deadlines. Test: build the engine configuration and assert that fuel is off.
- [LIF-128] The tick MUST be 10 ms in every process and the instance deadline MUST be `ceil(D / 10) + 1` ticks after the call starts. Test: read the engine configuration.

Time in host calls. A host call that a plugin makes in the middle of an export is synchronous, and its wall time counts toward the export's deadline. The epoch cannot interrupt the host while it runs inside the call, so a slow host call makes the export trap at the first safe point after the call returns. Calls that wait for something external, such as `http`, `process` or a service reply, are not synchronous. They return a request id at once, and the wait is not part of the deadline.

- [LIF-129] Wall time spent inside a synchronous host call MUST count toward the deadline of the export that made it. Time waiting for an asynchronous request MUST NOT. Test: a handler that calls a slow synchronous host function (fixture clock) and a handler that waits for a request.

### Async tasks, pending requests and orphans

- Each asynchronous request has its own timeout (for example 30 s for a command or service reply, 120 s for inference). See [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).
- When an instance is dropped or deactivated, every request it has pending completes as `cancelled`, every timer and watch ends, and no code runs for them. Exceptions: on a trap, completions of submissions are delivered to the new instance, and on revocation requests that need the revoked grant complete as `failed(revoked)` (see [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/)).
- A task that never completes is handled by its timeout. The plugin gets `timed-out`.

- [LIF-130] The host MUST complete all pending requests of a dropped or deactivated instance as `cancelled`, and MUST NOT call into the instance for them. Test: drop an instance with three pending requests and count outcomes.
- [LIF-131] A request that has no reply within its timeout MUST complete as `timed-out`. Test: a service that never answers.

### The sandbox helper (T2 and T3)

Third-party plugins run in a helper process. One helper hosts the T2 and T3 instances of one session server, at most 8 instances per helper. T1 plugins run in the Ilium process and have no helper.

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Heartbeat | The server sends a ping every 1 s. The helper answers on its control thread. |
| Hung helper | 3 missed answers (3 s) or a call that exceeds its deadline by 500 ms without a trap. The server sends SIGKILL to the helper. |
| Crash | A crash, a kill or an out-of-memory kill of the helper. |
| Effect on the plugin whose export was running | one counted failure |
| Effect on the other plugins in the helper | their instances are dropped and restarted in a new helper without a counted failure and without a delay; their pending requests complete as `cancelled` |
| Idle helper crash (no export running) | no counted failure for anyone |

- [LIF-132] A hung helper MUST be killed after 3 missed heartbeats or 500 ms past a deadline, whichever is first. Test: a helper that stops answering.
- [LIF-133] After a helper dies, the host MUST count one failure for the plugin that was running and none for the others, and MUST restart the others at once in a new helper. Test: crash a helper hosting three plugins and read the three windows.
- [LIF-134] The host MUST restart a helper after a crash at most 5 times in 10 minutes. After that, the T2 and T3 plugins of the session MUST move to the instance state `stopped-by-failure` on the server side with the reason `helper.unstable`. Test: kill the helper six times.

### Metrics

The host keeps these values per plugin and per side.

| Metric | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `calls` | export calls, per export |
| `p50_ms`, `p99_ms` | duration of calls, over the last 1,024 calls of each export |
| `near_misses` | calls that took at least 80% of their deadline |
| `traps` | counted traps |
| `queue_high_water` | the highest event queue length since the instance began |
| `memory_peak_bytes` | the highest linear memory plus table size |
| `quota_hits` | results of `quota-exceeded` and `rate-limited` returned |

Retention: counters are kept in memory for the life of the session server, in hourly buckets for the last 24 hours. They are not written to disk, and they reset at a server restart. The latest summary is written to the plugin log when an instance ends.

- [LIF-135] The host MUST keep the metrics above for each plugin and side, and MUST discard buckets older than 24 hours. Test: read the metrics after 25 simulated hours.
- [LIF-136] A server restart MUST reset the metrics. Test: restart and read.

### Surfaces

`ilium plugin status [<id>] --json` prints one line per plugin:

```text
{"type":"plugin-status","id":"com.example.notes","health":"degraded","reason":"near-misses","sides":[{"side":"server","state":"active","failures_in_window":1,"calls":4120,"p50_ms":0.4,"p99_ms":9.1,"near_misses":6,"traps":1,"queue_high_water":812,"memory_peak_bytes":9437184,"quota_hits":0}]}
```

The Plugins screen shows a health column ([Managing plugins](/pages/user-managing-plugins/)). The recovery page lists plugins that are not `healthy` first. The diagnostics report of [Diagnostics](/pages/core-plugin-diagnostics/) has a section `Plugins` with the same fields.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin status
<span class="t-dim">ID                    HEALTH     P99    NEAR</span>
ilium.core.tree       healthy    1.2ms  0
com.example.notes     <span class="t-warn">degraded</span>   9.1ms  6
com.example.cursor    <span class="t-err">failed</span>     -      -
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The status list shows health, the 99th percentile call time and near-misses.</figcaption>
</figure>

- [LIF-137] `ilium plugin status` MUST print the health and the metrics of every installed plugin, as JSON lines when output is not a terminal. Test: run it in a pipe and parse.
- [LIF-138] The diagnostics report MUST contain a `Plugins` section with the health of every plugin that is not `healthy`. Test: degrade a plugin and generate the report.

### Edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| A plugin is stuck in a loop inside `on-events` | The epoch traps it within the bound of LIF-125. One failure counts. |
| A plugin is stuck inside a slow host call | The call returns, then the epoch traps it at the next safe point. |
| `activate` never returns | The activate deadline traps it. One failure counts. |
| A T1 plugin loops while the UI waits for its render | The render deadline traps it within 30 ms on the client. The view shows its last good frame, marked stale. |
| The machine sleeps during a call | The monotonic clock may not advance; the host treats a jump larger than 5 s as a clock skip and does not count the call as a breach. |

# Host architecture

## Host architecture

This page is the normative description of the plugin host: which crates it is made of, which operating system processes run plugin code, which side and tier each process hosts, who owns each registry, how the host starts and stops, and what a failure takes down. A developer who implements the host builds it from this page and the pages it links. A test author derives the structural tests from the requirement ids in square brackets, for example `[HST-001]`.

The words MUST, SHOULD and MAY have their usual meaning in a specification. MUST is a requirement that a test checks. SHOULD is a default that an implementation may change with a stated reason. MAY is an option. The ids are collected, with a test method for each, in [Requirements: kernel and host](/pages/reference-requirements-kernel-host/).

Terms used here are defined once. A **host** is the code that loads plugin components, calls their exports and serves their imports in one process for one side. A **side** is one of `server`, `client` or `scene` (see [Worlds and sides](/pages/worlds-and-sides/)). A **tier** is T0 to T3 (see [Architecture](/pages/architecture/)). A **Store** is the Wasmtime object that owns the memory and state of one component instance. An **Engine** is the Wasmtime object that holds the compiler and its configuration. The **dispatcher** is the host component that turns kernel events into batches for plugin queues and turns returned submissions into kernel work. The **sandbox helper** is the separate process that runs T2 and T3 components.

## You will need

- The concept pages [Architecture](/pages/architecture/), [Worlds and sides](/pages/worlds-and-sides/) and [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).
- For the numbers that this page refers to, [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/), [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) and [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/).

## Crate layout

The platform adds four crates to the workspace and changes the boundaries of two existing ones. The rule that governs the layout is the existing layering rule of the repository: a pure crate has no I/O, an adapter crate owns one external system, and no crate reaches around the crate that owns a concern.

| Crate | Kind | Contents | Must not contain |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ilium-plugin-api` | pure | Manifest types, capability names and risk classes, contribution types, event, intent, outcome and error types mirrored from the WIT package `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, limit keys and ceilings, requirement-neutral constants such as epoch period | Wasmtime, V8, tokio, file or socket access |
| `ilium-plugin-host` | adapter | The Wasmtime embedding, linker construction, instantiation, the dispatcher, call classes and deadlines, quota accounting, the helper client, the telemetry registry, the conformance harness hooks | Terminal, tree or UI logic; direct `libc`, `std::os::unix` or `windows-sys` use |
| `ilium-plugin-helper` | binary | The sandbox helper: a small `main` that confines itself, owns one Engine and one Store set, and speaks the parent-helper protocol | Any path to the session server or the user's files except granted scopes |
| `ilium-plugin-sdk` | library for plugins | The Rust SDK that plugins depend on, generated from the WIT package, plus the `#[ilium_plugin]` macro (`@ilium/plugin-sdk` is the TypeScript counterpart) | Any Ilium crate dependency |
| `ilium-plugin-conformance` | test only | Language-neutral fixtures and the Rust and TypeScript guest components that exercise each interface | Production code |
| `ilium-plugin-bench` | test only | The benchmark programs B1 to B24 of [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/) | Production code |

The helper binary is installed beside the `ilium` and `ilium-server` binaries by the same installer, and the host finds it by looking in the directory of its own executable. A missing helper is not an error for T1-only installs: T2 and T3 packages are refused with `host.helper-missing` (see [Sandbox helper](/pages/reference-host-helper/)).

### Dependency edges

The table lists every allowed edge that involves a plugin crate. Any edge not listed is forbidden.

| From | To | Allowed | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ilium-plugin-host` | `ilium-plugin-api` | yes | The host serves the types the API crate defines |
| `ilium-plugin-host` | `ilium-execution` | yes | Quota groups and the job worker bank |
| `ilium-plugin-host` | `ilium-platform` | yes | Process control, secure file access, file locks, thread priority |
| `ilium-plugin-host` | `ilium-logging` | yes | The plugin log and host log |
| `ilium-plugin-host` | `ilium-transport` | no | The host does not own a connection to clients |
| `ilium-plugin-host` | `ilium-core` | no | The host sees the tree only through a trait that the server and client implement (the **kernel facade**) |
| `ilium-server` | `ilium-plugin-host` | yes | Owns the server host and implements the kernel facade |
| `ilium-client` | `ilium-plugin-host` | yes, through one module | Owns the client host and scene host |
| `ilium-client` UI modules (`ui`, `tree_ui`, `modal` and the other presentation modules) | Wasmtime types | no | UI code sees plugin output only as `ilium-plugin-api` values |
| `ilium-ipc` | `ilium-plugin-api` | yes | Carries typed plugin records |
| `ilium-ipc` | `ilium-plugin-host` | no | IPC never carries Wasmtime values |
| `ilium-core` | any plugin crate | no | Core stays pure domain |
| `ilium-detect` | any plugin crate | no | Detection stays a pure function |
| `ilium-pty` | any plugin crate | no | PTY code never learns about plugins |
| `ilium` (the bin) | `ilium-plugin-host` | yes | The CLI process host (`requires_server: false`) |
| plugin source | any Ilium crate | no | Plugins depend only on `ilium-plugin-sdk` |

- **[HST-001]** The workspace MUST contain the crates `ilium-plugin-api`, `ilium-plugin-host` and `ilium-plugin-helper`, and `ilium-plugin-api` MUST NOT depend on Wasmtime, V8, tokio or any I/O crate.
- **[HST-002]** The dependency edges in the table above MUST hold, and a workspace test MUST fail when `cargo metadata` shows a forbidden edge.
- **[HST-003]** `ilium-core` MUST NOT depend on any plugin crate.
- **[HST-004]** `ilium-ipc` MUST carry plugin traffic as typed records from `ilium-plugin-api` and MUST NOT carry or link Wasmtime values.
- **[HST-005]** Client presentation modules MUST NOT name Wasmtime types. Only one client module, `plugin_host`, MAY depend on `ilium-plugin-host`.
- **[HST-006]** `ilium-plugin-host` MUST reach the tree, panes, settings and commands only through the kernel facade trait, so that the host can be tested with a fake kernel and no PTY.

The kernel facade is a Rust trait with one method per intent family and one per host import family. Its shape is an implementation choice, but it MUST be object safe and MUST return the outcome types of `ilium-plugin-api`.

```rust
// ilium-plugin-host/src/facade.rs (illustration of the contract, not generated)
pub trait KernelFacade: Send + Sync {
    /// Apply one intent that the caller already authorised. The facade
    /// never sees Wasmtime values; it sees api-crate types only.
    fn apply_intent(&self, origin: &Origin, intent: Intent) -> IntentResult;
    /// Read-only views of the tree, panes and agents for host imports.
    fn tree(&self) -> &dyn TreeRead;
    fn panes(&self) -> &dyn PaneRead;
    /// Which side this facade serves (server, client or cli).
    fn process_kind(&self) -> ProcessKind;
}
```

## Process map

Four kinds of operating system process can run plugin code. The table is the complete list.

| Process | How many | Hosts which sides | Hosts which tiers | Thread that owns the host | When the process exits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session server (`ilium-server`) | one per session | `server` | T1 in process; T2 and T3 through helpers | The server runtime: the dispatcher task runs on the server's tokio runtime, calls run on the plugin executor | Shutdown sequence below; every helper it spawned is terminated; clients see the connection close |
| Client (`ilium`, attached) | one per attached client | `client`, `scene` | T1 in process; T2 and T3 through helpers | The client event loop owns the host object; calls run on the client plugin executor and the scene thread | The client host stops; the server and other clients are unaffected |
| CLI process (`ilium <subcommand>` for a `cli` entry with `requires_server: false`) | one per invocation | `server` component only | T1 in process; T2 and T3 through helpers | The CLI main thread owns the host; calls run on a one-thread executor | The host deactivates the plugin with `shutdown` and drops everything |
| Sandbox helper (`ilium-plugin-helper`) | one per T2 or T3 plugin per side per hosting process | the side of its plugin | T2 and T3 only | The helper main thread runs a single-instance call loop; the parent owns the helper | The parent counts a failure for that plugin side and restarts it under the restart rule |

A CLI process that connects to a running server (`requires_server: true`, the default) hosts nothing. It sends its request to the server, and the server host runs the plugin's `cli-invoked` handler.

- **[HST-007]** A plugin side MUST be hosted by exactly one process at a time: the session server for `server`, an attached client for `client` and `scene`, or a CLI process for a `server` component that is run for a `requires_server: false` entry.
- **[HST-008]** T1 components MUST run inside the process of their side and MUST NOT run in a helper.
- **[HST-009]** T2 and T3 components MUST run only inside a sandbox helper, and the parent process MUST NOT instantiate a T2 or T3 component in its own Engine.
- **[HST-010]** The exit of a client process, a CLI process or a helper MUST NOT stop the session server or any other plugin side.

The server does not run `client` or `scene` components, and a client does not run `server` components. This corrects the loose phrase "the Ilium process" that earlier pages used: wherever a page says that a T1 plugin runs "in the Ilium process", it means the process that hosts that plugin's side, as this table defines.

## Per-side hosting

### Server host

There is one server host per session server. It owns the Engine of the server process, the plugin executor of the server, the dispatcher, the quota accounting for server-side plugin sides and the telemetry registry of the server. It hosts every `server` side of every enabled plugin, and the server side of a two-sided package. It is the only host that subscribes to the event journal (see [Events](/pages/api-events/)).

- **[HST-011]** A session MUST have exactly one server host, and the dispatcher MUST be the only subscriber of the kernel event journal on behalf of plugins.
- **[HST-012]** Server-side plugin state (queues, failure counts, restart timers, quota buckets) MUST be kept per plugin per side in the server host and MUST survive the detach and attach of clients.

### Client host

There is one client host per attached client process. Two clients attached to the same session have separate client hosts, separate Stores, separate widget state, separate failure counts and separate restart timers. A plugin that fails in client A keeps running in client B.

- **[HST-013]** Each attached client MUST own its client host, and a failure in one client host MUST NOT change the failure count, restart timer or enabled state of the same plugin in another client.
- **[HST-014]** A plugin disabled by the restart rule in one client MUST stay enabled in other clients, and the notice MUST be shown only to the client that disabled it.

### Scene host

The scene host runs inside the client process. It is a separate set of Stores (one per running scene instance) that share the client's Engine and epoch ticker. It has its own thread, the scene thread, so a slow frame never delays the client's render or input thread. The scene thread produces frames into a double buffer, and the compositor reads the newest complete frame at each client frame. The details are in [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) and [Host rendering pipeline](/pages/reference-host-rendering/).

- **[HST-015]** Scene instances MUST live in Stores that are separate from the client host's Stores, and scene frame calls MUST run on a thread that is neither the client UI thread nor a client plugin executor thread.
- **[HST-016]** A scene frame that is not ready when the compositor needs it MUST NOT delay the client frame. The compositor MUST reuse the previous complete frame.

### Job instances

A plugin that uses `jobs.run` gets a second kind of instance: a **job instance** of the same component, created for one job from the `InstancePre` of the plugin side (design decision A21 in [Background jobs](/pages/background-jobs/)). Job instances are not the plugin's main instance. They have their own Store, their own memory limit (`job_memory_mib`) and no access to the plugin's main instance state. The number running at once is the plugin's `concurrent_jobs`. They run on the job worker bank of `ilium-execution`, not on the plugin executor. See [Jobs](/pages/api-jobs/).

- **[HST-017]** A job MUST run in its own Store, MUST NOT share linear memory with the plugin's main instance, and MUST run on the job worker bank.
- **[HST-018]** The count of live job instances of one plugin side MUST NOT exceed `concurrent_jobs`; further jobs wait in the job queue.

### CLI-process host

A `cli` entry with `requires_server: false` runs the plugin's `server` component in the CLI process. The host starts when the plugin is first needed for the command, activates the plugin with the trigger `cli:<name>`, delivers one `cli-invoked` event, waits until the plugin has returned its exit status (or the command deadline expires), and then deactivates with `shutdown` and exits. No tree exists in that process. Host imports that need the tree, panes or agents return `unavailable` with the message `no session`.

- **[HST-019]** A CLI-process host MUST host only the plugin named by the entry plus the services it `requires`, and MUST NOT activate any other plugin.
- **[HST-020]** In a CLI-process host, imports that need a session MUST return `unavailable` and MUST NOT start a server.

## Ownership

One Engine per process. One Store per plugin instance. The table assigns each registry to exactly one owner and says how others see it.

| Registry | Owner | Persisted where | How other processes see it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Package store (installed packages, content-addressed) | The package directory under the Ilium data directory, written by `ilium plugin install` | `<data dir>/plugins/packages/<id>/<version>/` | Every host reads it at start; the handshake carries id, version and content hash (see [Host IPC protocol](/pages/reference-host-ipc/)) |
| Grant store | The server host (single writer, file lock from `ilium-platform`) | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/grants.json` (mode 0600), written atomically | The server pushes `grants-changed` control records to clients; a CLI-process host reads the file under a shared lock |
| Contribution registry (commands, settings tabs, decoration slots, panes, toolbar items, keys, scenes) | Static part: each host for the sides it hosts. Retained part (decorations, virtual rows, status segments, frame slots, attention): the server host | Not persisted except what the plugin saves | Retained server contributions replicate to every client as `ContributionDelta` |
| Extension-point registry | The host of the side that owns the point | Not persisted | A client-owned point exists only in that client; a server-owned point only on the server (see [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/)) |
| Service registry | The server host for `server` providers, each client host for `client` providers | Not persisted | A service call is routed to the side that the manifest names; a cross-side call travels as a message |
| Plugin enable state and failure counters | The host of the side, in memory; the enable flag is stored in the user config | `config.toml` `[plugins.<id>]` for the flag only | The flag is read at start; counters never leave the process |
| Quota groups | `ilium-execution`, one group per plugin side per process | Not persisted | Telemetry only |
| Telemetry registry | Each host | Not persisted | `ilium plugin stats` reads the server's registry and each client's through the `Control` envelope (see [Host telemetry](/pages/reference-host-telemetry/)) |

- **[HST-021]** A process MUST create exactly one Wasmtime `Engine` for plugin use, and every Store in that process MUST be created from it.
- **[HST-022]** Each plugin instance, including each job instance, MUST have its own `Store`.
- **[HST-023]** The grant store MUST have a single writer at any time and MUST be replaced atomically, so a reader never sees a partial file.
- **[HST-024]** The retained contribution registry for server-side plugins MUST be owned by the server host, and a client MUST hold only a replica built from `ContributionDelta` records.
- **[HST-025]** The extension-point registry and the service registry MUST be per hosting process. A point or service owned by a client side MUST NOT be visible to server-side plugins.

## Startup and shutdown

### Server start

1. The kernel boots and loads the configuration (`config.toml`, including `[plugins]` and `[plugins.limits]`).
2. The kernel restores the snapshot (`restore_snapshot`). No plugin exists yet, so no plugin sees the restore as a series of events.
3. The host creates the Engine, starts the epoch ticker and the plugin executor (see [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/)).
4. The host loads the package store. For every installed and enabled package it verifies the manifest, the signature and the content hash, checks the API version, validates the component, and registers static contributions. These are the eager steps. Nothing is instantiated.
5. The host builds the service graph. A cycle in `requires` is refused; the plugin stays disabled with `manifest.requires-cycle`.
6. The host activates every plugin whose `activation` list contains `startup`, in dependency order: a service provider before its consumers. Other plugins stay inactive until their trigger fires. These are the lazy steps.
7. The dispatcher delivers exactly one `tree-changed` batch for the restored tree to each activated plugin that subscribes to it. The restore is never replayed.
8. The server accepts client connections. (Clients that connect earlier than step 6 completes are refused with the retriable error `server.starting`; a client retries for 5 seconds.)

Steps 3 to 7 have the time budget `HOST-START` in [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/).

### Server shutdown

1. The server stops accepting new clients and stops the services that depend on plugins in their declared order.
2. The host refuses new submissions. They complete as `cancelled`.
3. Each active plugin side receives `deactivate(shutdown)` in reverse activation order, each within `deactivate_deadline_ms`. The total for all plugins is bounded by 5 seconds; plugins not reached in that time are dropped without a call.
4. Pending requests are cancelled, helpers are terminated, instances are dropped and quota groups are released.
5. The server runs `drain_session_work` and writes the final snapshot. The plugin host has stopped, so no plugin intent can reach the snapshot after the writer starts.

### Client start and stop

On start, the client connects, completes the handshake, receives the full retained contribution replica, starts its `startup` client plugins, renders the first frame and activates other plugins when their trigger fires. On stop, the client host deactivates its plugins with `shutdown` (total bound 2 seconds), cancels in-flight submissions locally and disconnects. The server learns of the detach from the closed connection (see [Host IPC protocol](/pages/reference-host-ipc/)).

### CLI process

The CLI process creates an Engine, loads only the needed package, activates it, delivers the event, deactivates it and exits. Its time to first plugin call has the budget `CLI-COLD` in [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/).

- **[HST-026]** The server host MUST start after `restore_snapshot` and MUST deliver exactly one `tree-changed` batch for the restored tree to each plugin that subscribes to it, and no replay of restore steps.
- **[HST-027]** Manifest verification, signature verification, component validation and static contribution registration MUST be completed eagerly before any plugin is activated. Instantiation MUST be lazy except for plugins with the `startup` trigger.
- **[HST-028]** A service provider MUST be activated before the plugins that `requires` it, and a cycle in `requires` MUST leave the plugins in the cycle disabled with `manifest.requires-cycle`.
- **[HST-029]** On server shutdown the host MUST stop after the services stop and before `drain_session_work` and the final snapshot, and MUST refuse new submissions as `cancelled` before the first `deactivate`.
- **[HST-030]** `deactivate(shutdown)` MUST be called in reverse activation order, and the total shutdown time spent in plugin calls MUST NOT exceed 5 seconds.
- **[HST-031]** A client that connects before the server host finished step 6 MUST be refused with the retriable error `server.starting`.
- **[HST-032]** The client host MUST bound its own shutdown at 2 seconds in total, and a client that exits MUST NOT prevent the server from delivering outcomes for other clients.

## Safe start

A user who cannot start a session because of a plugin has two switches. Both apply to the process that hosts plugins and are passed by the `ilium` launcher to the server it starts.

| Switch | Effect |
|---|---|
| `ilium --safe-plugins` (or `ILIUM_SAFE_PLUGINS=1`) | Loads only the bundled T1 plugins with their default grants. All T2 and T3 packages stay installed but are not loaded. Every `replaces` entry is ignored, so the built-in core plugin runs. The footer shows `Safe plugin mode: third-party plugins are off.` |
| `ilium --no-plugins` (or `ILIUM_NO_PLUGINS=1`) | The plugin host does not start. The session boots with the kernel only: terminal panes, the tree with kernel-drawn plain rows, the layout, the keymap defaults and the recovery page work. Features that live in core plugins are absent. |

- **[HST-033]** `--safe-plugins` MUST load no T2 or T3 package and MUST ignore `replaces`, and `--no-plugins` MUST start no plugin host. Neither switch MUST change installed packages, grants or stored plugin data.
- **[HST-034]** A session MUST boot to a usable terminal, tree and recovery page with `--no-plugins`.

## Failure containment

The host contains each failure at the smallest unit that owns the broken state. The table states what each failure takes down and what must keep running.

| Failure | What stops | What must keep running |
|---|---|---|
| A guest trap (panic, unreachable, out-of-bounds, stack overflow) | That plugin side's instance. Pending requests it owned complete as `cancelled`; its retained contributions are marked stale. | Every other plugin, the kernel, other sides of the same plugin |
| A stuck queue (queue full with a never-dropped event) | That plugin side is restarted as a failure | Everything else |
| A deadline breach (hard) | The call traps, as above | Everything else |
| A helper crash or kill | The one plugin side in that helper | The parent process, other helpers, other plugins |
| A Rust panic inside a host import implementation | The call is caught at the import boundary (`catch_unwind`), the instance traps with `host.import-panic`, and the panic is logged with the import name | The parent process and every other plugin. The kernel facade is never left holding a lock across an import (see requirement HST-038) |
| A Wasmtime `Engine`-level error (for example an internal compilation error) | The affected load or instantiation fails with `host.engine-error`; the plugin is not activated | The Engine and other plugins. If creating the Engine itself fails, the host does not start: the server logs `host.engine-failed` and continues in `--no-plugins` mode |
| Out of memory in one Store (linear memory limit) | The growth traps the instance (the guest never observes -1) and logs `memory limit <N> MiB reached`; the plugin side restarts under the restart rule | Other Stores; the process |
| Session memory budget reached | A new instance is refused and logged, not counted as a failure | Existing instances |

- **[HST-035]** A guest trap MUST end only the instance that trapped. Pending requests of that instance MUST complete as `cancelled`, and its retained contributions MUST be kept and marked stale.
- **[HST-036]** A panic in a host import implementation MUST be caught at the import boundary, MUST trap only the calling instance with the error `host.import-panic`, and MUST NOT unwind into the dispatcher or the kernel.
- **[HST-037]** If the Engine cannot be created, the process MUST continue without a plugin host as if started with `--no-plugins`, and MUST log `host.engine-failed`.
- **[HST-038]** The host MUST NOT hold a kernel lock while a guest call is running, and an import MUST take kernel locks only for the duration of its own work.
- **[HST-039]** A helper process failure MUST NOT crash or hang the parent process.

### A core plugin that the restart rule disables

The 30 core plugins (see [Core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/)) carry features of Ilium. The restart rule applies to them like to any plugin, with one change: a core plugin that the rule disables makes the host show the **kernel recovery page**. The page belongs to the kernel, not to a plugin, so it works with every plugin off. It lists every plugin with its tier, state, last failure and an on or off switch, and it shows how to start with `--safe-plugins`.

- The session still boots. The disabled state is stored, so the plugin stays off at the next start until the user turns it on.
- The kernel recovery page opens once, automatically, in the client that is attached when the failure happens, and later through the kernel command `kernel.open-recovery`, which has the default key `Ctrl+Alt+R` in the kernel keymap and cannot be removed by a keymap plugin.
- A kernel fallback covers the features that would leave the screen unusable. If `ilium.core.tree` is disabled, the kernel draws tree rows as the node name and a status glyph only, with no decorations, virtual rows or toolbar. If `ilium.core.layout` is disabled, the kernel keeps the last split geometry. If `ilium.core.settings` is disabled, the Settings screen shows only the recovery page. Other features are simply absent until the plugin is turned on.
- A failure of `ilium.core.sessions` does not stop the final snapshot: the kernel snapshot writer runs without the plugin and writes the plugin's last stored sections unchanged.

- **[HST-040]** When the restart rule disables a core plugin, the session MUST keep running, the disabled state MUST persist across restarts, and the kernel recovery page MUST open once in the affected client.
- **[HST-041]** The kernel recovery page and the command `kernel.open-recovery` MUST work with every plugin disabled and MUST NOT be removable by a plugin.
- **[HST-042]** With `ilium.core.tree` disabled, the kernel MUST draw tree rows from node names and status only.

## Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Result | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Helper binary missing and a T2 or T3 package is installed | The package stays disabled with `host.helper-missing`; T1 plugins run | `host.helper-missing` |
| Engine cannot be created | Server continues without plugins | `host.engine-failed` |
| A client connects while the server host is still starting | Retriable refusal | `server.starting` |
| CLI-process host needs the tree | `unavailable`, message `no session` | `unavailable` |
| Two clients disable the same plugin at different times | Each client disables it independently | none |
| Server host shutdown takes longer than 5 s | Remaining plugins are dropped without `deactivate`; their restore bytes are not kept | `host.shutdown-timeout` (logged) |
| Panic inside an import | The calling instance traps | `host.import-panic` |
| The grant store file is unreadable at start | The host starts with default grants for T1 only and refuses T2 and T3 packages until the file is repaired | `host.grants-unreadable` |
| `--safe-plugins` and `--no-plugins` both given | `--no-plugins` wins | none |
| A package on disk is changed after install | The content hash check fails and the plugin stays disabled | `package.corrupt` |

- **[HST-043]** When both safe-start switches are given, `--no-plugins` MUST win.
- **[HST-044]** An unreadable grant store MUST NOT start T2 or T3 plugins and MUST NOT grant a T1 plugin more than its default grants.
- **[HST-045]** A package whose content hash differs from the recorded hash MUST NOT be loaded.

# Performance budgets and benchmarks

## Performance budgets and benchmarks

This page is the normative list of performance budgets of the plugin host and the benchmarks that check them. A budget is a number that the implementation MUST meet. A benchmark is a program in `ilium-plugin-bench` that measures one budget. The plugin author's view is in [Performance](/pages/performance/). Requirement ids are `[HST-300]` to `[HST-313]`.

## You will need

- [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/) for the Wasmtime configuration that the benchmarks record.
- [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/), [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/), [Sandbox helper protocol](/pages/reference-host-helper/) and [Rendering pipeline](/pages/reference-host-rendering/) for what B10 to B24 measure.

## How a benchmark runs

- **[HST-300]** Each benchmark MUST run at least 1,000 measured iterations after at least 100 warm-up iterations, on one pinned core, with the CPU governor set to a fixed frequency where the platform allows it.
- **[HST-301]** Each result MUST record the median and the 99th percentile, the Wasmtime version, the Wasmtime `Config` (as the output of `runtime_config()`), the CPU model, the core count, the operating system and the commit.
- **[HST-302]** A benchmark MUST fail the run when the budget is missed, except where the table says "record" (a result without a target).
- **[HST-303]** Benchmarks MUST run on a release build with the target features of the shipped binary, and MUST NOT use a debug build.

The reference machine is the one named in the results file. A budget is checked on that machine. The numbers on a slower machine scale; the release gate (see [Roadmap](/pages/roadmap/)) uses the reference machine only.

## Stop rule

A miss of more than 2x on B1, B3 or B4 stops the platform plan. The design assumes that a host call costs about a microsecond and that WebAssembly code runs within a small factor of native code. A miss of that size means the assumption is wrong, and the project returns to design.

- **[HST-304]** A result more than twice the budget on B1, B3 or B4 MUST be reported as a plan stop, not as an ordinary failure.

## Benchmark table

| Id | What it measures | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | Empty host call; host call with a 64-byte string; a 400 KB `list<u8>` lowered into a host resource (`write-rows`) | Median under 1 µs; 400 KB under 0.2 ms |
| B2 | Instantiation from `Component::deserialize` and `InstancePre`: Rust component, JavaScript components. Wall time and RSS per instance | Rust under 5 ms and 4 MiB; JavaScript recorded, no target |
| B3 | Beach and Carpet at 200 by 60 cells, 300 frames: native Rust (SIMD and portable), Rust wasm, TypeScript on V8 and on JavaScript components | Rust wasm 99th percentile within 1.3x native; JavaScript routes within 1.1x of V8 where V8 is the baseline, otherwise recorded |
| B4 | 200 decoration updates through the contribution store plus one tree re-render at 300 nodes, against the in-process path | Under 1 ms extra |
| B5 | One 50-event batch to 30 instantiated plugins through `on-events`, returning 0 and 10 intents each | Under 2 ms at the 99th percentile |
| B6 | Cold server start with 40 bundled components: embedded `.cwasm` via `deserialize`, embedded `.wasm` via `Component::new` with and without the compile cache, eager and lazy activation, on-demand against pooling allocation. Binary size delta | Selects the activation mode and the allocator; HOST-START under 150 ms; added RSS under 120 MiB for the chosen option |
| B7 | B3 Rust wasm with epoch interruption and a 10 ms ticker, against without | Under 5 % |
| B8 | Detection `classify` with a 200 by 60 screen through the `detector` export, 30 panes | Under 0.5 ms per pane |
| B9 | A 2 s CPU job in a second instance and on the plugin's own instance with epoch yields every 10 ms: start overhead, RSS per job, 99th percentile of concurrent `on-events` | Start under 5 ms; concurrent 99th percentile within 1.2x of idle; selects the jobs model |
| B10 | A hook chain of 5 handlers (1 per plugin, T1) with a 1 KiB payload | Under 1 ms for the chain, excluding handler bodies |
| B11 | Opening a dynamic menu with 3 menu providers returning 20 entries each | Under 5 ms from click to first frame |
| B12 | Fairness: one plugin spins at its deadline continuously; 99th percentile `on-events` latency of 29 other plugins | Within 1.5x of idle |
| B13 | A `ui-tree` of 4,096 nodes: `views.render` return, caps check, client diff against the previous tree with 5 % changed nodes | Under 8 ms from return to painted frame |
| B14 | Contribution delta replication: 1,000 increments per second to 4 clients | Server CPU under 5 % of one core; client mirror lag under 5 ms at the 99th percentile |
| B15 | Client submission round trip: client plugin returns an intent, the server applies it, the outcome arrives | Under 3 ms at the 99th percentile on a local connection |
| B16 | Key press to start of the plugin call, T1 and T2 | 1 ms (T1) and 1.5 ms (T2) at the 99th percentile |
| B17 | Key press to bytes at the PTY through a 0.1 ms plugin handler | Under 5 ms at the 99th percentile |
| B18 | Helper round trip of a forwarded import | 0.2 ms median, 0.5 ms at the 99th percentile |
| B19 | Delay of a PTY frame while the plugin queue is full (4 MiB) | Under 1 ms at the 99th percentile |
| B20 | Server decoration change to the client mirror | Under 5 ms at the 99th percentile |
| B21 | Helper start: spawn to `Ready` for a 2 MiB component | Record; under 80 ms median expected |
| B22 | Session memory: 40 bundled plugins plus 8 T2 helpers, steady state | Added RSS under 120 MiB for the bundled set; helpers under `memory_mib + 32` MiB each |
| B23 | `ilium` CLI cold run (CLI-COLD) | Under 60 ms with a warm file cache |
| B24 | Idle cost: 40 loaded plugins, no events, 10 minutes | Under 0.5 % of one core; at most 100 wake-ups per second |

The B1 to B9 rows are the phase-0 benchmarks of the platform plan, kept with their targets. B10 to B24 are added by this reference.

- **[HST-305]** `ilium-plugin-bench` MUST contain one program for each of B1 to B24, with the id in its name.
- **[HST-306]** The release gate MUST include B1 to B9 and B16 to B20 on the reference machine, and MUST fail when any budget is missed.

## Named budgets

| Name | Definition | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| HOST-START | Time from the server process start to the point where the host accepts its first IPC attach, with the 40 bundled plugins registered (lazy activation) and the compile step skipped through `.cwasm` | 150 ms |
| CLI-COLD | Time from the start of an `ilium` CLI subcommand that a plugin contributes (`requires_server: false`) to its exit, when the file cache is warm and the server is not running. It loads only the plugins that contribute that subcommand | 60 ms |
| KEY-PATH | Key press at the client to bytes at the PTY, when a plugin handles the key | 5 ms at the 99th percentile |
| ADD-RSS | Resident memory added by the plugin host with the 40 bundled plugins registered, none activated | 120 MiB (including all of the above) |

- **[HST-307]** HOST-START MUST be at most 150 ms on the reference machine for the 40 bundled plugins, measured by B6.
- **[HST-308]** CLI-COLD MUST be at most 60 ms, measured by B23, and MUST NOT start the server or any plugin that does not contribute the subcommand.
- **[HST-309]** The resident memory that the host adds with the bundled plugins registered MUST be under 120 MiB.

## Ratios against native code

| Workload | Ratio | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Beach and Carpet in Rust wasm | 99th percentile at most 1.3x | Native Rust |
| Beach and Carpet in TypeScript on a JavaScript component | At most 1.1x | The V8 path used today |
| Epoch interruption overhead | At most 5 % | The same workload without epochs |

- **[HST-310]** The Rust wasm scenes MUST be within 1.3x of native Rust at the 99th percentile on B3.
- **[HST-311]** The epoch overhead on B3 MUST be at most 5 % (B7).

## Choosing between options

Some benchmarks select an option rather than pass or fail:

| Benchmark | Decision |
|---|---|
| B6 | Pooling allocator is chosen only if the on-demand allocator misses HOST-START or B2, and pooling meets both with at most 16 MiB more RSS. Otherwise the on-demand allocator stays |
| B6 | Lazy activation is the default. Eager activation is chosen only if the lazy path misses KEY-PATH on the first key |
| B9 | If a job in a second instance meets the budgets, jobs use a second instance. Otherwise jobs share the plugin instance with epoch yields |

- **[HST-312]** The pooling allocator MUST be enabled only when B6 shows that on-demand misses HOST-START or B2, that pooling meets both, and that pooling adds at most 16 MiB of RSS.

## Runtime telemetry against the budgets

The host keeps the counters that these budgets need: call durations per class, queue depths and drops, quota rejections, helper round trips, render durations, and memory per plugin. See [Telemetry and plugin health](/pages/reference-host-telemetry/) for the names. The same data feeds the `degraded` health condition "near-misses" of [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/): 5 or more calls in 5 minutes that took at least 80 % of their deadline.

- **[HST-313]** The host MUST count a call as a near-miss when it ends in time but took at least 80 % of its deadline, and MUST use that count for the `degraded` health condition.

## See also

- [Performance](/pages/performance/) for the guidance to plugin authors.
- [Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/) and [Platform support](/pages/reference-platform-support/).

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Sandbox helper protocol

## Sandbox helper protocol

Plugins of tiers T2 and T3 run inside a helper process. This page defines how the host starts a helper, the messages between the host and the helper, how deadlines include the round trip, how helper memory is charged, what limits the helper count, and how a helper dies. The confinement of the helper (namespaces, seccomp, cgroup) is defined in the [Sandbox reference](/pages/reference-sandbox/) and is not repeated. Requirement ids are `[HST-150]` to `[HST-171]`.

## You will need

- [Sandbox reference](/pages/reference-sandbox/) for confinement and the trust rules for messages.
- [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/) for the Wasmtime configuration that the helper shares.
- [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) for heartbeats and restart counting.

## What a helper is

The helper is the binary `ilium-plugin-helper`, installed beside `ilium`. It contains the same Engine configuration as the host (one `runtime_config()` function, see [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/)) and a small call loop.

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Granularity | One helper per plugin per side per hosting process, as in the [Sandbox reference](/pages/reference-sandbox/). The server hosts one helper per T2 or T3 plugin side. Each client that runs a client half starts its own |
| Platform | Linux only. On Windows and macOS the host refuses T2 and T3 with `sandbox.unavailable` (see [Platform support](/pages/reference-platform-support/)) |
| Start | Lazy, at the first activation of the plugin side |
| Stop | At deactivation, at a trap, at shutdown, or when the host kills it |
| Instances | One Store at a time, one call at a time |

- **[HST-150]** The host MUST start one helper per T2 or T3 plugin side and per hosting process, and MUST NOT host two plugins in one helper.
- **[HST-151]** The helper binary MUST be `ilium-plugin-helper` in the same directory as the `ilium` executable, MUST use the same `runtime_config()` as the host, and MUST refuse to start if the host passes a different Wasmtime fingerprint.
- **[HST-152]** A helper MUST start only at the first activation of its plugin side.

## Starting a helper

The host starts a helper in this order. Each step is checked, and a failure stops the start with `helper.spawn-failed` and the failing step.

1. The host creates a `socketpair` (the dispatcher channel). It does not use a named socket or a path.
2. The host forks. In the child, before `exec`, it sets up bubblewrap-style namespaces, the mount layout, `no_new_privs` and the cgroup (or `RLIMIT_AS` and `RLIMIT_NPROC` when no controller is delegated), as in the Sandbox reference.
3. The child closes every file descriptor except the dispatcher channel and stdio on `/dev/null`, installs the seccomp filter, and executes `ilium-plugin-helper`.
4. The helper sends `Hello` with its protocol version and Wasmtime fingerprint.
5. The host checks the fingerprint and sends `Instantiate` with the component bytes (or their cache key), the grants, the limits and the `restored` bytes.
6. The helper compiles or loads the component, instantiates it and answers `Ready`.
7. The host then sends `CallExport` for `activate`.

The component bytes are sent over the channel in chunks of at most 4 MiB. The helper holds the file in memory only and never gets a path into the package store.

- **[HST-153]** The dispatcher channel MUST be an inherited `socketpair`. The helper MUST NOT create sockets or open any path outside its mounts to receive work.
- **[HST-154]** The host MUST treat a missing `Hello`, a wrong fingerprint or a `Ready` later than 5,000 ms after `Instantiate` as `helper.spawn-failed`, kill the helper, and count one failure only when the plugin had already started once.

## Messages

The channel carries length-prefixed `bincode` messages. A message is at most 4 MiB (8 MiB for a `terminal-view` frame), at most 5,000 messages per second per helper, as in the Sandbox reference.

| Message | From | Body | Reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Hello` | Helper | Protocol version, Wasmtime fingerprint, helper build | `Instantiate` |
| `Instantiate` | Host | Component bytes in chunks, grants, limits, restored bytes | `Ready` or `InstantiateFailed(code)` |
| `Ready` | Helper | Exports found, memory at start | none |
| `CallExport` | Host | Call id, export name, argument bytes, deadline in ms | `CallResult` |
| `CallResult` | Helper | Call id, result bytes, or a trap with its code | none |
| `HostCall` | Helper | Call id, import name, argument bytes | `HostReply` |
| `HostReply` | Host | Call id, result bytes or an error | none |
| `Cancel` | Host | Call id | none (the call ends in `CallResult` with a trap or its normal result) |
| `Shutdown` | Host | Reason | helper exits with code 0 |
| `Heartbeat` | Both | Counter | `Heartbeat` echo, answered on the helper control thread |
| `Log` | Helper | Level, line (max 16 KiB), call id | none |

- **[HST-155]** Messages MUST be length-prefixed `bincode`, MUST NOT exceed the sizes above, and a message of an unknown kind, a bad length or a schema violation MUST end the helper and count as a failure.
- **[HST-156]** The host MUST derive the plugin identity from the channel and MUST drop any message that names another plugin (see [Sandbox reference](/pages/reference-sandbox/)).
- **[HST-157]** A `CallResult`, `HostCall` or `HostReply` MUST carry a call id that the host issued. A message with an unknown or finished call id MUST be dropped and logged `helper.stale-call`.

## Data that is large

A bulk argument (a `ui-tree`, a surface write, a file chunk, an HTTP body) is sent as a sequence of messages, each at most 4 MiB, tagged with the call id and a chunk index. The sender marks the last chunk. The receiver assembles the chunks and enforces the same caps as [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/). There is no shared memory between the host and the helper: the seccomp filter and the descriptor rule of the Sandbox reference leave only the dispatcher channel open.

- **[HST-158]** Bulk data MUST travel in chunks of at most 4 MiB over the dispatcher channel. The host MUST NOT pass file descriptors or shared memory to a helper.

## Which imports run where

| Class | Imports | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Pure compute | `codec`, `vector`, `clock.now` (coarsened), `random`, `log` (batched) | In the helper. No round trip |
| Host state or effect | Everything else: `storage`, `fs`, `http`, `process`, `ui`, submissions, `messages`, `timers`, `jobs`, `inference`, `clipboard` | Forwarded to the host with `HostCall` |

A forwarded import takes one round trip. The budget of a round trip is 0.2 ms median and 0.5 ms at the 99th percentile on an idle machine. A call with 20 forwarded imports therefore spends at most 10 ms in round trips at the 99th percentile. Authors keep this in mind for the 20 ms batch deadline (see [Performance](/pages/performance/)).

The host evaluates the grant check, the quota and the limits for a forwarded import exactly as for a T1 import. The helper never decides a grant.

- **[HST-159]** Only the pure-compute imports MAY run in the helper without a round trip. Every other import MUST be forwarded and checked by the host.
- **[HST-160]** A forwarded import round trip MUST take at most 0.2 ms median and 0.5 ms at the 99th percentile on an idle reference machine (benchmark B18).

## Deadlines include the round trip

The deadline of a call is carried in `CallExport`. The helper sets its own epoch deadline from it, so a runaway guest traps in the helper at the first tick after `d` ms, exactly as in the host. The host also runs a timer.

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| The call returns inside the deadline | `CallResult` is delivered normally |
| The helper epoch deadline fires | The helper traps the instance and sends `CallResult` with `host.deadline` |
| No `CallResult` arrives within 500 ms after the deadline | The host sends SIGKILL (SIGTERM first is not used) and treats it as `helper.hung`. One failure is counted |
| Three heartbeats in a row are missed | Same as above |

The time spent in the host serving `HostCall` messages counts inside the call's deadline, because the guest is waiting. The time that the host spends before it sends `CallExport` (queue time) does not.

- **[HST-161]** The deadline of a helper call MUST include the time of every `HostCall` round trip made during that call.
- **[HST-162]** The helper MUST set its own epoch deadline from the `CallExport` deadline. The host MUST kill a helper that has not answered 500 ms after that deadline and MUST count one failure.
- **[HST-163]** The host MUST kill a helper after three missed heartbeats (a ping every 1 s).

## Memory

The memory of the helper is charged to the session. The charge for one helper is its plugin's `memory_mib` plus a fixed overhead of 32 MiB, which is the same overhead that the cgroup limit uses.

| Item | Charge |
|---|---|
| Helper | `memory_mib + 32` MiB |
| T1 instance in the host | `memory_mib` |
| Session total limit | `session_memory_mib` 1,024 (see [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)) |

When the charge for an activation would pass `session_memory_mib`, the activation is refused with `session.memory-exceeded`. This refusal does not count as a failure, because the plugin did nothing wrong. The side stays `inactive` with the reason `host-capacity` and activation is retried, as in [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).

With cgroup v2 delegated, the kernel enforces `memory.max`. Without it, the helper uses `RLIMIT_AS` and the host samples RSS once a second. An out-of-memory kill is reported as a trap `limit-exceeded(memory)` and counts as a failure.

- **[HST-164]** The host MUST charge `memory_mib + 32` MiB per helper to `session_memory_mib` at spawn and release it at exit.
- **[HST-165]** An activation that would exceed `session_memory_mib` MUST be refused with `session.memory-exceeded`, MUST NOT count as a failure, and MUST leave the side `inactive` with the reason `host-capacity`.

## Helper count

The number of helpers per session is capped by `session_helpers`: default 16, ceiling 32. A helper that is idle (the plugin has no calls and no work for 60 s) is shut down with `Shutdown` and restarted on demand; its Store is dropped after a `deactivate` with state saved.

When the cap is reached, the host refuses a further activation with `helper.too-many`. This refusal does not count as a failure, because the plugin did nothing wrong. The plugin shows as `installed-not-running` with the reason, and it activates when a helper is free.

- **[HST-166]** The host MUST cap live helpers at `session_helpers` and MUST refuse a further activation with `helper.too-many`, without counting a failure.
- **[HST-167]** The host SHOULD shut down a helper that has been idle for 60 s, after `deactivate`, and start it again at the next need.

## Death of a helper

| Cause | What the host sees | Effect on this plugin | Other plugins |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crash during a call | Channel closed | One failure; pending requests complete as `cancelled` | None, because helpers are per plugin |
| Crash while idle | Channel closed | No failure; the host restarts it at the next need | None |
| Hung (no answer) | Missed answer or heartbeats | One failure; the host kills it | None |
| Killed for memory | Exit signal | One failure | None |
| Protocol error | Bad message | One failure; the host kills it | None |
| Host asked it to stop | `Shutdown` | No failure | None |

The host restarts a helper at most 5 times in 10 minutes. The sixth start moves the server side of the T2 and T3 plugins of the session to `stopped-by-failure` with the reason `helper.unstable` (see [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/)). The restart rule for the plugin itself (1 s, 5 s, then disable) applies in addition.

On termination the host sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 2 s. On shutdown of the server, all helpers receive `Shutdown`, then SIGKILL after 2 s.

- **[HST-168]** A helper that dies during a call MUST count one failure for its plugin, and a helper that dies while idle MUST NOT count one.
- **[HST-169]** After a helper dies, every request pending on it MUST complete as `cancelled`, and no retained state in the helper MUST be assumed.
- **[HST-170]** The host MUST allow at most 5 helper starts in 10 minutes for a session, and MUST then disable the T2 and T3 plugins of that session with `helper.unstable`.
- **[HST-171]** Termination MUST be SIGTERM followed by SIGKILL after 2 s.

## Errors

| Id | When | Counts |
|---|---|---|
| `helper.spawn-failed` | A start step failed, wrong fingerprint, `Ready` too late | only after a first successful start |
| `helper.protocol-error` | Malformed or unknown message | yes |
| `helper.hung` | No answer 500 ms after the deadline, or three missed heartbeats | yes |
| `helper.stale-call` | Message for an unknown call id | no |
| `helper.too-many` | `session_helpers` reached | no |
| `helper.unstable` | More than 5 starts in 10 minutes | disables T2 and T3 of the session |
| `session.memory-exceeded` | Charge would pass `session_memory_mib` | no |
| `sandbox.unavailable` | Prerequisites missing, root user, or non-Linux platform | no |

## See also

- [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) for deadlines and cancellation.
- [Platform support](/pages/reference-platform-support/) for the platforms that can run a helper.
- [Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/) and [Threat model](/pages/reference-threat-model/).

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Plugin traffic over IPC

## Plugin traffic over IPC

Plugins run in the server and in each client. The two halves of one plugin talk through the same local connection that already carries pane frames. This page defines the messages, the handshake, the mirrored tree, how a client submission reaches the server and returns, what happens on reconnect, and how plugin traffic is kept from starving the terminal. Requirement ids are `[HST-100]` to `[HST-125]`.

## You will need

- [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/) for the process map.
- [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for submissions, outcomes and deduplication.
- [Messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/) for plugin-to-plugin messages.

## Transport

The channel is the existing local connection of `ilium-transport` (a Unix domain socket, a named pipe on Windows). `ilium-ipc` frames each message as a length prefix followed by a `bincode` body. The frame limit is 64 MiB. This page adds no new connection and no new framing.

| Direction | Existing type | New variant | Carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client to server | `ClientRequest` | `ClientRequest::Plugin(PluginEnvelope)` | Forwarded submissions, plugin messages, replies to server-initiated client requests, control messages |
| Server to client | `ServerEvent` | `ServerEvent::Plugin(PluginEnvelope)` | Outcomes, plugin messages, server-sourced events, client requests, control messages |
| Server to client | `ServerEvent` | `ServerEvent::Contributions(ContributionDelta)` | Retained contributions that the client draws |
| Server to client | `ServerEvent` | `ServerEvent::Rejected(Rejection)` | A refused handshake or envelope, with a named error |

```rust
pub struct PluginEnvelope {
    pub plugin: PluginId,        // owner of the traffic
    pub seq: u64,                // per connection and direction, from 1
    pub body: EnvelopeBody,
}

pub enum EnvelopeBody {
    Submit(Submission),                // client to server
    Outcome(OutcomeRecord),            // server to client
    Message(PluginMessage),            // both directions
    ClientRequest(ClientRequestCall),  // server to client
    ClientReply(ClientReplyBody),      // client to server
    Event(SourcedEvent),               // server to client, events the client half subscribed to
    Control(ControlBody),              // Subscribe, Resync, GrantsChanged, Stats
}
```

There is no `HookCall` variant. A hook never crosses a process (see [Scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/)).

- **[HST-100]** Plugin traffic MUST use `ClientRequest::Plugin`, `ServerEvent::Plugin`, `ServerEvent::Contributions` and `ServerEvent::Rejected` on the existing connection, and MUST NOT open another connection or change the framing.
- **[HST-101]** `EnvelopeBody` MUST NOT contain a variant that carries a hook call or any guest call. Guest calls MUST NOT cross a process boundary.
- **[HST-102]** `seq` MUST increase by one for each envelope in one direction of one connection. A receiver MUST treat a gap as a protocol error and close the connection with `ipc.sequence-gap`.

## Handshake

`Attach` and `AttachInteractive` gain a field `hello`.

```rust
pub struct PluginHello {
    pub plugin_protocol: u16,         // PLUGIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1
    pub contract: String,             // "0.1.0"
    pub installed: Vec<InstalledPlugin>,
}
pub struct InstalledPlugin { pub id: PluginId, pub version: String, pub content_hash: [u8; 32] }
```

`ilium-ipc` gains the constant `PLUGIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION: u16 = 1`. No such constant exists before the plugin system.

| Case | Server answer | Client behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin_protocol` and `contract` equal | `Attached` with the server's plugin set and a full contribution snapshot | Runs normally |
| `plugin_protocol` differs, or `contract` differs | `Rejected(ipc.protocol-mismatch)`, then close | Prints "client and server speak different plugin protocols; start the matching client" and exits with code 76 |
| Same protocol, but a plugin differs in version or hash between client and server | `Attached`; both sides list the skew | Only the client half of that plugin is disabled with `plugin.version-skew` |
| A plugin is installed in the client but not in the server | `Attached` | The client half is disabled with `plugin.server-missing` |
| A plugin is installed in the server but not in the client | `Attached` | The server half runs; its client-owned contributions are absent and shown as "needs client update" in the health view |

Code 76 and the key for the recovery page are chosen by this contract; see [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/).

- **[HST-103]** A client MUST send `hello` in every `Attach` and `AttachInteractive`. A server MUST answer a mismatch of `plugin_protocol` or `contract` with `Rejected(ipc.protocol-mismatch)` and close the connection.
- **[HST-104]** A client that receives `ipc.protocol-mismatch` MUST print the cause and exit with code 76 without drawing the interface.
- **[HST-105]** A plugin-set skew MUST disable only the client half of the affected plugin, with `plugin.version-skew` or `plugin.server-missing`. The server half and all other plugins MUST keep running.
- **[HST-106]** The protocol constant MUST be a `u16` named `PLUGIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION` in `ilium-ipc`, and MUST change only when the envelope or handshake layout changes.

## Contributions: the delta stream

Retained contributions that the client draws (decorations, status segments, frame slots, virtual rows, row actions, annotations that a server plugin owns) are replicated as a stream of **deltas**. The server owns the registry. Each client holds a mirror.

```rust
pub struct ContributionDelta {
    pub sequence: u64,             // per connection, from 1; snapshot has sequence 1
    pub kind: DeltaKind,           // Snapshot | Increment
    pub ops: Vec<ContributionOp>,  // Put(id, entry) | Remove(id) | Clear(plugin)
}
```

- On attach the server sends one `Snapshot` and then `Increment`s with consecutive `sequence`.
- A client that sees a `sequence` gap discards its mirror, sends `Control::Resync`, and the server answers with a new `Snapshot`.
- A delta is at most 4 MiB. A larger change is split into several increments.
- Increments are **coalescable**: when the writer queue is under pressure, several increments for the same id are merged into one.

- **[HST-107]** The first contribution message after attach MUST be a `Snapshot`, and every later one an `Increment` with the next `sequence`.
- **[HST-108]** A client MUST resync on a `sequence` gap, and the server MUST answer `Control::Resync` with a full `Snapshot`.
- **[HST-109]** A delta MUST NOT exceed 4 MiB.

## The mirrored tree

The client keeps a **mirror** of the tree: nodes, kinds, titles, status, attention and the metadata keys that plugins may read. The server sends tree changes as before, and a plugin half in the client reads the mirror.

The order matters for correctness. A plugin on the client submits an intent such as `create-pane`. The server applies it, the tree changes, and the client's plugin half expects to find the new node when it receives the completion.

- **[HST-110]** The server MUST send the tree change caused by a forwarded submission BEFORE the `request-completed` outcome of the same submission, on the same connection.
- **[HST-111]** The mirror MUST be updated before the client half's event queue receives the matching `tree-changed` event, and a `request-completed` MUST NOT be delivered to a plugin before the mirror shows the effect.

## Forwarded submissions

A client-hosted plugin cannot change the tree itself. Its intents are forwarded to the server in `Submit` envelopes. The sequence for one intent is as follows.

<text x="50" y="16" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor">Plugin</text>

<figcaption>The tree change is sent before the outcome, so the plugin finds the new node when it hears that the request completed.</figcaption>
</figure>

Deduplication works as in [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/), with one change for forwarded submissions: the dedup scope is the pair (plugin, client id), and the server keeps the table for 10 minutes, measured on the wall clock from the accepted time that the journal persists (a key is free at exactly 600,000 ms). Two clients that submit the same key for the same plugin are two submissions.

- **[HST-112]** A client MUST forward each submission of a client-hosted plugin in a `Submit` envelope and MUST NOT apply tree or session effects itself.
- **[HST-113]** The dedup scope of a forwarded submission MUST be the pair (plugin id, client id), the window MUST be 10 minutes, and the table MUST be held by the server.
- **[HST-114]** The server MUST check the grant of the plugin at the time of application, not at the time of sending, and a submission whose grant was revoked in between MUST complete as `revoked`.
- **[HST-115]** The server MUST answer each `Submit` with exactly one `Outcome`.

## Reconnect and outcome replay

A client can lose the connection and attach again. The server keeps outcome records for a client id for a **grace period of 30 seconds**.

- On re-attach with the same client id and the last `seq` that the client saw, the server replays the outcome records with a higher `seq`, up to 1,024 records, and then sends a new contribution snapshot.
- The client keeps the submissions that have no outcome. After re-attach it sends them again with the same dedup keys. The server answers a duplicate from the table.
- After the grace period, the server discards the records. Submissions of that client whose effects the server has not applied complete as `cancelled` and nothing replays them.
- A client that sends a `Submit` while detached queues it, with a limit of 256 submissions. The 257th queued submission completes as `refused(busy)` at once. Submissions still queued when the client exits complete as `cancelled`.

- **[HST-116]** The server MUST keep outcome records for 30 seconds after a client connection closes, at most 1,024 records per client id.
- **[HST-117]** On re-attach within the grace period the server MUST replay outcomes with a higher `seq` than the client reports and MUST then send a contribution snapshot.
- **[HST-118]** After the grace period, unapplied submissions of that client MUST complete as `cancelled`.
- **[HST-119]** A detached client MUST queue at most 256 submissions and MUST complete later ones as `refused(busy)` at once. Submissions still queued when the client exits MUST complete as `cancelled`.

## Writer fairness

The server writes frames to each client through one writer. Pane frames (terminal output) are the priority, because the user sees them as typing latency. Plugin traffic gets a guaranteed share so that it cannot starve either.

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Order | PTY frames first |
| Guaranteed plugin share | 1 plugin envelope for every 8 frames when both queues are non-empty |
| Plugin queue bound | 4 MiB or 4,096 records, whichever comes first |
| Overflow of the plugin queue | Coalescable increments are merged, then `Control::Resync` is flagged for that client |
| Hard cap | 16 MiB of queued plugin data disconnects the client with `ipc.client-too-slow` |

A client that reconnects after `ipc.client-too-slow` receives a snapshot. Pane output is never dropped by this rule.

- **[HST-120]** The writer MUST send PTY frames before plugin envelopes and MUST guarantee one plugin envelope for every eight frames while plugin data is queued.
- **[HST-121]** The plugin queue MUST be bounded at 4 MiB or 4,096 records. On overflow the server MUST merge coalescable increments first and flag a resync second.
- **[HST-122]** A client whose queued plugin data exceeds 16 MiB MUST be disconnected with `ipc.client-too-slow`.
- **[HST-123]** Plugin traffic MUST NOT delay a PTY frame by more than the time to write one plugin envelope.

## Payload limits

All caps are below the 64 MiB frame limit. The host checks them before encoding.

| Payload | Cap | Error |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin message body | 1 MiB | `ipc.payload-too-large` |
| Topic payload | 64 KiB | `ipc.payload-too-large` |
| `ui-tree` of a view | 1 MiB, 4 MiB with the T1 ceiling | `ipc.payload-too-large` |
| Surface write | 16 MiB | `ipc.payload-too-large` |
| Whole envelope | about 17 MiB | `ipc.payload-too-large` |
| Contribution delta | 4 MiB | `ipc.payload-too-large` |

An oversized item is refused at the sender. The sender's call completes with `failed(too-large)`.

- **[HST-124]** The sender MUST check the caps above and refuse an oversized item with `ipc.payload-too-large` before it is encoded.
- **[HST-125]** A receiver MUST drop an envelope above 17 MiB and close the connection with `ipc.payload-too-large`.

## Errors

| Id | When | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ipc.protocol-mismatch` | Different `plugin_protocol` or `contract` | Rejected; client exits 76 |
| `ipc.sequence-gap` | A gap in envelope `seq` | Connection closed; client re-attaches |
| `ipc.payload-too-large` | A cap above is exceeded | Item refused |
| `ipc.client-too-slow` | More than 16 MiB queued | Client disconnected |
| `plugin.version-skew` | Client and server plugin differ | Client half disabled |
| `plugin.server-missing` | Plugin not installed on the server | Client half disabled |

## See also

- [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) for what happens on the client between messages.
- [Persistence and restart](/pages/reference-persistence-and-restart/) for state across restarts.
- [Requirements: kernel and host](/pages/reference-requirements-kernel-host/).

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
