# Rendering pipeline for plugins

## Rendering pipeline for plugins

The client draws on every frame. A plugin never draws on a frame. This page defines how plugin output reaches the screen: retained contributions, views, annotations, token providers and scenes. It defines which thread does what, how often a plugin can be asked to render, what the client shows while a plugin is slow, stale or gone, and the size caps. Requirement ids are `[HST-250]` to `[HST-272]` and `[HST-495]`.

## You will need

- [Retained mode](/pages/retained-mode/) for the plugin author's view of the same model.
- [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) for threads and deadlines.
- [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/) for how server-owned contributions reach the client.

## The rule

The client UI thread paints from **data it already holds**. It reads the mirrored tree, the retained contribution mirror, the last `ui-tree` of each open view, and the last complete scene frame. It never waits for a plugin and never calls Wasmtime. When a plugin is slow, the UI shows the previous result. When a plugin is gone, the UI shows the previous result marked stale.

- **[HST-250]** The client MUST paint every frame from held data only, and a frame MUST NOT be late because a plugin call is pending.
- **[HST-251]** A plugin MUST NOT be asked to render per frame. It is asked when its view opens, after `ui.invalidate`, after a change of the view's area (a resize), and after a theme change.

## Retained contributions

| Kind | Owner | Stored in | Drawn by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decorations (badges, tints, markers) | server or client plugin | Contribution registry (server), mirror (client) | Tree view, per row |
| Status segments, frame slots | server or client plugin | Same | Status bar, frame |
| Virtual rows | server plugin | Same | Tree view |
| Row actions, toolbar buttons | server or client plugin | Same | Tree and pane chrome |
| Annotations (text spans) | client plugin | Client only | Terminal and editor views |

A plugin replaces the whole contribution list of one kind per call, or sends per-id puts and removes. The server (or the client, for client-owned kinds) validates it against the caps below and publishes a delta (see [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/)).

| Cap | Value |
|---|---|
| Decorations per plugin | `decorations` limit: 4,096 by default, 16,384 for T1 at most |
| Decorations per node per plugin | 8 |
| Status segments per plugin | 16 |
| Virtual rows per parent | 1,024 |
| Entry size | 16 KiB |
| Contribution update rate | 10 updates per second per kind, burst 30 |

Over a cap the update is refused with `contribution.too-many` (count) or `contribution.too-large` (entry size) or `rate-limited`. The earlier contributions stay.

- **[HST-252]** Retained contributions MUST be held by the owner of the point (server registry or client store) and drawn from a copy in the client.
- **[HST-253]** The host MUST enforce the contribution caps above and MUST keep the previous contributions on refusal.

### Stale contributions

A plugin that traps, is disabled, is restarted or is waiting for a helper keeps its contributions on screen. The host marks them **stale**: drawn dimmed with a marker in the health view. They are cleared in these cases only: the plugin replaces or clears them; the plugin is disabled by the user; the plugin is uninstalled; or the stale state lasts 60 s after the plugin side stops running without a restart scheduled.

- **[HST-254]** The host MUST mark the contributions of a stopped plugin side as stale and MUST clear them at the end of 60 s without a scheduled restart, at uninstall, and at user disable.
- **[HST-255]** A stale contribution MUST NOT accept user actions that would call the plugin; the action shows "plugin is restarting" instead.

## Views

A view is a panel, a pane body, a popup or a settings screen that a plugin describes with a `ui-tree`. The host calls `views.render` (client side) with the view id, the size in cells and the view state. The plugin returns a `ui-tree`.

Render triggers, in order of when they are coalesced:

| Trigger | Coalescing |
|---|---|
| View opened | Immediate |
| `ui.invalidate` | Several calls before the render starts become one render |
| Area change (resize) | One render with the new area, coalesced with the other triggers; at most one render per view per 16 ms. Until it returns, the host lays out the previous tree in the new area through the same constraint solver, so the screen never shows a stale size |
| Theme or font change | The host repaints the last tree of every open view at once with the new role colours, delivers `theme-changed`, and triggers exactly one render per open view, coalesced with any other trigger in the same 16 ms window. The plugin need not call `ui.invalidate` |
| User action in the view | The `ui-action` event is delivered first; the render follows after `on-events` returns |

The client draws the last tree until the new tree arrives. The new tree replaces it between frames, never partway through a frame. The render deadline is `render_deadline_ms`: 10 ms by default, 20 ms at most. A render that exceeds it is interrupted by epoch interruption and traps with `ui.render-timeout`, which counts as one failure under the restart rule. The view keeps its previous tree, drawn with the stale marker, until a later render succeeds.

The tree is diffed by the client against the previous tree, keyed by node `key`. Only changed subtrees are re-laid out.

| Cap | Value |
|---|---|
| `ui-tree` size | `ui_tree_kib`: 1,024 KiB by default, 4,096 KiB for T1 at most |
| Nodes per tree | `ui_tree_nodes`: 4,096 by default, 16,384 for T1 at most |
| Depth | 32, the root node being depth 1 |
| Text per node | 64 KiB |
| Views open per plugin | 16 |
| Renders per view | At most one in flight, at most one queued |

A tree over a cap, or any other invalid tree, is a plugin bug. There is one outcome: the host keeps the previous tree (marked stale), logs one error, and the instance traps with a `ui.*` code, counted under the restart rule, as in [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/). `views.render` returns a `ui-tree`, not a `result`, so no tree error is ever returned as `invalid-argument`. The codes are:

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `ui.invalid-tree` | Bad structure (a nonzero root, an out-of-range, backward or duplicated child index, an unreachable node), duplicate item ids, a prop out of range, more than 256 check-list items, more items than `max-items`, a bad validation regex, a tab title count that differs from the child count |
| `ui.duplicate-key` | Two nodes in one tree share a `key` |
| `ui.too-deep` | A node at depth 33 or deeper (root = 1) |
| `ui.too-large` | More than 4,096 nodes (`ui_tree_nodes`) or more than 1 MiB (`ui_tree_kib`) |
| `ui.widget-not-allowed` | A menu, list-editor or other input widget outside the allowed subset in a settings page |
| `ui.render-timeout` | `views.render` exceeded its deadline |

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 440 190" role="img" aria-label="View rendering: trigger, coalesce, render call, ui-tree, diff, paint">

- **[HST-256]** `views.render` MUST be called only on the triggers above, and MUST have at most one call in flight and one queued per view.
- **[HST-257]** The client MUST draw the previous tree until a valid new tree arrives, and MUST swap trees only between frames.
- **[HST-258]** A tree over a cap MUST trap the instance with the named error, MUST NOT be shown, and the previous tree MUST stay on screen, marked stale.
- **[HST-259]** Several `ui.invalidate` calls before a render starts MUST produce one render, and a render MUST be at least 16 ms after the previous render of the same view.

## Annotations and token providers

An annotator marks spans in a terminal or editor view (for example a link or an error line). The host calls `annotate` with the visible text lines and receives spans. The call has a soft deadline of 10 ms. The host calls it:

- when the visible content changes, at most once per 100 ms per view;
- never for rows outside the visible area plus 20 lines;
- never while the user is scrolling faster than 60 lines per second (the previous spans stay, and one call follows when scrolling stops).

A token provider (`tokens`) colours editor lines in the same way, with a 10 ms soft deadline. If the call is late, the lines stay plain and the host asks again at the next change.

Spans per call are capped at 2,048. Extra spans are cut and the log gets `annotate.too-many`.

- **[HST-260]** The host MUST call `annotate` and `tokens` only for visible rows plus 20 lines and at most once per 100 ms per view.
- **[HST-261]** A late `annotate` or `tokens` result MUST be discarded, and spans above 2,048 per call MUST be cut.

## Scenes

A scene is an animated background that a plugin renders. Scenes run on the dedicated **scene thread** of the client. The thread owns one Store per active scene and calls `renderer.render` at the frame rate of the scene.

- The frame rate is the scene's value capped by `frame_rate_cap` (1 to 60, default 30).
- Frames are **double buffered**. The scene thread writes into the back buffer. When `present` is called and the frame is complete, the buffers swap. The UI thread reads the front buffer. The UI thread never sees a half-written frame.
- The deadline is soft. A frame that is late is skipped, the front buffer stays, and the breach is counted. Thirty late frames in a row trap the scene instance. A late frame does not slow the UI.
- With a pre-rendered clip, the scene renders the clip once and loops it from host memory. The host does not call `render` again until the settings or palette change.
- The shared look (palette, colour mode, dithering) is applied by the host after the scene writes, never by the scene.
- A scene may use the GPU only through the `gpu.kernels` capability, and the host runs those kernels on its own queue, with a budget of 4 ms per frame.

| Cap | Value |
|---|---|
| Surface size | 512 cells wide, 256 cells high |
| Surface write per frame | 16 MiB |
| Frame rate | 60 |
| Scenes active per client | 1 |
| Clip memory | 256 MiB |

- **[HST-262]** Scene frames MUST be rendered on the scene thread into a back buffer, and the UI thread MUST read only a complete front buffer.
- **[HST-263]** A late scene frame MUST be skipped without delaying the UI, and the host MUST apply the shared look to each presented frame.
- **[HST-264]** The host MUST NOT call `render` for a pre-rendered clip while the clip is valid.
- **[HST-265]** Only one scene MUST be active per client, and the host MUST stop the scene thread work when the background is off or the window is hidden.

## Reconciliation, hit testing, focus and scrolling

The client keeps **view state** that the plugin does not own: scroll offsets, focus, text cursor positions, open popups and the expansion state of trees and menus. This state is keyed by the node `key` of the `ui-tree`, so a new tree with the same keys keeps its state.

- **Key-based reconciliation.** The client matches new nodes to old nodes by `key` across the whole view, so a keyed node that moves to another parent keeps its host-owned state. A matched node keeps its view state. A node without a match is new and starts with default state. A node that disappears loses its state after 2 seconds, so a plugin that rebuilds a tree with a short gap does not reset the scroll offset.
- **Hit testing.** The client resolves a pointer position to a node on the UI thread, from the laid-out tree, from the top layer to the bottom: popups, then the focused panel's overlays, then the content, then the frame. A node that is disabled or has `inert` set is skipped. The result is an event `ui-action` or `pointer` with the node `key`, queued for the plugin. The plugin is not called to decide the hit.
- **Focus.** Focus belongs to the client. A plugin may request focus for a key in the returned tree. The client grants it only when the view is focused or the user opened the view. Tab order follows the rule in [Focus order](/pages/ui-model/#focus-order). Focus moves are never delayed by a plugin call.
- **Scrolling.** The client scrolls a scrollable node by itself, from held data, without calling the plugin. A plugin that shows more rows than fit supplies all rows up to the node cap, or uses a virtual list, which asks for a window of rows through `list-virtual-children` as the user scrolls.
- **Input latency.** A key or pointer event that only changes client-held state (focus, scroll, caret in a text field) is applied in the same frame, before the plugin hears about it.

- **[HST-269]** The client MUST reconcile trees by `key` across the whole view, MUST keep view state for matched nodes, and MUST keep the state of a removed key for 2 seconds.
- **[HST-270]** The client MUST resolve hits on the UI thread in the order popups, overlays, content, frame, MUST skip disabled and inert nodes, and MUST NOT call the plugin to resolve a hit.
- **[HST-271]** The client MUST own focus and scroll state, MUST apply them in the frame in which the input arrives, and MUST grant a focus request from a plugin only for a view the user has focused or opened.
- **[HST-272]** Two nodes in one tree with the same `key` MUST trap the instance with `ui.duplicate-key`.
- **[HST-495]** A popup id is the `key` of a popup or dialog node and MUST be unique across all open views of one plugin instance. `open-popup` MUST search the last committed tree of each open view, MUST return `not-found` for no match and `invalid-argument` for two matches, and a fifth open popup in one view MUST return `quota-exceeded`. `close-popup` on an id that is not open MUST be a no-op that returns `ok`. A popup whose node is missing from the next tree MUST close and send `closed`.

## Server-owned contributions on the client

A server plugin owns most decorations, virtual rows and status segments. The client draws a copy. This has three consequences.

1. **Latency.** A change that a server plugin makes reaches the screen after the IPC delta and the next client frame. The 99th percentile on a local connection is 5 ms plus one frame.
2. **Staleness at detach.** A client that is detached keeps the last mirror. After re-attach it receives a snapshot. The UI shows the old contributions as stale until the snapshot arrives (see [Plugin traffic over IPC](/pages/reference-host-ipc/)).
3. **Client-owned points.** A plugin half on the client that owns a point (an annotator, a token provider, a view) does not depend on the server.

- **[HST-266]** A change made by a server plugin to a decoration MUST reach the client mirror in at most 5 ms at the 99th percentile on an idle local connection (benchmark B20).
- **[HST-267]** A detached client MUST mark mirrored server contributions stale until a snapshot arrives.

## Accessibility and theme

The client applies theme tokens and the accessibility settings to every plugin tree. A plugin supplies roles and labels and never colours. The host repaints at once and then triggers one render per open view on a theme change (see Views). See [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/).

- **[HST-268]** A theme or font change MUST repaint the last tree of every open view at once, MUST deliver `theme-changed`, and MUST trigger exactly one render per open view coalesced within a 16 ms window. The client MUST recolour retained contributions without calling the plugin.

## Errors

| Id | When | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `contribution.too-many` | A count cap is exceeded | Update refused |
| `contribution.too-large` | An entry is over 16 KiB | Update refused |
| `ui.invalid-tree` | Bad structure or prop (see Views) | Trap; counts as a failure |
| `ui.too-large` | More than `ui_tree_nodes` nodes or `ui_tree_kib` KiB | Trap; counts as a failure |
| `ui.too-deep` | Depth over 32 (root = 1) | Trap; counts as a failure |
| `ui.widget-not-allowed` | Widget outside the allowed subset | Trap; counts as a failure |
| `ui.render-timeout` | Render over its deadline | Trap; counts as a failure |
| `annotate.too-many` | More than 2,048 spans | Extra spans cut |
| `rate-limited` | Update rate exceeded | Update refused |
| `ui.duplicate-key` | Two nodes in one tree share a key | Trap; counts as a failure |

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin traps while a view is open | The last tree stays, marked stale, with a "restarting" notice |
| A view is open and the plugin is disabled | The view closes with a notice |
| `ui.invalidate` called inside `views.render` | Ignored once; logged `ui.invalidate-in-render` |
| Terminal resized while a render is in flight | One more render queued with the new size |
| `open-popup` names a key that two open views contain | `invalid-argument`; popup ids are unique across the open views of one plugin instance |
| Scene `render` returns without `present` | Frame dropped; warn once per second |

- [UI](/pages/api-ui/), [Surface](/pages/api-surface-glyph-plane/) and [Scenes](/pages/api-scenes/).

# Host runtime

## Host runtime

This page fixes how the host uses Wasmtime: which version, which build features, which `Config` values, how a component becomes a running instance, how imports are linked, what WASI the host offers, how time limits are enforced and what the host checks when a package is installed. A test author uses it to write the conformance and safety tests of the runtime. A host implementer uses it as the configuration to copy.

The requirement ids `[HST-050]` to `[HST-089]` belong to this page. They are collected, with a test method each, in [Requirements: kernel and host](/pages/reference-requirements-kernel-host/).

## You will need

- [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/) for the processes that own an Engine and for the rule that T2 and T3 components run in a helper.
- [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) for the call classes and their deadlines.
- A basic idea of Wasmtime. A **component** is a WebAssembly binary that follows the component model: it declares typed imports and exports instead of raw functions. A **`.cwasm`** file is a component that Wasmtime has already compiled to machine code for one target and one configuration. An **`InstancePre`** is a component whose imports have been resolved against a linker, so each new instance skips that work.

## Version policy

- **[HST-050]** Each Ilium release MUST pin Wasmtime to one exact version in `Cargo.lock` and in the workspace manifest (`=` requirement). The version at the time this contract was written is 49.0.2, which needs Rust 1.96 or later. The version in use is shown by `ilium plugin doctor` and recorded in every `.cwasm` header and in every benchmark result.
- **[HST-051]** A Wasmtime security release that fixes a vulnerability reachable from guest code MUST be taken into a point release of Ilium within 14 days of the Wasmtime announcement, and within 7 days when the advisory rates it critical or high.
- **[HST-052]** A Wasmtime version bump MUST NOT be merged until all of these pass on the new version: the full conformance suite for the Rust and TypeScript guests, the benchmark gate of [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/) with no regression beyond its thresholds, the test that every embedded `.cwasm` deserializes, and the safety tests listed under "Errors and edge cases" below.
- **[HST-053]** Every embedded `.cwasm` MUST be regenerated by the release build on every Wasmtime bump and on every change of a `Config` value that affects code generation. A stale `.cwasm` MUST fail the build, never ship.

## Build features and Config

The host depends on Wasmtime with `default-features = false`. The features are exactly these.

| Feature | State | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime` | on | Execution |
| `cranelift` | on | Compiling third-party and development components; precompiling bundled ones in the release build |
| `component-model` | on | Plugins are components |
| `std` | on | Host platform support |
| `parallel-compilation` | on | Faster first load of a large third-party component |
| `async` | on | `call_async`, `instantiate_async`, epoch yield |
| `cache` | on | The compile cache for third-party components |
| `component-model-async` | off | Not needed by contract version one; keeping it off keeps the host outside the affected code of CVE-2026-27195 |
| `winch`, `gc`, `threads`, `profiling`, `coredump`, `debug-builtins` | off | Not used; each adds attack surface or size |

- **[HST-054]** The host MUST build Wasmtime with exactly the feature set above, and a workspace test MUST fail when `component-model-async` is enabled.

The `Config` values are fixed. The same values apply in the release build that produces `.cwasm` files and in the running host, because a `.cwasm` only loads on an Engine whose relevant configuration matches.

| Setting | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `wasm_component_model(true)` | on | |
| `wasm_component_model_async(false)` | off | See `[HST-055]` |
| `async_support(true)` | on | All guest calls use the async API so that epoch yields and cancellation work |
| `epoch_interruption(true)` | on | Time limits; see the epoch section |
| `consume_fuel(false)` | off | Fuel adds a counter update to every basic block and costs more than epoch checks; epoch checks are enough because the contract limits wall time, not instruction counts |
| `max_wasm_stack` | 512 KiB | Stack overflow is a trap |
| `async_stack_size` | 1 MiB | Must be at least `max_wasm_stack`; stacks are allocated per call in flight, not per instance |
| `memory_reservation` | 4 GiB on 64-bit targets | Virtual address space only; lets the host use guard pages instead of explicit bounds checks |
| `memory_guard_size` | 32 MiB | Wasmtime default for 64-bit targets |
| `signals_based_traps(true)` | on for Linux, macOS and Windows | The server and client MUST NOT install their own SIGSEGV, SIGBUS or SIGILL handlers; on macOS the host uses Mach exception ports |
| `parallel_compilation(true)` | on | |
| `cranelift_opt_level(Speed)` | speed | |
| `wasm_simd(true)` | on | The Rust scenes use SIMD128 |
| `wasm_relaxed_simd(false)` | off | Relaxed SIMD results depend on the CPU, so a scene would render differently on two machines |
| `wasm_threads(false)`, `wasm_multi_memory(false)`, `wasm_memory64(false)`, `wasm_gc(false)` | off | Not part of the contract |
| `generate_address_map(true)`, `wasm_backtrace(true)` | on | Release traps show function names |
| `debug_info(false)` | off | `ilium plugin build --debug` is a plugin-side concern |
| `cache` | see "Compile cache" | |

- **[HST-055]** The host MUST set `wasm_component_model_async(false)`. A component that needs it MUST be refused at load with `component.invalid`.
- **[HST-056]** The host MUST fix the `concurrency_support` setting at build time to the value that keeps Wasmtime's concurrency APIs unused, and a test MUST instantiate, call and drop a component under that setting. (Disabling it makes those APIs panic, so the host never calls them.)
- **[HST-057]** The `Config` values in the table MUST be identical in the release build that produces `.cwasm` and in the host, and the host MUST compute a `config fingerprint` (a hash of Wasmtime version, target triple and every value in the table) and store it in the header of each embedded artifact.
- **[HST-058]** Epoch interruption MUST be on, and fuel MUST be off.
- **[HST-059]** `max_wasm_stack` MUST be 512 KiB and `async_stack_size` MUST be 1 MiB.
- **[HST-060]** Signals-based traps MUST be enabled on every supported platform, and the Ilium processes MUST NOT install handlers for SIGSEGV, SIGBUS or SIGILL on Unix.

### Compile cache

Third-party components are compiled on first load. The host stores the compiled code in the Wasmtime compile cache so that later loads are fast.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Location | `<cache dir>/ilium/plugin-compile/<wasmtime version>-<config fingerprint>/`, owner-only (mode 0700) |
| Size cap | 1 GiB total (`files-total-size-soft-limit`), 4,096 files |
| Eviction | Wasmtime's cleanup removes least recently used entries when a cap is reached |
| Invalidation | The directory name contains the Wasmtime version and the config fingerprint. At startup the host deletes every sibling directory with another name |
| Who writes | The host process that compiled the component, or for T2 and T3 the helper that compiled it, in its own subdirectory `<package hash>/` (see [Sandbox helper](/pages/reference-host-helper/)) |

- **[HST-061]** The compile cache MUST be owner-only, MUST be keyed by Wasmtime version and config fingerprint, and the host MUST delete caches of other keys at startup.
- **[HST-062]** The host MUST work with an unreadable, unwritable or full compile cache by compiling in memory and logging `host.cache-unavailable` once.

## Allocator

The default is the **on-demand allocator**: each instance gets its memory from the operating system when it is created. This is decision D6 of [Design decisions](/pages/design-decisions/).

The **pooling allocator** reserves a fixed number of instance slots at start. It makes instantiation faster and bounds address space, but it reserves virtual memory for the largest slot.

- **[HST-063]** The host MUST use the on-demand allocator unless the benchmark rule below selects pooling.
- **[HST-064]** The benchmark B6 selects pooling if and only if both of these hold on the reference machine class: on-demand misses `HOST-START` (150 ms for the 40-plugin bundled set) or the instantiate time `B2` (5 ms median), and pooling meets both while adding no more than 16 MiB RSS. A selection MUST be recorded in the benchmark results page together with the Wasmtime version.

If pooling is selected, the pool is sized as follows: `total_core_instances` 256, `total_memories` 256, `total_tables` 256, `total_stacks` 64, `max_memory_size` equal to the T1 ceiling of `memory_mib` (256 MiB), `table_elements` equal to the T1 ceiling of `table_elements` (50,000), and `max_core_instance_size` 1 MiB. Pooling is used for T1 and for helper Engines alike; an Engine never mixes allocators.

### Loading a component

- **[HST-065]** `Component::deserialize` MUST be used only for artifacts that the release build of this exact Ilium version produced with the host's Engine `Config`. It MUST NOT be called on bytes from a package, a download, a user path or a cache that the host did not write.
- **[HST-066]** A test MUST deserialize every embedded `.cwasm` on the host Engine and MUST fail the build if any artifact is rejected.
- **[HST-067]** T2 and T3 components MUST be loaded with `Component::new` (inside the helper), through the compile cache, and the host MUST NOT call `Component::deserialize` on package bytes. The Wasmtime compile cache is the only path that deserializes, and it reads only files that the same host wrote under its owner-only cache directory.
- **[HST-068]** A package that contains a `.cwasm` file MUST be refused at install with `package.precompiled-forbidden`.

### InstancePre and Linker

- **[HST-069]** The host MUST build one `InstancePre` per plugin side and MUST rebuild it whenever the grant set of that plugin changes (grant, revoke, upgrade). Existing instances keep running until they are re-activated as described in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/).
- **[HST-070]** The host MUST build one `Linker` per distinct grant set and MUST cache it under the SHA-256 of the sorted list of granted interface names plus the side and the tier. Two plugins with equal grant sets on equal sides share a `Linker`.

How an import is linked depends on what the manifest requested and what the user granted. Two levels exist, because a capability is finer than an interface: the interface `fs` has functions for reading and for writing, and the grants `fs.read:project` and `fs.write:project` unlock different ones.

| Case | Interface level (static) | Function level (dynamic) |
|---|---|---|
| Always-granted interface | Linked with real functions | Real functions |
| Capability requested and granted | Linked with real functions | Real functions |
| Capability requested and declined or revoked | Linked | The functions of that capability are stubs that return `not-permitted` |
| Capability never requested, but another capability of the same interface was | Linked | The functions of the unrequested capability trap with `host.capability-not-requested` (a plugin bug) |
| Interface that no requested capability unlocks and that is not always granted | The package is refused at install or load with `manifest.import-not-requested`; nothing is instantiated | Not applicable |

This is the reconciliation of the two earlier statements. A component whose binary imports an interface that its manifest never requested cannot be linked, so it never runs and never traps; it is refused when it is installed or loaded. A call to a single function whose capability was not requested, inside an interface that was linked for another reason, still traps at call time, because the host cannot refuse the interface. Both rules agree with [Capabilities and grants](/pages/capabilities/): a declined grant returns `not-permitted`, a never-requested one is a plugin bug.

- **[HST-071]** A declined or revoked capability MUST link its functions to stubs that return `not-permitted` without running kernel code.
- **[HST-072]** A component that imports an interface that is neither always granted nor unlocked by a requested capability MUST be refused at install or load with `manifest.import-not-requested`, and MUST NOT be instantiated.
- **[HST-073]** A call to a function whose capability the manifest never requested, inside a linked interface, MUST trap the instance with `host.capability-not-requested` and count as a failure.

## Store setup

Each Store is created with limits and data from the manifest `limits` after clamping to the tier ceiling (see [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)).

| Store limit | Source | On growth failure |
|---|---|---|
| Memory (bytes) | `memory_mib` for the main instance, `job_memory_mib` for a job instance | Trap. The guest never observes -1 [ABI-027] |
| Table elements | `table_elements` | Trap, as for memory |
| Instances, tables, memories per Store | 16, 8, 4 (fixed) | Instantiation fails with `host.engine-error` |
| Linear memory total over all Stores of the process | `session_memory_mib` | The new instance is refused with `session.memory-exceeded`. Not counted as a failure (reason `host-capacity`) |

The `ResourceLimiter` MUST trap on growth failure (`trap_on_grow_failure(true)`), so a guest never observes a failed growth as `-1`. The same rule applies to table growth past the table limit. The Store data record has this layout:

```rust
// ilium-plugin-host/src/store_data.rs (illustration of the contract)
pub struct StoreData {
    pub plugin: PluginId,
    pub side: Side,                  // Server, Client or Scene
    pub instance: u64,               // rises for each new instance of this plugin side
    pub kind: InstanceKind,          // Main or Job { job_id }
    pub authorization_epoch: u64,    // grant generation this instance was linked against
    pub quota: QuotaHandle,          // execution quota group handle
    pub call: Option<CallState>,     // class, start time, deadline, soft flag, late flag
    pub limits: StoreLimits,
    pub wasi: WasiCtx,               // see the WASI section
    pub resources: ResourceTable,
}
```

- **[HST-074]** Every Store MUST be created with `StoreLimits` taken from the clamped manifest limits and MUST have `trap_on_grow_failure(true)`.
- **[HST-075]** Each Store MUST carry the plugin id, side, instance number, kind, authorization epoch and quota handle, and every import MUST check the authorization epoch against the current grant generation before it acts. A mismatch returns `revoked`.

## WASI policy

Rust components built for `wasm32-wasip2` and TypeScript components built by `componentize-js` import parts of WASI Preview 2. The host links `wasmtime-wasi` Preview 2 with these rules.

| WASI interface | Policy |
|---|---|
| `wasi:cli/stdout`, `wasi:cli/stderr` | Captured line by line into the plugin log at level `info` (stdout) and `warn` (stderr). A line longer than 16 KiB is cut and marked `[cut]`. The `log_lines_per_second` limit applies |
| `wasi:cli/stdin` | Always empty |
| `wasi:cli/environment` | No variables; one argument, the plugin id |
| `wasi:cli/exit` | A call traps with `wasi.exit` |
| `wasi:clocks`, `wasi:random` | Allowed. Wall-clock time is the real clock; monotonic time is the host monotonic clock; random bytes come from the operating system |
| `wasi:io` | Allowed |
| `wasi:filesystem` | Linked, but with preopens only for scopes that an `fs.*` grant makes available, mapped through `ilium-platform` secure file access. With no `fs` grant the preopen list is empty |
| `wasi:sockets` | Refused. A component that imports it is refused at load with `component.wasi-forbidden` |
| `wasi:http` | Refused in the same way. HTTP goes only through the `http` capability, which applies allowlists, size caps and the outbound-request rules |

Package-time composition with `wasi-virt` is a supported alternative for a plugin author who wants a smaller import set. It does not change the host rules.

- **[HST-076]** The host MUST link WASI Preview 2 with captured stdout and stderr, an empty environment, no stdin, `wasi:cli/exit` as a trap, and preopens only from `fs` grants.
- **[HST-077]** A component that imports `wasi:sockets` or `wasi:http` MUST be refused at load with `component.wasi-forbidden` and MUST NOT be instantiated.
- **[HST-078]** A stdout or stderr line longer than 16 KiB MUST be cut at 16 KiB and marked `[cut]`.

## Epoch ticker and deadlines

Wasmtime's **epoch interruption** lets the host stop guest code without a per-instruction counter. The Engine has one counter, the epoch. A ticker thread increases it at a fixed period. Each Store can ask to be interrupted when the counter reaches a value.

- **[HST-079]** Each Engine MUST have exactly one epoch ticker thread, named `ilium-plugin-epoch`, that increases the epoch every 10 ms. The tick period is 10 ms on every platform.
- **[HST-080]** Before every guest call the host MUST install an `epoch_deadline_callback` for the Store. The callback runs on each tick while that call is executing. It compares the host monotonic clock with the call's deadlines and returns one of: continue, yield (only for yielding call classes), or a trap.
- **[HST-081]** The host MUST set the instance deadline of a call with deadline `d` milliseconds to `ceil(d / 10) + 1` ticks after the call starts. A guest that spins traps no earlier than `d` and no later than `d + 20` ms of wall time on a host that is not overloaded, and a call that returns at `d - 1` ms never traps. A 20 ms deadline traps between 20 and 40 ms.
- **[HST-082]** The ticker MUST continue while any call is in flight, and MUST detect a clock jump of more than one second between two ticks (for example after a system suspend) and in that case skip deadline decisions for that tick.

Two kinds of deadline exist. A **hard** deadline traps the instance when it fires. A **soft** deadline marks the call late: the host continues the call, discards its result, and traps only if a grace period of 100 ms past the soft deadline also expires. The call classes that are hard or soft, and the effect of a breach for each, are the single table in [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/).

- Only the call classes marked "yields" return `yield` from the callback: `activate`, job runs and long service calls. Their wall time still counts against the deadline. All other classes run to completion or to the deadline without yielding.
- A guest call that is waiting in a synchronous host import does not execute guest code, so no tick can trap it during the import. The trap fires on the first epoch check after the import returns. Time spent in such an import counts toward the deadline.
- Time that the host spends after a call has returned (applying the returned submissions, delivering later events) does not count toward the deadline of that call.

- **[HST-083]** A trap caused by an epoch deadline MUST carry the error `host.deadline` with the call class and the limit in milliseconds, and MUST be logged once.

## Component validation at install

The host validates a component when a package is installed and again when the package is loaded. T2 and T3 validation runs inside the helper, because parsing is done by `Component::new` there.

1. The bytes are a valid component (`wasmparser` validation with the features of the Config). Failure: `component.invalid`.
2. The component size is at most 32 MiB. Failure: `component.too-large`.
3. The component targets the world named in the manifest (`world`) of the right side. Failure: `component.world-mismatch`.
4. The export set equals the required exports of the world plus the optional exports listed in the manifest. Failure: `manifest.exports-mismatch`.
5. The custom section `ilium:api-version` exists and holds three big-endian unsigned 16-bit integers (major, minor, patch) equal to the manifest `api`. For contract version one the bytes are `00 00 00 01 00 00`. Failure: `component.api-version-mismatch`.
6. No single custom section is larger than 4 MiB and the custom sections together are at most 8 MiB. The `name` section MAY be stripped by `ilium plugin build --release`. Failure: `component.custom-section-too-large`.
7. Every import is an interface that the host can link under the rules above. Failures: `manifest.import-not-requested`, `component.wasi-forbidden`, or `component.import-unknown` for an interface that does not exist in `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

- **[HST-084]** The host MUST apply the seven validation steps in this order and MUST report the first failing step's error id.
- **[HST-085]** The `ilium:api-version` custom section MUST be exactly six bytes and MUST equal the manifest `api` in all three fields.
- **[HST-086]** A component larger than 32 MiB, a custom section larger than 4 MiB, or custom sections together larger than 8 MiB MUST be refused.

## Cargo and build notes for host implementers

The host crate compiles through ni-build on ni-vm like every crate of the workspace (see the project instructions). The release build step that produces `.cwasm` files is a build-script-free tool, `ilium-plugin-precompile`, that links the same `Config` function as the host (`runtime_config()` in `ilium-plugin-host`) so the two cannot drift. The step writes `<artifact>.cwasm` and a header with the config fingerprint (HST-057).

```rust
// ilium-plugin-host/src/runtime_config.rs (illustration of the contract)
pub fn runtime_config() -> wasmtime::Config {
    let mut config = wasmtime::Config::new();
    config
        .wasm_component_model(true)
        .wasm_component_model_async(false)
        .epoch_interruption(true)
        .consume_fuel(false)
        .max_wasm_stack(512 * 1024)
        .async_stack_size(1024 * 1024)
        .signals_based_traps(true)
        .parallel_compilation(true)
        .wasm_simd(true)
        .wasm_relaxed_simd(false)
        .wasm_threads(false)
        .wasm_multi_memory(false)
        .wasm_memory64(false)
        .wasm_gc(false)
        .generate_address_map(true)
        .wasm_backtrace(true);
    config
}
```

- **[HST-087]** The precompile step and the host MUST obtain their `Config` from the same function.

## Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Result | Id |
|---|---|---|
| A `.cwasm` was built by another Wasmtime version or another `Config` | `Component::deserialize` is not attempted when the fingerprint differs. The host loads the embedded `.wasm` with `Component::new` instead and logs a warning. A release build MUST have zero such fallbacks, and a CI test enforces it | `host.cwasm-incompatible` |
| Embedded `.cwasm` has no embedded `.wasm` to fall back to | The plugin is disabled and the build is considered broken | `host.cwasm-incompatible` |
| Package contains a `.cwasm` | Install refused | `package.precompiled-forbidden` |
| Component imports `wasi:sockets` or `wasi:http` | Refused | `component.wasi-forbidden` |
| Component imports an interface the manifest never requested | Refused at install or load | `manifest.import-not-requested` |
| Function of an unrequested capability called | The instance traps | `host.capability-not-requested` |
| Epoch deadline | The instance traps (hard) or the call is marked late (soft) | `host.deadline` |
| Guest memory growth refused | Trap; log line `memory limit <N> MiB reached` | none |
| Stack overflow | The instance traps | `host.stack-overflow` |
| Wasmtime internal compile error | Load fails; plugin not activated | `host.engine-error` |
| Component uses `wasm_component_model_async` | Refused | `component.invalid` |
| Compile cache unavailable | Compile in memory, log once | `host.cache-unavailable` |
| System clock jumps during a call | No deadline decision on the jump tick | none |
| API version section missing or wrong | Refused | `component.api-version-mismatch` |

- **[HST-088]** When the config fingerprint of an embedded `.cwasm` differs from the host's, the host MUST NOT call `Component::deserialize` on it, MUST fall back to `Component::new` on the embedded `.wasm`, and MUST log `host.cwasm-incompatible`. A release-build test MUST fail if any bundled plugin takes this path.
- **[HST-089]** A stack overflow in guest code MUST trap the instance with `host.stack-overflow` and MUST NOT crash the process.

# Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation

## Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation

This page is the single normative source for how plugin calls are scheduled: which thread runs which call, how calls into one instance are ordered, the deadline of every call class and what happens when it is missed, what happens to work in flight when an instance traps, how host work is cancelled, and how queues push back. Other pages that mention a deadline or a limit repeat the numbers of this page and link here. A test author derives the timing and ordering tests from the requirement ids `[HST-180]` to `[HST-216]`, which are collected in [Requirements: kernel and host](/pages/reference-requirements-kernel-host/).

## You will need

- [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/) for the processes and hosts.
- [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/) for the epoch ticker and the hard and soft deadline mechanism.
- [Events](/pages/api-events/) for the queue policy of each event kind, and [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for submissions.

## Thread model

Every plugin-hosting process has the same three kinds of thread besides its own main threads: the plugin executor, the epoch ticker and the job worker bank. The client has two more: the UI thread and the scene thread.

| Thread or pool | Process | Name | Count | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Server main runtime | Server | `ilium-server` runtime | as today | Kernel work, the IPC loop, the dispatcher task `plugin-dispatch`, helper I/O tasks. It never runs guest code |
| Plugin executor | Server and client | `ilium-plugin-N` | server `clamp(cores / 2, 2, 4)`, client `clamp(cores / 4, 1, 2)` | Every guest call except scene frames and job runs: `activate`, `deactivate`, `on-events`, `views.render`, annotator, detector, hook and provider exports, service and inference calls |
| Epoch ticker | Every process with an Engine | `ilium-plugin-epoch` | 1 | Increases the Engine epoch every 10 ms |
| Job worker bank | Server and client | `ilium-job-N` | `min(4, cores / 2)`, at least 1 | Job instances (`job-runner.run`) |
| Client UI thread | Client | the client main thread | 1 | Input, layout, painting, hit testing. It never calls Wasmtime |
| Scene thread | Client | `ilium-plugin-scene` | 1 | Scene `renderer` frame calls |
| CLI main thread | CLI process | main | 1 | The single plugin executor of that process is a one-thread pool |

- **[HST-180]** Guest code MUST run only on the plugin executor, the scene thread, the job worker bank or (in a helper) the helper call loop. It MUST NOT run on the server main runtime, the client UI thread or the epoch ticker.
- **[HST-181]** No plugin call MUST ever run on the client UI thread. The UI thread MUST send work to the plugin executor through a bounded channel and MUST apply results on a later frame.
- **[HST-182]** The plugin executor MUST have `clamp(cores / 2, 2, 4)` threads in the server and `clamp(cores / 4, 1, 2)` threads in the client. The job worker bank MUST have `min(4, cores / 2)` threads, at least one.
- **[HST-183]** The scene thread MUST be a single dedicated thread per client, and a scene frame MUST NOT occupy a plugin executor thread.

A client UI frame therefore never waits for a plugin. The UI thread draws the last result that it holds: the last `ui-tree` of each view, the last complete scene frame, the retained decorations.

## Per-instance serialization and fairness

A Store can run one call at a time. The host MUST NOT call into one instance from two threads, and MUST NOT interleave two calls.

Each plugin side has an **instance queue** of pending calls. The dispatcher picks the next call by priority, then by arrival order.

| Priority | Calls |
|---|---|
| 1 (highest) | `activate`, `deactivate` |
| 2 | Calls with a waiting caller: hook handlers, `collect`, `service-provider`, `inference-provider`, `menu-items`, `query-catalog`, `list-virtual-children`, `tokens`, `settings-validate`, `detector`, client-request answers |
| 3 | `on-events` |
| 4 | `views.render` (after `on-events`, so a render sees the state that the events produced) |
| 5 (lowest) | `annotate` |

Scene frames and job runs are not in this queue, because they run in their own Stores.

Between plugins the dispatcher is **round robin**: it keeps one ready list of plugin sides that have queued calls and gives each side one call per turn. A side gets at most 4 calls per 10 ms tick on one executor pass, so one busy plugin cannot starve the others.

- **[HST-184]** The host MUST run at most one call at a time in one Store and MUST pick the next call by the priority table, then by arrival order.
- **[HST-185]** The dispatcher MUST serve plugin sides round robin and MUST give a side at most 4 calls per 10 ms tick.
- **[HST-186]** One plugin's slow call MUST NOT delay another plugin's call by more than the other plugins' calls ahead of it in the round robin, and MUST NOT delay a client frame at all.

The cost of waiting in the instance queue is not part of the call's own deadline (the Store deadline starts when the call starts), but a call with a waiting caller has a second, **caller deadline** that starts when the call was queued. A call that cannot start within its caller deadline is abandoned and counted as a breach of the same class. The caller deadline equals the call's own deadline, except for `on-events` and `views.render`, which have none because nobody waits for them.

- **[HST-187]** A queued call with a waiting caller MUST be abandoned, with the same effect as a soft breach, when it has not started within its own deadline measured from the time it was queued.

## Call classes

This is the single normative table of calls. [Runtime model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/#2-calls-deadlines-and-interruption) and [Performance](/pages/performance/) link to it and copy its values exactly. A **hard** deadline traps the instance when it fires. A **soft** deadline marks the call late, so the host discards its result and counts a breach. A late call that also passes a grace period of 100 ms past the soft deadline is trapped. A soft class has a **streak limit**: that many breaches in a row, without a timely call in between, trap the instance. "Counts" says whether the effect is a failure under the restart rule.

All defaults are the same for every tier. The T1 column is the ceiling that a bundled plugin may ask for in its manifest `limits`, and the T2 and T3 column is the ceiling for third-party plugins. The values shown in brackets on earlier pages, for example `20 ms (50 ms)` in [Exports](/pages/api-exports/), are these T1 ceilings, not T1 defaults.

| Call class | Side | Default | T1 ceiling | T2/T3 ceiling | Kind | Effect on breach | Counts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `activate` | all | 2,000 ms | 5,000 ms | 2,000 ms | hard, yields | Trap; activation fails | yes |
| `deactivate` | all | 500 ms | 1,000 ms | 500 ms | hard | Instance dropped; no restore bytes kept; logged at warn | no |
| `on-events`, batch without a command | server, client | 20 ms | 50 ms | 20 ms | hard | Trap | yes |
| `on-events`, batch with a `command-invoked` event | server, client | 50 ms | 100 ms | 50 ms | hard | Trap | yes |
| `views.render` | client | 10 ms | 20 ms | 10 ms | hard | Trap | yes |
| `annotate` | client | 10 ms | 20 ms | 10 ms | soft, streak 3 | The annotation is skipped (late result dropped); the third breach in a row traps | trap only |
| `renderer` frame | scene | frame budget, at most 50 ms | 50 ms | 50 ms | soft, streak 30 | Frame skipped; 30 in a row trap | trap only |
| `detector` identify and classify | server | 20 ms | 50 ms | 20 ms | soft, streak 3 | Previous classification kept, no event; third in a row traps | trap only |
| `migrate` | all | 30,000 ms | 60,000 ms | 30,000 ms | hard | Migration fails, backup restored, update rolled back | no |
| `hook-handler` | owner side | 20 ms (5 to 50 ms by manifest) | 50 ms | 50 ms | soft | Counts as `pass`; third in a row disables the extension | no |
| `menu-provider.menu-items` | client | 20 ms | 20 ms | 20 ms | soft, streak 3 | Static entries only | trap only |
| `catalog-provider.query-catalog` | client | 20 ms | 20 ms | 20 ms | soft, streak 3 | Cached page used | trap only |
| `virtual-rows-provider.list-virtual-children` | server | 20 ms | 20 ms | 20 ms | soft, streak 3 | Spinner row stays | trap only |
| `token-provider.tokens` | client | 10 ms | 10 ms | 10 ms | soft, streak 3 | Lines stay plain; the host retries | trap only |
| `settings-validate` | client | 100 ms | 100 ms | 100 ms | soft, streak 3 | The save is refused, the previous value kept; the breach counts as a failure | yes |
| `service-provider` call | provider side | `command_deadline_ms` 50 ms | 100 ms | 50 ms | hard | Trap the provider; the caller's request completes `failed(timed-out)`; other deferred calls of the provider complete `failed(cancelled)` | yes |
| `inference-provider` `complete` and `models` | server | `command_deadline_ms` 50 ms | 100 ms | 50 ms | hard | Trap; the request is `failed(internal)` | yes |
| `job-runner.run`, CPU time | job instance | 2,000 ms | 60,000 ms | 10,000 ms | hard, own thread | `failed(timed-out)` | no |
| `job-runner.run`, wall time | job instance | 20,000 ms | 600,000 ms | 100,000 ms | hard, own thread | `failed(timed-out)` | no |
| Client-request answer (round trip) | client | request timeout, 5,000 ms | 30,000 ms | 30,000 ms | soft, request level | The request completes `failed(timed-out)` | no |
| Whole hook chain | owner side | 100 ms | 100 ms | 100 ms | soft | Remaining handlers skipped and logged | no |

Notes on the table:

- A `command-invoked` event in a batch selects `command_deadline_ms` for the whole call. A plugin that handles commands therefore gets 50 ms for the batch. This replaces the earlier wording that a command "shares" the 20 ms batch deadline.
- A hook handler's deadline is its `deadline_ms` from the manifest, clamped to 5 to 50 ms. The T2 and T3 ceiling of 50 ms is the same cap, because the manifest bound already applies to every tier.
- A late hook handler is not a plugin failure, because the contributor's plugin keeps running; the third breach in a row disables that one extension (see [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/)). Dynamic collect points call no export: entries arrive through the `extensions.register` import, so they have no deadline of their own.
- `detector` is the export of `agent.signatures`; its deadline is the new key `detector_deadline_ms`.
- The `deactivate` breach is not a failure because the plugin is already being stopped. The restore bytes are lost and the host logs `deactivate.deadline` at warn. A trap inside `deactivate` is treated in the same way.

- **[HST-188]** Every guest call MUST belong to exactly one row of the call-class table and MUST run under that row's default, or under the effective limit after clamping to the ceiling of the plugin's tier.
- **[HST-189]** A hard breach MUST trap the instance. A soft breach MUST discard the late result and count a breach, and a call that passes its soft deadline plus 100 ms MUST be trapped.
- **[HST-190]** The streak limits MUST be 3 for `annotate`, `detector`, `menu-items`, `query-catalog`, `list-virtual-children`, `tokens` and `settings-validate`, and 30 for scene frames. A timely call MUST reset the streak.
- **[HST-191]** A `deactivate` breach or trap MUST drop the instance, discard its restore bytes, log `deactivate.deadline`, and MUST NOT count as a failure.
- **[HST-192]** A batch that contains a `command-invoked` event MUST run under `command_deadline_ms`, and every other batch under `event_deadline_ms`.
- **[HST-193]** The effective deadline of a call MUST be clamped to the ceiling for the tier, and the clamp MUST be logged once per plugin and key.

## Deadline measurement

The clock is the host monotonic clock. The epoch ticker period is 10 ms. The host sets the instance deadline to `ceil(d / 10) + 1` ticks after the call starts. A guest that spins without returning therefore traps no earlier than `d` and no later than `d + 20` ms of wall time on a host that is not overloaded. A call that returns at `d - 1` ms never traps. A test asserts the trap time in [d, d + 20] ms (see [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/)) [HST-081].

- **Synchronous host calls count.** The deadline clock runs while the guest waits inside a host import. A deadline that expires during an import traps the instance when the import returns. A handler that makes five 5 ms synchronous calls has used 25 ms of its 20 ms budget.
- **Work after the call does not count.** The kernel applying the returned submissions, the later delivery of a `request-completed` event, and the work of an asynchronous host service (an HTTP request, a child process, a job) are outside the call. Only the time between "call started" and "call returned" counts.
- **Suspend and clock jumps.** The host uses a monotonic clock that does not advance during system suspend on Linux and macOS. The host MUST ignore a tick that follows a gap of more than one second.

<div class="note">
<p>This is the precise form of the earlier sentence that "native host work never counts against a plugin deadline". Host work that finishes inside the import counts, because the guest is waiting for it. Host work that finishes after the call returns does not count. See <a href="/pages/performance/">Performance</a>.</p>
</div>

- **[HST-194]** Time spent inside a synchronous host import MUST count toward the deadline of the call that made it, and time after the call returned MUST NOT.
- **[HST-195]** The deadline clock MUST be monotonic, and a gap of more than one second between two ticks MUST NOT produce a deadline breach.

## Activation and yielding

`activate` and long service calls may **yield**. A yield means that the call is suspended at an epoch tick and put at the back of the executor's ready list, so another plugin's call can run on that thread. The call resumes later. It is the only mechanism that lets a long call share a thread, and it applies only to the classes marked "yields" in the table.

- During the yield other calls to other plugins run. Calls to the same plugin wait in its instance queue, so the activating plugin sees no other call until `activate` returns.
- The yield time counts toward the 2,000 ms deadline, because the deadline is wall time.
- A service caller that triggered the activation waits for `activate` and then for its own call. Its total wait is bounded by `activate_deadline_ms` plus the reply deadline of the call, and it fails with `timed-out` when the activation deadline passes first.

- **[HST-196]** Only `activate`, job runs and service calls that wait for an activation MAY yield. All other classes MUST run on one thread without yielding until they return or fail.
- **[HST-197]** While a plugin side is activating, the host MUST queue its other calls and MUST NOT call into the instance until `activate` has returned successfully.

## Trap aftermath

When an instance traps (a panic, a hard deadline, a streak limit, a stuck restart or a helper crash) the host does the following, in this order.

1. The call that was running is abandoned. **No submission from that call is applied**, because a call that traps returns no value. Imports that act at once and were completed before the trap (`storage.set`, `log`, `ui.invalidate`, `timers`, `messages.send`) stay done; the host does not roll them back.
2. The in-flight event batch is **not redelivered**, with one exception. Events of the kinds in the "survives" list below, which were in the batch, are put back at the head of the new instance's queue once. If the second delivery also traps, they are dropped and the host logs `events.poison` with the event kinds.
3. Pending requests that the instance owned (jobs it started, HTTP streams, children, timers that are not durable) are cancelled. Durable timers and journal entries stay.
4. Retained contributions of the plugin (decorations, virtual rows, status segments, frame slots, row actions) stay on screen and are marked **stale** (drawn dimmed, see [Retained mode](/pages/retained-mode/)).
5. The restart rule decides when the new instance starts (see [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)).
6. The new instance is activated with `restored` bytes from its last `deactivate` (none after a trap) and then receives one `tree-changed` batch for every node, so it can read its state again.

The events that **survive** a stuck-plugin restart or a trap, because they cannot be recovered from the tree, are: `request-completed` (for submissions of this plugin), `durable-timer-fired`, `input-uncertain` and `message`. The events `command-invoked`, `key-pressed`, `key-released`, `ui-action` and `pointer` are discarded with the queue (the user sees the plugin restart). The calls behind `cli-invoked`, `http-called` and `client-request` are completed as `cancelled` (the HTTP caller receives status 503). Every other kind is replaced by the `tree-changed` batch of step 6.

- **[HST-198]** A trap MUST apply none of the call's returned submissions, MUST NOT roll back imports that already acted, and MUST NOT redeliver the in-flight batch except for the surviving event kinds.
- **[HST-199]** The surviving event kinds (`request-completed`, `durable-timer-fired`, `input-uncertain`, `message`) MUST be redelivered at the head of the new instance's queue once, and dropped with the log id `events.poison` if the redelivery traps again.
- **[HST-200]** A stuck-queue restart MUST discard the queue except the surviving kinds, MUST complete the calls behind `cli-invoked`, `http-called` and `client-request` as `cancelled`, and the new instance MUST receive one `tree-changed` batch for every node.
- **[HST-201]** Retained contributions of a trapped instance MUST stay and be marked stale until the plugin replaces or clears them.

## Queues and backpressure

Each plugin side has one event queue. Its size is `event_queue`: 1,024 by default, with a ceiling of 4,096 for T1 and 1,024 for T2 and T3.

| Policy | Events | When the queue is full |
|---|---|---|
| Coalesce | `tree-changed` (one merged list), `screen-changed`, `signal-changed`, `attention-changed` and the other events marked coalesced in [Events](/pages/api-events/) | Always, whatever the queue fill: the newer event merges into the pending event with the same kind and key and takes its position, so a key never holds more than one slot |
| Drop oldest | `output-matched` and other events marked drop-oldest | The oldest pending drop-oldest event of any kind is removed and counted under its own event and source. With none pending, an incoming drop-oldest event is discarded and counted. The next batch carries one `events-dropped` with the counts |
| Never dropped | All others | The plugin is **stuck**: it is restarted as a failure |

A plugin gets a **batch** of up to 256 events per `on-events` call. The dispatcher builds a batch when one of these is true: 256 events are pending; or 2 ms have passed since the first pending event; or the pending events include a latency-critical kind (`key-pressed`, `key-released`, `command-invoked`, `ui-action`, `pointer`, or a `request-completed` of a user action), which flushes at once. A `request-completed` of a user action is one whose submission came from an `on-events` call whose batch held a `key-pressed`, `command-invoked` or `ui-action` event. Such a completion is flushed at once instead of after the 2 ms window [HST-204]. The host splits a larger pending list into several calls in order.

Streaming events add **back-pressure** before the queue can fill. For `http-stream-data` and `child-output` the host gives each stream a **credit window** of 256 KiB. The host counts bytes that it has enqueued for the plugin and the plugin has not yet consumed. When the count reaches the window, the host stops reading the network socket or the child pipe. It resumes reading when the count falls to half the window. A chunk is at most 64 KiB. A fast peer is therefore slowed by the operating system's own flow control and a plugin never receives more than the window.

Rate limits are applied before enqueue: a source that produces events faster than its limit (for example more than 10 `set-meter` style updates per second) is refused at the source with `rate-limited`, so the queue never sees them.

The **execution quota group** `ilium-execution` limits a plugin's total CPU use. There is one group for each plugin side in each process, and it is defined in [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) and [Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/). It is a token bucket of 2,000 ms of CPU time that refills at 500 ms per second. The host charges the thread CPU time of each call, and 1 ms for every 64 KiB of payload in a submission. When the bucket is empty, submissions and calls that return a request id fail with `quota-exceeded`. The bucket balance can go below zero, because a call is charged after it ends. The bucket is empty when the balance is 0 or less. `retry-after-ms` = max(100, ceil_10(-balance_ms * 2)), where `ceil_10` rounds up to the next 10 ms: the wall time until the balance refills to 0 at 500 ms per second, never below 100. A balance of -100 ms gives 200. Calls into the plugin are not held: `on-events`, `views.render`, `activate`, `deactivate` and provider calls still run, and the plugin simply cannot submit until the bucket refills. A trap still charges the time used.

- **[HST-202]** Each plugin side MUST have one event queue of `event_queue` entries, and the policy of each event kind (coalesce, drop oldest, never dropped) MUST be the one in [Events](/pages/api-events/).
- **[HST-203]** A full queue with a never-dropped event MUST restart the plugin side as a failure.
- **[HST-204]** A batch MUST contain at most 256 events, MUST be flushed after 2 ms or at 256 events, and MUST be flushed at once when it contains a latency-critical kind.
- **[HST-205]** Streams MUST use a credit window of 256 KiB, chunks of at most 64 KiB, and the host MUST stop reading the socket or pipe at a full window and resume at half.
- **[HST-206]** Rate limits MUST be applied before an event is enqueued.
- **[HST-207]** The host MUST maintain one `ilium-execution` bucket per plugin side with capacity 2,000 ms and refill 500 ms per second, MUST charge thread CPU time and payload bytes as above, and MUST refuse submissions with `quota-exceeded` and `retry-after-ms` of at least 100 when the bucket is empty.
- **[HST-208]** An empty bucket MUST NOT hold `on-events`, `views.render`, `activate`, `deactivate` or provider calls.

## Cancellation

A request is cancelled by one of seven causes. The outcome tells the plugin which.

| Cause | Outcome | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| The plugin side stopped or trapped (instance dropped) | `cancelled` | Pending requests of that instance |
| Grant revoked | Synchronous calls that need the grant return `err(revoked)` from the moment of revocation. Pending requests that need it complete `failed(revoked)`, delivered before `deactivate(revoked)` | The plugin is re-activated with the reduced grants. Other pending `call(id)` requests are cancelled with the instance and their completions are not delivered; pending submissions follow the trap-aftermath rule |
| The plugin asked for it (`cancel(request)`, `jobs.cancel`) | `cancelled` | A cancelled job completes with the outcome `cancelled`. `jobs.cancel` returns nothing: cancelling a completed, unknown or already cancelled id is a silent no-op and produces no further completion |
| Server or client shutdown | `cancelled` | Submissions accepted but not yet applied at shutdown complete as `cancelled`. `refused(cancelled)` is used only for siblings of a refused batch |
| The request deadline passed | `failed(timed-out)` | For example the 30 s command reply deadline, or a provider that does not reply to a deferred service call within 30 s. The earlier of the two events wins |
| A service provider traps or restarts while callers wait | `failed(cancelled)` for every deferred call, at once | A breach of the 50 ms provider deadline completes the breaching call as `failed(timed-out)` and the other deferred calls as `failed(cancelled)` |

Cancelled host work is torn down within a bound.

| Work | Teardown |
|---|---|
| HTTP request or stream | The connection is aborted within 100 ms |
| File read, watch, scan | Stopped at the next chunk, within 100 ms |
| Child process | SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s (POSIX); see [Platform support](/pages/reference-platform-support/) for Windows |
| Running job | The cancel flag is set; `is-cancelled` returns true. If the job has not returned within 1,000 ms (`job_cancel_grace_ms`), the host traps the job instance at the next tick |
| Helper call | A `Cancel` message is sent; if the helper does not answer within the call's deadline plus 5 ms, it is killed |

- **[HST-209]** Each cancellation cause MUST produce the outcome in the table, and a completed request MUST NOT be changed by a later cancel. `jobs.cancel` of a completed, unknown or already cancelled id MUST be a silent no-op.
- **[HST-210]** Cancelled HTTP and file work MUST stop within 100 ms, child processes MUST receive SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 2 s, and a job that ignores the cancel flag MUST be trapped 1,000 ms after the flag is set.

## Hook chain execution

`run-hook` is asynchronous: it returns a request id at once, the chain runs on the host, and the result arrives as `request-completed` (the SDK `await` form hides this). The owner's current call is never blocked by the chain, so a 100 ms chain does not conflict with the owner's 20 ms `on-events` deadline.

- Handlers run **strictly one after another** in priority order, never in parallel, each in the contributor's own instance on the owner's side.
- A handler that cannot start within its own deadline measured from the moment it was due (the contributor's instance is busy) is skipped as `pass` with a breach counted.
- The 100 ms chain cap is measured from the start of the first handler call. Handlers not yet started when it expires are skipped and logged `extension.chain-cap`.
- A T2 or T3 handler's helper round trip (see [Sandbox helper](/pages/reference-host-helper/)) is inside the handler deadline. Its budget is 0.5 ms at the 99th percentile, so the usable deadline of a 5 ms handler is 4.5 ms.
- A hook on a client-owned point runs only handlers in that client. A hook on a server-owned point runs only handlers on the server. No hook crosses a process.

- **[HST-211]** `run-hook` MUST NOT block the owner's call, handlers of one chain MUST run strictly sequentially, and the 100 ms chain cap MUST be measured from the first handler's start.
- **[HST-212]** A handler MUST be skipped as `pass` when it cannot start within its own deadline, and a skipped or late handler MUST count a breach.
- **[HST-213]** A hook chain MUST run only handlers hosted by the process that owns the point.

## Latency of keys and input

A key that a plugin has grabbed (see [Keys](/pages/api-keys/)) travels like this: the UI thread decodes the key, finds the grab, and puts a `key-pressed` event on the client dispatcher channel. The dispatcher flushes it at once. An idle executor thread starts the `on-events` call. The plugin returns submissions. The host applies them, and a `send-input` submission reaches the pane.

| Step | Budget (99th percentile, idle machine) |
|---|---|
| Key decoded to the dispatcher channel | 0.1 ms |
| Channel to the start of the plugin call (T1) | 1 ms |
| Channel to the start of the plugin call (T2 or T3, helper round trip included) | 1.5 ms |
| Plugin returns to the intent applied (client-side intent) | 0.5 ms |
| Plugin returns to the intent applied on the server (forwarded over IPC) | 3 ms |
| Whole path, key press to bytes at the PTY, with a plugin handler of 0.1 ms | 5 ms |

The benchmarks B16 and B17 of [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/) measure these.

- **[HST-214]** A grabbed key MUST flush its batch at once, and the 99th percentile from the dispatcher channel to the start of the plugin call MUST be at most 1 ms for T1 and 1.5 ms for T2 and T3 on an idle reference machine.
- **[HST-215]** The 99th percentile from key press to bytes at the PTY through a plugin handler of 0.1 ms MUST be at most 5 ms on an idle reference machine.

## Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Result | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Two calls to one instance arrive together | They run one after the other by priority | none |
| Caller deadline passes while the call waits in the queue | The call is abandoned, a breach is counted | `host.queue-timeout` |
| A call yields during `activate` and another plugin runs | Allowed; the activating plugin gets no other call | none |
| Deadline expires inside a synchronous import | Trap when the import returns | `host.deadline` |
| System suspend during a call | The tick after the gap is ignored | none |
| Trap with a surviving event in the batch | Redelivered once to the new instance | `events.poison` on a second trap |
| Empty CPU bucket | Plugin submissions return `quota-exceeded` with `retry-after-ms`; `on-events` and other calls into the plugin still run | `quota-exceeded` |
| Job ignores the cancel flag | Trapped 1,000 ms later; the job completes `cancelled` | `cancelled` |
| Soft call passes the soft deadline plus 100 ms | Trap | `host.deadline` |
| Stream credit window full | The host stops reading the socket or pipe | none |
| Hook chain exceeds 100 ms | Remaining handlers are skipped | `extension.chain-cap` |

- **[HST-216]** A call that is abandoned in the queue MUST log `host.queue-timeout` and count a breach of its class.

## See also

- [Host runtime](/pages/reference-host-runtime/) for how deadlines are enforced.
- [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) for the limit keys and the restart rule.
- [Events](/pages/api-events/), [Intents](/pages/api-intents/) and [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/).
- [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/), [Menu provider](/pages/api-menu-provider/) and [Background jobs](/pages/background-jobs/).
- [Performance](/pages/performance/) for the plugin author's view.

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
