# Telemetry and plugin health

## Telemetry and plugin health

The host measures every plugin call so that it can enforce budgets, show health and help an author find a slow handler. This page defines the counters, where they live, how long they are kept, what is logged, and what is never collected. The health states and the `ilium plugin status` output are in [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/); this page defines the host-side measurements behind them. The user's view is in [Plugin health for users](/pages/user-plugin-health/). Requirement ids are `[HST-350]` to `[HST-363]`.

## You will need

- [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/) for the call classes that the counters are keyed by.
- [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/) for the budgets the counters are compared with.

## Principles

- **Local only.** Telemetry stays in the process and in the local log. The host MUST NOT send telemetry over the network, and no plugin can read the counters of another plugin.
- **Cheap.** Recording a call costs at most 200 ns. Counters use atomic integers and fixed histograms. Recording takes no lock on the call path.
- **Bounded.** Memory for telemetry is fixed per plugin side: at most 64 KiB.
- **Content free.** Counters hold numbers and names. They never hold event payloads, file names, URLs, terminal text or prompts.

- **[HST-350]** The host MUST NOT send telemetry over the network.
- **[HST-351]** Recording one call MUST take at most 200 ns at the 99th percentile and MUST NOT take a lock.
- **[HST-352]** Telemetry memory MUST be at most 64 KiB per plugin side.
- **[HST-353]** Telemetry MUST NOT contain payloads, paths, URLs, terminal text or prompts.

## Counters

Each plugin side has these counters. A **class** is a row of the call-class table in [Host scheduling](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/).

| Counter | Keyed by | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calls` | class | count | Calls started |
| `duration` | class | histogram | Call duration, buckets of 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000 ms and above |
| `near_misses` | class | count | Calls that took at least 80 % of the deadline |
| `breaches` | class, kind (hard, soft) | count | Deadline breaches |
| `traps` | trap code | count | Traps, by code (for example `host.deadline`, `host.stack-overflow`) |
| `queue_depth` | none | gauge, high-water | Event queue length |
| `events_dropped` | event kind | count | Events dropped by the drop-oldest policy |
| `events_coalesced` | event kind | count | Events merged |
| `quota_rejections` | none | count | `quota-exceeded` results from the `ilium-execution` bucket |
| `rate_limited` | import | count | `rate-limited` results |
| `cpu_ms` | none | counter | Sum of thread CPU time of calls (feeds the `ilium-execution` bucket) |
| `memory_peak` | none | bytes | Highest linear memory plus table size |
| `helper_round_trips` | none | histogram | Round trip of forwarded imports (T2 and T3) |
| `render_ms` | view | histogram | `views.render` duration |
| `restarts` | reason | count | Restarts, by reason |
| `failures` | reason | count | Counted failures, by reason |

The 99th percentile of `duration` is read from the histogram (the upper bound of the bucket that holds the 99th percentile). The `p50_ms` and `p99_ms` of `ilium plugin status` use the last 1,024 calls of each export; the histogram covers the whole retention.

- **[HST-354]** The host MUST keep the counters above for each plugin side, and the histogram buckets MUST be the ones listed.
- **[HST-355]** `near_misses` MUST count a call that ends in time and took at least 80 % of its deadline.
- **[HST-356]** A counter MUST NOT be readable by another plugin. Only the kernel, the CLI and the user interface read them.

## Retention

Counters are kept in memory in hourly buckets for the last 24 hours, and reset when the hosting process restarts. They are not written to disk. When an instance ends, one summary line is written to the plugin log (see below). This matches [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/).

- **[HST-357]** The host MUST keep hourly buckets for 24 hours and MUST discard older buckets. The summary line at the end of an instance MUST be written once.

## What is logged

The host writes its own lines to the plugin log under the plugin id, with the keys `plugin`, `side`, `kind` and the stable id of the condition. They are separate from the lines the plugin writes with `log`.

| Level | Condition | Id |
|---|---|---|
| info | Instance start and end, with a summary | `instance.started`, `instance.ended` |
| warn | A soft breach or a hard breach, with class and duration | `host.deadline`, `host.late` |
| warn | A call abandoned in the queue | `host.queue-timeout` |
| warn | Events dropped, with counts | `events.dropped` |
| warn | A clamp of a limit to the tier ceiling | `limits.clamped` |
| warn | A deactivate breach | `deactivate.deadline` |
| error | A trap, with the trap code (and a guest backtrace when debug info is present) | `host.trap` |
| error | A helper death | `helper.died` |
| info | Slow call report: top 3 slowest calls of the last minute, once a minute, when any call took over 50 % of its deadline | `host.slow-calls` |

Lines from the host are rate limited to 20 per minute per plugin side and kind. The rest are counted and summarized in one line: "N similar lines suppressed".

- **[HST-358]** The host MUST write the lines above under the plugin id, MUST include the stable condition id, and MUST rate limit them to 20 per minute per side and kind.
- **[HST-359]** The host MUST write `host.slow-calls` at most once per minute per side and only when a call took over 50 % of its deadline.

## Spans for host developers

With the environment variable `ILIUM_PLUGIN_TRACE=1` set on the server or client, the host records one span for each call with the plugin id, side, class, queue time, run time and the number of forwarded imports. The spans go to the host's own trace log, not to the plugin log, and the setting is off by default. A span has no payload.

- **[HST-360]** Tracing MUST be off by default and MUST record no payloads.

## Reading the data

| Surface | Shows |
|---|---|
| `ilium plugin status [<id>]` | Health, 50th and 99th percentile, near-misses, traps, queue high water, peak memory, quota hits (see [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/)) |
| `ilium plugin stats <id> --json` | Every counter above for 24 hours, one JSON line per class (read-only; requires no grant) |
| Plugins screen, detail, Resources tab | Memory, execution bucket level, helper state |
| Diagnostics report | The `Plugins` section |
| `plugin-info` import | Health and summary numbers for the plugin that asks about itself (`plugins.manage` is needed to ask about others) |

- **[HST-361]** `ilium plugin stats <id> --json` MUST print every counter for the retained buckets as JSON lines with a `type` field, and MUST exit with code 0 when the plugin exists.
- **[HST-362]** A plugin MUST be able to read its own summary through `plugin-info` without a grant.

## Health computation inputs

Health is computed from these counters and from lifecycle state, with the thresholds in [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/). The host adds the following to the host-side view; they do not change the health enum.

| Signal | Source | Where shown |
|---|---|---|
| Close to deadline | Near-miss rate | Detail view, "Why" line |
| Held by quota | `quota_rejections` in the last minute | Detail view and Resources tab |
| Waiting for a helper | `helper.too-many` active | Detail view |
| Memory near the limit | `memory_peak` over 90 % of `memory_mib` | Detail view |
| Stale contributions | Stale marker active | Detail view |

- **[HST-363]** The host MUST show the signal that put a plugin in `degraded` as a "Why" line with the counter values in the detail view.

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The server restarts | Counters reset; summary lines from before the restart stay in the log |
| A plugin is upgraded | Counters of the old version are closed with a summary; the new version starts at zero |
| The clock jumps | Buckets use the monotonic clock; a jump does not move data between buckets |
| A plugin makes 100,000 calls a minute | Histograms stay fixed in size; only counts grow |

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Install, update and uninstall reference

## Install, update and uninstall reference

This page specifies what the host does when a plugin is installed, updated, rolled back or removed, and where it keeps the result. A developer can implement the install transaction from it. A test author can derive crash, concurrency and update tests from it.

An **install** adds a plugin version to the machine. An **update** replaces an installed version with a higher one. A **downgrade** installs a lower one. A **rollback** returns to the version that was active before. An **uninstall** removes the plugin. A **transaction** is a change that either completes fully or leaves the earlier state intact. The **active version** is the one the host loads. A **session** is one running Ilium server with its clients.

Requirement ids such as `PKG-260` can be cited by tests. See [Requirements: manifest and package](/pages/reference-requirements-manifest-package/).

### You will need

- The validation stages: [Package format reference](/pages/reference-package-format/).
- Trust and tiers: [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/).
- The runtime states: [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) and [Plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/).

## Install sources

| Source | Form | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Local file | `ilium plugin install ./notes-1.2.0.iliumpkg` | The default |
| URL | `ilium plugin install https://example.org/notes-1.2.0.iliumpkg` | HTTPS only |
| Registry id | `ilium plugin install com.example.notes[@range]` | Needs a configured registry |
| Bundle | `ilium plugin install --from-bundle <dir> <id>` | Offline. See [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/#air-gapped-installs) |
| Project recommendation | A prompt from `.ilium/plugins.toml` | Never automatic. See [Finding and installing plugins](/pages/user-plugin-store/) |
| Development | `ilium plugin dev` | Tier T3, channel `dev` |

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-260] | A URL install downloads the file into the cache folder (`{cache}/plugins/downloads/`), then treats it as a local file. A URL with the scheme `http` is refused with `install.insecure-url`. The download follows at most 3 redirects, all to HTTPS. |
| [PKG-261] | The download is at most 300 MiB. A larger response is aborted with `install.size`. The server's content type is ignored. The file is judged only by the package format. |
| [PKG-262] | A URL install of an unsigned package needs `--allow-unsigned`, as a file does. A URL does not change the trust rules. |
| [PKG-263] | A registry id with a range resolves through [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/) to one version and then installs that package. The recorded `source` is `registry` and the record keeps the registry URL. |
| [PKG-264] | A file named in a project recommendation is treated like any other source after the user confirms it. The host MUST NOT download or install a recommended plugin without an explicit user action. |

## On-disk state

The folder layout, the registry file `installed.json`, the lock `installed.lock`, the immutable store `store/<id>/<version>/` and the staging area are owned by [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) and listed for users in [Plugin files on disk](/pages/reference-plugin-files/). This page uses those names and does not repeat them. It adds the distribution fields that a source, a channel and a signature need.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-265] | Each plugin entry of `installed.json` follows the one schema of [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/#the-registry-file): `source` is `bundled`, `file`, `url`, `registry` or `dev`; `channel` is `stable`, `beta`, `dev` or `file`; `key_id` is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters or null; `package_sha256` and `manifest_sha256` are 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; `skip` and `declined` are lists of version strings; `installed_at` is RFC 3339 in UTC with the suffix `Z`; `update` is null or `{ candidate, state, attempts, started_at }`. The page that owns the schema is the only place that lists the fields. |
| [PKG-266] | The package file is kept as `store/<id>/<version>/package.iliumpkg` next to the unpacked files, so that `verify` and `rollback` need no network. Files in `store/` are written once and made read-only. An update writes a new folder and never changes an old one. |
| [PKG-267] | The user trust store is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/trust.json` (Linux `~/.local/state/ilium/trust.json` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is unset), mode 0600, written atomically. The variable `ILIUM_TRUST_STORE` replaces it and holds an absolute file path. The format is that of [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/#the-trust-store). Downloads in progress live in `<cache>/plugins/downloads/`. Cached registry metadata lives in `<cache>/plugins/registry/<hash-of-url>/`. |
| [PKG-268] | The compiled cache `<cache>/plugins/compile/` is derived data, keyed by the component SHA-256 and an engine id (the Wasmtime version and settings). The host MUST be able to delete it at any time and recompile. |
| [PKG-269] | A crash leaves `installed.json` unchanged, because the registry file is the single commit point (steps 6 below). Orphans in `staging/` are deleted at the next start. |

## The install transaction

An install is the following steps in order. A failure at any step leaves the earlier state.

1. **Acquire** the lock `installed.lock`.
2. **Fetch**: read the file, or download it (URL, registry).
3. **Validate**: run stages 1 to 10 of the [validation order](/pages/reference-package-format/#the-validation-order).
4. **Review**: show the review dialog, or read `--grant` and `--yes` flags.
5. **Stage**: copy the package to `staging/<uuid>/`, unpack it, make files read-only, then rename the folder to `store/<id>/<version>/`.
6. **Commit**: write the new `installed.json` (atomic rename). This is the single point at which the install becomes true.
7. **Notify**: tell running servers that the state changed.
8. **Release** the lock.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-270] | A second install, update or uninstall that starts while the lock is held polls every 100 ms for up to 30 s and then fails with `install.locked`, exit code 4 (LIF-066). The lock is an exclusive OS advisory lock, so a crashed holder releases it by process exit and no takeover rule exists. |
| [PKG-271] | A crash before step 6 leaves the previous `installed.json`. The next start deletes the `staging/` directories that `installed.json` does not reference. A crash after step 6 and before step 7 leaves a complete install that the running servers see when they watch `installed.json` (LIF-089). |
| [PKG-272] | The host MUST NOT instantiate any component before step 6 has finished and step 7 has been sent. |
| [PKG-273] | The platform gate is stage 9: on Windows and macOS an install of a T2 or T3 package is refused with `package.platform-unsupported` before the review dialog. T1 bundled plugins are not installed by this path. |
| [PKG-274] | An install of an id that is already installed at the same version with the same manifest SHA-256 is a no-op: it exits 0 and prints `install.already-installed` as a warning. With `--reinstall` it rewrites `store/<id>/<version>/` from the package. A different manifest SHA-256 at the same version is refused at stage 9 with `package.version-reused`, exit 1. The manifest hash is compared, not the package hash, because the signature document changes the package bytes (LIF-072). |
| [PKG-275] | `--dry-run` runs steps 1 to 4 without writing anything. It prints the plan and exits 0 if all stages pass. |

### Running servers and several sessions

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-276] | The installed set is per user, not per session. Every session of the same user sees the same `installed.json`. |
| [PKG-277] | Step 7 sends the message `plugins-changed` to every server of the user. A server that cannot be reached reads `installed.json` when it next starts or when its watcher sees the file change. |
| [PKG-278] | A new plugin is registered and activated by its triggers in each server that gets the notice. An update does not touch running instances: the candidate waits in `store/<id>/<version>/` with `update.state: staged`, and the old version keeps running until it deactivates with reason `upgrade`, then the candidate activates. The server does this at the next safe point: when the plugin is idle, or at the next server start. The user can force it with `ilium plugin restart <id>`. |
| [PKG-279] | When two sessions run the same plugin, each switches independently. The order across sessions is not defined, and no plugin may rely on two sessions running the same version at one moment. State kept in `data/` is shared, so a plugin that changes its data format MUST handle both versions during the switch. |

## Update

An update is an install of a higher version of an installed id.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-280] | Versions compare with the precedence of [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/#plugin-versions). A prerelease is lower than its release. An equal version is not an update. |
| [PKG-281] | Grants: new grants (strings that the active version did not request) are asked in the review. Removed grants are dropped from the record. Grants that the user declined before stay declined and are not asked again, unless the new manifest requests them again in a different form (a different argument is a different grant). |
| [PKG-282] | A new high-risk grant, a new `replaces` entry or a new high-risk extension point contribution always needs confirmation. `--yes` does not confirm it. The flag `--grant <side>:<grant>` for that exact grant does. |
| [PKG-283] | A publisher key change follows [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/#publisher-key-change-and-rotation). |
| [PKG-284] | Settings values, plugin data and storage are kept. The old version deactivates with reason `upgrade`, which lets it save state, and the new version activates and reads the same data. See [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/). |
| [PKG-285] | After a successful update the host keeps the previous version folder in `store/` and deletes older ones, which matches LIF-076: exactly one previous version stays on disk. |
| [PKG-286] | The candidate becomes `active_version` only after its first `activate` returns `ok` on the server side. If that first `activate` fails, traps or misses its deadline, the host rolls back at once to the previous version and its pre-update data snapshot, marks the candidate `skip`, logs `update.rolled-back` and does not count the failure in the failure window (LIF-075). Failures after a successful first activation follow the normal failure window and never roll back by themselves. |

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin update example.notes
<span class="t-dim">step</span>   resolve    1.2.0 > 1.3.0
<span class="t-ok">ok</span>     verify     signature, key 5647 5aa7
<span class="t-warn">new</span>    grant      http:api.example.com
<span class="t-dim">asked</span>  kept       tree.read ui.panels
<span class="t-ok">ok</span>     commit     1.3.0 active at restart
<span class="t-hi">done</span>   example.notes 1.3.0
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. An update that asks for one new grant.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Downgrade

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-287] | A package whose version is lower than the active version is refused with `package.downgrade` unless `--allow-downgrade` is given. |
| [PKG-288] | A downgrade or rollback to a version whose `data_version` is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope is refused with `migration.data-newer`, exit 1, unless `--restore-backup` or `--discard-data` is given (LIF-079). The host never converts newer data downward. |
| [PKG-289] | A downgrade keeps the replaced newer version as the one previous version on disk, so a later update to it needs no download. |

## Rollback

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-290] | `ilium plugin rollback <id>` makes the one previous version in `store/` active. It runs the same transaction as an update, but without the version comparison, and keeps the current grants where the old manifest still asks for them. |
| [PKG-291] | Rollback is refused with `install.no-previous` when no earlier version is on disk. |
| [PKG-292] | After a rollback the rolled-back version is marked `skip` and is not offered by update until a still newer version exists or the user clears the mark with `--unskip`. |

## Uninstall

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-293] | `ilium plugin uninstall <id>` deactivates the plugin (reason `disabled`), withdraws all of its contributions, removes the record from `installed.json` and deletes `store/<id>/`. |
| [PKG-294] | Without `--purge` the folders `data/<id>/` and `storage/<id>/`, the stored settings and `backups/<id>/` remain, so a later reinstall finds its configuration. No prompt is shown: the command prints the kept paths as `warning` lines (LIF-082). Grants, first-use answers, durable timers, failure counters and decorations are deleted on every uninstall (LIF-083), so a reinstall asks for grants again. |
| [PKG-295] | `--purge` also deletes `data/<id>/`, `storage/<id>/`, `backups/<id>/`, `locks/<id>.*`, the plugin log, the stored settings values of the plugin (including project-scoped ones in `.ilium/` of the current project only), the plugin cache and the compiled cache entries. It never deletes anything outside these paths. It prints the number of bytes freed. The grant entry is deleted without `--purge` as well. |
| [PKG-296] | The trusted key stays in the trust store. Uninstall never edits trust. |
| [PKG-297] | Dependants follow [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/#effects-on-update-and-uninstall). A plugin installed by a system administrator as read-only is refused with `policy.managed-plugin`. |
| [PKG-298] | The uninstall of a plugin that is currently `failed` or `disabled` works the same way. |
| [PKG-299] | A T1 bundled plugin cannot be uninstalled. It can be disabled. The command is refused with `install.bundled`. |

## Auto-update

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-300] | The setting `[plugins] auto_update` has the values `off` (default), `notify` and `install`. With `off` the host never checks the network by itself. With `notify` it checks and shows a notice. With `install` it checks and installs updates that need no new grants. |
| [PKG-301] | The check runs at server start, then every 24 hours while the server runs, with a random delay of up to 1 hour. `[plugins] auto_update_interval_hours` (1 to 168) changes it. |
| [PKG-302] | Auto-install never installs an update that adds grants, adds `replaces`, changes the publisher key, or crosses to a channel the user did not select. Those updates produce a notice and wait. |
| [PKG-303] | When the network is marked metered (the operating system says so, or `[plugins] metered = true`), the host does not check. |
| [PKG-304] | A notice lists the plugin, the old and new version, the new grants and the link to the changelog. The user can **Update**, **Later** (which hides the notice for that version for 7 days) or **Skip this version**. |
| [PKG-305] | Auto-update is a policy item. An administrator can set `off` and lock it. |

## Codes and JSONL lines

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `install.locked` | Another transaction holds the lock for more than 30 s |
| `install.insecure-url` | A URL used `http` |
| `install.download-failed` | The network failed during a download |
| `install.size` | A download or upload was too large |
| `install.state-corrupt` | `installed.json` was unreadable |
| `install.no-space` | The disk is full |
| `install.needs-input` | A decision is needed and no person can answer |
| `install.already-installed` | The same version is installed |
| `install.not-installed` | The id is not installed |
| `install.no-previous` | There is no earlier version for a rollback |
| `install.bundled` | The target is a bundled plugin |
| `install.cancelled` | The user closed the review dialog |
| `package.downgrade` | A lower version without `--allow-downgrade` |
| `package.version-reused` | The same version with a different hash |
| `package.platform-unsupported` | T2 or T3 on a platform with no sandbox |

Each step prints one JSONL line with `type` `progress`, `step` (`acquire`, `fetch`, `validate`, `review`, `stage`, `commit`, `notify`) and `status`. The final line has `type` `result` with `id`, `version`, `tier`, `action` (`installed`, `updated`, `downgraded`, `rolled-back`, `uninstalled`) and `active_from` (`now` or `restart`). Exit codes are in [Plugin command line](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/#exit-codes) and [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/).

## Worked example: a crash during an update

The user updates `example.notes` from 1.2.0 to 1.3.0 and the machine loses power at step 5, while the new folder is being written.

1. `installed.json` still says `active: 1.2.0`, because step 6 did not run.
2. `staging/<uuid>/` exists.
3. At the next start, the host deletes the orphan, loads 1.2.0, and shows no error.
4. The user repeats the update. It succeeds.

If the power fails after step 6, `installed.json` says 1.3.0 and `store/example.notes/1.3.0/` is complete, because the rename of the folder came first. The server loads 1.3.0.

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The disk is full at step 5 | The staging folder is removed. The error is `install.no-space`, with the free space |
| Two `install` commands for different ids | The second waits for the lock, up to 30 s |
| The package file is deleted during install | The host works on its own copy from step 2 |
| `--yes` without `--grant` flags | Installs with the default grants: normal grants on, high-risk grants off |
| An id that is both bundled and in a file | Refused with `manifest.id-reserved` |

## What the user sees

The user sees a progress line per step, the review dialog and the result. After an update the plugin shows **restart pending** in Settings > Plugins if the old version is still running. See [Finding and installing plugins](/pages/user-plugin-store/).

- [Package format reference](/pages/reference-package-format/)
- [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/)
- [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/)
- [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/)
- [Plugin command line](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/)
- [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/)

- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)

# Reference, install, update and uninstall

## Reference, install, update and uninstall

This page specifies how a plugin package gets onto a machine, how it is replaced by a newer version, how an update is undone, and what is kept or deleted when it is removed. It also lists every `ilium plugin` command that manages installed plugins, with arguments, JSON line output, exit codes and error codes. The build and signing commands (`new`, `build`, `pack`, `keygen`, `sign`, `trust`) are in [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/).

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. A registry is optional (decision D27); see [Install and update](/pages/reference-install-and-update/) for the registry path. A package is a file, and every step on this page works offline ([offline and low disk](/pages/reference-offline-and-low-disk/)).

### Terms

- Package store: the directory that holds unpacked, verified packages. It is immutable after install.
- Registry: the file `installed.json`. It says which version of each plugin is active.
- Active version: the version the registry points to. Instances run from it.
- Staging: a private directory where a package is unpacked and checked before it enters the store.
- Data version: the number `data_version` in the manifest. It describes the layout of the data a plugin stores. See [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/).

### On-disk layout

All paths are relative to the plugin root, `<data dir>/plugins/`, where `<data dir>` comes from the `directories` crate (`~/.local/share/ilium` on Linux). The cache directory is `<cache dir>/ilium/plugins/`.

```text
<data dir>/plugins/
  installed.json            registry, versioned format
  installed.lock            exclusive OS advisory lock; holder pid and boot id for messages
  store/<id>/<version>/     immutable package: manifest.json, manifest.sha256, components, files
  staging/<uuid>/           uncommitted unpack of one operation
  locks/<id>.migrate.lock   cross-process lock of one data migration
  backups/<id>/<version>-<utc timestamp>/   pre-migration copy of data and buckets
  data/<id>/                the plugin data directory (fs data scope)
  storage/<id>/global.db    global bucket
  logs/<id>.log             plugin log
<state dir>/trust.json      the user trust store, mode 0600 (not under the plugin root)
<cache dir>/ilium/plugins/
  <id>/                     the plugin cache directory
  compile/                  compiled components for T2 and T3, see offline and low disk
```

The user trust store is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/trust.json` (Linux `~/.local/state/ilium/trust.json` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is unset), mode 0600, written atomically. Its format is in [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/#the-trust-store). The variable `ILIUM_TRUST_STORE` replaces the path with an absolute file path. In `backups/`, `<version>` is the version that was active before the update, and the timestamp is `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` in UTC, for example `backups/com.example.notes/0.3.0-20261012T091404Z/`.

The project and session buckets live with the project, under `<project>/.ilium/`. See [scope and sessions](/pages/reference-plugin-scope-and-sessions/).

### The registry file

`installed.json` is a JSON object that carries its own format string, so that a future host can read an old file. It is serialised with 2-space indentation, LF line endings and one final LF. The array `plugins` is sorted by `id` in byte order. This page owns the schema; every other page links here.

```json
{
  "format": "ilium-installed/1",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "id": "com.example.notes",
      "active_version": "0.3.1",
      "previous_version": "0.3.0",
      "state": "installed-enabled",
      "source": "registry",
      "source_url": "https://registry.example.org/",
      "channel": "stable",
      "publisher_id": "com.example",
      "key_id": "46ef773ed515997e3f107ae73619e6a31921c98f96d468eb858a02b48d5ae011",
      "package_sha256": "807e3b71e81cd569717e02318607832667fac642717e8b0e0eeb2426e030a34c",
      "manifest_sha256": "7ff76366f824af4ec0b54fdee14ff3661b38567668e38f90c13920662f05deea",
      "pinned": false,
      "skip": [],
      "declined": [],
      "failure_stopped": [],
      "installed_at": "2026-10-12T09:14:04Z",
      "update": null
    }
  ],
  "purge_tombstones": []
}
```

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The plugin id. |
| `active_version` | string | The version the host runs. |
| `previous_version` | string or null | The one version that rollback returns to. |
| `state` | string | The stored package state: `installed-enabled`, `installed-disabled-by-user`, `disabled-untrusted`, `disabled-blocked` or `uninstall-pending`. The other package states are derived at load. See [plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/#package-states). |
| `source` | string | `bundled`, `file`, `url`, `registry` or `dev`. An install from an offline bundle records `file`. |
| `source_url` | string or null | The URL or registry address the package came from. |
| `channel` | string | `stable`, `beta`, `dev` or `file`. |
| `publisher_id` | string or null | The publisher id bound to the signing key; null for T1 and T3. |
| `key_id` | string or null | The key id of the signer: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; null for T1 and T3. |
| `package_sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the package file, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. |
| `manifest_sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the packed `manifest.json`, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The host compares it at every load. |
| `pinned` | bool | The user pinned the version; update does not offer a newer one. |
| `skip` | list of strings | Versions that update does not offer. |
| `declined` | list of strings | Versions whose review the user declined. The declined grants themselves are in its entry in `grants.json`. |
| `failure_stopped` | list of strings | The sides stopped by the third counted failure. The only value in 0.1.0 is `server`. |
| `installed_at` | string | RFC 3339 in UTC with seconds precision and the suffix `Z`. |
| `update` | object or null | An update in progress: `{ "candidate", "state", "attempts", "started_at" }`. `state` is `staged`, `migrating` or `trial`. `attempts` is an integer from 0 to 2. `started_at` has the form of `installed_at`. |
| `purge_tombstones` | list (top level) | Plugin ids whose project and session data must still be deleted. |

The data version of each bucket is stamped with the bucket, not in this file; see [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/). The tier is not stored; the host computes it again at every load from `key_id` and the trust store.

The JSON Schema of the file:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "ilium-installed/1",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["format", "plugins", "purge_tombstones"],
  "properties": {
    "format": { "const": "ilium-installed/1" },
    "plugins": { "type": "array", "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/plugin" } },
    "purge_tombstones": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "sha256": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" },
    "utc": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$" },
    "plugin": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["id", "active_version", "previous_version", "state", "source",
                   "source_url", "channel", "publisher_id", "key_id", "package_sha256",
                   "manifest_sha256", "pinned", "skip", "declined", "failure_stopped",
                   "installed_at", "update"],
      "properties": {
        "id": { "type": "string" },
        "active_version": { "type": "string" },
        "previous_version": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
        "state": { "enum": ["installed-enabled", "installed-disabled-by-user",
                            "disabled-untrusted", "disabled-blocked", "uninstall-pending"] },
        "source": { "enum": ["bundled", "file", "url", "registry", "dev"] },
        "source_url": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
        "channel": { "enum": ["stable", "beta", "dev", "file"] },
        "publisher_id": { "type": ["string", "null"] },
        "key_id": { "oneOf": [{ "$ref": "#/$defs/sha256" }, { "type": "null" }] },
        "package_sha256": { "$ref": "#/$defs/sha256" },
        "manifest_sha256": { "$ref": "#/$defs/sha256" },
        "pinned": { "type": "boolean" },
        "skip": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
        "declined": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
        "failure_stopped": { "type": "array", "items": { "enum": ["server"] } },
        "installed_at": { "$ref": "#/$defs/utc" },
        "update": {
          "oneOf": [
            { "type": "null" },
            { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
              "required": ["candidate", "state", "attempts", "started_at"],
              "properties": {
                "candidate": { "type": "string" },
                "state": { "enum": ["staged", "migrating", "trial"] },
                "attempts": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 2 },
                "started_at": { "$ref": "#/$defs/utc" }
              } }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- [LIF-065] The host MUST write `installed.json` atomically: write a temporary file in the same directory, fsync it, rename it over the old file, then fsync the directory. Test: kill the writer at each step (fault injection) and assert that a reader sees the old or the new file, never a partial one.
- [LIF-066] `installed.lock` is an exclusive OS advisory lock (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows, through the `file_lock` module of `ilium-platform`) on `<data dir>/plugins/installed.lock`. The file also holds the holder's process id and boot id, for messages only. The host MUST hold the lock while it changes the store or the registry. A crashed holder releases the lock by process exit, so no takeover rule exists. A second writer MUST poll every 100 ms for up to 30 s, then fail with `install.locked` and exit code 4. Test: hold the lock and start an install; kill the holder with SIGKILL and assert that the next install gets the lock at once.
- [LIF-067] The host MUST refuse a registry whose `format` is a higher number than it knows (for example `ilium-installed/99`), with `install.registry-format`, and MUST NOT rewrite it. Test: set `format` to `ilium-installed/99`.
- [LIF-282] The host MUST validate `installed.json` against the schema above at start and refuse a file that does not match it with `install.state-corrupt`, without rewriting it. Test: write one file per property with a wrong type, an extra key, a short `key_id` and a local-time `installed_at`, and assert `install.state-corrupt` for each.

### The install pipeline

`ilium plugin install <file.iliumpkg>` runs these steps in order. A failure at any step stops the pipeline, removes what the pipeline created and leaves the registry unchanged. Step 2 is the validation order of [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/#the-validation-order) (PKG-149); this page does not define a second order.

| Step | Action | On failure | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Take `installed.lock`. | Wait, then give up. | `install.locked` |
| 2 | Run validation stages 1 to 11: archive, manifest-parse, schema, semantic, inventory, components, signature, trust, policy, dependencies, review. Stage 11 shows the grant review and records the answers. | Nothing is written yet. | the codes of the failing stage in the [catalogue](/pages/reference-manifest-schema/#error-catalogue) |
| 3 | Unpack to `staging/<uuid>/`. | Delete the staging directory. | `install.io`, `install.no-space` |
| 4 | Prepare the components: T1 ships precompiled code; T2 and T3 are compiled into the compile cache. | Delete the staging directory. | `install.compile-failed` |
| 5 | Rename the staging directory to `store/<id>/<version>/`. Write `manifest.sha256`. | Delete the staging directory. | `install.io` |
| 6 | Update `installed.json` atomically (see LIF-065). Write the plugin's entry in `grants.json`. | Delete the new store entry. | `install.io` |
| 7 | Tell the running servers (see Propagation). Release the lock. | A failed notification is a warning only. | `install.notify-failed` |

- [LIF-068] The host MUST NOT instantiate or run any code of the package before step 2 has finished. Test: install a package whose start function writes a file and decline the review; assert the file is absent.
- [LIF-069] A failure at any step MUST leave the registry byte for byte unchanged and MUST delete the staging directory and any new store entry. Test: inject a failure at each step and compare the registry hash.
- [LIF-070] An install MUST NOT require network access. Test: run the install in a network namespace with no interfaces.
- [LIF-071] Validation MUST run in the stage order of PKG-149, so that the cheapest checks refuse first and no prompt appears for a package that would be refused later. Test: a package with an invalid manifest (stage 3) and an invalid signature (stage 7) reports `manifest.schema` and no signature code.
- [LIF-072] Installing the same id and version with the same manifest SHA-256 MUST be a no-op that exits 0 and prints `install.already-installed` as a `warning` line; with `--reinstall` it rewrites `store/<id>/<version>/` from the package. A different manifest SHA-256 for the same id and version MUST be refused at stage 9 with `package.version-reused` (exit 1). The host compares the manifest hash and not the package hash, because the signature document changes the package bytes. Test: install a package twice, then a modified copy with the same version, then the same manifest signed again.

Grant review in a non-interactive run (no TTY): normal grants are accepted only with `--yes`; a high-risk grant is accepted only when named with `--grant <name>`. Without them the install ends with `install.needs-input` and exit code 1 (PKG-430).

### Update

A higher version of an installed id is an update. It is the same pipeline, committed beside the old version, followed by a swap. The candidate lives in `store/<id>/<version>/` from step 5 on, so the waiting period never depends on `staging/`.

1. Steps 1 to 5 run as for an install. The dialog shows only the new capabilities. The package state is `update-staged`.
2. Step 6 writes `previous_version` and `update: { candidate, state: "staged", attempts: 0, started_at }`, and leaves `active_version` unchanged.
3. Each running server receives the change. At the next safe point ([Install and update](/pages/reference-install-and-update/), PKG-278) each live instance receives `deactivate(upgrade)` and returns its restore bytes ([LIF-044](/pages/lifecycle/)).
4. Before the host calls `migrate`, it writes `update.state: "migrating"` to `installed.json` with fsync. The data migration runs ([Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/)). If the host stops while the state is `migrating`, the next start restores the backup, increments `attempts` and runs the migration again; when `attempts` reaches 2 the host rolls back with `migration.interrupted` and marks the candidate `skip`.
5. The host sets `update.state` to `trial` and the server activates the candidate. The context carries `restored`, unless the data version changed, in which case the bytes are dropped.
6. The candidate becomes `active_version` only after its first `activate` returns `ok` on the server side. Then the host sets `active_version` to the candidate, sets `previous_version`, sets `update` to `null` and logs `update.ok`. The update is committed.
7. If that first `activate` fails, traps or misses its deadline, the host rolls back at once: it restores the data snapshot if a migration ran, reactivates the previous version and sets `update` to `null`. It marks the candidate `skip`, logs `update.rolled-back`, shows the toast `Update failed, rolled back`, and does not count this failure in the failure window.

Failures after a successful first activation follow the normal failure window ([Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart)) and never roll back by themselves.

- [LIF-073] The first server to apply an update MUST decide it. After step 6, a failure on another server MUST follow the normal failure rule and MUST NOT roll back. Test: update with two servers running, fail the second server's activation and assert the version stays.
- [LIF-074] An update MUST be atomic: after any interruption, either the old or the new version is active, never neither. Test: kill the installer or the server at each step and assert that a plugin version is active after restart.
- [LIF-075] The candidate becomes `active_version` only after its first `activate` returns `ok` on the server side. If that first `activate` fails, traps or misses its deadline, the host MUST roll back at once to the previous version and its pre-update data snapshot, mark the candidate `skip`, log `update.rolled-back`, and not count the failure in the failure window. A failure after a successful first activation MUST follow the normal failure window and MUST NOT roll back. Test: install a candidate whose `activate` returns an error and assert the failure window of the plugin is empty; then fail a later call and assert no rollback.
- [LIF-076] The host MUST keep exactly one previous version in `store/` and delete older ones after a committed update. Test: update three times and list `store/<id>/`.
- [LIF-077] A blocked candidate MUST NOT be tried again unless the user installs it again explicitly. Test: roll back, restart the server and assert that no activation of the candidate occurs.
- [LIF-078] An update MUST NOT send grants to the new version beyond those the user accepted. A new version that asks for more is `update-staged` until the review is answered. Test: update with an extra grant and decline.

Disk cost: the store holds the active and the previous version, so a plugin uses about twice its package size, plus the newest pre-migration backup, which lasts until the next committed update.

If activation of the new version is deferred (a lazy plugin has no trigger yet), the update stays in `trial` until the first activation. The previous version is not removed in that time.

### Rollback and downgrade

`ilium plugin rollback <id>` makes the previous version active. `ilium plugin install --allow-downgrade <file>` installs a lower version than the active one. Both follow the same data rule.

- [LIF-079] Activating a version whose `data_version` is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope MUST be refused with `migration.data-newer` (stage I, exit 1), unless `--restore-backup` or `--discard-data` is given. This applies to downgrade and rollback. The user can pass `--restore-backup`, which restores the data snapshot taken before the update and loses what was written since, or `--discard-data`, which deletes the plugin's buckets and data directory. Test: update to a version that migrates data, write data, roll back without a flag and assert `migration.data-newer`; repeat with each flag.
- [LIF-080] `--restore-backup` MUST fail with `rollback.no-backup` when the snapshot is gone. Test: delete the backup and roll back with the flag.
- [LIF-081] Rollback MUST send `deactivate(upgrade)` to the running instances and activate the previous version with the same rules as an update. Test: read the reasons in the log.

### Uninstall

`ilium plugin uninstall <id>` removes a plugin. The table says what is kept and what is deleted.

| Item | Default uninstall | With `--purge` | With `--keep-data` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Store entries (all versions) | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Data directory | kept | deleted | kept |
| Cache directory and compile cache | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Global bucket | kept with the data directory | deleted | kept |
| Project bucket | kept | deleted for this project, tombstone for others | kept |
| Session bucket | kept until its session is deleted | deleted for this session, tombstone for others | kept |
| Shared bucket | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Settings values | kept | deleted | kept |
| Grants and first-use answers | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Node metadata in snapshots | kept, inert | deleted for the live session, tombstone for others | kept, inert |
| Persistent decorations | removed | removed | removed |
| Durable timers | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Backups `backups/<id>/` | kept | deleted | kept |
| Migration locks `locks/<id>.*` | kept | deleted | kept |
| Journal entries of the plugin | kept until normal expiry | kept until normal expiry | kept until normal expiry |
| Trusted publisher keys | kept | kept | kept |
| User extension order entries | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Failure counters | deleted | deleted | deleted |
| Log files | kept 7 days, then deleted | deleted | kept 7 days |

- [LIF-082] An uninstall without `--purge` MUST keep the data directory, the buckets, the settings values and `backups/<id>/`, with or without a TTY, and MUST NOT ask a question. It prints the kept paths as `warning` lines. `--keep-data` is accepted and means the same as the default. Test: run it with standard input closed and again on a TTY, and assert no prompt and the warning lines.
- [LIF-083] The host MUST delete grants (its entry in `grants.json`), first-use answers, durable timers, failure counters and persistent decorations on every uninstall, with or without `--purge`. Data, storage and settings are kept unless `--purge` is given. A reinstall MUST ask for grants again. Test: install, grant, uninstall, install and assert the review dialog appears.
- [LIF-084] Node metadata and session data of an uninstalled plugin MUST stay inert: the host never passes them to another plugin, and keeps them in the snapshot. A reinstall of the same id MAY read them again. With `--purge` the host MUST delete them in the live session and add a tombstone, so that other projects delete theirs when they next open. Test: purge, reopen another project and assert the keys are gone.
- [LIF-085] Uninstall MUST first set `uninstall-pending`, then stop all instances, then delete files. After a crash, the next start MUST finish it. Test: kill the host after the state is written.
- [LIF-086] Uninstall MUST NOT delete data of other plugins, and MUST NOT remove a publisher key. Test: compare the other plugins' directories before and after.

### Command reference

All commands print JSON lines when output is not a terminal, or when `--json` is given. Every line has a `type`: `progress`, `result`, `warning`, `error` or `summary`. Paths are explicit fields.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ilium plugin install <file> [--allow-unsigned] [--allow-downgrade] [--yes] [--grant <name>]...` | Install or update from a package file. |
| `ilium plugin update <file>` | Same as install, but fails with `install.not-installed` when the id is not installed. |
| `ilium plugin uninstall <id> [--purge] [--keep-data]` | Remove a plugin. The two flags exclude each other. |
| `ilium plugin enable <id> [--scope <scope>] [--session <name>]` | Turn a plugin on. |
| `ilium plugin disable <id> [--scope <scope>] [--session <name>]` | Turn a plugin off. |
| `ilium plugin list [--json]` | List plugins and states. |
| `ilium plugin info <id> [--json]` | Show one plugin: manifest summary, grants, state, health. |
| `ilium plugin rollback <id> [--restore-backup] [--discard-data]` | Activate the previous version. |
| `ilium plugin reinstall <id>` | Repair the store entry from the cached package. |
| `ilium plugin logs <id> [--tail <n>]` | Print the plugin log. |
| `ilium plugin reset-failures <id> [--session <name>]` | Clear the failure window and the failure stop. |
| `ilium plugin status [<id>] [--json]` | Print health and metrics. See [health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/). |
| `ilium plugin stats <id> [--json]` | Print resource usage. See [resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/). |
| `ilium plugin bisect start\|good\|bad\|reset` | Find a bad plugin. See [safe mode](/pages/user-safe-mode-and-troubleshooting/). |

Exit codes are those of the one table in [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/#exit-codes): 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 findings, 4 environment or locked, 5 not found, 6 no session, 7 policy, 8 network, 130 interrupted. This page keeps no table of its own. A declined review exits 1 with `install.review-declined`.

JSON line examples:

```text
{"type":"progress","step":2,"of":7,"message":"validating package"}
{"type":"warning","code":"install.notify-failed","message":"session /home/u/proj not reached","session":"default"}
{"type":"result","id":"com.example.notes","version":"0.3.1","previous":"0.3.0","state":"installed-enabled"}
{"type":"error","code":"manifest.file-hash","message":"files/panel.wasm hash differs","path":"files/panel.wasm"}
{"type":"summary","ok":false,"errors":1,"warnings":0}
```

- [LIF-087] Every command MUST print only JSON lines on standard output when output is not a terminal, MUST use the exit codes of the table in [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/#exit-codes) and MUST give each error line a `code` from the [error catalogue](/pages/reference-manifest-schema/#error-catalogue). Test: run each command in a pipe and parse every line.
- [LIF-088] `enable` and `disable` MUST be idempotent: they exit 0 and print a `result` line with `changed: false` when nothing changes. Test: disable twice.

### Propagation to running servers

Ilium runs one server per project session, so one install can reach many servers.

- [LIF-089] A running server MUST apply an `installed.json` change within 2 s with a file watcher, and within 6 s when watching is unavailable (polling every 5 s). The installing CLI MUST also send a `plugins-changed` message to every server it can find in the runtime directory; a server it cannot reach is reported as a `warning` line with `install.notify-failed` and picks the change up at its watch or at its next start. Test: install with two servers, assert both log `registry.changed` within 2 s with the watcher on and within 6 s with the watcher off.
- [LIF-090] A server that is not running MUST use the registry as it finds it at start. Test: install, then start a server and assert the new version is active.
- [LIF-091] A change MUST be applied to a server under the per-plugin serialisation of [lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/). Test: install an update during a disable.

### Install or update while the plugin is active in many sessions

Every server swaps its own instances, as in the update steps. Their order is not defined, and the first to finish decides (LIF-073). A session that cannot swap yet because the plugin is busy in a call waits at most the deactivate deadline, then drops the instance. A session on another project whose plugin data is shared (the global bucket) takes the migration lock, as [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) describes.

### Interrupted install and recovery

- [LIF-092] At start, and at the start of every `ilium plugin` command that takes the lock, the host MUST delete `staging/` directories whose creating process is gone or that are older than 1 hour. `installed.json` never references `staging/`: a staged update lives in `store/<id>/<version>/` (step 5) and is never touched by this rule. Test: create an orphan staging directory and start a server; stage an update, wait past 1 hour and assert the candidate is still in `store/`.
- [LIF-093] A store entry that no field of `installed.json` references (`active_version`, `previous_version` or `update.candidate`) and that is older than 1 hour MUST be deleted at start. A registry entry whose store entry is missing or fails its hash check MUST put the plugin in `refused-at-load` with `package.corrupt`. `ilium plugin reinstall <id>` MUST repair it from the cached package or fail with `package.cache-missing`. Test: truncate a file in the store.
- [LIF-094] After a power loss the host MUST find either the old or the new registry, because of LIF-065, and MUST finish or undo an `update` in `staged`, `migrating` or `trial` by the rules above at the next activation. Test: kill the machine at step 6 (simulated) and restart.

### Error codes

The catalogue in [Manifest schema and error catalogue](/pages/reference-manifest-schema/#error-catalogue) is the only list of codes. This table names the codes that this page raises and the check that provokes each.

| Code | Meaning | Test hint |
|---|---|---|
| `package.manifest-missing` | The archive has no `manifest.json`. | Remove `manifest.json` from a package. |
| `package.entry-unexpected` | An entry is outside the allowed layout. | Add `extra.txt` at the root. |
| `manifest.file-hash` | A file hash differs from the inventory. | Flip a byte in a component. |
| `package.corrupt` | The store entry fails its hash check at load. | Truncate a stored component. |
| `package.cache-missing` | Reinstall has no cached package. | Delete the cache, run reinstall. |
| `manifest.signature-invalid` | The signature does not match. | Edit the manifest after signing. |
| `trust.key-unknown` | The signer is not trusted and the user declined or could not answer. | Install a package of a new key without `trust add`. |
| `trust.key-revoked` | The signer key is on the revoked list. | Add the key to the revoked list. |
| `policy.tier-denied` | The tier is not allowed on this machine by policy. | Deny T3 in the policy file. |
| `package.api-unsupported` | The package API window does not include this host. | Set `api` to a window above the host. |
| `manifest.service-cycle` | The non-optional `requires.services` entries form a cycle. | Install a cycle. |
| `policy.blocked` | The administrator policy forbids the plugin. | Block the id in the policy file. |
| `install.review-declined` | The review was declined. | Answer No in the review dialog. |
| `install.needs-input` | A decision is needed and no person can answer. | Run with no TTY and no `--yes`. |
| `install.locked` | The install lock is held for more than 30 s. | Hold the lock. |
| `install.io` | A file operation failed. | Make the store read-only. |
| `install.no-space` | Too little free space before writing. | Fill the volume. |
| `install.compile-failed` | The component could not be compiled. | Install a component with invalid code. |
| `install.not-installed` | `update` was used for an id that is not installed. | Update an unknown id. |
| `install.already-installed` | Warning: same id, version and manifest hash. | See LIF-072. |
| `package.version-reused` | Same id and version, different manifest hash. | See LIF-072. |
| `install.registry-format` | The registry format is newer than the host. | See LIF-067. |
| `install.state-corrupt` | `installed.json` does not match its schema. | See LIF-282. |
| `install.notify-failed` | A running server could not be told. | Remove the socket of a server. |
| `install.no-previous` | There is no earlier version for a rollback. | Roll back a first install. |
| `migration.data-newer` | The data is newer than the target supports. | See LIF-079. |
| `migration.interrupted` | The migration was interrupted twice. | See LIF-110. |
| `rollback.no-backup` | The pre-update snapshot is gone. | See LIF-080. |
| `update.rolled-back` | Warning: the candidate failed and the host returned. | See LIF-075. |

### Edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Install of a package while the user edits grants in Settings | The install waits on the lock for the registry, up to 30 s. |
| Install of an id that exists in the store but not in the registry | Treated as a new install; the old store entry is replaced. |
| Update to a version that the policy blocks | `policy.blocked`, nothing changes. |
| Rollback with no previous version | `install.no-previous`, exit code 5. |
| Uninstall of the plugin that provides a service others require | The consumers stay active and get `not-found`. The CLI prints a `warning` per dependant. |
| Disk full during step 3 or step 5 | `install.no-space` before writing, or `install.io` during it. The staging directory is removed. See [offline and low disk](/pages/reference-offline-and-low-disk/). |

### What the user sees

A successful install adds the plugin to Settings > Plugins. A failed install prints its errors and runs no plugin code. A rolled-back update shows the toast `Update failed, rolled back` and keeps the old version. The screens are described in [Managing plugins](/pages/user-managing-plugins/).

### See also

- [Plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/)
- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)
- [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/)
- [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/)
- [Security model](/pages/security/)
- [Plugin scope and sessions](/pages/reference-plugin-scope-and-sessions/)
- [Requirements, lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/)

# Kernel and boot reference

## Kernel and boot reference

This page states what stays in the Ilium kernel when every feature becomes a core plugin, in which order the server and the client start, which core plugin starts at boot and which starts on first use, and what the user keeps when a core plugin is disabled, replaced or crashes. It also lists the environment variables of the platform and says which changes apply live and which need a restart.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. The platform is not implemented. This page is the specification that the implementation and its tests follow. Requirement ids have the form `[COR-nnn]` and are collected in [Core plugin parity requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-core-parity/).

<div class="note">
<p>The word <strong>kernel</strong> means the Ilium code that is not a plugin: the server and client crates, the tree, the terminal engine, the settings store and the plugin host. The word <strong>core plugin</strong> means one of the 30 first-party plugins in the table of <a href="/pages/core-plugins/">Core plugins</a>. A core plugin is bundled, has tier T1 and an id that starts with <code>ilium.core.</code>.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- What stays in the kernel
- Server boot order
- Client boot order
- The CLI-only transient host
- Startup and lazy activation of the 30 core plugins
- The minimum kernel
- Safe start
- What the user keeps when a plugin is off
- Replaceable and disableable
- Scene world and extension points
- Environment variables
- Live reload and restart
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### What stays in the kernel

A feature moves into a plugin only when the kernel can still run, draw a frame and save a session without it. The table lists the parts that never move, with the reason. Everything not listed here is a core plugin or part of one.

| Kernel part | Why it stays | What a plugin gets instead |
|---|---|---|
| PTY spawn, the `vt100` screen model, resize and mouse encoding | A plugin cannot own a file descriptor. The terminal must work with no plugin. | Reads through `terminal.read-screen`, `terminal.read-cells`, `terminal.history`. Writes through `terminal.write` and `terminal.raw-input` |
| The tree model: nodes, groups, panes, ids, undo of structure changes | Every plugin refers to node ids, and a wrong tree breaks every consumer | `tree.read`, `tree.write`, `tree.metadata`, `tree.decorate`, `tree.restructure` |
| IPC, framing, the transport and the version handshake | The plugin host itself rides on them | Typed records in `ilium-ipc` |
| Session snapshot writer, atomic restore and the final snapshot | Crash safety. A failed plugin must not lose a session | The `snapshot-sections` point of `ilium.core.sessions`, where a plugin adds a section with a `schema_version` |
| `config.toml` and `.ilium/config.yaml`: parse, validate, atomic write, defaults | One reader and one writer keep the files valid | `settings` for a plugin's own values, `kernel-settings` for kernel tabs, `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` for the one owner of a tab |
| The settings store and the 25 kernel tab ids | Frozen ids are the contract (see [kernel settings and keymap](/pages/api-kernel-settings-and-keymap/)) | The Settings plugin draws the screen. Each tab has one owner plugin |
| The keymap: chord parser, resolver, user remaps, the kernel commands | A broken binding must never lock the user out | `keymap.read`, `contributes.keybindings`, `keys.intercept` |
| Layout solver, compositor, frame diff, `ratatui` rendering, the theme | One frame budget, one theme | `ui` trees (retained mode), `ui.panels`, `ui.chrome` |
| Animation look application, dithering and cell painting | The look is global and applies after the scene draws | Scenes draw tone into a raster. The Ambient look plugin owns the controls |
| The scene host, cached loops and frame pacing | Frame pacing cannot wait for a plugin | Scene components in the animation world |
| The plugin host: package store, manifest checks, grants, trust, policy, quotas, the restart rule | A plugin cannot police itself | `plugins.manage` for the Plugins screen (T1 only) |
| The kernel recovery page and the command `kernel.open-recovery` | It must work with every plugin off | None. A plugin cannot remove it |
| The loopback HTTP listener on the configured API port (default 8872) | One process binds one socket, and the bind must not fail because a plugin is off | `http-api.route` lets a plugin register routes (see below) |
| Process and OS facts: process tree, runtime dirs, locks, secure files (`ilium-platform`) | Only one crate reaches the operating system | Imports such as `process`, `fs` and `clock` |
| CLI parsing of kernel commands: attach, `new-session`, `ls`, `kill-session`, `new-pane`, `plugin` | The user needs a way to reach a broken session | `contributes.cli` for every other command |

The HTTP listener is a kernel part because the port setting, the bind and the loopback rule belong to one owner. The Fleet plugin registers the route `POST /create_agent` with the grant `http-api.route:/create_agent`. If Fleet is off, the kernel answers `404` with `{"code":"not-found"}` for that path and keeps the socket open. See [HTTP API](/pages/api-http-api/).

### Server boot order

The server start in [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/) has eight steps. This table adds the kernel parts that those steps refer to and the core plugins that take part. The restore always happens before any plugin exists, so no plugin sees the restore as a series of events.

| Step | Owner | What happens | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kernel | Resolve runtime, config and data folders. Take the session lock. Read `config.toml` and `.ilium/config.yaml` | A file that fails to parse is moved aside as `config.toml.broken-<timestamp>` and defaults are used. The recovery page shows the message |
| 2 | Kernel | Restore the snapshot into the tree. Plugin sections stay as stored JSON. No plugin runs | A snapshot that fails to parse is moved aside the same way, and the session starts with one empty shell pane |
| 3 | Kernel | Apply the start flags `--no-plugins` and `--safe-plugins` and their environment variables | Both given: `--no-plugins` wins |
| 4 | Plugin host | Create the Engine, verify packages, register static contributions, build the service graph | A plugin that fails verification stays off. The others continue |
| 5 | Plugin host | Activate every server side whose `activation` contains `startup`, in dependency order | A failure counts for the restart rule |
| 6 | Plugin host | Deliver one `tree-changed` batch for the restored tree to each activated plugin that subscribes | None |
| 7 | Plugin host | Hand each plugin its stored snapshot section through the `snapshot-sections` point (see [the config migration page](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/#snapshot-sections)) | A section with an unknown `schema_version` is kept unchanged and the plugin is told `section-unsupported` |
| 8 | Kernel | Bind the IPC socket and accept clients. The HTTP listener binds here, and routes appear as their plugins register them | A client that connects early gets the retriable error `server.starting` |

[COR-020] has the order as a testable rule.

### Client boot order

| Step | Owner | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Client kernel | Enter the alternate screen, read the theme and the keymap, connect to the socket, complete the handshake |
| 2 | Client kernel | Receive the tree, the pane viewports and the retained contribution replica |
| 3 | Client kernel | Draw the first frame with kernel chrome only. The tree uses its kernel rows (name and status glyph) until `ilium.core.tree` has drawn |
| 4 | Plugin host | Activate every client side with the `startup` trigger, in dependency order. The core plugins in this group are Tree, Settings, Ambient look, Agent toolbar, Terminal and Keys and help |
| 5 | Client kernel | Redraw with the plugin contributions. A plugin that is slow keeps its previous frame, and the client never waits for a plugin to draw |
| 6 | Plugin host | Activate other plugins when their trigger fires |

`startup` on a client side means the client host starts, and on a server side it means the server host starts. The same word is therefore used on both sides and starts only the side that declares it. See [Activation triggers](/pages/reference-manifest/#activation-triggers).

### The CLI-only transient host

A command from a plugin that declares `requires_server: false` can run with no session. The `ilium` process then creates a transient host. The rules:

- The transient host loads only the plugin that owns the command and the services that plugin `requires` (HST-019). It never activates another core plugin.
- Imports that need a session (`tree`, `panes` of the local session, `terminal`) return `unavailable` with the message `no session`. The command decides how to report that.
- Commands that look across sessions (`ilium panes`, `ilium broadcast`, `ilium recap`) list live sockets with `sessions.cross` and talk to each running server themselves. They do not need a local session.
- The transient host starts no server, takes no session lock and writes no snapshot.
- The host exits when the command finishes. Its time to first plugin call has the budget `CLI-COLD` in the performance budgets of the host.

The commands that work this way are `ilium panes`, `ilium broadcast`, `ilium recap` and `ilium voice say` (the last one only for its argument check). `ilium chat`, `ilium progress` and `ilium wait` need the session of the pane they run in and use the socket from `ILIUM_SESSION_SOCKET`. They set `requires_server: true`.

### Startup and lazy activation of the 30 core plugins

A plugin that starts at boot costs time in every session. A plugin that starts on first use costs time at the first use. The rule used here: a plugin starts at boot only when it must see events from the first moment, must be present on the first frame, or must restore state that outlives the process. Everything else is lazy. The Plugins screen shows the column **Starts** with `at boot` or `on use`.

| Core plugin | Server side | Client side | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent detect | `startup` | `view:agent-detect.panel` | Detection needs every screen update from the start |
| Agent setup | `settings:setup`, `command:refresh`, `service:install` | `settings:setup` | Used when the user opens Setup |
| Agent toolbar | `event:agent-state-changed` | `startup` | Buttons are on the first frame |
| Ambient look | none | `startup` | The look is applied from the first frame |
| Chatroom | `startup` | `topic:chatroom` | File watch for `CHATROOM.md` and hook text must work without a client |
| Compaction | `event:agent-context-low`, `service:compact` | `view:compaction.optimizer` | Runs when an agent needs it |
| Cost | `startup` | `view:cost.panel` | Usage accrues from transcripts while nobody looks |
| Diagnostics | `startup` | `view:diagnostics.warnings` | Collects warnings from the first line of the log |
| Editor | none | `pane-kind:editor` | Native in v1 (see D4). In plugin form it starts when a file opens |
| Fleet | `cli:panes`, `cli:broadcast`, `http:/create_agent`, `service:broadcast` | `command:ask-for-update` | Used on demand |
| Inference | `service:ilium:inference/provider` | none | Starts when a consumer calls it |
| Kanban | none | `pane-kind:kanban` | Native in v1. In plugin form it starts with a board pane |
| Keys and help | none | `command:keys-and-help.open`, `settings:keyboard` | Used on demand. Bindings work without it |
| Layout | `command:layout.preset` | `view:layout.presets` | Used on demand. The kernel keeps the geometry |
| Notifications | `startup` | none | Must catch the first state change |
| Progress | `startup` | `startup` | Monitors are restored from storage and run without a client |
| Recap | `cli:recap`, `command:recap` | none | Used on demand |
| Scenes | none | `scene:*` | Starts when a scene is selected (scene side only) |
| Scheduler | `startup` | `view:scheduler.queue` | Due timers must fire after a restart |
| Search | `command:search`, `job:index` | `view:search.panel` | Used on demand |
| Session convert | `command:convert`, `service:convert` | `view:session-convert.progress` | Used on demand |
| Sessions | `startup` | `view:sessions.list` | Offers the snapshot sections to the kernel writer |
| Settings | none | `startup` | The Settings screen frame and the guided setup |
| Smart copy | `service:copy` | `command:smart-copy` | Starts on the copy gesture |
| Terminal | `event:terminal-screen-changed` | `startup` | Links and the context menu need the first frame |
| Text triggers | `startup` | `view:text-triggers.rules` | The output filter must be in place before the first byte |
| Titles | `startup` | none | Triggers fire on agent events from the start |
| Tree | `startup` | `startup` | Rows, bookmarks and locks are on the first frame |
| Voice | `command:voice.toggle`, `cli:voice` | `command:voice.toggle` | The key F8 is a keybinding that fires the command, which starts the plugin |
| Worktrees | `command:new-agent`, `service:create` | none | Used on demand. `new-pane --worktree` calls the service |

[COR-020] and [COR-021] state the rules that make this table testable: the plugins marked `startup` appear in the activated list at boot, and the others do not appear until their trigger fires.

### The minimum kernel

The command `ilium --no-plugins` (or `ILIUM_NO_PLUGINS=1`) starts a session with the kernel only. The minimum the user must have is:

- terminal panes that run a shell, with input, output, scrolling, copy and resize;
- the tree with kernel rows (the node name and a status glyph), and new, close and rename;
- the layout geometry that was last saved;
- the default keymap, and the kernel commands `kernel.open-recovery`, `kernel.quit`, `kernel.detach`;
- the settings store, with the recovery page as the only Settings screen;
- the session snapshot writer.

<figure><pre class="term">╭─ ilium --no-plugins ─────────────────────────╮
│ Session: default   plugins: off              │
│                                              │
│ Pane 1  shell ………………………………………………………… running │
│                                              │
│ <span class="t-hi">Ctrl+Alt+R</span> recovery page                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre><figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The kernel frame with no plugin: one shell pane, a plain row and the key for the recovery page. There are no agent states, no cost, no toolbar and no animation.</figcaption></figure>

<figure><pre class="term">╭─ Recovery ───────────────────────────────────╮
│ Core plugins            <span class="t-dim">state</span>                │
│ ilium.core.fleet …………………………… off (3 crashes) │
│ ilium.core.tree ………………………………………………………………… on │
│ ilium.core.settings ……………………………………………………… on │
│                                              │
