# Plugin files on disk

## Plugin files on disk

This page lists every file and folder that the plugin platform creates, where it lives on Linux, macOS and Windows, what format it has, who writes it and what removes it. It is the one table that the user pages, the administration guide and the troubleshooting page point to. A host implementer uses it to place files. A test author uses it to check what an install, a grant change or an uninstall left behind.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[USR-nnn]` and are collected in [User and administrator requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-user-admin/).

<div class="note">
<p>Decision status. The platform is not implemented. Folder and file names below are the proposed layout. They are marked normative here so that tests can be written, and the platform owner may still rename a file. Names that other pages already use, such as <code>installed.json</code> and <code>plugins/staging/</code>, are kept.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- How paths are chosen
- The table of items
- The plugin log
- File permissions
- What each action leaves behind
- Back up and move plugins to another machine
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### How paths are chosen

Ilium never writes a hard-coded `~`. It asks the operating system for three roots through the `directories` crate, with the project name `ilium` and no organisation. The roots are the configuration folder, the data folder and the cache folder.

| Root | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Configuration (`<config>`) | `~/.config/ilium` | `~/Library/Application Support/ilium` | `%APPDATA%\ilium\config` |
| Data (`<data>`) | `~/.local/share/ilium` | `~/Library/Application Support/ilium` | `%APPDATA%\ilium\data` |
| Cache (`<cache>`) | `~/.cache/ilium` | `~/Library/Caches/ilium` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ilium\cache` |

On Linux the roots follow `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` when they are set. The rest of this page writes `<config>`, `<data>` and `<cache>` and never repeats the system paths. A project folder (`<project>`) is the canonical launch folder of a session. Project-scope files live in `<project>/.ilium/`.

- [USR-200] The host MUST resolve `<config>`, `<data>` and `<cache>` with the `directories` crate for the project name `ilium`, and MUST NOT write plugin files anywhere else. Test: start Ilium with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` pointing at three empty folders, install a plugin, and assert that no plugin file appears outside those folders and the project's `.ilium` folder.

### The table of items

Paths start at `<config>`, `<data>`, `<cache>` or `<project>`. The plugin root is `<data>/plugins/`. The layout of the plugin root is owned by [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/); this table repeats it for users and adds the user-facing files.

| Item | Location | Format | Written by | Removed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry (which plugins exist, versions, enabled flags) | `<data>/plugins/installed.json` | JSON | Install, update, enable, disable, uninstall | Uninstall edits it. Nothing deletes the file |
| Registry lock | `<data>/plugins/installed.lock` | Exclusive OS advisory lock on this file; the file also holds the holder's process id and boot id for messages | Every command that changes the registry | The lock is released when the holder exits |
| Installed packages | `<data>/plugins/store/<id>/<version>/` | `manifest.json`, `manifest.sha256`, components, files | Install, update | Uninstall. An update removes the old version after the swap |
| Unpacking area | `<data>/plugins/staging/<uuid>/` | Same as a package | Install, update | The rename into the store, a failed operation, or the next start (older than 1 hour or its process is gone) |
| Pre-migration copies | `<data>/plugins/backups/<id>/<version>-<utc timestamp>/` | Copy of data and buckets | Update with a data migration | The next committed update keeps only the newest; `uninstall --purge` deletes them |
| Plugin data | `<data>/plugins/data/<id>/` | Whatever the plugin writes | The plugin, through `fs.write:data` | `uninstall --purge`, or Delete data in the uninstall dialog |
| Global storage bucket | `<data>/plugins/storage/<id>/global.db` | Key-value database | The plugin, through `storage` | Same as plugin data |
| Project and session buckets | Inside `<project>/.ilium/` and the session snapshot `<project>/.ilium/sessions/<session>.json` | Database and JSON | The plugin and the host | Same as plugin data, for the open project and session. Other projects get a tombstone |
| Grants and consent answers | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/grants.json` and `consents.json` (one file each for all plugins) | JSON | Review dialog, Capabilities tab, `ilium plugin grants`, first-use prompts | Every uninstall |
| Trusted publisher keys | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/trust.json`, or the path in `ILIUM_TRUST_STORE` | JSON list of `{publisher, fingerprint, public_key, added_at}` | `ilium plugin trust add` and the trust prompt | `ilium plugin trust remove` |
| Plugin settings, user scope | `<config>/config.toml`, table `[plugins."<id>"]` | TOML | The Settings screen | `uninstall --purge`, Forget settings |
| Plugin settings, project scope | `<project>/.ilium/config.yaml`, key `plugins.<id>` | YAML | The Settings screen | Same two actions, for the open project |
| Plugin limits | `<config>/config.toml`, table `[plugins.limits]` | TOML | The user | The user |
| Plugin cache | `<cache>/plugins/<id>/` | Whatever the plugin writes | The plugin, through `fs.write:cache` | The host may evict it at any time. Every uninstall removes it |
| Compile cache | `<cache>/plugins/compile/` | Compiled components | Install of a T2 or T3 plugin | The host, when space is low |
| Plugin log | `<data>/plugins/logs/<id>.log` and rotated files | Text, four columns | The plugin and the host | Rotation. See below |
| User extension order and toggles | `<config>/config.toml`, table `[plugins.extensions]` | TOML | The Extensions tab | Every uninstall of the owner |
| Replacement record | `<config>/config.toml`, table `[plugins.replaces]` | TOML | The replace confirmation | Undoing the replacement |
| Administrator policy | See [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) | TOML | The administrator | The administrator |
| Audit log | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/audit/audit.jsonl` (see [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/)) | JSON lines | The host | Rotation by `audit.max_mib` and `audit.keep_days` |

The two last settings-adjacent tables, `[plugins.extensions]` and `[plugins.replaces]`, are proposed names that the owner of [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) confirms.

- [USR-201] The host MUST keep each item at the location in the table, and MUST create the parent folders on first use. Test: on a clean profile, run install, grant, trust add, enable, disable and uninstall, then list the folders and match each file against the table.
- [USR-202] The host MUST write `installed.json`, the grant files and the trust store atomically: it writes a temporary sibling file, flushes it and renames it over the target. Test: kill the process during a grant change and assert that the file holds either the old or the new content, never a mix.
- [USR-203] Grants MUST be stored per user and per plugin, and MUST NOT be stored in a project folder. Test: grant `fs.read:project` while a project is open, open a second project and assert that the grant applies there and that `<project>/.ilium/` holds no grant.

### Contents of the user-facing files

The grant file has one entry per side. A grant value is `granted`, `declined` or `revoked`. A grant that the manifest never requested has no entry. Consent answers for the prompts that are not grants sit in the same file.

```json
{
  "server": { "tree.read": "granted", "http:api.example.com": "declined" },
  "client": { "ui.panels": "granted" },
  "consent": {
    "open_external": ["https://status.example.com"],
    "http_hosts": ["api.example.com"],
    "location_geocode": true,
    "first_start_not_now": 1
  }
}
```

`first_start_not_now` counts how often the user chose Not now at the first-start prompt of a bundled plugin. See [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/#first-start-of-a-bundled-plugin).

The fingerprint of a key is shown as 32 uppercase hexadecimal characters in 8 groups of 4 separated by `-` (see the CLI reference). The short form in dialogs shows the first 4 and the last 4 characters joined by an ellipsis, for example `3F2A…9C01`.

### The plugin log

Each plugin has one log, shared by all its sides. The host writes refusals, traps, restarts and process runs into it, and the plugin writes its own lines through the `log` import. See [log](/pages/api-log/).

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| File | `<data>/plugins/logs/<id>.log`, with rotated files `<id>.log.1` to `<id>.log.3` |
| Line format | Four columns: local timestamp `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, level padded to five characters, plugin id, message |
| Rotation | When the file passes 1 MiB it becomes `.1`, `.1` becomes `.2`, `.2` becomes `.3`, and the old `.3` is deleted |
| Retention | At most 4 files per plugin. Rotated files older than 14 days are deleted at server start |
| Rate limit | 200 lines per second for a standard plugin. Extra lines are dropped and counted in one `warn` summary line |
| Who can read it | The user who owns the folder. A plugin cannot read its own log |
| After uninstall | Kept for 7 days, then deleted. `--purge` deletes it at once |

- [USR-204] The host MUST rotate the log at 1 MiB, MUST keep at most three rotated files, and MUST delete rotated files older than 14 days at server start. Test: write 5 MiB of log lines through a test plugin and list the folder; then age `<id>.log.2` by 15 days, restart, and assert it is gone.
- [USR-205] Each log line MUST have the four columns timestamp, level, plugin id and message, with the timestamp in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`. Test: read the log and match every line against the pattern.

### File permissions

On Linux and macOS, every folder under the plugin roots has mode `0700` and every file has mode `0600`. On Windows the host sets an access list that allows only the current user. A package that ships files with other modes does not change this: the host extracts files with the modes above.

- [USR-206] The host MUST create plugin folders with owner-only access and plugin files with owner-only read and write access. Test: after an install, run `stat` on every created path and assert mode `0700` for folders and `0600` for files on Linux.
- [USR-207] The host MUST refuse to read a grant file or the trust store when another user can write to it, and MUST treat every third-party plugin as not allowed to run until the file is fixed. Test: set the mode of a grant file to `0666`, start Ilium, and assert that T2 and T3 plugins are refused at load with the code `grants.unsafe-permissions` while core plugins still run.

### What each action leaves behind

The default uninstall, `--purge` and `--keep-data` are specified in the table of [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/#uninstall). The rows that matter to a user:

| Action | Package | Grants | Settings | Data, storage | Cache | Extensions order | Log | Trusted keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disable | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| Uninstall, default | removed | removed | kept | kept when there is no terminal, otherwise asked | removed | removed | kept 7 days | kept |
| Uninstall `--purge` | removed | removed | removed | removed | removed | removed | removed | kept |
| Uninstall `--keep-data` | removed | removed | kept | kept | removed | removed | kept 7 days | kept |
| Forget settings (recovery page) | kept | kept | removed | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| `trust remove` | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | key removed |

Trust entries are never removed by an uninstall, because one key may sign several plugins. After `trust remove`, plugins signed with that key stay installed and show `untrusted` in `ilium plugin list`.

- [USR-208] A default uninstall MUST remove the package, the grants, the cache and the Extensions order entries, and MUST keep settings. Test: install a plugin, write one setting, uninstall with no flag, and list what remains.
- [USR-209] `--purge` MUST also remove settings, data, storage buckets and the log, and `--keep-data` MUST keep data and storage without asking. The two flags exclude each other. Test: run each flag on a copy of the same profile and compare the remains with the table.

### Back up and move plugins to another machine

Copy these items, in this order, with Ilium stopped:

1. `<data>/plugins/store/` and `<data>/plugins/installed.json`, so the same versions install again.
2. The trust store `trust.json`, so signed packages are still trusted.
3. `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/grants.json` and `consents.json`, if you want the same answers. Skip it to be asked again on the new machine.
4. `<config>/config.toml` and the `.ilium` folders of your projects, for settings.
5. `<data>/plugins/data/` and `<data>/plugins/storage/`, for the plugin's own data.

Skip the cache, the logs, the staging folder and the backups. A machine that runs a different operating system cannot run T2 and T3 plugins unless it is Linux (see [Plugins overview](/pages/user-plugins-overview/)). Core and bundled plugins need no copy, because they ship with Ilium.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| `installed.json` is missing | The host treats the profile as empty and starts with core plugins only. Packages in `store/` stay on disk and are not listed. `ilium plugin reinstall <id>` repairs a store entry from the cached package |
| `installed.json` does not parse | The host starts with core plugins only, writes one error to the Ilium log, and opens the recovery page. It does not overwrite the file |
| A grant file does not parse | The file is renamed to `grants.json.corrupt-<YYYYMMDD-HHmmss>` and the server logs `grants.unreadable`. T2 and T3 plugins start as not installed with no grants; T1 plugins start with only normal grants ([HST-044]) |
| A package folder is missing but the registry lists it | The plugin is refused at load with the code `package.corrupt` |
| The disk is full during a write | The action stops, the old file stays, and the error is `install.io` or `io` |
| Two Ilium servers share one profile | Each write takes `installed.lock`. The second writer waits up to 5 s, then fails the action with `conflict` |

- [Plugin privacy](/pages/user-privacy/)
- [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/)
- [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/)
- [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/)

# Reference, plugin lifecycle states

## Reference, plugin lifecycle states

This page is the closed state model of a plugin. It lists every state a plugin package and a plugin instance can be in, every transition between states, the guard that allows it, what the host does in order, and what the user and other plugins see. A host that implements these tables has no state that this page does not name. A test author can derive one test per row.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[LIF-nnn]`. They are collected in [Requirements, lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/). Failure counting and restart delays are defined once, in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/). This page refers to them and does not repeat the numbers.

### Two state machines

A plugin has two layers of state.

- The package state is stored on disk. It says whether the plugin is installed, whether it may run, and why not. It survives a server restart and a reboot.
- The instance state is held in memory, once per side and per world. It says whether code is running now. A side is `server`, `client` or `scene`. The server side has one instance per session server. The client and scene sides have one instance per attached client.

A package state decides which instance states are allowed. An instance can be `active` only while its side is allowed to run.

### Package states

| State | Stored where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `not-installed` | no record | The id has no entry in the installed registry. |
| `installed-enabled` | `installed.json`, `state` | The package is installed and the user allows it to run. |
| `installed-disabled-by-user` | `installed.json`, `state` | The user, the CLI or `plugins.set-enabled` turned it off. |
| `disabled-untrusted` | `installed.json`, `state` | The signing key was removed from the trust store with `trust remove --force`. The files, grants and settings stay. It leaves this state when the key is trusted again, or with `enable <id> --accept-risk`. |
| `disabled-blocked` | `installed.json`, `state` | The signing key was revoked as `compromised`, or a registry takedown named this version. It leaves this state only with `enable <id> --accept-risk`, or with an update signed by another trusted key of the same publisher. |
| `disabled-by-policy` | policy file, or the start flags | An administrator rule or safe mode forbids it for this run. Not written to `installed.json`. |
| `refused-at-load` | recomputed at every load | The host checked the package and refused to run it. The reason is a code, for example `package.api-unsupported`, `trust.key-revoked`, `policy.tier-denied`, `package.corrupt` or `policy.blocked`. |
| `update-staged` | `plugins/staging/` | A newer version is unpacked and verified, and the swap has not happened. |
| `uninstall-pending` | `installed.json`, `state` | The user asked for removal and an instance is still stopping. |

Rules for package states:

- [LIF-001] The host MUST give every installed plugin exactly one package state at any time. Test: list a plugin through every transition below and assert one state in `ilium plugin list --json`.
- [LIF-002] A stop by failure belongs to one side, not to the package. It is the instance state `stopped-by-failure` of that side, and the package state stays `installed-enabled`. A stop of the client side MUST NOT stop the server side. Test: trap the client side three times and assert the server side stays `active`.
- [LIF-003] A package with state `refused-at-load` MUST NOT be instantiated, and the refusal code MUST be shown in `disabled-reason`. Test: install a package whose api window the host does not support and read the list output.
- [LIF-004] `disabled-by-policy` and safe mode MUST NOT be written to `installed.json`. Test: start in safe mode, stop, start normally and assert the plugin is `installed-enabled` again.

### Instance states

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inactive` | The side is allowed to run and has no instance. It waits for a trigger, or for host capacity. |
| `activating` | The instance exists and `activate` is running. The activate deadline applies. |
| `waiting-dependency` | The side is allowed to run, but a required plugin or the provider of a required service is not `active`. It leaves to `activating` when every requirement is `active`, or to `inactive` with the refusal `dependency.unresolved` shown in the row after `wait_ms` ([PKG-326](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/)). A wait is not a failure. |
| `active` | `activate` returned `ok`. The host calls the other exports. |
| `deactivating` | `deactivate(reason)` is running. The deactivate deadline applies. |
| `failed` | A counted failure just dropped the instance. The state lasts only until the host picks `restart-scheduled` or `stopped`. It is visible in events and logs, not in lists. |
| `restart-scheduled` | The instance was dropped after a failure and a timer will activate it again. The record carries the due time `restart-at`. |
| `stopped-by-failure` | The third counted failure in a window stopped this side. No restart is scheduled. The server side is stored in `installed.json` as `failure_stopped: ["server"]`. A client or scene side is held only in memory and is dropped when its client detaches. See [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart). |
| `stopped` | The side may not run now. The package state says why. |

- [LIF-005] An instance MUST be in exactly one instance state, and only the transitions in the tables below MAY occur. Test: a state-machine fuzz test drives random triggers and asserts every observed transition is in the table.
- [LIF-006] The host MUST NOT call `handler`, `views`, `renderer` or provider exports on an instance that is not `active`. Test: send an event to an instance in `activating` and assert it is queued, and an event to `stopped` is dropped.

### Package-state transitions

The trigger column names who or what causes the change. The effect column is what a user sees. Event names are defined in the section after the tables.

| Row | From | Trigger | Guard | Host actions, in order | Events and log | User-visible effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `not-installed` | `ilium plugin install` | all install checks pass | Run the install pipeline. Write the registry entry. Set state. | `plugin-state-changed`, log `install.ok` | Plugin appears in Settings > Plugins |
| P2 | `installed-enabled` | disable | none | Record the desired state. For every side: run I9. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `user` | Switch off, contributions withdrawn |
| P3 | `installed-disabled-by-user` | enable | not refused, not blocked by policy | Record the desired state. Clear the failure windows. Activate per trigger rules. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `user` | Switch on |
| P4 | `installed-enabled` | third counted failure | side-specific | Drop the instance. Do not schedule a restart. Set the side `stopped-by-failure`. The package state does not change. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `failure`, log `failure.disabled` | Footer notice, red mark in the list |
| P5 | `installed-enabled` | enable, reset-failures or update | a side is `stopped-by-failure` | Clear the failure window. Set the side `inactive`. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `user` or `update` | Notice cleared |
| P6 | `installed-enabled` | policy file lists the id or version | policy loaded | Stop all sides. Set the overlay. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `policy`, log `policy.blocked` | Row shows `Blocked by policy` |
| P7 | any installed state | package check fails at load | API window, tier, signature, hash, trust, policy | Refuse. Keep the files. | log `load.refused` with the code | Row shows the code and the fix |
| P8 | `installed-enabled` | update downloaded and verified | install pipeline step 6 committed | Keep the candidate in `store/<id>/<version>/` beside the active version, with `update.state: staged` | `plugin-state-changed` reason `update` | none until the swap |
| P9 | `update-staged` | swap | the first `activate` of the candidate returns `ok` on the server side | Run data migration. Activate. Set `active_version` to the candidate. | log `update.ok` | New version shown |
| P10 | `update-staged` | swap | the first `activate` fails, traps or misses its deadline | Roll back at once to the previous version and its pre-update data snapshot. Mark the candidate `skip`. Do not count the failure. | log `update.rolled-back` | Toast: `Update failed, rolled back` |
| P11 | any installed state | uninstall | no uninstall already pending | Set `uninstall-pending`. Stop all sides. Remove files. | log `uninstall.ok` | Plugin disappears |
| P12 | `uninstall-pending` | server start after a crash | files still present | Finish the uninstall | log `uninstall.recovered` | none |
| P13 | `installed-enabled` | `trust remove <key_id> --force` | the key signed this plugin | Stop all sides. Record `state`. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `policy`, log `trust.removed` | Row shows `Untrusted`, with a badge |
| P14 | `disabled-untrusted` | the key is trusted again, or `enable --accept-risk` | none | Record `installed-enabled`. Clear the failure windows. Activate per trigger rules. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `user` | Switch on |
| P15 | any installed state | key revoked as `compromised`, or registry takedown of this version | none | Stop all sides. Record `disabled-blocked` and the reason. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `policy`, log `trust.key-revoked` or `registry.takedown` | Row shows `Blocked`, with the reason |
| P16 | `disabled-blocked` | `enable --accept-risk`, or an update signed by another trusted key of the same publisher | none | Record `installed-enabled`. Clear the failure windows. | `plugin-state-changed` reason `user` or `update` | Switch on |

- [LIF-007] Enabling a plugin that is `refused-at-load` or `disabled-by-policy` MUST return `not-permitted` with the refusal code in the message, and MUST NOT change any state. Test: call `set-enabled(id, true)` on a policy-blocked plugin.
- [LIF-008] A failure that moves the server side to `stopped-by-failure` MUST be written to `failure_stopped` in `installed.json`, so it survives a server restart. A client or scene side is not stored. Test: cause three failures, restart the server and read the list output.
- [LIF-009] Enabling, resetting failures or installing an update MUST clear the failure window of the sides it affects. Test: two failures, then enable, then one failure restarts after the first-failure delay.
- [LIF-010] A candidate whose first `activate` fails MUST roll back to the previous version, as P10 says, and MUST NOT leave the plugin in `update-staged`. A failure after a successful first activation MUST NOT roll back. Test: stage a version whose `activate` always errors and assert the old version is active.
- [LIF-283] The package states `disabled-untrusted` and `disabled-blocked` MUST follow rows P13 to P16, MUST be stored in `installed.json` and MUST survive a restart. A plugin in either state MUST NOT run, and MUST keep its grants, settings and data. Test: remove the signing key with `--force`, restart the server and assert `disabled-untrusted`; revoke a key as `compromised` and assert `disabled-blocked`; leave each state by the stated way.

### Instance-state transitions

| Row | From | Trigger | Guard | Host actions, in order | Deactivate reason | Events and log | User-visible effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | `inactive` | activation trigger fires | pool memory available, concurrency cap not reached | Create the instance. Call `activate`. | none | log `activate.begin` | none |
| I2 | `inactive` | activation trigger fires | pool memory full | Stay `inactive` with reason `host-capacity`. Retry on release, and after 1 s, 5 s and 30 s, then every 60 s without end while the plugin is enabled ([LIF-034](/pages/lifecycle/)). | none | log `activate.deferred` | Row shows `waiting for memory` |
| I3 | `activating` | `activate` returns `ok` | within deadline | Mark `active`. Flush queued events. | none | `plugin-state-changed`, log `activate.ok` | none |
| I4 | `activating` | `activate` errors, traps or misses its deadline | none | Drop the instance. Count one failure. Run I6 or I7. | none | log `failure.counted` | none, or notice on the third |
| I5 | `active` | trap, deadline breach, queue overflow or memory limit | none | Drop the instance. Withdraw dynamic contributions. Keep decorations, marked stale. Cancel pending requests. Count one failure. | none | log `failure.counted` | Decorations shown stale |
| I6 | `failed` | counted failure number 1 or 2 | not stopping | Schedule the restart timer. | none | log `restart.scheduled` with the delay | Row shows `restarting` |
| I7 | `failed` | counted failure number 3 in the window | none | Set the side `stopped-by-failure`. Run P4. | none | log `failure.disabled` | Footer notice |
| I8 | `restart-scheduled` | timer fires | side still allowed, server not stopping | Run I1. | none | log `restart.begin` | none |
| I9 | `active` | disable | none | Stop accepting calls. Call `deactivate(disabled)`. Withdraw contributions. Release locks. Cancel requests. | `disabled` | log `deactivate.ok` | Row dim |
| I10 | `active` | server stop begins | none | Call `deactivate(shutdown)` in reverse start order. Store the bytes. | `shutdown` | log `deactivate.ok` | none |
| I11 | `active` | client detaches | side is `client` or `scene` | Call `deactivate(shutdown)`. Send the bytes to the server if the link is up. | `shutdown` | log `deactivate.ok` | none |
| I12 | `active` | update swap or dev reload | none | Call `deactivate(upgrade)`. Then run I1 for the new build. | `upgrade` | log `deactivate.ok` | none |
| I13 | `active` | grant revoked or granted | none | Bump the authorization epoch. Call `deactivate(revoked)` or `deactivate(granted)`. Run I1 with the new `granted` list. | `revoked` or `granted` | `plugin-state-changed` | none |
| I14 | `restart-scheduled` | disable, update or uninstall | none | Cancel the timer. No `deactivate` call, there is no instance. | none | log `restart.cancelled` | none |
| I15 | any | `deactivate` misses its deadline | none | Drop the instance. Discard the bytes. | as sent | log `deactivate.deadline` | none |
| I16 | `inactive` | activation trigger fires | a required plugin, or the provider of a required service, is not `active` | Set `waiting-dependency`. Start the wait of `wait_ms` per provider. Activate the missing requirement if it is lazy. | none | log `activate.waiting` | Row shows `waiting for <name>` |
| I17 | `waiting-dependency` | every requirement is `active` | none | Run I1. | none | log `activate.begin` | none |
| I18 | `waiting-dependency` | `wait_ms` runs out | none | Set `inactive` with the reason `dependency.unresolved`. Retry when a requirement becomes `active`, and after 1 s, 5 s and 30 s, then every 60 s without end while the plugin is enabled. | none | log `activate.wait-expired` | Row keeps `waiting for <name>` |

- [LIF-011] The host MUST apply row I2 when the session memory pool cannot admit the instance, and MUST NOT count that refusal as a failure. Test: fill the pool with other plugins, trigger activation and assert the failure window of the refused plugin is empty.
- [LIF-012] A trap, an error from `activate` or a deadline breach in `activating` or `active` MUST follow rows I4 or I5 and MUST drop the instance without calling `deactivate`. Test: trap in `on-events` and assert no `deactivate` call is logged.
- [LIF-013] The host MUST apply row I14 when a plugin is disabled, updated or uninstalled while a restart is scheduled. Test: schedule a restart, disable the plugin and assert the timer never fires.
- [LIF-014] Rows I9 to I13 MUST send exactly one `deactivate` call per live instance, with the reason in the table. Test: for each row, count `deactivate` calls and read the reason.
- [LIF-015] A client or scene instance MUST receive `deactivate(shutdown)` when its client disconnects cleanly, and MUST receive no other reason. After a crash or a kill of the client process no call is possible: the server uses the last restore bytes it stored. Test: kill the client process and read the server log for the stored restore bytes.
- [LIF-284] A side whose required plugin or service provider is not `active` MUST be in the instance state `waiting-dependency`, MUST NOT count a failure, and MUST follow rows I16 to I18. Test: activate a consumer while its provider is disabled, assert `waiting-dependency`, enable the provider and assert `activating`; repeat with a provider that stays off for longer than `wait_ms` and assert `inactive` with `dependency.unresolved`.

### Events and counters

Two events report state changes. Both are delivered only to plugins that hold `plugins.manage` ([capability](/pages/capability-plugins-manage/)). The kernel also publishes the first one on the topic `ilium.plugins/state` for the settings screens.

| Event | Fields | When |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-state-changed` | `plugin`, `side`, `scope`, `from`, `to`, `reason`, `at-unix-ms` | Every row of both tables that changes a package or instance state |
| `ilium.extensions/changed` | `point`, `owner` | A contributor to an extension point appears, changes or disappears. See [extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/) |

The `reason` is one of `user`, `failure`, `policy`, `update`, `uninstall`, `trigger`, `capacity`, `server-start`, `server-stop`, `detach`, `grant` and `dev`.

- [LIF-016] The host MUST emit `plugin-state-changed` once per state change, in the order the changes happened, to every subscriber with `plugins.manage`. Test: record events through a full disable, enable and failure sequence.

### The `plugin-info` record

The record of [help and plugins](/pages/api-help-and-plugins/) has 19 fields, numbered in the table below. `enabled` and `failed` stay as derived fields, so a plugin that reads only them keeps working.

```wit
enum package-state { not-installed, installed-enabled, installed-disabled-by-user,
                     disabled-untrusted, disabled-blocked, disabled-by-policy,
                     refused-at-load, update-staged, uninstall-pending }
enum instance-state { inactive, activating, waiting-dependency, active, deactivating,
                      restart-scheduled, stopped-by-failure, stopped }
enum health-state { healthy, degraded, restarting, failed, disabled, dormant, refused }

record side-state {
  side: string,                       // "server", "client" or "scene"
  scope: string,                      // "server", or the attached client id
  state: instance-state,
  failures-in-window: u32,
  last-error-code: option<string>,    // for example "trap.deadline"
  restart-at-unix-ms: option<u64>,
}

record plugin-info {
  id: plugin-id, name: string, version: string, tier: string,
  enabled: bool, failed: bool,
  state: package-state,
  side-states: list<side-state>,
  scope: string,                      // "global" in 0.1.0
  disabled-reason: option<string>,    // a code such as "user", "untrusted", "blocked", "policy.blocked"
  health: health-state,
  publisher: string,                  // display name from the manifest
  publisher-key: option<string>,      // key id; none for T3
  source: string,                     // "file", "url" or "registry"
  channel: string,                    // "stable" or "beta"
  pinned: bool,
  update-available: option<string>,   // newest allowed version, from cached registry data
  deprecated: bool,
  yanked: bool,
}
```

| No. | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `id` | `plugin-id` | The plugin id. |
| 2 | `name` | string | Display name from the manifest. |
| 3 | `version` | string | Version of the active package. |
| 4 | `tier` | string | `T1`, `T2` or `T3`. |
| 5 | `enabled` | bool | Derived, see the rules below. |
| 6 | `failed` | bool | Derived, see the rules below. |
| 7 | `state` | `package-state` | The package state. |
| 8 | `side-states` | list of `side-state` | One record per side and scope. |
| 9 | `scope` | string | `global` in 0.1.0. |
| 10 | `disabled-reason` | option of string | Why the plugin is off. |
| 11 | `health` | `health-state` | The health value. |
| 12 | `publisher` | string | Display name from the manifest. |
| 13 | `publisher-key` | option of string | Key id; none for T3. |
| 14 | `source` | string | `file`, `url` or `registry`. |
| 15 | `channel` | string | `stable` or `beta`. |
| 16 | `pinned` | bool | The user pinned the version. |
| 17 | `update-available` | option of string | Newest allowed version, from cached registry data. |
| 18 | `deprecated` | bool | The registry marks the plugin deprecated. |
| 19 | `yanked` | bool | The registry marks the active version yanked. |

| Derived field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` when `state` is `installed-enabled` or `update-staged` |
| `failed` | `true` when any side has the instance state `stopped-by-failure` |
| `disabled-reason` | `none` when enabled, otherwise `user`, `untrusted`, `blocked`, `policy.blocked`, `safe-mode` or a refusal code |

- [LIF-017] `plugins.list` MUST return one record per installed plugin with every field of the `plugin-info` table, in table order. Test: install two plugins, disable one and compare the records with the table.
- [LIF-018] `enabled` MUST equal the rule above in every state. Test: parametrised over the nine package states.

The CLI shows the same data. `ilium plugin list --json` prints one JSON line per plugin, with the type `plugin`:

```text
{"type":"plugin","id":"com.example.notes","version":"0.3.1","tier":"T2","state":"installed-enabled","scope":"global","health":"healthy","enabled":true,"failed":false,"disabled_reason":null,"side_states":[{"side":"server","scope":"server","state":"active","failures_in_window":0,"last_error_code":null,"restart_at_unix_ms":null}]}
```

The JSON uses snake_case keys, as all JSONL output of the CLI does. A final `summary` line gives `plugins` and `problems`.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin list
<span class="t-dim">ID                    VER    STATE      HEALTH</span>
ilium.core.tree       0.1.0  <span class="t-ok">enabled</span>    healthy
com.example.notes     0.3.1  <span class="t-ok">enabled</span>    healthy
com.example.cursor    0.2.0  <span class="t-err">failed</span>     failed
com.example.old       1.0.0  <span class="t-dim">off(user)</span>  disabled
vendor.ext            0.1.0  <span class="t-warn">refused</span>    refused
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The default list prints one row per plugin. Add <code>--json</code> for the full record.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Idempotency and concurrency

- [LIF-019] `set-enabled(id, true)` on an enabled plugin and `set-enabled(id, false)` on a disabled plugin MUST return `ok` and change nothing, and no event MUST be emitted. Test: call twice and count events.
- [LIF-020] The host MUST serialise all transitions of one plugin id. Transitions of different plugin ids MAY run in parallel. Test: issue disable and uninstall at the same time and assert one runs after the other.

How a request behaves while another transition of the same plugin is in flight:

| In flight | A new `set-enabled` | A new install, update or uninstall |
|---|---|---|
| `activating` | recorded at once, returns `ok`, applied when activation ends | queued behind the transition |
| `deactivating` | recorded at once, returns `ok`, applied when the deactivate ends | queued behind the transition |
| update swap | refused with `conflict` | refused with `conflict` and the message `update in progress` |
| `uninstall-pending` | refused with `conflict` | refused with `conflict` |

The last recorded desired state wins. A queued request never waits longer than the sum of the deadlines of the transition in flight. The call returns when the change is recorded, never when the transition ends.

### Edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Disable during `activating` | The desired state is recorded. When `activate` returns, the host calls `deactivate(disabled)`. If `activate` never returns, the activate deadline drops the instance. |
| Enable a plugin with a scheduled restart | The plugin is already enabled, so the call returns `ok`. The timer is not changed. |
| Two clients attached, one fails three times | Only that client's side becomes `stopped-by-failure`. The other client keeps the plugin. |
| Server stops while a restart is scheduled | The timer is cancelled. See [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart). |
| The registry file cannot be written | The transition is refused with `io` and the state stays as it was. See [offline and low disk](/pages/reference-offline-and-low-disk/). |

### See also

- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) for activation order, failure counting and restart delays
- [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/)
- [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/)
- [Plugin scope and sessions](/pages/reference-plugin-scope-and-sessions/)
- [Persistence and restart](/pages/reference-persistence-and-restart/)
- [Safe mode and troubleshooting](/pages/user-safe-mode-and-troubleshooting/)
- [Requirements, lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/)

# Plugin policy

## Plugin policy

An administrator can limit which plugins a machine may run. The limits are written in one file, the admin policy. This page is the user-facing companion to the [Admin policy reference](/pages/reference-admin-policy/), which is the only normative definition of the file: its paths, every key, the merge rules and the evaluation steps. This page does not repeat the key table. It maps the short names that older notes used to the real keys, and it lists what a user sees when the policy blocks something. The [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/) shows how to use the file in practice.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[USR-nnn]`, collected in [User and administrator requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-user-admin/). The security rows of the policy are `SEC-180` to `SEC-199` in the [security requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-security-policy/).

<div class="note">
<p>A policy can only make Ilium stricter, never looser than the defaults in <a href="/pages/security/">Security</a>. The platform owner confirms the key names before release.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- Where the file lives
- Format and loading
- Keys
- How the keys combine
- What the user sees
- The audit log
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### Where the file lives

The file is `policy.toml`. On Linux it is `/etc/ilium/policy.toml`, on macOS `/Library/Application Support/Ilium/policy.toml`, and on Windows `%ProgramData%\Ilium\policy.toml`. An optional user file `<user config dir>/policy.toml` can only make the result stricter ([SEC-181]). The system file is owned by an administrator; a file that group or others can write is ignored ([SEC-182]).

### Format and loading

The file is TOML with `version = 1`. The server reads it at start only ([SEC-188]). A change takes effect at the next start, and a running plugin is not stopped by an edit. A malformed or unreadable file makes T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load with `policy.invalid`, and T1 plugins run normally ([SEC-187]).

### Keys

The keys are defined in the [schema of the Admin policy reference](/pages/reference-admin-policy/#schema). This table maps the names that older pages and notes used to the keys of that schema.

| Older name | Key in `policy.toml` |
|---|---|
| `install.allow_third_party` | `packages.allow_third_party` |
| `install.allowed_tiers` | `packages.allowed_tiers` |
| `install.allowed_publishers` | `publishers.allow` |
| `install.denied_ids` | `plugins.deny_ids` |
| `install.allowed_ids` | `plugins.allow_ids` |
| `grants.forbidden` | `grants.deny` |
| `grants.forced_declined` | removed; it meant the same as `grants.deny` |
| `registry.allowed_urls` | `packages.allowed_sources` |
| `registry.allow_url_installs` | `packages.allow_url_installs` |
| `update.allowed_channels` | `packages.allowed_channels` |
| `audit.enabled`, `audit.path`, `audit.retention` | removed; the audit log is always on, see below |

A plugin that the policy blocks is in the package state `disabled-by-policy` and has the disabled reason `policy.blocked` (see [Plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/)). The state is not written to `installed.json`, so removing the key lets the plugin run again after the next start.

A grant that matches `grants.deny` never fails an install and never disables the plugin ([SEC-198]). The review dialog shows the row locked off with the text "Blocked by your administrator", and a call returns `not-permitted` with the reason `policy`.

- [USR-214] A grant that matches `grants.deny` MUST NOT be granted, MUST be shown as locked in the review dialog and in the Capabilities tab with the text "Blocked by your administrator", and MUST make calls return `not-permitted`. Test: deny `clipboard.read`, install a plugin that requests it, and assert the row is locked and a call returns `not-permitted` with the message starting `policy: ` and the log line `refused clipboard.read by <function> (policy)`.
- [USR-215] A plugin whose manifest requests a denied grant MUST still install and run, with that grant refused. Test: install such a plugin and assert state `enabled` and the refusal log line.
- [USR-216] `plugins.deny_ids` MUST win over `plugins.allow_ids`. Test: list one id in both and assert it cannot be installed, with the code `policy.blocked` and the message starting `policy.id-denied: `.

### How the keys combine

At install the host evaluates the policy at step 6 of the install pipeline, after the signature and manifest checks and before any prompt. Inside that step it checks these keys in this order and stops at the first failure.

1. `packages.allow_third_party`
2. `plugins.deny_ids`
3. `plugins.allow_ids`
4. `packages.allowed_tiers`
5. `publishers.deny` and `publishers.allow`
6. `packages.allowed_sources`

Grants are not checked at install. A user can make the result stricter with their own declines, never looser. Core plugins ignore every `packages`, `plugins` and `publishers` key, because they ship with Ilium. They do respect `grants.deny` for third-party callers only.

- [USR-217] The host MUST check the policy keys in the order above and report the first failing key as the detail code. Test: write a policy that fails four keys at once and assert the detail code is the first in the order.
- [USR-218] The policy MUST NOT stop a core plugin or a bundled T1 plugin from running. Test: set `packages.allow_third_party = false` and `packages.allowed_tiers = []`; assert all 30 core plugins still start.

### What the user sees

The install command and the review dialog name the policy and the key that blocked the action. They do not say how to remove the block, because the user cannot.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin install notes.iliumpkg
<span class="t-err">error</span> policy.blocked
Cannot install Notes 1.2.0.
policy.tier-denied: tier T3 is not allowed.
Nothing was installed.
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. Install blocked by the policy.</figcaption>
</figure>

Every block is reported with the one install error code `policy.blocked` (step 6 of the install pipeline in [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/)). The message starts with a detail code from this table, followed by a colon and a space.

| Detail code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `policy.third-party-denied` | `packages.allow_third_party` is `false` |
| `policy.tier-denied` | The tier is not in `packages.allowed_tiers` |
| `policy.publisher-denied` | The signing key is denied or not in `publishers.allow` |
| `policy.id-denied` | The id is in `plugins.deny_ids`, or not in `plugins.allow_ids` |
| `policy.source-denied` | The package source is not in `packages.allowed_sources`, or URL installs are off |
| `policy.grant-forbidden` | A grant matches `grants.deny`. This is never an install failure. It is the detail shown next to the locked row, and calls fail with `not-permitted` and the reason `policy` |

### The audit log

The audit log is always on. It is defined only in the [Audit log reference](/pages/reference-audit-log/) ([SEC-220] to [SEC-228]). Policy may set only `audit.sink`, `audit.max_mib` and `audit.keep_days`. The events `policy-loaded` and `policy-violation` record what the policy did.

- [USR-219] The host MUST write a `policy-loaded` audit record at start when a policy file exists, and a `policy-violation` record when a plugin or file violates it, and MUST NOT write plugin data into either. Test: start with a policy that denies one installed plugin and count the two records.
- [USR-220] The host MUST delete rotated audit files older than `audit.keep_days` at server start ([SEC-224]). Test: age a rotated file by 366 days and restart.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| No policy file | Defaults apply: everything the security model allows is allowed |
| `version` is not `1` | The file is malformed: T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load with `policy.invalid` |
| A key lists a plugin that is not installed | Accepted, no effect |
| An installed plugin is forbidden after the fact | At the next start it is disabled, shown as `Blocked by policy`, and kept on disk. Removing the key lets the user enable it again |
| The audit file cannot be written | No action is refused. The server queues up to 1,000 records, retries every 10 s and shows a notice ([SEC-225]) |
| A user sets their own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | No effect on the system file. A user file can only add restrictions |

- [USR-210] The host MUST read the policy file before it loads any third-party plugin, and MUST NOT load a third-party plugin when the file exists but cannot be read or parsed. Test: make the file unreadable and start Ilium; assert that core plugins run and that every T2 and T3 plugin refuses to load with `policy.invalid`.
- [USR-211] The host MUST ignore a system policy file that a non-administrator can write, MUST show a persistent notice, and MUST record the audit event `policy-violation` with the reason `policy-file-writable` ([SEC-182]). Test: set the mode to `0666`; assert the notice and the audit record.
- [USR-212] The host MUST treat a policy with an unknown key or a wrong type as malformed and MUST name the line of the first error in the notice. Test: write a policy with the key `allow_thirdparty`; assert that T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load, T1 plugins run, and the notice names line and key.
- [USR-213] The host MUST read the policy at server start only. Test: set `packages.allow_third_party = false` while a T2 plugin runs and assert that nothing changes; restart and assert the plugin is shown as `Blocked by policy` with the message `policy.third-party-denied`.

### See also

- [Admin policy reference](/pages/reference-admin-policy/)
- [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/)
- [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/)
- [Plugin files on disk](/pages/reference-plugin-files/)
- [Security](/pages/security/)
- [Permissions explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/)

# Reference, plugin scope and sessions

## Reference, plugin scope and sessions

A user may run several Ilium sessions, and may open projects with different needs. This page defines where a plugin is installed, where it is enabled, how a change reaches the other sessions, and which failure state is shared.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

### Install scope

In 0.1.0 a plugin installs globally, for the user. There is no project-scope install. A package in a project folder could run code the moment a repository is opened, so the platform leaves it out until workspace trust exists. The shared package store, `installed.json`, grants and the global storage bucket serve every session of the user.

- [LIF-160] The host MUST accept installs only into the user scope in 0.1.0, and MUST refuse `--scope project` for install with `install.scope-unsupported`. Test: run the command.

### Enable scope

A plugin is enabled or disabled at three levels. A lower level overrides a higher one.

| Order | Level | Where stored | Set by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | global | `installed.json` | `ilium plugin enable <id>` |
| 2 | project | `<project>/.ilium/plugins.toml` | `ilium plugin enable <id> --scope project` |
| 3 | session | session state | the Plugins screen toggle with "this session only" |

The effective value is the session value if set, else the project value if set, else the global value. A plugin disabled by policy or by safe mode stays off whatever the levels say.

The WIT call is `set-enabled(id, enabled, scope)` with `scope` one of `global`, `project`, `session`.

- [LIF-161] The effective enabled value MUST follow the order session, project, global. Test: set the three levels in all eight combinations.
- [LIF-162] `plugins.toml` MUST be read as a request only. It MUST NOT install, grant or raise a tier. Test: list a package that is not installed.

### Propagation to other sessions

A global change reaches running sessions within 2 seconds. Each session server watches `installed.json`. A session that is mid-call finishes the call, then applies the change. The CLI command fans out: it prints one JSONL line per reachable session with its result. An unreachable session gets the change at its next start.

```text
{"type":"session-result","session":"default","project":"/home/u/app","ok":true}
{"type":"session-result","session":"review","project":"/home/u/lib","ok":true}
```

- [LIF-163] A global enable, disable or uninstall MUST reach every running session of the user within 2 seconds. Test: two fake sessions and a changed file.
- [LIF-164] The CLI MUST print one `session-result` line per session and exit 0 only when all succeeded. Test: make one session unreachable.

### Locks

Writes to `installed.json` take the lock `<data>/plugins/.lock`. A second writer waits up to 5 seconds, then fails with `conflict`. An update that is in progress holds a per-plugin lock, so two sessions never run the same trial.

### Failure scope

The failure window is per session, per plugin side. A plugin that fails three times in one session is disabled in that session only, and a note is written to the shared registry so that other sessions show the warning. It is not disabled elsewhere.

- [LIF-165] A failure disable MUST apply to the session where it happened and MUST NOT disable the plugin in other sessions. Test: fail a plugin in session A and call it in B.

### Grants and the "Not now" counter

Grants are global and are stored in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/grants.json`. The counter of "Not now" answers for a bundled plugin's first-start prompt is stored with the grants, so the prompt does not repeat in each session.

- [LIF-166] A grant change MUST apply to every session and the "Not now" counter MUST be shared. Test: answer in one session and open another.

### See also

- [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/)
- [Plugin files on disk](/pages/reference-plugin-files/)
- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)
- [Requirements, lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Project templates

## Project templates

`ilium plugin new` writes a complete, working project from a template. This page lists the exact files that each template writes in each language, the flags of the command, the refusal codes, the placeholder rules and the guarantees about a fresh project. The older pages showed only the first three files. This page replaces those lists.

A template is a plain set of files. The command copies them and replaces a few placeholders. It runs no build and needs no network. A project made from a template builds, passes its own tests, and is ready to edit.

Terms:

- **Template**: a named set of files, one set per language.
- **Side**: one of `server`, `client` or `scene`. A plugin has one or more sides, and each side builds to its own component.
- **Placeholder**: a token such as `@@id@@` that `new` replaces when it writes a file.

## You will need

- The `ilium` binary. The command works offline and needs no toolchain.
- A plugin id, for example `example.agent-tools`, and a language, `rust` or `typescript`.
- Background reading: [Set up a toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/) and [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/).

## The command

`ilium plugin new <dir> --id <id> --lang <rust|typescript> (--template <name> | --side <name>) [--name <text>] [--publisher <text>] [--first-party] [--ci <github|gitlab|none>] [--force]`

| Flag | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `--id` | none, required | Matches `[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+`. Fails with `new.id-invalid`. |
| `--lang` | none, required | `rust` or `typescript`. |
| `--template` | none | One of the eight names below. |
| `--side` | none | An alias for `server`, `client`, `both` or `scene`. |
| `--name` | the last label of the id, with the first letter in capitals | The display name. |
| `--publisher` | the operating system user name | The `publisher` value. |
| `--first-party` | off | Allows an `ilium.` id. Needed for `core-style`. |
| `--ci` | `none` | Adds a CI file. See [CI recipes](/pages/guide-ci-recipes/). |
| `--force` | off | Writes into a non-empty folder without deleting any file. |

- **[DEV-260]** `--template` and `--side` MUST name the same template when both are given. `--side` accepts only `server`, `client`, `both` and `scene`. All other templates are reachable only through `--template`.
- **[DEV-261]** `new` MUST fail with `new.dir-not-empty` for a folder that holds files, `new.id-invalid` for a bad id, `new.id-reserved` for an `ilium.` id without `--first-party`, and `new.template-unknown` for an unknown name. No file MUST be written when a check fails.
- **[DEV-262]** `core-style` MUST require `--first-party` and an id that starts with `ilium.`. Every other template MUST refuse an `ilium.` id, even with `--first-party`, with `new.id-reserved`. A package built from `core-style` that is not bundled in the Ilium source tree is refused at install by `manifest.id-reserved`.
- **[DEV-263]** `new` MUST be deterministic. The same flags and the same `ilium` version MUST write byte-identical files.
- **[DEV-264]** The placeholders are `@@id@@`, `@@name@@`, `@@publisher@@`, `@@package@@` (the last label of the id, which is the Cargo package name or the npm package name) and `@@sdk@@` (the SDK version). `new` MUST replace them in the files marked in the tables below and MUST leave no `@@` token in any written file.
- **[DEV-265]** `--name` and `--publisher` MUST be written as JSON strings or TOML strings with escaping, so a quote or a backslash in the value cannot break the file.
- **[DEV-266]** The entry source of a TypeScript side MUST be `src/<side>.ts`: `src/server.ts`, `src/client.ts` or `src/scene.ts`. The entry source of a single-side Rust project MUST be `src/lib.rs`. This replaces the earlier spellings `src/main.ts`, `src/plugin.ts` and `src/index.ts` on other pages.
- **[DEV-267]** A Rust project with two sides MUST be a Cargo workspace with one crate per side (`server/`, `client/`) and one shared crate (`shared/`). Each side crate MUST declare its side in `[package.metadata.ilium]` as `side = "server"` or `side = "client"`, which is how `build` finds the crate for a side.
- **[DEV-268]** Every template MUST write `.gitignore` with the lines `dist/`, `.ilium/`, `target/` and `node_modules/`.
- **[DEV-269]** Every template MUST write `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` skeletons and a `help/overview.md` topic that `contributes.help` lists, so `lint.readme-missing`, `lint.changelog-missing` and `lint.help-topic-missing` pass on a fresh project.

## The guarantees about a fresh project

- **[DEV-270]** A project made by `new`, with no edits, MUST pass `ilium plugin check`, `ilium plugin lint --deny warnings`, `ilium plugin build` and then `ilium plugin test` on a machine where `ilium plugin doctor` reports no `fail`, with zero warnings.
- **[DEV-271]** A fresh project MUST pass its own native unit tests (`cargo test`, `bun test`).
- **[DEV-272]** A fresh project MUST request the smallest grant set that its template needs and no more.
- **[DEV-273]** A fresh project MUST run activation without logging at `warn` or `error`.

## Common files

These files are the same in every template, with the placeholders replaced.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | The manifest of the template, see below. Placeholders in `id`, `name`, `publisher`. |
| `.gitignore` | `dist/`, `.ilium/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`. |
| `README.md` | Title `@@name@@`, one paragraph, the build and test commands, the list of requested grants. |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Keep a Changelog header with an `Unreleased` section. |
| `help/overview.md` | A help topic with a title line and two short paragraphs. |
| `tests/fixtures/sample.json` | A fixture, see [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/). |
| `tests/fixtures/sample.expect.json` | The expectation of that fixture. |
| `tests/golden/overview.txt` | The golden render, in templates with a view. |
| `.github/workflows/plugin.yml` or `.gitlab-ci.yml` | Only with `--ci github` or `--ci gitlab`. |

The README skeleton:

```markdown
# @@name@@

A plugin for Ilium. Describe what it does in one paragraph.

## Build and test

    ilium plugin check
    ilium plugin lint --deny warnings
    ilium plugin test
    ilium plugin build

## Grants

List each requested grant and why the plugin needs it.
```

The CHANGELOG skeleton:

```markdown
# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- First version.
```

The help topic skeleton:

```markdown
# @@name@@

One sentence that says what the plugin adds.

Name each command, setting and view the plugin adds, one line each.
```

## The eight templates

| Template | Sides | Purpose | Requested grants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | server | Reacts to events and sets tree decorations | `tree.read`, `tree.decorate` |
| `client` | client | A panel with one view | `ui.panels` |
| `both` | server, client | A server that sends one message to a client view | `ui.panels` |
| `scene` | scene | An ambient background scene | none |
| `pane-kind` | client | A new kind of pane with a view | `ui.panels`, `panes.provide-kind` |
| `core-style` | server, client | A first-party replaceable plugin with an extension point | `tree.read`, `ui.panels` |
| `service-provider` | server | Provides a named service | `services.provide:@@id@@/greeter` |
| `extension` | server | Fills a hook point of a core plugin | `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy` |

- **[DEV-274]** The requested grants of each template MUST be those in the table, and the manifest `capabilities` object MUST list them per side.

### server

Files, Rust: `manifest.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/handler.rs`, `tests/fixtures/sample.json`, `tests/fixtures/sample.expect.json`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `help/overview.md`.

Files, TypeScript: `manifest.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `src/server.ts`, `tests/handler.test.ts`, and the same fixtures and documents.

The manifest:

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "@@id@@",
  "name": "@@name@@",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "@@publisher@@",
  "description": "Marks agents that start working.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "server": {
    "entry": "server.wasm",
    "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0",
    "exports": []
  },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.read", "tree.decorate"] },
  "contributes": {
    "decoration_slots": [{ "id": "work", "placement": "badge", "priority": 50 }],
    "help": [{ "id": "overview", "file": "help/overview.md", "title": "@@name@@" }]
  }
}
```

The Rust `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "@@package@@"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.90"

[package.metadata.ilium]
side = "server"

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]

[dependencies]
ilium-plugin-sdk = "@@sdk@@"

[dev-dependencies]
ilium-plugin-sdk = { version = "@@sdk@@", features = ["testing"] }
```

The Rust `src/lib.rs`:

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetDecorationSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Plugin;

impl Lifecycle for Plugin {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("activate: {} ready", context.plugin));
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for Plugin {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. }) = event
            else {
                continue;
            };
            if current != AgentActivity::Working {
                continue;
            }
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
                node,
                slot: "work".into(),
                content: vec![Span::plain("work")],
                icon: None,
                sort_key: None,
                persist: false,
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

The Rust `tests/handler.rs`:

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::testing::FakeHost;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;
use @@package_ident@@::Plugin;

#[test]
fn working_agent_gets_a_badge() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::for_manifest("manifest.json").expect("manifest");
    host.activate::<Plugin>();
    let submissions = host.deliver(vec![Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent {
        node: 42,
        previous: AgentActivity::Idle,
        current: AgentActivity::Working,
        revision: 1,
    })]);
    assert_eq!(submissions.len(), 1);
}
```

`@@package_ident@@` is the package name with hyphens replaced by underscores.

- **[DEV-275]** `new` MUST replace `@@package_ident@@`, the package name with hyphens replaced by underscores, in the Rust test files, in addition to the placeholders of rule DEV-264.

The TypeScript `package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "@@package@@",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": { "@ilium/plugin-sdk": "@@sdk@@" },
  "scripts": { "test": "bun test" }
}
```

The TypeScript `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "types": ["bun-types"]
  },
  "include": ["src", "tests"]
}
```

The TypeScript `bunfig.toml`:

```toml
[test]
preload = ["@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing/setup"]
```

The preload registers the reset hook of the harness, which gives each test a fresh host (see the isolation rules in [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/)). The TypeScript `src/server.ts`:

```ts
import { definePlugin, type Event, type Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';
import { span } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

let nextCorrelation = 1n;

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) {
    log('info', `activate: ${context.plugin} ready`);
  },
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const submissions: Submission[] = [];
    for (const event of batch) {
      if (event.tag !== 'agent-activity-changed') continue;
      if (event.val.current !== 'working') continue;
      submissions.push({
        intent: {
          tag: 'set-decoration',
          val: {
            node: event.val.node,
            slot: 'work',
            content: [span('work')],
            icon: undefined,
            sortKey: undefined,
            persist: false,
          },
        },
        correlation: nextCorrelation++,
        dedupKey: undefined,
      });
    }
    return submissions;
  },
});
```

The TypeScript `tests/handler.test.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { createFakeHost } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing';

test('working agent gets a badge', async () => {
  const host = createFakeHost().forManifest('manifest.json');
  await host.activateModule('../src/server');
  const submissions = host.deliver([
    { tag: 'agent-activity-changed', val: { node: 42n, previous: 'idle', current: 'working', revision: 1n } },
  ]);
  expect(submissions.length).toBe(1);
});
```

The fixture `tests/fixtures/sample.json` and its expectation:

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "events": [
    { "tag": "agent-activity-changed", "val": { "node": 42, "previous": "idle", "current": "working", "revision": 1 } }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "submissions": { "match": "ordered", "items": [ { "intent": "set-decoration", "node": 42, "slot": "work" } ] }
}
```

### client

Files, Rust: `manifest.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/view.rs`, `tests/handler.rs`, `tests/fixtures/sample.json`, `tests/fixtures/sample.expect.json`, `tests/golden/overview.txt`, and the common documents.

Files, TypeScript: `manifest.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `src/client.ts`, `tests/view.test.ts`, `tests/handler.test.ts`, and the same fixtures, golden file and documents.

The manifest differs from `server` in these keys:

```json
{
  "client": { "entry": "client.wasm", "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["views"] },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels"] },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [{ "id": "open", "title": "Open @@name@@", "icon": "layout-sidebar" }],
    "panels": [{ "id": "main", "title": "@@name@@", "icon": "layout-sidebar", "modal": false }],
    "help": [{ "id": "overview", "file": "help/overview.md", "title": "@@name@@" }]
  }
}
```

The view draws a block with one text line. The golden file `tests/golden/overview.txt` is the render at 40 columns by 4 rows:

```text
╭  ≡ ● · Example ────────────────────────╮
│ Hello from the plugin                  │
│                                        │
╰────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

- **[DEV-276]** The golden file MUST be the exact output of the test render at the size used by the test, with Unicode box characters. The sample view test MUST compare against it with `assert_golden`.

### both

The manifest has both a `server` and a `client` entry, `capabilities` for the client only, and the client exports `views`. The server sends a `message` intent on channel `hello` when a client attaches, and the client view shows the received text. No grant is needed because messages between the sides of one plugin are always allowed.

Files, Rust: `Cargo.toml` (a workspace), `shared/Cargo.toml`, `shared/src/lib.rs` (the `Hello` message type with `serde`-free manual encoding), `server/Cargo.toml`, `server/src/lib.rs`, `client/Cargo.toml`, `client/src/lib.rs`, `manifest.json`, `tests/session.rs` (a `FakeSession` test), and the common documents and fixtures.

Files, TypeScript: `manifest.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `src/shared.ts`, `src/server.ts`, `src/client.ts`, `tests/session.test.ts`, and the common documents and fixtures.

The Rust root `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[workspace]
members = ["shared", "server", "client"]
resolver = "2"
```

- **[DEV-277]** The `both` template test MUST use `FakeSession` to start the server and one client of the package and assert that the client view shows the message text after the server handles `client-attached`.

### scene

Files, Rust: `manifest.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/frame.rs`, `tests/golden/frame-tones.txt`, and the common documents. Files, TypeScript: `manifest.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `src/scene.ts`, `tests/frame.test.ts`, `tests/golden/frame-tones.txt`, and the common documents.

The manifest differs from `server` in these keys:

```json
{
  "scene": { "entry": "scene.wasm", "world": "ilium:scene/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "contributes": {
    "scenes": [
      {
        "id": "waves",
        "title": "Waves",
        "family": "procedural",
        "modes": ["live"],
        "frame_rate_cap": 30,
        "settings_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {} }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The scene draws tone only. Colour, dither and display settings are never scene settings, and the template adds none. The golden file holds a tone grid in digits 0 to 9 for a 16 by 4 surface at frame 3. See [Ambient scenes](/pages/api-scenes/).

### pane-kind

The manifest adds `pane_kinds` and the grant `panes.provide-kind`:

```json
{
  "client": { "entry": "client.wasm", "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["views"] },
  "capabilities": { "client": ["ui.panels", "panes.provide-kind"] },
  "contributes": {
    "pane_kinds": [
      { "id": "board", "title": "@@name@@", "icon": "layout-board", "primitive": "basic", "wants_keys": true, "persist": "metadata" }
    ],
    "help": [{ "id": "overview", "file": "help/overview.md", "title": "@@name@@" }]
  }
}
```

The global id of the pane kind is `@@id@@.board`. The view test renders `ViewTarget::Pane` at 40 by 6 and compares the golden file. The handler test sends a key through the `key-pressed` event and asserts the next render.

### core-style

`core-style` writes a plugin in the style of the bundled first-party plugins: both sides, the `ilium.` id, tier T1, `limits_tier: "first-party"`, `replaceable: true`, and one declared extension point. It is for plugins that live in the Ilium source tree.

```json
{
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "id": "@@id@@",
  "name": "@@name@@",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "publisher": "Ilium",
  "limits_tier": "first-party",
  "replaceable": true,
  "surface": [],
  "server": { "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "client": { "entry": "client.wasm", "world": "ilium:client/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["views"] },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["tree.read"], "client": ["ui.panels"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extension_points": [
      { "id": "before-open", "kind": "hook", "mode": "veto", "title": "Before open", "deadline_ms": 20, "max_handlers": 8, "version": "0.1.0" }
    ],
    "help": [{ "id": "overview", "file": "help/overview.md", "title": "@@name@@" }]
  }
}
```

The `surface` list is empty until the plugin defines what a replacement must provide. The tests include a hook test that runs `before-open` against two stub contributors with `FakeSession`.

- **[DEV-278]** `core-style` MUST write the file `docs/EXTENDING.md` with the table of the plugin's extension points, so a plugin that extends it has a document to read.

### service-provider

```json
{
  "server": { "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["service-provider"] },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["services.provide:@@id@@/greeter"] },
  "contributes": { "services": [{ "provides": ["@@id@@/greeter"] }] }
}
```

The Rust handler implements `ServiceProvider::handle(call) -> ServiceReply` and replies with `{"greeting":"hello"}`. The test calls the service through `FakeSession` and a stub consumer, and asserts the reply JSON.

### extension

The `extension` template fills a hook of a core plugin. It requests `extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy`, exports `hook-handler`, and declares one entry in `contributes.extensions`:

```json
{
  "server": { "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": ["hook-handler"] },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["extensions.contribute:ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy"] },
  "contributes": {
    "extensions": [
      { "point": "ilium.core.smart-copy/after-copy@0.1.0", "id": "strip-keys", "priority": 70, "handler": "strip_keys" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The test builds a `HookCall` with a payload that holds a secret, runs the handler with `host.run_hook` and asserts `HookReply::Replace`. The core plugin point is described in [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/).

## Edge cases

- **Existing folder.** An empty folder is accepted. A folder with only a `.git` directory counts as non-empty because of the file rule, so use `--force` for it.
- **Both language files.** The template never writes `Cargo.toml` and `package.json` together, because the build refuses that.
- **Case in the id.** Upper-case letters in the id fail the pattern. The error names the first bad character.
- **Template drift.** A new `ilium` release can change a template. The README of the project names the `ilium` version that wrote it, in a comment on its first line.
