# Registry reference

## Registry reference

A **registry** is a service that lists plugins and serves their packages. It is an optional source. A file install works without any registry, and a user who sets no registry never contacts one. This page specifies the registry protocol, the index format, namespaces, publishing, policy, mirrors and offline use. It is decision D27, which supersedes D3 for distribution only. The package format, the signature and the contract `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` do not change. See [Design decisions](/pages/design-decisions/).

A **mirror** is a copy of a registry that clients use instead of the original. A **bundle** is a directory or file that holds an index and packages for an offline install. A **yank** withdraws a version from new installs but leaves it working where it is installed. A **namespace** is the set of plugin ids that one publisher owns. A **client** is the Ilium host that talks to a registry.

Requirement ids such as `PKG-361` can be cited by tests. See [Requirements: manifest and package](/pages/reference-requirements-manifest-package/).

### You will need

- The signature rules: [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/).
- Version and channel rules: [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/).
- The user view: [Finding and installing plugins](/pages/user-plugin-store/).

## Roles and design

There are four roles: the **registry operator**, who runs the service; the **publisher**, who uploads packages; the **client**, which reads the index and downloads packages; and the **mirror operator**.

The registry is a set of static files: signed JSON documents and package blobs. Any web server or file share can host them, so mirrors and air-gapped copies are plain file trees. Only the upload side needs a service.

The metadata follows the model of The Update Framework (TUF). Four properties matter: signed metadata, a freshness window, rollback protection and key thresholds. A client that trusts the registry root keys learns whether the index is current and untampered, even when a mirror served it.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-361] | A registry MUST be usable as a static file tree over HTTPS for reading. Reading MUST NOT need a server-side program. |
| [PKG-362] | A client MUST verify every metadata document against the registry root keys before it uses any value from it. |
| [PKG-363] | A client MUST verify the SHA-256 and the length of a downloaded package against the index before it parses the package, and then run all install stages of [Package format reference](/pages/reference-package-format/). The registry never replaces those checks. |

## File layout

All paths are relative to the registry base URL, for example `https://plugins.example.org/ilium/v1/`.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `root.json` | The root keys, role keys and thresholds |
| `timestamp.json` | The hash and version of `snapshot.json`; short expiry |
| `snapshot.json` | The hashes and versions of `index.json`, `revocations.json` and every `plugins/<id>.json` |
| `index.json` | A summary of every plugin for search and listing |
| `plugins/<id>.json` | All versions of one plugin |
| `revocations.json` | Revoked keys and blocked ids |
| `blobs/<sha256>.iliumpkg` | One package, named by its hash |
| `categories.json` | The closed list of categories (optional; a built-in list applies when absent) |

## Metadata documents

Every metadata document is a JSON object `{ "signed": { ... }, "signatures": [ { "key_id", "signature" } ] }`. The signature is Ed25519 over the bytes `ilium-registry-metadata-v1`, `0x00`, then the canonical form of the `signed` value: the JSON Canonicalization Scheme of RFC 8785 (JCS). The client parses the document with refusal of duplicate keys, serialises `signed` again with JCS and verifies over those bytes. Whitespace in the file and the position of `signed` before or after `signatures` do not matter.

**Vector.** The `signed` value `{ "version": 17, "type": "revocations", "expires": "2026-10-19 12:00:00", "keys": [ { "publisher_id": "example", "key_id": "56475aa75463474c0285df5dbf2bcab73da651358839e9b77481b2eab107708c", "reason": "compromised", "effective": "2026-10-12 10:00:00" } ], "blocked_ids": [] }` has these JCS bytes (253 bytes, keys in code point order, no whitespace), whatever the order in the file:

```text
{"blocked_ids":[],"expires":"2026-10-19 12:00:00","keys":[{"effective":"2026-10-12 10:00:00","key_id":"56475aa75463474c0285df5dbf2bcab73da651358839e9b77481b2eab107708c","publisher_id":"example","reason":"compromised"}],"type":"revocations","version":17}
```

Their SHA-256 is `2ad56689abaf8da83199f2beca98b7342dab7a5fd2269e5a0616acb514b94130`.

All times are `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` in UTC.

### root.json

```json
{
  "signed": {
    "type": "root",
    "spec": "ilium-registry/1",
    "version": 3,
    "expires": "2027-10-12 00:00:00",
    "keys": { "<key_id>": { "algorithm": "ed25519", "public_key": "<base64url>" } },
    "roles": {
      "root": { "key_ids": ["<key_id>"], "threshold": 1 },
      "timestamp": { "key_ids": ["<key_id>"], "threshold": 1 },
      "snapshot": { "key_ids": ["<key_id>"], "threshold": 1 },
      "targets": { "key_ids": ["<key_id>"], "threshold": 1 }
    }
  },
  "signatures": []
}
```

### timestamp.json and snapshot.json

```json
{ "signed": { "type": "timestamp", "version": 4821, "expires": "2026-10-13 12:00:00",
    "snapshot": { "version": 4821, "sha256": "<hex>", "length": 18233 } }, "signatures": [] }
```

```json
{ "signed": { "type": "snapshot", "version": 4821, "expires": "2026-10-19 12:00:00",
    "files": { "index.json": { "version": 4821, "sha256": "<hex>", "length": 90211 },
               "revocations.json": { "version": 17, "sha256": "<hex>", "length": 412 },
               "plugins/com.example.notes.json": { "version": 9, "sha256": "<hex>", "length": 2104 } } },
  "signatures": [] }
```

### index.json

One entry per plugin, with only what search and listing need.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Plugin id |
| `name` | string | Display name, at most 64 characters |
| `description` | string | At most 500 characters |
| `publisher_id`, `publisher` | string | Namespace owner and display name |
| `categories` | list | 1 to 3 values from the category list |
| `keywords` | list | At most 8 words of at most 24 characters |
| `latest_stable`, `latest_beta` | string or null | Highest non-yanked version of each channel |
| `license` | string | SPDX expression |
| `icon` | string | Tabler icon name |
| `updated` | string | Time of the newest publish |
| `deprecated` | object or null | `{ "message", "successor" }` |

### plugins/&lt;id&gt;.json

```json
{
  "signed": {
    "type": "plugin", "version": 9, "id": "com.example.notes", "publisher_id": "com.example",
    "versions": [
      {
        "version": "1.2.0", "channel": "stable", "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
        "url": "blobs/<sha256>.iliumpkg", "sha256": "<hex>", "length": 523044,
        "key_id": "<publisher key id>", "countersigned": true,
        "host": ">=0.1.0", "platforms": ["linux"],
        "categories": ["editors"], "license": "MIT", "published": "2026-10-12 10:00:00",
        "yanked": null, "deprecated": null
      }
    ]
  },
  "signatures": []
}
```

`yanked` is null or `{ "reason", "at" }`. `deprecated` is null or `{ "message", "successor" }`. `platforms` lists `linux`, `windows`, `macos`, matching the platform gate.

### revocations.json

The document has the wrapper of every metadata document and is signed with the `timestamp` role keys of `root.json`:

```json
{
  "signed": {
    "type": "revocations",
    "version": 17,
    "expires": "2026-10-19 12:00:00",
    "keys": [ { "publisher_id": "example", "key_id": "<64 hex>", "reason": "compromised", "effective": "2026-10-12 10:00:00" } ],
    "blocked_ids": [ { "id": "example.notes", "reason": "<text>", "at": "2026-10-12 10:00:00" } ]
  },
  "signatures": [ { "key_id": "<key id>", "signature": "<base64url>" } ]
}
```

A `revocations.json` without a valid signature of the threshold of those keys is refused with `registry.signature-invalid`.

### Rules for the documents

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-364] | `root.json` MUST be signed by at least `threshold` of its own `roles.root` keys. A new root MUST also be signed by the threshold of the previous root's keys, and its `version` MUST be the previous version plus 1. |
| [PKG-365] | The client MUST stop and report `registry.metadata-expired` when a document's `expires` time is in the past, unless the client works in offline mode with a cached index (see below). |
| [PKG-366] | Version numbers are integers that never go down. A client MUST remember the highest `version` it has seen for each document and MUST refuse a lower one with `registry.rollback`. |
| [PKG-367] | `timestamp.json` MUST expire within 1 day of its issue. `snapshot.json` SHOULD expire within 7 days, `root.json` within 1 year. A registry operator renews the first two by re-signing without content change. |
| [PKG-368] | `index.json` and each `plugins/<id>.json` MUST match the hash, length and version in `snapshot.json`. A mismatch is `registry.hash-mismatch`. |
| [PKG-369] | The maximum sizes are: `root.json` 64 KiB, `timestamp.json` 16 KiB, `snapshot.json` 4 MiB, `index.json` 32 MiB, each `plugins/<id>.json` 1 MiB, `revocations.json` 4 MiB. A larger response is aborted with `registry.size`. |
| [PKG-370] | The sequence in which a client refreshes is: fetch `timestamp.json`; if its snapshot version is unchanged, stop; fetch `snapshot.json`; fetch each changed file listed in it. A client fetches `root.json` first only when the timestamp signature fails with the known keys. |
| [PKG-652] | The signature of a metadata document covers the JCS (RFC 8785) form of its `signed` value. A client MUST parse with refusal of duplicate keys, serialise `signed` again with JCS and verify over those bytes. The result for the vector of the metadata section MUST have the SHA-256 given there. |
| [PKG-653] | `revocations.json` MUST carry the `signed` and `signatures` wrapper and MUST be signed with the `timestamp` role keys. Without a valid signature of the threshold it is refused with `registry.signature-invalid`. |

## Transport

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-371] | A client MUST use HTTPS. A plain `http:` base URL is refused with `registry.insecure-url`, except for `localhost` in a development configuration (`[plugins.registry] allow_insecure_localhost = true`). |
| [PKG-372] | The client MUST send `If-None-Match` with the stored `ETag` of a document and accept `304 Not Modified`. It MUST follow at most 3 redirects and only to HTTPS. |
| [PKG-373] | Timeouts: 10 s to connect, 30 s to the first byte of a metadata document, 120 s total for a metadata document, 600 s total for a package download. Retries: up to 3 attempts for connection errors and for 5xx responses, with waits of 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. A 4xx response is not retried. |
| [PKG-374] | The client reads `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` and the `[plugins.registry] proxy` setting. The setting wins. |
| [PKG-375] | A download is written to a temporary file under the cache folder and renamed only after the hash and length match. A resumed download MUST use `Range` and MUST verify the final hash. |
| [PKG-376] | The only request data the client sends is the HTTP request itself: the path, the standard headers and `User-Agent: ilium/<version>`. It sends no identifier, no list of installed plugins and no install count. A registry operator who wants statistics reads their own server logs. |
| [PKG-377] | The configured registries are listed in `[plugins.registry] urls` in order (default: none). A registry marked `default` is searched first. A client with no URLs makes no network request. |

Offline behaviour: the client keeps the last verified set of metadata in the cache folder. When the network fails, it uses the cached metadata and shows its age. [PKG-378] A cached index MAY be used after its `expires` time only when the user passes `--offline` or sets `[plugins.registry] offline = true`; the client then shows a clear warning that the data is stale. Without that setting the expired metadata is refused with `registry.metadata-expired`.

## Search and categories

Search runs on `index.json`. A client that has downloaded it can search with no further network use.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-379] | A search query is a string of at most 200 characters. The client splits it on whitespace into terms, folds case and accents (Unicode NFKD, remove combining marks) and requires every term to match as a prefix of a word in `id`, `name`, `description`, `keywords` or `publisher`. |
| [PKG-380] | The relevance score of a match is the sum over terms of: 8 for a match in `id`, 6 in `name`, 4 in `keywords`, 2 in `publisher`, 1 in `description`. Ties break by `updated` (newer first), then by `id`. |
| [PKG-381] | Ranking uses no download counts and no user ratings in version 0.1. |
| [PKG-382] | Sort orders: `relevance` (default with a query), `name` (A to Z, default without a query), `updated` (newest first). |
| [PKG-383] | Pagination: the client shows pages of 20 results. `ilium plugin search --limit <1..100> --offset <n>` applies the same rule. |
| [PKG-384] | The `category` filter takes one value from the list below. A plugin lists 1 to 3 categories. A value outside the list is refused at publish with `registry.category-unknown`. |

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| `agents` | Detects, controls or reports on AI agents and their sessions |
| `appearance` | Themes of the interface other than ambient scenes, icons, status and tree chrome |
| `scenes` | Ambient background scenes |
| `editors` | Editing, viewing and language support |
| `git` | Source control and worktrees |
| `inference` | Model providers and cost tracking |
| `notifications` | Sounds, alerts and reports |
| `search` | Finding text, panes or files |
| `terminal` | Terminal behaviour, links and filters |
| `tools` | Utilities that fit no other category |
| `voice` | Speech input and output |

The same list is used by `ilium plugin search --category` and by the store view. A client may fall back to a built-in copy when `categories.json` is absent.

## Namespaces

A **namespace** is the set of plugin ids that start with a publisher id and a dot. The publisher id `com.example` owns every id that starts with `com.example.`.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-385] | A registry publisher id is one of: a reverse-DNS name of a domain that the publisher controls (`com.example`), or a registry account name written `user.<name>`, where `<name>` is 3 to 32 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`. |
| [PKG-386] | A domain publisher id is claimed by proving control of the domain: the publisher adds a DNS TXT record `_ilium-publisher.<domain>` with the value `ilium-publisher=<publisher_id>;key=<key_id>`. The registry checks the record at claim time and again every 30 days. A domain whose record disappears loses new-publish rights after a 14 day grace period, but its published versions stay. |
| [PKG-387] | The reserved prefixes are `ilium.`, `core.`, `local.`, `test.` and `example.`. A publish with such an id is refused with `registry.id-reserved`. The prefix `user.` is reserved for account ids and cannot be claimed as a domain. |
| [PKG-388] | A plugin id MUST start with the publisher id of its signature plus a dot (rule [PKG-218]). A publish whose id belongs to another namespace is refused with `registry.namespace-unowned`. |
| [PKG-389] | **Confusable check.** At claim and publish the registry computes a skeleton of the id in this order: 1, NFKC normalisation, then lowercase; 2, each non-ASCII character is mapped with `confusables.txt` of Unicode 16.0.0; 3, the characters `-`, `_` and `.` are removed; 4, in one pass from left to right, `rn` becomes `m`, `vv` becomes `w`, `0` becomes `o`, `1` and `l` become `i`, and `5` becomes `s`. A new id or publisher id whose skeleton equals the skeleton of an existing different one is refused with `registry.confusable`, and a human reviews the exception. Vectors: `r-n.tool` and `m.tool` give `mtooi`; `vv.tool` and `w.tool` give `wtooi`; `Ilium.Tool` and `ilium_tool` give `iiiumtooi`; `examp1e.n0tes` and `example.notes` give `exampienotes`; `corn` gives `com`. |
| [PKG-390] | **Transfer.** The owner of a namespace can transfer it to a new publisher id by publishing a transfer statement signed by a trusted key of the current owner, naming the new publisher id and key. The registry records the transfer in the plugin metadata (`transferred_from`). Installed clients accept the new key because the registry countersignature chain covers it (see revocation) or because the user adds it with a rotation statement. |
| [PKG-391] | **Disputes.** A claim dispute is decided by the registry operator under the published policy. An id is never reassigned to a different publisher when its versions are still installed by users, except by a takedown and a clearly marked new publisher. |

## Publishing

Publishing is the only part of the protocol that needs a server. The upload API is specified here so that one client works with any registry that follows it.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-392] | `ilium plugin publish <file> --registry <url> [--channel stable\|beta]` sends the package with `PUT <base>/publish/<id>/<version>` over HTTPS. The body is the package. The `Authorization` header holds a registry token from `ILIUM_REGISTRY_TOKEN` or the credential file of the registry. Tokens are never written to a log. |
| [PKG-393] | The server runs every install stage 1 to 6 and the signature check (stage 7) on the upload, and a policy check. It refuses the publish with the same codes as the client would, plus the registry codes. |
| [PKG-394] | A version number is **immutable**. A publish of an existing `id@version` is refused with `registry.version-exists`, even when the content is identical. A fixed package needs a new version. |
| [PKG-395] | On success the server adds the version to `plugins/<id>.json`, stores `blobs/<sha256>.iliumpkg`, adds a registry countersignature to a copy of the signature document (a second entry of `signatures`, see [PKG-207]), recomputes `snapshot.json` and `timestamp.json`, and answers `201` with a JSON body `{ "id", "version", "sha256", "url" }`. |
| [PKG-396] | **Yank.** `ilium plugin yank <id>@<version> --reason <text>` marks a version as yanked. Clients do not choose it for a new install or update. Installed copies keep working. `unyank` reverses it. |
| [PKG-397] | **Deprecate.** `ilium plugin deprecate <id> --message <text> [--successor <id>]` marks the whole plugin. Clients show the message and offer the successor. Installs still work. |
| [PKG-398] | **Unlist.** A publisher can `unlist` a plugin: it disappears from `index.json` and from search, but `plugins/<id>.json` and the blobs remain so that installed copies update safely and lock files still resolve. |
| [PKG-399] | A publisher MUST NOT delete a published blob. Removal happens only through takedown (below). |
| [PKG-400] | Upload limits: 300 MiB per package (the package format cap), 20 publishes per hour per publisher id. A larger upload is refused with `registry.size`. |

## Policy

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-401] | **Review levels.** Level A: automated checks only (all package checks, a scan for known-bad hashes, the confusable check). Level B: a human review is also required when the package requests any high-risk grant (`process.run`, `fs.write` outside the plugin scope, `http` with `*`, `agent.control`, `commands.invoke:*`) or `replaces`, or when it is the first publish of a publisher id. A registry MUST state which level applies to which version on the plugin page. |
| [PKG-402] | **Content policy.** A registry refuses plugins that: contain malware or hidden data collection, impersonate another publisher or product, hide behaviour that the manifest does not declare, or break the law of the registry's jurisdiction. The operator publishes this policy at `policy.json` or on its site. |
| [PKG-403] | **Takedown.** An operator removes a version or a plugin by adding it to `revocations.json` (`blocked_ids`) and removing the blob. The reason and time are recorded. At the next metadata refresh the client moves the installed copies that match to the package state `disabled-blocked` ([plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/)), with the reason `registry.takedown` and the registry's reason text, and shows both. `ilium plugin enable <id> --accept-risk` enables the plugin again. |
| [PKG-404] | **Appeal.** A publisher can appeal a takedown once, in writing to the contact in `policy.json`. The operator answers within 14 days. A reinstated plugin gets a new version number. |
| [PKG-405] | **Emergency revocation** of a publisher key follows [PKG-242] to [PKG-247]. The registry adds the key to `revocations.json`. |
| [PKG-406] | **Ratings and reviews.** User ratings and reviews are **out of scope for 0.1**. A registry compliant with this page MUST NOT show a rating, and a client MUST NOT send one. A later version of this page may add them. The policy for any future rating: only users of a version may rate it, a rating needs moderation, and paid ratings are forbidden. |

## Revocation

Revocations travel in `revocations.json`. [PKG-407] A client MUST fetch it on every metadata refresh, and MUST apply `keys` to its trust store (status `revoked`, `added_by: registry` is not used for revocations) and `blocked_ids` to its installed plugins. The effects are those of [PKG-244] to [PKG-247] for keys and [PKG-403] for ids.

## Mirrors

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-408] | A **full mirror** serves a byte-identical copy of the file tree. Because every document is signed and the blobs are named by hash, the signature chain survives mirroring unchanged. |
| [PKG-409] | A **partial mirror** serves a subset: a list of plugin ids with their dependencies. It MUST include the metadata files, `index.json` filtered to the subset and a `snapshot.json` that lists only the mirrored files. A partial mirror re-signs `index.json` and `snapshot.json` with its own keys and has its own `root.json`. Clients treat it as a separate registry with its own root, set in `[plugins.registry]`. |
| [PKG-410] | `ilium plugin mirror sync <dir> --registry <url> [--allow <id>...] [--channel stable\|beta]` copies the metadata and the blobs to `<dir>` and verifies every hash. For a full copy, omit `--allow`. The command is idempotent: it downloads only changed files. |
| [PKG-411] | A client configured with a mirror URL uses it exactly like a registry. The root keys are the ones in the client's configuration (`[plugins.registry] root`), never fetched from the mirror alone, except at the first setup where `ilium plugin registry add <url> --root-key <key_id>` pins them. |

## Air-gapped installs

A machine with no network can install from a **bundle**: a directory with the same layout as a registry, or a `.tar` file of it.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-412] | `ilium plugin export-bundle <dir> <id>[@range]... [--with-deps]` writes a bundle with the signed metadata of the registry, filtered to the listed plugins, and their blobs. The bundle keeps the original signatures. |
| [PKG-413] | `ilium plugin install --from-bundle <dir> <id>` installs from the bundle. The client verifies the metadata with the root keys pinned in its configuration, enforces expiry (unless `--offline`) and rollback rules against its stored versions, and runs the normal install stages. |
| [PKG-414] | A bundle's `snapshot.json` expires like any other. For a long-lived air-gapped setup the operator re-exports a bundle regularly or sets `offline = true`. |

## Client error codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `registry.unreachable` | The network failed after retries and no cache applies |
| `registry.insecure-url` | A non-HTTPS URL was configured |
| `registry.metadata-expired` | A metadata document is past its `expires` time |
| `registry.rollback` | A document has a lower version than one seen before |
| `registry.signature-invalid` | A metadata signature or threshold failed |
| `registry.hash-mismatch` | A document or package differs from the hash in the metadata |
| `registry.size` | A document, package or upload exceeds its cap |
| `registry.not-found` | The plugin id or the version is not in the index |
| `registry.yanked` | The version is yanked and was requested by exact version without `--allow-yanked` |
| `registry.version-invalid` | A version has build metadata or is malformed |
| `registry.version-exists` | A publish of an existing version |
| `registry.id-reserved` | A publish with a reserved prefix |
| `registry.namespace-unowned` | The id is outside the publisher's namespace |
| `registry.confusable` | The id looks like an existing one |
| `registry.category-unknown` | A category is not in the list |
| `registry.auth` | The token is missing or refused |
| `registry.policy` | The package fails the registry policy |

Message templates are in [Manifest schema and error catalogue](/pages/reference-manifest-schema/).

## Client behaviour on each failure

| Id | Failure | Required behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| [PKG-415] | Network unreachable | Use the cache if valid. Otherwise report `registry.unreachable`, exit 8. A file install is unaffected |
| [PKG-416] | Metadata expired | Refuse to install from it. Offer `--offline` |
| [PKG-417] | Rollback | Refuse, keep the old cache, report the two versions |
| [PKG-418] | Hash mismatch on a package | Delete the partial download, refuse, never retry the same URL more than the transport retries |
| [PKG-419] | Signature threshold not met | Refuse. Do not use the document at all |
| [PKG-420] | A version the user asked for is yanked | Refuse unless `--allow-yanked`. Dependency resolution skips yanked versions silently |
| [PKG-421] | Revoked key in a freshly fetched package | Refuse with `trust.key-revoked` |
| [PKG-422] | A different registry returns the same id | The first registry in the configured order wins. `--registry <url>` selects one. A plugin installed from one registry updates only from it |

## Worked example

An administrator sets up a mirror for a team:

```text
ilium plugin registry add https://plugins.example.org/ilium/v1/ --root-key 9c0b...e41d
ilium plugin mirror sync /srv/ilium-mirror --registry https://plugins.example.org/ilium/v1/ \
    --allow com.example.notes --allow com.example.git
```

They serve `/srv/ilium-mirror` over HTTPS at `https://mirror.team.example/ilium/`. On each machine:

```text
ilium plugin registry add https://mirror.team.example/ilium/ --root-key 9c0b...e41d
ilium plugin install com.example.notes
```

The client checks the metadata with the pinned root key, so a compromised mirror cannot serve a changed package. At worst it can serve old metadata, and the freshness and rollback rules limit that.

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The index lists a version whose blob is missing | `registry.not-found` for that version. Other versions work |
| The clock of the client is far in the future | Metadata looks expired. The message shows both times. Fix the clock or use `--offline` |
| Two versions with the same number but different hashes appear in two mirrors | `registry.hash-mismatch`. The version number is immutable |
| The registry root key changes | A new `root.json` signed by the old threshold is followed automatically. Otherwise the client stops and the user re-pins |

## What the user sees

The user sees the registry only through search results, plugin detail pages and update notices. Errors appear as a short line with the code and a hint. See [Finding and installing plugins](/pages/user-plugin-store/).

# Requirements for the host API

## Requirements for the host API

Normative behaviour of host functions: the error record, traps, the restart and disable rule, limits, clamps, quotas and install reporting. Contract version: ilium:plugin@0.1.0.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `API`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [API-001] | A fallible host function MUST return result<T, plugin-error>. The record MUST carry code, message and an optional retry-after-ms. | [the plugin error record](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#the-plugin-error-record) | (sync-return) call any fallible function with a bad argument -> the result is err with the three fields. |
| [API-002] | The error code MUST be one of the 15 codes: not-permitted, not-found, invalid-argument, conflict, quota-exceeded, rate-limited, busy, timed-out, cancelled, unsupported, pane-not-ready, revoked, io, network, internal. | [the plugin error record](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#the-plugin-error-record) | (sync-return) provoke each documented failure -> the code is in the list of 15 and no other value appears. |
| [API-003] | retry-after-ms MUST be set for rate-limited and for quota-exceeded caused by the CPU budget. A plugin MUST NOT match on message text. | [the plugin error record](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#the-plugin-error-record) | (sync-return) exceed the toast rate -> rate-limited with retry-after-ms greater than 0. |
| [API-004] | Every function that returns a result MAY return not-permitted, revoked and internal. A function that returns a request-id MAY also return busy. | [the plugin error record](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#the-plugin-error-record) | (sync-return) call a request-id function with 4,097 requests pending in the session -> err busy. |
| [API-005] | For a call that returns a request-id, grant, scope, syntax and per-call cap checks MUST fail in the call. Disk, network, process and user failures MUST arrive in the completion as failed(code). | [the plugin error record](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#the-plugin-error-record) | (sync-return) fs read of a path outside the scope -> err at once. (completion) read of a file that vanished -> failed(not-found). |
| [API-010] | Calling an import whose capability the manifest never requested MUST trap. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) call an import without its grant in the manifest -> the instance traps and the log names the interface and function. |
| [API-011] | An invalid ui-tree MUST trap: an index out of range, a graph that is not a tree, a duplicate key in one tree, more nodes than the effective ui_tree_nodes limit, or a layout whose child count differs from its constraint count. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) return a tree with 4,097 nodes at the default limit -> trap. |
| [API-012] | A deadline breach in an export that has no result type (on-events, views.render, deactivate) MUST trap. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) sleep 100 ms inside on-events at the 20 ms deadline -> trap and a log line "on-events 100 ms (limit 20 ms)". |
| [API-013] | Exceeding the linear memory or table limit MUST trap. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) allocate past memory_mib -> trap. |
| [API-014] | A Rust panic or an uncaught TypeScript exception in an export MUST trap. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) panic in on-events -> trap. |
| [API-015] | A trap MUST end the instance. The plugin MUST be restarted under the restart rule. A plugin MUST NOT be able to catch a trap. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (restart-schedule) trap once -> new instance after 1 s. |
| [API-016] | Every not-permitted result and every trap MUST be logged with the plugin id, the interface and the function. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (log-line) call a function without its grant -> one log line with the three fields. |
| [API-040] | The restart rule MUST apply per plugin and per side. The first failure in a 10-minute window restarts after 1 s. The second restarts after 5 s. The third disables the plugin on that side. No 30 s step exists. A failure older than 10 minutes MUST NOT count. | [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule) | (restart-schedule) failures at 0, 2 and 4 minutes -> restart after 1 s, restart after 5 s, disabled. Failures at 0 and 11 minutes -> both restart after 1 s. |
| [API-041] | A disabled side MUST stay disabled until a manual enable. A manual enable MUST reset the failure count to zero. A successful run MUST NOT clear a failure sooner. | [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule) | (restart-schedule) disable, enable in Settings, fail once -> restart after 1 s. |
| [API-042] | A trap, a deadline breach and an activate call that returns an error MUST count as failures. A revoked re-activation, a disable, an upgrade, a shutdown and a failed job MUST NOT count. | [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule) | (restart-schedule) revoke a grant three times in a minute -> re-activated each time, never disabled. |
| [API-043] | A manifest limit above the tier ceiling MUST be clamped and logged. The install MUST NOT fail for it. | [resource limits in the manifest](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#resource-limits-in-the-manifest) | (install-error) request http_streams 99 as T2 -> install succeeds. (log-line) a clamp line names the key and 4. |
| [API-044] | A failing view MUST count against the plugin and not against the view alone. | [restart and disable rule](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#restart-and-disable-rule) | (restart-schedule) trap in views.render -> the plugin restarts, not only the view. |
| [API-045] | A scene failure MUST count as a failure of the whole plugin on that side. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (restart-schedule) trap in a scene frame -> the client side restarts after 1 s. |
| [API-046] | When the memory budget of the session is reached, a new instance MUST be refused and logged. The refusal MUST NOT count as a failure. The side MUST stay inactive with the reason host-capacity. | [edge cases](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#edge-cases) | (log-line) activate beyond 1,024 MiB total -> refusal logged, state inactive, failure count unchanged. |
| [API-060] | Truncations and clamps MUST be only those in the exception table. Every other over-limit call MUST return an error and MUST NOT cut silently. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) pass a 65 KiB raw input -> err invalid-argument and no bytes sent. |
| [API-061] | A cap that depends on held or cumulative state MUST return quota-exceeded. A cap the plugin can check in advance MUST return invalid-argument. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) read-cells with 1,001 rows -> quota-exceeded. send-input with 17 stages -> invalid-argument. |
| [API-062] | A call over a fixed cap such as 1 MiB for a synchronous fs.read, 8 MiB per HTTP request, or a timer interval under 50 ms MUST return invalid-argument. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) set a timer of 10 ms -> err invalid-argument. |
| [API-070] | Session-wide limits MUST count across all plugins of the session: 64 HTTP streams, 16 children, 4,096 pending requests, 65,536 decorations, 32 key grabs. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) two plugins open 32 streams each, one opens a 65th -> quota-exceeded. |
| [API-071] | Rate rules MUST be enforced per plugin as listed: toast 3 per 10 s, geocode 1 per second, notify 6 per minute, play-sound 4 per second, topics.publish 100 per second, journal.log-event 20 per second, send-input 20 per second per pane. Each rate MUST be a sliding window; a refused operation MUST NOT enter the window; and the refusal MUST carry `retry-after-ms` until the oldest counted operation leaves the window. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) call notify 7 times in one minute -> the 7th returns rate-limited; call notify 6 times at second 55 and once at second 65 -> the call at second 65 is refused. |
| [API-072] | The execution quota group MUST be a token bucket of 2,000 ms of CPU time refilling at 500 ms per second. The bucket is empty at a balance of 0 or less, and the balance MAY go negative. An empty bucket MUST make submissions and request-id calls return quota-exceeded with retry-after-ms = max(100, ceil_10(-balance_ms * 2)). | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) spend 2,500 ms CPU in jobs, then submit -> quota-exceeded with retry-after-ms between 100 and 400; drive the balance to -100 ms, submit -> retry-after-ms 200. |
| [API-073] | Pending requests MUST be limited to 64 per plugin by default. A request MUST count from the return of its id to the enqueue of its completion; refused submissions and synchronous calls MUST NOT count. A further call MUST return busy. | [Reference summary](/pages/reference/#limits) | (sync-return) start 65 slow calls -> the 65th returns busy. |
| [API-074] | A timer MUST NOT fire inside the call that set it; the first timer-fired MUST be queued after the delay counted from the return of timers.set; timers.cancel MUST remove a queued, undelivered timer-fired of that timer; cancelling an unknown id MUST be a silent no-op. | [clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/#rules) | (event-delivery) set a 50 ms timer, cancel it at 40 ms with a queued tick -> no timer-fired is delivered. |
| [API-080] | The install MUST stop at the first failing step and MUST report every failure found inside that step, in the documented order. The exit code MUST be 1 when any error line was printed. | [install checks and error codes](/pages/reference-manifest/#install-checks-and-error-codes) | (install-error) a package with a bad id and an unknown key -> only the id code. A package with two unknown keys -> both codes. |
| [API-081] | A trap MUST carry exactly one of the eight codes `trap.deadline`, `trap.memory`, `trap.table`, `trap.submission-batch`, `trap.invalid-ui-tree`, `trap.import-not-requested`, `trap.abi` and `trap.panic`, and the log line of the trap MUST name it. | [trap codes](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#trap-codes) | provoke each trap and read the code in `ilium plugin logs` |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Requirements for author guides

## Requirements for author guides

This page lists every requirement with the prefix `AUT`. They come from the author guides (patterns, performance, compatibility, publishing, quality, accessibility, internationalisation, porting and troubleshooting) and from the pages those guides amend. The table is generated from the pages by a script, so each row repeats the sentence of its page.

Rules for ids:

- An id is never reused and never renumbered, even when its requirement is removed.
- A requirement that is removed stays in the table with the statement `withdrawn`, so that a test that cites the id can still be traced.
- Ranges: 0nn patterns, 1nn performance and limits, 2nn compatibility, 3nn publishing, 4nn quality, 5nn accessibility, 6nn internationalisation, 7nn porting, 8nn troubleshooting and debugging.
- A statement uses MUST for a rule a tool or test can check, SHOULD for a strong recommendation, and MAY for an allowed choice.

The column "Testable how" says what kind of check settles the requirement. Where the check is a review, no automatic test is possible.

| Id | Statement | Page | Testable how |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUT-001 | A core MUST NOT call the clock itself, and a handler SHOULD read the clock once per batch and pass the value in. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-002 | A debounce MUST cancel the pending timer before it arms a new one. Otherwise each change leaves a timer behind, and a busy editor reaches the limit of 64 held timers. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-003 | The handler MUST compare the id of each `timer-fired` event with the id it stored, and ignore every other id. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-004 | A debounce delay MUST be 50 ms or more, because a shorter delay is refused with `invalid-argument`. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-005 | A plugin SHOULD keep its own send rate under the host rate, and SHOULD NOT depend on `rate-limited` as flow control. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-006 | After `rate-limited`, the plugin MUST wait at least `retry-after-ms` before it sends the same kind of call again. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-007 | *Traps.** A throttle MUST take its time from `monotonic-millis`, because wall time can jump backwards and then `now - last` underflows in unsigned arithmetic. The code above uses `saturating_sub` for this reason. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-008 | Data that the plugin can rebuild MUST go to the `shared` bucket or to `/cache`, never to a durable bucket, so that it does not fill the 16 MiB bucket. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-009 | A cached value MUST carry its fetch time as `now-unix-millis` inside the stored bytes, and the reader MUST compare it with the current time. The host does not expire entries by age. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-010 | When several sessions can refresh the same entry, only the caller whose `lease` returned true MAY refresh it. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-011 | A view MUST render only the rows in the visible window plus a small margin, and MUST NOT put all rows into the tree. The ceiling is 4,096 nodes and 1,024 KiB for the whole tree. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-012 | A view that hides rows behind a window MUST show how many rows exist and where the window is, for example `41 to 60 of 3,212`, so that the user knows more exist. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-013 | A plugin MUST NOT retry `not-permitted`, `revoked`, `invalid-argument` or `unsupported`. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Run the plugin with the grant refused and check the result |
| AUT-014 | A retry loop MUST have a maximum attempt count and a growing delay. A suggested schedule is 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up to 60 s, with at most 5 attempts. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-015 | A submission whose repeat would harm the user (a notice, a sent line) MUST carry a `dedup-key` built from what makes the action unique, such as an id and a revision. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-016 | A `dedup-key` MUST NOT be reused for different content within 10 minutes. The second submission is dropped as `duplicate` even though its content differs. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-017 | A mismatch MUST fall back to defaults. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-018 | State that must outlive a trap MUST be written to storage when it changes, not only in `deactivate`. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-019 | A plugin that starts work for a changing input MUST keep a generation number, store it with the request, and discard a completion whose generation is not the current one. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-020 | The handler MUST process every event of the batch in order, and MUST return before the event deadline (20 ms, 50 ms for tier 1). | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-021 | After an `events-dropped` entry, the handler MUST rebuild its picture from a read call instead of trusting its incremental state. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-022 | Work that can take longer than 10 ms MUST run as a job or a request. A handler that spends its 20 ms deadline on work traps the instance. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-023 | A server side that needs data from the client MUST use a client request with an explicit timeout, and MUST handle `timed-out` and `not-found` (the client is gone). | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-024 | A plugin that changes how it stores data MUST raise `data_version` and MUST provide a `migrator` export that converts the old layout, instead of reading both layouts inside `activate`. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-025 | A `migrate` function MUST be idempotent and MUST write the new value of a key before it removes the old one, so that an interrupted run can start again from the same arguments. | [guide-patterns-cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-101 | A plugin MUST be designed to run within the default of its tier, not within the ceiling. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-102 | A plugin SHOULD stay under half of each default budget in normal use, so that a bad input does not trap it. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-103 | Rebuildable data MUST NOT go into a durable bucket, as rule AUT-008 of the cookbook also requires, because it uses up the 16 MiB that user data needs. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-104 | A plugin that reports its own timing SHOULD read it with `monotonic-millis` and SHOULD NOT depend on a host tool being installed in the user's setup. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-105 | Timings for comparison with the targets MUST come from a release build. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-110 | When two pages differ, the defining page decides, and a page that cites an install code MUST use the cause that the defining page gives. | [reference-errors-and-limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) | Review of the project files and release notes |
| AUT-111 | An author MUST treat a limit as a trap and not as a warning. | [errors-and-limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-201 | A plugin MUST raise `version` for every package that it publishes, because the host refuses a second package with the same version and different content. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-202 | A plugin MUST NOT rename or remove any name of this table in a release that keeps the same `id`. To change a name, add the new name, keep the old one working, and document both. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-203 | The old name SHOULD keep working for at least two minor releases of the plugin before it is removed, and a removal MUST be announced in the changelog of the release that removes it. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-204 | The old command SHOULD be hidden from the command list and from the palette once the new one exists, but it MUST still run when a key or a script calls it. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-205 | Code that needs the new grant MUST check the call result and fall back when the call returns `not-permitted`. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-206 | A plugin MUST write the restore bytes in a layout whose first byte identifies the format, and MUST accept restore bytes of the format of the previous release, or MUST fall back to defaults. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Unit test on the fake host |
| AUT-207 | Data that must survive a layout change MUST live in storage and be converted by a `migrator`, because restore bytes are dropped when the `data_version` differs. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Unit test on the fake host |
| AUT-208 | A plugin SHOULD keep its data readable by the previous release for one release, by adding keys instead of changing the meaning of old ones. A user who rolls back then loses nothing. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-209 | A plugin SHOULD rebuild and publish against each new minor contract version within the lifetime of the previous one, so that users never hold a plugin outside the window. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-210 | A published plugin MUST NOT list an unstable feature unless the plugin is for development use, because a T2 or T3 package that lists one is installable only in development mode. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-211 | A package that is meant for testers MUST carry a prerelease part in its version, so that it cannot be taken for a release. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Unit test on the fake host |
| AUT-212 | A plugin MUST declare a `requires` range no wider than the versions it was tested with. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Unit test on the fake host |
| AUT-213 | A plugin that provides a service or an extension point MUST raise the major version of the point when it changes the payload incompatibly, and MUST keep the old major working for as long as it lists the old major as supported. | [guide-compatibility-and-upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-214 | The plugin MUST keep every name of the stable public list across its own releases. | [versioning](/pages/versioning/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-215 | A plugin MUST NOT rely on a deactivate reason or a restore value to detect that an update happened, because `upgrade` is also the reason used by `ilium plugin dev`. | [lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) | Unit test on the fake host |
| AUT-301 | Until those two pages agree, an author MUST treat the package file as the only publishing route that is certain to work, and MAY add a registry as a second route when the host supports it. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Review of the project files and release notes |
| AUT-302 | A release MUST pass `check` without errors and SHOULD pass `lint --deny warnings`. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-303 | A release package MUST be built with `--release`, because a package that carries debug information or source maps is larger and fails `lint.debug-info-in-release`. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-304 | A package MUST NOT contain a secret, a key or a token. The package is a file that anyone can open. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-305 | A signed package has one more rule: its id MUST start with the publisher id of the signing key and a dot, and an id that does not is refused with `manifest.id-publisher`. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-306 | The secret key MUST NOT be committed, packaged or printed. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-307 | A release MUST be signed after the last `pack`, and the signed file MUST be the file that users receive. Signing twice with the same key gives the same bytes. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-308 | The author SHOULD publish the full fingerprint on a channel separate from the download, such as the project page, so that a user can compare the two. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-309 | A leaked key MUST be announced to users on the same channel as the releases, with the fingerprint of the key that replaces it. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-310 | Release notes MUST name every new grant and every raised `data_version`. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-311 | A project SHOULD ship `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, because `lint.readme-missing` and `lint.changelog-missing` report their absence. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-312 | Wherever the file goes, the author SHOULD name the file `<id>-<version>.iliumpkg` and SHOULD NOT rename it. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-313 | A release page MUST state that signed and unsigned third-party packages need Linux. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-314 | `--unredacted` works only for a plugin installed with `ilium plugin dev`, so an author MUST NOT ask a user for unredacted output from a normal install. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-315 | A plugin that logs MUST NOT write secrets, tokens, file contents or whole payloads to the plugin log. A log line is 16 KiB at most, so write a count or an id. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |

| AUT-317 | A plugin that cannot be fixed SHOULD be deprecated with a successor named, when a registry is in use. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-318 | An author MUST publish a way to reach them, in the README and in the package description, before the first release. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-319 | A version number, once published, MUST NOT be reused for different content. The host refuses it with `package.version-reused`. | [guide-publishing-and-support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |

| AUT-402 | A release SHOULD pass `ilium plugin lint --deny warnings`, and every suppression SHOULD carry a reason that a reviewer can read. | [guide-quality-checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |
| AUT-403 | A plugin SHOULD NOT list an `unstable` feature in a release, because the shape of that feature can change without a major version. | [guide-quality-checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) | Run `ilium plugin check` or `lint` and read the finding |

See Performance. | [guide-quality-checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) | Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result |
| AUT-407 | A plugin MUST give every interactive widget a stable `key`. | [guide-quality-checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) | Inspect the package and repository, or run `ilium plugin verify` |
| AUT-408 | A plugin MUST have at least one test for activation, one for deactivation and one for each error code that its code handles. | [guide-quality-checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) | Unit test on the fake host |

# Requirements for capabilities

## Requirements for capabilities

Normative behaviour of grants: syntax, risk, install checks, dependencies, per-side grants and revocation.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `CAP`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [CAP-001] | A grant string MUST be name or name:argument. The first colon MUST split name and argument. Later colons MUST belong to the argument. | [grant syntax](/pages/reference-capabilities/#grant-syntax) | (install-error) fs.read:picked:x -> argument is picked:x and the grant is judged on that. |
| [CAP-002] | An unknown grant name MUST fail the install with manifest.grant-unknown. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/reference-capabilities/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (install-error) list "files.read" -> manifest.grant-unknown. |
| [CAP-003] | A wildcard in a forbidden place MUST fail with manifest.grant-wildcard. commands.invoke:com.example.notes/* MUST be valid and commands.invoke:*/notes MUST be refused. | [grant syntax](/pages/reference-capabilities/#grant-syntax) | (install-error) list commands.invoke:*/notes -> manifest.grant-wildcard. |
| [CAP-004] | A grant that takes no argument MUST fail with manifest.grant-argument when given one. A grant that needs an argument MUST fail with manifest.grant-argument-missing when it has none. | [grant syntax](/pages/reference-capabilities/#grant-syntax) | (install-error) list process.run with no program -> manifest.grant-argument-missing. |
| [CAP-005] | A grant limited to bundled T1 plugins MUST fail with manifest.grant-tier in any other tier. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/reference-capabilities/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (install-error) a T2 package lists a T1-only grant -> manifest.grant-tier. |
| [CAP-006] | A grant MUST be refused with manifest.grant-side when listed on a side where it is not available. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/reference-capabilities/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (install-error) list a client-only grant under capabilities.server -> manifest.grant-side. |
| [CAP-007] | fs.pick MUST need fs.read:picked or fs.write:picked, and settings.write-all MUST need settings.read-all. A missing dependency MUST fail with manifest.grant-dependency. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/reference-capabilities/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (install-error) list fs.pick alone -> manifest.grant-dependency. |
| [CAP-008] | An fs scope that is unknown, or that does not accept the access, MUST fail with manifest.grant-scope: fs.write:package, fs.write:agent-sessions:<agent>, and an absolute path without a path template. | [Write grants](/pages/capability-fs-write/#grants-and-scopes) | (install-error) list fs.write:package -> manifest.grant-scope. |
| [CAP-009] | A process.run grant with arguments, a wildcard or a relative path with a separator MUST fail with manifest.grant-program. | [Run grants](/pages/capability-process-run/#grants) | (install-error) list "process.run:git status" -> manifest.grant-program. |
| [CAP-010] | Grants MUST have a risk tier of always, normal or high. The install dialog MUST list them by tier. A high grant MUST be listed and MUST be unchecked by default. | [grant syntax](/pages/reference-capabilities/#grant-syntax) | (screen-text) install a package with a high grant -> the dialog row is unchecked. |
| [CAP-011] | The always-granted capabilities (log, clock, timers, storage, settings, codec, fs.read:package, fs.read:data, fs.write:data, fs.read:cache, fs.write:cache, own-side messages, ui.invalidate for own views) MUST need no manifest entry and no user grant. | [always granted](/pages/reference-capabilities/#always-granted) | (sync-return) call log, storage and fs.write:data with an empty capabilities list -> every call succeeds. |
| [CAP-012] | Grants MUST be recorded per plugin and per side. A server grant MUST NOT authorize a client call. | [who grants what](/pages/reference-capabilities/#who-grants-what) | (sync-return) the client calls a server-only import -> not-permitted. |
| [CAP-013] | When the user declines a grant the plugin MUST still load. Calls that need it MUST return not-permitted. The granted list MUST omit it. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/reference-capabilities/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (sync-return) decline fs.read -> activate succeeds, fs.read returns not-permitted, granted omits fs.read. |
| [CAP-014] | A refused call MUST be logged as: refused <grant> because <reason>. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/reference-capabilities/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (log-line) call without the grant -> a log line starting "refused ". |
| [CAP-015] | Revoking a grant at run time MUST re-activate the plugin with the reduced set. In-flight calls that depended on it MUST end with revoked. Contributions that depended on it MUST be withdrawn. | [changing grants while the plugin runs](/pages/reference-capabilities/#changing-grants-while-the-plugin-runs) | (completion) revoke fs.read during a read -> failed or err revoked, then a new activate with granted reduced. |
| [CAP-016] | An upgrade that asks for new grants MUST show the user only the new grants. | [changing grants while the plugin runs](/pages/reference-capabilities/#changing-grants-while-the-plugin-runs) | (screen-text) upgrade adding one grant -> the dialog lists one grant. |
| [CAP-017] | The table of grant forms MUST list 87 forms. A grant used in a capability page MUST exist in the table. | [table](/pages/reference-capabilities/#table) | (install-error) run the check tool over the pages -> no grant string is missing from the table. |
| [CAP-018] | An import whose capability the manifest never requested MUST trap. An import whose grant the user declined or revoked MUST return not-permitted. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) call an import never requested -> trap. (sync-return) call one the user declined -> err not-permitted. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Core parity requirements

## Core parity requirements

These requirements say that the core plugins keep every feature of Ilium. Each row has an id, a MUST statement, the page that explains it and a test. The ids use the prefix COR. They follow the style of [requirements](/pages/reference-requirements/).

Related pages: [feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/), [kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/), [config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/), [CLI compatibility](/pages/reference-cli-compatibility/), [roadmap](/pages/roadmap/).

| Id | Statement | Page where explained | Testable how |
|---|---|---|---|
| [COR-001] | Every feature F-001 to F-116 MUST behave as in the baseline when its owner is enabled. | [Feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/) | Run the baseline user-doc scenario for each row against the plugin build and compare the observable result. |
| [COR-002] | Every feature MUST have exactly one owner. | [Feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/) | Script: count rows per id in the table; the count is 116 and each owner cell is non-empty. The duplicates section lists no open claim. |
| [COR-003] | A row of the traceability table with Kind `native-kernel` MUST name `kernel` first in its Owner cell, and every config table named in its Config keys column MUST appear in the key-by-key table of the migration page. | [Feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/) | Script: parse the table; check the Owner prefix of each `native-kernel` row; check each named table against the key-by-key table. |
| [COR-010] | Kernel parts MUST stay in the kernel and MUST work with `--no-plugins`: PTY and vt100, tree model, IPC, snapshot writer, config store, keymap, layout, look painter, scene host, plugin host, recovery page, HTTP listener, kernel CLI. | [Kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/) | Start with `--no-plugins`; attach, create a pane, type, split, detach, reattach and open the recovery page. |
| [COR-011] | Every plugin-owned feature MUST keep its settings, keys, CLI output, data files and defaults. | [Feature traceability](/pages/reference-feature-traceability/) | For each plugin, diff the Behaviour contract table against the plugin build: settings rows, key actions, config keys, CLI records and data paths. The diff must be empty. |
| [COR-020] | The server MUST restore the snapshot before any plugin is instantiated, activate `startup` plugins in dependency order and bind the client socket last. | [Kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/) | Spy plugin with `startup` records the tree at `activate`; it sees the restored tree. |
| [COR-021] | Exactly the core plugins marked `startup` MUST be active at boot; the others MUST stay inactive until their trigger fires. | [Kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/) | Boot with no client; list active plugin sides; compare with the activation table. |
| [COR-022] | Disabling a core plugin MUST have the stated effect, MUST NOT delete its data and MUST leave the recovery page working. | [Kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/) | For each of the 30 plugins: disable it, check the table row, check stored data, open recovery. |
| [COR-023] | The scene world MUST NOT import `extensions`, and `capabilities.scene` MUST NOT hold extension grants. | [Kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/) | Manifest with `extensions.contribute` under `capabilities.scene` fails with `manifest.grant-side`. |
| [COR-024] | Each change in the live reload and restart table MUST apply as stated. | [Kernel and boot](/pages/reference-kernel-and-boot/) | Change one value of each kind with a client attached; check whether the running side sees it without a restart. |
| [COR-030] | A kernel tab MUST have at most one holder of `settings.write-kernel:<tab>`. | [Config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/) | Install two T1 fixtures asking for the same tab; the second fails with `manifest.settings-owner`. |
| [COR-031] | `settings.write-kernel:<tab>` MUST be T1 only and high risk; `settings.read-kernel:<tab>` MUST be open to every tier. | [Config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/) | T2 with the write grant fails with `manifest.grant-tier`; T3 with the read grant installs. |
| [COR-032] | Plugin state in a snapshot MUST use `snapshot-sections` with a `schema_version`; a section over 256 KiB MUST be dropped without losing the previous value; a failed plugin MUST NOT block the snapshot. | [Config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/) | Write a 300 KiB section; the previous value survives and the snapshot is written. |
| [COR-033] | The plugin build MUST NOT rename or move any key in `config.toml` or `.ilium/config.yaml` and MUST keep unknown keys. | [Config and data migration](/pages/reference-config-and-data-migration/) | Run the build on a config with an unknown key, change one setting, diff the files; only that setting differs. |
| [COR-040] | A plugin MUST declare every `ilium` subcommand it owns; no built-in command without a declared owner MAY remain. | [CLI compatibility](/pages/reference-cli-compatibility/) | Compare `ilium --help` with the ownership table; every non-kernel command names a plugin. |
| [COR-041] | Arguments, options, defaults, output records and exit codes of every command MUST equal the baseline CLI reference. | [CLI compatibility](/pages/reference-cli-compatibility/) | Replay the examples of `cli-reference.md` and compare the JSONL records and exit codes. |
| [COR-042] | A disabled or failed owner MUST give exit code 1 and a record with `cli.owner-disabled` or `cli.owner-failed` that names the plugin. | [CLI compatibility](/pages/reference-cli-compatibility/) | Disable chatroom; run `ilium chat tail`; check record, plugin id and exit code 1. |
| [COR-043] | Every manifest and sample on a core-plugin page MUST pass `ilium plugin check` with the `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` rules. | [Core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/) | Extract the Complete manifest block of each of the 30 pages and run the check; zero errors. |
| [COR-050] | Each of the 30 core-plugin pages MUST hold a Complete manifest section whose sides, worlds, grants and contributions match its tables; the core-plugins index MUST state 30. | [Core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/) | Script: parse each manifest; compare sides and grants with the page tables; compare the index count with the page count; every number of pages stated in `core-plugins.md` equals the count of `core-plugin-*.md` files; every `cli` key in a page's Manifest fragment appears with the same value in its Complete manifest. |
| [COR-060] | The roadmap MUST give each wave a gate test. | [Roadmap](/pages/roadmap/) | Every wave row has a non-empty gate column that names a test. |
| [COR-061] | The roadmap MUST state what stays native in each wave. | [Roadmap](/pages/roadmap/) | Every wave row has a non-empty native column. |
