# Requirements for developer tooling

## Requirements for developer tooling

This page lists every requirement with the prefix DEV. Each row gives the id, the statement, the page that defines it and a way to test it. The tests for the plugin command line, the check and lint rules, the project templates, the test harness, the conformance suite, the debugging tools and the CI and documentation guides are written from this table.

Words: MUST and MUST NOT are required. SHOULD is expected unless a reason is recorded. MAY is allowed. An id is never reused. The statement here is the same text as on the page. If the two differ, the page wins and this table has a defect.

## You will need

- The pages named in the "Page" column. Each id appears there as `[DEV-nnn]` at the start of a bullet.
- A scratch project made with `ilium plugin new`. See [Project templates](/pages/reference-project-templates/).

## How to read the table

- The id ranges are fixed by area. See the area headings below.
- "Testable how" says what a test does. It is a method, not a test case.
- Rows are grouped by area and sorted by id.


## CLI conventions

| Id | Statement | Page | Testable how |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEV-001 | `<dir>` MUST default to the current working directory. A command that takes `<dir>` MUST treat it as the project directory, the one that holds `manifest.json`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-002 | A command that builds MUST detect the language from the project files. A `Cargo.toml` means Rust. A `package.json` means TypeScript. Both files together fail with `toolchain.language-ambiguous`. Neither file fails with `toolchain.language-unknown`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-003 | Every command MUST accept the global flags in the table below. A flag that does not apply to a command MUST be accepted and ignored, except `--session`, which a command that never contacts a session MUST also ignore without error. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-004 | A session command MUST find its session this way: the session named by `--session`, in the project that `--cwd` names, defaulting to the session called `default` of the current directory. No session found at that address MUST fail with `session.unreachable` and exit code 6. A command MUST NOT start a session itself. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-005 | The commands in the offline column of the table below MUST work with no running session, no network and no home-directory configuration beyond the trust store. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-006 | A session command that cannot reach its session MUST print one `error` record with the code `session.unreachable`, then `summary`, then `result`, and exit with 6. It MUST NOT retry. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-007 | Every command MUST exit with one of the codes below, and the `exit_code` field of its `result` record MUST equal the process exit code. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-008 | Exit code 0 MUST be returned only when `result.ok` is `true`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-009 | Exit code 1 MUST be returned for any failure that is not covered by a more specific code. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-010 | Exit code 2 MUST be returned for a usage error before any work starts. The command MUST NOT write files before it returns 2. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-011 | Exit code 3 MUST be returned when a `check` finding of severity `error` exists, when `lint --deny warnings` has any finding, when a lint rule of severity `error` fires, or when at least one test case does not pass. A finding of severity `warn` under `check` or plain `lint` returns 0. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-012 | Exit code 4 MUST be returned when a `toolchain.*` code stops the command, and when `doctor` reports any item with status `fail`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-013 | Exit code 5 MUST be returned for `plugin.not-found`, `trust.not-found` and `inspect.id-unknown`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-014 | Exit code 6 MUST be returned for `session.unreachable` and `session.not-found`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-015 | Exit code 130 MUST be returned after an interrupt. The command MUST print `summary` and `result` with `ok` set to `false` before it exits, and MUST leave no half-written output file (see the atomic write rule below). | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-016 | A JSONL command MUST print one JSON object per line on standard output, with the field `type` as the first key. Human text, if any, MUST go to standard error. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-017 | A JSONL command MUST print exactly one `summary` record and then exactly one `result` record, in that order, as its last two lines. This fixes the older disagreement between pages. The `summary` comes first, and the `result` is always the final line, so a script can read the last line to get the outcome. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-018 | Every size MUST be an unsigned integer in bytes. Every duration MUST be an unsigned integer in milliseconds, and its key MUST end in `_ms`. Every hash MUST be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256. Every path MUST use `/` and be relative to the project directory unless the key says `absolute`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-019 | A record MUST NOT contain a field that this page does not define for its type, except `details`, an optional object that a record MAY carry. A consumer MUST ignore fields it does not know, so later minor versions can add fields. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-020 | `--quiet` MUST suppress `progress` records and nothing else. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-021 | The `step` field of `progress` MUST be one of `toolchain`, `compile`, `bundle`, `component`, `api-version`, `strip`, `inventory`, `pack`, `sign`, `check`, `lint`, `test`, `install`, `watch`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-022 | The `kind` field of `artifact` MUST be one of `component`, `package`, `source-map`, `build-info`, `key`, `public-key`, `signature`, `replay`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-023 | The `severity` field of `check` and `lint` MUST be `error` or `warn`. A `lint` record MAY also use `info`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-024 | The `status` field of `test-case` MUST be `pass`, `fail`, `trap` or `skip`. The `status` field of `doctor-check` MUST be `ok`, `warn` or `fail`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-025 | The `side` field MUST be `server`, `client`, `scene` or `host`. `host` marks an entry that the host itself wrote. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-026 | A command listed as JSONL in the table below MUST print JSONL always. `--json` on such a command MUST be accepted and have no effect. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-027 | A command listed as text MUST print text by default for a person and JSONL with `--json`. The JSONL form MUST end with `summary` and `result` records, as for any JSONL command. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-028 | Text output MUST be stable enough to read but is not a contract. Scripts MUST use `--json`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-029 | A flag MUST override the environment variable that has the same effect. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-030 | Output files that a command replaces (`dist/*.wasm`, the package, the signature, golden files, replay files) MUST be written to a temporary file in the same folder and renamed into place, so an interrupt never leaves a half-written file. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |

| DEV-040 | `new` MUST require `--id`, `--lang` and one of `--template` or `--side`. With `--force` it MUST overwrite only files that the template writes and MUST leave every other file alone. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |

| DEV-043 | `new` MUST fail with `new.template-unknown` for an unknown template name, before it writes any file. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-044 | `new` MUST print one `progress` record with step `inventory` for each file it writes, and the message MUST be the relative path of the file. The watch set and its ignore rules are the ones of `dev`. | DEV-184 | The first install by `dev` MUST show the review dialog. A rebuilt manifest that adds grants MUST show the dialog again for the new grants only. `--grant-all` MUST grant every non-high-risk grant without a dialog. A high-risk grant MUST always ask. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-185 | `dev` MUST watch the project directory and MUST ignore `dist/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.ilium/`, `.git/` and the paths in `.gitignore`. | DEV-186 | A change that arrives during a build MUST be queued. When the build ends, `dev` MUST run exactly one more build for all queued changes. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-187 | On a successful rebuild, `dev` MUST reload each rebuilt side in turn. The server side reloads first, then every attached client side. Each reload deactivates the old instance with the reason `upgrade`, activates the new one with the restore bytes and prints one `reload` record. A failed rebuild MUST keep the running instance, print the compiler errors, and send no `deactivate`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-188 | When restore bytes exceed 1 MiB they are dropped and the `reload` record MUST have `restore_dropped` true and `restored_bytes` 0. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-189 | On Ctrl+C `dev` MUST deactivate the plugin with the reason `disabled`, uninstall the development copy, keep its data folder unless `--purge-on-exit` is given, restore any plugin that `--replace-installed` disabled, print `summary` and `result`, and exit with 130. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-190 | `logs` MUST print oldest entry first. With `--follow` it MUST print the entries in the file, then new ones as they arrive, until interrupted, and exit with 130. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-191 | `logs` of an id that is not installed and has no kept log MUST fail with `plugin.not-found` and exit 5. | DEV-195 | `log-level` with no argument MUST print the current threshold. | Id | Statement | Page | Testable how |

| DEV-200 | `check` MUST run exactly the install checks of [Packages and manifests](/pages/packages/), in the same order, with the same codes, and MUST NOT run any plugin code. | DEV-202 | Every `check` finding is an `error`, except `signature.absent`, `component.size-warning` and `check.stale-build`, which are `warn`, and `signature.fingerprint`, which is `info`. ## Conformance suite

| Id | Statement | Page | Testable how |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEV-600 | `--subject plugin` MUST run only the cases marked `plugin` in the catalogue below. It MUST skip cases that need a grant the plugin does not request, with the reason `grant-not-requested`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-601 | `--subject sdk` and `--subject host` MUST be refused with exit 2 and `usage.subject-unavailable` in a normal install. They are available only in the Ilium source tree, where the maintainer enables them with `ILIUM_CONFORMANCE_MAINTAINER=1`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-602 | The suite MUST print one `conformance` record per case, then a `summary` record. A `fail` verdict makes the exit code 3. A suite with only `pass` and `skip` exits 0. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the command and assert the exit code and the error code |
| DEV-603 | `--case <id>` MUST run one case. An unknown id MUST fail with exit 2 and `usage.invalid-value`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-604 | The case ids MUST be stable. A case MUST NOT change meaning. A changed rule gets a new case id, and the old id is retired in the retired list at the end of this page. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-605 | Every case MUST be deterministic. It MUST use the fake clock and the default seed. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-606 | One case MUST finish within 10,000 ms of wall time. A longer case is a `fail` with the message `case exceeded 10000 ms`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-607 | Durations in case expectations are fake-clock milliseconds, except the call time measured in fuel. A case that needs a deadline breach MUST use the built-in probe plugin `conformance-probe.wasm` with its fuel-burn import, never the plugin under test. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the deadline cases and read their duration units and plugin name |
| DEV-610 | The catalogue above MUST be the minimum. A release of the suite MAY add cases and MUST NOT remove a case without a retirement note. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-611 | Cases for the restart rule MUST use fake time. No case waits for real seconds. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-612 | A case for a limit MUST test the value just under the limit (pass) and the value just over (fail), unless the table says otherwise. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-613 | A `skip` MUST carry a reason: `grant-not-requested`, `side-not-built`, `subject-mismatch` or `needs-session`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-620 | A project case id MUST start with `PROJ-` so it can never clash with a suite case id. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-621 | `sample_batch(n)` MUST return `n` valid events for the grants of the host, using the fuzz generator with the host seed. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-622 | `assert_within_budget(host, kind, millis)` MUST compare the recorded time of the last call of that kind with `millis`. `kind` is one of `'event'`, `'render'`, `'activate'` and `'deactivate'`, and `millis` is an integer in milliseconds (Rust `u32`, TypeScript `number`). It MUST be skipped in native mode with the reason `needs-component`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-624 | `conformance::case` and `conformance.case` MUST pass a `FakeHost` for `manifest.json` in component mode with the default seed to the body. The body MUST NOT build its own host. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run a case and assert the host argument is for manifest.json in component mode |
| DEV-630 | `--conformance` MUST run in component mode only. It MUST NOT run in native mode, because the limits are not enforced there. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-640 | A `fail` record MUST carry `expected` and `actual` fields that describe the difference, as strings of at most 200 characters. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-641 | The `summary` record MUST list `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` and `duration_ms`. `passed` plus `failed` plus `skipped` MUST equal the number of case records. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-642 | Case order in the output MUST be the order of the catalogue on this page, area by area. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |
| DEV-643 | A case that cannot drive the plugin to the claimed state MUST be a `skip` with the reason `subject-mismatch`, never a `pass`. | [reference-conformance-suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/) | Run the case by id and assert the verdict |

| DEV-656 | The log rate limit is 200 lines per second for an ordinary plugin and 1,000 for a trusted T1 plugin. Lines over the limit MUST be dropped and counted. | DEV-764 | The exit codes MUST be those of [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/). A CI step fails on any non-zero code. | DEV-778 | A forked pull request MUST NOT receive the secret. GitHub and GitLab do this by default for forks. Do not enable secrets for forks. | [guide-ci-recipes](/pages/guide-ci-recipes/) | Run the pipeline or lint in a scratch project and assert the result |

## Documentation conventions

| Id | Statement | Page | Testable how |

| DEV-786 | A help topic MUST NOT exceed 20 KiB. `lint.help-topic-too-large` warns for a larger file. | [guide-plugin-documentation](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/) | Run the pipeline or lint in a scratch project and assert the result |

| DEV-788 | A help topic SHOULD name each command, setting and view the plugin adds, so a search in the help viewer finds them. | [guide-plugin-documentation](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/) | Run the pipeline or lint in a scratch project and assert the result |

| DEV-791 | Every command in `contributes.commands` MUST have a `title` in sentence case with no final period. | [guide-plugin-documentation](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/) | Run the pipeline or lint in a scratch project and assert the result |

| DEV-796 | Dates in the changelog MUST use `YYYY-MM-DD`. | [guide-plugin-documentation](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/) | Run the pipeline or lint in a scratch project and assert the result |

| DEV-820 | `trace` MUST need a session and MUST fail with `plugin.not-found` for an unknown id. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-821 | `--last` MUST default to 50 records. `--kinds` MUST accept a comma list of the kinds in the debugging tools page. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-822 | `--record <file>` MUST write a replay file of the recorded events and MUST print an `artifact` record of kind `replay`. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |
| DEV-823 | `--unredacted` MUST be refused with `trace.unredacted-denied` for a plugin that is not a `dev` install. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run the command in a scratch project and assert the output and exit code |
| DEV-830 | `profile` MUST default to `--duration 10`, MUST accept 1 to 600, and MUST print one `timing` record per export that ran, then a summary. | [reference-plugin-cli](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) | Run with --json and assert the records and their field order |

## Performance of tooling

| Id | Statement | Page | Testable how |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEV-850 | Tracing MUST add no more than 5 percent to the time of an event batch, and profiling MUST NOT change call time by more than 5 percent. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Benchmark on the build host and assert the target |
| DEV-851 | A native-mode harness test of one event batch SHOULD finish in under 10 ms, and a component-mode test in under 100 ms, on the build host, excluding the one-time load of the component. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Benchmark on the build host and assert the target |
| DEV-852 | `ilium plugin check` SHOULD finish in under 2 s for a package of 10 MiB or less, and `ilium plugin lint` in under 5 s. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Benchmark on the build host and assert the target |
| DEV-853 | `ilium plugin dev` SHOULD reload a plugin within 1 s after the build finishes, and the debounce of a change is 300 ms. | [performance](/pages/performance/) | Benchmark on the build host and assert the target |

## Decision codes

The tooling decisions that these requirements rest on are recorded in [Design decisions](/pages/design-decisions/). The code `D27` (registry publishing) governs `publish`, and the codes of the restart rule and of the limits table govern the harness and the conformance cases. A requirement that conflicts with a decision is a defect in the requirement.

# Requirements for events and intents

## Requirements for events and intents

Normative behaviour of event delivery, ordering, payloads, intents, the input journal and prompt events.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `EVT`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [EVT-001] | The host MUST deliver events to on-events in batches, in the order they happened, one call at a time per plugin side. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) emit three events in order -> one batch holds them in that order. |
| [EVT-002] | A plugin MUST receive only events for which it holds the grant and has subscribed. | [event catalogue](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#event-catalogue) | (event-delivery) subscribe without panes.read -> no pane events arrive. |
| [EVT-003] | An on-events call MUST finish within its deadline. A breach MUST trap and count as one failure. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) block 100 ms in on-events -> trap. |
| [EVT-004] | A full event queue MUST admit a drop-oldest event by evicting the oldest queued drop-oldest event of any kind, count it, and put an events-dropped event at the start of the next batch. When the queue is full, no drop-oldest event is pending and a never-dropped event arrives, the host MUST restart the instance as a failure, and the new instance MUST receive tree-changed for every node. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) overflow the queue with output matches -> events-dropped with a count appears first in the next batch. |
| [EVT-005] | pane-lifecycle-changed MUST carry pane, state and by, and MUST never be dropped. | [events](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#events) | (event-delivery) freeze a pane -> one event with state frozen and by set. |
| [EVT-006] | ui-action events MUST carry the widget key and an action value of the kind documented for that widget. | [ui action kinds and action values](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#ui-action-kinds-and-action-values) | (event-delivery) click a button with key "save" -> ui-action with key "save". |
| [EVT-010] | Every intent MUST be submitted as a submission in a return list of on-events. Intents MUST NOT be callable as functions. | [submissions and outcomes](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#submissions-and-outcomes) | (completion) return a send-input submission -> one request-result for it. |
| [EVT-011] | An intent whose shape is malformed MUST be the batch-level offender (the lowest index) and complete as refused(invalid-argument); every other submission of the batch MUST complete as refused(cancelled). An intent with a well-formed but invalid value MUST complete as refused(invalid-argument) alone. | [intent table](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#intent-table) | (completion) submit freeze-pane with a text node id -> refused(invalid-argument). |
| [EVT-012] | An intent that needs a grant the plugin lacks MUST be a batch-level offender when no shape offender has a lower index, and MUST complete as refused(not-permitted); every other submission of the batch MUST complete as refused(cancelled). | [intent table](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#intent-table) | (completion) submit freeze-pane without panes.lifecycle -> refused(not-permitted). |
| [EVT-013] | An intent for a node that no longer exists MUST complete as failed(not-found) or refused(not-found) as the table states. | [intent table](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#intent-table) | (completion) submit a pane intent for a removed node -> not-found. |
| [EVT-014] | The WIT outcome variant MUST contain ok, ok-node, duplicate, refused, failed, cancelled and ok-epoch. | [submissions and outcomes](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#submissions-and-outcomes) | (sync-return) build the WIT with the check tool -> the seven cases exist. |
| [EVT-020] | send-input MUST be refused with pane-not-ready for a restored pane whose process has not started. | [pane states after a restore](/pages/api-panes/#pane-states-after-a-restore) | (completion) send-input to a restored pane -> refused(pane-not-ready). |
| [EVT-021] | send-input and agent-action MUST carry a dedup key. A submission of either kind with no key MUST be a shape offender: it completes as refused(invalid-argument) and the other submissions complete as refused(cancelled). | [duplicate submissions and dedup keys](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#duplicate-submissions-and-dedup-keys) | (completion) submit send-input with no dedup key -> every submission completes refused. |
| [EVT-022] | send-input with journal true MUST write the journal entry before the keys reach the pane. | [uncertain input after a restart](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#uncertain-input-after-a-restart) | (log-line) restart the server between journal write and outcome -> input-uncertain on activation, no replay. |
| [EVT-030] | The settings-changed event MUST carry the changed keys and their new values, delivered once per debounce window. | [extended payloads of existing events](/pages/api-events/#extended-payloads-of-existing-events) | (event-delivery) change two values inside the window -> one event with both keys. |
| [EVT-031] | cli-cancelled MUST be a distinct event from a cli exit with a signal. | [extended events](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#extended-events) | (cli-exit) cancel a CLI call -> cli-cancelled and exit code per the CLI page. |
| [EVT-040] | A prompt sent by a plugin, a schedule or voice MUST fire input-submitted only, and not a user-typed prompt event. | [event catalogue](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#event-catalogue) | (event-delivery) a plugin sends a prompt -> input-submitted only. |
| [EVT-041] | A plugin MUST NOT see tree-changed for a node after its node-removed. The host MUST remove the node from pending tree-changed lists and discard pending coalesced events keyed by that node when node-removed is queued. | [event catalogue](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#event-catalogue) | (event-delivery) remove a node with a pending tree-changed -> no tree-changed after node-removed. |
| [EVT-042] | Events about the plugin own actions MUST be delivered unless the table marks them as suppressed. | [event catalogue](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#event-catalogue) | (event-delivery) set a title as a plugin -> title-changed arrives as documented. |
| [EVT-043] | A coalesced event MUST always merge with the pending event of the same kind and key, whatever the queue fill, and keep the newest payload at the position of the newest occurrence. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) send 2,000 screen-changed for one pane -> one queued event with the newest revision. |
| [EVT-044] | agent-activity-changed MUST be a never-dropped event. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) send 1,500 agent-activity-changed to a queue of 1,024 -> none dropped and the instance is restarted when it cannot fit. |
| [EVT-045] | events-dropped MUST be coalesced by (event, source), MUST never be dropped, and MUST sit at the head of the next batch. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) drop output-matched twice -> one events-dropped with one record whose count adds up. |
| [EVT-046] | The event_queue ceiling MUST be 4,096 for T1 and 1,024 for T2 and T3; a larger request MUST be clamped and logged. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (log-line) ask for 4,096 as T2 -> effective 1,024 and one clamp line. |
| [EVT-047] | After every activation of a plugin that holds tree.read, the first batch MUST start with exactly one tree-changed event listing every node in pre-order. Without tree.read nothing MUST be sent. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) activate with 3 nodes -> one event with 3 ids. |
| [EVT-048] | Events produced while a plugin activates MUST be queued and delivered after activate returns ok, and MUST be discarded without an events-dropped report if activate fails or breaches its deadline. | [how events are delivered](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#how-events-are-delivered) | (event-delivery) emit events during a failing activate -> no events-dropped on the next activation. |
| [EVT-049] | Pending tree-changed events MUST merge into one event whose list is the union of the node ids, in tree pre-order without duplicates. | [event catalogue](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/#event-catalogue) | (event-delivery) change nodes 5 and 3 in separate events -> one event [3, 5]. |
| [EVT-050] | A refused send-input attempt MUST NOT take a rate token. | [send-input](/pages/api-intent-send-input/) | (completion) refuse 25 send-input for pane-not-ready, then one valid -> accepted. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Requirements for extension points

## Requirements for extension points

Normative behaviour of extension points, hooks, collect points and the 66 core points.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `EXT`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [EXT-001] | A plugin MUST declare at most 16 extension points and at most 64 extensions. More MUST fail the install with manifest.extension-limit. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (install-error) declare 17 points -> manifest.extension-limit. |
| [EXT-002] | A caller MUST hold extensions.provide to own a point and extensions.contribute:<id> to contribute. Without the grant the call MUST fail with extension.not-granted and base code not-permitted. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) run-hook without the grant -> err not-permitted, message starts "extension.not-granted: ". |
| [EXT-003] | An extension code MUST be carried by a plugin-error whose code is the mapped base code and whose message starts with the extension code, a colon and a space. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) veto a hook -> message starts "extension.vetoed: com.example.quiet-hours: ". |
| [EXT-004] | A payload over 64 KiB MUST fail as extension.cap-exceeded with base code invalid-argument. A payload within the cap that fails payload_schema MUST fail as extension.schema-mismatch. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) 65 KiB payload -> cap-exceeded. 1 KiB payload of the wrong shape -> schema-mismatch. No handler runs in either case. |
| [EXT-005] | When a chain reaches 100 ms the handlers not yet started MUST be skipped as pass, and each skip MUST be logged with extension.chain-cap and MUST NOT count as a breach. A handler that started before 100 ms MUST run until its own deadline_ms. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (log-line) point with deadline_ms 50 and four handlers of 40 ms each -> handlers 1 to 3 start at 0, 40 and 80 ms; handler 4 is skipped and logged extension.chain-cap. |
| [EXT-006] | A contribution that names a version MUST be active when its major equals the owner major and its minor is at least the requested minor and at most the owner minor; for major 0 the minor MUST be equal; the patch MUST be ignored. A contribution without a version MUST match any owner version. Otherwise it MUST be dormant. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (event-delivery) owner 1.2.0: @1.0.0 and @1.2.0 active, @1.3.0 and @2.0.0 dormant. Owner 0.1.2: @0.1.0 and @0.1.9 active, @0.2.0 dormant. |
| [EXT-007] | Two extensions on one point with the same priority MUST run in plugin id order, then in extension id order (byte-wise ASCII comparison). A T1 contribution MUST run before a T2 or T3 contribution of any priority, unless the user order says otherwise. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (event-delivery) two handlers at priority 10 -> the lower plugin id runs first. A T3 handler at priority 0 runs after a T1 handler at priority 90. |
| [EXT-008] | A lower priority number MUST run first. The user order from the Extensions tab, stored as a list of (plugin id, extension id) per point, MUST win over priority and tier. Items not in the list MUST follow it in default order. An update MUST keep the stored position and an uninstall MUST remove it. The same order MUST apply to list on collect points. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (event-delivery) user moves handler B above A -> B runs first. A contributor installed afterwards runs after both. Update A -> position kept. |
| [EXT-010] | observe MUST call all handlers and ignore replies. The outcome MUST be ok. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (completion) observe hook with one replace reply -> ok and the reply logged as extension.reply-not-allowed. |
| [EXT-011] | transform MUST pass each handler the output of the previous one. take-reply MUST return the final payload only when at least one replace was accepted, and MUST return none otherwise. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (completion) two replace handlers -> second sees the first output. Two handlers that both pass -> take-reply none. |
| [EXT-012] | veto MUST stop at the first refuse. The outcome MUST be refused(conflict) with extension.vetoed. Without a refuse the outcome MUST be ok. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (completion) first handler refuses -> refused(conflict) and the second handler is not called. |
| [EXT-013] | first MUST stop at the first answer. take-reply MUST return the answer, or nothing when nobody answered. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (completion) no handler answers -> ok and take-reply is nothing. |
| [EXT-014] | A reply that the mode does not allow MUST count as pass and MUST be logged as extension.reply-not-allowed. A transform replace MUST be validated against payload_schema, and every field not listed in reply_schema.properties MUST equal its input value. A first answer MUST be validated against reply_schema. A reply that fails MUST count as pass, MUST be logged as extension.schema-mismatch and MUST count as a breach. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (log-line) refuse in observe mode -> pass and one log line. A transform replace that changes a field outside reply_schema -> pass and extension.schema-mismatch. |
| [EXT-020] | A handler MUST get deadline_ms of 5 to 50, 20 by default. A handler that times out, traps or errors MUST count as pass. A timeout MUST NOT veto. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (log-line) handler of 80 ms at the default -> pass and extension.handler-timeout logged. |
| [EXT-021] | A breach is a timeout, a trap, an error return, a reply over 64 KiB, a replace or answer that fails its schema, a CPU budget overrun, or a skip because the contributor's instance was busy. reply-not-allowed and a chain-cap skip MUST NOT be breaches. The counter is per contributor, point and extension id, and an accepted reply within the deadline MUST reset it to 0. The third consecutive breach MUST stop the extension until the contributor's instance restarts or the user presses Reset. The stop MUST NOT be persisted. The user MUST see a notice and a Reset button. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (log-line) three timeouts -> extension.disabled logged on the next run. Two timeouts, one good call, two timeouts -> still active. Restart the contributor -> active again. |
| [EXT-022] | A run-hook on any point already on the current chain stack, directly or indirectly, MUST fail with extension.reentrant and base code conflict. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (sync-return) handler of A runs B and B's handler runs A -> err conflict, message prefix extension.reentrant. |
| [EXT-023] | A payload, a reply and a chain result MUST each be at most 64 KiB, and an entry at most 16 KiB. A collect point MUST hold at most max_entries (at most 256) and a hook point at most max_handlers (at most 8). | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) register entry number max_entries + 1 -> quota-exceeded with extension.cap-exceeded. |
| [EXT-024] | A call to a point that is not declared by an installed and enabled owner MUST fail with extension.unknown-point and base code not-found. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) run-hook on "x/y" -> err not-found. |
| [EXT-025] | register and unregister on a point that is not dynamic MUST fail with extension.not-dynamic and base code unsupported. | [dynamic collect points](/pages/api-extension-points/#dynamic-collect-points) | (sync-return) register on a static point -> err unsupported. |
| [EXT-026] | The kernel MUST send the topic ilium.extensions/changed to the owner only, once per point, after any change to the active set (install, uninstall, update, enable, disable, register, unregister, user toggle or reorder, breach stop, Reset, dormant or active change). The payload MUST be {point} with the global point name. Changes within 50 ms MUST merge into one event. No grant is needed. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (event-delivery) a contributor installs -> the owner gets one topic and no one else does. Three registers within 50 ms -> one topic. |
| [EXT-027] | A contribution MUST be dormant when its owner is not installed, is disabled, or does not satisfy its @version. An inactive owner MUST NOT make it dormant. The install MUST NOT fail for a missing owner. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (install-error) install a contributor first -> succeeds, contribution dormant. |
| [EXT-028] | A handler MUST run on the side that owns the call and a contributor MUST declare it on that side. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (install-error) declare a client handler for a server point -> manifest error. |
| [EXT-029] | For veto, transform and first points the owner MUST hold the one action until the chain completes (at most the 100 ms cap plus one deadline) and keep serving other events. For observe points the action MUST NOT wait. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (event-delivery) a veto handler refuses after 30 ms -> the action does not happen. An observe handler of 30 ms -> the action completes first. |
| [EXT-030] | Install MUST NOT fail because a point is full. The active set MUST be the first max_handlers handlers (or max_entries entries) in run order, the rest MUST be dormant with the reason "point full (<n>)", and the owner MUST get ilium.extensions/changed after a recompute. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (event-delivery) 9 contributors on a point with max_handlers 8 -> the last in run order is dormant. |
| [EXT-040] | The core set MUST hold 66 points across 30 core plugins. Hook modes MUST number observe 5, transform 11, veto 10, first 1. | [hook modes at a glance](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/#hook-modes-at-a-glance) | (install-error) run the check tool over the core tables -> counts 66, 30 and 5, 11, 10, 1. |
| [EXT-041] | A point id MUST be <plugin-id>/<point>, where plugin-id is the id of this plugin or the id of a core plugin named in this package's replaces list; such names are accepted only for items listed in that core plugin's surface. | [core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/#core-extension-points) | (install-error) declare a point "tree" with no plugin id -> manifest error. A foreign prefix outside replaces -> manifest error. |
| [EXT-042] | Every core plugin MUST state whether another plugin may replace it, and its points, services and topics MUST be listed on the core points page. | [summary](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/#summary) | (install-error) run the check tool over the core pages -> every core plugin has a Replaceable value. |
| [EXT-043] | An entry field service MUST name a service with the contributor's own id as prefix that the contributor provides, otherwise the install MUST fail with manifest.extension-entry-invalid. The owner MUST be able to call it without services.use, with the 30 s timeout and 1 MiB caps. | [entry-bound services](/pages/api-extension-points/#entry-bound-services) | (install-error) entry names a service of another plugin -> manifest.extension-entry-invalid. (sync-return) owner calls the entry service with no services.use -> accepted. |
| [EXT-044] | on_failure (pass or refuse) MUST be allowed only on a hook point of risk high and mode veto or transform, final_check (boolean, default false) only on a transform point, and guard (boolean, default false) only on a contributor entry for a point with final_check true and a handler. Otherwise the install MUST fail with manifest.extension-point-invalid. A guard MUST be called once after the transform chain with the final payload, and any refuse MUST end the chain as refused(conflict) extension.vetoed. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (install-error) on_failure on an observe point -> manifest.extension-point-invalid. (completion) a guard refuses the final payload -> refused(conflict). |
| [EXT-045] | reply_schema MUST be required on transform and first points and MUST be refused (manifest.extension-point-invalid) on observe and veto points. | [hook modes](/pages/api-extension-points/#hook-modes) | (install-error) veto point with reply_schema -> manifest.extension-point-invalid. |
| [EXT-046] | The outermost chain MUST be depth 1. A run-hook from a handler at depth 3 MUST fail with reentrant, base code conflict and message prefix extension.depth-exceeded, MUST count as pass and MUST NOT be a breach. The inner chain MUST run after the handler returns, complete as request-completed at the handler's plugin, and not count toward the outer deadline. | [rules for payloads deadlines ordering and failure](/pages/api-extension-points/#rules-for-payloads-deadlines-ordering-and-failure) | (sync-return) run-hook at depth 3 -> err conflict, prefix extension.depth-exceeded, no breach counted. |
| [EXT-047] | register with a priority above 100 MUST fail with base code invalid-argument and a message prefix extension.schema-mismatch. | [functions](/pages/api-extension-points/#functions) | (sync-return) register priority 101 -> err invalid-argument. |
| [EXT-048] | run-hook above 200 calls per second on one point MUST return rate-limited with retry-after-ms. extension.depth-exceeded, extension.entry-rejected and extension.veto-overridden MUST be logged as listed in the code table. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-extension-points/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) 201 run-hook calls in one second -> rate-limited. |
| [EXT-049] | An entry's identity MUST be the contribution id (contributes.extensions[].id), given to the owner as ExtensionEntry.extension. Equal ids from two plugins MUST both stay. | [functions](/pages/api-extension-points/#functions) | (event-delivery) two plugins contribute id ocean -> list returns two entries with different contributor. |
| [EXT-050] | A command field in an entry MUST name a command declared by the contributor or one for which it holds commands.invoke, otherwise the install MUST fail with manifest.extension-entry-invalid. An entry that runs a program (worktrees/post-create-steps.command, progress/probe-kinds.command_template) MUST need a matching process.run grant of the contributor (manifest.grant-dependency otherwise). | [core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/#entry-rules) | (install-error) entry names ilium.core.fleet/broadcast without commands.invoke -> manifest.extension-entry-invalid. |
| [EXT-051] | A replacement's points item MUST match only with the same kind, the same mode and the same major version, and a services item only with the same method names and major version. Otherwise manifest.replaces-surface-incomplete MUST name the item and the reason. The surface MUST be checked again at each enable and after each Ilium update; an enabled replacement that no longer covers it MUST be turned off, the built-in plugin MUST come back and a notice MUST name the missing items. | [replacing a core plugin](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replacing-a-core-plugin) | (install-error) replacement point with mode veto for a transform point -> manifest.replaces-surface-incomplete. |
| [EXT-052] | Every core point MUST have a Side (server or client), Version, Deadline, Max and Dynamic value in the core points table. A handler declared on the other side MUST fail the install with manifest.extension-side, a handler MUST get the table's deadline, and register on a point whose Dynamic value is no MUST fail with extension.not-dynamic. | [all points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/#all-points) | (sync-return) register on ilium.core.smart-copy/recognisers -> ok. Register on ilium.core.tree/node-sorts -> err unsupported. |
| [EXT-053] | Several installed packages MAY replace one core plugin, and at most one MUST be enabled. Enabling another MUST ask the user and turn the previous replacement off. A replaces list with its own id or an id twice MUST fail with manifest.replaces-cycle, and more than 4 ids with manifest.schema. | [replacing a core plugin](/pages/extending-core-plugins/#replacing-a-core-plugin) | (event-delivery) enable replacement B while A is enabled -> prompt, then A is off. |
| [EXT-054] | Records written by a log-sinks handler during its call, and the host's extension.* records about log-sinks handlers, MUST NOT be delivered to log-sinks. Records MUST be batched: one chain per 250 ms with up to 64 records. | [diagnostics](/pages/core-plugin-diagnostics/#extension-points) | (event-delivery) a log-sinks handler logs at warn -> no new chain starts from it. |
| [EXT-055] | The chain on ilium.core.terminal/before-send-input MUST NOT run for keystrokes typed into a pane. It MUST run once per write that Ilium makes on someone's behalf (paste, dialog, broadcast, voice, plugin write-input). | [terminal](/pages/core-plugin-terminal/#extension-points) | (event-delivery) type 10 keys -> no chain. Paste once -> one chain with source paste. |
| [EXT-056] | A snapshot reply over max_bytes MUST be dropped, logged sessions.section-too-large and not stored. restore MUST be called after before-restore completes and before panes respawn, with 2 s per call. | [sessions](/pages/core-plugin-sessions/#extension-points) | (event-delivery) a section replies max_bytes + 1 -> not stored, log line present. |

# Requirements: kernel and host

## Requirements: kernel and host

This page lists every normative statement of the kernel and host lane. Each statement has a stable id `HST-NNN`, appears under the same id in the page named in the third column, and has a test method in the fourth. A test author cites the id in the test name. Ids are not dense: the blocks are HST-001 to 045 (architecture), 050 to 089 (runtime), 100 to 125 (IPC), 150 to 171 (helper), 180 to 216 (scheduling), 250 to 272 (rendering), 300 to 313 (budgets), 350 to 363 (telemetry), 380 to 388 (platform), 400 to 412 (errors and limits, owned by [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)), 450 to 457 (agent signatures), 470 to 478 (extension points and menu provider) and 490 to 494 (intents and tree). Unused numbers are reserved and have no requirement. If a statement and its page differ, the page wins and this table is regenerated.

## Words and ids

- **MUST** and **MUST NOT** are absolute. **SHOULD** and **SHOULD NOT** allow a stated exception. **MAY** is optional.
- Ids are fixed once published. A removed requirement keeps its id and is marked withdrawn. An id is never reused.
- Ranges: 001-049 host architecture and crates; 050-099 runtime and Wasmtime; 100-149 IPC; 150-179 sandbox helper; 180-249 scheduling, deadlines, cancellation and backpressure; 250-299 rendering; 300-349 budgets and benchmarks; 350-379 telemetry; 380-399 platform support; 400-449 limits and the restart rule; 450-469 detection loop; 470-489 hooks and providers across sides; 490-499 client-side tree and intent semantics.
- Test methods: unit tests in `ilium-plugin-host`, integration tests that start a host and plugin fixtures, conformance fixtures, IPC round-trip tests in `ilium-ipc`, benchmarks B1 to B24 with the thresholds of [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/), platform CI lanes, and manual checks.

# Requirements, lifecycle and operations

## Requirements, lifecycle and operations

This page lists every normative statement of the lifecycle and operations lane, one row each, with its test. The ids have the form `LIF-nnn`. Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

### How to read the rows

- MUST and MUST NOT mark a rule a host has to meet. SHOULD marks a rule to follow unless there is a stated reason. MAY marks a choice.
- An id is never reused. A removed rule keeps its number and is marked removed.
- Each row links to the page that explains the rule. The page is the source. This table is built from it.
- The platform is not implemented. A test is a description of how to check, written for the fake host and for a real host.

### Plugin states and transitions

| Id | Requirement | Test | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIF-001 | The host MUST give every installed plugin exactly one package state at any time. | list a plugin through every transition below and assert one state in `ilium plugin list --json`. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-002 | A stop by failure belongs to one side, not to the package. It is the instance state `stopped-by-failure` of that side, and the package state stays `installed-enabled`. A stop of the client side MUST NOT stop the server side. | trap the client side three times and assert the server side stays `active`. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-003 | A package with state `refused-at-load` MUST NOT be instantiated, and the refusal code MUST be shown in `disabled-reason`. | install a package whose api window the host does not support and read the list output. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-004 | `disabled-by-policy` and safe mode MUST NOT be written to `installed.json`. | start in safe mode, stop, start normally and assert the plugin is `installed-enabled` again. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-005 | An instance MUST be in exactly one instance state, and only the transitions in the tables below MAY occur. | a state-machine fuzz test drives random triggers and asserts every observed transition is in the table. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-006 | The host MUST NOT call `handler`, `views`, `renderer` or provider exports on an instance that is not `active`. | send an event to an instance in `activating` and assert it is queued, and an event to `stopped` is dropped. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-007 | Enabling a plugin that is `refused-at-load` or `disabled-by-policy` MUST return `not-permitted` with the refusal code in the message, and MUST NOT change any state. | call `set-enabled(id, true)` on a policy-blocked plugin. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-008 | A failure that moves the server side to `stopped-by-failure` MUST be written to `failure_stopped` in `installed.json`, so it survives a server restart. A client or scene side is not stored. | cause three failures, restart the server and read the list output. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-009 | Enabling, resetting failures or installing an update MUST clear the failure window of the sides it affects. | two failures, then enable, then one failure restarts after the first-failure delay. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-010 | A candidate whose first `activate` fails MUST roll back to the previous version, as P10 says, and MUST NOT leave the plugin in `update-staged`. A failure after a successful first activation MUST NOT roll back. | stage a version whose `activate` always errors and assert the old version is active. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-011 | The host MUST apply row I2 when the session memory pool cannot admit the instance, and MUST NOT count that refusal as a failure. | fill the pool with other plugins, trigger activation and assert the failure window of the refused plugin is empty. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-012 | A trap, an error from `activate` or a deadline breach in `activating` or `active` MUST follow rows I4 or I5 and MUST drop the instance without calling `deactivate`. | trap in `on-events` and assert no `deactivate` call is logged. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-013 | The host MUST apply row I14 when a plugin is disabled, updated or uninstalled while a restart is scheduled. | schedule a restart, disable the plugin and assert the timer never fires. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-014 | Rows I9 to I13 MUST send exactly one `deactivate` call per live instance, with the reason in the table. | for each row, count `deactivate` calls and read the reason. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-015 | A client or scene instance MUST receive `deactivate(shutdown)` when its client disconnects cleanly, and MUST receive no other reason. After a crash or a kill of the client process no call is possible: the server uses the last restore bytes it stored. | kill the client process and read the server log for the stored restore bytes. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-016 | The host MUST emit `plugin-state-changed` once per state change, in the order the changes happened, to every subscriber with `plugins.manage`. | record events through a full disable, enable and failure sequence. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-017 | `plugins.list` MUST return one record per installed plugin with every field of the `plugin-info` table, in table order. | install two plugins, disable one and compare the records with the table. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-018 | `enabled` MUST equal the rule above in every state. | parametrised over the eight package states. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-019 | `set-enabled(id, true)` on an enabled plugin and `set-enabled(id, false)` on a disabled plugin MUST return `ok` and change nothing, and no event MUST be emitted. | call twice and count events. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |
| LIF-020 | The host MUST serialise all transitions of one plugin id. Transitions of different plugin ids MAY run in parallel. | issue disable and uninstall at the same time and assert one runs after the other. | [Reference, plugin lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/) |

### Failure counting, restart and activation

| Id | Requirement | Test | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIF-025 | The host MUST keep one failure window for each combination of plugin id, side and scope. The scope is the session server for the `server` side, and one attached client connection for the `client` and `scene` sides. | attach two clients, trap the plugin twice on client A and once on client B, and assert that `failures-in-window` is 2 and 1. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-026 | Two clients MUST NOT share a window. Disabling the plugin by failure on client A MUST NOT stop it on client B or on the server. | as above, with a third trap on client A. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-027 | A window MUST be a sliding window of 10 minutes on a monotonic clock. A failure counts while its age is less than 600 s. | with the FakeHost `advance_clock`, trap at 0 s, advance 599 s and assert the failure counts, advance 2 s more and assert it does not. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-028 | The first counted failure in a window MUST schedule a restart after 1 s. | trap once and read `restart-at`. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-029 | The second counted failure in a window MUST schedule a restart after 5 s. | trap twice within 10 minutes. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-030 | The third counted failure in a window MUST stop that side with the instance state `stopped-by-failure` and MUST NOT schedule a restart. The package state stays `installed-enabled`. | trap three times within 10 minutes and assert no activation follows. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-031 | The host MUST NOT use any other restart delay. There is no step after the second, because the third failure stops the side. | after a stop, advance the clock one hour and assert the side is still stopped. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-032 | The host MUST NOT add random jitter. The delay timer starts when the instance is dropped. The next activation MUST NOT begin earlier than the delay, and SHOULD begin within 250 ms after it. | assert the begin time is in the range delay to delay plus 250 ms. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-033 | The host MUST count each kind in the table as the table says. | a parametrised test, one case per row, reading `failures-in-window`. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-034 | A refusal caused by host capacity MUST NOT count against the plugin. The instance stays `inactive` with the reason `host-capacity`. The host MUST retry the activation when pool memory is released, and in any case 1 s, 5 s and 30 s after the refusal, then every 60 s without end while the plugin is enabled. | fill the pool, trigger activation, assert `failures-in-window` is 0, free memory and assert the activation runs. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-035 | A failed job MUST NOT count. | trap inside a job and assert `failures-in-window` is unchanged. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-036 | Enabling the plugin, the command `ilium plugin reset-failures <id>`, the Enable action of the recovery page and installing an update MUST clear the failure window of the affected sides. | two traps, then each action, then one trap restarts after 1 s. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-037 | The instance state `stopped-by-failure` of the server side MUST be written to `failure_stopped` in `installed.json` and MUST survive a server restart. The failure window itself MUST NOT; it starts empty. The state of a client or scene side MUST be dropped when its client detaches. | stop the server after a stop-by-failure and assert the state after the restart; detach and reattach a client and assert the client side runs again. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-038 | When a server stop begins, the host MUST cancel all pending restart timers and MUST NOT schedule a new one. A failure during shutdown is logged and not counted. | schedule a restart, begin a stop and assert no activation. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-039 | When the user disables the plugin while a restart is pending, the host MUST cancel the timer and move the side to `installed-disabled-by-user`. | schedule, disable, advance the clock past the delay and assert no activation. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-040 | When an update arrives while a restart is pending, the host MUST cancel the timer, clear the window and activate the new version by its normal triggers. | schedule, update, assert the new version activates. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-041 | A revocation or grant while a restart is pending MUST keep the timer. The new instance MUST receive the current `granted` list. | schedule, revoke a grant, assert the restarted instance sees the shorter list. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-042 | An essential core plugin (see [Core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/)) MUST never be stopped by failure. Its third and later failures in a window MUST restart after 5 s and MUST raise the essential-failure banner. | trap `ilium.core.tree` three times and assert it restarts and the banner shows. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-043 | The enum `deactivation-reason` MUST have the six values above, and the host MUST send `crash-restart` never. | enumerate the reasons seen across a full lifecycle test. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-044 | A production update MUST send `upgrade` to every live instance of the old version before the swap. | update an active plugin and read the deactivation reason. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-045 | The host MUST compute the start order of `startup` plugins with Kahn's algorithm over the edges of the non-optional `requires.plugins` entries and of the `requires.services` entries to their providers. A provider's `activate` MUST return before any consumer that requires it begins `activate`. | three plugins, A requires B requires C, record the order of `activate.begin`. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-046 | At each step of that algorithm the host MUST take the ready node with the smallest key: the tier number (T1 first), then the plugin id in ascending byte order. | install T1 `b`, T2 `a` and T1 `a` with no dependencies and assert the order T1 `a`, T1 `b`, T2 `a`. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-047 | Independent plugins MAY activate in parallel. The host MUST run at most 4 concurrent activations per side, and MUST start them in the order of LIF-046. | 12 independent plugins, each blocking in `activate`, and assert the peak is 4 and that the begin order is the key order. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-048 | A cycle in the non-optional `requires.services` entries MUST be refused at install, at stage 10, with `manifest.service-cycle`. A cycle in `requires.plugins` is refused with `dependency.cycle`. The rules for both are in [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/). | install two plugins that require each other's services and read the code and the cycle order. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-049 | Dependencies are `requires.plugins` and `requires.services`. The host version is checked only through `requires.host`, which is refused with `dependency.host-version` at stage 10. A key named `engines` is refused with `manifest.unknown-key`. | install a manifest with `requires.host` above the running release, and one with an `engines` key. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-050 | On server stop the host MUST call `deactivate(shutdown)` in the exact reverse of the start order, one at a time, so that a consumer stops before the providers it requires. The order of completion of the starts does not matter. | record the order of `deactivate` calls after a start in which activations finished in a different order. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-051 | A consumer MUST stay active when its provider fails, is disabled or is uninstalled. | disable the provider and assert the consumer state. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-052 | The host MUST return the code in the table for a service call. | one case per row. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-053 | The host MUST send the event `service-availability-changed` (`interface`, `available`, `provider`) to every active consumer when the availability of a required interface changes. | disable and enable the provider and read the events. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-054 | When the user disables a plugin that is a provider for other plugins, the disable dialog MUST list the dependants, and the CLI MUST print a `warning` line for each dependant. The disable is not blocked. | disable a provider and read the dialog text. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-055 | The host MUST activate the owner of an extension point before its contributors. After the owner's `activate` returns, the host MUST activate in the background the lazy contributors of its points, so that a contribution needs no trigger of its own. | a lazy contributor to a hook point becomes `active` after the owner activates. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-056 | A hook call MUST NOT wait for a contributor that is not yet `active`. The host skips it, treats it as `pass` and logs `extension.contributor-not-ready`. | call a hook while the contributor is `activating`. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-057 | If the server and a client run different versions of one plugin, each side MUST keep running the version it has until it receives the change notice for the update. The host MUST NOT block messages between the sides. | update a plugin while a client is attached and assert both sides finish on the new version. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-058 | A client whose API version differs from the server's MUST be refused at the handshake with the message `api-version mismatch` naming both versions. | connect a client with a different API version. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| LIF-059 | The client SHOULD render its first frame when the essential client plugins are active, or after 1,000 ms, whichever comes first. Plugins that are not active by then continue to activate in the background, and the first frame shows a `starting plugins` mark. | delay a non-essential plugin by 3 s and assert the first frame appears within 1,100 ms. | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |

### Install, update, rollback and uninstall

| Id | Requirement | Test | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIF-065 | The host MUST write `installed.json` atomically: write a temporary file in the same directory, fsync it, rename it over the old file, then fsync the directory. | kill the writer at each step (fault injection) and assert that a reader sees the old or the new file, never a partial one. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-066 | The host MUST hold `installed.lock` while it changes the store or the registry. A second writer MUST wait up to 30 s, then fail with `install.locked` and exit code 4. | hold the lock and start an install. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-067 | The host MUST refuse a registry whose `format` is higher than it knows, with `install.registry-format`, and MUST NOT rewrite it. | set `format` to 99. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-068 | The host MUST NOT instantiate or run any code of the package before step 7 has finished. | install a package whose start function writes a file and decline the review; assert the file is absent. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-069 | A failure at any step MUST leave the registry byte for byte unchanged and MUST delete the staging directory and any new store entry. | inject a failure at each step and compare the registry hash. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-070 | An install MUST NOT require network access. | run the install in a network namespace with no interfaces. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-071 | Steps 2 to 6 MUST run in the order of the table, so that the cheapest checks refuse first and no prompt appears for a package that would be refused later. | a package with a bad signature and a bad manifest reports `signature.invalid`. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-072 | Installing the same id and version again MUST succeed without change when the manifest hash is equal, and MUST fail with `install.same-version-different-content` when it differs. | install a package twice, then a modified copy with the same version. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-073 | The first server to apply an update MUST decide it. After step 6, a failure on another server MUST follow the normal failure rule and MUST NOT roll back. | update with two servers running, fail the second server's activation and assert the version stays. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-074 | An update MUST be atomic: after any interruption, either the old or the new version is active, never neither. | kill the installer or the server at each step and assert that a plugin version is active after restart. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-075 | A failed activation of the candidate MUST roll back to the previous version and its data snapshot automatically. | install a candidate whose `activate` returns an error. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-076 | The host MUST keep exactly one previous version in `store/` and delete older ones after a committed update. | update three times and list `store/<id>/`. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-077 | A blocked candidate MUST NOT be tried again unless the user installs it again explicitly. | roll back, restart the server and assert that no activation of the candidate occurs. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-078 | An update MUST NOT send grants to the new version beyond those the user accepted. A new version that asks for more is `update-staged` until the review is answered. | update with an extra grant and decline. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-079 | Activating a version whose `data_version` is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope MUST be refused with `migration.data-newer` (stage I, exit 1), unless `--restore-backup` or `--discard-data` is given. This applies to downgrade and rollback. `--restore-backup` restores the data snapshot taken before the update and loses what was written since. `--discard-data` deletes the plugin's buckets and data directory. | update to a version that migrates data, write data, roll back without a flag and assert `migration.data-newer`; repeat with each flag | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-080 | `--restore-backup` MUST fail with `rollback.no-backup` when the snapshot is gone. | delete the backup and roll back with the flag. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-081 | Rollback MUST send `deactivate(upgrade)` to the running instances and activate the previous version with the same rules as an update. | read the reasons in the log. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-082 | Without a TTY, an uninstall with neither `--purge` nor `--keep-data` MUST keep the data directory and the buckets. | run it with standard input closed. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-083 | The host MUST delete grants, first-use answers, durable timers, failure counters and persistent decorations on every uninstall.
