| LIF-084 | Node metadata and session data of an uninstalled plugin MUST stay inert: the host never passes them to another plugin, and keeps them in the snapshot. A reinstall of the same id MAY read them again. With `--purge` the host MUST delete them in the live session and add a tombstone, so that other projects delete theirs when they next open. | purge, reopen another project and assert the keys are gone. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-085 | Uninstall MUST first set `uninstall-pending`, then stop all instances, then delete files. After a crash, the next start MUST finish it. | kill the host after the state is written. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-086 | Uninstall MUST NOT delete data of other plugins, and MUST NOT remove a publisher key. | compare the other plugins' directories before and after. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-087 | Every command MUST print only JSON lines on standard output when output is not a terminal, MUST use the exit codes above and MUST give each error line a `code` from this page. | run each command in a pipe and parse every line. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-088 | `enable` and `disable` MUST be idempotent: they exit 0 and print a `result` line with `changed: false` when nothing changes. | disable twice. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-089 | A server MUST watch `installed.json` and apply a change within 2 s of the write. If the watch is not available, it MUST poll every 5 s. The installing CLI MUST also send a `plugins-changed` message to every server it can find in the runtime directory; a server it cannot reach is reported as a `warning` line with `install.notify-failed` and picks the change up at its watch or at its next start. | install with two servers, assert both log `registry.changed` within 2 s. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-090 | A server that is not running MUST use the registry as it finds it at start. | install, then start a server and assert the new version is active. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-091 | A change MUST be applied to a server under the per-plugin serialisation of [lifecycle states](/pages/reference-plugin-lifecycle-states/). | install an update during a disable. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-092 | At start, and at the start of every `ilium plugin` command that takes the lock, the host MUST delete staging directories whose creating process is gone or that are older than 1 hour. | create an orphan staging directory and start a server. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-093 | A store entry with no registry entry and older than 1 hour MUST be deleted at start. A registry entry whose store entry is missing or fails its hash check MUST put the plugin in `refused-at-load` with `package.corrupt`. `ilium plugin reinstall <id>` MUST repair it from the cached package or fail with `package.cache-missing`. | truncate a file in the store. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |
| LIF-094 | After a power loss the host MUST find either the old or the new registry, because of LIF-065, and MUST finish or undo an `update` in `trial` by the rules above at the next activation. | kill the machine at step 11 (simulated) and restart. | [Reference, install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) |

### Data migration and storage

| Id | Requirement | Test | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIF-100 | The manifest key `data_version` MUST be an unsigned 32-bit integer. When absent it MUST be 1. A value of 0 or a non-integer MUST be refused with `manifest.data-version`. | install manifests with 0, 1, "2" and 4294967295. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-101 | The host MUST store the data version of each bucket and of the data directory in a place the plugin cannot read or write, and MUST stamp it only after a successful migration or on first creation. | read the stamp through the CLI `ilium plugin info <id> --json` after a migration. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-102 | The host MUST NOT migrate data it did not stamp itself. A bucket with no stamp (created before the plugin ever stored data) MUST be stamped with the current `data_version` at first write. | first `put` on a new plugin. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-103 | The host MUST drop restore bytes when the `data_version` of the running version differs from that of the version that produced them, and MUST log `restore.dropped-data-version`. | change `data_version` between two builds and read `restored`. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-104 | For each bucket, the host MUST call `migrate(from, to)` at most once per update, the first time a host instance activates with that bucket in scope and the bucket stamp is lower than `data_version`, with `from` less than `to`. The global bucket and the data directory migrate at the first activation after the swap. A project or session bucket migrates when its session first activates the plugin. | update from 1 to 3, open two sessions, and assert one call `(1, 3)` for the global bucket and one for each session bucket | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-105 | A call that returns an error, traps or misses the deadline MUST be a migration failure (LIF-108). It MUST NOT count toward the failure window of the plugin. | return an error from `migrate` and read `failures-in-window`. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-106 | `migrate` MUST be idempotent. The host MAY call it again with the same arguments after an interrupted run (LIF-110). | run the call twice on a fixture and compare the data. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-107 | The host MUST copy the global, project and session buckets in use and the data directory to `backups/<id>/<version>-<utc timestamp>/` before it calls `migrate`. The timestamp has the form `YYYYMMDDTHHmmssZ`. The host MUST refuse with `install.no-space`, before touching any data, when free space is less than twice the data size plus 100 MiB. The backup size is capped by the key `migration_backup_mib` in the `[plugins]` table of `config.toml` (integer 0 to 1048576, default 2048; 0 disables backups). Data above the cap is refused with `migration.backup-too-large` (stage I, exit 1) unless `--no-backup` is given, and then a failed migration cannot be undone. A copy-on-write copy MAY replace the full copy. | fill the disk and update; set the cap to 1 and update with 2 MiB of data, with and without `--no-backup` | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-108 | On a migration failure the host MUST restore the backup, keep the previous version active, log `migration.failed` with the plugin's error code and message, and mark the update rolled back. | fail `migrate` after it wrote half the keys, then compare the buckets with the backup. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-109 | After an update that succeeded and was activated, the host MUST keep only the newest backup of that plugin and delete older ones in `backups/<id>/`. | update twice and list the backups | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-110 | At the next start the host MUST restore the backup, increment `update.attempts` in `installed.json` and run the update again from the beginning. The host MUST write `update.state: "migrating"` and the attempt count with fsync before it calls `migrate`. When `attempts` reaches 2 it MUST roll back with `migration.interrupted` and mark the candidate `skip`. | kill the process in the middle of `migrate` twice and assert the rollback and `skip` | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-111 | The host MUST refuse to activate a version whose `data_version` is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope, with `migration.data-newer`. The user may run the command with `--restore-backup` (the host restores the backup taken before the update) or `--discard-data` (the host deletes the plugin's buckets and data directory). | roll back after a migration, with and without each flag. This is the same rule as [LIF-079](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/). | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-112 | A migration that touches the global bucket or the data directory MUST hold the cross-process lock `plugins/locks/<id>.migrate.lock`. The other servers MUST first deactivate their old instances with `upgrade`, then wait for the lock for at most the migrate deadline plus 5 s, and then skip the migration when they find the stamp already new. | update with two servers, count calls to `migrate`. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-113 | While the stamp of the global bucket is higher than the data version of a running instance, a `put`, `write-batch` or `remove` from that instance MUST return `conflict` with the message `stale-data-version`. | leave one server on the old version and write to the global bucket. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-114 | A project bucket and a session bucket MUST be migrated by the session that opens them, each with its own backup. | open two projects after an update. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-115 | `put` and `write-batch` MUST return only after the data is committed to stable storage with a flush, so that a power loss after the return does not lose it. | kill the process after a `put` returns and read it back. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-116 | If a plugin must change several files of its data directory, it SHOULD write a new set of files first and write a version marker file last, so that a crash leaves either the old set or the complete new set. The host does not give transactions for files. | kill the host between the two writes and assert the plugin reads the old set. | [Guide, data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| LIF-117 | `write-batch` MUST apply all its entries or none of them. A batch holds at most 256 entries and at most 4 MiB of key and value bytes together; more is `invalid-argument`. A refused batch keeps every previous value. | write a batch whose last entry breaks the quota and read all keys. | [storage](/pages/api-storage/) |
| LIF-118 | `put`, `remove` and `write-batch` MUST return only after the change is flushed to stable storage, so that a crash or power loss after the return cannot lose it. A crash before the return leaves the previous value. | kill the process in the middle of a batch and read back. | [storage](/pages/api-storage/) |
| LIF-119 | A write that fails because the disk is full MUST return `io` with the message `no-space`, never `quota-exceeded`, which is only for the plugin's own quota. | fill the disk and `put`. See [offline and low disk](/pages/reference-offline-and-low-disk/). | [storage](/pages/api-storage/) |
| LIF-120 | Several session servers can write the same `global` or `project` bucket. The host MUST serialise writers with a lock per bucket, so that each `put` and each batch is atomic across processes, and the last writer of a key wins. There is no compare-and-set; use a version key and `write-batch` if you need one. | two servers write the same key and read it back. | [storage](/pages/api-storage/) |
| LIF-121 | The bucket also carries a data version stamp that the plugin cannot see. A write from an instance older than the stamp MUST return `conflict` with the message `stale-data-version`. See [data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/). | see LIF-113. | [storage](/pages/api-storage/) |

### Health and watchdog

| Id | Requirement | Test | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIF-122 | The host MUST compute `health` from the first matching row of the first table, and MUST report it in `plugin-info`, in `ilium plugin status` and on the Plugins screen. | drive a plugin into each state and read the value. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-123 | The host MUST use the thresholds and time spans in the second table. | with `advance_clock`, produce 4 and then 5 near-misses and assert the change, and wait 5 minutes and assert the return to `healthy`. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-124 | A plugin that is stopped, disabled or dormant MUST NOT be reported `degraded`. | disable a degraded plugin. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-125 | The host MUST interrupt a call that runs longer than its deadline `D` at a time `t` with `D <= t <= D + 20 ms` of wall time measured from the start of the call, on a host that is not overloaded. | a plugin that loops forever; assert the trap time is in [D, D + 20] ms, and that a call that returns at D - 1 ms never traps. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-126 | The host MUST NOT interrupt a call before its deadline. | a call that takes 0.9 times `D` completes. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-127 | The host MUST NOT use fuel to enforce deadlines. | build the engine configuration and assert that fuel is off. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-128 | The tick MUST be 10 ms in every process and the instance deadline MUST be `ceil(D / 10) + 1` ticks after the call starts. | read the engine configuration. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-129 | Wall time spent inside a synchronous host call MUST count toward the deadline of the export that made it. Time waiting for an asynchronous request MUST NOT. | a handler that calls a slow synchronous host function (fixture clock) and a handler that waits for a request. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-130 | The host MUST complete all pending requests of a dropped or deactivated instance as `cancelled`, and MUST NOT call into the instance for them. | drop an instance with three pending requests and count outcomes. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-131 | A request that has no reply within its timeout MUST complete as `timed-out`. | a service that never answers. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-132 | A hung helper MUST be killed after 3 missed heartbeats or 500 ms past a deadline, whichever is first. | a helper that stops answering. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-133 | After a helper dies, the host MUST count one failure for the plugin that was running and none for the others, and MUST restart the others at once in a new helper. | crash a helper hosting three plugins and read the three windows. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-134 | The host MUST restart a helper after a crash at most 5 times in 10 minutes. After that, the T2 and T3 plugins of the session MUST move to `stopped-by-failure` on the server side with the reason `helper.unstable`. | kill the helper six times. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-135 | The host MUST keep the metrics above for each plugin and side, and MUST discard buckets older than 24 hours. | read the metrics after 25 simulated hours. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-136 | A server restart MUST reset the metrics. | restart and read. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-137 | `ilium plugin status` MUST print the health and the metrics of every installed plugin, as JSON lines when output is not a terminal. | run it in a pipe and parse. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |
| LIF-138 | The diagnostics report MUST contain a `Plugins` section with the health of every plugin that is not `healthy`. | degrade a plugin and generate the report. | [Reference, health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/) |

# Requirements for manifest and package

## Requirements: manifest and package

This page lists every requirement id of the form `PKG-nnn`. The ids cover the manifest, the package format, signing and trust, the registry, install and update, dependency resolution, the distribution commands, administration, publishing and the plugin store. The table is generated by a script from the definitions on the other pages. Do not edit it by hand. Each row gives the id, the statement, the page that defines it and how a test checks it.

Id ranges: 001 to 099 manifest, 100 to 199 package format, 200 to 259 signing and trust, 260 to 305 install and update, 310 to 360 dependency resolution, 361 to 422 registry, 423 to 446 distribution commands, 460 to 489 administration, 490 to 529 publishing, 530 to 559 plugin store, 560 to 589 manifest schema, 650 to 659 package lifecycle additions (signature document, registry signing and dependency cycles).

Count: 468 requirements. Duplicate definitions: 0. Cited without a definition: 0.

| Id | Statement | Page | How to test |
|---|---|---|---|
| PKG-001 | The manifest MUST be the entry `manifest.json` at the root of the package, at most 1 MiB, encoded as UTF-8 without a byte order mark and valid under RFC 8259. A source manifest in a project folder has the same form. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Assert code manifest.json |
| PKG-002 | The top-level value MUST be an object. A JSON array, string, number, `true`, `false` or `null` is refused. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Conformance test of the stated behaviour |
| PKG-003 | The installer MUST refuse this input with `manifest.duplicate-key`: no object may hold the same member name twice. The check applies at every depth and before any key is interpreted. It stops the validation.. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Review against the page text |
| PKG-004 | Comments, trailing commas, single-quoted strings and unquoted keys are not JSON and MUST be refused. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Conformance test of the stated behaviour |
| PKG-005 | Every key MUST be one the schema defines for that object. An unknown key is refused at every depth. The only objects that accept other names are the JSON Schema subsets (`arguments_schema`, `entry_schema`, `payload_schema`, `reply_schema`, `settings_schema`) and the `entry` object of an extension, w | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Conformance test of the stated behaviour |
| PKG-006 | `null` is not a value. A key that is not needed MUST be omitted. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Conformance test of the stated behaviour |
| PKG-007 | A number that must be an integer MUST be written without a fraction or an exponent (`10`, not `10.0` or `1e1`) and MUST be inside the range of its key. Numbers that are not integers are used only where a key says `number`. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Conformance test of the stated behaviour |

| PKG-014 | `id` MUST have 2 to 8 segments joined by `.`. A segment has 1 to 32 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, and does not start or end with `-`. The whole id has at most 128 characters. | PKG-017 | `publisher` is a display name. It MUST equal the display name stored with the signing key (PKG-219) for a signed package. It is not an identity. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Conformance test of the stated behaviour |

| PKG-026 | The installer MUST refuse this input with `manifest.schema`: `activation` entries follow [Activation triggers](#activation-triggers).. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | Review against the page text |

# Requirements for panes

## Requirements for panes

Normative behaviour of pane states, restored panes, lifecycle intents, restructuring and pane creation.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `PAN`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [PAN-001] | A pane process MUST be in exactly one of running, frozen, restarting, exited. Every change MUST be reported by pane-lifecycle-changed with pane, state and by. | [states of a pane process](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#states-of-a-pane-process) | (event-delivery) freeze, unfreeze -> two events with states frozen and running. |
| [PAN-002] | freeze-pane MUST move running to frozen. unfreeze-pane MUST move frozen to running. unfreeze-pane on a pane that is not frozen MUST be refused(conflict). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) unfreeze a running pane -> refused(conflict). |
| [PAN-003] | freeze-pane on Windows MUST be refused(unsupported). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) freeze on Windows -> refused(unsupported). |
| [PAN-004] | replace-pane-command MUST put the pane in restarting, keep node id, title, place and size, and end in running once the new process started. A cwd of none MUST keep the pane directory. | [replace the command terminate the process](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#replace-the-command-terminate-the-process) | (event-delivery) replace the command -> restarting then running, same node id. |
| [PAN-005] | terminate-pane-process MUST ask the process to end, wait grace-ms, then kill. The outcome MUST be ok when the process has exited. The pane MUST stay open and show the exit status. | [replace the command terminate the process](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#replace-the-command-terminate-the-process) | (completion) terminate with grace 3,000 -> ok and pane-exited; the node stays. |
| [PAN-006] | terminate-pane-process with grace-ms above 10,000 MUST be refused(invalid-argument). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) grace-ms 10,001 -> refused(invalid-argument). |
| [PAN-007] | A pane that exited MUST move to restarting with replace-pane-command. | [states of a pane process](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#states-of-a-pane-process) | (event-delivery) replace the command of an exited pane -> restarting then running. |
| [PAN-008] | For one node the event order MUST be pane-created, other events of that pane, pane-exited, then node-removed. A plugin MUST NOT see tree-changed for the node after node-removed. | [pane events](/pages/api-panes/#pane-events) | (event-delivery) close a running pane -> pane-exited, node-removed, nothing after. |
| [PAN-010] | A restored pane MUST exist in the tree with its saved title and size before its process starts. It MUST NEVER report a size of zero. | [pane states after a restore](/pages/api-panes/#pane-states-after-a-restore) | (sync-return) read a restored pane -> is-restored true, size from the snapshot. |
| [PAN-011] | An intent that needs a running process (send-input, signal-pane) sent to a restored pane MUST be refused(pane-not-ready). signal-pane to an exited pane MUST be refused(not-found). | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-panes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (completion) send-input to a restored pane -> refused(pane-not-ready). |
| [PAN-012] | is-restored MUST be false after the process starts. | [pane states after a restore](/pages/api-panes/#pane-states-after-a-restore) | (sync-return) read after pane-created and tree-changed -> is-restored false. |
| [PAN-020] | resize-pane MUST be refused(conflict) when the layout cannot give the size, and the message MUST name the neighbour. | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) resize beyond the neighbour minimum -> refused(conflict). |
| [PAN-021] | restructure MUST accept at most 256 operations. More MUST be refused(invalid-argument). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) 257 operations -> refused(invalid-argument). |
| [PAN-022] | restructure with a failing operation MUST be refused(conflict) with the operation index in the message, and nothing MUST change. | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) operation 3 of 5 fails -> refused(conflict) naming index 3, tree unchanged. |
| [PAN-023] | revert-restructure after a later change touched the nodes MUST be refused(conflict). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) revert after renaming a moved node -> refused(conflict). |
| [PAN-024] | rename-node with a stale expected-revision MUST be refused(conflict). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) rename with revision 3 when it is 4 -> refused(conflict). |
| [PAN-025] | set-inferred-icon over a manual icon MUST be refused(conflict). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) set inferred icon on a manually set icon -> refused(conflict). |
| [PAN-026] | open-external with a scheme other than http, https or mailto MUST be refused(not-permitted). | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) open-external with file:// -> refused(not-permitted). |
| [PAN-030] | create-pane with a cwd whose scope is not granted MUST be refused(not-permitted). With a cwd folder that does not exist it MUST be refused(not-found). With a program that cannot start it MUST complete failed(io). | [errors and edge cases](/pages/capability-panes-create/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (completion) cwd project/missing -> refused(not-found). command ["nope"] -> failed(io). |
| [PAN-031] | create-pane with command none and content-kind ilium.terminal MUST run the login shell from SHELL, or /bin/sh when SHELL is unset. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/capability-panes-create/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (screen-text) create with SHELL unset -> /bin/sh prompt. |
| [PAN-032] | panes.lifecycle MUST be a high-risk grant and every use MUST be written to the plugin log. | [errors and limits](/pages/api-pane-lifecycle/#errors-and-limits) | (log-line) freeze a pane -> a log line names the intent and the pane. |

# Requirements for pane primitives

## Requirements for pane primitives

Normative behaviour of the terminal, agent, editor and basic pane primitives.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `PRI`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [PRI-001] | A terminal read MUST need terminal.read-screen. read-cells MUST accept at most 1,000 rows per call and return quota-exceeded above that. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/primitives-terminal/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (sync-return) read-cells with 1,001 rows -> quota-exceeded. |
| [PRI-002] | history-text over 4 MiB MUST keep the newest 4 MiB. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) read history of 5 MiB -> 4 MiB, the newest. |
| [PRI-003] | send-input MUST accept at most 16 stages, a total stage delay of 10 s and 64 KiB of raw bytes. Above any of them it MUST refuse with invalid-argument. | [primitives terminal input](/pages/primitives-terminal-input/) | (completion) 17 stages -> refused(invalid-argument). |
| [PRI-004] | Check order for send-input MUST be: capability, stage and size rules, if-current precondition, then the lock. A failed precondition MUST refuse the intent before any lock is taken. | [capability terminal input lock](/pages/capability-terminal-input-lock/) | (completion) stale if-current on a locked pane -> refused(conflict) and the lock unchanged. |
| [PRI-005] | An input lock MUST last at most 2 s. There MUST be one lock per pane. A second lock MUST return conflict. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) lock a locked pane -> conflict. |
| [PRI-006] | A terminal output filter MUST accept at most rate_per_second matches per filter instance and pane. A match above the limit MUST be dropped and counted, not delivered. | [capability terminal output filter](/pages/capability-terminal-output-filter/) | (event-delivery) 500 matches in a second at rate 10 -> 10 delivered, the next batch starts with events-dropped. |
| [PRI-007] | A pointer claim MUST belong to one plugin at a time. A second claim on the same cell MUST return conflict. | [primitives terminal pointer](/pages/primitives-terminal-pointer/) | (sync-return) two plugins claim one cell -> the second gets conflict. |
| [PRI-008] | screen-changed MUST be delivered at most 10 times per second per pane. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (event-delivery) change a screen 100 times a second -> at most 10 events. |
| [PRI-010] | register-signature MUST return invalid-argument for a rule with a bad id, process names, aliases, icon, action count or key size, and conflict for an id the manifest already contributes. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/primitives-agent/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (sync-return) register a signature with an empty id -> invalid-argument. |
| [PRI-011] | A signature of the user MUST win over a plugin signature, which MUST win over a built-in one. An overlap MUST be logged as a warning. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/primitives-agent/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (log-line) two signatures match one process -> one warning, the user rule applies. |
| [PRI-012] | set-toolbar-state MUST return not-found for a button that is not the plugin own or a pane that does not exist, and not-permitted without the grant. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/primitives-agent/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (sync-return) set state for another plugin button -> not-found. |
| [PRI-013] | agents() MUST return an empty list when agent.read is declined. view, session and last_prompt MUST return none. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/primitives-agent/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (sync-return) call agents() without the grant -> empty list. |
| [PRI-014] | A transcript per call MUST hold at most 512 turns or 4 MiB. The oldest turns MUST be dropped. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) read a 600 turn transcript -> 512 turns, newest. |
| [PRI-015] | A pane MUST have no activity before its agent-identified event. A restored pane MUST report none. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/primitives-agent/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (sync-return) read activity of a restored pane -> none. |
| [PRI-020] | read-lines MUST accept at most 10,000 lines per call. Over that MUST return invalid-argument. | [limits](/pages/primitives-editor/#limits) | (sync-return) read 10,001 lines -> invalid-argument. |
| [PRI-021] | A plugin MUST hold at most 64 buffers. The 65th create-buffer MUST return quota-exceeded. create-buffer text MUST be at most 16 MiB. | [limits](/pages/primitives-editor/#limits) | (sync-return) create a 65th buffer -> quota-exceeded. |
| [PRI-022] | editor-apply-edits MUST accept at most 10,000 edits and refuse more with refused(invalid-argument). | [limits](/pages/primitives-editor/#limits) | (completion) 10,001 edits -> refused(invalid-argument) and the buffer unchanged. |
| [PRI-023] | An annotator MUST be called at most once per 100 ms per buffer. Extra calls MUST NOT be made. | [limits](/pages/primitives-editor/#limits) | (event-delivery) edit 20 times in 100 ms -> one annotator call. |
| [PRI-024] | Decorations or gutter marks MUST be at most 10,000 per layer; the session total MUST be at most 65,536. | [limits](/pages/primitives-editor/#limits) | (sync-return) 10,001 marks in a layer -> invalid-argument. |
| [PRI-030] | A basic pane MUST draw its body from views.render and MUST receive on-events like any plugin side. | [body and lifecycle](/pages/primitives-basic/#body-and-lifecycle) | (screen-text) open a basic pane -> the rendered body appears. |
| [PRI-031] | set-dirty with true MUST mark the pane as holding unsaved work, and closing it MUST ask before discarding. | [pane activity and dirty state](/pages/primitives-basic/#pane-activity-and-dirty-state) | (screen-text) set-dirty true, then close the pane -> a confirmation appears. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Requirements for rendering

## Requirements for rendering

Normative behaviour of frames, the frame budget, scenes, surfaces and the shared look.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `RND`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [RND-001] | The frame budget MUST be 1,000 ms divided by the effective frame rate, rounded down: 33 ms at 30 fps. frame_deadline_ms MAY raise it to at most 50 ms. | [api exports](/pages/api-exports/) | (trap) render 40 ms at 30 fps -> the frame is skipped. |
| [RND-002] | A frame that passes the budget MUST be skipped. Thirty breaches in a row MUST trap. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (trap) 30 slow frames in a row -> trap on the 30th. |
| [RND-003] | A render call that returns without present MUST drop that frame, and a warn line MUST be written once per second. | [surface rules](/pages/api-scenes/#surface-rules) | (log-line) return without present for 3 s -> three warn lines. |
| [RND-004] | write_rows MUST accept whole rows only: width bytes in gray8, 3 x width in rgb8, 4 x width in rgba8. A remainder MUST be dropped and a warn line written once per second. | [surface rules](/pages/api-scenes/#surface-rules) | (log-line) write width + 1 bytes in gray8 -> the extra byte is dropped. |
| [RND-005] | Rows at or past height MUST be ignored. | [surface rules](/pages/api-scenes/#surface-rules) | (screen-text) write row height + 1 -> no change on screen. |
| [RND-006] | write_cell_colors MUST be ignored unless uses-cell-colors is true. occupancy() MUST return none unless wants-occupancy is true. pointer() MUST return none outside the scene area or when wants-pointer is false. | [surface rules](/pages/api-scenes/#surface-rules) | (sync-return) call occupancy() with wants-occupancy false -> none. |
| [RND-007] | readiness that returns Failed, or stays Preparing for more than 10 s, MUST count as one failure. The host MUST stop calling render until the restart. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (restart-schedule) stay Preparing for 11 s -> one failure, restart after 1 s. |
| [RND-008] | reconfigure returning false MUST restart the renderer with the new spec and MUST NOT count as a failure. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (restart-schedule) reconfigure returns false -> new renderer, failure count unchanged. |
| [RND-009] | Settings that fail settings_schema MUST be refused before the scene sees them and the previous values MUST stay. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (event-delivery) change a value to an invalid one -> the scene sees no change. |
| [RND-010] | Revoking a grant MUST restart the renderer with the reduced grants and MUST NOT count as a failure. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (restart-schedule) revoke http -> a new renderer, failure count unchanged. |
| [RND-011] | A scene MUST follow the shared look: the host applies colour, palette, brightness, contrast, dithering and display controls per cell, and a scene MUST NOT add its own. | [renderer surface](/pages/api-scenes/#renderer-surface) | (screen-text) change the palette in Settings -> the scene colours follow with no plugin code. |
| [RND-012] | A scene MUST receive the current palette as palette_rgb (empty in greyscale and monotone modes) and MUST get set-palette when it changes. | [renderer surface](/pages/api-scenes/#renderer-surface) | (event-delivery) change the palette -> set-palette is called with the new 0xRRGGBB values. |
| [RND-013] | A scene failure MUST count as a failure of the whole plugin on that side. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (restart-schedule) trap in a scene frame -> the client side restarts after 1 s. |
| [RND-014] | A scene memory limit of 32 MiB MUST be the default, with ceilings 256 MiB (T1) and 128 MiB (other tiers). A breach MUST trap. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-scenes/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (trap) allocate 64 MiB at the default -> trap. |
| [RND-015] | views.render MUST finish within its deadline (10 ms by default, ceiling 20 ms). A breach MUST trap with ui.render-timeout, and the previous tree MUST stay on screen marked stale. | [traps](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#traps) | (trap) render sleeps 200 ms -> trap ui.render-timeout. |
| [RND-016] | write-glyphs MUST accept at most 131,072 cells per frame. Over that MUST return quota-exceeded. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) 131,073 cells -> quota-exceeded. |
| [RND-017] | A pre-rendered scene loop MUST be at most 30 fps, 3,600 frames and 128 MiB. Over that the install MUST fail with manifest.scene-prerender. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (install-error) a 3,601 frame loop -> manifest.scene-prerender. |
| [RND-018] | Decoration frames MUST be at most 16, each shown for at least 90 ms. Otherwise invalid-argument. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (sync-return) 17 frames -> invalid-argument. |
| [RND-019] | Plugin text MUST be sanitised before drawing: control characters and escape sequences are removed, TAB expands to the next multiple of 4 cells, and single-line fields turn CR, LF and CRLF into one space. The host MUST log at most one ui.text-sanitized warning per view. | [text sanitising](/pages/ui-model/#text-sanitising) | (screen-text) a label with ESC [31m -> shown without the sequence, one warning. |
| [RND-020] | The depth limit of a ui-tree MUST be 32 levels with the root as level 1. | [limits](/pages/reference-host-rendering/) | (trap) 33 levels -> ui.too-deep. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Requirements for requests and outcomes

## Requirements for requests and outcomes

Normative behaviour of submissions, request-ids, outcomes, dedup keys and the input journal.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `RQO`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [RQO-001] | Every submission MUST complete exactly once. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) submit ten intents -> ten request-results, one each. |
| [RQO-002] | A call that returns a request-id MUST complete once with a request-result and the matching request-id. | [two kinds of identifier](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#two-kinds-of-identifier) | (completion) start a slow call -> one request-result with that id. |
| [RQO-003] | Submissions of one batch MUST be applied in order. A later submission for a node an earlier one removed MUST complete as failed(not-found). | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) remove a node then rename it in one batch -> second is failed(not-found). |
| [RQO-004] | duplicate(original) MUST be returned while now_wall_ms - accepted_wall_ms < 600,000 for the dedup key, naming the ref of the first submission. Nothing MUST be applied. | [duplicate submissions and dedup keys](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#duplicate-submissions-and-dedup-keys) | (completion) submit the same key twice -> the second is duplicate and no second effect; at 600,000 ms the key is free. |
| [RQO-005] | ok-epoch(u64) MUST be the outcome of a send-input applied to an agent pane and carry the new prompt epoch. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) send-input to an idle agent pane -> ok-epoch with a number greater than the previous one. |
| [RQO-006] | cancelled MUST be used when the request stopped because the plugin stopped, the user cancelled or the host shut down. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) cancel a slow call -> cancelled. |
| [RQO-007] | A sibling of a refused submission MUST complete as refused(cancelled) and not as cancelled. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) refuse a batch of three -> all three are refused, siblings with code cancelled. |
| [RQO-008] | A completed result MUST be held for 30 seconds or until the first take. After that take MUST return none and the SDK wrapper MUST return not-found. | [limits](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#limits) | (sync-return) take after 31 s -> not-found. A second take -> not-found. |
| [RQO-009] | When a malformed submission and a missing grant exist in one batch, the host MUST run the shape check for the whole list before the grant check and report the lowest-index malformed submission. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) batch with both defects -> refused with invalid-argument and the index of the malformed one. |
| [RQO-010] | More than 256 submissions from one on-events call MUST trap. It MUST count as one failure, apply no submission and complete none. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (trap) return 257 submissions -> trap, none applied. |
| [RQO-011] | A refused batch MUST apply nothing, MUST reserve no dedup key and MUST log 'batch refused: submission <index>' with a 0-based index. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (log-line) refuse a batch -> the log names the index. The same keys are then usable again. |
| [RQO-020] | A dedup key MUST be 1 to 128 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : / -. | [duplicate submissions and dedup keys](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#duplicate-submissions-and-dedup-keys) | (completion) submit a 129 character key -> refused(invalid-argument). |
| [RQO-021] | A dedup key MUST be scoped to the plugin id and reserved for 10 minutes from acceptance. | [duplicate submissions and dedup keys](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#duplicate-submissions-and-dedup-keys) | (completion) two plugins use the same key -> no duplicate between them. |
| [RQO-022] | A retry of an accepted submission that failed MUST use a new dedup key. The old key stays reserved for 600,000 ms. | [the outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#the-outcomes) | (completion) failed(io) then retry with the same key -> duplicate. |
| [RQO-030] | The kernel MUST journal the keys of send-input and agent-action before it writes to the terminal, so a duplicate is caught after a server restart. A key never stays unusable for more than 10 minutes and input is never replayed. | [uncertain input after a restart](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#uncertain-input-after-a-restart) | (completion) restart the server and resubmit within 10 minutes -> duplicate. After 10 minutes -> accepted. |
| [RQO-031] | After a restart that interrupted a send-input the plugin MUST receive input-uncertain once and MUST NOT receive a replay. | [uncertain input after a restart](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#uncertain-input-after-a-restart) | (event-delivery) kill the server mid-input and activate -> one input-uncertain. |
| [RQO-040] | A hook run MUST complete with the outcome of the chain: a veto becomes refused(conflict) with extension.vetoed in the message. | [hook runs](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/#hook-runs) | (completion) a veto handler refuses a submission -> refused(conflict) and the message starts "extension.vetoed: ". |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Security and policy requirements

## Security and policy requirements

Every normative statement of the security pages with its id. The columns are: id, the statement (shortened), the page that explains it, and how to test it. A statement uses MUST, SHOULD or MAY as in RFC 2119 on its page; this table repeats only the subject. Rows whose test column names a fixture refer to the suite in [Security testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/).

### You will need

- The pages listed in the third column.

## Decision labels

| Label | Subject | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| D5 | Sandbox on Linux only; other platforms run T1 only | SEC-055, SEC-057 |
| D12 | `process.run:sh` is T1 only | SEC-031 |
| D23 | Consent for hosts from settings | SEC-074, SEC-312 |
| D25 | Origin consent for open-external | SEC-043 |
| G4, G5, G6, G8 | Review dialog, bundled consent, revocation, key trust | SEC-100 to SEC-124 |
| D16, D17, D20, D21, D22, D24, SE10, C38 | Cross-session, extension and replacement rules | SEC-286 to SEC-306 |

| SEC-327 | When a blocklist entry matches an installed plugin, the plugin is disabled at the next load, its data is kept, the user sees `Blocked: | [reference-security-response](/pages/reference-security-response/#sec-327) | Process review; safe-mode end-to-end test |
| SEC-328 | `ilium --safe-mode` without a value is `--safe-mode=third-party`. `ILIUM_SAFE_MODE` accepts `third-party`, `all-optional`, `1` (the same as `third-party`) and `0` (off); any other value exits 2 with `usage.invalid-value`. `--safe-plugins` is an alias of `--safe-mode=third-party`, and `--no-plugins` starts no plugin host. | [reference-security-response](/pages/reference-security-response/#sec-328) | Process review; safe-mode end-to-end test |
| SEC-329 | A persistent badge `SAFE` is shown in the status bar while safe mode is on. | [reference-security-response](/pages/reference-security-response/#sec-329) | Process review; safe-mode end-to-end test |
| SEC-330 | The server writes `safe-mode` to the audit log at start. | [reference-security-response](/pages/reference-security-response/#sec-330) | Process review; safe-mode end-to-end test |
| SEC-331 | An advisory in Wasmtime or a codec that applies to the pinned version is handled as in [SEC-171]: | [reference-security-response](/pages/reference-security-response/#sec-331) | Process review; safe-mode end-to-end test |
| SEC-340 | Each target below MUST exist in the repository, with corpus seeds and the stated invariants. | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-340) | Fuzz or probe suite run in CI |
| SEC-341 | Each fuzz target runs for at least 10 minutes in CI on every change that touches its code, and for at least 4 hours per target before each release. | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-341) | Fuzz or probe suite run in CI |
| SEC-342 | A fuzz crash, hang or invariant failure is a release blocker. | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-342) | Fuzz or probe suite run in CI |
| SEC-345 | A hostile test plugin (guest) and a hostile child program (started with `process.run`) MUST each attempt the actions below, and each attempt MUST fail with the defined result. | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-345) | Fuzz or probe suite run in CI |
| SEC-346 | manual | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-346) | Review dialogs at 48 columns |
| SEC-347 | Tests exist for: | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-347) | Fuzz or probe suite run in CI |
| SEC-348 | The hostile-input fixtures (archives, manifests, path corpus, spoofing strings, catastrophic patterns) live in `tests/security-fixtures/` of the repository and are released with the SDK. | [reference-security-testing](/pages/reference-security-testing/#sec-348) | Fuzz or probe suite run in CI |
| SEC-370 | Guest-visible clocks (`clock` and the virtualised `wasi:clocks`) for T2 and T3 plugins MUST be coarsened to 1 ms and jittered by up to 1 ms, to limit timing attacks. | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-370) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-371 | The `screen-changed` event for a pane is coalesced to 10 per second. | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-371) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-372 | Each T2 or T3 plugin side runs in its own helper, so Spectre-style attacks between plugins need a kernel exploit, not a shared address space. | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-372) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-373 | An error returned to a caller without the right grant MUST be the same for "plugin not installed" and "plugin installed but not granted" (`not-permitted`, reason `unavailable`). | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-373) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-374 | Errors returned to guests MUST NOT contain absolute paths of the host or ids of other plugins. | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-374) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-375 | Storage quota errors MUST NOT depend on the content of other plugins' data. | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-375) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-376 | Comparing the HTTP API token and the lock tokens MUST use a constant-time comparison. | [reference-threat-model](/pages/reference-threat-model/#sec-376) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-377 | Kernel security UI (review dialog, trust dialog, consent prompts, breach notices, recovery page, safe-mode badge) is always drawn on top of plugin UI. | [reference-extension-security](/pages/reference-extension-security/#sec-377) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-378 | Plugin toasts, tree chrome, palette entries, help pages and intent chrome are drawn in the plugin style. | [reference-extension-security](/pages/reference-extension-security/#sec-378) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-379 | A plugin cannot read or draw over the cells of a kernel dialog. | [reference-extension-security](/pages/reference-extension-security/#sec-379) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-380 | Every plugin-supplied text shown by the client (labels, titles, toast text, reasons, status segments, help text) is sanitised: | [reference-extension-security](/pages/reference-extension-security/#sec-380) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |
| SEC-381 | Display names are 3 to 40 characters, must not equal or start with `Ilium` or `Kernel` unless the plugin id starts with `ilium.`, and are checked at install (`manifest.display-name`). | [reference-extension-security](/pages/reference-extension-security/#sec-381) | Unit test with a spoofing corpus |

# Requirements for services and topics

## Requirements for services and topics

Normative behaviour of services, topics and peer messages.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `SVC`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [SVC-001] | A service call MUST need services.use:<name> and a provider MUST need services.provide:<name>. Without it MUST return not-permitted. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-services/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) call without services.use -> not-permitted. |
| [SVC-002] | A call with no installed and enabled provider MUST return not-found at once. | [errors and limits](/pages/services/#errors-and-limits) | (sync-return) call a service nobody provides -> not-found. |
| [SVC-003] | A call payload or a reply over 1 MiB, or one that fails its schema, MUST return invalid-argument. The provider MUST NOT be called for a bad payload. | [errors and limits](/pages/services/#errors-and-limits) | (sync-return) 1 MiB + 1 payload -> invalid-argument, provider log empty. |
| [SVC-004] | A method not in the provider schema MUST return unsupported. | [errors and limits](/pages/services/#errors-and-limits) | (sync-return) call method "x" -> unsupported. |
| [SVC-005] | A caller MUST be limited to 64 pending requests. The 65th call MUST return busy. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-services/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) 65 open calls -> busy. |
| [SVC-006] | A provider is compatible when the major version equals the required one and the minor is at least the required one. For major 0 the minor MUST be equal and the patch MUST be ignored. | [names versions and grants](/pages/services/#names-versions-and-grants) | (event-delivery) require 0.1.0, provide 1.0.0 -> consumer stays inactive. Provide 0.1.5 -> activates. |
| [SVC-007] | No reply within 30 seconds MUST complete the call as failed(timed-out). | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-services/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (completion) provider never replies -> failed(timed-out) at 30 s. |
| [SVC-008] | A provider that stops, restarts or is disabled before answering MUST make its pending callers complete as failed(cancelled). | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-services/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (completion) kill the provider mid-call -> failed(cancelled). |
| [SVC-009] | A reply that fails the result schema MUST complete the caller as failed(invalid-argument) and the provider MUST log an error. | [errors and limits](/pages/services/#errors-and-limits) | (completion) reply a number where a string is required -> failed(invalid-argument). |
| [SVC-010] | take-reply MUST return the JSON once. A second take MUST return none. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-services/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) take twice -> second is none. |
| [SVC-011] | A reply after 30 seconds MUST return not-found. | [edge cases and error codes](/pages/api-services/#edge-cases-and-error-codes) | (sync-return) reply at 31 s -> not-found. |
| [SVC-012] | Activation of a consumer MUST wait for a compatible provider. | [activation order](/pages/services/#activation-order) | (event-delivery) install the consumer first -> it activates after the provider. |
| [SVC-013] | Plugin-defined services are unstable in 0.1. A consumer MUST be updated together with its provider when the service API changes. | [names versions and grants](/pages/services/#names-versions-and-grants) | (event-delivery) bump a provider to a new service API version -> the old consumer goes inactive until updated. |
| [SVC-014] | A provider MUST have at most 64 calls in flight. The 65th MUST return busy at the call. | [errors and limits](/pages/services/#errors-and-limits) | (sync-return) 65 concurrent calls to one provider -> busy. |
| [SVC-020] | A plugin MUST publish only topics that start with its own plugin id and a slash. Another prefix MUST return not-permitted. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (sync-return) publish "other.x/y" -> not-permitted. |
| [SVC-021] | A topic not declared in contributes.topics.publishes MUST return invalid-argument. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (sync-return) publish an undeclared topic -> invalid-argument. |
| [SVC-022] | A topic name over 128 characters, or a payload that is not JSON or is over 64 KiB, MUST return invalid-argument. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (sync-return) 65 KiB payload -> invalid-argument. |
| [SVC-023] | More than 100 publishes per second per plugin MUST return rate-limited with retry-after-ms. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (sync-return) 101 publishes in a second -> rate-limited. |
| [SVC-024] | A subscription pattern MUST be an exact topic, a prefix with /*, or a bare *. A star in any other position MUST be invalid. | [topic names and patterns](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#topic-names-and-patterns) | (install-error) subscribe "a*b" -> a manifest error naming the pattern. |
| [SVC-025] | A subscriber without the grant MUST receive no events and no error. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (event-delivery) subscribe without the grant -> nothing arrives. |
| [SVC-026] | A full queue for topic-published MUST drop the oldest event and count it. A full queue for message MUST NOT drop and MUST restart the plugin. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (event-delivery) overflow each queue -> events-dropped for topics, a restart for messages. |
| [SVC-027] | A message to a peer without messages.peer:<plugin-id> MUST complete as refused(not-permitted). To a plugin not installed or disabled MUST complete as refused(not-found). | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (completion) message a disabled plugin -> refused(not-found). |
| [SVC-028] | A message channel MUST match [a-z0-9.-] and be at most 64 characters. A payload MUST be at most 1 MiB. Otherwise refused(invalid-argument). | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (completion) channel "Bad Name" -> refused(invalid-argument). |
| [SVC-029] | A message to an installed plugin that is not active MUST activate it and deliver after activate. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (event-delivery) message a dormant plugin -> it activates, then gets the message. |
| [SVC-030] | When the receiver queue of a message is full and holds no drop-oldest event to evict, the message intent MUST complete refused(busy) and queue nothing, and the receiver MUST NOT be restarted. An accepted message MUST NOT be dropped. | [messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/) | (completion) fill a receiver queue with never-dropped events, send a message -> refused(busy), receiver still active. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Requirements for settings

## Requirements for settings

Normative behaviour of settings tabs, sections, rows, values, validation and saving.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `SET`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [SET-001] | A plugin MUST have at most 2 settings tabs, 8 sections per tab, 24 rows per section (a group counts as one row plus its children) and 12 children per group. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (install-error) 25 rows in a section -> manifest.settings-limit. |
| [SET-002] | A plugin MUST have at most 128 value keys. A value key MUST be unique inside the plugin. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (install-error) two rows with key "a" -> manifest.settings-key-clash. |
| [SET-003] | Tab, section and row titles MUST be at most 32, 40 and 48 characters. A description MUST be at most 200, info text 120, a button label 20. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (install-error) a 49 character row title -> manifest.settings-limit. |
| [SET-004] | A first-party plugin (limits_tier first-party) MAY raise the settings caps. Others MUST NOT. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (install-error) 9 tabs as T2 -> manifest.settings-limit. |
| [SET-005] | Plugin sections beyond 6 in one built-in tab MUST be dropped with settings.section-dropped. Plugin tabs beyond 16 in the rail MUST be dropped with settings.tab-dropped. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (load-warning) 7 plugin sections in one tab -> one is dropped and the warning is shown. |
| [SET-010] | Every default and option MUST be checked at install. | [validation and saving](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#validation-and-saving) | (install-error) a number default above max -> a manifest.settings-* error naming the JSON path. |
| [SET-011] | A stored value that no longer matches its row MUST be ignored and the default MUST apply. | [validation and saving](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#validation-and-saving) | (event-delivery) restore a stored value 99 with max 10 -> the value read is the default. |
| [SET-020] | The host MUST NOT clamp a stored value. A number typed outside min and max MUST be refused with the row note and the stored value MUST stay. The stepper MUST stop at the bounds. | [validation and saving](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#validation-and-saving) | (screen-text) type 99 in a number with max 10 -> the row note shows and the stored value is unchanged. |
| [SET-021] | Saving MUST run in this order: schema check, settings-validate, the write, settings-changed. | [validation and saving](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#validation-and-saving) | (event-delivery) save a valid value -> the plugin sees settings-validate before settings-changed. |
| [SET-022] | A settings-validate answer MUST arrive within 100 ms. On timeout the save MUST be refused. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (completion) answer in 150 ms -> save refused and the old value stays. |
| [SET-023] | Toggle, choice and dialog confirm MUST be written at once. Number steps and typed numbers or text MUST be written 600 ms after the last change or after debounce_ms. A text-area MUST be written 1 s after the last keystroke. | [validation and saving](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#validation-and-saving) | (event-delivery) type three characters in 300 ms -> one settings-changed, 600 ms after the last. |
| [SET-024] | A text value MUST be at most 4,096 characters, a text-area value 65,536, and all values of one plugin 256 KiB. Above that save MUST fail with invalid-argument. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (sync-return) set-json with 300 KiB -> invalid-argument. |
| [SET-031] | set-json MUST write at once. | [validation and saving](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#validation-and-saving) | (event-delivery) set-json -> settings-changed without delay. |
| [SET-050] | The calls set-info, set-choices, set-row-note, set-row-state, set-item-states, set-choice-items, set-info-rich and set-meter MUST be limited to 10 per second per plugin together. A call over the rate MUST return rate-limited and the previous state MUST stay. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (sync-return) 11 calls in a second -> the 11th returns rate-limited. |
| [SET-051] | set-info and set-row-note text MUST be at most 120 characters. Longer MUST return invalid-argument. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (sync-return) 121 characters -> invalid-argument. |
| [SET-060] | A choice or list MUST have at most 64 options or items; a map at most 64 entries; a meter at most 8 segments; a notice text at most 200 characters. | [limits](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#limits) | (install-error) 65 options -> manifest.settings-limit. |
| [SET-061] | A row whose depends_on names a missing key MUST fail with manifest.settings-depends. | [error codes](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#error-codes) | (install-error) depends_on "nope" -> manifest.settings-depends. |
| [SET-062] | A row key that is not a valid key MUST fail with manifest.settings-key. | [error codes](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#error-codes) | (install-error) key "A b" -> manifest.settings-key. |
| [SET-063] | A button command, glyph, help id or tab anchor that does not exist MUST fail with manifest.settings-command, settings-glyph, settings-help or settings-tab-anchor. | [error codes](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#error-codes) | (install-error) a button naming an unknown command -> manifest.settings-command. |
| [SET-064] | A settings schema that uses a keyword outside the supported subset MUST fail with manifest.schema-keyword. | [error codes](/pages/reference-settings-schema/#error-codes) | (install-error) use "oneOf" in a schema -> manifest.schema-keyword. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)
