# User and administrator requirements

## User and administrator requirements

This page collects every requirement of the user and administrator documentation, one row for each id. Each requirement has a test. The ids are written `[USR-nnn]` where the page states the rule, and each row here links to that page.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. The platform is not implemented yet, so every row describes behaviour that the platform must have.

### You will need

- The [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/) page, for the words used here.
- The [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/) for the policy rows.

### Id ranges

| Range | Subject | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| USR-001 to USR-003 | Overview promises | [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/) |
| USR-010 to USR-014 | Install and manage | [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-020 to USR-022, USR-080 to USR-088 | Permissions in plain words | [Permissions explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-030 to USR-033, USR-100, USR-101 | Troubleshooting, safe mode, logs | [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-040 to USR-043 | Core plugins | [Core plugins for users](/pages/user-core-plugins/) |
| USR-050 to USR-054 | Extensions tab | [Extensions tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/) |
| USR-060 to USR-062, USR-102, USR-103 | Privacy | [Plugin privacy](/pages/user-privacy/) |
| USR-070 to USR-073 | Administration | [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/) |
| USR-110 | FAQ | [Plugin FAQ](/pages/user-faq/) |
| USR-120 to USR-129 | Update, trust and keys | [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/), [Packages](/pages/packages/) |
| USR-130 | Failure notice N14 | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| USR-140 to USR-143, USR-172 | Uninstall and its effects | [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/), [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| USR-160 to USR-164 | Recovery page and Plugins tab | [Settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/), [Settings plugin](/pages/core-plugin-settings/) |
| USR-170, USR-171, USR-173 | Install check order and update | [Security](/pages/security/), [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| USR-200 to USR-209 | Files on disk | [Plugin files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-210 to USR-220 | Policy file and audit log | [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |

### Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Test | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| USR-001 | The user documentation MUST state that all 30 core plugins ship with Ilium and need no install. | search the page for the count 30 and the phrase "ship with Ilium". | [user-plugins-overview](/pages/user-plugins-overview/) |
| USR-002 | Ilium MUST NOT fetch, list, recommend or update plugins from the network on its own. | run Ilium with all network traffic logged for one hour with two plugins installed and assert that no request is made for a plugin package or a plugin list. | [user-plugins-overview](/pages/user-plugins-overview/) |
| USR-003 | Ilium MUST show every grant a plugin requests before the plugin runs, and a grant the user does not give MUST stay locked. | install a plugin that requests five grants, leave two unchecked, and assert that calls that need those two return `not-permitted`. | [user-plugins-overview](/pages/user-plugins-overview/) |
| USR-010 | Installing MUST NOT run any code of the package before the user has answered the permission review. | install a package whose start function writes a file, decline the review, and assert that the file does not exist. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-011 | A failed install MUST leave the installed plugins and their settings unchanged and MUST print one error that names the failed check. | install a package with a bad file hash, list plugins before and after, and compare. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-012 | The review dialog MUST list every requested permission, MUST start HIGH rows unchecked, and MUST record exactly the checked rows. | install a package with three normal and two HIGH rows, accept the defaults, and assert that the grant file holds three granted and two declined entries. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-013 | The plugin MUST be on after a successful install, unless the user chose to leave it off. | install, then run `ilium plugin list` and assert the state. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-014 | The first-start prompt MUST appear at most once per start, MUST NOT block other plugins, and after Not now MUST appear at most 3 more times in total. | answer Not now at four consecutive starts and assert that the fifth start shows no prompt. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-020 | A permission MUST apply to one plugin and one side, MUST be stored per user, and MUST NOT be shared through a project folder. | grant a permission to the client side only, then call it from the server side and assert `not-permitted`. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-021 | A plugin MUST NOT obtain a permission that its manifest does not list. | call a host function whose permission is not in the manifest and assert that the call traps with `host.capability-not-requested`. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-022 | The review dialog MUST start every HIGH row unchecked and every normal row checked. | open the dialog for a package with both and assert the initial states. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-030 | Safe mode MUST switch off every T2 and T3 plugin for the run, MUST leave core and bundled plugins on, and MUST NOT write the state to the registry. | start in safe mode, stop, start normally and assert every plugin is as before. | [user-troubleshooting](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-031 | Safe mode MUST show a banner on every screen and MUST label every third-party row as off with the reason `safe-mode`. | render the tree and the Plugins tab in safe mode. | [user-troubleshooting](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-032 | The recovery page MUST stay reachable when the Settings plugin is off or failed, and MUST NOT be replaceable by a plugin. | turn off `ilium.core.settings`, open the recovery page, and re-enable it. | [user-troubleshooting](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-033 | Forget settings MUST delete only that plugin's settings values and MUST NOT delete permissions or data. | set a value, forget, and compare the grant file and data folder. | [user-troubleshooting](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-040 | The Plugins tab and `ilium plugin list` MUST list all 30 core plugins with the tier T1, and MUST NOT offer to install or uninstall one. | list plugins on a fresh profile, count 30 rows with ids `ilium.core.*`, and try `ilium plugin uninstall ilium.core.tree`, which must fail with `plugin.not-removable`. | [user-core-plugins](/pages/user-core-plugins/) |
| USR-041 | The Plugins tab MUST refuse to turn off a core plugin marked "no" in the table, and MUST say why. | press Space on `ilium.core.tree` and assert the refusal text. (Pending decision: the set of "no" plugins.) | [user-core-plugins](/pages/user-core-plugins/) |
| USR-042 | A request to replace `ilium.core.settings` or `ilium.core.sessions` MUST fail at install with `manifest.replaces-not-replaceable`. | install a package with such a `replaces` entry. | [user-core-plugins](/pages/user-core-plugins/) |
| USR-043 | Ilium MUST ask the user to confirm every `replaces` entry at install, MUST allow at most 4 entries, and MUST NOT replace without a yes. | install a package with 5 entries and assert the install is refused; with 1 entry assert the prompt and the choice Install without. | [user-core-plugins](/pages/user-core-plugins/) |
| USR-050 | The Extensions tab MUST list contributors of each point in run order, MUST let the user move a contributor up or down, and the user's order MUST win over priority. | set priorities 10 and 20, move the second above the first, call the point, and assert the new order. | [user-extensions-tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/) |
| USR-051 | The host, not the plugin, MUST store the user's order and the toggles, and MUST keep them across restarts. | reorder, restart, list. | [user-extensions-tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/) |
| USR-052 | A hook that times out, traps or errors MUST count as "no change", and a timeout MUST NOT block or veto. | let a veto handler sleep past its deadline and assert the action goes ahead. | [user-extensions-tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/) |
| USR-053 | Three breaches in a row MUST stop the extension, MUST show a notice and a Reset button, and the stop MUST NOT be written to disk. | cause three breaches, restart the contributor, and assert the extension is active again. | [user-extensions-tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/) |
| USR-054 | An extension whose owner is missing or off MUST show "waiting for <owner>" and MUST become active when the owner returns. | remove the owner, check the label, reinstall. | [user-extensions-tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/) |
| USR-060 | Ilium MUST NOT send the list of installed plugins, plugin use, plugin logs or plugin errors to any remote party. | run Ilium for one hour with five plugins and request logging, and assert that no request carries a plugin id. | [user-privacy](/pages/user-privacy/) |
| USR-061 | A plugin MUST NOT read terminal text, history, agent prompts, transcripts, the clipboard, audio or location without the matching grant. | for each item call the function without the grant and assert `not-permitted`. | [user-privacy](/pages/user-privacy/) |
| USR-062 | Install, verify, update, uninstall and list MUST NOT use the network. | run each in a network namespace without interfaces and assert success. | [user-privacy](/pages/user-privacy/) |
| USR-070 | A policy MUST only restrict. No key of the policy MAY enable a plugin, grant or tier that Ilium refuses without a policy. | set `allowed_tiers = ["T3"]` on Windows and assert that T3 is still refused. | [guide-administration](/pages/guide-administration/) |
| USR-071 | A non-interactive install without `--yes` MUST fail with `install.review-required`, and `--yes` MUST NOT grant a HIGH permission that is not named. | install a package with one HIGH row with `--yes` and assert that the row is declined. | [guide-administration](/pages/guide-administration/) |
| USR-072 | An administrator MUST be able to block a running plugin by id, and the host MUST disable it at the next server start. | add the id while the plugin runs, restart the server and assert the state `Blocked by policy`. | [guide-administration](/pages/guide-administration/) |
| USR-073 | The documentation MUST state that the policy only restricts, where the file lives per system, and how to respond to a bad plugin. | search this page for the three statements. | [guide-administration](/pages/guide-administration/) |
| USR-080 | The Capabilities tab MUST show the plain wording, the grant string, the risk and the state (granted, declined, revoked) of every permission the plugin requests. | open the tab for a plugin with ten requested grants and compare. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-081 | A package that requests a bundled-only grant MUST fail to install with `manifest.grant-tier`. | request `plugins.manage` in a T2 package. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-082 | A grant string MUST be shown exactly as it will be matched, including its argument, so that the user can see the host, program or place. | request `http:api.example.com` and assert the dialog shows that string. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-083 | Ilium MUST ask the user before it opens a link from a plugin, for each target website and plugin, and MUST remember the answer. | open two links to the same site and one to another site and count prompts: two. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-084 | Ilium MUST NOT contact a host from a `http:setting` grant until the user has confirmed that host. | set a new host in a setting, call, and assert no connection before the answer. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-085 | A revoke MUST take effect for calls started after it, MUST make calls in flight return `revoked`, and MUST restart the plugin with the smaller set. | start a long call, revoke, and assert `revoked` and a restart in the log. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-086 | A HIGH grant MUST ask for confirmation in the attached client. | run `ilium plugin grants <id> --grant terminal.write` with a client attached and assert the prompt. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-087 | Ilium MUST show a footer indicator for 3 s after a plugin reads or writes the clipboard. | read the clipboard from a test plugin and watch the footer. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-088 | Ilium MUST drop toasts beyond 3 per 10 s per plugin and MUST end an input lock after 2 s. | send ten toasts at once, count the visible ones; lock input and time the release. | [user-permissions-explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/) |
| USR-100 | The plugin MUST restart after 1 s, then after 5 s, and MUST stay off at the third failure within 10 minutes. | make a test plugin fail on start and measure. | [user-troubleshooting](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-101 | Turning a plugin on MUST clear its failure count. | reach the stop, turn on, fail once, and assert a restart after 1 s. | [user-troubleshooting](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| USR-102 | A T2 or T3 plugin MUST have no network access except through `http:` grants and the providers named above. | from a test plugin, try a raw socket and a request to an ungranted host, and assert failure. | [user-privacy](/pages/user-privacy/) |
| USR-103 | Ilium MUST refuse a request to a host that the plugin has no grant for, including a redirect target. | redirect from a granted host to an ungranted host and assert `not-permitted`. | [user-privacy](/pages/user-privacy/) |
| USR-110 | The documentation MUST answer, in this FAQ, whether a store exists, which systems run third-party plugins, what declining a permission does, and how to leave a bad plugin behind. | search the page for each of the four answers. | [user-faq](/pages/user-faq/) |
| USR-120 | Ilium MUST show the full key fingerprint on request and the short form (first 4 and last 4 characters joined by an ellipsis) in the prompt, and MUST NOT trust a key without an explicit user answer. | install a package signed by an unknown key and assert that the prompt appears and that declining installs nothing. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-121 | Removing a trusted key MUST NOT remove, disable or change any installed plugin, and MUST mark plugins that it signed as `untrusted` in `ilium plugin list`. | remove the key and list. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-122 | An update of a T2 plugin MUST be signed by a trusted key. A key that signed the installed version MUST NOT be replaced silently by a different key. | install version 1 signed by key A, then offer version 2 signed by unknown key B, and assert that the trust prompt appears and that the dialog names both fingerprints. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-123 | An update MUST show only permissions that the installed version did not request, and MUST keep the answers already given. | update from a package with two grants to one with three and assert one new row. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-124 | A failed update MUST restore the previous version and its data and MUST show "Update failed, rolled back". | update to a package whose activation fails and assert the version in `ilium plugin list`. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-125 | Ilium MUST NOT check for, download or install updates by itself. | with two plugins installed, run for one hour with request logging and assert that no update request is made. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-126 | An update MUST keep the plugin id and MUST have a higher version. The signature MUST come from the key that signed the installed version, or from a key that the user trusts after seeing both fingerprints. | offer an update signed by a second key and assert the prompt shows the old and the new fingerprint. | [packages](/pages/packages/) |
| USR-127 | Trust MUST be per key, MUST be stored in the user's trust list, and MUST NOT be created by installing a package without a prompt. | install with a new key in a script without `--yes` and assert the install is refused. | [packages](/pages/packages/) |
| USR-128 | A T2 package whose key was removed from the trust list MUST keep running and MUST show `untrusted` in `ilium plugin list`. A later update MUST ask for trust again. | remove the key, list, and offer an update. | [packages](/pages/packages/) |
| USR-129 | A publisher MUST keep the private key offline and MUST NOT put it in a package. A lost key means new packages need a new key and a new trust prompt. | review `ilium plugin keygen` output for the path of the private key and its mode `0600`. | [packages](/pages/packages/) |
| USR-130 | The notice N14 MUST read `Plugin <name> stopped after 3 failures in 10 minutes: <export> <code or trap>. Turn it on again in Settings > Plugins.` The `<export>` is the failing export. It names the view, as in `views.render trap (sidebar)`, only when the failing export was `views.render`. The tree footer and the row in Settings > Plugins MUST show the same text. | trap a plugin three times and compare the footer text and the row text with the template. | [lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| USR-140 | Uninstall MUST first mark the plugin as being removed, then stop it, then delete files, and after a crash the next start MUST finish the removal. | kill the host after the mark and start again. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-141 | Uninstall MUST NOT delete the data of any other plugin and MUST NOT remove trusted keys. | compare the other plugins' folders before and after. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-142 | A pane whose plugin is gone MUST stay in the tree with a placeholder and MUST come back to life when the plugin is installed again. | remove, check the placeholder, reinstall, check the pane. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-143 | Plugins that depend on the removed plugin MUST become dormant, not failed, and MUST wake up when it returns. | remove the owner, check the state of the dependent plugin, reinstall the owner. | [user-install-and-manage](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| USR-160 | The recovery page MUST offer the actions enable, disable, reset failures, uninstall, forget settings, safe mode and open config file, each with the key in the render, and MUST open from `Ctrl+B` then `:` when `ilium.core.settings` is off. | turn the Settings plugin off, press the keys, and assert the page and each key. | [settings-screens](/pages/settings-screens/) |
| USR-161 | The Plugins tab, `ilium plugin list` and the recovery page MUST use the row words of this table for the corresponding states, and MUST NOT introduce another word for the same state. | put one plugin in each state and compare the words on the three surfaces. | [core-plugin-settings](/pages/core-plugin-settings/) |
| USR-162 | The Plugins tab MUST list every installed plugin including core plugins, with its tier badge and state. | install two plugins, count the rows, and compare with `ilium plugin list`. | [core-plugin-settings](/pages/core-plugin-settings/) |
| USR-163 | The tab MUST offer Forget settings on a plugin's Details page. It MUST delete that plugin's saved settings values for the user and the open project, MUST ask for confirmation, and MUST NOT touch permissions or data. | set a value, forget, assert the value is the default and the grant file is unchanged. | [core-plugin-settings](/pages/core-plugin-settings/) |
| USR-164 | The state words MUST be the same in the footer notice N14, which is defined in [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/#failure-counting-and-restart). | stop a plugin and compare. | [core-plugin-settings](/pages/core-plugin-settings/) |
| USR-170 | Install, update and the Plugins screen MUST run the checks in the order of the table above, and MUST name the failing step's code in the error. | build one package for each failing check, install each, and assert the code and that nothing is written to the store. | [security](/pages/security/) |
| USR-171 | The error text for a refused install MUST begin `Cannot install <name> <version>.` and MUST name the check in plain words after it. | assert the first line for a hash failure and for a tier failure. | [security](/pages/security/) |
| USR-172 | An uninstall MUST apply the effects of the table above in the same host step that removes the plugin from the registry. | remove a provider with a consumer, a contributor and a pane, and check each row. | [lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| USR-173 | An update MUST keep the grants the user already answered and MUST ask only for new ones. A failed update MUST roll back to the previous version. The user-facing rules are USR-123 and USR-124 in [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/#update-a-plugin). | update with one new grant and count the rows in the dialog. | [lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| USR-200 | The host MUST resolve `<config>`, `<data>` and `<cache>` with the `directories` crate for the project name `ilium`, and MUST NOT write plugin files anywhere else. | start Ilium with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` pointing at three empty folders, install a plugin, and assert that no plugin file appears outside those folders and the project's `.ilium` folder. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-201 | The host MUST keep each item at the location in the table, and MUST create the parent folders on first use. | on a clean profile, run install, grant, trust add, enable, disable and uninstall, then list the folders and match each file against the table. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-202 | The host MUST write `installed.json`, the grant files and the trust store atomically: it writes a temporary sibling file, flushes it and renames it over the target. | kill the process during a grant change and assert that the file holds either the old or the new content, never a mix. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-203 | Grants MUST be stored per user and per plugin, and MUST NOT be stored in a project folder. | grant `fs.read:project` while a project is open, open a second project and assert that the grant applies there and that `<project>/.ilium/` holds no grant. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-204 | The host MUST rotate the log at 1 MiB, MUST keep at most three rotated files, and MUST delete rotated files older than 14 days at server start. | write 5 MiB of log lines through a test plugin and list the folder; then age `<id>.log.2` by 15 days, restart, and assert it is gone. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-205 | Each log line MUST have the four columns timestamp, level, plugin id and message, with the timestamp in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`. | read the log and match every line against the pattern. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-206 | The host MUST create plugin folders with owner-only access and plugin files with owner-only read and write access. | after an install, run `stat` on every created path and assert mode `0700` for folders and `0600` for files on Linux. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-207 | The host MUST refuse to read a grant file or the trust store when another user can write to it, and MUST treat every third-party plugin as not allowed to run until the file is fixed. | set the mode of a grant file to `0666`, start Ilium, and assert that T2 and T3 plugins are refused at load with the code `grants.unsafe-permissions` while core plugins still run. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-208 | A default uninstall MUST remove the package, the grants, the cache and the Extensions order entries, and MUST keep settings. | install a plugin, write one setting, uninstall with no flag, and list what remains. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-209 | `--purge` MUST also remove settings, data, storage buckets and the log, and `--keep-data` MUST keep data and storage without asking. The two flags exclude each other. | run each flag on a copy of the same profile and compare the remains with the table. | [reference-plugin-files](/pages/reference-plugin-files/) |
| USR-210 | The host MUST read the policy file before it loads any third-party plugin, and MUST NOT load a third-party plugin when the file exists but cannot be read or parsed. | make the file unreadable and start Ilium; assert that core plugins run and that every T2 and T3 plugin refuses to load with `policy.invalid`. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-211 | The host MUST ignore a system policy file that a non-administrator can write, MUST show a persistent notice, and MUST record the audit event `policy-violation` with the reason `policy-file-writable` ([SEC-182]). | set the mode to `0666`; assert the notice and the audit record. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-212 | The host MUST treat a policy with an unknown key or a wrong type as malformed and MUST name the line of the first error in the notice. | write a policy with the key `allow_thirdparty`; assert that T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load, T1 plugins run, and the notice names line and key. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-213 | The host MUST read the policy at server start only. | set `packages.allow_third_party = false` while a T2 plugin runs and assert that nothing changes; restart and assert the plugin is shown as `Blocked by policy` with the message `policy.third-party-denied`. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-214 | A grant that matches `grants.deny` MUST NOT be granted, MUST be shown as locked in the review dialog and in the Capabilities tab with the text "Blocked by your administrator", and MUST make calls return `not-permitted`. | deny `clipboard.read`, install a plugin that requests it, and assert the row is locked and a call returns `not-permitted` with the message starting `policy: ` and the log line `refused clipboard.read by <function> (policy)`. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-215 | A plugin whose manifest requests a denied grant MUST still install and run, with that grant refused. | install such a plugin and assert state `enabled` and the refusal log line. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-216 | `plugins.deny_ids` MUST win over `plugins.allow_ids`. | list one id in both and assert it cannot be installed, with the code `policy.blocked` and the message starting `policy.id-denied: `. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-217 | The host MUST check the policy keys in the order above and report the first failing key as the detail code. | write a policy that fails four keys at once and assert the detail code is the first in the order. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-218 | The policy MUST NOT stop a core plugin or a bundled T1 plugin from running. | set `packages.allow_third_party = false` and `packages.allowed_tiers = []`; assert all 30 core plugins still start. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-219 | The host MUST write a `policy-loaded` audit record at start when a policy file exists, and a `policy-violation` record when a plugin or file violates it, and MUST NOT write plugin data into either. | start with a policy that denies one installed plugin and count the two records. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| USR-220 | The host MUST delete rotated audit files older than `audit.keep_days` at server start ([SEC-224]). | age a rotated file by 366 days and restart. | [reference-plugin-policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |

### Pending decisions

These rows are proposals. The manual states them so a test can be written, and the owner of the platform must confirm or change them before release.

| Subject | Proposal in this manual | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Safe mode | Third-party plugins are off for one run and nothing is written to `installed.json` ([LIF-004]). | [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) |
| Administrator policy file | A TOML file in a system folder that only restricts. | [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| Audit log | Always on, with rotation and retention set by `audit.max_mib` and `audit.keep_days`. | [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |
| Which core plugins a user can turn off | The "can you turn it off" column of the core plugin tables. | [Core plugins for users](/pages/user-core-plugins/) |
| Data choice at uninstall | The dialog asks keep or purge. The default without a terminal is keep. | [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| Update asks again | Only new permissions appear in the dialog. | [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/) |
| Check order | The table of check order against the 12-step pipeline. | [Security](/pages/security/) |
| Row state words | One table of state words for the tab, the CLI and the recovery page. | [Settings plugin](/pages/core-plugin-settings/#plugin-row-states) |

# Requirements for widgets

## Requirements for widgets

Normative behaviour of the ui-tree, the 51 widgets, keys, actions, popups, focus and render-time caps.

The rows follow the format and the observation channels of the [requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/). The id prefix is `WID`.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Observable test |
|---|---|---|---|
| [WID-001] | The widget catalogue MUST hold 51 widgets in 7 families. A plugin MUST describe a view only with these widgets. | [the seven families](/pages/widgets-index/#the-seven-families) | (install-error) run the check tool over the widget pages -> 51 distinct widget names. |
| [WID-002] | A ui-tree MUST be a flat list of nodes whose root is node 0. Every child index MUST be in range and greater than its parent index, and a node MUST have at most one parent. Any violation, including a cycle, MUST trap with ui.invalid-tree. | [the ui tree](/pages/ui-model/#the-ui-tree) | (trap) return a node whose child index is 99 of 5 nodes -> trap ui.invalid-tree. |
| [WID-003] | A key MUST be unique across the whole view, not only among siblings. A duplicate key MUST trap with ui.duplicate-key. | [the ui tree](/pages/ui-model/#the-ui-tree) | (trap) two nodes with key "save" in different branches -> trap ui.duplicate-key. |
| [WID-004] | A tree MUST NOT hold more nodes than the effective ui_tree_nodes limit, 4,096 by default. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/layout/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (trap) 4,097 nodes -> trap. |
| [WID-005] | A layout MUST have as many constraints as children. A mismatch MUST trap. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/layout/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (trap) layout with 3 children and 2 constraints -> trap. |
| [WID-006] | A layout percentage above 100 MUST be clamped to 100. | [errors and edge cases](/pages/layout/#errors-and-edge-cases) | (screen-text) percentage 150 in a 40 column row -> the child gets 40 columns. |
| [WID-007] | Fixed, min, max, percentage, ratio and fill constraints MUST be solved in the order given on the layout page, and the cells MUST sum to the area width. | [how the solver divides one row](/pages/layout/#how-the-solver-divides-one-row) | (screen-text) fixed 10 and fill in 40 columns -> 10 and 30. |
| [WID-008] | A widget action MUST reach the plugin as a ui-action event carrying the node key and the action value. | [actions back to the plugin](/pages/ui-model/#actions-back-to-the-plugin) | (event-delivery) click a button with key "save" -> ui-action key "save". |
| [WID-009] | Host-owned state (scroll offset, text cursor, selected tab) MUST survive a re-render when the key is unchanged. | [keys and host owned state](/pages/ui-model/#keys-and-host-owned-state) | (screen-text) scroll a list, re-render with the same key -> the offset stays. |
| [WID-010] | A node with pointer-events and without focusable MUST send no pointer actions. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/ui-model/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (event-delivery) click such a node -> no ui-action. |
| [WID-011] | Escape MUST be reserved by the host and resolved in this order: a capturing key-capture, a text selection, the topmost popup, then a modal panel. A modal popup MUST send closed. | [Escape](/pages/ui-model/#escape) | (event-delivery) press Escape in an open modal popup -> closed arrives and the popup is gone. |
| [WID-012] | More than 4 open popups in one view MUST make open-popup fail with quota-exceeded. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/ui-model/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (sync-return) open a fifth popup -> err quota-exceeded. |
| [WID-013] | A code-view on a buffer the plugin did not create MUST need editor.read, and a terminal-view MUST need terminal.read-screen. Without the grant the widget MUST draw an empty frame with the text "not permitted". | [edge cases and errors](/pages/ui-model/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (screen-text) terminal-view without the grant -> frame with "not permitted". |
| [WID-014] | views.render has no result type. A render that breaks a limit (ui.too-large, ui.too-deep, ui.widget-not-allowed, ui.invalid-tree, ui.duplicate-key) MUST trap the render call with the matching ui.* code. The host MUST log one error with the widget path, keep the last good tree on screen marked stale and count one failure. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/ui-model/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (trap) check-list with 257 items -> trap, the previous tree stays, and one log line with the widget path. |
| [WID-015] | A tooltip longer than 200 Unicode scalar values MUST be cut at 199 and end with the ellipsis. It MUST NOT be an error. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/ui-model/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (screen-text) tooltip of 300 characters -> 200 cells ending in the ellipsis. |
| [WID-016] | In a settings view, a widget outside the allowed subset MUST trap the render call with ui.widget-not-allowed: the host logs one error with the widget path, keeps the last good tree and counts one failure. | [settings views](/pages/ui-model/#settings-views) | (trap) render a terminal-view in a settings view -> trap ui.widget-not-allowed, previous tree stays. |
| [WID-020] | check-list MUST accept at most 256 items and list-editor at most 64 (1,024 with limits_tier first-party). | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (trap) list-editor with 65 items as T2 -> trap with invalid-argument logged. |
| [WID-021] | meter MUST have at most 8 segments, minimap at most 4,096 marks per layer, and spinner at most 16 custom frames. | [requestable limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/#requestable-limits) | (trap) meter with 9 segments -> trap with invalid-argument logged. |
| [WID-022] | The calendar widget (unstable) MUST show one month with Monday first, and MUST need the unstable list to include it. | [calendar](/pages/widgets-data-display/#calendar) | (install-error) use calendar without listing it in unstable -> manifest.unstable-missing. |
| [WID-023] | A ratio below 0 or above 1 MUST be clamped to the range and NaN MUST draw as 0. A progress-row percent above 100 MUST be clamped to 100. | [edge cases and errors](/pages/widgets-data-display/#edge-cases-and-errors) | (screen-text) gauge ratio 1.5 -> drawn full. NaN -> drawn empty. |
| [WID-024] | chart MUST draw Braille where the terminal supports it and a text-line fallback otherwise. | [chart](/pages/widgets-data-display/#chart) | (screen-text) same chart at two capability levels -> Braille and text-line renders. |
| [WID-025] | Text widgets MUST wrap at the area width. paragraph spans that carry an action MUST send it when clicked. | [widgets text](/pages/widgets-text/) | (event-delivery) click an action span -> ui-action with that action. |
| [WID-026] | Input widgets MUST send their change per the debounce rule: toggles, choices and confirmations at once, typed text after the debounce. A text-area with debounce-ms unset MUST wait 600 ms up to 10,000 bytes of text and 1,000 ms above, re-evaluated at each keystroke. An explicit debounce-ms MUST win. | [when the plugin hears about a change](/pages/widgets-input/) | (event-delivery) type 10,001 bytes into a text-area -> changed after 1,000 ms; with debounce-ms 200 -> after 200 ms. |
| [WID-027] | The ui-action event MUST carry five fields, and action-id MUST be a copy of key in 0.1.0. | [keys are action ids](/pages/widgets-input/#keys-are-action-ids) | (event-delivery) click toggle key "dark" -> ui-action key "dark" and action-id "dark". |
| [WID-028] | An image whose asset is missing, corrupt, unsupported or over 16 MiB MUST draw an empty frame with the text "image not available". A code-view or terminal-view that names a missing buffer or pane MUST draw an empty frame with the text "not found". | [widgets media and embedded](/pages/widgets-media-and-embedded/) | (screen-text) image with a missing asset -> frame with "image not available". terminal-view of a closed pane -> "not found". |
| [WID-017] | A tree deeper than 32 levels, counting the root as level 1, MUST trap with ui.too-deep. | [the ui tree](/pages/ui-model/#the-ui-tree) | (trap) a chain of 33 nested blocks -> trap ui.too-deep. |
| [WID-018] | Tab MUST visit focusable nodes with tab-index 1 or more in ascending order, then nodes with none or 0 in tree pre-order, and MUST skip negative values and nodes with disabled-reason. | [focus order](/pages/ui-model/#focus-order) | (event-delivery) tab-index 2 then 1 then none -> focus visits 1, 2, none. |
| [WID-019] | Cell width MUST follow one rule for every widget: the host width of a string in cells, with wide glyphs as 2 and combining marks as 0. | [cell width](/pages/ui-model/#cell-width) | (screen-text) a label of 3 wide glyphs in 6 cells -> fits without cut. |
| [WID-029] | A popup or dialog node MUST take no space in its parent layout. A popup id MUST be the node key and unique across a plugin's open views, and close-popup on an unopened id MUST be a no-op that returns ok. | [popups and anchors](/pages/ui-model/#popups-and-anchors) | (screen-text) a length(0) slot holding a popup leaves the sibling area unchanged. |
| [WID-030] | A theme change MUST repaint the last tree of every open view, deliver theme-changed and trigger exactly one views.render per open view. | [rendering triggers](/pages/reference-host-rendering/) | (event-delivery) switch theme -> one theme-changed and one render. |

### See also

- [Requirements index](/pages/reference-requirements/)
- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Requirements index

## Requirements index

This index lists the numbered requirements of the Ilium plugin manual. A requirement is one testable statement about what the host, the SDK or a plugin must do. The statements come from the contract pages, so a test author can derive a test from a row without reading the prose around it. Contract version: ilium:plugin@0.1.0.

### Meaning of a requirement

A requirement has one id, one statement, one source and one observable test. The statement uses one keyword.

| Keyword | Meaning |
|---|---|
| MUST, MUST NOT | The behaviour is mandatory. A test fails when it differs. |
| SHOULD, SHOULD NOT | The behaviour is expected. A test records a deviation as a warning. |
| MAY | The behaviour is allowed and optional. A test does not fail either way. |

A statement holds one keyword. A statement that needs two keywords is two rows.

### Id rules

- An id is a prefix of three capital letters, a hyphen and three digits: `[API-040]`.
- Ids are never reused. A removed requirement leaves its number unused.
- An id appears as a definition in exactly one requirements page. Other pages cite it in square brackets.
- Numbers inside a page are grouped in tens. The first group holds the general rules and later groups hold a topic each.

### Prefixes

| Prefix | Area | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `API` | Host API: errors, traps, restart rule, limits, quotas | [Host API](/pages/reference-requirements-api-host/) |
| `CAP` | Capabilities and grants | [Capabilities](/pages/reference-requirements-capabilities/) |
| `WID` | Widgets and the ui-tree | [Widgets](/pages/reference-requirements-widgets/) |
| `PRI` | Pane primitives: terminal, agent, editor, basic | [Pane primitives](/pages/reference-requirements-primitives/) |
| `EVT` | Events and intents | [Events and intents](/pages/reference-requirements-events-intents/) |
| `RQO` | Requests, submissions and outcomes | [Requests and outcomes](/pages/reference-requirements-requests-outcomes/) |
| `SVC` | Services and topics | [Services and topics](/pages/reference-requirements-services-topics/) |
| `EXT` | Extension points and hooks | [Extension points](/pages/reference-requirements-extension-points/) |
| `SET` | Settings | [Settings](/pages/reference-requirements-settings/) |
| `PAN` | Panes and their lifecycle | [Panes](/pages/reference-requirements-panes/) |
| `RND` | Rendering and scenes | [Rendering](/pages/reference-requirements-rendering/) |
| `LIF` | Plugin lifecycle and operations (other lane) | [Lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/) |
| `AUT` | Author guides (other lane) | [Author guides](/pages/reference-requirements-author-guides/) |
| `PKG` | Packages, install, signing and trust (other lane) | [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/) |
| `SEC` | Security and sandbox (other lane) | [Threat model](/pages/reference-threat-model/) |
| `HST` | Host internals (other lane) | [Host architecture](/pages/reference-host-architecture/) |
| `DEV` | Developer tools (other lane) | [Check and lint rules](/pages/reference-check-and-lint-rules/) |
| `USR` | User documentation (other lane) | [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) |

### Row format

Every area page is one table with four columns.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Id | The id in square brackets, such as `[RQO-004]`. |
| Requirement | One statement with one keyword. |
| Source | A link to the page and the anchor that states the behaviour. |
| Observable test | The channel in parentheses, the input, an arrow, and the expected result. |

### Observation channels

A test names the channel on which it looks. Each channel is something a test can read without help from the host internals.

| Channel | What a test reads |
|---|---|
| sync-return | The result of a host function call: ok or a plugin-error code. |
| completion | The request-result event for a submission or a request-id: the outcome. |
| install-error | The JSONL error lines and the exit code of `ilium plugin install` or `check`. |
| load-warning | A warning shown at load that does not stop the plugin. |
| log-line | A line of `ilium plugin logs` for the plugin. |
| trap | The end of an instance, shown as a log line with the plugin id, interface and function. |
| restart-schedule | The delay between a failure and the next instance, and the final disable. |
| event-delivery | The events a plugin receives in `on-events`, their order and batching. |
| screen-text | The text of the rendered screen, read from a terminal capture. |
| cli-exit | The exit code and output of an Ilium command. |

### Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Side | One of server, client or scene. A plugin runs once for each side it declares. |
| Grant | A capability string in the manifest that the user accepts. |
| Trap | A plugin bug that ends the instance. The plugin cannot catch it. |
| Failure | An event that counts toward the restart and disable rule. |
| Submission | One intent that a plugin returns from `on-events`. |
| Outcome | The result of a submission: ok, ok-node, ok-epoch, duplicate, refused, failed or cancelled. |
| Dedup key | A string of 1 to 128 characters that makes a submission safe to repeat for 10 minutes. |
| Extension code | A code such as `extension.vetoed`, carried as a base code plus a message prefix. |
| Tier | T1 (bundled), T2 or T3. The tier sets the ceilings of the limits. |

### Index

Each area page below lists its requirements with an id, a rule and a test.

| Area | Prefix | Page | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Host API | `API` | [Host API](/pages/reference-requirements-api-host/) | 27 |
| Capabilities | `CAP` | [Capabilities](/pages/reference-requirements-capabilities/) | 18 |
| Widgets | `WID` | [Widgets](/pages/reference-requirements-widgets/) | 25 |
| Pane primitives | `PRI` | [Pane primitives](/pages/reference-requirements-primitives/) | 21 |

| Services and topics | `SVC` | [Services and topics](/pages/reference-requirements-services-topics/) | 24 |
| Extension points | `EXT` | [Extension points](/pages/reference-requirements-extension-points/) | 25 |
| Settings | `SET` | [Settings](/pages/reference-requirements-settings/) | 20 |
| Panes | `PAN` | [Panes](/pages/reference-requirements-panes/) | 21 |
| Rendering | `RND` | [Rendering](/pages/reference-requirements-rendering/) | 18 |

### Coverage rule

Every behaviour that a page states with must, never, only or a fixed number MUST appear in one requirements row. Check the rule with these commands from the manual folder.

```
rg -o '^\| \[([A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{3})\]' -r '$1' pages/reference-requirements-*.md | sort | uniq -d
rg -o '\[(API|CAP|WID|PRI|EVT|RQO|SVC|EXT|SET|PAN|RND)-[0-9]{3}\]' pages --no-filename | sort -u > /tmp/cited.txt
```

The first command must print nothing. A printed id is defined twice. The second command lists every cited id. Each listed id must also be a row id in an area page.

### Reading order

- [Error codes and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) for the numbers behind most rows.
- [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/) for the grant table.
- [Events and intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/) and [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for the submission rules.
- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) for the other lane requirements.

# Reference, resource accounting

## Reference, resource accounting

This page defines how the host measures what a plugin uses, which budget wins when several apply, what a plugin sees when a budget runs out, and how the user reads the numbers. The default and ceiling values are in [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) and are not repeated here.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

<div class="note">
<p>The numbers in Errors and limits reference are normative for 0.1.0.</p>
</div>

### What is measured

| Resource | Unit | Measured how | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linear memory | bytes | Wasmtime store limiter, on each `memory.grow` | one instance |
| Tables | elements | Wasmtime store limiter | one instance |
| CPU | ms of thread time | thread CPU clock, read before and after each call | one plugin side in one process |
| Wall time | ms | monotonic clock | one call or one request |
| Storage | bytes | sum of key and value sizes in a bucket | one bucket |
| Disk | bytes | sum of file sizes in `data` and `cache` | one plugin |
| Queues and request counts | items | counters | one plugin side |
| Session memory | bytes | sum of instance memory limits actually in use | one session server |

### Execution quota

The `ilium-execution` quota group is a token bucket. It holds 2,000 ms of CPU time and refills at 500 ms per second. There is one group for each plugin side in each process. A call spends its thread time. A submission also spends 1 ms for every 64 KiB of payload.

- When the bucket is empty, a new submission returns `quota-exceeded` with The bucket balance can go below zero, because a call is charged after it ends. The bucket is empty when the balance is 0 or less. `retry-after-ms` = max(100, ceil_10(-balance_ms * 2)), where `ceil_10` rounds up to the next 10 ms: the wall time until the balance refills to 0 at 500 ms per second, never below 100. A balance of -100 ms gives 200.
- A call already running is not stopped by an empty bucket. Its deadline stops it.
- A refused call is not a failure and is not counted toward the restart rule. It counts as a quota hit in the metrics of [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/).

- [LIF-139] The host MUST charge thread CPU time of each call to the `ilium-execution` group of the plugin side, and MUST refuse a submission with `quota-exceeded` and a `retry-after-ms` when the bucket is empty. Test: a plugin that submits in a loop; assert the refusal, the retry value, and that the plugin is not restarted.
- [LIF-140] A refusal for quota MUST NOT count as a failure. Test: read the failure window after 100 refusals.

### Session memory pool

One session server has a pool of 1,024 MiB (`session_memory_mib`). Each instance reserves its configured linear memory limit at activation, not what it uses. Admission works in this order.

1. Core T1 plugins reserve first, at server start.
2. Other plugins reserve when they activate, in activation order.
3. When a reservation does not fit, the host first drops unused compile cache pages, then tries once more.
4. If it still does not fit, the instance does not start. The side stays `inactive` with the reason `host-capacity`. The refusal is logged and shown in the plugin detail. It is not a counted failure.
5. When another instance deactivates, the host retries waiting sides in activation-request order.

- [LIF-141] An instance whose reservation does not fit MUST stay `inactive` with the reason `host-capacity`, MUST NOT be counted as a failure, and MUST start when memory is freed. Test: fill the pool with a small `session_memory_mib`, activate one more plugin, then deactivate another.
- [LIF-142] A core T1 plugin MUST be admitted before any third-party plugin at server start. Test: set a pool that fits exactly the core plugins plus one more, and start with a third-party plugin that activates on `startup`.

### Which limit wins

Three sources can set a limit: the tier ceiling, the manifest request and the user configuration. The host takes the manifest request, or the default when none. The user value in `[plugins.limits]` replaces it. The tier ceiling then clamps the result. The clamp is logged once per start.

```toml
# config.toml
[plugins.limits]
event_queue = 2048

[plugins."com.example.notes".limits]
memory_mib = 64
```

Example. A T3 plugin asks `memory_mib: 200` in its manifest. The user sets nothing. The ceiling for T2 and T3 is 128, so the plugin gets 128 and the log says `limit memory_mib clamped 200 to 128`. If the user sets 64 for this plugin, it gets 64. If the user sets 256, it gets 128.

- [LIF-143] The effective limit MUST be `min(ceiling, first set of [plugins."<id>".limits] value, [plugins.limits] value, manifest value, default)`; 0 or a missing value means not set, so the next source applies. The user can raise a value up to the ceiling and can lower it. Session keys have no manifest value and the user may only lower them. Test: the three cases of the example.
- [LIF-144] A per-plugin user value MUST win over a user value for all plugins. Test: set both and read the effective value.

### Helpers and cgroups

T2 and T3 instances run in the helper process of [Sandbox helper](/pages/reference-host-helper/). The helper is placed in a cgroup on Linux with a memory limit equal to the sum of the reservations of its instances plus 32 MiB for the runtime, and a CPU weight below the main process. A cgroup out-of-memory kill is a helper crash and follows the helper rules of [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/). The per-instance limits stay in force inside the helper, so the kill happens only when the runtime itself grows.

- [LIF-145] The helper cgroup `memory.max` MUST equal the sum of the hosted instances' `memory_mib` plus 32 MiB, the same amount charged to `session_memory_mib` by HST-164. Test: read the cgroup file for a helper with two instances.

### Reading the numbers

`ilium plugin stats [<id>] --json` prints the current use and the effective limit, one line per resource:

```text
{"type":"plugin-stat","id":"com.example.notes","side":"server","resource":"memory","used":9437184,"limit":33554432,"source":"default"}
{"type":"plugin-stat","id":"com.example.notes","side":"server","resource":"execution-ms","used":1240,"limit":2000,"source":"fixed"}
```

`source` is `default`, `manifest`, `user` or `ceiling`. The Plugins screen detail tab Resources shows the same rows ([Managing plugins](/pages/user-managing-plugins/)).

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-prompt">$</span> ilium plugin stats com.example.notes
<span class="t-dim">RESOURCE     USED     LIMIT    SOURCE</span>
memory       9.0 MiB  32 MiB   default
exec bucket  1240 ms  2000 ms  fixed
storage      3.1 MiB  16 MiB   default
disk         12 MiB   256 MiB  default
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. Each row shows use, the effective limit and where the limit came from.</figcaption>
</figure>

- [LIF-146] `ilium plugin stats` MUST print use, effective limit and source for memory, the execution bucket, storage and disk. Test: parse the lines for a fixture plugin.

### Edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| The user lowers a limit below current use | The plugin keeps running. The next growth is refused. Storage over the new limit rejects writes, not reads. |
| The user raises a limit above the ceiling | Clamped and logged. |
| The pool shrinks at a config reload | Running instances keep their reservation. New activations see the new pool. |
| Disk quota reached | Writes return `quota-exceeded`. See [Offline and low disk](/pages/reference-offline-and-low-disk/). |

### See also

- [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/)
- [Reference, errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)
- [Performance](/pages/performance/)
- [Health and watchdog](/pages/reference-health-and-watchdog/)
- [Requirements, lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Runtime model

## Runtime model

This page describes what the host guarantees while it runs a plugin component: which threads exist, how a call is interrupted, in what order events arrive, how memory and time are bounded, which WASI interfaces a component may link, and what happens when a plugin fails. The [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/) lists the functions. This page lists the rules that the functions rely on. Every rule has an id of the form [ABI-NNN], and the [requirements page](/pages/reference-requirements-wit-abi/) repeats each id with its test.

### What you need

- **The WIT reference.** Names such as `on-events`, `request-completed` and `take-response` are defined in the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/).
- **A running plugin or the test harness.** The [testing page](/pages/testing/) describes the fake host. The fake host follows the same rules as this page.
- **The limits page.** Numeric limits that this page quotes are owned by [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) and [Performance](/pages/performance/). This page repeats a value only where the rule needs it.

## 1. Instances and threads

- A plugin has one component per side (server, client, scene). The host creates **one instance of the component per plugin per side**. A plugin that has a server part and a client part therefore has two instances, in two processes, that cannot share memory.
- An instance is **single-threaded**. A component has no threads and no `wasi:threads`. The host never calls two exports of one instance at the same time [ABI-025] [ABI-049].
- A job (`job-runner.run`) runs in its own instance, created for the job and dropped after it. A job instance is not activated and has no event handler. It shares nothing with the main instance of the plugin except through `storage`, `fs` and messages.
- Every export call runs to completion on the host thread that owns the instance. The host does not preempt it between instructions. It interrupts it by the epoch mechanism in section 2.
- An instance lives from `activate` until `deactivate`, a trap, or a restart. All its memory is lost at that point. The only state that survives is what the plugin wrote to `storage`, `fs`, settings or the bytes that `deactivate` returned.

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭  ≡ ● · One instance per side─────────────────────╮
│ server  acme.git-status  instance 3  active      │
│ client  acme.git-status  instance 1  active      │
│ job     acme.git-status  parse-report  running   │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. Two instances of one plugin, plus a job instance. Instance numbers count activations of one plugin on one side.</figcaption>
</figure>

## 2. Calls, deadlines and interruption

The host runs every export under a deadline. It enforces the deadline by **epoch interruption**: the engine checks a counter at function entries and loop back-edges, and a host ticker thread advances that counter every **10 ms**. The host sets the instance deadline to `ceil(d / 10) + 1` ticks after the call starts. A guest that spins therefore traps no earlier than `d` and no later than `d + 20` ms of wall time on a host that is not overloaded, and a call that returns at `d - 1` ms never traps [ABI-026] [ABI-042].

- A deadline is wall time, from the start of the call to its return. Host work that runs inside a synchronous import counts, because the plugin waits for it.
- A hard deadline breach traps the instance. The trap counts as a failure (section 12), except a `deactivate` breach, which never counts [ABI-044]. A soft deadline breach discards the late result and traps only after the streak or grace in the scheduling table. A job deadline breach does not trap the main instance: the job completes as `failed(timed-out)`.
- The deadline of each export is a **per-export deadline**. A call of one export does not borrow time from another. The single normative table of call classes, kinds and effects is [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/#call-classes). The table below repeats only the deadlines for orientation and always yields to it. A plugin may ask for another value within its tier ceiling with the manifest `limits` block.

| Export | Default deadline | Ceiling, T1 | Ceiling, T2 and T3 | When breached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lifecycle.activate` | 2,000 ms | 5,000 ms | 2,000 ms | Trap, activation fails |
| `lifecycle.deactivate` | 500 ms | 1,000 ms | 500 ms | Instance dropped, no restore bytes |
| `handler.on-events` | 20 ms | 50 ms | 20 ms | Trap |
| `views.render` | 10 ms | 20 ms | 10 ms | Trap |
| `annotator.annotate` | 10 ms | 20 ms | 10 ms | Soft: annotation skipped; the third breach in a row traps |
| `catalog-provider`, `menu-provider`, `virtual-rows-provider` | 20 ms | 20 ms | 20 ms | Soft: static fallback |
| `token-provider.tokens` | 10 ms | 10 ms | 10 ms | Soft: lines stay plain |
| `settings-validate.settings-validate` | 100 ms | 100 ms | 100 ms | Soft: the save is refused and the previous value kept |
| `job-runner.run` (CPU time) | 2,000 ms | 60,000 ms | 10,000 ms | `failed(timed-out)` |
| `renderer.render` | frame budget, at most 50 ms | 50 ms | 50 ms | Soft: frame skipped; 30 in a row trap |

The CPU deadline of a job counts CPU time only. A job that waits in `jobs.wait-request` spends no CPU budget, but its wall time counts against `job_wall_ms` (20,000 ms by default).

`deactivate` may return at most 1 MiB. A larger return is dropped, one warn line is logged, and the next activation gets no `restored` value. It does not count as a failure [ABI-044].

`views.render`, `annotate` and `settings-validate` are **pure** calls. An effectful import (any import that submits an intent, starts a request, writes storage or starts a timer) called inside them returns `err(not-permitted)` with the message `effectful import in a pure call`, and the call continues. Read-only imports such as `ui.display-width`, `clock` and `tree` reads stay allowed [ABI-048].

**Worked example.** A handler that decodes a 2 MiB image inside `on-events` spends 31 ms. The deadline is 3 ticks, so the call is interrupted between 20 and 40 ms. The host logs `deadline breach in on-events: limit 20 ms`, traps the instance, applies none of the submissions of that batch, and schedules a restart (section 12).

## 3. Re-entrancy

The host never calls an export of an instance while another export of the same instance is on the stack [ABI-049]. A host import therefore never runs plugin code of the caller in the middle of the call, with two documented exceptions that stay on the same stack and do not re-enter the instance:

- `services.call` to a service that the calling plugin provides itself is **queued**. The provider export `handle` runs after the current call returns, as its own call [ABI-050].
- `extensions.run-hook` on a point that the calling handler is running returns `reentrant`. A chain on another point is allowed to depth 3, and a deeper chain returns `reentrant`.

An import that completes work later (every function with a `take-*` partner) never calls back. It delivers `request-completed` in a later batch.

**Edge case.** A plugin submits `invoke-command` for its own command from inside `on-events`. The host does not run the command at once. It queues `command-invoked` and delivers it in a later batch, in order [ABI-050].

## 4. Event delivery

An event is a fact that the host reports. The host delivers events to `handler.on-events` in batches.

- A batch holds **at most 256 events**. A longer backlog is split into several batches, in order [ABI-045].
- Each plugin side has **one queue**, filled in the order of host emission across all event kinds. The queue holds **1,024 events by default**. The manifest key `event_queue` asks for another size. The ceiling is **4,096** for T1 and **1,024** for T2 and T3 [ABI-045].
- Order is kept per node: `pane-created` first, then other pane events, then `pane-exited`, then `node-removed`. `agent-identified` precedes `agent-activity-changed` for the same pane.
- A plugin that is not active receives nothing. Events for an inactive plugin are not queued. Events produced while the plugin is activating are queued and arrive in the first batch after `activate` returns `ok`. If `activate` fails, they are discarded without an `events-dropped` report [ABI-046].
- After every activation of a plugin that holds `tree.read`, the first batch starts with exactly one `tree-changed` event that lists every node in tree pre-order. Without `tree.read` nothing is sent [ABI-047].

Each event case has one of three **delivery policies**. The policy of every case is listed in the [event matrix](/pages/reference-host-conformance/#4-event-matrix).

| Policy | What the host does when the queue is full | Counted in `events-dropped` |
|---|---|---|
| Coalesced | Always merges an event with the pending event of the same kind and key (node, buffer, timer, job, watch, pane or signal), whatever the queue fill. Only the newest state stays, at the position of its newest occurrence. Pending `tree-changed` lists merge into one union. | No |
| Drop oldest, counted | Removes the oldest event of that kind from the head of the queue. | Yes |
| Never dropped | Keeps the event. If the queue is full, no drop-oldest event is pending and such an event arrives, the plugin is treated as stuck: the host restarts the instance as a failure, and the new instance receives `tree-changed` for every node. | Not applicable |

A full queue admits a drop-oldest event by evicting the oldest queued drop-oldest event of any kind, and counts it [ABI-033]. The next batch after a drop starts with one `events-dropped` event. It carries a list of `dropped-count { event, source, count }` records, one per event name and source. `events-dropped` is coalesced by (event, source) and never dropped, and a new count merges into the pending record [ABI-036].

**Worked example.** A plugin is busy for 400 ms in a long job callback, and 2,000 `screen-changed` events for one pane arrive. They share one coalescing key (the pane), so the queue holds one event with the newest revision. `agent-activity-changed` is never dropped. A plugin that also received 1,500 `output-matched` events (drop-oldest) with the default queue of 1,024 loses the oldest 477 of them, because one slot holds the coalesced `screen-changed` event. Its next batch starts with `events-dropped([{ event: "output-matched", source: none, count: 477 }])`.

## 5. Submissions

A handler returns submissions. The host applies them in order after `on-events` returns.

- **More than 256 submissions trap the call.** This is not a refusal: the call counts as one failure, **none** of the submissions is applied, and none of them completes [ABI-008].
- Two **batch-level checks** run over the whole list, in index order, before any effect: shape (wrong shape, or a missing dedup key on `send-input` or `agent-action`), then grant. Inside one submission the shape check wins over the grant check [ABI-031].
- Every other check (target exists, pane ready, value valid, rate, quota, conflict, `if-current`) is **per submission** and affects only that submission [ABI-032].
- The lowest-index offender completes as `refused(invalid-argument)` (shape) or `refused(not-permitted)` (grant). Every other submission completes as `refused(cancelled)` with the message `batch refused: submission <index>`, where `<index>` is the 0-based position of the offending submission [ABI-009].
- A refused submission does not reserve its dedup key.
- A dedup key has 1 to 128 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`. It is scoped to the plugin and reserved while `now_wall_ms - accepted_wall_ms < 600,000`. The accepted time is persisted in the journal on the wall clock [ABI-010] [ABI-034].
- A repeat completes as `duplicate(original)`, where `original` is the ref of the first submission. The outcome makes no claim about the result of the original, and the host does not check that correlation numbers are unique [ABI-035].
- `correlation` is chosen by the plugin. Values below 2^63 belong to the plugin. Values from 2^63 up belong to the SDK [ABI-011].

The `intents.submit` import is for use outside a batch. It carries one submission, queues it, and answers `request-completed` with the request ref `submission(correlation)`; the value returned by `submit` is the `request-id` of the call.

## 6. Slow calls and results

A function whose result type is `result<request-id, plugin-error>` is a slow call. It returns at once with a request id (or a synchronous error) and completes later.

1. The call returns `ok(request-id)`. A synchronous refusal returns an error instead: `not-permitted`, `invalid-argument`, `busy` and similar.
2. Later, an event `request-completed` arrives with `request-ref call(request-id)` and an `outcome`.
3. On `ok`, the plugin calls the matching `take-*` function once.

A result is **held for 30 seconds**, or until the first take [ABI-012]. The hold starts when `on-events` returns for the batch that delivered the `request-completed` event, not when the host emitted it [ABI-037]. A take before completion, a second take, a take after the hold and a take of an unknown id all return `none`. The SDK wrappers hide this: they return the result or fail with `not-found` [ABI-014]. A `request-id` is unique per plugin side for the whole server run and is never reused, also across restarts [ABI-040].

A plugin has at most 64 pending requests by default (ceiling 256 for T1), and a session at most 4,096. The call that exceeds a limit returns `busy` at once [ABI-013]. A request counts from the return of its id to the enqueue of its completion. Refused submissions and synchronous calls do not count [ABI-041].

When a plugin is disabled or shut down, its pending requests are cancelled. After a trap, the surviving events are redelivered once at the head of the new instance's queue, completions of submissions are delivered to the new instance, and completions of `call(id)` requests are discarded [ABI-038]. When a grant is revoked, requests that need it complete as `failed(revoked)` before `deactivate(revoked)`; the other pending `call(id)` requests are cancelled with the instance [ABI-043].

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::http::{self, HttpRequest};

/// Fetches a page and returns the body. The wrapper hides request-completed and take-response.
pub async fn fetch_notes(url: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let request = HttpRequest {
        method: "GET".to_string(),
        url: url.to_string(),
        headers: vec![],
        body: None,
        timeout_millis: 5_000,
    };
    match http::fetch(request).await {
        Ok(response) if response.status == 200 => Some(response.body),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { fetch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';

/** Fetches a page and returns the body. The wrapper hides request-completed and take-response. */
export async function fetchNotes(url: string): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const response = await fetch({ method: 'GET', url, headers: [], body: undefined, timeoutMillis: 5000 });
  if (response.status !== 200) throw new Error('unexpected status');
  return response.body;
}
```

## 7. Memory

Each instance has a memory cap, and the session has a pool for all instances.

| Budget | Default | Ceiling, T1 | Ceiling, T2 and T3 | When exceeded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `memory_mib` (one instance) | 32 | 256 | 128 | Trap, counts as a failure |
| Session memory pool (all instances) | 1,024 MiB | 4,096 MiB, all tiers (user config only) | same, no per-tier ceiling | The new instance is refused with `session.memory-exceeded`. Not counted as a failure. |
| `job_memory_mib` (one job instance) | 64 | 512 | 256 | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |

The server total of 1,024 MiB is the default of the pool. At activation an instance charges its effective `memory_mib` to the pool, and a sandbox helper charges its `memory_mib` plus 32 MiB [HST-164]. Growth below the limit never fails on the pool. An instance that grows past its cap traps at the growth call; the guest never sees `-1` from `memory.grow` [ABI-027]. A refusal because the pool is full is logged as `host-capacity` and the plugin can be started again when memory is free.

## 8. JSON in strings

A field or parameter whose name ends in `-json` carries UTF-8 JSON text. The host and the SDKs apply one rule to all of them [ABI-016].

- **Grammar.** RFC 8259. A document that is not valid JSON is `invalid-argument`. A byte order mark, comments, trailing commas and `NaN` or `Infinity` are not allowed.
- **Depth.** At most 64 levels of nesting. A deeper document is `invalid-argument`.
- **Size.** The limit of the field applies. The default is 65,536 bytes for a service payload, a command argument or a topic payload, and 1 MiB for settings. A larger document is `invalid-argument`, or `quota-exceeded` where the field's page says so.
- **Numbers.** A JSON number is read as a 64-bit float. An integer beyond 2^53 loses exactness, so a value that may exceed 2^53 MUST be sent as a string. Ids (`node-id`, `request-id`, `buffer-id`) are `u64` and are written as JSON strings in every `*-json` field. A `bigint` in TypeScript is written as a string by the SDK.
- **Keys.** Duplicate keys in one object are `invalid-argument`. Key order is not significant.
- **Strings.** The text is UTF-8. An unpaired surrogate escape such as `\ud800` is `invalid-argument`.

**Edge case.** A service payload `{"id": 9007199254740993}` is read by the host as 9007199254740992. The plugin that needs the exact value sends `{"id": "9007199254740993"}`.

## 9. Strings and text at the boundary

All `string` values are UTF-8. A string that is not valid UTF-8 never reaches the host or the plugin: the canonical ABI traps at the boundary, and the call counts as a failure [ABI-017]. A limit in characters counts Unicode scalar values and a limit in bytes counts UTF-8 bytes. A terminal width counts cells, as given by `ui.display-width`.

## 10. WASI subset

A component links only the WASI interfaces below. Any other import is refused at load.

| WASI interface | Allowed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `wasi:cli` stdout and stderr | Yes | Written to the plugin log at `info` and `error`. |
| `wasi:cli` environment, arguments, exit | Yes | The environment and arguments are empty. `exit` traps the instance. |
| `wasi:clocks` | Yes | Wall and monotonic clocks, see section 11. |
| `wasi:random` | Yes | Secure random bytes from the host, see section 11. |
| `wasi:io` | Yes | Streams and polling, for the interfaces above only. |
| `wasi:filesystem` | No | Use `ilium:host/fs`. |
| `wasi:sockets` | No | Refused at load. Use `ilium:host/http`. |
| `wasi:http` | No | Refused at load. Use `ilium:host/http`. |

A component that imports `wasi:sockets` or `wasi:http` is refused at load [ABI-024]. The check runs when the package is installed and again when the instance is created.

## 11. Time and randomness

- **Wall clock.** `ilium:host/clock.now-unix-millis` and `wasi:clocks/wall-clock` read the same host clock. It can jump when the user changes the time.
- **Monotonic clock.** `clock.monotonic-millis` and `wasi:clocks/monotonic-clock` read one host source. It never goes backwards inside the host. Values from two instances are not comparable.
- **Randomness.** `wasi:random` returns bytes from the operating system generator. A plugin MUST NOT depend on a fixed sequence.
- **Timers.** A volatile timer fires `timer-fired` in a later batch, never inside the call that set it. A durable timer fires `durable-timer-fired` and reports how late it is.

## 12. Failures and restart

A **failure** is a trap (deadline, memory, illegal instruction, invalid UTF-8, more than 256 submissions), an error from `activate`, or a stuck queue. A failure ends the instance and schedules a restart. The back-off is:

| Failure inside 10 minutes | Wait before the restart |
|---|---|
| First | 1 s |
| Second | 5 s |
| Third | Not restarted. The plugin is disabled on that side until the user turns it on again. |

A restart that follows a 10-minute quiet period starts the count again at the first failure. A job failure never counts. `host-capacity` refusals never count. The `deactivation-reason` `crash-restart` is reserved and never delivered, because a crashed instance cannot be called [ABI-028].

The new instance gets `restored: none` in `activation` after a trap, because `deactivate` did not run. A restart after a clean `deactivate` (for example an upgrade) passes the bytes that `deactivate` returned.

## 13. Link-time grant enforcement

The host links imports **per instance**, from the grants of the manifest. An interface whose capability is not granted is not linked, or is linked to a stub:

- A component that imports a function of a capability its manifest never requested traps when it first calls the function, with `host.capability-not-requested`. It counts as a failure.
- A function whose grant the user declined returns `not-permitted`. The plugin keeps running.
- A grant withdrawn during a call makes later calls that need it return `err(revoked)`. Pending requests follow the rule in section 6 [ABI-043]. The plugin is re-activated with the reduced grants.
- A component whose `exports` differ from the required exports plus the manifest list is refused at install with `manifest.exports-mismatch` [ABI-023].

## 14. Determinism in tests

The fake host in the test harness follows this page. It fakes the clock, the file system, processes, the network, storage and settings. A test sets the clock, delivers batches in a chosen order, and checks the submissions that come back. A fake is deterministic: the same input gives the same result. A call to a fake process or network that a test did not declare fails the test.

- The fake clock starts at a fixed instant and moves only when the test advances it. The epoch ticker is not simulated: a test sets the deadline outcome with `host.breach_deadline(export)`, which applies the effect of the call class in the scheduling table, and changes grants with `host.grants_changed(list)`, which follows section 13.
- The fake queue enforces the same batch size, policies and queue sizes as the host.
- `fuzz_run(seed, rounds)` delivers random valid batches. A failure prints the seed.

- [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/)
- [Host conformance matrix](/pages/reference-host-conformance/)
- [ABI evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/)
- [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/)
- [Performance](/pages/performance/)
