# ABI evolution

## ABI evolution

This page states how the plugin contract `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` may change after its first freeze, how a component records the version it was built for, and how the host decides whether it can load a component. The rules protect the binary layout of the contract (the canonical ABI), not only its names. The [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/) is the contract. [Versioning](/pages/versioning/) explains the author side. The [requirements page](/pages/reference-requirements-wit-abi/) lists each rule with its id and its test.

### What you need

- **The WIT reference.** Case names and orders on this page refer to the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/).
- **A built component.** The `ilium:api-version` section is written by the SDK. You do not write it by hand. To inspect one, run `ilium plugin inspect <package>`.

## 1. What is versioned

There is exactly one contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. It is an umbrella identity. It is not a WIT package. The WIT packages `ilium:types`, `ilium:host`, `ilium:primitives`, `ilium:exports`, `ilium:server`, `ilium:client` and `ilium:anim` all carry the version `@0.1.0` and change together [ABI-003].

The version appears in three places, and the host requires that they agree:

| Place | Form | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest key `api` | the string `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` | at install, stage 3 |
| Custom section `ilium:api-version` of each component | three big-endian `u16` values: major, minor, patch | at install and at load |
| Package names in the WIT imports of the component | `@0.1.0` | at link time |

The bytes of the custom section for `0.1.0` are `00 00 00 01 00 00`: major 0, minor 1, patch 0 [ABI-004]. A component with no section, with a section of another length, or with values that differ from the manifest is refused with `manifest.api-version`.

## 2. What may change

After the first freeze of 0.1.0, a later version may only **add**. The canonical ABI makes the following parts of the contract binary-significant, so a change to one of them is a break:

| Part | Rule |
|---|---|
| Case order of a `variant`, `enum` or `flags` | Fixed. A case is only appended at the end [ABI-019]. |
| Fields of a `record` | Fixed. A field is never added, removed, reordered or retyped. A new optional value goes into a new record or a new function. |
| Parameters and results of a function | Fixed. A new capability is a new function. |
| Function and type names | Fixed. A name is never reused for another meaning. |
| Interface and world names | Fixed. A new interface is added beside the old one. |
| Required exports | `lifecycle` and `handler` (server and client), `lifecycle` and `renderer` (scene) never change. |
| Limits | A limit may be raised. It is lowered only in a major version. |

Why records are fixed: a record is flattened into a sequence of fields. A host that reads a field that an older plugin did not write would read the wrong bytes. Appending to a `variant` is safe, because an older plugin never produces the new case. Delivering a new case to an older plugin is not safe, so the host filters (section 5).

**What counts as "shape" in 0.1.0.** Several records carry optional fields in 0.1.0 itself, for example `ui-node`, `popup-anchor`, `send-input-spec`, `set-decoration-spec`, `rename-node-spec`, `notify-spec`, `set-virtual-rows-spec`, `choice-option` and `menu-entry`. They are part of the first freeze. They are listed as "shape" items in [Versioning](/pages/versioning/) and they are not open to later change.

## 3. Markers and unstable features

Every item of the contract has one of two markers:

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `@since(version = 0.1.0)` | The item exists from that version and keeps its shape in later minor versions. In the WIT reference a stable item carries no marker, because every item of 0.1.0 has this one. |
| `@unstable(feature = <name>)` | The item may change or disappear inside 0.x. Only a plugin whose manifest `unstable` key lists the name may use it. |

Version 0.1.0 has **four** unstable features: `ui-calendar`, `plugin-services`, `gpu-kernels` and `websocket` [ABI-022]. In the WIT listing an unstable item has a `// @unstable(feature = <name>)` comment on the line before it. A comment is used because a gate on a single variant case is not part of the WIT text format.

| Feature | Items it gates |
|---|---|
| `ui-calendar` | the `calendar` widget and `calendar-spec` |
| `plugin-services` | `services.call` between plugins, and the grants `services.use:<name>` and `services.provide:<name>` |
| `gpu-kernels` | `gpu.run`, `gpu.available` and the grant `gpu.kernels` |
| `websocket` | `http.open-websocket` and `http.send-websocket` |

The manifest checks run before any code loads:

| Code | When it fails |
|---|---|
| `manifest.unstable-unknown` | A name in `unstable` is not a feature of this host. |
| `manifest.unstable-tier` | A T2 or T3 package lists a feature outside development mode. |
| `manifest.unstable-missing` | The component imports an unstable item and the manifest does not list the feature. |

## 4. The window and the refusal codes

The host loads the **current minor version and the previous one**. The window counts minor numbers. Each released minor is kept as a frozen copy under `wit/since_v0_N/`, and the host reads the older minor through a hand-written adapter.

| Situation | Code | Stage |
|---|---|---|
| `api` is not a well-formed `ilium:plugin@X.Y.Z` string | `manifest.schema` (see [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/)) | manifest |
| `api` is well formed and outside the window | `package.api-unsupported` | install, stage 3 |
| `api` is inside the window, but the component section differs from it | `manifest.api-version` | install and load |
| The component imports an interface that no requested capability unlocks | `manifest.import-not-requested` | install |
| A manifest lists a grant that its API version does not have | `manifest.grant-unknown` | install |

There is one refusal for each situation. A single package never gets two codes: the host reports the first failing check in the order of the table [ABI-021].

<figure>
<pre class="term">
╭  ≡ ● · Install check─────────────────────────────╮
│ old-titler 1.2.0 ……… api ilium:plugin@0.1.0  ✓   │
│ future-x 1.0.0 …… api ilium:plugin@0.3.0  ✕      │
│   package.api-unsupported: host supports 0.1.0   │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. A plugin built for a newer minor than the window is refused.</figcaption>
</figure>

## 5. What an older plugin sees from a newer host

A host of minor N+1 runs plugins built for N. To keep them correct, the host adapts what it sends:

- **Events.** The host does not deliver an event case that is newer than the plugin's API. The plugin never sees it, and it is not counted in `events-dropped`.
- **Outcomes.** A newer outcome case is mapped to the nearest older one: `ok-epoch(n)` would be delivered to a plugin of an earlier API as `ok`.
- **Intents.** A plugin cannot send a newer case, because its bindings do not have it.
- **Reasons.** A newer `deactivation-reason` is delivered as `shutdown`.

[ABI-029] A host MUST NOT deliver an event, outcome or reason case to a plugin whose API version predates the case. It maps the case as described above, or it does not deliver it.

An SDK enum is non-exhaustive, so a plugin compiled for N still compiles when N+1 bindings add a case.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

fn describe(outcome: &Outcome) -> &'static str {
    match outcome {
        Outcome::Ok => "applied",
        Outcome::OkNode(_) => "created a node",
        Outcome::Duplicate(_) => "already done",
        // A case that a later API adds lands here.
        _ => "other",
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { Outcome } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';

export function describe(outcome: Outcome): string {
  switch (outcome.tag) {
    case 'ok': return 'applied';
    case 'ok-node': return 'created a node';
    case 'duplicate': return 'already done';
    default: return 'other'; // A case that a later API adds lands here.
  }
}
```

## 6. A change in practice

Suppose a later minor version, called N+1 here, adds an intent `pin-node(node-id)`. The authors do these steps:

1. Append `pin-node(node-id)` as case 43 of `intent`, after `dismiss-toast`. Never insert it in the middle.
2. Add the case to the frozen snapshot of N+1 and keep `wit/since_v0_1/` as it is.
3. Write the adapter that maps the 0.1 view of the host to the N+1 view.
4. Add the grant `tree.write` to the row of the intent in the [intent table](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/).
5. Update the case counts on the pages that state them, and the [requirements page](/pages/reference-requirements-wit-abi/).
6. Run the contract check: a diff of the case order of every `variant`, `enum` and `flags` type against `wit/since_v0_1/` must show only appended cases.

Results for the three kinds of plugin:

| Plugin | Host N+1 |
|---|---|
| Built for 0.1.0, installed on N+1 | Loads. It never sends `pin-node`. |
| Built for N+1, installed on N+1 | Loads. It may send `pin-node`. |
| Built for N+1, installed on 0.1.0 | Refused with `package.api-unsupported`. |

## 7. The cases that the first freeze fixes

The counts below are the sizes of the main variants and enums in 0.1.0. A later minor can only make them larger.

| Type | Cases in 0.1.0 | Appended after the base set |
|---|---|---|
| `event` | 56 | 18 |
| `intent` | 42 | 23 |
| `outcome` | 7 | 1 (`ok-epoch`) |
| `widget` | 51 | 0 |
| `action-kind` | 17 | 0 |
| `action-value` | 12 | 0 |
| `deactivation-reason` | 6 | 0, with `crash-restart` reserved |
| `error-code` | 15 | 0 |

The event catalogue shows 35 rows for the base events, because three rows each describe two cases (`editor-opened` and `editor-closed`, `key-pressed` and `key-released`, `client-attached` and `client-detached`). The count of cases is 38 for the base events [ABI-002].

## 8. Edge cases

- **A patch release.** A patch version changes no interface. A component built for `0.1.0` and a host at `0.1.1` still need the exact `api` string match, so a package states the patch it was built for. The host at a later patch of the same minor loads it through the same adapter.
- **A reserved case.** `crash-restart` exists in `deactivation-reason` so that the numbering never changes. The host never delivers it [ABI-028].
- **A removed feature.** An unstable feature may be removed. A package that lists it fails with `manifest.unstable-unknown` after the upgrade.
- **Names kept by users.** Pane kind ids, command ids, settings keys, decoration slots and topic names are stored in user snapshots and keep their spelling for ever.

- [Runtime model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/)
- [Errors and limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/)

# Host conformance matrix

## Host conformance matrix

This page is the checklist for a host implementation, and for a test that wants to prove one. It lists every import, export, event, intent and widget of `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` with the side that may use it, the grant it needs, the delivery policy or deadline, and the error a host must return. The names and shapes are defined in the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/). The rules behind the columns are in the [Runtime model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/). Each matrix has a row for every member, so a missing row in a host test is a missing test [ABI-030].

### What you need

- **The WIT reference.** Row names are the names in the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/).
- **A host or a fake host.** The tests below run against the real host or against the test harness described in [Testing](/pages/testing/).
- **The counts.** 45 import rows (39 host interfaces, 4 primitives, 2 scene interfaces), 16 export rows, 56 event rows, 42 intent rows and 51 widget rows. A matrix with another count is out of date.

## 1. How to use the matrices

The columns S, C and A mean server, client and scene. A cell says whether a plugin of that side may import or export the interface. A call from a side that is not allowed fails at link time: the interface is not linked, and the component is refused with `manifest.import-not-requested` when no requested capability unlocks it.

For each row a conformance test does four things:

1. Calls the member from an allowed side with the grant, and checks the documented result.
2. Calls it without the grant, and checks `not-permitted` (or, for an interface the manifest never requested, the trap `host.capability-not-requested`).
3. Calls it with an argument over a limit, and checks `invalid-argument`, `quota-exceeded` or the documented code.
4. For a slow call, checks the `request-completed` outcome and the `take-*` rules: one take, a hold of 30 seconds, and `none` after that [ABI-014].

## 2. Import matrix

Every grant name is in the [capability index](/pages/capabilities/). A slow call is a function that returns `result<request-id, plugin-error>`, and its take partner is in brackets.

| 2 | `handler` | yes | yes | no | yes | none | none | 20 ms per batch |

| 4 | `detector` | yes | no | no | no | `detector` | `agent.read` | 20 ms |

| 9 | `settings-validate` | yes | yes | no | no | `settings-validate` | none | 100 ms |

**Notes.**

- A deadline breach of `menu-provider` or `token-provider` falls back to static content and does not fail the user action.

## 7. Error behaviour that every host shares

| Situation | Result | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Call without the grant | `not-permitted` | Call each row without its grant |
| Function of a capability the manifest never requested, in a linked interface | trap `host.capability-not-requested` | Call a function of an unrequested capability |
| Interface that no requested capability unlocks | install refused with `manifest.import-not-requested` | Install a component that imports `clipboard` with no clipboard grant |
| Call from a side that may not import it | not linked, install refused | Import `ui-host` from a server component |
| More than 256 submissions | trap, none applied | Return 257 submissions |
| Malformed submission in a batch | whole batch refused, siblings `refused(cancelled)` | Return one bad submission among 3 |
| Take twice | second take returns `none` | Take a result twice |
| Event queue full | policy of the event case | Fill a queue of 1,024 events |

**Rust test sketch**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::testing::{FakeHost, Grants};

#[test]
fn clipboard_write_needs_its_grant() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::client(Grants::none());
    let result = host.call_clipboard_write("hello");
    assert_eq!(result.unwrap_err().code, ErrorCode::NotPermitted);
}
```

**TypeScript test sketch**

```ts
import { FakeHost, grants } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing';

test('clipboard write needs its grant', () => {
  const host = new FakeHost('client', grants());
  expect(() => host.clipboard.writeText('hello')).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'not-permitted' }));
});
```

# Requirements for WIT and ABI

## Requirements for WIT and ABI

This page lists every normative rule of the WIT contract and the binary interface of `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Each row has an id, the rule, the page that explains it, and the test that proves it. The ids appear inline as [ABI-NNN] on the pages that state the rule. The contract is in the [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/).

### What you need

- **The WIT reference.** [WIT reference](/pages/reference-wit/) is the owner of all type definitions.
- **The conformance matrices.** [Host conformance matrix](/pages/reference-host-conformance/) lists the members that rule ABI-030 covers.

## Rules

| Id | Rule | Owner page | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABI-001 | The WIT reference is the only canonical definition of the contract. Other pages MUST hold excerpts only. | [reference-wit](/pages/reference-wit/) | check.py excerpt check |
| ABI-002 | Case order and case counts of event (56), intent (42), outcome (7), widget (51), action-kind (17), action-value (12), error-code (15) and deactivation-reason (6, of which five are delivered) MUST match the WIT reference. | [reference-wit](/pages/reference-wit/) | case-count diff against wit/since_v0_1 |
| ABI-003 | All seven WIT packages MUST carry the one version 0.1.0 and change together. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | package version scan |
| ABI-004 | Each component MUST carry the custom section ilium:api-version with bytes 00 00 00 01 00 00. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | inspect a built component |
| ABI-005 | A WIT excerpt on another page MUST match the declared names and cases in the WIT reference. | [reference-wit](/pages/reference-wit/) | check.py excerpt check |
| ABI-006 | The optional exports a component has MUST equal the optional exports its manifest lists. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | install a component with an extra export |
| ABI-007 | The manifest exports list MUST NOT differ from the component. A difference MUST refuse install with manifest.exports-mismatch. | [reference-host-conformance](/pages/reference-host-conformance/) | install with a missing optional export |
| ABI-008 | A plugin that returns more than 256 submissions MUST trap the call; the host MUST apply none and none completes. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | return 257 submissions |
| ABI-009 | The lowest-index offender of a batch-level check MUST complete as refused(invalid-argument) (shape) or refused(not-permitted) (grant), and every other submission MUST complete as refused(cancelled) with the message 'batch refused: submission <index>', where index is 0-based. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | batch of 3 with 1 bad |
| ABI-010 | A dedup key MUST be 1 to 128 characters from [A-Za-z0-9._:/-] and is mandatory for send-input and agent-action. | [events-and-intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) | repeat a key twice |
| ABI-011 | Correlation numbers below 2^63 MUST belong to plugins. Numbers from 2^63 up belong to the SDK. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | submit with a high number |
| ABI-012 | The host MUST hold a finished slow-call result for 30 seconds. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | take after 31 s |
| ABI-013 | The host MUST allow 64 pending requests by default per plugin (ceiling 256 for T1) and 4,096 per session. Over the limit MUST return busy. | [reference-errors-and-limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) | start 65 requests |
| ABI-014 | A take before completion, a second take, or a take of an unknown id MUST return none. The SDK wrapper returns not-found. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | take twice |
| ABI-015 | Each event case MUST follow its delivery policy: coalesced, drop-oldest-counted or never-dropped. Loss of a drop-oldest event MUST be reported in events-dropped. | [reference-host-conformance](/pages/reference-host-conformance/) | fill a queue of 1,024 |
| ABI-016 | Names MUST use kebab-case in WIT. JSON inside strings MUST be UTF-8. | [reference-wit](/pages/reference-wit/) | scan |
| ABI-017 | A string that is not valid UTF-8 MUST trap the call. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | pass bad bytes |
| ABI-018 | Required exports (lifecycle, handler, renderer) MUST NOT be listed in the manifest exports. | [reference-manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/) | list handler in a manifest |
| ABI-019 | Cases of a variant, enum or flags MUST only be appended after the freeze. Records MUST NOT gain fields. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | case-order diff |
| ABI-020 | The Rust and TypeScript SDKs MUST map WIT names by the rules in the WIT reference section 10. | [reference-wit](/pages/reference-wit/) | SDK binding test |
| ABI-021 | The host MUST compare api versions by minor window and MUST report one refusal code per package, the first failing check. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | install a 0.3.0 package |
| ABI-022 | Version 0.1.0 MUST have exactly four unstable features: ui-calendar, plugin-services, gpu-kernels and websocket. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | list features |
| ABI-023 | A requested grant not in the API MUST refuse with manifest.grant-unknown. An unrequested import MUST refuse with manifest.import-not-requested. A call of an unrequested capability MUST trap host.capability-not-requested. | [reference-host-conformance](/pages/reference-host-conformance/) | three installs |
| ABI-024 | The host MUST NOT link wasi:sockets or wasi:http. | [security](/pages/security/) | import wasi:sockets |
| ABI-025 | Each plugin side MUST run one single-threaded instance, and a host call MUST NOT re-enter a plugin export. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | call an export from an import |
| ABI-026 | The host MUST interrupt a running export by an epoch ticker of 10 ms against the export deadline. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | spin in on-events |
| ABI-027 | A memory growth over the instance limit MUST trap. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | grow memory |
| ABI-028 | The deactivation reason crash-restart is reserved. The host MUST NOT deliver it. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | crash a plugin |
| ABI-029 | The host MUST NOT deliver an event, outcome or reason case to a plugin whose API predates the case. | [reference-abi-evolution](/pages/reference-abi-evolution/) | run a plugin built against 0.1.0 on a host that adds a case after it |
| ABI-030 | A host test suite MUST have a test for every row of the import, export, event, intent and widget matrices. | [reference-host-conformance](/pages/reference-host-conformance/) | row count check |
| ABI-031 | The kernel MUST run two batch-level checks over the whole submission list in index order before any effect: shape first, then grant. Inside one submission shape wins over grant. | [events-and-intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) | batch with a missing grant at index 1 and a bad shape at index 2 -> index 2 is invalid-argument only if checked first; the shape check runs for the whole list before the grant check, so index 2 is the offender and the others are cancelled |
| ABI-032 | Every check other than shape and grant (target, readiness, value validity, rate, quota, conflict, if-current) MUST be per submission and MUST affect only that submission. | [events-and-intents](/pages/events-and-intents/) | batch of 3 with a stale revision at index 1 -> only index 1 is refused |
| ABI-033 | A full queue MUST admit a drop-oldest event by evicting the oldest queued drop-oldest event of any kind and counting it. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | fill a queue of 1,024 with output-matched, send 1,500 -> 477 dropped counted |
| ABI-034 | A dedup key MUST be reserved while now_wall_ms - accepted_wall_ms < 600,000, measured on the wall clock and persisted in the journal. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | repeat a key at 599,999 ms (duplicate) and at 600,000 ms (accepted); restart the server between |
| ABI-035 | A repeated dedup key MUST complete as duplicate naming the ref of the first submission. The host MUST NOT check correlation uniqueness. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | submit a key twice with the same correlation -> two completions |
| ABI-036 | events-dropped MUST be coalesced by (event, source) and MUST never be dropped. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | drop two kinds twice -> one events-dropped event with two records |
| ABI-037 | The hold of a slow-call result MUST start when on-events returns for the batch that delivered the request-completed event. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | delay the batch by 40 s -> take still succeeds |
| ABI-038 | After a trap, surviving events MUST be redelivered once at the head of the new queue, completions of submissions MUST be delivered to the new instance, and completions of call(id) requests MUST be discarded. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | trap with a pending submission and a pending http call |
| ABI-039 | A coalesced event MUST NOT be reported in events-dropped when its queued event is merged. | [reference-events-and-intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/) | send 2,000 screen-changed -> no events-dropped |
| ABI-040 | A request-id MUST be unique per plugin side for the whole server run, start at 1 at server start, and never be reused, also across restarts. | [requests-and-outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) | restart a plugin -> new ids exceed the old ones |
| ABI-041 | A request MUST count toward pending_requests from the return of its id to the enqueue of its completion; refused submissions and synchronous calls MUST NOT count. | [reference-errors-and-limits](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) | 64 slow calls then a refused submission -> count stays 64 |
| ABI-042 | The instance deadline of a call with deadline d ms MUST be ceil(d / 10) + 1 ticks, so a spinning guest traps in [d, d + 20] ms and a call that returns at d - 1 ms never traps. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | spin with d = 20 -> trap in [20, 40] ms |
| ABI-043 | On revocation, synchronous calls needing the grant MUST return err(revoked), pending requests needing it MUST complete failed(revoked) before deactivate(revoked), and other pending call(id) requests MUST be cancelled with the instance. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | revoke http with one http and one fs request pending |
| ABI-044 | A deactivate breach or trap MUST drop the instance and its bytes and MUST NOT count as a failure. Returned bytes over 1 MiB MUST be dropped with one warn line and MUST NOT count as a failure. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | breach deactivate three times -> plugin still restarts |
| ABI-045 | A batch MUST hold at most 256 events, and event_queue MUST default to 1,024 with a ceiling of 4,096 for T1 and 1,024 for T2 and T3. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | deliver 600 queued events -> 3 batches |
| ABI-046 | Events produced while a plugin activates MUST be queued and delivered in the first batch after activate returns ok, and MUST be discarded without events-dropped if activate fails. | [reference-events-and-intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/) | emit pane-created during activate |
| ABI-047 | After every activation of a plugin that holds tree.read, the first batch MUST start with one tree-changed event listing every node in pre-order. | [reference-events-and-intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/) | activate with 3 nodes -> one event, 3 ids |
| ABI-048 | An effectful import called inside views.render, annotate or settings-validate MUST return err(not-permitted) with the message 'effectful import in a pure call', and the call MUST continue. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | call intents.submit inside views.render |
| ABI-049 | The host MUST NOT call an export of an instance while another export of that instance is on the stack. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | call an export from an import |
| ABI-050 | A services.call to the caller's own service and an invoke-command for the caller's own command MUST be queued and run as later calls. | [reference-runtime-model](/pages/reference-runtime-model/) | invoke own command inside on-events |
| ABI-051 | Every WIT function that returns `request-id` MUST have an awaiting wrapper with the WIT name and a starting wrapper with the suffix `_request` in Rust and `Request` in TypeScript. A WIT name that ends in `-json` MUST keep the suffix as `_json` in Rust and `Json` in TypeScript. | [reference-wit](/pages/reference-wit/#wrapper-names-in-the-sdks) | SDK binding test: list the wrappers of `http`, `jobs`, `services`, `inference` and `settings` |

## How the rows are tested

Three kinds of test cover the rows.

1. **Static checks.** `_tools/check.py` compares each labelled WIT excerpt with the WIT reference (ABI-001, ABI-005). A diff of case order against the frozen snapshot covers ABI-002, ABI-003 and ABI-019.
2. **Install tests.** A test installs a crafted package and expects the refusal code (ABI-004, ABI-006, ABI-007, ABI-018, ABI-021, ABI-023, ABI-024).
3. **Runtime tests.** A fake host runs a plugin that breaks the rule and the test expects the trap, the refusal or the outcome (ABI-008 to ABI-017, ABI-025 to ABI-050).

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::testing::FakeHost;

#[test]
fn more_than_256_submissions_trap() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::new();
    host.grant("tree.write");
    let result = host.run_on_events_returning(257);
    assert!(result.is_trap());
    assert_eq!(host.applied_count(), 0);
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { createFakeHost } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing';

test('more than 256 submissions trap', () => {
  const host = createFakeHost();
  host.grant('tree.write');
  const result = host.runOnEventsReturning(257);
  expect(result.trapped).toBe(true);
  expect(host.appliedCount()).toBe(0);
});
```

## Edge cases

- A batch of exactly 256 submissions is valid.
- A dedup key of 129 characters is a malformed submission, so the whole batch is refused (ABI-009, ABI-010).
- A take at 30 s plus one tick returns none (ABI-012, ABI-014).

# Widget input map

## Widget input map

This page lists, for each of the 51 widgets of `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, whether it takes focus, which keys and mouse actions it handles, which `ui-action` it sends and which state the host keeps under its key. The rules behind the columns are on the [UI model](/pages/ui-model/) page: the [focus order](/pages/ui-model/#focus-order), [Escape](/pages/ui-model/#escape) and the [action values](/pages/ui-model/#actions-back-to-the-plugin). Widgets without a key send nothing and keep no state. The word none means the widget does nothing for that column.

## The map

| Widget | Focus | Keys | Mouse | Sends | Host state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layout` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `block` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `tabs` | yes | Left, Right, Home, End | click a title | selected(index) | tab(u32) |
| `popup` | no (children yes) | Esc closes | click outside closes a non-modal popup | closed(none) | none |
| `clear` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `scrollbar` | no | none | click track pages, drag thumb | scrolled(index) | none |
| `split` | only if resizable | Left, Right, Up, Down move the divider | drag divider | resized(number) | split(u16) |
| `separator` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `dialog` | no (buttons yes) | Tab, Enter, Esc | click a button | activated(text), closed | none |
| `scroll-view` | yes | arrows, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End | wheel, drag scrollbar | scrolled(index) | offset(u32) |
| `paragraph` | if scroll is set | arrows, PageUp, PageDown | wheel, click a span | scrolled, activated | offset(u32) |
| `markdown` | if it has a link or task item | Tab between links, Enter | click a link | activated(text) | none |
| `leader-row` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `key-hints` | no | none | click a hint runs its command on the host | none | none |
| `diff-view` | yes | arrows, n, p | wheel | none | offset(u32) |
| `%list` | yes | Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End, Enter | click, double click, wheel | selected, activated, scrolled, context-requested | selected, offset, ids |
| `table` | yes | as %list | click row, click header sorts | selected, activated, scrolled | selected, offset, ids |
| `tree-list` | yes | Up, Down, Left collapses, Right expands, Enter | click, click arrow | selected, toggled, activated | ids, expanded |

| `check-list` | yes | Up, Down, Space | click item | toggled(item-state) | tri |
| `list-editor` | yes | Up, Down, Enter, Delete | click item | changed, selected | ids |

| `sparkline` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `bar-chart` | no | none | none | none | none |

| `canvas` | no | none | none | none | none |

| `progress-row` | no | none | click | activated | none |
| `meter` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `minimap` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `button` | yes | Enter, Space | click | activated(none) | none |
| `toggle` | yes | Space, Enter | click | toggled(flag) | checked, tri |
| `choice` | yes | Left, Right step; Enter opens dialog | click | selected(index) or changed(text) | selected, text |
| `number` | yes | Up, Down, plus, minus, digits | click buttons, drag slider | changed(number) | number |
| `text-input` | yes | typing, Enter submits if submit-on-enter | click sets cursor | changed(text), submitted | text |
| `text-area` | yes | typing, Enter inserts a line | click sets cursor | changed(text) | text |
| `schema-form` | one stop per row | per row widget | per row widget | changed, filter-changed | per row |
| `key-capture` | yes | Enter starts capture; Esc cancels | click | changed(text), closed | text |
| `color-picker` | yes | Enter opens dialog | click | changed(text) | text |

| `image` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `video` | no | none | none | none | none |
| `surface` | no | none | click, move | activated(cell), pointer | none |
| `terminal-view` | if interactive | all keys go to the terminal | click, wheel | pointer | none |
| `code-view` | yes | arrows, PageUp, PageDown | click, wheel | changed | offset(u32) |

## Rules for every row

- A widget takes focus only if it is listed as focusable here or has `flags.focusable`. A node with `disabled-reason` is never focused.
- `scrolled` carries the first visible row as `index(u32)` and is coalesced.
- Colour roles and stable-glyph substitutes of each widget are on its family page and on [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/).
- The text-area `changed` delay is `debounce-ms`; unset it is 600 ms up to 10,000 bytes of text and 1,000 ms above.

# Theming and readable output

## Theming and readable output

Plugins never choose the exact colour of their text. A view names a colour role, such as `danger` for a failed check, and the host paints that role with the theme tokens of the dark or light theme the user selected. One plugin build therefore renders correctly in both themes. This page lists the roles, the theme extras (reduced motion, density and icon mode), the colour roles of every widget family including the status and feedback widgets, and the styled-text fields. It shows one complete view in Rust and in TypeScript, and states which part of readability the host guarantees and which part stays with the plugin.

### You will need

- **Grants.** The styling fields need no grant. `theme()` and `display-width()` belong to the `ui` interface, so the plugin needs the `ui.panels` or `panes.provide-kind` grant of the view it draws.
- **Side and exports.** Views are drawn on the client. Use `side = "client"` in Rust or `side: 'client'` in TypeScript, and export `lifecycle`, `handler` and `views`.
- **Widgets.** The `paragraph`, `leader-row` and `markdown` widgets of [Text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/) carry the styled text. Forms use the leader rule described in [Building settings screens](/pages/settings-screens/).
- **Status and feedback widgets.** `badge`, `spinner`, `notice`, `icon`, `meter`, `progress-row`, `diff-view` and `minimap` take their colours from roles or from a `tone`. See [Widget colour roles](#widget-colour-roles).
- **Event.** `theme-changed`, listed in [Events and intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/).

## Colour roles

The host gives every view one `theme-tokens` record. A role names a token, so a plugin never needs the palette itself.

```wit
enum color-role { foreground, muted, accent, success, warning, danger, info, selection, border }

record theme-tokens {
  foreground: u32, background: u32, accent: u32, muted: u32,
  success: u32, warning: u32, danger: u32,
  is-dark: bool, stable-glyphs: bool
}
```

| Role | Painted with | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `foreground` | `foreground` token | Primary text |
| `muted` | `muted` token | Help lines, hints, secondary values |
| `accent` | `accent` token | Focus and the active tab |
| `success` | `success` token | A healthy plugin, a passed check |
| `warning` | `warning` token | Attention that is not a failure |
| `danger` | `danger` token | A failure or a destructive action |
| `info` | `info` token of `theme-extras` | Neutral information; the `ℹ` tone of a `notice` |
| `selection` | `selection` token of `theme-extras`, reversed | The highlighted row of a list or table |
| `border` | `border` token of `theme-extras` | Block borders, separators, dividers and the scrollbar track |

Colour tokens are packed `0x00RRGGBB` numbers. `background` is not a role. The host paints the panel background, and a plugin cannot choose it. Read `is-dark` only when a choice cannot be expressed with a role, for example when a scene picks a natural image for the theme.

## Theme extras

`theme-tokens` holds the seven base colours. The contract also defines `theme-extras`, a second record read with `theme-extras()`. It carries the three colours that the roles `info`, `selection` and `border` use, and three settings that change how a view should behave.

```wit
record theme-extras { reduced-motion: bool, density: density, info: u32, selection: u32, border: u32, icon-mode: icon-mode }
enum density { compact, normal, comfortable }
enum icon-mode { normal, stable }   // stable only when the user opted in
theme-extras: func() -> theme-extras;   // in host::ui
```

| Field | Meaning | What a plugin does with it |
|---|---|---|
| `reduced-motion` | The user asked for less motion. | Stop its own timers that animate. The host already shows one static frame in `spinner`, `progress-row` busy state and decoration frame animation, and draws no hover or scroll animation. A change of the setting delivers `theme-changed`. |
| `density` | `compact`, `normal` or `comfortable`. | Choose row padding, for example one blank row between groups only in `comfortable`. |
| `info`, `selection`, `border` | Packed `0x00RRGGBB` tokens. | Rarely needed: roles already use them. Read them for a `canvas` or a `surface` that draws its own frame. |
| `icon-mode` | `stable` only after the user turned on stable glyphs. | Keep icon names unchanged. The host swaps the glyphs. `theme().stable-glyphs` is derived and always equals `icon-mode == stable`. |

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui::{self, Density};

fn row_gap_rows() -> u16 {
    let extras = ui::theme_extras();
    if extras.reduced_motion {
        stop_own_animation_timer();
    }
    match extras.density {
        Density::Compact => 0,
        Density::Normal => 0,
        Density::Comfortable => 1,
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { themeExtras } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';

function rowGapRows(): number {
  const extras = themeExtras();
  if (extras.reducedMotion) stopOwnAnimationTimer();
  return extras.density === 'comfortable' ? 1 : 0;
}
```

`stopOwnAnimationTimer` stands for your own code that cancels a timer from the `clock` import. Read the extras again after `theme-changed`.

## Widget colour roles

The host paints every widget from roles, so a plugin that uses the widgets and tones below needs no colour of its own. The table is the colour column of the widget reference, for the widgets that carry state.

| Widget | Roles and tones | Glyphs the host draws |
|---|---|---|
| `block`, `separator`, `split` | `border`; `accent` for a focused block and a dragged divider | rounded corners `╭╮╰╯`, `─`, `│` |
| `tabs` | `muted`, `accent` (selected), `border` | divider ` │ ` |
| `%list`, `table`, `tree-list`, `menu` | `selection` for the highlighted row, `muted` for hints and disabled items, `danger` for danger items | highlight symbol, submenu `›` |
| `diff-view` | `success` added, `danger` removed, `muted` context and gutter | gutter `+`, `-` |
| `gauge`, `line-gauge`, `meter` | `accent` filled, `muted` remainder; `meter` takes the `tone` of each segment | `█`, `░`, `━`, `─` |
| `progress-row` | `warning` error, `muted` waiting, `accent` running, `success` done | `!`, `○`, `▶`, `✓` |
| `badge` | the `tone` | `●` or a short label |
| `notice` | the `tone` and `border` | `ℹ`, `✓`, `!`, `✗` |
| `spinner` | `accent`; one static frame with reduced motion | `⠋ ⠙ ⠹ ⠸ ⠼ ⠴ ⠦ ⠧ ⠇ ⠏` |
| `toggle`, `check-list` | `success` on, `muted` off or disabled, `accent` focus | `[x]`, `[ ]`, `[-]` |
| `text-input`, `path-field` | `danger` for an invalid or missing value, `muted` placeholder | `[ value ]`, `••••` for secrets |
| `key-capture` | `accent` while capturing, `warning` on conflict | `⌨ press keys…` |
| `leader-row` | `foreground` label, `muted` leaders | `…` |

The `tone` values are `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` and `muted`. They map to the roles of the same name, so the dark and the light theme both stay readable.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Roles at work ────────────────────────╮
│ <span class="t-hi">ℹ</span> The provider sends place names off site.   │
│ <span class="t-warn">!</span> Quota is at 92 percent.                    │
│ <span class="t-err">✗</span> The index build failed.                    │
│ <span class="t-ok">✓</span> The index was built.                       │
│ <span class="t-hi">⠋</span> Indexing 412 sessions                      │
│ <span class="t-ok">▶ RUNNING</span>  37%  <span class="t-hi">█████████</span><span class="t-dim">░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░</span>     │
│ Today ………………………………………………… <span class="t-ok">████████████</span><span class="t-err">██</span><span class="t-dim">░░░░</span> │
│ <span class="t-ok">+ added line</span>                                 │
│ <span class="t-err">- removed line</span>                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. A notice in the info, warning, error and success tone, a spinner, a progress row, a meter with a danger segment and the diff colours.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Styled text

Every visible string in a view is `styled-text`, a list of spans. A span holds text and a style. A style has an optional foreground colour, an optional background colour, and two modifier sets: one to add and one to remove.

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:types/text in reference-wit
variant color { role(color-role), rgb(u32), indexed(u8) }
flags modifiers {
  bold, dim, italic, underlined, slow-blink, rapid-blink, reversed, hidden, crossed-out
}
record style { fg: option<color>, bg: option<color>, add: modifiers, remove: modifiers }
record span { text: string, style: style }
```

An empty style inherits the theme. A colour given as `rgb` or `indexed` is painted exactly as given. Use it only where a scene or an editor needs a natural colour. The host's contrast guarantee covers roles. A plugin that picks its own colours is responsible for contrast on both backgrounds.

## The full surface

| Name | Kind | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `theme()` | function in `host::ui` | Returns the current `theme-tokens`. It never fails. Read it again after `theme-changed`. |
| `display-width(text)` | function in `host::ui` | Returns the cell width the host uses for the text, as `u16`. Call it before you cut text yourself. |
| `theme-extras()` | function in `host::ui` | Returns reduced motion, density, icon mode and the `info`, `selection` and `border` tokens. Rust `ui::theme_extras()`, TypeScript `themeExtras()`. |
| `invalidate(view)` | function in `host::ui` | Draws the view again with the current tokens. |
| `theme-changed` | client event, no payload | Sent once for a burst of theme changes. Always delivered on the client. |
| `color-role` | enum | The nine roles of the table above. |
| `color` | variant | `role(color-role)`, `rgb(u32)` or `indexed(u8)`. |
| `style`, `span`, `modifiers` | records and flags | The fields described above. |
| `paragraph` | widget | `lines: styled-lines`, `wrap`, `alignment`, `style`, `scrollable`. |
| `leader-row` | widget | `label: styled-text` and `value: styled-text`, joined by the `…` leaders. |
| `markdown` | widget | `source: string` and `link-command`, rendered by the host's Markdown renderer. |
| `stable-glyphs` | flag in `theme-tokens` | `true` when the user chose the opt-in stable glyph mode. |

## Worked example: a checks panel

This client view shows the number of failing checks on a leader row, a muted note, and a redraw when the theme changes. The Rust version comes first, the TypeScript version follows.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::layout::Area;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::{ColorRole, Modifiers, Style};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::{UiTree, ViewTarget};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::ui::build::Tree;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "client", exports = ["views"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct ChecksPanel {
    failed_checks: u32,
    last_view: Option<ViewTarget>,
}

impl Lifecycle for ChecksPanel {}

impl Handler for ChecksPanel {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let theme_changed = batch.iter().any(|event| matches!(event, Event::ThemeChanged));
        if let (true, Some(view)) = (theme_changed, self.last_view.clone()) {
            ui::invalidate(view);
        }
        Vec::new()
    }
}

impl Views for ChecksPanel {
    fn render(&mut self, view: ViewTarget, _area: Area) -> UiTree {
        self.last_view = Some(view);
        let mut tree = Tree::new();
        let value = vec![Span::styled(
            format!("{} failing", self.failed_checks),
            Style::role(ColorRole::Danger).add(Modifiers::BOLD),
        )];
        let row = tree.leader_row(vec![Span::plain("Failed checks")], value);
        let note = tree.paragraph(vec![vec![Span::styled(
            "Run the checks again to refresh.",
            Style::role(ColorRole::Muted),
        )]]);
        let panel = tree.block().title("Checks").child(row).child(note);
        tree.finish(panel)
    }
}
```

The panel names roles only. The danger colour is bold, and the note is muted, so both read on the dark and the light background. The handler keeps the last view target and redraws it when `theme-changed` arrives.

**TypeScript**

The TypeScript version uses the same roles. It reads `theme()` to show the active theme name, and it redraws on `theme-changed`.

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import type { Event, Submission } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';
import { invalidate, theme } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';
import { block, leaderRow, paragraph, tree } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';
import { role, span, type ViewTarget } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/types';

const FAILED_CHECKS = 3;
let lastView: ViewTarget | undefined;

export const { lifecycle, handler, views } = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  activate() {},
  onEvents(batch: Event[]): Submission[] {
    const themeChanged = batch.some((event) => event.tag === 'theme-changed');
    if (themeChanged && lastView !== undefined) invalidate(lastView);
    return [];
  },
  render(view: ViewTarget) {
    lastView = view;
    const { isDark } = theme();
    const value = [span(`${FAILED_CHECKS} failing`, { fg: role('danger'), add: { bold: true } })];
    const row = leaderRow([span('Failed checks')], value);
    const note = paragraph([[span(isDark ? 'Dark theme' : 'Light theme', { fg: role('muted') })]]);
    return tree(block({ title: 'Checks' }, [row, note]));
  },
});
```

The TypeScript field `isDark` is the camel-case form of `is-dark`. The `add` object uses the modifier names as keys, so `{ bold: true }` sets bold.

## Glyphs and icon widths

The host draws icons with their normal UTF-8 glyphs and measures them with their real cell width. A plugin must not replace an icon with a plain stable glyph to fix a width problem. The stable-glyph mode is an explicit user setting, `ui.stable_glyphs`, and the `stable-glyphs` flag tells the plugin that the user chose it. Icon names in the manifest, such as the `icon` of a command or a settings page, are Tabler icon names from the host icon set. The `icon` widget takes a `slot` of the `ilium.icons` catalogue and follows the icon preset the user chose, so a plugin never hard-codes an emoji for a state that the host already has a slot for.

## The leader rule

A label and a value far apart are joined by grey dotted leaders made of the `…` character, one cell each. The `leader-row` widget applies the rule for you.

- One blank cell sits on each side of the dots.
- A gap shorter than five cells stays blank.
- The leaders never overwrite label text, glyphs or values.
- The leaders are inert. They are never part of a click or hit target.
- When label and value do not fit the row, the value is cut first, with `…`.

A plugin that builds its own row with spaces produces a gap that does not match the host's rows, so use `leader-row` for every label and value pair that can sit far apart.

## Markdown and terminal output

A `markdown` widget takes a source string and renders it with the host's Markdown renderer, so headings, lists and links match the rest of Ilium. Plugins never send raw ANSI escape sequences. The host removes them from every text field and logs one warning per view. Use `styled-text` and the roles instead.

## What the user sees

The dark theme is the default. Dark renders stay dark: the host never draws a white card inside the dark theme. Panels have rounded corners, and the title carries the host's title icons.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Checks ───────────────────────────────╮
│ Failed checks …………………………………………………… <span class="t-err">3 failing</span> │
│ <span class="t-dim">Run the checks again to refresh.</span>             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. The checks panel in the dark theme, 48 columns by 4 rows. The danger role marks the count, and the muted role marks the note. The light theme draws the same characters.</figcaption>
</figure>

The light theme shows the same widgets with the same roles on a light background. The layout does not change, so a plugin that is correct in one theme needs no second layout. Only the colours of the border, the text and the roles differ, so the same characters appear in the render above.

## Edge cases and errors

| Case | What happens |
|---|---|
| Text contains an ESC sequence | The host removes the sequence and logs one warning per view at level warn. |
| `rgb` colour with weak contrast | The host paints it as given. The plugin owns that contrast. |
| Label and value do not fit a `leader-row` | The value is cut first, with `…`, then the label. |
| Badge text wider than 12 cells | The host cuts it and ends it with `…`. Widths use `display-width` rules. |
| Theme changes during a render | The next render uses the new tokens. Bursts of `theme-changed` arrive as one event. |
| Stable-glyph mode is on | The host draws the stable glyphs. The plugin keeps its own glyph names unchanged. |
| Reduced motion is on | `spinner` shows one static frame. A plugin timer that animates should stop. |
| Tree above 4,096 nodes or 1,024 KiB | The plugin traps. Repeated traps count toward the restart and disable rule. |
| `render` runs past 10 ms | The render is a trap, like any other `views.render` failure. |

The styling functions return no error code. `theme()` and `display-width()` always answer, and styled-text fields have no validation error. Limits show up only as traps or as cut text.

## Checks before you ship

- Open the view in the dark and in the light theme. Each status mark must stay readable against the background.
- Check that every label and value pair that can sit far apart uses `leader-row`.
- Turn on the stable-glyph setting and confirm that icon widths still line up.
- Handle `theme-changed` by calling `invalidate` for each open view, so the view is rendered again with the new tokens.
- Search the plugin for `rgb` and `indexed` colours. Each one needs its own contrast check.
- Turn on reduced motion and confirm that nothing in the view still moves.
- Check that every state has a glyph or a word as well as a colour, for example `✓` and `✗` with a `notice`, so the state reads without colour.

### What the contract does not provide

`ilium:plugin@0.1.0` has no accessible-label, screen-reader or high-contrast import, and no locale import. The terminal has no accessibility tree, so the plugin carries meaning in text. A plugin MUST NOT use colour as the only carrier of meaning, and MUST give every status a word or a glyph beside its colour role. [AUT-501] A plugin MUST read `reduced-motion` and stop its own animating timers when it is true. [AUT-502] A plugin SHOULD work in `compact` density at 40 columns and in both icon modes, and SHOULD end every icon-only control with a text label that stays when icons are not drawn. [AUT-503] A plugin SHOULD use the nine colour roles and avoid `rgb` and `indexed` colours, because only a role follows the theme and the user's contrast choice. [AUT-504] The list for release time is in [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/), and width rules for other scripts are in [Internationalisation](/pages/guide-internationalisation/).

# Performance

## Performance

Every plugin call runs under a deadline, and every plugin has a memory, queue and I/O budget. A call that exceeds its deadline traps the instance, and the host restarts the plugin. Keeping each call short is the only way to keep a plugin responsive. This page lists the deadlines and budgets, the performance targets the host checks, where time is charged, and how to move slow work into a job.

### You need

- A plugin that builds and runs, so you can measure where its time goes. The toolchain is in [Getting started: toolchain](/pages/getting-started-toolchain/).
- The `jobs.run` grant for any background work, and `fs.read:project` for the example in this page. Grants are listed in [Capability table](/pages/reference-capabilities/).
- Rust with `ilium-plugin-sdk`, or TypeScript with `@ilium/plugin-sdk`. Both examples target the API version `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
- For the extended-widget costs below: knowledge of the widgets in [Widget catalogue](/pages/widgets-index/).

## Deadlines and budgets

The values below are the defaults, copied from the single table in [Scheduling, deadlines and cancellation](/pages/reference-host-scheduling/#call-classes). The manifest `limits` block can ask for a smaller value, or a larger one up to the ceiling for the plugin's tier (see [Limits you can change](#limits-you-can-change)).

| Call | Default deadline | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `on-events` | 20 ms | One batch of up to 256 events. The host splits a larger batch. |
| `on-events` with a command | 50 ms | A batch that contains a `command-invoked` event runs under `command_deadline_ms` instead of 20 ms. |
| `views.render` | 10 ms | Called on open, on `ui.invalidate` and on resize only. |
| `annotate` | 10 ms | At most once per 100 ms per buffer. A breach skips the annotation; the third in a row traps. |
| `activate` | 2 s | May yield. |
| `deactivate` | 500 ms | Returned bytes are kept, up to 1 MiB. A breach drops the instance and the bytes, and does not count as a failure. |
| Scene `render` (frame) | The frame budget, at most 50 ms | Breached frames are skipped. |
| Job, CPU time | 2 s | Runs on a worker, not in a handler. |
| Job, wall time | 20 s | Includes time spent waiting for I/O. |
| Job, memory | 64 MiB | Concurrent jobs per plugin: 2. |

A breach of a hard handler deadline is logged, the instance is trapped and the plugin restarts. A soft deadline (`annotate`, scene frames, providers) discards the late result and traps only after the streak or a 100 ms grace in the scheduling table. A `deactivate` breach never counts as a failure. The first restart waits 1 s and the second 5 s. A third failure inside 10 minutes disables the plugin on that side until the user turns it on again. A job failure never counts toward this rule.

<pre class="term"><span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:17</span> <span class="t-err">error</span> deadline breach in on-events: limit 20 ms
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:17</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>  restarting in 1 s (failure 1 of 3 in 10 minutes)
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:02:18</span> <span class="t-ok">ok</span>    example.notes is running again
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:09:02</span> <span class="t-err">error</span> deadline breach in on-events: limit 20 ms
<span class="t-dim">2026-10-11 10:09:02</span> <span class="t-warn">warn</span>  plugin example.notes is now disabled (failure 3 of 3)
</pre>

Illustrative, not generated. The first breach restarts the plugin after 1 s. The third breach inside 10 minutes disables it.

## Limits you can change

The manifest `limits` block sets a value per plugin and side. The host clamps a request above the ceiling to the ceiling and logs the clamp. It never refuses the manifest for that reason. The user can set the same keys under `[plugins.limits]` in `config.toml`, for every plugin or for the whole session.

```json
{
  "limits": { "event_deadline_ms": 40, "job_wall_ms": 60000 }
}
```

| Key | Default | Ceiling, T1 | Ceiling, T2 and T3 | Effect when breached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `event_deadline_ms` | 20 | 50 | 20 | Trap |
| `command_deadline_ms` | 50 | 100 | 50 | Trap |
| `render_deadline_ms` | 10 | 20 | 10 | Trap |
| `activate_deadline_ms` | 2000 | 5000 | 2000 | Trap |
| `job_deadline_ms` (CPU) | 2000 | 60000 | 10000 | `failed(timed-out)` |
| `job_wall_ms` | 20000 | 600000 | 100000 | `failed(timed-out)` |
| `job_memory_mib` | 64 | 512 | 256 | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| `job_io_mib` (input and output, each) | 16 | 64 | 16 | `invalid-argument` |
| `concurrent_jobs` | 2 | 8 | 2 | Further jobs queue |
| `job_queue` | 16 | 64 | 16 | `busy` |

The contract also has nine requestable limits in the same form. They bound the host services that cost the most.

| Key | Default | Ceiling, T1 | Ceiling, T2 and T3 | Effect when breached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `http_streams` (open streams) | 4 | 16 | 4 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `children` (spawned child processes) | 2 | 8 | 2 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `durable_timers` | 64 | 256 | 64 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `vector_indexes` | 4 | 16 | 4 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `vector_entries` (all indexes) | 10,000 | 200,000 | 50,000 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `shared_cache_mib` | 64 | 256 | 128 | Oldest entries evicted |
| `journal_entries` (per pane) | 5,000 | 20,000 | 5,000 | Oldest trimmed |
| `toasts_pending` | 3 | 3 | 3 | Oldest replaced |
| `package_assets_mib` | 64 | 256 | 64 | `manifest.asset-size` |

A bundled plugin with the top-level manifest key `limits_tier: "first-party"` also lifts the settings caps and the `list-editor` cap. That tier is for bundled `ilium.` plugins only.

Tier T1 is a bundled plugin. T2 is signed by a publisher key the user trusts. T3 is an unsigned local package. A per-kind `deadline_ms` or `memory_mib` in `contributes.jobs` overrides the job defaults for that kind, within the same ceilings.

## Fixed caps

These caps do not change. A value over a per-call cap that the plugin can know in advance is refused with `invalid-argument`, and nothing is written or sent.

| Item | Cap | Error when exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Storage key / value | 256 bytes / 1 MiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Storage bucket (default quota) | 16 MiB | `quota-exceeded` |
| Node metadata value | 64 KiB per node | `quota-exceeded` |
| `fs.read` per call | `max-bytes` up to 1 MiB, `max-entries` up to 4,096 | `invalid-argument` |
| `fs.read-all` file (default limit) | 64 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| HTTP response (default limit) | 8 MiB | `failed(quota-exceeded)` |
| Topic payload | 64 KiB | `invalid-argument` |
| Log line | 16 KiB, cut and marked | Line cut, not refused |
| Log lines per second, third-party | 200 | Dropped and counted |
| Dedup window for `dedup-key` | 10 minutes | A retry after the window is a new submission |
| `check-list` items / `list-editor` items | 256 / 64 | `invalid-argument` on render |
| Popups per view | 4 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Minimap marks per layer, meter segments | 4,096 / 8 | `invalid-argument` |
| Catalogue page | 256 items | Clamped |
| `read-cells` rows per call | 1,000 | `quota-exceeded` |
| `history-text` | 4 MiB, newest kept | Truncated |
| `write-glyphs` cells per frame | 131,072 | `quota-exceeded` |
| Pre-rendered scene loop | 30 fps, 3,600 frames, 128 MiB | `manifest.scene-prerender` |
| HTTP stream chunk | 1 MiB | Split |
| `vector.embed` | 256 texts of at most 8 KiB | `invalid-argument` |

## Further deadlines and rates

New provider exports run under short deadlines. A breach counts like any other deadline breach, except that `menu-items` and `tokens` fall back to static content instead of failing the user action.

| Call | Deadline |
|---|---|
| `catalog-provider.query-catalog`, `menu-provider.menu-items`, `virtual-rows-provider.list-virtual-children` | 20 ms |
| `token-provider.tokens` | 10 ms per call |
| `client-requests.request` timeout | 1 to 30,000 ms, set per request |

The host also limits how often a plugin may call some imports. A call over the rate is refused with `rate-limited` and `retry-after-ms`, so a plugin that updates a widget in a loop spends nothing on the refused calls.

| Rate | Limit |
|---|---|
| `toast` | 3 per 10 s per plugin |
| `geocode` | 1 request per second per plugin |
| `set-status-segment`, `set-frame-slot` | 10 per second per slot |
| `set-row-state`, `set-item-states`, `set-choice-items`, `set-info-rich`, `set-meter`, `set-info` | 10 per second per plugin, together |
| `journal.log-event` | 20 per second per plugin |
| `screen-changed` delivery | At most 10 per second per pane |

Session-wide, at most 64 HTTP streams and 16 spawned children are open across all plugins, and a pane has one input lock at a time.

## What the new widgets and services cost

Most of the 51 widgets cost nothing between renders, because the host draws the tree. The table lists where a plugin does pay.

| Feature | Where the cost lands | Advice |
|---|---|---|
| `spinner`, decoration frame animation | The host steps frames. The plugin is not called per frame. | Use them instead of a timer that calls `ui.invalidate` every 100 ms. |
| `chart` with many points | Render size: the tree limit is 4,096 nodes or 1,024 KiB. | Send a series with `resample: min-max` and let the host reduce it to the width of the chart. |
| `check-list`, `list-editor`, `%list` | Items are part of the tree. | `check-list` is capped at 256 items and `list-editor` at 64; a larger one fails at render time with `invalid-argument`. A `%list` has no item cap, but the whole tree is limited to 4,096 nodes and 1,024 KiB by default. Render a window of rows from the host-owned `offset` (read through `ui.widget-state`) and add a Load more row. Virtual-row providers are for sidebar rows of the tree only. See recipe 4 of the [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/). |
| `choice` with a catalogue `source` | The host pages the catalogue, 256 items per page, with a 20 ms provider deadline. | Return one page per call. Never build the whole catalogue in `query-catalog`. |
| `terminal-view`, `video`, `surface` | Native decode and frame pacing. The plugin pays only for the frames it writes. | Prefer `prerender` for a scene that loops, so `render` is called once per frame and then never again. |
| `screen-changed`, `http-stream-data`, `child-output` | Event volume. | Read only the rows in `first-row` to `last-row`. Handle a whole batch in one call. |
| `set-meter`, `set-row-state` and friends | Rate limit, 10 per second together. | Update when a value changes by a visible step, not on every sample. |
| `vector` index | The host does the exact cosine search. | Stay under the `vector_entries` limit. Call `embed` with up to 256 texts at once. |
| `process.spawn` | Low priority under the plugin CPU quota. | Use `line-mode` so the plugin gets whole lines. |

<div class="note">
<p>The deadline is wall time from the start of your call to its return. Host work that runs inside a synchronous import counts, because your code is waiting for it. Host work that finishes after your call returned does not count: the rendering of a <code>surface</code> frame, a <code>chart</code> resample, a <code>video</code> decode, an HTTP request and the application of your submissions. A call that returns a request id costs you only the call. See <a href="/pages/reference-host-scheduling/">Host scheduling</a>.</p>
</div>

## One table of budgets

The limits of a plugin are spread over several pages. This table puts the ones that decide whether a plugin stays alive in one place, with the action the host takes. The values are defined in [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) and repeated here only so that you can compare them. When the two pages differ, the reference wins.

| Budget | Default | Ceiling, T1 | Ceiling, T2 and T3 | When exceeded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `memory_mib` (one instance) | 32 | 256 | 128 | Trap, counts as a failure |
| Session memory pool (all instances) | 1,024 MiB | 4,096 MiB, all tiers (user config only) | same, no per-tier ceiling | The new instance is refused with `session.memory-exceeded`; no failure. Each instance reserves its `memory_mib` at activation |
| `storage_bucket_mib` (one bucket) | 16 | 256 | 16 | `put` fails with `quota-exceeded` |
| Restore bytes from `deactivate` | 1 MiB | 1 MiB | 1 MiB | Dropped, one warn line |
| `deactivate_deadline_ms` | 500 | 1,000 | 500 | Instance dropped, no restore bytes |
| `ilium-execution` quota group | shared | shared | shared | Submissions return `quota-exceeded` with `retry-after-ms` |

A plugin may ask for more in its manifest, and the host clamps the request to the ceiling of its tier (see [Limits you can change](#limits-you-can-change)). A plugin MUST be designed to run within the default of its tier, not within the ceiling. [AUT-101]

A plugin SHOULD stay under half of each default budget in normal use, so that a bad input does not trap it. [AUT-102]

## Caching: where to keep rebuildable data

Storage has three durable buckets (`global`, `project`, `session`), one cache bucket (`shared`) and the `/cache` folder of the `fs` scope. They differ in who clears them and what they count against.

| Place | Cleared by the host | Counts against | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `global`, `project`, `session` | Never | `storage_bucket_mib` | Data you cannot rebuild |
| `shared` bucket | At any time, oldest first | `shared_cache_mib` | Small rebuildable values shared by all sessions |
| `/cache` in `fs` | At any time | `disk_mib`, with `data` | Large rebuildable files |
| Memory | On restart | `memory_mib` | Data rebuilt per run |

Rebuildable data MUST NOT go into a durable bucket, as rule AUT-008 of the cookbook also requires, because it uses up the 16 MiB that user data needs. [AUT-103] The recipe with the lease and the time limit is in the [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/).

## Measuring from outside the plugin

The host and the command line give four ways to see where time and memory go. They are specified in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) and [Resource accounting](/pages/reference-resource-accounting/).

| What you want | Command or call | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Time of one handler while you build | `clock.monotonic-millis` around the work, shown in a `meter` or written to the log | Your own number, available in every build |
| Timings while you edit | `ilium plugin dev --timings` | Time per export call during a development session |
| A profile of a running plugin | `ilium plugin profile <id> --duration <seconds>` | One timing record per export that ran |
| Use against the limits | `ilium plugin stats <id>` | Current use and the effective limit of each resource |
| Static weak spots | `ilium plugin lint` | Rules such as `lint.limit-above-ceiling` and `lint.activation-startup` |

A debug build (`ilium plugin build --debug`) is slower than a release build. Timings for comparison with the targets MUST come from a release build. [AUT-105]

A plugin that reports its own timing SHOULD read it with `monotonic-millis` and SHOULD NOT depend on a host tool being installed in the user's setup. [AUT-104]

## Measuring a handler

The `clock` import gives a monotonic millisecond counter. A plugin can time its own work and show the result in a `meter`, so a slow handler is visible long before it breaches the 20 ms deadline. The panel below shows the share of the event deadline that the last batch used.

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Handler budget ───────────────────────╮
│ Last batch ………………………………………………………………………… <span class="t-ok">8 ms</span> │
│ <span class="t-ok">█████</span><span class="t-dim">░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░</span>   8 of 20 ms       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯</pre>
<figcaption>Illustrative, not generated. A plugin panel that shows how much of the 20 ms event deadline the last batch used. The bar turns to the warning colour above half the deadline.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::clock;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ui::MeterSegment;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::text::Tone;

const EVENT_DEADLINE_MS: u64 = 20;

impl Handler for Notes {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let started = clock::monotonic_millis();
        let submissions = self.handle_batch(batch);
        self.last_batch_ms = clock::monotonic_millis() - started;
        submissions
    }
}

fn budget_segments(used_ms: u64) -> Vec<MeterSegment> {
    let tone = if used_ms * 2 > EVENT_DEADLINE_MS { Tone::Warning } else { Tone::Success };
    vec![MeterSegment { label: "batch".into(), value: used_ms as f64, tone }]
}
// In render: tree.meter(budget_segments(self.last_batch_ms)).max(EVENT_DEADLINE_MS as f64).show_values(true)
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { monotonicMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import { meter } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/ui/build';

const EVENT_DEADLINE_MS = 20;
let lastBatchMs = 0;

// inside onEvents(batch)
const started = monotonicMillis();
const submissions = handleBatch(batch);
lastBatchMs = Number(monotonicMillis() - started);

// inside render
const tone = lastBatchMs * 2 > EVENT_DEADLINE_MS ? 'warning' : 'success';
const budget = meter([{ label: 'batch', value: lastBatchMs, tone }], { max: EVENT_DEADLINE_MS, showValues: true });
```

## Performance targets

The host has a fixed set of budgets and a benchmark for each. They are not rules for your plugin, but they show what the host promises: an empty host call under 1 µs, an event batch to 30 plugins under 2 ms, a cold start of 40 bundled plugins under 150 ms, and a key press to the terminal in 5 ms. The list, the method and the thresholds are in [Performance budgets and benchmarks](/pages/reference-host-budgets/). The detector budget is in the [detection loop](/pages/capability-agent-signatures/#detection-loop).

### Costs by tier and language

| Choice | Cost | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| T1 plugin | A host call is a function call inside the process: about 1 µs. | Nothing special. |
| T2 or T3 plugin | Each host call that has an effect, such as `storage.set` or a submission, is one round trip to the host: 0.2 ms median and 0.5 ms at the 99th percentile. Pure imports such as `codec` and `vector` run inside the helper with no round trip. | Batch work. In a 20 ms batch, 20 forwarded calls can use half of the budget. Read once, write once. |
| T2 or T3 start | A helper process starts at the first activation: record 20 to 80 ms. | Use lazy activation triggers; do not activate at startup without need. |
| Rust component | Instance about 4 MiB, start under 5 ms. | The default choice for scenes and detectors. |
| TypeScript component | Includes a JavaScript engine: a larger component and instance, and slower code than Rust. Budget it at several times the memory of a Rust plugin and measure your handlers. | Keep TypeScript handlers short. Put heavy loops in a job, or write them in Rust. Measure a TypeScript scene against its frame budget. |

Memory counts against `memory_mib` for the plugin and, for T2 and T3, `memory_mib` plus 32 MiB against the session. See [Sandbox helper protocol](/pages/reference-host-helper/).

These are the targets for the tools in [Debugging tools](/pages/reference-debugging-tools/) and [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/). They apply to the test and profile tooling, not to a plugin.

- **[DEV-850]** Tracing MUST add no more than 5 percent to the time of an event batch, and profiling MUST NOT change call time by more than 5 percent.
- **[DEV-851]** A native-mode harness test of one event batch SHOULD finish in under 10 ms, and a component-mode test in under 100 ms, on the build host, excluding the one-time load of the component.
- **[DEV-852]** `ilium plugin check` SHOULD finish in under 2 s for a package of 10 MiB or less, and `ilium plugin lint` in under 5 s.
- **[DEV-853]** `ilium plugin dev` SHOULD reload a plugin within 1 s after the build finishes, and the debounce of a change is 300 ms.

## Where time is charged
