
Widget state set by the host includes `check-list` item states (`tri`), `geo`, `number`, `split` (per mille) and `ids` cases. At most four popups are open per view.

## Reacting to UI actions

A `ui-action` event carries `view`, `key`, `kind` (`ActionKind`) and `value` (`ActionValue`). There are 17 kinds (including `hover-enter`, `hover-leave`, `pointer`, `drag-over`, `resized` and `filter-changed`) and 12 value cases (including `pointer`, `drag-over`, `item-state`, `geo` and `ids`). `scrolled`, `pointer` and `drag-over` are coalesced; the others are never dropped.

| New kind | Sent by | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `hover-enter`, `hover-leave` | nodes with `HOVER_EVENTS` | none |
| `pointer` | nodes with `POINTER_EVENTS` | `pointer(ViewPointer)` with kind, button, modifiers, column, row, `sub_x`, `sub_y`, clicks |
| `drag-over` | drop targets during a drag | `drag-over(DragOverValue { source_key, target_key, index, accept })` |
| `resized` | `split` | `number` (per mille) |
| `filter-changed` | `list`, `choice` | `text`, debounced 150 ms |

| New value | Rust | TypeScript |
|---|---|---|
| view pointer | `ActionValue::Pointer(ViewPointer)` | `{ tag: 'pointer', val: {...} }` |
| drag feedback | `ActionValue::DragOver(DragOverValue)` | `{ tag: 'drag-over', val: {...} }` |
| check item | `ActionValue::ItemState(String, TriState)` | `{ tag: 'item-state', val: [id, state] }` |
| place | `ActionValue::Geo(GeoPoint)` | `{ tag: 'geo', val: { lat, lon } }` |
| selection | `ActionValue::Ids(Vec<String>)` | `{ tag: 'ids', val: ['a', 'b'] }` |

**Rust**

```rust
// Answer a drag: the next render sets the target's accept prop.
let Event::UiAction(UiAction { key, kind, value, .. }) = event else { return };
match (kind, value) {
    (ActionKind::DragOver, ActionValue::DragOver(over)) => {
        self.accept = if over.index == 0 { DropAccept::Before } else { DropAccept::Inside };
    }
    (ActionKind::Pointer, ActionValue::Pointer(pointer)) if pointer.kind == PointerKind::Down => {
        self.start_selection(&key, pointer.column, pointer.row, pointer.sub_x);
    }
    (ActionKind::Resized, ActionValue::Number(per_mille)) => self.remember_split(per_mille),
    _ => {}
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// Answer a drag: the next render sets the target's accept prop.
if (event.tag !== 'ui-action') return;
const { key, kind, value } = event.val;
if (kind === 'drag-over' && value.tag === 'drag-over') {
  accept = value.val.index === 0 ? 'before' : 'inside';
} else if (kind === 'pointer' && value.tag === 'pointer' && value.val.kind === 'down') {
  startSelection(key, value.val.column, value.val.row, value.val.subX);
} else if (kind === 'resized' && value.tag === 'number') {
  rememberSplit(value.val);
}
```

## Events and intents

The 18 events listed below arrive in `on_events` / `onEvents` like any other. The 23 intents and the five extended ones are submitted the same way (see [Events and intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/) for every payload). Names follow the naming rule: `Event::ScreenChanged(..)` and `{ tag: 'screen-changed', val }`, `Intent::FreezePane(FreezePaneSpec)` and `{ tag: 'freeze-pane', val }`.

| Area | Intents | Extended intents |
|---|---|---|
| Pane lifecycle (`panes.lifecycle`) | `freeze-pane`, `unfreeze-pane`, `replace-pane-command`, `terminate-pane-process`, `resize-pane` | `send-input` (`if-current`, `lock-user-input`, returns `ok-epoch`) |
| Tree (`tree.restructure`, `tree.write`, `tree.attention`) | `create-group`, `create-folder`, `create-project`, `create-split`, `set-bookmarked`, `set-expanded`, `restructure`, `revert-restructure`, `set-inferred-icon`, `mark-attention`, `ack-attention` | `rename-node` (`expected-revision`), `set-virtual-rows` (parents, drops) |
| Chrome (`ui.chrome`, `notify.toast`, `open-external`) | `open-external`, `set-status-segment`, `clear-status-segment`, `set-frame-slot`, `clear-frame-slot`, `toast`, `dismiss-toast` | `set-decoration` (spans, tooltip, frames), `notify` (coalesce key) |

**Rust**

```rust
// Freeze a pane for a stable read, then send guarded input.
let freeze = Submission::keyed(
    Intent::FreezePane(FreezePaneSpec { pane }),
    dedup::key_for(&["freeze", &pane.to_string()]),
);
let send = Submission::new(Intent::SendInput(SendInputSpec {
    if_current: Some(self.last_epoch),
    ..SendInputSpec::text(pane, "continue\n")
}));
vec![freeze, send]
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// Freeze a pane for a stable read, then send guarded input.
return [
  { intent: { tag: 'freeze-pane', val: { pane } }, correlation: 1n, dedupKey: `freeze:${pane}` },
  { intent: { tag: 'send-input', val: { pane, text: 'continue\n', ifCurrent: lastEpoch } },
    correlation: 2n, dedupKey: undefined },
];
```

The 18 events, all appended to the `event` variant: `screen-changed`, `user-line-submitted`, `signal-changed`, `agent-model-changed`, `editor-pointer`, `editor-viewport-changed`, `http-stream-data`, `http-stream-closed`, `child-output`, `child-exited`, `pane-lifecycle-changed`, `attention-changed`, `client-request`, `kernel-settings-changed`, `keymap-changed`, `durable-timer-fired`, `input-uncertain` and `display-mode-changed`. In Rust they are `Event::ScreenChanged(..)` and so on; in TypeScript `{ tag: 'screen-changed', val }`. Each needs the grant listed on [Events and intents](/pages/reference-events-and-intents/). Match on the tag and ignore tags you do not know.

## Host services

Each service is a module in the table above, gated by a grant. All of the following run in both SDKs; slow calls are awaited as described earlier.

**Rust**

```rust
// catalogs (server or client): query a provider, page with the cursor.
let page = catalogs::query(CatalogQuery { catalog: "ilium.palettes".into(), filter: Some("sun".into()), cursor: None, limit: 50 }).await?;
// geocode (client, location.geocode): search and reverse.
let places = geocode::search("Lisbon", 5).await?;            // Vec<GeoPlace>
// fs: atomic write with a revision guard, and a tail for logs.
let written = fs::write_atomic(&path, bytes, Some(revision)).await?;     // Revisioned
let chunk = fs::tail(&path, cursor, 64 * 1024).await?;                    // TailChunk
// http: a streamed response (server-sent events).
let stream = http::open_stream(StreamRequest { request, framing: StreamFraming::ServerSentEvents, max_chunk_bytes: 16 * 1024 }).await?;
// vector: embed text, store, search (inference.embed).
let ids = vector::embed(&["notes on retries".to_string()], "search").await?;
// process: spawn a long-lived child (process.long-lived).
let child = process::spawn(SpawnSpec { process: spec, stdin_open: true, line_mode: true })?;
child.write_stdin(b"ping\n")?;
// durable timers and journal.
timers::at("nightly", 86_400_000, true)?;
journal::log_event("moved", &payload)?;
// kernel settings and keymap (read-only).
let value = kernel_settings::read("terminal.scrollback")?;
let chord = keymap::bindings("palette.open")?;
// client requests: ask the attached client to do something.
let answer = client_requests::request("pick-file", &args).await?;
// sessions (server): list and send to another session.
let all = sessions::list_live()?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as catalogs from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/catalogs';
import * as geocode from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/geocode';
import * as fs from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/fs';
import * as http from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/http';
import * as vector from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/vector';
import * as proc from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/process';
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';
import * as journal from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/journal';
import * as kernel from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/kernel-settings';
import * as keymap from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/keymap';
import * as clientRequests from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/client-requests';
import * as sessions from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/sessions';

const page = await catalogs.query({ catalog: 'ilium.palettes', filter: 'sun', cursor: undefined, limit: 50 });
const places = await geocode.search('Lisbon', 5);                         // GeoPlace[]
const written = await fs.writeAtomic(path, bytes, revision);              // Revisioned
const chunk = await fs.tail(path, cursor, 64 * 1024);                     // TailChunk
const stream = await http.stream({ request, framing: 'server-sent-events', maxChunkBytes: 16 * 1024 });
const ids = await vector.embed(['notes on retries'], 'search');
const child = proc.spawn({ process: spec, stdinOpen: true, lineMode: true });
child.writeStdin(new TextEncoder().encode('ping\n'));
timers.setDurable('nightly', 86_400_000n, true);
journal.append('moved', payload);
const value = kernel.get('terminal.scrollback');
const chord = keymap.lookup('palette.open');
const answer = await clientRequests.request('pick-file', args);
const all = sessions.list();
```

Terminal, agent, editor and basic primitives gain the following functions, each behind the grant named in the table.

| Primitive | Rust | TypeScript | Grant |
|---|---|---|---|
| terminal | `read_cells`, `modes`, `foreground_process`, `freeze_snapshot`, `history_text`, `search_history`, `lock_input` | `readCells`, `modes`, `foregroundProcess`, `freezeSnapshot`, `historyText`, `searchHistory`, `lockInput` | `terminal.read-cells`, `terminal.history`, `terminal.input-lock` |
| agent | `model`, `prompt_epoch`, `transcript` | `model`, `promptEpoch`, `transcript` | `agent.transcript` for `transcript` |
| editor | `viewport`, `set_minimap_marks` | `viewport`, `setMinimapMarks` | existing editor grants |
| basic | `report_activity`, `set_dirty` | `reportActivity`, `setDirty` | none beyond `basic` |
| cli | additions listed on [cli](/pages/api-cli/) | same, camelCase | `cli` |
| ui | `open_popup_with`, `theme_extras` | `openPopupWith`, `themeExtras` | `ui.chrome` for chrome surfaces |

`gpu` is `@unstable`: import it only from a scene and expect it to change. Ten of the 23 grants are high risk and prompt the user with a separate consent line: `terminal.history`, `terminal.input-lock`, `terminal.raw-input`, `panes.lifecycle`, `tree.restructure`, `sessions.cross`, `process.long-lived`, `agent.transcript`, `settings.read-kernel:api` and `settings.write-kernel:<tab-id>`. See [Capabilities](/pages/reference-capabilities/) and [Security](/pages/security/).

## Settings rows, meters and row state

The manifest `settings` object declares 18 row types. The plugin updates a row's state at run time without republishing the manifest.

**Rust**

```rust
// Meter row filled from the plugin, and a state banner on a row.
ui::set_meter("usage.spend", vec![MeterSegment { label: "today".into(), value: 4.2, tone: Tone::Info }])?;
ui::set_row_state("provider.key", RowState { kind: RowStateKind::Warning, message: "Key expires in 3 days".into() })?;
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
// Meter row filled from the plugin, and a state banner on a row.
setMeter('usage.spend', [{ label: 'today', value: 4.2, tone: 'info' }]);
setRowState('provider.key', { kind: 'warning', message: 'Key expires in 3 days' });
```

The manifest side, identical for both languages:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "settings": {
      "sections": [{
        "id": "usage", "title": "Usage",
        "rows": [
          { "id": "usage.spend", "type": "meter", "label": "Spend" },
          { "id": "provider.key", "type": "text", "label": "API key", "secret": true },
          { "id": "sky.location", "type": "location", "label": "Location" }
        ]
      }]
    }
  }
}
```

See [Settings schema](/pages/reference-settings-schema/) for all 18 row types.

## Provider exports

Each optional export is a small trait or object.

**Rust**

```rust
impl CatalogProvider for MyPlugin {
    fn query_catalog(&mut self, query: CatalogQuery) -> Result<CatalogPage, PluginError> {
        let items = self.palettes.iter()
            .filter(|p| query.filter.as_deref().map_or(true, |f| p.name.contains(f)))
            .map(|p| CatalogItem::new(&p.id, &p.name)).collect();
        Ok(CatalogPage { items, next: None, total: Some(self.palettes.len() as u64) })
    }
}
impl TokenProvider for MyPlugin {
    fn tokens(&mut self, buffer: BufferId, first_line: u32, lines: Vec<String>, state_in: Option<Vec<u8>>)
        -> (Vec<Token>, Option<Vec<u8>>) {
        let found = lines.iter().enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(i, l)| l.find('#').map(|c| Token { line: first_line + i as u32, start: c as u32, length: (l.len() - c) as u32, kind: TokenKind::Comment }))
            .collect();
        (found, state_in)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const provider = definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  queryCatalog(query) {
    const items = palettes
      .filter((p) => query.filter === undefined || p.name.includes(query.filter))
      .map((p) => ({ id: p.id, label: p.name }));
    return { items, next: undefined, total: BigInt(palettes.length) };
  },
  tokens(buffer, firstLine, lines, stateIn) {
    const found = lines.flatMap((l, i) => l.includes('#')
      ? [{ line: firstLine + i, start: l.indexOf('#'), length: l.length - l.indexOf('#'), kind: 'comment' as const }]
      : []);
    return [found, stateIn];
  },
});
```

The manifest lists the exports and the contribution keys that point at them: `catalogs`, `tree_toolbar`, `row_actions`, `tree_orderings`, `status_segments`, `pane_frame_slots`, `display_modes`, `client_requests` and `languages`, plus the top-level `limits_tier`. All are explained on [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/).

## Extension points

The `extensions` host interface lets a plugin read the contributions to its own points and run hooks. A plugin that contributes handlers implements `hook-handler`. The contract is in [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/). The examples below are illustrations and are not compiled.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::extensions;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::exports::HookHandler;

// Owner: needs extensions.provide:com.example.notes/after-save
let entries = extensions::list("com.example.notes/recognisers")?;
let request = extensions::run_hook("com.example.notes/after-save", &payload_json).await;
// Outcome ok: take the reply. refused(extension.vetoed): do not perform the action.

// Contributor: needs extensions.contribute:com.example.notes/after-save
impl HookHandler for MyPlugin {
    fn handle_hook(&mut self, call: HookCall) -> HookReply {
        match call.extension.as_str() {
            "strip-tokens" => HookReply::Replace(strip(&call.payload_json)),
            "no-secrets" if has_secret(&call.payload_json) => HookReply::Refuse("secret in text".into()),
            _ => HookReply::Pass,
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { list, runHook } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/extensions';

// Owner: needs extensions.provide:com.example.notes/after-save
const entries = list('com.example.notes/recognisers');
const outcome = await runHook('com.example.notes/after-save', payloadJson);

// Contributor: needs extensions.contribute:com.example.notes/after-save
const plugin = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  hookHandler(call) {
    if (call.extension === 'strip-tokens') return { tag: 'replace', val: strip(call.payloadJson) };
    if (hasSecret(call.payloadJson)) return { tag: 'refuse', val: 'secret in text' };
    return { tag: 'pass' };
  },
});
```

Reply constructors: Rust `HookReply::Pass`, `HookReply::Replace(json)`, `HookReply::Refuse(reason)` and `HookReply::Answer(json)`. TypeScript `{ tag: 'pass' }`, `{ tag: 'replace', val: json }`, `{ tag: 'refuse', val: reason }` and `{ tag: 'answer', val: json }`. A reply that the point's mode does not allow counts as a pass. `register` and `unregister` work only on collect points with `dynamic: true`. The owner receives the topic `ilium.extensions/changed` and calls `list` again.

## Scenes

A scene plugin (`side = "scene"`) draws into a surface and follows the shared look; colour, dither and display settings are never scene settings.

**Rust**

```rust
#[ilium_plugin(side = "scene", exports = ["renderer"])]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Waves { phase: f32 }

impl Renderer for Waves {
    fn frame(&mut self, surface: &mut Surface, delta_ms: u32) {
        self.phase += delta_ms as f32 * 0.001;
        surface.clear();
        for x in 0..surface.width() { surface.set_tone(x, (self.phase + x as f32 * 0.2).sin() * 0.5 + 0.5); }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export const { lifecycle, handler, renderer } = defineScene({
  frame(surface, deltaMs) {
    phase += deltaMs * 0.001;
    surface.clear();
    for (let x = 0; x < surface.width(); x++) surface.setTone(x, Math.sin(phase + x * 0.2) * 0.5 + 0.5);
  },
});
```

The glyph-plane surface adds font loading through `anim::fonts` (`Font` resource) and palette delivery. See [Porting IliumAnim](/pages/porting-iliumanim/) and [Performance](/pages/performance/).

## Worked example: a working badge

The plugin puts a short badge on every agent that starts working.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::log::{self, Level};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::events::AgentActivityEvent;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::intents::SetDecorationSpec;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::tree::AgentActivity;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Hello;

impl Lifecycle for Hello {
    fn activate(&mut self, context: Activation) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        log::log(Level::Info, &format!("hello from {}", context.plugin));
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Handler for Hello {
    fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
        let mut submissions = Vec::new();
        for event in batch {
            let Event::AgentActivityChanged(AgentActivityEvent { node, current, .. }) = event
            else { continue };
            if current != AgentActivity::Working { continue; }
            submissions.push(Submission::new(Intent::SetDecoration(SetDecorationSpec {
                node, slot: "hello".into(), content: vec![Span::plain("hi")],
                icon: None, sort_key: None, persist: false,
                ..Default::default()   // the optional fields: spans, tooltip, frames, tone
            })));
        }
        submissions
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { log } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/log';

export const { lifecycle, handler } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  activate(context) { log('info', `hello from ${context.plugin}`); },
  onEvents(batch) {
    return batch.flatMap((event) =>
      event.tag === 'agent-activity-changed' && event.val.current === 'working'
        ? [{ intent: { tag: 'set-decoration', val: {
              node: event.val.node, slot: 'hello', content: [{ text: 'hi' }], persist: false } },
             correlation: 0n, dedupKey: undefined }]
        : []);
  },
});
```

The manifest, shared by both:

```json
{
  "server": { "entry": "server.wasm", "world": "ilium:server/base@0.1.0", "exports": [] },
  "capabilities": { "server": ["agent.read", "tree.decorate"] },
  "contributes": {
    "decoration_slots": [{ "id": "hello", "placement": "badge", "priority": 50 }]
  }
}
```

## Testing

The test double runs a plugin against a fake host in the same process. Rust enables it with the `testing` feature; TypeScript imports `@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing` and runs under `bun test`. The exact methods, limits and error codes are in [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/). The how-to is [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/).

| Operation | Rust (`testing::FakeHost`) | TypeScript (`createFakeHost()`) |
|---|---|---|
| Create from the manifest | `FakeHost::for_manifest("manifest.json")?` | `createFakeHost().forManifest('manifest.json')` |
| Grant a capability | `.grant("tree.decorate")` before activation, `grant_now` after | `.grant('tree.decorate')`, `grantNow` after |
| Activate | `host.activate::<Hello>()` returns a `PluginHandle` | `await host.activate({ lifecycle, handler })` or `await host.activateModule('../src/server')` |
| Build events | `events::activity(node, previous, current)`, `events::command(name, arguments_json)` | `events.activity(node, previous, current)`, `events.command(name, argumentsJson)` |
| Deliver events | `host.deliver(events)` returns `Vec<Submission>` | `host.deliver(events)` returns the submissions |
| Deliver outcomes | `host.settle()` | `await host.settle()` |
| Render | `host.render(ViewTarget::Panel("main".into()), 62, 12)` | `host.render({ tag: 'panel', val: 'main' }, 62, 12)` |
| Read the screen | `screen.row(n)`, `screen.cell(row, column)` | `screen.row(n)`, `screen.cell(row, column)` |

```rust
#[test]
fn badge_is_set_when_agent_works() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::for_manifest("manifest.json").unwrap();
    host.activate::<Hello>();
    let submissions = host.deliver(vec![events::activity(7, AgentActivity::Idle, AgentActivity::Working)]);
    assert_eq!(submissions.len(), 1);
}
```

```ts
import { test, expect } from 'bun:test';
import { createFakeHost, events } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing';

test('badge is set when agent works', async () => {
  const host = createFakeHost().forManifest('manifest.json');
  await host.activateModule('../src/server');
  expect(host.deliver([events.activity(7n, 'idle', 'working')]).length).toBe(1);
});
```

The harness has a golden-file helper, `assert_golden`, a pointer helper, `click`, and `FakeSession` for tests with several plugins. See the reference page.

## Package surface

The SDK does not build packages. The `ilium plugin` command does that, from the files of the project. A plugin author touches the package in three places: the manifest, the `help/` folder and the `dist/` output. The build stages, the package layout and the signing steps are in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/) and [Packages](/pages/packages/). `ilium plugin pack` builds an unsigned package. `ilium plugin sign` signs it.

## SDK versioning policy

The SDK version has its own number, separate from the contract `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. A new SDK release that keeps the contract compatible raises the minor or patch number. An SDK release that needs a new contract version raises the contract and writes the change in the changelog of the SDK. `ilium plugin check` fails with `component.api-version-mismatch` when the component and the manifest name different contract versions. See [Versioning](/pages/versioning/).

## Edge cases

- A batch holds at most 256 events and a submission list at most 256 entries; a larger list traps the instance with `trap.submission-batch`.
- A crashed instance restarts after 1 s, then 5 s; the third failure within 10 minutes disables the plugin until the user enables it.
- `on_events` has a 20 ms deadline, `render` 10 ms, `activate` 2000 ms and `deactivate` 500 ms. A breach traps the instance.
- Instance memory is capped at 32 MiB (the `memory_mib` manifest key can raise it, up to 128 MiB for T2 and T3 plugins).
- A log message over 16 KiB is cut and ends with `…[truncated]`.
- An await that never completes is cancelled with `timed-out` when its request timeout elapses.
- `toolchain.sdk-missing`, `toolchain.language-ambiguous`, `manifest.exports-mismatch` and `package.old-format` stop `ilium plugin build` with a clear message.

# Plugin administration guide

## Plugin administration guide

This guide is for the person who looks after Ilium on a shared or managed machine. It shows how to allow, limit or forbid plugins, how to approve publishers, how to install plugins for people without prompts, how to keep an audit trail, and what to do when a plugin goes wrong. Everything here uses the admin policy file. The exact keys are in the [Admin policy reference](/pages/reference-admin-policy/); [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/) lists what users see.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[USR-nnn]`, collected in [User and administrator requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-user-admin/).

<div class="note">
<p>Decision status. The platform is not implemented. The rules about what a policy may do (stricter only) are fixed. The platform owner confirms the key names before release.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- What you control and what you do not
- Choose a stance
- Write the policy
- Approve a publisher
- Install for users without prompts
- Keep the audit trail
- Respond to a bad plugin
- Roll out a change
- Machines that are not Linux
- Check that the policy works
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### What you control and what you do not

You control which plugins may be installed, which tiers, which publishers, which grants may be given and where the always-on audit log is also sent. You do not control what a user decides inside those limits. Within the policy, each user still chooses their own permissions.

| You can | You cannot |
|---|---|
| Forbid all third-party plugins | Stop core or bundled plugins from running (they ship with Ilium) |
| Allow only signed plugins from named keys | Give a user a permission that the plugin did not request |
| Forbid chosen grants for every plugin | Read a user's plugin data through Ilium |
| Deny or allow plugin ids | Make a plugin run when the user turned it off |
| Read the always-on audit log of plugin events | Replace the kernel recovery page or hide it |

A policy can only make Ilium stricter. It cannot allow what the security model refuses, such as a third-party plugin on Windows or macOS.

- [USR-070] A policy MUST only restrict. No key of the policy MAY enable a plugin, grant or tier that Ilium refuses without a policy. Test: set `packages.allowed_tiers = ["t3"]` on Windows and assert that T3 is still refused.

### Choose a stance

| Stance | When it fits | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| Open | Personal or developer machines | no file |
| Signed only | A team that builds its own plugins | `packages.allowed_tiers = ["t1","t2"]` and `publishers.allow = [<your key>]` |
| Approved list | Regulated machines | `plugins.allow_ids = [...]` plus signed only |
| No third-party | Kiosks, shared lab machines | `packages.allow_third_party = false` |
| Open with limits | Mixed use | `grants.deny = ["http:*", "process.run:*"]` |

### Write the policy

The file is at the path for your system:

| System | Path |
|---|---|
| Linux | `/etc/ilium/policy.toml` |
| macOS | `/Library/Application Support/Ilium/policy.toml` |
| Windows | `%ProgramData%\Ilium\policy.toml` |

On Linux, create it as root, with the mode `0644`, owned by root. Ilium ignores a policy file that a normal user can write, shows a persistent notice, and records `policy-violation` in the audit log.

```sh
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/ilium
sudo install -m 0644 -o root -g root policy.toml /etc/ilium/policy.toml
```

A first policy for a team with its own signing key:

```toml
version = 1

[packages]
allowed_tiers = ["t1", "t2"]

[publishers]
allow = ["3f2a91c07b6d1e44a1b20c9e55d3f7a8b6c102e94d7798af13c56e0bd2f48a19"]

[grants]
deny = ["process.run:*", "sessions.cross"]

[audit]
keep_days = 180
```

Ilium reads the file when the server starts. A change takes effect at the next start, and a running plugin is not stopped by an edit. At that start a plugin the policy forbids is disabled and shown as "Blocked by policy". Its data stays on disk. A grant the policy denies is removed from the plugin, and the plugin keeps running without it.

### Approve a publisher

A fingerprint is the identity of a signing key. To approve a publisher:

1. Get the publisher's public key file (`publisher.pub`) from them by a route you trust.
2. Print its fingerprint: `ilium plugin trust add publisher.pub` prints it when run as a user, or read it from the package with `ilium plugin inspect notes.iliumpkg`.
3. Confirm the fingerprint with the publisher by a second route.
4. Put the fingerprint, in the 64-character form, into `publishers.allow`.

Users still see a trust prompt for the key on their first install, unless they already trust it. The policy decides whether the install is allowed at all; trust is each user's own answer. Removing a fingerprint from `publishers.allow` blocks the key's plugins at the next start.

To check a package before you hand it out:

```sh
ilium plugin inspect notes.iliumpkg --verify
```

This works offline. It recomputes every hash and compares it with the package's file list. A difference exits with 1 and the code `inspect.hash-mismatch`.

### Install for users without prompts

For scripts, images and setup tools there is no terminal, so the review dialog cannot show. Use:

```sh
ilium plugin install notes.iliumpkg --yes
ilium plugin install notes.iliumpkg --yes --grant terminal.history
```

`--yes` accepts every normal permission the package requests. A HIGH permission is given only if you name it with `--grant`. This runs as the user, writes to the user's folders, and is limited by the policy. Without `--yes` and without a terminal, the install fails with `install.review-required`.

There is no machine-wide plugin folder. Each user installs into their own profile. To give a plugin to many users, run the command in each user's login script or setup step, or place the package file where users can read it and let them install it.

- [USR-071] A non-interactive install without `--yes` MUST fail with `install.review-required`, and `--yes` MUST NOT grant a HIGH permission that is not named. Test: install a package with one HIGH row with `--yes` and assert that the row is declined.

### Keep the audit trail

The audit log is always on; there is nothing to enable. The host appends one JSON line for every install, update, uninstall, enable, disable, grant change, consent change, trust change, policy event and sandbox kill. The events are listed in the [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/) reference. A line holds the UTC time `ts`, a sequence number, the actor, the plugin id, the event and the result. It holds no plugin data and no setting values. Policy may set only `audit.sink`, `audit.max_mib` and `audit.keep_days`.

```sh
jq -r 'select(.event=="grant-given") | [.ts,.plugin_id,.grant] | @tsv' "$XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/audit/audit.jsonl"
```

The audit file is per user, in the user's state folder, because Ilium runs as that user. For a central copy set `[audit] sink = "syslog"` or `"journald"`. If the file cannot be written, no action is refused: the server queues up to 1,000 records, retries every 10 s and shows a notice.

### Respond to a bad plugin

1. **Stop it now.** Add its id to `plugins.deny_ids`. At the next server start every copy is disabled and shows "Blocked by policy".
2. **Block its key.** If a whole publisher is at fault, remove its fingerprint from `publishers.allow`.
3. **Find who has it.** Search the audit log for the plugin id.
4. **Clean up.** Ask users to run `ilium plugin uninstall <id> --purge`. The policy does not delete anything on its own.
5. **Remove the key.** Users can run `ilium plugin trust remove <publisher>`. Plugins signed with it then show `untrusted`.

Users see "Blocked by policy" and the detail code, for example `policy.id-denied`. See [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/).

### Roll out a change

1. Write the new policy to a temporary file next to the real one.
2. Check it for syntax. An unknown key or a wrong type makes the file malformed: at the next start T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load with `policy.invalid`, and the notice names the line.
3. Rename it over the old one. The rename is atomic.
4. Restart the sessions. Each server reads the policy at start only.

Test the policy on one machine first. A policy that forbids `ilium.core.*` has no effect, because the policy never stops a core plugin.

### Machines that are not Linux

On Windows and macOS, third-party plugins are refused at install, with or without a policy. The policy file is still read there. `grants.deny` has little effect, because only bundled plugins run, and the bundled plugins ignore `install` keys. Use the same file to keep your fleet uniform, and expect the refusal text "Cannot install <name> <version>."

### Check that the policy works

After writing a policy, check it with a throwaway user:

1. `ilium plugin doctor` warns when the platform allows T2 and T3 and a policy disables T3.
2. Try to install a package that the policy should block and read the error. Look for `policy.blocked` and the detail code.
3. Install an allowed package and open its Capabilities tab. Check that denied grants are locked and off.
4. Look at the audit log for the `policy-loaded` event and any `policy-violation` events.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| The policy file is unreadable | T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load with `policy.invalid`. Core and T1 plugins run |
| The policy file is writable by a user | The file is ignored, a persistent notice appears and the audit log records `policy-violation` |
| A bad edit (wrong type, unknown key) | The file is malformed: T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load with `policy.invalid`, and the notice names the line |
| The policy denies a grant a running plugin holds | At the next start the grant is removed. Calls return `not-permitted` with the reason `policy` |
| A user has their own `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | No effect on the system policy path |
| Two policies (system and per user) | The user file at `<user config dir>/policy.toml` can only add restrictions |

### Requirements

- [USR-072] An administrator MUST be able to block a running plugin by id, and the host MUST disable it at the next server start. Test: add the id while the plugin runs, restart the server and assert the state `Blocked by policy`.
- [USR-073] The documentation MUST state that the policy only restricts, where the file lives per system, and how to respond to a bad plugin. Test: search this page for the three statements.

### See also

- [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/)
- [Plugin files on disk](/pages/reference-plugin-files/)
- [Security](/pages/security/)
- [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/)
- [Plugin privacy](/pages/user-privacy/)
- [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/)
- [CLI reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# CI recipes

## CI recipes

This guide shows how to build, test, package and sign a plugin in a continuous integration (CI) pipeline. CI means a service that runs your commands on a clean machine after each push. The recipes use GitHub Actions and GitLab CI. The same commands work in any other system.

Terms:

- **Pipeline**: the list of CI steps.
- **Runner**: the machine that runs the steps.
- **Reproducible build**: two builds from the same source give the same package bytes.
- **Secret**: a value kept by the CI service and not stored in the repository.

## You will need

- A plugin project from [Project templates](/pages/reference-project-templates/), in a Git repository.
- The `ilium` binary on the runner. It is a single file. Download it in the first step and check its hash.
- For signing: a signing key made with `ilium plugin keygen`. See [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/).

## The pipeline in five steps

| Step | Command | Exit 0 means |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Check | `ilium plugin check --json` | The manifest and the component are valid |
| 2. Lint | `ilium plugin lint --deny warnings --json` | No warnings or errors |
| 3. Test | `ilium plugin test --json` | All fixtures pass |
| 4. Build | `ilium plugin build --release --json` | A release build in `dist/` |
| 5. Pack | `ilium plugin pack --json` | A package in `dist/` |

- **[DEV-760]** A CI pipeline SHOULD run the five steps in this order and stop at the first step that fails. The order puts the cheap steps first.
- **[DEV-761]** Every command MUST work with no terminal and no session. The commands in this table are all offline commands, so a runner needs no running Ilium.
- **[DEV-762]** With `--json` every command MUST print JSONL on standard output only. Progress text goes to standard error.
- **[DEV-763]** `NO_COLOR=1` MUST be set in CI. Commands MUST also disable colour when standard output is not a terminal.
- **[DEV-764]** The exit codes MUST be those of [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/). A CI step fails on any non-zero code. Code 3 (findings) from `lint` fails the pipeline when `--deny warnings` is set.

## GitHub Actions

`ilium plugin new --ci github` writes this file as `.github/workflows/plugin.yml`.

```yaml
name: plugin
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
env:
  NO_COLOR: "1"
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: never
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install ilium
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o ilium.tar.gz "$ILIUM_URL"
          echo "$ILIUM_SHA256  ilium.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check
          tar -xzf ilium.tar.gz -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        env:
          ILIUM_URL: ${{ vars.ILIUM_URL }}
          ILIUM_SHA256: ${{ vars.ILIUM_SHA256 }}
      - name: Doctor
        run: ilium plugin doctor
      - name: Check
        run: ilium plugin check
      - name: Lint
        run: ilium plugin lint --deny warnings
      - name: Test
        run: ilium plugin test --coverage --min-coverage 70
      - name: Build
        run: ilium plugin build --release
      - name: Pack
        run: ilium plugin pack
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: package
          path: dist/*.iliumpkg
```

- **[DEV-765]** The generated file MUST pin each third-party action to a major version tag and MUST read the `ilium` download URL and hash from repository variables, so no URL is hard coded.
- **[DEV-766]** The `Install ilium` step MUST verify the SHA-256 hash of the download before it runs the file.

## GitLab CI

`ilium plugin new --ci gitlab` writes this file as `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

```yaml
stages: [verify, package]
variables:
  NO_COLOR: "1"
default:
  before_script:
    - curl -fsSL -o ilium.tar.gz "$ILIUM_URL"
    - echo "$ILIUM_SHA256  ilium.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check
    - tar -xzf ilium.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin
verify:
  stage: verify
  image: rust:1.90
  script:
    - ilium plugin doctor
    - ilium plugin check
    - ilium plugin lint --deny warnings
    - ilium plugin test
package:
  stage: package
  image: rust:1.90
  script:
    - ilium plugin build --release
    - ilium plugin pack
  artifacts:
    paths: [dist/*.iliumpkg]
    expire_in: 30 days
```

A TypeScript project uses an image that has Bun 1.2 or later in place of `rust:1.90`.

## Reproducible builds

A package is reproducible when two builds from the same commit give the same bytes. Reproducibility lets a reviewer rebuild the package and compare hashes.

- **[DEV-770]** A release build MUST be reproducible on the same toolchain version and the same `ilium` version. `dist/build.json` records `toolchain` and `input_hash` so a reviewer can pick the same versions.
- **[DEV-771]** A build MUST NOT read the wall clock, the user name, the absolute path of the project or environment variables other than those listed in [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/). Package time stamps are fixed.
- **[DEV-772]** The lock file (`Cargo.lock` or `bun.lock`) MUST be committed, and CI MUST build with `--locked` (Rust) or `--frozen-lockfile` (Bun). `build` SHOULD pass the flag by itself when the lock file exists, and MUST fail with `toolchain.lockfile-missing` when it does not exist and `--release` is set.
- **[DEV-773]** A reviewer check is `ilium plugin build --release && ilium plugin pack` followed by `sha256sum dist/*.iliumpkg`. Two runs MUST give the same hash.

## Signing in CI

A signed package proves who published it. Sign only release builds from a protected branch or tag.

```yaml
      - name: Sign
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        run: |
          printf '%s' "$ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/key"
          ilium plugin sign dist/*.iliumpkg --key "$RUNNER_TEMP/key"
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/key"
        env:
          ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY }}
```

- **[DEV-775]** The secret key MUST be stored as a CI secret and MUST NOT be written to the repository, the build log or an artifact. `ilium plugin sign` MUST read the key from `--key <file>` or from the environment variable `ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY` and MUST NOT print it.
- **[DEV-776]** `pack` MUST NOT sign. Signing is a separate step so a pull request build never needs the key.
- **[DEV-777]** The pipeline SHOULD verify the signed package with `ilium plugin inspect dist/*.iliumpkg --verify` and compare the printed fingerprint with the fingerprint published for the plugin.
- **[DEV-778]** A forked pull request MUST NOT receive the secret. GitHub and GitLab do this by default for forks. Do not enable secrets for forks.

## Caching

Cache the Cargo registry (`~/.cargo/registry`) or the Bun cache (`~/.bun/install/cache`). Do not cache `dist/` or `.ilium/cache/` across commits that change the toolchain, because the build cache key includes the input hash and a stale cache only costs time but never gives a wrong result.

## A release workflow

Build and sign only on a version tag. The workflow below runs the five steps, signs, verifies and attaches the package to a release.

```yaml
name: release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install ilium
        run: ./ci/install-ilium.sh
      - run: ilium plugin check
      - run: ilium plugin lint --deny warnings
      - run: cargo test --locked
      - run: ilium plugin test
      - run: ilium plugin build --release
      - run: ilium plugin pack
      - name: Sign
        run: ./ci/sign.sh
        env:
          ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY }}
      - run: ilium plugin inspect dist/*.iliumpkg --verify
      - name: Hash
        run: sha256sum dist/*.iliumpkg | tee dist/SHA256SUMS
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            dist/*.iliumpkg
            dist/SHA256SUMS
```

- **[DEV-740]** A release pipeline SHOULD run the conformance suite in component mode before it packs: `ilium plugin test --conformance`.
- **[DEV-741]** The tag name SHOULD equal `v` plus the manifest `version`. A pipeline step MUST fail when they differ. A shell test is `test "v$(ilium plugin inspect --json . | jq -r .version)" = "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"`.
- **[DEV-742]** The release MUST publish the SHA-256 of the package next to the package, so a user can compare it.

## Reading a failure

Each step fails with an exit code and, with `--json`, an `error` record. The table shows what to look for.

| Step | Exit | Record to read | Typical cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| check | 3 | `check` record with a `rule` such as `manifest.*` or `component.*` | A manifest key is wrong |
| lint | 3 | `lint` with `severity` `warn` | A warning under `--deny warnings` |
| test | 3 | `test-case` with `status` `fail` or `trap` | An expectation file differs or the component trapped |
| build | 4 or 1 | `error` with code `toolchain.*` | Toolchain missing or a compile error |
| pack | 1 | `error` with `pack.stale-build` | The build is older than the sources |
| sign | 1 | `error` with `sign.*` | Wrong key or publisher |

```json
{"type":"error","code":"pack.stale-build","message":"dist/server.wasm is older than src/lib.rs","fix":"run ilium plugin build --release"}
{"type":"summary","duration_ms":38,"warnings":0,"errors":1}
{"type":"result","ok":false,"exit_code":1}
```

- **[DEV-743]** A CI log MUST be enough to find the cause without a terminal. Every `error` record MUST carry `code`, `message` and, when known, `fix`.

## Matrix builds

A plugin that supports two languages or two sides builds each in its own job so a failure names the part. The `build` command takes `--side`. A matrix over `side: [server, client]` runs `ilium plugin build --release --side ${{ matrix.side }}`, and a final job runs `pack` on the merged `dist/` folder. `pack` MUST refuse a `dist/` folder that misses a declared side with `pack.not-built`.

- **[DEV-744]** `pack` MUST fail with `pack.not-built` when a side that the manifest declares has no component in `dist/`.

## Edge cases

- **Offline runners.** Set `ILIUM_PLUGIN_OFFLINE=1`. `build` then fails with `toolchain.network-needed` instead of downloading.
- **Coverage tool missing.** `--coverage` exits 4. Install `cargo-llvm-cov` in the runner image.
- **Golden updates.** `ILIUM_PLUGIN_UPDATE_GOLDEN` is refused in CI (`harness.golden-update-in-ci`). Update goldens on a developer machine and commit the files.
- **Debug build in pack.** `pack` refuses a debug build. The Build step above uses `--release`.

## See also

- [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/)
- [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/)
- [Conformance suite](/pages/reference-conformance-suite/)
- [Packages](/pages/packages/)
- [Plugin documentation guide](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/)

API checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Compatibility and upgrades

## Compatibility and upgrades

A plugin lives longer than the build that you first ship. Users keep it for years, Ilium changes under it, and you change it yourself. This guide tells you which changes are safe, which ones break a user's saved state, and how to ship each kind of change. It covers the five version numbers that a plugin touches, the names that you may never change, the update path that the host runs, and a worked upgrade from version 1 to version 2.

Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-200` to `AUT-299`. The complete list is in [Requirements for author guides](/pages/reference-requirements-author-guides/). The rules of the contract itself are in [Versioning](/pages/versioning/), and the exact update pipeline is in [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/).

### You need

- A packaged plugin that you have shipped, or plan to ship. See [Package and share](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/).
- The data rules of [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) if your plugin stores data.
- The version rules of [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/) if your plugin depends on other plugins.

## The five version numbers

A plugin carries five numbers. They move independently, and mixing them up is the most common source of upgrade bugs.

| Number | Where it is written | Who reads it | When you change it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plugin `version` | `manifest.json`, semantic version with an optional `-prerelease` | The installer, the user, the resolver | Every release. A version that is already installed with different content is refused with `package.version-reused`. |
| Contract `api` | `manifest.json` and the `ilium:api-version` section of each component | The installer | When you rebuild against a newer SDK. In `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` there is only this one value. |
| `data_version` | `manifest.json`, an integer, default 1 | The migration step | When the layout of your stored data changes. |
| Extension point or service version | The declaration of the point or service | Contributors and callers | When a payload or reply schema changes. |
| Restore format byte | The first byte of your restore bytes | Your own `activate` | When the layout of the bytes from `deactivate` changes. |

A plugin MUST raise `version` for every package that it publishes, because the host refuses a second package with the same version and different content. [AUT-201]

The contract version has no effect on your own versions. A plugin at version 3.2.0 may target `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`, and a plugin at version 0.1.0 may target a later contract.

## Names that you may not change

Some names are saved by the host in the user's snapshot, settings and keymap. A rename leaves the old saved value pointing at nothing.

| Name | Saved where | What a rename does to the user |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin `id` | Registry, grants, settings, storage | The plugin becomes another plugin. Grants, storage and settings are not carried over. |
| Pane kind id | Session snapshot | Saved panes of the old kind cannot be restored. |
| Command id | Keymap, saved layouts, scripts that call `ilium` | A bound key does nothing. |
| Settings key | `config.toml`, settings storage | The saved value is ignored and listed on the recovery page. |
| Decoration slot | Persistent decorations | The old decoration stays until the user clears it. |
| Topic name | Subscriptions of other plugins | Subscribers get nothing. |
| Storage key | The plugin's own buckets | The plugin loses its data unless it migrates it. |
| Service and method names | Callers that declare `requires.services` | Callers fail with `not-found`. |
| Extension point id | Contributors | Contributions go dormant. |

A plugin MUST NOT rename or remove any name of this table in a release that keeps the same `id`. To change a name, add the new name, keep the old one working, and document both. [AUT-202]

The old name SHOULD keep working for at least two minor releases of the plugin before it is removed, and a removal MUST be announced in the changelog of the release that removes it. [AUT-203]

### Keep an old command id working

A new version may want a clearer command id. The pattern is to declare both ids, and to let the old one call the same code.

```json
"contributes": {
  "commands": [
    { "id": "export-notes", "title": "Export notes" },
    { "id": "notes-export", "title": "Export notes (old name)" }
  ]
}
```

**Rust**

```rust
fn on_command(&mut self, id: &str) -> Vec<Submission> {
    match id {
        // "notes-export" is the name used before 2.0.0. Keep it until 4.0.0.
        "export-notes" | "notes-export" => self.start_export(),
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
function onCommand(id: string): Submission[] {
  switch (id) {
    case 'export-notes':
    case 'notes-export': // used before 2.0.0, kept until 4.0.0
      return startExport();
    default:
      return [];
  }
}
```

The old command SHOULD be hidden from the command list and from the palette once the new one exists, but it MUST still run when a key or a script calls it. [AUT-204]

## What each kind of change needs

| Change | Bump | Breaks users? | What you must do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bug fix, no data or name change | Patch | No | Ship it. |
| New command, setting, pane kind or topic | Minor | No | Give new settings a default so that old saved values stay valid. |
| New grant | Minor | The update waits for review | The user sees the new grant. Until they accept, the old version stays active. Work without the grant. |
| Removed grant | Minor | No | Drop it from the manifest. |
| New data layout | Minor or major | Yes, if unmigrated | Raise `data_version` and ship a `migrator`. |
| Renamed name (table above) | Major, and keep the old name | Yes | Keep the old name working. |
| Changed payload of a topic, service or extension point | Major of that point | Yes for callers | Raise the point version. Contributions that name the old major go dormant. |
| New build for a newer contract | Minor | No, if the host supports it | Rebuild and set `api`. |
| Dropped support for a platform | Major | Yes | Say so in the package description and the changelog. |

A new grant MUST be treated as optional at run time. The update stays `update-staged` until the user answers the review, and a user who declines keeps the old version. Code that needs the new grant MUST check the call result and fall back when the call returns `not-permitted`. [AUT-205]

## What the host does when it updates your plugin

The host runs an update in a fixed order. Your code sees three of the steps.

1. The new package is checked like an install. A higher version of an installed id is an update.
2. The new version is staged beside the old one.
3. Each running instance of the old version gets `deactivate(upgrade)` and returns restore bytes.
4. If `data_version` rose, the host takes a backup and calls `migrator.migrate(from, to)` once per side.
5. The new version is activated. It gets the restore bytes only when its `data_version` equals the one of the build that wrote them.
6. If activation succeeds, the update is committed. If it fails, the host restores the backup, reactivates the old version and shows `Update failed, rolled back`.

| Your code | Runs when | Must |
|---|---|---|
| `deactivate(upgrade)` | Old version, before the swap | Return restore bytes that start with a format byte, within 500 ms and 1 MiB |
| `migrate(from, to)` | New version, once per side, before `activate` | Be idempotent and finish within its deadline |
| `activate` | New version | Check the restore format byte and the length, and fall back to defaults |

A plugin MUST write the restore bytes in a layout whose first byte identifies the format, and MUST accept restore bytes of the format of the previous release, or MUST fall back to defaults. [AUT-206]

Data that must survive a layout change MUST live in storage and be converted by a `migrator`, because restore bytes are dropped when the `data_version` differs. [AUT-207]

## Downgrades and rollbacks

The user can roll back with `ilium plugin rollback <id>` or install a lower version with `--allow-downgrade`. The host refuses a rollback with `migration.data-newer` when the stored data version is higher than the target supports. The user can then restore the backup taken before the update, which loses what was written since, or discard the data.

A plugin SHOULD keep its data readable by the previous release for one release, by adding keys instead of changing the meaning of old ones. A user who rolls back then loses nothing. [AUT-208]

## Upgrading Ilium under your plugin

The host loads the contract version it ships and the one before it. A package whose `api` falls outside that window is refused with `package.api-unsupported`. Version 0.1.0 is the first release and has no previous version.

| Situation | What happens | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| The user upgrades Ilium and your `api` is still in the window | The plugin keeps working | Rebuild when it suits you |
| Your `api` falls out of the window | A package outside the window is refused with `package.api-unsupported`. See [Versioning](/pages/versioning/) for the window. | Rebuild with the current SDK and publish a new version |
| Your plugin lists an unstable feature that was renamed | Refused with `manifest.unstable-unknown` | Read the changelog of Ilium before upgrading, and update the name |
| An item you use is marked `@since` a newer version than your `api` | Refused with `manifest.grant-unknown` or an import error | Raise `api` and rebuild |

A plugin SHOULD rebuild and publish against each new minor contract version within the lifetime of the previous one, so that users never hold a plugin outside the window. [AUT-209]

A published plugin MUST NOT list an unstable feature unless the plugin is for development use, because a T2 or T3 package that lists one is installable only in development mode. [AUT-210]

## Version syntax, prereleases and channels

A version is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional `-prerelease`, for example `2.0.0-beta.1`. A leading `v` is refused with `manifest.version-invalid`. A prerelease sorts below its release, so `2.0.0-beta.2` is older than `2.0.0`. A prerelease does not satisfy a plain range such as `^2.0.0` on the stable channel. See [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/).

| Release kind | Version example | Channel | Who gets it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Release | `2.0.0` | stable | Everyone who updates |
| Release candidate | `2.0.0-rc.1` | beta | Testers who chose the beta channel |
| Fix of a release | `2.0.1` | stable | Everyone who updates |

A package that is meant for testers MUST carry a prerelease part in its version, so that it cannot be taken for a release. [AUT-211]

## Depending on other plugins

A plugin that needs another plugin declares it in `requires` with a range. The range is the promise that the other plugin keeps its names and schemas within that range.

- Use `^MAJOR.MINOR` for a dependency that follows the rule above. It accepts later minors of the same major.
- Declare a dependency as `optional` when the plugin can work without it, and test both cases.
- A range that cannot be met blocks the install with `dependency.unresolved`. A cycle is refused with `manifest.requires-cycle` or `manifest.service-cycle`.

A plugin MUST declare a `requires` range no wider than the versions it was tested with. [AUT-212]

A plugin that provides a service or an extension point MUST raise the major version of the point when it changes the payload incompatibly, and MUST keep the old major working for as long as it lists the old major as supported. [AUT-213]

## Worked example: from 1.4.0 to 2.0.0

The plugin `com.example.notes` stores its notes under one key in the `global` bucket. Version 2.0.0 splits them into one key per note, renames a command and adds a setting and an optional grant.

The manifest changes are:

```json
{
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "publisher": "Example Labs",
  "api": "ilium:plugin@0.1.0",
  "data_version": 2,
  "exports": ["migrator"],
  "capabilities": { "server": ["notify.toast"] },
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "id": "export-notes", "title": "Export notes" },
      { "id": "notes-export", "title": "Export notes (old name)" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The migration code reads the old blob and writes the new keys. It writes the new keys first and removes the old key last.

**Rust**

```rust
impl Migrator for NotesPlugin {
    fn migrate(&mut self, from: u32, to: u32) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if from >= 2 || to < 2 {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let Some(blob) = storage::get(Bucket::Global, "notes") else {
            return Ok(()); // nothing to convert, or a second run
        };
        for (index, note) in split_notes(&blob).into_iter().enumerate() {
            storage::put(Bucket::Global, &format!("note:{index:06}"), &note)?;
        }
        storage::remove(Bucket::Global, "notes");
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export const migrator = {
  migrate(from: number, to: number): void {
    if (from >= 2 || to < 2) return;
    const blob = storage.get('global', 'notes');
    if (blob === undefined) return; // nothing to convert, or a second run
    splitNotes(blob).forEach((note, index) => {
      storage.put('global', `note:${String(index).padStart(6, '0')}`, note);
    });
    storage.remove('global', 'notes');
  },
};
```

The test calls `migrate` twice on the same fixture and compares the data. The second call must change nothing. The fake host can start with an old data version (`with_data_version`) and a stored snapshot (`with_storage_snapshot`), so the test starts from the layout of version 1.4.0. See [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/).

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | What happens | What the author does |
|---|---|---|
| Same version, different content | Refused with `package.version-reused` | Raise the version |
| Lower version than installed | Refused with `package.downgrade` unless `--allow-downgrade` | Publish a higher version that contains the fix |
| Update asks for a new grant | Staged until the user answers | Work without it |
| Update fails to activate | Rolled back, backup restored | Read `ilium plugin logs <id>` and fix |
| `migrate` fails | Backup restored, old version stays | Make the migration idempotent and test it |
| Rollback after a migration | Refused with `migration.data-newer` | Keep data readable by the previous release |
| `api` outside the window | `package.api-unsupported` | Rebuild |
| Restore bytes from an older `data_version` | Dropped, one log line | Do not keep needed data only in restore bytes |
| Two servers update at once | The first to finish decides | Nothing, the host serialises it |

## What the user sees

An update shows the new grants in a review dialog and keeps the old version active until the user answers. A failed update shows `Update failed, rolled back`. A rollback that cannot keep data offers two choices, restore the backup or discard the data. In Settings > Plugins the version and the state of the plugin are shown. See [Managing plugins](/pages/user-managing-plugins/).

## See also

- [Versioning](/pages/versioning/) for the contract rules
- [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) for the `migrator` export and the backup
- [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/) for the pipeline
- [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) for releases and changelogs
- [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) for a pre-release review

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

<!-- source: http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/guide-data-migration.md -->
# Guide, data migration

## Guide, data migration

A plugin that stores data will one day change how it stores it. A key gets a new name, a blob is split in two, a file moves. This guide tells you how to ship that change safely: the data version, the `migrate` export, the backup that the host takes first, what happens when the migration fails, and how a downgrade is handled. It is normative, and every rule has a requirement id.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

### The mechanism in one paragraph

The manifest declares a number, `data_version`. The host remembers which data version each bucket and the data directory were last written with. When a new version of the plugin starts with a higher `data_version`, the host takes a backup, calls the optional export `migrator.migrate(from, to)` once, stamps the new number when it succeeds, and only then calls `activate`. If `migrate` fails, the host restores the backup and keeps the old version. A plugin that never changes its storage layout declares nothing and needs none of this.

You will need:

- A plugin that stores data in `storage`, in its data directory or on tree nodes ([storage](/pages/api-storage/), [file access](/pages/file-access/), [node metadata](/pages/capability-tree-metadata/)).
- The manifest key `data_version` and the optional export `migrator`, listed in `exports`. See [Reference: manifest](/pages/reference-manifest/).
- The `FakeHost` of [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/) for the tests below.

### What is versioned

| Data | Versioned | How it is migrated |
|---|---|---|
| Storage buckets `global`, `project`, `session` | yes, each bucket has its own stamp | by `migrate`, with `storage` |
| The `shared` bucket | no | it is a cache; the host clears it when `data_version` changes |
| The data directory | yes, one stamp | by `migrate`, with `fs` on the data scope |
| Node metadata the plugin owns | yes, one stamp per snapshot | by `migrate`, with `tree.metadata` and `tree.read` |
| Persistent decorations | no | the plugin sets them again after `activate`; the old ones are shown stale until then |
| Settings values | no | the kernel ignores a value that no longer fits its row and lists it on the recovery page. A plugin may copy its own values in `migrate` with the `settings` import. See [settings extension](/pages/settings-extension/) |
| Restore bytes | tagged | dropped when `data_version` differs from the version that wrote them (LIF-103) |
| Durable timers and journal entries | no | they keep their names and ids |

- [LIF-100] The manifest key `data_version` MUST be an unsigned 32-bit integer. When absent it MUST be 1. A value of 0 or a non-integer MUST be refused with `manifest.data-version`. Test: install manifests with 0, 1, "2" and 4294967295.
- [LIF-101] The host MUST store the data version of each bucket and of the data directory in a place the plugin cannot read or write, and MUST stamp it only after a successful migration or on first creation. Test: read the stamp through the CLI `ilium plugin info <id> --json` after a migration.
- [LIF-102] The host MUST NOT migrate data it did not stamp itself. A bucket with no stamp (created before the plugin ever stored data) MUST be stamped with the current `data_version` at first write. Test: first `put` on a new plugin.
- [LIF-103] The host MUST drop restore bytes when the `data_version` of the running version differs from that of the version that produced them, and MUST log `restore.dropped-data-version`. Test: change `data_version` between two builds and read `restored`.

### The `migrator` export

```wit
// Excerpt of ilium:exports/migrator in reference-wit
interface migrator {
  migrate: func(from: u32, to: u32) -> result<_, plugin-error>;
}
```

`from` is the lowest data version found among the buckets and the data directory the plugin can see in this run. `to` is the new `data_version`. The call has the same imports and grants as `activate`. It runs on a migration instance, before `activate`, and `activate` runs on a fresh instance afterwards.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Deadline | hard, default 30,000 ms; T1 may request up to 60,000 (`migrate_deadline_ms`) |
| CPU | charged to the plugin's execution quota like any call |
| Memory | the plugin's `memory_mib` |
| Side | each side that exports `migrator`, server first; a client side runs at its first attach after the update |
| Skipped when | `data_version` is unchanged, or the plugin has no `migrator` (the host only stamps the new number and logs `migration.skipped`) |

- [LIF-104] For each bucket, the host MUST call `migrate(from, to)` at most once per update, the first time a host instance activates with that bucket in scope and the bucket stamp is lower than `data_version`, with `from` less than `to`. The global bucket and the data directory migrate at the first activation after the swap. A project or session bucket migrates when its session first activates the plugin. Test: update from 1 to 3, open two sessions, and assert one call `(1, 3)` for the global bucket and one for each session bucket.
- [LIF-105] A call that returns an error, traps or misses the deadline MUST be a migration failure (LIF-108). It MUST NOT count toward the failure window of the plugin. Test: return an error from `migrate` and read `failures-in-window`.
- [LIF-106] `migrate` MUST be idempotent. The host MAY call it again with the same arguments after an interrupted run (LIF-110). Test: run the call twice on a fixture and compare the data.

### Backup and failure

Before `migrate`, the host takes a backup of the buckets in scope and the data directory.

- [LIF-107] The host MUST copy the global, project and session buckets in use and the data directory to `backups/<id>/<version>-<utc timestamp>/` before it calls `migrate`. The timestamp has the form `YYYYMMDDTHHmmssZ`. The host MUST refuse with `install.no-space`, before touching any data, when free space is less than twice the data size plus 100 MiB. The backup size is capped by the key `migration_backup_mib` in the `[plugins]` table of `config.toml` (integer 0 to 1048576, default 2048; 0 disables backups). Data above the cap is refused with `migration.backup-too-large` (stage I, exit 1) unless `--no-backup` is given, and then a failed migration cannot be undone. A copy-on-write copy MAY replace the full copy. Test: fill the disk and update; set the cap to 1 and update with 2 MiB of data, with and without `--no-backup`.
- [LIF-108] On a migration failure the host MUST restore the backup, keep the previous version active, log `migration.failed` with the plugin's error code and message, and mark the update rolled back. Test: fail `migrate` after it wrote half the keys, then compare the buckets with the backup.
- [LIF-109] After an update that succeeded and was activated, the host MUST keep only the newest backup of that plugin and delete older ones in `backups/<id>/`. Test: update twice and list the backups.

An interrupted migration (power loss, kill) leaves the registry entry `update.state: "migrating"`.

- [LIF-110] At the next start the host MUST restore the backup, increment `update.attempts` in `installed.json` and run the update again from the beginning. The host MUST write `update.state: "migrating"` and the attempt count with fsync before it calls `migrate`. When `attempts` reaches 2 it MUST roll back with `migration.interrupted` and mark the candidate `skip`. Test: kill the process in the middle of `migrate` twice and assert the rollback and `skip`.

### Downgrade

- [LIF-111] The host MUST refuse to activate a version whose `data_version` is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope, with `migration.data-newer`. The user may run the command with `--restore-backup` (the host restores the backup taken before the update) or `--discard-data` (the host deletes the plugin's buckets and data directory). Test: roll back after a migration, with and without each flag. This is the same rule as [LIF-079](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/).

### Many sessions on one machine

Each project session has its own server, and the package store and the global bucket are shared by all of them.

- [LIF-112] A migration that touches the global bucket or the data directory MUST hold the cross-process lock `plugins/locks/<id>.migrate.lock`. The other servers MUST first deactivate their old instances with `upgrade`, then wait for the lock for at most the migrate deadline plus 5 s, and then skip the migration when they find the stamp already new. Test: update with two servers, count calls to `migrate`.
- [LIF-113] While the stamp of the global bucket is higher than the data version of a running instance, a `put`, `write-batch` or `remove` from that instance MUST return `conflict` with the message `stale-data-version`. Test: leave one server on the old version and write to the global bucket.
- [LIF-114] A project bucket and a session bucket MUST be migrated by the session that opens them, each with its own backup. Test: open two projects after an update.

### Several keys at once, and durability

The `storage` import has a batch write, `write-batch`, that applies several changes all at once or not at all ([storage](/pages/api-storage/)). Use it to write a split in one step.

- [LIF-115] `put` and `write-batch` MUST return only after the data is committed to stable storage with a flush, so that a power loss after the return does not lose it. Test: kill the process after a `put` returns and read it back.
- [LIF-116] If a plugin must change several files of its data directory, it SHOULD write a new set of files first and write a version marker file last, so that a crash leaves either the old set or the complete new set. The host does not give transactions for files. Test: kill the host between the two writes and assert the plugin reads the old set.

### Worked example: rename a key and split a blob

Version 1 of a notes plugin stores everything in the project bucket under `prefs` as a JSON object with the fields `theme` and `layout`, and it counts opened notes under `count`. Version 2 stores `theme` and `layout` as two keys, and it renames `count` to `opened`. The manifest of version 2 sets `"data_version": 2` and lists `"migrator"` in `exports`.

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::storage::{self, Bucket, Entry};
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;

#[ilium_plugin(side = "server")]
#[derive(Default)]
struct Notes;

impl Migrator for Notes {
    fn migrate(&mut self, from: u32, to: u32) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if from < 2 && to >= 2 {
            migrate_v1_to_v2()?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn migrate_v1_to_v2() -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    let mut entries = Vec::new();
    if let Some(blob) = storage::get(Bucket::Project, "prefs") {
        let prefs: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&blob)
            .map_err(|error| PluginError::invalid_argument(format!("prefs: {error}")))?;
        for field in ["theme", "layout"] {
            if let Some(value) = prefs.get(field) {
                entries.push(Entry::put(field, value.to_string().into_bytes()));
            }
        }
        entries.push(Entry::remove("prefs"));
    }
    if let Some(count) = storage::get(Bucket::Project, "count") {
        entries.push(Entry::put("opened", count));
        entries.push(Entry::remove("count"));
    }
    // One atomic write: a crash leaves version 1 data or version 2 data, never a mix.
    storage::write_batch(Bucket::Project, &entries)
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { get, writeBatch } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';

function migrateV1ToV2(): void {
  const entries: { key: string; value?: Uint8Array }[] = [];
  const blob = get('project', 'prefs');
  if (blob !== undefined) {
    const prefs = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(blob));
    for (const field of ['theme', 'layout']) {
      if (field in prefs) {
        entries.push({ key: field, value: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(prefs[field])) });
      }
    }
    entries.push({ key: 'prefs' });
  }
  const count = get('project', 'count');
  if (count !== undefined) {
    entries.push({ key: 'opened', value: count });
    entries.push({ key: 'count' });
  }
  writeBatch('project', entries);
}

export const { lifecycle, handler, migrator } = definePlugin({
  side: 'server',
  migrate(from: number, to: number) {
    if (from < 2 && to >= 2) migrateV1ToV2();
  },
});
```

An entry with a value writes the key. An entry with no value removes it.

### Testing a migration

Test the migration against a stored fixture of the old layout. The `FakeHost` can load a storage snapshot and set the data version it believes is stored (see [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/)).

**Rust**

```rust
#[test]
fn migrates_v1_prefs_and_count() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::new()
        .with_storage_snapshot("tests/fixtures/notes-v1.json")
        .with_data_version(1);
    let outcome = host.migrate::<Notes>(2);
    assert!(outcome.is_ok());
    assert_eq!(host.storage_get("project", "opened"), Some(b"7".to_vec()));
    assert_eq!(host.storage_get("project", "prefs"), None);
    assert_eq!(host.storage_get("project", "theme"), Some(b"\"dark\"".to_vec()));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { createFakeHost } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/testing';

test('migrates v1 prefs and count', () => {
  const host = createFakeHost().withStorageSnapshot('tests/fixtures/notes-v1.json').withDataVersion(1);
  expect(host.migrate(2).ok).toBe(true);
  expect(host.storageGet('project', 'prefs')).toBeUndefined();
  expect(host.storageGet('project', 'theme')).toEqual(new TextEncoder().encode('"dark"'));
});
```

Also test the failure path: feed a corrupt `prefs` value and assert that `migrate` returns an error and that the storage is unchanged. Because the batch is atomic, nothing is half written.

### Edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| `data_version` goes up with no `migrator` | The host stamps the new number, drops restore bytes, clears the `shared` bucket and logs `migration.skipped`. |
| The plugin is disabled when the update arrives | The migration runs at the first activation after the plugin is enabled. |
| Two versions in a row (1 to 3) | One call `migrate(1, 3)`. The plugin handles the steps itself. |
| `migrate` calls a host function the grants forbid | `not-permitted`; the migration fails. |
| The update was installed with `--no-backup` and `migrate` fails | The previous version stays active, the data may be half migrated, and the host logs `migration.no-backup-failed` at level error. |
| The data directory is read-only | `migration.io`; the update rolls back. See [offline and low disk](/pages/reference-offline-and-low-disk/). |

### What the user sees

An update shows a progress line `Updating data of Notes (2 of 5 steps)` in the CLI. In Settings > Plugins the row shows `migrating` while the call runs. A failure shows the toast `Update failed, rolled back` and the log line `migration.failed`.

### See also

- [Install, update and uninstall](/pages/reference-install-update-uninstall/)
- [Storage](/pages/api-storage/)
- [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/)
- [Versioning](/pages/versioning/)
- [Persistence and restart](/pages/reference-persistence-and-restart/)
- [Requirements, lifecycle and operations](/pages/reference-requirements-lifecycle-ops/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
