# Enterprise deployment

## Enterprise deployment

This guide is for people who run Ilium for others: a team lead, a system administrator, a security engineer. It shows how to decide which plugins are allowed, how to ship a plugin to everyone, how to run on shared machines and in CI, and how to check that the policy does what you think. The rules themselves are in [Admin policy](/pages/reference-admin-policy/). This page is the how-to.

### You will need

- Administrator rights on the machine, to write a root-owned file.
- Ilium installed for each user. Each user keeps their own settings, stores and sessions.
- Linux, if any third-party (T2 or T3) plugin should run. See [Sandbox](/pages/reference-sandbox/).
- A text editor and the CLI: `ilium plugin policy show`, `ilium plugin audit`, `ilium plugin inspect`.

## Choose a stance

Pick one of three stances before you write any policy.

| Stance | Who it fits | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| Built-in only | Regulated sites | `allowed_tiers = ["t1"]` |
| Signed from known publishers | Most companies | `allowed_tiers = ["t1","t2"]`, `allow_unsigned = false`, `publishers.allow = [...]` |
| Open with guard rails | Developer teams | Defaults, plus `grants.max_risk`, `deny_combinations` and a `deny` list |

## Worked examples

### Lock to one publisher

Create `/etc/ilium/policy.toml`, owned by root, mode 0644:

```toml
version = 1
[packages]
allowed_tiers  = ["t1", "t2"]
allow_unsigned = false
allow_dev_mode = false
[publishers]
allow = ["3f2a91c07b6d1e44a1b20c9e55d3f7a8b6c102e94d7798af13c56e0bd2f48a19"]
trusted_keys = ["3f2a91c07b6d1e44a1b20c9e55d3f7a8b6c102e94d7798af13c56e0bd2f48a19"]
```

The key in `trusted_keys` needs no user prompt. Everything else fails at install with `policy.publisher-denied`.

### Block all high-risk grants except a list

```toml
version = 1
[grants]
max_risk = "normal"
[grants.preapproved]
"example.git-tools" = ["process.run:git"]
```

`max_risk = "normal"` refuses high-risk grants. The preapproved list shows that a specific plugin may still receive `process.run:git`. A grant in `preapproved` is not checked against `max_risk`, so list only what you reviewed.

### An offline site

```toml
version = 1
[network]
offline = true
[packages]
allowed_sources = ["/srv/ilium-plugins/"]
```

No plugin egress, and installs only from `/srv/ilium-plugins/`. The default inference provider, the remote Kilo Gateway, stops working; set `[inference] allowed_providers = ["local"]` and configure a local provider.

### Preinstall a team package for everyone

1. Put the signed package in a root-owned folder, for example `/srv/ilium-plugins/example.team-rules-1.0.0.iliumpkg`.
2. Add the publisher key to `trusted_keys`.
3. Add the id to `force_enabled` and list its grants under `grants.preapproved`.
4. Each user runs `ilium plugin install /srv/ilium-plugins/example.team-rules-1.0.0.iliumpkg` once, or the login script does. Because the grants are preapproved, no dialog opens.

Ilium does not install `force_enabled` plugins for the user. The policy states what must be on; the administrator makes sure it is installed.

## Multi-user machines

**[SEC-194]** Each user has their own stores: grants, consents, trust, project trust, secrets, audit log and plugin install directory, all below the user's own directories and with owner-only modes. No file is shared between users and a user's decisions never apply to another user.

**[SEC-195]** The system package directory, if you use one, is read-only to users. Installs from it copy into the user's install directory.

**[SEC-196]** Sockets and runtime directories are per user (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ilium/`, mode 0700). Sessions of one user are not visible to another, and `sessions.cross` lists only the same user's sessions.

**[SEC-197]** Do not run Ilium as root. The server refuses T2 and T3 plugins when its effective uid is 0 ([SEC-056]).

## CI and headless use

Where no client is attached, no one can approve a dialog ([SEC-116]). Use `preapproved` for the exact plugins your pipeline needs, and set `allow_unsigned = false`. A pipeline step that tries `ilium plugin install --yes` fails with `approval.no-client`. Pipelines can verify packages without installing:

```text
ilium plugin inspect ./dist/example.team-rules-1.0.0.iliumpkg
```

## Verify the policy

1. Run `ilium plugin policy show`. Check that every file you wrote has `"used": true` and the owner is root. A file with `"used": false` is ignored ([SEC-182]).
2. Try a forbidden install. It should fail with the `policy.*` code you expect.
3. Run `ilium plugin audit --event policy-loaded` and `--event policy-violation`.
4. Look at the Plugins screen. A forced or locked item shows a lock mark.

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A user edits `/etc/ilium/policy.toml` as root, adds a typo | `policy.invalid`; third parties stop loading; the notice shows the line |
| A user copies the system policy to their own folder | The user file can only make it stricter |
| An old plugin is installed before the policy exists | Disabled at next start if it violates the policy |
| A laptop leaves the office network | `offline = true` still applies; use the proxy key for site networks |

### See also

- [Admin policy](/pages/reference-admin-policy/)
- [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/)
- [Network egress](/pages/reference-network-egress/)
- [Plugin CLI](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/)

Contract: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Author FAQ

## Author FAQ

Short answers to questions that plugin authors ask often. Each answer points to the page that holds the rule. This page adds no requirements. If an answer and the linked page differ, the linked page decides.

### Getting started

**Which language should I use?** Rust or TypeScript. Both build to the same kind of component. Rust gives smaller files. TypeScript is quicker for small views. See [Rust SDK](/pages/rust-sdk/) and [TypeScript SDK](/pages/typescript-sdk/).

**How do I start?** Run `ilium plugin new <dir> --id <id> --lang <language> --side <side>`, then follow [Tutorial step 1](/pages/tutorial-01-agent-badge/).

**Which side do I need?** Server for terminals and agents, client for panels and settings pages, scene for animated backgrounds. See [Porting from other plugin systems](/pages/guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems/) for a table.

**Can one plugin have more than one side?** Yes. Each side is its own component with its own grants, and the two talk by messages.

**What is the contract version?** `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. It is the only version. See [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/).

### Capabilities and limits

**Why does my call return `not-permitted`?** The grant is missing from the side that calls, or the user declined it. Optional grants can be refused at any time, so handle the error.

**Can I ask for a grant later?** No. Grants are in the manifest, and a new grant needs an update that the user reviews.

**How much memory can I use?** 32 MiB by default. The ceiling is 256 MiB for bundled (T1) plugins and 128 MiB for T2 and T3. See [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/).

**How long may a handler run?** Events 20 ms (T1: 50 ms), commands 50 ms, render 10 ms, `activate` 2 s, `deactivate` 500 ms. Longer work goes to jobs. See [Performance](/pages/performance/).

**What happens when I break a limit?** The instance traps and restarts after 1 s, then 5 s, then 30 s. The third failure in 10 minutes disables the plugin on that side.

**Can I use threads?** No. A component is single-threaded. Use jobs or requests for background work.

**Can I use the network?** Yes, with an `http:<host-pattern>` grant. A process started with `process.run` has no network.

### Data and state

**Where do I keep data?** In a storage bucket: `global`, `project` or `session`. Keys are 256 bytes at most and values 1 MiB. Use `shared` only for data you can rebuild. See [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/).

**Is memory kept across restarts?** No. Keep what you need in storage or restore bytes.

**How do I change my data layout?** Raise `data_version` in the manifest and export `migrator`. See [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/).

**Do timers survive a restart?** `timers.set` timers do not. Durable timers do. See [Clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/).

**How do I get the user's time zone or language?** You cannot. The contract has no such call. See [Internationalisation](/pages/guide-internationalisation/).

### Interface

**Why must widgets have keys?** The host keeps the state of a widget (selection, scroll, text) by key. Without it the state is lost on each render.

**Can I draw my own colours?** Use the nine colour roles. They follow the theme. See [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/).

**Can I show HTML?** No. A view is a tree of widgets that the host draws.

**How do I measure text?** With `display-width`. Do not count characters.

### Testing

**How do I test without a running Ilium?** Use the fake host. See [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/).

**Why does my timer not fire in a test?** The fake host never runs timers by itself. Call `advance_clock` and then `settle`.

**Can I test an upgrade?** Yes. Load a storage snapshot of the old version and run the new one. See [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/).

### Publishing

**How do I share a plugin?** Pack it, optionally sign it, and send the file. See [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/).

**Do I need to sign?** Not for a local plugin. A signed package (T2) shows a publisher and key fingerprint in the review dialog.

**Can I rename my plugin?** The id is permanent. A new id is a new plugin.

**Is there a registry?** The manual specifies an optional one, in [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/). The package file works without it.

**What if I lose my key?** You cannot sign new releases under it. See the key table in [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/).

**Does it run on Windows or macOS?** Only bundled (T1) plugins. T2 and T3 packages need Linux.

### Problems

**My plugin was disabled. Why?** Three failures in 10 minutes. Read the first trap in the log. See [Troubleshooting](/pages/guide-troubleshooting/).

**How do I see what my plugin did?** `ilium plugin logs <id>`, `trace`, `stats`. See [Debugging tools](/pages/reference-debugging-tools/).

**How do I check a release?** Use the [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/).

## See also

- [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/)
- [Glossary](/pages/glossary/)
- [Troubleshooting](/pages/guide-troubleshooting/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Internationalisation

## Internationalisation

This guide tells an author what `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` gives a plugin for text in many languages, what it does not give, and what to do about the gaps. Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-600` to `AUT-699`.

Terms:

- **Cell**: one column of the terminal grid. A character takes one or two cells.
- **Display width**: the number of cells the host uses for a piece of text.
- **Grapheme**: one character as a reader sees it. It can be several code points, such as a letter plus an accent.
- **Locale**: the language and regional settings of the user, such as date order and decimal mark.
- **UTC**: Coordinated Universal Time, the zone without an offset.

### What the contract provides and what it does not

| Need | In `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`? | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Cell width of a string | Yes, `display-width(text)` in `host::ui` | Call it before you cut or pad text |
| Wide characters (two cells) | Yes, the host lays them out | Never count bytes or code points for width |
| Wall-clock time | Yes, `now-unix-millis` in UTC | Format it yourself. See below |
| The user's locale | No | Offer a setting, or keep text locale-neutral |
| The user's UTC offset or time zone | No | Offer a setting, show UTC, or show relative time |
| A message catalogue or translation function | No | Ship your own tables |
| Right-to-left layout | No mirroring | Treat text as left-to-right cells |
| Accessible labels | No | Put meaning in text. See [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/) |

A plugin MUST NOT assume that it can learn the user's locale or time zone from the host. [AUT-601]

## Width

A terminal draws a grid. A Latin letter takes one cell. A Chinese, Japanese or Korean character, and most emoji, take two. A combining accent takes none, because it joins the letter before it.

| Text | Bytes | Code points | Cells |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` | 5 | 5 | 5 |
| `café` (precomposed) | 5 | 4 | 4 |
| `cafe` plus a combining accent | 6 | 5 | 4 |
| two CJK characters | 6 | 2 | 4 |

A plugin MUST measure width with `display-width` and MUST NOT use `len()`, `chars().count()` or `String.length` for layout. [AUT-602]

A plugin that cuts text to fit MUST cut at a grapheme boundary, and SHOULD end a cut with `…`, which takes one cell. [AUT-603] The host cuts a badge at 12 cells and ends it with `…`, using the same width rules.

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::ui;

/// Cut `text` to at most `max_cells`, never inside a grapheme.
fn fit(text: &str, max_cells: u16) -> String {
    if ui::display_width(text) <= max_cells {
        return text.to_string();
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    for grapheme in graphemes(text) {
        let candidate = format!("{out}{grapheme}");
        if ui::display_width(&format!("{candidate}…")) > max_cells {
            break;
        }
        out = candidate;
    }
    out.push('…');
    out
}
```

`graphemes` stands for a grapheme splitter from the `unicode-segmentation` crate. In TypeScript use `Intl.Segmenter`.

```ts
import * as ui from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/ui';

export function fit(text: string, maxCells: number): string {
  if (ui.displayWidth(text) <= maxCells) return text;
  const segmenter = new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, { granularity: 'grapheme' });
  let out = '';
  for (const { segment } of segmenter.segment(text)) {
    if (ui.displayWidth(out + segment + '…') > maxCells) break;
    out += segment;
  }
  return out + '…';
}
```

The call to `display-width` crosses into the host. A plugin SHOULD NOT call it once per character for a long text. Measure once, and cut only when the text is too wide. [AUT-604]

### Label and value pairs

Use `leader-row` for a label and a value. It shrinks the value first, then the label, with `…`. A translated label is often longer than an English one by 30 percent or more. A plugin SHOULD leave room for a longer label and SHOULD NOT depend on a fixed width. [AUT-605] See [Layout constraints](/pages/layout/).

## Text that the plugin does not control

File names, branch names, notes and agent output come in any language. A plugin MUST treat text from outside as data: it MAY contain wide characters, combining marks, text in any direction and any length. [AUT-606] The host removes terminal escape sequences from text a plugin passes to a widget, so such text cannot move the cursor or change colours. See [Text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/).

## Right-to-left text

The host draws each line as a sequence of cells from left to right. It does not reorder bidirectional text and it does not mirror a layout. A plugin SHOULD NOT promise correct display of right-to-left scripts, and SHOULD state this in its README if its users need them. [AUT-607] Keep right-to-left text in its own row, so that it is not mixed with left-to-right labels in one line.

## Your own strings

There is no catalogue function. The usual pattern is a table of strings by a message id, with English as the fallback.

```rust
fn message(language: &str, id: &str) -> &'static str {
    match (language, id) {
        ("de", "saved") => "Gespeichert",
        ("fr", "saved") => "Enregistré",
        (_, "saved") => "Saved",
        (_, _) => "?",
    }
}
```

The plugin must learn the language from somewhere. Because the host provides no locale, offer a `choice` settings row.

```json
{ "type": "choice", "key": "language", "title": "Language", "default": "en",
  "options": [ { "value": "en", "title": "English" }, { "value": "de", "title": "Deutsch" },
               { "value": "fr", "title": "Français" } ] }
```

A plugin that ships several languages MUST fall back to one default language for any missing message, and MUST NOT show a message id to the user. [AUT-608] The settings row `title` and `help` are text in the manifest and have one value. A plugin that wants a translated settings page SHOULD keep the manifest titles in one language and put the translated text in views it draws itself. [AUT-609]

Do not build sentences by joining pieces. Word order differs between languages.

| Avoid | Prefer |
|---|---|
| `"Deleted " + count + " notes"` | A message with a placeholder: `"Deleted {count} notes"` |
| A plural by adding `s` | One message for each plural form the language needs |
| A translated word inside a command id | Keep command ids, keys and codes in English |

Command ids, setting keys, error codes and event names are identifiers. A plugin MUST NOT translate them. [AUT-610] Titles shown to people, such as a command `title`, are text and MAY be in any language.

## Time

`now-unix-millis` returns milliseconds since 1970-01-01 in UTC. The contract has no function for the user's offset. Choose one of three ways.

| Way | Good for | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Show UTC with the zone written out | Logs, records, shared data | Users must convert |
| Show relative time (`3 min ago`) | Recent events | Needs a refresh timer |
| A setting `utc_offset_minutes` | A clock for one person | The user must set it, and daylight saving changes are manual |

A plugin that shows a time MUST write the zone or say that it is relative, and MUST store times as UTC milliseconds, never as local text. [AUT-611]

The manual uses the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` for dates, which has the same order in every language. A plugin SHOULD use it for absolute times unless the user chooses another form. [AUT-612]

```rust
/// Format UTC milliseconds as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` plus an offset in minutes.
fn format_time(unix_millis: u64, offset_minutes: i64) -> String {
    let seconds = (unix_millis / 1000) as i64 + offset_minutes * 60;
    let days = seconds.div_euclid(86_400);
    let rest = seconds.rem_euclid(86_400);
    let (year, month, day) = civil_from_days(days);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02} {:02}:{:02}:{:02}",
        rest / 3600, (rest % 3600) / 60, rest % 60)
}
```

`civil_from_days` stands for a standard day-count to calendar conversion. A date library is simpler. A plugin that formats time MUST be tested with the fake clock, which starts at 2030-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. [AUT-613] See [Clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/).

### Numbers, units and sizes

The decimal mark and the group separator differ by region. A plugin SHOULD use a dot and no group separator in machine-readable output, and SHOULD use metric units for sizes it shows. [AUT-614] A setting for the decimal mark is cheap and welcome.

## Sorting and search

Byte order is not alphabetical order in most languages. The host sorts storage keys by byte order. A plugin that sorts names for people SHOULD fold case and accents before comparing, and SHOULD NOT claim a language-correct order. [AUT-615]

## Testing

| Test | How |
|---|---|
| Width of wide and combining text | Render a view with `"日本語"` and `"café"` and check no row is wider than the area |
| Long labels | Use a label twice as long as the English one |
| Missing translation | Ask for an id absent in `de` and expect the English text |
| Time | `set_clock` and check the string for two offsets |
| Escape sequences in input | Pass `"\u001b[31mred"` and check that the view shows no colour change |

```rust
#[test]
fn wide_text_never_overflows() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::for_manifest(MANIFEST).expect("manifest").grant("ui.panels");
    host.activate();
    host.with_fixture("tests/fixtures/wide-titles.json");
    let tree = host.render("notes");
    assert!(tree.max_row_width() <= 40);
}
```

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| A wide character at the last cell of a row | The host moves it to the next row or cuts it |
| An empty string | Width 0. Do not pad with a space for it |
| A combining mark with no base | Width 0. It may attach to the previous cell |
| A cut inside a grapheme | A broken character. Cut at boundaries |
| Text with an ESC sequence | The host removes the sequence and logs a warning |
| A badge over 12 cells | Cut with `…` |
| A translated label longer than the row | The value is cut first, then the label |

## See also

- [Text widgets](/pages/widgets-text/)
- [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/)
- [Layout constraints](/pages/layout/)
- [Clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/)
- [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Patterns cookbook

## Patterns cookbook

This page collects twelve recipes that most plugins need sooner or later: debounce, throttle, cache with a time limit, windowed lists, retry with backoff, idempotent submissions, state that survives a restart, stale-result guards, batch handling, slow work in jobs, talking between the two sides, and migrating stored data. Each recipe states the problem, lists the limits that shape the answer, gives Rust and TypeScript code, shows a test, and lists the traps.

The recipes use one idea over and over: keep the decision logic in a plain function or struct that takes the current time and the incoming event as arguments, and keep the host calls in a thin handler around it. The core is then testable with plain numbers. The fake host also has a fake clock (`advance_clock`, see [Test harness reference](/pages/reference-test-harness/)), so the tests below call the core directly where the logic is pure and use the fake host to check the glue and the timers.

Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-001` to `AUT-099`. The complete list is in [Requirements for author guides](/pages/reference-requirements-author-guides/).

### You need

- A plugin that builds and activates. Start with [Your first plugin](/pages/getting-started-first-plugin/) if you have none.
- The grants named in each recipe. The clock, timers and storage need no grant.
- The limits below. Every number comes from [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/) and [Performance](/pages/performance/). This page does not define them again.

| Limit | Value | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Timer minimum, timers per plugin | 50 ms, 64 | [Clock and timers](/pages/api-clock-and-timers/) |
| `on-events` deadline | 20 ms (50 ms for tier 1) | [Performance](/pages/performance/) |
| Storage key, value, bucket | 256 bytes, 1 MiB, 16 MiB (`storage_bucket_mib`) | [Storage](/pages/api-storage/) |
| Restore bytes from `deactivate` | 1 MiB | [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| Dedup window | 10 minutes | [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) |
| Toast rate | 3 per 10 s | [Toast](/pages/api-toast/) |
| Tree limits | 4,096 nodes, 1,024 KiB | [UI model](/pages/ui-model/) |
| Topic payload | 64 KiB | [Messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/) |

### The shape of every recipe

Rust plugins keep a `Core` struct with pure methods. A method receives `now` in milliseconds and returns what the handler should do, as a small enum. The handler turns the enum into host calls.

```rust
/// What the handler must do after the core decides.
pub enum Action {
    Nothing,
    ArmTimer { after_millis: u32 },
    CancelTimer,
    Run,
}
```

The TypeScript version is the same, with a discriminated union.

```ts
export type Action =
  | { tag: 'nothing' }
  | { tag: 'arm-timer'; afterMillis: number }
  | { tag: 'cancel-timer' }
  | { tag: 'run' };
```

A core MUST NOT call the clock itself, and a handler SHOULD read the clock once per batch and pass the value in. [AUT-001]

## Recipe 1: debounce

**Problem.** The user types or resizes, and your plugin gets an event for every change. You want to act once, a short time after the last change.

**Constraints.** A timer needs at least 50 ms. A plugin holds at most 64 timers. Timer events coalesce while they wait, so a late handler sees one `timer-fired`. There is no "reset" call. You restart a debounce by cancelling the old timer and setting a new one.

**Rule.** A debounce MUST cancel the pending timer before it arms a new one. Otherwise each change leaves a timer behind, and a busy editor reaches the limit of 64 held timers. [AUT-002]

**Rule.** The handler MUST compare the id of each `timer-fired` event with the id it stored, and ignore every other id. [AUT-003]

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::timers;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::prelude::*;
use ilium_plugin_sdk::types::ids::TimerId;

pub const QUIET_MILLIS: u32 = 300;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Debounce {
    pending: Option<TimerId>,
}

impl Debounce {
    /// Call on every change. Restarts the quiet period.
    pub fn touch(&mut self) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if let Some(old) = self.pending.take() {
            timers::cancel(old);
        }
        self.pending = Some(timers::set(QUIET_MILLIS, None)?);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Call for every timer-fired event. True when the quiet period ended.
    pub fn fired(&mut self, timer: TimerId) -> bool {
        if self.pending == Some(timer) {
            self.pending = None;
            return true;
        }
        false
    }

    /// Call from deactivate. Timers are lost on restart anyway; this keeps the count honest.
    pub fn stop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(old) = self.pending.take() {
            timers::cancel(old);
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import * as timers from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/timers';

export const QUIET_MILLIS = 300;

export class Debounce {
  private pending: bigint | undefined;

  touch(): void {
    if (this.pending !== undefined) timers.cancel(this.pending);
    this.pending = timers.set(QUIET_MILLIS, undefined);
  }

  fired(timer: bigint): boolean {
    if (this.pending !== timer) return false;
    this.pending = undefined;
    return true;
  }

  stop(): void {
    if (this.pending !== undefined) timers.cancel(this.pending);
    this.pending = undefined;
  }
}
```

**Test.** The fake host moves time only through `advance_clock`, and `deliver` never runs timers. The test below types three times, 200 ms apart, and expects one action after the quiet period.

```rust
#[test]
fn three_changes_give_one_action() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::new();
    host.activate::<Editor>();
    for _ in 0..3 {
        host.deliver(vec![text_changed()]);
        host.advance_clock(200);
    }
    assert!(host.submitted().is_empty());      // 200 ms after the last change
    host.advance_clock(100);                   // 300 ms: the quiet period ends
    assert_eq!(host.submitted().len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn unknown_timer_is_ignored() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::new();
    host.activate::<Editor>();
    let submissions = host.deliver(vec![Event::TimerFired(TimerId(999))]);
    assert!(submissions.is_empty());
}
```

**Traps.**

- A debounce delay MUST be 50 ms or more, because a shorter delay is refused with `invalid-argument`. [AUT-004]
- Timers are lost on restart. A debounce that was pending when the plugin restarted does not fire. Treat the next change as the start of a new quiet period.
- Do not use a repeating timer and a "last change" stamp to simulate a debounce. It wakes the plugin every period for nothing.

## Recipe 2: throttle and rate limits

**Problem.** An event arrives many times per second, and your reaction is a host call with a rate limit: a toast, a status segment, a meter update.

**Constraints.** A toast is limited to 3 per 10 s. A status segment and a frame slot are limited to 10 per second per slot. A meter family is limited to 10 per second. Over the rate, the call fails with `rate-limited` and the error carries `retry-after-ms`.

**Rule.** A plugin SHOULD keep its own send rate under the host rate, and SHOULD NOT depend on `rate-limited` as flow control. [AUT-005]

**Rule.** After `rate-limited`, the plugin MUST wait at least `retry-after-ms` before it sends the same kind of call again. [AUT-006]

**Rust**

```rust
/// Allows one action per `interval_millis`. The caller passes `now`.
pub struct Throttle {
    interval_millis: u64,
    last: Option<u64>,
}

impl Throttle {
    pub fn new(interval_millis: u64) -> Self {
        Self { interval_millis, last: None }
    }

    pub fn allow(&mut self, now: u64) -> bool {
        match self.last {
            Some(last) if now.saturating_sub(last) < self.interval_millis => false,
            _ => {
                self.last = Some(now);
                true
            }
        }
    }

    /// Call when the host answered rate-limited with a retry delay.
    pub fn back_off(&mut self, now: u64, retry_after_ms: u32) {
        self.last = Some(now + u64::from(retry_after_ms).saturating_sub(self.interval_millis));
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export class Throttle {
  private last: bigint | undefined;
  constructor(private readonly intervalMillis: bigint) {}

  allow(now: bigint): boolean {
    if (this.last !== undefined && now - this.last < this.intervalMillis) return false;
    this.last = now;
    return true;
  }

  backOff(now: bigint, retryAfterMs: number): void {
    const wait = BigInt(retryAfterMs);
    this.last = now + (wait > this.intervalMillis ? wait - this.intervalMillis : 0n);
  }
}
```

**Test.** Both tests call the core with plain numbers, so no clock is needed.

```rust
#[test]
fn throttle_allows_one_per_interval() {
    let mut throttle = Throttle::new(100);
    assert!(throttle.allow(1_000));
    assert!(!throttle.allow(1_050));
    assert!(throttle.allow(1_100));
}

#[test]
fn back_off_delays_the_next_send() {
    let mut throttle = Throttle::new(100);
    assert!(throttle.allow(0));
    throttle.back_off(0, 2_000);
    assert!(!throttle.allow(1_500));
    assert!(throttle.allow(2_000));
}
```

**Traps.** A throttle MUST take its time from `monotonic-millis`, because wall time can jump backwards and then `now - last` underflows in unsigned arithmetic. The code above uses `saturating_sub` for this reason. [AUT-007]

## Recipe 3: cache with a time limit

**Problem.** You fetch something slow, such as an HTTP answer or a scan, and you want to reuse it for a while.

**Constraints.** Buckets are `global`, `project`, `session` and `shared`. The first three are durable and count against `storage_bucket_mib` (16 MiB for tiers 2 and 3). The `shared` bucket is a cache: the host may clear it at any time, it is shared by all sessions of the user, and it counts against `shared_cache_mib`. A value is at most 1 MiB. The `lease` call lets exactly one caller per key refresh. A folder named `/cache` in the `fs` scope is a different thing: a file area, counted with `data` in `disk_mib`.

| Data | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Can be rebuilt, shared by sessions | `shared` bucket | The host may clear it. Entries evict oldest first. |
| Can be rebuilt, large, a file | `/cache` in `fs` | Files suit big data. The host may evict it. |
| Cannot be rebuilt (user choices, counters) | `global`, `project` or `session` | Durable. Not cleared by the host. |
| Rebuilt per run | In memory | Lost on restart. Cheapest. |

**Rule.** Data that the plugin can rebuild MUST go to the `shared` bucket or to `/cache`, never to a durable bucket, so that it does not fill the 16 MiB bucket. [AUT-008]

**Rule.** A cached value MUST carry its fetch time as `now-unix-millis` inside the stored bytes, and the reader MUST compare it with the current time. The host does not expire entries by age. [AUT-009]

**Rule.** When several sessions can refresh the same entry, only the caller whose `lease` returned true MAY refresh it. [AUT-010]

**Rust**

```rust
use ilium_plugin_sdk::host::{clock, storage::{self, Bucket}};

const TTL_MILLIS: u64 = 10 * 60 * 1000;

fn encode(fetched_at: u64, body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = fetched_at.to_le_bytes().to_vec();
    out.extend_from_slice(body);
    out
}

fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<(u64, &[u8])> {
    let (head, body) = bytes.split_at_checked(8)?;
    Some((u64::from_le_bytes(head.try_into().ok()?), body))
}

/// Returns fresh bytes, stale bytes while another session refreshes, or None.
pub fn read_cached(key: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let now = clock::now_unix_millis();
    let stored = storage::get(Bucket::Shared, key);
    let fresh = stored
        .as_deref()
        .and_then(decode)
        .filter(|(at, _)| now.saturating_sub(*at) < TTL_MILLIS);
    if let Some((_, body)) = fresh {
        return Some(body.to_vec());
    }
    if storage::lease(key, 60_000) {
        return None; // the caller fetches, then calls write_cached
    }
    stored.as_deref().and_then(decode).map(|(_, body)| body.to_vec())
}

pub fn write_cached(key: &str, body: &[u8]) {
    let _ = storage::put(Bucket::Shared, key, &encode(clock::now_unix_millis(), body));
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import { nowUnixMillis } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/clock';
import * as storage from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/storage';

const TTL_MILLIS = 10n * 60n * 1000n;

export function readCached(key: string): Uint8Array | undefined {
  const now = nowUnixMillis();
  const stored = storage.get('shared', key);
  const parsed = stored && stored.length >= 8 ? split(stored) : undefined;
  if (parsed && now - parsed.at < TTL_MILLIS) return parsed.body;
  if (storage.lease(key, 60_000)) return undefined;
  return parsed?.body;
}

function split(bytes: Uint8Array): { at: bigint; body: Uint8Array } {
  const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, 8);
  return { at: view.getBigUint64(0, true), body: bytes.subarray(8) };
}
```

**Test.** `encode` and `decode` are pure, so test them without the host. `read_cached` takes `now` as an argument in a production plugin, so the TTL branch can be tested with fixed numbers.

**Traps.**

- A `put` into `shared` of a value over 1 MiB fails with `invalid-argument`, not `quota-exceeded`.
- The lease is not a lock. It prevents duplicate work, not races. Two callers can still write. The last write wins. That is fine for a cache.
- Never keep the only copy of user data in `shared`. The host may clear it.

## Recipe 4: lists larger than the tree

**Problem.** You have thousands of rows, such as search hits, log lines or files. A tree is limited to 4,096 nodes and 1,024 KiB, and a render must finish in 10 ms.

**Constraints.** The `%list` and `table` widgets keep `selected` and `offset` as host-owned state, which the plugin reads through `ui.widget-state`. There is no view-level virtual list. Virtual-row providers exist only for sidebar rows of the tree, with cursors and a Load more row. The caps `check-list` (256 items) and `list-editor` (64 items) are enforced at render time with `invalid-argument`.

**Rule.** A view MUST render only the rows in the visible window plus a small margin, and MUST NOT put all rows into the tree. The ceiling is 4,096 nodes and 1,024 KiB for the whole tree. [AUT-011]

**Rule.** A view that hides rows behind a window MUST show how many rows exist and where the window is, for example `41 to 60 of 3,212`, so that the user knows more exist. [AUT-012]

**Rust**

```rust
pub struct Window {
    pub first: usize,
    pub len: usize,
}

/// Window for a list of `total` rows, a host offset and a visible height.
pub fn window(total: usize, offset: usize, visible: usize) -> Window {
    let margin = 4;
    let first = offset.saturating_sub(margin).min(total);
    let end = (offset + visible + margin).min(total);
    Window { first, len: end - first }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function window(total: number, offset: number, visible: number): { first: number; len: number } {
  const margin = 4;
  const first = Math.min(Math.max(offset - margin, 0), total);
  const end = Math.min(offset + visible + margin, total);
  return { first, len: end - first };
}
```

A plugin that cannot hold all rows in memory pages them from its source. A catalogue provider returns pages with `limit` (1 to 256), a `next` cursor and `total`. A sidebar virtual-row provider returns rows with a cursor and the host adds the Load more row. See [Catalogs](/pages/api-catalogs/) and [Virtual rows provider](/pages/api-virtual-rows-provider/).

<figure>
<pre class="term">╭  ≡ ● · Search hits ────────────────────────╮
│ 41 to 60 of 3,212                          │
│ src/lib.rs:41                              │
│ src/lib.rs:57                              │
│ src/app.rs:3                               │
│ ...                                        │
│ Load more                                  │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The count line tells the user that the window is part of a larger list.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Test.**

```rust
#[test]
fn window_is_clamped_to_the_list() {
    let w = window(10, 8, 5);
    assert_eq!(w.first, 4);
    assert_eq!(w.first + w.len, 10);
    assert_eq!(window(0, 0, 5).len, 0);
}
```

**Traps.** Do not size the tree by the number of rows. A width change or a resize calls `render` again, and a plugin that rebuilds 3,000 rows per render misses the 10 ms deadline.

## Recipe 5: retry with backoff

**Problem.** A request fails, and some failures are worth another try.

**Constraints.** A request completes with an outcome. A failed one carries an error code. Of the fifteen codes, only some describe a passing problem.

| Code | Retry? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `timed-out`, `busy`, `network`, `rate-limited`, `io` | Yes, with backoff | The cause can pass. For `rate-limited`, wait at least `retry-after-ms`. |
| `quota-exceeded` | After freeing space | A retry fails the same way until something is removed. |
| `not-permitted`, `revoked`, `unsupported` | No | The user or the host decided. A retry cannot change it. |
| `invalid-argument`, `not-found`, `conflict` | No | The request is wrong. Change it. |
| `cancelled` | Only on the next trigger | The plugin or the user stopped it. |
| `pane-not-ready` | Yes, after the next pane event | The pane process has not started. |
| `internal` | Once, then report | A host fault. |

**Rule.** A plugin MUST NOT retry `not-permitted`, `revoked`, `invalid-argument` or `unsupported`. [AUT-013]

**Rule.** A retry loop MUST have a maximum attempt count and a growing delay. A suggested schedule is 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up to 60 s, with at most 5 attempts. [AUT-014]

**Rust**

```rust
pub fn is_transient(code: ErrorCode) -> bool {
    matches!(
        code,
        ErrorCode::TimedOut | ErrorCode::Busy | ErrorCode::Network | ErrorCode::RateLimited | ErrorCode::Io
    )
}

/// Delay before attempt `attempt` (1-based), or None when to give up.
pub fn backoff_millis(attempt: u32, retry_after_ms: Option<u32>) -> Option<u32> {
    const MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 5;
    if attempt > MAX_ATTEMPTS {
        return None;
    }
    let base = 1_000u32.saturating_mul(1 << (attempt - 1)).min(60_000);
    Some(base.max(retry_after_ms.unwrap_or(0)))
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export function backoffMillis(attempt: number, retryAfterMs?: number): number | undefined {
  const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5;
  if (attempt > MAX_ATTEMPTS) return undefined;
  const base = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** (attempt - 1), 60_000);
  return Math.max(base, retryAfterMs ?? 0);
}
```

The retry itself is a timer: `timers.set(delay, None)`, and the `timer-fired` handler starts the request again. The attempt count lives in memory. A restart loses it, which is the right result, since the failure may be gone.

**Test.**

```rust
#[test]
fn backoff_doubles_and_gives_up() {
    assert_eq!(backoff_millis(1, None), Some(1_000));
    assert_eq!(backoff_millis(3, None), Some(4_000));
    assert_eq!(backoff_millis(2, Some(9_000)), Some(9_000));
    assert_eq!(backoff_millis(6, None), None);
}

#[test]
fn failed_request_is_logged_not_trapped() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::new().grant("http:api.example.com");
    host.activate::<Fetcher>();
    host.deliver(vec![command("com.example.fetch/run")]);
    let request = host.pending_requests()[0];
    host.complete(request, Outcome::Failed(ErrorCode::Network));
    assert!(host.logs().iter().any(|line| line.message.contains("retry")));
}
```

## Recipe 6: idempotent submissions

**Problem.** An event can repeat, and your reaction must not repeat with it: a notice, a decoration, a send-input.

**Constraints.** A submission may carry a `dedup-key` of 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:`, `/` and `-`. The key is scoped to the plugin id and stays reserved for 10 minutes. A second submission with the same key completes as `duplicate` with a reference to the first.

**Rule.** A submission whose repeat would harm the user (a notice, a sent line) MUST carry a `dedup-key` built from what makes the action unique, such as an id and a revision. [AUT-015]

**Rule.** A `dedup-key` MUST NOT be reused for different content within 10 minutes. The second submission is dropped as `duplicate` even though its content differs. [AUT-016]

**Rust**

```rust
fn finished_notice(node: u64, revision: u64) -> Submission {
    let mut submission = Submission::new(Intent::Notify(notice_for(node)));
    submission.dedup_key = Some(format!("finished:{node}:{revision}"));
    submission
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
function finishedNotice(node: bigint, revision: bigint): Submission {
  return {
    intent: { tag: 'notify', val: noticeFor(node) },
    correlation: nextCorrelation++,
    dedupKey: `finished:${node}:${revision}`,
  };
}
```

**Test.** Complete the same key twice in the fake host and check that `outcomes()` shows `Outcome::Duplicate` for the second. Check that the key string matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{1,128}$`.

**Traps.** The window is 10 minutes. After it, the same key is accepted again. If an action must be once for all time, record it in storage too.

## Recipe 7: state that survives a restart

**Problem.** The plugin stops and starts, and some state must come back.

**Constraints.** `deactivate` returns up to 1 MiB of restore bytes, with a deadline of 500 ms. The bytes come back as `restored` in the next `activate`. After a trap, the instance is dropped and `deactivate` is never called, so nothing is saved. The restore bytes are not a migration path, and the host drops them when `data_version` differs from the build that wrote them.

**Rule.** The first byte of restore bytes MUST be a format version, and `activate` MUST check the version and the length before it reads. A mismatch MUST fall back to defaults. [AUT-017]

**Rule.** State that must outlive a trap MUST be written to storage when it changes, not only in `deactivate`. [AUT-018]

**Rust**

```rust
const FORMAT: u8 = 1;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Counter {
    pub value: u32,
}

impl Counter {
    pub fn save(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = vec![FORMAT];
        out.extend_from_slice(&self.value.to_le_bytes());
        out
    }

    pub fn load(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
        match bytes {
            [FORMAT, a, b, c, d] => Self { value: u32::from_le_bytes([*a, *b, *c, *d]) },
            _ => Self::default(),
        }
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const FORMAT = 1;

export function save(value: number): Uint8Array {
  const out = new Uint8Array(5);
  out[0] = FORMAT;
  new DataView(out.buffer).setUint32(1, value, true);
  return out;
}

export function load(bytes: Uint8Array | undefined): number {
  if (!bytes || bytes.length !== 5 || bytes[0] !== FORMAT) return 0;
  return new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset).getUint32(1, true);
}
```

**Test.** The core test needs no host. The host test uses the lifecycle methods of the fake host (`deactivate`, `restart_with`).

```rust
#[test]
fn restore_round_trip() {
    let mut host = FakeHost::new();
    host.activate::<Editor>();
    let bytes = host.deactivate("upgrade");
    host.restart_with(bytes.clone());
    assert_eq!(bytes[0], 1);                   // the format byte
}

#[test]
fn bad_restore_bytes_fall_back_to_defaults() {
    assert_eq!(Counter::load(&[]).value, 0);
    assert_eq!(Counter::load(&[9, 1, 0, 0, 0]).value, 0);
    let saved = Counter { value: 7 }.save();
    assert_eq!(Counter::load(&saved).value, 7);
}
```

## Recipe 8: ignore stale results

**Problem.** The user changes the query while a request for the old one is running. The old answer must not overwrite the new one.

**Rule.** A plugin that starts work for a changing input MUST keep a generation number, store it with the request, and discard a completion whose generation is not the current one. [AUT-019]

**Rust**

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Latest {
    generation: u64,
    by_request: HashMap<u64, u64>,
}

impl Latest {
    pub fn start(&mut self, request: u64) {
        self.generation += 1;
        self.by_request.insert(request, self.generation);
    }

    /// True only for the newest request.
    pub fn accept(&mut self, request: u64) -> bool {
        self.by_request.remove(&request) == Some(self.generation)
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
export class Latest {
  private generation = 0;
  private byRequest = new Map<bigint, number>();
  start(request: bigint): void {
    this.generation += 1;
    this.byRequest.set(request, this.generation);
  }
  accept(request: bigint): boolean {
    const mine = this.byRequest.get(request);
    this.byRequest.delete(request);
    return mine === this.generation;
  }
}
```

**Test.** Start two requests, accept the first (false), accept the second (true). Also check that an unknown id is rejected.

A request can also be cancelled when it supports cancellation (jobs do, through `jobs.cancel`). Cancelling saves work but does not replace the guard, because a completion may already be in the queue.

## Recipe 9: handle a whole batch

**Problem.** `on-events` receives a batch, not one event.

**Rule.** The handler MUST process every event of the batch in order, and MUST return before the event deadline (20 ms, 50 ms for tier 1). [AUT-020]

**Rule.** After an `events-dropped` entry, the handler MUST rebuild its picture from a read call instead of trusting its incremental state. [AUT-021]

```rust
fn on_events(&mut self, batch: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Submission> {
    let now = clock::monotonic_millis();
    let mut submissions = Vec::new();
    for event in batch {
        match event {
            Event::EventsDropped(_) => self.resync(),
            Event::TimerFired(timer) => self.on_timer(timer, now, &mut submissions),
            other => self.core.apply(other, now, &mut submissions),
        }
    }
    submissions
}
```

The batch gives you a free coalescing step. If three `agent-activity-changed` events for one node arrive together, apply them all and submit one decoration for the final state.

## Recipe 10: slow work belongs in a job

**Problem.** A step takes more than a few milliseconds: parsing a large file, hashing, formatting.

**Rule.** Work that can take longer than 10 ms MUST run as a job or a request. A handler that spends its 20 ms deadline on work traps the instance. [AUT-022]

A job runs under 2 s CPU, 20 s wall and 64 MiB, and reports progress. Start it from the handler, keep its request id, and read its output after `request-completed`. The full worked example, with cancellation and progress, is in [Performance](/pages/performance/) and [Jobs](/pages/api-jobs/). Combine it with recipe 8 so a result for an old input is dropped.

## Recipe 11: choose how the two sides talk

| Need | Use | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| News nobody answers | Topic publish | Payload 64 KiB, valid JSON, dropped and counted when the queue is full |
| A direct note to a known plugin | Message | Never dropped. A full queue marks the receiver stuck. |
| One answer from one client now | Client request | At most 16 kinds, timeout 1 to 30,000 ms |
| Durable data that both sides need | Each side keeps its own copy in storage; the other side asks with a client request | Atomic `put` per key, no multi-key transaction. Do not use the `shared` bucket: the host may clear it. |

**Rule.** A server side that needs data from the client MUST use a client request with an explicit timeout, and MUST handle `timed-out` and `not-found` (the client is gone). [AUT-023]

See [Client requests](/pages/api-client-requests/) and [Messages and topics](/pages/api-messages-and-topics/).

## Recipe 12: migrate stored data

**Problem.** A new version stores data differently.

**Constraints.** The host owns the migration. The manifest key `data_version` (an unsigned 32-bit integer, default 1) names the layout. When a new version declares a higher number, the host takes a backup, calls the optional export `migrator.migrate(from, to)` once per side before `activate`, stamps the new number when it succeeds, and rolls back when it fails. The `shared` bucket is not migrated: the host clears it when `data_version` changes. The full rules, the backup, the downgrade case and the tests are in [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/). `put` is atomic for one key only, so a migration that touches several keys must be safe to run again.

**Rule.** A plugin that changes how it stores data MUST raise `data_version` and MUST provide a `migrator` export that converts the old layout, instead of reading both layouts inside `activate`. [AUT-024]

**Rule.** A `migrate` function MUST be idempotent and MUST write the new value of a key before it removes the old one, so that an interrupted run can start again from the same arguments. [AUT-025]

```rust
fn migrate(from: u32, to: u32) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    if from < 2 && to >= 2 {
        if let Some(old) = storage::get(Bucket::Global, "notes") {
            storage::put(Bucket::Global, "notes.v2", &upgrade_notes(&old))?;
            storage::remove(Bucket::Global, "notes");
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

If `notes` is already gone, the step does nothing, so a second run is harmless. Compare with the version rules in [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/).

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | What happens | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| Timer id not tracked | Ignore the event | 1 |
| Wall clock jumps backwards | Use monotonic time for intervals | 2 |
| `shared` cleared by the host | The reader sees no value and refetches | 3 |
| Window offset beyond the list | Clamp, show an empty window | 4 |
| `rate-limited` with `retry-after-ms` | Wait at least that long | 2, 5 |
| Same `dedup-key`, different content | Second submission is a duplicate | 6 |
| Restore bytes over 1 MiB | Dropped with a warn line | 7 |
| Trap | No `deactivate`, no restore bytes | 7 |
| `events-dropped` | Resync from a read | 9 |
| Completion for an old input | Discard by generation | 8 |

## What the user sees

Nothing of these patterns directly. They see the effects: a panel that settles after typing, a notice that appears once, a list that says `41 to 60 of 3,212`, and a plugin that is not disabled after a restart. The failure cases show up in `ilium plugin logs <id>` (see [Debugging](/pages/debugging/)).

## See also

- [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) for a review list that covers these patterns
- [Troubleshooting](/pages/guide-troubleshooting/) when a pattern misbehaves
- [Performance](/pages/performance/) for deadlines and budgets
- [Testing](/pages/testing/) for the fake host
- [Requests and outcomes](/pages/requests-and-outcomes/) for outcomes and error codes

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Plugin administration

## Plugin administration

This guide is for the person who runs Ilium for a team. It shows how to decide which plugins people may install, which registries they may use, and how to run a private registry or an offline mirror. A plugin is a signed package that adds features to Ilium. The administrator sets the rules in one policy file. Users cannot loosen them.

### You will need

- The policy file format: [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/).
- The trust model: [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/).
- The registry protocol: [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/).

Requirement ids such as `PKG-460` are collected in [Requirements: manifest and package](/pages/reference-requirements-manifest-package/).

## Choose a stance

| Goal | Policy | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Allow only plugins from your company | `publishers.allow` with your key fingerprint, and `packages.allowed_sources` with your registry | [PKG-460] |
| Allow only bundled plugins | `packages.allow_third_party = false` | [PKG-461] |
| Block one plugin | `plugins.deny_ids = ["com.example.bad"]` | [PKG-462] |
| Block a risky grant everywhere | `grants.deny = ["process.run:*"]` | [PKG-463] |
| Stop beta builds | `packages.allowed_channels = ["stable"]` | [PKG-464] |

A policy that fails an install returns a `policy.*` code and exit 7 (see [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/#exit-codes)). The user sees the message "Blocked by your administrator".

## Pre-trust your key

Put the key of your company in the machine trust store so that users do not see a trust prompt. The trust store format and the `trust add` command are in [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/#the-trust-store).

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-465] | An administrator MAY add a key with `ilium plugin trust add <file> --tier T2 --system`. A key added this way has `added_by: admin` and the user cannot remove it. |
| [PKG-466] | A key in the trust store never overrides a revocation. A revoked key stays revoked. |

## Run a private registry

A registry is a folder of signed files on a web server. You need no database. Follow [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/#file-layout) for the layout. Steps:

1. Create the root key offline and keep it on a device that is not on the network.
2. Publish `root.json`, `timestamp.json`, `snapshot.json` and `index.json` to an HTTPS folder.
3. Give every client the root key id with `ilium plugin registry add <url> --root-key <key_id>`, or write it in the user configuration under `[plugins.registry]`.
4. Set `packages.allowed_sources` in the policy to the same URL.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-467] | A registry MUST be served over HTTPS. The client refuses plain `http:` except `localhost` in development (PKG-371). |
| [PKG-468] | The timestamp document expires after one day. The operator MUST re-sign it at least daily, or clients report `registry.stale`. |
| [PKG-469] | To rotate the root key, publish a rotation document signed by the old and the new key. See [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/#rootjson). |

## Mirror and air-gap

A mirror copies a registry so that machines without internet can install. Run `ilium plugin mirror sync <dir> --registry <url> --allow <id>` on a connected machine, copy the folder to the isolated network and serve it. For a single machine, use `export-bundle` and `install --from-bundle`. Both copy signed bytes without change, so the signatures still verify.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-473] | A mirror MUST NOT be signed by the mirror operator. Clients check the signatures of the original registry. |
| [PKG-474] | With `packages.allowed_sources` set to the mirror, a client that cannot reach the mirror reports `registry.unreachable` and never falls back to another registry. |

## Policy keys for registries and sources

The keys `packages.allowed_sources` [PKG-470], `packages.allow_url_installs` [PKG-471] and `packages.allowed_channels` [PKG-472] are defined in [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/#keys). Rules:

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-475] | `packages.allowed_sources` compares the scheme, host and path prefix of the configured URL. A trailing slash does not matter. |
| [PKG-476] | A package installed before the policy changed is not removed. It follows the existing `disabled-by-policy` rule of the policy page. |

## Audit

The audit log is always on. Each install, update, removal, trust change and policy refusal writes one record. See [Audit log](/pages/reference-audit-log/).

## Automatic updates

Automatic updates are off. A user can set `[plugins] auto_update` to `notify` or `install` in their configuration. The administrator controls the effect through `packages.allowed_channels` and `plugins.deny_ids`, because an automatic update passes through the same policy check as a manual one. Details: [Install and update](/pages/reference-install-and-update/).

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-477] | An automatic update MUST run all install checks, and MUST NOT install when new grants or a new signing key would need a prompt. It then notifies only. |

## Edge cases

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Policy file is invalid | The host refuses to start plugins and shows `policy.invalid`. See [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/#errors-and-edge-cases). |
| Two policies conflict | The stricter value wins. |
| User adds a registry not in `packages.allowed_sources` | `policy.source-denied`, exit 7. |
| Mirror is missing a dependency | `dependency.unsatisfied` names the id. Add it with `--with-deps`. |

## See also

- [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/)
- [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/)
- [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/)
- [Plugin store](/pages/user-plugin-store/)

# Plugin documentation guide

## Plugin documentation guide

This guide says what documentation a plugin ships and how to write it. Good plugin documentation is short and exact. The `lint` command checks the parts it can check. See [Check and lint rules](/pages/reference-check-and-lint-rules/).

Terms:

- **README**: the file a person reads first, in the repository and on the package page.
- **Help topic**: a Markdown file inside the package that Ilium shows in its help viewer.
- **Changelog**: the list of changes per version.

## You will need

- A plugin project. `ilium plugin new` writes the skeletons.
- The manifest keys `description`, `license` and `contributes.help`. See [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/).

## What a plugin ships

| File | Required | Checked by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | yes | `lint.readme-missing` | First read: what, how to build, which grants |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | yes | `lint.changelog-missing` | Changes per version |
| `help/<id>.md` | one per `contributes.help` entry | `lint.help-topic-missing` | In-app help |
| `docs/` | no | none | Longer guides for authors |
| `LICENSE` | when `license` is set | `lint.license-file-missing` | The license text |

- **[DEV-780]** A plugin MUST ship a README, a changelog and one help topic for each `contributes.help` entry. A project from `new` already does.
- **[DEV-781]** The README MUST list every requested grant with one sentence on why the plugin needs it. The manifest has no field for a reason, so the README is the place. `lint.grant-unexplained` warns when a grant name does not appear in the README.
- **[DEV-782]** The README MUST give the commands to build and test the plugin.
- **[DEV-783]** The changelog MUST follow Keep a Changelog headings: `Added`, `Changed`, `Fixed`, `Removed`. The top section of a release MUST match `version` in the manifest, or be `Unreleased`.

## Writing a help topic

A help topic is Markdown with these rules.

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Format | Markdown, headings level 1 to 3 |
| Title | First line, `# Title`, same as the manifest `title` |
| Length | At most 20 KiB |
| Images | Not supported. Use text. |
| Links | Other topics as `help:<topic-id>`. Web links open in the browser. |

- **[DEV-785]** A help topic MUST start with a level 1 heading equal to the `title` in the manifest entry. `lint.help-title-mismatch` warns otherwise.
- **[DEV-786]** A help topic MUST NOT exceed 20 KiB. `lint.help-topic-too-large` warns for a larger file.
- **[DEV-787]** A link `help:<topic-id>` to a topic that the plugin does not ship MUST be a `lint.help-link-broken` warning.
- **[DEV-788]** A help topic SHOULD name each command, setting and view the plugin adds, so a search in the help viewer finds them.

## Style

Follow the style of this manual.

- Short sentences. One idea each.
- Sentence case for headings.
- Name each thing the same way every time.
- Show a command with its exact flags, and show the exact text it prints when that helps.
- Put a warning before the step it applies to, in words, not in symbols.

## A good README, step by step

1. Write one paragraph that says what the plugin adds to Ilium.
2. List the requested grants and why.
3. Show the install command for a package: `ilium plugin install <file>`.
4. Show how to build and test.
5. Say which sides the plugin has and which Ilium versions it supports.
6. Link the changelog and the license.

An example:

```markdown
# Agent tools

Marks agent panes that are working with a badge in the tree.

## Grants

- `tree.read`: reads agent activity.
- `tree.decorate`: sets the badge.

## Build and test

    ilium plugin check
    ilium plugin lint --deny warnings
    ilium plugin test
    ilium plugin build

## Install

    ilium plugin install dist/example.agent-tools-0.1.0.iliumpkg
```

## Documenting settings and commands

- **[DEV-790]** Every setting row MUST have a `help` text in the settings schema or a help topic that names the row.
- **[DEV-791]** Every command in `contributes.commands` MUST have a `title` in sentence case with no final period.

## Docs for extension points

A plugin that declares an extension point MUST describe it in a document: the point id, its kind, the payload, the reply rules and the deadline. `core-style` templates write `docs/EXTENDING.md` for this.

- **[DEV-795]** A declared extension point MUST appear in the README or in `docs/EXTENDING.md`. `lint.extension-point-undocumented` warns when its id is absent from both.

## A complete changelog

```markdown
# Changelog

## [0.2.0] - 2030-02-01

### Added

- A command that clears all badges.

### Changed

- The badge now shows for agents that wait for approval.

### Fixed

- A badge no longer stays after the agent pane closes.

## [0.1.0] - 2030-01-01

### Added

- First version.
```

- **[DEV-796]** Dates in the changelog MUST use `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **[DEV-797]** The newest version MUST come first.

## A complete help topic

```markdown
# Agent tools

Agent tools marks agent panes that are working.

## Commands

- Clear badges: removes every badge the plugin set.

## Settings

- Show badge for approval: also marks agents that wait for approval.

## Grants

The plugin reads agent activity and sets decorations. It needs no
other grants.
```

## Review checklist

| Question | Where it is checked |
|---|---|
| Does the README say what the plugin does in one paragraph? | A person |
| Does every requested grant have a sentence? | `lint.grant-unexplained` |
| Does every command have a help line? | A person |
| Do help titles match the manifest? | `lint.help-title-mismatch` |
| Do help links resolve? | `lint.help-link-broken` |
| Does the changelog top section match the version? | A person, or a CI shell step |
| Is the license text present? | `lint.license-file-missing` |

## Edge cases

- **Translated help.** Ship `help/<id>.<lang>.md` for another language. The viewer falls back to the base file.
- **Very long READMEs.** The package page shows the first 64 KiB.
- **No help topic.** A plugin with `contributes.help` empty passes lint but shows no help entry.

## See also

- [Check and lint rules](/pages/reference-check-and-lint-rules/)
- [Project templates](/pages/reference-project-templates/)
- [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/)
- [CI recipes](/pages/guide-ci-recipes/)

API checked against `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Porting from other plugin systems

## Porting from other plugin systems

This guide helps an author who knows VS Code extensions, Neovim plugins or tmux plugins (TPM) move an idea to Ilium. It maps concepts, lists what has no equivalent, and shows a small port of each. Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-700` to `AUT-799`.

The three systems are different from Ilium in one main way. Their plugins run with the full rights of the user, in a process they share with the editor or can start by shell. An Ilium plugin is a WebAssembly component in a sandbox. It can do only what its grants allow, in the time its deadlines allow. A port starts from that fact. [Security](/pages/security/) and [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/) say more.

### Choosing the sides

Ilium plugins have up to three sides: server (S), client (C) and scene (A). The server owns terminals and agents. The client draws the interface.

| Your plugin does | Side |
|---|---|
| Watches terminals or agents, reacts to output | S |
| Draws a panel, pane kind or settings page | C |
| Draws an animated background | A |
| Runs a command in the palette | The side that owns the command's data |

A port SHOULD put logic about panes and agents on S and drawing on C, and SHOULD send messages between them rather than share state. [AUT-701] See [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) for the message pattern.

## From VS Code

### Concept map

| VS Code | Ilium | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `package.json` `contributes.commands` | Manifest `contributes.commands` | Id becomes `<plugin-id>/<id>` |
| `contributes.keybindings` | `contributes.keybindings` | Chords and modes `global`, `prefix`, `pane:<kind>` |
| `contributes.configuration` | `contributes.settings` | A JSON schema subset. See [Settings schema](/pages/reference-settings-schema/) |
| `activationEvents` | `activation` | `startup`, `command:<id>`, `view:<id>` and others. Lazy by default |
| `vscode.window.showInformationMessage` | A toast intent | Rate limited to 3 per 10 s |
| WebView panel | `panels` with widgets | No HTML. You return a widget tree |
| TreeView | `virtual_rows` or a `list` widget | Sidebar rows or a list in a panel |
| Status bar item | Status segment | 10 updates per second per slot |
| `workspaceState`, `globalState` | Storage buckets `project`, `global`, `session` | Key 256 bytes, value 1 MiB |
| `context.subscriptions` | `deactivate` | There is no disposable list. Cancel your timers and requests yourself |
| `fs` | `fs.read:<scope>`, `fs.write:<scope>` | Scopes, not paths |
| `child_process` | `process.run:<program>` | High-risk grant, no network |
| `fetch` | `http:<host-pattern>` | Host allowlist |
| `vscode.workspace.onDidChange...` | Events | Delivered in batches |
| Language server client | No equivalent | See below |
| Debug adapter | No equivalent | |
| Extension API of another extension | `plugin-services` (unstable) | Four unstable features exist. Avoid them in a release |

### What does not port

Ilium has no editor-language protocol, no debugger protocol, no webview, no extension-to-extension object access, no Node.js and no way to load native modules. A plugin cannot run arbitrary code in the host. Work that needs a long process is started with `process.run` and the `process.long-lived` grant, and then the plugin only reads its output.

### Example: a "Word count" command

VS Code:

```ts
vscode.commands.registerCommand('wc.count', () => {
  const text = vscode.window.activeTextEditor?.document.getText() ?? '';
  vscode.window.showInformationMessage(`${text.split(/\s+/).length} words`);
});
```

Ilium (TypeScript, client side). The editor primitive gives the lines of the active buffer, and a toast shows the count. The command id is declared in the manifest. The sketch below shows the shape only.

```json
{ "contributes": { "commands": [ { "id": "count", "title": "Count words" } ] },
  "activation": ["command:example.wc/count"],
  "capabilities": { "client": ["editor.read", "notify.toast"] } }
```

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk';
import { editor } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/editor';
import { intents } from '@ilium/plugin-sdk/host/intents';

export default definePlugin({
  side: 'client',
  handler: {
    onCommand(id: string) {
      if (id !== 'count') return;
      // Read the lines of the buffer in the focused pane (see the editor page).
      const text = readActiveBufferText(editor);
      const words = text.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length;
      // Send a toast intent (grant notify.toast).
      intents.submitToast(`${words} words`);
    },
  },
});
```

`readActiveBufferText` and `submitToast` are placeholders for the calls described in the pages below. Take the exact signatures from [Editor primitive](/pages/primitives-editor/) and [Toast intents](/pages/api-intent-chrome/) before you copy them. A port MUST declare every grant its calls need, and `ilium plugin check` reports an import without a grant as `component.import-ungranted`. [AUT-702]

## From Neovim

### Concept map

| Neovim | Ilium | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin/*.lua` run at start | `activation: ["startup"]` | Lazy is the default and is better |
| `vim.api.nvim_create_user_command` | `contributes.commands` | Appears in the command palette |
| `vim.keymap.set` | `contributes.keybindings` | Or `keys.intercept` (high risk) for raw keys |
| `vim.g.*` options | `contributes.settings` | A schema, shown in Settings |
| Autocommands (`BufWritePost`) | Events | Match on event name in `handler` |
| `vim.loop` timers | `timers` | Minimum 50 ms, 64 held |
| `vim.fn.jobstart` | `jobs.run` (a declared job kind), or `process.run` | Jobs have 2 s CPU, 20 s wall, 64 MiB |
| Floating windows | `panels` with `modal`, popups | Anchors are in [UI model](/pages/ui-model/) |
| Statusline components | Status segment | |
| `vim.fn.system` | `process.run:<program>` | One program per grant, no network |
| `:h` help | `contributes.help` | Markdown topics, 20 KiB each |
| Lua `require` of other plugins | Not available | `plugin-services` is unstable |
| `nvim_buf_set_lines` | `editor.edit` | Through intents, not direct writes |
| Treesitter and LSP | No equivalent | |

### What does not port

A Neovim plugin may change anything at any time because it runs in the editor's process. An Ilium plugin changes things only through intents, and the host may refuse them. There is no `eval`, no global state shared between plugins and no synchronous block while a job runs. A port that waits in a loop MUST be rewritten as events: start the work, return, and handle the result when `request-completed` arrives. [AUT-703]

### Example: a timer that refreshes a status

Neovim:

```lua
local timer = vim.loop.new_timer()
timer:start(0, 5000, vim.schedule_wrap(function()
  vim.g.build_status = vim.fn.system("make -q") 
end))
```

Ilium (Rust, server side). The timer fires every 5 s. The handler starts a job of a kind declared in `contributes.jobs` (grant `jobs.run`) and returns at once.

```rust
fn activate() -> Result<(), PluginError> {
    timers::set(5_000, Some(5_000))?;
    Ok(())
}

fn handle(event: Event) {
    if let Event::TimerFired(_) = event {
        // Start the declared job kind; the result arrives later as `request-completed`.
        let _ = jobs::start_request("build-status", &[]);
    }
}
```

The fake host does not run timers by itself. A test calls `advance_clock(5_000)` and then `settle()`. See [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/).

## From tmux plugins (TPM)

tmux plugins are shell scripts that call `tmux` commands and set options. Ilium panes are not tmux panes, and a plugin cannot run shell code in the host.

| tmux plugin | Ilium |
|---|---|
| `set -g @plugin '...'` in `.tmux.conf` | `ilium plugin install <file>` |
| `bind-key` | `contributes.keybindings` with mode `prefix` |
| `status-right` with `#(script)` | A status segment filled by the plugin |
| `display-message` | A toast intent |
| `capture-pane -p` | `terminal.read-screen` |
| `send-keys` | `terminal.write` (high risk) |
| `split-window`, `new-window` | `panes.create`, the `create-split` intent |
| `run-shell` hooks on events | Events, with the matching grant |
| `pane-title-changed` hooks | Events from the tree and pane primitives |
| `resurrect`-style save and restore | Restore bytes and storage. See [Persistence and restart](/pages/reference-persistence-and-restart/) |
| Copy-mode plugins | Not available |

A tmux plugin that only wraps shell commands often becomes a plugin with a `process.run:<program>` grant. A port SHOULD prefer the typed primitive (`terminal.read-screen`) over a program, because the primitive needs a weaker grant. [AUT-704]

### Example: a "log the last screen" binding

tmux:

```bash
bind-key L run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p > ~/screen.log"
```

Ilium: a command with a key chord and two grants, `terminal.read-screen` and `fs.write:<scope>`. The plugin writes the file to a granted scope, not to an arbitrary path. A port MUST NOT ask for a write grant wider than the folder it writes to. [AUT-705]

## Cross-cutting differences

| Topic | Other systems | Ilium |
|---|---|---|
| Rights | Everything the user can do | Only granted capabilities |
| Time | Unbounded | Deadlines: events 20 ms, commands 50 ms, render 10 ms |
| Failure | An error message, the editor continues | A trap, restart after 1 s, 5 s, 30 s, disabled at the third failure in 10 minutes |
| State | Variables in the process | Lost on restart. Use storage or restore bytes |
| Language | Lua, JavaScript, shell | Rust or TypeScript, built to a component |
| Distribution | A git clone or a marketplace |  A signed or unsigned `.iliumpkg` file |
| UI | HTML, Lua floats, status strings | A widget tree. The host draws |
| Updates | The editor reloads | Staged update, `deactivate(upgrade)`, migrate, activate |

## A porting method

1. List what the old plugin does in one sentence each.
2. Mark each item as a command, an event reaction, a view or a background job.
3. Look up the capability for each in [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/). An item without one is out of scope.
4. Write the manifest first, with the smallest grant set.
5. Port logic with tests on the fake host.
6. Run the [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/).

A port SHOULD be written as a new plugin with a new id, and SHOULD NOT reuse the name of the original in a way that suggests it is the same product. [AUT-706]

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The old plugin needs a long-running shell command | Use `process.spawn` with `process.long-lived`, and read output only |
| The old plugin edits files directly | Use `fs.write:<scope>` for a granted scope |
| The old plugin reads the environment | Not available. Use a setting |
| The old plugin uses a network from the editor | `http:<host-pattern>`, one pattern per host |
| The old plugin needs a different language runtime | Not available. Compile to a component |
| The old plugin depends on another plugin | Use a documented extension point, not a private call |

## See also

- [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/)
- [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/)
- [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/)
- [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/)
- [Tutorial: agent badge](/pages/tutorial-01-agent-badge/)
- [FAQ](/pages/guide-faq/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
