# Publishing and support

## Publishing and support

This guide covers the last mile of a plugin: preparing a release, signing it, giving it to users, writing a changelog, answering a bug report, and handling a lost key. It follows the order in which an author meets these tasks. The commands are the ones of the [Plugin command-line reference](/pages/reference-plugin-cli/), and the signing rules are in [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/).

Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-300` to `AUT-399`. The complete list is in [Requirements for author guides](/pages/reference-requirements-author-guides/).

### You need

- A plugin that passes its tests. See [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/).
- A release build. A debug build is for development only.
- For a signed (T2) release, an Ed25519 publisher key made with `ilium plugin keygen`.

## What publishing means in version 0.1.0

In `ilium:plugin@0.1.0` the supported way to publish is to hand over files. A release is three things:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<id>-<version>.iliumpkg` | The package, a deterministic ZIP file |
| `publisher.pub` | The public key of the signer (signed releases only) |
| The SHA-256 of the package | Printed by `ilium plugin pack`, written in your release notes |

Users add the key once with `ilium plugin trust add publisher.pub` and install the package with `ilium plugin install`. A newer version of an installed id is an update.

The manual also specifies an optional registry, a set of signed static files that a client can read (see [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/)). It adds search, channels, yank and deprecate. The command `ilium plugin publish` is described there, while the command-line reference marks it as reserved in this contract version. Until those two pages agree, an author MUST treat the package file as the only publishing route that is certain to work, and MAY add a registry as a second route when the host supports it. [AUT-301]

## Before you release

Run these in the project folder, in this order. Each is offline.

```bash
ilium plugin check
ilium plugin lint --deny warnings
ilium plugin test
ilium plugin build --release
ilium plugin pack
ilium plugin verify dist/com.example.notes-1.4.0.iliumpkg
```

| Step | Catches |
|---|---|
| `check` | Mistakes that would stop an install or trap at run time. It reports the same codes as the installer. |
| `lint` | Weak spots such as an unused grant, a missing help topic or a debug build in a release |
| `test` | Behaviour against your fixtures |
| `build --release` | A release build without debug information |
| `pack` | The deterministic archive with the `files` inventory |
| `verify` | Offline replay of the install stages 1 to 8 on the finished file |

A release MUST pass `check` without errors and SHOULD pass `lint --deny warnings`. [AUT-302]

A release package MUST be built with `--release`, because a package that carries debug information or source maps is larger and fails `lint.debug-info-in-release`. [AUT-303]

The release checklist of [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) lists what each of these checks and what they cannot check.

### What goes into the package

| Item | Include | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Components (`*.wasm`) | Yes | The plugin |
| `manifest.json`, `files` inventory | Yes | Written by `pack` |
| Help topics, icons, assets | Yes | Declared in the manifest |
| `README.md`, `LICENSE` | Yes | The package page and the review dialog use them |
| `src/**` | Only with `--include-src` | Reviewers can read it. The host never loads it. |
| `.cwasm` precompiled files | Never | Refused with `package.precompiled-forbidden` |
| Test fixtures, build caches | No | They add size and no value |

A package MUST NOT contain a secret, a key or a token. The package is a file that anyone can open. [AUT-304]

## Names, ids and versions

The `id` is permanent. It is `[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+`, usually a reverse domain name that you control, such as `com.example.notes`. The prefix `ilium.` belongs to first-party plugins and is refused for others with `manifest.id-reserved`.

A signed package has one more rule: its id MUST start with the publisher id of the signing key and a dot, and an id that does not is refused with `manifest.id-publisher`. [AUT-305]

Pick the id once. A rename is a different plugin, and users lose grants, settings and storage. See [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/).

## Keys

A signed release needs a key pair. Make it once for each publisher.

```bash
ilium plugin keygen --publisher-id com.example --publisher "Example Corp" --out ~/keys/example
ilium plugin sign dist/com.example.notes-1.4.0.iliumpkg --key ~/keys/example/publisher.key
```

`keygen` writes `publisher.key` (the secret, mode 0600) and `publisher.pub` (the public part). It refuses to overwrite either file with `trust.key-exists`. `sign` refuses a key file that other users can read with `sign.key-permissions`, and refuses a manifest whose `publisher` differs from the key with `sign.publisher-mismatch`.

| Rule | Reason |
|---|---|
| Keep `publisher.key` outside the project and outside version control | A key in a repository is a leaked key |
| Keep an offline copy | A lost key cannot be recovered |
| Sign last | A later `pack` writes a new archive without a signature |
| Sign in a clean environment, or give CI the key through `ILIUM_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY` | The key never appears in a command line or a log |

The secret key MUST NOT be committed, packaged or printed. [AUT-306]

A release MUST be signed after the last `pack`, and the signed file MUST be the file that users receive. Signing twice with the same key gives the same bytes. [AUT-307]

### Show users the fingerprint

The key fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the raw public key. Users see its short form (for example `3f2a…9c01`) in the trust dialog. The author SHOULD publish the full fingerprint on a channel separate from the download, such as the project page, so that a user can compare the two. [AUT-308]

### Lost, leaked or changed keys

| Situation | What happens | What the author does |
|---|---|---|
| Key lost | No new signed release for that publisher id | Make a new key and a new publisher id, publish a new plugin id, and tell users |
| Key leaked | Anyone can sign as you | Stop shipping, tell users to run `ilium plugin trust revoke <key_id>`, publish under a new key |
| A known publisher id arrives with another key | Refused with `package.publisher-key-changed` | Users must remove the old key and add the new one on purpose |
| Registry in use | A key can also be revoked in the registry metadata | Publish the revocation there too |

A leaked key MUST be announced to users on the same channel as the releases, with the fingerprint of the key that replaces it. [AUT-309]

## Release notes and changelog

Keep a `CHANGELOG.md` in the project. Use one block per version, newest first, with the date in `YYYY-MM-DD` form and three kinds of entry.

```text
## 1.4.0 (2026-10-12)

Added
- Export to Markdown (command `export-notes`).

Changed
- The old command id `notes-export` still works and is hidden. It will go in 3.0.0.

Fixed
- A note with an empty title no longer traps the panel.
```

| Include | Why |
|---|---|
| New or changed grants | The update review dialog will show them |
| Raised `data_version` and what the migration does | Users with large data will wait |
| Renamed or removed names | See [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) |
| The SHA-256 of the package | So that users can check the file |
| The contract version (`api`) | So that users know whether their Ilium supports it |

Release notes MUST name every new grant and every raised `data_version`. [AUT-310]

A project SHOULD ship `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, because `lint.readme-missing` and `lint.changelog-missing` report their absence. [AUT-311]

The in-product help of the plugin is a separate matter and is covered in [Plugin documentation guide](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/).

## Distribution channels

| Channel | Good for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A project page with a download link, the fingerprint and the SHA-256 | Public plugins | Keep old versions available so that users can roll back |
| A shared folder or file host | A team | Send `publisher.pub` once, out of band |
| E-mail | One user | Attach the package and send the fingerprint another way |
| A registry, when the host supports it | Search, channels, updates | Adds `yank` and `deprecate` |

Wherever the file goes, the author SHOULD name the file `<id>-<version>.iliumpkg` and SHOULD NOT rename it. [AUT-312]

A user can check a file before installing it: `ilium plugin verify <file>` runs the install stages offline, and `ilium plugin inspect <file> --verify` recomputes the hashes.

## Platforms

T2 and T3 packages run only on Linux in version 0.1.0 and are refused on Windows and macOS with `package.platform-unsupported`. A release page MUST state that signed and unsigned third-party packages need Linux. [AUT-313]

## Supporting your users

A bug report is useful when it lets you see what the plugin did. The user has four tools, and you tell them which to use.

| Ask the user for | Command | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| The plugin log | `ilium plugin logs <id> --tail 200` | Traps, restarts, deadline breaches, refusals |
| The state and failures | `ilium plugin status <id>` | Health and the failure window |
| Resource use | `ilium plugin stats <id>` | Use against each limit |
| A recorded trace | `ilium plugin trace <id> --last 100 --record trace.replay` | The events and calls, with payloads redacted |
| An environment check | `ilium plugin doctor` | Host and sandbox facts |
| The version and grants | `ilium plugin info <id>` | What is installed and what was granted |

Payloads in a normal trace are redacted and print as `<redacted N bytes>`. `--unredacted` works only for a plugin installed with `ilium plugin dev`, so an author MUST NOT ask a user for unredacted output from a normal install. [AUT-314]

A plugin that logs MUST NOT write secrets, tokens, file contents or whole payloads to the plugin log. A log line is 16 KiB at most, so write a count or an id. [AUT-315]

### A template for bug reports

Put this in your README, so that users send what you need:

```text
Plugin id and version:        (ilium plugin info <id>)
Ilium version:                (ilium --version)
Operating system:
What you did:
What you expected:
What happened:
Plugin log, last 100 lines:   (ilium plugin logs <id> --tail 100)
Status:                       (ilium plugin status <id>)
```

### Reproducing a report

With a replay file from `ilium plugin trace --record`, you can run `ilium plugin test --replay trace.replay` and see the same events. The fake host runs on a fake clock, so timing problems are reproduced with `advance_clock`. A report that cannot be reproduced SHOULD be turned into a fixture once you understand it, so that it never returns. [AUT-316]

### Triage

| Symptom in the report | First place to look |
|---|---|
| Plugin disabled after three failures | The first trap in the log. Later restarts repeat it. |
| `not-permitted` | The user declined or revoked a grant. Your code must work without it. |
| Install error with a `manifest.` or `package.` code | [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/), install code index |
| Works on your machine only | Sandbox paths, network allowlists, tier differences |
| Slow or stuck | `ilium plugin stats` and `ilium plugin profile` |

[Troubleshooting](/pages/guide-troubleshooting/) lists these by symptom for authors.

## Security reports

If someone reports a vulnerability, treat it as private until a fix is out. Publish a fixed version with a higher number, state in the release notes that it is a security fix, and tell users to update. If the vulnerability needs a grant to be exploited, say which grant. A plugin that cannot be fixed SHOULD be deprecated with a successor named, when a registry is in use. [AUT-317]

An author MUST publish a way to reach them, in the README and in the package description, before the first release. [AUT-318]

## Withdrawing a release

| Goal | How |
|---|---|
| A bad version must not be installed new | Publish a higher fixed version. With a registry, `yank` the bad one. Installed copies keep working. |
| The whole plugin is obsolete | With a registry, `deprecate` with a message and a successor |
| Users must stop using it at once | Tell them to run `ilium plugin disable <id>` or `uninstall <id>` |

A version number, once published, MUST NOT be reused for different content. The host refuses it with `package.version-reused`. [AUT-319]

## Edge cases and errors

| Situation | Result | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest `publisher` differs from the key | `sign.publisher-mismatch` at sign, `manifest.publisher-mismatch` at install | Use the same publisher string and publisher id |
| Package signed, then packed again | The signature is gone | Sign last |
| Key file readable by others | `sign.key-permissions` | `chmod 600` |
| Package renamed | Still installs. The id comes from the manifest. | Keep the standard name |
| Package built with `--debug` | `lint.debug-info-in-release` | Rebuild with `--release` |
| User on Windows or macOS | `package.platform-unsupported` | Say so on the release page |
| Same version, new content | `package.version-reused` | Raise the version |

## What the user sees

Before install, the review dialog lists the publisher, the tier, the signature state, the key fingerprint and every grant, one row each. A key that is not trusted is offered with `Trust publisher`. After install the plugin appears in Settings > Plugins with its version. See [Managing plugins](/pages/user-managing-plugins/).

## See also

- [Package and share](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/) for the first release step by step
- [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/) for key and signature formats
- [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/) for the archive
- [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/) before each release
- [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) for version rules

# Publishing guide

## Publishing guide

This guide shows how to take a finished plugin and publish it so that other people can install it. You will create a signing key, build a package that others can reproduce, sign it, check it and upload it to a registry. Support and issue handling are in [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/).

### You will need

- A plugin that passes `ilium plugin check` and `ilium plugin test`. See [Tutorial: package and share](/pages/tutorial-09-package-and-share/).
- The manifest rules: [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/).
- The key and signature formats: [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/).

Requirement ids such as `PKG-490` are in [Requirements: manifest and package](/pages/reference-requirements-manifest-package/).

## Choose an id and a version

Your id starts with a namespace that you own, such as `com.example.` or your registry handle. The registry checks this when you publish. See [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/#namespaces).

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-490] | The first segment pair of the plugin id MUST match the publisher id in the signing key (PKG-218). Otherwise signing fails with `manifest.id-publisher`. |
| [PKG-491] | Use SemVer. Raise the major number when you remove a command, a service function or a setting. See [Versions and dependencies](/pages/reference-dependency-resolution/#plugin-versions). |
| [PKG-492] | A version is immutable once published. A fix needs a new version (PKG-394). |

## Create a signing key

Run `ilium plugin keygen --publisher-id com.example --publisher "Example Labs" --out ~/keys/example`. Keep the private file offline and back it up. If you lose it, users must trust a new key. If someone steals it, follow the runbook in [Signing and trust](/pages/reference-signing-and-trust/#a-compromised-key-the-publisher-runbook).

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-493] | The private key MUST NOT be stored in the plugin repository. For CI, put it in a secret store and pass it through `ILIUM_PUBLISHER_KEY`. |
| [PKG-494] | Encrypt a key kept on disk. Pass the passphrase through `ILIUM_KEY_PASSPHRASE`, never on the command line. |

## Reproducible builds

A build is reproducible when two machines make the same package bytes from the same source. Reproducible builds let users and registries confirm that a package really comes from the source you published.

`ilium plugin pack` already writes a deterministic archive: fixed entry order, fixed timestamps, no extra fields (see [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/#the-ilium-plugin-pack-algorithm)). The remaining source of difference is the WebAssembly component that your compiler writes.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-495] | Pin the toolchain version in the repository (`rust-toolchain.toml` or `package-lock.json`). |
| [PKG-496] | Build with the lock file frozen (`cargo build --locked`, `npm ci`). |
| [PKG-497] | Do not embed the build time, the user name or an absolute path. In Rust set `--remap-path-prefix`. |
| [PKG-498] | Write `build-info.json` with the toolchain name and version and the source commit. `pack` includes it and the registry shows it. |
| [PKG-499] | Verify: build twice in clean folders and compare `sha256sum` of the two `.iliumpkg` files. They MUST be equal. |

If the two hashes differ, unpack both with any ZIP tool and compare the entries one by one. The differing entry is almost always a `.wasm` file.

## SBOM

An SBOM is a list of every library that went into your component, with versions and licences. It helps users and administrators answer "does this plugin contain the vulnerable library?".

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-500] | Put `sbom.json` in the project root. `pack` includes it as `sbom.json`. |
| [PKG-501] | The file SHOULD be CycloneDX 1.5 JSON or SPDX 2.3 JSON. The host reads it as opaque data and does not validate its content. |
| [PKG-502] | The file MUST be at most 4 MiB. A larger file fails with `package.size-limit`. |
| [PKG-503] | Generate it from the lock file, for example `cargo cyclonedx` or `npx @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm`. |
| [PKG-504] | A registry at review level B MAY require an SBOM (PKG-401). |

## Pack, sign, check

```
ilium plugin pack
ilium plugin sign dist/com.example.git-tools-1.4.2.iliumpkg --key ~/keys/example.key
ilium plugin verify dist/com.example.git-tools-1.4.2.iliumpkg
```

`verify` runs the install stages 1 to 7 without installing. A signed package has a `signature` entry that covers the exact bytes of `manifest.json`.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-505] | Sign only after the final `pack`. Changing any file after signing makes `manifest.file-hash` or `manifest.signature-invalid`. |
| [PKG-506] | Run `verify` and install the file on a clean machine before you upload. |

## Publish

```
ILIUM_REGISTRY_TOKEN=... ilium plugin publish dist/com.example.git-tools-1.4.2.iliumpkg --registry https://plugins.example.com
```

The server repeats the checks and, at review level B, a person looks at it. Your version appears in `index.json` after approval.

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| [PKG-507] | A publish limit of 20 per hour per publisher applies (PKG-400). |
| [PKG-508] | Start new plugins on the `beta` channel with `--channel beta`, then publish a later version to `stable` once beta users report no problems. |

## After publishing

- To withdraw a bad version, run `ilium plugin yank <id>@<version> --reason "<text>"`. Installed copies keep working.
- To retire a plugin, run `deprecate` with `--successor`.
- Never delete a blob. Takedown is the registry operator's decision (PKG-403).

## Edge cases

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Same version published twice | `registry.version-exists`, exit 1 |
| Unsigned package | `publish.unsigned`, exit 1 |
| Namespace not yours | `registry.namespace-unowned` |
| Two builds differ | See Reproducible builds |
| Token expired | `registry.auth`, exit 1 |

## See also

- [Distribution commands](/pages/reference-plugin-distribution-cli/)
- [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/)
- [Registry reference](/pages/reference-registry/)
- [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/)

# Quality checklist

## Quality checklist

This guide is the review list an author runs before each release. Every item says what to check, which command checks it, and what no command can check. The rule codes are those of [Check and lint rules](/pages/reference-check-and-lint-rules/). Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-400` to `AUT-499`.

### How to use the list

Work top to bottom. The first five sections can be run by a machine. The last three need a person. A release is ready when every item is checked or has a written reason in `lint.toml` or in the release notes.

A release MUST have no `check` error and no unsuppressed `lint` error. [AUT-401]

A release SHOULD pass `ilium plugin lint --deny warnings`, and every suppression SHOULD carry a reason that a reviewer can read. [AUT-402]

## 1. Package and manifest

| Item | Command | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Manifest is valid and complete | `ilium plugin check` | `manifest.*` codes |
| Components exist for every declared side | `check` | `component.missing`, `component.invalid` |
| Exports match the manifest | `check` | `manifest.exports-mismatch` |
| SDK version matches `api` | `check` | `manifest.api-version` |
| `description` is one paragraph of 280 characters or less | `lint` | `lint.description-missing` |
| `license` is an SPDX expression and `LICENSE` exists | `lint` | `lint.license-missing`, `lint.license-file-missing` |
| `unstable` is empty | `lint` | `lint.unstable-feature` |
| Package is below 100 MiB | `lint` | `lint.package-size-near-cap` |
| Release build, no debug information | `lint` | `lint.debug-info-in-release` |

A plugin SHOULD NOT list an `unstable` feature in a release, because the shape of that feature can change without a major version. [AUT-403]

## 2. Grants and privacy

| Item | Command | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| No grant without a use | `lint` | `lint.grant-unused` |
| Every grant is explained in the README | `lint` | `lint.grant-unexplained` |
| High-risk grants are needed | `lint` | `lint.high-risk-grants` |
| The plugin works when each optional grant is refused | Test | none |
| No secret or whole payload in a log line | Review | none |

A plugin MUST request the smallest grant set that works, and every grant MUST be explained in the README with the feature that needs it. [AUT-404]

A plugin MUST handle `not-permitted` for every call of an optional grant and MUST keep working with a reduced feature set. [AUT-405]

## 3. Resource use

| Item | Command | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Limits are inside the tier ceiling | `lint` | `lint.limit-above-ceiling` |
| No `startup` activation without need | `lint` | `lint.activation-startup` |
| Contribution lists are not near their cap | `lint` | `lint.contribution-near-cap` |
| Handlers stay below deadlines | `dev --timings`, `stats` | none |
| Render stays below 10 ms for the largest realistic view | `profile` | none |
| Memory stays below 80 percent of `memory_mib` | `stats` | none |

A plugin SHOULD keep every measured use below 80 percent of its limit on the largest realistic data set, because the limit is a trap, not a warning. See [Performance](/pages/performance/). [AUT-406]

## 4. Views and keys

| Item | Command | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Every interactive widget has a `key` | `lint` | `lint.widget-missing-key` |
| Every declared view renders with an empty fixture | `lint` | `lint.render-trap` |
| Dedup keys use the allowed characters | `lint` | `lint.dedup-key-charset` |
| Icon names exist | `lint` | `lint.icon-name-unknown` |

A plugin MUST give every interactive widget a stable `key`. [AUT-407]

## 5. Documentation

| Item | Command | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` exist | `lint` | `lint.readme-missing`, `lint.changelog-missing` |
| Help topic for every command, pane kind, panel and settings page | `lint` | `lint.help-topic-missing`, `lint.settings-help-missing` |
| Help titles equal the manifest titles | `lint` | `lint.help-title-mismatch` |
| Help links resolve | `lint` | `lint.help-link-broken` |
| Topics are 20 KiB or less | `lint` | `lint.help-topic-too-large` |
| Extension points are documented | `lint` | `lint.extension-point-undocumented` |

See [Plugin documentation guide](/pages/guide-plugin-documentation/).

## 6. Behaviour (tests)

No lint rule can tell whether a plugin is correct. These tests are the minimum.

| Test | What it proves |
|---|---|
| Activate and deactivate | Both finish inside their deadlines and leave no state behind |
| Every command with empty and with large input | No trap, no timeout |
| Every `err` code the plugin can receive | The user sees a sentence, not a crash |
| Restart (`restart_with`) | State comes back from restore bytes or storage |
| Whole batch of events | Handlers do not assume one event per call |
| Upgrade from the previous release | `migrator` keeps old data. See [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/). |

A plugin MUST have at least one test for activation, one for deactivation and one for each error code that its code handles. [AUT-408]

A plugin that changes the layout of stored data MUST test the upgrade from the previous release with a storage snapshot of that release. [AUT-409]

## 7. Accessibility and appearance

No command checks these. Use [Accessibility and theming](/pages/accessibility-and-theming/).

| Item | Check |
|---|---|
| Colour roles only | No hard-coded colours. Use the nine colour roles. |
| Meaning without colour | Every status has a word or a glyph, not only a colour |
| Reduced motion | Animation stops or slows when the host asks |
| Density | Layout works in compact and comfortable density |
| Icon mode | Every icon has a text fallback |
| Width | A view is usable at 40 columns |
| Wide text | Widths use display width, not byte or character counts. See [Internationalisation](/pages/guide-internationalisation/). |

A plugin MUST NOT use colour as the only carrier of meaning. [AUT-410]

## 8. Support and release

| Item | Check |
|---|---|
| Version raised, changelog entry written | Manual |
| New grants and `data_version` named in the release notes | Manual |
| Package passes `ilium plugin verify` | Command |
| Package installed once on a clean profile, log read | Manual |
| Key kept offline, package signed last | Manual |
| Contact address in the README | Manual |

See [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/).

## What the tools cannot check

| Gap | What to do |
|---|---|
| Correct behaviour | Tests (section 6) |
| Good wording of messages | Read them aloud |
| Accessibility | Section 7 by hand |
| Performance on a real session | `profile` and `stats` on a large project |
| Interaction with other plugins | Install the most common ones together |

## Suppressing a rule

A suppression lives in `lint.toml` with a rule, an optional `key_path` and a reason. A suppression without a reason is an error (`lint.suppression-reason-missing`). One that matches nothing is a warning (`lint.suppression-unused`). Prefer fixing over suppressing.

## Edge cases

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| No fixtures | Fixture-based rules print `lint.skipped` |
| Rule not known to an old CLI | `lint.suppression-unknown` on the suppression |
| Warning is wrong for the plugin | Suppress it with a reason |
| `check` passes, install fails | Look at the install code index in [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/) |

## See also

- [Check and lint rules](/pages/reference-check-and-lint-rules/)
- [Testing plugins](/pages/testing/)
- [Performance](/pages/performance/)
- [Security](/pages/security/)
- [CI recipes](/pages/guide-ci-recipes/) to run the list on every commit
- [Troubleshooting](/pages/guide-troubleshooting/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Troubleshooting for authors

## Troubleshooting for authors

This page lists problems an author meets, by the symptom seen and by the phase of work: build, install, activation, run time, update and release. Each row gives the likely cause and the fix. Users who meet a problem with a plugin they installed should read [Troubleshooting for users](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) and [Safe mode and troubleshooting](/pages/user-safe-mode-and-troubleshooting/).

Requirement ids of this page are in the range `AUT-800` to `AUT-899`.

### First steps for every problem

1. Run `ilium plugin check` and `ilium plugin lint`. They find many causes without running the plugin.
2. Read the log: `ilium plugin logs <id> --tail 100`.
3. Read the state: `ilium plugin status <id>`.
4. For a slow plugin, run `ilium plugin stats <id>` and `ilium plugin profile <id>`.
5. Reproduce it in a test on the fake host. A bug without a test returns.

An author SHOULD turn every fixed run-time bug into a test before the next release. [AUT-801]

## Build

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `component.missing` from `check` | A declared side was not built | Run `ilium plugin build`, and check `side` in the manifest |
| `component.invalid` | The file is not a WebAssembly component (a plain module) | Use the SDK build command, not `rustc` alone |
| `component.world-mismatch` | The component was built for another world than the manifest names | Make `world` and the SDK entry agree |
| `manifest.api-version` | The SDK that built the component is another version than `api` | Rebuild with the SDK of the contract you target |
| `manifest.exports-mismatch` | The exports differ from the manifest list | Update `exports` or the code, then rebuild |
| `component.import-ungranted` | Code calls a function whose grant the side does not request | Add the grant to the correct side, or remove the call |
| `component.import-unknown` | The code imports something outside the contract | Use SDK imports only. Check for a host-specific crate |
| `component.size-warning` | A component is over 8 MiB | Strip dependencies, build `--release`. Above 32 MiB it is an error |
| Build passes, `lint.debug-info-in-release` | A debug build was packed | Pack after `build --release` |

## Install

The install stages are listed in [Package format](/pages/reference-package-format/). Run `ilium plugin verify <file>` first. It runs the stages offline. The complete code list is the install code index in [Errors and limits reference](/pages/reference-errors-and-limits/).

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.unknown-key` | A key not in the schema, often a typo | Compare with [Manifest reference](/pages/reference-manifest/) |
| `manifest.key-missing` | A packed manifest has no `files` | Run `ilium plugin pack`, which writes it |
| `manifest.id-invalid` or `manifest.id-reserved` | Bad id pattern, or an `ilium.` id | Use a reverse-domain id you control |
| `manifest.file-unlisted`, `manifest.file-missing` | The package and `files` disagree | Run `pack` again after the last change |
| `manifest.file-length`, `manifest.file-hash` | A file changed after `pack` | Run `pack` again |
| `manifest.signature-invalid` | The manifest changed after signing | Sign last |
| `manifest.publisher-mismatch` or `manifest.id-publisher` | The `publisher` or the id prefix differs from the key | Use the publisher id of the key as the id prefix |
| `manifest.grant-unknown` | A misspelled or removed grant | Check [Capabilities](/pages/capabilities/) |
| `manifest.grant-tier` | A grant only for bundled plugins | Remove it, or ship another way |
| `manifest.grant-dependency` | A grant that needs a companion | Request both (for example `process.long-lived` needs `process.run:<program>`) |
| `package.version-reused` | Same version, other bytes | Raise the version |
| `package.downgrade` | An older version than the installed one | Raise the version, or use `--allow-downgrade` in testing |
| `package.api-unsupported` | `api` is outside the window of this Ilium | Build for a contract this Ilium supports. See [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) |
| `package.platform-unsupported` | T2 or T3 on Windows or macOS | Use Linux for these tiers |
| Install asks to trust a key | The key is not in the trust store | `ilium plugin trust add publisher.pub` after checking the fingerprint |
| Install refused without a message | The user declined the review dialog | Run again and read the dialog |

An author MUST read the code in an install error before changing anything, because each code names one cause. [AUT-802]

## Activation

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin never starts | Lazy activation, and nothing used a contribution | Invoke a command, or add a trigger to `activation` |
| `activate` times out (2 s) | Slow work in `activate` | Return at once. Start the work as a request. See [Lifecycle](/pages/lifecycle/) |
| `activate` traps | A call failed and the code unwrapped the error | Handle every `Result` |
| Plugin starts but timers are gone | Timers are lost on restart | Arm timers in `activate` every time |
| `not-permitted` at start | The user declined an optional grant | Run with a reduced feature set |
| Server side active, client side not | Each side activates on its own | Check `activation` and the log of each side |
| `pane-not-ready` | A call on a pane that is still starting | Wait for the pane event and retry |
| Migration fails and the old version returns | `migrator` returned an error or trapped | Fix `migrator`. The backup was restored. See [Data migration](/pages/guide-data-migration/) |
| `migration.data-newer` | An older plugin met data from a newer version | Install the newer version, or run the command again with `--restore-backup` or `--discard-data` |

## Run time

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin disabled after three failures in 10 minutes | Repeated traps | Fix the first trap in the log. Then `ilium plugin reset-failures <id>` |
| Event handler trap on time | A handler ran over 20 ms (50 ms for T1) | Move slow work to jobs or requests |
| Command trap on time | Over 50 ms | Return a pending state and finish later |
| Render trap | `render` over 10 ms, or a tree over its limit | Cut the tree. See [Performance](/pages/performance/) |
| Tree over 4,096 nodes or 1,024 KiB | Too many rows | Window the list. See [Patterns cookbook](/pages/guide-patterns-cookbook/) |
| `quota-exceeded` | A limit is full (storage, timers, requests) | Free space, or lower use |
| `rate-limited` | Toast, status segment or request rate | Coalesce updates |
| `busy` | The host is serving too many requests | Retry with backoff |
| `timed-out` | A request ran past its limit | Make the work smaller or use a job |
| `conflict` on a submission | The state changed since it was read | Read again and retry |
| `duplicate` outcome | The same `dedup-key` was seen in 10 minutes | This is correct for a retry. Use a new key for new work |
| `unsupported` | The host or the target does not offer it | Check before use and degrade |
| Memory trap | Over `memory_mib` (32 MiB by default) | Free large buffers. Raise the limit in `limits` only inside the tier ceiling |
| Widget loses its selection on every render | Missing or changing `key` | Give a stable `key` |
| A list shows all rows after scroll | Reading `selected` and `offset` as your own state | These are host-owned. Read with `ui.widget-state` |
| Timer never fires in a test | The fake host does not run timers by itself | Call `advance_clock(ms)`, then `settle()` |
| State gone after a crash | State was only in memory | Write restore bytes or storage |
| Text misaligned for wide characters | Width counted in characters | Use `display-width`. See [Internationalisation](/pages/guide-internationalisation/) |

## Update

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Update stays on the old version | A failed stage rolled back | Read `ilium plugin logs <id>` and the update result |
| Old settings lost | A settings key was renamed | Keep old keys, or migrate them |
| Old data unreadable | Layout changed with no `migrator` | Raise `data_version` and add `migrator`. See [Compatibility and upgrades](/pages/guide-compatibility-and-upgrades/) |
| Users asked to review grants again | A new grant was added | Expected. Say so in the release notes |
| A command no longer works for users | Its id changed | Keep the old id as a hidden alias |

## Release

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Users cannot verify the package | No SHA-256 or fingerprint published | Publish both. See [Publishing and support](/pages/guide-publishing-and-support/) |
| `sign.key-permissions` | The key file is readable by others | `chmod 600` the key |
| `trust.key-exists` | `keygen` found existing key files | Choose another `--out` folder |
| Users report a problem you cannot see | Traces are redacted | Ask for `logs`, `status` and `stats`, not unredacted traces |

## When it still fails

`ilium plugin bisect` halves the set of enabled third-party plugins, so it finds a plugin that clashes with yours. Start Ilium in safe mode to see whether a third-party plugin is the cause. See [Safe mode and troubleshooting](/pages/user-safe-mode-and-troubleshooting/). A report to the host project SHOULD contain the Ilium version, the plugin id and version, the manifest, the last 100 log lines and a test that reproduces it. [AUT-803]

## See also

- [Debugging](/pages/debugging/) and [Debugging tools](/pages/reference-debugging-tools/)
- [Errors and limits](/pages/errors-and-limits/)
- [Quality checklist](/pages/guide-quality-checklist/)
- [FAQ](/pages/guide-faq/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Core plugins for users

## Core plugins for users

Everything Ilium does is done by a plugin. The 30 core plugins ship with Ilium, need no install and are maintained by the Ilium project. This page tells you what each one does in plain words, what you lose when you turn it off, which ones other plugins may replace, and what happens to your data when you do. If you write plugins, read [Core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/) instead.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[USR-nnn]`, collected in [User and administrator requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-user-admin/).

<div class="note">
<p>Decision status. Which core plugins a user may turn off is a pending decision. The column "Can you turn it off" below is the proposal. The two rules that are not pending: a core plugin never needs an install, and the kernel recovery page can never be turned off or replaced.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- What a core plugin is for you
- The 30 core plugins
- Turning one off
- Replacing one
- What a replacement does to your data
- Updates
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### What a core plugin is for you

You do not have to know about core plugins to use Ilium. They are the parts of the program, split so that each part has one job and a documented edge. The split gives you three things.

- You can turn a feature off if you never use it. The feature disappears from menus, keys and settings.
- You can see and change a feature's permissions like any other plugin's. A core plugin is fully trusted (T1) but it uses the same permission rules for high-risk abilities. See [Permissions explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/).
- Another plugin can add to a core plugin, for example a step that runs after Smart Copy, or can replace it. See [The Extensions tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/).

Core plugins have ids of the form `ilium.core.<name>`. They appear in **Settings > Plugins** with the tier T1 and the badge `core`. They do not appear in a package list, because they have no package.

- [USR-040] The Plugins tab and `ilium plugin list` MUST list all 30 core plugins with the tier T1, and MUST NOT offer to install or uninstall one. Test: list plugins on a fresh profile, count 30 rows with ids `ilium.core.*`, and try `ilium plugin uninstall ilium.core.tree`, which must fail with `plugin.not-removable`.

### The 30 core plugins

The column "Can you turn it off" is a proposal, see the decision status above. "Replaceable" says whether a third-party plugin may take over the job with `replaces`.

#### Tree and panes

| Plugin | What it does for you | If you turn it off | Can you turn it off | Replaceable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tree (`ilium.core.tree`) | The project tree: groups, folders, moving, renaming, bookmarks, locks | The tree stops working. Ilium has nothing to show | no | yes |
| Layout (`ilium.core.layout`) | Split views, focus, moving between panes, resizing with the mouse | Panes can no longer be arranged | no | yes |
| Terminal (`ilium.core.terminal`) | Terminal panes: processes, scrollback, input, links | No terminal panes | no | yes |
| Smart Copy (`ilium.core.smart-copy`) | Selecting text, the right-click menu and Smart Copy | Plain selection only | yes | yes |
| Editor (`ilium.core.editor`) | Editor panes, highlighting, Markdown view, file explorer | Editor panes show a placeholder | yes | yes |
| Kanban (`ilium.core.kanban`) | Board panes backed by Markdown files | Board panes show a placeholder | yes | yes |

#### Agents

| Plugin | What it does for you | If you turn it off | Can you turn it off | Replaceable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent detection (`ilium.core.agent-detect`) | Knows which coding agent runs in a pane and whether it works, waits or is idle | No agent badges or states. Features that use them go quiet | yes | yes |
| Agent toolbar (`ilium.core.agent-toolbar`) | The last-prompt banner and per-agent buttons | The banner and buttons disappear | yes | yes |
| Fleet (`ilium.core.fleet`) | Send a message to many agents, the local HTTP API | `ilium` pane messaging and the HTTP API stop | yes | yes |
| Cost (`ilium.core.cost`) | Spend, quotas and session statistics | Spend indicators disappear | yes | yes |
| Titles and organisation (`ilium.core.titles`) | Automatic titles and AI tidying of the tree | Panes keep their names | yes | yes |

#### AI and alerts

| Plugin | What it does for you | If you turn it off | Can you turn it off | Replaceable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inference providers (`ilium.core.inference`) | Connects Ilium to AI providers and models | Every feature that uses AI stops. Plugins that ask for `inference` get `unavailable` | yes | yes |
| Notifications (`ilium.core.notifications`) | Sounds, desktop notifications, toasts, attention marks | No alerts | yes | yes |
| Voice (`ilium.core.voice`) | Voice control and speech output | No voice features | yes | yes |
| Scheduler (`ilium.core.scheduler`) | Scheduled input and the prompt queue | Scheduled items do not run | yes | yes |
| Text triggers (`ilium.core.text-triggers`) | Rules that watch terminal output and send text | The rules do not fire | yes | yes |

#### Work and sessions

| Plugin | What it does for you | If you turn it off | Can you turn it off | Replaceable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Progress (`ilium.core.progress`) | Progress monitors and `ilium wait` | Monitors stop reporting | yes | yes |
| Chatroom (`ilium.core.chatroom`) | The shared chat file between agents and `ilium chat` | `ilium chat` fails | yes | yes |
| Worktrees (`ilium.core.worktrees`) | Agents in Git worktrees and branch status | Worktree features disappear | yes | yes |
| Sessions (`ilium.core.sessions`) | Snapshots, restore, detach and reattach | Ilium cannot save or restore a session | no | no |
| Compaction (`ilium.core.compaction`) | Compacting agent context | The compaction features stop | yes | yes |

#### Settings and look

| Plugin | What it does for you | If you turn it off | Can you turn it off | Replaceable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Settings (`ilium.core.settings`) | The Settings screen, auto-save, guided setup | The Settings screen goes away and the recovery page is the only way to change plugins | no | no |
| Keys and help (`ilium.core.keys-and-help`) | The prefix key, key bindings, the key reference, help topics | Ilium keeps only the fixed kernel keys | no | yes |
| Workspace search (`ilium.core.search`) | One panel to find agents, terminals and files | No search panel | yes | yes |
| Ambient look (`ilium.core.ambient`) | Colour, palette and dither for backgrounds | Backgrounds lose the shared look | yes | yes |
| Scenes (`ilium.core.scenes`) | The animated background scenes | No animated backgrounds | yes | yes |
| Recap (`ilium.core.recap`) | `ilium recap`, short and long summaries of panes | `ilium recap` fails | yes | yes |
| Session conversion (`ilium.core.session-convert`) | Converts a transcript between agent formats | The converter command fails | yes | yes |
| Agent setup (`ilium.core.agent-setup`) | Installs the Chatroom and Progress instruction blocks into agent config files | No setup tab | yes | yes |
| Diagnostics (`ilium.core.diagnostics`) | File logging, log levels, the diagnostics report | No file logging | yes | yes |

A plugin you replace or turn off keeps its settings and data on disk. See [Plugin files on disk](/pages/reference-plugin-files/).

The two plugins that cannot be replaced, Settings and Sessions, hold data and roles that a replacement cannot take over safely. The kernel recovery page, which is not a plugin, can never be turned off or replaced either.

- [USR-041] The Plugins tab MUST refuse to turn off a core plugin marked "no" in the table, and MUST say why. Test: press Space on `ilium.core.tree` and assert the refusal text. (Pending decision: the set of "no" plugins.)
- [USR-042] A request to replace `ilium.core.settings` or `ilium.core.sessions` MUST fail at install with `manifest.replaces-not-replaceable`. Test: install a package with such a `replaces` entry.

### Turning one off

Open **Settings > Plugins**, select the core plugin and press `Space`. Or run `ilium plugin disable ilium.core.cost`. The feature disappears at once, with its menu items, keys and settings pages. Other plugins that need the feature show "Waiting for <owner>" and wake up when you turn it back on. Your settings and data stay.

Turning off a feature that other features use can have effects you did not expect. Example: with Agent detection off, features that react to an agent finishing, such as notifications about agents, get no events. The plugin page in Settings shows a list "Used by" before you confirm.

### Replacing one

A third-party plugin may declare `replaces` for a core plugin. That means: while this plugin is on, the built-in one is turned off. Ilium asks you to confirm every replacement. One plugin may replace at most 4 core plugins.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Replace a built-in plugin? ─────────────────╮</span>
│ Notes Titles wants to replace:               │
│                                              │
│   Titles and organisation                    │
│                                              │
│ While it is on, the built-in plugin is       │
│ off. Turning it off or removing it turns     │
│ the built-in plugin back on. The built-in    │
│ plugin's data stays and is not read.         │
│                                              │
│   [ Replace ]   [ Install without ]          │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The replace confirmation.</figcaption>
</figure>

- Choose **Replace** to confirm. The replacement then owns the job.
- Choose **Install without** to install the plugin and keep the built-in one. The replacement is not active.
- To undo a replacement later, turn the replacement off in the Plugins tab or uninstall it.

- [USR-043] Ilium MUST ask the user to confirm every `replaces` entry at install, MUST allow at most 4 entries, and MUST NOT replace without a yes. Test: install a package with 5 entries and assert the install is refused; with 1 entry assert the prompt and the choice **Install without**.

### What a replacement does to your data

The built-in plugin's data stays on disk, unread and unchanged. The replacement does not read it. It starts with its own data folder. If you turn the replacement off or remove it, the built-in plugin comes back and finds its data as it was.

If the replacement imports the old data on its own initiative, it needs a permission to do so, for example reading a path, and you see that in the review dialog.

### Updates

Core plugins are updated together with Ilium. You never update one on its own. When you update Ilium, every core plugin changes to the version inside it. Third-party plugins are unaffected. A third-party plugin built for an older interface version may be refused after an Ilium update with `api.window`. See [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/).

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| You uninstall a core plugin | Refused with `plugin.not-removable` (pending decision: code name). Turn it off instead |
| Two plugins replace the same core plugin | Only one can be on. Turning on the second turns off the first and tells you |
| A replacement fails three times | It is turned off by the usual rule and the built-in plugin comes back |
| You turn off a core plugin that a replacement needs | The replacement shows "Waiting for <owner>" |
| Your administrator blocks replacements | The install fails with `policy.blocked` |

### See also

- [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/)
- [The Extensions tab](/pages/user-extensions-tab/)
- [Core plugins](/pages/core-plugins/)
- [Extending core plugins](/pages/extending-core-plugins/)
- [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# The Extensions tab

## The Extensions tab

Plugins can add to what other plugins do. A plugin may add a step after Smart Copy copies text, a rule that checks a trigger before it sends, or a new entry in a list that another plugin keeps. The places where this is allowed are called extension points. The Extensions tab shows these additions for one plugin, lets you turn each one off, and lets you decide the order in which they run. This page explains the tab for users.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[USR-nnn]`, collected in [User and administrator requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-user-admin/). The technical reference is [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/).

<div class="note">
<p>Decision status. The platform is not implemented. The wording in the renders is a working text.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- Owners and contributors
- Open the tab
- The owner view
- The contributor view
- Change the order
- Turn an extension off
- The two special states
- What the host does to protect you
- Replacements
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### Owners and contributors

- The **owner** of an extension point is the plugin that offers it. Smart Copy owns "After copy". It runs the extensions at the right moment.
- A **contributor** is a plugin that adds an extension to a point it does not own.

One plugin can be both. Core plugins own many points: every core plugin page has an Extension points section, and [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/) lists all of them.

An extension is only an extension. It is not a permission. A contributor needs a permission to fill each point, and you see it in the install dialog in the group **Adds to other plugins**. Points marked high risk, such as a rule that can stop a trigger from sending text, start unchecked.

### Open the tab

1. Open Settings with `Ctrl+B` then `:`.
2. Choose **Plugins** and select a plugin.
3. Choose the **Extensions** tab.

The tab shows two lists: the points that the plugin owns, with everyone who contributes to them, and the extensions that the plugin contributes to other plugins. A plugin that neither owns a point nor contributes to one has no Extensions tab.

### The owner view

Select an owner such as Smart Copy. Each of its points lists the contributors in the order they run.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ Smart Copy &gt; Extensions ────────────────────╮</span>
│ After copy (transform)                       │
│  1 [x] com.example.tickets  strip_tokens     │
│  2 [x] com.example.redact   mask_emails      │
│  3 [ ] com.example.legacy   old_filter       │
│                                              │
│ Recognisers (collect)                        │
│    [x] com.example.tickets  jira-key         │
│                                              │
│ Up/Down move   Space on or off   r reset     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The owner view.</figcaption>
</figure>

The number is the place in the chain. `[x]` means on. `[ ]` means you turned it off. The word in brackets after the point name tells how the owner uses the extensions:

| Word | What the owner does |
|---|---|
| observe | Tells every contributor what happened. Their answers are ignored |
| transform | Passes the data from one contributor to the next, in order |
| veto | Asks each contributor in order whether to allow it, and stops at the first no |
| first | Asks each in order, and takes the first answer |
| collect | Gathers entries from all contributors into one list |

### The contributor view

Select a contributor such as `com.example.tickets`. The tab lists, for each point it fills, the owner and the point, with a switch.

<figure>
<pre class="term"><span class="t-hi">╭─ com.example.tickets &gt; Extensions ───────────╮</span>
│ Smart Copy &gt; After copy                      │
│   [x] strip_tokens                           │
│   stopped after 3 timeouts          [Reset]  │
│                                              │
│ Notes Plus &gt; Export hook                     │
│   [x] stamp_header                           │
│   waiting for com.example.notes-plus         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
</pre>
<figcaption>Rendered at 48 columns. Illustrative. The contributor view.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Change the order

By default extensions run in the order of their priority, a number the contributor sets. Lower runs first. A tie goes in plugin id order. You can override this. Select a row in the owner view and press `Up` or `Down`. The order you set is saved by Ilium, not by the plugin, and it wins over the priority. A new contributor goes to the end of your order.

- [USR-050] The Extensions tab MUST list contributors of each point in run order, MUST let the user move a contributor up or down, and the user's order MUST win over priority. Test: set priorities 10 and 20, move the second above the first, call the point, and assert the new order.
- [USR-051] The host, not the plugin, MUST store the user's order and the toggles, and MUST keep them across restarts. Test: reorder, restart, list.

### Turn an extension off

Press `Space` on a row. The extension stays installed but the owner does not call it. Your choice is saved and survives a restart, an update of the contributor and a turn-off and on of the contributor. It ends only when you turn the row on again, or when you uninstall the contributor. If the contributor is uninstalled, its entries are removed from your order.

Turning an extension off does not change the contributor's permissions.

### The two special states

**Waiting for <owner>.** The contributor adds to a point whose owner is not installed or is turned off. The extension does nothing and your switch keeps its setting. When the owner returns, the extension starts working again without any action from you. Installing a plugin never fails because its owner is missing.

**Stopped after 3 timeouts.** An extension must answer quickly: each one gets between 5 ms and 50 ms, 20 ms by default, and a whole chain gets 100 ms. A slow or failing extension is skipped for that call, as if it had said "no change". A veto extension that is slow never blocks. If an extension is slow or fails three times in a row, Ilium stops it, shows a notice, and the row reads "stopped after 3 timeouts" with a **Reset** button. The stop is not saved on disk. It ends when the contributor restarts or when you press Reset.

- [USR-052] A hook that times out, traps or errors MUST count as "no change", and a timeout MUST NOT block or veto. Test: let a veto handler sleep past its deadline and assert the action goes ahead.
- [USR-053] Three breaches in a row MUST stop the extension, MUST show a notice and a Reset button, and the stop MUST NOT be written to disk. Test: cause three breaches, restart the contributor, and assert the extension is active again.
- [USR-054] An extension whose owner is missing or off MUST show "waiting for <owner>" and MUST become active when the owner returns. Test: remove the owner, check the label, reinstall.

### What the host does to protect you

- A payload that goes to an extension is limited to 64 KiB. An extension sees only the data of the point and nothing else of the owner.
- An extension cannot call the point that is running it.
- An extension runs inside the contributor, with only the contributor's own permissions.
- The host logs every breach in the contributor's log. See [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/).

### Replacements

Instead of adding to a core plugin, a plugin may replace it. This is separate from extensions and asks you to confirm. See [Core plugins for users](/pages/user-core-plugins/).

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Two contributors have the same priority | Plugin id order decides, until you set an order |
| You turn off the owner | The extensions go dormant, "waiting for <owner>" |
| You turn on a contributor you had switched off | The row stays as you set it, and you switch it on |
| The contributor is stopped and you restart Ilium | The stop is gone. After three more breaches it stops again |
| A package adds to a point that does not exist | Install does not fail. The extension waits for the owner |
| Your administrator blocks a contributor | The row shows "Blocked by policy" and does nothing |

### See also

- [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/)
- [Core plugins for users](/pages/user-core-plugins/)
- [Extension points](/pages/api-extension-points/)
- [Core extension points](/pages/reference-core-extension-points/)
- [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.

# Plugin FAQ

## Plugin FAQ

Short answers to the questions users ask most about plugins. Each answer points to the page that explains it fully.

Contract version: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`. Requirement ids have the form `[USR-nnn]`, collected in [User and administrator requirements](/pages/reference-requirements-user-admin/).

<div class="note">
<p>Decision status. The platform is not implemented. Answers describe specified behaviour.</p>
</div>

### Contents

- Basics
- Installing
- Permissions
- Safety and privacy
- When things go wrong
- Administrators
- Errors and edge cases
- Requirements

### Basics

**Do I have to use plugins?** No. All 30 core plugins ship with Ilium and work as before. Third-party plugins are optional. See [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/).

**Is there a plugin store?** Only if you set up a registry. Ilium ships none and runs no central store (decisions D3 and D27). See [Plugin store](/pages/user-plugin-store/). A plugin is a `.iliumpkg` file that someone gives you. Ilium never searches for plugins. See [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/).

**Do plugins work on Windows and macOS?** Only the bundled plugins. A third-party plugin is refused at install with "Cannot install <name> <version>." The sandbox that makes third-party plugins safe exists on Linux only. See [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/#where-plugins-run).

**What is the difference between T1, T2 and T3?** T1 are plugins from the Ilium project, built in. T2 are signed by a publisher you trust. T3 are unsigned and show a `dev` badge. T2 and T3 run in a sandbox.

**Can I write a plugin?** Yes. Start at [What a plugin is](/pages/getting-started-overview/). This FAQ is for users.

### Installing

**How do I install a plugin?** `ilium plugin install file.iliumpkg`, or Settings > Plugins > Install from file. See [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/).

**Do I need administrator rights?** No. Everything is stored in your own folders. A policy file, which only an administrator can write, may limit what you can install.

**What does "trust a publisher" mean?** You tell Ilium that packages signed with a key come from a person or company you believe. Check the fingerprint with them by a second route. Removing a key later does not remove the plugins.

**Why does the install ask so many questions?** Each question is one decision only you can make: trust a key, accept each permission, accept a replacement of a built-in feature.

**Can I install an unsigned plugin?** Yes, with `--allow-unsigned`, but only on Linux. Do it only for a plugin you built or read.

**Does Ilium update plugins by itself?** No. You get the new file and install it. The dialog shows only the new permissions. See [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/#update-a-plugin).

### Permissions

**What if I say no to a permission?** The plugin still installs and runs. The calls that need the permission fail, and the plugin may show less. See [Permissions explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/).

**Can I change my mind later?** Yes, in the plugin's Capabilities tab or with `ilium plugin grants`. A permission you turn off takes effect at once.

**What does HIGH mean?** The permission can read private text, act for you, run programs or change much. HIGH rows start unchecked.

**Are permissions per project?** No. They belong to you and the plugin. Giving `fs.read:project` once lets the plugin read the project folder of whichever project is open.

**Why does a plugin ask for a permission it does not seem to need?** Ask the plugin's author. If there is no good answer, leave the row unchecked.

### Safety and privacy

**Can a plugin read my files?** Only the folders you granted, and its own folders. See [Plugin privacy](/pages/user-privacy/).

**Can a plugin send my terminal text to a website?** Only if you granted both a way to read it and a network host. Think about the combination.

**Does Ilium send anything about my plugins?** No. See [Plugin privacy](/pages/user-privacy/#what-ilium-itself-sends).

**Can a plugin change the install dialog?** No. Ilium draws it. A plugin cannot draw or restyle it.

**Can a plugin hide the recovery page?** No. The kernel recovery page can never be replaced.

### When things go wrong

**A plugin shows Failed.** It failed three times in 10 minutes. Read its log, then turn it on again. See [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/).

**Ilium misbehaves after I installed a plugin.** Start with `ilium --safe-mode`. All third-party plugins are off for the run. Then use `ilium plugin bisect start` to find the one.

**A pane says the plugin is not installed.** The plugin that made the pane was removed. Install it again to get the pane back, or close the pane.

**An update failed.** Ilium puts the old version back and says "Update failed, rolled back".

**A plugin says "Waiting for <owner>".** It adds to a plugin that is off or missing. Turn the owner on or install it.

**Can I get back my notes after I uninstalled?** Yes, if you did not use `--purge`. Reinstall the same plugin and it reads its data again.

### Administrators

**Can I stop users from installing plugins?** Yes, with the policy file. See [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/) and [Plugin policy](/pages/reference-plugin-policy/).

**Can I allow only signed plugins from my company?** Yes. Set `allowed_tiers` and `allowed_publishers`.

**Can I see what was installed?** Turn on the audit log in the policy.

### Errors and edge cases

| Situation | Answer |
|---|---|
| The question is not here | Read [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/) or the page for the topic |
| You have a plugin you no longer trust | Turn it off, then uninstall it with `--purge`, then remove the key with `ilium plugin trust remove` |
| You lose the package file | Installed plugins keep working. Keep the file if you want to reinstall on another machine |

### Requirements

- [USR-110] The documentation MUST answer, in this FAQ, whether a store exists, which systems run third-party plugins, what declining a permission does, and how to leave a bad plugin behind. Test: search the page for each of the four answers.

### See also

- [Plugins for users](/pages/user-plugins-overview/)
- [Install and manage plugins](/pages/user-install-and-manage/)
- [Permissions explained](/pages/user-permissions-explained/)
- [Plugin privacy](/pages/user-privacy/)
- [Troubleshooting plugins](/pages/user-troubleshooting/)
- [Administration guide](/pages/guide-administration/)

API version checked: `ilium:plugin@0.1.0`.
